title: Affordable fatbike mount.
text:
This mount was exactly what I needed. I had built a fork mount roof rack for my fatbike out of an old Thule rack. I originally used a sunlite fatbike fork mount, but after the nut fell off that mount and not being able to buy a new one, I had to replace the whole unit.
I bought the 135mm X 9mm fork mount. This fits fatbike forks with 135mm spacing with quick release. I have. 2014 Specialized fatboy and it fits perfect. It won't fit through axle forks like the Bluto which are 150mm X 15mm. This mount does not come with a 135mm skewer, so you can either buy an extra, or use the one from your wheel. The rear wheels of most mountain bikes is 135mm so they are pretty common and affordable. The fork rests on two short metal tubes the same size as your axle, and just like your axle the skewer goes through the metal tubes to anchor your fork to the mount. This design is ingenious. There has been mention of misalignment in other reviews, mine did not have that problem. If the skewer falls off or someone steals it, you only have to replace the skewer and not the whole unit. This mount is good quality and should last awhile.

title: Decent value but burner isn't great
text:
Overall, it's a decent little kit for the price. It has pretty much everything one might need at a budget price. However, I have two issues:
1) I can't get the burner to stay lit at more than halfway up. It lights ok but not always on the first strike. The real problem begins when I turn the control past what I would consider "halfway". It begins to sputter and goes out, every single time. Seems to burn fine at the low settings. I can't recommend this kit unless you already have a mini-burner that you like.
2) The lid/top of the cook set doesn't snap into place by any means that I can find. The smaller cup simply sits atop the larger cup. Several times I have attempted to pick up the unit only to have the top come away in my hand. It's not a major problem but I do find it annoying.

title: Solid board for the price.
text:
This is a great first board. It provides a stable ride, and it very sturdy. It looks exactly as pictured.

The wheels are solid, although they don't work well on rougher pavement. The bearings are great out of the box, but after the first ride, they lost their luster. Now on rougher surfaces, I find myself pushing a lot more than I should, so I will be cleaning and or replacing the bearings. This doesn't bother me too much, however, since good bearings are cheap.

The trucks come pre-set to a great tightness setting for a beginner, which is always nice to see. Obviously you can adjust them, but I had no problem turning, while still feeling stable pushing.

Overall, this was a great board. Would definitely recommend buying.

title: Great kayak! Winner on lakes, bays, and the ocean.
text:
I purchased this kayak primarily for bays and lakes, but now that I've braved the ocean with it, I'm convinced this is a great, sturdy kayak! It is quite wide, so while initially it seems like it doesn't keep a straight line as well as the slimmer, hard-shell kayaks, I think this is a positive point for intermediate/casual users like myself. Out on the ocean, the kayak didn't rock too much, and withstood 2-3 foot swells with ease.

The only thing I don't really like is that it doesn't have any "machinery" for the clip-on seats with some back support. I've learned that wearing a small backpack helps with back support, but as is, the kayak is not "tall" enough for you to comfortably sit and lean into.

It is very easy to inflate and then put away, and I found all the instructions very self-evident. Overall, I think this is a great option for anyone looking to save a bit of room in their storage options, and appreciates a bit of a wider load for stability and speed.

title: Pointless, a case of 10 is available here for less than half the price per.
text:
The manufacturer of these sells them on Amazon for under $5 apiece in a 10-piece kit.

The variety isn't great and I hate the shortbread cookie (they all come with an oatmeal cookie, a shortbread cookie, two brown sugar poptarts, peanut butter and strawberry jam, some amazing vegetable crackers and two random "mains" that are also vegetarian and surprisingly great) but as a while, these are a great day's worth of food.

I only wish they came with a coffee and/or tea. But still, just buy a case. they're perfectly edible and less than half the price of this seller.

title: Barebones but truly fantastic for camping, occasional meal planning and your emergency home kit
text:
Firstly, all of mine were well within their expiration date and I got 2 of all meals 1-5. For your home emergency kit, these are a great budget option. They were all completely fresh and nothing was stale or poorly packaged.

They're all also vegetarian, but I found the mains to still be super satisfying.

Personally I think they're such a ridiculously good value that I find myself eating one every week or two, spread across the week.

They are very spartan - a tiny bit more than they need to be, IMO. I'd have paid an extra $0.50-$1.00 for them to include a coffee and tea bag (they come with sugar but no beverage) as well as one more package of vegetable crackers or just all that instead of a cookie, since all the mains pair insanely well with the vegetable crackers. The matches work, but suck (but that hardly matters, we aren't living in refugee camps) and the spoon is of good quality, it comes with black pepper and red chili flakes (both of which are very welcome)

The variety is also pretty wanting and very over-heavy on the sweets, which is disappointing since the savory components are genuinely phenomenal - every one came with two unfrosted actual brand-name brown sugar/cinnamon pop tarts (my favorite, so no complaints there) as well as a shortbread cookie, oatmeal cookie, peanut butter and strawberry jam. The savory components are all vegetarian, with two retort pouches and a package of vegetable crackers.

As for the food taste itself, I'll start with the weak points. I don't have a huge sweet tooth, so I was a little disappointed in that part. The poptarts are exactly what you'd expect - Brown sugar/cinnamon is the only flavor I like, so that's great. The oatmeal cookie is very dry and dense but satisfying, not too sweet and the peanut butter helps it a lot. I was a lot less keen on the shortbread cookie, which was also very dry, dense, and not to my taste. It is palatable with the strawberry jam to take up some of the dryness, but it's not satisfying to me at all. The peanut butter and jam themselves are quite good.

Now for the strengths. The savory parts are the real standout. They're all vegetarian, and the portions seem small, but I'm not out fighting a war, so they work out to be absolutely perfect portions. I just had the vegetable barley stew with some triscuits and the oatmeal cookie + peanut butter for dinner since my wife's not home this evening, and I'm super full.

There are only a few different mains too, rice and vegetables, vegetable barley stew, "peas" and tomatoes (Black eye peas), etc. And they are all generally same-y, but with some of the crushed pepper, they've all got a lovely flavor and very satiating. They also all somehow make great dips for tortilla chips or crackers.

And the star of the HDR is the vegetable crackers. I genuinely wish I could buy those things by the case, they're straight up fantastic on their own - not dry, not stale, not bland, but they really elevate the mains with some crunch and more savory flavors. Seriously, I wish I knew where to buy them on their own, I'd never buy chips, saltines or triscuits again. The only downside is that you only get one pack per HDR and both rations really need them, so I wind up supplementing them with a tortilla or aforementioned triscuits.

I didn't notice them being "gassy" like another reviewer mentioned. I like meat, but I think that person might just need more fiber in their daily diet.

I find myself using about one a week on its own, bringing a little collapsible silicone bowl for microwaving the mains and a baggie of crackers or tortilla chips to supplement the vegetable crackers. I'll eat the poptarts if I don't have time to make breakfast, I'll have the cookies if I'm in the university library and studying, and I'll have a main for lunch a couple times a week. I carry my own hot-sauce, so a little of that also livens up the mains. The only way they could be better for this is if the shortbread cookie was replaced with a granola bar or another pack of those crackers (two big cookies a day is just too much), include some kind of beverage like instant coffee and/or tea, and if there was some way to (and this is truly a first world problem) make the retort pouches microwave-safe.

Oh, and the bags they come in are super sturdy and tolerate being knocked around like a champ.

So overall, for under $5 for an entire day's worth of calories, I'm seriously nitpicking. These are solid for camping, good to keep one or two in your car's emergency kit, and worth keeping a couple cases at home for your disaster kit. I find them a great way to have portion control for the occasional meal throughout the week, too. They were a godsend when I worked in the field as a paramedic and sometimes went an entire 12-24hrs without seeing my station.

Seriously though. It's an entire day's worth of pretty wholesome food for $5. The fact that it's edible at all is kind of insane.

title: Perfect upgrade for a cheap, heavy Ebike
text:
Walmart special hyper ride ebike that weighs like 65lbs had a habit of falling over with its stock kickstand if you put anything on its rack. This was a direct swap with one single screw, then adjusting the leg length to where it just brings the rear wheel off the ground.

Side benefit is it lets me service the thing, since my normal bike stand doesn't really like the 65lb chonk hanging on it. Makes removing the wheels and adjusting the chain much easier to just have a center stand.

Very easy to kick the bike up and off the stand.

Only complaint is my other ebike doesn't have a mounting hole on the bottom of the frame so I can't buy another one for that!

title: Stellar upgrade for tektro dual pivots
text:
My Ride1up V2's factory pads were finally wearing out so I did some research and heard that the salmon kool stop's were the business for rainy/cold weather. I commute in the insanely rainy Seattle weather and these were an immediate, very noticeable upgrade. They're quieter, grippier, have infinitely better feedback, clear the rain/debris from the rim faster, and the pad holders are a one-time investment, with the pads themselves being quite cheap.

If you have rim brakes, grab some kool stops.

title: Woo! they're back in stock so I can recommend them again!
text:
I don't know why this style of rack isn't everywhere, I've never found another one like it. The sides swing out and lock very, very securely, it was easy to fit to my belt-drive Ebike (ride1up V2 roadster) I only had to mount it inside the frame posts instead of outside. Other than that, some gentle bending of the seat post rods to maneuver around the rim brake caliper (they're good quality aluminum so bend them gently and slowly) and the rack fit right on the bike. It can hold a ton of weight, I've put enough groceries on the thing to make the bike quite literally not sit with the front wheel on the ground.

It's also plenty sturdy enough to pick the bike up by, I've been using the front of the rack as a hand hold for over a year now, climbing/descending multiple flights of stairs a day and the wings are still smooth and the finish pristine, despite 5 days a week hanging off the back end of a Fast Ferry, getting soaked in saltwater.

The post spacing and overall shape are perfect for a variety of panniers. I have a few different kinds with hooks and straps, and it's accepted them all. The only thing I might want different is it'd be nice if the wings locked in the down position - as it is, they just stay down with friction, which is fine unless you want to use the wing as a hook point for a bungee strap, in which case it will open up, so you have to go lower for a hook point. But it's only a minor issue and one I've learned to work around.

I get comments from other cyclists on the rack all the time and I always felt bad because it wasn't for sale for the better part of the last year. But now that it is, grab one!

title: Long term, incredibly reliable and durable
text:
I've had mine for over five years, thought it was a cute gimmick when I got it, but this thing WORKS. SO. WELL. I use it in my ultralight camping setup, have climbed Mt. Rainier with it, and nothing else even comes close to this at even twice the weight. I've never had it die on me, it still inflates and deflates easily, and the battery lasts for hours and hours, it doesn't even mind fairly muted sunlight. Two of these weigh less than a simple AA powered lantern and take up a quarter the space and provide 2-5 times the light (the reflector is what makes them so freaking good)

The plastic/vinyl is still soft and supple, holds its air, and hasn't discolored.

For a tent lantern, I cannot possibly think of a reason to use any other lantern.

title: Well made, holds a standard tac-flashlight perfectly.
text:
I use them with this flashlight [[ASIN:B072P61XJB Military Grade 5 Mode CREE XML T6 2000 Lumens Tactical Led Waterproof Flashlight - Get 2 for Only $19.95]] , and the pairing is perfect, these are light, just small enough, and fit on my thick belt securely.

I'm a paramedic, so my flashlights get a lot of use, and this gets open and used at least ten times a day. it's been a month now, and no issues. I gave the other flashlight/holster to my partner and he's reported zero issues either.

title: Might not be quite right for friction buckles
text:
Bought to replace the strap on a nylon work belt. It's nice enough material, has thusfar been rugged enough (hasn't started fraying after several months of use) but for my purposes, it's too thin to adequately lock on my friction belt buckle, and requires I double the material back through the belt buckle. It's not the end of the world, it's still plenty usable, and I'll definitely find other uses for it (the material itself seems quite well made) But for my purposes, it didn't work quite right, so have to knock one star off.

It's not paper thin, just not super thick like the old material on the belt was. If you need it to be softer and more flexible, this stuff is great.

Otherwise, happy with shipping and everything else.

title: Ridiculously amazing value for an ultralight chair.
text:
I've been wanting an ultralight chair since my buddy bought a mantis last year. A year ago these chairs were $150. Amazing how quickly a good idea disseminates.

Is it quite as nice in the fit/finish as the expensive ones? nope. But so far, it's got some great design features and doesn't feel rickety at all.

Goes together easily, every tube is elasticized to the hole. If the elastic ever breaks, you can still assemble it easily, so don't sweat that.

You assemble it by first putting the bottom of the chair on the posts (after you get all the posts stuck together) and then in the pockets where the upper poles mount are... two finger rings! absolutely genius! they make stretching the fabric tightly enough to fit the poles a breeze. Great little idea.

It's small enough to fit into a backpack but holds my 6'3, 180lb butt so comfortably. It's a good seating position, you can recline in it or sit hunched forward for eating, so the ergos are spot on. Very balanced to sit in, doesn't feel like you'll fall at all. Sure, it's a couple pounds, but when you get to camp and your friends are all sitting on a cold, wet log trying to find the good spot around the fire, you'll be lounging in comfort.

title: It's about as big as a chimney starter gets, ...
text: It's about as big as a chimney starter gets, but honestly, I want a starter that can hold an ENTIRE cooking session's worth of charcoal. It might work for briquettes, but I use chunk charcoal, and I have to use two loads to get a full grill on my modestly sized weber 22 inch kettle.

title: Very easy to put together
text: Fixed my backpack ladderlock that my puppy chewed to bits. Very easy to put together, I put a drop of medium duty loctite on the screw thread and it's stayed put for over a year with no indications of failing. Gets beaten on every day as a motorcycle pack.

title: great lenses for driving
text: Well made, great lenses for driving. I spend all day in an ambulance, and these shades are a lifesaver. about 4 months in, no strange issues or wear and tear to note.

title: Perfect (if Tiny) Bag!
text: I like this little guy. It's perfectly-sized for my vape mod and wallet, or phone and wallet... etc. You know. It's about *that* size. It's not going to hold a ton of stuff, but it will carry IMPORTANT things close to you, leaving your pockets free, and it looks good doing it. Check it out!

title: Better than nothing. Maybe.
text: Meh. I guess they were better than nothing, but I was working in 30° temps in insulated boots and I thought my toes were going to freeze off. I never felt heat from them. Ever. But maybe it would have been worse without them.

title: Another Awesome Bassdash Product!
text:
I love this fly case! It's light, closes tightly, and is the perfect size. I have several fly boxes, but there's always something about them I don't like. Some are too thick, some don't hold flies very well, some are just awkward to use. This one doesn't have any of those drawbacks.

I also enjoy the fact that I can open this box one-handed. It's easy to get in and out of, and that's important when you're on the water.

The silicone material used to hold the flies is is nice and firm, and the slits are nice and deep, and will hold your flies tightly and securely.

You can't go wrong with this box. It looks nice, is easy to use, and works very well. Grab yourself a couple today!

title: VERY High Quality Gaiter! Get you some!
text:
Buying neck gaiters is always a gamble. You never know what you're going to get. Some of them are thick, high quality accessories that protect you from the elements, abs some are nothing more than cotton tubes that stretch and fall apart. These Bassdash gaiters are definitely the former.

I've had gaiters that feel just like someone cut the sleeves off of a tshirt, but since I work outside all day and fish hard when I'm not at work, I need good gaiters that will keep the wind, sun, add other elements off of my face. That's why I trust Bassdash. They don't put trash out. Everything of theirs that I've bought has been fantastic, and this is no different. Buy with confidence!

Edit: I just hit the water this morning. 27°plus wind. This gaiter was AWESOME! My fingers nearly froze off, but my face was nice and (relatively) toasty. The best part about the Gaiter was that it wasn't all wet from my breathing when I took it off. I've tried a lot of them that seem to collect moisture. This one wicks it really well and lets it evaporate. I'll be buying more of these for sure!

title: Hands Down THE BEST Arm Sleeves on Amazon!
text:
I work 10-12 hours a day, and I'm outside in between white concrete structures all day. It's like being in an oven and I go home burned every day. I've purchased sleeves from probably 7 different vendors and have been profoundly disappointed with them all. Too thin, too short, too cheap feeling, it just a basic failure of quality control in the "finished" product. But I kept buying them in the hopes that I'd find a decent brand because I NEED them. Even in December, the sun will be strong enough to burn in 30 minutes even if it's below freezing.

So I decided to try these SHINYMOD sleeves, and I'm so happy I did! They are amazing. Nice seams, soft, and stretchy enough that even when I have them pulled all the way up to my shoulder (and I have long arms), they are still not all the way stretched.

These are NOT light material, at least when compared to the dozens of other pairs I've purchased. But even though they are a little thicker, they do an incredible job of wicking sweat add c you have lots of room to adjust.

The thumbholes are super cool, abs like everything else about them, the perfect details come together to make the PERFECT product. Buy these. You'll be glad you did.

title: Fantastic Floating Fly Line
text: This is great stuff. Cats and shoots very well, turns over reliably, and floats like it's supposed to.

title: Best leaders I've ever used
text: Title says it all. They're thin, light, pliable, and STRONG. These leaders have saved my life on more than one occasion when I know a big fish would have snapped me off (I know from experience). Buy a pack and check them out

title: ASTONISHING Value in this Rod. I WANT MORE
text:
You see all of these reviews and they all start to sound the same, so I'll tell you where I'm coming from, my thoughts on the rod, and give my verdict.
I love fishing. There's nothing I'd rather do on the whole world. Nothing. You know what I mean... Lol! I've been fishing for decades, but have only been fly fishing for 3 years or so. I have several spinning rods in the $100-$200 range, and they are amazing. Unfortunately a $200 fly rod isn't the same as a $200 spinning rod. You can easily spend $3000 on a high end fly rod!

Well, I don't want to. I don't think it's necessary. But I've been fishing long enough that I can feel a great rod when I handle one. That's good, because I've seen lots of very expensive rods that were trash, and a few hidden gems that punched WAY above their weight. The Maxcatch Premiere line is one of those hidden gems. I picked this 3WT up just to check out, and after I effortlessly my fly 55' and landed it precisely where I wanted it. Over and over again. I mean it is so accurate that it's almost boring lol! And it's a $55 rod!

The blank is very sensitive, very light, very well finished and attractive, and the cork and dark chromed accents are beautiful. I'm surprised at how nice the cork is at this price point!

So I fish. A lot. I used to sell fishing equipment for a living, and I've handle a lot of gear. Is this Maxcatch a Loop or high end Sage? No. But it's also not $400-$900. However, I'd put this up against ANY Reddington, Fenwick, or lower end Sage any day and put money on the Maxcatch.

Get this rod. You'll be glad you did. You'll catch a ton of fish if you do your part, because this is a magnificent tool at an amazing price!

EDIT: I caught that monster 'Bow on the 4wt. Great fight! The rod was bent in half for 5 minutes, and held up great. And I felt every run, head shake, and dive. Great rods!

title: My favorite Tippet
text: I go through a fair amount of tippet and I've tried them all. Tippet can get expensive, but it's a necessity. This SA stuff is by far the best in my opinion. The spools interlock easily yet spin freely, the line has great abrasion resistance, low stretch, And simply put you can count on it to work. Great knot strength, too

title: Best vest at amazing price!
text:
This vest is absolutely incredible! I love the endless uses and storage solutions it provides. It comfortably carries my box of nymphs, box of dries, box of streamers, tippet holder, nipper, two hemostats, two spare reels, gloves, suntan lotion, trash bag (for the garbage other people leave on the water), my self defense solution, and still has room for more. I'm a big guy, but this vest is adjustable to fit me whether I'm wearing just a t shirt or even 3 layers plus a bulky jacket.

This is the best vest out there. Don't bother with any other vest. This is the one you need!

title: If you can't untangle fly line then you shouldn't be fly fishing.
text: Great line. I feel bad for these people who can't untangle the line from the spool. Even if this line gets Tangled up (as has happened to me even with SA line costing three times as much), you just take five minutes to untangle it. You simply cannot beat this line at this price

title: I'm Amazed at the Quality at this Price!!
text:
I ordered this Fishing on the Fly reel for a couple of reasons. The reel I keep my sinking line on took a dump last time I was on the water, and I needed something to replace it. I went with this because of its clicking on retrieve (my preference), it's design, and of course, its price.
It reviewed well, and I figured that even if half of what people said were true, it would be a decent reel for the "price" as people always say.
This isn't just a decent reel "at the price"; it's a nice reel. It would be a nice reel at twice the price, and perhaps even at 2.5x the price. I used to work at a big box Outfitter outlet with a tin green roof, and this EXACT reel, with a better known branding and packaging, sold for more than twice the price. And I sold a lot of them.

The reel is tight, tolerances are close, setting the drag is positive and tactile, and it's light yet sturdy feeling. It handles fish very well, and stripping line out feels good.

I like the packaging, I love the little felt reel bag, and there's a form letter from the company owner that makes it sound like he is rely interested in the customer being happy with the product. And even though the reel is made in China, the literature included is in English. Proper English that wasn't just run through Google Translate. If I were to have an issue with this reel (which I don't foresee), I get the impression he would want to make it right.

My wife bought this reel for me, so even though this isn't a "confirmed purchase" out whatever it's called, we did pay for this, and I'm glad we did!

Basically stated, I like this reel a lot. I'll buy another one. The only thing I'd like to see is other color options. That's really the only complaint I'd want to see addressed in a reel of this build quality at anywhere below $90. You can't go wrong picking one of these up!

title: Amazing Value in this Great Rod!
text:
Let's just say it. This is a darn nice rod. Is it a Sage? A Reddington? A Loop? Of course not. But it's also not $400.

I got this rod because I have 5wt and 6wt rods which were a bit more costly, but I wanted a 4wt for some smaller streams I'm going to be hitting. I won't spend much time there, and money is not abundant, so I figured I would try one of these. Boy was I surprised! I was expecting some moderate (slow) action rod, sloppy, and Heavy. This is light, crisp, and a joy to cast! The cork is great for this price point, and it's all put together and presented quite nicely.
There's an attitude in fly fishing that if it's not expensive, it's not worth using. Unfortunately we don't all have the ability or desire to spend $500 on a rod. For those of us in that situation, this is a magnificent option.

Look at it like this. You buy a rod at Scheels or Cabela's because you're getting a quality product at a slightly discounted price because it's store brand rather than big name brand. And that usually is the case and works well. Some of the best fishing gear I've got, and I've got a lot, was got from those brands I just named. These Maxcatch rods are built on the EXACT same blanks that the Scheel's Outfitter MDD fly rods are built on. And those were being sold for $100.

With that in mind, know that when you get one of these you aren't getting a Loomis rod. But this is probably the best sub-$120 fly rod you can get, and that leaves a lot of money for flies, tippet, line, and a reel.

I'll update this review with pics next time I go out. Buy one of these with confidence. I'll probably buy another for my wife and get a 3wt for me. I'm sold on this brand!

title: You'll Never Want a Different Mono
text: This has become my go-to line. I've used it all from 2lb-10lb, and it's just amazing stuff. VERY supple, VERY abrasion resistant, and VERY tough. My favorite is to use the 2lb for trout (my favorite!), because it is so very fine. It casts tiny lures a mile, and it has never snapped off after probably 150+ fish. I hope that this line will be available forever, because I never want to have to use a different line again

title: Great Line, Great Value
text:
Ok. I bought this line because of the cost, and if you're here looking, then you're probably in the same boat (not wanting to spend $80 on "premium" sinking line). So let's look at this line through that filter rather than comparing it to lines costing 8 times more.

This is nice line. Welded loops at each end, uniform color, and uniform size. It is thin, and so I wondered if maybe it was either advertised above weight or if I had been sent the wrong weight. So I spooled it up, attached my leader, and took it out to see how it throws.

This line casts BEAUTIFULLY! I was surprised at how well it casts. And it sinks just as well. I don't know if it sinks as well as the Rio or other more expensive lines, because quite frankly I can't afford them (too many other hobbies requiring too many purchases). However I know that it got my streamers down to where the fish were in the river I was in. I was happy with its performance.

When the ice melts and I get back to fishing big, deep stillwater, we'll see how quickly it gets down to 50'. But until then I'm not going to worry about it, because I'm sure it will do just fine

title: Great line! Buy with confidence!
text:
I'm surprised! I bought this line half expecting it to be wanting in the quality/consistency department, but it's really awesome stuff! It's even, thin for weight, and STRONG. I'm ordering another spool right meow.

I *do* won't if I really got 575 yards on my spool, but I did two full reels with it, so it's close enough. I'll probably measure the next spool I get, but you can't beat the price for the quality. I'll put it up against Stren or Trilene any day!

title: PERFECT Angler's Vest!
text:
[[VIDEOID:8c0dbd28e52fc090fb343e30665d5eae]] I'll start here. I'm a big dude. And a lot of the time vests like this that are "one size fits all" just don't fit. I've even bought some of these vests from companies that offer them in 5X and even those don't fit (even though I only wear 2X shirts from the store). Plus my phone, vape, knives and other self defense items (when kayaking and camping in the wild by rivers, you never know what kind of beasts you may encounter!). And it's even got a net ring on the back! It's great for every kind of fishing!

On top of fitment and the amount of gear the vest holds, it's very well made. I'm expecting a long service life from this piece of equipment.

Long story short, buy this vest. It works well and looks great, whether you're small, a bit wide around the middle like me, or somewhere in between. You'll be glad you did!

title: I LOVE the Bassdash Alien!
text:
Great reel! I got the Alien 2000 yesterday and took it out on the lake this morning. I was lucky enough to get into some very nice Cutthroats, and I was amazed at how well this reel fought them in.

The reel is very smooth, very attractive, and the drag is accurate and smooth. The EVA on the handle feels premium, too. I've bought reels for $20 more than this that didn't work half as well.

This is a great Reel, and I won't hesitate to buy another (3000 next time) for some other fishing I do. These are fantastic!

title: Next Time I'll Just Use Thread From My Socks
text: Ok. I see a lot of negative reviews of things, but I always temper them with the idea that "most people won't write rave reviews for a product just because it works the way it's supposed to". Meaning people are more likely to write bad reviews than good. So I bought a 330 yd spool of the 6lb "Ultimate Mono". Yipes. So I'm on the water in the canoe, and I start fishing. Trolling close to the bottom, the line snaps. There goes a spinner. But I figured I smashed something. I hate losing terminal tackle, but we all know it happens. Anyway, I begin casting, and as I throw the new spinner out, the line just snaps! Poof! No reason. It's a 3/16oz spinner. Why did it snap?! Still I try to give this Spiderwire the benefit of the doubt. So I try to cast some bottom bait out with a sinker. 1/4oz, a number 4 hook, and some bait. And again, the line snaps mid-cast? I can't believe it! This stuff is awful! Granted, it's very supple and manageable, but none of that matters if you can't get your lure where you want it and have it still attached to your Reel. Do yourself a favor. Save 50%, buy some Trilene XL, and catch some fish!

title: Fantastic Hi-viz Mono Line!
text:
I really love this line! The color is brilliant, and so it's easy to see, both in low light and direct sunlight! This is a huge benefit to me, since I'm generally working more than one line at a time (I've purchased extra licenses), and so I need to be able to see line movement easily and at Short distances. It's also great for bassin', because you can easily see the line jump out go slack when the fish takes the lure on the fall.

My ONLY CAVEAT is this; it's not as supple as, say, Triline XL or the Spiderwire Ultimate Mono (let alone the various flouro or flouro-coated offerings out there), so memory is an issue on my Pflueger Presidents and Trions in the 20-25 sizes. It's not an issue on my reels larger than those.

That said, it is so amazing line. Great abrasion resistance, knot strength, and of course, visibility. I just use a shock leader of 15' (along with a leader of smaller line), and I'm GTG. I've landed NUMEROUS 4-5lb bows and bass on this line, and I'm only using the 4lb line! I know that's light for bass, but I was targeting trout with spinners lol.

But this line with confidence. It's great stuff!

title: Nice spinners at a great price
text:
These are really nice spinners for the price. They're well put together, they have good action, and they run deep. I lost 4 of them on the river today, and that sucks. But at this price I can buy more.

The sweet case they come in its an added bonus, and those are worth $4 on their own. Grab some of these! They're Grrrrrrreat!

title: A step up in fly line for me
text: I'm just getting into fly-fishing, and I'm pretty bad at it. With that in mind, I've been buying the cheapest fly line I can find. I decided to spend a little more on this stuff, and the jump in quality is evident. This is great stuff. It casts better than the cheap Chinese stuff I've been using, and I expect it to last longer as well. Plus, this is a highly trusted name. Great product, good company, good seller, great price. What more can you ask for?

title: Perfect backing for my fly reels!
text: This line is too big for me to use for anything I fish for, but I only got it to use as backing on my fly reels anyway. In that role it's perfect! But even though I'm not casting it, I can tell it's good line. If it came in 10lb test I would definitely use it for throwing spinners into some of the places I go after big Farios.

title: Nice Line!
text: This line is the gold standard. Inexpensive, strong, supple, holds knots well, and has great abrasion resistance. At $14 for a 600yd spool, there's no reason to not grab some and spool up your reels!

title: This is the PERFECT River Tackle Bag!
text:
[[VIDEOID:20f4e0ee207590123179d48b39a19b2]] This thing is AWESOME! It's just the perfect shape to carry everything I could need (as you can see in the video). title: Awesome Spinners!
text: I love these Vibrax spinners. They're good for throwing with all of my rigs, they attract and trigger fish, and they don't cause lines twist. I've got 5 of these in my tackle box, but I've bought 20 of them. Spinners get lots on the river. That's three sacrifice to the River Gods lol

title: No better reel at even twice the price
text:
I can't say enough about this reel. I don't have a lot of money, but I love to fish. One day I decided I was going to treat myself and buy a $150 reel. I spent any hour and a half in Cabela's and about the same at Sportsman's. I tried every reel in the place, and still ended up with the Pres 30. It's just the best feeling reel I've ever used, and I've borrowed plenty over my 40+ years.

But it's not just great to play with in the store. I've caught probably 200 trout on mine, and it's been beat up. Dropped, submerged, dragged through mud, and covered in clay. I treated it the same way I did my Abu ProMax, and that piece of garbage died after 2 months.

If you're looking for a great reel and you have $150 to spend, get this and use the extra money to buy a nice rod, some good copoly line, and gas up your truck. Go fish!

title: Very nice braid!
text:
I love this stuff! It's strong, you can feel every nibble, the color stays, and, unlike Spider Wire, it doesn't stick to itself on your reel.

Another thing that I've noticed is that unlike many brands I've purchased here, these guys give you all of what's advertised. I can't tell you how many "short spools" I've purchased, but this is all there. Thanks guys! I'll buy again!

title: Great rod for the money
text:
I wrote a big, detailed review of this reel, and Amazon ate it. I don't have the energy to rewrite it, so here it is.

This is a great reel for the price. It's not an Orvis or Sage, but it works great, looks very nice, and functions flawlessly. Order one. Whether you need a spare for the trunk, a backup just to have, or want to see if fly-fishing is for you before you buy a $600 rig, you can't do much better thank a reel of this quality at this price.

title: A bit disappointed
text:
This reel is not like other Sougayilang Reels I own. This is my fourth, and it's not as nice as the others. Lots of play on the main shaft, tool marks all over, and the paint is marred all over this brand new reel. I'm not excited about this. Luckily I have others I can use.

All of that being said, it's still number than my Abu ProMax that I paid twice as much for.

title: Sougayilang Reels are an AMAZING VALUE!
text:
Ok! I just got this reel (the 3000) model, and it's just awesome! This is my 4th Sougayilang reel, 3 spinners and a caster), and while my first one was bought to have just in case, the rest have been purchased because I love the feel, performance, and value. I've caught 30 trout on my reels in just the last few weeks, so they've all seen plenty of time in the water.
I've fished them in clear water and water that looked like chocolate milk. They've been dropped in the mud, on the pavement, and have generally taken a beating already. Will they hold up as well as my Pflueger and Abu reels? IDK. But they're a fraction of the cost, and, more importantly, all signs are showing that they will in fact hold up. I won't tell people to run out and buy a Sougayilang reel for every rod they own. But I WILL STRONGLY suggest that you buy one of these reels, beat on it, use it, and review it objectively. I'll bet you won't find another $30 reel that is anywhere near this one in performance

title: Great line, great company!
text:
Howdy! Add someone sort of "born again" to fishing (fished a lot as a kid, but then didn't fish for nearly 30 years), I've been trying as many different things for trout and bass fishing as I can. Things have changed a lot! What hadn't changed though, is that there are good/bad and cheap/inexpensive/expensive kinds of tackle. I've spent a fair bit of money looking fort good line that meets my needs, and I've probably thrown away a mile of garbage line.

That's where this KastKing line comes in. This stuff is DEFINITELY the Good/inexpensive stuff! I've already caught probably 20 rainbows on this line, and it's amazing stuff. Disappears underwater, holds knots like it was glued, and simply doesn't break. I've had to horse a couple of fish out of some nasty spots, and this stuff is as great as I could hope. It honestly outperforms the spider wire I had on!

If you want great, solid line that will perform under very adverse conditions, look no further. This KastKing flourokote is the stuff!

title: Great line, but very thick
text: This is very strong, high quality line. But it's thinker than usual 30# braid. I'll bet you could use it to chop down a tree. Great for horsing fish through vegetation.

title: Nice braided line! Highly recommended
text: This stuff is only 4 stand, but it's put together very nicely. It's retained it's color as well as Spiderwire and Cabela's brand braid, and it hasn't even frayed at the edges. If it continues to hold up I'll redo my review to 5 stars. You can't go wrong with this line, especially at this price point

title: Good enough line, but watch your knots
text:
Knot strength is awful. I lost 4 hooks (with sinkers) and a rapala before I unwound my reel and threw this stuff in the trash. It's only two-pound test, so I had anticipated losing terminal tackle were I to get caught up in brush. This stuff didn't break, so maybe that's a good thing. But when I relied it in I could see the stretched coils that formed when I tied my knots. I use two different knots, and they've literally never failed me. Not even with braided line.

So I guess the choice is yours. The line won't snap off any more easily than with any other line. But once I've lost faith in a line's ability to hold a tried and true set of knots, it will be hard for me to be confident enough to use it ever again.

EDIT: I've found out that this stuff makes pretty decent VB 6X or 8X tippets for fly-fishing. By using either double uni or double surgeon's knots, the difficulty with knot integrity is mitigated. The line is plenty strong, so this is actually a great value for tippet material.

title: Solid Heavy Spinning Reel!
text:
I'm impressed with the feel of this reel! I'm hoping to spool it up and get it on the water tomorrow, at which point I'll update my review. However, a lot of the time you can tell if an inexpensive product is junk just by holding it, and this is NOT the cases with the Sougayilang W5000. Honestly, and bear in mind that this statement should be taken with the fact that I haven't used it yet, if you put an Abu, Shimano, or Lew's decal on this it would EASILY sell for more than twice this price, and people would love it.

Anyway, I'll update this review tomorrow or the day after. But my prediction is that it will perform on par with many "big name" reels in the $35-$50 range. It's no Pflueger President, but it feels as good as my Abu ProMax reel that cost a little more than twice as much

UPDATE:
After a day on the water, I have to say I'm impressed. This is truly up there with reels in the $50+ range from the bigger names. Buy it with confidence!

title: It's OK so far ...
text:
It seems OK ...

I'm giving it five stars to start with because it is what it said it would be and it fits my center console very well. It looks a lot nicer than the green plastic tarp I was using to keep my console dry. I ordered and received the gray color option.

It's fairly lightweight and folds/rolls up into a nice small package when it's stored in the bag that came with the cover. Most boaters will appreciate that as stowage on a boat is always at a premium. Putting it in its little bag keeps it from catching the wind and blowing away when towing the boat or on the water.

I've only had it for a couple of weeks so time will tell regarding longevity. The problem with most of these things is that they either last or they don't. If it falls apart in an unreasonable amount of time I'll be back to add to this review. I consider 5 years on a fabric cover of any type to be a "reasonable amount of time" for them to remain serviceable. Properly treated exterior grade fabrics should last quite a while. I have a Bimini top that has been on my boat for 15 years and it's still in serviceable condition. The top is deployed from April to October and I tow the boat with it up (it's only 3 miles to the ramp and it's 45 MPH or less speed limit all the way) so that's a good example of good service from an exterior grade fabric.

For some reason unknown to me the drawstring is NOT as shown in the item description. It's not on the aft side of the console where the drawstring and the cutout are located in the picture. It's on the starboard side of the console. Which is a little irritating because that's the side I usually store tackle boxes, coolers etc. to keep them handy to the helm and the fore deck both. So I have to move stuff around to use this console cover, which is not a big deal or a deal killer but I do wish these sellers would get their act together and provide ACCURATE pictures of what they're selling and we're buying.

Because while I like online shopping for the huge array of choices and the availability of things I may or may not find locally, or may have to drive miles to find and still might not be successful -- online shopping is always a crapshoot. You can't pick up and look at what you're buying, you can't walk in a store and see it set up on display so that you can examine its construction and quality. All you have to go by are pictures, item description and subjective reviews of others who have purchased the item. So it would seem to me that if sellers don't want to get returns and charge-backs they ought to pay very close attention to their pictures and item descriptions.

title: Very nice wheel at a very good price.
text:
This is a very nice, solid, sturdy Destroyer wheel. I have a 16 ft. center console and when I replaced the steering gear (steering box, cable) I wanted to put a new wheel on the boat too. The old wheel (heavy emphasis on the word "old") was made of some sort of plasticized hard rubber and it was frankly nasty. Years and years of hand oil, motor oil, motor fuel, fish slime and general grunge had accumulated on and eaten up the wheel. It was time to find a new wheel.

It's hard finding the right size Destroyer wheel because I needed a 13 inch wheel and most of them are bigger. A 13 inch wheel is all that will comfortably clear everything else on the console. Many of the wheels I looked at cost around twice as much as this one did.

The wheels spokes are gathered and locked into a central star and a cover made of what looks like teak wood snaps over the top. The description says "bakelite cover" but mine doesn't look like bakelite, nor does the product picture. Mine looks like the one in the picture. My boat, being a center console, has grab rails around the console but I often find myself using the wheel as a grab hold when moving around on the boat. I'm not a small person, so that's likely considerable stress on the wheel itself. It's not a problem, I've been using this wheel for several months and it's as solid as the day I mounted it.

This wheel is rock solid and a perfect finishing touch for my new steering system. I'm very happy with it and never have hand/fish/oil/fuel/grunge on my helm any more!

title: Very good fins, one minor irritation.
text:
These are great fins, their thrust vector is excellent, they are easy to get on and off, the clips on the strap work well and are very heavy duty, all in all a very good fin.

I just have one problem with them and it's not such a problem that I'd go looking for a different fin. The heel strap tends to work down off my heel over time no matter how much I tighten it up, and you don't want it so tight that it pinches and gets uncomfortable over time as you wear it. This might be partly because I wear a 3mm neoprene wet sock with them. I do that because putting flippers on in sand without a wet sock (a sock made of wetsuit material) is asking for abrasions on your foot. The heel strap tends to pull the sock down and the whole thing eventually slips off the bottom of my heel. This is the first time I've used an open foot fin with socks, usually I use a full foot fin and this isn't an issue. Every so often I have to reach down and pull the heel strap up. It's not a deal killer, I'm not sorry I got this fin, it's a minor irritation that is most likely due to the way I use them.

That's the only problem I've had with these fins so I'm describing it to be honest and thorough about this item.

title: Classy, vintage bag. Works great even if you're really tall.
text: The color in this photo is a little off, but I was quite happy with the bag I received. Mine was much more of a khaki color with tan straps rather than the light suede color & dark brown stripes depicted here. It still has a wonderful "vintage WWI-ish" look to it and it suits me perfectly. If you're a tall person like myself you'll be happy to find out that the adjustable shoulder strap is still quite long enough to accomodate your height. Americans are big...I'm 6' 4" tall...and the strap is long enough when adjusted all the way out to hang at a comfortable hip-level when worn cross-body style. (Did that make any sense? Sorry.) Main compartment has plenty of room yet the bag isn't "oversized" and awkward...it's just right for me. Side pockets are on the small side...you can comfortably stash one deck of cards in one of them, or some ink pens, wireless mouse, etc. The small zipper-closure pocket inside the main pocket is a great place to stash charging cords, earphones, a power-bank for your phone or tablet, etc. And I repeat: it looks great and all "classy vintage".  :-)

I was getting really tired of playing "bike seat du jour" trying to find one that didn't inflict pain on me and so far this is the most comfortable one I've tried. I will warn you though that as a big cruiser-bike seat, it's too wide to put one of those gel or memory-foam seat covers on it for extra padding.

title: Great tail light, lousy headlight.
text:
I ordered this set of battery powered lights for my Trek hybrid. The rear light works okay, though I really don't need 6 (six!) different settings for flashing red lights. A simple "on" and "off" would have been sufficient...I know it's not a big deal, but having to press the power button literally 7 times to get back to the "off" setting is mildly annoying. That said, the rear light is bright red, reliable and plenty visible to traffic.

What truly, deeply sucks is this crap-tastic headlight. It's about as "bright" as your average Liberal Arts college grad. I've seen brighter light from a lit candle. The light from it is so faint you barely see the pavement in front of your front tire. And the mount is fragile, using thin "rails" to slide the dinky little flashlight into place when you "seat" it onto the handlebar mount...I installed it on my bike and a couple days later I accidentally bumped it against my bicycle rack on the rear of my vehicle (I promise, it wasn't a hard bump) and the cheap plastic broke and the light fell to the ground. I now have a lousy little 1-lumen flashlight in my glove compartment for my trouble. I would return this piece of junk if I hadn't already accidentally broken the mount when it bumped against my bike rack.

Avoid this piece of junk...again, the rear light is okay if you should need 6 different forms of flashy, blinky red lights. You could make a better headlight in Jr. High science class.

title: A good piece of equipment, but lacks capacity for Arizona desert hikes
text:
The canteen is well made and light weight. The polymer lining looks to be thick and even. Capacity is exactly 1.0 liter - I could have used a bigger size, if available. I bought the model with the large plastic cap. Not as sexy as the metal cap with chain, but it does not leak and the opening is big enough that you can easily inspect the inside for crud buildup, and run in a bendable wire brush to scour the walls.. 4 stars instead of 5 because 1.5 to 1.8 liters would have been better. As it is, it is the same capacity (or less) than the 2 bottles on my fanny pack.

title: Works great to convert a Deore XT FH-M756 Disc Hub from QR to Solid Axle on a 29er!
text:
I got tired of the rear tire shifting around on my heavily modified SE Stout 29er with the Deore XT FH-M756 Disc Hub in QR. I had to get this with to stop it from happening. The QR wasn't holding on during excessive/extreme braking.

This product is a life saver!

What I did was just use the track nuts and the axle, I had to re-use the bearing races because they were designed specifically for the Deore hub. I flushed out the old lube and used Moly red lithium with a Timken OK load index of 55. I also installed new BC Precision bearings. I tightened everything up and had it on my bike in less than an hour. These track nuts hold on like there is no tomorrow!

I feel so much more confident going down black diamonds now that I don't have to worry about my rear wheel shifting around.

title: get one with black hand grips â€”Â sunlight makes the colored ones slimy/sticky
text:
These are amazing scooters. Our four-year-old twins really fly on these, and even our almost two-year old zips around the drive.

I want to caution you away from one with color-coordinated hand grips. Only get one with black hand grips. The colored ones are not UV-safe, and after less than a year of use in the backyard the handgrips turned sticky and soft and I had to replace them. They were stored covered some of the time, but they're kids' toys — they're going to get used outside and left out.

We bought two of these — a blue one with black hand grips, which are still perfectly fine, and a red one with red hand grips, which have since been replaced with black handgrips from the local bike shop ($12).

Also, the red platform on this scooter is now an ugly faded orange, but still functional. The blue scooter still looks a perfect blue and is not faded at all.

Also, our twins enjoy running into things and into each other and the colored bits at the fronts of the scooters are all cracked and chipped away, which I think a slight design change could avoid, but I wouldn't take off any stars for that. Just one each for the fading deck and slimy grips.

===============================
Update after two years
I'm increasing my star review from three to five — Micro Mini replied to my review and offered replacement parts. I hadn't realized they sell replacement parts at all — http://www.microkickboard.com/mini-micro-parts . This alone I think puts them a cut above other toy manufacturers, that their stuff is durable and you can replace individual parts rather than tossing the whole thing. They replaced the grips gratis, but I still opted for black ones.

title: Easier than ultrasonic cleaning.
text:
[[VIDEOID:4d97ce6c49de579dc9b8d7678abf3b9f]] Maybe it is a little early for this review since I got this yesterday but I am very impressed and this has been run about 16 hours out of the last 20. I set it on a smart plug timer so it could even do a late night batch without running all night. I used to do ultrasonic cleaning but I hated the drying process and the less pleasing lack of that brassy shine you get with tumbling.
A couple pieces of advice....I saw reviewers mentioning the center bolt dinging up brass, the fix is SUPER easy. A simple drinking straw to cover the threads. I even found a blue one that matches the tumbler.
Second piece of advice, don't be dumb like me. I had a handful of .223 that I decided to add to the .40 cal I was tumbling. .223 fits in the .40 cal so many of the .223 had unpolished bases. Just remember 9 mm fits in .40 and .40 fits in .45. so pay attention if you mix brass. Make sure it can't fit inside the other type.

title: Not as bright as I had hoped.
text: Not nearly as bright as I had hoped. I bought a Radwagon 4 and I wanted to add more light to the underwhelming stock headlight. This light has a couple problems for me. Second, the focus of the light, or in other words the size of the bright disc of light it throws, is the same size as the stock Radwagon 4 light. So the effect of the light is very minimal and I think I will end up buying another, bigger, brighter light to do what this one could not. I should have known, to be honest. There is no end to cheap, chinese flashlights and headlights with exaggerated claims about brightness along with long exposure photos taken at night to make them look powerful. I would pass on this one if you honestly need good lighting. This is really better for being seen by cars than for you to see where you are riding.

Oh, and these come with a bright yellow rain cover that I haven't used yet and probably never will (Utah doesn't get a ton of rain and I don't intend to ride in the rain). title: Great fun for three to five year old My Little Pony fans!
text:
There's plenty to like in they My Little Pony scooter, perfect for the three to five year old set. The three-wheel platform is sturdy and textured, and the stop-on rear brake allows for easy stopping, and the handle-bars are easy to grip and hold. The "Exciting" Lights and Sounds Handlebar" has --- I suppose you could call them exciting lights and sounds -- has four functional buttons that make various noises when depressed. If you're wrapping this to put under the Christmas tree, don't feel confident that it's going to be a surprise, as the unopened box spoke to me several times before I even opened the package -- "I'm Twilight Sparkle!" "I'm Rainbow Dash!" "I'm Pinkie Pie!" -- I when the handlebar buttons were somehow depressed by pressing on the side of the box.

The scooter is licensed by Hasbro but manufactured by Dynacraft, which makes a variety of wheeled products. The assembly manual is clearly written and easy to follow. The scooter appears to be relatively well-made and sturdy, and looks like it would withstand plenty of use and survive in good enough shape to be passed down to the next generation.

title: Much sturdier than I expected -- and it weighs next to nothing
text: This little blanket arrives in a little drawstring bag about the size of a deck of cards -- so I admit, I wasn't expecting much when I opened it -- but boy was I surprised.  The material is actually fairly sturdy, with a silvery coating on one side and a green coating on the other.  The blanket is large enough to stop around the shoulders of two people -- 6 feet by 6.5 feet, and it really does hold body heat in and keep you warm.  The best part about it-- after you use it, you can fold it up and put it back in the little pouch to keep it safe until next time you need it. title: Like the device -- but the band keeps BREAKING and BREAKING.
text:
The device works fine. I don't think the step count is particularly accurate, as it seems to be based on hand motion as much as anything else (as I really racked up the mileage while chopping vegetables), but it's definitely in the ballpark and gives you a pretty good idea of your level of activity. I really like the e-mail and text alerts.

What I don't like: THE BAND. I purchased this device in December 2016 and didn't get around to wearing it until January 2017. It is now March. The band has broken TWICE -- it comes detached on the buckle side, where the band attaches to the device. Once it becomes detached, it will never stay secure again. Although I can slide it back together, it easily comes off when I'm pulling off a coat or a sweater. I can understand this happening once, but TWICE??? Never had this problem with my Charge.

Fortunately, FITBIT customer service is very helpful. They have sent replacement bands at no charge, which I truly appreciate. However, I would much prefer the device just stayed in one piece and I didn't have to mess with the replacement band over and over. I've tried to figure out if I'm doing something wrong -- but the instructions for replacing the bands are pretty straight-forward, so I'm not sure how you'd go wrong.

Overall, I like the functionality of the device but sure wish the band would stop breaking!

title: Simple, fun-to-use paddles to increase stroke efficiency for competitive swimmers of all levels
text:
These Speedo Preflex Paddles are designed to help competitive swimmers focus on initiating the catch at the fingertips in order to swim faster and more efficiently. The paddles are one size fits all, the they have adjustable rubber tubing that can be loosened or tighter to fit most hands. I have large hands for a woman and they fit fine. I don't know if they would fit or provide much benefit for someone with exceptionally large hands. I have used paddles in the past -- these are different in that the are scalloped around the point of entry, similar to how one's fingers would actually enter the water; they are perforated, letting some water through, and they are somewhat flexible with a high design in the middle, rather than being flat. The hinge purports to make the paddles beneficial for ALL strokes -- although I am ignorant of the science that supports that statement.

Overall, these are a great tool to change up your water workout and help improve your stroke. Give them a try.

title: Keeps the heat of the sun out in summer
text:
The sun hits a front window hard in our house, adds to heat that wastes the air conditioning. Even though we have plastic blinds on that window, and it's double glass, plus insulated curtains, it was still not enough. I put duct tape across the top of one of these space blankets to prevent ripping, used cafe curtain rings with clips that clip onto the duct-taped top, ran the rings onto some 1/4" dowels that I laid across the curtain holders. It works excellently; that corner of the room, even in late afternoon, is dark and not hot anymore.

They keep the heat OUT in summer, keep the heat IN in winter. These do seem to be stronger than the average space blanket, though one of mine had about a 6" rip in the side when I took it out of its little baggie; I just duct-taped the rip.

They work. Which is the big point.

title: Good rack, but it should come with instructions.
text:
I am pleased with the rack. However, it did not come with any instructions. I was able to figure it out anyway. You have to take off your rear brake and mount the bracket on the brake bolt between the brake and the frame. You put your wheel skewer through the holes on the bottom. Note that this makes it annoying to remove the rear wheel.

As another reviewer noted, the bracket needs to be bent in order to fit. This is unavoidable because different bicycles have different frame geometry. It is easy to bend with pliers and I had it bent correctly in about 2 minutes.

Note also that it is a narrow rack and is meant for mounting bags or baskets on the sides. Mounting to the top is iffy. (I mounted a basket to the top anyway, using enough zip ties to make sure it won't move).

This rack is much more securely mounted than my old one, which was mounted with p-clips. It is also much lower and closer to the wheel which helps keep the weight down low so it doesn't affect handling as much.

If you have a road bike, you can definitely use this rack to increase your cargo capacity. I was looking for something like this for a while and I'm glad someone makes it.

title: Less than it seems...
text:
While this could be a serious upgrade for an Old, photo-only trail cam that doesn't take videos, there are several drawbacks to using this device, and slightly misleading info that makes it seem, or you would think, it does more than it can. Not true, it's actually a very limited, though clever, device.

First of all, as to its 'near universal' fit, it ONLY works in cameras with a full-size HC-SD card slot. That means it will not fit if your camera has a micro SD card slot. They say this, true enough, but hunters/ cameras seem to use the term SD indiscriminately. They say there are no plans to develop a micro SD adapter (that connects the cell link to your camera. )

Second, if your camera takes videos, you will never see any of them, they are not saved anywhere, and as they say, they aren't transmitted and you won't see them in the app, either. Videos are out, gone, might as well turn that setting off in your camera. It will not copy, store or transmit videos, and with your camera's memory slot taken up by the adapter, there is No Video Capability of the camera with this attached.

Third (geeks, this is for you), there is no two-way connectivity between your camera and the (yes, wait for it! ) Micro SD card you must install in the cell link. In other words, the cell link extracts still images from your camera, and stores them in the micro SD card you supply on the cell link (for the cell link to later transmit), but your camera can never see those images again, it's just a one way dump. So if your camera has any high falutin functions (good screen, wifi, etc.) you'd like to use in the field, it will never be able to read the images it captured. Gone (to cell link. )

I did not try to reproduce the cable-crimp problem, I tested this all with open compartments.

The manual is Excellent. The app and storage plans seem very good. It was easy to set up, and even in my remote neck of the woods I was able to get connected to Verizon in a few seconds (my phone cannot often boast the same.) I used a third party antenna booster (at 1/4 the cost of spypoints, it worked excellently boosting 1-2 bars. ) It does have an external 12V jack for a battery or appropriate solar panel/ battery.

The concept is excellent. The manufacturing seems first class. And it's pretty cheap! If you've got old hunting cameras you don't want to be going to check, just know where the game is, this could be very valuable. If you're thinking you can kluge some high tech security system out of this, you will probably also be disappointed. Like I was, and returned it.

title: Some great features, great bottle.
text:
My water bottle should:
1. Open easily with one hand
2. Keep the water cold
3. Be tough
4. Be easy to drink from
5. Be easy to clean.
6. (Extra credit) Be really easy to carry. Or not be bad at it.

I don't want to suck the water; I prefer to pour it into my mouth. So a tiny hole or straw is a no-go.

I had an Aladdin that was all that, but the spring eventually broke. Can't open one-handed anymore.

I bought a variety of water bottles to try out. This is my favorite. It's all of the above, with one caveat and one addition.

It opens easily, as long as there's no vacuum lock (i.e. you didn't put ice in and close it, resulting in the air inside cooling and forming suction.) The thermos is great. It's made of metal and heavy plastic.

IF you move the handle (the white ring) back BEFORE you open the bottle, it's easy to drink from. Otherwise the spout doesn't really come out far enough to get it close to your mouth. But that's easy to do.

Fully dishwasher safe. And very easy to carry, especially with that large handle/carry ring. Which is a solid loop. An example of this done badly is many of the UnderArmor bottles, which have a split ring for carrying that you really can't carry with a finger when full because the prongs of the split point in and dig into your finger.

The Extra Credit: There's a screen to prevent random ice bits from going into your mouth. It's removable, but I love this thing. I like my sports-water cold, but don't want to chew on ice during exercise.

title: Frustrating to Set Up
text:
I bought this to replace a Specialized computer that only lasted a few years, regardless of battery changes.

The Good:
1. It's relatively inexpensive.
2. It's wireless (between the wheel sensor and the computer), which is *amazing* at this price.
3. The display is decent.
4. I prefer two-button over one-button bike computers.
5. If you have a very oddball configuration, it can handle it.

The Bad:
Oh my, let's count the ways.
1. Somewhat unclear manual
2. Incomplete manual - missing super-common bicycle tire sizes. I bought this for a Trek DS8 commuter bike, which has a 700x38. Not listed.
3. Their solution to that? Roll the bike carefully along the ground and measure it. Yeah, right. I guessed, and will work it out later.
4. Unrealistic specs. The manual is clear that the magnet must come within 5mm (1/2cm or less than 1/5th of an inch) of the sensor. Which is not realistic. Compounding this, their magnet's shape requires it be mounted where spoke cross... which many bikes have another mounting point at.
Fortunately, it isn't really that picky.
5. To change the computer mount orientation, you must unscrew four-to-five (seriously, depending on desired orientation) tiny itty bitty screws, re-orient, and replace all or nearly all (seriously... you may no longer have access to some holes) of them.
6. The display is decent, but it really doesn't resemble the one in the photos. In reality, it's much lower contrast (and, of course, not as large as the photos imply, but normal size for a bike computer.)
7. You get, seriously, about 15 seconds after inserting the battery to choose MPH vs KPH... but... much of that time is spent getting the battery door back on and flipping it over. I don't think there's a way to do it other than initially. (To switch it at that point, hit the RIGHT side button. Oddly, the "Mode" button doesn't change modes between K and M, and it doesn't stand for Miles ;)... if you hit M, you have to take out the battery and try again.)

That sounds pretty bad. But all of this is first-time-setup stuff. It really is a VERY nice bike computer even for much more than the price. I'll provide more updates after I've calibrated the tire correctly.

title: Crap.  Doesn't work.  And I'll tell you why...
text:
Perhaps these come in batches, some good, some bad. Mine is bad. This type of bottle requires you drink from the straw, sucking, rather than pouring the liquid into your mouth. But... as you'll see from some other questions and reviews... some people get as much air as water from it.

That's my case. And the reason is... the silicon tube that folds and unfolds when you close/open it, has to form a tight gasket/seal with the straw. The straw screws on, but only as far as the threads and nut let it. So if that silicon tube's gasket is not pushing down hard enough... you get air.

I can fix it... for a single open cycle... by unscrewing the straw, adjusting, reattaching the straw and closing the lid. But the problem re-appears when I close and reopen the drinking tube. It's not worth it.

title: Great glasses and some tips.
text:

The frame fits perfectly. (This is the Carabelle, for medium/large heads. If you have a tiny head, the Lagoon will probably fit better.) The lens quality is very good. I've had mine quite a while and they haven't gotten scratched, but I don't put them in a pocket unprotected as some other reviewers have done. And they 're dark enough, with a good reading area.

The one thing to know is, darkness. The grey is the "dark" lens, amber is the "less dark." Blue is grey+mirror (so a bit darker, better for cutting glare), green is amber+mirror (less dark than blue.)

The reading area is visible from outside the glasses. It won't be in your way, but others can notice it. Which has been a positive conversation piece for us, such as on a cruise when other travelers notice and are suddenly jealous.

title: Great for stationary use, perhaps less so for mobile.
text:
The Lockdown Gun Magnet is almost... almost what I needed.

It has the two thicker discs, connected by ferrous metal, with a soft rubber coating. The magnetism is on the logo'd side; it won't even hold itself up against a fridge on the other side. So make sure you mount it correct-side-out.

It seems nicely made and equipped. The rubber is non-scuffing and won't hurt the guns. The screw-holes are counter-sunk. It comes with drywall anchors and three lengths of black screws. (The packaging claims two sets of screws.) Both sides of it are rubber-coated, so no rattles or vibrations. The first impressions are great.

It is decently strong; it can lift a 5-pound weight disk. But that's a pretty perfect case; flat metal, smooth, full contact, being lifted straight up. And it isn't a strong grip on the 5-pound disk; you can shake it loose pretty easily.

And that's the problem. A typical handgun (e.g. Star Firestar - 2#, Browning Hi-Power 2.3#, Colt 1911 2.5#) weighs about half that weight disk... but it doesn't have all the metal on the surface and doesn't have a smooth flat contact patch. So the Lockdown doesn't hold a typical handgun tightly enough for the odd placement and motion in a vehicle. In fairness, the Kahr PM9 is about 1.3 # loaded, the Beretta Nano 9mm about 1.1# loaded and the Colt Mustang Pocketlite .380 and Beretta Pico .380 barely 3/4-pound, but they also have less ferrous metal in them for the magnets to grip.

The only flaws are that after a month it still curls in at the edges from being rolled up when manufactured/shipped, and the bottom is very slippery. No aerobics on this one! title: Mosquito "tent"
text:
Last year, then-10 year old girl went to camp and was eaten alive by insects. So this year she wanted a mosquito net. This one was a bit on the expensive side, but highly rated, so why not. Opening it up was a no-brainer. Closing it, well, they suggest you watch the videos. Take that suggestion. You NEED to watch the videos.

When I dropped her off this year, I was very surprised to notice how many children had these exact same things. It's almost like it was standard camp issue! Not only that, it seems as if the camp even rents these out (reservation required). And if I had any doubts about her ability to close it down, there's plenty of kids and councilors to help assist.

It is pretty roomy inside. She's above average in height but we were both able to sit inside. The mesh holes are very small, and seems to impede airflow so it got a bit uncomfortable, but I guess the small holes are necessary, otherwise insects will still get in. I guess the tradeoff is that it's a bit warm but you won't be itching like mad the next morning. Carrying it is not a real issue. title: So far so good
text:
I've had this for a little while now. I'm short and overweight, and usually fail at my daily walking goals, BUT, I've been very pleased with this purchase. Being the aforementioned short and overweight, the preset workouts are just a bit much for me, but it wouldn't take too much work to get there, I don't think. Probably my favorite feature is its simplicity. A lot of people want bells and whistles and wouldn't be happy with this, but it's perfect for this not-athletic person. I'll never get up to the faster speeds, but to be honest, it shakes enough under my weight when I attempt a light jog, that I'd be just a little leery of pushing it any more. Otherwise it feels sturdy though, and I'm not afraid of it breaking or anything.

As others have said, a second set of hands really helps when putting it together initially. It's not hard, just awkward. My mom helped me by just holding things still or handing me parts. It maybe took a half hour from start to finish, and I was taking my time. Getting it exactly where I wanted in my small room was the hardest part. Folding it up is easy - it's heavy, but I'd be scared to use anything lighter!

This is my first treadmill, and I think it's perfect for a casual user. I doubt I'll ever be an avid walker/jogger, but this at least gives me ample opportunities for exercise when I need it, without worrying about time of day or weather.

title: A Great Little "Oven"
text: We are in our RV for much of the time, and did not want to use up our propane for cooking during the cold months.  The Omnia does not work on an induction stove, but works very well on a gas stove -- no surprise there.  I purchased an electric hot plate to use with the Omnia, and this combination works well.  I have baked muffins, cornbread, cakes, chicken casserole, cinnamon rolls, etc. and been quite pleased with the outcome. When I made a cake, iced it and sprinkled it with colored sprinkles, it looked like a giant donut.  I didn't hear anyone complaining, though!  Really, I couldn't be more pleased with this Omnia oven.  Food does not brown on the top as it would in a regular oven, but that may be because I use a hot plate as opposed to a gas fire -- don't know.  Would I purchase an Omnia again?  Absolutely!!  In fact, I have purchased this twice.  I made the mistake of placing a very hot Omnia on microfiber towels.  The synthetic towels melted to the bottom of the Omnia, and could not be removed. :(  So I learned the hard way to place a hot Omnia on  a silicone pad or 100% cotton toweling. I did purchase the 2-pack silicone liners which makes clean-up a breeze.  I also purchased the rack which keeps the bottom of food from over browning.  The oven and its bits and pieces all fit in the bag that comes with the Omnia, so when I grab the bag I have everything I need minus the hot plate.  The purchase of this Omnia is among the best purchases I made for our RV.
