title: Great tool for filing nails, but could be even better.
text:
This is a great little nail drill with lots of positives, but there's still room for improvement. This is basically a miniature Dremel tool for fingernails.

PROS:
• Very quiet.
• USB cord is lighter than electrical cord.
• Nice range of speeds from slow to fast.
• Speeds are variable so you're not stuck with just a few predetermined speeds.
• Can reverse the spin direction.
• Came with more accessories than you'll ever need (and they're in really cute little containers).

NEUTRALS:
• Easy to hold, but still a little bulky. Would be better if it was smaller: thinner and shorter.
• Nice smooth metal case, but it easily slips when holding it – I added a gel pencil grip which stopped the slipping problem.

CONS:
• Must be plugged in to use – it would be great if it had a rechargeable battery.
• Switches for on/off, direction, and speed are inconveniently placed – Instead of being on the tool itself, they're on the cord, about a foot away from the tool. You have to reach down the cord for each adjustment. They move around as the cord moves.
• The drill rolls – Anytime you put it down, it rolls away. The cord can help limit the rolling, but when it's unplugged, there is nothing to stop it from rolling off the table. I put a gel pencil grip on the drill to help stop this.
• The nail bits are kept in two mismatched plastic containers with different lengths, widths, and thicknesses. When combined with the bag for the sanding bands, you end up needing a container to hold all the containers! It would be better if at least the nail bits were all in one, single container.

Overall, this is a good little tool for filing nails. Hopefully, newer versions will be even better.

title: Short lived - PLASTIC screw part on bottle breaks - Paint flakes off
text:
I really loved these bottles at first, so much so that I bought 8 of them. They keep my water very cold for a long, long time and I like the lids (I use them without the straws). I can hook them onto whatever I need to help me carry them, as well.

Unfortunately, my love affair with these bottles has ended all too soon. The first thing I noticed is that the paint started coming off. The red one is the worst. The paint is flaking off to the point that it would be better off if I pull the rest of it off to turn it silver instead of blotched red. But I could have lived with that.

What got me was when I started to fill one up only to discover that the plastic ring around the top of the bottle that you use to screw the lid in has split. It split completely down. There was nothing I could do. It had to either go back to the manufacturer or the trash. Since I'm a grad student, the last thing I have is extra time so I put it in the trash.

I started checking my other bottles and discovered that the plastic ring was put on at a tilt on some of the bottles (based on the amount of space under the ring not being uniform on all bottles).

Then I looked at my other bottles and noticed that the Hydro Flask's ring was metal, not plastic. I like those bottles just as much, but had to buy the straw lids separately. However, now that I see the flaw in the Eco Vessel bottles, I'm going to start replacing them with the Hydro Flask brand. Not only are they completely metal (except the lid, of course), but the finish does not show signs that it will flake off.

All in all, the plastic ring used to screw the lid onto the bottle is a fatal flaw for these bottles.

UPDATE: I added pictures showing the paint flaking off and the warped plastic at the top. I did not take pictures of the one that broke, but I thought showing one that's not broken yet, but clearly warped, might be helpful.

title: The ULTIMATE cold drink coozie!
text:
If you like cold drinks, this is the ultimate coozie to get! They not only keep your drinks cold for hours, but they can actually make your drinks colder than they were from the refrigerator!

That is because each coozie has two main layers that work together to chill the drinks: an inner gel layer and a thick outer styrofoam layer.

When you put the coozie in the freezer, the gel layer freezes. This layer can actually drop the temperature of whatever drink you put int the coozie. It's like wrapping your drink in a blanket of ice! Then the styrofoam layer makes sure all that great coldness stays there. Drinks normally stay cold for several hours!

Another nice feature when using these coozies is that there is no problem with leaving wet rings on the furniture because the coozies prevent the normal condensation problem you have with cold drinks in a warm environment. I think this is because of the thick insulation layer. The cold inside is insulated from the warm outside which prevents condensation.

I know these coozies last for years. I originally found these coozies on MisterCold.com in 2006 and used them constantly ever since. I have taken them with me everywhere I go. They have held up very well for so much use. After 7 years of use, they finally began to show signs of wear (slight fraying at the bottom) so I decided it was time to get new ones. I was thrilled to find them here on Amazon! The new ones I got are just as good, if not better, than the original ones I bought years ago.

If you want to enjoy drinks that are cold, cold, cold and stay that way for hours, this is the perfect item for you. Just be sure to get a bunch because once your family and friends try them, they'll use them all the time. So you need plenty on hand to be sure there's always a cold one waiting for you! The rule in my house is you can use them as long as you don't take the last one. That way there's always at least one chilled and ready to go!

text: I had a guest coming for a week and as the date approached realized that my extra bedroom probably needed a bed, after having been turned into a makeshift gym over the past year. After combing page after page of Amazon search results, I settled on a deeply discounted "Like New" listing for this one. It came with the box, storage bag, and instructions, and was very easy to inflate. I slept on it one night to test - it was comfortable, the sheets stayed put, and there wasn't noticeable deflation, but I did still wonder about what flaws a 6'5 person would find in this queen-sized air mattress that my 5'2 self did not. The morning after my guest arrived, he emerged to announce unprompted that it was the best air mattress he'd ever slept on, and better than some regular mattresses, too. It's had a fair amount of use since with no complaints and much praise. At one point it was used for almost a month straight with just a small amount of air topping off. Having said that I would urge people reading these reviews to remember the intended use case of an air mattress - it is not a traditional mattress, so it is not expected to hold up to months (or even *a* month) of continuous use. Adjusting expectations accordingly, I think anyone would be pleased with this air mattress.

text: This is the 2nd Black Diamond Sprinter headlamp that I have purchased and have been extremely pleased with them. title: Great Dynamic Punching Bag for Kids and Adults
text:
Great purchase! Delivered with no damage and all parts accounted for. Assembly instructions were clear and easy to follow. They provided tools that will work but I used own. Easy to assemble, took less than 10 minutes. All the parts fit together easily, and seem very well made.

The base is very heavy when filled with water. It also has suction cups on the bottom that work very well on the smooth concrete surface of my garage. In fact too well. It makes moving it around a challenge, but on the plus side it dies not move at all no matter how hard I punch or kick it. Thinking about removing the suction cups because the base is so heavy when filled with water don't think it will move.

The spring is responsive and can handle some pretty hard hits or kicks without the shaft/bag hitting the floor. It's response time to return upright isn't too bad, just don't expect to rapid speed punch if you're going to really hit hard.

The red bag itself is super dense foam, not a leather covered inflatable bag as I've seen on others. It takes quite a pounding and it feels more natural than hitting a leather covered balloon. I've hit it without gloves no issues, but longer workouts need gloves.

The height is adjustable. I'm about 6ft tall, my son is about 5ft tall, and it easily accommodates our heights. A big plus. It's easy to adjust too, and locks in place very securely and stays locked throughout use.

Overall it is a great product and good value for what you pay. Well made, high quality feel that seems it will take a beating and last. Highly satisfied. Would recommend to a friend or family.

One suggestion: after assembly and initial couple of uses, retighten all the fasteners. Initial use may slightly loosen them. After the retighten they'll stay locked in place. I haven't had any issues with things loosening after the first couple of uses.

title: GREAT bike rack for the price!
text:
I purchased the Premier Locking Quick Release 4-Bike Carrier for 2" Hitch on Vehicles with Spare Tire, Model 400QR , Black.

I've used it 4 times since I've purchased it in early April. It was delivered within a week with my Prime membership. Very easy to assemble with great instructions, took less than 10 minutes. It is well made and everything fit together nicely. Easy to install on my previously existing hitch. I have a 2" hitch on my 2014 Ford F-150, and it fit perfectly in it. The locking feature is easy to use and keeps the rack snug in the hitch, no wobble or looseness, and with the key lock I can leave the rack in place while I ride knowing it won't get stolen. I purchased the carrier model for vehicles with a spare tire, and that allows me to lower or pivot/swivel the carrier, while still installed in the truck hitch, and be able to completely lower the tailgate of my truck without hitting the carrier.

It is very easy to mount bikes to it, the supports can adjust to fit various frames. Female bike frames - I'd suggest getting an adapter to cross between the seat stem base and the handlebar base. Those are less than $40, and it makes mounting them just as easy and keeps them better leveled on the carrier as a male frame bike. I've carried up to 3 adult size frame mountain bikes of varying weights, and the carrier was able to easily accommodate them and handle the load. Getting a 4th bike on the carrier would be no problems at all. The rubber straps very securely hold the bikes to the carrier. I carried 3 adult size mountain bikes on a 7 hour ride (one way) and they did not move a bit. It comes with a long binder-type strong nylon strap that you can thread between all the bike frames and around the carrier's main post to stop the bikes from swaying going down the road, but I suggest getting some velcro straps to secure the wheels to the bike frames so they don't spin going down the road. You can get a 12-pack for under $20.

Overall I am VERY happy with this purchase. Considering this carrier is about a third or so of the cost of big name brands such as Thule, Yakima, etc, I think it is a very good quality item and a great value.

We can pack it full of drinks, thin ice packs, snacks, and sandwiches for a day at the beach for 4 (2 of which are pre-teen boys with bottomless appetites for food and drink). I could not justify spending $300 on a Yeti / Yeti knockoff, plus those empty are heavy as it is. We were at a SC beach in early August, had the cooler packed, used 2 larger ice packs and 2-3 thin (space saver) ice packs, and everything was still cool at the end of the day after an 8hr day (keeping the cooler in shade as much as possible). There are some complaints of the zipper being a little tight, but some zipper lube quickly took care of that. The pockets on the sides and front are a HUGE help, and the pop-top quick access in the lid helps keep thing cool. Straps, hardware are durable and well made. We've had this cooler for 2 months, made several trips to the pool and beach, and it has taken all the beating we've given it with style. text: For many people this will be the perfect mini trampoline and I have to say that I am very impressed with the quality so far. For me personally the only thing I would like is if the handle bar or stability bar was a little more...well, stable.  It fastens into two brackets (the brackets are fastened to two of the legs of the trampoline) with those little pop out pins... you know the kind you squeeze to push them down and then the bar can be pushed into the bracket and then the pins pop out through little holes to hold the handle bar on. Yes it holds the handle bar on but it is a little wobbly and if you have any type of stability issues already it could take a little while to build up trust.  I cannot use the trampoline without holding onto the bar and I haven’t had any problems yet but it’s just taking some time for me to trust it LOL  For the average person I doubt that this would be even a thought but like I said for me personally I would prefer the handlebar to be a little more solid feeling. Do I use it yes! Am I enjoying it yes! Will it be up for sale in six months no!  I chose this particular one because I wanted springs rather than the bungee type cords that could wear out faster  It does make a little spring noise but if you have music going you’re not going to notice it at all. The jump area was larger than expected and very nice. I am getting serious workouts on this thing with very limited movements on my part.  Putting it together was super simple it came in a taco shape and you just opened it up and then lifted the legs up and they went into place. The instructions did note to be careful when I unfolding which I did not read and I did smash my finger LOL my instructions showed a different stability bar that had bolts to hold it in.  I don’t know if that was for an older model or what but it makes me kind a wish that the handle did fasten with bolts.  Don’t be scared of my negativity though as far as the handle goes I am only reviewing this on how I feel about it for my own personal use and like I said I do have very restricted mobility and balance.  I would recommend this to others. You can get a serious workout in 20 to 30 minutes. For those of you wondering about the size; if you are familiar with the round Costco dog beds it’s about the same size as that.

title: Row, Row, Row Your Boat
text:
I have owned most types of exercise equipment out there: treadmills, climbers, Spinbikes, recumbent bikes, total gym, ab machines, ellipticals, weight benches and all sorts of small do-hickys that were made to help you maintain or get into shape. No, I'm not a shopaholic LOL I am naturally small to average size but need to stay fit and healthy. Over the past year or so I have hit that dreaded time my mom and Aunts always warned about: that time when everything you ate stayed with you and loosing a quick five pounds was no longer a simple thing. One big note here though; One of the reasons I have had so many different types of exercise equipment over the years is, I have cerebral palsy and need to stay at a healthy weight and try to keep flexibility and cardiovascular health as high as I can have. Unfortunately I have found that many types of exercise equipment have something that prohibits me being able to use them effectively. For example, the total gym is a great piece of equipment however most of the exercises that I want to use involve laying on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the slide board. For me it is nearly impossible because of my muscle tightness I am unable to do that as well as a lot of the other exercises that require a bit of balance or flexibility that I just don't have. I also have weaker leg muscles so a lot of the other equipment seemed to either wear me out immediately, or I'd have to used my upper body exclusively. Several months ago I began thinking about a rower. I actually ordered and canceled a different, less expensive rower that had gotten good reviews here because I'd been reading independent review sites and the Concept 2 had always gotten great reviews and I knew I wouldn't be happy with lower quality. The water rowers looked good too but frankly I couldn't swing the cost especially since as much as I hoped a rower would work for me I knew the odds were I'd be selling it if it wasn't something I could use well.
Assembly was probably the easiest of anything I've ever owned. The hardest part was getting the two pieces out from the Styrofoam! LOL Eight screws and the screwdriver was included. The item is well-made and feels sturdy but wasn't too heavy for me to assemble on my own very easily. All you are doing is attaching a V shape bracket to the rower and then down to the flat piece that sits on the floor. Once assembled you just lift the front piece of the machine (one handed it's not too heavy) and the back part has a little hook shaped end that goes down on a bar on the front piece and you lower the machine and the parts lock together. The machine is long but narrow. Storing may not be as easy as a machine that just folds but stays in one piece, but on the other hand having the two pieces come completely apart could make storage easy if you needed to put each piece away in different area.
Now for the usage: As I have said I do have limitations and I do know they make a different model that sits up higher off the ground and it is supposed to be easier to get on and off if you have any type of balance or mobility issues however I chose this model because I felt it would be easier for me to get on and off. I did have to make one adaptation: because I do not have normal flexibility, I found that once my feet were strapped in I could not quite reach the handlebar to begin rowing, so I borrowed my Service Dogs tug rope she uses to open doors and attached it to the handlebar of the rower. It gives me the extra length that I need that once I am seated with my feet strapped in I can use the rope and pull the handle bar up to begin rowing. If you are heavier or built where you're not able to reach the bar comfortably this is an easy fix.
When I first began using the rower I found as I had expected that I was using very little to no legs, however after just a week I am able to use my legs some. Nowhere near the "normal" amount of a correct row form where your legs are doing about 60% of the work, but I have seen enough improvement already to know that as I continue my leg strength will improve enough to where I will be rowing in a more full body natural form. The reason I am saying this is just to let you know that even if you are limited and you're not able to start out with the "correct" rowing style, you can still use this machine. I think it is important however to know what the correct form is. I would suggest going to the Concept2 website and watching a video. It's not difficult at all but I do like to remind myself as a row that it's legs core arms and then arms core legs. Since I did not have leg strength to begin with I needed to be aware of not pulling with my back. They also have a great video on adaptive rowing for those with physical limitations. So you can see that this really is something that everyone can use and benefit from.
The machine is quite. Not silent but you can watch TV while using it without having the volume to max. You set the amount of air to allow through the machine by sliding a "damper" lever. The more air the more resistance but your pull also makes a difference so you can get a more challenging workout just by changing when and how fast you pull. The monitor is small but the numbers are large and easy to read. It has several features but I find the "Just Row" is what I'm using now. I also have an app on my phone and the rower and my phone connect via Bluetooth and it will log my information so I can have a record of my workouts. The app also offers a verbal feature so if you are visually impaired you can know how you are rowing as far as distance and time.
They also have software that allows you to see yourself in a boat rowing against other people that you can see on a monitor or your tv.
Even though I've only had the machine two weeks I can easily say it will be one of the very few that I will keep and use. It is by far my favorite and I'm already seeing improvements. I have lost 5 pounds and know that I am improving not only my cardiovascular system but I am getting stronger and more flexible as I can see improvements in my leg use. I started with 0% legs and now am maybe 10% and that's a big improvement that will only get better. Oh and I will add that it is FUN!!! I actually enjoy rowing. Something about the repetitive movements and sound I find enjoyable.
I do not give five stars often at all because I am extremely critical and consider all factors. This rower and the company has not only met but exceeded my expectations and I would recommend it without hesitation.
I'm looking forward to using this for years and seeing a real improvement in my health and happiness. If you have been considering this rower I would say go for it!

title: Love it!
text: I have a Spinner brand Spinbike with a narrow, hard-as-a-rock seat and decided to get this seat pad in hopes a more comfortable ride would entice me to ride more. The seat cover isn't as wide and bulky as it looked in the photo. It might not work on an extra wide beach cruiser type seats but for regular and narrow it should be fine. It slips over the seat and a string and toggle are used to  cinch it tight.  If using this on an outdoor bike you will probably need or want to cut the strings shorter or maybe tie a bow once it's fastened on.  I was kind of concerned that this would be a little slippery because the material is slick but I haven't had a problem staying on the seat when spinning quickly.  I would also like to note that when I ride I do not usually wear cycling or work-out shorts and the shorts I do wear have seams in them so before I got this seatcover I was experiencing quite a bit of discomfort,  but I don't want to have to go in and change my clothes to exercise because it's just another excuse to not do it.  My first ride when I received the seat cover was just over 30 minutes and I was wearing a pair of cargo shorts. I had very little to no discomfort while riding and even the next day I only noticed the slightest hint when riding again. I am very pleased with this seat cover. If it lasts well I will have no reservations to recommend this to everyone. For now it getting a solid five stars based on fit, ease of use (it would be very easy to take with you to the gym and put on/take off their bikes) and comfort. Oh and I'm a female if that's helpful.

title: Very nice cooler.
text:
I don't have a Kayak but was looking for something to take camping. Initial impression is that it is thin, but that is deceiving because there is actually quite a bit of space to carry stuff. Easily fit a couple of six packs, sandwiches and other snack items. Interior is definitely leak proof. I actually filled it up with water & ice and left it overnight. No leaks at all and about 1/3 of the ice left. One really nice feature about this is that the whole 'cooler' is covered in a waterproof material so it would not get wet when splashed with water. The quandary here is the waterproof part. I have confidence that the interior and exterior will repel water, the zipper has a nice water seal. There is zipper compartment on the front of the cooler that is also lined with rubberized fabric. Not really sure why you need to make the interior of a zippered pocket waterproof if it doesn't have the same water seal zipper
It has lots of attach points around the case to tie things onto. Several ball stretch tie offs are included. It is interesting that there are attach points for a shoulder strap but one did not come included. Main thick rubber carry handle with double stitching.

All in all a very nice cooler keep everything dry in some reasonably heavy rain, and if it fell off the kayak.

For my use case a definite recommend and it will be part of my regular camp gear.

title: Interesting but needs a lot of work.
text:
Just came back from a camping trip and this looked like a great idea so I was really looking forward to it getting here. Unfortunately I have been underwhelmed. Much smaller and less solid that I expected. And not waterproof at all. I have other flashlights in the same size range and they feel much more sturdy. The beam of the flash light is pretty weak and diffused. A small bright spot in the middle and thin weak circle surrounding it. Not really useful at all beyond 5 or 6 feet. The lens cover is a very thin plastic and likely to be very easily scratched or broken. There is no water seal around the lens. On the other end you have the arc lighter. While works well, it is too small to be any more useful that lighting a cigarette. If you wanted to use it camping you have use it to light a piece of paper and then use the paper to light something else. The USB charging port is under the cap that covers the Arc lighter. This cap is not waterproof and the minute you get this area wet the whole thing is ruined.
Given that it is clearly not designed to be used as a camping tool (which is exactly what comes to mind when looking at the listing.) I am not sure where it fits. Maybe if you are a smoker that has to walk outside to smoke? This is an interesting concept that was poorly executed.

Unfortunately this is a 'Not Recommend'. Wouldn't spend my own money on it.

title: Nice yoga mat
text:
As a yoga beginner, I have few comparisons for this mat, except for the two classes I took before I owned the mat, in which I used mats provided by each respective yoga studio. The studio mats were of "normal" thickness, and although they were sticky enough, they were too thin. The Aurorae mat offered a significant improvement in thickness, although for some poses I still have to use additional padding, such as a blanket (but then everyone in the class is doing that, regardless of the mats they're using).

As the instructions advised, I did thoroughly wash and dry the mat before using it. I washed it with a large sponge in a bathtub filled with very warm water and a few generous squirts of dishwashing detergent. The first time I used the mat after washing it, I noticed my hands slipping a bit during downward dog, so when I got it home, I washed the mat again, and for the second washing I scrubbed the mat's surface with a soft body brush.

That seemed to help, although I suspect if you're sweaty, you'll get some slippage even when the mat's clean. I think it's important to remember to wash your hands (and feet?) before yoga practice, if you want to minimize slippage on the mat.

Overall I'm happy with the product, and I'd buy one again if I needed another mat.

The hiking poles are so cool! I have had MS for a bit over 30 years and have been using a cane to help with balance but it is unwieldy and has me listing to one side. I believe that using these two hiking poles will improve my posture, give me more sensory input to help me maintain my balance and thus, making it easier to walk further, especially on uneven ground.

The hiking poles come with directions to adjust the poles to the correct length and how to check for stability. There is a chart to give the length of the poles and the poles have the the corresponding numbers printed on them to facilitate adjustment. The grips fit my hands nicely. The poles are light weight and remarkably sturdy.

I am looking forward to trying them out at the beach using the snow tips. My cane and walker are both useless in soft sand. I like that I can get replacement tips if necessary.

I’m attending a wedding out of state next month at a farm/barn type wedding venue. I’m sure these poles will help me maintain my balance on uneven ground better and reduce my fear of falling. I’m probably not ever going to hike the Appalachian trail but these poles will help me to be less fearful of walking on uneven ground.

Also, the top half falls apart quite easily if you pick it up. If you pick it up via the sides, the front and back panel will slide right off and crash. There is no way to secure the sides in place once you put it together. I wish they made it so screws could hold it together at the ends, like the bottom half which was designed very well. But no, they didn't do that for some reason.

So overall, gravity keeps the top in place, but it will fall apart if tilted or bumped into. The top half just literally sits on the bottom half, and has four 1/3" pems that sit loosely inside the holes to guide it into looking like one large cabinet. VERY DANGEROUS. low effort top design. text: I have been looking for a vest for my camera equipment.  I got tired of lugging a camera bag around and having to set it down to use the camera.  I was looking at both this vest and the Uncle Milty Travel Vest.  Even though this is listed as a fishing vest I was leaning towards this over the other because of the price since they both had a 4.5 rating.  Because there questions on both vests about sizing I hadn't decided what to do.  Then a last minute deal came up for some travel I had to take.  I couldn't order a vest and get it in time.  I checked the web site for a Dicks Sporting Goods store close to where I live and they had vests in their fishing tackle department.  I went over and found a medium that fit just right.  I'm slender at 140# and 5-8 and have a hard time finding clothes over the internet.  I tried on a small that was more a juvenile size and not adult. The large was too roomy for me.  For people any larger than me a large size would work fine.  The funny thing is the vest I bought is the same exact same one here.  Mine says "Master Sportsman" and not Prestige but looks exactly like this picture.  It was the same price of 24.99.  I used it for my travel and several times since and it is really handy.  I've gotten away for SLRs and use a high end point and shoot camera: Canon PowerShot G12 and a Speedlite 270EXII.  Everything, including batteries and chargers and other stuff, fits in the vest just fine.  While the vest seems heavy when I first put it on I don't notice the weight wearing it.  It is so handy to reach in and get the camera, take some pictures and then slip the camera back in its pocket.  I'll never go back to a camera bag.  I have a small Eddie Bauer hand duffle that I use to carry the vest in.  I just fold the vest in half and roll it up and it fits in the handle duffle just fine.  Because of the weight I use a wooden hanger for the vest to store it on.  I hope the picture shows what everything look like.  It is a really great for around $25.  Enjoy!

title: One Bore Sight For ALL my Firearms!
text:
Works perfectly magnetized to the end of the barrel. This is obviously for scoped weapons as it's diameter is too large for open sights. If you have a scoped pistol this will work for it as well, otherwise you'll want an actual caliber chamber-fitted bore sight IMO.

This is a no-brainer. No adjustments are available for the laser. It either does or doesn't do the job. To test it, simply place it on a flat level surface and roll it back and forth on the flat. The dot should maintain it's position. If it doesn't, return it for a replacement!

Remember, ALL bore sights are simply to get your rifle or pistol on paper at 25 yards without wasting a box or two of ammo trying to achieve the same result. Once there, fire a few rounds at the desired distance, adjusting your scope each time until it's zeroed in at the yardage you desire.

It doesn't matter that this bore sight isn't perfectly centered, as most aren't anyway contrary to popular belief. Even chamber fitted caliber-specific bore sights aren't perfect and you'll still need to fire a few rounds to be sure your actually sighted and zeroed in at the desired yardage. You can center this by hand on the end of the barrel. It doesn't need to be perfect and will be within a half inch or less of barrel center on target anyway.

At today's ammo prices, this will save you enough in ammo costs and time sighting in so that you'll be able to have more ammo for game or target shooting and put you in the field hunting faster than without one. It's "extremely rare" and I stress, "extremely rare" contrary to the claims here and there that a bore sight zeros you in to that 1/2" group at 100 yards. "Extremely rare". Be prepared to finalize your sighting in at 100 yards to zero with a few rounds after you get on paper.

Be knowledgeable and wise about what a bore sight is designed to do and you'll be happy with your purchase. As long as it gets you on paper so you can see your shot on the paper target in your scope or sighting monocular, the rest is up to you!

Only reason many reviewers leave less than a 5 star rating for this bore sight with few exceptions, is because they don't know how to use it or how to sight in a rifle or pistol in the first place. This is the ONLY bore sight you'll ever need to get your scoped firearms on paper for a good starting point. Like I said, the rest is up to you.

It works! If you don't know the exact procedure to zero your scope in, don't be afraid to ask for help.

I wasn't payed or compensated to state my opinion here. The above opinion comes from understanding what these tools are for, a little logic about what your trying to achieve with them, and a lot of experience. Get some if you don't have any and enjoy your firearm and it's accessories to the best they are capable of performing.

title: Great Fishing Pole ! -- You Just Have To Be Smarter Than The Pole !!!!!
text:
I'm fairly impressed for a light duty compact travel fishing pole. The design is brilliant! Great for pan fish and as pictured, some big ones too if you know how to wear them out and not try to muscle a 10-20 pounder in if your lucky enough to hook one with this rig! You shouldn't be baiting and gearing up for big ones to start with using this pole. Like I said, pan fish as in blue gill, crappy, brook trout, small 2-4 lb bass etc is what this is designed for.

Think about finessing any big ones with your fly-fishing technique if you're lucky enough to hook a 5-10 or 20 pounder. Let them wear themselves out and then real them in once they're whooped and have no fight left. Make the fish work, not the rod... but you knew that right?

I have a small lite duty spin-casting reel with 8 lb line on it (typical lite gear) that I keep in a reel pouch with some "basic" tackle and a couple small lures. That and this pole inside my back-pack or saddle bag on the HD and I'm ready to fish anywhere I stop. All I need to rig up is either a small lure, or a hook and some bait. If there's fish in the water, dinner's pretty much a sure thing!

I'm blown away by the incompetence of some of these reviewers though. You just have to be smarter than the darn pole people!!!

First off, there are several 'presumably' carbon fiber sections that telescope in and out. Instead of forcing them as some are obviously doing, simply hold the section stationary below the one you want to move in or out. Then twist the section above the stationary one you're holding to loosen or tighten it as your pushing it in or pulling it out respectively.

Use the string guides to hold and "lightly" twist one way or the other. I can't stress enough to do this lightly folks! Don't get all Magilla Gorilla with it.

It doesn't take much effort to secure or loosen the sections. The very thin tip section should be held and twisted at the base where it is connected to the next section below it to prevent breaking it off (duh).

DON'T FORCE THEM! This isn't rocket science folks! It's simple grade school physics. Friction on a tapered shaft. A little lite twist and push or pull is all you need to extend or compact this pole. Mount your lite duty fishing reel on it, a bobber, hook and worm, and enjoy your day!!!

Life recently changed and as I searched for ways to stay in shape I found an old cheap jump rope in the closet. After 3 weeks of trying, with some moderate success, I realized that the rope I was using was holding me back. I needed a longer, heavier, sturdier rope.
I spent a good amount of time comparing reviews. I just got back from a workout with this product.

1. The rope is easily adjustable. I am 6'4" and it is a good height for me, but others who are average height will need to adjust. You will need basic tools (phillips screw driver and strong cutters), but you can always ask a handy friend or family member to help.
2. The rope is thick, and the handles are large. They work perfectly for me, but if you have small hands or issues with hand/joint pain you may want to take that into consideration.
3. The product is made out of good quality plastic. It shows signs of wearing from the first use, but that is to be expected. I would warn people to be careful and not throw this on the ground, the handles would likely easily crack/break or cause gouges out of the plastic that could be painful on your hands.
4. The rope is 1.5 pounds, and the weight is in the ROPE.
5. The rope performs well, is sturdy, and offers good swing and feedback. You can easily slow down or speed up as you're jumping, and the rope keeps a nice arc even on windy days.
6. One reviewer said this left red marks on their legs, I don't see how anyone could do that with this rope without some intention. It does weigh 1.5 pounds though and is fast, so be careful of your surroundings.

Overall this is a good purchase and addition to my isolation routine. I wanted a solid $30 option, and this product fit the bill.

title: Physical Therapy at Home WONDERFUL MAT
text:
I had a hip replacement over a year ago, and things haven't gone as planned. I'm still in physical therapy. It's been discouraging, to say the least. I'm only 50, and people 20 years older than me recover better. I've been losing motivation to do my exercises at home, because I get on a damn yoga mat, and everything hurts. I got online to find an exercise mat I'd like more, trying to reinvigorate my motivation. I thought this would be "ok" . Somehow I thought the 2" of thickness would probably be a lot of air along with cushioning. I was wrong: This mat is great. If you're in PT a lot, like I have been, you will appreciate and LOVE THIS MAT.

Other than the excellent cushioning (I weigh 180 lbs, at 5'8), I love that I don't have to roll it. The handles are perfectly positioning to pick it up straight, fold it, and tuck it behind a door. The fold doesn't create a big gap at all when it's flat, you really can't even notice it. The thing doesn't slide easily. It doesn't have grippy material, but for some reason, it barely moved on my hardwood floor, which is great when you're doing PT exercises. A slippy mat would have been dangerous. I can't even think of one thing wrong with it. If you are doing PT, or know someone who is, get this mat. Would be a great gift for someone doing PT.

title: Husband loves this adjustable day pack.
text: Finally got a chance to take the bag out and put it though it’s paces. We don’t have any camping trips planned for now, but we put a towel and 10 lbs of weight and off we went. He’s 6 feet and skinny for reference. Took it for a thirty minute walk in 90 degrees F and 49% humidity. The pack felt good. The air gap was great, and kept him from overheating. He said the bag sat well and didn’t shift once secured. He is right handed and a lot like my other hiking backpacks, there is only a zipper pocket in the left waist band. This is because you don’t usually reach across to get something in your waist pocket on a hike. The right side is a non zip folded pocket. The rain cover stuffs in a Velcro pocket on the bottom and fits snugly over the entire pack. The large roomy main compartment fits everything I would need for a weekend hike, or a long day hike. Food, camp stove, change of clothing, single man tent, jacket and the large capacity reservoir. There is a hook to put the reservoir on so it doesn’t slip down as you empty the bladder. The bite valve is the standard camelback with shut off (this is important if you have ever been hiking and broken your bite valve and didn’t have time to dig out a spare until base camp.) this is Not a carry your laptop and tootle around town pack. This is a well made solid day/weekend hiker. Yes it would be nice to have a small inner zip pocket, but that’s what carabiners and dry sacks are for. It has a mesh two compartment pocket, and a larger pocket the whole bag length. Water reservoir has its own zippered compartment, and there is one center small zip pocket for quick access item like headlamp. Has a large adjustable mesh pocket on the outside that you can put a helmet, or ground roll. Can’t wait for camping to open up again, I may just steal this from my husband for scout campouts. title: This is a good idea just not executed well.
text:
I was looking for people who had similar problems with my UP and saw that several folks had the exact same problem.

First I have owned the original and the 2.0 Up. Mine has been replaced a (if you count the replacement in the works) twice. Mu husband's once. I do not shower with mine or wear it during heavy workouts. It is not very accurate on exercise, so I just log the workout and move on. We bought this because I am a programmer, and my husband is a lawyer so the fact this one reminds you to "get up and move" by buzzing is wonderful. That is about the only thing great about it. BUT it is a _big_ great since if it can save your life I don't care how many of these things I have to go through.

Now for the bad....

I thought mine was the only one that grew bigger. The band starts off fitting loose (i wear the medium), and after a few months it swells becoming tight and uncomfortable. Both bands that have failed have done so at the push button end. It stops working after some kind of firmware failure..or could be battery since it won't hold a charge, or it could be any number of things (the band itself feels mushier than when I first received it) But either way, it worked like a champ until it didn't, then an exchange of phone calls and emails with customer service results in a new band and we start over again.

There is nickel in the silver end cap (I am allergic to it) and if I forget to turn the cap around so the metal does not touch my skin I end up with a wonderful itchy rash. I have painted the ends of my cap with a clear coat of nail polish which lasts about a week before I have to repaint it, but that does fix the nickel problem. Still, with a sizable percentage of the population allergic to nickel (see fit bit recall), you would think they could design a band without it. Make the whole end silicone, or offer two caps in the package, one with the silver, one without.

I exercise regularly but either my activities are not available, or I have to take the band off to swim and it does not record biking accurately so for me the activity tracker is sort of useless. I use other systems to track swimming and biking. I have a very good bike computer and comparing UP data and the bike computer made me laugh.

The sleep tracking algorithm is really strange. It records me in bed and asleep hours before I am asleep, and sometimes does not record that I had to get up and let the dogs out at 3am. and Yes I am hitting the sleep mode making the band go "moon" as we say here. I don't believe the sleep data beyond I hit the moon and wake up and hit the sun... so it tells me the elapsed time between those two button pushes.

Other folks have commented on it, but I cook my own food and a lot of it is asian. So.... food tracker it pointless. I don't eat fast food or things with bar codes I can easily figure out the calories of. Though I do use the tracker to see how much water I have drunk in a day. This is especially helpful on campouts and hikes.

If I get a replacement for this band, I will probably give it to my son and let him wear it. I am ready to find one without nickel and that won't break after only a few months of wear.

Customer service has been terrific. Both my husband's and my replacements have been quick and easy. Though no one believes I know what I am talking about. I am a programmer, my husband is an EE and a lawyer. Please believe me when I say I have done the soft reset and it is not working. I even performed a hard reset... nada, but ok I will do it again with you on the phone...twice, and no it still is not working :-P...OK call me back in two hours when it should be charged... meh.

I have other things to do with my time like make some $$ so I can buy a different band that will work for longer than a few months at a time.

In the end it is a good idea just not executed well.

title: Love the features -- the fit doesn't work for me
text:
I've been using a Fitbit One for years now. Really love it. But I wanted to get the pulse tracking feature, so purchased the Charge HR recently.

I do love it for the HR monitor, and sleep tracking is a lot easier on the HR (having to put on that wristband to track via the One was an added annoyance). And the caller ID feature is cool.

But there are two things I don't like as well. First, I have a very petite wrist (small bone/frame). The Charge HR looks huge on my wrist, and really doesn't sit well. The inflexible part with the face sticks out beyond my wrist, where on someone with a bigger wrist it would flex where it needs to bend around. Hard to explain!

The other thing, which is probably related, is that when I wear a winter coat, the sleeve pushes the FB down on my wrist where it digs in and hurts.

This isn't significant unless you are competing against others rather than just against yourself like I do, but I think the Charge HR counts more steps than my One does. I haven't changed my routine, but I find I'm hitting my 10,000 much earlier in the day than before.

Oh, and I have to charge the HR more frequently than I did the One.

After 4 months of street/easy trail riding (that my 6 year old can do - not extreme or punishing on a bike), the right pedal arm fell off of the crank. It clamps down on a hex shaft, using a hex head bolt to tighten it, but as much as I could tighten the bolt it will not stay on. The crank assembly is also coming loose, and needs constant fighting in between reattachments of the right pedal.

This bike is going on the curb shortly, and I’ll be in the market for a higher quality BMX bike.

Could have been a fluke on this one. Maybe the tolerances from manufacturing were out of standard - whatever - but if you can toss in another hundred or two I would look for a higher quality bike.

1) beautiful packaging - attractive sturdy box, professional labeling, etc. Does not seem like a typical mass-produced "China Special."

2) good design - two hand warmer in one, with a magnetic connections that keeps them together.

3) comes with carrying pouch

4) rechargeable

5) available in different colors

6) you get TWO hand warmers in one - perfect for those of us who have two hands, two pockets to keep warm, etc.

7) they feel sturdy yet are relatively lightweight.

Now the bad news: the first set I received worked well ONCE. The second time around, one of the halves wouldn't charge.

I requested a replacement through Amazon and returned the first set.

After 3 uses, one of the "halves" in the second set stopped receiving a charge as well. Thus, this set is going back to Amazon.

The concept of rechargeable hand warmers is great. However, the technology itself seems to need refinement, especially when it comes to recharging.

title: I wanted to love this product...but design needs improvement.
text:
This infuser water bottle has many positive attributes but could use design improvements.

The good:

* plastic feels solid and of good quality

* comfortable bottle size - fits one's hand perfectly

* lightweight - easy to throw in your bag for hydration throughout the day

* generous "basket" for inserting herbs, fruit, etc.

* infusion works great! I inserted fresh mint and am loving the way the water tastes, even after filling up a few times.

Areas for improvement:

* the area between the top of the infuser and edge of water bottle is too small. Thus, when drinking my upper lip touches the orange insert. Similarly, my nose (which is not big to begin with) also has the potential to hit the "handle" of the orange insert

* infusion basket is somewhat difficult to remove. Having a tab/handle with a hole would make gripping it easier.

* bottle is not insulated and "sweats" with cold water. Not a deal-breaker, though.

Update 7-9-2016

I've been using this infusion bottle for a few days and just knocked another star from my review. :-(

I find sipping from this bottle very uncomfortable...to the point that I'm going to leave it in my 'fridge all the time and use it as a "pitcher" of infused water. Bummer...

So I had to carry it when I went hunting which defeated the whole purpose of having a "backpack" stool and made it a major pain in the butt. Otherwise it worked once I carried it to my hunting blind. I'm sure it will be fine when I don't have to wear a heavy coat but I did buy it to use during deer season. I'm going to try to find some strap extensions to try to fix it for next year.

title: Great Purchase
text:
Purchased this little pop up in August 2018 and have used it almost monthly since then. Most of the "beads" that the rainfly loops attach to have popped off but overall, the tent has held up well (I clip the rainfly to the tent to keep it from flapping around).

It was originally purchased it as a beach shelter but it has only been used it as a wood & gear tent. During rainy weather I throw a tarp over it so cannot speak to how well it does in rainy conditions if you're sleeping in it.

text:

Absolutely love all the little pockets! Unfortunately one of the straps has started to fray at the seam after one month of use. Thankfully, it's not an important strap so.

title: Uncomfortable & they do not stay up
text:
First of all, these socks do not stay up on me.

Secondly, they provide heat on the top part of the foot. In boots or tennies, they do not provide a feeling of warmth when outdoors since the heating elements are essentially between your feet & the cold weather. They may be more effective with insulated footwear though.

When indoors, they heat quite well but are uncomfortable. I personally do not like the feeling of heat on the top of my feet. My toes have never been warm in these socks, which defeats the purpose of purchasing them. I like my piggies warm.

They were worth a try but I'm off to find something that provides heat under my feet and toward my toes.

While these may not be my warming footwear of choice, they may work for you.

title: Held up as well as my AquaQuest
text:
Purchased this for a two week camping trip on the Oregon Coast. Due to wind and coastal mist, I used it as an extra large rainfly over my hammock. Each day I would secure the ocean side of the tarp to a tree for visibility and at night I'd secure them to the ground for wind block. There were wind gusts up to 25 miles and it held up remarkably well. I use bungees w/my tarps at the coast to provide some give in the varying winds and reduce stress on the tarps.

This Gold Armour held up as well as the AquaQuest tarp I setup over my picnic table. Very pleased with the quality of this tarp for the price and plan on purchasing another one.

They are also invaluable between the two layers of socks I wear to bed but that generally makes me too hot so I stick them on various places in my sleeping bag so that I can move my feet closer to them when needed. Be warned though - they can get quite hot so I would not recommend placing them against your skin.

title: Not strong enough to tighten properly - pole would not stay extended
text:
Unfortunately, these tarp poles did not work for me at all. I tried a set out last weekend and one of the poles would not stay extended. I tried to tighten it up as much as possible but it kept on retracting, which collapsed that corner of my tarp. I purchased two sets and am sadly returning both.

I am a mid-forties lady who primarily camps alone and my hands are not the strongest. These poles may work well for someone with stronger hands & better grip. If you need to ask someone to open jars for you (like me), these tarp poles may not be the best.

Aside from not being strong enough to tighten them up properly, these poles seemed well built and sturdy. I live in the rainy PNW so was a little concerned about them holding water (as mentioned in a different review) but did not have an opportunity to find out. Love the compact nature of this product and the carrying bag. Wish they had worked for me.

9/26/2018 Update

Itai from Green Elephant emailed me asking why I returned the product so I sent a screenshot of my Amazon review. Below is the reply I received.

"Hi Kimberly
I'm very sorry that our poles did not suit you
This is the first time we received such a complaint and we are definitely are going to research it.
To this day, our customers have not mentioned this problem
We usually have the ability to compensate the customer
In your case and since you have already returned the poles we have no way of compensating you
The review you left is legitimate and important, but gives the impression that the product is defective, which directly caused a drop in sales.
We would appreciate it if you would be kind enough to change the review slightly so that the damage would be smaller.
Thank you for your cooperation
Itai "

title: Perfect Fireside Blanket
text:
My dog likes to sit in my lap when we're by the campfire. I purchased this to cover her up and protect her from any stray sparks & pops. It is FABULOUS. We used our old blanket (an old synthetic bed cover) for years but it was in no way fire retardant and it took one good spark to make the blanket smoke. It was extinguished quickly but my dog was not comfortable near the fire afterwards. (I know it was ignorant to use a synthetic blanket next to a campfire but I grabbed it heading out the door for our first camping trip and since it worked didn't change it. DERP)

After our fiasco, my dog was scared of fire so I decided to purchase something wool and after careful consideration ended up with the Ektos blanket. Best purchase ever! She loves the blanket and is on my lap again. I love the blanket too. It is heavy but not overwhelming and not nearly as scratchy as other reviews made it out to be. Mind you, I'm not laying my bare skin against it. Bet it would be uncomfortable if I were wrapped in it half nekkid and sweating ...but I'm not, so it is perfect for what we're using it for. Both myself & my dog have piece of mind using this blanket as something of a campfire shield for her.

9/7/2018 Update

My husband used our campfire blanket as an extra layer to sleep in. He said it was perfect so I just ordered another blanket for him!

The original blanket I purchased is obviously still in great shape & being used regularly. I wash it on delicate and put it in the dryer on extra low. The first dry will produce a good deal of lint but the lint tapers off after that. It has been washed several times and has softened up a bit since purchase. I suspect we will end up purchasing a few more of these over the next few years since it is so hardy and versatile.

I would absolutely recommend this blanket others.

5/17/21 Update
...and I'm back to purchase yet another blanket! In a pinch, I had to use one of my campfire blankets in my hammock. It worked so well I am picking up another one to store with my hammock gear (along with another underquilt). Old Ektos are still go with us on every camping trip!

text:
I've been using a Lightspeed Sun Shelter for years now for both camping & beach time. The old one is getting a little worn down so thought it best to order a backup to have on hand. I also want to spray it a few times with scotch guard and use some seam sealer on it before taking it out. I have been known to use my shelter during rainy weather with a plastic drop cloth draped over (and under it). That said, change to a structure that was (to me) perfect will take some time.

I am not a huge fan of the new double draw open (the one I have been using opened with a single rope - like drawing a bow string back) but it should be okay. I am also not keen on the new double push down closure method as it is abrupt and throws your body off balance when the structure "unlocks."

title: Great car camping tent - easy one person setup & it's held up very well in the wind & rain
text:
I camp or yurt at least once a month during winter and up to three times a month during warmer weather. Yurts are great during cold & rainy months but in the Pacific NW, a gal has to prepare for rain every weekend no matter what the time of year.

Set the Cabin Tent up for a trial run in the garage this weekend. I am in my early 40's and stand a towering 5'0". I was tickled to have it setup within minutes, first time. Putting the rain fly on was a bit trickier due to my height but manageable.

Interior of the Core 6 is spacious. Easily enough room for a full sized air mattress, table and gear

Breaking the Core 6 down was a snap.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
09/13/17 Update

I have used the CORE 6 many, many times since my initial review. It has held up very, very well in PNW rain. I do wish the rain fly either extended down or out a bit more as I am not able to open the windows during a down pour without water dripping in them. Aside from that the tent itself has kept the rain out beautifully.

There is A LOT of airflow in this tent and I have tried multiple ways of covering the ceiling netting before attaching the rain fly in hopes of trapping some heat inside. A blanket over the roof (and under the rain fly) kept the heat in very well but it got rather humid.

The bottom of the door can be a bugger to zip up. I have found that making sure the tent is not staked out too tautly in front helps but it does not alleviate the issue. Two hands are definitely needed to zip around the bottom corner of the door.

The Man borrowed the tent for a camping trip with The Boys and loved it. They were able to sit inside with a table and lawn chairs to play poker while it was raining.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
10/12/2018 Update

Recently camped on the Oregon Coast and was notified of a storm warning. Packed my gear & firewood in the Core 6 and reinforced the stakes. It was noisy inside with all the wind so the dog and I ended up sleeping in the car. Winds hit 26 mph and the Core 6 took a pounding but stayed intact and functional. There was a little bit of puddling inside the next morning but that was on a side where the tent lifted and the footprint shifted out from under it and collected rain.

text:
Does exactly what it is meant to do, provide heart rate. It does not come with bells/whistles & basic is what I was looking for in the purchase of my first HR monitor. The chest strap is comfortable.

There are two features that might not suit me:

1.) After activating heart rate monitor, the unit automatically changes modes between HR, current time & exercise time when monitor is brought close to chest strap. This can be irritating when cross training;

2.) I do not think the wrist monitor works does not consistently work if not being worn. I have taken it off to avoid the auto mode change and sometimes it will display "00" other times it seems to work fine. Reviewing the user manual to see if this is an issue of user error.

All in all, it was good purchase. Inexpensive, effective & a great starter monitor. Next purchase I will have a better idea of what features to look for to compliment my workouts.

title: Far from perfect, but the best I've found yet.
text:
This is the best thermos I've owned to date, but it's far from perfect.

If you put piping hot coffee in it, it will keep it hot for about 45 minutes, and keep it warm for about 2 more hours after that. I haven't used it for cold drinks.

I love the handle style; that's my favorite part about it. Most handled thermoses have this infuriating issue of the mouthpiece never lining up properly with where the handle is, so you always have to hold them weirdly to drink from them. On this thermos, the handle is fabric, and can be adjusted 360 degrees around the thermos, so no matter where the mouthpiece ends up, you can just adjust the handle to be right where you need it. the other nice thing about the fabric handle is that you won't break it by bumping it into things or dropping it.

The worst part about this thing is cleaning it. The entire head of it is very complex, with lots of moving parts, springs, and plastic bits - ALL of which are submerged in whatever you are drinking. So, when you take the lid off, you have disassemble the whole thing and either soak all the parts, or wash them all individually. Don't be lazy and put off cleaning it until the next day or you'll have whatever you drank caked all though the innards. If you don't mind keeping it clean, it's really nice. I'm very happy with it.

title: Damaged on arrival, and noxious to boot.
text:
When this vault arrived, the fist thing I noticed was that it's not actually Caldwell brand, it was some other random safe brand (it was either lockdown, or bulldog I think, something like that). the second thing I noticed, as I opened the packaging, was that the vault was smashed shut, so that the two edges, or lips, weren't flush with each other, but instead completely overlapping on one side with a big gap on the other. It sort of looked like a big crooked overbite. The hinge in the rear was also clearly bent out of shape too as a result.

It took a lot of prying with a crowbar to get the dang thing open, which was a big mistake on my part. This vault has the same problem that a lot of the other brands that make this type of vault do: the foam lining on the inside smells so impossibly strong that it is absolutely choking. Let me put it this way: I had this vault open for less than one minute before wrapping it back up, and getting it boxed back up to be returned the next day. My apartment stunk to high heaven of that foam for four stanky days after it was gone. The thing had barely been opened! Anything that would have been placed in that vault would have probably stunk well beyond the end of the universe.

As for whether it actually fits a large handgun, well, there was no way I was putting mine in there for fear that it would be forever polluted. The safe was large enough to fit an 8 inch overall handgun, but I don't think that it was thick enough to close over a revolver; but maybe a thinner pistol.

title: Guess I got a lemon...
text:
I read so many raving reviews about this Fort Knox safe that I waited for months for them to come back into stock (the entire internet was sold out!). Once they finally came back onto Amazon ("The Safe Place" was the vendor), I immediately bought one. Upon examination, the safe itself was very well built. Quality metal and extremely sturdy. Then it came time to program the combination.... Oh my, what a mess. As others have stated, the combination is kind of difficult to figure out. You need to completely unscrew and remove the lock from the safe to reprogram it, which is a mess because it's underneath a layer of foam padding totally covered in glue (which gets EVERYWHERE).

The problem for me started once I did manage to get the combination reset and put back into the safe. For whatever reason, although the combination part of the lock was functioning fine, the actual unlocking mechanism on the safe kept failing. What this resulted in was the combination working (click!), but the safe failing to unlock. Humorously enough, while I was packing the safe back up to return it, it spontaneously burst open when I turned it on its side. Thinking perhaps it had fixed itself, I tried relocking it and reentering the combination. "Click!"...... Stuck locked again....

So, it did end up going back. Unfortunately, the vendor wouldn't pay return shipping on it, and this thing is HEAVY, thus it cost a fortune to ship it back. This thing ended up costing me a whole lot of time, effort, and money, and I'm glad it's gone. With so many positive reviews, I have to believe that I may have just received a lemon. The vendor offered to exchange it for me, but I was too nervous to lock valuables inside of even a new one, with the fear lurking inside me that whatever I put in there may stay there for good. I am giving it two stars though, because even though it didn't work, the build was very impressive, and had it worked, I would have loved it.

title: Satisfied with a few issues
text:
As there are plenty of reviews, I'm going to do a review that assumes you've read the rest and I will try and hit some of the criticisms. I've owned my DMT for about a month and a half. I'm not an overly picky or difficult person, as some reviewers seem to be. Not criticizing them, just letting you know that I may be easier going than you are. I got mine at $2399 so for me this was a bit of an investment and I read all the reviews I could find. Since Smooth only seems to publish the great reviews on their website, I am publishing mine here. I do think the Treadmill Doctor reviews are fair and accurate, but they seem to have a chummy relationship with Smooth.

I ordered the unit and the Smooth Sync Bluetooth module. I ordered it with the white glove service as I'm lazy and it's heavy. First, the ordering process, here is my timeline:

- 12 Jan 13, Order placed with Smooth via web
- 12 Jan 13, Email confirmation of order
- 18 Jan 13, Credit card charged
- 18 Jan 13 Product Shipped Notice
- 27 Jan 13, Contacted by shipping/assembly company
- 28 Jan 13, Product received/assembled
- 29 Jan 13, Smooth Sync received/installed

The unit arrived in one large box and one ridiculously large box. It would have been difficult for my 21 year-old son and I to get it in the house. Unless you are awfully burly or have moving equipment (a standard dolly won't get it) then at least have it delivered to the room where you want to set it up. When assembled, even using the wheels, if I moved it by myself I would be hurting the next day. As others have said, the assembly duo (from CEVA Logistics) had never seen one before, but had assembled similar items. They assembled it correctly without damage to the unit or anything else in about an hour. I'm pretty handy and I think I could have done it a bit quicker. If you assemble it yourself, you are primarily assembling the upright portion. When we tried using it the first time, something was banging. They disassembled one section, reassembled and everything was grand.

Smooth forgot to ship the Smooth Sync so it wasn't available day one, but UPS ground got it here the next day. It installed in just a few minutes with no problems.

I did quite a bit of research before buying. I use ellipticals at the gym and I own a top of the line Bowflex. The Agile DMT replaced a Proform 7.0 Treadmill that gave up the ghost after 14 years and several moves. In terms of engineering, construction and features, there is absolutely no comparison between this and my Proform. This is a gym quality machine with more features than any gym will ever pay for. Contrary to what others have said, the speakers are not bad. The fan is a bit cheap, but on the highest setting it provides a little breeze. The display/control panel is functional but not impressive.

Others commented on all the plastic. While it seems a little silly, it does cover a lot of the moving parts such that you can move around the device without hooking or snagging and it prevents dust and dirt and will make it easier to clean.

As I mentioned, I bought the Smooth Sync. While $130 seems like a lot, if you consider that you are paying for the hardware, the app and the integration, it is not bad. The MySmooth app is good. The video application is interesting, but definitely not something I would pay $20 a video for. It appears Smooth spent quite a lot to shoot the videos. In the current market, they would probably be better off letting users upload their own with the MySmooth app controlling the speed of play. The Android app does not record workouts and accessing the History button crashes the application. Smooth does not have a page with news about the app.

As for customer service, I've never received any response from Smooth that appeared remotely human. It took 6 days to get another email after I placed my order. When the CEVA tracking showed that my machine had been in town for a week and I had received no call, I sent an email to Smooth. I got no reply, but I noted on the bill of lading that Smooth had contacted CEVA and told them to get moving. CEVA called me the day after I sent the email (email Saturday, call Sunday, delivery Monday). When I sent Smooth an email to ask about my Smooth Sync (several weeks after I ordered it) my response was the UPS email notice with no other response. The device arrived the next day via UPS ground. In my book, this is adequate but certainly well below average. I would have expected the order confirmation to provide some type of information on when I could expect a follow-up on shipping. I would have expected them to ship my Smooth Sync so that it was here when the machine arrived. For the price, I would expect at least a follow-up email to see how the delivery/install went and if I had any problems. All of this would really merit a "very good" not an "exceptional" these days. I get follow-up emails from eBay sellers to see if I'm satisfied with a .99 cable.

Smooth was recently purchased. The new owner is continuing the product line and honoring all warranties, etc. Supposedly they are investing millions. Hopefully the person in charge of customer service takes his or her buyout and moves on to be replaced by someone more competent. I say that as I think the products are excellent, so it is too bad when one person brings the company down to simply being good.

As for the white glove delivery install, I live in the DC area. If you don't get experienced assembly people here, odds are you won't elsewhere. My installers got it together with no problems and didn't take all day. I'm satisfied and would do it again.

This is an observation, not a criticism. In my opinion, the bands don't offer enough resistance to really be used for building muscle size. They might be better considered as used for toning. What I've done is combine all five bands together, which do provide a fair amount of resistance (I've also had to tie on a 6th loose band to get the resistance I want). Fortunately, the 'D' ring that the bands attach to on the handle is large enough to add several bands. This kit does appear to be of high quality, and I have no issue with that, and for certain exercises I'm sure one or two bands work fine. I got them to hang on the door, and do the "band pull-up" move where I have one knee and one foot on the floor, and pull them toward me. My suggestion is to hang them close to the hinge side of the door so you don't put extra pressure on the doorknob side, lest it burst open (trust me on that one).

EDIT: I have to update this, because I kind of messed up. I failed to notice these come in a variety of tension sets. I ordered the "105 pound" set, which means if you add up the tension in all 5 bands, it comes to 105 pounds, which I didn't find to be enough. I should have ordered the "150 pound" set. In fact, I did go ahead and exchange the smaller set for the larger one with no problem. Just be careful to order the correct set of tensions!

title: Good, but not perfect
text:
First, to establish my street cred, I'm retired and play lots of golf. Last year I played 118 rounds. I play year around and walk/carry, walk with push cart, and ride in a cart, mostly depending on weather. I need a bag that is easy to carry but also also works on carts. I like to have all my stuff with me in my bag. Rain gear, extra gloves, rangefinder, umbrella, sunscreen, water bottle, Advil, windbreaker, cigars, towels, balls, tees, etc. you get the picture.

This bag is nice looking, but after playing a few rounds with it, it seems it was designed by a designer, not a golfer. It's attractive and generally speaking, it's functional. But there are a few things I can mention that are why I'm deducting a couple stars. Golfers like me will know what I'm talking about.

The good things: I like the dividers. There are several and they keep the clubs well-separated so you can easily see each iron and don't have to shuffle the heads around to find your 9-iron. The legs pop out solidly and pop back in crisply when you pick it up. It is very, very light....so all the weight you will feel is from the stuff you load into it. The carrying straps are wide and comfortable and there is some nice padding on the side that hits your back. The insulated cooler pocket is nice, but I haven't had a chance yet to see how it does in 100 degree Texas heat. Gotta be better than nothing though right?

The issues: While not necessarily show-stoppers, these things could be better. When you load this bag onto an electric golf cart, the golf cart strap you pull around your bag to hold it on comes right across the top of two zippered pockets. In other words, if you want to get into those two pockets on your bag, you have to either a) unhook the strap holding your bag on, or b) keep those zippers halfway down to be able to get into them.

The next thing is also somewhat minor, but worth mentioning. I have a Sun Mountain Speed Cart, which is a 3-wheeled push cart you set your carry bag on when you don't to carry it. This bag is a little bigger than my old Titleist carry bag, and it doesn't "nest" into the arms of the push cart perfectly. It works, but this bag kind of sits a little awkwardly in the Speed Cart.

The zippers. The reason I needed a new bag was that the nylon zippers on my old bag finally failed. You know how nylon zippers will ultimately just not zip? The zipper thing goes up and down, but the two sides stay apart. Well anyway, this bag has nylon zippers too of course, and these seem to be of lighter duty than my old bag. They may end up working fine for years....but they are definitely of a smaller and more dainty construction.

Finally...the thing I am most disappointed in is the zippered pockets themselves. Remember I said this was created by a designer rather than a golfer? Well, when you unzip the pockets, you can slide your open hand in and feel both sides of the pocket pressing on your hand! It's like they are designed for small flat stuff! The big front pocket for golf balls is the only one with ample room. The others are very tight and I'm worried cramming all my stuff in there is going to put too much pressure on those dainty zippers!

The price is attractive, and hopefully it will hold up to the beating I am about to give it. If somebody reminds me in a few months, I'll update my review after putting it through the paces of several dozen rounds. Fore!

When I first got it, I thought, there's no way I'm getting that tiny thing over my giant deformed knee.  But, with not that much effort I DID.  And, it wasn't gappy.  And, I was doing step aerobics (low impact) comfortably - which I haven't in ages.  I was and am thrilled.  For me, this thing is a game changer.  I think that part of my problem is that my knee innards are actually sloshing around in there.  It FEELS like that, but with this support, no sloshing.  My knee is stablized.  My knee is one bendable thing instead of a bunch of loose parts.  My knee is happy.  I am happy.  I'm MORE than happy.  Like I said.  I'm thrilled.

title: Well thought out and organized, but...
text: I loved the thought and organization put into this book. Having said that I was somewhat at a loss as to what to rate it because some of the pluses could also be considered minuses. It covers 4 pieces of stability equipment: Bosu Trainer, Extreme Balance Board, Balance Cushion and Wobble Board. On the one hand these pieces of equipment are readily available, but since it only covers these 4 pieces of equipment you are limited to these. The book is around 60 pages, small enough to put in a gym bag (and it is part of a series that appears to be designed for that purpose) and handy for reference, but some may feel it is more of a booklet. The exercises are divided into upper and lower body exercises and the pages are color coded on the edge so you can easily locate these sections. The exercises are further defined by type: static, dynamic, reactive (act-react) and by novice and advanced. Each exercise shows what muscles are worked and which of the other pieces of equipment can be used as a substitute. There are also some body diagrams so the muscles can be identified if you are unfamiliar with the names/locations. Everything is kept brief, but clear. Personally I prefer the small book to the huge, heavy exercise bible you will probably never pick up and refer to.

title: All things considered, not good enough
text:
Pros:
1. It DOESN'T have an SOS mode (thank you, Suboos). Simple button cycles through low/med/high/off.
2. As the product description states, the light output and design is suited to tent camping. A small light you can hook at a high point to provide general lighting.
3. Kinda cute and simple.
4. Hook is useful, and light can hold its position somewhat to the angle you set, though it's not real stable.
5. Fairly inexpensive. It's basically a flashlight.

Cons:
1. "Ultra bright" is an overstatement. It's good general lighting for a small space, like a personal tent. I bought it as a reading light for a small space, but it's not bright enough -- has to be about 1 foot from the book to be bright enough, so, would have to lay down and put it under my chin to read. Not. And that's on the brightest setting.
2. It's not waterproof, so why call it "outdoor"?
3. Why use AAA batteries? I never understand why flashlight manufacturers do that. And in this instance, replacing batteries is a tedious process of loading a cartridge (in just the right way) then installing the cartridge in just the right way.
4. Cold, bluish colored light. Would be better if it were a warmer color.

All things considered the "cons" outweigh the "pros" so I give it a thumbs-down.
