title: IMPORTANT Info to help people set up the Hi-Rise legs EASILY!
text:
A few people have complained about putting the Hi-Rise legs on the WaterRower, and they gave it a low rating for that reason. I’m an old lady and I figured out how to do it. I’m writing this review with a few tips to show that it really is EASY. The WaterRower is a fantastic way to keep old tired muscles in shape, and even people who are not that good at DIY (like me) can put it together themselves.

#1 You need a POWER DRILL for the screws (only for the Hi-Rise screws, not for the rest of the WaterRower). Reason is because the screws are going into hard wood. Same “screw hole,” but these are different screws. An “extender” for the screw bit is useful, but may not be necessary (my screw extender is around 4”). Everybody should have a power drill. Borrow one if you don’t have one.

#2 IMPORTANT: The screws to attach the Hi-Rise are not the same screws as for the rubber pads. They are shorter, have a flat head, and different screw threads. You're supposed to get a bag of 16 DIFFERENT screws for the Hi-Rise. If you try to use the screws from the rubber pads that came on the rails, you will not be able to get them into the hard wood, so don’t even try. I ordered my WaterRower from a third party on Amazon, and it was perfect, except that the bag of screws for the Hi-Rise was not included. If that happens, call WaterRower. They sent me a bag of screws, even extra screws, and I got them in the mail the next day.

#3 Get a DRY bar of soap (or some hard wax, like from a candle). Roll the screws back and forth in the dry soap wax to cover as much of the screw’s thread as possible, including the tip of the screw.

#4 You don’t need to drill a pilot hole for the screws because they already have a pilot hole from the screws for the rubber pads that came on the rails. You don’t need to drill the hole bigger.

#5 Use the power drill to slowly drill the screws in as far as they comfortably go, without any strain, then back them out. Do this a few times, in and out, and they will then go all the way in without effort. If you manhandle the screw, it can strip the screw and then you’d have to use Vice-Grips to get the screw out. If you go in and out, slowly, several times, with the soap wax on the screw, it will go all the way in without effort, without any manhandling.

The rest of the assembly of the WaterRower is a breeze. A few people have complained about putting on the Hi-Rise legs, but it sure does make a difference getting on and off the machine, especially if you are an old lady with arthritis in the knees.

ALSO, if you buy from a third party, know that if you call WaterRower, they will register your machine (get the serial number off the back of the meter on it), and you will get two additional years of Warranty for FREE. I was also told, after registering, that the water purification tablets are free, for the lifetime of the machine. They sent me a few extra tablets with the screws.

AND ALSO - please note: I asked WaterRower if it's a good idea to install the Hi-Rise legs first, before assembling the rest of the machine, and they said yes, it's fine, no problem with assembling the rest if you do the Hi-Rise legs first.

If you live within driving distance they will even assemble your machine for you for free, no matter where you bought it, if you have a vehicle that can transport it back home. They can’t ship a fully assembled WaterRower.

The WaterRower people are friendly, helpful, and very accommodating!

title: 4 month upadate
text: I'm a 75 year old man who has been riding a regular bike for years and years but my knees were telling me that hills were no longer their friend. I moved from a place with NO hills to a place where hills are everywhere so I decided to look in to an ebike that was within my budget. This bike seemed to be just what I needed so I decided to give it a shot...First thing was it was very easy to assemble (Youtube helped)..then I decided to take it for a spin. This bike is a completely different experience so my advise would be to practice in a place that's deserted...so here's the low down on my first week of riding on a regular basis....first, this bike will get up and go and reach 20 mph very fast, and for me that was my first surprise, then getting a feel for the 5 levels of resistance 1 being the most and 5 is where you hardly pedal at all, but here's where you need to pay attention....the throttle takes up about half the right handle bar so it's very easy to accelerate when you don't want to so pay attention...then there the issue with the kick stand which seems be very wobblily and a little unstable....having said that, I really like this bike, it's very easy and fun when you get used to it...quick note, I would not leave my house with charger plugged it just to be safe...So now on July 13th or having the bike for over a month the only thing that is driving me nuts is the kick stand...it flops down over and over again even after tightening the so called locking mechanism..it is aggravating and turns my bike ride into a hassle.....it's a terrible TERRIBLE design....................*******.........So I've  owned the bike almost 4 months and I continue to love this bike, I replaced the kick stand and replaced the seat with one a lot more comfortable, The one thing that, for me, makes the ride safer and more predictable is....if I'm riding near people or on roads with intersections I keep the resistance on 1 or 0 and use the hand throttle to provide power to the bike. I used to keep it on 2-4 but found that when I wanted to stop if any pressure was put on the pedals when trying to stop immediately throws the bike forward when you're not expecting it..I learned the hard way and it wasn't pretty..In my opinion controlling the bike with the hand throttle is the safest except if your riding on a trail or on a road with no stop and go...This in my opinion is the best and safest way to operate the bike with the electric assist....aside from that this is a great entry level bike at a very good price.  I look forward to many more miles of fun...

title: revised review
text:
I purchased this charger as part of a system replacing my 15 year old Trace inverter/charger. This a very nice charger- the front panel readout is fantastic- no more guessing what my batteries are doing or what level of charge they are at. I particularly like the equalize feature; my batteries may go through as many as three charge/discharge cycles in a day so it's very important that I am able to equalize them on a regular basis. My only criticism is the size of the terminals for hooking up the battery cables; they are rather small and close together. Standard automotive cables will have too large of a terminal to connect to the posts on this charger without touching each other. The ac input wiring was a little akward too- just a pigtail of three wire with no way to cover the connection without installing a junction box.

Revision: for several months this charger has been intermitantly overheating and not charging my battereies. I thought it was a battery problem since they were reaching the end of their lifespan however I've replaced the batteries and continue to have the same problem. The last time I called Xantrex for warranty issues they were extremely unhelpful but I will give them another chance. Stay tuned for updates.

It’s still pretty new, so I can’t say how it will hold up but I hope it does because I’m pleased with it so far.

title: Quality & thought out details
text:
This Stanley cookware camp set is of a nice quality food grade pro level stainless steel. The set is Sized for limited storage space in mind yet useable decent size… as well as for easily fitting on camp stoves. Car, Jeep or trailer camping. They stack/nest nicely & have well thought out details.
The 4 stars for ? Of lightweight.. because these are a heavy layered bottom pans to cook more evenly. .not one layer & a light weight pan type. The bottom is even & heavy, with flip up (& can detach)handles with a slide down ring to steady /keep handle locked in proper use. . Flip over for when storing. Lids doubles as a strainer & the pot lid also has a double use, can be used as lid on skillet plus it includes decent spoon, spatula set, they are snapped together easily & taken apart, stored in set with good size silicon Pot holders. The cutting board, lol.. until some breaking in time, can be challenging but is of a decent size, Appreciate you at least have a cutting surface included. I like the top bungie strap that keeps the whole set snuggly tight, so no rattling. Usually it’s only 2 of us at camp, except when we family Vaca camp with our grown kids.. this set is good but I do bring additional iron skillet for needed additional cooking needs.
Follow directions on seasoning.. use with enough oil or butter, use at a lower heat to stop sticking but cleans up easily if happens. Use a low heat with soapy water to soak some for stuck on foods. Outside of pots, you can try to help keep nicer, some say rub a soap on to help in clean up later but open flames will tarnish shinny new look. . & if using over one. Flame, over coals preferred. But it’s the way this set heats up & cooks that counts. Clean to keep build up of oils, etc off set. I’m pleased & will be using set hopefully for a long time. I caught my set on sale making this set a great deal. If deciding, go with this set, you won’t be disappointed.

title: I love this treadmill!
text:
Like so many of you who reviewed this treadmill, I did my research. It took a while but I finally settled on the Horizon T101-04. It got great reviews everywhere I looked.
My treadmill arrived on time and undamaged. I asked the driver to take it down a slight grassy hill and around thru my back door and he did. I was concerned about damage because so many reviewers had problems with broken parts. I have some blemishes on the arms of the treadmill and a tiny crack on the arm of the console but other than that, it's in perfect condition.
My friend Tom (with me "helping") put it together in about 40 minutes - from box to completion. No problem with assembly and the instructions were straight forward. There weren't a lot of parts so that was a good thing. I liked that all the screws were in little plastic bags and marked as to which ones to use first. The tools needed to assemble the treadmill were included except for a screwdriver. We did not lube the belt prior to use.
Everything worked as soon as I plugged it in. Yes, the warning beeps are LOUD but I live alone so only the dog is startled when I turn the treadmill on.
This is a good solid machine. I did my first 3 miles on it yesterday and nothing moved except me. No squeaks either. I am 5'8" and 147 lbs. My long stride presented no problems. And, this treadmill is very quiet. It has 2 cup holders and I use one to hold the TV remote. Ironically, I watched "CHOPPED" while I did my work out. The fan is not very powerful, neither are the speakers but I don't care about that. I liked that you can program your workout and I am doing 18 minute miles. You can also increase or decrease the speed as you go along and the incline is great.
This treadmill has more bells and whistles than I care about but it's nice that they are there.
The machine is resting on a mat which is on carpet and again, nothing moves but me.
I love this treadmill. I am beyond happy that I bought it. It's so nice to not have to worry about weather and sidewalk cracks when I am walking along. I received this treadmill just in time - the weather man is predicting some snow showers for Sunday!

title: I'm glad I bought it!
text:
I have wanted a screen room for ages now as it's impossible to enjoy dinner outdoors after dusk due to the mosquitos and various other bugs. I researched many screened shelters at all price points and decided to give this one a try due to good reviews and affordability.
My friend (male) and I put it up yesterday. Yes, it was easy to put up but not as easy as some other reviewers indicated. Once we got the hang of it, we could see that next time we would get it up in a couple of minutes. As it was, it took about 10 minutes.
Remember that the poles are on the OUTSIDE of the tent. Also, don't extend the poles until you have the screen room in place. Make sure the zippers are open so you don't tear the screen.
OK so the screened room is terrific. It is exactly what I wanted and given the price, I can't believe how happy I am with it. My table and 4 chairs fit nicely into the space. You couldn't really fit more than that in it. We have it on my deck. If I had it on grass or the ground, I would be concerned about bugs coming in through the bottom but as it is, I think it will be ok. My only complaint is that there is not enough weight on the bottom to keep the bottom flaps stationery. I think we may put some 10 lb weights on every side so the flaps don't move in the breeze. I still can't figure out how to keep the zippered flaps open but that's a minor issue. We attached the screened room to the deck so it wouldn't blow away. The instructions say that you shouldn't keep it up for long periods of time because it wil fade in the sun. Since I don't care about that, I'm hoping to keep mine up all summer.
So, in summary - if you are looking for a screened room that does the job and doesn't cost a fortune, buy this. You will be happy with your purchase.

title: A satisfied customer  STILL
text:
I researched ellipticals for quite a while before ordering the Schwinn 430. My friend, Tom, also researched this type of equipment until his eyes fell out of his head. He wound up buying the Sole for about twice the cost of the Schwinn. In any event, he recommended the Schwinn as a good buy for the price. I then read just about all 400 Amazon reviews and FINALLY made my purchase.
I ordered my Schwinn 430 from Amazon on 3/1/10 and it was delivered on 3/8/10. I was delighted that it was delivered so fast and also happy about the free shipping.
My machine was delivered by ABF Freight Co. I know that some reviewers have complained about the shipping company but I had no problems at all. The driver was wonderful. He took the box down a small hill to the back of my house, up two steps onto the deck and then into the house. He was great!!!!!
It took Tom about 1-1/2 to 2 hours to put the machine together. He had just recently put together his Sole and so the parts were recognizable to him although I nearly passed out when I saw the photo of all the parts in the manual. Tom said that the manual was straight forward although there was an addendum for a particular washer. We didn't see that until I said "hey, what's this piece of paper saying?" All the pieces were accounted for and all the holes lined up perfectly. He used some of his own tools but used the supplied allen wrench where indicated. We didn't lube the parts as recommended by some reviewers.
I've used it for 3 days now and there is not a squeak to be heard, except for the creaking of my knees. I'm 5'7" and about 150 lbs and the 18" stride is fine for me. I'm a former runner and in good shape (I thought). I have the elliptical on level 1 and after 20 minutes, I've worked up a good sweat.
I agree that a backlight for the computer would have been nice but it's not a deal breaker for me. The 6 programs are more than enough.
I think this machine is well made and feels very solid. There is no rocking or moving. I have it on a carpet and did not buy a mat. I love that it has a small footprint. The longer machines would not have fit into the space alloted for the elliptical. For the price, it can't be beat. I highly recommend it.
I'll post again in a month to let you know if there is any squeaking. It's been almost 3 months now and I still love the machine. No squeaking at all. Good workout and still happy with my purchase. It did develop a squish (not a squeak) but then worked itself out.

title: Really is Easy to Set Up!
text: I am slow brained at mechanical things and my first Coleman tent I bought a decade ago took way too much time and frustration from my vacation in the great outdoors to figure out and it had too many pieces so I had to keep referencing the manual.  Plus I had to buy a duffle bag to keep it in because no average human could refit it in the case it came in.  Looks like Coleman too was slow brained, but now it's the opposite with this tent.  It really did take just a few minutes my first time setting it up.  I'm sure my second will be 60 seconds or less.  And afterward I was able to fit it in the carrying case, though I wish it were just a little bigger because I needed help squishing the sides together when zipping...like me now at size 14 trying to get into my wedding dress of 30 years ago.  I'm so glad I can put the tent up by myself.  I use an extra long cot from Walmart and had to set it on the diagonal to fit and even then it's poking the tent fabric a little on the outside.  There isn't much room left on either side of the cot's interior.  I'll keep this tent, but I wish I bought the tent for six people, even though I often camp alone.  I like having space to set a little desk and walk around.  I haven't been in rain yet, but I did spray the outside with water repellant.  I looked all around at the seams and didn't see the seam irregularities some here complained about.  It looks really pro.  In the middle of the day I went inside to take a nap on a day that was about 80-85 degrees.  It was pretty warm even with all the windows unzipped.  The sun was beating down directly overhead, so I'm ordering the rain top even though it doesn't rain much in So CA.  I'm thinking and hoping that maybe that rain top will deflect some of the heat from direct sunlight.  If you too are slow brained, I'd strongly suggest watching some online videos like on YouTube to see how people set up this tent before you begin.

title: Not a Good Self Defense Knife
text:
Well, first off this is my first assisted opening knife, so operationally it was new to me flicking it out. Anyway, about the knife, it is a very well made. I have no problems with the quality of the construction of the knife.

But, how would it work for self defense situations? I carried it this weekend to see how easy it would be to get to it in a quick deployment situation. What I found is that the clip was to tight and it would be difficult to get off of my pocket. ok, no big deal, pair of needle nose pliers and it is looser. But what I noticed beyond that was that the single button used for locking and releasing the blade can cause deployment problems. Wanting to show off my new knife to a buddy of mine, I pulled it out of my pocket and tried to flip the blade. Damn, it was locked, good thing it wasn't a bad guy. What I found is that when you put the blade in your pocket, or when you reach for it, there is a very very good chance you have put the button in the lock position. So when you pull it out to deploy if it is locked, it is locked and you have to unlock it before flicking it out. Unfortunately you cannot disable this feature because this button also serves to lock the blade out and releases the blade for folding. So, unless you can train yourself in a very stressful self def situation to use fine motor skills to unlock a button, I wouldn't use it in that capacity.

So bottom line, good knife, but wouldn't use it for self defense purposes. I'll keep carrying my other non assisted opening Gerber knife for self defense.

title: Didn't know the inlet/outlet openings were only 1/4" but fortunately I had a 3/4" garden hose reducer with a ...
text: Got this to pump water out of a 55 gal barrel using a 12v battery charged by 45 watt solar panel.  Didn't know the inlet/outlet openings were only 1/4" but fortunately I had a 3/4" garden hose reducer with a 1/4" opening at the opposite end.  I connected 1/4" tubing to the pump.  Put one end of the tubing (connected to inlet side) up over the barrel into the water, & pushed the 1/4" outlet tubing (side with arrow pointing out) into the reducer which was screwed onto a 40 ft garden hose which was stretched out uphill.  I wasn't sure this small pump would move water uphill from a 55 gal barrel for that distance, but after several minutes, water started trickling out of the garden hose onto one of the bushes I wanted watered.  The trickle was just right to have it soak in as I did other chores then came back to move the hose to the next bush.  The arrow on the pump that shows which way the water should flow thru the pump is kind of hard to see, so turn the pump at different angles to the light until you see it.

title: Great Kayak!
text:
We bought this kayak a year ago & used it heavily last summer. I'm amazed at how it has performed. It has a permanent place in our RV. It isn't as bulky as the Sea Eagle Paddle Ski we have & is easier to get to the water. My husband used it for exercise about every other day. I LOVE fishing from it. You can paddle into the tightest & shallowest places to fish & you're sitting (or kneeling) right in the water without getting wet. I would fish for hours comfortably. I would let a large rock in the water hold the boat steady while I fished a spot & not see wear-marks on the hull afterwards, so it became a regular fishing strategy. Especially effective is drifting with the current with a line out. Make sure you carry a large net if you're going to fish from it. I used to carry a one-hand net until I caught a 40" Northern Pike from it. Now I take a pole net.

That's another advantage in using it for fishing. When I realized I had something larger than a bass on my hook, I let out the drag & let it pull me around in the kayak. What a hoot! About 5 minutes later, I saw it was a Pike.

It is also very stable & fun to cross large wakes in. I admit I'm disturbed when in our hard-sided boat, other boats rock ours with large wakes. In the Tahiti I love seeing a wake come my way.

The Tahiti moves easily in the water. We put a skeg on it, which I recommend. It made a difference in tracking. If our boat wears out, we will definitely get another Tahiti. We've already gotten our money's worth out of this one.

title: Great pictures and videos but too many problems
text:
I was looking forward to having found a good camera here, but disappointed. Similar to a sister company's Primos 02 camera that I tried, I found that the field of the motion sensor was misaligned with the field of the picture. I determined this by walking past the camera to observe the results. Consequently, animals to the right of the picture field of view would set it off and you might not get them in a picture at all. And animals walking from left to right would not trigger it until well past center of the picture. The Primos 02 misalignment was worse but the Bushnell wasn't good.

On the positive, the pictures and videos from this camera were very good; superior to the Primos 02 and another camera I tried. The wide screen picture was perfect for my use. The settings allow for both shutter speed and LED intensity which certainly should be useful to adjust for how far away your primary target area is. It is because of the picture quality that I thought I had found the right camera for me. The Hybrid feature to take both pictures followed by videos is great. Unlike the Primos 02, I didn't have excessive false positive pictures.

But then, I changed the shutter speed and LED settings to take pictures on a closer target area which resulted in the camera taking pictures and videos constantly, nearly 1000 in a 24 hour period. If the "Field Scan" were set to ON, that might have been the result but I had it set to OFF. Of course, two days of this drained the batteries.

Another difficulty is that when set to take three burst pictures, the delay was too quick. Per the time stamp, all three would snap within a single second and you cannot adjust this. So your animal hardly had any time to move further through the field of view.

The camera came with current firmware, so an older version firmware was not to blame for these issues. Possibly the product was defective but I returned it for refund rather than exchange, largely because with my Primos 02 experience an exchange of cameras did not fix the misalignment.

title: Good for the price!
text:
This stand is for bikes with NUTS not skewers and the plastic end caps are not necessary. I get better more secure mount without them.
This is a good stand for the money. The weather is wet and cold here and I used to hang my mountain bike up all winter. Here's what I have learned so far. The plastic caps that come on the axle mounts can shear right off if the axle does not protrude enough. One side of my axle stuck out a bit more than the other and the SHORT side was supporting all the weight on the plastic cap. It dropped off this morning and startled me a bit. I looked and saw the problem right away. I threw the mangled cap away and reset the axle after loosening the roller part. The metal to metal connection is much better and no harm comes to the bike nut or frame because only MILD torque is required to secure your bike axle. the weight is vertical, if you see the frame of the stand SPREAD at all you have over torqued! Just snug is fine. It's easy to move the tire to track in the middle of the roller, just loosen one side and then snug the other side till your tire is dead center. The roller tension is kind of by feel. If your tire is really inflated like mine you will need a bit of pressure to keep it from slipping, you can usually feel if the tire is slipping on the roller. Find a medium gear and stick with it, shifting gears is pointless and you'll run the roller to death on high gear anyway. The adjustment for roller resistance is a nice big knob that comes off and on with no tools. My street tires make almost no noise. If you are taking the bike off and on frequently. FIRST take the resistance knob off your handlebars and set it out of the way. SECOND take the roller pressure off so that it's free of the rear tire. THIRD remove the block riser from under the front tire or it will make it hard to get off the rear axle. FOURTH loosen the axle holders, it will help if another person can steady the bike while you do this but I did it by myself (this time). The riser block I got was a bit tall (3 inches) as a reviewer said the stand raised the rear wheel about 3 inches. That put me about 1/2 inch high in the front, but you don't want a lot of pressure on your hands anyway since you are stationary and not going anywhere. I found a short step stool helps me on and off the bike as it is now pretty high. Get on and off as carefully as you can. I will add more if needed to this review.

title: Big improvement
text: I was using a Schwinn No Nose seat which was keeping pressure off my perineum, but was a bit hard and somewhat slippery. I used it for several seasons and wanted a tractor style seat but could not find anything I liked. This seat does NOT come with the rail assembly that bolts to your seat post. I used the rails that came with my Schwinn saddle and they are compatible. To install this seat you must remove your old seat from the rails and LOWER the seat post. This is more work than just putting a new seat on the post as you might normally when replacing a bike seat, but not difficult to do. I find this seat is softer, has a spring like feel as you go over bumps and also has a degree of control that my other seat did not have. I don't feel as if I'm slipping off the seat as I did with the Schwinn no nose seat. I am putting less pressure on my handlebars as well which is welcome as my hands tend to get pins and needles after a while. I'm 65 and in good shape, really enjoy short bike rides and this seat is a good one. It DOES rub a bit on my inner thigh, but it's about the same as when I had a seat with a nose. I wrapped some fabric around the area of contact. You can move the seat a little on the rails to set it forward more. Overall an improvement from other seats for men who are looking to protect their perineum area. Maybe not the ultimate seat but a step in the right direction!

title: Hose connecting nuts were tight WAY beyond specs
text: These brakes were decent until i decided to internally route the rear hose and shorten it a bit.  After trying for many hours to remove the hose from the lever, so I could route my hose internally, I decided to try removing the hose from the caliper end. The connecting nut was so tight, it wouldn't budge. I know how tight they are supposed to be, and this was tight far beyond specs. Almost as if they were never meant to come apart at all. So I took the bike to my local bike shop. After a half hour of trying to remove the hose, they told me there's a risk of breaking something,  land they aren't able to do it because they don't want to be responsible if something breaks. The connecting nut on the lever was far too tight as well. But I was able to break it loose in the beginning. But i was not able to remove the hose, probably because the olive was so deformed from the overtightened nut to begin with. And the nut on the caliper end won't budge at all. So basically, im stuck with a 1 piece break set. Nothing will come apart, because the factory overtightened everything so tight, its impossible to take apart without breaking something.  Im forced to take this 70$ loss, but I do not recommend these brakes if u have  any intentions of ever needing to take them apart for whatever reason. I don't see other reviews with this problem,  so its possible I have an error set, and they aren't all like this. But from a personal perspective, my experience is 100% dissatisfaction.  I'm beyond the return time frame. Lesson learned. Sometimes, even the good reviews can lead to a bad purchase. Unfortunately, I am ordering Shimano like my gut told me to from the beginning.  I'm not weak man, and am Very familiar with all components of a mountain bike,  and whoever or whatever tightened these nuts on both ends of the brake line went WELL BEYOND tight. U may as well have welded them.

title: 4 month review—Not comfortable at all
text:
Ordered in October and it is now February. 4 months of use. Sort of.
The exercise-work-bike took a total of 3 days to put together, and had I been doing it alone, I probably never would have gotten it. There is some form of blue “insta-glue” on the pedal screws that made them nearly impossible to screw in. 3 neighborhood kids and teenagers tried their best to help a lady out, but to no avail. Eventually, I hung my head in shame and begged the assistance of male-friend to demonstrate his masculinity and wield tools to get the pedal screwed in.
I am 5’8. That’s 68 inches or about 172cm.
The next issue came when I realized that even at the lowest adjustment, the one recommended for 5’1-5’4 heights, I still struggled to reach the pedals, sitting with my back comfortably against the backrest. If I scooched forward just enough that half my cheeks were off the front of the seat I could reach the pedals, the backrest, and still use the desk for my laptop! But the desk was still a bit high, so I used the tilt-a-table adjustment to relax my wrists and type with perfectly non-ergonomical T-Rex arms.
And now the clunking noise. I can’t stand it. It started off quiet, but after maybe 100 miles of use, it makes a clunking noise from the pedals and no matter how many times I tighten the bolts (almost to stripping them), the seat keeps wobbling and the handle bars offer very little support.

Overall, as a workout bike, it give options that a regular bike doesn’t have—a table.
As for the rest, I am very unhappy with the very little use I got out of it, the lack of structural support for a solid working/workout of cycling, and how fast it has started having issues.

title: Citronella is a joke. Pure and simple.
text:
If you take the time to research the product, regardless of who markets it, you will find that citronella, as a mosquito repellent, does not, will not, CAN NOT do what it is advertised to do.
The best mosquito repellent is a slight breeze. These insects have extreme difficulty flying/navigating in the slightest breeze.

The reason you see dead mosquitoes in the wax, flame (or light of most types) attracts them. When they fly into the flame, wings, antennaeI, and proboscis get burned off. They fall into the hot wax, and die.

I buy these, locally, to use while fishing. Buy only for the light provided.
To sum it up: people have been told, for decades, that citronella repels mosquitoes, they are persuaded that it works, not noticing a slight breeze, in stead it’s, “Oh, my word! This stuff works!!!”
Do some research. Read a bit. And save your money.
Type in your search engine: how citronella works.
Be amazed !!!

title: Fantastic. Delivered early.
text:
Fantastic!!
I bought the hooks more for decoration, since nothing in our waters here have anything big enough to use a 28/0 hook for.
Tracking info said “...delivery 27 April to 7 May...”
They arrived on 23 April.

I don't understand the reviews:
"Made just like a real hook."
It IS a real hook. Just too big for non-anglers to realize it's real.

It will catch a fish, IF you fish in water that is home to something big enough. Like a 300+ pound grouper, or a big Great White off the coast of Australia. Of course, the rest of your gear would have to be able to handle it also. Rod, reel, line, leader. Everything you put out needs to be capable of handling it.

"Dulled hook to keep grandkids from poking themselves."
These hooks can be dangerous around small children. Teach them the fact that fishhooks of any size are not toys. They can hurt little people. Heck, if you're not careful, they can hurt big people.

But, these are REAL fishhooks. Excellent quality, strength and workmanship.

I presume it wouldn't leak so much if they made sure to push it closed every time they've finished drinking, but my kids just can't remember to do that...

title: Don't want to live without it.
text:
This review is a commentary on my personal experience with Ironman IFT 1000; it is not a recommendation for treatment for any kind of physical ailment or injury. Please see your doctor.

Pertinent info: I'm a 5' 1", 150 lb. 65 year old woman with no other back/neck problems of which I'm aware.

I can't begin to tell you the pain I was in from a pinched nerve in my neck. For a week, I couldn't stand up for more than five minutes without my neck starting to burn and feel like someone was stabbing me. Bad enough that sometimes I really, really wanted to scream. I had to lie down on a small neck bolster with a heating pad on high to stop the pain, which took up to half a hour. Then I was stuck on my back until I was willing to endure the pain again. This was the seventh or eighth episode of this neck pain in the past couple of years, each episode worst than the last as to length and degree of pain. I missed seven days of work this time.

The success of the bolster/heat treatment is what led me to a self-diagnosis of a pinched nerve. You should see your doctor for diagnosis.

I first tried aTENS unit, which was a miserable failure for my particular condition. (I'm returning it to Amazon.) I ordered this inversion table and had friends assemble it for me since I absolutely couldn't do it. (Not nearly as simple as it looks like it should be.) I spent several hours up and down from bed making small adjustments to the unit until I had it right for me. (Tip, although I'm 5'1", the correct height setting for me on the boom arm turned out to be 5'7". I have the strap configured to allow the table to tilt no more than 35 to 40 degrees off the horizontal plane. This is FAR from completely inverted, which would be 90 degrees. However, when on the table, it feels like I'm close to upside-down.)

Once I had it adjusted to my satisfaction, I suspended myself for ten minutes, then waited to see how long it would take the pain to return while standing. 45 minutes! For someone who hadn't been able to eat anything in an upright position for a week, this was a miracle, and such a relief. Went back to bed for a couple of hours, then got back on the table again for 15 minutes. (I recommend sticking with a maximum of ten minutes as it states in the instructions.) I repeated this a couple of times in the next hour or so, sticking to ten minutes. Then I waited for the pain again. I went to bed for the night around three hours later with no pain. I woke up, got out of bed to see how long it would take the pain to hit again. When eight hours had passed and I was still pain free, I went ahead and used the table a couple of times during the remainder of the day as recommended in the instructions. That was yesterday and I'm still pain free and fixing to use the table for the first time today.

I plan on following the ten minutes, twice a day routine forever. I've read that inversion can reverse some of the damage gravity does to the internal organs over the years, compressing them and forcing them down out of their original positions. I'm hoping this will also help keep my heart, lungs, kidneys, liver, etc., from deteriorating.

I didn't buy this model for the heat function, but turns out it works just fine, at least on the first try. I'll probably not use it often, maybe in the winter to pamper myself sometimes. I'm pretty hot natured and additional heat isn't always comfortable for me. If the heat breaks, the table stays!

I'm impressed with the solid construction, the comfort of the ankle holders and the simplicity of the design. I would prefer more padding on the table, but that would probably interfere with the heat function. Attaching a piece of memory foam to the table somehow would probably work great if you don't care about the heat.

I must say that lifting my body forward to step down off the table is a little straining on my back, and someone with existing back issues might want someone else present to act as a "spotter " to aid in that, as well as to help with setting and releasing the ankle holders. You have to bend over at the waist to do that. To lean forward, I find it helps to bend my knees a little, which helps my hips act as a fulcrum. That makes it easier to lean forward to unlock the ankle holders and step off the table.

Please be aware that you may be slightly light headed when you return the table to it's upright position. Allow a few seconds for your head and inner ears to right themselves before you bend over to release the ankle holders. One final tip: If you have the slightest upset stomach, DON'T USE THE TABLE. Your stomach is likely to empty itself without warning - mine did. Probably best not to use the table on a full stomach, either. Gravity is a powerful force to move stomach contents the wrong direction, and the slight dizziness when returning to the upright position will exacerbate the problem.

I hope this review helps you make your purchasing decision.

title: Stable, easy to inflate, fun
text:
We have an expensive Vibe Ocean Kayak weighing nearly 100 lbs and have really enjoyed it for the past 18 months but felt we wanted something easier to load, unload, use and go about our days so we could just go kayaking for half a day, no huge strain, portable, but didn’t want to sacrifice sturdiness and durability so we ordered the Excursion Pro for about $174 each, we ordered 2.

We found it took about 15 min for each kayak when us old buggers blew up the three chambers and, it was doable. We kayaked for a few hours and it felt great, we felt safe in the mangroves.. even with alligators around, we had about 300 lbs and it could have handled more. The Kayak itself said it held only 260 or something but online it said 400 so we ignored the boat itself. It can easily handled 400- 450 lbs..

If I had a negative comment it would be the oars are poor quality so we will use our better oars for them. Also, there is a bit of a learning curve. It took an hour first time and 15 min 2nd time. title: If there's fish to be caught, this'll find them.
text: I've used a red/white daredevil spoon for years to catch northerns in lakes and rivers and never thought I'd need another lure.......until I decided to try a red eye wiggler. I was invited to go to a private lake where northerns were aplenty. It just so happens that I had gone to the tackle store the day before looking for anything perch colored and found the hot mackerel version of this lure in the 2-1/2 ounce. It looked cool along with a few other daredevil spoons so I grabbed them. The biggest ones I could find. The next morning it was a clear day with the water as smooth as glass. The water was a bit murky but I was assured the fish were there and hungry. I decided to strap on the hot mackerel first thing and got to work. 1 cast, 2 casts, 3 casts, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8......... Nothing. I was thinking that I had chosen the wrong lure but was not going to give up. On the 9th cast..............I finally had a bite! Wasn't that big. Just a hammer handle of a northern. Oh well, he was a bit ambitious. I let him go and made another cast just to the right of the previous cast. Had just about reeled it back in and "BAM".....right in front of me just feet from where I was standing in waist deep water with my waders on I had another. And this was no hammer handle, ladies and gentlemen! This one put up an awesome fight! I gave it some time to wear itself out and finally got to put my eyes on it. I sh!t you not, this one was a giant keeper. I had her up to me on my side and could barely hold on to her next to my side. SHE WAS BIG! I'm talking 3-1/2  to 4ft long big! I couldn't believe my eyes. Was finally able to get her on the metal clasp stringer and let her float around for a little while. She just swam around me tied to my leg and then it happened. What I should have done if I really wanted to keep her was wacked her on the head to knock her out, but instead I just stood there in awe of her enormous size. She had other plans to continue living on for another day and jumped up out of the water, thrashed her head side to side, popped that stringer hook open and danced away like she hadn't even been caught.................sigh..................what a disappointment. All I could do is stand there and stare at the water and with disgust. I was a fool, and she knew it. She ended up being a worthy opponent and laughed her way back to the waters where she came from. But don't you worry, fellow fishermen. I didn't give up. I made many more casts that day and caught another bunch of lake snakes, some almost as big as her, many on the smaller side. This lure proved to be better than any other I had tried. I will be sure to always keep one of these at all times readily available and chomping at the bit to be cast into the depths of any body of water that has these prowlers in them. This is a gem. You need to have it (Hot Mackerel) as something you can try if you have northerns in the vicinity. Cast it enough and you'll find them. Great lure. I wish I had 20 of them. Fish on, Ya'll!!!

This past weekend I had a cookout with friends we had the Campfire and my friend had a propane grill.

Start off with some small tinder in the bottom then a squirt of alcohol hand sanitizer as an accelerant, set it off with a lighter.

Begin adding on processed twigs from thinnest to thickest. I would say it was only about 5 minutes for the fire to get big enough
for the gassification effect to kick in and the blazing fire was eating the thicker branch peices with ease.

On this cold day we all enjyed standing around the Campfire to stay warm.

The stainless pots heated up nicely and evenly as we boiled water for tea.
The pot was easy to remove from flame with fold out handles or the bail handle.

When you want a campfire without a campfire ring and campfire mess, this is the ticket.

Highest quality product, highly recommended with no reservations!

title: Perfect Companion To The Solo Stove Titan!

For my test burn it was already dark and chilly by the time I arrived at my test camp site, so I opted for using my Trangia alcohol burner inside of the Titan instead of foraging for sticks and kindling. After getting the alcohol lit and up to full burn, I placed 20oz of water exactly (I know thanks to the handy imprinted measuring lines built into the pot) on the stove and set my timer. At 4 minutes, I had surface bubbles forming at the bottom of the pot. At 6 minutes I saw some rolling bubbles and had a lot of vapor filling the chilly air when I lifted the lid by it's silicone coated lid tab. At 8 minutes I had a full boil and removed the pot from the fire by its cool fold out handles. This winning combo is going to be my go to camp cooking kit. I love it and highly recommend it!

Now, it doesn't work at all. They want me to pay $15/month for the privileged of creating MY OWN WORKOUTS???? Nope! I am updating my warning. They have terrible customer service. The goggles fog up and leak. They're uncomfortable. The app is pretty useless. And SOOOOOO not worth the price or the subscription. They're junk.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I bought them directly from FORM. I'm reviewing here to warn others!

I'll start with the positive: I get a lap split and stroke count that I can see every 25. That's it. That's the only good thing I can say.

They leak, despite trying EVERY nose bridge piece. Customer service strung me along telling me to try different things until it was too late to return for a refund. The app is worthless to me. I don't need canned workouts. I have a coach that writes my workouts. Workouts I can't re-create or import in the Form app. The final blow was after a software update notification, I was not able to update them nor use them at all! They bricked! I've only used them twice a week for 3 months! After a week of repeating the same trouble-shooting steps over and over again, they are sending me a new pair. Not what I wanted. I would have preferred a refund! I wouldn't GIVE these to my worst enemy, let alone recommend them. Take my advice: Don't buy them.

title: Constantly dropping connection during swim!
text: I bought this specifically because it's supposed to work with the FORM swim goggles. Unfortunately, it does not. At least not for me. The goggles are quite wide. So, when I attached the HR monitor to my goggle strap as instructed, it was on the outside of my swim cap! So, I had to wear my goggles under my cap. Not great for my hair, but not the end of the world. During the first swim, the HR would disconnect from the goggles as soon as my face was in the water! OK. The next swim, I tightened the straps. Nope. That wasn't it. So, the next swim, I switched caps to a cap that I don't wear as it's too tight. But I thought maybe it would help. Nope! The connection STILL dropped as soon as my face was in the water. After exporting the FORM .fit file and importing it into GarminConnect (my preferred system of tracking my swim/bike/run workouts), I could see that the connection was definitely dropping. I tried everything I could think of to get it stayed connected, but sadly, it just wouldn't. VERY disappointed. Hopefully, FORM will figure out how to connect with GARMIN devices, like the 945 I wear on my wrist! It has an optical HR monitor. Unfortunately, since FORM hasn't done a deal with Garmin, I have to use it at the same time I'm using the FORM goggles but view the HR data AFTER I'm done swimming. :-(  I love Garmin and their customer support has been AMAZING! I've been using their products for 15 years. This is my first Polar product. I'll be returning it.

text:

What I like: they fit into the pockets of my running vest and the straws are long enough that I don't have to remove the flasks to get a drink. No leaking on the first run. Will update if it does.

Don't like: the fill opening is so small! I like to put ice in my hydration bottles in the summer to keep the fluid nice and cold as long as possible for my long runs in the heat and humidity. The opening for these flasks is way too small to get an ice cube into, even the long thin ice cubes!. The bite valve is pretty flimsy. One of them got screwed up on the first run and I was sucking air instead of fluid. Not sure if I can fix it.

Bottom line: Would I recommend these? It depends. For me, I will probably use these only for winter runs. If they hold up. I'll have to purchase the top of the line insulated soft flasks for summer runs.

My *only* issue with this VaporHowe model is that I wish it came with soft flasks with long straws as opposed to coming with a 1.8L bladder. I like to take my hydration mix (skratch) AND water along for my runs. I had to buy 2 500ml soft flasks to carry in the front pockets. I'll use the flasks way more than I will the bladder. title: The pros and cons of the F35
text:
Pros: This is an excellent hydration system for TT / triathlon bikes. It stays put without rattling around, even on bumpy roads. You have to tighten the little screws to set the mount on the bars correctly or it will rattle (just follow the directions that come with it!). I experienced no sloshing of liquids out of the unit except when I overfilled it (totally my fault, lesson learned). It's easy to drink out of when in aero position. The aero design is excellent. The computer mount is exactly where I need it! I don't have to look down to see my Garmin 920xt mounted on its quick release to the F35 computer mount. It's very heads up without costing anything aerodynamically. The compartment for extras holds quite a bit. I can jam some bonk busters and gels into it and the bands keep them from flying out. Super easy to refill on the go. I have one bottle cage on the front tube. I can easily take that large bottle, turn it upside down and refill the F35 without breaking or stopping.

Cons: Not easy to take off for cleaning. The mounts are supposed to stay on the bike and you're supposed to just remove the hydration chamber. However, the TINY little velcro strap to release the chamber is in a hard to get to spot and if you have anything more than tiny hands with tiny fingers, you will struggle to grab the velcro to release and then re-attach it. Can be a BEAR to clean! Fortunately, I have what amounts to a oversized pipe cleaner that I use for my thermos and bottles so I'm able to get into the nooks and cranies to clean it. The straw is difficult to get back in if you remove it for cleaning (which ya kinda need to do!). The little o-ring where the straw goes into the unit can pop into or out of the unit when re-inserting the straw after cleaning. All of these cons are very easy to deal with if you realize it.

Major con (and the loss of one star): The cost! Sheesh! Expensive for what you get. I got mine for $77.77 here on Amazon. Shop around to get the best price.

title: This is a very good bike for the price
text:
This is a very good bike for the price. Some people are like 'oh it took only a few hours to put together', but I am a student who has a flexible schedule and I can say it took longer than a few hours. The initial assembly took a few hours - around 4 - but the tweaking took a few days. When I first put it together I felt glorious - like I had finished building a colosseum. I decide to take this work of art out for a spin at 11pm. Once I get outside, I get onto the sidewalk and prepare for take off. I mount the bike and immediately take a dive as both the seat and handle bar give in. It was painful.. for my ego. So I go back inside and tinker away. Then come out and hooray, the seat is kind of stable, but the handlebar is shaky. I throw caution to the wind and start riding.. or peddling.. then I see that the chain is like not in place or something? I'm not a mechanic. But I use some of the wisdom my father passed on to me to fix the chain (align it with the gear.. it was not hard or complicated lol.. but if you're not expecting it, then you feel like a fool).. anyway, I am telling you all of this so that when you buy this awesome bike, you won't feel disheartened by the fact that it might not take a minute to put together. Also, don't go to a repair person until you just need it to be tightened.. because you'll have a much better experience if you know why your bike messes up and how to fix it easily when it does. I ended up going to get it tightened because the seat and handlebar war just not tightening with my arm. So the guy who did it also gave my bike a check up and totally validated my pride by saying I did a great job. He only charged $5 for labor (but others did the same for free). Another bike repair man filled my bike with air and also adjusted the seat for me, since I had it a bit high. A lot of people will give you advice on how to sit on your bike, but don't change all the time. Test it out, and if it feels weird and to laborious then go back. Sometimes the advice is for efficiency, but a lot of times it given by veteran bikers who found their way after years of biking.
anyway, good luck.

title: Recommended
text:
Just installed the Mirrycle bicycle mirror today and took it for a test run.

A few observations and comments.

Agreed, assembly is not entirely easy. As mentioned by numerous reviews, the screws drive hard to the point that you think you’re actually cracking the plastic plus the included Allen wrench requires some strength to turn. But not to worry. Read the instructions and they’ll confirm the hard drive and that you will not crack the plastic. I didn’t try WD40 or any other lubricant so cannot say if that would ease the assembly.

I installed the Mirrycle onto a GT hybrid bicycle and after using a Dremel tool to create an opening in the end of my handle grip I found the handlebar opening accepted the smaller of the two wedges for mounting. I chose to follow the alternative down and under installation mentioned on Amazon reviews which is quite clever and works very well however I believe you may get a better site picture using the “normal” above and to the side installation which would facilitate not having to move your eyes so far from your frontal path to do so. The primary disadvantage to the “normal” up-and-out installation is that the mirror really sticks out there very exposed and if/when you dump your bike or ride close to any shrubs, etc., your mirror will be the early casualty, plus the storage shed where we keep our bikes is small which would necessitate tucking the mirror in upon each return. Do whichever works best for you.

From the lower mounting position I could see both myself and directly behind me but I don’t believe that provides the maximum field of view. On my initial trip I stopped a couple times to adjust the mirror in a similar manner to what you would do with a car, i.e., if you can see part of yourself/your bike in the mirror, tilt it out just a little further until you can’t and that should be about right. Once adjusted properly you only need to tilt your head a tad one way to see either part of yourself directly behind the mirror or a tad the other way to see much more of the road to your direct left.

I was amazed at how solid this mirror rode exhibiting absolutely no jitter or vibration. The large convex shape offered a wide, clear field of view which allowed me not only to see what was coming from behind me but also what was to the near left rear of me as well.

This was only my first day with this product but I’m impressed with the quality and the flexible mounting options it offers.

title: I’m a very satisfied buyer who has only just opened the box
text:
I’m a very satisfied buyer who has only just opened the box. I’m not a knife expert, just someone who wanted a good, inexpensive survival type knife.

My knife was delivered razor sharp and as flawless as a $37 knife can be – perhaps as flawless as knives costing substantially more. I read many reviews of this knife prior to purchase and agree that it falls comfortably into the category of survival knife rather than fighting knife.

A couple suggestions. First, check the tightness of all four handle screws with a 2.5mm hex/Allen wrench before you use the knife for anything as they all needed tightening on mine. You might also consider using red thread locker to further secure them. The combination of these two adjustments should eliminate any problem of the grips loosening. To me, the large grips feel just great and I have medium sized hands. Second, the sheath is amazingly adequate. If you feel the sheath rides too low, take it to a sewing or shoe repair shop and either have them move the inner piece of Velcro lower on the sheath or sew an additional piece below the existing piece, which will allow you to fold the outside flap down further thus raising the sheath on your belt. I like the adjustable length handle strap w/snap and detachable front pouch on the sheath.

No doubt this a hefty blade. It may not win any beauty contests or look as threatening as a combat knife, but it looks fully functional for the purpose for which it was intended. I look forward to many years of satisfied service from it.

title: FAST-FAST-FAST
text:
An absolutely awesome cooking system. Fast, fast, fast! Our initial use for the system will be to boil water for single serve instant coffee packets and to re-hydrate freeze dried food which will keep us and perhaps others happy while camping with the scouts.

Here's a common sense but helpful hint for someone using the Jetboil system for the first time - a no-brainer for anyone who has already cooked with this system:

- If you're just boiling water to pour into another vessel or coffee cup for example, go ahead and fully snap the lid on before beginning your boil. You can conveniently pour through the sipping hole.
- If you're boiling water for the purpose of adding food to the pot such as ramen for example, either lay the lid loosely on top or leave it off altogether.

Why? Because once you snap the lid all the way on and the contents come to a boil you'll burn your fingers trying to get it off unless you use a hot pad or other insulating material.

Highly recommended.

title: Not paired properly, poor compatibility with Ibera Plus
text:
Since three vastly different items are in one listing: This is for the individual panniers. They seem solid enough. A bit of a loose seam or thread here or there, seen a lot worse. They have a good bit of space inside, I reckon 3 2-liter soda bottles a side with some stuff along the sides, but it'll be wonky because of the round bottom. The design of the top makes them water resistant, it's not a zipper. The stiffening material is thicker than I expected, will definitely provide protection and support for fairly heavy items. The clips and D-rings don't feel cheap or fragile.

The problems:

I ordered two and got two left-side panniers instead of a matched pair. I didn't even IMAGINE this would be a problem. Title, bullet points and description all need to say "left side only" if that's what it is, AND THE RIGHT SIDE OPTION NEEDS TO BE IN THE SAME LISTING. In any case I don't think heel striking will be a problem, they just look weird.

The top clips are sized for rails no more than 9mm(based on the diameter of the inner clearing, measured by caliper) while the side rails on an Ibera Touring Carrier Plus are 10.5mm. So it only clips on with the first clearing, not very strongly. They also come contracted shut- I had to stretch them out by putting 11.5mm thick pens in each one and leaving them overnight(see attached image.) Now I can at least get the clips on over the rail.

The next problem is that the Ibera rack has no good place to hook the stabilizing bungee. I will need to hook it somewhere weird, which means the panniers can't be taken off with one hand which is a disappointment.

I will try them a couple of times carrying groceries, the purpose I got them for. Their fate is up to how well they do the job.

title: Decent, convenient workout with a handful of drawbacks
text:
I bought this 11 months ago because I didn’t (and still don't, despite being fully vaccinated) feel safe exercising in a gym, and it can be too cold/hot to exercise outdoors. I also enjoy being able to exercise any time without worrying the gym is too busy, and I have to wait for a machine. So, despite the number of cons below, I still am glad I made this purchase.

Pros: I can get a good workout with an elevated heart rate and some sweating. It is indeed compact, and has wheels if you need to move the machine. Low cost compared to other ellipticals. In terms of sturdiness, it still (knock on wood) is working fine after 11 months, and I use it 1-3x/week.

Cons: It took an hour for me to just remove the tape from all the components. I swear you could have dropped the box from a 10-story building, and the contents would have remained taped together. Then it took 3 hours to assemble alone, though part of that was me constantly washing my hands to avoid getting grease on everything. Assembly wasn't technically difficult, but you had to pay particular attention to the details, and the pictures were very small. The trade-off for the compactness is the smaller stride. I’m only 5’3”, so it’s not too bad for me, but many reviewers advise against this machine if you’re taller than 5’6” or so (knees would also hit the bars). Because the wheel is right below you, the footrests are spaced apart more than the ellipticals in the gyms, so it’s a bit uncomfortable, but I got used to it. Others have noted bolt loosening after workouts, and I do have that issue, but thankfully, it's only one of the bolts on the left handle. The black grease along the pedal joints started drying at some point and now flakes off onto the floor (and staining my rug beneath until I started putting paper beneath). You can apply WD40, but this dries out after only a few uses of the machine, so you have to keep re-applying, which is annoying. Those wheels that allow you to move the machine will scratch your hardwood floors (found that out the hard way), so I bought a large plywood sheet to place beneath on the occasion I have to move the machine. I haven’t had an issue to warrant contacting customer service yet (knock on wood).

title: Great tool at a great price! Update on Sept. 15
text:
I looked for a crop with a loop, so I could hang it from the saddle horn when my horse keeps a consistent gait. In truth, I rarely have to use it. Just knowing I have it is enough for him to maintain gait. That said, I never hit him hard, simply a light tap when needed to get him to understand what I want him to do. I first bought a short crop that didn't help at all.

This crop is the perfect length, and it was shipped quickly. I had it two days after my order. [[ASIN:B001CD1O2C Intrepid International Riding Whip, 36]]

I'm happy to report that I no longer need to carry my crop to get my horse to maintain gait. He now understands what I want with only use of light cues. I believe I'll use the crop to tap him when working on new things, but again, I recommend never hitting your horse. A simple tap should do it because horses are so sensitive.

It serves to hold water, and a few other things -- very few. That's about it. The nylon pockets are somewhat flimsy, so you don't want to overstuff the pouches.

There's not enough room for dog treats, and I attach my MP3, keys, and training remote to my clothing or the waistband belt. title: Love it! Love it! Love it! Great Beginner Workout for all ages.
text:
I just turned 61, and have put too much weight over the past few years. I've been walking daily, and going to the gym with little results. I've had my Empower Kettlebell with Gin's DVD workouts for a little more than 3 weeks, and can't say enough good things about it. I'm hooked! While this particular set may not be appropriate for hard-core athletes or experienced "Kettlebellers," I find this an ideal way to get into Kettlebells.

From my first workout, I felt the muscles changing throughout my entire body. No more do I need to move from machine to machine, and spend more than an hour at the gym. With Kettlebells, and get the speedy results someone like me needs to keep motivated. Within three weeks, I lost five pounds, and a total of 5 inches -- mostly in my waist and hips.

I started with the Empower 10-Pound Kettlebell with DVD, which worked well for most exercises. But I later needed to purchase a 5 lb. Kettlebell for the level 2 workouts that required more shoulder strength. I've ust started level 3. You'll never be bored because there are tons of Kettlebell workouts available to help you progress.

I like the Empower Kettlebells so much, I sent a set to my older sister for her birthday. I have no doubt that she'll be happy with this fun and convenient program. [[ASIN:B001O0EG82 Empower 5-Pound KettleBell with DVD]]

title: A fast way to get in shape :)
text:
Admittedly, it may seem too early for me to review the Empower Kettlebell & DVD I received yesterday. However, based on past workout purchases, and experiences, I believe this one's a keeper. I went for the 10-pound Kettlebell, and feel this is a good choice. It comes with a DVD with three levels of workouts, starting with one for beginners such as myself. It also includes warmup and cool-down routines, which are highly recommended before and after each workout respectively.

I started today, and after just one workout, I can already feel my core, leg, and arm muscles reacting to workout #1. While I have a little trouble with the 10-pound weight for some of the curl exercises, I modify the exercises to accommodate my lack of strength, and believe the 10-pound bell was a good choice because it allows me more room to grow -- which will be marked by my eliminating the need for modifications before moving on to the second workout.

In facing my 61st birthday, I'm active, and want to stay that way. This is why I'm determined to get in the best shape of my life (even in my early years, I've never been big on exercise). I started a month ago by purchasing a pair of Skecher Shape-ups, and taking brisk walks with my dogs each morning. To break the monotony, I purchased an MP3 player, and download books from the library. The time flies by!

I added resistance weeks ago with a trip to the gym, intent on going and working out every other day. Then reality hit. It took too long to get dressed, get my walk in, and then go to the gym, work out, come home and clean up. My mornings were shot. So I needed another way to achieve my goal.

A friend told me about Kettlebells. Now, after just one short Kettlebell workout, I've accomplished as much as when using several machines at the gym. The best part is it's fast. I can hop out of bed, and get it done quickly.

Based on numerous past workout experiences and money wasted on a variety of machines and other programs and gimmicks, I'm convinced this is what I've been searching for. I'd recommend it to anyone thinking of starting to get in shape, and wanting fast results. If you're new to working with weights, which I am not, you might want to start with the Empower 5-Pound KettleBell with DVD, and then work your way up to heavier Kettlebells. [[ASIN:B001O0EG7S Empower 10-Pound KettleBell with DVD]]

title: Great phone for the casual user
text:
I bought this phone to replace my 2 1/2-year old Samsung Vi660. I've been a big fan of the Samsung line, and thought about buying their comparable version to the Katana (the A900) but the reviews of the Katana's superior battery life won me over. I am not much for the fancy features of cell phones - I just wanted a slimmer phone that had a lower radiation emissions level than the Vi660, a built-in speakerphone, and bluetooth connectivity. After using the phone for a few weeks, here are my impressions so far:

The good:

* Excellent sound quality (in each direction) and none of that "echo" effect I used to get with the Samsung
* Long battery life with many powersaving features
* Beautiful screen, and with web access, is capable of diplaying Google satellite/map info that is just as clear as it is on a PC
* Menu design is very functional, with Favorites and Contacts being directly accessable through the touch of a button
* The "Favorites" button brings up a customizable list of 12 shortcuts, which can be either web addresses or any tool/function/menu item within the phone's own menus (it's like having a programmed navigation button with 12 different options)
* This phone emits the least radiation of any phone in the Sanyo line, and is in the bottom half of the list when compared to other manufacturers (the top being the highest emitters).
* Did you lose your Katana? Send it a specific text message and upon receiving it, the phone will lock itself up, erase its contents, and display a "lost phone" message on the outside screen with the sprint customer service phone number
* The center navigation button links directly to the "Missed Alerts" feature, which keeps a running list of missed voicemails and text messages
* Bluetooth functionality is wonderful. It is easy to make and receive calls from the bluetooth headset, and the sound quality is almost better than that from the in-phone microphone
* The phone has four different types of vibration patterns that you can assign to different types of calls/text messages, and an easily accessable "silence all" feature (no rings, no button beeps, etc) that is ideal for business meetings
* There is a feature on the Katana that allows you to screen calls as the callers are leaving a message
* Menus and Contact information are arranged for easy text-messaging access and message drafting

The bad:

* The VGA camera is not the greatest, and pictures are usually come out with a blueish or orangish cast unless the color balance is adjusted manually beforehand (settings to do this are on the phone)
* Sound quality from the speakerphone is great but the microphone isn't sensitive enough, and my callers frequently complain that I sound too far away
* The only feature I sorely miss from the Samsung phones is their far-superior voice dialing capability, which is second-to-none. The Katana relies on user-recorded tags for its voice recognition capabilities, whereas the Samsung phones just recognized my voice without any prior setup. That functionality also let me dial any phone number by saying the digits; a feature lacking in the Katana. Voice recognition does work, however sometimes you must repeat the name a few times to get it to work. If good voice dialing capabilites are a dealbreaker for you, I'd stick with the Samsung line.
* the charging port on the Katana is on the side of the phone, covered by a rotating rubber insert that is a bit flimsy. This makes it awkward to talk on the phone while it is connected to a charger.
* The volume controls on the side of the phone are on the upper portion of the handset and they are *very* slim, making them a bit hard to use.

The Katana seems to be marketed towards a slightly less business-oriented demographic (it's available in cherry-blossom pink, that should be your first clue), and its features reflect this. This is more of a phone for the casual user who is interested in a stylish phone with good basic functionality, and doesn't need many of the fancier functions of its competitors.

6 MONTH UPDATE: Would I buy it all over again? Maybe, maybe not.
It's been almost 6 months since I bought my Katana, and I have to say, I'm on the fence about it. It isn't a bad phone, it gets STELLAR reception compared to the old Samsung, texting is a snap, and its got a great screen for web browsing. But I've given up a lot of great features on my old Samsung and I don't seem to have gained a whole lot of new ones. I don't ever use the speakerphone because everyone asks if I'm having problems with my connection. I am really missing the ability to digit dial by voice. Talking on the phone with the charger sticking out of the side (especially in the car) is pretty awkward, as is trying to connect the charger when you don't exactly have your hands free. Sprint gives you 2 weeks to make up your mind on the phone, I'd take a look at these issues during that time and try to decide how much of an issue these things really are.

title: Best coffee ever
text:
Takes a bit of practice to figure out how much coffee you want to use and how long you want it perked, but once you do, it's great.

For a 12-cup pot, I use 6 scoops of coffee and cook on medium-high until I see the first perk-bubble, usually about 15-20 minutes. Then I turn the burner down to medium. You don't want hard-perking, or you'll end up with grounds in your coffee. Perk gently for about 5-7 minutes. Turn burner to low, pour a cup, and enjoy!

I leave the basket and spindle in until I'm ready for my second cup, allowing the coffee grounds to steep a little longer. I use my dishwashing gloves to do this; the basket and spindle are hot.

It's not necessarily a quick way to have your coffee, but it is worth it.

title: Doesn't work unless your arm is down at your side.....
text:
I've had my Fitbit Flex for about a week. At first, I was fairly impressed when I actually counted my steps and compared it to the Fitbit calculations. However, it can be very quirky and inaccurate under certain circumstances. I have mine on my right wrist, and I am right-handed, so I made sure to set it to the "Dominant" wrist setting. But, to get truly accurate readings, your arm really needs to be at your side. If I'm carrying things around the house, I don't get an accurate count. If I'm walking through the store, pushing a grocery cart, I don't get an accurate count. It seriously under counts my steps. I'd like to send it back and exchange it for the Fitbit One, which I have since heard is more accurate. However, I didn't realize that Amazon only takes returns on unopened items, and otherwise charges a restocking fee. And, I'm not sure this is defective. I think it's just not accurate. Should have bought this from a Brick & Mortar store.

Edited 4/1/2014...Ok, I've been using my Fitbit for a few more days. Today I was out for several hours and my step count was still really low as, described previously, I don't walk with my hands down at my side. I'm usually busy doing other things. I had contacted Fitbit regarding the problem, but the only thing they could say was that it compared to other wrist-trackers on the market....which isn't saying a lot. I'd really like to return or exchange this thing, but can't. When I got home this afternoon, and saw that my step count was again very low, I decided to try taking the Flex unit out of the wrist band and I put it in my pocket. So far, that seems to give me a better step count. Not sure how it will work that way with the other functions. But, frankly, after using the Flex for over a week, I'm not confident in the accuracy of the other functions and will probably never use them. There is an Omron brand clip-on that gets rave reviews. Check that one out before you decide to buy the Flex.

Edited 4/3/2014...I pursued my issues with Fitbit customer service, and this is what they said: " Flex will count your steps when you're walking with your arms stationary, as we do want to give you credit for this activity. This includes walking while pushing a stroller or shopping cart, or holding on to a treadmill. However, because your hands are not moving, your step count may be a bit lower during this activity."

So, they have finally admitted the count is not accurate unless your arms are down at your side. I do dispute the fact that it is a "bit lower." My steps are hardly being counted at all, unless my arm is down at my side. So, for this reason, I have now lowered my rating to two stars. I did contact Amazon customer service and explained what was going on. They are allowing me to return it, without restocking charges, because it is not working as intended. THANKS AMAZON!!!

title: Does not hold air for more than a few hours. Manufacturer will not honor warranty. Buyer beware!
text:
This mattress looked great out of the box. Now less than ten days later it's on its way to the garbage bin.

It looked good at first. The material seemed high-quality and the built-in pump worked great to inflate it, relatively quickly. I went online while the mattress was inflating and read all of the manufacturer's suggestions, including the one to inflate it and let it sit overnight before use to "stretch out", then add more air. I followed all the instructions carefully.

Just a few hours after fully inflating the mattress and without anyone using it or even sitting on it, I pressed on it with my hand and noticed it was already mushy and not nearly as firm as when first inflated, so I topped the air off again and let it sit overnight without using it. The next morning it was mushy again, but I figured maybe this was the "stretching" the manufacturer was talking about. That night I inflated the mattress to full firmness, made up the bed, and went to sleep. About three hours later I woke up with the hard floor under me and a tangle of deflated air mattress wrapped around me.

So clearly, the mattress was defective and had arrived with a leak. Well, that happens. It was really unfortunate because I had no other bed at the time to use, but I had gotten a cheerful email from the manufacturer here on Amazon right after I ordered, telling me if I had any problems to contact them and they would be sure to honor that warranty twhich hey make such a big deal of offering, and make things right.

I emailed them to let them know that right out of the box the mattress was leaking air badly. They replied with the same instructions I found online, saying it was probably "stretching out" and I just needed to top the air off. I replied that I had now spent two nights on the mattress, and the only way to use it was to set an alarm to wake up every two-and-a-half hours to reinflate it before it went completely flat. I asked them to please do as they said and work with me to make it right.

That more than a week and three emails ago. I have emailed them over and over (the only way to reach them.) The manufacturer simply stopped responding after the first email. They did not provide any customer support, no advice, nothing. They did nothing at all to honor the warranty they offer. I tried finding a patch kit on my own for this thing, but I can't even find the leak, it seems to be in the sealing of one of the seams. It's basically garbage at this point, because it's useless. The photo is of it sitting waiting to go out with the trash less than two weeks after being bought.

If you look at the one and two star reviews, many people have had the same issue. With this mattress, it seems like either you are one of the lucky ones and it works perfectly out of the box, or it just doesn't hold air at all and you are screwed, because the manufacturer is not going to keep their word and honor that reassuring-sounding warranty that they offer to entice people into buying their expensive air mattress.

So, if you need a bed and want to roll the dice, try your luck. I did, and I certainly regret believing the untrustworthy, dishonorable shysters who manufacture the King Koil.

$150 dollars, straight out into the trash.

text: I had to stop biking when it got to be December/January last year (I live in Chicago), so this year I was determined to find a way to stay warm through winter. I put these on my bike (took 30 seconds), put two pairs of gloves on, and rode off in 25°F (-5°C) weather, waiting for my hands to get cold.
