The larger wheels make it possible to scooter on dirt roads and over small debris. We have many steep hills by our home and having our son ride a scooter with larger wheels brings peace of mind that he won't wipe out on a small branch, rock or piece of glass.

I've ridden this scooter as well (6' - 215 lbs) and its capable of supporting my weight. We have another scooter with a hand brake on it and this scooter would be PERFECT if it also came with a hand brake (hand brakes should be standard on all large-wheeled street cruisers like this).

Also note that the kickstand actually works and the scooter won't just fall over like the kickstands on MANY other scooters.

title: Beautiful commuter helmet
text:
Received this helmet for my wife who is commuting by folding bike and eKickScooter. Its her 4th helmet this year. She's really been trying to get a good fit, as well as have something stylish. The Batfox Commuter does a great job at providing both.

A very, very stylish helmet. Clean. Classic look. Highly visible during the day and night. For eKickScootering you need a helmet light since any lights on the scooter are too low to really be seen by motorists who may be behind you.

Good straps and fitment. Decent venting for summer wear.

The brim is a true sun shade unlike many helmets which just have a hard plastic lip. The brim is very important when cycling, but super necessary when scootering to reduce glare since its hard to take a hand off the steering to cover your eyes.

Recommended!

title: Decent grips
text:

Our replacement is usually the Ergon series. GP1 as of late.

Our son took a spill on his bike and somehow destroyed his grips. Really ground them down. We saw these on Amazon and figured we'd give them a try as they are very similar to the Ergon GP2.

They have been a pleasant surprise. While not quite as comfortable as Ergon grips (harder material), they generally provide a similar range of hand placement and are easy to install.

They have held up well over the past month of sweaty (and sometimes rainy) riding.

Would I purchase them for my bike? No. I'm very sensitive to the material of my grips and softness and texture are critical over the long rides I take. However, these are great for a city/commuter bike.

Recommended.

title: Excellent

title: Excellent - good mix of inexpensive components - closer to a low end Dahon than a Walmart special
text:
I have several folding bikes for use by the family. We swear by them.

Our first folding bike was a Euromini Campo. I bought one, then we purchased one for my wife. Those bikes were a nice low-end introduction to folding bikes with a $200 price point. About a year later I purchased a Dahon Vigor. An excellent bike at a $750 price point. An order of magnitude superior to the Euromini bikes in terms of many components and build and ride quality (one Euromini frame has a crack near the seatpost and we had to replace both bottom brackets after only a year).

This CyclingDeal bike, although a brand unknown to me, provides a level of quality on par with my Dahon Vigor. In terms of features, the CyclingDeal comes with superior brakes (disc), equivalent quality tires/rims and several features the Vigor lacks (fenders, quality rear rack). Other components such as headset, bars and grips are of significantly lower quality. The CyclingDeal shifting, while inferior to the SRAM system of the Dahon, is equivalent to the Euromini Campo, consisting of a 7 Speed Shimano with Revoshifter. The Aluminum frame is MUCH lighter and somewhat stiffer than the Campo and ride quality is closer to that of the Dahon. This is also the lightest adult folding bike I've ever used. About 2 lbs heavier than my son's folding Vilano cuiser (we added a longer seat post, brakes and a sprung saddle). If you have a Campo, you'll notice how much lighter the CyclingDeal is...

If this bike said Dahon on the side, no one would bat an eye. From a distance. A closer inspection of the frame shows a slightly lower weld quality/frame construction as well as low-end consumer detailing ("super easy folding system...")

If you're looking for a first folding bike on Amazon. This should definitely be in the running. You will only need to replace the bar grips with some Ergon GP1s. And maybe the saddle if you weigh more than 200 lbs.

To like: quick release wheels, disc brakes, lightweight frame, fenders, rear rack
To hate: low-end detailing, cheap grips, no magnetic closures on folding system

Recommended!

I'll update this review after 100 miles...

title: Nice helment
text:
This is a good commuter-style helmet. Suitable for biking and electric kick-scooter usage. You know, the stylish type with a brim that everyone else seems to pay top dollar for...

I'm a 6' tall, 215lb male with a large head. This fits me well with a tiny bit of space left over.

The helmet is large without appearing overly bulbous. It has a decent number of vents and a good strap that should fit a wide variety of heads. The styling is excellent and the brim is very securely affixed using a lot of Velcro fasteners. There is a good amount of padding on the inside of the helmet. The hole for locking this to my scooter is very necessary and appreciated.

Overall this is an attractive helmet and allows me to bike and scooter in protected style. The appearance is very much in-line with helmets costing twice as much. So if you need something cheap and cool-looking to get your kid (or husband) to wear a helmet - this is a great choice.

title: Fantastic
text:
I received the Mier 60L backpack and immediately put it to use on my electric kick scooter. First I transported a huge load of dirty linen for my wife from her massage therapy business to the laundry via scooter (3/4 capacity). Then I swung by Trader Joe's supermarket and loaded up at least 30 lbs of food and scootered home (2/5 capacity).

The Mier backpack performed extremely well. The 60L volume is HUGE. Huuuge. I am 6' tall, 215 lbs, fit. This is ALL you need for standard transport. The 150L (at more than double the volume of the 60L) should be able to hold a body... A use for the 150L would likely be transporting bulky, light loads (e.g., 25 food trays that need to be kept vertical).

These are truly MEGA packs.

If you're working for a food delivery service, and need to use a backpack, this is your product. Super dense, sturdy material. Good strong shoulder straps with reinforced connection points. Padding on the straps is decent for usage in 30 minute stints under max load or all day under light loads. And while not officially listed as insulated, the thickness and type of material makes me think this would be good for food delivery as it should keep in the heat, keep out the cold, and be very easy to keep clean.

The only downside was my back sopping with sweat due to the pack exterior not being made of breathable material.

Highly recommended.

Recommended!

title: Mediocre for heavier riders
text:
If you weigh over 190lbs, please read below. If you're using these pedals on a child's bike, or if you are a very casual rider under 190lbs, ignore...

---

I weigh 215 lbs and regularly commute (and go for hard weekend rides) on a folding bike with these pedals installed. Something I've noticed about these pedals over the past 6 months of usage is that while substantially sturdier than all plastic/nylon folding pedals, they are prone to becoming loose/saggy. The design of these pedals requires that you regularly tighten the two Philips screws as they work themselves loose making the pedal feel wobbly with usage. The wobble becomes so great that you actually can feel the pedals slanting under your feet.

I've gone on to replace these with KOOTU Folding Mountain Bike Pedals. They cost almost twice as much, but they look alot better and feel alot better to my 215lbs when pedaling under pressure. In addition the KOOTU pedals don't suffer from the same design issue.

I'd give it 5 stars if it only showed women and slender men in the advertising and chalk it up to me overusing it or being too heavy. But the super-ripped guy on the product page lead me to believe it was a bit heavier duty than it actually is.

title: Excellent Scooter - Rear Fender (on non-pro version)  Breaks Under Normal Road Vibration
text:
I just purchased the KS5 Pro. Here are my comparisons with the KS5.

Larger deck. Both feet fit more comfortably. Heavier. Harder to move around but feels sturdier when riding. Problems with rear fender appear to be solved (see old review). Extra bracing metal stops fender from flopping around like on my KS5. Handlebars are 2-3” higher than the KS5. This is a scooter that should be able to handle 6’6” riders easy…

Max speed drops approx 20% when at two bars and 30% when at one bar. Ex: my max speed when riding in sport mode at one bar is 13-15mph on flats. Max downhill speed is 22mph

My KS5 delivers almost full speed up until one flashing bar...

Max range is about 19 miles.

I weigh 220lbs.

Overall this is a great and sturdy scooter that reduces range anxiety and should be able to get you anywhere within a city.

Note: initially my regen brakes would cut on fully (and seemingly randomly) when I put very light pressure on the brakes. This would happen once for every ~50 times I hit the brakes. This lead to unexpected moments where I would almost get thrown off the scooter. Completely unexpected and super dangerous. I'm very experienced at scootering, skateboarding, biking, and this almost wiped me out each time. This happened for the first week, then suddenly stopped. I had just set the scooter up for return shipping and my last ride (to be completely sure) did not have the problem.

——————-old KS5 review—————-
Update: I’m on my fourth rear fender. They break under normal road vibration. Fracture, crack, break at the base where the fender rises from the deck of the scooter. Four different fenders. No collisions or crashes. This one part needs a redesign.

———————

When the scooter first arrived I was VERY impressed by the build and weight. This thing is a beauty. Ship packaging was adequate with lots of cardboard keeping everything separate and stationary.

Assembly was very simple. Just a few screws to attach and an app to download from the IOS appstore.

Second impression was pretty poor however. Could not get the handlebar post straight - even with max strength. And could not get the headlights to turn on without first using the phone app.

Turns out both were my mistake (and somewhat the fault of the mediocre documentation/startup docs).

You can't access any scooter functions while its charging. So when you first open the box and logically go to charge it, double-tapping to turn on the headlights won't work. You may also need to adjust the screw at the base of the handlebar post. It used a different Allan key size than the included key, but tightening it up a bit will make it easier to open/close.

The app is sufficient. It definitely could use some user interface redesign - its lost opportunity to turn this into an exceptional product - but it suffices for what it is. I set the unit to hi regen on braking and "baby mode" for my first test runs.

Tires are hard. There is some give - but these feel pretty much like solid tires to me. If there is a honeycomb design inside, it will likely show itself on the most heinous road bumps and not by simply pushing a finger or pen into the tire material.

Shocks were pretty sticky when I tested them in my house. Not smooth at all. They loosened up considerably after a 5K test run. And about that test run...

I rode to a smooth track near my house and did about 10 laps. On the perfect surface I was able to focus on the acceleration and handling of the scooter. Very, very good. In S mode has a great pickup, and I achieved MAX speed in a few seconds. Braking was very good. I immediately came to a stop with double as well as single brakes. Regen seemed to bring me to a stop - but was not very aggressive feeling - even on max. That might be due to my weight.

I am a fit 215lbs and am 6' tall. Size 11 feet. The scooter feels like it was built for me. Deck is plenty spacious and handlebar grips are at the perfect height for me. I've been on scooters that felt fragile - this is NOT one of them. I pulled on the bars as I cornered and pushed on them as I braked. No wiggle. No squeek.

After the smooth track, I went to a nearby jacked-up parking lot, filled with cracks, weeds and bumps. The scooter handled 1" lips and 2-3" gaps in pavement well. The shocks did their jobs, but the wheels gave me little joy. I felt significant road vibration. Maybe the wheels need a break in period as well...

As for the weight and storage ... I commute using a folding bike (Dahon Vigor D9) and this scooter weighs significantly more (50%) and is much harder to handle when walking it or when folded. I've gotten into a habit of taking my Dahon with me everywhere possible and I fold it down quickly and roll it around or pick it up when I need to.

This is a bulky scooter and you won't want to pick it up and carry it often. I was able to use it as an unpowered kick scooter pretty easily. So running out of power when on the road should not be a problem. But multimodal commuting might be annoying if you have a lot of stairs to climb or will be on a tight train.

The charge outlet is well-protected with a spring loaded cap. There is also some rubber backing in the cap to help create a better water seal. Should be good for splashes. But I'd stay away from a puddle deep enough to immerse the bottom of the board.

The front and rear lights are very bright. No additional lights are needed.

Changes?

Improve the quality of the app. Make it so good/informative that people will want it open on the handlebar of the scooter while they're riding. Do more quality control of the text as well.

Maybe provide wheels with a tiny bit more cushion. Wheel tech is steadily improving and a softer core wheel (keep it solid) will definitely make folks happier. I can't imagine anyone wanting harder wheels.

Improve your documentation and startup tips card. Larger font. Clearer layout. Put things in order of importance for the best startup experience. A large, colorful startup tips card that says things like (lights won't turn on when charging, adjust handlebar base, etc). And change the screw on the handlebar base to the same size Allan key as the rest of the screws on the scooter. I have tools, some may not.

Excellent scooter and highly recommended!

----------------

Update:

Today I went for a 10 mile ride. I used ECO for 75% and SPORT mode for 25%. MAX speed almost all the way. There were three significant uphills (1/4 mile each) and several large downhills. I used regenerative braking as much as possible. When I got home I had 1 bar left, flashing.

I weight 215 lbs, which is approaching the upper limit of the scooter's spec. So on a full charge I can reliably get about 10 miles out of the scooter judiciously using SPORT mode. For me, this scooter is good since my office is 3 miles away from my house. I can just blast on SPORT both ways.

Since I've owned the scooter the APP has gone through an update adding a few new features. Its still pretty poor quality and does not seem to save my changes to settings like regenerative braking, etc.

------UPDATE-------

I've lowered the star rating by one due to the following issues.

1. Noise. The rear fender makes a LOT of noise when riding. Constant clunking sounds as it flops around. Its very irritating. They also break under the vibration load. I’M ON MY FOURTH REAR FENDER UNDER WARRANTY!!! AND IT JUST BROKE AS WELL. THEY ALL CRACK AND THEN BREAK AT THE SAME SPOT!!!

2. Range anxiety. From a full charge, the scooter drops down to one flashing bar at 8.5 miles on me, regularly. Far short of 25 miles and I'm wistful... It would make sense that the flashing bar is really 25% power remaining instead of 10% or less - but I don't want to test it. I usually need 10 miles of range when I ride the scooter (its a round trip) and I can just eek it out if I only use sport mode for the first 10-20% of my ride (when I need more speed to better negotiate car traffic). By the time I'm heading home using standard mode exclusively I'm stressing range. So I guess I can lose 15 lbs to get better range... Carrying the charger and recharging on the road is not an option in this use case.

3. Accelerator glitches. The scooter has gunned uncontrollably on two occasions. Both times I was sitting at a light, then I pressed the accelerator and the scooter took off at max speed and would not stop, even when I hit the brakes! I had to turn off the power... The first time I thought it was something I did. Second time I realized it was the scooter. VERY dangerous situations for me both times. I can only guess that it may have something to do with cruise control as it did not happen before I turned that on (may be coincidental). I'll turn off cruise control for the time being when riding in traffic/pedestrian settings and will try to replicate the issue in a parking lot and see if its some type of user error...

4. Aftermarket service has been excellent thus far. Yadea have sent me replacement parts for the rear fender. As well as PDF and video instructions on maintenance. Very responsive to requests. Scooter front shocks are still quite sticky. Can’t seem to lube or adjust them to be smoother. Side reflectors are a pain to get off in order to service rear wheel or replace rear fender. However, once you have performed maintenance on the scooter, repeat sessions are easy.

title: One of the best folding pedals on Amazon
text:
I have several folding commuter bikes for the family. A variety of low and high end brands. After a year or so I’ve needed to replace the included folding pedals that were made from mosty nylon with sturdier pedals (some with metal cores).

Of all the folding pedals I’ve acquired on Amazon, these have the sturdiest construction. No “give” while pedaling. Substantial metal components provide the needed stiffness. They also look great on the bike. Sleek and attractive, for a folding pedal...

If there is a downside it’s that the folding mechanism is a bit tight when first installed. Just add a bit of oil. Most folding pedals break in and fold easier after a month or so of use.

These are on par with the standard Dahon folding pedals in terms of ride feel. They just don’t fold as easy when you first install them.

Update: just wanted to circle back and say these are WORTH the extra cost. A joy to have folding pedals on my folding bike with no wobble. Highly recommended.

title: Excellent - Super Visibility
text:
I needed to replace the reflectors on my folding commuter bike. The old ones (two large inter-spoke models) had cracked and fallen off after only a year of riding.

These are a worthy replacement.

Superior brightness and they really do create the illusion of a large reflective surface when the wheel is in motion.

A little bit tedious to put on, but when you factor in how long they'll be on the bike, and the fact that you don't have to worry about them falling off like the larger inter-spoke reflectors, its worth the trouble.

I'll be getting a set for my wife and son's bikes as well.

Recommended.

title: Great light - just on the small side
text:
My wife gets anxious when we ride in the city's street bike paths. Cars coming from behind, moving at high speed, rush past alarmingly. She has fairly poor peripheral vision so these can often come as a shock. She wanted a rear view mirror to give her a view of cars coming from waaaaay behind so she wouldn't be surprised as much.

This is a well made product. Seem fairly sturdy and easy to mount.

Sadly, we weren't able to find a good position to place this mirror. Too much moving of the body to get a good view from behind.

If she did not use Ergon GP1 grips, she might be able to mount them on the bar ends. Maybe. But we'll probably wind up going with a mirror that mounts into the end caps instead.

title: Excellent bike lights for Wife's commuter bike and helmet
text:
My wife needed a good headlight for her bike when commuting home in the evenings.

Headlight - this is one of the brightest lights we've tried out of three different models (some with higher lumen ratings). Very sturdy build quality, large button that works with gloves on, and a nice clamp-style handlebar mount. The yellow illumination on the side is a nice touch.

Rear light - this red rear light, while not not very bright (adequate for city commuting) provides great flexibility. You can use it on your rear rack, seat post or even attach it to the back of your helmet using the provided straps/clip.

Highly recommended.

title: Beautiful helmet.  Visor design flaw
text:
This is a really nice looking helmet. Great graphic pattern. Good straps and padding. Beautiful touches like the golden screws that affix the visor.

Sadly, the screws that affix the visor do not fit into the screw hole on the right side. The hole seems to be poorly threaded. It’s a metal screw hole embedded into the foam. To use the helmet I’ll have to epoxy the screw into the hole (and perhaps epoxy the visor on as well).

This is an incredible oversight - every helmet should be checked before shipping...

Perhaps it’s just my helmet. But it could be a symptom of quality-control issues.

title: Decent helmet
text:
There are a LOT of helmets on Amazon that look like this. I won't name names, but I've owned three myself...

These are comfortable - and this one has VERY nice foam inserts and chin strap.

Its weakness is the low quality of the sun shade. Ill-fitting with sharp corners on it. And the attachment area is falling apart already (worn about 10 times).

If they can improve the sun shade fitment would be an excellent helmet.

----

Updated review: Sunshade no longer stays on brim. Connector is falling apart. Used about 15 times. Reducing rating.

title: Huge.  Huuuge.
text:
Received this for a folding bike used for city commuting and immediately realized its way too large. If I were commuting along a highway, or were using a non-folding eBike on city streets this would be ideal.

I'll likely add this when we go bike touring this Summer.

That said - this provides GREAT visibility. Others I've tried are too small to see details, this is quite the opposite. You can literally make eye contact with riders who are behind you. :-)

Was easy to put on and stayed stable on my bars the entire day I used it.

Recommended.

title: Great lights
text:
Received these to replace a set of aging lights on my folding commuter bike that were no longer responding to on/off presses. Superior brightness. Superior design (backs do not scratch my stem and seat post, seems more waterproof).

Highly recommended.

title: Great for Spring camping
text:
Great for snap cold during Spring camping or hiking. Just pop into your pack and you're all set.

Comes well-packaged in a semi-hard case with a clip (the 4 individual packs are inside). While I would not clip this to my pack - Its a nice option.

title: Necessary
text:
I have a folding commuter bike with folding pedals. It sees a lot of action in the rain and slush - so there is always the danger of the pedals locking onto the frame.

That time has come.

Even though I greased the pedals before putting them on - they still somehow locked in. And the tiny little monkey wrench I keep at home was not up to the task.

This spanner saved the day. Flipped the bike upside down and 1-2-3, powered those pedals off.

You may not need it much if you're just a regular Joe. But when you need it - there is no substitute.

This has a good design, a nice grip, and looks sexy next to your bike. :-)

title: Great chain
text:
Needed this to replace a two year old chain on my Dahon Vigor folding commuter bike. Its seen a LOT of COVID miles recently...

This worked like a charm.

I didn't put it on myself - but the tech who did had no problems and completed the work quickly.

title: Great Bell
text:
Some bells are obnoxious sounding and anger people when you are coming up behind them on your bike. This bell is the opposite. It has a bright, somewhat cheery ring, reminiscent of classic bike bells.

While not an urgent call to action like a horn or electronic bell - a few relaxed taps from a suitable distance is enough to get the attention of anyone but those insufferable headphone-wearing road hogs.

Recommended.

title: Excellent!
text:
I have a Dahon Vigor folding bike that I use mainly for city riding and commuting. I don't carry a pump because I'm always a cab ride away from home (or have mass transit available).

Lately I've been going out of town to do country rides. I've taken a medium sized pump with me but prefer to fit everything I need into my jersey pockets or my saddle bag. This small CO2 inflator fits the bill perfectly.

Sturdy build. Small size. Enough cannisters for a year of flats.

Recommended.

title: Excellent brakes
text:
Just installed these on my Dahon Vigor folding bike.

Excellent stopping power.

They make a great replacement brake for the stock item.

Recommended.

title: Get more than one
text: These comfortable joggers are my wife's favorite comfy loose lounge pants. She has them in multiple colors. The high waist is flattering and comfortable. The baggy crotch, with extra deep pockets and tapered legs make it easier to  pull on and go. You cannot go wrong with these.

title: Must haves for your yoga/exercise collection
text: My wife loves wearing these high waisted leggings. They cover your entire tummy which creates a flattering contour. Bending over is not a hazard, there is no "butt show." The size pockets are cute and deep enough to hold a cell phone but not much else. It stretchers, but you may need to wiggle a bit to get them over broad hips. Comfortable enough for every day wear not just to gym or yoga.

title: Great for cycling
text:
I use this gaiter for commuter cycling on my folding bike. Works great to keep out the elements and acts as a simple COVID breathing barrier while outside. Ear loops ensure it stays up.

I tend to use the well-ventilated side while riding and then rotate the mask to the more closed side when transitioning to my desk (and my proper surgical mask).

Stylish, functional and warm.

title: Everything included ... poor packaging
text:
This is a complete set of tools to clean your bike: frame, chain, cogs, everything...

If you own a commuter bike and ride in a variety of weather, eventually the gunk will catch up with you. Stuff you can't just "oil and wipe" away. This kit provides you with the tools to really scrub through the gunk and get that frame and chain shining like new.

The only downside is the lack of packaging materials besides a cardboard shipping box. That could just be an artifact of having received this through Amazon Vine however.

Recommended.

title: Extremely bright, great fastening system
text:
We needed a light for evening commuting on our folding bikes. This fit the bill.

The front light does a VERY good job of keeping the city streets in view. It is 3x as bright as the typical tiny lights people add to their city commuting bikes and it can be seen from blocks away. You can be sure cars headed towards you will be aware of your presence.

The rear light has a large number of flash patterns and brightness settings. Its also a decent size, so you can be sure you're visible from the rear.

The fastening system for the front light is very secure, but you'll likely need to cut some excess plastic after you've set it up or you'll have a single long strand pointing at you from your handlebars... The rear light uses the typical rubber connectors which work fine on seat posts or on the backs of some types of cycling helmets. The kit includes extra fastening material for the front and rear lights - which is a GREAT addition.

Battery life seems appropriate. We've used it for three evenings of 30 minute commuting and have not had to recharge yet.

Recommended.

title: Bright - easy to set up
text:
Overall a decent rear light. Good visibility while commuting at night. Easy to remove and charge.

Recommended.

title: Works!

Received these tires right on time! Had to replace two flats received while commuting. Glass "dagger" penetration. Tires already had several patches in them so I decided to replace the tube.

These work just as expected.

If I still have a few tubes left in the Spring, I'll take them with me when I go touring New England by bike.

Recommended.

title: Replacement tubes for my commuter bike
text:

If I was touring I'd keep it in my under seat bag - but since I don't ride more than 10 miles in the city and am never more than a $25 cab ride from home, I primarily use these to replace unfixable flats when I'm at home.

Recommended.

title: Great multipurpose light
text:
I used to just have a small white light in the front and a small red light in the back of my folding commuter bike. Just for visibility to cars/pedestrians. Not for seeing the road ahead (I relied on street lights). Then I went out to the countryside with my bike and got caught out at night. Yes. True darkness...

This light is great for when you need to transition between a visibility light that lasts for a loooong time and a true light to see the road in pitch black conditions.

I don't use the horn, preferring to use a friendly sounding bell instead.

Recommended.

title: Great light that's easy to remove/replace
text:
While not the brightest headlight that I have, the fact that this is sooo easy to remove/replace means that I can carry it with me once I've left my bike. In some situations, particularly camping, this is a tremendous benefit.

The light is bright enough to comfortably illuminate the road in front of me to a distance that allows me to react to potholes and other obstacles. Being rechargeable means I don't have to fumble with batteries. +100 in my book.

One downside is the rubber connector on the red light tore on me during my first use. I secured it to the back of my helmet and at the end of the day noticed it was ripped 3/4 of the way through the rubber... So now I don't have a rear light unless I can rig up some replacement attachment method.

Great light set otherwise.

title: You need these, whether you realize it or not...
text:
That new set of boots you own ... have you tested them on ice? I bought a pair and like most, did not test them on ice. I mean, unless you live in Canada/Alaska you usually have them for months before you get to wear them out in inclement conditions (purchase Winter boots in the Summer for the best prices!)

Well, everything was fine - boots were great - until I hit my first patch of ice. Something about the sole material caused me to slip and slide like a drunkard... I was about to relegate the boots to the closet when I saw these crampons were available. Amazing!

The crampons I know about are from nature shows I've seen on TV. Huge spikes. Only put on when you reach the icy end of the Earth... Whereas these crampons are GREAT for walking around the city in snowy weather. Or the day after a snow when daylight heating and nighttime freezing have created a tremendous number of icy patches.

They have given my step confidence. Literally.

Recommended!

title: My wife loves this
text:
A great cap and scarf set.

My wife has been using this for over a month and loves the way it keeps her warm. In particular she's moved over from a traditional scarf to this 'neck warmer/tube' style scarf which provides a greater amount of trapped air and warmth.

The hat is also stylish and very warm. We'd love to see this in wool/cashmere, but synthetic is OK.

Recommended.

title: Top Notch Quality
text:
This is a heavy (2-3x typical weight) but incredibly high quality mat. If you have a permanent setup for yoga, this is the mat you want to pull out at your location for your clients...

A few things:

- The cork top does not create a sop of sweat like cheap foam mats. It remains dry and non-sticky far longer than synthetic mats I’ve used.

- The top is somewhat more grippy (in a dry non-sticky way) so you won't slip as much as some other mats.

- The bottom surface is super grippy so this mat is NOT going anywhere. No sliding.

- No additional straps. This makes sense since this is really not the type of mat you want to toss over your shoulder or put onto your bike and ride to a class.

- reflects body heat - and yet also absorbs it. Stays warm AND cool during use. Natural materials win again!

Highly recommended!

title: Incredible for the price
text:
This is such an incredible cycle computer for this price. I primarily use it to track the basics: speed, cadence, distance. And sometimes I use the map feature. Functionally it has everything I need.

The button interface can be a bit confusing and frustrating to novices. Almost counterintuitive. However, after a few rides it becomes a non-issue. Its a clunky UI and I bet that this may be the swan song of non-touch UI on devices with this level of functionality.

I found the route/map features laggy and frustrating to use on device and app, so I navigate with my phone since it is much, much easier. I CAN use the maps, its just that the UI and responsiveness add 'friction' to the map interaction making it less pleasant than it should be. If you want to leave your phone at home you definitely can, you just have to work at it.

Screen size and configurability of info display is perfect. Phone app is surprisingly good as well. Not the best UI, but much better than I expected and once you fiddle with it for 30 minutes you will grok it.

Holds a decent charge for daily commuting and weekend riding usage. I recharge once a week to be safe, but could probably go longer.

I'm using it on my Dahon Vigor D9 folding bike with a Tern Andros stem. The 420 fits nicely in the center of the Andros (see pic).

If you're thinking about getting this - do it. You won't be disappointed.

title: Does all it says - attachment clip is problematic
text:
I received this light for my Dahon folding commuter bike. Previously I was using a small rechargeable light that was more for visibility to oncoming cars than to actually see the ground.

This extra illumination of this light has made a significant difference for me when commuting at night. I used to avoid areas with low illumination. The XOSS illuminates the ground in front like a car headlight allowing me to ride in total darkness. I tilt the light so can see everything coming at me from about 20-30 feet away, which is enough time to react at my normal riding speed.

I have also used both the automatic on/off motion sensor and standard on/off modes and they each worked well.

The handlebar attachment/removal system allows me to use the XOSS as a flashlight (have done this several times) and more easily charge it. However, the attachment clip has an issue - if you tighten it onto the handlebars too much, the screw will enter a hole on the bottom of the light and restrict it from being put on or removed. Be aware...

Recommended!

(update) The bracket snapped under fairly normal usage. Maybe it was the cold weather making the plastic a bit brittle... Rather than toss the light or turn it into a flashlight, I 3D printed a replacement part. You can find it on thingiverse. Just search for "XOSS Enfitnix Bike Headlight Bracket"

title: Surprisingly good helmet from a "no-name" brand...
text:
I have a GIRO Reverb bike helmet with a fabric brim. The fitment is great, but the brim is flimsily attached to the helmet with Velcro/adhesive and it is ALWAYS falling off. I had to rig up a new system of self-adhesive and Velcro to keep it on.

This helmet, although technically a 'no name' brand, has what appears to be higher construction quality on the brim, padding and head straps.

While I hope I never find out whether it is more protective in a crash - if this helmet carried the GIRO name you might find yourself assuming it was a higher-end helmet.

Recommended!

title: GREAT LIGHT - clearly shows your braking
text:
I keep two rear lights on my folding commuter bike to ensure that at least one is charged and working. One on my seat post and another clip-on attached to my underseat bag.

I added this light to replace the light attached to the underseat bag, and now have two on my seat post.

EVERY light should function like this one. It clearly shows the braking/energy state of my bike and makes me feel much safer while riding at night in the city. It also has a fantastic attachment system that makes charging easy since you don't have to unfasten then seat post clip. Just unscrew the main light body and charge, then screw back on. A superior design all around!

I'll be replacing the tail lights on my wife and son's bikes with these models.

Recommended.

title: Great massage roller!
text:
We have several different massage rollers at our house. One is made from cheap plastic. Hard as a rock and very uncomfortable to use. Needless to say, that one doesn't see much action.

The other is large, with a dense nylon core and a rubber/foam exterior. We use that one, however it is VERY large, and probably more appropriate for use in a professional gym setting. Another issue is the foam is too soft and is now no longer evenly distributed across the roller's surface.

The AQUANIMOUS cork roller is just the right size for using around the house in front of the TV. My wife is a massage therapist and has also used this roller in her practice.

We like the idea of natural materials and have made a resolution for 2021 to try to only purchase items that are made from primarily natural sources. This is a good start.

Highly recommended.

title: Did not work for us
text:
COVID + FACE MASKS = recipe for foggy glasses.

Everyone in my family wears glasses and we desperately need a solution to stop all the fogging-up that's going on.

We tried this "nano tech" defogger on several pairs of our glasses. In several sets of conditions from dry cold, to humid cold, to indoors.

Cool name. Nice bottle. But no effect.

Maybe we got a bad batch...?

title: Decent amount of storage - stylish
text:
We're using this on my wife's folding bike as a light storage bag. Good for transporting groceries or picnic items. We were caught in a light rain and the waterproofing did protect the clothes that were inside. Nothing got wet.

The bag is also easy to clean. Several times we've ridden through puddles with no rear fenders and it acted as a fender on its own.

The primary bike light is incredible! Super bright. Illuminates better than anything I've ever seen. You definitely want this if you are riding on back roads or areas outside the coverage of town/city streetlights.

title: Wife LOVES this
text:
Received this for my wife and she just LOVES it. She is 6' tall, 190lbs with a 38DD bust. This is very flattering on her (great hang off the bust, doesn't look bunchy when worn). She also loves the fit of the sleeves, color, material, everything.

This was a real winner.

Recommended.

title: Great for kids classes with open windows due to COVID
text:
We received this and immediately put it to work with my 10 year old son. He uses it in his classroom to keep his hands warm. The windows need to stay open due to COVID and the old building's heating system can't keep up.. He said the room was getting so cold his fingers were too numb to write.

Since using this, he's had a much better time. It easily lasts all day at school and sometimes two days in a row.

Highly recommended.

title: Excellent bike bag
text:
I am using this pannier bag for my wife’s folding bike. Has some great features:

- Large storage capacity
- Secure fasteners
- Attractive styling
- Appears to be truly water resistant
- Fits a folding bike

My wife is able to ride without constant heal strikes and the bag is able to be easily removed and replaced for convenient supermarket shopping.

Highly recommended!

(Note: you don’t need to have that strap going across the rack like I do in the pics - that is used to secure the top of the bag. The pannier is very sturdy on its own. )

title: Awesome for folding bikes!
text:
I have 4 folding bikes for my family that I need to service. I'd purchased another bike stand that really was only good for standard bike frames as it used a hook-style holding mechanism instead of a clamp.

This stand can hold a folding bike via the frame or seat post (pictured). The clamp exerts a LOT of force.

Extremely sturdy and easily folds up small to go into the closet or under a bed.

Assembly was also very fast.

Highly recommended.

title: COVID can't hold me back
text:
THIS was what was missing from our COVID gym at home. Fits in the kitchen doorway and allows the family to get in our pathetic number of reps each morning.

Being able to quickly place it and remove it is a critical feature.

Recommended!

title: Using this to secure a Dahon Vigor folding bike
text:
This is a great lock for securing my Dahon Vigor folding bike (also works with a Zizzo Campo). I can run the cable through the frame, tires and through the seat when folded with the seat fully dropped. This protects the bulk of my bike components.

I usually take my folding bike with my wherever I go. But once in a while I know in advance I won't be able to keep it with me (i.e., college classes, inside Doctor's office, gym). For those occasions, this lock fits the bill.

I'd trust this as a short-term deterrent for high-traffic areas where a thief would not know if the owner was observing them. However, while this is a great lock, I would not trust it outside overnight.

In fact, I wouldn't trust any lock outside overnight...

Recommended.

title: Keeps it cool longer
text:
After using a regular bottle this summer and feeling like I was sipping hot tea, I was glad to receive this insulated bottle.

Drop in several ice cubes, chilled water, and this keeps the affair cool for several hours. Long enough to do several loops in the park, sit on the bench, and get home in time to still have tiny pieces of ice left.

Fits in a standard size bottle cage and the "loop" makes it much easier to grasp while riding.

Recommended.

title: Great product for small spaces
text:
This jump rope is a great way to get cardio in a very small space. Just attach the weighted option to the handles instead of the rope/cable.

I did have some problem with one arm being better at using the 'rope' than the other arm. This was never really apparent when using a regular jump rope. I eventually evened out the accuracy and timing of my jumps - and I'd say my noticing this biomechanical discrepancy is a "feature" of this product, rather than a bug.

Recommended!

title: Good, basic pump
text:
Its great to have a 'sorta' floor pump with a pressure gauge. There are other, similar pumps without the gauge, which really makes them much less useful - unless you know the precise 'feel' of your tires when they are at proper pressure.

This is a basic pump. Construction is somewhat shoddy (doesn't feel like it will last too many seasons). But it gets the job done and is quite small for the amount of air it pushes.

Recommended.

title: Awesome!
text:
Our family has several folding bikes which we use to commute in the city - and reflectors and lights are a must.

The bikes have long seat posts on which we place reflectors and battery powered mini lights. As you can see in my pictures, the YHN tail light is larger than my existing mini light (purchased on Amazon). It’s also brighter, and more importantly, gives cars coming up behind me an indication of my speed. I feel a LOT safer with this light. I’ll keep my old light as a backup - but this new light is superior in every way.

Recommended.

Note- the fastening system is GREAT. Much easier to use and adjust than my old light. And I use this light in manual on/off mode rather than automatic since I fold and roll my bike through stores a lot and don’t want the light always coming on.

title: Very attractive and functional
text:
My family has several folding bikes for day rides and commuting, and a hodge podge of rear and front racks as well as handlebar and saddle bags for storage.

For my stylish Dahon Vigor D8 folding bike (solo weekend rides), I have a Brooks Cambium C17 saddle. It deserved something better that a flappy sack under it.

This saddle bag is a great match for the Cambium and would also be a match for a natural finish carbon fiber bike frame. The locking mechanism secures it tightly to the seat and post so you don’t get any wobble as with a cloth bag.

It’s huge, and not exactly aero. So I don’t recommend it for racing bikes. Just touring and commuting.

For me, the interior is missing a key fob to ensure your keys don’t get lost when you open it up. The mesh zippered compartment inside is too large to ensure this and will most likely have tools in it anyway.

I ride with it containing: multi tool, extra tire, patch kit, tire irons, nylon fabric grocery bag (rolled up), keys, ID, bank card and phone. All that fits inside.

Recommended

title: Good bearings
text:
I'm using these to create a filament spool holder for my 3D printer. 8 bearings with spacers. Enough for two sets of spool holders.

Excellent quality with great, free spin. No "grindiness..."

Recommended.

title: The best grips for a folding bike - period
text:
I’ve purchased three sets of these already. Wasted money on cheap knockoffs when I should have went for the real McCoy.

Other, cheap “ergonomic” brands get sticky - reacting with sunlight and hand oils. They also show hand wear very fast. Ergonomic grips feel better, last longer and are cooler to the touch in the summer.

These grips are great for twist shifters on folding bikes. I have two pairs in use with Euromini Zizzo bikes. Another, regular pair on my Dahon Vigor.

Excellent product.

title: Both sprung leaks in three uses - poor construction
text:
These seem like a great item. But they popped somewhere on one of the seams after a just three short uses. Great idea with lackluster execution.

Caveat - if you weigh under 100 lbs this is likely going to work for you. Avoid if over 150.

title: Easily the best grips I've owned for a folding bike
text: Purchased these to pair with a new Dahon Vigor D9 folding bike.  The bike has a lower handlebar post than other folding bikes I've owned, leading to a more aggressive body position with the seat post extended properly for my 6' of height.  This lead to much more weight transferred to my hands.  The stock Dahon grips are great - but these Ergons provide a significantly improved experience.  I've used no-name Ergon-like knockoffs in the past, and while they provide a similar surface area, the texture, materials and contour of the Ergon is dramatically superior.  Especially if you ride without gloves.

title: Great value
text:
Works perfect in my folding bike. Bought several more for a short family touring trip.

[update] I've had three (out of 4 purchased) break at the point where the valve inserts into the inner tube. Each time during pumping. Three different bikes at various times. Old stock? Recent production flaw?

title: Great value.  Bright.  Poor aesthetics.  Loose on frame.  Poor USB cover.
text:
Pro - very bright. Long lasting. High utility (fits variety of locations). Inexpensive. USB recharge. Side illumination.

Con - very unattractive for a bike light. Ill fitting when used on a post (lopsided and asymmetrical). Loose and bouncy on frame compared to other lights with similar type of attachment. The USB cover is far from watertight and on one light actually hangs open!

If your main (or only) concern is price/performance, these are a great option. If you ride in inclement weather you may want to look elsewhere due to poor USB recharge port protection.

title: Good bottle, but should be called “cool” not “chill”
text: Cool-looking bottle with protective lid for dirty riding...  Keeps water cooler than a standard plastic water bottle and ice cubes last about 90 minutes MAX in 75-80 degree weather.  Less when it’s warmer.  Update: After a year using this I’ve upgraded to a another bottle with better thermal properties.  (Polar Insulated, ice lasts 2x longer)

title: Attractive - but scratches water bottles
text:
This is an attractive and well built holder. However, the material and design of the upper portion abrades plastic water bottles with repeated use. The texture and flat nature of the surfaces also collects particles which accelerate abrasion.

If you are a lover of pristine water bottles this is three stars - look elsewhere. For all others 5 stars.

title: No front shock absorber
text:
While this is a very nice scooter at first glance - it does not come with a shock absorber. I am contacting the seller and will update my review when I have more information.

Update: while the scooter does not have the features I was after I’m keeping it as the seller resolved my issues.

title: Awesome - brighter than expected - good value
text: I purchased a single safety light from another manufacturer here on Amazon - it was impossible to open to change batteries and half as bright.  This seller provides 4 lights for less than the price of two from the other seller.  Also includes tiny screwdrivers to open them.  Highly recommended.

title: Impossible to open in order to change battery (great light otherwise)
text:
...sadly, even with the proper screwdrivers - this was impossible to open in order to change batteries. Super hard screws, somehow embedded so tightly that they can't be unscrewed even with manly torque! After 20 minutes was only able to remove one screw and ruined two separate fine point screwdrivers. For this reason I can't recommend. It’s basically a disposable unit that I’ve already replaced.

Has anyone successfully changed the batteries in this unit?

title: Very comfortable - mediocre quality of Velcro - not low profile (Great Gazoo...)
text:
This is a very comfortable helmet. Decent styling. But simply put, it is huge. Definitely mushroom-like in the large size. You may look like the Great Gazoo... (yabba dabba doo)

Also two pieces of the Velcro that attaches the visor came unglued when I removed the visor to inspect the helmet (5 minutes after it was delivered).

title: Attractive.  Great concept.  But problems...
text:
I really, really like the idea of a helmet that simplifies your commute. Something to block the wind. A back-up warning light to protect you at night. No more forgetting your ride glasses or forgetting to charge your warning light and not having a backup...

PRO:
Great looking in pictures online. Great concept - eliminate a separate set of cycling glasses and also include a night time safety light. Good padding and adjustment strap. Extra safety light included!

CON:
Poor fit - overly round and not oval-like a normal head (my head 22 5/8"). Too tight on forehead and loose on sides. Visor blocks some wind and channels the rest directly into your eyes! But now you can't wipe them because the visor is blocking your access. Visor ships with sharp burrs on it that need to be clipped and sanded. If you bump something the sharp bottom of the visor will likely lacerate your face.

OVERALL:
I'd accept the low utility visor if the helmet fit, or I'd accept the somewhat odd helmet fit if the visor blocked the wind. As it is, I can't recommend this product without some significant modifications.

title: Great purchase at discount prices.  Phone app blocks some biking functionality needlessly.
text:
I came to this device from the Microsoft Band 2.0. So I was expecting a lack of functionality balanced by increased software support, community support and customization (bands).

This is a great minimal hardware design. Really like it. However software gates on cycling functionality (having to use your phone to start a “run” and convert it to a bike ride to see map data) are a bit annoying. If the user has turned on the connected GPS “feature,” why not just auto detect the bike ride AND show the map data when they're done?

The rotate wrist to turn on screen feature is accurate 50% of the time in real world usage. When you’re sitting at a desk or standing it is more like 90% accurate. When you are reclining on a couch, on your side, on your back, on your stomach, in bed, it does not work, at all. Get used to ensuring both arms are free so you can double tap the screen.

I purchased a braided metal band and the styling is great! I mean really nice compared to the Microsoft Band I owned previously. Almost elegant... I also like the professional look of the Alta HR with a black leather band.

After a week of use I would say that I probably should have purchased the Charge 2 HR or Charge 3 instead. They are also quite attractive, look good on a male wrist, and have significant additional functionality. Well I guess I"ll wait until the Charge 4 and hope it adds a GPS and returns to a chrome/brushed metal design similar to the Charge 2 HR (I’m not a fan of the finish options of the Charge 3).

Recommended for bikers as an inexpensive tracker if you tend to always have your phone on you and don’t mind activating ride tracking on your phone as a ”run” and converting it to a “ride” at the end of your session via phone app menus.

title: Broke.  Not even sure how...
text:
I would have given these a 5 star rating. However one broke during normal use (without falling down). Not even sure how the metal snapped. Maybe I brushed up against something while carrying the bike? Amazing how badly it failed and in how many places.

The odd thing is that I’d only ever used it with an empty water bottle on a commuter bike...

title: Awesome for the money
text:
Wow. It really feels good to have grips that aren’t always sliding around. I was looking for black grips that would fit a twist shifter and these were the only non-slip ones I could find. Even though the grey is a bit lighter than shown in the main product picture, these look and feel fine. Aesthetically superior to the all-black version I was seeking. Recommended.

Note that these get VERY sticky. Almost
Like they are covered in glue. Perhaps a better material could have been chosen. If the tactile properties are important to you and you don’t wear gloves, you might want to spend more and get something made from a better material.

title: Great kit for commuter bike cleaning
text: I purchased a folding bike for a 10k round trip daily commute.  After a few weeks I realized I needed to start maintaining the bike or pay a bike shop for a monthly cleaning/tune ups.  I decided to pull together some basic maintenance materials and this is a great starter kit.  Paired with some dry lube, a multi tool and a cheap bike stand - my bike can now be safely maintained for an entire season between visits to the bike shop.

title: Tiny - Does the Job
text: This is one tiny pump.  Does the job, and the gauge is great if you are familiar with your tires.  I know proper pressure of mine by feel, so guesstimating a bit with the gauge is fine.  Someone new to biking and manually pumping may be a bit uncomfortable with using it the first few times.

title: Awesome.  Holds more water than larger competing products.  Dents very easily.
text:
Awesome water bottle. The ONLY problem I have with it is the fact that it DOES NOT come with a small rubber sleeve (1" tall) for the base (or as a purchasable option). It dents SO easily that soon after purchasing you won't be able to sit it flat on a surface without it wobbling. Each dent will cause it to wobble a bit more. If you go to the park and sit it down on cement, you might just dent a it a bit... Etc. Etc. After a few weeks it will be wobbling like a weeble.

Please Rubbermaid, take my money and offer a rubber base sleeve. It would perfect an already awesome design.

title: Good sound - great price
text: Loud, but not obnoxiously so.  Good ring action.  Have used for two weeks now and is still holding up.  Nice size for folding commuter bike with 20" wheels.

title: Atractive, cool
text: Great inexpensive helmet that fits a variety of head types.  Cool while riding on hot summer days. Hope I never get to test out how truly protective it is...

title: Great city commuter lights
text:
While about 20% overpriced for what they offer - these are a high quality item. Sturdy and durable. The red light is bright enough to catch the attention of rearward cars, alerting them to your presence. The white light, while only 1/2 bright enough to properly illuminate the ground directly in front of a cyclist, is PERFECT for catching the attention of motorists and people opening car doors into bike paths at night. Highly recommended for city biking at night on streets that are already moderately illuminated. Variety of flash settings make for great flexibility as riding environment changes.

If you need serious illumination (woods, rural, dark and pothole-filled streets) try something at least 3x brighter and with a beam you can focus to an areas about 10-20 feet in front of the bike.

Update: reduced one star. The white light only lasts 3 hours at most. Brightness drops off and light goes dead in about 3 minutes. There is NO warning. You WILL find yourself on the road with no light.

Update 2: After about 9 months of use and recharging, still going strong. I have about a 20 minute commute in the evening, so I wind up recharging the set every two weeks.

title: Very sturdy for 6' 230lb male.  Moderately heavy.  Good folding mechanism.
text:
Great folding pedals, although ~20% heavier than my old stock pedals. Very sturdy. I'm 6' 230lbs. Riding on a folding bike with 20" wheels. Feel good and stable in and out of saddle in all gears. Been riding a few days, never in the rain. Will update after a month.

Still going strong after almost a year. I'll probably replace them out of mercy at the 18 month point.

I haven’t had any zipper issues they are metal which is nice. I really like all the additional pockets. Great for any number of things. The padding on the back is very comfortable on you back and I don’t feel any coldness coming thru it. Seems quite durable.

text: It was awkward getting 149# up the stairs with help; but did it rather quickly. Setup was easy except I could not pull out the pin that lowers the bars. Phoned Customer Service on Friday, then read reviews about their service. This is the time for holiday business; so, I figured I would wait until Monday to phone again. Tried to pull out the pin again after lowering the back bar, and it pulled out. Got the call from Customer Service Sunday night. Informed I fixed the problem. He was courteous and patient. Nice and short in length, too. This is the season to have patience because we all want things now, and there are others ahead of us. HAPPY HOLIDAYS!

title: HAPPY STEPPER!
text: Received yesterday! Pieces lighter in weight than I thought; but on the whole, quite heavy to move once put together. It took my friend and I about 3 hours total to put together because both of us have knee issues getting up and down off the floor regarding the screws. So much easier than I expected because the diagrams were quite clear, along with the lettering of the washers and other parts. I briefly tried it before going to bed. The pedals are quite tall in height, but if you hold onto the 2 handle bars, it is easy to mount. I LOVE the ease in walking forward and back. I also realized you can walk as fast as you want and slow down, too, without any tension adjustments. I am so glad I did my research everywhere for the right one-time buy of something I never had before, but wanted and needed. I used to own a Schwinn bicycle in my High School days - late 60's; so, I know it is a great product. Still does not disappoint!

The spout to drink out of will not let you just drink some water when pulled open. I have to squeeze the bottle to force the water out. I not just sits in my cabinet. title: Rain or shine a great buy
text:

text:
We haven't used it yet but was bought for use on Boy Scout trips. My son is 12 yrs old, 63in tall and about 85lbs. the pack fits him well. The sleeping bag compartment holds his compression/mummy style/30 degree sleeping bag, and there's a little room left over. The remaining pack space seems enough for a 2-3 night hike. Some of the plastic snaps do feel a little weak/cheap. Was also looking at the TETON 4000, but I think it would have been a little to big for him.

Update- 9/27/2016
My some used it for a 8 mile hiking trip over the weekend. He is tall and a little skinny. With the waist strap adjusted to the tightest setting we were UNABLE to tighten it enough to transfer the weight off his shoulders and onto his waist. The pack became too heavy and the hike was not a fun experience for him. Also - There are two small mesh pockets on the lower outer side portion of the pack and two larger zippered compartments above the mesh pockets. The boy scouts use the larger pockets to hold water bottles. The pack would be better if the larger pockets were on the bottom and the mesh pockets were in the middle, overall for better weight distribution. And - with items in the pack and in the sleeping bag compartment, the zippers are not easily opened and closed. Overall its a good pack but my son will have to grow into it. I will still keep an eye out for a better pack.

Some caution though, it does have a paint smell especially the seat.. maybe it really was freshly manufactured but I don't know if it has health hazards.. parts made in China can sometimes have hazardous/safety concerns but the smell does goes away.

title: Love, love, love!
text: This compact stepper is perfect for small spaces.. like a 1 bedroom apartment, studio, or your office!  In my included photo, I place the machine next to my personal paper shredder so that you can see that it's not that big.  The machine came already assembled.  The only thing that I had to do was pull the safety tab from the battery compartment of the digital display, put the display in its designated spot on the machine, attached the resistance bands, and adjust the step height.  Instructions are super simple to follow and the machine itself is easy to use.  You should find an extra battery for the display in the box as well which was great of them to include.  The machine weighs about 14.2 lbs, so I can easily move it around.  I love that it has a display which will tell you the number of steps, the length of time that the steps are done in, and how many calories have been burned.  The display powers on either when the red button on the display is pushed or when the steps are put in motion, and it will auto shut off after not being used for 4 minutes.  You can easily pick up where you left off by powering on the display, and it retains the info until you reset it.  Resetting the display is easy - just press the red button for a few seconds until the display resets.  The instructions do advise you to place an exercise mat under the machine to protect your floors.  I use this machine every day while I watch TV, and I can see toning in my lower abdomen, thighs, and bottom from it.  I do have to admit that I don't use the resistance bands very often, so I just lay those to the side and do the steps, but I do like that I have the option to use them.  I am NOT an exercise enthusiast - I'm getting older & was advised to be active at least 30 minutes/day, so this was an easy solution for me.  The ONLY improvement that I would make to this machine is having a lighted display.  I have a hard time seeing the display while I'm using the machine because it's somewhat dark.

title: Good design
text:
This ab wheel isn't anything too fancy. It's just another tool to help build your six pack. However, if using an ab roller is your thing, this is the one to go with.

My gym has some different ab wheels that all get the job done. But they don't have one of these, which I think feels better and provides for a better ab workout. It requires some assembly but it's relatively easy. Just make sure when you put the handles on that you align the finger grips so they both face the same way. Otherwise you will have to fight the grips off and redo them. It also takes a little bit of effort to get the grips on!

The wheel has a nice rubber texture that sticks to the floor so it won't come out from under you or slide around. The handles feel good and provide for a nice grip. This product also comes with a short paper providing some information on how to use it, but it should be rather self explained.

However, do not expect to get a six pack from using this ab wheel alone. This is merely just another tool to help you work your abs. In reality, you need to be working your abs with several different exercises. So keep in mind that this will be just one more tool in your toolbox. It is not the "key" to six pack abs.

title: These make your legs burn!
text:
Anyone who swims competitively or simply to stay in shape should get a pair of these! I used them several years ago while on a swim team and forgot how good they are, so I bought another pair recently. A few things about these fins:

TYR's sizing chart worked great for me. I wear 10.5 shoes, so I bought size large for shoe sizes 9-11. This worked perfect for me. They slip on easy, and they seemed to stay on fine. Once they were on I never had to adjust them. I would recommend putting them on once in the water. They are also quite easy to walk in, and I had no problem at all doing flip turns with them.

These fins are definitely geared toward competitive swimmers because they have short blades. This allows you to kick at a faster cadence, unlike long blade fins that require minimal kicking. I would highly recommend buying these instead of long blade fins if you are a lap swimmer. They give you a great workout and really make your legs burn.

I have no issues with mine. The fit is perfect, the material is a strong rubber, the color on my large fins is a nice looking red and black. No issues with them hurting my feet or toes. It is possible to get blisters on the back of your ankles if you do not buy a correct size, and/or wear these for a long swim, so keep that in mind. Some people wear socks which helps if the fins are too big, but I would just follow their size chart and you will be fine.

Highly recommend for the price and what they do for your workout.

title: Light, Mobile, & Quiet
text:
I was hesitant about purchasing this but, I decided to take a risk after seeing comparables online that were more expensive. The treadmill stores easily on the wall and I can move it into place whenever I want to use it. It is easy to control the roll even on a hardwood floor.

For Setup:
1. Place a little lube between the platform and running belt (Oil is included)

For Use:
1. Best to use on a hard surface (Hardwood / Tile)
2. Plug in Treadmill (Fold Handle Up if Needed - Highly suggested for initial use)
3. Stand on the end opposite of the digital readouts
4. Slowly take THREE steps forward (3 dashes stacked up on top of each other will appear on the digital readout)
5. The treadmill will slowly begin to move and continue to increase speed while you walk close to the readout screen
6. To hold a certain speed, walk on the middle section of the treadmill
7. To slow down, walk on the end furthest away from the digital readout
8. Keep in mind the machine will continue to speed up when you walk closest to the digital readout AND it will continue to slow down when you walk furthest from the readout, until it comes to a stop
9. If it comes to a stop and you want to continue your session, step off the treadmill and go back to step 3 of this section

It does take practice to get familiar with the treadmill and how speed adjustments are made. During familiarization, I suggest using the support handle that is on the machine. This is not your typical treadmill that has speed adjustment buttons. Hence, it will take time getting used to how it operates so be careful in the beginning.

For Belt Adjustment:
1. A wrench is included in the box
2. If the running belt tends to slide to the right during use, loosen the adjustment screw on the right side (the screw is on the opposite end of the digital readout)
3. If the running belt tends to slide to the left during use, loosen the adjustment screw on the left
4. Make 1/2 to 1/4 turn adjustments (extreme adjustments can make the tuning process more frustrating)
5. Take your time

I've always unplugged the machine after each use and store it against a wall. The running belt "ran" away from me a couple of times when I first got the treadmill and I prevented my fall by using the handrail. Every time I've had an issue with the speed on the treadmill, it's been due to operator error. I've had to remind myself and be cognizant of the fact that speed adjustments are done differently on this treadmill. I wanted something new, intuitive, easy to store, easy to move, and easy to operate. This treadmill met my criteria and is well designed and built.

I watched a lot of videos online before I purchased it. By the time it arrived, I was familiar with how to use it, what to avoid, and possible safety issues I'd have to keep in mind. I recommend this treadmill for OFFICE USE, WALKING, and LIGHT JOGS. For a workout, I recommend using a traditional treadmill with manual speed & incline adjustments.

title: Fun way to exercise, well made hoola hoop
text:
I looked at tons of weighted hoola hoops on Amazon and saw many of them has some not so great reviews because they were no sturdy or would break apart. This hoola hoop is definitely very sturdy and well made.

It comes in several pieces that link together so you can adjust it to fit your waist and ideally remove pieces as you lose weight. The pieces link together very well, it feels very secure. The weight is also very secure in the hoola hoop.

I find it to be a really fun way to work out. You do feel the burn with this especially if you do the full recommended 30 mins. It took me 2 days to get the hang of it, I watched a couple youtube videos for some tips. Basically, you want to shift your weight side to side rather than do a full circular motion with your hips.

I have been using it for about 2 weeks now - about every other day and I noticed a slight decrease in my waist but nothing crazy yet, though I do believe doing this for a month at least 5 days a week will give you noticeable results.

Currently, I am able to go for about 10 mins straight without stopping at all. Whenever I stop, I switch directions. The only downside that I have noticed is when I use it in the opposite direction, the counter on the hoop doesn't count those spins. It only counts going in one direction. I don't know if that's just something wrong with my counter or if that's how it's made but ultimately it's not that big of an issue (though it would be nice to have an accurate count of my total spins at the end of the workout).

Also, it is loud like others have mentioned - but I think all of these kind of hoola hoops are. If you wear headphones you can easily listen to a podcast or watch youtube or something - but you can't really without headphones.

Overall, if you're looking for a weighted hoola hoop, this one is a good one!

title: No Regrets
text:
Surprised myself by investing in this bike. I've never purchased any major exercise equipment before, but I did take a spin class years ago that just completely kicked my butt. I always felt interested in trying it again, but I am the not the type who enjoys going to gyms or attending classes in person. So the iFit setup and such intrigued me enough to give it a try.

Firstly, don't believe Amazon when they allow you to schedule a date of delivery. I scheduled my bike to be delivered weeeeeeks in advance. The delivery date was missed with no call or update. It was also impossible to reach a customer service rep. Thankfully my husband works from home, so I wasn't taking time off of work to wait around for no reason.

When the bike did arrive, it was easy to unbox and assemble, though I did have help from my husband. One issue we encountered was the seat was misthreaded into the holder. This was bad as when I went to adjust it, you couldnt turn it to loosen or tighten it. The seat was all half on there, and unfortunately not coming out. Thankfully my husband is super handy as he had to drill it out, rethread the setup and got it installed. Whew!

I have now had the bike for a good few months with no other issues. It's quiet, takes up a small footprint, and quite a challenge for a weakling like myself.

Now, if this bike didn't have the iFit programs, I likely wouldn't use it. Those programs make the bike work for me. I love the selection (though I wish there were more beginner programs). I still need to do more of the off-bike workouts as well.....and I haven't tried the live classes yet. But the fact that I have so many options that keep changing makes me come back. I also love the series styled workouts. :)

All in all I am way happy with this bike. I can see myself using this for years to come, and I will gladly continue my iFit subscription after my trial is over.

title: despite shortcomings it's a keeper
text:
I have ordered 7 40" digital electric smokers this past year from Home Depot (because of their one year return policy using the house credit card). Three MasterBuilt, two Smoke Hollow, and this LEM unit twice. Bluetooth, regular and with RF remote control. All have been returned except for this one.

My original LEM Big Bite was serial #0004. My current one is #0048. My first one registered 40° higher than my external thermometer, blew out the chip tray half way with flames belching out (luckily I was near it at the time to prevent fire to the deck) during the burnin (I had the vents closed) and the not so secured gasket around the door. Scary. ABut on paper it seemed to be the best.

Since I was locked into HD (they just credit your HD credit card for a return), I went through all of their 40" digital electric smokers. With the new season coming, their inventory filled with pellet smoker/grills (I sold my Cookshack Fast Eddy PG 500, wanting to go the electric smoker route. So I took a chance and reordered the LEM.

Holds temperature to within 15° of my external thermometer (which reads higher.) All the other smokers read higher than my external one so basically they could not get to their supposed top temperature (as was evidenced by my cooks not being quite done in the usual time.) So at worst it's hotter inside than the set temp which is easily adjusted for but it may just be the location of my external thermometer vs the builtin one which I rally can't find as yet.

In any case I believe I can trust the temperature I set and use meat probes to determine the end of the cook anyway.

As to the shortfalls, the loose door gasket had not changed. I used some Gorilla glue in a few spots to further adhere the gasket to the door.

I do not use the included chip tray, opting for the Masterbuilt external smoke unit, a 10' dryer hose, 3" metal duct and duct tape to secure the external smoker unit into the slot where the chip tray was. I prefer the cleaner smoke produced with the creosote clinging into the 10' tubing instead of into the smoke profile. To illustrate, three of my smokers had glass doors. Using the chip trays, the glass was orange/brown following a 6 hour smoke. Using the external smoke generator the glass doors remained clear. That's creosote which can leave that tingly feeling on the tip of your tongue.

I keep both vents closed as smoke escapes from them anyway and a small amount from the closed door. (It would be nice it the door latch could be adjusted to be tighter like other smokers provide.) This provides enough air flow to keep the smoke going.

My unit arrived by UPS with some carton tears and a couple of small dents on the rear wall.

I don't need Bluetooth or an rf remote control. The display panel is easily read in bright sunlight. The control buttons are very intuitive, more so than any of my other electric smokers.

It's the keeper and I can stop my search. Not perfect but better than the rest so far. Just hope it lasts. The 5 year warranty might suggest that.

Forgot to mention that there is absolutely no assembly required, not a single screw. Just remove the plastic ties that secure the shelves for shipping. Plug and play.

It's very stabile and quiet, and seems to be sized for a 2-3 year old, or maybe even a 4-year old.

title: Excellent product and associated app. Used it to lose weight and very happy with the results.
text:
Best gift I've ever received. The day after I received this from my wife for Christmas, I set it up and entered my weight loss plan and set my goals. I've worn it every day since and followed the plan with will power and determination. My plan is simple: 1. Entered and tracked everything I ate to stay under my daily calorie intake goal, 2. Set a goal for steps per day and tried to achieve it every day. Started off modestly at 5000 steps per day and increased to 8000 as endurance increased and weight came off.
That's it! No complicated diet plan that takes too much time to figure out, keep track of and lose interest in after a few weeks of struggle. So, the only plan that worked for me is the one described above and the one we hear all the time. Watch what you eat and exercise. That's it! I've lost 52 pounds in seven months so it was a steady, healthy loss. My doc took me off my blood pressure meds two weeks ago because my blood pressure was a little too low. My cholesterol numbers went from high to the lower end of the normal range. I'm over 65 and feel better and have more energy than I've had in years. It takes some work, commitment and a lot of will power but I'm here to tell you that it can be done.
The device itself is fairly easy to set up and sync with your mobile phone. It gives you a lot of information about your daily activity and keeps track of your sleep and the food you eat (you have to enter the food type and quantity using their food data base). Once you get used to it you'll find that it doesn't take much time at all to make the entries for food intake by selecting them from the extensive Fitbit food data base. The Fitbit app builds up a little personal data base of the foods you eat frequently and most recently. It also lets you enter your own foods or meal if it's data base doesn't have it. You can also enter a food by scanning its bar code. Simple.
I know this sounds like a paid ad but I haven't received any compensation or product discount for my review. Just want to share my experience.
