title: Tension Cable holds manufactured extremely poorly
text:
There is a youtube video put out by the distributor Sunny Health & Fitness that in 40 seconds shows how to assemble the tension cable. The bottom tension hold on my unit arrived tightened to a hollow screw encasing the tension cable which made the cable 1/4 inch too short to assemble. It was not supposed to be attached to the screw at all. Six hours of trying to loosen the cable holder off the screw finally worked but upon final assembly there is really now only one working speed to this elliptical. It takes two hands and the whole body to change the tension setting and it maxes out at level 3. And we think level 3 is easier than level 1. That means I don't have the other 5 tension setting levels. Where did they go? To reinspect the tension cable the entire elliptical has to be disassembled. Yikes!! A quality nightmare. If you are considering buying after the date of this review, then this is strongly not recommended. Assembled the day it arrived.

Other than the tension cable, the elliptical is extremely easy to assemble. 8 hours on the tension cable assembly and 1.5 hours on everything else. We're extremely disappointed in the extraordinary poor quality.

So, the noise level is very managable, mostly because the tension setting is so bad it is hard to use.

title: This is not a good purchase for a quality home reformer
text:
There are several issues here to consider prior to purchasing.

1. Will the carriage roll smoothly? Even after cleaning the rails, my stott SPX failed to roll smoothly. This is a really important point.

2. Are the hand/foot loops large enough to accommodate normal sized, adult hands and feet? My stott SPX came with super tiny hand/feet loops that wouldn't work for a six year old, let alone an adult. And I have very small, adult hands.

3. Is the carriage padding sufficient? My stott SPX arrived with very thin padding and it hurt the back during movements.

4. Is this the best price on the market? Absolutely not. This package sells elsewhere on the internet for up to $500 less with additional dvd's included.

5. Will stott respond to inquiries? My phone calls and emails were ignored. It's as if this company only responds to large commercial accounts. You're completely on your own and out of luck if there is a problem or if you have a question.

6. Is the delivery box manageable? My stott SPX came in one box, approximately 14 feet long. Inside this massive box there were a couple smaller boxes. But you're talking something akin to tremendous problems getting it from curbside into the house, and if like me, you return it for being an incredible waste of money and a huge disappointment, it is painful to deal with a 14 foot box that won't fit into any normal car or suv. Hope you have a truck handy.

7. Check out other reformer brands. For a little more money the quality soars. You might think cheap is ok now, but you won't use a poor quality reformer in the long run.

The temperatures dropped down into the 50s and had a strong wind making it feel much cooler.  This blanket fit over me and my daughter sitting next to me in another chair so the sizing is great for 2 people.  We were each only wearing long-sleeve shirts and pants so I'm glad we had the blanket. I will say it is not as thick as I anticipated so I would not expect it to work as well in extremely cold events or freezing weather, but it is great for cooler fall and windy weather. title: Tried a handful of different shin guards and these were the best

When she first started I liked having the ankle protection of most youth shin guards; however, as she aged and became more competitive, I wanted to get her slide ins for more comfort and better ankle movement. I had been using Dash Sport shin guards, but she outgrew those and they stopped at Youth Medium. They also had itchy straps that she said bothered her when she sweat so I knew it was time to test some new brands.  She is age 9, but very tall for her age (just shy of 5') so she definitely needed Youth Large. I ordered 4 different brands that had slide in options and we ended up going with these after trying them on.  They fit her perfectly and provide great protection/coverage as a midfielder and also goalkeeper. I've washed the mesh sleeves a handful of times now and hang dry them; there has been no snags or tears yet and the shin guards have held up really well. I definitely recommend these for youth as they age. My daughter says they are very comfortable, don't itch, and don't hold in sweat the way others tend to.

title: Finally!  Yes, you can convert a western/Aussie D cinching system to a English style girth!
text:
I have spent endless hours trying to figure out how to convert a western saddle and a hybrid Brisbane Aussie saddle that uses a traditional D ring for rigging. Trust me, there’s more products that convert an English to western rigging but I was determined to call Australia and known saddlery companies to see if any product exists. I hit pay dirt here at Amazon after seeing them advertised at Elite Saddleworks in AU. Seems they sell their converters here at Amazon and my search is over.

As far as the product goes, these converter straps are beautifully made with heavy quality leather and a nice solid buckling system. So simple to use. Quite frankly, I did not think I was going to be able to find a correct product to make the conversion but I am delighted that these are on the market for those riders who do not like the typical Western strapping system for cinching. I find using a traditional English/Australian girth with a buckling system to be much safer for the rider and the horse… And you do not have to dismount to make any adjustments if the saddle becomes loose or needs re-positioning due to the girth.

So let me save you hours of trouble if you’re the type that has the rings on your saddle for cinching and you want to go to a buckled girth. My other suggestion is I bought at Amazon the ovation neoprene girth with elastic bands on one side and they are amazing for the price as the quality is excellent and very very comfortable for the horse. The only issue you may have is the sizing as if you read through the descriptions, some folks seem to see the girth being true to size and others suggest buying slightly larger.Other wonderful Amazon reviewer’s wrote me and made suggestions as far as finding the correct size if you have the saddle billets to measure from or actually taking a string and measuring the horses girth area. I didn’t take a chance and I actually bought four different sizes to make sure I found the correct size and will return the wrong sized ones. Looks like it’s a bit of a science as far as finding the right size for your horse or pony but the girth got incredible reviews and the price is exceptional for the value and the quality of the item..

title: Excellent
text:
I placed this bike rack onto my 2003 Nissan Sentra. I knew this was the correct rack to buy thanks to the website that provides a list (Visit the fit list FIRST before purchasing an Allen bike rack): [...]

Anyway, since this bike rack had such good reviews and it was the right one for my car, I decided to buy it. Hooking it up was fairly easy. I'll admit, I struggled a little bit only because it was my fist attempt, but I know that it will be a peace of cake from now on. Once you get it right the first time, the future attempts will be perfectly easy. When I was finished, I put my body weight onto it to ensure it was sturdy enough for a bike, and it was definitely safe! That bike rack was not going to go anywhere! The straps and everything ensured it was sturdy and safe for the road!

I had to pick up my new bike today (A Schwinn Riverside 26" female bike that looks like this: [...]. As you can tell by the photo, my bike is a female bike. Because it is a female bike WITHOUT a straight bar, I had to purchase a second part that is also by Allen seen here: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000ELSSZE/ref=oh_details_o00_s00_i00. This bar is easy to install as well. It took me about ten seconds to place it onto my bike securely. This allowed me to easily put my bike onto the rack without any issues. Keep in mind, this is only for bikes that do NOT have a straight bar. You may or may not need this part. I needed it for mine.

Once I placed the bike onto the rack, I tightened up the straps. One thing I noticed is that the front wheel of the bike was not secure. It was free to turn as I drove, which would bang into my car, so I simply got a bungee cord and wrapped it in a way to prevent it from moving while I drove. I also got a bungee cord for the back wheel to prevent that wheel from spinning (this is not necessary, but I just prefer to do this). The peddles of the bike hit the bumper, so I would also recommend socks or clothes of some sort to be wrapped around them so they don't scratch the paint of your car.

Anyway, my bike and I made it home perfectly fine. The bike was very secure and sturdy on the bike rack. That bike was not going anywhere, even though I went up and down hills and made a lot of turns on my way home at around 50mph. I have not gone on the highway with it yet, but based on my experience so far, I am certain it is fine.

Overall, I recommend this product! It's great!

title: Great on a cold day!!!
text:
I was at work one day. I work retail and our store is always FREEZING due to them not wanting to turn the heat on in order to save themselves money. I went into work one morning while it was -7 degrees outside. My store was obviously not as cold as outside, but like I said they refuse to turn on the heat so it's pretty cold in the store as well.

Anyway, I was standing at my register waiting for customers to come by. While waiting another employee asked "Are you cold?" and I replied that I was and that my hands were the most cold, so she handed me hot hands, which immediately wowed me! It was so warm the second I put my hands on it and it really helped me out between customers for quite a number of hours. She allowed me to keep it, thankfully, so I was able to see how long it would last. It lasted throughout my entire shift and basically the rest of the day.

I plan to buy more of these because normally my hands get dry and start to bleed when they are exposed to cold air for too long at my job (yes, I know it sounds crazy that my store is this cold. Trust me, I believe it is crazy as well to force employees and customers to stand it ... I get customers complaining to me every day that it is too cold in the store). But anyway, I just have to tolerate the super cold air in my store. If I purchase these and use them each time it'll help me out quite a bit. I highly recommend these to anyone who has to put up with exposing their hands to cold air for long periods of time.

title: Good investment for your health
text:
I have been using this pedometer for 4 weeks now, and it works great.
The pros:
It comes with a clip and tether. You can clip it or put it in your pocket. You can even clip it to your purse, but I like it on my pants so I can count every single step of the day.
It counts steps, distance, calories. Don't ask me if they are all accurate. I'm only tracking steps and working towards a goal.
You can look back up to a week of steps, in case you are keeping track.
It resets every midnight (no, it never turns off).
Small enough to fit in a pocket.
The cons:
Well, con. Only one up to now. I tried hooking it to my bra or neckline (sometimes I wear dresses) and it doesn't record steps very accurately. I'll be walking for 10 minutes and the number of steps doesn't change. So on dress days, I hook it to my purse, or my underwear if the dress is baggy.

In the last 4 weeks I've gone from an average of 4,000 steps per day to 7,000 steps! It's fun to keep track.

I used 2 2x6 boards to mount to studs. I would recommend using 2x8 if I did it again. I anchored them with 8 - 5" lag bolts at the outer edges and 12 - 4" structural screws at the middle studs.

for anyone having problems getting the lags in that are on the upper side of the bottom bracket. mount the top section of the pull bar first. drill your pilot holes in the correct location for the bottom brackets. once you've done this, hand thread in your lag bolt with the bracket free. tighten the bolt down almost all the way then reattach the top of the pull up bar to the support bracket with the supplied bolts. you might have to flex the upper section to align the bolt holes. if you don't do this you'll have to angle the lag bolts in.

I had both my 2 sons on this and myself and it's holding strong. roughly 300lbs. My wife has said the bar is smaller diameter than our current pull up bar. I don't think it'll be an issue. title: Made in China. Unable to tighten fully.
text:

It has a nice grip feel to the bar and there is a sleek design to the blades.
The only con is the adjustable band (to make the pole shorter/longer) isn't secure. You can actually pull/push the pole in/out. There doesn't seem to be an easy way to adjust the screw or nut for tightness. So, I carefully opened the tab, twisted it one full circle then closed it to make a together grip. Plus there is a minor issue but puzzling... why is the adjustable band made out of plastic...while the poles are metal? The adjustable band should be made out of metal as well. That's the only reason why I rated it 4 stars.

This paddle is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon.

title: Made in China.  Great color.
text:

The paddle part has an outward curve with a slight concave shape on the inside to allow ease when you put the paddle into the water and have a smooth start with stroking. The concave allows you to have more pressure on pushing water and get you moving faster.

2. As mentioned, that section is plastic and with wear and tear, it will crack then you will not be able to adjust the length. When that happens, you will just need to drill and put in a screw to secure them together.

Suggestion for the company:

The keys that come with the scooter are also extremely convenient. With the NFC feature it’s easy to unlock, all you have to do is touch the key to the scooter’s digital interface.

Making sure you have enough battery is important if you are planning on going somewhere far. The gauge on the scooter doesn’t give you an accurate idea of how far you can go, and the apps percentages aren’t very accurate either.

One other thing I wish it had was a longer pole. It is tall enough for my hand to reach it when I’m standing but it has to be fully extended so it can be awkward and unsafe. If it was a little bit longer, it’d be perfect for sitting and standing.

title: Made in China.  Hand brakes only.
text:
The bike arrived in good shape. Nothing was dented up and it was a reasonably smooth assembly. The tires arrived with enough air to get a few test rides in, but I wouldn't assume this to always be true and you will need to add air to the tires.

The listing states a novice can assemble this bike in 15 minutes. Unless you assemble bikes for a living it will take you longer than 15 minutes. However, this is the second bike I've assembled lately and the cycmoto was definitely easier. It will take you about 10 minutes just to unbox and remove all the foam and plastic ties. Then you will want to spend at least 10 minutes skimming through the instructions to brief yourself on the tasks at hand. I spent about 20 minutes getting all the necessary pieces together and partially tightened. Then I spent another 30 minutes adjusting, straightening, leveling and right sizing the seat, handlebars and brakes. You will want to refer to the instructions when adjusting the front brake. I did not install the training wheels, the basket or the splash guards (see comments below). So, if you just plan to assemble just the main pieces you should expect to spend about 75 minutes. If you plan to install all the extras then you should add another 30 minutes.

It comes with a flat metal multi tool and a dual size Allen wrench that can be used to completely assemble. I used the included tools to assemble. It was a little difficult for certain bolts, but it can be done. The only additional tool I used that was not included was a simple Phillips head screwdriver.

You should note that this bike has front and back hand brakes and not a coaster brake (if you pedal backwards it will spin backwards freely and not brake). The front brake (right handlebar) has two pads that squeeze the wheel to stop. The back brake (left handlebar) has a different stopping mechanism that is build into the crank system. The one concern I have with the brakes is that they are plastic. I hope they don't crack or break if the bike falls. Learning to use the hand brakes early could be better if you think the kid will grow into a mountain or bmx style bike.

A few things to note:

1) the instructions did not include a section for installing the splash guards. I am fairly confident I know which guard goes in the front/back by looking at the pictures in the listing. It would have been nice to have this in the instructions.

2) there are instructions for installing the basket, but I am either missing parts (the plate, small metal sheets and screws) or the instructions should be updated to describe attaching the basket using a ziptie like piece that was included. Personally, I would like to attach the basket as described in the instructions, but those parts were not included.

I did not install either the basket or splash guards. These are advanced attachments that should be used for kids who already know how to ride a bike with two wheels or if you plan to use training wheels. If you are purchasing this bike to train someone how to ride without training wheels then you should assume there will be a fall or two. By waiting to attach the splash guards and the basket you will avoid damaging while practicing to learn to ride a bike.

I would recommend not using the training wheels at all because it could make training without them more difficult. However, uou can adjust the height of the training wheels. So, if you start with the training wheels completely on the grown then you can slowly raise them off the ground.

Overall, the bike looks nice and feels solid.

The fit is nice, it is comfortable to wear, has good ventilation and it is lightweight. You can adjust the circumference size (turning a nob inside the helmet) and the straps that buckle to secure the helmet on your head. Even though this helmet looks like it would be nice for a child, it is definitely an adult (or older kid/ teenager) sized helmet. It easily fit two average adult heads. One nice feature is that it comes with a detachable cushion that helps pad the strap pressed against the underside of the neck/throat area. Very nice touch on the extra cushion. A bonus is that you can remove and easily wash it.

Please note that this helmet is not intended to provide protection while participating in motorized sports such as a moped. There are no details on a maximum speed that you should avoid. To be safe I would only use this helmet for bike riding, skating, ect.

It comes with a one month warranty, but you can email the company to extend the warranty to one year.

title: Not cheap, but so much better than most of the others I've tried.
text: This is quite inexpensive backpack, at least for me, but it is truly exceptional. It’s much more comfortable than others I’ve tried. The straps are nicely padded. There is a mesh fabric against your back for breathability so your back doesn’t sweat. Of course there are pockets inside and out as well as loops and so on to make packing and attaching a breeze.

title: Made in China. Really nice for what it is. Great for all ages.
text:
I have a little indoor putting green which is used by multiple people both kids and adults. This is a nice “toy” putter that can be used by a multitude of different ages and heights. title: Made in China. Easy set up. Great for on the go or at home.
text:
The Weierfu Pickleball net is perfect for the sports enthusiasts who are looking for convenience. There is nothing worse than travelling to the local shared court only to find that the court is full! Problems solved! This metal set is very sturdy and fairly easy to set up. The net is regulation size and made of a tangle free design. Pair with a set of paddles and balls (not included) and you will be set for a night of fun! The storage bag is heavy duty and makes the set easily portable.

This portable net is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon.

title: Made in China. Crazy expensive. Can be used both in your home and in your car.
text:
This inflatable air mattress can be used both in your home… Outside… And also in your car. Of course is made to be used in your truck or car, but it can be used in other places as well.

It is very compact and easy to store. It is nice that it comes with a 12 vote air pump. You certainly would not want to try and blow this thing up yourself.

This air mattress is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 55 bucks it is certainly twice the price it should be, but overall it is fine.

title: Nonelectronic. Easy set up and storage.
text: I like this is putting green is not electronic. The ball simply drop down and rollback. So there’s nothing to plug-in. It’s fairly compact when not in use. Actually a lot more compact than I was expecting. I nice surface with a nice feel to it. It’s nothing overly fancy, but it’s exactly what I was looking for. title: Made in China. I like the dumbbells better than the barbells.
text:

I more impressed with the dumbbells that I am with the barbells. Obviously your taking one thing and trying to make it work for another. But having the option is nice.

title: Made in China. Lower-priced options are offered.
text:
If you have ever played with wooden paddles… Then you know it can be a bit of a chore. These graphite battles are super lightweight and are so much better and more enjoyable to play with then wood.

These paddles are made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 106 bucks they are quite expensive, but they do include extra grips and 6 balls. If you don’t need the extra grips, you can certainly find something similar for less… Perhaps purchasing 2 sets of 2 paddles. But overall they are nice.

text:

title: Fun on the water in the beach. You'll need an inflation device.
text:

Though you can have up to 3 writers, I found that if you actually have 3 you will probably need to go at a slower speed otherwise the 2 outside passengers will be thrown off rather easily. If there is a single passenger, then you can go a bit faster.

You can also use this to lie or sit on the beach. Kind of like an air mattress.

title: Made in China.  Works for camping, etc.
text:
This chair, in it’s case, measures 14 inches long, 5 inches tall, and 4 inches deep. Assembled, the seat itself measures about 20 inches wide, and about 23 inches long, and stands about 27 inches high at the back. It does weigh the indicated 2 lbs, which is about right for all but the most high end ultralight chairs. The chair is as comfortable as you would expect a lightweight camping chair to be. I’m sitting in it while writing this review. It is assembled with poles that are fastened together by shock cords. When assembling the canvas seat onto the pole structure, I can say that it is pretty difficult to get the final two pole tips inserted into their corners. It does help to have two people, which initially was a little concerning. However, I left the set assembled overnight, with about 30 lbs of weight in it, and when I disassembled and reassembled, it was definitely easier. It just needs to be stretched out, so I’ll be storing it, at least for a while, in that same way.

This chair is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. The listing shows it can hold up to 300#. . . .Good luck with that! I weigh 180, and certainly would not consider using this chair for anyone over 200#.

title: Made in China. Very clear picture.
text:
This is a very cool camera. . . but. . . there are a few things to know. . .

#1. There’s not only is plastic covering on the screen… There is also a tiny plastic cover that needs to be removed on the camera itself.

#2. Make sure you watch the video for installation instructions. This information is not in the packaging.

#3. Make sure you turn/adjust the camera before tightening. Though you can turn the screen anyway you like, it’s best to rotate/adjust the camera 1st to make sure it is in the right position and level before you start rotating the screen.

#4. Though there are buttons on back of the screen, there are no labels on the buttons. Though there is information in the instructions, it is not clear and does not give you much information. You really just have to play with it to see how it will works. But to be honest, I was quite happy with the settings as they were from the start and did not tinker with anything.

#5. The screen is charged using a micro USB cord. One is included, but a wall charger is not included.

#6. It takes a couple of seconds for the screen to turn on after you press the power button. Also, you are not to turn the screen on until after you have plugged the camera cable in.

I’m quite impressed with the quality of the picture. It is very clear. It shows that it’s 1080 P and I assume that’s correct.

This is a “generic” bike rearview camera. There is no branding on the box. So it could be sold by any number of different companies. It is made in China.

title: Made in the Philippines. A pricey, but incredible love.
text:
This is one sweet glove. Super soft feel. It’s certainly going to take a bit of time to break in. But it feels quite comfortable. The stitching and leather work is quite nice. It is made in the Philippines. Below is a little information about “Kip Leather”.

Where things get a bit more premium and specialized are the Kip Leather baseball gloves. These can be found in both USA Kip Leather and Japanese Kip Leather. Kip leather is usually the most preferred leather among professional players due to the light, firm, feel and higher quality of the leather. Kip leather comes from younger cattle, which creates a lighter hide that is extremely durable and taut, while also being a little bit easier to break in when compared to USA premium steerhide gloves.

Selecting Your Leather:

Cowhide Leather - Heavy leather, fastest break in time, medium quality, short durability, ideal for youth players.

Steerhide Leather - Heaviest leather, longest break in time, high quality, longest durability, ideal for high school and college players.

Kip Leather - Lighter leather, medium break in time, higher quality, long durability, ideal for college and pro players.

Japanese Kip Leather - Lightest leather, medium break in time, highest quality, long durability, ideal for elite pro players.

title: What an "upgrade" from "rental scooters"!
text:
If you’ve used rental scooters, then you’ll know that sometimes they leave “something to be desired”. Well. . . This Segway scooter is what you desire! ;-)

Better power. . . Better stability. . . Better range. . . Built better. . . Better tires. . . .

Comes well packaged. Super easy to assemble. The only thing you really have to do is attach the handlebar and bell. Equipment to do that included.

Keep in mind that there are a few things that you’ll need which are not included. . . For example. . . A helmet. . . as well as lock. Segway offers their own branded helmet. . . and lock. . .as well as several other accessories for your scooter, but you can purchase them elsewhere as well.

Folding is easy. . . But. . .This is not a super lightweight scooter. It has a weight of just over thirty-six pounds. So the picture of someone just carrying it into a store. . . easy-breezy. . . is not necessarily the case.

The lights are cool too. ;-)
