[[ASIN:B002I0HHJC Franklin Sports NHL Foam Mini Hockey Balls, Assorted Colors, 6 Count]]

[[ASIN:B013TL8TBI Franklin Sports NHL Foam Mini Hockey Balls - 12 Pack]]

title: Tight
text: This is almost like a “compression” top. . . at least if you order your usual size.  It’s quite tight.  For more of a comfortable fit, you might want to order a size larger.  It’s 100% polyester, so it’s easy to wash.  It’s very nice for layering.  My one main issue is the cost.  Hopefully it will last through several seasons (and my size won’t change much).  Overall I like it.  . . .Just wish they were charging a more “reasonable” price for an imported product.

title: 6X4 Goal
text: This is a great home or school practice net. The metal poles are solid construction and the yellow net is easy to see. This net is 6'X4' which is great for home use because it does not take up the entire yard, but is large enough for practice and play. It contains stakes that keep the net from tipping over, but the poles are heavy enough that it will stay in place under most circumstances. The net is attached with Velcro strips which makes assemble easy, but durability in the weather could be questionable. It comes nicely packed in plastic and can be assembled by one person. Overall the construction, and quality is very good.  The only concern that I have is the long term effects of the weather on the Velcro strips.

title: Made in China bag
text: This is a light weight, functional, but not very durable bag.  It has a black and gray color combination with white accents which make it very nice looking.  The "CALLAWAY" logo is on each of the side pockets.  It weighs 3.5 lbs. and easily light enough for a woman or young person to carry. There are ten spaces on top for golf clubs that goes the full length of the bag with padded dividers between each one. It has 6 additional pockets that all face forward, which makes it easy to get in and out of. All 6 of the pockets have nice zippers that work easily. This bag has a padded nylon handle and a 3 1/4 inch padded shoulder strap that is adjustable or can be removed. The bag does not stand on it's on and will fall over.  It is not the best quality, but looks good and would be a great starter bag for someone learning to play.  It’s Made in China, so you’re paying a lot for the name, and not much for the bag.

title: Nice design
text: This ball is actually a little better than I expected.  There’s actually real stitching, and laces are real, and not just painted or glued on.  I like the artwork.  Though it’s not super crisp, but it works for this football.  If football is not your sort of thing, this same design comes in other balls as well, such as soccer, kickball and basketball.  At the current price of twenty bucks for Made in China, it’s a bit expensive, but of course you’re paying for the “Frozen” design.  Overall I like it.

title: Not the greatest design
text: This is trying to be a “one-size-fits-all” sort of thing. . . .and that might not work for you, all depending upon your wrist.  If you have a smaller wrist, then it can rotate around when you’re pulling on the Velcro.  The paper / cards slide-in on the end, and the ends are open, so if it’s raining, they can get wet, rendering them useless unless you laminate them before inserting.  It’s Made in China, so a bit expensive as well.

title: Nice bases
text: This is a set of rubber bases that can be used for baseball or softball. It comes in 5 pieces, which would be first, second, third base, home plate, and the pictures mound. They are made with quality, durable rubble that can withstand outside weather and constant use.  The bright orange color makes them very visible and easy for player to see. These can be use by personal, home, and school fields. The bases need no special installation or instructions to use. They are quality made, easy to see, and make any backyard game a lot more fun.  FYI. . . These look identical to BSN brand bases, which are currently at a slightly lower price.  You might want to check both.

title: Nice basic set
text: This table tennis set is made for home use and is of the quality that you would expect for a game room. There are four paddles and six balls to the set. The handles are made of a blonde wood that was smooth and flared at the neck of the paddle for comfort and control. The paddles themselves have black knobby rubber on one side and red on the other. Aesthetically they have a great look.  The "KILLERSPIN" logo is on each of the balls. The paddles and balls are packaged securely and nicely.  This is a nice set for home and personal use.

title: Great for Frozen Fans
text: This is a size 3 ball, so it’s a smaller version.  (Size 5 is the full-size adult ball).  It’s very colorful and the graphics are nice.  It’s nice that it’s sewn together, like a “real” ball, and not just one large ball with painted-on stitching as with some inexpensive balls.  Franklin Sports offers some other balls (not just soccer balls) with the Frozen theme as well.  Great for fans of the movie.  If you’re going to actually use it, it gets scuffed-up fairly quickly, but the graphics are still there.

title: I prefer foam
text: The box shows “indoor” archery target set. . . but. . .  .This is a “toy” which needs open space. . .  Either a open/empty basement. . . garage.  .. or outdoors.  As it states … . . Adult supervision is required.  Such a “toy” can be dangerous.  You may want to use some superglue on the tips, so that they don’t come off.  They were a little loose on my set.  Personally, I prefer the bows which use foam darts simply due to safety. . . they of course they are not completely safe either.

title: Not the best option. .  .in my opinion
text: This is a crazy expensive Made in China set which is missing the bases.  It’s really kind of “confusing”.  By that I mean it would have better to include all the bases and do without the “homerun wall”. .  . .and charged a lower price. Franklin Sports (and others) offer different t-ball sets geared for kids in a similar age range. . . . Though I don’t have anything against this set really other than price. . . I just think that there are better options at lower price points which would be more enjoyable overall.

title: Check your bag size before purchasing this travel bag
text:
This bag can work. . . depending upon how compact your golf bag is. If you check the listing, it even states that it holds a “medium size” golf bag. If you use what’s called a “carry bag” for your clubs, then this travel bag should work fine. If you don’t typically use a “carry bag” for your clubs, then you might want to get one, and switch your clubs when you travel (or have a second set of “travel clubs”) simply because many travel bags will not hold the larger golf bags.

This AmazonBasics travel bag is quite nice though. Several pockets. . .padding. . . rear wheels. . . good handle construction. It really works quite well, and is reasonably affordable. Don’t forget your TSA travel locks.

title: Should be a lot less expensive
text: The best way to describe this is it’s a metronome for athletes.  For swimming, this easily attaches to your swim cap.  If you’re using this for running, you’re going to either have to wear a headband or cap to attach it to so that you can hear it.  It’s small and waterproof.  My only real “issue” with this item is the cost.  For such a “basic” device, it should be a fraction of the cost.

title: Perfect Travel Item
text: This is the PERFECT take-along for traveling.  It comes in SO handy!  It’s very compact.  It’s very handy when you’re going to take a day-trip. . . Example:  You’re in Paris, and you’re going to take a day-trip to the Palace of Versailles.  It also comes in handy to take along when you’re going shopping and find some “treasures” along the way.  It has mesh pockets on each side for water bottles.  It’s Made in China, and the overall construction is quite reasonable.  I have the red one, and it’s very nice and bright, just like the picture.

title: Multitude of uses
text: The “AXIS BUOY” is multi-functional for swimmers. It can be used to help inexperienced swimmers learn proper technique while helping to build upper body strength. The competitive swimmer will find the buoy a great training tool to improve body position, engage core muscles, increase speed in the water. For most tri-athletes, the swimming in open water is the most difficult part of a race. The design of this buoy allows for it to be used as a leg buoy or as an ankle float, so that it accommodates different styles and levels of training. For people with hip injuries, the “AXIS BUOY” helps to keep the hips and/or the ankles elevated and stabilized so that a person can get the exercise they want without pain or further injury to their joints. This buoy has a new and improved design and will easily move from the ankles to the legs. It is comfortable to use, promotes proper swimming technique, and builds upper body and core strength. For anyone that is using the old traditional buoy, I would recommend giving this one a try.

title: Can be used by both kids and adults
text: This “FRANKLIN PITCH RETURN” is a fun and easy way to help a “newbie” learn to throw a ball and catch a ball as well as help an experienced player practice his skills. It is the type of training tool that can be used with an adult assisting or a child can throw and play by him or herself. The instructions are not very good, but fortunately it is not very difficult to put together with a little common sense. I was pleasantly surprised at how sturdy the metal tubing for the frame is. The netting is a quality material and holds up well outside in the weather. It has multiple angle settings and a curved frame.  As a player gets better and more experience, he or she can adjust the pitch return so that the ball will come back at different angles. It also has an area for the “strike zone”. This is nice set up, easy to assemble, and has some great features for anyone wanting to learn or improve their throw and catching skills.

title: For ages 6 and up . but not much older
text: “Stinger Bee” is a line of items offers from Franklin Sports.  Though none are very high quality, this one is slightly better than some of the others.  One plus is that it’s adjustable.  Still, overall, it’s a rather low quality Made in China item.  Inflating it takes a bit of time.  .. Even putting it together is a little more challenging than one would expect.  It’s for kids ages six and up. . . .and not very much “up” from that.  Older kids will tear it apart in seconds.

title: It's just a blow-up ball
text: This is one of several “Stinger Bee” items that Franklin Sports.  Like the others, this one is really “lightweight”.  It’s simply a blow-up ball.  That’s all there is to this expensive Made in China item.  The tubing that attaches to the door is not adjustable and will be too high for most kids.  This is obviously for little kids. . . so they won’t even be able to use it.  If you really want a speed bag, there are much better options, as a much better price.

title: Pricey
text: Franklin Sports is the leader in expensive, low-quality, Made in China sports games such as this.  This particular game is a simple toss-the-ball game.  Due to the low quality, it’s really better for younger kids, as older kids and adults could destroy it rather easily.  It’s rather easy to put together, but once together, it’s a bit large, so you have to have space to store it somewhere.  At the current price of thirty-five bucks, it’s quite expensive for what it is.

title: Super grip. . . but little padding
text: If you’re looking for a mat which is simply going to keep you from slipping / sliding about, then this one will work just fine.  But if you’re looking for a mat with padding, then this one is quite thin.  Because it’s so thin, it certainly rolls-up very small.  I really love it because it has such great grip. . . . but then there is simply so little padding.  I feel like I need to put another mat on top of this one for comfort.

title: 19 Decals combine for one great moment
text: The top picture gives you an example of how this collection can look.  This collection offers 19 wall decals. . . both with words, and then the hearts.  So you can arrange them to suit you.  Note that the color of the wall will show through the words.  If you’re going to be painting prior to applying the decals, then you’ll want to wait at least three-weeks.  The surface must be smooth.  Great way to add a little something to a room, at a very reasonable price.  Being that they are Made in the USA makes even better!

title: Inexpensive. . but also cheap
text: This tail light is pretty cheaply made. It does have a seal that supposedly makes it water resistant. The light was pretty difficult to get apart so you could install batteries. It does not come with batteries. It has a seat post mount with several adapters, but I can tell you, there are a lot of larger seatposts that this light won't fit. This red tail light has a fair amount of brightness, but very disappointingly does not have a flasher feature. The flasher feature, especially for any taillight, cheap or expensive, is something you'd expect.  I’m giving it three-stars, simply because of the current inexpensive price of five bucks.

title: Like the camo look
text: Franklin Sports makes several different batting gloves.  Most of them are similar, other than the design.  This one has the camo design, which looks really nice.  I could do without the Franklin logo, but so it goes.  It’s Made in China, as is 99% (if not indeed 100%) of Franklin Sports items.  Quite comfortable and fit well.  I will say if you’re going to try and use these for anything other than baseball, you’re probably going to have some issues with sweating.

title: Little Kids Set
text: This is one of those “odd” items where it’s a bit “off” from reality. . .  .but it still works.  By that I mean that the bat is only 21” long not really the right shape. . . but it’s meant for little kids, so it does a good job of working for that age group.  Being foam, it’s safer overall.  At the current price of twenty bucks, I think it’s a bit pricey for what it is.  I have the New York Yankees version, and some teams are a bit less expensive.  Overall I like it.

title: Tap. .  Tap. .  .Tap. . . .
text: The golf tags tracking system is designed to work with an android or downloaded iPhone app that will provide real time tracking, actual club distances, ranges and scoring with each swing. There are 15 tags to a box and they must be placed on the end of the golf clubs. Tap the tags before each shot and it records the information to your phone so that it can be reviewed immediately or after you finish the round of golf. It works great, but it can be cumbersome to carry a phone around to check each shot. The tags must be tapped before each and every shot and sometimes you have to tap it several times, which can be very distracting. It is a high tech system placed in low tech plastic tags. I will say that I don’t have a “smartwatch”, and I think having that might make it a little easier / better.  Overall I like it, but I certainly won’t use it each time I play.

title: Just don't expect it to be a "regular" pillow.
text:
This is one of those items where it all depends upon your comfort level and expectations. I have one of each of these pillows. The “large” is quite large, even when deflated. It takes-up way too much room in a carry-on bag. The “regular” is about half the size, so it works a little better if you’re packing it.

For camping, it’s a nice item to have. It also works well in a hammock. But if you’re traveling and staying in a hotel somewhere, then of course a “regular” pillow is much nicer.

title: Get Your Jump On!
text:
I have both the Ergo handles and the “Fly” rope. I really like the handles. They are very comfortable and what I call “ordinary” jump rope handles. Both the handles and rope are Made in China. The rope is adjustable. The “Fly” rope is 9.5’ in length. Super easy to change ropes. . . .Just clip on/off.

Note that SPRI offers several different jump rope combination sets. Some can be slightly lower in price, purchased as a set, rather than individually on this listing. An example is the set shown below.

[[ASIN:B00G8UK2PO SPRI Premium Adjustable Speed Jump Rope]]

title: Not nearly as good as I had hoped
text:
At first, I thought this Made in China item might be worth the current price of just under nine bucks. . . but. . . after I received it. . . I changed my mind.

First of all, the net that holds the ball is NOT “heavy duty” as described. It’s VERY flimsy and is not going to last more than a couple of days. It’s not easy to get the ball in the net either. You’ll certainly want to have an extra ball to keep in the net, and not try to remove it (until after the net is destroyed). It should be a simply process of getting the ball in-and-out. . but it’s not.

The waist strap will go around a 26” waist, at most.

The cord from the waist to the ball gets “twisted-up” rather quickly as well. There should have been a “loop screw” sort of thing so that the cord doesn’t twist.

title: Stop your wheels from turning
text: These stop your wheels from rolling.  Plain-and-simple.  I’m not sure what they are made of.  They feel harder than rubber, but they are flexible, so not hard plastic either.  They are very easy to put-on and take-off.  Four are included.  You can put them on all four wheels, or just two.  They fit from 49 – 65mm wheels.  The video at the top of the listing shows how they work. . . . but you’ll also find some videos online, if you need help getting started with them.  I like the fact that they are Made in the USA. . . but. . .  I think at the current price of twenty-four bucks, they are crazy expensive for what they are.

title: Great Kids Goggles
text: These are the perfect swim goggles for children. They come in a variety of fun colors, well made, easy to adjust the fit, and compare in quality to much more expensive goggles. They fit around the face like a swimmer’s goggle, but have a large site area like diving goggles. They are made WITHOUT latex which makes will reduce the possibility of having an allergic reaction to the material. They are curved for a better fit and have UV lenses.  The release on the side makes them easy to adjust and accommodate a larger range of age groups, or if you have a younger child, these will adapt to his or her growing needs.  My grandchild loves to wear these during bath time while playing in the tub, plus it makes it easy for me to wash her hair and rinse it without tears.  She is quite rough on these goggles and they have held up wonderfully without scratches on the lens and I have never seen them fog up. They come in a clear, hard plastic case that is perfect for storage and maintaining the goggles when not in use. The only slight issue that I have is that they only come in clear lens and for outdoor swimming and water play, a tinted lens would be nice.

title: This is a FAST-PITCH SOFTBALL GLOVE. . . . not a baseball glove.
text:
Important: This is NOT a baseball glove. It is a Fast-Pitch Softball glove, as it states on the label on the glove. I’m attaching a picture. Granted, you can use it any way you wish.

I was impressed with this glove as soon as I took it out of the box. The leather is very soft and supple, and the combination of camel color and black is impressive. It does not have to be broken in and can go from the box to the field. It has a hand formed pocket with braided black leather. This glove is made for fast pitch softball and would be an exceptional glove for a novice player or for the more experienced fielder. It is well made and very durable. The glove is comfortable on the hand. A nice option if you’re looking for an affordable fast-pitch softball glove.

title: Not quality construction
text: For the casual player or someone learning to play this is a great set. It contains two paddles, one red and one blue. It also comes with 3 standard pin pong balls. This is not an upgrade model, but just a replacement kit for the home table tennis set.  The paddles are covered with rubber surface that has small dimples that enables the paddles to better grip the balls. They have the appearance of being poorly put together and even for a basic set.  They are Made in China.  If you can get them cheap, as “back-up” paddles, then they are ok.

title: Stone / Opal REVO Lens
text: These goggles are designed to accommodate multiple winter sports. The look and design is super cool and at the same time has tremendous function. They do not have a hard frame on the outer edge which adds to comfort and the ability to have a greater range of vision. The lenses work great in different weather conditions in that it reduces glare and radiation from the sun, but additionally provided increased peripheral vision. The frames have small vents in them that keep the lenses from fogging over. They also have a “foam” layer around the frame and nose area for increased comfort, but does not interfere with your breathing. It has an adjustable strap that can fit directly around the head or be adjusted to fit around your helmet. They come with a nice pouch with the “TRAVERSE” logo on it.  These are scratch resistance and a very reasonable price. I love the styling, fit, and function of these goggles.

title: Not cheap, but built to last
text: This glove is could easily be called beauty and the beast. It has soft beautiful leather that looks expensive and feels comfortable on the hand. This glove “breaks in” easily because the leather is so nice. It is the perfect combination of great styling, functionality, and durability. The accent color and laces is a cobalt blue which gives the glove some pop.  It is well made, well designed and attractive. This is not a starter glove and would be a great step-up for team player. It is a good value considering the craftsmanship, the quality of the leather, and the pro styling.  It is expensive, but a glove that will last, and be handed down for many years.

title: A bit pricey, but great for what they are
text: These balls are great for a young person that is learning to hit or for a more experienced player that has limited space to practice. They look more like  whiffle balls, but are made with a product that has more flexibility that collapse on impact. They immediately regain their shape. This allows for increased accuracy in hitting, but keeps the ball from traveling long distances. That makes these balls perfect for home use, but not necessarily for school or league use. They come eight to a package and arrive in a nylon net bag that doubles as storage when it's time to clean up. The draw string allows for easy closure and hang-up. This a product for an avid player that wants to practice, but does not want to chase baseballs down the street.

title: Cute Boston Terrier
text: The Boston Terrier looks more like a child's stuffed animal or puppet than a serious golfer's club headcover. Do not be mistaken. This is well made, purposeful, and very useful to any golfer that is bored with the plain, simple covers. If you happen or know someone who has a love of dogs, specifically Boston Terriers and plays golf, this is the perfect item or gift. The cover has a significant amount of white and shows stains and dirt easily. It has very realistic looking eyes and nose that are well attached. The matching inside color is black and very nicely lined. This cover fits tight over the club, but still comes off relatively easy. A Boston Terrier cover may not be for everyone, but for someone with a desire to  have a quality cover and a conversation piece at the same time, you can't go wrong with this one.  It is a little expensive for Made in China, but if you have a Boston Terrier, then you’ll have to have it.

title: A bit of shedding
text: This is a wonderful product for the avid golfer that wants to add a little personality to his game. This is a great conversation piece, but is definitely a serious golfer's piece of equipment. The horse is mostly brown, but does have a white face that gets dirty after a while. It has beautiful detailed, brown and black eyes that are well attached and no worries of them falling off. The main is about 4 inches long and sheds. The outside material is soft like a stuff animal and has beautiful detail for what it was made to do. It is lined with cream colored fleece that does a great job of protecting clubs from scratches and the outside elements.  It has an elastic band on the inside near the neck of the horse to keep it snuggly on the club. This elastic band can also make it difficult to get it on and off of the club. The opening is about 4 inches across and should fit most standard clubs. The DAPHNE'S HORSE HEADCOVER is  well made, does what it's suppose to do (protect the club) and does it with flair, if you don't mind the shedding of the mane or  its' ability to show dirt.

title: A bit "awkward" but cute
text: The Ladybug Headcover has a black body with 3 legs on each side. It has two red wings that are sewn in at the top, but are attached mid-way down the back. With constant use these wings get pulled out and cause a small tear in the headcover. This does not affect the functionality of the product but does make a difference in the look. The eyes are small and plastic, about the size of a pencil eraser and are well attached.  It has two antennas which gives the ladybug the final detail it needs. The inside is a fleece material that will serve even the most particular golfer well. The inside is black which will hide dirt, while protecting the club at the same time.  The legs and wings of this headcover make it a little bit cumbersome and hurts the ability to use it regularly. If that aspect doesn't matter, it is a good protective cover.  For Made in China, it’s also a bit pricey. .  .but again, it has the “cute factor”.

title: A couple of "issues", but a fun cover
text: The Lion Headcover is two toned tan and white. The front of the neck extending under the chin and around the nose is white. This looks good brand new, but quickly gets dirty and soiled. The back and top of the face is tan with black plastic eyes. The eyes are well attached with no worries of them coming off. The nose and mouth are also black, but more of a soft felt material. The mane is long and impressive, but does shed a bit. This lion has whiskers, which shows the attention to detail on this product.  The inside is lined with a soft protective material, but it is a little tight inside. It does have an elastic band in the neck which helps to hold the cover in place, but can make it difficult to get the club in and out.  If you are looking for a cover with personality and are willing to account for a couple of minor issues, this is the one.

title: Almost as I rembered
text: The Sock Monkey golf club cover is very unique and functional at the same time. It is a wonderful version of the sock monkey I remember as a child. This cover is soft, and well made. The body is tan is and the face is an exaggerated version of the original one. There are two fuzzy red balls on the front for buttons and one on each hand . The face is very soft and padded and the Sock Monkey face is all stitching with no hard items attached.  It has a red ribbon around its neck and is wearing a cap that has the same fuzzy ball matching the ones used for buttons. It has a tail that matches the material and color of the body with a cream color tip.  The material on the inside appears to be lambs wool and is very soft. The opening is large enough to accommodate most any golf club. This product is well made and designed to protect even the most particular golfer's clubs, while adding some personality to their game.

title: See size chart in review
text:
Currently, the information shown does not give size charts. . but here is what I have found from the manufacturer:

Medium:
Head Size: 21” – 23.5”
Fitted Hat Size: 6.75” – 7&5/8”

Large:
Head Size: 23.5” – 26”
Fitted Hat Size: 7&5/8” – 9”

Yes, it’s very light. Made of “pleather” (synthetic leather). It feels durable. It’s Made in Pakistan, so at the current price, it’s a bit high. It laces on the back, for a better fit. Overall it offers fairly good protection.

title: For "Caddyshack" Movie Fans
text: The gopher is a product with a sense of humor. Yes, if you’re a fan of the movie “Caddyshack”, then this cover is for you.  His back, head, and face is made of a longer, straighter fur like material that does have some shedding. The back part is a silver color, but it has brown ears and paws. The chest and under his chin is very soft, plush material and is a cream color. It has a pouch on its belly that contains a golf ball. It has a 5" tail extending on the bottom extending from the opening. It has small round black eyes, brown nose, and two large bucky teeth. The eyes and nose are made of plastic, but the teeth are made of leather. The interior is lined with what looks to be lamb's wool.  This cover will protect your clubs and show some personality at the same time.

title: More of a pup. . . than an adult
text: The weimaraner is an exceptional product for anyone that wants to protect his or her clubs from the elements. Granted, I think the cover looks more like a pup than an adult dog, but perhaps that’s just me.  The outside is soft and could easily pass for a stuffed animal or child's puppet. The eyes on this headcover look real. This headcover is very plush, well made and for golfer that love dogs or especially Weimaraner’s this would be a great conversation piece as well as good protection for the clubs. It is a gray color with 6 inch ears. The eyes and nose are plastic. The inside is lined and cream color. This headcover has personality, function, and quality.

title: Shark Attack!
text: If you are looking for a conversation piece for the avid golfer, this is it! The shark golf club headcover is hilarious but extremely functional at the same time. Made in China (and a bit pricey). . .  The material is very soft  and has groves running all through it. There is no mistaken the very recognizable shark dorsal fin on his back as well as the two additional fins on the side of his body. The look is amazingly real.  The body of the shark is gray with the gills sown in on the sides and the eyes are some type of plastic that are aqua blue and black. They are eyes are quite nice.  He has a mouth with sharp teeth made out of a stiff felt. The mouth for the most part is not very noticeable. The underside is white and gets dirty pretty quickly. The inside is lined in a very soft thick material. The inside material is black in color and the opening measures about 6". This is a fun product with a mission. It is well made and will serve its purpose well.

title: Go Tigers!
text: The tiger headcover is an absolute hoot! The colors are bright and give any set of clubs the protection and personality you are looking for. The head, ears, and neck are orange with black stripes.  He has a white nose area and white bred. There is a black plastic nose with  yellow and black realistic looking eyes. The nose and eyes are well attached and no worries of them falling off. The fur is super soft and no doubt that it is a tiger. The material on the inside is very fuzzy like lambs wool. On the inside about 3/4 of the way up the neck, there is an elastic band used to secure the club. The interior color is cream and securely attached. The opening measures 6" across and accommodates most standard clubs. This product is well made and well designed.  I will say that for Made, in China, it is a bit expensive, but I still like it.

title: When you're looking for something different
text: The NINJA head covers are perfect for the quirky golfer with a sense of humor.  Kind of fun, yet albeit expensive for Made in China.  The outside has a lot of detail and is well made to endure multiple wear when taking them on and off of your golf clubs. The inside is very soft, plush, and well-constructed.  The cover fits nicely and protects from scrapes, scratches, and dings.  The material is high quality inside and out. This cover is fits snuggly, yet it is easy to remove when you are ready to use your club. This is a great cover for anyone that wants something out of the ordinary.

title: Pricey, but nice cover
text: The Zebra head cover is a unique way to give some personality to your golf clubs and give them the protection they need at the same time. The Zebra is so soft that it looks and feels like a child’s stuff animal. The outside is very well constructed with lots of details, such as the eyes and mane.  It may look like a child’s toy, but it built rugged for the outdoors. The inside is made with a thick lining that protects but also has a large opening that adapts to almost any club. It has a label on the inside that guarantees replacement for life that should something go wrong.  Well made, durable product. But at twenty-five bucks, it’s quite expensive for what it is.

title: Nice overall shields
text: These shin protectors are made of a durable plastic that fits nicely over the leg. The inside that is next to the skin has a layer of lining that gives a bit of cushioning as well as helps with comfort.  The shield can be adjusted due to a strap attached to the back of the shield. This is a very durable product, but the length is short.  If you have longer legs, that should be taken into consideration and get the next size up. These shin protectors are good quality for the price, comfort and fit.

title: Check-out the set as well
text:
This is the single towel offering by CaddyDaddy. They actually offer a set of two towels and divot, which is a little better value (see below).

This is a “microfiber “towel with a waffle weave. I’ve always found microfiber to be a bit “scratchy”, but I like the way they work. They wash well, and you really want to wash all microfiber separately. If you mix with cotton, for example, then the microfiber will pick-up all the loose cotton threads.

[[ASIN:B01KWT6MYQ CaddyDaddy Golf Microfiber Towel Set & Divot Tool]]

title: Nice towels
text:
This is a three-piece set of two towels and one divot tool. The towels are made of “waffle weaver” microfiber. Though I like how microfiber works, I’ve never really liked the feel of microfiber, which is still the case here. It has kind of a “scratchy” feel to me. Though I must say that I’m one of the few people I know who feel that way.

The towels are nice sizes with one being 16X24” and the other 12X12”. The same company offers the 16X24” towel by itself, but at the current price, it’s worth it to go with this set. . . though I think this set is a bit prices for what it is as well.

title: Ok for kids
text:
First of all, you’ll want to either have some sort of pad on your table. . . or. . . put something under the “feet” of this game. You certainly don’t want to put it right on top of a table, and scratch the table.

The quality is exactly what you would expect for Made in China plastic. It’s not great, but it’s “reasonable”. At the current price of thirty bucks, it should be better than “reasonable”. . .but again. . it’s what you get for Made in China. I will say that this tabletop game was easier to assemble than some of the other tabletop games offered by Franklin Sports, so that’s a plus. Overall, it’s fine for what it is.

title: Tabletop Foosball
text: For a “tabletop” version of foosball, this one is kind of what one would expect from such an item.  It’s okay for what it is.  Nothing is ever going to match a full-size version, but for a bedroom / dorm room, it’s fun to pull-out from under a bed and play.  Some assembly is required, and that’s usually not fun, and so it goes here.  But once you get it put together, it works fine.  At the current price of thirty bucks for Made in China plastic, it’s a bit expensive, but not crazy expensive.

title: Nice design / look / feel
text: These gloves are really comfortable.  Easy-on. . . . Easy-off.  Honestly, I’ve tried lots of different Franklin Sports items over the years, and lots of times the quality just isn’t there.  No so with these gloves.  They and feel like they are “above average” at least.  I also like the look / color / design.  Granted, they are a little pricey, but overall I’ve been quite pleased with them.  The “powerstrap” makes them easier to get off compared to others that I’ve used.

title: Nice "toy" stick
text:
I have the Boston Bruins version of this stick.

I think of this as more of a “toy” than a real hockey stick. It’s for street hockey, and mostly plastic. The graphics on it are nice. It comes in a variety of teams, and also right or left handed, which is nice. The current price isn’t too bad at twenty-five bucks. If you have kids who like to smack a puck or ball around outside, this stick will work fine.

title: Don't forget the sandpaper.
text:
This is a very inexpensive set of four paddles and six balls. It’s so inexpensive, that I think they forgot to sand the wood in China before shipping them out to the U.S. So you might want to also order some light sandpaper if you order this set. It’s nice to have the tote for the paddles and balls as well.

If you’re a regular player, of course this is certainly not the set for you. But if you are an occasional player. . .just want to have some extra paddles . .. that sort of thing, then these are decent for the price.

title: Probably not the paddle you want
text:
This is certainly a step above a basic wooden pickleball paddle . .but not by much. There are a few “issues” with this paddle.

First of all, it’s smaller than most pickleball paddles. I’m not sure why they didn’t make it “regulation size”.

Though it’s supposed to be aluminum, it’s only partially aluminum. There is a “honeycomb core”, and that makes this paddle a bit heavy.

If you’re really wanting to get into the sport, then this is certainly not the paddle you want. On the other hand, if you’re just wanting to give pickleball a try, then you could certainly start with this paddle.

title: Size Small should be Extra Small
text: I have always wanted an exercise top like this to wear around the house. I like this particular one as it is very flattering and keeps everything in place (if you know what I mean). The only thing that I am disappointed in is that it is a very small “size small.” It really should be an extra small. I have a hard time getting in and out of it. But, it is very good quality.

title: Three AAA Batteries Not Included
text: This is a tabletop game. . .  .designed around basketball.  Granted, it really has little to do with basketball, but it’s fun nonetheless.  Instead of simply throwing the balls through the baskets, you have to bounce them on the bottom first, and then they shoot up and (hopefully) go through a basket.  I think it works better to be a couple of feet away.  As with most Franklin Sports items, it’s Made in China and cheap.  You’ll have to use your on intuition as far as putting it together, as the instructions don’t help a lot.  Three AAA batteries are not included.  Still. . . in the end. . . it’s ok, for the price.

title: Stinger Bee is a Hit
text: This is a great (and fun) way to let kids go at it and get some of the pent-up energy out.  It’s very bright and colorful.  You place water in the bottom as an “anchor” to keep it from knocking over.  It’s Made in China, so it’s not the greatest quality in the world, but it looks like it will last, at least for the short term.  If you have an air pump, it will certainly help. . . Otherwise it will take some time to blow-up both the punching bag, as well as the gloves.

title: Standing punching bag is better option
text:
This is a very small item. The bag is only 12” high by 4.75” wide. The picture makes it look larger than it really is If you want to get more “bang” for your buck, you may wish to give the standing Stinger Bee Punching Bag a try. (see link below) It’s a lot larger, and the current price is the same.

Speaking of price, this is a crazy-expensive item at the current cost of twenty-five bucks for Made in China.

[[ASIN:B01DGD60WO Franklin Sports Stinger Bee Punching Bag & Gloves]]

title: Nice overall slackline package
text: There are lots of different slacklines offered.  This one is on the lower end of the current price range, but offers everything others do, including training line, and tree protectors.  I actually like the ratchets on this line a little better than some others that I’ve tried.  The overall quality is fine.  Great for kids. . . adults. . . There are several online videos of how to set-up a slackline correctly.  If you’re new to this, then I highly recommend you watch to make sure you’re setting it up correctly and safely.

title: Single set of oversized gloves
text:
Franklin Sports makes a few assorted boxing items in the “Stinger Bee” collection. These are the oversized boxing gloves. You simply inflate them and start walloping!

I actually prefer a couple of other “Stinger Bee” sets, which include not only the gloves, but a bag to punch as well. But this set of gloves can come in handy if you already have one of the other sets, as the other sets come with only one pair of gloves.

[[ASIN:B01DGD60WO Franklin Sports Stinger Bee Punching Bag & Gloves]]

[[ASIN:B01DGD611Y Franklin Sports Stinger Bee Youth Punching Bag & Glove Set]]

title: Works on my heels.
text: I apply this to my heels when I plan on doing a lot of walking.  So far, I think it’s helping.  Depending upon how much walking I’m doing, I may have to reapply, but I don’t mind as long as it helps. The fragrance is neither strong nor bad.  Fairly mild.  It’s a bit expensive, but you don’t have to use very much, so. . . at least for me and my feet. . . it will last a good long time.

title: Five Pound Weight
text: I have the five-pound weight, which is bright orange.  This weight is covered in neoprene.  It has a slight rough and “tacky” texture to it.  There are some bumps / lines / discoloration to the neoprene, but it doesn’t really cause any problems with using the weight.  I wish they were told in pairs.  Personally, I prefer kettlebells to this sort of weight, but it can all depend how you’re using it.  FYI, this particular weight was a little than an ounce below the actual weight.

title: Kids Only Playset
text: This is a “kids-only” multi-game tabletop item.  It’s only 18.5 X 10.5”.  So bit “adult hands” don’t work with this.  But for kids, it’s lots of fun.  All of the games are simple.  It’s not high-quality, but at the current price of thirty bucks, you don’t really expect that either.  One side is soccer. . . the other is pool.  You place inserts on the pool side for the three other games.  It’s nice to have different games to play without having to purchase different sets.

title: Size 4 - Can't beat the price
text: This ball comes in three sizes.  I have the size “4” which is super-cheap right now at under five bucks as an “add-on” item.  You really can’t beat the price for such a ball.  It’s really a “nothing fancy” ball, but again. . . for the price. . that’s fine.  Just make sure you purchase the right size for your child.  A size “4” is for ages 8 – 12-years.  So far, this ball has held air without a problem.  It comes inflated.

title: Nice "leisure" ball
text: This is a nice looking size 5 (adult) soccer ball.  It comes inflated. It has a good feel / bounce to it.  This is a “leisure” ball which does not have any “official approval”.  (FIFA / NCAA)  But it’s a fraction of the cost of a high-end ball.  So overall it’s fine for what it is.  After a few days of kicking it around, I haven’t had any issues with air loss.  Overall a decent ball.

title: Worth the money
text: This is a fairly easy device to set-up.  Though it will work on both a phone and iPad, I like the iPad better.  Perhaps, just because it’s easier to see.  But of course a phone can be more convenient.  There is a ton of information which can be captured.  It’s nice that the sensor stores actions even when your phone/iPad is out-of-Bluetooth range.  The in-app training videos are helpful.  You’ll certainly improve your game if you’re willing to put in the time to use the app and analyze the information.  Well worth the cost.

title: Great bands
text: The AmazonBasics resistance bands are very well made.  It is to tie onto a bar for workouts.  The size of the band makes it easy to slip your foot into it to assist you in doing pull-ups. The size of the band is also good for stretching exercises.  After using the resistance band, you can easily curl it back up, secure it with the strap that came with it, and store it.  You’ll probably want all of them, to change-up your workouts.

title: A Baseball. . . Kickball???
text:
This is kind of “funny” to begin with. . . .A kickball with MLB Baseball markings. Not sure why Franklin Sports thought that was a good idea. You’re certainly paying extra for the MLB logo. . . a LOT extra. This “set” is Made in China, and couldn’t have cost more than a few bucks to produce.

The “bases” really are a joke. They are VERY thin, rolled-up foam. I think you might even be better using paper plates for bases.

The ball itself is nice enough though. But if you’re just looking for a kickball, there are much less expensive options out there, and just as good as this one.

title: A little "smelly" when you first take it out of the package
text: The KhelaSport Armband package is very simple.  When you first pull the armband out of the package there is a strong smell.  This smell diminishes after it has been out of the package for a while.  The armband seems to be very durable.  There are no instructions, but it is pretty self-explanatory.  My iPhone was easy to insert and to attach my headphones.  It was easy to operate my phone through the plastic cover.  It has a place to insert your key, but no place for a debit/credit card (even though a picture of a credit card is on the back of the package).  You would have to put your card in the in the area where you place your phone.  The armband was easy to put on and felt good...not too heavy.  It stayed in place during by walk/run.

title: Great for "loaner" or beginners
text: This is a nice paddle and ball set. The paddles are aesthetically appealing. It has a plastic border around the paddles that would protect them from floor hits. The grip has a good feel to them. The action of the ball coming of the paddle is about what you'd expect from any wooden paddle. The balls are of good quality. They are decent paddles. I'll use them mostly as a loaner when playing with those who are new to the game and want to give it a try.

title: Nice Junior Ball
text: Though it states it at the top of the listing. . I just like to repeat the fact that this is a “Junior” (smaller) ball, and not full-size.  For the most part, it’s for smaller kids, just starting to enjoy the sport of Basketball.  On the box it shows from ages 5 – 7.  Otherwise, it’s just like a full-size basketball.  So far, it’s holding air well.  I like the red. .  white. . . and blue color combination.  Franklin Sports makes more “flashy” balls, like with a Batman logo, but I really prefer these “real” basketballs.

title: A bit like compression socks
text: First of all, make sure you look at the sizing chart.  These are a bit like compression socks, but not quite as tight as some compression socks that I have.  They make it easier to put on your boots or wetsuit because they are kind of slick.  They also help keep your legs / feet warm, though I haven’t found them to be too hot.  They are hand-wash only.  I have a front-load washer, and run them through a quick “speed wash” which takes only 15-minutes from start-to-finish, and that works.  I hang them to dry.  They are Made in the USA, which I really like, but I think that the current price of thirty-three bucks is a bit high.  Nonetheless, I like them.

title: Good value for an inexpensive paddle
text: This paddle is aesthetically appealing. Of course, that's not the main thing to look for in a paddle. It has a plastic border around the paddle that would protect it from floor hits. I don't care much for the feel of the grip, as it's a little short for my medium sized hand. For smaller hands, I'm sure it's fine. The action of the ball coming of the paddle is about what you'd expect from any wooden paddle. Really, for the current price of ten bucks, how could you go wrong. It's a decent paddle. I'll use it mostly as a loaner, opting for a more expensive paddle for regular use.

title: Check the Viper as well
text:
This is a very nice looking and feeling paddle. The grip is slightly larger in length than the Viper, which is a carbon paddle. It has a smooth surface, as opposed to the Viper's textured surface. I prefer the textured surface, which would enable you to impart good spin on the ball. I'm not really sure what the advantage of the smoother surface would be. The construction appears to be very good quality. The ball has a good feel coming off paddle, though noticeably different from the Viper. The aluminum Python has, to me, a softer feel of the ball, whereas with the carbon Viper, the ball seems to have more "pop" and speed coming off the paddle. Based on overall cost of Pickleball paddles, I believe the Python is very good quality and value.

[[ASIN:B01HCV0ANQ Franklin Sports Carbon Fiber Viper Pickleball Paddle]]

title: Nice overall paddle
text: This is a very nice looking and feeling paddle. The grip is a perfect size for my medium-large hand. It has a textured face that enables you to impart good spin on the ball. The construction appears to be very good quality. The ball has a good feel coming off the paddle and I believe its construction is such as to give it good versatility of use for both power and finesse shots. Based on overall cost of Pickleball paddles, I believe the Viper is very good quality and value.

title: Better than many
text: This is a nice, overall, goalie stick for street hockey.  It’s not the least expensive on the market, but it’s not the most expensive either.  For the price, it’s not bad.  It’s ambidextrous, so can be used by left-handed or right-handed players.  From the looks / feel of it, I think it’s going to last longer than some sticks that I’ve had.  I wish the blade were black, but that’s really a personal preference.  Overall I like it.

title: Affordable Set
text: Franklin Sports makes several different sets like this. . . . in different sizes, colors, some sticks only. . . some goal only.  This set includes all three main components required to play.  . .. two sticks. . . goal . . . and ball.  The goal is 36” wide by 24” deep by 24” high.  This is not a “fancy” or “high-end” set.  It’s a simple, beginner set for young kids.  At the current price of twenty-eight bucks, I think it’s affordable and a nice overall set.

title: 55# - "Real" Goal
text:
When you see that the shipping weight is over fifty-five pounds. . . You know this is no flimsy hockey goal. It’s the “real deal”. At the current price of over two-hundred twenty-five dollars. . . it’s also not cheap. It’s Made in China.

Of course assembly is required. It will take you an afternoon, believe it or not. Currently Amazon is offering assembly, at least in my area, but it’s just over a hundred bucks. So not really worth it to me.

title: Needs stakes and/or weight
text:
This large 7’ X 7’ sports training net system is actually better than I expected it to be (knowing Franklin Sports products) but there are a few “issues” with it.

First of all, there are no stakes included to anchor it to the ground. You’ll have to purchase those separately. If you’re using it on a driveway, or other such surface, you’re going to need sandbags (or something else like bags of mulch / dirt) to put on the back bottom to keep it stable and keep it from tipping over.

It’s Made in China, so at the current price of a hundred bucks, it’s expensive. . .But other such nets are not that far off.

title: Really Nice Gloves
text:
The gloves that I have are a size “Large”. The following is the sizing chart from the manufacturer. Measure around your four fingers (excluding thumb) at the base of your fingers.

Small / Youth: 6” – 7.5”
Regular: 7.25” – 8.75”
Large: 8.5” – 9.75”
XL: 9.5” – 10.5”

These are great workout boxing gloves. They are really comfortable and fit perfectly. Great padded protection. The stitching is all very good. On top of everything else, they are also affordably priced. Overall I really like them.

title: "Junior" Football
text:
The football that I have is the “Junior” model.

This football came inflated just right. The ball measures 25.5” around lengthwise by 18.5” around in the center. Though some players still prefer leather, it’s more slick so the texture of composite balls are sometimes preferred. This one has a good feel to it. The stitching is fine. The lacing also looks top-notch.

Currently the price of this football is just over thirty-eight bucks. A comparable Wilson GST is under twenty-five bucks. For the difference, I would go with Wilson. But it can be a personal preference as well.

title: Blue/White - 5
text: The ball that I have is the White / Blue size 5.  Size 5 is the “regular” / “adult” size soccer ball.  It also comes in a size 4.  Note that this ball comes deflated.  You’ll need to make sure you have a pump / needle.  It has the look / feel of a really nice ball.  I don’t see any flaws (so far) in the manufacturing.  Of course it has a cool look to it as well.

title: Batman!
text: This Batman size 3 soccer ball also comes in a Superman version.  It comes inflated, but it also includes a inexpensive little pump, which is kind of a nice addition.  A size 3 ball shows to be for kids under the age of 8. . . but. . . of course anyone can play with it.  A size 3 is between 23 and 24”.  This ball has a nice feel to it.  It’s Made in China and at the current price of twenty bucks, it is a little expensive, but not crazy expensive.

title: Basic Jr. Bag
text: This bag shows that it’s for baseball / softball, but it can really be used for just about anything.  Note that it’s not very large at 34” X 9” X 6”.  It’s made so bat handles stick out the end.  It shows that it stores up to three bats.  It will also hold more items like balls, glove, cleats, etc.  It has both handles on the top, and an over-the-shoulder strap.  It’s your basic canvas sort of bag.  It’s Made in China.  Overall it’s a decent bag.

title: Not as pictured. . . but what I was expecting
text: Franklin Sports makes a variety of these over-the-door basketball net sets.  This one is a bit “odd” because it looks a bit different from what it shows on the picture.  The ball is actually orange.  The backboard is a little more “glitzy” now. It’s not inflated very well, but you can use your own needle / pump to inflate it a little more, if you like.  The ball does not glow.  Overall, this is just a very cheap (albeit not that inexpensive) Made in China set.  For what it is. .. there is nothing all that great about it. . . or. . . horrible about it.  I was expecting exactly what I got.

title: Band only - Purchase the system separately
text:
Make sure you understand that this listing is for an additional band only for the SwimSafe system. You have to purchase the system separately. There are currently different listings for the system. Each listing includes a different number of bands, so you’ll want to check all of them out. But if you need additional bands, then that’s what this listing is for.

The front of the band is actually black. There are three colored covers included. Pink. .. Blue. . . Orange.

Around the inside of the band is about fourteen inches. An “extender” is included which will add about four additional inches or a total of eighteen. So it can be used not only on smaller kids, but older kids, and possibly some adults.

title: A system that will surely save lives.
text:
Let me first say. . . This is one incredible system. It really works. It’s very easy to set-up. There are four levels so depending upon if your child can swim a little. . a lot. . . or not at all. . . it will alert. There are other pool alarms on the market which will tell you when the pool has been disturbed, but this system goes far beyond that letting you know about each swimmer.

Note that the band is about 14 inches around on the inside. But there is an included “extender” which will make it about 18 inches. So it’s good with not only small kids, but older kids as well. .. and possibly some adults.

I do have one “issue”. . . and that’s the cost. This is the one-band listing. Extra bands cost about one hundred fifty bucks. But if you look, you will see that currently there is a listing for a two-band set, which is even less expensive than the one-band set. . . and you get two bands. There’s also a four-band set, which can save you some money if you need that many bands. I’m just saying to check all the listings before purchasing. You’ll want bands not only for your own kids, but any visiting kids as well. I really think this system is going to save a lot of lives. You just have to make sure you use it each time you’re around water. It won’t work. . if you don’t use it.

title: Don't Forget the Helmet
text: Though it should be obvious.  .. I think it’s important to note that this bike does not have peddles / chain. It’s a “balance bike”, so the only power it has is by pushing with your feet on the ground.  It’s for learning how to ride a bike.  It’s questionable as to whether this is the better way to go, or just go ahead and get a “real” bike.  If you’re going with a “balance bike”, this is a very nice one.  Note that it is quite small though.  31.5 x 17.3 x 18.5”.  It’s quite lightweight.  Small and easy to carry, or place in the trunk of a car.  Don’t forget the helmet, which is not included.

title: Check-out the plastic version as well
text:
Franklin makes a couple of different versions of this mini goal. This is the “steel tubing” version. But they also make one with plastic tubing. . . . but with the plastic one, you receive two goals. . . 4 player sticks and 2 foam mini balls. . . all for less than the cost of this single goal. Granted, this listing is for the steal version, so that’s certainly a plus. . . but if you don’t mind plastic, then have a look as well.

[[ASIN:B00NF9NVMM Franklin Sports NHL Mini Hockey Goal Set of 2]]

title: PVC Net
text: This is a simple, PVC tubing net.  It’s quite lightweight.  You’ll want to check to make sure that all of the pieces are inside as soon as you receive it.  My box had some “wear-and-tear” from the delivery company, and bits were falling out, but it was all there.  It’s easy enough to put together.  It does not fold, but it’s also easy enough to take apart for storage as well.  At the current price of almost fifty bucks, it’s kind of expensive for plastic Made in China, but overall, it’s not a bad net.

title: One of a few
text: Franklin Sports makes at least a few of these.  They are all the same, it’s just the design that is different.  This one is “Batman”.  Overall it’s a nice face mask.  The one thing that I don’t care for is the chin strap.  Not really the strap itself, but the “cup” your chin fits in.  It’s very “flimsy”.  Kind of odd as the rest of the helmet / mask is quite sturdy.  The graphics are nice as well.  Granted, for Made in China, and at the current price of eighty bucks, it’s quite expensive.

title: Check-out the "knock-out" targets as well
text:
This is a set of four targets only. The net is not included. These are fine, though I think they are quite expensive at the current price of twenty-two bucks. But they should last. FYI. . . Franklin Sports also offers “knock-out” targets. With the knock-out targets, you’ll know if you hit the target or not. . . but. . you have to replace them once you hit them, so there’s both plus / minus to those. But I like them both.

[[ASIN:B013LPVAJK Franklin Sports NHL "Knock Out" Shooting Targets]]

title: Data. . . Data. . . and more Data
text: The main part of this system is the wristband, which is included, and the sensor which fits into it.  You really need to make sure that the sensor is fully-charged before you begin play.  Then you download the app and all the data is analyzed and from there you will be able to compete with the best at the world.  You should go ahead and start planning your trip to Wimbledon. Ok, so the last part is not really true, but it does give you all of the data to let you know where you stand, so that you can make improvements.  I’m not a huge fan of the feel of the wristband, but I’m getting used to it.  This same company makes the “Pop” sensor, which is currently about half the price of this one.  Honestly, I’m not exactly sure of the differences, other than this being the “newer” model.  I also believe that this one gives more data overall.

title: So much more padding than most.
text: This bleacher seat has a lot more padding that most.  Of course it has quick-and-easy set-up.  Because of the padding, this seat is a little more “bulky” than some, but in the end, the comfort is worth the extra “bulkiness”.  It can certainly be used at other times, other than bleachers on game day, as well.  It’s Made in China.  At the current price of forty bucks, it’s not cheap, but it’s not crazy expensive either.  Overall I really like it.

title: Know for sure if you're hitting the target
text: Note that this listing is for the four knock-out targets only.  The goal / net is not included.  These targets are to help with accuracy, especially around the corners.  Because they are “knock-out”, you know for sure if you’re hitting the target or not.  Granted, either you. . . or someone else. . . will have to constantly reset the targets.  For that reason, it’s better to have at least one other person.  Overall they are make just fine.  At the current price of twenty bucks, the cost is a bit high for Made in China, but not bad.  Worth it overall.

title: Check-out the full-set version as well.
text: This is the single-club version.  Arccos also makes a “full-set” version which will give you a lot more information.  If you like to keep-up with your stats when you drive. . . . or. . . if you just like gadgets. . . then this can be a nice little addition.  But it’s not always 100% accurate, though you are able to edit.  More often than not, it’s “good enough”.  You will want to make sure you have a fully-charged battery when you start.  .or battery back-up.  Overall it works fine. . . but again, if what you’re looking for are ALL of your stats, then you really need the “full-set” version.

title: Basic straps at a nice price
text: Reebok, which is owned by Adidas, offers these nice lifting straps at currently a nice price of just over seven bucks.  They are made reasonably well. . .. .  Have a slight bit of padding. . . Just a touch of stretch. .  . .and overall work quite well.  There is nothing super special about them, but they do the job and look nice too.  I could do without the logo, but that’s really not a big deal.

title: More of a stand
text: If you’re looking for a stand for your ball.. . . . Then this might work, but there are other.  . .  less expensive. . . options for a ball holder.  Your ball will certainly roll right of the ring with ease.  So it all depends upon what sort of exercise you’re doing as to whether this ring is going to help you or not.  If you’re sitting in place, and using mostly your upper body, then it certainly can work.

title: Not worth the money
text: Though it shows that this net is “multi-sport”. . . it’s really not.  It’s not even that great for golf.  It’s easy to set-up.  But overall this is a very “cheap” (not meaning inexpensive) net.  You really need to be using foam balls if you’re going to use this net.  Otherwise, there is a good chance that the ball will go right through the net.  Currently it’s over fifty bucks, for something really cheap Made in China.  Five bucks would be more like it.

title: I like the small size
text: This is a rather small (1’ X 2”) practice mat.  That’s nice, because you can take it anywhere.  I’m not sure how long this mat is going to last.  It doesn’t look to be that well made.  For the occasional user, this might work without a problem. . . . but if you’re going to be using it frequently, you might want to check other options.  But I like the fact that it’s small and I can take it with me easily.

title: Just unroll. . . and you're done!
text: The glow-in-the-dark aspect of this is not a big deal to me.  I’m not playing ball at night anyway.  But as far as a five-piece base set, it’s fine.  It’s not-so-thick plastic which can be unrolled and set-up quick-and-easy.  You can take it virtually anywhere.  You can, of course, use it for playing any sort of ball where you use bases.  I will say that the current price of thirty bucks is a bit high, but Franklin (and others) make slightly less expensive sets, which are not glow-in-the-dark.

title: Simple ball game for two
text: This is a bit like Jai alai .  .. but two are supposed to play and toss the ball back-and-forth.  If you don’t catch the ball, then it’s easy enough to scoop it up from the ground.  Personally I prefer tossing a baseball back-and-forth.  . .but.. . this is a lot less expensive than buying gloves (if you don’t already have them).  Franklin Sports makes a plethora of these sorts of simple, two-man games.  Though it’s Made in China, and could be a bit less expensive than the current nine bucks, it’s not crazy expensive.  Nice to have if you’re going to the park. . or camping. . . or just in the back yard.

title: Might want to add wheels.
text: This is a “premium” lacrosse rebounder, as compared to some other less-expensive models.  At 63#, it’s quite heavy.  Though it does fold, the one thing I think it’s missing are wheels.  I really wish they had added wheels to the back, so you could roll it around.  That’s probably something I’m going to add on my own.  The construction is decent.  I like that it’s all steel.  Though this is for lacrosse, it’s possible that you could use it under a basketball goal for rebounding as well.  Though I like it, I think it’s quite overpriced for Made in China at the current price of over two-hundred thirty bucks.  But it is a solid piece of equipment.

title: Fun Costume
text: This is certainly a “costume” and not something you would want to use for “real” football play.  The “jersey” and “pant” is very thin.  But they are great for “dress-up” to watch football on TV. . .  .or go to out on Halloween. . . . and things like that.  The current prices of no more than twelve bucks are also reasonable.  The “list price” of fifty bucks reaches the level of “crazy expensive” and would certainly not be worth that.

title: Need sizing information
text: These certainly take time and effort to get on.  I’m assuming / in hopes that it will get easier with time.  Once they are on, they feel ok.  I think they will be better for Winter.  They have a nice look to them.  They also washed without a problem.  The cost is a bit high, and it’s kind of crazy that currently the size large is thirty bucks higher than the small.  I wish they would list something so that you know which size was correct.

title: Nice but pricey
text: These are nice compression sleeves.  They actually go right above the knee, unlike others which go below the knee.  Believe it or not, I actually use these on long flights.  I like the overall look and feel of them.  At forty bucks, I think they are a bit overpriced.  Nonetheless, I like them.  They are great not only for running but biking and any and all sorts of exercise.  I’ve also washed them without a problem.

title: Not "deluxe".  ..but ok
text: Honestly, these pickleballs were the very first I've used. I got a pair of inexpensive wooden paddles and took these outdoor balls out on my driveway and hit them against my brick wall. They worked very well and were very lively. I had done some investigation online about the differences between outdoor and indoor balls. One of the differences were that the indoor balls are more "predictable" and allow for longer volleys. I would say that is exactly true. These outdoor balls, compared to indoor balls came back at me much faster and I spent more time chasing them. I will say that after about 15 minutes of use, the balls cracked at the seam. However, as I said, I was using them against a brick wall. I will most likely try to purchase some foam balls for that kind of extreme use. As for the quality of what they are purported to be.  I will say that they are quite expensive for three plastic balls Made in China.

title: A bit pricey, but a nice ball
text: This ball looks shiny / glossy in the picture, but it’s actually matte / dull.  It still looks nice though.  It’s about half the size of a “regular” basketball.  It has the same look / feel.  It’s Made in China, so at the current price of almost fifteen bucks, it’s kind of expensive for what it is.  . but.. . . it’s still a nice ball, and for lovers of Batman, it would make a nice gift.

title: Quite sturdy
text: I thought the rackets were going to be plastic. . . but. . . they are not. I believe they are metal.  The handles are also quite sturdy.  For the price, the rackets are quite nice overall.  I wish they were a little more like badminton racquets, meaning longer.  But these are fine just to play around with.  There’s no net included, so you’ll just have to make your own, or not use a net.  The rubber ball on the end of the shuttlecocks is actually a bit hard/heavy.  That means they will go further, but are a little more “dangerous”.  Franklin Sports makes a lot of these inexpensive two-man sort of games.  Great for family gatherings.. .  play dates. . . etc.

title: Simple fun
text: Franklin Sports makes a lot of this type of inexpensive two-man sort of games.  This one uses round discs, which to your hand on the back with Velcro.  The front is also Velcro, which causes the ball to stick to it.  You simply toss the ball back-and-forth.  Of course you can make-up your own game. . . . who can toss it the highest and so on.  It’s a very simple sort of thing good for both kids and adults.  This is one of those Made in China items which is currently priced about right.

title: You're going to need (at least) two sets
text: First of all, unless you going to only use one glove, you really need to have two pairs for two to “box”.  These are very “flimsy”.  They are Made in China and probably didn’t cost more than a buck or two to make.  At the current cost of over thirteen bucks..  ..  and you’ll probably need at least two sets. . . then it’s not a good buy.  I would recommend spending that money on something which is going to last longer.

title: Pricey wrist wraps
text: These are rather small wrist wraps.  They are your typical style with thumb loop.  They are made decent, but not great.  They are Made in Pakistan, and at the current price of twenty-five bucks, you’re really paying a lot for the Adidas name.  There are certainly other better.  . longer. .. .  .less expensive. . . wrist wraps out there.  But if you want to advertise for Adidas, then these are okay. . . just not great.

title: Nice gloves
text: These gloves are fairly comfortable.  They offer an easy Velcro strap for on/off.  They look nice enough.  Though there are some “holes” for “breathability”. . . my hands still sweat in them, but that’s really going to happen with any such gloves.  They are Made in Pakistan, so they are a bit expensive, though not too excessive.

title: With they had leather palms
text: These fitness gloves are ok. . . but. . . . I the palms are not leather-lined, like  some of the Reebok gloves.  Reebok is owned by Adidas, but they offer different products.  If you don’t need the leather palms, then these work.  There is some extra padding on the palm though.  They are “reasonably” made, though not great.  I like the fact that there is a center ring which makes it easier to pull them off.  The ring is not shown on the picture.

title: Okay. . . but not great
text: These are nice cotton with neoprene padding lifting straps. . . but. . I think they are charging quite a bit “extra” for the Adidas name.  A bit pricey, if you ask me.  Unless you’re just wanting the Adidas name, less expensive options abound.  If you don’t mind paying the price, then there are some better straps out there.  These just seam a bit on the “cheap side”.  The construction isn’t great.  Nonetheless, they will work for the short-term.

title: Other designs are available.
text: These are reasonably nice “breathable” training gloves.  If you’re not a huge fan of the camo print, they come in other designs as well.  Though you can’t see it in the picture there is a ring-pull on the center to make them easier to remove.  They are also leather padded on the palm.  Note the size chart.  I find the sizes run pretty true.  FYI in one place you will see them listed at Reebok and another Adidas. ..  .but Adidas owns Reebok, so I guess that’s why.

title: Nice leather belt
text: This is a strong, fairly well made leather belt.  It has a 4” width, which is “standard”.  Though you cant really see it from the picture, it has a double-pronged buckle.  I’m not a huge fan of the Adidas logo being stitched on it.  I would have preferred it to be embossed (if at all) but it’s really not a big deal.  It certainly doesn’t affect the comfort level at all.  Overall it’s a nice belt.

title: Check the strap type as well
text:
I’m not sure if these come in different colors or not. The ones that I received are neon green, and not yellow, as in the pictures on the listing. These guards have a nice amount of firm cushioning on the back. The compression sleeves are fine and are also machine washable.

If you prefer the strap type guard, Franklin also offers them and they may be less expensive, all depending upon the size you need and the current price. See the listing below.

[[ASIN:B005LFXQKK Franklin Sports Superlight Shin Guards (Medium, Assorted Colors)]]

title: More "heavy-duty" than some.
text: This bag is Made in China.  The listing shows that it’s made of “PE”, which means Polyethylene, . . . or in other words. . . plastic.  It’s “rough”, but I think / hope that’s going to help keep it from ripping.  So far, it’s holding-up just fine.  I know it shows that you can also use this as a laundry bag, but personally, I don’t think I would do that, due to the roughness of the bag.  But for sports equipment, it’s fine.  Though this is a decent bag, I think it’s crazy expensive for ten bucks.  I could not have cost more than a few cents to make in China.

title: Fun tabletop games
text: Franklin sports makes a variety of these “tabletop” sports games.  At the current “add-on” price, they are quite affordable.  Though I don’t think I would pay full-price for them.  They are certainly more fun that making a paper football, for example, but this takes it to the next level. But a “paper football” can go with you anywhere. . . and through you certainly can put these back in their box, and travel with them, it’s certainly not as easy as with a paper football.  Nonetheless, at the current add-on price they are worth having.

title: It's a "pass" on this one
text: Franklin Sports has not done a good job with this one.  This overpriced, tiny Made in China helmet is a miniature with just a couple of stickers.  It’s really nothing more than that.  I’m just baffled as to why the current price is thirty bucks.  I guess the NHL is getting the major part of the money.  If you want a real souvenir, I would say you’re better off picking-up something at a game from your favorite team.  This one is a “miss” for me.

title: Crazy Expensive, but a nice bag
text:
As bags of this type go, this is a nice one. The colors are very bright. The craftsmanship is very “reasonable”. FYI, the zipper pocket on the front goes all the way down the front, so you can fit quite a bit of “stuff” inside. The mesh on both sides allows air to flow. Though this is a boxing glove bag, it could also be used for other things.

Overall I like it. . . The only thing I don’t really care for is the current price of almost nineteen bucks. I’m not sure where it’s made, but I would assume China. It’s listed neither on Amazon nor the bag itself. If it were made in the USA, then I’m 100% sure it would show that in large letters all over. As that’s not the case, I can only assume It’s Made in China. That being the case, if it were at a third the current price, then it would be “reasonable”. But for nineteen bucks, it’s crazy expensive. Nonetheless, overall it’s a decent bag and if not for the price, I would give it five stars.

title: Check other options
text: At the current price, this is a crazy expensive Made in China item. .  .. especially because the poles are not included.  I “get” what the item is trying to accomplish, Franklin Sports (and others) offer the exact same thing for a fraction of the current price of this one.  You’re simply paying for the Tuukka name.  This is also quite thin material.  I can’t see it lasting all that long.  Unless you simply want it for the Tuukka name, you might want to check other options.

title: Cheap. .. but not inexpensive. .  .
text: The JEF World of Golf Universal Club Brush is a very nice feeling brush to handle. It's got metal bristles on one side that definitely do a good job of cleaning irons. There are plastic bristles on the other side that work well on the woods. The retractable pointed groove cleaner is a very nice feature. While I really like that it has a retractable attaching cord, I'm a little suspect of the quality of the retraction reel and the clasp device to attach to the bag. Both seem a little flimsy. For that reason, I'm giving this brush a three-star rating. Since the clasp is literally a part of the reel, if it breaks, the reel is rendered useless. The plastic piece attaching the reel to the brush isn't much better.  Because it's Made in China.. . . it could also be more affordable than the current price.

title: Not really better than a manual brush
text: The Groove Caddy motorized club cleaner comes with a USB charger and a detachable USB charged cord of adequate length. I plugged the device into a wall outlet and the red "Charging" indicator light came on. I'm not exactly sure how long it took to charge, since I left it charging overnight. The light was green, indicating charging complete when I got up the next morning. I took the device with me to the driving range and it seemed to work pretty well. I wouldn't say it worked great on my irons with very impacted grass and dirt, however I do think it would work fine with clubs that start out clean and the device is used "hole-to-hole". It recommended applying water to club face for optimum performance, and I'd definitely say that's the case.

title: Nice. . . for the price. . .
text: The Pinemeadow PGX 500 driver comes with a very nice head cover. The club itself has a nicely visible green alignment dot on top of the head. I found the grip to be comfortable and secure in my hands. While I was not able to drive balls as far with this club as another club in my bag, it did a good job. I would consider myself an intermediate golfer at best. Over the years, when hitting a graphite shaft, I was always told to slow my swing down. I definitely hit the ball more accurately when I slowed my swing down. My understanding is that this club has a "mid-stiffness" shaft.
