title: Very good, felt the burn, 4 of us tried, 4 of us liked
text:
UPDATE: It's been a few weeks back in the water and my wife and I love these dumbbells. Seeing results. I put them through a solid workout - 3 sets of about 4-5 different movements at 15 reps. And I am HARD on them. You can get good, solid feel moving slowly, but I go fast and hard for a much heavier resistance to get my arms back up and they can take it! VERY HAPPY!

This Sportneer Water Weights Aquatic Exercise Dumbbells set is excellent. My wife and I love our time in the water, but one wants something more than swimming laps. And we've found the low impact of water workouts lets us do more of a workout each week, but with less strain - meaning we do other things like weights and cardio, but we also do time in the pool, giving us move overall workout time, but with lower impact. So, does that mean we also then get a solid burn? Yes.

I love power walking in the water and working my legs that way. She does more laps (ear issues keep me from joining her). So I wanted something that gave me an upper body workout. Late last year I got another set of dumbbells that are great. However, these are now (for both of us) our favorites. Why?

This Sportneer Water Weights Aquatic Exercise Dumbbell set is a bit larger and gives us slightly more resistance because of it than the older pair we have. It is also slightly heavier and in turn, more resistance. We've talked about how these things look like a joke (water dumbbells), but in reality give a good, solid workout, just without the stresses that can sometimes come when you don't have the buoyancy of water. So not only great for rehab (which I used last year following surgery), but also in weekly workouts - again we feel we can get more workout time, with great results, and less stress on areas of the body giving us more overall workouts and outcomes during a week.

Taking this set into the pool, another, older couple was there (he's also recovered from past surgery, she's a PA) and asked about it. I let them try these Sportneer Water Weights Aquatic Exercise Dumbbells and they loved them. Said they could do things they cannot out of the water and have thought about them in the past, now think they'd get a set (though they did not ask the brand).

The set comes UNASSEMBLED, but no big deal. It's very intuitive and easy to put together. I opened it and put them together after scanning the instructions, the only part of which I caught "to make sure of," being a "pop" when you put the end pieces on. The set includes 2 extra end pieces in case you loose on. The connection is strong and tight. These are a good weight out of the water, meaning for us they are substantial and made with good materials. In the water they have a great buoyancy, so you are working to get them under the water, while they are under, and yes, you'll feel the burn. This set also has handles with straps to go around, but not lock in, the hands. I am not 100% sure it keeps them from coming off and floating away if you lost your grip - I tried and they did sort of stay in place - but I feel like I prefer the straps on these to not having them on the others. We had them out of the water, on the edge, for about 20 minutes before we left the pool and they were mostly dry. Like most areas of the country this summer, we are extremely hot and humid, so while they did not fully dry, it was enough to let them go back to where we keep them in the house - meaning they were not dripping nor made a puddle.

A set of exercises are suggested on an included sheet, which I tried to remember them while out there, but also found myself making stuff up - some of it fun and some to get the workout "look," but all of them made me work and feel it. In the end my wife and I both love these Sportneer Water Weights Aquatic Exercise Dumbbells and will use them often. We can use both sets together, or I think we'd both pick this set over the other when alone, just because of the increased sized and connected increased effort. Very happy with these Sportneer Water Weights Aquatic Exercise Dumbbells.

title: Not pros, but we think these are going to work for us
text:
My wife and I are not professional weight lifters and do our own stuff at home. We like to have a variety of ways to workout and we've talked about a farmer's carry before. I had the chance to grab these Synergee Farmer Walk Straps and we decided to give it a shot. For us - total amateurs - this seems like a good set up. We did a little research and know there are those who swear by things that are more bar-like, but for us at this point, these have what we need and are good for us.

The Synergee Farmer Walk Straps have a rubber handle with a decent grip to it. I've carried them with and without my workout gloves and it was fine. The materials seem to be solid and strong, well constructed, and that they'll give us longevity. I can't remember the weight limits, but we're well within I'm sure. The biggest thing for us will be getting the straps attached and lockdown well enough. You run the strap through the hole(s) on the weight you are using - we are starting with 1 X 25lbs each. Then lock it off in the buckle and wrap the rest around itself and out of the way. It's not as easy as it seemed it would be - we need practice - but it was by no means dangerous and did keep the strap out of the way and the weight secure. We'll get better. Then carrying the weight was fine - easy. We are slightly different heights, but we both felt comfortable with our first try length on the strap. That said, the one thing that IS a CON: deciding HOW LONG the strap and weight placement should be without testing and retesting. We ended up guessing and it seemed fine, nothing was hurt and hit when carrying, but it was not the easiest nor most efficient way of going about it. But it's no big deal at this point. If we get to a larger load point that exceeds that we think the straps can do - say more than 2 X 25 lbs weights that would then be swinging next to our leg, we'll maybe go for something else. We're open to seeing how this plays out. ** The last photo is me holding up the strap and handle to show the length of the strap, but not sure it shows it well enough.

So, for a beginner, we feel like this Synergee Farmer Walk Straps gets us going and on a good path, but for longer term, yes, we expect we'll outgrown these and go for something more "professional." Should one start off that way? No idea - we are unsure about the idea of the metal bar style and weight and felt this was more comfortable for getting started.

title: Not even taking the time to bother at this point
text:
I'm going to be honest up front and put this all into perspective: my wife and I have decided (at least for the foreseeable future) to not even bother attempting to put this Vilaxing 50’’ Trampoline with 5 Levels Adjustable Handle Bar together. We have both just spent 8 weeks sick from head colds that became worse. I'm strong guy, but I've had a double ear infection and I'm coming back from that, so weakened and not up to this level of assembly. I want to say that by way of saying, for someone else or for us in a month or so, we would have the strength to do this.... but we talked about it, and I'm not sure we'd even do it then.

This Vilaxing 50’’ Trampoline with 5 Levels Adjustable Handle Bar came 100% disassembled and that alone makes us not want to do it.

We have had 3 previous personal trampolines over the years just like this is supposed to be - we only got rid of them due to moving and once, lack of use. Every single one of those came with the round mesh surface 100% assembled on the frame and only the legs needing to be screwed in, then required tightening from time to time to maintain its safety. You are asking someone to jump repeatedly on something that needs to stay together and endure that kind of pressure.

In this case you have to even assemble the round frame - THEN add the however many links to that - and then maintain it over time. No thanks.

If we'd been in a store and they'd brought out this box to us, we would have known and not purchased. In this case, if we'd bought it rather than receiving it as a part of the Vine Program to review, we would have returned it. As part of the Vine Program we do not have the option to return it, but that also gives us the chance to state that we personally do not feel that for us, this level of assembly is safe enough. We know the level of use we get out of them and to be sure that the main from is safe enough is not something we feel we will get out of the assembly.

So as of this writing, we have decided not to put the time and energy into this Vilaxing 50’’ Trampoline with 5 Levels Adjustable Handle Bar, something that needs to stay together while you jump on it repeatedly. I'm not going to give it a 1 star as we feel others might feel fine putting in the effort and feeling comfortable with the outcome, and get use out of it. But for us, it's a no-go out of the box. We've put it on a shelf in the garage. We want our equipment safe and while I get some assembly is at times required - in the right ways - this alone made our decision for us. This gets 3 stars for horrible assembly while giving way to the idea others might not find it as dangerous.

title: Well, I've already lost them... to my wife...
text:

The first thing I always notice in new sunglasses is weight. NOT that they have to be "heavy" to "be good," but they need to be "substantial," meaning "have something to them." Too flimsy or weak and you're replacing them. Too heavy and they can grow uncomfortable to wear. So far these have been spot-on with substantial weight and substance to them. They feel as though they're going to have longevity and be there for (me) her long term, and I like that.

The polarizing thing works. Testing them outside in our (hot and humid) summer and they let me see just fine. Great view, seems like they'll be great on the water when we get back out there. Testing also meant going from AC out into the heat and humidity and so far, no fogging. That's a huge plus.

So I put them on and love the look and feel. I tend to not do as well with "wrap around" sunglasses, but these were great. Really grabbed my attention. And again, no fogging - another issue I have from sweating to going cold to hot. But in the times I was allowed to wear them, nothing. I have a larger head and many sunglasses actually end up looking good on me. These really impressed...

Then the mistake... I let my wife try them on.

She has the opposite head - her's is small and oval and she usually HATES how sunglasses look on her. She has only a couple pairs because she cannot find ones she likes... until this Parallel Eyewear Yosemite Polarized Sunglasses... so... she said she's going to steal them.

I gave them to her. She does look great and they made her happy...

She loves them.

So...

I normally do not comment on price due to the nature of being a reviewer. But in this case, I want to - my criteria for doing so is, would I spend the price point to buy the item? In this case, yes, I think I would. As of this writing, these are listed at $95.

We do not know the Parallel brand; neither of us have heard of it before. I have a couple Ray Ban (the only "brand" I truly know), a few sunglasses in the $20 - $49, and a few between $50 - $99. I think I need my wife to wear these for awhile before making a final decision, but so far they are a solid, feel-like good materials and good construction, well weighted sunglasses. They look great on both of us. They do not fog. And my wife is loving them. So yea, I think they would be something for which I would be willing to spend the money... to get myself a pair. (someday)

5. As you can see in the video... set up IS decently easy. Now that we've done it, it SHOULD be far easier when we get out to the beach next. My wife did it side-side-side-top and that worked. We talked about top first, but have not tried it yet. Taking it down was very similar, freaky a little easier now that she knew the strength it took and what would happen. Frankly, it's a cool design and works well. There is a "bottom" to it that's mainly a connected piece that you sort of unfold out and sticks out the front for an overlay onto the sand. It's a nice touch. Once out you can lay other ground clothes on it, blankets, whatever, and that should help hold it down. Again, there are stakes, but we did not try for this test.

We are hoping to get to the beach this upcoming weekend - weather permitting - so as soon as we do - if needed, we'd come back to update - but only if things don't go as planned. Not sure on the overall shade coverage, but the short period of time we were out there, the sun was directly over us and it did give us some decent shade. We feel like we'd set this up in combination with the umbrellas for an overall area of protection for me - and while we might leave the umbrellas in place, we'd move this Old Bahama Bay Pop Up Beach Tent with the sun/shade movement so I don't have to 1. get out of the shade and 2. it seems lighter and easier than unscrewing the umbrellas out of the sand and moving them 2+ times as we often do.

In the end, this seems like a nice option and we are happy to have it. It should work - again, will update if that doesn't happen - and we are happy to have something that already seems very easy to use. Very pleased.

title: We think this set is going to be a continuing great addition to our workout gear
text:
This DASKING Portable Home Gym Resistance Band Bar Set has been a great addition to the workout gear my wife and I are using to get (back into shape since the flu) into shape, and an excellent compliment for what we already have - including another resistance band set and well known body weight set. The reason I mentioned these is because not only does nothing really do it all, but 1. with the other resistance band set we are now mixing and matching items, and 2. the body weight set works in ways resistance bands do not and vice versa, so we have come to use them as complements to one another.

1. This set arrives in an outer white bag and inner black, carrying bag. You can use the inner bag only and dump the white outer one, but, we thought about holding onto the outer bag to store extra pieces in when not in use - it's that good of a bag. That black bag is great with handles and shoulder sling. Good quality on the materials and well contracted. This is a good bag - and the pieces do fit in well, though you'll be undoing the bar each time to fit.

2. The pieces of the set arrive inside, each type of piece or pieces in individual plastic bags. Again we are currently keeping the pieces in these bags to see if they help store and travel better, but honestly, not sure how long we'll keep that up - though it comes across as a nice detail and helps up the set in our view.

3. All of the "anchor" pieces - those pieces you attach to a door or bench or item to anchor - as well as those attached to you to anchor to you are well done, good quality materials, well constructed. I think where my wife and I are still on the fence is the comfort of the parts that wrap around your ankle and you hold - these are the kinds of things that take time to break in and until they are, they can hurt a bit when rubbing. That is not to say they are bad per se, or that they are not well padded - these are done fairly well - but that stiff, tough material can grow tiresome after so many reps and getting sweaty. So time will help... we hope.

4. The bar is great - it feels strong, sturdy, and that it'll last. My wife has used it - I have not yet - but she loved it. It's long enough to sit well on both our shoulders, but not so long as to be overdone. It is "comfortable' in the way you are wanting one to be - that you can grip it, hold it, and brace it on your shoulders or somewhere and not be in pain. It breaks into three parts for storage. Easily put together and taken apart. They include a label on it - as well as in the instructions - how to care for it by adding lubricant every so often to keep it working well. It's a nice remind being on the bar itself.

5. I really like the anchor for the door. We have another set that this will compliment - both on it's board and on our doors - and the one thing we both find is a bit weak with that set - *** Weak due to the size of the space around the door itself, not the anchor of the set - is that as just stated, that anchor piece is too small and we cannot use it on the bottom of the door. It's also not the best on the side, though no issue on the top, as compared to this DASKING Portable Home Gym Resistance Band Bar Set which has a door anchor that is a bit larger, therefore, it can be used on the bottom of the door we use. But also, it sits a bit nicer around the edge and top as well. The one weird thing - that after searching the instruction pictures we finally figured out - should have sooner - is the loop that is attached to this piece. It sits on the "side" if you will and we were not getting it... but we did... it is to allow you to loop it over a bench or some such thing as another option for anchoring. All well done, strong, and secure, and should give us a solid anchor to trust. - You never know until you try and so far, we both feel safe and secure.

6. The resistance bands themselves are very nice. I think it's the red set are the 40 and the blue are the 50 lbs. There are two each of two each - 40 X 2 = long, 40 X 2 = short, same with the blue. So you can adjust the length somewhat to what you need. We like this as a way to use the shorter or longer or longer still... but also, we tried interplay, by using a short red with a long blue (I think that was the way we did it) for a mix of weights. And here is a way we are talking about mixing our sets - using part of the other set with this for a variety of strengths/weights to switch up the workouts. We're pretty sure it's going to be a great option for us - we only tried it once, but it did work, so... In general what we both like about the resistance band thing is that it gets the muscles working to a burn quickly as your body works WITH the pull and "shaking" of the bands. Hey - NOT an expert in this - but we do love that way our muscles have to adjust and work the core and the muscle groups to control the movements with that shake. We feel that burn so quickly and see that muscle pump equally as quick. Then combining it with regular weights and/or the body weight version, it's not only fun, but it keeps the muscles working and guessing, and the results overall seem to come pretty quickly.

7. The attachments for the bands are solid - there was one press that seemed a bit weaker and easier to push than all the others, so the question is, will it last? We hope so. We hope the whole set lasts. It seems like it will, but yes, when there is a "weak spot" like a push part that is not as "strong" as the others, you wonder. But for now, we are choosing to remain positive.

In the end, this DASKING Portable Home Gym Resistance Band Bar Set is an outstanding set and we are happy to have it. We believe it will continue to aid our workouts and give us fun ways to stick with it, great results, and allow us to stay physically healthy. We're very happy with this DASKING Portable Home Gym Resistance Band Bar Set.

title: Didn't know what to expect: thrilled with what we got
text:

title: Serious fun, easy and great to ride! We love it! Can't wait for more adventures!
text:
[[VIDEOID:7c963067c4b7ab3cf11ca74bdcaddaa3]] So my wife loves roller blading and after trying it a number of years back, we discover it is NOT my cup of tea. For all the things I can do, that is NOT one of them. So I miss out when she goes... and I started to see these eScooters and thought... why not? Had the chance to get one a couple of weeks ago, but then had the chance to get this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter and grabbed it. We like both - and now we can each have one for things other than her blading. Each has a couple "cons," but nothing we can't get over or around. And in the end, we really like them - both. But... I think I actually like this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter slightly more... here's our take:

1. It comes in a perfect box - meaning the packing and all was great for taking care of the EVERCROSS Electric Scooter while inside and throughout delivery. It is also great for gifting - the recipient will open it up to find... a fully put together scooter. The ONLY things you have to do: pull up and pop into place the front stick and handle bars and adjust the height of the handle bars. Both totally easy. There is literally NOTHING to assemble. You are only adjusting the handle bars to a comfortable height and it's totally easy. And you are popping that front stick with the handle bars because this thing is collapsable.

2. I repeat, it is collapsable. That means you can take it almost anywhere. If I had had this back in college... life would have been easier! You can literally break that front stick and bars down, and put them into the INCLUDED BAG that lets you carry this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter anywhere. Think about the student in your life! That huge campus! Or how about that "commute" in your city or town and then NOT wanting to leave the eScooter outside! This bag is well built, with solid materials and lets you take this thing anywhere! Oh where were you in college...

3 We got out there and tested - my wife on the first one, me on this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter. One of the reasons I do like this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter a little better is that i's weight limit is slightly higher that the other one. That means the weight I recently put on due to an illness does not keep me off of it until I get the weight back off - I'm out there now, not in a few weeks!

It is smooth, easy to ride, and you are up and going within minutes of getting it out of the box! The instructions feel a little intense - a lot to pick up and know, mostly around the box with all the information you're given while riding (mph, what level you are at, etc). I'm part of the way through, but I wanted to ride - so out we went. I can ride a SEGWAY with ease - when you get on this you'll understand that comparison - as this is about balance and the like. For we of GenX, (think skateboards and roller blades - neither I was great at) the SEGWAY was something I could master. So this eScooter I thought I was also in a good position to take on, and I was right. Balance is there, eases of use, turning, stopping... all there. Kids today... they'll rock this thing quickly.

4. Breaking. This is another point for the EVERCROSS Electric Scooter. The other one we have will stop on a dime! I mean, you hit the breaks and according to my wife, you STOP. That IS great for certain situations - and like this in reverse - you simply have to get used to it. (like driving a car). BUT, on the EVERCROSS Electric Scooter the breaks act more like a slowing device ... not a STOPPING one!
You hit them and SLOW down, NOT STOP. I like this from the standpoint that I feel as I have more OVERALL control as I am riding AND stopping. For me this is a plus. For someone else, they/you might prefer the STOP of that break system. My wife thinks she likes this slowing option better (and at some point we will be able to switch and she can use this while I try that), but for now, this is mine (maybe I won't take off that weight... ). Again, this slowing type stop means I can control the stop, the turns, and maneuvering while NOT stopping outright, but when I need to stop, I bring it down in speed, then you step off to stop. So far it has NOT been a problem and actually, again, I really like it.

5. There is a GREAT light! Do not let your wife, child, or anyone else "Test" it while you are looking directly into it!

6. There is an "emergency break" in that you can step on the back fender to STOP it - read the instructions. Apparently you DO NOT want to do this often or you'll wear out the tire.

7. The tires are great! I have ridden around our community and over bumps, "flat" speed bumps, those lines that are always painted with slick paint (motorcycle riders get it), and leaves and twigs... so far it's been great and I feel safe and in control. Fastest I've gone: 10 mph. We live in a community with kids and cars, so until I can get somewhere I can open it up... but so far so great and I'm having fun!

8. That weight thing... Check your weight and what it can handle. I did put on a few pounds and until I get those off and back to moving down, I cannot use the other eScooter. But this one I was fine within the limits. Which made me wonder, because this eScooter is actually slightly smaller overall. Including the wheels. So... why? No worries, I can still use this and it moves. I have gone up and down hills here in the area fine - we are NOT talking about LARGE hills, but enough that with my weight I should have noticed any issues and did not. It never felt like it was working any harder.

9. And once you get comfortable, there is a readout box on the handle bars you can track things like mph and the like. There are (I think my wife said) three speed levels - we quickly moved me up to #2. I am very comfortable at this level and should not take long to try out and use #3 - again, I am very comfortable on a SEGWAY, and again, this is important as the concept of balance and speed are very similar. The box is easy to read, though I've not even tried to change anything while riding and my wife being the one to read the instructions, made adjustments when we'd stop. I THINK this is how it is set up - to only adjust on a stop, but do not quote me on that. When making said adjustments, it's easy to use and to see. I am again, GenX with a need for reading glasses when... reading. BUT I did not need them to see perfectly fine and clearly the printouts on the box.

10. The handlebars... are good. This is another SLIGHT "con" in that they do "SHAKE" while you are riding. In order to fold up and then go down with the front stick in order to pack it away, they are bendable. HOWEVER, that means in the locked position there IS a noticeable shake or wobble to them. I REALLY noticed it at first and it did "shake my confidence," BUT I quickly got used to them and was fine. It is something my wife said, as she tried it, that it made her uncomfortable and it was one thing she put in the WIN column for the other eScooter. SO... it'll be a personal preference.

11. There is a kickstand to keep it up on its own. Well designed and easy to use!

12. SIZE MATTERS... Or does it?
We both agree the other eScooter IS bigger... platform, height, wheels, but... we also both agree, it doesn't much matter. I have put on that weight, I do not fit into the other one's weight limit, but I do on this smaller one... so.... does size matter? For weight, apparently not. FOR COMFORT... I did have to try a couple positions to decide how I felt I fit best on the PLATFORM. When standing you are likely not going to be standing front to back, but facing to one side or the other - this appears to be common on the eScooters we have seen. Okay, no worries... and I tried one direction (left) and was not at all comfortable. Flipped myself to the right and all was great! I fit - BUT I also notice I am in a smaller space than the other eScooter... but it honestly was not a problem for me. BUT a larger (read taller) person might find the shortness of the deck uncomfortable.

Overall, we LOVE this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter and are THRILLED to have it! Whether we take turns and switch off, this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter is a welcome addition for my wife and I. I'll be able to go with her when she blades or we can each take one and have time out. We have NOT had to recharge yet - we haven't been far enough yet to need it - so I cannot yet speak to that process. If it is anything but great, I'll come back to UPDATE. But we are expecting it to be as easy as the rest of our experience with this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter. In the end, would I pick one or the other?????? Ad of right now... yes, I think I would pick this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter over the other - for me. I 1. like the slowing of the breaks, 2. that it takes my weight - even when I loose it I like that idea, 3. that it fully and easily breaks down and goes into the included bag. BUT that does not mean the other eScooter does not have great elements to it. In the end... as far as THIS EVERCROSS Electric Scooter how do we like it? WE LOVE IT! This is a great eScooter for adults!

title: For the price point it has a nice fit, looks good, good light; we like this helmet
text:
Between her roller blades and our eScooters, my wife and I needed two new bike helmets. This was the one we got her and so far, we really like it. I normally do not talk about price points, but in this case: for the price point it feels, looks, and acts like a solid choice. We hope to never have to find out about the "protective" elements, but hope it holds up to that standard as well.

1. The Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light is a good looking helmet, so if looks are important, this has a nice look to it. We like the blue we picked and the overall look is cool.

2. The fit is good. My wife has a smaller head than mine, so we got one that was very adjustable - not really by choice in that we would have order one "size specific" if needed, but again, for her needs. In this case, the Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light allows you to adjust the size in a "one size fits all" situation. The dial on the back adjusts for you and so far it works well. She likes the fit she gets and feels comfortable between that adjustment and the strap.

3. There is no way to "test" this helmet without falling - and we are not test dummies - so we must trust this will have the good if ever needed. She took a good spill once off a SEGWAY and had a helmet on - which truly saved her - and so we swear by wearing head gear. Here I jump to the idea of "You get what you pay for." BUT this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light fits like the ones we have had in the past and has a similar feel, so we are "trusting" it to take care of her if ever needed.

4. The inside lining IS thinner than mine. There is a difference in that kind of thing - bringing us back to, if we had the money we WOULD upgrade. But for what it is, this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light feels good on her head and she is comfortable.

That said, we have no intention of being out at night, but even in the daylight, it IS something that catches your eye.

In the end and overall we are very pleased with this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light and are happy to have it. Does price matter? You tell me. Yes, there IS a difference for a MUCH higher price point. But if the idea is to get something good on your head to keep you. safe, we think this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light offers us a great option.

title: Serious fun, easy and great to ride! Love it!
text:
So my wife loves roller blading and after trying it a number of years back, we discover it is NOT my cup of tea. I miss out when she goes and was trying to think of ways I might still be able to go. I started seeing these eScooters and thought... why not? Had the chance to get one a couple of weeks ago and grabbed it. A short time later I would have the chance to get a second and grabbed it as well, allowing us both to use them when she's not blading.

We like both. Each has a couple "cons," but nothing we can't get over or around. And in the end, we really like them - both. They are each great fun to ride, easy to learn, and have let us enjoy some fun evening rides. Here's our take:

1. Our arrived in the very large box, folded, and needing some assembly before use.

2. There was sadly some damage to the box upon arrival, but didn't notice until - as we worked on the data box - that something seems to have poked a hole through the box, the interior stuffing, the instructions, and finally the end of the handlebars, leaving a gash in the material. It's disappointing, though we do not think caused any damage to how works. We worry about it getting wet in there - as parts to control the bike lie within - but we'll be careful. Though again, disappointing. It's not "brand new perfect."

3. The assembly was mostly easy. Pull up the handle into place, you do have to tighten/loosen/adjust with the included wrench that was truly not worth the cost of making it. One twice and it was slightly bent - but enough it wouldn't grip anymore. Had to use our own adjustable wrench. Got that worked out. Took a few adjustments, but it allows you to lock down the stick holding the handle bars. Once secure the stick and handles bars are very secure throughout the ride. The other eScooter we have allows the handlebars to drop down to fold in and carry in a bag - this does not - and while a nice feature, those also jiggle in a way that makes my wife unfordable while riding. I don't have a problem, but it is a consideration. So this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults makes for a smoother ride for my wife in that regard.

4. Once the stick and handlebars are locked into place, you're pretty much ready to go. It does go down, so you can store it folded, into a smaller piece. The rest of the footprint remains the same - meaning you only loose the height. We have left both open since assembly and find it is easy to get it in and out, but appreciate this feature. The one thing the other eScooter does is to fold down into a smaller overall package - though again, the same footprint size - and fits into an included carrying bag. This SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults does not do that. It is one feature that puts a point into the box for us with the other eScooter and not with this one. If you're working, going to school on a college campus, or maybe out for a ride and want to go in somewhere, being able to pack it into a bag and carry it is a nice feature this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults does not offer - though you can break it down and carry it by hand.

5. The SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults is also noticeably heavier than the other eScooter we got, but for each of us, not so much so we couldn't carry it a distance. You would notice the weight more quickly on this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults, but to/from a house, car, or the like it's easy enough.

6. The deck here is pretty decent - size, shape, and traction. My wife feels comfortable on it, but has said a little more room would be nice. But these are eScooters and designed for being useful, but not big. Ironically I'm a bit bigger than her and I am fine - though note the size on both - but ride the smaller other one. Because...

7. With a bit of added weight, I currently do not fit within the posted weight limit of this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults - which is decidedly lower than the other eScooter. Therefore, for safety, I have not even tried this one yet. My wife rides it and does love it. However, the weight difference is interesting in that this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults IS larger and a bit heavier, but the other one comfortably takes my weight in it's posted limits. So it's a bit weird. We feel like this one would likely be fine as well, but won't try. But it also puts another check in the box for the other one.

8. Great bell. Decent light. We both feel like the bell - which sounds similar to a bike bell - is far better on this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults, but the light are better on that one. This is doable, but not as large or as bright.

9. There are included tools for assembly, but again, the wrench was worthless after one turn, the others fine. We tossed the wrench, but kept the others if we need to adjust anything.

10. The range on this and the speed are great. I can't tell you off the top of my head what either are listed as, but we've been out and about over a few nights and gone a bit further each time. We're GenX and desk jockeys, so our activity levels had taken a dive - injuries and flu knocked us off our higher actives over the last year or so, though ironically not due to Covid. But getting on these has been a bit of a pacing task. We have been having to adjust to the standing in such a small spot and not moving - no room - so our feet are a bit... they are adjusting. It's been working and each ride we have been more and more comfortable - to the point we no longer stop for our feet being sore. Anyways, the point being, we are both still on the original charge, and we have gone some good distance as we learn and have fun. So we have not charged it yet to know how long. But we are very impressed with the distances we have so far gotten.

11. The speeds are excellent. Again, I've been riding the other one, but my wife easily keeps up. On that one I noticed my current weight does not limit my speed. That one has three speed levels and I'm in the middle. I THINK this one does as well and that she too is using the middle option. Her weight - well within the range of this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults - is no obstacle for her or this eScooter - she can go fast and feel it. We have done some decent "hill" climbing and decent and there is no struggle.

12. The Breaks - WORK! You STOP and you STOP! I mean, hit the breaks and she says it STOPS! The other one has a more reducing speed element - you push the button and it slows you, then you STOP with your feet. In her use of both eScooters, she actually prefers mine - the slowing rather than the STOP. She feels it's far TOO strong and she has to be careful of this so as not to knock herself off. It's not bad - not like she won't use it or is scared of using it - but the reducing speed almost feels like it gives her more control. We have not - yet and hopefully never - had a need to just STOP, but if we did, she's golden.

13. But the reducing speed on the other one allows me to go into controlled corners without stopping, but rather controlling the eScooter. I have a far wider range of speed levels it gives me to do intricate and controlled movements, rather than having to let it "naturally" slow down and do the same on this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults. So two different experiences of control in this way.

In the end, this is a REALLY FUN and well built eScooter. My wife loves it and I look forward to being able to try it when the weight is back down. In the mean time, we can both get out there, go for rides, and have fun. We are thrilled to have it. But... if we had to pick a single eScooter type/make to have, we both agree, we'd likely pick the other one. There is nothing they could have done - again, we feel it was a delivery issue - about the damage to the handlebar. It's disappointing, but we do not hold the eScooter or company responsible.

So that leaves the idea the other one can be broken down and carried in a bag, this one only broken down. This one IS a bit heavier. This one is a bit more of a process to put the handlebars up and down. This one does not have the same weight restrictions as the other - by a long shot of at least 30 lbs difference - meaning larger folks are more limited - check before you buy how much it can hold - so this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults one right away eliminated me from using it until I get these pounds back off. And the STOPPING of this being so abrupt is not our preference.

But in the end, we still truly love this eScooter. It IS a great ride and we have had fun being out. My wife is enjoying it very much. Would we pick the other if we had to? Yes. But for an eScooter, this one is really nice. We cannot - at present - give it anything less than 5 stars for what it does do - meaning we wouldn't drop any stars because of what it doesn't. We're happy to have this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults.

title: My wife is excited to use it
text: Due to just enough height differences, this TRX Training Weighted Jump Rope will be my wife’s. title: This organizer is going to work great for our day trips
text:
While this 2 Layer Golf Trunk Organizer is designed and marketed for golf, frankly it has a lot of uses for carrying along extra clothing, shoes, and other items.

My wife and I love our day trips, weekenders, and vacations. In a hot weather state you often find yourself wanting to change what you're wearing from time to time, what with the sweat that can occur. We also play pickle ball and have a need to change from time to time into better clothes and shoes. So we can take our day bags and carry them on our backs - getting hotter, sweatier, and more uncomfortable, or, with this 2 Layer Golf Trunk Organizer, we can carry those items and run to the car when we want to change. Okay, that might sound like a pain - having to go back to the car in order to change - but we never know if we're going to want to - there are plenty of times we just deal - and rather than carrying stuff around, he end up leaving stuff in the car already. But the bags we stuff things into can wrinkle them, you're putting shoes with clothes, and whatever other difficulty a bag like that can create.

So when I saw this 2 Layer Golf Trunk Organizer I grabbed it - my wife loved the idea the second I showed her. When it arrived I got it together as quickly as possible, and so far we are excited for our next getaway - which is soon.

1. It arrives with the separate pieces needing to be put into the mushed down main bag. NO worries, there is a video online on the product page. I recommend you watch it to check out how this thing works, then watch again for the shoe compartment. I thought I was doing it right, but it came out backwards. Watched twice just to make sure - yep, backwards. Made a quick flip and it was spot on. Slide the large "T" like piece into the base, pull the various sides out to form around the bottom of the bag, and it gives it the basic foundation.

2. The shoes do fit, but... I have smaller feet, so mine fit front to back completely easily. I was able to get the gym shoes in no problem, but the flip flops were a bit too wide. I did try altering them - one shoe forward, the other backwards - but they still needed to tilt to the side to fit. 3. The other pieces easily go in where you want and velcro to the sides - alter as needed. You do need the long piece for the short ones to work and that does set a pretty basic option, but one that we can use for shirts, shorts, pants, you name it. They stay in place and hold a good amount of stuff.

4. The zippers are solid and well constructed, so should have a good life of use.

5. There are handles on the two ends so you can carry from car to home and back again. We will be doing this every weekend and day trip and trip...

7. It takes up a pretty good amount of space. We plan to mainly keep it in the trunk, fill it, and either change in the car or transfer items to a bag and take it in wherever - though the car means not having to put stuff in the bag for those wrinkles... but we have options. In the end, this 2 Layer Golf Trunk Organizer is well done and perfect for what we complain about whenever we are out - we want to take extra clothes, but... now we have an easy way to take clothes, keep them nice, and get the dirty stuff home. There IS space for golf supplies - like the shown tees and such on the product page - but those spots can also be used for underwear, deodorant, brush or comb, and who knows what else you could come up with. We are thrilled with this 2 Layer Golf Trunk Organizer and cannot wait to use it this weekend and many more trips afterwards. I will update if things don't go as planned - but we can't image that being an issue - this is a great organizer!

title: I am no pro, but this helmet is outstanding!
text:
We recently got an electric scooter, plus my wife rides roller blades, and we’re talking about an electric bike - or recumbent, not sure which. We have a need for a couple bike helmets. I will fully admit, we are NOT experts in this area and have done no research beyond knowing they need to be rated and that there are good ones and bad. We have each owned in the past - that kind that looks similar to this, but with that point at the back, which always makes us think, what happens if you land on the back and that point slams the helmet forward...

So when I had the chance to grab this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) I took it without hesitation. Not only does it look good, but in wearing it, it feels great and gives us a sense of being safer than without a helmet. And for all the helmets we have owned, that this has the blunted back, answers that “what if,”

So this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) arrived and we broke in right away - had to see it in person. We were blown away by the presentation - it comes in a nice box - make sure to take care of this box, it is your storage box! Inside you’ll find the helmet and a bag. Open up and the helmet goes in the bag in the box - it is a GREAT way to store your helmet! Our previous helmets always end up on a shelf somewhere. This is excellent and we were already impressed.

Next... the helmet. It looks cool. Not only the color - I’m a blue guy and it’s perfect - but the overall design is so cool. We both liked the matted look - over the glossy really - but in person it looks even better. And on, it looks seriously cool. I tried it with both my reading glasses - no point other than to see how well it handles glasses - and my sunglasses - one of several I own, so one design style - and in both cases they fit perfectly under the sides of the helmet. I felt like I could wear them for an hour and have no rub or discomfort. I have not actually worn them out riding yet, but in this situation, the test was impressive.

As to that idea we always wondered about - what happens if you land on the back and that point - this is blunted, meaning there is no point. You land and it makes sense - you’ll have the back side make contact, but in a way that appears it’ll cushion the head and not shove it or the helmet forward.

The helmet is really light weight and you cannot believe how it feels like it could be that light and protect your head. So we put it on... and for me it fit perfectly. I got the large due to my large head. I had to open the strap slightly, but one half turn on the wheel and it was perfect - snug, but not tight nor uncomfortable. Now we only have this one, so when my wife went out to test the scooter, she had to wear this one. She has a much smaller head than mine, but it was nothing to size this down for her - while she technically doesn’t fit their size chart at this size, it worked well - she was comfortable and felt completely secure in it. It was very easy to size down for her, then bring it back up for me. It was easy and quick and we both felt great with it on.

I’ll be honest - this price point is above what we would normally spend. I was able to get it as a Vine Reviewer and for that I am grateful. I normally do not speak to price because of that, but in this case, wish to address it. In talking about it, we WOULD spend the money to get a second one for her. We feel that the safety this “promises” is worth the money. Now that said, We would do much more research first - we are not experts on the safety aspects of helmets and would make sure first. There is NO way we would go out and test this - meaning risk our head to see that is does what it promises. But if our further research shows what we think it would, yes, we would consider spending the money. Brain safety is important and we want something good. Now that said, if there is a product at a lower price that provides equal safety, we would seriously consider that - money is something we are careful with, but so too our safety. In the end, this is an excellent helmet that fits well and comfortably. Safety is the priority. But we do have to be realistic about cost. So if we could afford it and our research indicates it is a value, then yes, we would pay, but if not, if we found something as good at a lower price point, we’d have to look in that direction.

But we both love this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) helmet and are thrilled to have it.

title: Good for a beginning, it's a pretty basic, simple journal; not the best option for moderate-advanced
text:
Following a few injuries my wife and I are getting back to our workouts, but wanted to get some bigger steps this time and specific outcomes, so we decided to grab some journals. I had gotten one that leans on more of a weight-centric program. My wife is more mixed between cardio and weights, so I thought this one might be of help. In the end, this is an okay, not good nor great journal, but will do something to at least let her track. She will use it, but we agree, it is not the best option for anyone beyond a beginner starting out.

1. It is made from decent materials with a hard cardboard front and back to give stability when working inside. The binding is spiral, allowing it to fully open and not bunch up the pages. From this aspect, it is well done.

2. The options within are more limited than mine and others we have looked at.

A. The introduction of Why is pretty basic, but good for beginners, but limited for those beyond.

B. There are places to track your weight and body shape changes at the beginning, 30 day, 60 day, and 90 day marks. There are no spots for doing so between, which in my expense and from my reading, one should not track weight and other elements daily. Some suggest weekly or monthly. In this case, it is monthly (every 30 days). My journal offers weekly tracking with more options on WHAT to track and HOW to do it. I think this is notable in that while mine and this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker tracks the same elements of the body, mine provides little diagrams of WHERE on the body these points lie. As I think this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker is lacking this information, which if geared towards beginners, would be helpful information.

C. My journal offers far more options on all of these aspects across the board. For example, mine has space for 13 exercises per page and Sets 1 - 6 whereas this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker has it strangely set up in Sets 1 - 5 with Weight and Reps. It's as if they see a Set as an exercise and think you are doing five exercises. At least that's how we are reading it. Then you put in how many reps. in each set.

D. Things like Water intake in this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker are just a question: Water Intake? In mine (and others) they tend to have a way to track, such as something open you fill in when you have a glass or something you check off. I prefer such a way in that you tick it off with each one as opposed to this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker which is answering a question - "5." Now you're having to keep track to fill it out. YES, you can certainly check off or make tick marks - but that really should be set up in the design.

E. Little things like tracking what area of the body or muscles you worked (legs, core, back, etc) are NOT included here which is a shame. But they do include things like "Next session modifications and/focus"... not even sure what that would mean - I THINK it's their way of having you in fact track if you did core, legs, chest, etc. The space available for these question answers is pretty limited.

F. Another reviewer noted there are "Examples" provided in some pages but are printed on the lines and you have to write over it. It is true how they printed it and it's kind of annoying. Why would I want to keep writing over it?

G. While not as bad in the wording and grammar of many products made in China, there are some obvious (glaring) strange parts. Nothing one cannot workout and that make this a bad book, but they are notable.

In the end, this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker is okay and would be fine for many beginners looking to workout and track that journey for the first 90 days. It is not in your face, it is a way to learn and pace yourself and and get the information down. I don't think it's all that bad that it would be with a 1 or 2 star rating, but certainly does not earn 4 or 5. In the end I went with 3 because it is workable, easy to use and write in, and it does provide elements one wishes to track when getting into a practice. That said, there are much better options on the market, even for beginners, and I would personally look elsewhere.

title: Well made, but can’t test for a few more weeks
text:

title: So far so good...
text:
So far so good with this GoSports Core Hub Fitness Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration. I’d seen a similar product in commercials and wondered if it would actually work for planking - or was it a gimmick. When I had the chance to grab this GoSports Core Hub Fitness Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration I took it, hoping it would add to my workout options. For various reasons I prefer not to plank directly on the ground, so would this be of help? The answer for me is, yes. As I continue to adjust to using it.

It arrives with the platform itself, pump, and instructions. One assembles the platform simply by pumping air into the ball on the bottom. My wife and I found this was a two person job - the long needle easily went in, however, it also easily pumped out until I had her hold it in place. At that point the ball quickly and easily pumped to full size. Pulling the needle out the air stayed in and there was no leaking - with nothing to plug it - and a week later holds the air perfectly. They included a second pin for the end of the pump - great if the first breaks or is lost, but we’ve found the first one wouldn’t even come off after we secured it.

There is a plastic covering on the phone “t” so don’t forget to remove it. It easily comes off and the foam under holds the phone in place just fine - though I haven’t used the phone or any app for working out at this point - I do have it there for stop watch.

I’ve put some pounds on since surgery so I wondered how it would hold the weight and so far it’s fine. I don’t feel any weakness or bowing or any issue in holding me up. As a shorter guy with shorter arm length I do find that positioning my arms in a spot to make placement comfortable is not exact. In fact, I end up testing my forearms a bit to hold on. And it’s taking time to find the best spot for being comfortable on the platform. Plus having the platform lay right in oder to balance correctly. Still working it, but also, still getting a solid workout. In fact I come away each time feeling the burn and it’s been a solid way to plank. It can be used in either the kneeling or full out, extended leg position and while I’ve only done it fully extended, I can see the benefits to both options.

So, does the movement and/or height add to the benefit of planking? I have to think it does. I like being up off the floor and having a nice, comfortable surface under my arms. As for the movement, it does work the fuller core area and I feel the burn in more than just one spot. I’ve only done this for a week, twice a day most days, and I’m doing better at time at the end of that week. I will maybe add in the app-games, but right now that is not my personal interest - but I can see how it could add to the fun (I’m not a gamer).

Any cons? So far it’s a little too early to know overall - will the board last, how does the app work...
I did notice there is a ’sound’ when laying on the board under the forearms. It seems like it might indicate the surface material could separate from the hard plastic base.

I do have an issue in reaching the handles under the platform - for grip I hold the side of the platform. It might be nice to have a grip along the side one can hold onto other than these two handles.

As long as the ball holds up - and I so far do not see why it won’t hold up - it can be a good, solid exercise platform. But that foam on the top needs to also remain. If that comes off, it will affect the platform itself. So far it’s fine, but again, what does that sound mean - other times I’ve heard it things have separated.

In the end I so far believe this GoSports Core Hub Fitness Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration is a great find and will help me with my workouts and to improve physically. I’m enjoying the experience and I’m enjoying the possibilities of how to continue planking in a fun manner. So yes, I do like this GoSports Core Hub Fitness Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration and happy to give it a 5 star rating.

title: So far, so good: comfortable, supportive, and will get used
text:
I grabbed this Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair with a thought towards our days at the beach. Sometimes we have chairs, sometimes just the towels, but I thought this Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair might offer me a nice, supportive place to sit. My wife tends to lay out for sun, but I like watching the water and thinking... but I can get tired and start to hurt on the hard sand. This is smaller and easier to carry overall (I thought), so why not. In the end, I think I’m going to be correct in my assessment. We’re not getting back out there (yet), but the time is soon upon us for our beach days and I can’t wait.

The Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair is a cool idea - a stadium seat type set up: flips open, cushion, back support. I’ve tried one or two such seats and thought, eh. But we don’t do stadiums enough. We do, however, sit on the floor from time to time, go to the beach, mediate, and so forth. Hitting that “middle age” timeframe, my wife and I would love to have something more comfortable.

1. I gave it 5 stars because overall it feels like that’s right for comfort, ease of use, and so forth. I would consider a 4 star for the magnets that hold the seat to the frame. I’ve had the seat cushions pop off every time I’ve picked it up to carry/move, or take pictures. My wife has not as such luck, only having them fall a couple time. Closed they’d slide up coming off for me, so I’d be worried about loosing one or two or all three - though I’m sure one would notice that many.

2. The cushions are nice for comfort. It comes with three, with one having a strap on the back to hold it onto the other - so you can have a double seat cushion, which is a nice add on.

3. Seems to hold a good amount of weight. I’ve got some extra pounds on right now and it seems to handle me well. I’m taking it off, so hoping it won’t be there all summer as I plan to use it, but so far, so good.

4. The frame seems solid and like it’ll hold up. Again, it holds our weight (individually) and allows us to feel well supported. My wife has tried it more, sitting both cross legged and straight and feels like she can sit there for a good amount of time in both positions.

5. The seat cushions are good - not too thick (though thicker is always better), but not too thin. They were comfortable on both the back and seat.

6. This Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair comes with a strap that you can remove, attaching to the base of the frame allowing you to carry it over the shoulder. My wife did this and felt like both the strap was comfortable, while the chair was not too heavy. We both agree this is a solid, with a noticeable weight to it, but nothing most folks couldn’t handle (we think), finding the strap to be a good addition to aiding that. This is where you’ll want to be aware of the magnets not necessarily holding the seat in place - at least one popped off each time I tried, but only once for my wife. Because of how it sets when you are carrying on the strap - with the open side downward - it would allow the cushion to slip out onto the ground. I grabbed it before it did, but one needs to be aware, so as not to loose any. We talked about adding a strap of our own (sort of a bungie type thing) to hold the cushions in place. But that could be used for other things as well - we just don’t know what that is at this point.

7. Back support - we have only used it on the bed (that was not working too well as we’d fall over, but it was fun trying) and floor in the living room. But the back support was solid and let us feel comfortable. We both felt like it would be a nice support and keep us from hunching over and getting sore quickly.

In the end we are both impressed with this Pebbl Portable Yoga and Meditation Chair and plan to get some solid use out of it. I think this will be one item where time will tell - does it hold up, does it allow for longer periods of sitting, does it take different surfaces (beach, floor, grass, etc)? We’re happy to have it.

title: This is a nice chair, better than most we’ve tried
text:

title: We love this Ringside for our workout goals
text:

title: Got it for a footstool, can use it for more
text:

title: Going to be very helpful to keep our workouts on track and fresh
text:
My wife and I have been working out, getting into great shape and living a healthier lifestyle. We use a variety of types (weights, body weight, kettle bells, TRX) in order to give us a good, solid, all around workout, primarily weight training, but like to use other means to work the whole body and muscles in various ways. We have articles, workout research, and videos we turn to for ideas and how to do it properly, but when you’re in there, it’s a bit of a pain pulling them up on the computer. So when I saw this [12-PACK] Laminated Large Workout Poster Set I decided to give it a try.

Note: I had the option of either the black or white background and chose the black. I’m glad I did. Even on the product page it seemed it would be harder for our eyes to clearly and comfortably read the images - especially from a distance - and in reality, it was a good call. We do not have the white background to compare in real life, but the black background is excellent, easy to see, and as thought, comfortable on our middle age eyes. We both like how the images pop and make seeing them easier both up close and further away.

The [12-PACK] Laminated Large Workout Poster Set offers a range of options for how to workout, giving us things we were doing, combined with new ideas. There are few we won’t use right away as we are not using that type of workout - for example, we do not have an exercise ball at present - but the ones we will are already giving us more ideas. The kettle bell and suspension are of particular interest to us, but now that we have had the chance to see them, we have each found something of use and interest on all the posters.

What really grabbed us is that they break the exercises into groups: Back, core, lower body... so that we know what we are working out, along with the proper form. title: Enjoyable for beginners, midlevel skaters
text:
[[VIDEOID:6a9dae27c4383bb5bbbf63af76ea0b65]] A year ago my wife was using roller blades, but wanting a pair of roller skates to also enjoy. A year ago, she severely broke her foot and was sidelined for seven months, but limited as she came back. Now she’s able to do more, cleared for roller blading, but she had been wanting those skates... so when I had the chance to grab her this pair, I took it. She had to wait awhile, but now she’s had a chance to get on them... These NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates are decent, what she described as good for beginners and moderate skaters, but she had a few things to mention. First, she has a foot size that can be spot on 9 or 9.5 with a range that could workout between, based on the show and it's cut. In this case, ordering online, she wasn’t able to try them on first. In the end, she feels like the overall fit around the foot is good, but snug. The front of the boot - at the toes - is the tightest. She first tried with thicker socks, but settled for compression socks, which worked much better. Leather can sometimes adjust to a foot, stretching a bit to hug a foot, but in this case, we’re not sure. She says the front at the toes is tough - the leather hard - so she can’t imagine it stretching. In the end, she feels like if you’re spot on a size, you should be okay, but if there is even a slight “off” about a foot size, there could be an issue.

Second, The skates look nice, and overall the materials. - leather - seems good. The materials in the base and wheels seem good. They have wheels that are supposed to light up as they role - they do, but it’s hard to see in the light/daylight. We have not tried them in the dark, and we do see a little sparkle, but overall, you’re not going to be rolling in the dark, so what we are seeing, it’s not overly impressive. There is a little video above, but yea, the “light up” to us is not impressive. Third, She loved roller skating as a child through to young adult and wants to go back to doing it again. She loves loves loves roller blading, but there is something about skating she holds dear... We will say, her being unable to do anything like this in a year has made it hard for her - she felt it hard/big/painful and has to take this slowly getting back to it. She got up, she went, and she really liked it a lot. She felt like it’s coming back and she enjoyed the experience. She feels like these NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates are going to let her get back up and going - with time to develop - and she’s going to be able to enjoy it. But she also feels like these are beginner to moderate level. The ground itself - the surface - is important. The place we took them (parking lot) was rough and uncomfortable for her. She does have an area she loves for blading, but during several months a year (current) we have a massive amount of acorns that fall and she cannot, for safety, blade (or roller skate) in the area. So this parking lot showed her not every surface is going to work with these skates.

Overall, these ARE decent skates. Things to consider: size, type of sock, surface for skating. These will have an affect on the experience. She sets them best for beginner to moderate. And in the end, she does like them and thinks she’ll get a good amount of use out of them.

title: So far like them, but... a couple of things
text:
UPDATE: I’ve been able to get back to working out and wearing these headbands while lifting weights, hitting a heavy bag, and on walks. In all cases they work out great and do as intended. I’ve been keeping the sweat out of my eyes and staying comfortable. Please read the rest of the review where I address why I still can’t give them 5 stars.

First, I grabbed these Tennis Headbands for Men, Under Armour Headbands Men(3 Pack) because I tend to seat a lot when working out and am tired of the sweat dripping down my face and into my eyes. I thought they looked cool.

I have debated on 4 or 5 stars, which I address below.

1. So, they do look as cool in person. My wife is not a big fan of headbands - thinks they look weird - but she saw them and immediately said they looked great. I agree. I like the solid black, but I equally like the patterns. Happy to wear them from that standpoint. The material feel nice. I find them comfortable on. To this point I think they are 5 stars.

NOTE: I strained my knee badly and have been off it for a week and told I need to give it several more days. therefore, I have not been able to wear them during a workout yet. I will come back and update IF they are anything but great. To this point I can only give 4 stars, with 5 a possibility.

2. Under Armour??? I am a big UA fan with a lot of UA gear. The title on the product page caught my attention, but mainly because 1. I love UA and 2. I did not see any UA logos on the product page. The headbands themselves do not have the UA logo. So I am confused as to why they are allowed to use the Under Armour brand name when as far as I can tell, they are nothing of the kind. To this point, I have to give them 4 stars. Without them being actual Under Armour they are still a fine product, but I am not okay with using the brand name when from everything I can tell, these are not made by nor sold by UA. My wife and I have both looked at all 3 headbands separately and together - there is NO Under Armour logo or labeling.

3. The sizing is mostly the same, but... I found that the solid and the blue pattern are the same size. I have a larger head (usually a baseball hat L-XL), but in this case while they fit spot on, the black pattern was slightly larger. Not working out, merely having them all, it was fine, but I will be curious if they all stay on the same. A smaller ahed might have an issue with the one, but I “think” smaller heads would be okay with the two. To this point I decide to go with a 4 star, as they are not consistent and I do expect them to be.

4. I cannot speak to their ability to keep the sweat off. My injury happened shortly after I ordered these and before they arrived, so that’s kept me from using them for their intended purpose. So right now I can only give them a 4 star rating. But to be fair, even if they come back 100% as expected, I am still bothered enough by the use of the Under Armour name - a brand name I do use often - on the product page when nothing on the actual product indicates they are UA - such as the UA logo. Therefore, for me, I could still not give these a full 5 star rating as I consider this action deceptive. This is a personal opinion and is mentioned here so as to fully explain why I would still consider this a 4 star product.

In the end I do - so far - like these headbands and think I’ll get some good use out of them. But Would rather they not use a brand name to promote them. When you literally write - Tennis Headbands for Men, Under Armour Headbands Men(3 Pack) as the title of the product then I expect they would be an Under Armour product and again, I cannot find any evidence of this being the case on the actual headbands. As stated above, my wife and I have both looked at all 3 headbands separately and together - there is NO Under Armour logo or labeling.

title: So far seems like this is going to be a great SUP
text:

In the mean time, we finally had a chance to blow up this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and so far so good - we are sure this is going to turn out to be a great thing for us! This H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board comes with several items to get you going (able cuff, repair kit, pump), but do not forget, you’ll want to have some sort of safety vest (required by law in our state - NOT INCLUDED in this kit).

The pump to get it inflated is included and for us, worked pretty well. We took turns to pump it up and while it took some time (and strength we’re both currently lacking post surgery and injury) we were still able to get it “almost fully inflated.” I say “almost” because the company recommended 15 PSI and we only got to 10. That 15 is for “optimal use” and no higher. We felt like the 10 would be good, but when we are out there (and I have more energy back) we will go a bit higher than the 10 As you can see in the pics, it is very inflated and looks good, my wife able too and on it and feel firm and secure. Standing on it she said it felt like (on water) it’ll have good, solid balance and allow a feeling of security on the water. This SUP looks and feels “narrow and long” to us based on our experiences on tours, but something we both would feel comfortable on. We will update this review once we can get out there. In the mean time, we are really happy with this SUP and how easily it went together. Or blown into shape. The removal of air was easy and took only a couple minutes. I’ll say, when she first opened the valve there was a LOUD HIGH PITCHED!!! sound that hurt both our ears, but it went away pretty quickly. Then completed the air removal. title: Overall this seems like it’s gonna be a great board
text:
So far this NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board is pretty darn good and we think it’ll turn out to be a great SUP for us. Unfortunately for us, it’s taken a longer than desired time to get a chance to try them - and due to weather (storms, hurricanes) and my recovery from surgery, we’ve been unable to get onto the water. So at this point we are only able to review based on the specific SUP and it’s kit - I will update when if need be when we get it on the water. In the mean time, this is a nice set up and we think it’s gonna be a great SUP. The kit is excellent, with items such as a dry bag for your pone included. There is a patch kit. Also a carrying bag. The carrying bag is a little... weird. The bag sets high - the actual straps are set low on the bag so the top of the bag is higher - at the head or perhaps above depending on your size. But it works on. My wife wore it for the pictures and said it was comfortable, but that it set “weird,” and she felt she could wear it from the car to wherever we were to launch, comfortably. But, I did have to help her get it on and off due to the placement of the straps.

Pumping the SUP: It took us a bit to figure this process out, but once we had it, it went fine. The instruction book is pretty tiny writing, so we took a picture and adjusted it. We can also keep the instructions with on our phones for when we’re out. The tube was easy to insert - took a few times popping out to get it to stay on - there is a way to adjust the pump as it gets harder to pump and we did use it. My wife pumped for awhile, then I did. It IS a bit tough to do. NOT the actual pumping, but the amount of time and it does get harder - adjust the dial - but we only got as high as the 8 PSI not to the 15 they recommend. As we get back into shape following being off workouts for awhile, we’ll get better at it, but between us - for this test run - we were only able to hit that 8 and we had to give up. It FELT fine at this level, but WOW....! We WILL TRY to get to that 15, but ... WOW! My wife stood on it and it felt great, but she said she sees how the 15 would be “better,” yet... will we ever be able to get that high. There are two blades on the bottom - and you add the fin - they are in a holder to protect them when it’s down.

Deflating was really easy. And it took only minutes. This SUP has you use the pump to help clear out the final air and that worked great. The prong you push in the air hole is really easy to use and my wife was thrilled with it.

Overall we are impressed with this NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and look forward to FINALLY being able to use it on the water - when it’s safe. It comes with a break-apart paddle. We have not used it nor put it together, but we did get ourselves another paddle - we think it’s lighter. We’ll keep them both and take both with. It’s a practice we were taught - to have a backup. But right now I can’t speak to how good theirs is. But we are impressed. at this point, we can’t wait to get out there on this NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board!

title: This is a nice home set for family, friends
text:
After weeks of bad weather and then surgery (and recovery) and then more bad weather, we finally had a day we could get out with this Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set and give it a try. The big plus for us was the rule book. Again, we’re only starting out and played some club stuff just before Covid. This is letting us get up to speed ahead of getting back to thing. So thrilled that was included.

The Net: this was what we really got the Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set for. Again, our tennis courts can fill up when the weather allows and we were not getting any time. In the end my wife and I are thrilled - not only to finally get to start using things - but with both the paddle/bag/ball/rules portion of the Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set and the net part. together or separate, you’ll find a nice beginner and/or family set for a lot of fun. title: It’s good, 5 stars with an *
text:
I’m far more old school than my wife when it comes to tracking my workouts and eating. Part of it is that I tend to forget to do it if I don’t see it and part is the act of writing things out - rather than clicking and typing while fighting autocorrect.

So I grabbed this Food and Fitness Journal Diary Workout Wellness Log Notebook for myself. In general, it’s good, but with an *. First, it’s all pink. Hey, I’m not hung up on the color - pink does not impinge my confidence. That said, I’m not a big fan of pink and a lot of guys out there would prefer something other than pink. But the same with ladies. My wife looked at it when it arrived and all she could say was, “wow. Really pink, isn’t it?” She wasn’t all that drawn to it. Other color options might help. Second, this Food and Fitness Journal Diary Workout Wellness Log Notebook is well constructed. It’s hard front and back covers are nice - I think they’ll last - not sure what happens if they ever get wet, but what book survives that? The inside pages are fine - a bit glossy - I have a pen that works fine. With the spiral on this, you can lay it flat open to both pages or just one - both lay fine and are easy to work with open. The pictures I provide are pretty much copies of the ones on the product page - it looks exactly the same. So basically what you’re getting is a place to record your starting sizes (body) and data, places to record calories of favorite foods (not a lot of slots, but enough for faves), and places to lay out meals and exercises. In general, you have plenty of room. If you need more, stick in your own paper pages, or supplement with a computer program. As for those calories - you are not given a lot of places for food items, but again, you can always supplement with things you find online and fill them in here when you eat them. Meaning you are not given a lot of options of choices with food data, but with SO many options even today’s dynamic food apps don’t always include ALL potential food options, so even there you’re doing a bit of research at times. And if you’re limiting your intake, you don’t (necessarily) need a lot of lines for that.

For me the idea is that I keep this on my desk and it’s always visible. I’m not forgetting to open an app and I’m thinking about what I want to record - it’s right there. It is old school, but some of us are better able or more comfortable at such methods of keeping track. For that this is going to work well. Unlike a computer app you have a finite amount of space - if that is an issue - but you can either get another or... For me right now, my plan is to use it as long as I’ve got space in order to secure some habits and then I’ll likely let it go. It’s good what what it is - hence the 5 stars - but has it’s limits hence the *.
