The bike pump does not look very well made, but it did work well enough to add air to the cushion. I'm not sure how to release air from the cushion, though. One side of the cushion is covered with small knobs (about 1/32" tall) and the other side was covered with 3/16" knobs. Both sides were comfortable when pressed against skin (at least for the short period of time that I used it). When partly filled, the cushion wobbles very freely. When filled full, the cushion has slightly convex (rounded) sides which also allow a wobble when seated or standing on it.

title: Grips the floor and feet well when used for stretching or an activity mat
text: This is a yoga mat that is 5 mm thick and measures 68" x 24". The design I chose is a rug pattern on one side and plain gray on the other. I was looking for an exercise mat that would not have toxicity concerns. We love the design and it grips well on our bare feet and on the concrete floor where we're using it. I have two young nieces that like to play on the floor, but concrete is so hard. This mat gives them enough padding to be comfortable when sitting or lying down and enough grip that they can do dancing, crawling, exercises, etc. It doesn't shift under their bodies while at play, so it adds grip and security as well as potential padding if they fall. Keep in mind, though, that 5 mm is about one fourth of an inch, so it's not that thick in terms of padding. When they go home, I use it for stretching – so it's not like I'm getting sweaty nor are the girls. However, it's working quite well as an activity/exercise mat for us.

title: Buttons are stiff and required a firm push
text: This digital stopwatch has a clock, an alarm, and hourly chime (which you can turn off), and the stopwatch function. There is also a whistle that is attached to the same lanyard as the stopwatch. It is relatively simple (in terms of steps) to set the time, turn on and off the alarm and chime, and uses a timer. It can be used as a standard timer, split timer (time individual laps), and to track finish times for multiple racers. Unfortunately, I find that the buttons have too much resistance for easy use. You have to push pretty hard to get it to switch, so I have to pay attention to see if it really did start/stop/whatever. This may not be a problem for people with stronger hands than mine.

title: Very loud, easy to use whistle
text: This whistle can be attached to your key ring and is small and light enough that it doesn't add much bulk. The whistle measures 2.25" long by 5/8" wide by 5/16" deep. It also comes with a red cord lanyard with 37 inches of cord (in a circle) with a metal clip to attach the whistle. Even a small puff on the whistle creates a loud sound that echoed and caught people's attention when I tested it. I keep it on my keychain to used to draw attention if I feel threatened (though I never have) or draw attention if I'm injured (which I did once with an inferior whistle, and it didn't work). This whistle gives me much more confidence that it will draw attention. The sound also seems to be directed away from the user, so it didn't hurt my ears like I expected even though it was loud. I also tested this while standing about 100 yards from someone who didn't know I was going to blow it, and this usually oblivious person looked up towards me when I blew the whistle. I would highly recommend this whistle.

title: The AA batteries are a very tight fit to get in
text: This portable LED lamp requires 3 AA batteries, which were nearly impossible to get in due to the very tight fit. I'm not sure how we'll get them out again when these batteries run down. The light is basic: hit the power button for a blue-white light to turn on and hit the button again to turn it off. The light head can be tilted somewhat up and all the way down. It's lightweight but feels like it would break if dropped on a hard floor. The light does illuminate a reading area well. I'm using this in a dark room that I sometimes need for reading, but it'd also work fine as a flashlight. Probably not practical for everyday use due to the battery fit issue.

title: Kid-sized set of knee pads, elbow pads, and wrist guards
text: This set contains kid-sized 2 knee pads,  2 elbow pads, and 2 wrist guards. They are a yellowish-green and black color. They each have top and bottom adjustable velco closures. We got these for my niece to use when using her scooter. No spills so far, but they look well made for light use like this and like they'll stay on and protect her. They can be stored in the mesh bag that comes with the set.

title: 1.5" wide nylon belt with metal quick release buckle. Sturdy.
text: This nylon tactical belt comes in a box with a ribbon on top and no instructions. This is a strong, sturdy-looking belt. It measures 1.5" wide (top to bottom), 50" long (including the buckle), and nearly 1/8" thick (3mm). The metal buckle is 2 5/8" long x 2" wide. You thread the nylon end through the buckle at whatever length is correct for you, then you press the two golden metal prongs inward for a quick release of the belt rather than un-threading the belt. This is fairly easy to work once you figure out how to do it. There is a sliding piece on the belt to hold the tail in place against the belt. The product description suggests, "You could measure your real waist size and cut the excess part of belt, melt the end of the belt with a lighter." The belt comes with two hanging attachments that attach to the belt with velcro (and also a snap, in one case).

title: Wimpy light & alarm sound.
text:
The LED light is bright enough to help you get your key into a lock, but it'll only dimly light your path. The alarm sound is not very loud--not as loud as a car alarm or a whistle or a smoke alarm. It doesn't help that the speaker is on the back, where your hand naturally covers it to some degree. It makes a weird noise that didn't even grab the attention of a man sitting 70 feet away because it sounded like just another mechanical noise rather than an alarm. The stun gun made more noise! Personally, I'd hoped the light and the alarm noise would warn most potential attackers away, but I doubt they'll be much help. Since the light and the sound aren't as impressive as they advertised, I do wonder if the stun gun will be very effective, but I'm not going to test it out on anyone! They say it's most effective on certain parts of the body, so you have to be close and even aim somewhat, not just touch the current to some body part.

Anyway, you get a USB charging cord and have to charge the stun gun 12 hours before the first use and 4-5 hours each week. Though the green (full charge indicator) light turns on after only a couple hours, they stress the length of time spent on charging more than the indicator light. There is an on/off switch than must be turned on before the alarm sound or the stun gun button will work. The light button will work at all times. The buttons are easy to use, though the labeling on them is not easy to read (especially at night). The light stays on until pressed off, which means it can be turned on if something presses the button when in your purse. This could run the battery down so it's not effective when needed. Some way to check how much charge is left would have been useful. I've never seen or used a stun gun before, but this seemed more hype than useful.

title: Easy to hold and fold/unfold. Not really for hot drinks.
text: This water bottle can hold 18 oz of liquid. It can handle hot to cold liquid, but the silicone is not really insulation between the liquid and your hand when holding the bottle, and that limits how hot the liquid can be. The bottle's body is made of 100% food-grade silicone. The lid, top collar/rim, and maybe a bottom collar is made from PP #5 plastic to make it rigid. The bottle is about 2.75" across at the bottom or 3.5" wide when measuring in the carry handle. It's 8" tall when stretched out or 5" tall when collapsed. It's easy to collapse and extend when empty--just open the lid to allow air in. The flip lid is a bit stiff to flip, but not really a problem.  It doesn't leak. The bottle is easy to hold on to and isn't heavy when empty. Works well for taking water on trips where I don't want a large, rigid bottle to tote around (like an airplane trip).

title: Small but helps make me visable. Has metal clip & bike clip.
text:
[[VIDEOID:afd47ca70db008e2d8762412bb10e24a]] This Rechargeable Bicycle Taillight measures 3 3/8" long x 1" wide x 1" deep (counting the clip). It can be clipped onto clothing and such with a metal clip that's on the back. I use this when I'm out walking for exercise. Or the provided pieces allow you to loop a rubber grip around a tube (handle, bike seatpost, etc.) and attach it to a plastic piece that the light will clip into. The metal clip has a square cut-out that snaps over a plastic button/projection in the bike grip to hold it securely in place. You lift the clip off this button and slide the clip up and off when you need to charge it.

The bottom of the light is removable and you plug the light directly into a USB charging port to charge the light. The bottom (USB connector cover) is easy to remove without being in any danger of falling off by itself. The power button is on top and pressing it cycles between modes: all lights on high, on medium, on low, slow blinking, warning flashes, and fast blinking. Press the power button for 2 seconds to turn off. It's bright, small, and easy to use for my purposes--warning people I'm there and to watch out for me. Power: 1 W. Charge current: 0.5A. Battery: lithium. Net weight: 4g.

In the video, the first three modes look about the same because the camera compensates for the lower light level, but it is getting progressively dimmer.

title: A convenient and secure way to carry water bottles
text:
This well-made water bottle carrier has three ways to carry it: a lightly-padded, adjustable shoulder strap or a carry handle (both of which easily snap onto and off of metal D rings on the carrier, so you don't need to leave both on at the same time) or a buckled strap on the back which can be attached to backpacks and such. This snap isn't exactly comfortable when the carrier is resting against my body, but it's not uncomfortable, either (though I might change my tune when I take this on a long hike).

The main pouch is 10" deep and has a somewhat slick lining that allows metal water bottles to easily slip in and out. Glass water bottles with a silicone sheath do not slip in and out as easily but still work fine. The top opening can remain open or be pulled partly closed. This main pouch easily holds a water bottle that is 3.25" across and should be able to hold a bottle with a circumference of up to 10.5" or maybe even 11". It's fairly easy for me to get the 3.25" across by 8" tall metal bottle out, but I do have to push up on the bottom of the pouch to push it high enough that I can get a good grip on the top of the bottle. This may or may not be more difficult for thicker bottles.

On the front, there are two smaller pockets with zipper closures. The smallest is 4" deep and 4" wide. The other is 6" deep and 4.5" wide. It has an elastic strap across the width and a hard-to-work metal snap hook for keys or whatever. My smart phone fits in the larger pocket, behind the elastic band. This carrier has been working well for me, but I also rarely carry it for more than an hour or two at a time..

title: One of the two sticks won't "lock" and so isn't useable. No instructions on how to adjust and use.
text:
I've never used a walking/trekking stick before, so I can't compare these with others. However, I really wish they'd included some directions as it's an experimental, hit-and-miss method of trying to use them. Also, one of the two sticks won't lock. One stick is fine--I could unscrew the pole (twist the pole, not the black part between the segments), pull the length out, and screw until locked on both the bottom and top segments of the stick. It only took about 4-5 twists to unlock and then again to lock this pole. The second one locks on the bottom section, but that's only tall enough for a child. The top portion won't lock even after being twisted in the lock direction for several minutes. That stick decreases in height with every step and so is useless, thus the low star rating. I can unlock and collapse both poles without problem.

The tip can be used with a 1" textured, rubber tip attachment for sidewalks and such. This tip simply pulls off to expose the permanent, (3/16" across) tungsten carbide tip. A 2" wide plastic disk can be slipped over the tip and screwed into place about 2" up the pole to prevent the stick from sinking too far in sand. There is an adjustable, padded wrist strap. The sticks are a lightweight metal and seem reasonably sturdy. You have to keep track of any tip attachments when not using them as they don't come with a pouch or container.

title: Easy to put on and adjust.
text:
My niece tolerates this Puddle Jumper life jacket better than the old fashioned kind, and she's currently just big enough to fit it. It fits children 33 to 55 lbs. The zipper is on the child's back, so they can't remove it on their own. The zipper works very smoothly and easily. The zipper length is 12.75" (to give you an idea of how it'll fit your child). There is an adjustable buckle on the back to ensure a secure fit. The buckle is easy to adjust and fairly easy to release. This life jacket can be used instead of a Type III personal flotation device and is also certified for use on a boat. Approved by the US Coast Guard and Transport Canada. It has a sewn-in rash guard that offers UPF 50+ sun protection and blocks 93% of UVA and UVB rays. Made in Cambodia.

Care instructions: do not dry clean or machine wash. Sponge with warm, soapy water or use methods recommended for 'hand' washing synthetic fabrics. Dry thoroughly after each outing. Store in a dry, cool place out of direct sunlight.

title: Cork top suface. Appears durable and well made
text: This yoga mat has cork on one side and TPE on the other. It is 68" x 24" x 5mm thick. It is thin enough to allow good balance in standing positions while thick enough to provide some cushioning when sitting or kneeling on it. I like having the top surface be cork rather than a synthetic material. I'm actually using this for stretching exercises rather than yoga, and I would be more comfortable when kneeling if the mat was a little thicker. However, the mat seems to be durable, fairly easy to tote around, and doesn't slide or stretch when I'm moving about on it.

title: Not for hot liquids. Not for children under 3 years old. Works fine.
text:
[[VIDEOID:60e1a032000f745b3d1151a200deb48c]] This water bottle is 2 5/8" across and 7" tall. It holds 12 ounces (350 mL). It has double wall vacuum insulation, but you aren't supposed to use it with hot liquids. They claim it keeps drinks cold for over 12 hours. So far, I've only tried it for a few hours, and it does keep cold water cool. The body of the bottle is food grade 18/8 stainless steel. The lid is BPA-, lead-, and phthalate-free. The lid is a hard plastic (recycling symbol 5, Polypropylene) with a plastic straw on the inside. Because of the straw, you hold the bottle upright when drinking rather than tipping the bottle. The straw can be removed and reattached. The spout flips up to drink and down to seal the bottle so it's non-leak. I initially had trouble getting the lid to screw on, but once I did it once, I've never had trouble again.

Use instructions: Cold liquids only. Not for use with hot liquids. Hot liquids may cause burns. Do not put in freezer. Bottle is not microwave safe. Not for use with carbonated drinks. Not for children under 3 years of age. Made in China.

Care instructions: Wash all parts with soap and warm water prior to use and after each use. Rinse thoroughly. While bottle and cap are top rack dishwasher safe, we recommend washing by hand to preserve the life of the graphics and the bottle.

title: Comfortable for short people. Maybe a bit small for tall or overweight people.
text:
This camping chair is very similar to ones that I already own and enjoy. This chair is sturdy and well-made. The seat edge hits my legs further back from behind my knees than usual. Since I am 5' 4", I find this more comfortable than some bigger chairs. The seat is about 16.5" from the back seam to the front edge. The entire chair is 35" tall from floor to the back top. There is a cup holder on the right armrest. On the right side of the seat, there's a hanging magazine holder that is 10.5" across with a front, mesh flap that is 7" deep. There is an insulated cooler in the left chair arm that both zips and velcros shut, and it's 7" deep, 2.5" across, 7" high. The chair can fold up and be stored in a carry bag.

Update 5/15/18: This chair is narrower than our usual camp chairs, which means the supports/legs come through the seat right against my thighs. This will be true for most people. When my legs are tired from a long walk, sitting in this chair for more than a few minutes just makes my legs stiffer (rather than being restful) since my sore muscles partly rest against the supports. Anyway, I initially gave the chair 5 stars, but now I give it 4 stars.

title: Soft touch bottle leaks. Need to change carbon filter after 25 gallons.
text:
This kit comes with a LifeStraw, a backwashing syringe, and a soft-touch bottle. They recommend using the syringe to backwash the LifeStraw once before using and a minimum of twice a day during use to prevent the filter from getting clogged and to help remove any trapped particles. The LifeStraw is 6.5" long, 1.5" across, and has a two stage water filter. The first stage is a hollow fiber membrane filter that removes 99.999999% of bacteria and 99.999% of protozoa. It is good for 2,000 liters (500 gallons). The stage one filter will no longer filter water when the product has reached the end of its working life. The second stage is a replaceable active carbon fiber capsule that reduces lead and chlorine, improves taste, reduces bad odor and organic chemical matter. It lasts 100 liters (25 gallons). Both ends of the LifeStraw unscrew for easy access to the filters or to allow it to dry out when not in use.

You start by backwashing the LifeStraw, which is fairly simple to do and does not require clean water. I then filled the soft-touch bottle with water and screwed the LifeStraw in place. The first 5 to 10 sips through the LifeStraw tasted very nasty and I spit it out. Then the water started tasting clean. It was not difficult to suck the water through the straw when the filters are new. Evidently, it gets harder as the filter life gets near its end, so you might not get a full 500 gallons use in real life. Also, you can squeeze the soft-touch bottle to force water through the LifeStraw, which I was able to do.

I set the soft-touch bottle down on its side as there is no way to set it (or hang it) upright. I came back 10 minutes later to find a puddle of water under the joint where the soft body joins with the harder material of the neck of the bottle. The leak was not where the LifeStraw screwed into the bottle but was a flaw in the bottle. You can also simply place the end of the LifeStraw in a cup of water and suck in the water, which I have been doing since this incident. It can also be used with a gravity filter, a hydration bladder, or screwed into the top of any standard plastic bottle.

I was disappointed that the soft-touch bottle leaked and that there was no way to secure it upright when filled with water. The LifeStraw seems to work fine, and I've been wanting to try one for it years. The LifeStraw is a small enough size to be easily portable for use when hiking, but the syringe is nearly as big as the LifeStraw and so doubles the amount of room needed to pack both.

title: Helps keep food cool while traveling
text:
The main, cooled compartment is 10.5" x 7.5" x 7" tall. It is a family-sized cooler bag for food or beverages. The gel for cooling is in the front, bottom, and back walls of the cooler. The side walls are just canvas and do not contain gel, and I don't think the top has gel either. The cooler walls can be collapsed so the cooler is flatter and smaller when you place it in the freezer. They recommend cooling it in the freezer for 12 hours before use. There is a zippered, flat outside pocket in the front that is 8.5" wide and 5.5" tall. There is a handle on top of the of the cooler under which is a compartment that will hold things like napkins, phones, utensils, etc. The opening is 5.5" wide. There is no zipper to secure this pocket. Due to the handle being right above the opening for this area, it is not highly convenient to get things in and out. This compartment is about 2" deep and covers the entire width and length of the lid. There is also a zippered, flat outer pocket tucked away on the bottom of the bag. It has an attached pull-out bit of fabric, though I'm not sure what it's for. I'm also not sure what you'd want to place in this pocket, since it's between the ground and the bottom gel wall of the cooler and weight will be on it. The cooler also has an adjustable carry strap. The cooler interior is easy to clean up if there are spills. It seems to be working okay to keep food cool for a few hours while traveling.

This cooler contains polyethylene foam. The advertising says that the "cooler is made from nontoxic poly canvas and has a food-safe, water-resistant lining" and it is made from "...PVC-, BPA-, phthalate-, formaldehyde- and lead-free materials."

title: One goal didn't assemble without a fight, but the game is fun and seems sturdy
text:
I like the game, but there was a problem during the assembly. There are two goals with 3 colored rods that are screwed into the supports. The supports are uprights screwed into a base. Each upright slides over a projection on a base before they can be screwed together. Well, one goal assembled easily and quickly, but the other goal didn't. The projection on the base was too wide and we couldn't get the upright onto it until we used a power grinder to narrow the projection down. Also, one of the colored rods didn't want to screw on, though it can be done using force.

The game is for ages 6 and up. I don't know why this game is called a "golf toss" as there's nothing golf-related about it. It's a bolo toss. You hold one ball in your palm with the rest of the bolo hanging below, give an underhanded throw through the goal area, and get points if you get the bolo to wrap around a colored rod. The goals stayed upright without problem even when on uneven ground. I have no idea why they suggest placing the goals/players opposite each other and alternating throws as then you're throwing objects at your opposing players (unless you're really, really good at hitting the target).

We just put the goals side-by-side. There are 3 white bolos and 3 black bolos. They say each person has 4 throws per turn (yet don't explain why they only provided 3 bolos each). They also say adults should stand 25 ft away from the goal and kids 6-12 years old should stand 15 feet away. We've never done bolo toss before. At about 15 ft away with 6 tosses, I can usually get 2-3 tosses to wrap around the goal rods. At 25 ft., its 0 out of 6. The other players could only get points on 1 out of 6 tosses at 15 ft. Maybe we'll back up as we get better.

UPDATE 5/18/18: I've used this golf toss a fair amount, including using it as a game at a church "fair." No one was treating the game carefully, and it got a full days use. No problems with the bolos. The action of the bolos winding around the horizontals does slowly unscrew them, though, so we tighten the screws every few hours so the goal doesn't get too wobbly. People enjoy this game.

title: Easy to grip. Cold liquids only.
text:
Though made from borosilicate glass, the bottom of the silicone sleeve states that the bottle is made for "Cold liquids only." The "wide" mouth is 1" across inner measurement. So wider than a store-bought filtered water plastic bottle, but you still need a bottle brush to clean the inside. The bottle is 19" tall and 2.5" wide at the widest point (with the silicone sleeve on). This is a good width for me as wider bottles are too wide for me to get a secure grip. The lighter weight and silicone sleeve also allow a good grip. The bottle does hold 17 ounces of liquid and hasn't leaked when the cap is on. The outside of the cap is made from bamboo and the inside appears to be plastic (100% BPA free). According to the Q&A section of the product page, the plastic part is "BPA-free, lead-free, and phthalate-free tritan plastic."

Care instructions: CAP: Handwash only. BOTTLE: Wash bottle before first use. We recommend hand-washing with warm, soapy water or on the top rack of your dishwasher. Do not remove the sleeve. STORE WITH CAP OFF. Cation: This bottle is not suitable for hot liquids. Do not place the bottle in the microwave or freezer.

title: Fits waists from about 27" to 41" around
text: I measure this running belt as fitting waists from about 27" to 41" around. The waistband is elastic, so there is some give. The belt clips closed. There is a small reflective strip around the zipper and on the belt (which ends up near the pouch unless you have a smaller waist). The zipper opens and closes smoothly. The pouch expands, and the inside space is about 8.5" long by about 2.5" tall and the bottom can expand about 2.75" deep. Keep in mind that highly rigid objects won't be as comfortable as flexible objects in the pouch. My old flip cell phone and house key fit alright. The interior of the pouch looks like it's been waterproofed, but I haven't tested to see if it is. Overall, works fine for my daily walking routine.

title: Fun game
text:
This set comes with 2 blue rubber horseshoes, 2 green rubber horseshoes, 2 plastic ground stakes which can be pressed into soft soil (do not use a hammer!) and 2 free standing targets made up of a 1' wide rubber circle base, a weighted plastic stake, and a stake support base. The horseshoes are large (6.5" x 7.5")--much larger than a real horseshoe. You hold them by the top of the U and toss them at the stake. The instructions say that the stakes should be set up 10-15 feet from each other, with one team throwing from one side and the other team throwing from the other side. They suggest 4 people playing, but it works for 1-4 players. You score points if the horseshoe lands with the post inside the U (3 points) or the horseshoe touching the post (2 points) or a certain distance from the stake (1 point).

I initially used the 14" ground stakes pushed halfway into soft soil, and the stakes held well against horseshoes hitting them. The 6" free-standing stake is shorter, so a throw that might catch the ground stake and make a score might fly over the free-standing stake. I was surprised, but the free-standing stakes also took hits without falling over--probably because they're weighted and the wide circle base pulls them back down when hit. Anyway, the kids enjoyed this, though we started off much closer than 10' until they got a feel for the game. The free-standing stakes were easy to put together and take apart for storage. They do need to have dirt and grass brushed off before storage.

title: Works
text: This is a silicone lube. You can spray using the straw nose for very targeted control or spray a wider area when the straw is down. I used the straw and sprayed the whole vertical track, then realized I'd used too much as it ran down the length and pooled. However, it did work as the window now slides more easily. They spray is clear and protects against corrosion as well as lubricates. They say it's safe to use on most materials (metal, wood, and most plastics and vinyl (except clear polycarbonate and polystyrene). So don't get it on your eye glasses, as they may be polycarbonate.

title: Problems with the buttons, but fit as expected
text:
These pants fit as expected. The side-elastic in the waistband doesn't have much give, but it does make bending over more comfortable. The "Break-Up Country" design was of brown leaves, twigs, and tree trunks against a vague, dark-green background. So brown and greens in color. The pants have a metal zipper that worked smoothly. However, the top button was difficult for me to get through the opening as the hole was nearly too small. (Update: this top button has actually gotten easier to use as I've worn the pants, so it's not so much an issue anymore.) There are deep, open pockets at the hips. There are also deep, hidden-button pockets on your butt and along the upper legs. These buttons slip into holes that are covered with a flap of fabric, so it's very difficult to button them. However, the pockets sag open (even if empty) if you don't button them. I've ended up buttoning them and just not using those pockets. The pants are a light-weight polyester fabric style that I'm not used to, but I find them comfortable.

Care Instructions: Machine wash cold. Only non-chlorine bleach. Tumble dry medium. Do not iron. Do not dry clean. Pre-shrunk.

title: Heavy, but plastic-free, wide mouth for pouring liquids into the bottle, and works well
text: The first thing I noticed is that it's heavy. Heavier than another, smaller glass bottle that I have. After you add up to 20 ounces of liquid, it's even heavier. A gray, textured silicone sleeve covers the bottle and provides a good grip, so I'm not worried about dropping it, but this is heavier than I'd care to take on a hike. The silicone sleeve provides a slight amount of insulation, so hot tea isn't a burn threat, but the bottle isn't meant to keep liquids cool or hot. The widest part (including the sleeve) is 2 7/8 inches across. The mouth of the glass jar is wide, 2" across, so it's easy to pour my tea into it or wash the glass parts. There's metal lid that you screw to the top of the glass jar so that you have a narrower, easier to drink from outlet. The lip of this metal lid has a curve that helps prevent spills or dribbles while drinking. There's a silicone plug to stick into the top of the metal lid to keep the liquid inside when you're not using it. I've used it several times now, and I've had NO troubles at all with leaking, opening, using, or cleaning it.

title: May be too big for a woman's hand
text: I'm a woman, and I wear large gloves due to my long fingers. The pictures all show this ring in a man's hand, so I didn't realize how big it'd be in my hand. When I'm gripping the ring ready to flex it, it reaches from my palm to my fingers with the end joints of my fingers just on top. So I'm trying to bend this ring with the tips of my fingers, which really stresses my tendons. My mom, who has "medium glove" sized hands, could also barely flex the ring in part due to how big the ring was in her hand. I'd either recommend that women try this ring in person before buying it or avoid it. However, I asked two men to try it, and they had no problem with the size and could use it as intended. Both men had men's "large glove" sized hands. Everyone thought it was harder to flex than "medium" would suggest, though. It probably wouldn't work as a physical therapy device for someone recovering from an injury. I was hoping to use it to strengthen my weak hand from a long-ago injury, but I couldn't even use it in my good hand. This ring is 3.5" across at it's widest point and about 13/16" thick.

title: Might want to try these on for correct sizing
text:
I'd recommend trying these gloves on in person to make sure you get the right fit. I normally wear ladies-large for gardening gloves, mainly because I have long fingers. I wear medium ladies gloves for fingerless gloves. Since the back of this glove is made of stretchy material and the velcro strap over the wrist allows adjustment across the palm and wrist area, I was sure this Medium size would fit me. And they do...kinda. The thumb and pointer finger sleeves have a snug fit which helps keep that part of the glove in place, but the rest of the glove fits more loosely. I'm not sure how a "fitness glove" is supposed to fit, but I guess I expected the stretchy material to actually need to stretch. Perhaps regular weight lifters have more muscle in their hands than I do.

Anyway, the outside of the palm side of the glove has leather patches over the base of fingers and thumb, along the edge of the hand, and at the ends of each finger. This gives a good grip and protects your hand. The glove material doesn't look particularly sweat-absorbent, yet my hand didn't get sweaty-slick while doing hard exercise with these on.

Made in Pakistan. There was no care (washing) instructions. Palm: 60% polyester, 34 polyamide, 6% PU. Back: 80%polyester, 10% nylon, 10% elastane.

Update: The circumference of my hand just below the knuckles (not including my thumb) is 7", so according the the glove size chart (Medium = 7-7.5" or small = 6.5-7") and medium should fit me though a small size might have as well.

title: Borosilicate glass bottle with cross-hatch silicone sleeve for good grip
text:
I've wanted a glass bottle for some time, so I was excited to get this. It's 9" tall, a 2.75" diameter at the bottom, and holds about 18 fluid ounces. The bottle is made from borosilicate glass, so it's strong (for glass) and more resistant to heat or cold shock than soda-lime glass. The outer, threaded part on the lid contains plastic, but the parts that contact the liquid are a metal inner "plug" and an O-ring. The lid is easy to screw on (and I have weak hands). I've not had any leaks when the bottle tips over with the lid on.

The mouth of the bottle is 1 1/8" across on the inside. If you're getting water from the faucet, it's easy enough to fill the bottle. I've ended up using a funnel when filling the bottle with my hot tea, though, as I apparently don't have a consistently steady hand. I can get a bottle brush into the bottle's mouth, though you can also put the bottle through the dish washer.

I've got size "medium womens" hands, and I've never felt like I might drop the bottle as the cross-hatch silicone sleeve design provides a good grip. The bottom of the sleeve covers the entire bottom of the bottle, which provides some padding and non-slip effect. The cross-hatch design allows my fingers to contact the hot (from my tea) side, though. I just wait for the tea to cool, but that might not be convenient for some people. Obviously, this bottle isn't insulated, so the liquid will cold or warm up to room temperature fairly quickly. It's a nice bottle.

title: Look like a good beginner set
text:
This set seems like a good, basic exercise-bands kit. There are 5 resistance bands:

yellow = extra light = 2-4 lbs resistance
blue = light = 4-6 lbs resistance
green = medium = 10-12 lbs resistance
black = heavy = 15-20 lbs resistance
red = extra heavy = 25-30 lbs resistance

You choose a band with the desired resistance, clip it to the 2 handles or a handle and the Velcro ankle strap, and do the desired exercises. There's also a "door anchor" nylon strap with a fat weight in one end. You thread the exercise band through the loop on one end on the anchor, then place it along the edge of the door and close the door. The fat end prevents the strap from slipping through the gape in the door and thus you can do some exercises with the exercise band centered above or level with you. This does, however, put some stress on the door. Not so much with the lighter weights, but I suspect it would with the heavier weights. The equipment seems well-made and so far I've had no problems with it in its first week of light use. They have a book with 18 exercises described and several illustrated with a color photo. They provide a lifetime warranty.

Some of their warnings:
-Do not overstretch the resistance bands [though they don't say exactly how far is too far]
-Always wear safety glasses when using resistance bands [and safety glasses are not included]

title: Made with NATURAL rubber latex; only strength exercises in booklet
text:
Now, who wouldn't love owning a giant rubber band? :D I'm mildly allergic to synthetic latex, but I'm fine with natural latex. This resistance band is made with natural rubber latex, and I've had no allergic reaction to it. I've only used it for a few days now, and a certain latex smell does rub off onto my hands and skin from use, but I'm assuming this will disappear with use. The band is 0.5" wide, 0.25" thick, and about 40" in length (or a 84" outer circumference).

The band comes with a booklet with arm and leg strength-building exercises. Ten use just the band and your body. Nine require a door anchor (not included) along with the band. The product video--available online--briefly shows ways to use the band to improve speed or to assist exercises. The box says it can be used to improve flexibility, but I haven't seen any suggested exercises for the band with that focus.

I like resistance bands, but most are uncomfortable to stand on or difficult to grip. My right hand is weak, so doing strength exercises with bands that require a strong grip aren't very useful to me. This band looked like something I could get my whole body into (somewhat literally) so I thought I could modify the exercises so my weak grip wouldn't matter. Well, most of their suggested exercises do have you gripping the band with your hands, but other suggested exercises do work well for me. I had no problem standing on the band--it's squared rather than round and 0.25" thick. The band appears to be well-made and likely to last well.

I'm a 5'4" woman and I live on a farm, so I regularly lift 25-50lbs. If I bought a resistance band, I'd probably go with the Low rather than Medium, at least to start out. I could do the leg exercises with the Medium band, but most of the arm strength exercises were very difficult (partly due to my weak hand). My dad--nearly 6' tall and still strong at 68 years old--could do both leg and arm exercises and get a good workout from them. He even modified some exercises to do while sitting down as he's wanted some exercises he can do while watching TV. I do wish they had more suggested exercises than the arm and leg strengthening ones, but I'm sure I can modify some traditional exercises.

There is a limited, 1 year warranty. It's made in Thailand.

title: Works well for my needs
text:
I've been looking for a folding knife that I could use around the farm. This knife is 4.5 inches long and 1.5 inches wide when folded, so it has a nice sized blade while still being small enough not to get in my way when clipped onto my pocket. (There is a strong, nearly 3-inch-long metal clip securely screwed into the knife handle.) The entire knife appears to be made out of a sturdy, stainless steel. The handle has a texture and finger indentations to assure a secure grip when used.

I've never used a folding knife with a locking mechanism, but I expected at least some advertising pointing out how the special double-locking mechanism works. There wasn't any information included with the knife, but it was fairly easy to figure out. The linear lock is beneath the blade and automatically locks when the blade is fully extended. The safety switch is a toggle on the handle behind the blade. You can push it up when the blade is open to prevent the linear lock from being depressed (which would allow the blade to close). To close the blade, push the toggle back to the original position and depress the linear lock while folding the blade. Once I figured it out, it was easy to do.

Since it's winter, I haven't had much time to test the blade out for how well it keeps it edge or other wear issues. I'll post an update is anything significant comes up.

title: Very bright, yet dimmable. Would be great for camping
text:
I got this LED lantern to use as an emergency light and for when we need an area flashlight at night on our farm. It's worked well for this purpose. I no longer camp, but my first thought on testing this lantern was that I wished I'd had something like this back in my camping days. It's very bright compared to other lantern flashlights I've had in the past, but you can dim the light to about half strength using the dimmer button. You can use the lantern as a directional light or extend the light up above the base to make it an area light. There's a stand that can be pulled out from the back of the base so you can put the lantern on a table or floor. The orange grip is lightly textured and rubber-like for a secure hold when carrying it.

When you rotate the light upward, the white plastic back reflector is exposed. This is how you access the battery area. There are two flat-screw-head type locks that need to be rotated clockwise by a quarter turn to access the batteries. I actually opened them using the back of a clothespin. lol. The lantern comes with 4 batteries, but it can take 8 AA batteries--for longer life, I assume, but I've not tried it.

The on-off button is on the back of the base. You push the button to turn the light on or off, or you hold it to dim the light and release the button when the light is at the desired level. At first, I occasionally had trouble with not removing my finger quickly enough from the button and getting a dim instead of turning the light off. I just needed to learn to "jab" the button rather than taking my time. The lantern looks fairly durable and easy to clean, but I've only given it light use so far.

The instruction manual is pretty brief, but it does cover all the "how to use" information. Instructions you might wish to know now: "To disable Try Me mode, remove batteries from compartment and wait 10 seconds. Reinsert batteries and wait 10 seconds before pressing switch." and "Lantern is water resistant and suitable for use outside. Do not submerse or attempt to operate under water."

According to the packaging, the light was made in China and the batteries were made in Singapore.

title: Very nice, inexpensive ski goggles
text: These are a pretty nice quality item given the price.  These are by no means a professional set of goggles that will last you forever, but if you are, like me, an inexperienced, once-a-year skier, then this pair will likely last you a good long while.

title: Pretty heavy
text: As far as kickstands go, this one is well-made, but it's pretty heavy.  With nothing to it but some plastic sizers, some chrome bolts and the black kickstand itself, this is a very easy install, and it works well to hold up my bike, much better than the traditional "beneath the pedals" variety that this item replaces.  Good value, easy install, and a bit heavy.  Works perfectly.

title: Camping Blanket
text: Material is nice, blanket is warm, the included bag fits the blanket when it's tightly folded.  Even with this though, the blanket is a bit poofier than I'd expect from a military-style blanket, but it provides a little more comfort than a traditional stiff woolen blend.  Overall, it makes for a good car emergency bag that will fit into a tight space, and can be used as a picnic blanket in a pinch.  Good value too.

title: Great for beginners
text: This is a nice beginner's skateboard.  Obviously, it can't compete with something where the trucks themselves cost twice what this entire board does, but this one has a nice combination of parts that are cost-effective for learners.  The trucks are metal, although they're a lightweight metal.  The wheels are a nice composite plastic that spins fine and rolls smoothly.  The board itself has good griptape, minimal flex and a nice pattern on the underside.  It won't work for someone who knows what they're doing - neither the board nor the trucks will sustain too much repetitive impact - but for someone who needs to learn how to move, travel and maybe do an ollie or two, this will allow them to satisfy their desire to learn the basics without spending a few hundred dollars.

title: It's smaller than you'd think
text:
This is a nice half "Bosu" ball like you'd see in your local gym...except it's a lot smaller than the ones you're used to. Obviously, there's a nice price discount you get with this one, and it can still do everything you'd expect - balance exercises, push ups, basic arm exercises, etc. It's just small.

It does have a set of feet on the bottom that really make it quite convenient to use on a hard floor.

My biggest concern aside from the size is that the resistance bands that come with the kit are pretty low-quality, won't last too long, and barely provide any resistance. I'm tall, and I still don't feel them stretching until I'm at my shoulder height.

title: 2/3 worked perfectly
text:
Instructions for installing this system are short, but adequate for the job. It really isn't very hard, but if you'd like more than a picture and a few half-sentences, you won't find it. The kit comes with everything you need, but includes zero extra pieces.

We installed 2/3 of this rack with no problem. The third segment continued to pull away from the wall no matter how we hung it. Looks like a few of the wall anchors failed, and ultimately, it needs to hold quite a bit of weight if you're using all three segments to capacity, so we felt safer putting up just two.

Fortunately, the other two segments hold all the bikes we need it to, and it holds them well. We fit four wide, although this is the kind of system that requires you to remove pretty much all of the bikes when you are trying to pull a specific bike. It works for our family if we hang them in an alternating pattern, and it feels very sturdy.

I don't know if this is a glowing recommendation or one that should be followed with caution, so three stars feels appropriate.

title: All the benefits, none of the hassle
text:
This is a nice set of cordless jump rope handles that are perfect for the uncoordinated. I'd love to jump rope, but I don't have the patience for interrupting my exercise to wrestle with the cord that I mistimed for the 100th time. This gives you all the benefit with none of the hassle. Balls spin easily on the cords with minimal effort needed.

Handles and balls have a bit of weight to them, but the weight is removable. One does feel slightly heavier than the other, but unfortunately, I don't have a scale to test this.

title: Nice wool socks
text: These are nice wool socks that fit well, and are nicely colored.  I ran a few pairs through my washing machine and dryer at various temperatures, and they did not shrink, lose color or resize.  They are comfortable socks that are slightly warming, but not too thick or too hot.  You can wear them with dress shoes as easily as with hiking pants, and that's a nice touch.  I'd buy more at this price.

title: EVANTEK First Aid Kit
text:
A nice pouch with a nice mix of various first aid items, from band-aids to wraps to pins and wipes. Most of the materials are good enough of quality to do the job quickly on your way home or to the hospital.

I have a few complaints. The towelette has instructions in a foreign language. Instructions in general are a bit lacking with the items inlcluded here. The first aid kit includes a lot of survival gear, including a whistle and a flashlight with charger, that might come in handy in a pinch, but could have been better utilized with a better variety of items that are more specifically first aid related.

Overall, yes, it's a little odd for a first aid kit, but for a vehicle emergency kit, this is a good kit that has everything you need for basic first aid.

title: Nice jump rope
text:
The handles are well-constructed, and it comes with two cables that you can cut or stuff to ensure that you're gettng the right size of equipment. The ropes swing easily on the handles, and it looks very difficult to damage or break. When you're done, there is a storage bag you can use, but I am allowing gravity to work out some of the spiraling and I'm hanging mine on the wall of the home gym.

There are no instructions that come with this item. That's the only downside, but Youtube can provide you with a few tutorials on how to set this up.

title: No give, very stiff, high quality
text: This is a very nice, very stiff foam roller for stretching out aching muscles post workout.  There is no give to this thing whatsoever, and it is not soft, so if those are two things you're looking for, look elsewhere.  If you want a durable foam roller that is stiff and will help you after an exercise, this is it.  It looks like it should be pretty easy to dent, but it isn't, and is lightweight and able to survive being thrown around a bit.

title: How useful is this?
text:
This is a heavy tool with steel construction. Hinges swing smoothly, and there are a lot of tools included. I don't know how useful many of them are, though. There's a bottle opener, for example. I can't imagine needing that in a pinch to fix my bike. The nail puller is the kind you'd use to remove a nail from a board, but using that tool on a bike tire, it's much less useful. The hex-wrenches require you to use the middle body of the tool, so the applications of this are quite minimal, as the nut would have to be sitting in exactly the right location in order to use this.

It would work, and it looks like it's handy, but on closer inspection, you can find much better tools out there.

title: Good storage, you might want a different phone holder.
text:
This is a bulky bag with a clear plastic pocket on top that allows you to hold your smartphone in an easily accessible spot right below your handlebars. The storage aspect of this is strong, the bag will certainly hold up, and it will hold a good amount of stuff. It's also quite easy to install on any bike, and it will fit every standard sized cell phone.

The phone holding aspect might need a little work. Yes, it does work, and you can access your screen buttons through the plastic. If you're using this for an "always on" function - like Maps or Youtube Music - then you'll think it's just fine. If you want any acces to your power and volume buttons, or your headphone jack, or if you plan on listening to a podcast or music that doesn't require your screen to be on, then you'll need to stop in order to adjust or turn on your screen, as these functions will be hidden underneath a stiff zipper and a velcro pad.

There are other phone holding devices you can clip on your bike that will allow you full access to everything, and if this is what you need, then you should buy those products instead of this one. If you want a deep storage compartment for bike tools or other items, and want "always on" functionality, then this is a great buy.

title: Overall, quality kits
text:
This is a kit of varying strengths of resistance bands, along with the handles you'll need to use them effectively.

The unfortunate part of this is that most similar kits are going to contain a more detailed description of what strength the bands are (i.e. 10 pounds), while this one only declares them to be "very light resistance" and so forth. As with many of these sets, the resistance feels very limited, though you can double or triple up on the bands to make it substantially more difficult.

In total, having worked with a few sets of these in the past, these are pretty good in terms of construction, and don't seem set to tear or break. Handles are well formed, easy to grip and use. The bag could be a lot bigger, and that would certainly add some convenience. The included instructions were surpirsingly readable, and contained some good information, as well as a few suggested exercises, which is great for beginners who haven't used resistance bands before.

title: Nice camping mess kit
text: This is a very lightweight camping accessory that really serves it's purpose well.  The spoon, fork and knife arrive stored outside of the compartment, but that's just for show - they fold in perfectly and seal tightly when you rearrange the contencts of the kit (the knife and spoon are the same utensil, you just need to detach them from their snap-in slot and you can use them freely).  As for the kit itself, the cup and plate have rubber grips on the bottom, which is greatly appreciated, and the cup appears to be well-constructed; I don't think I'll be needing to replace it, even though it does collapse to fit inside the normal compartment.  If you need to be on the move, you can simply seal up the kit with the mess inside and not worry about it seeping out to destroy and dirty your other supplies.  Highly recommended.

title: Good Goggles, reasonable price
text: These are not bad goggles.  We go through a ton over summer, and about a half-ton over the winter at the indoor pool, so we need as many as we can get at a reasonable price.  Our 6-year-old gives these a seal of approval because of their bright colors and "they don't hurt my eyes" like googles with more serious suction.  These are great for kids.  The high age limit of 15 is pretty ambitious - I think you'll be stretching it to put these on a ten or twelve-year old - but for younger children, these are good goggles at a reasonable price.

title: Good Quality
text:
A basic, no-frills yoga mat that comes with a bag. The mat itself is good quality, made of a good-feeling material, and it won't slip. I personally prefer a thicker mat, but this is pretty average for the market. Color looks good, and it appears rather durable.

The bag is lower-grade plastic and mesh, and it doesn't feel good at all. Its kind of an unadvertised bonus, but I think if you use it frequently, you'll want something nicer.

title: Good little tote for your bike
text:
This is the kind of thing that every biker should have. It's feather-light, portable storage that won't get in the way with your pedaling while you're out and about. Admittedly, it doesn't hold much, but it could easily store a portable phone charging device, a few snacks for the road, your wallet and keys and a multitool all together, and that's a valuable storage item.

I took off a star for two reasons. First, it sits very low on my mountain bike, dangling a bit under my seat, while it's tight underneath my wife's. Secondly, there is a pouch on the underside that seems functional, and is when the bag is fully packed, but if there is any give in the structure of the bag, the pouch is quite loose.

Overall, though this is a great item.

title: Bulky, but it works
text:
This little firestarter kit is nice, but it's not compact. For those with fumbling fingers who can't manipulate a smaller kit, this will be great, but for those who value a tiny, concealable, EDC item, this will not suffice. I suppose that technically, you could mount this to your keyring, but you wouldn't want to carry it in your pocket. No, this is a separate item that you're likely packing in your kit for camping, or putting somewhere for storage, not typical use.

That said, it's a steel and magnesium sparking kit that is going to last some time. It's easy to use if you've used any other similar items.

title: WHy batteries?
text:
This is a scooter that will earn a lot of points for uniqueness. None of the kids in the neighborhood have seen anything like it. It appears to have very good construction overall from a stability standpoint, and I don't feel like it's going to fall apart any time soon. Construction is literally one screw and one nut, although it's awkward to install given that both screw head and nut are recessed into the structure.

That said, there are a few questionable design points that lower it's score for us. The lights are controlled by batteries rather than the motion of the wheels, the latter of which would not only save us from replacing the batteries as frequently as we are, but also would keep us from having to adjust them, which we need to do on a pretty consistent basis. It's a scooter, so it sees some pretty rough play, and that can often jar a battery loose since they don't sit particularly tightly.

In addition to this, despite my comment about overalll good construction, the switch that controls whether it is folded or open is made of some very cheap plastic, and appears likely to break quickly, espeically with how difficult it is to pull when tightened.

Overall, it's a gimmick that, if you really want to put up with, is pretty cool. For an everyday use item, you probably want something simpler that won't require constant monitoring.

title: Tremendous training tool
text: This is a great piece of exercise equipment.  It's a punching bag that fills with heavy sand or water, ensuring that you have enough weight to substantiate heavy hitting, but it's thin enough that it stores nicely.  What makes it a little different is that the punching surface is supported by a spring, meaning that you can punch from any direction and the bag will push back instead of tipping over.  It doesn't take up too much room, but it's also not too heavy to move back and forth from a corner if you're forced to work out in an enclosed space.

title: Quite pleased
text:
This is a very nice bike light/battery combo. With a simple twisting motion, you can turn it on, and then an additional slight twist runs it through 5 alternate modes - super bright, very bright, low light, strobe, occasional blink - and it lasts long enough at low light setting to last for some time.

A few caveats - if you plan on doing an extremely long night trip, you have to use a low-light setting, as the high power setting drains the battery quickly. At 3350 mAh, the battery doesn't last an extremely long time (I had about 25% charge left after 4 hours use at low setting), but it charges quickly, and for a combo device, it's not too heavy (it's also clearly meant to take a bit of a beating, so I'm sure that part of it's bulk is thicker than usual casing). I find the mounting bracket to be very secure, and it includes a rubber tightener in case you have a slim handlebar rack.

Overall, I'm quite pleased with this device. It offers exactly what I need, without being too excessively bulky.

title: Great hiking pack
text: This is an excellent, lightweight backpack that can go anywhere.  I love the built-in hydration pack, which is very useful for any outdoor adventure, and there is reflective and high-colored spots that will help you stand out to other humans in the forest - helpful if you're deep in a hunting territory.  This backpack can hold quite a lot of equipment, and even has small pouches on the bottom wrap-around sections that go across your stomach.  I am a small bit concerned with the fabric, as it is thin, and very lightweight, but it's waterproof and tear resistant.  Seems like it will hold up for plenty of use.

title: An excellent choice for a smaller sized football.
text: This football looks great in Chicago black and orange, and ships ready to play.  It lights up when it hits the ground or on a stiff impact, which makes it easy to find in night games, and it's made of nice materials.  It will even come with a tool that helps you remove the battery cover to replace the batteries when needed.  An excellent choice for a smaller sized football.

title: Excellent Product.
text: There's really only two concerns that I have regarding these kinds of products - is it durable, and does it give your water a funny aftertaste?  The material is fantastic - thick matte plastic whose edges won't get stuck on other parts of your clothes.  Aftertaste?  Nothing discernible.  The valve that secures the tube to the bag clicks in place, you remove the guard on the tip and you're good to go.  Excellent product.

title: 2.5 person football shaped tent.
text: I'm not really all that big on camping, but I got this tent to take a little overnight trip to our backyard with my daughter, who loved the novelty.  I do have enough camping experience to know that a "4-person" really means that two is going to be a tight fit, and this tent is no exception.  This tent was much easier to assemble than the last 4-person tent I tried to put together, and the bright color really stands out, which is nice.  The footprint of this tent was a little footballish, where is is longer in the middle than it is in corners, but that really helped to accomodate my 6'2 frame.  Like all tents, you won't ever be able to get it back in the box once it's out, but it still does stay rather compact.

title: Football gloves
text: These gloves fit nice, and are not bulky in any way.  My hands tend to run as XLs, but the Larges fit tightly, so that's good.  They are coated with a sticky substance, so they're not really "All Purpose" - they're for catching footballs mostly, and they'll do that nicely.  As a test, I ran then under both hot and cold water, and they retained their stickiness.  I image that they'll be somewhat difficult to clean in between uses, as hairs and fibers seem to stick to them quite well, but that's well within their rights.  Great product

title: One of my most important puchases ever.
text:
I don't go anywhere without this thing.

Personally, I think this is by far the best of the fitbit line, and only the writstband model would be competition. The bit itself is accurate, durable, and my wife's has even survived a few trips through the washing machine unharmed. The case is perfectly molded to the body of the bit, and fits easily on pant pockets, or, as Fitbit recommends, on underwear. It's bluetooth enabled, and unloads your data automatically, although if you replace a battery, it does need to be Synced manually so the time will match up.

We had the bar version earlier, and we didn't like the way that it felt. It was significantly larger than this model, and didn't clip onto our clothes as nicely, and as a result, we broke both of our models soon after getting them. The wristband model is decent, although it is much more expensive, and it's not nearly as discreet, and it's hard to justify wearing it in certain environments.

Both my wife and I have found that it's excellent motivation to get up and get moving, and that's exactly why you'd want one.

title: AB rocket twister
text:
For about 5 years, I've been the not-so-proud owners of a much lesser piece of abdominal training equipment, the kind that cushions your head and helps you roll through crunches. It's been nice, but it hurts my neck and it doesn't do anything for your lower abs, which is probably the biggest problem I have with it, and which is the reason that I use it far less than most of my other exercise equipment.

When I saw the Ab Rocket Twister, I immediately saw this as an improvement over what I had. It is that, certainly. The main function of this machine is actually opposite of what my old machine was used for - with the ab rocket twister, you usually end up pushing down rather than up. This has the added advantage of working your lower back muscles just a little bit as you work out, though I did notice that my abs were less strained after going through the exercise video with this than with my other piece of equipment.

It's a bit of a pain to assemble, and it's garishly colored, but it's pretty good for what it does. Keep in mind when you're looking at this that you could certainly do all of the exercises without the machine, and many more, without getting it. A good crunch-and-bicycle kick will do you far better than this will. However, if you need a stepping stone, then this is a good product to look at.

title: Works,but hard to do...
text:
I tried the shake weight, knowing full well that I would have to do the shaking. Many of the negative reviews of this product seem to think that the weight itself should be shaking, and that's the sole reason why they don't like it.

Overall, I thought this product was pretty good. It's very difficult to learn how to use, in order to keep it shaking while moving it around, and I think you have to make sure that you reverse your grip from time to time in order to get even work on both arms (if you hold it with your left hand on the bottom and the right hand on top, you're probably not working both evenly). The DVD, nor the product manual seem to indicate this, but I found that it was easy to figure that out by trying it.

If you're not going to take the time to work with this, just like any product, you will not succeed. You probably won't even figure out how to do it right, the shaking of the weight while trying to keep your muscles mostly stationary as they say you should do is actually very difficult. It will take practice, but for upper body exercise at home, I think this is a pretty good solution for home strength training.

I would have liked to see a wider range of weights, or at least a notch or something to add an extra one pound weight or something. As it is, once you use this often enough, you'll outgrow their "6 minute workout" and start needing something else.

title: Perfect for me
text:
I recently started playing disc golf again after about 20 years off. Right now I only throw 5 molds and 3 drivers, a mid and a putter. I have the putter in two different plastics, all others I just have one disc of, so I need to carry a total of 6 discs.

I do anticipate cycling the drivers and mids in base plastic, so I foresee me carrying 10-12 discs eventually, but this bag will still handle that. Right now, as a 46-year-old dad, I play with my 4-year-old and 9-year-old boys. This means I carry the 4-year-old's discs and a small jacket for him. I also actually carry a full-size bath towel right now because...boys and water hazards. And there's still plenty of room in this bag.

The putter pocket carries my driving/approach putter and my soft putting putter, the 3 slots inside carry my main three discs that I throw besides the putter, and there's room for all the other discs and kid gear that I carry.

The bag is comfortable to wear, the strap can be moved to the bottom right or bottom left side depending on how you want to carry it. When carried over my right shoulder and across my chest, the bag sits at a slight angle on your back. This is nice because it means you can leave the main compartment slightly unzipped to access your discs and not worry about them falling out as the zipper ends up being at an angle up from the ground. It stands up fine on the ground when it's full of discs and equipment, and it's pretty easy to get the discs in and out of, which was my only concern when I bought it.

As other reviews mention, it won't fit a huge 32 oz Nalgene water bottle, but I kind of plan on carrying something else in the drink compartment anyway. I could get my Klean Canteen in there and I would imagine there are others that fit just fine. The small compartment in the back carries three minis for me and I don't even feel them when it's on my back, but I also feel like my wallet, phone or anything else could be stowed in there without a problem. The carabiner is great and could hold a smaller golf towel when the summer months roll around for me or my car keys depending on what I want to do.

I really like that I can carry all my discs and still have room for a jacket or other supplies in the main compartment.

If you carry a fairly minimalist bag, are considering discing down, want a travel bag or a loaner bag to hand to a beginner friend on introductory rounds, this thing is perfect. I plan on using it for a long time to come.

title: Works Way Better Than Expected
text:
I ordered this item to have a handy way to inflate a slam ball after they lose air over time. Honestly, I wasn't expecting much. However, this little unit worked incredibly well.

And is super compact & lightweight (6.29" x 1.4" & weighing only 6.5oz).

I haven't tried, but don't see why you couldn't even inflate a bicycle tire with this unit as well. However, I probably wouldn't try with anything larger like a car or truck tire out of concern of damaging the pump.

There is an auto-shut off option (IE: when you use a ball preset the pump will turn off when it dispenses the appropriate amount of air for the selected ball), however, there is no pressure gauge. So, if you don't use the preset, then you have to go by feel (or have an air gauge on hand).

As far as my experiment, I didn't even use the presets. Just popped in the needle into my slam ball & turned on the pump. It inflated (my very deflated) slam ball in a matter of seconds. A success!

If you're constantly using a foot pump or bike pump to inflate your sports equipment, bike tires, etc.., then seriously consider this portable pump instead. Makes this process super easy. There's even an attachment that looks like it's to be used for blowing up balloons! Very cool!

title: A Little Assembly Required, But A Great Elliptical Once You're Done
text:
Expect a BIG box to arrive! This sucker weighs about 100lbs. So you may need help to move it & get it unboxed.

The manufacturer states 90% assembled, but it's probably more like 50%. The flywheel & deck components will come pre-assembled. You are in charge of basically 5 main assembly groups: the feet/legs, the vertical tube screws, the handles, the console (computer) & finally the pedals. All tools are included to allow you to get right to work.

It's not a hard assembly, but the documentation isn't the easiest to follow. Luckily, the manufacturer has an assembly video on their Amazon listing. So if you need help, definitely check that out. In fact, you may want to watch it first.

The most cumbersome part of the assembly is the feet/legs. This is b/c you must hold up the entire unit (front or back) to get the respective leg on. If you have a helper, then this will be easy. If, however, you're a lone wolf, then use something to "jack" up the bike. It makes this part MUCH easier. I had a scrap piece of 2x4 that I used (see pic) & it was very helpful.

Once the feet are on, you will move on to the vertical tube screws, then handles, then console & lastly, the computer. Again, these are all very easy parts to put together. Just lay out all parts first, watch the video & review which bolt/screw goes where BEFORE you start the assembly. It will make a big difference towards minimizing your frustration.

Also, BE AWARE that some bolts ARE ALREADY PRE-SCREWED INTO THE BIKE. So they will not be in the bolt bag. For example, I found this was the case for the pulse handle.

Once assembled, the bike works exactly as advertised. It's near silent, very compact (for an elliptical), but still feels very roomy, has 16 levels of resistance (magnetic) controlled by an adjustment dial & has a number of functions & biometrics that can be tracked such as distance, calories burned, time, etc..

Please note - to track PULSE, you must hold the center handles (called the PULSE HANDLES) as there are sensors built in that your palms will contact. However, if you remove your grip, then the pulse biometric will disappear from the computer screen.

A more accurate method, would be to use a fitness tracker (like a FitBit, Apple Watch or dozens of other makes & models). This way you can track all of your stats in one place (steps, cals burned, distance, etc..) & have that data logged in your smartwatch app. Plus your stats will be far more accurate than the built-in computer on the bike.

However, for convenience & simplicity, the bike computer will do just fine. One option that I would have liked to have seen is a built in light in the LCD panel. If you're in a room with low light then the display can be hard to read.

It's worth mentioning that there's no external power required to run this bike. So you don't need to plug into an outlet. The computer will need 2x AA batteries. However, the manufacturer conveniently ships these with the bike.

So, to wrap things up, the build is going to take a little time, but nothing you can't handle! Once assembled, this bike is very comfortable to use & definitely feels well constructed for a consumer level elliptical. I think the price of $550 w/ free shipping (using Prime & a $50 coupon - at the time of this review) is very fair for this unit.

Overall, this is a great elliptical that will help you meet your daily step, cardio or high intensity workout goals. I definitely can recommend!

title: A Medicine Ball vs A Slam Ball
text:
In my photo, I show a side-by-side comparison of a medicine ball (the Nordic Fitness ball on the left) & a slam ball (the smaller ball on the right). These are similar animals, but still very different.

Yes, they're both round & heavy. However, a medicine ball is usually (as in the case of this Nordic Fitness model) much larger & will have a slight bounce to it.

The slam ball is usually small & very dense. And normally will not bounce much (unless it's over inflated).

So while both can be used for similar exercises, if you really want to round out your routines, it's best to have both.

This medicine ball from Nordic Fitness is very well made & comes with a basic exercise guide & welcome letter.

title: Will Get The Job Done, But Not Sure For How Long
text:
I've reviewed another ab roller around this price point (< $20.00). The other roller was a single, larger wheel. And I had my concerns about that design.

The roller that I'm reviewing here has 2 smaller wheels (side by side). Both rollers rotate directly against their hollow stainless steel axle/handle. So there's no bearing to take the pressure/friction off of the axle/wheel. And the wheels are made of plastic with a foam "tire" around the plastic rim.

However, that has to be expected at this price. Honestly, I think most ab rollers are made this way. And why most are under $30.00.

In my opinion, this 2 wheel version is better than the single larger wheel. You're closer to the ground so it feels more in control. However, even with that consideration, I'm not sure how long this unit would last under heavy, daily use.

If you rotate it out in your exercise routine, then I think it would hold up for a while. However, for use in a gym environment or for multiple daily users (or daily uses), I'm not sure of its lifespan.

The good thing is that it's relatively inexpensive. So, in the event you need to replace, it's not gonna be too painful on your wallet.

title: Very Well Made, But Be Aware That This Is A Rear Clip Harness
text:
Super, high quality harness with size adjustments on ALL straps. The buckles & clasps are all constructed of plastic, but still very durable. The material used for the harness looks to be thick nylon or composite. I might even say it's a little too stiff. But again, this speaks towards the quality of the product.

I had no issues getting it on our pup (Yorkie mix) & he didn't mind it at all.

The one caveat here is that that this is a REAR CLIP harness. If you (or your fur kid) is not used to a rear clip harness, then please be aware. Especially if he or she is used to a front or middle clip.

As with front or middle clip, your pup can be pulled back or away from a dangerous or unwanted situation. You can still do that with a rear clip, but he/she won't respond to the tug. So you won't be able to "steer" for lack of a better term. Basically, it would be like turning them butt first!

I believe the rear style clips are more suited for situations where your guy has a little more freedom to walk, jump or run, but you still want the harness in place. This way you can intervene & keep keep them from hurting themselves (IE: if he or she jumps, & the leash gets stuck, they are not hanging by their neck on the harness!)

So, In my opinion, not the best style harness for daily walks that require more control. However, if your needs are more for recreation or hiking or situations where you pup has more freedom, then this harness is a great solution.

title: A Lot Of Good Reviews, But The Quality Is Concerning
text:
There are many positive Amazon reviews on this ab roller. And there are definitely some good points for sure.

The wheel is WIDE. So it's very stable during movements. The width also allows easy turns. So you can create a variety of angles for your ab workouts. It also has a spring mechanism that prevents the roller from over-extending. Therefore keeps you from hyper-extending! Or at least that's the concept.

However, my main concern, is with the construction.

It's made entirely of plastic (namely the handles) with a thin tread of rubber to act as the gripping portion of the wheel. Although there is a "metal" rod that acts as the axle, I'm not sure if it's steel. And during use, you are exerting A LOT of force on these plastic handles. And while it appears that they are sturdy, something feels just a little questionable. The rolling mechanism is not smooth. As if the handles may give out mid-exercise.

I would have preferred steel & rubber for the axle/handle assembly. It would have just felt more durable/comfortable. And I'm not sure if there are any bearings, but this would have at least taken the friction off of the axle. As it appears to be rolling directly against the plastic of the wheel. Of course, this unit is under $30.00. So possibly that's not to be expected at this price point.

However, you don't want your mind focused on the quality of your exercise equipment while your working out. So if that's at all a concern for you, possible consider a higher end ab roller (if such a thing exists!).

title: Convenient If You Don't Have Room For A Full Jump Rope
text:

If you're going to use without the rope, make sure to attach the weighted balls to the end of each handle. The handles themselves are also weighted & have a spinning tip at the end of each handle. This is where either the jump rope or weighted balls are attached.

One of the handles is equipped with a counter mechanism that will count your time, calories & laps. You will need to enter your weight (In KG only. LBS are not supported) in order for the calorie tracker to properly estimate your calories burned.

This setting can be a little tricky at first. However, just use the instructions on the back of the box & you will be fine.

The weighted balls are needed to simulate the weight of the actual jump rope. This ensures that the handle tips spin & your activity can be properly recorded on the handle tracker.

Ropleless jumping takes a bit of practice, but makes for a great workout once you get the hang of it!

title: A Great Little Gear Bag With LOTS Of Room!
text:

It looks & is designed just like a mini back pack.

And even with its scaled down design, there's still lots of storage at roughly 12" x 7" x 4".

In my testing, the bag will hold hold a Samsung Galaxy Note 4 (10.5" tablet - in a case) or Surface Go tablet (in a Targus BlackBelt case - which is very bulky).

However, only one tablet will fit at a time. Although, if these tablets were not in cases, then they both may fit in the bag together.

Even with one tablet, there is still plenty of room left for other gear. Phone, headphones, wallet, glasses, water bottle, books, etc..

You can jam all of that stuff into this pack & keep it neat & easily accessible.

The front vertical zipper pocket is a very nice touch as you don't have to reach down into a pocket to grab stuff.

If I had to make one suggestion it would be to add double zippers the 2 large outer pockets. This would make zipping up larger items (like a tablet) a little easier.

Add to the mix an EASILY adjustable strap, padded pockets, water resistance & a very lightweight profile.

Makes this is a great pack to add to your bag arsenal!
