title: Excellent addition to a prep box or backpack.
text: I was laid off in Sept 2013 from a govt contract job. My family has been reduced to living in an RV. We are always looking for ways to reduce our expenses. I found this product by accident. I was at Big 5 buying a diamond knife sharpener. They had these sitting on the check out counter. The price was right at $12.99. I have used and made similar products in the past with mixed results, such as solar yard lights. I bought one. I turned it on when the sunset after charging for about an hour. We have our RV parked behind an abandoned house in the Arizona desert.  It gets real dark, real fast. This little light lit up our whole front yard area. It held the charge for a few hours. Inside the RV it was even better. I bought 3 more the next day! I have one in the bathroom, one in the living room, and two for the bedroom. I charge them by hanging then from our clothes line or one of the mesquite trees. I can get a few nights intermittent use from them on a single day in the sun. They have quickly become a necessary peice of gear for our involuntary reduced life style. When we spend a nice evening outside I place them in the trees and the four lights illuminate the yard better than 4 strands of 100 clear led xmas lights. I will buy more. We have friends in the homeless community and they will be getting these as gifts as funds allow. Waterproof, rugged, renewable. Two things would make them perfect, a USB port for emergency device charging,  and a photocell circut to allow them to charge during the day and come on automatically at night. I'm an Iraq war vet and I wish these were available in 2008. We were always losing power and we never lacked sunshine during the day. Batteries were not always available and being an avid reader due to insomnia, this product would have saved me many a boring night staring into darkness.

title: I ordered 3!! UPDATE: Delivered!
text:
I have not received my knives yet.
I did go to my local knife shop and handled one before I placed my order.
I handled the Normal mora first. I was impressed with the blade size and quality. At .10 inches thick I thought it was plenty wide for most tasks.
Then I inspected the .125 inches thick Mora of the style I eventually ordered. Wow, the blade was very beefy. The handle has great ergonomics and fit my hand very nice. The blade was hellaciously sharp. Use with caution! The sheath had a very positive retention system that held the knife firmly with no rattling or movement. The sheath belt loops appear very robust and over built. This blade is simple and cheap, but do not underestimate it! The blade would make short work of most butchering tasks. Its long enough to be adequate as a fighting knife. I cant wait till they arrive so I can torture test one to death. I need knives that I can rely on, that can hold up under pretty bad conditions. I need a knife I can depend on for my life. I think I found it! I'll post more when I actually test it out.

***** UPDATE Jan 14th *****

I received my 3 mora knives yesterday. Shipping was very fast. They came packed well in a box. Each knife was in its own sealed ziploc style bag. No documentation besides the shippers receipt arrived with the knives. First thing I did was cut at the box they came in. They were all absurdly sharp but one was a tad sharper than the others. That one is now my EDC (Every Day Carry). I have already added a patina to my EDC and my back up. I have left the third mora bare. I used the boiling vinegar method. Boil vinegar. Degrease blade with rubbing alcohol. Put blade in vinegar for 15 mins. Clean blade to remove residue. Repeat as many times as you need to get the blade as dark as you want. I only did two runs. This treatment will reduce the possibility of rust and corrosion forming on the blade.

I'll be doing some bush-craft in the next few days and putting them through their paces in the kitchen. More to come.

text:
It didn't take me long to figure out how to assemble it, even if there were no instructions. The description says this is heavy duty, and that's why I got it. Not the best golfer in the world, I wanted something that would withstand the chaos and natural disaster that constitutes my golf swing.

It comes with several soft golf balls to hit into the net. This is fine and dandy, but nothing quite replaces the feel of hitting a real, live (so to speak) golf ball. So, I broke out the real buggers and begin hitting into the net. So far, I've hit probably a thousand balls into the net. It's held up well. I leave it assembled and outside, and it's held up to the weather decently. A stiff wind WILL knock it over, however.

As to heavy duty, that's why I only gave it 4 stars. I've hit several of my typical errant shots right off the back bar brace that runs along the back of the net. It's but a nice little dent--a reminder of my burgeoning skills--complete with the golf ball dimples. Currently, I have two such dents. It seems to be holding up despite the abuse, but I expected something called "heavy duty" to withstand such impacts with a yawn and a sheepish grin. No such luck.

One of my spectacularly mishits (again using a real golf ball) hit the back bar with enough force and with the right angle that it deflected over my head and landed on the roof of my house. Hmmm. I was the one with the sheepish grin, yes sir.

I do put two bricks on the sides to keep the net firmly anchored. It does come with its own anchors, but I wasn't able to use them because the ground upon which it sits is too rocky. Not the golf net's problem. That one is my Arizona yard's personal demon. You might not have such a problem.

The hitting mat is awkward in my opinion, being so small, and unless it is anchored it will certainly move when you strike the ball, which is irritating. I even tried to anchor it, but my trench digging golf swings soon uprooted it, much to my annoyance. Also, it will raise the ball up slightly unnaturally, so you will need to find something else to stand on to make sure it is the same height as the mat. Nope, not for me. I bought a 4x5 mat that I could stand on.

Over all, I recommend this net!

title: Great For Occasional Golfer
text:
No amount of technology will ever completely straighten out my slice. Only practice will do that. However, with that being said, and coming purely from an at best, occasional golfer, I've been able to hit balls further than ever with this driver. By adjusting where the weight goes, I've been able to cut down on the severity of my slice and have hit balls straighter on a more frequent basis. But I can slice it with the best of them, so more practice will be necessary if I ever want to fully get rid of this weakness.

I enjoy the driver and the adjustable loft is an added bonus. I set it at what I think will work and leave it at that. Again, my inexperience doesn't allow for a consistent golf swing so I'll sometimes launch it into the stratosphere or run it a foot off the ground for seventy five yards--or something in between--regardless of the loft setting. title: Am I the ONLY person with really sensitive soles???
text: Okay, I think this elliptical is a decent, portable version, especially for those without room for a full size machine (would love one, but really could not fit one in my house!).  The problem I have had with it is the roller massagers.  Don't get me wrong, I love a good foot massage...but rollers don't work for me and my sensitive soles.  If they were tiny, like no larger than a BB pellet, that might work, but these feel honkin' BIG against the soles of my feet and they HURT.  Plus, they are still right there in the pedal even when you aren't getting a message.  I have dry eye syndrome and have a kind of space age-looking eye cover that has similar massager balls that goes around and "squeeze" my eyeballs and these don't bother me.  I just can't handle a lot of things against the soles of my feet - rocks felt through my shoes nearly bring me to tears, that's how bad it is with my feet.  So...I did my best to work around the issue with thickly padded pieces that fit over the pedal area to nullify the feeling of the massage balls against my skin and that's working, but I shouldn't have to do that.  I do enjoy using the machine - I am older and need the exercise and this is good for getting in steps even when the weather is bad and I can't just walk in pouring rain, 60 MPH winds or really cold weather.  Just wish the massager part was made differently.  Heck, I have a "foot massager" that is like a giant Tens unit pad that transmits a small shock of electricity to the skin and deeper, to the muscle tissue.  That actually gives me a really decent "massage" that soothes and calms my aching feet if I've been walking/standing too long.  I mention this as a possible suggestion for a different type of massage that won't require large rollers!  Maybe if you don't suffer from sensitive feet this machine will work great for you just as it is.

title: A nice, portable coffee table!

As I said, it isn't lightweight, but that also means it can hold quite a bit if you are having a fun camping trip with lots of "finger foods" that you can just put on this table and let everybody just dig in, grab what they like and be done with lunch or dinner!  Or you might have a table top (biofuel) firepit that you can roast marshmallows and make s'mores around and on this table.  The medium size is perfect, I think - not too big or too small.  Easy to pack and store, easy to put up - it is always on my list to take with us on a camping trip!

title: I have wanted one of these since I first saw it!
text: I have a 10x10 foot pop up tent that came with four mesh sides (to keep bugs out) and this inner tent works so well inside it.  The mesh sides keep the bugs out and that's a big plus!  I have water weight bags for the pop up tent plus I tie it down so with this Kamperkeeper tent attached inside, it's a really sturdy camping option plus for me, it's plenty of room.  I use a tall (22" high) queen air mattress with an internal pump for sleeping and it fits well in this tent.  I have a folding bamboo table for a light by the bed and a really sturdy fold up camping chair (not a cheap metal one with webbing, but a sturdy cross-braced frame with thick canvas-like material) and they fit as well inside this Kamperkeeper tent.  Now, I do bring along a smaller pop up tent (the kind where the four sides pop out and then you push up the ceiling) and that's more or less my kitchen/dining area as it is a net-side pop up as well, but it is 6x6 - too small to camp in, but for cooking/eating without bugs around, it's a good little shelter.  So, I now have the tent I had been looking at and I love it!  The nicest part is that with my 10x10 pop up that this one attaches to - it can be four mesh sides like mine or I could change out the sides for solid ones or those with plastic sections to see through, the point of those if it rains I would have a "double layer" to keep the rain away from me and my sleeping area.  Definitely I would recommend this to anyone who would like to try this style of tent.

title: I have built a Vardo-style trailer/camper
text: I'm not completely finished yet, but I purchased a used 6x12 foot utility trailer and built a Vardo or Gypsy-style camping, pull-behind trailer.  I wanted to do this build from the ground up as I have been teaching myself different skills, like putting together an emergency solar power station with a pair of solar panels, a 200AH lithium battery, a 2000watt inverter (with some other pieces) in a milk crate strapped to a dolly for easy moving - electricity goes off?  No problem!  But I have been looking into tying a system together for a camping trailer as well.  I mention this because I have investigated many choices people who do the nomading/boondocking thing and one gripe that comes up a lot is stepping into your RV/trailer.  You go to the beach, to the desert, to the mountains, to the lake and you will be dragging dirt, snow, water - all that stuff inside!  This boat flooring made perfect sense to me.  I lived aboard a houseboat and can affirm that if you spend time on a boat (just like an RV/trailer), you will be tracking dirt onto your decks.  So this is made tough to take all that and assist in cleaning the inevitable dirt and crud up without damaging the surface of this material.  I mean, think about alternatives - carpet, rugs, plain wood or faux wood flooring?  Plain wood might be sort of easier - sweep and mop, and it's cleaner, but once inside, do you really like the feel of that wood underfoot?  A bit of cushioning like this material has will feel better underfoot.  So, yes, I have installed this in my Vardo and I love the feeling underfoot.  It's a tough, easy to clean material made for boats, RVs, pop up campers...and even home built camping trailers.

title: For the price it could be better
text: This was for shower/dishwashing in my camper and what bothers me most is, if you are the manufacturer and know this will be used by people in RVs/campers, then WHY didn't you add an inlet that can be either attached to an exterior wall or at the very least, be long enough/flexible enough to attach to a hose for filling WITHOUT having to move the bladder.  Don't know about YOU but I cannot pick up a bladder holding 40 gallons of water and move it!  Now, secondly, this bladder should arrive ready to use or at the very least provide you with a cleaner - add it to the first or second flush of the interior of the bladder to remove the oily sheen I noticed when checking the outlet.  I wouldn't want THAT on my skin OR my clean dishes.  So...for the price, I expected more and feel more should have been provided by quality control during/after manufacturing.

title: Wanted for my indoor recliner
text: Winter is so much easier to bear when your behind is warm, right?  I had tried another one meant for the car, also with a USB cord and while it warmed, the part against my back began to dig into my back and hurt.  I mean, it may have been a bit more padded than this one, but it had no "give" so that I didn't feel IT under me, if that makes sense.  This one may be thinner, but it feels comfortable against my rear and my back.  I have a "double-ended" USB cord that is attached to a power strip that has several USB outlets as well.  So I attached this seat to that cord (no power bank needed for me!) and did the press 3 seconds to turn it on.  Cycled through the three heating levels - green, blue and red - the red had the back of my legs (through pants) almost burning!  So red may be perfect for those really, really cold nights.  The green which appears to be the lightest heating just barely seemed to warm my backside, but the blue level, as Goldilocks would say was just right.  I felt the heat, but it wasn't so hot that it bothered my skin.  For my purpose, this is so much better than a heating pad - they require a three-prong outlet and the one I was using had to constantly be rearranged as it would fall down as soon as I got up.  It heated well, but jeez, why do I want to futz with a heating pad every single time I get up out of my chair?  This, being made for a chair is sitting and staying put just fine!  I am happy with this heated pad for a chair - indoors or out.

title: Very versatile for camping and emergency use
text: I have a nice little lamp piece that screws onto these cannisters to provide a neat little light. Good to be prepared for emergencies or camping trips by taking a couple of these along with a light, a heater and a cooker...just in case!

title: I'm not a traditional prepper, but I have worked to be prepared
text:

So over the last year or so I have made sure that I have lights, cooking and heat options that do not require grid electricity. This is one of my cooking options - I love that it can be used with both propane and butane cannisters. I have both for emergencies and while I have both a propane camp stove and a Little Buddy propane heater, I have the butane cannisters so that if I'm without power longer than a day or two, I still have other ways/methods to cook food. title: Excellent size for camping and emergency use
text: Small, lightweight and with the zippered and handled cover, this is a wonderful little heater/cooker.  I have a larger kerosene heater made in a similar fashion, but of course, it is heavier.  I like having both this little one because it is perfect for hiking - add a carabiner clip to the handle and make sure to take a cannister of fuel, and you have warmth on a chilly evening plus the power to heat water for coffee/tea or soup/noodles.  For the price, this is a perfect little heater/cooker to have on hand.  Be prepared!

title: This is so cool - packs down so small!
text: Of course, you need the fuel, too, but for emergencies, this is great to have on hand during camping/hiking visits.  When packing for a camping trip, space can be an issue.  This little lamp is a wonderful night time item - to have light in the darkness.

title: Be prepared for power outages both in cold and hot weather
text: I have spent time getting prepared for power outages in winter (having lived through 5 days without power during Texas' blizzard when my house was 32 degrees inside during the day).  But spring and summer storms can also knock out power (maybe not that long), but if it's warm and  muggy, it's about as bad as being really cold, right?  So I got this nice little fan with a light so that if I'm sitting in a dark house without electricity, I can have a nice breeze and a light to see by.  I do have a solar powered fan for sitting on the porch if it gets too warm.  Always good to have a couple of fans, right?  And this one is smaller so I can hook it/hang it in the house near me to provide a good breeze.  With the remote, I don't have to get up to change the settings either!  Perfect for the price.

title: When I was a kid my dad had a kerosene hand warmer
text: I remember he would squirt kerosene on the wadding inside the half piece, light it, and then slide the empty piece back on, slip it inside the padded bag.  He would then hand it to me - ah, so nice and warm on a cold day (especially fishing out on the lake) in my little hands.  When I charged this pair of warmers up and held them in my hands, that's exactly how it felt - taking me back to that time as a kid with the toasty warmth in my chilled hands.  The coolest part, though, is that these can be pulled apart so each hand has a warmer to keep my fingers warm!  The other part is that this pair of warmers have low-medium-high instead of the really HOT of my dad's kerosene hand warmer that got cooler and cooler as the fuel was spent.  Medium is fine with me and that lasts a decent amount of time.  What can I say?  These warmers are the better idea of what I remember as a child - "breaks" in two so both hands have one, stays warmer longer (on medium) and I don't have that initial HOT time as I did with the kerosene hand warmer, and with the USB charging, it's a fast charge to get them back in my hands when needed!

title: Whew!  Do get rechargeable D batteries!
text: Okay, so the other part is I have an immersion heater "wand" so that I fill up my 5-gallon bucket, put the immersion heater in the water, wait a few minutes and that way I have warm water - it's isn't hot like you get at home, but it's not cold either!  I did happen to invest in a whole set of rechargeable batteries - AAA's to D's so it wasn't like I didn't have them, but my thought is, how many people keep D batteries around the house?  I did because I still keep an older flashlight that uses D's.  I have a couple of newer flashlights that are USB rechargeable too - good to have both in my opinion.  For a camp shower, this works well.  Like I said, I warm the water plus I do have a shower tent which has a clip near the top so I don't have to hold onto the showerhead while taking my shower.  This works and that's all I need for a camp shower.

title: I have another, similar unit
text: This one has a bit more and is also a bit larger - not in the unit itself, but the case.  Both of the units I have are very lightweight and easy to add to a backpack.  I took them both to the lake that is about a quarter mile from my house to get a feel for the real deal - lake water is...well, lake water and not something you would drink unless you had no other choice.  Both this unit and my other one performed quite well.  The one this this unit came with that the other one didn't is the fold-away drinking bag.  Then again, I have a few of these at the house for emergencies (some are smaller for carrying, others are larger for storing a few gallons of water should that be necessary).  All in all, this is an excellent hiking/survival companion to ensure you have drinkable water when it may be difficult to get it in any other way.

title: Amazingly large tent for camping
text: Weighs a bit more than I would like to carry on my own to the place I'm setting up, but then I did have help getting it set up.  It is a well-made, roomy tent with the attached canopy "room" that has sides in case it is windy/rainy.  I really like this tent, but I'm thinking I may give this one to my brother and his wife as I sometimes like to go camping alone and while I do love having the space with this one, I do have a pop up screen room and a smaller "instant" tent that I can put up in about 2 minutes by myself.  The pop up screen room is a bit heavier and takes a bit longer, but having two pieces works better for me when I'm on my own.  This tent, in my opinion, is better for two (or more) people as it really isn't a tent that one person would want to put up by themselves.  Well, maybe a big guy, but not a smaller lady like me.

title: Okay, but could use some improvement
text: I will say that this feels nice on my feet - soft and cushy and large enough for my size 9 feet.  Not sure if it would work for people with really large feet, though!  What I feel it lacks is ANY way for me to make it work for ME an my cold feet!  It has a USB cable that hides in a zippered area in the bottom and this foot warmer MUST be plugged in in order to heat up.  There is no control on the cord - it is JUST a USB plug, so you plug it in and the foot warmer heats up, but it's a very mild heat, period.  No way to crank it up or turn it down, just...hope that the heat it delivers is all you need.  Other than that, I found it to be okay...just okay.

title: One star off for the cover fit
text: I pulled this table out and really felt it did well for camping - lightweight and easy to set up - loved the drink insets in the top.  It folds up easily enough but OMG, trying to get it back into the cover it came with!  I mean, I understand that you want the cover to be snug on the table for carrying, but jeez!  I had to have help in doing a pull-push action to get the table back in the cover so it would be easy to stow when leaving.  So, table is 100% great but please please work on that cover!  Maybe make it a zip up?  Make the cover out of stretchy material?  I don't know the best way to make it a better cover, but I do know it needs some re-working.

title: Good to use with an immersion heater for a hot shower
text: I do have a propane water heater that I have set up to be "portable" but it is larger and with a 5 gallon bucket and the pump, it isn't terribly portable if I'm doing the minimal camping.  This is the best option as it packs down small plus I do have a pop up shower tent to make it easier to stay clean.  I found the shower to be a pretty decent one - good for washing off dishes as well!  I can actually add the immersion heater in with this shower kit and be good to go!  Now, if I were to wish for any changes to this kit, I'd ask that one of those silicone fold-down buckets be included instead of the one that is in this kit.  I have several of the fold down buckets and I really like them because they are very sturdy yet take up so little space.  In fact, I have not only buckets, but a camp sink that folds down and a few kitchen strainers  - all of them that semi-stiff silicone that pops up or down.  That type of bucket in this kit would make it more valuable kit for the price.  Just my opinion of course.  What you get for the price in this kit is a very good deal.

title: I absolutely love this handwarmer
text: During the winter, I can be sitting watching a movie and suddenly realize my hands are FREEZING!  I mean, I have a few different cozy winter slippers that are fuzzy and warm on my feet, but don't really wear my warm gloves sitting around watching a movie!  It's right at the beginning of fall, so it's not really cold enough to use this handwarmer as the evening temps are barely below 65 degrees yet!  But I did try it and oh man, the warmth it radiates to my hands is amazing.  I know that this hand warmer is going to be in a special place right by my recliner so that when I feel my hands getting cold, I can grab this item, put my hands in (after turning it on) and feel the warmth creeping into my finger bones - yes!

title: I LOVE this dual fuel rocket stove!
text: I have had a relationship with rocket stoves for about 20 years - the very first time I saw instructions on how to make a cheap/easy rocket stove from a paint can and large vegetable can with insulation material in between the two cans and then the next one I made was from concrete blocks.  Both were learning experiences and I fell in love with the idea of how they use very little fuel to create a decent fire.  This Light Me Bright rocket stove is not just a simple wood-burning one, but can be "changed out" to use charcoal briquettes as well.  Too cool!  But of course, the reason that I really love about this stove is that you can gather up some small twigs and pieces of wood - pinecones work too - and start a really impressive fire that cooks/boils water fast and easily.  Then, if you want to use charcoal instead, leave off the "rack" that holds wood, nearly close that front door and start your charcoal inside the stove.  Works well if you want a less "intense" fire, but however you use it, this is a nice sized, very portable rocket stove for camping or even for use outside (on my porch) during a power outage - you can still cook a meal if you have a tiny bit of wood or some charcoal.  This is one of the best stoves out there!

title: I have a real thing for rocket stoves!
text: Several years ago I saw information on rocket stoves that intrigued me so I followed some instructions to create a small one (using a paint can and a larger vegetable can with insulation in between them) and then making one with concrete blocks.  Those worked and I loved them, but having one like this that is extremely well made and very compact and portable, has been a game-changer for me!  I love the fact that just twigs and very small slivers of wood can make a wonderful fire both for heat and for cooking.  For camping, for emergency cooking (outside of course), this is an amazing rocket stove.  The way it is made, it's near-impossible for wind to blow it out unless you have it set up in the direction of the prevailing wind!  Cooking and boiling water is fast and easy on this very stable rocket stove.  I will take this with me each and every camping trip and know that if the power is out for any length of time, I can set this up on my front porch and make a meal with just a few twigs gathered from the trees on my property.  Excellent rocket stove!

title: An excellent larger tent
text: A bit heavy for an older lady, but not too bad.  It took me longer to put this up the first time, but that's sort of a learning process.  My old tent is the kind with the snap-together rods that you thread through the loops.  Even that tent took me a minute to learn the best and fastest way to put it together, so y'know, everything new is a bit of a learning experience, right?  Now, for the tent - I love the roominess of it and how I can arrange my stuff so that I have the most standing space when walking in/out/around the tent.  I have a 10" twin air mattress with an internal pump so once I had this tent set up and my bed was fully-inflated, bringing in the cooler, a small table, hanging a solar lamp - I was done within an hour and man, I had one heck of a good-looking camping set up!  Of course, just looking good isn't the point.  It was hot that first day, but with a clip on solar fan moving air inside the tent was not bad at all, plus the mesh front and back flaps allow good air movement.  I'm very happy with the tent itself, but I wish this had come with a separate "awning" - it didn't need to be attached.  Maybe backing up your SUV, using the open back for holding two ends and poles to hold the other two ends so you have a sheltered space outside the tent for relaxing (out of the sun or rain) would be appreciated.  Other than that, this is an excellent tent.

title: Nice, but wish is was able to hold more weight
text: Okay, so I'm near the upper limit of the treadmill's rated weight support.  I got this as a way to get myself walking regularly.  Understand that I live in Texas and until this week when we had 24 hours of rain that resulted in 10 inches of rain - nearly as much as we were down for 3 months...before that we had I believe 67 days in a row of 100+ degree days with even the night temps barely dipping below 90.  Skinny people may be okay walking in that heat, but not a fat person trying to lose weight!  So, for me, I have been walking slow and in short "bursts" to get acclimated and able to move up in speed and time.  T had been wanting an easy treadmill to store as I live in a small house - a mobile home which is the early version of a tiny house, before tiny homes were a "thing."  Anyway, I have this in my bedroom stashed behind a chair next to my bed.  It is easy to pull out and step on to begin my walk.  At the moment, I am walking about 15 minutes at a time.  My goal is to get to 1 hour and then I can begin walking faster to get some cardio involved with the walk.  I have also incorporated yoga so that I am working on muscle strength as well.  This treadmill is helping, but I was afraid, when I got it, that it wouldn't work well for me because I was a bit too heavy for it.  That's why I would ask that the people who make this should look into making it sturdier for those of us who are trying to improve our heath by using a treadmill.  Make it handle 300 or maybe up to 350 pounds would make it helpful for those who want to take charge of their weight loss at home.

title: I don't eat fresh eggs fast enough
text: When you live alone, keeping perishable fresh items like eggs or milk is something I've learned to keep and use as powdered items so the fresh kind doesn't spoil on me.  I do have and use regularly canned milk and I have a cannister of ready to use powdered milk gravy.  What always surprises me is how tasty dried eggs cook up when hydrated.  These are really decent dried eggs and will last me for a while.  The price is rather high, but then, for me using these dried eggs in recipes (and adding extra fluids to compensate), these dried eggs have been used in several recipes and they taste great!

title: Maybe I do go further than most to be prepared...
text: I live in Texas and in the February blizzard we had last year, I was stuck in my home without power for 5 days.  20 degrees outside, it was around 34 inside...for 5 days.  I did turn on my water faucets so that my pipes did not freeze and burst, and I was lucky enough to have a loaf of bread, peanut butter & jelly, and powdered milk.  So, in the months and months since then, I have gotten solar panels, a 200 amp hour LifePO4 battery, a 3000 watt inverter...but also have camp stoves run with propane, a propane heater and now this really nice little alcohol burner.  I also have a couple of mini-firepits that use 99% alcohol for fuel which is what this little burner uses as well.  I can at least boil water on this little burner with the power out, but with the included screen, it can be used outside as well (with the screen keeping any breeze from causing a problem).  When wondering how long you may be in the dark during a power outage, having a couple of solar lights and a way to heat up soup or make coffee on this little burner gives me peace of mind.  I love the carry case - I do have a propane cook stove that has a carrier and that makes it easy to store them both for the next time I need to use them.  I do think the price is a bit high, but again, having "redundancy" in emergency situations is important to me and I'm happy with adding this burner to my emergency use for heating food/drinks.

title: For me, this works okay
text: I have a USB powered screw on pump that fits the threads of this container.  If I were to get this for the way it is meant to be used, then I would not have given it 4 stars - 3 maybe.  The reason being the spigot supplied with this container means it was "meant" to be sitting on a "side" yet this is a circular container!  Want to make it accordioned like it is, then make it square!  But as I said, I have one of those screw on USB pumps - flip up the handle, press the button on the top and the water pours from the tubing down inside the water container.  Because my pump allows this accordioned container to sit upright, the roundness of it is not a problem.  It works though the one other issue is trying to get the very last dregs of water out of this container.  Not sure how to fix that issue, but it can be one if you are done with it for a while and you want to store it.

title: My boys and their dad play golf
text: I am not a golfer but this is a way for my boys to spend time with their dad - understand that my sons are in their late 20s and their dad is in his 70s.  They get together maybe once a month for a golf outing but that time spent together is a good thing.  I got this rangefinder for them to use - they all have good golf club sets, good bags, etc. but they didn't seem to have ever used a rangefinder so I got them this one.  I asked them to tell me how well it worked for them and my ex-husband was the one who really used it most, but all three said it was something they could have used a long time ago and were glad I got it for them!  What I recall them saying it that it helped them in choosing the most appropriate club based on the distance (and a few other factors) - understand that my ex-husband's father was a senior pro that won many tournaments in his day and taught his sons and grandsons to play golf, so they are sort of "serious" golfers if that makes sense.  For the price, and usefulness, I think this was an excellent addition to their golf game.

title: I love that these are smaller-more portable
text: I have a fairly small house, but I also have woods behind my house with a plethora of wildlife living there.  These night vision binoculars are perfect to store near my front door for those pleasant evenings when I sit outside and want to check out the critters that come out at night.  I've seen coyotes, deer and their fawns, a big owl in a tree near my house, of course raccoons but the biggest surprise was a bobcat!  They are not often seen, but I read afterwards they are fairly common though very secretive.  These smaller binoculars work well for me in how I use them.  Very good quality for the price.

title: Haven't taken it camping yet
text: What I did was put this on my bed with the backrest blown up to check it out.  It really is a very comfortable mattress and with the backrest - then again, I DO sleep on a 20" queen size air mattress and I keep a 2" piece of foam under the fitted sheet.  I had a twin size piece of foam and pulled it out to try on this mattress.  I would recommend that extra "squishiness" to make this mattress a bit more comfy for a night's sleep, but the wedge as a backrest is great.  Sit up for a while, read a book, work on your laptop/tablet, watch a movie or whatever, then let out a bit of the air to lower the wedge section so you can sleep and there you go!  The weight is pretty good - both in carrying it and what weight load it can hold.  Now, if I had a wish, I'd like it to be taller, like the air mattress I sleep on every night.  Maybe not that tall, but maybe 10" tall to give a bit more cushion in the mattress.  Very comfortable to sleep on (with an extra foam pad on top).

title: I sleep on an air mattress every night
text: And I have slept on a 20" tall, queen-sized mattress for the last 5-6 years.  Best mattress and sleep I've had.  I got this one for camping and I really, REALLY like the separate backrest (that can be blown up or not) for during the day and then let it out at night so I can sleep on a flat mattress.  I did get a very small, portable (about the size of a soda can) air pump that works great to fill this mattress fast and is usb rechargeable so I don't have to have a hand pump to use this mattress.  Because I do regularly sleep on an air mattress, I think I'm more than uniquely qualified to say that this is a wonderful spare for guests, for camping, for use in the game room - lots of places and ways to use this mattress and it is well worth having for all those reasons!

title: For an "economy" treadmill, this is worth it
text: I recently decided the exercise bike I have takes up too much space for the little time I use it.  It's not the best bike so...this treadmill that can fold up allows me to keep a larger space clear in my house.  The treadmill is definitely an economy one - I used to use both treadmills and stairsteppers at a membership place, but really can't afford a membership any longer.  So I do know what a high-end treadmill has and feels like, but I am now quite a bit older with some health issues.  Being able to use the treadmill to walk is really all I want at this point and this one will work for me to do just that.  If you want a good treadmill for serious, daily running, you might want to look elsewhere, but for those who are beginners or have some health issues that gentle daily walks or just getting (back) into running, this might be a good bet for home workouts.  Again, I like that this has a smaller footprint that a fixed exercise bike, especially when folded up.

title: Pop up once, never get it back into the bag it came in!
text: I'm not saying this is a bad shower/changing/toilet tent - it's perfect for all of those things.  What's problematic is that once you pop this open, it's going to be a bear to get it back into that small, poppable shape it came in ever again!  Okay, maybe some folks have the magic touch, but I sure don't.  As far as serving it's purpose - this is a very well-thought-out shower tent that is tell enough and fairly roomy for doing whatever business you have to do inside it.  I have a propane shower unit that requires a bucket/pump or water hose hook up to provide hot water for a shower.  The flaps in this tent work well with my water set up for taking a nice shower.  The only thing I would wish for is a better way to pack this changing/shower tent away.

title: I have balance issues so had my nephews try it out
text: They were fighting over it after the first try!  I did not give it to them, but asked them to try it out for me as I do have balance issues and didn't want to fall first time trying it out.  I watched them and was confident I could stand on it while moving.  It took a few tries, but I was able to move down the driveway and back which gave me the confidence to try it right around my house on the street.  It is a lot of fun and it holds me - a larger, older lady - just fine.  I'm 5' 4" but the handlebars seemed to be at a good height for me so that starting/steering was/is easy.  Storing it is a snap - fold it down and it takes up a very small space!  This would be perfect for taking downtown to get around if you are visiting the museums and such all in a day - zip from one to the other and no worries in finding a place to park!  I love this scooter!

title: Excellent portable table for camping, tailgating, etc.
text: When I go camping I do consider the weight of things.  I have a net tent that weighs about the same as this table but it is 10x10' and I have a small propane firepit that weighs about 15 pounds, but because of its size and how it can safely put out heat, I take it in the fall.  I say this to explain that for the size of this table and its weight, I definitely take it with me every camping trip and I have also used it in my yard when I decided to cook out on the spur of the moment.  I have a regular little charcoal grill and having a quick up, larger table helps me as I'm not just grilling, I have a camp propane stove that I will put a pot on, boil water and cook corn on the cob while grilling chicken breasts or a steak.  During the summer I sure don't want to produce heat in the kitchen, so having a quick outdoor kitchen set up is a good thing.  The grill may cook food, but plates and sauces and other items need a place to sit - this table fills that need perfectly and it is fast and easy to take down and store as well.

title: I have another IDOO - an 18" queen size bed that I sleep on every night
text: This sturdy little air-couch is little different than their bed and by that I mean, well-made and can take the weight but still stay fully inflated.  What I really like about this couch is that, like my IDOO queen size bed, it has an internal air compressor so you don't have to purchase an air compressor (or find that one you have for inflating pool toys).  The cord, once the couch is inflated, folds completely away and the very best part is that this couch can be inflated (and deflated) within 2-3 minutes!  My queen size bed can be fully inflated/deflated within 5 minutes.  That's helpful should you find several surprise guests show up at your house - grab this couch, plug it in and 5 minutes later you and your guests are enjoying a wonderful if unexpected visit in comfort!  Okay, so there is one downside and that is an air couch (and my air mattress) are so lightweight that they can rock forward when trying to stand up.  I have a large rug under my mattress to combat that rolling/moving motion when standing up.  It works more or less, but this couch's width works against it.  I don't know if maybe having a couple of weighted bags that attach to the back/bottom of this couch with velcro strips might work or not, but it's a thought I may try.  Again, for the ease of storing (in its own bag in a closet), ease of inflation/deflation, and being completely self-contained (with its own air compressor), this is a wonderful instant seating option for me and probably many others.

title: Building a 22 foot x 8 foot trailerable boat
text: I can get by with 1, but I thought from looking at the posting that you got a white light for near the bow and a color one for the stern.  It has some great qualities, but for the price I think the batteries should last a lot longer for LED lighting.  Granted, this one white light can be bright, but I would have also preferred to have the colored one for the stern so that my boating lights were easily seen, front to back.  With such a small boat, one may be enough, but for this price, I expected to get a set, one white, one multicolor.

title: This set is perfect for camping
text: I have a very portable tall net tent that weighs 18 pounds and now a table and benches for enjoying meals without bugs trying to horn in.  This set is also lightweight so I'm not lugging heavy stuff during a camping trip (four times - at home both into and out of the car, at the camp grounds both out of and back into the car).  The only thing I might wish for is that this set be a bit taller.  I mean, my bed is about 20" tall and easy for me to get up off of and I think most chairs are a bit taller, say, 18 inches which is only 3" taller, but when you are older, those 3" make a big difference when trying to get up!  All in all, I do like this set and am happy that it fits well in the net tent I have.

title: Like your hammock?  You need this!
text: I have some old live oaks around my property and while the do provide shade, they are very trashy trees - dropping leaves, twigs and of course, in the fall, acorns.  So I have to fold up chairs or cover them when I'm not sitting in them, otherwise I have to brush off or blow off leaves and twigs constantly.  The same with my outdoor hammock and I hate that.  My hammock is a macrame style woven one and it traps leaves 'n stuff all too easily.  What I like about this cover is that you can "retract" so that it's still on the hammock and all you have to do when you are done lasing around is to pull it back down.  This also keeps your hammock's design/color more vibrant - my macrame one is blue, green and purple and still looks as good as ever, keeping the UV rays from bleaching the colors out.  Easy-peasy to use and keeps hammocks ready for a nice day of lasing around!

title: The best truck tent I've had
text: This is an easy tent to put up (compared to some older ones I've tried) and the awning part is great, especially if going to a favorite fishing hole on a day that decides to let loose with some rain.  The other tents that don't have an awning had a bit of drip-through around the front opening and with the awning, it keeps the rain completely away from the tent opening.  That way you can sit on the edge of the tailgate, drink some coffee and enjoy the rain in comfort!  I also really like that the awning does NOT require staking to the ground and is as much a part of the truck bed set up as the tent itself.  Best trunk tent I've ever had, but of course, do be sure it will fit YOUR truck's bed before purchase.

title: Baby brother to the "regular" camp stove I have
text: This one is really made for an overnight backpacker - someone wanting to take just enough gear to see them for an overnight in the woods.  So lightweight and with a 1 pound propane can, you will have enough to heat a can of stew for dinner, heat up some powdered, reconstituted eggs for breakfast and make a cup of coffee to chase the eggs.  It's a well-made, sturdy "micro-size" camp stove.  Would also be great just for regular camping trips as it truly is a small, lightweight pack.  For those who are into RVing and converting vans 'n such, this little camp stove is definitely a good one to have on hand - would fit inside a smaller drawer than a traditional propane camp stove, taking up less space when space is at a premium.  All in all, it really is a handy tool for camping and hey, tuck it away in a drawer in your kitchen for that emergency time when the electricity goes out and you still need to cook dinner.  It will serve you in a pinch!

title: I have this set up on my fence and aimed at a set of bird feeding stations
text: I have a couple of stupid squirrels that have been trying their best to get to the seed feeders I have hanging on the feeding station poles.  See, I have four different bird feeding poles with hooks - I have four different seed feeders (two donut types and two more traditional ones with baffles), five nectar feeders for the hummingbirds in the area, two suet cake cages as well as four bird baths.  I like having this trail camera mounted where I can see the birds in real time on my camera (when I'm in the house) so they are not scared away by me being outside when they are wanting to come in for food/water.  I've had quite a few different bird species come in for food, but I have to say, watching the little hummingbirds zip in and out for a drink is so cool!  Where this trail camera comes in handy, though, is at night to see if any rats are trying to get to the bird food.  That's right - nasty, yucky rats.  I have seen a few show up in the night vision, but they can't find a way to get to the food yet - pole's too smooth to climb and the stations are too far from any trees to jump (same for the squirrels).  The only thing that is really funny is the squirrel I've seen hanging from one of my bird baths trying to get a drink.  It's hot and even little critters need a drink, right?  This trail cam has been useful in watching my bird feeders, for sure.

title: So...should be posted as a pool floaty
text: This is not an inflatable boat for a lake or even a shallow river as it is made from flimsy pool toy material.  I mean, if you have ever sat in a real inflatable boat, the material used is like night and day.  I can't even compare this to my inflatable SUP!  The skin on my SUP is a very heavy-duty vinyl while this really is like a cheap blow up donut people use in their backyard swimming pools.  If you want to use it in your pool, this might be a lot of fun, but please do think twice about trying to float in a nearby lake or river in this.

title: This is my "family" board
text: I have an SUP all my own, but should my daughter or other family member stop by and want to spend a few hours at the lake (about a quarter mile from my house) on a hot day, then I have an SUP for them to use!  I tried this one out and debated on whether to make this my board as I love the graphics/colors on this board (mine is white and blue), but in the end, this became the "guest" board.  Now, I do have to say I cannot stand up on a stand up paddleboard because of inner ear/balance issues, but I love wading out and then sitting on the SUP.  Paddling around while sitting is just as fun for me as it is for those who can stand up on their board.  This one, like my own board, comes with all the accessories for enjoying time on the water.  I did replace the hand pump with a small USB rechargeable air pump which works great to get the board pumped up fast and easy, plus my little pump is quite a bit smaller and lighter weight, so more easily packable in the carry case.  This is a really nice board for yourself or like I use it, as a guest board for those who drop by and decide to spend some time at the lake with me.

title: Excellent SUP for the price
text: It is such a nice way to spend a few hours paddling around on the lake near my home.  I can't stand up on it due to inner ear balance issues, but dangling my legs in the water, paddling around and splashing water on myself to stay cool - much more fun than sitting in a chair at lake's edge!  This paddleboard comes with pretty much everything you'd need, though I replaced the bicycle pump with a small, rechargeable, battery-powered pump that is small and can inflate this SUP quickly and easily, plus the pump is much smaller than the bike pump (and lighter weight) so I'm saving space.  For me (an older lady with arthritis) this board is a bit bulky to carry to the water, but that's just a temporary issue for me, probably no one else.  The biggest thing is sitting on it and paddling around - I love it!

title: A nice board but very pricy I'm thinking
text: I have another SUP that was around $200 or so and for me, that one has been a great way to spend time at the nearby lake.  I did have to wonder about an SUP at this price point - could it be that much better or special?  So...I'm not any sports nerd so to speak so as far as my own use, this paddleboard is pretty much the same as my other one.  Now there may be people who feel this is a higher-end board worth the price and I would never dispute them - I'm no expert!  So if this is the one for you, go for it!

title: Not sure this is worth so much more unless this is "your sport"
text: I have another, much less expensive stand up paddleboard.  I wondered if there was a big difference in my $200 or so board and this one.  Well, it's a nice board, but...in all honesty, at least for someone like me who can't even stand up on a paddleboard (I have inner ear balance issues) it's just another board to me.  Again, this is not my main sporting activity (heck, it's just a fun way to spend time when out camping at one of the nearby lakes).  So for those who are more into SUPs, perhaps this brand has something the others don't have that I'm not aware of.  If so, then perhaps this is the SUP for you.

title: I have been using this to track how close critters come to my yard
text: I do have a chain link fence around the front of my house while the back area is open (without fencing).  My area is abutted by Army Corp of Engineer "wild" land that goes (about a quarter of a mile) to a large lake not far from my house.  Just this past week my neighbor and I spotted a bobcat in the wild land back there!  We have coyotes, wild boars, raccoons, opossums, armadillos and a few other critters we've seen and documented.  This laser range finder has allowed me to get an idea of how close some of the wild life is getting to my yard.  I have small dogs and the coyotes worry me more than most of the other critters.  So when I spot one slinking around the edge of the woods, I grab this range finder and document when, where and how far they were from me.  At some point, if they get to be a bit too bold, the neighbors and I will have to report the pack as being dangerous.  Having documented the times, the places and how far they were from me, a human, will be helpful in proving that they need to be trapped and moved or dealt with in some other way.  I know this range finder is good for golf or even hunting - I guess my use is more akin to hunting, but I will say that it is easy to use, sighting in on the critter to find the distance.  That's what I need to know!

title: Have this second board for my friends to use
text: I have a board that I have used on the lake near my house, but paddling around by myself isn't nearly as fun (or as safe) as having someone out on the lake with you.  So I got this one for a couple of friends that I spend time with - we are all retired, so have the freedom to go places when most folks are working or otherwise disposed.  Another lady near my age was the first to try this board and she had more fun on this new way to spend time at the lake.  She was able to stand on the board without a problem - I have inner ear balance issues so the best I can do is straddle the board and paddle around, but I love doing that.  She said it was a very different way to experience the lake - standing on the SUP, using the paddle to propel herself around on the water.  She did ask me about buying it, but I told her if she wanted to borrow it, it was here for her to use, though I'd like to go with her if that was okay.  We've been out 3 times now - it's now summer and hot, so spending time on the lake is the best!  Get this SUP and enjoy time on whatever body of water is near you!

title: This is a really great beginner's board
text: Not to say this isn't a good board for anyone - it is - but the size (10.6) is easier for the beginner to handle over the longer SUPs.  This one is very colorful, too.  Not that color plays a big role, but it's like buying a car - if you have a choice of colors, you will most likely pick something other than black or white, right?  So the color makes it easy for you to pick out your paddleboard if you are out with friends at the local lake on a warm, sunny day.  Me, I cannot stand up on this paddleboard as I have inner ear issues that cause me to have balance problems when things are...movable.  I can, however, sit and use the paddle to get around and with my legs dangling in the water, I have a fun day paddling around near the lake's shore, spending time outside in the sunshine on a pretty lake.  What could be better than that?  This SUP comes with everything you need, though I did get myself a small USB-powered air pump so I can pump this SUP up faster and my pump is about the size of a cell phone so the hand pump can be left behind, leaving a bit more space for the rest of the SUP's stuff.  So, for the price, this is a decent paddleboard that I have been enjoying using at the nearby lake (I live about a quarter mile from a fairly large lake).  Try an SUP - you'll have fun, I promise!

title: I absolutely love rocket stoves!
text: I have another one that is a one-piece standing unit - it doesn't come apart - with the only added pieces were the bolt on legs and the "grates" at the top.  It works well and what I love about rocket stoves is how easy they are to get a fire started and keep it started.  This collapsible rocket stove is like an updated version of the other one that isn't collapsible.  See, I wanted to take the other rocket stove camping, but it's a bit cumbersome so I use it mostly in my yard, next to the cheap BBQ grill.  I can boil a pot of water, dump in fresh corn while the chicken is cooking on the grill and have them both done at the same time.  But now with this collapsible rocket stove, I can take it with me when I go camping!  It fits in with my gear much better - I happen to have a small hibachi style charcoal grill for cooking, but the rocket stove can be used with found/gathered sticks and twigs - any small stuff that can be burned.  It's so easy to put this rocket stove together - fast and easy - and to get a fire started is a snap. Cooking on it is no problem - it has enough weight to it that balancing a pan on the grate pieces is easy enough, too.  Cook bacon, boil water, make pancakes - you can use this portable rocket stove for anything you'd like to cook out!

title: Good idea that needs a bit more work to make it useable
text: Okay, so, first, it does spray water - at least my testing of this camping shower kit did prove that it works.  The water bucket is odd - I have some of the harder, plastic collapsible buckets that would have worked better with this kit.  Second, washing off beach sand may be good, but for an actual shower, who would want cold water?  I happen to have immersion heaters so could heat up a 5 gallon bucket of water to have a pleasantly warm shower with this system.  And last, the battery that is attached to the pump end of the shower, I would have appreciated a longer line so that it could be kept further from the water.  So, in the end, this is a good idea that needs a bit of improvement to make it a better, more useable system.

title: Excellent for survival, camping and water emergencies
text: Have you ever heard from your city/county that your water is going to be off for 24 hours (or longer) while they fix an old water main that broke?  The brown water coming out of the faucet is nasty!  This little water filter can clean the water and that's amazing!  It's really more of a survival thing - water needed is not clean and after using this little water purifier with the filter it has been made drinkable.  I'm very impressed with what this little unit can do - excellent little portable water filter!

title: Excellent for extending the diversity of cooked items in my outdoor kitchen
text: I have a charcoal grill and love the smoky flavor it imparts to meats and other foods when I'm do the great outdoors chef thing.  The thing is, in summer I do love corn on the cob with a grilled chicken breast or burger and am not all that thrilled by the roasted corn on the grill.  I'd rather cook it the traditional way with a large pot of boiling water on a burner.  With this portable gas burner, I can do just that.  I also have this nice stovetop for emergencies, like when the electricity goes off longer than expected and I still want a good, cooked meal.  And of course, taking it with me when I go out camping.  I have a 6-pack of the 1-pound propane tanks so using this stovetop is fast and just as easy popping in the propane tank and turning this stove burner on.  Very sturdy and appears to be a durable stovetop that I'll be able to use for years.

title: I have no grass in my yard
text: What I have is hard pan clay covered with a bit of sand.  Even weeds have issues growing in my yard!  So, when it rained, the yard would turn into a really gross and sticky red mud mess.  Walking down my front porch step is an older concrete pad that has been there for some time.  It is also a bit higher than the surrounding clay/soil.  My first attempt for me to walk as well as keeping my dog's paws cleaner (and not tracking mud in the house after it rained) was the RV plastic rugs and that works, but because of the change in height from the clay/soil to the concrete pad, I had tripped a few times when moving things around in the yard.  So, what I did with these mats is interlock four of them, laid them down, interlocked two more and laid those on top of the other four, then laid the large, doubled-over plastic RV rug down on top of the mats.  NOW I have a "change of elevation" so that when I step off the concrete pad, these mats (under the plastic rug) make up the difference and make it easier for me to walk around the yard without tripping.  These are also cushy, so when I step off the concrete pad, it's like being on plush carpet in a way.  I have picked them up, hosed them off and they are very sturdy and durable for my outdoor use.

title: This inversion bench is made for fit people - not plump people with back problems
text: I attempted to use this, but because I am not a lithe and slim person but a somewhat plump lady, I was a bit dubious...and not without cause.  It did not feel as if it would hold up if I'd been willing to place all my weight on it.  I did not want to find myself on the floor tangled up with this bench in worse shape than when I tried to sit down.  I can't recommend this to anyone that I'd say is over 160 pounds.  Maybe my balance issues causes me more issues with this bench, but I still say the weight limit is MUCH lower than listed.

title: Excellent rectangular pail
text: Not sure I'd actually call this a sink since it does not have a drain or way to remove water without just turning it over.  That does not mean it's not a bad pail to hold things or even to use as a sink.  I have a round pail that is collapsible similar to these and really like how they can be stored in such a small space when not in use - that's the most important part!  The material they are made of is very sturdy and while they are collapsible, collapsing them isn't just poof and done - the popping up and down takes a little bit of pulling/pushing.  That just shows me how the thick plastic will stand up to the use and storing of the pail.  Definitely a nice pail that works well!

title: This 10.6 foot board is perfect for beginners and old folks like me!
text: I did get one of the longer boards that is better for my nephews as they are bigger and more athletic than me.  I don't stand on my board.  I wade out, slide on the board with my legs dangling on each side and use the paddle to move around near the lake's shore (I live about a quarter mile from a big lake in the area).  My nephews do what everybody else does - the paddle out and then stand on the board, using the paddle to move around on the lake.  What I can say about this paddleboard is that it's fast and easy to inflate (I use a small USB-chargeable air compressor to pump it up instead of the hand pump included), easy to carry to the water and the paddle makes it easy to move around on the water.  I really love my paddleboard even if I can't stand up on it (I have inner ear balance issues).

title: I use this every day
text: My hose is long, but not long enough to extend to the bird feeding area I set up in my front yard.  In that feeding area I have a couple of bird baths that I keep water in for the birds to get a drink or take a bath as they want.  The problem is, I live where it gets very hot and dry and pretty much every day the baths are very low/almost dry.  I do have a couple of pole feeders that have small water bowls, but it's the larger bird baths I make sure are full each day.  And that's where this bucket comes in - I fill it with water from the hose and walk it out to the birth baths.  It's lightweight and easy to use.  I haven't collapsed it back down as I do use it every day, but when winter comes around again, I'll collapse it down and store it in the shed.  For now, it works GREAT and is so useful every day!

title: This is the grown up version of a kid's scooter
text: I never owned one as a kid - I had friends that had scooters and I did get up on one, kick myself along and thought it was cool.  Okay, I preferred my bike, maybe, but hey, that was just me!  Now though, with this scooter, it's a whole different thing!  No push-kick along with this one - and faster than I ever was able to push kick myself along with a "manual" scooter.  Also, those regular scooters, I don't recall them being foldable - they were always in my friend's garage leaned up against the wall.  This one is so portable with the handle section folding down to make it easier to store and carry.  Now, being a downtown worker, I have seen those rental electric scooters zipping around the downtown area and thinking that this one is similar, but much better as those are like the "manual" ones in that they don't fold down.  I don't live downtown, but this scooter would be great if you are an urban dweller as well as urban worker.  Don't need a car to get around, just jump on the scooter to get to work and back!  Fun no matter where you live or use it, though!

title: Very good portable shower/toilet
text: This was just what I needed for my camping trips!  I have a propane heated shower that I modified with a pump and a hose reel hanger that I can use in a primitive campground without access to a hose/running water.  So with my heated shower set up, I can step inside this stand up shower tent and clean off the sweat and grime after a 2-3 hour hike.  Nobody wants to climb into bed stinking of dried sweat, right?  So having the ability to step into this shower tent and wash it away, means I have a more comfortable and pleasant camping trip.  Setting up is very easy and taking this tent down isn't too bad - I have a front car window shade that is closed in a similar fashion so it's a matter of getting the "twist" down pat to get this tent packed up.  It's not that hard to learn, but it does take a minute to figure it out.  It's a great shower tent and I take it each time I go camping.

title: This one I gave to my nephew
text: The one I kept was a bit smaller/lighter and for an older (and short) lady, the other one fit me better.  My nephew is over 6 feet tall and this board was perfect for him.  It is a beautiful board and like mine, very easy to inflate.  Now, my nephew can stand and paddle and from watching him on this board, he had no issues while paddling on the lake, meaning it is sturdy and stable.  Me, I have balance issues so instead of standing, I wade out a few feet into the water, get myself seated on the paddleboard and with my legs dangling in the water, I paddle is that seated position.  I had looked at different ways to enjoy the lake - an inner tube you just float and while it's nice to kind of lay back and float, you can't really be proactive in getting yourself here or there in an inner tube.  I really looked at kayaks seriously (and the prices are way out of my price range), but getting in a kayak is a bit more tricky than this paddleboard.  So this is paddleboard, while it is larger and more suited to my nephew, is still a wonderful board that I would have kept had I not found one that fit my frame better.  For taller folks, this is a great board that comes with everything you need to have fun on the water!

title: I can't stand on an SUP, but I still enjoy paddling around on it
text: I have a balance issue in my inner ear - had it for years, so standing up on a board that rocks with the water isn't something I can do, but this paddleboard is great anyway.  I can wade out into the lake with it and then sit on it with my legs in the water and paddle.  Who says you have to stand on it?  Okay, it's in the name - stand up paddleboard, but it is easier to use than, say, a kayak or even a small johnboat.  It's more comfortable and easier to maneuver around on than an inner tube as well.  I have a lake very close to my house and this is a nice way to spend a couple of hours enjoying the weather and the lake.  All SUPs seem to be a bit pricy, but that's just my opinion.  I'm older and remember when you could buy a house for what cars cost nowadays!  This SUP is easy to inflate and deflate - I happen to have a small, usb-powered air pump so I don't have to use the hand pump and having an air-inflated board makes it so lightweight it's easy for me to carry to the water.  I'm happy with this SUP and how it allows me to spend a few hours of rest and relaxation at the lake.

title: Oh how I wish this was made for a big person like me!
text: My nephew loves stuff like this and he's younger and slimmer than his much older aunt.  But to understand, he is a police officer and he works with those really cool and very expensive drones that big city police offices have.  And having mentioned that, for him to find a "gadget" cool, it must be high level cool.  He absolutely was blown away by the folding electric bike.  He has a big truck and a fast car, but I think he got his fascination with "scooters" from his grandpa - my dad.  My dad wasn't allowed to ride them, but he fixed up broken/non-working ones and sold them.  My nephew just loved the size and while the top speed is 15 MPH - for a small electric bike, that's pretty darn fast!  I actually have some great-nephews (my nephew's sister who lives about an hour away) that may end up with this bike and I'm sure they will also find it pretty cool...well, for what it is.  One has just gotten his driver's license and I remember when I was that age, I wanted a fast car.  Still, I think this scooter, while a bit pricy, is a very cool, portable electric bike!

title: For my niece
text: I got one for myself - it's a little different than this one - but my niece and great nephews came to the lake near my house on a day when I was there paddling around on my paddleboard.  I am in my late 60s and have balance issues so I can't stand on my board, but it is easy to wade out, straddle the board and then go paddling around the shoreline.  On a very warm day, it's just a nice way to spend the day.  So when my niece saw me paddling around, she asked about the board and I let her use it.  She has no problem balancing so it was fun to see her up on it the way lots of people use these boards.  So I got this one and called her up, asked if she and her boys might come to the lake and when they showed up, I gave her this one for her own.  Her boys were jealous, but she's a single mom and I like for her to get something before her boys do once in a while.  The boys did get their chance on the board and they love it, but she was so surprised and happy to get this board.  I let her use my electric pump even though a hand pump comes with this board.  It was easy to inflate and very sturdy - the design/artwork on it looks nice as well.  Very sturdy board that I believe my niece will get a lot of enjoyment from during the summers on the lake.

title: Okay so I finally tried this one
text: This is like my third one, but the other two I gave to my great nephews and this one was for my niece so she and her boys could go paddle-boarding out on the lake near their home.  They got me on this one - sitting, as I have balance issues at my age, but sitting and paddling on the lake was a lot of fun for me.  I didn't go too far and then came back to shore - it is still my niece's, but I have to say, it was loads of fun and now I can see why my great nephews love taking them to the lake regularly.  They, of course, can stand up on them (which I cannot do) and paddle out into the lake (much further than I would ever go) and considering where we live, that the summer days can go up to the 90s and 100s regularly, finding a way to cool off is important and having fun with this paddle board while doing it is the coolest way to do that!  Yes, these are a bit pricey, but then a kayak isn't cheap either, so it's a relative thing for price, right?

title: Got this for my old but still used Creative Zen MP3 player
text: Yes, I still have a Creative Zen which, oddly enough, is worth about the same as when I bought it many years ago!  I love that little MP3 player and do use it, but lately I had "lost" it in the house for a few weeks.  Part of the reason is, it's just a small "box."  Very small.  So once I found it again, I wanted to get a pouch to put it in and with a handle so I could hang the pouch to make it easier to store and find when I want it.  This pouch is perfect - the Zen fits in the netted side and the small usb power pack and cable plus a pair of wired earphones all fit in the pouch.  I had a spare keychain handle/strap that hooked to the ring on the back.  I have the packed pouch with the Zen, small power station (it is a very small one that's about the size of a credit card), the power cord and earphones hanging from a hook on my entrance "tree."  So for me, this pouch is doing exactly what I got it for - and that's what counts, right?

title: I received some oversized ones similar to these
text: I can't say anything bad about these - they are 12x12 inches and are very easy to put together, have good cushion for a play area for kids or as I have used these, across my kitchen floor.  But I also received some oversized ones that, for me, were just a little bit better than these.  Mostly because with them being 24x24 in both black and blue, they are a bit cooler to look at and cover more space (quickly) because of their size.  Again, if you prefer the 12x12 size, these are great.  I actually wish these were some color other than black.  Light blue, a pale green or even packed in a multicolor package for kids - bright primary colors so that when you put them down, they look like a kid's play area!  I do like that this comes with the pieces to "square off" the edges, but I'd really prefer more of those pieces since it's not a "given" on how I will put these tiles down, if that makes sense.  I mentioned for a play area for kids, but these do have may uses.  I know a guy who does a lot of lathe work in his garage which is concrete and used a set of these to provide padding to the area near his workbench.  Good for exercising both standing and sitting to provide cushion - anyplace where the floor is hard, these would be great cushioning and easy to install.

title: Pricy but worth it if you want to see critters at night
text: I'm so pleased with the night vision and comfort of these binoculars - they are easy to use and it is fun to focus in on the armadillos trying to creep around my house or those coyotes I've heard howling at night.  I'm in a fenced yard, so it gives me a bit of comfort that the coyotes don't come in my yard - at least so far as I've been able to see with these goggles!  I like that I can save a shot of say, an owl sitting on a tree just outside my yard.  That, for me, is just too cool!  I wish the price of night vision goggles would go down a bit, but for now, these are wonderful for what you pay for them.

title: Heavy, but takes up a smaller space than I thought it would when stored
text: Looking at the front with the water "bottle" I thought this would be harder to fold and store, but it isn't too bad.  I got this because I am older and have no upper body strength.  I have a fold up exercise bike that I like but of course, it does not exercise my arms/upper body!  I like that the resistance is changeable by how much water is in the "bottle" - I started in a similar fashion by using empty liter bottles of soda half-filled with water that I tied inside a plastic bag so I could lift them in different ways (to the side or front).  That's one of the main reasons I really looked at this rowing machine - being able to change/increase the resistance with water.  So simple!  Okay, if you want to decrease, that means draining some of the water which isn't the easiest thing to do, but it's not that difficult.  I'm happy with how this rowing machine works and am glad to feel the burn in my arms!

title: I gave this to my son who is a golfer
text: But before handing it over, I wanted to test the rangefinder as I happen to have a very new phone on the market that is sort of marketed for contractors 'n such - it actually has a rangefinder (a compass and the laser can be used to measure walls and calculate paint needs) which I think is way cool.  This rangefinder is easy to set up and then I was right in for the testing and found that this rangefinder and my phone's rangefinder were almost exactly the same each time I measured to a specific item (like a tree).  This will work great for my son when he goes golfing with his dad - nice and small enough to fit in his pocket and easy to use, I think he'll improve his golfing skills at least a little bit and that's a good thing!

title: Excellent cooker
text: I have a cheap grill that I love to use in summer (love marinated chicken breasts cooked on the grill!) when heating up the kitchen inside my house would simply cause the a/c to come on more often, causing higher electricity bills.  So I have the grill set up near my patio furniture and have an easy-wipe fold-away table next to it for "preparation," but this cooker I've used for boiling corn while my chicken breasts cook.  Sometimes I also have enough fresh-picked green beans and will snap the beans, then quick boil them, grab another pan, throw a couple of pieces of bacon, some onions, a small sweet pepper and then throw the fresh boiled beans in to "crisp."  I do love fresh green beans cooked this way and with chicken, corn and green beans, that is a meal I could eat again and again during the summer months!  This little stove top works wonderfully - no electricity needed and I get a mouth-watering meal that saves my house's interior from heat, plus I can sit on my patio and have a fine meal while enjoying the weather.  Having an "outdoor kitchen" is great - doesn't have to be a fancy, expensive one.  A grill and a cooktop with an easy to clean table is all I need!  Of course this will be a wonderful cooktop for camping as well.

title: Oh I wish I was younger!
text: I'm in my late 60s so am not exactly thrilled about falling so this is something I can watch my great nephews use and be happy with.  It really looks like a LOT of fun - these two boys are definitely outdoor kind of kids and when I brought this hoverboard over, their eyes lit up.  And then they started fighting over who went first, so had to play a guessing game to settle the fight, plus agree on a time limit for their turns.  My niece lives on a very quiet cul de sac residential area so they were able to zip down her driveway and onto the circle, down the straight-a-way and back again in no time - whew!  It's actually faster than I expected it to be!  It's so cool-looking - maybe "tough" looking would go better for two boys, but hey, that was just an observation from a girly point of view.  One of my great nephews found that this can be attached to a seat section and with their own money decided to order that piece.  I didn't even know it could become a "recumbent bike" kind of vehicle, but that's cool, too - sit down, stand up, I think these two boys are going to have a lot of fun with this hoverboard.  Yes, it is a bit pricey, but considering what it is, I feel the price is decent for what you get.

title: Really nice outdoor loveseat
text: I have a decent camping chair - a single - that has a cupholder and even a place to hold a magazine.  It is a nice chair, but this is a loveseat and is comfy for two people.  It isn't just a cheap-looking metal, folding chair either - the frame looks like wood and the canvas material is very sturdy and weatherproof.
