The material may be sturdy, but the fabric is comfortable against skin - I mean, if you are in shorts, the fabric isn't too rough against your skin.  Carrying it to and from the car is easy enough - it doesn't way that much at all.  So all around, this is a wonderful addition to your camping trips - a great place to sit!

title: My great nephew is a serious fisherman
text: I'm not kidding when I say that.  He has won several catch and release trophies for the amount, length, size, etc.  He takes a fishing pole with him wherever he goes!  So I wanted him to have an entire fishing retinue to take with him wherever he goes.  I know his mom will drop him at a nearby lake to fish for a few hours while she runs errands so having a handled back with everything he needs to fish is a great thing - along with a small bag to hold a couple of drinks and a folding stool and he's good to go!  This is a wonderful set for the fishing person in your life.

title: Really roomy, sturdy chair
text: This is a perfect carry with me anywhere chair - camping, kid's sporting events, and other events.  I'm just too old to sit on the ground any longer.  Trying to get up is embarrassing - my hips screaming in arthritic pain and really needing a hand or arm from a stranger or family member to steady myself when getting up off the ground.  So a chair is something I need when going places where I can't guarantee I'll find a place to sit up off the ground.  I like that I have a place to sit my drink that keeps it safe from getting knocked off.  This chair is easy to open and close and not too heavy for me to carry around.  Roomy enough for a larger-sized person like me, it's so worth having that I keep it in my car trunk so I'm ready to go wherever and be assured I can sit down on this chair after I get there!

title: Gonex makes some great outdoor items, including this tent
text: I have found that I have received several items recently that are made by Gonex and all I can say is that each one was high quality - a fishing rod kit (with accessories) and hunter blind/tent and a few other items.  This tent is super easy to put up for one person, especially considering its size.  It's a very roomy tent, though as far as being for 10 people, I would have to say if they are very friendly!  Still, for maybe 6 at most, this would be perfect and I love the big openings so you get lots of fresh air when it is nice, can close up so the people inside stay dry during bad weather.  Many tents are including pockets for electronics like cell phones and tablets, but I do have to add that this tent has several which is a good thing.  I think if there was one thing I'd add would be an awning so you could set up a chair and table to hang out under during the heat of the day to keep you shaded.  Other than that, this is an awesome tent!

title: Emergency and camping - great grill
text: Last year I was in my house for 5 days without power - brutal bone cold for Texas - and in the intervening year I have prepared my home and myself so I am not like a hibernating bear under a pile of covers for days. I have off-grid heat and off-grid light and off-grid cooking alternatives.  That last one, alternative cooking, is where this camping grill comes in.  I did test it with a 1 pound propane bottle and had no trouble getting it lit.  I prepared a bit of my home made pancake mix.  Sprayed the pan with olive oil, poured in some batter and watched them cook.  Not bad!  I am happy with this camping grill's first cook and have it stored in the emergency box in the kitchen - having hot, just cooked food on my own camping grill/pan - well, when it's 35 degrees inside your house, that nice hot food is worth every penny.  This unit seems like a good, sturdy one that should last a good long time too.

title: Excellent but for...
text: Okay, I'm not sure WHO created this skull cap, but jeez, could you have thought through your choice of location of the battery pack?!?  I love the warmth that this skull cap puts off when the battery pack is charged up and put in the "sleeve" made for it, but WHERE that sleeve is is right smack-dab in the back of this cap.  Meaning if you are wearing it and sitting outside...then want to put your head back, your skull will be resting on the battery which will be jammed against the wall or chair back.  PUT THE BATTERY IN THE TOP or even the side...duh!  And last, why the heck would you have an actual PLUG instead of a USB cord??? I had to charge this battery pack in my bathroom where is the only place I had an open electrical plug.  I have USB outlets literally everywhere which made me a bit mad at this choice as well.  USB would have worked great, would have been easier...but no...both my gripes are technical in nature.  The skull cap was comfy to put on and warms up well to keep my head warm and that's what I really want and the reason I gave it four stars.

title: My old bike had been having issues
text: I'm not good at tech/mechanical stuff, so I'm not real sure what the problem is, other than it has gotten more and more difficult to pedal.  I mean, the bike had a knob to dial up or down the resistance, but I had not changed or touched that knob in months.  Anyway, I gave the bike to my next door neighbor who is mechanically inclined so he can probably fix it.  Fortunately, I got this one and had it set up in my old bike's place - nice, it's a bit smaller - yay!  I love the arm resistance bands that I can use to work my flabby arms while riding this bike.  The biggest difference is that my old bike was a solid presence in my living room - this one doesn't fold like totally flat (like those ones I've seen on TV that slide under the bed), but I can fold it and lean it against the bookshelf behind it and allow me to have more room when not using the bike.  All in all, I really love this basic bike!

title: Using with the simplest human waste method when camping
text: I have a large bucket and bags to fit it, a toilet seat that fits snugly over the bucket and a large bag of sawdust I carry with me when I go camping.  Can't always be sure I'll find a place near a restroom and because I'm older, sometimes trying to make it to a bathroom isn't all that easy!  So, with my set up (inside my tent) I also wanted to ensure that the liquid part would be less of an issue by using these to make them more solid as well as remove any lingering scent.  So when I sit down on my camp toilet, I throw one of these in to do its job and then throw a bit of sawdust on top.  When I empty the bucket, the bag has solids only - no possibilities of leakage.  That makes it less worrisome for me!

title: For the price and what you get, this is a good deal
text: I am not the SUP person, but both my nephews are and they spend quite a bit of time at the lake near my house.  I got this one for the younger one because he had not saved enough to get his own like his older brother.  Now they can both get out on the lake and have a good time during the summer!  I realize that these can get quite pricey and maybe now he can save for one of those really expensive ones later on, but for now, he's really impressed with this one.  At 13, he is a sturdy guy, but not the biggest kid for his age and he's able to carry this one to the lake's edge.  Easy to pump up and then get out either standing or sitting on the board's surface, he was able to paddle around and that look on his face - it was worth it!  As I said, I understand this is more like a beginner board and that's how it is being used which means, it is perfect for my nephew's needs at this time.

title: 1000 yards is what a good golfer needs in a rangefinder
text: I got one for my two sons and their dad (my ex) who all get together and play golf usually at least once a month, but the other rangefinder's limit is 700 yards.  Okay, from what they tell me.  I'm no golfer, but when I got this one and they took it out on the course for the first time, they could focus much further to the current hole when needed and especially for their dad who has been golfing since he was a young boy and who is now in his late 60s, he found this rangefinder to be "the" one!  Nobody in my family is really into hunting but I'm sure this could be used to zoom in on a buck during hunting season.  For the price, this is a great golfing aid and possibly good for hunters as well.

title: My ex and my two boys play golf together at least once a month
text: My ex's dad did the same with his two sons so it's a nice generational thing that dad and sons play golf - it's a great way for them to get some exercise and fresh air walking the course (as opposed to using a golf cart). Plus the time spent together gives them an excuse to actually talk to each other!  Anyway, I got this rangefinder as a way to help them with their golf games (the reason they spend time in nature together!).  My ex said this was a very accurate little tool that did help him and both my boys in choosing the best club to get them nearest to the hole.  It is a bit pricy, but helping them with their game means it was worth it!

title: Good but could be a bit better
text: A blind means you will probably be in it for some time waiting for game to come within range - even if you've staked out the area with game trail cameras - and because of that, you want a blind that's comfy.  Especially for this price.  So, for a couple of big guys, this is going to be rather cramped. by width and height.  Add a bit of both to this tent to make it more usable for a regular guy, please!  The weight isn't too bad, but could have been lighter weight for carrying into a more remote hunting area.  I mean, wool is heavy and warm, but polar fleece is also warm and quite a bit lighter - it seems there should be some material that would not sacrifice sturdiness but be lightweight for carrying.  Not a bad blind but could use some improvements.

title: In a handled carry bag this is perfect for camping trips
text: This fits well in my car with my glamping stuff.  I set up a 10x10 pop-up tent and then attach a tent underneath it so I have a fully stand-up inside tent that I put a twin 22" tall air mattress in with a zero gravity chair, solar lanterns and yes, power packs to keep things powered while I'm out camping.  I needed an easily portable table to set my light on when I'm ready to get into bed and that's where this table comes in.  Perfectly portable, easy to set up and take down and easy to fit back into it's carry case - this is a great table!  Now, I did bring it out under my awning as a table to use my propane stove so I could cook a meal from the items I'd brought from my cooler.  Again, excellent portability/usability while camping but would be great for the yard at home as well.

title: I happen to watch a really neat video that uses a table like this
text: I'm not a serious prepper or anything, but I did live 5 days last February without power during the blizzard in Texas.  I have spent the subsequent months getting ready for another time like that again.  The video I watched was a cool way to heat an area in your house when the power is off.  I already had the rectangular paving stones/bricks to place on this table as well as the little alcohol burners.  The idea is to place the cement stones/bricks (the flat ones, not the large ones with holes in them) around the alcohol burner.  The alcohol burner transfers heat to the bricks which in turn release the stored heat over a longer time in the area where they are set up.  Obviously this can't be set up on the floor, so a table that can handle the stored heat is what I needed.  I set the cement blocks up on this metal camping table, put the alcohol burner in the middle and let it "work."  This camping table is the perfect size for my emergency room warming set up with the bricks an burner.  I know it will work fine for a table to use my propane cookstove on as well, but for the moment it is in an emergency box in my house along with the cement bricks and the alcohol burner (and a bottle of rubbing alcohol).  I'm very happy with how this table worked out for my purposes.

title: Expensive, but my nephews are having loads of fun with it
text: My two nephews are teenagers and need outdoor activities to keep them from playing video games all day and this was a great way to do that.  A bit pricey, but I get that with the motor and remote control that it isn't "just a skateboard."  Their house has a long semi-circular driveway and they live right at the entrance to a cul-de-sac, so zooming around on this was first done in a safe area.  I was amazed at how fast this skateboard can go!  Being teenagers, these boys are fearless, but they have the balance and the remote is a cool way to get going on this board.  I am impressed and they seem to be happy with this new outdoor "toy."

title: Disappointed
text: Okay, so I felt a little bit of warmth from these, but in an emergency these would NOT be helpful and that's what I got them for.  My idea was to put some in the car and some in my house emergency package (that has candles, a propane heater for the house, gel alcohol stove and several other items), but what's the point if they won't heat up enough to keep your fingers and toes from going numb in the cold?  See, I spent 5 full days without any power last February in the Texas blizzard.  The inside of my house was about 30 degrees.  I had three layers of clothes on, several blankets swaddling me and I was lucky to have bread, peanut butter and jelly to make sandwiches to eat twice a day.  I have since made changes and have power stations charged, solar panels to recharge them, solar camping lights, tea candles and many other items to make it through another blackout like that, but these one-use hand/body warmers are not worth it.

title: Last February I had only one hand warmer during the Texas blizzard
text: I spent FIVE DAYS in my house without electricity and while I did have one hand warmer, at that time I didn't have but one power station which got used up rather quickly.  I have made some changes, gotten myself an emergency box that has candles (both real ones and rechargeable USB powered candles), a little buddy propane heater, a propane camp stove and solar lights, but considering my house was 20 degrees inside, having this handwarmer will ensure that my fingers are freezing this time!  I have this and my other hand warmer charged up and I can tell you that this one I think can go longer on battery power than the old one.  If I can get over 24 hours on both of them, I'll be a happy and warm camper!

title: great for watching sports events
text: I have a couple of grandkids that participate in soccer and on those cool/cold nights they are playing, I bring my comfy folding chair that's easy for me to get up out of (with arthritic knees) and this muff.  I do have gloves/mittens I could wear, but I love the warmth that the muff provides and I can still take my hands out to scratch my nose or cup around my mouth to scream my granddaughter's name should she score!  The warmer in the muff stays warm longer than I usually need it at games so that's perfect.  I plug it in the recharge for the next time it comes with me to a game!

title: I like that this is a set and not just one
text: I have A hand warmer - I like it (can get hot on the higher setting) but it is one and kind of "fat" which bothers me (will make sense in a minute).  I got these because first they are a set!  Yes!  I can hold one in each hand instead of keeping my hands wrapped around one.  Second, these are "skinny" and I can, if I want, tuck them into the palm section of my gloves if I'm watching my grandson play soccer on a cold evening.  I mean, I don't have to be USING my hands when I'm sitting at the game, but being older, my fingers and toes get colder faster than they did when I was younger (poor circulation, I'm sure) especially when I'm out in cool/cold weather.  I love that these charge up fast and they have two settings though I have not really needed the high setting - the low setting in the palm of my gloves keeps my hands toasty and that's all I expect!  Would make a GREAT gift!

title: Excellent camping and emergency cooktop
text: I went 5 days without heat last February during the blizzard in Texas - no lights, no heat, no hot food to eat either.  Not going to happen THIS year!  Texas' grid system has done NOTHING to fix the problem so I'm glad I have this really sturdy stovetop, just in case.  Yes, I also have propane to ensure I can cook with it - it is easy to set up and easy to get fired up as well.  I love that it comes in it's own case for storage in my emergency box as a just in case when I'm not using it for camping.  Great idea for a gift, too.

title: My next door neighbor boys are having a blast with this!
text: I am an old lady, not a skateboard person, but my neighbor is a divorced dad who gets his two boys every other weekend and because he has a roommate to help pay bills, I know he doesn't have a lot of money to spend on his kids when he gets them, so on occasion I have gotten a few things for them because I'd rather hear kids laughing and having fun than whining at their dad because he can't afford to buy them all the newest, coolest things.  So having said that, my intentions are also to benefit me, too!  I took this over before the boys were to be dropped off and he was so happy - I did apologize that I couldn't get two of them but hoped they would share.  About an hour later I heard them squealing so figured their dad had brought out this skateboard and was preparing to read them the riot act if they didn't share.  I looked up in time to see the older boy - he's maybe 10 or so - zoom past my house and the grin he had just made me laugh.  He was obviously loving the ride!  He came zooming past again and in another couple of minutes, the younger one - I think 7 or thereabouts - zoomed by.  His eyes were wide and he had the biggest grin on his face!  That's really all I wanted to see - that they liked it and I believe their dad was so happy to have a cool thing for them to play with at his house.  I mean, I can't say how it feels to be on it or anything like that, but I can say that two little boys had a fun weekend with their dad riding, I'm pretty sure, was their first ever skateboard and it was motorized and could be controlled with the remote control to boot!  If you are a grandparent or a parent of a young person (10 or younger, in my opinion), this skateboard is going to be a perfect gift for Christmas or their birthday.

title: For emergencies these are great
text: We are coming into fall now and I was in my house for 5 days without power in February during the Texas blizzard.  I had a usb handwarmer that I used sparingly, but after it was over I made it my mission to arm myself with an emergency kit.  These have become a part of my kit.  At least some of them!  I put several in my car and I have a couple of them in my purse.  Now, if you compare these to the usb handwarmer I have, they aren't as warm - my usb handwarmer gets so hot I have to turn it off for a time and then turn it back on!  But these will definitely keep you warm and they do last.  If you go camping, if you have had a power outage in winter or been stuck in your car during cold weather waiting on a tow truck - get these!  Put them in your car, in with your camping gear, in your purse - they are worth it!

title: My granddaughter loves her girly SUP
text: I have given a black and red one to my grandson, but this pink one was just for her.  She is like many teenagers and wants to be cool - the cool thing right now is sitting or standing on one of these paddleboards.  When I took the black and red one over to give to my grandson, she gave me a look...and I knew what that meant:  Where's mine?!?  So a couple of days later, I went over to my son's place to give her this pink board.  She lit up like Christmas in July!  The whole kit is a bit big and bulky, but she's able to carry it and she and her dad got it out and pumped it up in the backyard so she could learn to do it herself when going to the lake.  See, I live near a lake so when they come over to give their mom and dad some alone time, I can take them over to the lake and let them spend part of the day paddling around until they are tired.  I have a metal detector so while they paddle, I walk and look for "buried treasure."  The one thing I can say is that both my grandchildren have really enjoyed their stand up paddleboards - my granddaughter really loves this pink one - and getting them out of the house, doing exercise is the best thing I can think of!  Excellent paddleboard for a girl (or woman)!

title: Perfect for your go-bag in an emergency
text: I don't know how many people have a go-bag, but I would say that it is important to have one as weather conditions can change our lives almost instantly, forcing us to leave our homes.  Flooding, tornadoes, fires - we've seen them on television.  People being rescued from their homes and having nothing with them.  That's why a go bag is perfect - you don't know where you will end up and having straws that can filter water in a place where the water has been compromised.  As small as these straws are, they can take up a small amount of space in a go bag, alongside a sleeping bag, a blanket, matches, a couple of candles - y'know, things that will make you somewhat comfortable in a bad situation.  Drinking water is a must so get these straws for that moment, that just in case time you need them.

title: How often do you hear of an area mandated to boil their water before use?
text: Emergencies happen all the time - burst water pipes from freezing or just being old and then what comes out of your faucets is suspect.  I do have a filtration system to put water through should that kind of thing happening, but if you are forced to leave your home?  This set of straws are in my go-bag should I have to leave the house due to bad weather or other, similar emergency situation.  I understand these are not a magic panacea for filthy water - you want water as clean as possible and if I had to, I might even try to put together a natural filter using sand from around where I live.  At the least, the water will be clearer and I can then use one of these straws for a better, cleaner sip of water.  The real reason to have these is for the emergency you don't plan for.  They are small and easy to use, so perfect for packing in an emergency bag where my filtration system at home is not - it does a great job of filtering water, but a bit too large to stuff in a bag.  Definitely worth having on hand!

title: Thought this would be a way to get rid of my full-size exercise bike
text: My big bike takes up quite a bit of room in my living room and I thought this one would be a great way to still get the exercise but take up less floor space.  Sadly, it isn't a well-thought-out, quality made product and I will be getting rid of it instead and sticking with the big bike.  So, first off, the pedals are not adjustable to your seating situation - note that in the item's posting, they do not show anyone sitting and using this "bike."  It's not comfortable - not in my recliner, not in a metal folding chair, not any chair I have in my house!  So if I can't get comfortable with pedaling this "bike" in any chair, then I'm not going to use it.  That's the bottom line - it has to be used to be useful, right?

title: I have two emergency kits/boxes in my house now
text: I stayed in my house in 20 degree weather without power for 5 days this past February in Texas and it was at that time that I made myself a promise that I would NOT be caught unprepared again.  I mean, in the intervening months the Texas grid has NOT been updated or fixed in any way so if they are going to leave me in the cold again, I at least will be as prepared as possible.  Not just for cold, but should there be water issues and that's where this water filter comes in.  I mean, if we have no power and the water lines froze and burst, then the water is going to need to be boiled at the very least (I could see a run on grocery stores and the shelves holding water are bare), but if I have a water filter - this one - I can at least feel my water is clean and boiling it will give me double confidence I can drink it.  Definitely something everyone should have in an emergency box, along with matches/lighter, candles, solar radio, hand warmers...several other items, but you get where I'm going with the emergency box.  This gravity water filter is a perfect inclusion in that box.  Would be great for a long hiking trip or just taking on a camping trip just in case.

title: I have a couple of these seats
text: I LOVE these!  So easy to store, so easy to carry and this one, I think the LED light in the center section is a way cool addition.  Take it to a night game and have a light right there that won't bother others like a flashlight or other bright light.  This is more of a night light so you can see just right around your immediate area.  These seats are great because, like this one, they can hold a good-sized person without a problem, but they can also serve as a footstool.  Easy to open and pull up to the right height and the same with collapsing and storage.  Excellent for camping, sporting and even at home if you find more guests show up than you have seats for!

title: I LOVE this set!
text: I had my next door neighbor set it up as he has two boys - this is the perfect game for us to play!  I've played with the large, wooden boards which isn't an easy set to carry around.  I mean, I've seen some gorgeous corn hole sets that are decorated in wickedly awesome ways, but really aren't terribly portable.  This is the best, portable corn hole set I've ever seen and it works great for playing with - can be portable, but if you can't play the boards, then what's the point, right?  Excellent portable game!

title: In my emergency kit
text: I have made sure that I have a whole bunch of ways to keep warm, to make food and have light and some portable power in my house without power.  This folding stove is a small one that should I have to, I can use as both a water heater, but to provide a small amount of warmth to the house in a fairly safe way.  I do have a half dozen of the canned fuel so I am prepared!  This was an inexpensive way to be prepared for longer power outages or to take on a camping trip.  Not bad!

title: Bought for both a camping stove and a Little Buddy heater
text: Both items are a part of my emergency kit - last February I lived through 5 days without power in the Texas blizzard.  My house, at times was 20 degrees inside and I did NOT have a way to make hot food or hot tea to help keep me warm.  I have since made sure to be prepared and with the little propane camping stovetop that uses propane and the Little Buddy heater that also uses propane.  These bottles are perfect for both stove and heater.  I have tried a bottle out on them both so I am ready should a brutal cold snap take out the power grid again.  Texas has not done anything to fix the grid that went down so...I'm prepared!

title: I got this one for my grandson
text: I did get the long board motorized one for my son who used to be a serious skateboarder when he was a teenager.  Now that he's almost 30 and has two kids of his own, he's been teaching his son things that he knows and loves from his own past.  He plays electric guitar and started teaching his son on an acoustic guitar and now, sharing skateboarding seems to have brought the little kid back in my son as he teaches his own son the stance and the moves for skateboarding.  The kicker is that his long board and this one for my grandson are motorized!  They have a large semi-circular driveway that is nearly flat so they have plenty of space in getting comfortable on their skateboards before going down the street to the park on them.  I love watching them riding together like this - it's just so much fun!  While this is a bit pricey, it is a great way to get around their neighborhood.  They do have some bumps they both will have to negotiate if they ride them on the street, but their neighborhood also has sidewalks they may be able to use, too.  My grandson grabbed me and hugged me and said, "Thank you Grandma!"  And that was worth it all!

title: My own son was a skateboarder
text: And now he has a son of his own.  I took this over and my own boy's eyes lit up - fun for dad, fun for son!  I mean, my grandson can ride a bike and has for several years, but this is something his dad can teach him all over again, but the cool part is, this one is motorized!  I was laughing so hard watching my own son get on it and learning how to use the remote control and "drive" it before trying to teach his son.  I love it and it was so worth that kind of family fun - jus the first time - which I hope to share several more times!

title: Very comfortable chair for outdoor use
text: Would make a great dual purpose camping chair and sleeping cot, too.  This has a nice carry bag to make it easy to carry it to your car for that camping trip and then back to the porch when you come home.  I purchased a long chair cushion to make it a little more comfortable to sit and snooze in.  I might recommend getting a cushion if you want to use it for a sleeping cot, but that's just me.  This is a sturdy lounge chair that I use regularly on my patio.

title: My nephew is an on the water kind of person
text: He's also a teenager and loves to do the stand up paddleboard stuff that his friends do on the lake, but he'd been using a regular (hard) board that was bulky and harder to transport.  I got this for him as I'm an old lady and not really good at this kind of stuff.  So I went to the lake (it's within a quarter mile of my house) with him and watched as he pulled the deflated board out, attached the pump and wow - in just a couple of minutes he had this long, sturdy board that didn't look a whole lot different than the regular (hard) board.  I watched him paddle out and do his thing - standing up and using the paddle to move on the water.  He looked like he was really enjoying himself.  When, after a few hours, he came back to shore, he told me Wolf Armor makes a great paddleboard.  It didn't take long to deflate it and stash it back in the bag it came with.  What I can say is that he is extremely happy with this paddleboard and from the time that I spent with him, I know he will use it many times during the summer months.

title: I went a little overboard, but better prepared this time around
text: I have never lived through the flooding and hurricane emergencies or the fires that have burned through many communities, but I have lived through a couple of blizzards.  One in the 70s in Ohio that took out power for days to a large chunk of central Ohio.  Fortunately at that time the house had natural gas for the oven/stove so we could heat food/water and stand in front of the stove for warmth every few hours.  This past year in Texas, in an all electric house, I spent 5 days without power.  Because I had moved from Ohio to Texas, I had plenty of heavy blankets and warm winter clothing to keep me from freezing in a house that was near 20 degrees during the day and colder at night.  Since then, I have picked up items to ensure that I will NOT go through that again.  This little portable stove is one of those things.  I have a fire mat to put underneath it, but in case I'm without power, I can at least fire this up with some alcohol I bought for that purpose and heat some water for tea or warm up a can of soup.  I tried this out and it works great!  Not only can it make me a nice hot cup of tea, I can stand near it and get my hands warm.  Should I decide to go camping, I'll take this little stove as it is such a perfectly portable one!

title: In my 60s and am amazed at what devices like this can do
text: Believe it or not, I still remember, when I was a little girl, that our doctor would make house calls when necessary although back then we didn't call the doctor very often.  Currently, just trying to get a doctor's appointment means you have to look to the future two-four-six months before you can get into their office!  Anything requiring immediate attention seems to be emergency room visits with few in-between choices.  What it seems to me is that we are going to virtual office visits, first with Nurse Practitioners who will refer to Physicians only those cases they feel a doctor should see.  Having this Kardiamobile device, for me, is wonderful as I can monitor my heart rate.  At the present time, I don't seem to be having any issues, but what I really wish is that I could text/email or in some other way send an electronic version of my current record to be added to my medical record.  I mean, at my age, I would think that having a weekly/monthly electronic records (heart rate, O2 sats, sleep-breathing issues, etc) would begin to paint a picture for my doctor that could help him prescribe specific meds and/or tweak others based on these records.  Along with these records, a 10-15 minute Zoom face-to-face with my doctor would be the way of the future.  Still, that may be the next iteration of the app.  For now, printing out my record is the next best thing.  I will say that this little device is something anyone my age or anyone with heart issues should have - easy to use, small enough to carry with you wherever you go and very accurate as well.  Oh, the last thing - I happen to have a couple of small clamshell cases (old harmonica cases) that works well to carry this device, but I would love it if it came with a small case so you have no excuse to leave it behind when you are out of the house...why?  Because that's when your heart issues may flair up and if you can capture that on record, it is an invaluable thing for your doctor to see!  As far as the cost goes, yeah, I wish it was cheaper, but this is SO worth the price!

title: I'm no hunter, but these are fun to use
text: I have woods behind my house that go down to the lake nearby and it has quite a variety of wildlife from deer and coyote to owls and hawks.  Later in the evening I have heard the coyotes near my back bedroom and that's why I like having these night vision binoculars.  I can sit quietly on my porch and look through these goggles to see what critters are hanging around my house.  I do have a chain link fence, so I'm not terribly worried of meeting a coyote in my yard, but having one sniffing around the back of my house where the fence butts up against that corner doesn't make me all that happy.  What I love about this set of goggles is that I can save a video to my phone and share it with my kids and grandkids.  Where I live I also have armadillos that scurry about and they are the strangest looking little things, plus they are night creatures.  You seldom see them during the day so I have been able to catch and record a few glimpses of them.  If you have kids and go camping much, these are great for showing your children what's out there, or like me, you might be surprised at what you find sneaking around your back yard at night!  The pictures taken with this during the day are great, but of course, it's the evening where the goggle's night vision takes over and considering it is delivering pictures in low/no light, they are pretty good.  These are so cool!

title: After spending 5 days in my house last winter without power...
text: I vowed to be ready the next time Texas' grid went down because of poor management and maintenance on it and I am now ready.  Solar powered (and can be charged with an USB if necessary) lights, I have a solar powered, hand crank radio, a propane heater that can be used in the house, and this is one of two different ways for me to heat water or cook food.  Light, heat, hot water/food in a house that got down to about 20 degrees would have been helpful last year.  It will be more than helpful this year as I am ready should it happen again.  This little camp stove works with the alcohol I bought and I also have another little camp stove that works with the small gel type cans of fuel.  I have propane for a traditional camp stove (and a heater), the gel containers and then this stove that uses alcohol.  Best to be double-triple sure and with this nice little camp stove I will not be surprised by bad weather/power outages again!

title: This will be great for camping, but when not camping...
text: I got this (and a propane heater) for emergency blackout times.  The blizzard this year in Texas in February saw me in a house for five days with no heat, no electricity while keeping my kitchen and bathroom faucets on a running trickle so they didn't freeze.  I made it through those five days because I wore three layers of clothing, two pairs of socks, two hats and covered up with three blankets, plus I had water to drink, bread and peanut butter to eat...yep, I learned my lesson.  This burner will be an emergency way to heat water or food should the power ever go out like that again.  I have had this burner on outside and it works great.  Bought a 6-pack of the 1 pound propane canisters and just in case, I have a back up to this back up with the smaller, hiker's version that runs on the small sterno cans which I also got in a 6-pack.  The point is that this can be used in your yard as a side-by-side to your BBQ grill to heat up the chili to smother your grilled hot dog in or if you are sitting in your house, in the dark and need something hot in your belly - tea or tomato soup - this little burner can do the job.  I understand that you do have to be careful of the fumes, but I also have a carbon monoxide detector that I watch when using this item in the house.  This stove top is so easy to use - insert the propane canister, turn the knob to start and then adjust the flame to what you need and then turn it off when done.  When cool, remove the propane, put it back in the case and you're ready for it's next use.  Pricewise, I think it's fairly reasonable for summer camping and emergency use.

title: For my use, this works great
text: I have three bird feeders in my yard - they are all three very close to each other.  I have five different nectar feeders and three seed feeders as well as bird baths.  I set this camera up so I could see who all are coming in for food and water.  It's been fun seeing the hummingbirds hovering to sip the sugar water and the Chickadees and other small birds come for the seeds.  I have a traditional bird bath but watching with the trail camera, I found that the birds like my solar water "fountain" made from an automatic cat water fountain - I followed a video and used a small styrofoam ball with a hole through it and the tube from the water pump just a little over the top of the foam ball.  The hummingbirds love holding onto the foam ball and sipping water, even dunking their little heads in the bubbling water.  It's been fun watching them without disturbing them - that's why I love this camera.  The birds are used to it sitting there and don't even pay attention, all the while I get to see what they are doing.  So cool!

title: I had more fun just watching
text: My next door neighbor is a divorced man with weekend visits with his two young boys.  I've watched him get frustrated because the boys are bored doing the same old outdoor stuff.  I had a small drone at the house one day and took it over and man, he and those boys had so much fun that day!  So I saw this set of suction arrows that actually make noise and got it for the boys on their weekend visit with their dad.  Oh man, I can't tell you how much fun it was watching these two boys (and their dad) zinging arrows all over their lawn!  I know their dad is always a bit strapped for cash because he does pay child support so he's trying to find things to do with his kids that don't cost much money.  I can tell you that for the price, this bow and arrow set was way worth it!  And for me, it's so much fun to watch these kids running around outside being physically active rather than sitting in the house watching TV or playing video games.  Definitely worth it!

title: I've been having a blast with these the last few nights
text: It's finally getting cooler so I can sit out on my porch in the evenings.  Behind my house is a strip of wild woods - land owned by the Army Corps of Engineers as a part of the lake not too far away from my house.  Because it connects to the lake, this property has quite a bit of wildlife - coyotes, armadillos, wild pigs, deer and I've seen a large, horned owl land on a tree limb not too far from me, but I doubt I would have seen it had I not had the night vision goggles.  What is really cool is being able to snap a picture when I see something neat with them.  I really haven't tried a video, but maybe if I see an armadillo waddling past I'll take a short video - they do seem to move around more at night.  The coyotes are not shy about coming right up to my back fence which is rather creepy, but at least they don't try to jump the fence.  Anyway, having the night vision goggles has given me a new insight into what goes on just past my fence at night.  Interesting, a bit creepy, but worth knowing about for sure!

title: Good range finder
text: I handed this Peakpulse range finder off to my ex-husband and my two boys as they play golf together regularly.  I don't play golf, but figured they would give me a good review of this unit.  My ex-husband told me that it is accurate and my sons both told me it is easy to use. Now, I did give them another range finder to use when out golfing and while they said this Peakpulse unit performs well, it is second choice behind the Wellray unit I gave them earlier.  With both units, they can check accuracy between the two and have fun on the course.  I think my ex glommed the Wellray and one of my boys is holding onto the Peakpulse - good to have on hand!

title: Works for small things
text: No matter what this posting boasts, this is NOT the pump for a good-sized pool or inflatable boat.  It simply doesn't have the power.  For a pool floaty or something like that, yes, this little pump can do the job.  I have an electric Intex air pump that can stand up to almost anything and get whatever pumped up in a reasonable amount of time - boat, chair, pool - it can handle the job, but of course, it is electric and needs to be plugged in to work well.  I guess what I really need to look for is an air pump with a detachable and rechargeable lithium battery (like several of my power tools) to get the power needed to pump up larger items without an electric cord.  This little one just can't do that job.  Keep it for floaties for the pool...that's as good as it can get.

title: My ex and my two boys play golf regularly
text: The first range finder I got for my ex to help him, but also to teach my boys a bit more about the game.  They all loved using that range finder so this one is my second one so the boys have one to use between them while their dad uses the one I gave him earlier.  This is not quite as "fancy" as the first one, but both boys have used it and tell me that it is a good range finder - the slope angle probably is useful for most courses, but considering my boys and their dad live in Colorado where pretty much all the courses they play are naturally hilly, the slope finder has helped them out quite a bit they tell me.  If you have a golfer in your circle of family or friends, this would be a great tool to help them improve their game!  I was thinking that those who are bow and arrow hunters, might find this range finder helpful in setting up a shot.  I'm no hunter, but around my area there is a season specific to bow hunters and it occurred to me they might find it useful as well.  My sons love their shared range finder and I'm happy - they are out on the course, walking instead of riding, so getting exercise and learning a sport that also allows them to talk and have a pleasant time while walking the course.  This range finder is also helping them improve their game.  Can't get much better than that!

title: Packs a lot in such a small package
text: My ex goes out with our two sons regularly on the golf course.  His own father did that with him and his brother.  A nice way to spend a day walking in a nice setting and spend time talking with our boys, catching up on their lives.  This rangefinder was a way for me to contribute since I don't play golf and really have no great interest in the sport.  But having given this to my ex for his next golf date, I heard back from him that it was amazing.  He has always been old school, like his father - eyeballing the hole and gauging his shot, but having used this cool little gadget for the first time, he was struck by all the features that gave him loads of information like the magnification so he can zoom in to check out those difficult parts on a hole that can cause you to problems, or the touch screen and he loved the voice that talked to him so he didn't have to check on a distance by taking the rangefinder away from his eye - he could just listen to it.  This little guy is lightweight, too, so carrying it along on the golf course is not a problem at all.  One of my sons plays golf regularly with a group of guys he works with and told me that he would be getting this rangefinder to take with him next time they play.  Now, I realize this could be used for a few different things, like hunting, but it really is an ideal and extremely useful tool for golfers.  Considering what golfers pay for their clubs and membership to golf courses and such, the price of this gadget is fairly reasonable considering what it does.

title: I absolutely LOVE this stove!
text: I have messed around with DIY rocket stoves with some success - my best was in using concrete blocks.  They work, but who wants to carry around 4 or 6 concrete blocks in their car?  It's not awful, but this rocket stove is lighter weight and works pretty much the same way.  One really good deal with this rocket stove is that it has the slide on grate pieces so that a pot/pan can be put on top to cook food, boil water for coffee or whatever.  It also gives off heat so when you are out camping, you can sit near it while cooking and not worry about the wind changing direction and open flames burning you as might happen with a regular fire.  Not just that, but with this rocket stove, you can gather small twigs that wouldn't keep a regular fire going and in a rocket stove, they burn well.  I think if I were to make any changes to this design, I'd change the legs.  I'm no engineer, but I think a folding mechanism could be used so the legs are permanently attached, but fold down so the rocket stove is as small as it is now (without the legs being removed and possibly lost).  The same with the slide on grate pieces.  Again, I am not an engineer so it may be that hinges that close to heat might be an issue, but if the grate pieces could be slightly curved so they rest against the stove pipe section, then the same would be accomplished with them as the legs.  The less you have to keep track of, the less that can be lost, right?  Of course if you have a "rocket rucksack" to store it in and maybe the inside is that heat mat stuff so you could place it under the stove while using it and then fold it up to store the stove in it...hey, just some suggestions to the manufacturer for the next iteration!  As far as this rocket stove goes, I am very pleased with it's performance.

title: I took this to my "next door neighbor" to try
text: I live in a small mobile home park and on the other side a strip of woods is a horse ranch that specializes in taking people down riding trails to the nearby lake.  I took this megaphone over to the lady who runs the horse ranch because that is how she imparts instructions to the folks who come to ride her horses on the trails.  I know this because I hear her on her own megaphone every day!  Megaphones are meant for talking to a crowd and while I am not often trying to talk to a crowd, my neighbor is (in a sense).  She was thrilled to try this one out and found the usb prepared content ability was perfect as there are things she says as they move along the trails - so regularly that having it programmed to say it saves her voice at the end of the day.  That is the same with the ability to record when she has special groups and using their group's name during the talks she gives on the megaphone helps her to acknowledge special groups.  I had meant for her to just test it out for me, but she was so taken with it that I now have a standing invitation to come ride the trails while she uses the megaphone!

title: Received this in summer - waiting for winter!
text: I love how this warms my head, though right now is not the time I want to have a warm head...it's middle of the summer and HOT where I live, but winter will be here soon enough and having a skull cap that can keep my head warm, now that's worth wishing winter come soon!  The batteries are small enough they aren't obtrusive - I have heated socks so I'm used to or at least expect a small bump/lump from a battery.  Otherwise, where would the heat come from?  If you suffer from a cold head in winter - your fuzzy hats don't warm your noggin, then try this heated skull cap - love the heat!

title: Absolutely cool!
text: I lived on a houseboat 24/7 for 3 years - it was an experience very few people have tried and I have to admit it has its ups and downs, but I wouldn't trade the memories for anything!  I got this sextant for ME, to remind me of my time on the houseboat.  It may not have been a blue water boat (able to cross oceans), but it was a boat able to navigate inland waterways.  Many a night I spent sitting out on my "front deck" looking up at the night sky, the boat rocking in the water...it's such a different way of life and I know that sextants are something sailors used to navigate while out to sea.  When I visit my grandchildren, I do like to talk to them about pursuing things or ways of life that may be different than what others tell them to (or feel they should) - I tell them about living on a boat and how many people have done the same in the past and still do and those who cruise the world and keep a sextant similar to this one just in case their electronics fail and they need to go back to how it was done in "ancient" times.  This sextant and its box have been reproduced in a faithful, authentic manner - its gorgeous and I love it!

title: just to be doubly sure...
text: I have a hanging kit for use with a hammock or hanging chair with straps and hooks, but I'm paranoid about weight limits and what-not, so...I got these to double up on the hooks to hold my hanging chair.  When sitting in it, I want to make sure nothing is gong to give way when I try to sit in the chair.  I have a pair of straps on both sides and doubled the carabiners - one fails, I have others to hold it in place.  These are working to keep my hanging chair hanging and that's all I could ask for!

title: I have an old shed with lots of stuff in it
text: But like right now, during summer, I use my weed whacker, lawn mower, trimmer - all those summer things a lot.  So instead of trekking them back to the shed, I have set up this bike tent on one side of my front porch that people can't see.  I can store my summer machines in there and they are close at hand for when I need to mow the bit of lawn I have or weed whack around the fence line.  This has given me a good place to store my stuff out of the weather as, zipped up, it's weather-proof, but also keeps everything near at hand.  Not a bad deal for my needs at all!

title: Using for yoga standing postures
text: I have a standing and sitting set of yoga that I do and I have tried holding onto the backs of chairs, counter and shelf unit - all of which are not all that great for various reasons.  This ballet barre is the best thing I've come up with for several of my standing yoga poses to keep my balance and strengthen my muscles (and my focus).  The great thing about this barre is that I can slide it near the wall so it is out of the way but available for my next yoga practice session.  I'm sure it would be great for those who practice ballet to stretch their muscles in preparation for a ballet practice session, but for me, it works to assist me in my yoga sessions.

title: Comfortable and easy to set up / take down
text: It's a bit on the heavy side, but as a camping chair, that's fine.  I'm driving to a camping site, not hiking to it and having a comfortable chair to sit in after a day at the lake or hiking the trails is necessary for my old bones!  The material on this chair is suede-like so it doesn't rub sunburned skin raw and the chair itself is sturdy to sit in and get up from.  When I go camping I have a pop up tent, a pump up mattress that is 20" tall so I am not trying to get up off the ground and this chair.  That's all I need (as well as food and a book for later).  The price is pretty good considering the quality of the chair itself.

title: I needed a quick, easy to use shovel that I could stow in a small space
text: I have an issue at my mobile home park...I like where my home is situated, but the way the owners graded the land, when it rains I get water that runs from the next set of homes, the gravel road in front of my house and all that sand, dirt and grit runs under my chain link fence gate and causes it to get blocked so I can't easily open the gate and really causes issues to close it back.  What I needed was a small shovel that could clear this crap out fast so I could open it and the shovel through another couple of inches of detritus to allow my gate to close easily.  This shovel is exactly what I needed as it is smaller and very easy to break down and store for the next time it rains...

title: For the back of my SUV this is a decent mattress
text: When I feel like tent camping, I have a cot sleeper that gets me up off the ground and is easier for me to get up off of it.  When I want to do a quick night's sleepover (sometimes when I reserve a space, it's for one night because that's all that's available) and instead of getting all my camping gear for a weekend trip, I'll put down the back seats and throw this mattress in to sleep on.  It gives the hard base of my SUV interior a little cushion and making it more comfortable for a night's sleep.  I've found this mattress easy to use and easy to stow which is the best thing I can say for a camping tool.

title: This is my second telescoping seat
text: I got this second one for my granddaughter who is like me - when we are watching her brother's soccer game, sitting in the dirt (no stands and little grass) is just not fun.  Even getting a blanket to cover the ground, at least for me, is not sufficient since I still have to get up off the ground and with arthritis in most of my joints, it usually hurts to get up.  What I love about these chairs is how portable they are - they weigh almost nothing so carrying them around is not a problem at all.  Opening them and then closing them is so easy - just a slight twist and it is extended so you can sit down.  A slight pull and twist again and it closes up to a small, round, easy to carry instant seat!  What's really nice is that I can extend my seat to it's full size and be comfortable while my granddaughter, being a smaller person, can extend her seat less so that it is at a height she is comfortable sitting on.  I've had a few carry with me chairs and while many were good chairs to sit in, none of them were or are as lightweight and portable as this seat.  Soccer games, camping, even hiking when you want to pause and take a rest, this is the best seat to take with you!

title: Oh man, so simple to put up - what could be easier?
text: I'm old enough to remember the tents that took 30 minutes to an hour to put up and that's if you had all the parts AND you were lucky!  I remember the first tent I had that you had to put together these hollow-tube rods and then thread them through loops on the edges of the tent and THEN try to connect them to some piece at the top...I remember working for an hour in the sun, in my driveway to get that stupid tent up and working before going on a camping trip and ended up throwing it in the trash and packing the older tent I had.  This fantastic tent will not disappoint you - it WORKS and the setup is literally a minute!  What's more, I like that this is a taller tent so no stooping over to walk around inside or having to get on your hands and knees to get inside.  I mean, if you are going hiking in the far backwoods, your tent is going to be different than if you are pulling into a camping site with your car and setting up there.  This is a GREAT camping site tent for a couple of adults and even a few kids.  It's breathable (unlike my old tent) and has some nice features, like the mesh ceiling to watch the night sky after turning in for the evening and the mesh bag for cell phones/tablets as well as an included electric cord should you have/need a back-up power generator while away from home.  This tent, for the price and what you get, it really is the best!

title: My grandson HAD to try it right after I got it
text: My grandson was at my place while his mom and dad were attending a concert my granddaughter was performing in.  They knew he wouldn't have fun sitting through all the other performances, so they dropped him at my house to spend the night.  After visiting the neighboring horse ranch and feeding the horses some apples, we came back to find this had been delivered.  He saw the picture on the side of the bag and got so excited - I'm thinking he believed this was planned just for him!  So I said we'd set it up on the back porch and he could sleep out there if that's what he wanted to do.  Heck yes!  So...pulled it out and set it up.  Man, it is sturdy!  But my grandson said it is comfy and he liked that he had a place to put his tablet.  I stayed up most of the night to watch him on the cot - I sure didn't want him wandering off, but he seemed to sleep like he dead which tells me that this cot IS comfortable.  Easy to set up, a little more effort to take down, but this cot is a hit with my grandson - he put dibs on it for the next time he comes over.  I might have to get a second one for my granddaughter...

title: I have a smaller pop up tent
text: And I do like that tent as it is very easy to set up, but wow...this one is my first pump it up tent and it is amazing!  Larger than my other tent, this one seems to have been thought out so well with the tarp to put down first, the pump (so often with items like this - think kiddie pools and such you have to supply your own pump) and the awning and what I found the coolest is two separate areas.  Mom and dad in one section, kids in the other, or a place for gear like backpacks, extra chairs, cooler - what have you.  All in all, this is one of the best tents I've ever had.  My only negative is that it is much heavier.  This is NOT a backpacking kind of tent.  It's the type you pull your car up to the camping area, pull it out and set it up.  Other than that, it's GREAT!

title: Great for a casual fishing day
text: I'm not great fishing person, but I do enjoy going out to the lake, setting up camp and heading to the shore where I'll set up a chair near the waterline, get this fishing rod and reel and out and cast my line out into the water.  Half the time I don't get a bite, but I'm not focused so much on the catching as I am having a nice, peaceful day at the lake.  I have caught a fish with this gear so I'm not saying there's anything wrong with it - what I can say is that when I'm going to the lake, carrying a fold up chair, a small jug with cold lemonade, and this portable fishing kit, is easy peasy and when I'm ready to get back to camp for either fresh grilled fish or a packed sandwich, I'm not feeling weighed down with too much to carry.  This is extremely portable and for a casual fishing person like me, it is perfect.

title: I just got an inflatable tent...
text: Yes, an inflatable tent!  Instead of those sticks you put together or just the pop up kind, this tent has air tubes that you fill and that's what raises the tent!  Yeah, different huh?  But for me, anything to make camping easier is my mantra.  Who wants to spend hours trying to get a tent up and then be so exhausted all they want to do is lay down in it!  So, it's not like these are huge tubes, but instead of using a hand pump, I tried this neat little USB rechargeable pump and in just a few minutes I had a fully-inflated tent - woo-hoo!  This little compressor will work on my car tires if they are low, oh, and it did inflate the double air mattress I used in the tent, too. As small as this is, it will be part of my car's emergency roadside kit that covers the basics (water for the radiator, oil, a small jump-starter and a few other items) because, well, tire inflation is part of the basics and this little compressor is up for the job as well as many other inflation jobs as well...might need to have two of these...one in the house, one in the car...

title: My friend's youngest grandchild is at that stage
text: You know, if you remember having them or if you are a parent IN that stage - where they are so full of energy it seems they can't STOP!  And usually at the same time they zone into everything they shouldn't touch or have.  I remember my daughter at that age and tried my best to teach her to leave things alone...she would go after everything I said "no" to with that gleeful look in her eye!  Yeah, that's what this trampoline is for - they can bounce and bounce and bounce and get a LOT of that excess energy out of them without YOU having to chase after them or clear the room of anything they might get their hands on.  My friend has a covered back porch where we set this up and between the two of us, I think it took about 20 minutes.  It looks smaller in the picture than it seems when we put it up, but hey, that's a picture versus the actual item.  We sat down at the table to relax for a minute before her daughter brought over the little ball of energy that is her grandson.  Her daughter came out to see for herself and we all had a laugh when she put him in the trampoline enclosure.  At first he wasn't sure he liked it until he started bouncing and and squealing at the same time.  He was having a blast!  It's too bad he didn't have a brother or sister just a year or so older - they both would have had so much fun together!  But, the nice thing is, we had this set up outside, so he was getting his exercise in the fresh air, but in the shade so he didn't cook in the sun and we could sit nearby and sip ice tea and laugh and talk to him without having to chase him around.  Ah, that was the best part of having this trampoline - better than TV for watching and less strenuous than tearing around through the house after him for 3 hours before his internal battery winds down!

title: I live in a mobile home park
text: And both my neighbors are retired, like me, and both have younger grandchildren like me.  I asked them both if they would help in setting it up that it would be the "communal" trampoline for our collective grandkids.  They were both tickled pink to help putting it together and my one neighbor's two grandchildren were the first to try it out - they had a blast jumping and laughing and grandma was taking pictures to send to her son so he could see how much fun they were having (and wearing themselves out in the process)!  The mobile home park is near some walking trails that go by the lake and that's great for when us old folks have the energy, but having this trampoline is a great way for the kids to release a lot of their boundless energy when we're just not able to keep up with them.  Fun to watch them bouncing around, too!  This trampoline was easy for the three of us to put up right behind our homes so it's just a couple of steps outside our back doors and with a folding chair handy, any one of us can sit and watch them play.  It sure seems sturdy - I hope it lasts a long time, too!

title: I have gone through a few tents in my time
text: I still have a "throw" one that's just like the window screen I use in my car - the kind that literally pops open and up.  It's small, but if I'm going to be out for just a night, like joining some friends at a nearby campground for someone's birthday or something, it is adequate, but if I'm going camping myself which is usually a 3-4 day thing, I want a tent that is more comfortable for me to spend time in/around.  That, is THIS ONE!  First, being able to more or less STAND UP inside a tent is a MUST for me.  I'm older and crawling around on the floor, trying to literally crab-walk out just to stand up - no...I want to be able to get up on two feet inside the tent and be able to walk out of it.  I may have to bend my head a little bit, but with this tent and my height, that's not much.  Okay, the other part about this tent is how FAST it goes up - like wicked-fast!  That sold me on this being THE tent for me - and then having the canopy for sitting in shade - this is perfect, just the one for me.  Okay, so this says 4/6 people and I am a person camping alone, but that's okay, I like having a roomy tent.  I'm not a hiker going off into the wild back-country having to tote everything on my back.  I drive into a campground of a national park and set up in a camping area.  So for me, taking this from the backseat or trunk of my car and setting it up on my campsite is easy-peasy.  Put my air mattress on the floor, sleeping bag on top of the air mattress, then set up my chair and I'm good to go!  Then it's time to go to the lake or take a walk on a nearby trail knowing my tent is up and everything is ready when I come back!

title: Just tested not a full use yet
text: Where I live we do not get freezing weather this time of year - just cool/cold that a regular blanket can deal with so I can only test this without putting it through a full use until winter comes again.  What I can say is that it heats something like the battery-powered sockets I bought last winter.  They have batteries the size of my pocket camera and charge via usb.  Their charge lasts about 3-4 hours depending on the heat level I choose.  Because I have a cell phone, tablet and those socks, I have a few power packs charged to ensure I can always keep my electronics topped up.  I mention this because that's how I tested this sleeping bag - I attached one of my larger power packs and set the bag to medium heat.  It warmed up really quick and was somewhat uncomfortable in the weather I was testing it in.  Turned it down to low and it was warm yet very comfortable.  Had it been winter and quite cold, this heated bag would have been perfect!  Of course, like my heated socks where I'm wearing shoes and have heavy pants over the socks which translates to having a good thermal blanket over/around this bag to keep the heat directed at your body.  So, the bag works great; however, make sure you have powerpacks and a thermal blanket to ensure the bag keeps YOU warm.

title: Wish it was a fast pop-up
text: I have a tent that literally, can be erected in less than 3 minutes - it's a wonderful pop-up tent, but this, because it is for changing, showering and pooing in, it really should be a fast pop-up as well.  I mean, when you gotta go, you gotta go!  When I plan a camping trip, I often end up in the more primitive sections because they are often more available than those with amenities.  That's okay, I have all the equipment to make a weekend stay pleasant and that includes this shower tent.  I like that I can stand up and change - so much easier than all that maneuvering around in the regular tent because it isn't tall enough for me to fully stand up when changing clothes.  Besides, after a day walking the trails or spending time by the lake, when I step in this shower tent and take a shower, I'll be changing out of sweaty clothes to clean ones - all done in this tent.  Then there is the other personal matter...I have a camp toilet and when I have to do my business, this tent also comes in handy.  For those with an RV that has all the comforts of home, they may still find this useful if the kids are coming back from the lake - just let them shower off in the tent so they don't track dirt in the RV.  But for me, this tent is a must-have for the more primitive camping I'm used to for staying clean and fresh even in the "rough!"

title: After taking this tent out camping...
text: For me - an older lady that goes camping alone - this tent is great. What I do have to say is that it states for a pair of adults and a pair of kids this tent would be great and I'm saying, well...maybe, but I doubt the four of them would be comfortable in this tent.  Me, if I were talking tents for families with kids, this is a good tent for the kids alone.  I say this because I'm 5' 4" and found this to be a snug fit.  I have a foot pump mattress pad and a 3-season sleeping bag so I am comfy when using this tent for myself.  What is the best part for me is the ultra-fast set up.  I've used tents for years and I remember my first time with a "pop-up" tent where I had to put together a bunch of straw-like tubes and then thread them into a tent channel...times four...I'm telling you that it was a PITA and ended up being thrown in the trash!  So with this one, it is truly a quick, pop-up tent and for me - for one person - it is roomy and comfortable.

title: Just what I needed
text: I am retired, but the majority of my working life was spent working on a computer.  I have arthritis in my hands, wrists and while it could be the same in my shoulder, I believe the pain there is from carpal tunnel syndrome due to years of typing hour after hour on a computer. I tried this ball to see if it would assist in building up a bit of strength in my arms and to see if it could dissipate a bit of the pain in both my wrists and shoulders.  It did take me a few failed attempts to figure out how to use this ball, but once I got what I needed to do to keep the ball moving I could feel the benefits.  Well, maybe not while I was holding the ball and moving my hand/arm around, but after I stopped on my right (dominant) side, I could feel my shoulder kinda tingly, but no immediate pain like it usually feels when I stretch or move that area.  I am going to keep using this ball every day and hope that it truly makes some permanent changes to how my shoulders feel.  I don't expect it to completely rid me of pain as that is a part of being older, but if it can reduce it to a manageable level, then I'm good with that!

title: My great nephew loves it
text: With my arthritic hands I cannot set this up myself.  Trying to get the fabric over the frame requires more strength than I can muster without pain in my hands and wrists.  I loved the look of the chair and when I received it, I was surprised at how small and lightweight it was.  Had hoped that when I go to an event or out camping that this would work for me, but putting it together isn't an option so I asked my great nephew what he does when he goes out fishing.  That young man would spend as many days as possible fishing - he LOVES to fish!  He told me he usually just sits on the ground when he gets tired of standing, so I gave him this chair.  I watched this strong kid assemble it without a problem and he seemed quite happy sitting in it - that it was comfortable.  He told me the next time his mom dropped him at the lake for a day of fishing, he would take the chair to spare his jeans from becoming so dirty - in other words, no more sitting on the ground.  I've seen the pack he takes with him - food, water, a zippered case for his fishing stuff - this chair will fit in his pack and since he's not walking miles, just being dropped near the lake for a day of fishing, this chair will be easy to take and I think make his fishing day at least a little more comfortable!

title: I was looking for a "new" outdoor game
text: Bocce ball is not new, but what I was looking for was something besides horseshoes, cornhole and badminton - something easy to play and didn't have many rules - just something fun and easy.  Getting these Bocce balls filled that bill exactly!  Easy to play, they come in a nice zippered bag making them very transportable - fast to "set up" and "tear down" so to speak and pretty much anybody can play from child to adult.  The balls are well made and highly visible and will be a great addition to our outdoor games for several years.

title: I like to go and spend the day at the lake.
text: I'm not a fishing person, but my great-nephew is.  He's won a few trophies from his catch and release club and he loves and I mean LOVES to fish!  I brought this nice, contained little zippered pouch with everything it to his mom's house and his eyes lit up.  We made a date to go to the lake near my house and he brought this rod with him.  Now, he may be in his early teens, but he has been fishing for about 7-8 years and winning trophies for the past 4 years so he knows what he likes in a fishing rod.  He got himself set up and let his line fly.  A couple of hours later and a few catch and release's later, he said that the rod I gave him was now his favorite and he would be taking it with him the next time his catch and release group was out on the lake.  I pronounce this a great gift to any avid fisher-person you may know!

title: This is a great smaller table for outdoor use
text: Anywhere you want to go, this table is perfect to bring along.  It isn't too large and is a fast set up.  It has it's own carry case so if you want to use a little camp stove while out, this table will be perfect for it.  I have a few lightweight items that I always take with me - my favorite folding chair, a pack kit with a cook stove, pan, plates and utensils and this table.  Quick to pack, takes up very little space and off I go!  Definitely get one for your trips to the woods and/or the lake - you'll be ready for anything!

title: For my neighbor and I to watch the night time wildlife
text: Our row of houses has a wooded area behind them that belongs to the US Army Corps of Engineers which is a part of the lake that isn't too far from our houses.  We have coyotes, armadillos, raccoons and a few more critters that regularly visit our yards.  My neighbor was thrilled to try these out after I'd had the first try - I did see a coyote pass by my chain link fence at the back of my yard and I'm pretty sure the odd things I saw were armadillos...hard to tell exactly because they are faster than you'd think, but considering the humped back, I'm almost positive the three I saw were armadillos...this works well for what I wanted to use it for.  My lot is not terribly deep and the government sends out a bush hog about once a month to keep the woods from crowding too close to our back fences so there is a somewhat "clean" band or swath of about 10 to 12 feet they clear.  Keeps the critters from taking over, I'd imagine.  Anyway, my next door neighbor is positive that she has had armadillos trying to dig around the edge of her foundation - maybe looking for grubs?  I don't really know, but that's what she borrowed them for - to see if she could catch them in the act.  I explained how to use them and did tell her that they use a bunch of batteries so if they went off, it might be that the batteries would need recharging.  She said she had a bunch of AA's - the next day she told me she did not catch one scratching around her foundation, but that she did see a couple run by on her side yard.  I told her she could keep them for a few days to keep and eye out on her nocturnal "guests."  These night vision binoculars are rather cool, though this is my first time using any so I don't have anything to compare them with.  For me, I think the price point seems high, but again, this is my first pair.  I can say that they work for what I'm using them for - it is interesting to watch the night time creatures that live behind my house.

title: I have a solid black one like this
text: I love all the colors and these are the coolest portable seats ever!  Very lightweight, has a handle so it's easy to carry or if you don't want to carry it, I clip it to my crossbody purse with a carabiner - have telescoping seat will travel!  And hands' free!  I've had more people make over this telescoping seat - it's so easy to pop up to the full height for me to sit on and I am a big person...it holds my weight just fine.  You can pop up the seat to a lower height if you have a little person with you who gets tired of standing and you don't want them sprawling on a dirty sidewalk or whatever.  It's also easy to close this seat down - just a twist and a push and bam!  Closed!  Great to take camping or if you are going to a large event and will want to sit at some point.  This is a cool seat!

title: After working in the garden a few hours
text: This is what I need when I first come inside.  Granted, I am going to take a shower very soon, but in the meantime, I'm getting a drink and putting one of these around my neck cools me down faster so I don't feel so fatigued when I do step into the shower to rinse off.  If I expect to be out longer in the yard, I can wet one from the garden hose and slip it around my neck to give me some relief from the heat.  Nice to have around, just in case!

title: This weighs absolutely nothing!
text: Which is NOT to say it is nothing - what a neat, easily portable chair to clip to your backpack and carry with you.  It reminded me of putting up a tent with the aluminum poles that make up the frame of the chair.  Be prepared to work to get that last pole to slide into the fabric part of the chair as it does require a bit of tension in order for the chair to be useful.  What's impressive is how much this chair can hold as I am not a small, skinny person.  It's reasonably comfortable even for a bigger person.  I have a small, foldable "table" I use to put my feet up.  While it's not my overstuffed recliner at home, this chair is great for carrying with me when camping and comfortable at the end of the day when I'm sitting by the fire.

title: Wow...
text: I thought this would be a great way to carry some very delicate, breakable items I have, but didn't think much beyond that when I saw this.  This is a BRUTE of a box!  It's big, it's somewhat heavy and man, if you had something breakable tucked inside this case, a gorilla could throw it around and I'd say your delicate item would still be fine inside!  Okay, I don't know that it would be totally protected if a gorilla really did throw it around, but I can say this is one tough case!  I am mightily impressed by this case - it's thick outer layer, the fact that it is somewhat waterproof, and if you had more than one, it's stackable.  My use was to keep several of my hand guns in one place, easy for me to get to, yet together.  I cut the foam into three pieces and then cut spaces into the layers so that I can keep several of my hand guns in one place.  Nice case!

title: Warm, but...
text: I have a pair of heated socks and have issues with them because of the batteries that take up space and seem to cause problems when trying to keep them up on my calves.  I'm a larger person so I was a bit upset that the makers didn't realize that they should make the area where the battery resides a bit larger so as to accommodate both the battery AND my meaty calf!
