I mention this because I was a bit worried about how the batteries would work in these gloves.  That worry was taken care of with regard to the gloves and I'm glad that is a non-problem with them.  The thing that works intermittently was the touch-screen finger with my phone.  Not sure what the issue is, but if it is noted in the information to sell these gloves, then it should work!  Aside from that, these gloves heat up well and while I think the highest heat level is a bit uncomfortable, that's just me.  Because I also have arthritis in my hands/fingers, when I'm outside in cold weather, I really, REALLY need for my hands to be warm, otherwise those joints hurt so bad trying to flex and hold things, it just isn't worth it,.  So I am happy with how these heat and how long the battery power lasts.  Just either work on the touch finger or leave it off.  Oh, and the cinch around the wrist is great for keeping out cold and snow!

title: This idea is great, the execution could use a bit more thought
text: I am a larger person and older so trying to just "go in the woods" is pretty much impossible for me.  I need to sit and this sort of fits the bill, but my thought was that it is a fixed height which makes its use somewhat limited.  I mean, if you are travelling with little people (and I remember this when I was a small child on road trips with my parents) that when they say they have to go, they mean right now.  As a kid, my parents opened the front and back passenger car doors as a way to shield us from people driving by and then just having to squat like kids can do...but I can't do that any longer with my arthritic knees.  Anyway, the height of this is not helpful for me as it is too short for me to get up easily but might be too tall for a small child.  My thought about using it was that I have a neat camping seat that telescopes up and "hooks" into place and can be telescoped all the way up for an adult or left with several rings of the base left "down" so a small child can sit on it.  My thought was how that design could possibly have been used to create a potty similar to this that would be height adjustable for the user.  Not that this is awful - it works for what it is - its just that the height is...a problem for me.

title: This is a neat little set, but...
text: Okay, I was impressed with it when I opened the box and I still think it is a neat little set that will be useful when needed, BUT...first, there are no instructions.  Okay so the one piece doesn't need any instructions - fill with lighter fluid and use it to soak the material on the base of the other piece.  Duh.  But let's look at the lighter itself.  How do I change out the wick when needed?  And how do I get the wick material out of the holder that was included?  How do I change out the flint pellet?  I mean, am I going to take the entire thing apart and figure it out on my own?  That's my problem with this set.  It is brass, it feels quality made and comes with extras and that's perfect, but...just include some instructions please!

title: Everyone should have one of these!
text: I have a few other portable chairs, but this is by far my favorite.  It is lightweight, has a handle to carry it or what I do is use a carabiner to clip it to my purse or backpack, is so easy to pop up to use and then twist and make it into a "pancake" again - last, it is very sturdy!  I'm not a small person and I feel comfortable sitting on this stool without feeling like it might go out from under me.  Standing on line (at elections, for tickets, etc.) or spending time at large events (I have used this for a couple of riverfront events where sitting on concrete would have been so uncomfortable) and being able to twist it closed afterwards was so easy for transporting back to the car.  Then, of course, there's camping and hiking - this is perfect for taking with you on a hike and you want to take a rest break but don't want to sit on the ground.  This is my go-to portable seat!

title: For being outside shoveling snow these are great
text: That was the reason for getting these in my case.  Standing outside, shoveling snow, cleaning off the car, even standing in the snow while my dogs do their business (I have little dogs so sometimes they have issues in snow) my hands can get COLD in leather gloves or even good mittens.  I thought I'd try these and they do keep my poor old arthritic fingers from popping and cracking when it is that cold outside and I'm spending an hour shoveling the walk in front of my house...I guess the people who make these may have some parameters for how the heating elements run in the gloves - the heat is on the outside of the palm and the fingers.  Maybe because the elements could get damaged when shoveling snow if they were in the palm?  I don't know, but it sure would be great if the heat was all-over if possible.

title: Not bad, but why a manual inflating pillow?
text: The pad itself is decent - it self-inflates fine and helps keep you up off the ground.  I use it with a sleeping bag so it's more than enough, but the pillow on it has to be blown up by hand?  What's with that?  Either make the mat flat and extend it to the pillow portion or somehow change the pillow section to be self-inflating as well.  Personally, I would prefer to get rid of the manual inflate pillow section and make the mat longer and flat.  I have a camp pillow I bring, so not a problem for me.

title: It is really cold at the moment
text: So I'm not out camping - not until the weather around my area stabilizes to more spring-like instead of frigid dead of winter, but I did put this on my bed and check it out. It is a nice sleeping bag.  It mentions 3 season which is okay, but I'd put it at the higher temps on the edges of fall and spring unless you have supplemental bedding.  I have a self-inflating mattress pad that keeps me off the ground so my body heat doesn't dissipate into the ground under me. I also have a down-style camping blanket to throw on top of this sleeping blanket to assist in trapping my body heat in between the inflatable mattress pad and the blanket in order to keep me as warm as possible.  This sleeping bag by itself is great for the higher temps, say above 50.  As far as the bag itself, it is warm and soft when zipped inside.  It took a bit of work to roll it up tight enough to fit back it its bag, but it can be done - just have to get it small and keep the rolling up tight.

title: Nice addition to my camping gear
text: I have a small tent, a self-inflating camp mattress and a double size sleeping bag for 3 season use. I have a nice portable chair, a small table, a set of cooking gear, a cooler and now this. I thought this was a great idea considering my hands get messy or sticky when I'm out and about. I also have a water bladder to be sure I have extra water handy should I end up at a primitive campground and that's why this sink is a great addition to my camping gear. It's a bit bulky but fits in my SUV fine and since I go camping by myself, I do have room for what I need as well as what I want to take with me. Being able to use a bit of water to clean cooking gear, hands, face or what have you just makes me feel better. I'm not taking my home with me like an RVer, but I do like being able to have some cleanliness when I'm out.

title: I would hawk these on the street if I could!
text: I absolutely LOVE this portable seat!  Considering we all have had to spend time on lines these days - waiting to sign up for a COVID shot, voting, waiting in line to receive a COVID shot...and I have trouble standing for long periods of time because I am older, but others may have physical issues - back issues, knee injuries, you name it.  This stool is extremely light weight and has a handle so you can carry it with you or use a carabiner to clip it to your backpack if you take it with you on a hike.  What is amazing is how fast and easy it is to open and close this stool. Basically it's a pull-twist motion that engages the "sheaths" that are the spine of this stool. The opposite to close/shut the stool - just a quick pull-twist and then push to close it like an accordian.  The best part of this stool is that if you have children and they are tired of standing, this stool can be pulled to a shorter height for a child to sit on. Fully open, it is a nice height for an adult and then shorter for kids. Last and best is that it is STURDY!  I am a big girl and it holds me without a problem.  Get one, get two - take them camping, hiking, to stand on lines, whatever, whenever - no better portable seat out there!

title: I like to try things against my home made camp cooker
text: I followed some online instructions and made myself a paint-can size rocket stove that is fairly lightweight, has a handle (I have a small carabineer clipped to the handle so the stove can be clipped to my backpack) and burns small, gathered twigs gathered onsite or carried with me.  This little cooker is very small and easily packed which is a good thing; however, because it is so small, it isn't as sturdy to hold pots/pans well.  This little stove requires a very level spot or it could tip.  I am comparing it, again, to my home made rocket stove which is sturdy, which holds up to any pot/pan and can take more twigs and small pieces of wood to keep the fire going for as long as you may need.  Again, this isn't a bad little camping burner and might be the perfect one for others, but I'll keep my home made one as my go-to camping stove.

title: This blanket is lightweight but warm!
text: I am astounded by this blanket - it comes in such a small pack and it is light, very light.  Then when you pull it around you on a cold night, it is very warm.  The material repels moisture and is very sturdy.  I have a padded self-inflating mat for my tent, a bottom "blanket" that has a moisture resistant side and a fleece side that I will sleep on and then this will be my cover blanket when I'm out camping.  For sitting by the fire and then for keeping me warm when I'm sleeping in the tent - this is my go-to blanket!  Easy to pack for camping trips!

title: This is great stuff!
text: I have been using powdered milk and milk products (powdered butter and sour cream) for a while because I live alone and buying fresh that goes bad before I can finish it is not financially good for me.  With the powdered, I can make just what I want and with this product, I also get the addition of a great many vitamins and minerals needed every day.  It tastes good too!  If I were to change anything, my other powdered milk came in a large canister that had a molded handhold and a screwtop.  Makes it easier for me to pick up from the high shelf in the cabinet and the screwtop just made it easier for me to open when I first got it.  That's just a preference on my part, but older folks like me do have arthritis quite often and that's just a thought for the container and how it is picked up and opened.  Other than that, this is a great shelf-stable drink to have on hand.

title: Sitting outside on a cool night
text: I have a nice, heavy-duty PVC set of two folding chairs and a round table.  My dogs like to spend time in the yard, wandering around sniffing everything an because I have a very small, old teacup poodle, I will not let her stay outside by herself - even her "big" sister is small at 7 pounds!  I live near a wood line with many wild critters - coyotes, owls and hawks to name a few that could be a problem for my little fur-girls.  So I sit outside with them and when it's cool, I bring this blanket out and wrap it around me.  It's soft on the inside and with the weather-resistant outer material, if it has rained and my chair is a tad damp, I don't have to worry about having wet pants when I come back in.  This blanket is easy to clean and while it does take a little effort to get it folded and rolled into a "log" the size of the carry-bag, it's worth it.  I have a great blanket for home and should I go camping or attend an outdoor function, I can grab the bag and take this blanket with me.

title: Well...warm toes/front upper foot
text: The picture shows that the heat is along the sides.  I had hoped that with heating elements along the sides would keep my entire foot warm.  Nope.  The heating elements are concentrated on the upper section of the foot, over the toes and not all the way to my ankle .  Now for the batteries - OMG these batteries are THICK!  Nearly 3/4ths of an inch thick!  I charged them up and thought, oh well, if I didn't want to wear my boots...because I wouldn't be able to zip or tie either of my pairs of winter boots over the tops of the socks because of the thick batteries.  Now the reason in particular that I gravitated to this pair of socks was the remote control.  That works fine.  I mean, if I want to change the heat level or turn them off, bending down and pushing a button on both socks to change heat or turn them off seemed stupid to me.  So I can say the remote works well.  As for the heat, I'm just not happy with the concentration just on the top-front of each foot.  The picture is misleading - state that the heating elements are ONLY on the top-front of each sock so consumers are better informed.  Last, does the battery packs HAVE to be that thick?  You literally cannot have these on and put a leg up under you or the battery pack will jab your leg (or any way you are not simply sitting with each foot straight in front of you).  I gave them four stars because they do work, just not in the way I expected they should.

title: This is my second one and I love them!
text: These are the very best "emergency" seating ever made!  I went out for early voting this year and took my other one like this one with me in the car, just in case.  I mean, this portable seat, when closed is lightweight, as big a round as the seat and it has a handle for easy carrying.  For when you may expect to sit in a line waiting (like voting or getting tickets to a great event), this is the best seat!  The finger-holes make it easy to pop it open or closed.  When closed, it is easy to store.  That is why I ordered a second one.  When I have someone going with me to watch the fireworks or whatever, having a pair of these seats keeps an old lady like me from having to try to gracefully get off the ground!

title: Nice pop up tent
text: I have to say I do have another faster pop up tent, but it is basically a one-person tent!  It is made like those car sun visors that you twist to pop open and twist to pop closed.  Can't get much faster than that!  But this tent is not far behind in the quick pop up and of course, it is larger.  I will take this one when I am staying put in a campground and my other when I am hiking and plan on sleeping "in the wild" when hiking.  With this one, it is definitely a sturdy tent and I do like how compact it is for packing in my car with my other camping gear.  Excellent tent for two adults or one adult and a couple of kids.

title: Lightweight and FAST set up
text: I'm not much of a backwoods hiker that would go as far as I can and then set up camp wherever, but if I was, this is the tent for such a hike.  Me, I have a small car and when I go camping, it's just me, so this tent is perfect for me.  Now, the set up is so fast it's scary.  It is just like the pop-open car window shades you've seen (with one difference), but for real, that's pretty much how it pops up.  The material is sturdy and the tent itself should fit most folks (maybe not a 6 foot tall person) and has great ventilation so you breathe and sleep easier.  If there is the possibility of rain, be sure to use the piece for the top vent so the rain doesn't come in.  The zipper is sturdy as well and with the tent staked down, I felt quite comfortable inside on my air mattress bed, and safe that a breeze was not going to blow my tent over/away.  This is a great little tent that takes up very little space, sets up in a minute and is comfortable for sleep in.  Definitely worth it!

title: I had a cam set up on a porch pole
text: And this one I set up on my neighbor's porch pole so we had a cross section.  The camera I have had for about a year does fine for what I use it for - to see what critters come in my yard, but this one that I attached to my neighbor's porch pole...wow.  I mean the difference between the two is like night and day!  My old one takes okay pictures of the opossums and the smaller armadillos that can squeeze through the larger openings between my shed and the fence posts (not big, but big enough apparently), but my neighbor has heard lots of scratching around her home and so I thought this way she could see what was coming in her yard.  She doesn't have it fenced...anyway, this camera caught excellent stills of the huge armadillos (okay, compared to the bitty ones getting in my yard) coming into her yard.  They have huge claws and not sure if they are finding grubs around the edge of her house's foundation or what, but I think we figured out what's scratching around her house thanks to this camera!  My old one would have seen them as well, but the quality of the pictures just isn't there.  I'd recommend just about anyone interested in what critters may be coming in their yard at night try out this camera - you'd be surprised at what shows up!  For the price, it is SO worth it!

title: It's always hands and feet (okay and nose)
text: Those three are definitely our cold spots in winter and if you live where it snows regularly, feet are the coldest part even when wearing winter boots.  So having a heated pair of socks is an amazing thing!  It is just the beginning of winter where I live so I have used these socks more indoors than outdoors so far.  These are very comfortable socks and with the battery charged, the heat they give out is wonderful!  My toes are almost always cold and man, these socks made them nice and toasty.  I got so comfortable with the heat infusing my toes and feet that I sat down and promptly fell asleep the first time!  Yeah, I know, but with warm feet, I was just so comfortable I just leaned back in my chair, closed my eyes and bam!  Woke up about an hour later.  Still with quite warm feet - aaaahhhh!  If I were to offer the designer/manufacturer a suggestion, it would be to extend the heating elements the length of the sides of the feet.  What I mean is feeling warmth all along the instep and arch areas of the feet.  Other than that, these are going to be my best friends come the really cold weather this winter, but for now, they are great for wearing inside my cool house (with the thermostat dialed down).

title: This one is mine!
text: I did get another handwarmer that splits in two for my granddaughter, but this one is for me.  When I was a child, my father had an old-fashioned hand warmer that I remember fondly - him filling it with lighter fluid, lighting it, sliding the metal cap on it and man, did that thing get HOT!  So I'm happy that this one has different heating levels and is charged by usb connection.  I love having it in my cardigan or coat pocket and put my hand on it, pull it out and hold it in both hands and feel the warmth around my palms and fingers.  The light around it at night is kind of nice - not that I need it, but it is helpful when dark out to shine a bit of light (especially if I fumble the hand warmer and drop it).

title: Hat is toasty warm
text: I read somewhere that people lose most of their body heat from their head as well as their feet.  Now, in the winter, we all wear shoes and socks so at least our body has a fighting chance of keeping body heat in from that end, but many of us go out without a hat on our head!  So okay, at hat by itself would help, but man, having a hat that actually warms your head when the wind is blowing at it's 20 degrees, now that's a gift!  This hat does just that - wraps your head in blessed warmth.  It is a tiny bit big, but that works in my favor because I have long hair and usually stuff most of it up in my hats.  Now, it isn't always just an outdoor hat...I don't know why my cubicle area is always cold in winter - I have a ceiling vent nearby, but I have often worn fingerless gloves to at least part of my hands warm while sitting at the computer and now with this hat, I can stay even warmer in the refrigerator that is my workplace!  This hat is a bit pricey, but well worth it if you work out in the winter weather or like me, have a really cold cubicle.

title: Cold feet no more!
text: Let me first say that a few years ago we had one of those horrible, bitter cold winters where the daytime temps didn't go above 20 degrees for several weeks on end.  At the time I was living on a houseboat with just space heaters to warm my floating home.  I wore a pair of thin summer socks, a pair of woolen winter socks, a pair of fleece-lined slipper socks and then put my feet inside a pair of oversize faux fur slippers with memory foam atop the rubber sole.  Even with all that, my feet were so cold!  Understand that boats, sitting in water, end up with ambient temps near what the water temp is.  So, cold?  Yes, I know cold!  These socks make the cold less of a problem and more of an anticipation!  Yes, let it get cold so I can wear these and laugh in the face of freezing air!  HA!  My toes are warm, the bottom of my feet are warm and that's what I need - no numb toes, ever again!  I will say that the wiring seems to be less than sturdy which it should be considering we are talking about socks, but I will be careful because I LOVE having warm feet!

title: Not yet bitter cold, but I'm ready with these!
text: Every year we get some really brutal days and I have always worn gloves or mittens and usually had to put them in coat pockets just so my fingers wouldn't go numb.  Winter is just like that, right?  Oh, but with these mittens my fingers will not feel as if they are freezing solid on those 5 degree days with a strong wind blowing.  The day may be EEEeeewww, but with these mittens it can also be Aaaahhhh!  It's like my car - it has a heated passenger and driver's seat and while most people blast their heater in the car, when I slide onto the driver's seat, it's that AAaaaahhh moment feeling the warmth of the seat radiating to my backside.  So much better than feeling a blast of air in my face.  What I mean is that the radiating warmth of these mittens is so much better than pretty much any other way of trying to warm my hands - just feels good on a bitter-cold day.  When the weatherman states it will be really cold, first thing I am going to do is grab these before going outside!

title: hand warmer for me!
text: When I was a kid my dad used to hand me his hand warmer when we were outside during cold weather.  It was a "manual" kind - the interior had something like rock wool that was soaked in butane and lit and then the metal casing was slid inside a thick insulated bag and put in your pocket.  It could get rather hot!  I mention this because it brings back fond memories, but also to illustrate the difference in the "old fashioned" hand warmers and this one.  I love how easy this is to charge, even in my car, and the 3 levels of warmth depending on how cold it is and/or what you are doing.  I can put this in my pocket on low heat while I'm scraping the ice off my windshield and windows, then grab the warmer and let my fingers regain some feeling before trading the scraper for the shovel and shoveling the snow away from the car and off the sidewalk.  However many times I need to, I can stop shoveling and grab the warmer to keep my hands and fingers from going numb - that's what I appreciate having this handwarmer!  If you have kids that wait at the bus stop or have to walk to school even in winter, giving them a handwarmer might be just the thing to give them a "boost" of warmth while standing in the cold!

title: This works well
text: I actually sleep on an air mattress every night.  Not one like this, but I think that makes me uniquely suited to say that for what this is, it works well.  It's not like my 24" air mattress, but when you are out hiking or camping or maybe just going to the beach this gets you up off the ground.  When you are laying on the ground and the ground is wet...and it sucks your body warmth from you...that's how this mattress works well - to keep you dry, to keep the ground from draining off your body warmth and at the beach in particular, keeping you from sinking in the sand!  Okay, so you won't sink unless you chose quick sand to lay on, but my point is that when you want/need to lay on the ground, whether it is to sleep or just relax, having a mattress between you and the ground gives a bit of extra comfort to make it nicer to be where you are!  This mattress is easy to inflate and deflate, it is lightweight and great for carrying with you wherever you go.

title: Years of frozen fingers when cleaning snow off my car
text: And around my house...it hasn't been cold enough YET for me to need these this year, but I have tried them out and my oh my do these work great!  I'm an older lady that lives alone so when it snows and I have to go out, I'm the one out there knocking the snow off my car, scraping ice off my windows, shoveling snow from the sidewalk and around my car so that I can get from my house to my car and back again.  Okay, so I don't have a huge house but even 20 feet of sidewalk in front of my house and then another 15 or so feet of sidewalk to the stairs leading to the front door...maybe that gives the timeframe it takes for me to do what I need out in the cold.  And in the time I'm out there, my hands FREEZE!  Not any longer though - these gloves are so warm, keeping my fingers toasty.  I also got a pair of heated socks - my boots keep the snow off, but my toes would go numb in the cold - having warm fingers (and toes) when having to shovel another 20 feet of snow is worth a great deal to me.  Meaning, what I paid for these gloves was so worth it!!!

title: Excellent to sleep on in the tent
text: I remember those horrible blow up air mattresses that SQUEEEEK every time you moved when laying on them!  Not so with this one and I do appreciate the fact that I didn't have to spend fifteen minutes trying to blow it up.  This mat is comfortable and insulates from the ground cold creeping in.  I don't go hiking with a sleeping mat, but I think if I did, this might be a bit much to carry, considering one would be also carrying water and food.  But for me, using this in my tent while camping at national parks, this mat is great - comfy and keeps me from getting too cold (from the ground).  It packs well in my car alongside my pop up tent and other camping gear.  It will be used a great deal on my camping trips.

title: Fast and easy for an old lady to put up
text: I used to have an SUV and now have a regular car.  When I had the SUV I had a tent that attached to the back of the vehicle and I could sleep in my car.  Now that I have a regular sedan, I needed a "regular" tent when I go to the national parks.  This was a great tent for my needs - I like having a larger size as I am a bigger lady, but it's not so big that it was difficult for me to put up by myself.  The ventilation in this tent is quite good.  Years ago, when I went out camping with my husband, it was a pain to put up the tent with two of us working on it and at night, it always seemed rather warm and stifling inside.  I have a nice self inflating bed and sleeping inside this tent on the bed - it's great!  Easy to put up and take down plus store in my car's trunk, this tent works well for me.

title: This is my first camping shower unit
text: And I am happy to have it.  I am a "senior" and bought the senior parks pass that allows me to stay at a very small cost at many national parks as well as many state parks.  Sometimes I have found a place I want to camp that is more "rustic" than others - meaning no toilets or showers available.  I have a camping "porta-potty" and now I have this camping shower which is great!  What I added to this unit is a large bucket I got from the local grocery story - a large white bucket with a lid that I spray painted black.  That way, if I'm camping near a lake at a primitive campsite and go for a swim or hike around the lake, I will have the bucket sitting in the sun, full of water, and being black, it will warm the water up so it isn't just cold water I shower with when I come back from my swim or hike.  The size of the bucket works really well with this shower unit since the pump hangs higher on this bucket which seems to make the unit more stable.  The bucket itself is heavier with the amount of water I can add to it - I have a pair of "hydration bladders" which I fill before going out to the campsite, so using one of them for showering is fine for me.  I do think it's very odd that this usb charging unit has a plug that is not compatible with any other usb device you might have.  I mean, I have three types of usb plug that I use already and this adds number four to the mix.  Very strange...plus I have a few headsets that have a soft plug cover that can be difficult but this one is even more so - it's fragile, so I have taken great care not to accidentally snap it off.  When I go to primitive camping areas, I do have a larger "battery tender" that can charge my phone, laptop and this unit, but just in case, I have two small hand-size power packs and a solar charger just in case.  My tent is a good sized stand up tent with a front shade cover - for a shower area, I brought a couple of sheets and clothes pins so I can shower with a small amount of privacy - oh, and I have a fold up plastic bucket that is big enough for me to stand in so I can take much of the spent shower water and dump it away from the tent.  Yes, I may be camping primitive, but I do like having the civilized things like this shower unit with me.  Nice to feel clean after a sweaty hike!

title: If you've ever spent an hour (or longer) shoveling snow...
text: and even with wool socks and boots, you come in with cold, numb toes and feet then you'll love having a pair of these socks.  It's not yet winter, but I suspect I'll be out there shoveling snow from my sidewalk and driveway and if we get a heavy snow, I'll be out there longer.  I may go out with a coat on, but I've learned to layer and take off what I need to as I work.  The problem is always my feet.  I can't take anything off and even if I were to put on two pairs of socks - I have a pair of silk and wool just for that purpose - if I have to spend more than an hour shoveling snow on a cold (and especially windy) day, my feet will burn and then go numb with the cold.  I saw these socks and thought, yes!  Like a hand warmer!  I put them on to test them and they do get my toes all toasty and warm.  This time when winter weather dumps a boatload of snow on my driveway and sidewalk, I'll pull on these socks and know that I won't have to massage my feet after coming in just to get feeling and warmth back into my feet!  These work very well!

title: This is a great 2 in 1 for toddlers
text: And possibly a bit older, depending on the child's size (height and weight).  My nephews are still little guys and like most toddlers, they have enough energy to light a small city!  Having this scooter/bike is a great way for them to work off some of their excess energy.  This scooter/bike is well made and so easy even a little person can change it from a scooter to a bike without any help (after they have watched you of course).  I am always happy when something I give them is used a LOT and this has been in use for almost the entire time they have been awake!  If you have a little person in your life, get them one of these - they will hug you for it!

title: Not just size but comes with a carry strap
text: I have a smaller mat I like, but I had to purchase a carry strap to go with it - not a big problem, but I thought that with the size, this would be a good mat to switch off with my other one.  Problem is, I like this one quite a bit more than my old one!  I am a bigger lady and trying my best to get back flexibility with yoga (I'm also in my 60s) so having a larger mat is a good thing for me.  Last, it's my color - blue!  Definitely worth having this yoga mat!

title: So cool how these expand
text: They reminded me of these compressed sponges that kids could get inside a fairly large pill capsule - one you don't swallow - but that I used to get for my kids for the bathtub.  They would pull the capsule apart and the little round ball inside the capsule would drop in the water and turn into an animal shaped, very large (considering how small it was in the capsule) sponge that they used to wash themselves.  I don't know if they still make those, but when I opened my first little towel from this package and dropped a bit of water on it, WOW!  It literally blew up and when it stopped expanding, I had this really nice cotton towel.  It was damp and I ran it over my face - the material was soft, not scratchy and felt good (we are in a heat wave as I write this), nice and wet against the delicate skin on my face.  These are going to come in handy to have - a few tucked in my purse, a few in the glove compartment of my car, a few at my desk at work and of course, I will hand a few to friends and family for their emergency use as well.  I am very pleased with these tiny, little emergency towels that can be taken anywhere as small and light as they are.

title: Excellent water bottle
text: I should say that I'm happy my bottle came intact - apparently there was some sort of packing issue with it...I received the bottle in a cardboard box that fit it, but the "shipping container" was an open-ended bubble-plastic mailer!  How I got it considering the cardboard box was completely sticking out of the open-ended mailer is beyond me, but again, I am thankful this bottle came to me intact.  My only real complaint about this bottle is the size of the opening.  I say this because I carry a water bottle to work every day and I use ice cubes in my regular bottle to keep the water cold for a long time.  My traditional bottle has a wide-mouth opening and I have an ice cube tray that makes nearly 2 inch square ice cubes - big ice cubes that melt a bit more slowly that regular-sized cubes.  This water bottle has a fairly narrow opening so I might be able to fit smaller ice cubes in it which is fine, but I did like having the big ice cubes in my water bottle because they do melt more slowly, keeping the water cold longer.  So, back to the bottle itself - I like that you have a choice between the regular screw cap and the one that has a flip-open straw opening.  This one is a bit taller than my other water bottle, but not quite as big around so I'm pretty sure that, internally, they both hold the same amount of liquid.  Last, I chose the turquoise color as it is my favorite - it is a pretty bottle!  All in all I am happy with this bottle and am sure I will use it regularly, switching between this one and my other water bottle.

title: I'm older, heavy and have arthritis
text: When I was younger, I could sit cross-legged for meditation without a problem.  I can't do it at my age today.  This pillow helps elevate my behind just enough so that there is less pressure on my knees and ankles when I cross my legs.  Okay, so any pillow could work, right?  But this pillow is firmer, less "squishy" than a regular pillow and that's why it is good for sitting and meditating.  I love it - you might too!

title: The mouthpiece is the sticking point
text: Sorry - the mouthpiece is not easy to clean which is one of the rating points.  The bottle, the screw part of the cap are both easy to clean, but if you drink anything other than plain water, it will not get completely clean without a great deal of extra work.  Even if you do drink plain water, your mouth germs on it (and the "spit factor") means that you still will not have a completely clean mouthpiece without more work.  Just so that's out there...the bottle works as it should.

title: I have this hooked to my go bag
text: I've mentioned before that I have a go bag.  I'm not worried about zombies taking over the world, but I've watched too many news stories about flooding, fires, earthquakes, etc. to know that having a bag packed with essentials is a good idea.  I tested this air mattress on my bed and was very impressed at how easy it is to self-inflate and then deflate (so long as you spend the time and a bit of muscle) and roll back into a small pack to replace in the included bag.  It is lightweight so hanging it on my go bag works - it's right next to a very small and lightweight 3 season sleeping bag.  In my bag I have a small medical kit, a camping essentials (fire starter, water filtration system, dry noodles, compass, etc.) and a few more items.  Having reasonably comfortable sleeping arrangements during an emergency is worth investing in and this pad helps in that regard.

title: I'm average height, but heavy
text: And this ball/chair doesn't really support a heavier person well.  I have the larger size, but maybe because of my weight it "sinks" a bit more...don't really know, but I tried it at my computer desk - too low.  I tried using it as a chair to play my (musical) keyboard and it was too low - my wrists were bent which is not correct posture for playing a keyboard.  I'm not saying that this is a bad chair, but I would recommend it to smaller (weight and height) people than me.

title: Having taken my lunch nearly every day to work
text: I am a long-time user of ice packs.  These are just what I like - large enough to keep things cool inside my lunch box, but compact enough (thin enough) that they don't take up too much space that would otherwise be used to store food.  Having several means that if I need more than one in my lunch box on a hot day, I don't have to worry about putting these back in the freezer right away at the end of the day.  I have enough with this set to keep not just my lunch cold, but should I make up a lunch for my daughter to take to work, she can also have two in her lunch box and I'll still have extras.  Definitely worth it!

title: Works perfect for my needs
text: I do yoga at home and have an old trash can that I have kept my (semi) rolled yoga mat in after use.  With this strap, I can foll up my mat and hang it from the shelves near where I practice.  The best part is, while I am on my mat, I can use this to further my poses, helping me to stretch and achieve more in a pose.  I am quite happy with this sling and strap combo - helping me with my yoga!

title: I started an exercise program recently
text: I have been riding the stationary bike, doing standing and sitting exercises and when I am able, I want to walk the paths around the lake near my house.  Because they are Army Corps of Engineer pathways are very natural, a walking stick will be helpful as I am an older lady with arthritic knees.  I like the compass in the head of  the stick - I did check and it is pointing north so if I happen to get lost, and have an idea of which way I need to go, I can use the compass to get me back on track.  Screws together quickly and the pouch it came in makes it easy to store when not in use.

title: Not for sun, but for work
text: I have taken a position that requires loading items into cardboard boxes and I happen to have fairly thin skin - I bruise very easily - so these arm protection sleeves are just what I need to keep the rough cardboard from abrading my arms and causing me to have the little blood bruises that I get.  They are a bit tight up past my elbow so I folded them down a bit and they work and fit just fine.  Great for my needs.

title: For the price these are just not practical
text: Just because you can bury them in the soil and they will degrade?  C'mon!  I have several large packs of body wipes that smell like baby powder and if I'm out and cannot get to a shower but want to feel clean, I'll break out one or two of these body wipes and when I'm done, pack them in a zip lock bag and bring them back with me.  I am pretty sure they would also degrade if buried in the soil, but I'd rather just not leave anything behind.  My pack of body wipes cost around $4 and has, oh, maybe 50 in the pack.  That's a reasonable price point!  I would not buy these again unless they lower the price substantially.

title: For what this is, it's not bad
text: I mean, it's like an MRE, just add hot water and wait a few minutes.  Seriously, I tried eating it just as is, but I ended up adding some shredded cheese to it as I tried it at home, not when I was out camping.  The cheese helped make this a bit more edible for me.  The meal itself is okay.  Add the water, seal it, wait, eat it in the pouch if you are camping and then you have very little trash.  I had a bowl I poured it into, then dropped some shredded cheese on top, nuked it for a few seconds in the microwave to melt the cheese, stirred the cheese into the meal and it gave the chili mac a little more substance.  All in all, for camping purposes, especially if you are hiking and will stop along the trail for a meal, this might work so long as you do have the ability to heat water.  Personally, for hiking and stopping on a trail to eat, this isn't the best idea - there are MREs that don't require anything other than to open and eat.  But if you are staying at a campground and roughing it, this might be a good choice.

title: I have seen many pictures
text: My nephew loves to fish and is a part of the local catch and release group - he's even received a few awards for some of his catches.  But the pictures, he is usually just holding the fish up and I thought maybe with this he would be able to have photo evidence of the size and weight of each catch for his records.  I used to fish with my dad, though it was for food and not a catch/release program, so looking at this, I like the way it is designed for weighing/measuring the fish fast.  I do hope he finds it useful - it sure looks like it will be to me!

title: I have another camp set, but this is definitely the one I like
text: The other seemed to be made by someone who really didn't know much about how camping can be.  Y'know, messy and usually you burn yourself or at least almost burn yourself!  I made a great little rocket stove so that a few sticks can create a good fire and with an old stove burner trivet on top, this camping gear pans and kettle work great for making hot water for tea, throwing in some stew to heat for dinner or whatever.  I am quite happy with this set and know it will serve me well through many years of camping.

title: Not terribly impressed with this
text: I'm a big girl, but I have grandchildren and older grandnephews that might find this cool.  Problem is, they wouldn't be able to inflate it and I got frustrated trying to get enough air into it to make it puffy.  Couldn't y'all have made this a two-fer way to inflate?  Add a usb or even car charger piece, very small pump - doesn't have to be much larger than a deck of cards - so anyone could pump this thing up.  Two, if you are an adult that has ANY type of physical issues, DO NOT try to lay on this thing or you'll need three people to get you out of it!  For kids...okay, but getting it inflated is, at least for me, the biggest challenge.  I have a portable hammock I'd rather set up and use that this!

title: I used to live on a houseboat 24/7 year round
text: I can appreciate not having clean drinking water when you need it.  One winter was so cold that most of my onboard water tank froze so I had no water for drinking, for flushing the toilet, for taking a shower...yep, I know what it's like not to have water!  I worry about those emergencies that crop up - in my area floods can happen which means that I might have to leave my house in a hurry for higher ground and a shelter.  Filling water bladders and having a go-bag with essentials makes it easier on me to leave, knowing that wherever I end up, I have water to drink, some dried foods to eat, and other "comforts" that many may lack from having to vacate their homes quickly.  Not that I expect it to happen, but better to be prepared, right?

title: Good for camping, but I also got it for emergencies
text: Have you watched those new shows where people are being rescued from the roof of their house as the floodwaters are rising?  Or seen similar folks wading through 3 feet of water?  I wanted to have this on hand because I live in an area that can flood and with this, I can keep my essentials dry and with me should I need to leave quickly because of rising water.  Better to have an item and not need it that to need it and not have it, right?  This does come in different sizes.  I chose the medium sized one and am happy with my choice.  It can hold my wallet, cell phone, tablet and a few other things and that's what I need it to do!

title: This reminded me of a Pendleton wool blanket I've had since the early 60s
text: This one is much lighter and a bit larger, but the southwestern design is somewhat similar to my old wool blanket.  I have it laying across the bottom of my bed.  Last night was cold and my feet always seem to be cold under the cover, but with this blanket on top of the fleece/faux fur one on my bed, my feet stayed warm.  That is a big deal for me - who always has cold feet when the temps drop low - I am about ready for bed now and am happy thinking my feet will stay warm tonight too!  Pretty, giftable blanket - would make a wonderful house-warming gift!

title: Nice camping set
text: It is shown with a gas canister, but I made a rocket stove from a new, empty paint can and use that as my heat source instead.  I have a regular gas stove trivet that I use on top of the rocket stove as the place I set the cooker.  With the rocket stove all I have to have is a bit of found kindling picked up under just about any tree with branches - really doesn't have to be large wood at all.  Put a handful along with a strip or two of paper, light it and man, a rocket stove works great!  So, with my fire taken care of, I set this cooker on the fire, pour water in the pan, add the steamer pot, throw in some chopped onions, peppers, a bit of basil and thyme along with noodles and let it all steam together for a while.  Put some in the included bowl and eat with the included spork.  Camping good set!

title: It's good sized, but odd...
text: I mean, I've had beach towels over the years and this one...I guess the material used is why it is called "sand-free" since it isn't like terry cloth.  It's smooth, whatever it is made of.  The blue one that I received is a pretty pattern and I will use it at the pool this summer, but it's just not the same as those traditional cotton, loopy-thread, terry cloth kind of beach towel I've had for years.  Nothing wrong with trying something new, though, right?

title: This is one of the coolest portable seats I've ever seen
text: And it works great!  Comes in a super slim box, maybe 2" thick by the width of the seat top.  Pulled it out of the box and thought, yeah right...put my fingers into the two holes at the top and bottom (you can see the holes in the description's picture) and then pulled.  The accordianed pieces have an interlocking mechanism so when you pull, it pops up and locks each ring into place.  Fast and man, just so easy!  Now for the moment of truth - you see, I'm a big girl.  If I was a teenager, a skinny woman or anyone under 150 or so pounds, I wouldn't be worried at all, but I'm not any of those...I'm big.  I placed this collapsible seat next to my heavy duty stainless steel table just in case I needed to catch myself should it collapse under me.  It did not.  It felt very sturdy to sit on and I am just so pleased with how small this stool becomes - I mean, it could fit inside a backpack, could possibly fit in a larger purse.  This is the coolest portable seat and will come in handy camping or going to my nephew's soccer games, attending any outdoor events where seating is limited - I'll have my own stool with me!

title: Excellent portable stool
text: I'm a big girl and very seldom do I trust small things to hold me.  I'm older, too, so the thought of getting slammed to the ground with something that can't hold my weight...I don't need that at all.  This is fast to set up - just splay the legs out, telescope them to latch in the buttons and sit.  For that moment, I placed this stool next to my very sturdy stainless steel table so I could grab the table should this little stool decide to buckle.  It did not - other than one leg adjusting to the floor (I must not have splayed the legs out all the way), I felt safe to sit on this without feeling like it might collapse.  Lightweight, very portable and fast to set up - what more could you want?

title: Charge this up and man, do your hands stay warm
text: When I was a kid, my father had an old-fashioned one like this where you put butane fuel on a wad of what I suspect was rock wool packed down inside the metal shell.  Then you lit the rock wool, slid the top over the bottom section and put it in your pocket.  It warmed up fast and did its job of keeping your hands warm.  This is the updated version of that - no butane fuel needed, just charge it, turn it on and either hold it or put it in your pocket to warm your hands.  It works great!  The stripes make it easy to find in my purse and yes, I keep it with me just in case.  A cold wind blows, I'm gonna break this little gadget out and warm up my hands!

title: Like a duffle bag made into a backpack!
text: This is the best backpack I have owned.  Most backpacks can hold some stuff, some backpacks can hold a bunch of stuff, but this is in a whole different category - it can hold so much it's amazing!  I don't mean that it can pack inside more than any other backpack, but just by size alone, it can stow (either inside or outside) so much stuff, you could literally live for a time with just what you have on your back.  A few carabiners and you can hang several items on the outside of this backpack - I have a small lightweight sleeping bag, a wonderful rainproof blanket, an ultralight camp chair - all of which have their own sack with sturdy cords that would not add much weight to the pack, but clipped to the outside, that leaves inside room for other things.  I am a larger person and this pack is also very easy to adjust to fit me.  I am really impressed and pleased with this backpack.

title: This is the outdoor blanket to take with you
text: This blanket is very light weight and packed in the included sack, could be easily clipped to a backpack so that when you stop for short rest, to look around and sip some water, you can take this out, sit on it and then shake it off easily, roll it up and it also easily packs back into its sack.  Should it begin raining while out on the trail, this blanket repels rain as well!  Wind comes up?  Man, this blanket is warmer than it might appear!  If you need a good blanket to take with you - to the ball game, backpacking, camping or just sitting outside in your own backyard - this is the one!

title: This is sooooo cool!
text: It reminds me of the window sunscreen that I use in my SUV.  It has a similar pop-out style that can be "aggressive" if you want to think of it that way - I tend to actually get out of my car to open my sunscreen as it is big enough to fully cover the front window of my car and popping it open can be a big bizarre if I'm sitting behind the wheel!  Even so, I wouldn't change that sunscreen for the world - it FITS and works great!  Now, to close it takes a bit of finagling to get it to lay flat while I put the elastic around it to keep it closed.  I mention all this about my sunscreen because pretty much all it applies to this tent.  I can pop it open all by myself and with a bit of finagling, close it flat as well.  This little tent would be fun for a kid's night out in the backyard and many other uses.  It is exceptionally lightweight and could be exterior protection on a hike where you expect to sleep out before starting back (or going on).  It's not for subzero weather but if the weather decides to get drizzly this little tent could keep you drier than sleeping out on the ground!  I like this tent and will be taking it with me next time I'm out camping.

title: I am old and overweight, so in order to walk...
text: I really need a walking stick to give me a bit of "grip" when taking that next step.  Getting back into shape after being lazy for years  means I need to grit my teeth and get past some of the pain and with the help of this walking stick, taking to the paths around the lake near my home has been a bit easier on me.  At least while I'm walking with this cane I know I'm getting healthier one step at a time!

title: Very nice BBQ tool set
text: I have a camping stove and BBQ pit (stainless steel triangular deal with the legs holding it together) I can take with me when camping and now I have an excellent set of cooking tools to make my food while "roughing it."  It comes in a small, self-contained zipper bag with a handle that makes it even more convenient to carry with me while out at a national park for a few days.  Excellent set that I would recommend to anyone for tailgating, camping or even if you stay at home and grill in your own backyard!

title: This one is attached to my go bag
text: I live within 800 yards of a lake so I walked down there, scooped up some water and used this filtration system to test its ability to make regular lake water drinkable.  It may not be bottled water, but it was passably drinkable and in the case of flooding, fire and other natural emergency situations, having something like this to make found water drinkable is worth its weight.  I recommend that everyone get some type of water filtration system like this one just in case.  For the price and what it does, it's worth it.

title: I just got back into yoga
text: Luckily, because I have "double joints" in many parts of my body (a genetic "gift" from my father's side of the family - to have elongated joints that make some things easier, and some things harder) I can still bend down and touch my toes.  When doing yoga on a mat, touching my toes is not enough!  I need to be able to put my forehead to my knees and to facilitate that stretch, I just need a little bit of length...so I use one of these to be able to put it around the soles of my feet, grasping this on either side and pull just a bit to gain some length and stretch in my legs and hips to get lower.  Soon I will touch my forehead to my knees - with the help of this ring!

title: Just getting back into yoga after years
text: I'm in my 60s and over the course of several years I fell into inactivity as far as my own physical regime is concerned.  Yoga was a part of that regime and I have gotten back into it recently as a way to alleviate part of the aging process - of arthritis, of stiff joints, and of course, being fat.  The yoga band allows me to take my stretch to the next level.  Not pushing too far, just pushing a bit further so that each day I have a little higher success in recovering the flexibility I had in my youth.  This strap is perfect to help me with that.  If you too are getting into yoga, I would definitely recommend getting one to make your own comeback easier and faster!

title: Perfect for attaching to my go bag
text: Maybe some people will think I'm a bit nuts, but having watched the news with the flooding, the fires and other weather issues that create problem for people living in the area, I have a go bag set up as a just in case thing.  Having a sleeping bag means I'm not taking up a space others less prepared might need during an emergency.  This bag will keep me comfortable during a time when others caught unaware will need the available cots the emergency groups are able to provide.  All I need is a corner, out of the way or in the worst case scenario, with the tarp, rope and carabiners I have, I could construct an emergency camp on dry ground while waiting for things to settle down.  Very lightweight and as mentioned, it clipped with a carabiner to the side of my bag - if you are a hiker or camper, this would work perfectly!  Excellent sleeping bag!

title: Such a great board with games when it's bad out
text: I have some outside games like cornhole which is fine for those days when the weather is nice, but how to keep kids and adults physically active in a smaller house on those days when it's raining, sleeting or snowing or just really cold and miserable outside?  A dartboard with magnetic darts and hook rings!  Okay, so it may not be as physically active as badminton, but so much better than everyone sitting around staring at their phones and texting, right?  Besides, practicing hand/eye  coordination in a game of darts or ring toss, is good for everyone!

title: Strapped to my go bag
text: I have a go bag I have prepared for emergencies where, if I must leave my house due to flooding, fires, or any other emergency, this bag will have most things that will allow me to get by for several days without relying on the government to supply me with everything.  Having a tarp for putting up to provide a dry spot is essential and this is a great, portable pack that attached well to the go bag I have prepared.

title: I am getting back into yoga after a time away from it
text: I am a big girl and have not practiced yoga for a few years.  Having these straps will help me in getting the most from a good stretch without worrying over-much about hurting myself by trying to get that "big" stretch without help.  I don't go to classes; just do this on my own, so I have to rely on myself when stretching.  These straps help a great deal!

title: Tested on the lake water not far from my house
text: It works great!  I have a thing about being prepared.  I'm not a zombie apocalypse kind of person, but having a go bag with this water filtration system is a good thing.  I have some dried foods, a first aid kit, a multi tool, an extremely light weight chair, battery backups for electronics and an emergency radio with light, a tent/tarp and a sleeping bag in my go-bag.  If there is a natural disaster near me, I'll at least have some basic essentials that I can grab quick and get to safer ground be it flooding, tornadoes, or whatever.  Food I can live without for a few days, but water - we all need water every day to survive, right?

title: GREAT survival/camping/hiking first aid kit
text: Small, but packed to the gills with many of the things one might need in an emergency while away from hospitals or doctor offices.  Falling while hiking, cutting yourself while camping, burning a finger on the fire - I mean, that's just a few things you can take care of with this kit!  It will fit inside a backpack or could be strapped to the outside of a backpack, but definitely, wherever you are going in the great outdoors, make sure you take this pack along with you!  Store it in the car, carry it on the hike up the mountain, place it in the boat in case you get a fish hook in your finger...just take it with you!

title: This little shovel/trowel is tiny!
text: But they say big things come in small packaging or something similar!  I was just amazed at how small this shovel/trowel is.  That's a good thing, really - it is small, lightweight, extremely sturdy and will fit in your backpack to take hiking with you as a just in case item.  Or even to help in getting tent stakes in the ground.  This is one tough little digger!  If you like to spend time in the great outdoors, I would highly recommend getting this.

title: The flavor of filtered water depends on the water used
text: I added 4 stars for "flavor" but in reality, if in a situation where you need this filtering pump to get drinkable water, it may not taste like bottled water or even close to tap water.  My reason for getting this water filter was for emergency situations.  Think about recent disasters - hurricanes, tornadoes and fast-spreading fires - where people had to walk away from their homes and while the Red Cross or other agencies work to help all those affected, there may come a time when you will be left on your own to deal with being unable to return to your home right away and no place to go.  If you have a go-bag with some essentials, then at least you have options.  Having this water filter gives you a better chance to subsist for a while on your own.  That's my reasoning for having this item which is now in my go bag and it gives me much greater peace of mind than thinking the federal government is going to be there for me should a natural disaster occur in my area!  I would recommend this to anyone who like to hike in the woods as well as those who are stocking a go-bag.

title: A New Year's Resolution in a bag
text: I used to perform yoga every day when my children were young.  Over the years I got out of the habit and I am now getting back into yoga as I know it works for me.  Oh, I don't lose tons of weight or anything, but I gain muscle strength and balance which I have lost as I have aged.  So, a little at a time, always striving to do a bit more each day with the straps and then including the other items as I gain confidence and one day I'll feel like I did back in my 30's even though I'm now in my 60's!  That's the power of yoga and I would definitely recommend getting these "aids" to assist in the "body learning curve."

title: Updated version of a memory from my past
text: When I was a kid, my father had an old hand warmer.  It was made with wadding and if I remember correctly, my father squirted a bit of lighter fluid on the wadding inside the metal case, lit it, slid the metal warmer into the padded case and it a few seconds my chilled fingers would be warm again.  This is the safer version - charged via usb and has variable heating levels.  It is great!  Winter is just starting so having this in my purse to warm up my hands is invaluable.  It fits perfectly in my hand and when turned on, warms up quickly.  I haven't yet tested to see how long it will continue to work on one charge, but hopefully I won't have to!  If you are camping, hiking or spending any time out during chilly weather, I would definitely advise taking one of these along.

title: Took 1.5 hours to assemble
text:
That's not too bad - I read the instructions and inspected the pictures so I wouldn't have to take something apart and start over. It was a more or less successful build. The meter was the last thing to be added and it was the main problem and is still not attached. The curved bar that the meter slides down over is to be attached to the underside of the sliding desk, yet the places where that bar has to be attached is under a fixed piece of metal, blocking the screw holes. I can jerry-rig an adequate alternative, but that part of this bike is frustrating at best...the other thing is "storage" by "closing" the bike - nope, not going to happen. Oh, maybe it would work on a fully carpeted floor, but when I tried to fold it up, even on my living room rug, it slid and on my hardwood floor I couldn't even get it to close! Not any point in closing it anyway unless you have a closet to put it in right away after attempting to close it. On my floor, it has to remain open which defeats the concept of portable or compact for small spaces.

Still, for what it is an what it does, this is a decent exercise bike and I would get it again!

title: For camping, for storing in your car - this is a great blanket
text: Because it is lightweight, packs down easily to fit back into its own carrying case and is warm, this blanket is perfect whether camping or stored in your car for emergency use in winter.  This is also great to use for outdoor concerts and other events where you will be sitting on grass or concrete.  Bottom line, great addition to camping/emergency gear!

title: For the price, this is an excellent hammock
text: Not sure what some folks expect for this price point, but it is a good hammock!  The trees in my yard are not terribly big around - pin oaks that are sturdy trees, but their trunks are on the smaller side, so they work well with this hammock.  At the moment it's winter (in Texas) so not the most opportune time to lay out in a hammock, but come spring time I will be using it on those nice weekend days when I have a couple of hours to "hang around" and snooze!

title: These are what they are
text: I wanted to have an emergency rain poncho on hand in my car and one at work for when rain happens unexpectedly and I haven't brought my umbrella.  These aren't like an expensive raincoat or anything - just a bit better than wearing a garbage bag, but that's the point.  They were made to be emergency rain wear and having them on hand means I am prepared.  If preparation is your thing, these might be for you, too!

title: I am so glad that someone thought about adding touchscreen to gloves!
text: These are a great (two) pairs of touchscreen gloves that work fine.  No more ripping off a glove to answer a text in 20 degree weather sitting in your car, waiting for it to warm up!  If you haven't tried touch screen gloves, I highly recommend these - you won't be disappointed!

title: One can never have too many carabiner clips!
text: I use them to clip my keys to my purse and I have a "button screamer" (press the button if you are attacked and it emits a very loud, obnoxious sound) dangling from my purse on another carabiner.  I have other carabiners holding other items in my house...these are great things to have around!  This pack is a good one if you are in need of one or more for your keys or to clip a small lantern inside your tent...or whatever!

title: Came in a HUGE box!
text: I was worried when opening the box that this was going to be quite a bit larger that I expected, based on the information given about the sleeping bag, but for what it is (meaning a double sleeping bag), it came out of that huge box much smaller than the box it shipped in!  It's also fairly lightweight.  Why the camo coloring I'll never understand - am I supposed to be hiding in the woods all snuggled up in a sleeping bag that hides me from others?  Just a bit odd to me is all, but okay...the sleeping bag allows me to have both my dogs snuggled inside the bag on a cold night out.  They are great heat producers!  And they love being close to their "mom!"  Whether you have a sweetie or you hang with your dogs instead, this is a great double sleeping bag when out camping!

title: I think my nephew is going to love using this
text: If possible, he would be on or in the lake/river 18 out of 24 hours a day - knowing he has to eat, sleep and go to the bathroom once in a while the only time he'd leave!  He is also a part of the catch and release program and has won a couple of awards during competitions, so I thought for the holidays I would get him something for his favorite past time.  I can see that the netting is made to do as little harm as possible to the fish so that the hook can be removed, a picture taken and the fish released.  I do think he is going to be surprised and very pleased with the quality of this net!

title: Looks well made
text: My nephew is an avid fisherman and would spend probably 18 out of 24 hours of every day at or on the water fishing!  I know he participates in catch and release events and won a few times for largest bass (or other types of fish) caught.  I don't believe he has a tool like this - I think from the videos I have seen, he's used his fingers to remove the hook and apparently has had a hook go through the meat of his finger before (yuck)!  So I am hoping that this tool will assist him - I'm sure it will save his fingers if he uses it!

title: Going to knot this into something useful (lanyard, probably)
text: I have a semi-packed go-bag with several items and with the addition of a carbiner on one end, will attach this to my go-bag.  Having paracord handy when you need to leave the house immediately for any reason (tornadoes, floods, hurricane, fire, etc).  Washing and drying clothes?  Making a temporary tented structure?  Hanging your food high in a tree so varmits can't take it?  All of these questions and more can be answered by having a good-sized bunch of paracord!  Highly recommend having some on hand

title: I'm not into sports but this is an impressive bat!
text: My niece took her two boys to the Louisville Slugger museum while visiting in Kentucky - both of her boys are extremely athletic boys, into many sports, so this bat will go to them, but as I noted, it impressed me and I'm not into sports at all!  Very well made, well balanced and even for me, easy to hold and swing.  Louisville Slugger bats like this one are what you want for the sports child in your life!

title: Works well for my needs
text: I have both a laptop and a desktop computer (I hate the idea of being without a computer, so always have two working computers at a time).  The desk top computer stand has a slide out for the keyboard that has a slight tilt to it which encourages the keyboard to slide.  I added a couple of lines of this tape under the keyboard and it stays put!  I am sure I will find other uses for it around the house, but for now, keeping my keyboard from sliding is a good thing!

title: Who needs a wine glass when you have a wine mug!?!
text: I'm not a big drinker at all - I'm a sipper and a bottle of wine may last, in my refrigerator for two weeks to a month, but that's okay, right?  It is said a glass of wine a day is good for the body - blood and heart are mentioned - but why does it have to be a glass?  I love this mug for my little sips of wine every few days.  It's just not as pretentious as a wine glass (or as breakable) and feels good in the hand.  I tend to put a small ice cube in the glass to keep my wine cold while I sip and that seems to transfer to the stainless steel, meaning it keeps my wine nice and chilly.  I would definitely recommend this Mizu wine cup to anyone who regularly drinks wine or even those like me who are less frequent sippers - excellent cup!

title: HAH!  Now to smack around my nephews!
text: I have another pair of boxing gloves for them, but these are for me - going to put them on when I go over to see my nephews and smack them around!  At least with the gloves on we can't get hurt and it will be fun (play) pummeling them in their own house!  Of course, these are useful for working out, too!

title: A bit of a high price point, but having some of this line around is worth it
text: I'm not all zombie apocalypse is going to happen soon, but I do believe in being prepared for disasters like tornadoes and flooding - having a bit of line like this could save your life!  Say a flash flood traps you in your car and the water is moving really fast...and your car begins to move...if you had this line in your car, you could toss it to someone out of the danger zone and possibly get pulled to safety before your car floats away.  I'm just trying to illustrate that things do happen and being prepared is worth gathering a few things together - one of them being this type of line.  Great for a makeshift tent with nothing more than a cheap, plastic tarp, makes a good line to dry clothes, hang food off the ground and many other uses.  This line has earned a place in my go bag.  I'd recommend it to others as well.

title: Nice adult jump rope
text: When I was a kid I jumped rope with the dime store wooden handled, cotton rope jump rope and life was good.  Jumping rope for an adult is a bit different - we sure aren't as close to the ground as we were meaning you trip on the rope and fall, you fall further and it usually hurts more!  But hey, taking it easy with this rope is okay and then working up to how you used to jump when you were a kid may take a while, but it will come!  I like how it makes me feel as if I'm just having fun like I did when I was a kid, but it is a great work out in disguise!  Great jump rope for those of you looking to put a little fun in your work out.

title: Great yoga mat, for sure!
text: I get this mat out every day, put on my yoga socks and a baggy, long shirt and perform my 40 minutes of yoga.  What can I say other than that?  It is comfortable, easy to use, great for yoga poses and of course, rolls up and stores perfectly.  If you need a yoga mat - this is a great one to get!

title: I am not a professional by any means, but these will work for my needs
text: I got these for bag punching fitness.  I have very fat upper arms and think these will help me strengthen and tone my upper arms.  They fit me well - I'm an average-height woman, but a big/heavy one.  Of course, my hands are not fat like the rest of me, so these gloves will work fine to help me with punching the bag!

title: Color me impressed
text: First, the packaging is great - a nice, thick tube which I'm going to keep for when I am not using it - just a nice storage tube for it!  Okay, so when I slid the bottle from its tube, my first impression was, "looks like a sturdy stainless steel thermos bottle," then I unscrewed the top and looked at it very closely.  I was skeptical that such a small thing could sound any better than a tinny, cheap speaker.  Oh man, I was wrong!  Hooked the usb to my laptop, turned the speaker on to bluetooth discover mode and paired it with my phone which, like many phones does not have a great speaker.  Pulled up my Amazon music list on my phone and hit play.  Now I won't say this speaker is like having a music hall in your room, but the sound coming from the speaker was amazingly crisp and clear without any of the echo-y tinny-ness that I expected.  Very cool pairing of a well-insulated bottle and a capable little bluetooth speaker!  The size of the bottle is good as well.  The only thing I would wish for is that the price be lowered just a tad.  It is a cool dual-use gadget, but the price is just a bit north of comfortable for what it is.  Still and all, it is something I will use often and I expect a few people will stop and ask me about it as I've not seen others using it....yet!

title: Comfortable chair and the right team - what more could one want?
text: This is a nice, lightweight folding chair that is comfortable to sit in and, because I am a Cowboys fan, just the right logo!  Of course, if you happen to be crazy enough to root for other teams, you can find a chair with their logo...but why would you?  Cowboys rule!  Okay, get your team's logo on your chair, but definitely get this folding chair!

title: Better than spending money on a gym!
text: I loved jumping rope as a child and it is a great exercise for adults as well.  I have to be outside on the porch to jump rope since I don't have a house with high ceilings or lots of room to do it inside, but my point is why spend money on a gym membership when jumping rope can be done at home?  This jump rope is definitely different than the kid ropes I had, but that's a good thing - it is made for adults and for aerobic exercise.  Looking forward to many weeks and months of use to get and keep me in shape!

title: For what it is, I have to say it works well
text: I'm not a hiker, but I do have an SUV tent, an air mattress that fits the back of the SUV and now an air pillow.  I'm a bit different than most folks because I actually sleep on a 20" tall queen size air mattress every night and have done so for the past two years.  The thing is, with the air mattress I can move and sleep in may different positions and my body feels supported.  That's not exactly how or why I use a pillow.  Again, I'm not like most people - I have been sleeping with a 100% down pillow for so many years I can't even remember when I bought my first one.  I mention this because of the way I use a pillow when sleeping - it is molded, puffed out and reformed several times during the night.  That just can't happen with this air pillow.  For me, it serves more as a back prop for sitting up and reading on the bed.  Nice and firm, it gives me back support while sitting up in bed.  It does store well in the very small case it comes in and that's perfect!  As I have gotten older and had to move when I didn't really want to but circumstances made me, I have become addicted to "nomadic furniture" that is easier to move than traditional furniture.  An air pillow does fit within my parameters of small and packable!  Same with my bed - not quite a small, but certainly nothing like lugging around a heavy, floppy queen size mattress and box springs!  So, all in all, I am pleased with this air pillow at least for what I will use it for.

title: Makes me nervous, but getting children outside is important
text: My son had a skateboard and did "tricks" on it - hurt himself a few times - but that was before the information age where every child has a phone and/or tablet before they enter school.  My son has talked about teaching his son to skateboard which makes me nervous once again, but dad and son should bond over something that will be fun for both and that is why I got this for them.  It is a beautiful board...I just hope my son can teach his son how to ride safely!

title: Neat little yoga carry bag
text: When I pulled it out of the package, I thought, wow, this is so tiny!  And yes, it is a minimalist type of yoga carry bag, but it does have room for a cell phone, set of keys and the like.  Not tons of room, but just enough for essentials.  My daughter performs yoga mostly at home, but once a week she does go to a class at the rec center to help her correct any issues she's having with specific poses.  This bag will be perfect for her to carry on those days she goes to the rec center.

title: I'm not hardcore so this works perfect for my needs!
text: I'm not a hard-scrabble kind of person when out camping.  Don't get me wrong, I am out "roughing it" with the best of them, but my idea of roughing it is an SUV tent on the back of my Nissan Murano, a blow up mattress in the back of my car and this mummy bag for the colder nights I'm out at one of the national parks. Also, this is a small enough bag that it packs well in my car along with the cooler, change of clothes, and portable stove and gear. I wouldn't be out in the dead of winter, but I do like getting a head start in spring before others and going out later in fall.  This sleeping bag is great for my camping needs!

title: I like the feel of these darts
text: I'm getting better at a new hobby - darts and now have four different Viper style darts.  I like these longer, slender ones for throwing.  They feel very balanced in my hands.

title: Sometimes you need short, sometimes long
text: I have three sets of the Viper darts and a box of the shorter soft tip dart points.  These are the longer soft tip dart points.  I'm just learning to play darts, so am not an expert at the game, but I understand these, being longer, should be used only on certain boards.  Otherwise, the shorter tips are the better bet, but if your board is rated for this length, then these will work fine.  I haven't checked my board yet to see if these will work without causing an issue for the board or the tips.  They are well-made tips.

title: Second yoga mat, this is the better of the two
text: I have two yoga mats and while I'm not saying I dislike the other one, I am saying that this one is a bit wider, seems cushier and makes me feel more confidant when performing yoga poses whether floor poses or standing poses.  This is the one I will use most often - I recommend it to anyone looking for a yoga mat.

title: Sturdy zip case for three darts.
