text: I have another case that holds double this and like that one much better, but this is a great one for holding spare darts and tips.  It is the same size at the other one - very sturdy in the hand but small enough to carry without a problem.  I guess if I could wish for one thing it would be a wrist strap.  Other than that, this is a nice case!

title: These have a nice heft to them
text: The weighted section of these Atomic Bee darts feels good in my hand - I'm still a novice at darts, so can't say much about the accuracy as I'm still learning how to throw, but these seem to help my aim already.  New to darts - these are worth looking into and adding to your collection!

title: Easy to use?  C'mon!  This is a resistance band!!!
text: This is a great resistance band - nice and thick, large enough to be useful on several parts of the body - ankles, knees, elbows, etc.  It has a little storage bag of its own so that I can keep it in my exercise duffle bag where I keep as much of my exercise equipment (like this) as possible.  If I could make any changes, I would have this come in a set of three - one a bit smaller and one a bit larger so that it would be helpful for smaller/larger folks so they also have a "good fit" for whatever area is being worked.

title: I go out on my own and like camping in my SUV
text: Camping by yourself is a little different.  It's easier to have a tent that attaches to the back of my SUV so I can sleep in the back on a comfortable mattress - rain doesn't bother me, cold ground either.  I'm older and trying to get up from the ground isn't as easy as it once was, so sleeping in the back of my SUV is not just so I'm not cold or out of the rain, but so I can stand up without trying to lever myself up off the ground.  This mattress fits my Nissan Murano just fine and part of the reason I picked it is that if I have more stuff with me that I expect, I can store it on the one side and just not inflate the narrower side of the mattress.  Not a bad deal at all!

title: Excellent darts - my accuracy will improve I'm sure
text: I think it's funny that I am to rate their accuracy when that is really dependent on my abilities to a great extent!  These are very nicely weighted darts that are easy to hold and throw.  I'm still perfecting my arm, so I'm not terribly accurate, though I do hit the board and not the wall around it!  I'm a girl so I do have to say, these are really pretty too - maybe not a big deal to others, but hey, if I'm going to play, I do like having something that's not only nice to hold, but pretty to look at!  Great darts!

title: Perfect replacement tips
text: The Viper darts are excellent darts and of course, when throwing, once in a while (okay, I'm an amateur, so more often) a tip gets broken.  That's where these replacements come in - don't worry about messing up because you can fix the broken tips with this pack!

title: Professional dart case carries 8 darts and spare tips
text: I do love it when I have a professional case for an item - a well-built, well-thought-out, everything in it's place type of case and this one, in my opinion, fits the bill.  I'm not a professional, but when I opened this case and looked through it, I felt like I could walk into any tournament with this case and be taken as a professional!  It does have room for 8 darts and spare tips, zip around and compact enough it would fit in my purse without a problem.  Probably, for a guy, it would fit in cargo pants pockets - not real sure about regular pockets like those on jeans.

title: Great darts - accuracy depends on the thrower!
text: I'm not the best - I'm still perfecting my throw, but these are well-weighted, excellent darts.  Maybe those who play in serious tournaments use other darts, but for me and my skill level, I'm quite happy with these!

title: I recently purchased the Ohio State lunchbox
text: This backpack will go quite well with it and is a great back to school set.  What other would be appropriate when one lives in Ohio? :)

title: Haven't taken it out to hang yet
text: I don't have any trees in my yard so I'm going to take it with me the next time I go camping and string it up next to my tent for a place to hang after hiking and kayaking on the lake.  It is small and light enough that if you were to go on an extended hike and need a place off the ground to sleep, this would be a great idea.  Could be stuffed inside your backpack or hung on the outside if there's no room inside.  Great hammock!

title: Nice fan-branded lunchbox for Ohio State
text: The only thing I wish this lunchbox had was a shoulder strap so it did not need to be carried..  Still, it is a nice lunchbox - just the right size to hold a good lunch and of course, if one is an Ohio State fan, it is perfect!

title: PERFECT!
text: I have not been swimming much in the last few years because I have dry eye syndrome which means I spend quite a bit of time daily adding lubricating drops to my eyes.  Due to this issue with my eyes, I cannot dunk my head underwater.  Receiving these swim goggles has made me extremely happy - have them adjusted to fit my head and am looking forward to being able to go underwater with my eyes open!

title: Really nice folding chair
text: Came in a great carrying case with a shoulder strap and surprisingly, the chair itself has a carry sling on it.  This is a great, folding chair - yes, it is a Dallas Cowboys logo on it so if you are not a fan, might want to look for a chair with your sport's logo on it, but for me this is a great chair, period!

title: Four stars because I wish it was bigger!
text: This towl is so soft!  I just wish it was larger - as it is, it's a great neck towel.  Can't hurt to wish for more, though, right? :)

title: My ankles and wrists seem to be my weakest points
text: Don't need these for weight lifting unless speaking about me lifting my own weight out of a chair - having my wrists wrapped gives me peace of mind that when I use my hands and wrists as leverage to get up out of a chair, that my wrists won't give way.  Being older, I worry more these days about fractures and other bone/ligament/muscle damage.  Support given with this wrist wrap allows me to have more confidence in getting up intact.  Would recommend to anyone for similar purposes.

title: Not sure why they didn't include...
text: One side that inclines for doing a yoga pose like the camel pose.  These have an indentation in the middle with four sides that are the same.  Seems to me if this is for yoga, the people who made it would understand that...gave it four stars because they are comfortable on your knees, but not really constructed for real yoga poses done on your knees...

title: Disappointed no shoulder strap
text: This soft-sided lunchbox is nice - has good, rubberized zipper tabs that make it easy to open and close the two compartments and it does have a mesh section on the outside for a water bottle, but instead of having to carry this box everywhere by the handle, I would have liked to see d-rings on the side and a shoulder strap to free your hand(s).  So long as you are looking for a handle-carry lunch box, this is a decent one.

title: Nice set but was damaged
text: The first photo doesn't really show how chewed up the box was and because I could smell something, I checked the two bottles and found the one (second picture) that had leaked.  It was just a few drops, so no problem.  This is a great little mat cleaning set with everything needed.  The scent is mild and pleasant, not too strong, and it cleans the yoga mat.  Four stars for the damaged box.  Would recommend to anyone.

title: I LIKE this yoga/duffle bag
text: The elephant pattern on this yoga/duffle bag is very pretty.  The handles are nice and sturdy and it is really large!  Should be able to fit your yoga mat, a towel and change of clothing and probably more.  The only thing I would add is a shoulder strap but that's just a little thing.  If you like the pattern and need a good-sized duffle, this will work for you!

title: Great for the gym or exercise class
text: This backpack is large enough to hold a change of clothes, whether it be the sweats or stretchy leggings/top to perform your workout or street clothes to  change into after the workout is finished.  It holds your yoga mat, has a special spot for a water bottle.  My only wish is that this were convertible from a backpack to a shoulder strap bag just because I'm more likely to carry it as a shoulder/crossbody bag than a backpack.  Other than that, it is a nice bag, the outer material seems to be rain resistant, the pack itself should hold as much and more than most people to would carry.

title: Silly design for serious exercise
text: I love what yoga does for the body as well as the mind (and the soul), but I have had trouble over the years performing yoga poses on hardwood or carpeted floors.  Yoga requires exceptional stillness - holding poses for the minute or more to feel the loosening needed in order for the body to make progress in flexibility as well as strength.  I say all this because the poses either standing or floor need to be done on a non-slip surface.  This mat fits that requirement exactly.  It is a wonderful mat - perfect size and shape, the bottom has the "nibs" to keep it just where you put it in the first place.  Highly recommend this mat if you are into yoga or other exercise where this mat would be useful.

title: Not your childhood jump rope
text: This would be considered a professional rope by anybody's standards!  The steel wire is very fine and the handles are plenty large enough to hold onto comfortably.  Lightweight, but the rope works as it should, turning freely, giving you an easy workout. The bag it came in has a jump rope schedule which I will try to follow - I like the ease of jumping rope.  By that I don't mean that it's easy as far as getting fit goes, but easy in the way it's just you, the rope and room to jump for however long you can keep it up.

title: Not just a spork!
text: I'm not sure how one would include the knife word into spork, but this is a spoon, fork and knife.  I really like the idea of adding the serrations of a knife onto the edge of the fork.  Sometimes trying to cut with the side of a fork just doesn't work so I think these serrations will help if eating something a bit meaty or thick that's larger than bite-size.  Since this is a hard plastic, the serrations aren't likely to cause scrapes or cuts to an adult mouth.  Kids, on the other hand, might well have issues using this...spornk?  Just trying to name it properly!  For me, I will use this spork when camping and be glad for the knife part!

title: Like this camping set
text: This is a really nice, self-contained camping set that states it's made of a type of recycled bio-plastic.  Everything packs tight with a strap to hold it in place and a drawstring bag to store the set.  Note the green cup and the pink cup - the cups can be expanded and retracted for ease of storage.  The cup sides are a soft, flexible plastic.  The sporks are great - I'm used to the one-sided spork with the dip of a spoon and small "tines" of a fork at the edges of the spoon.  I like this set's sporks much better.  The plates are a decent size - large enough to hold a sandwich and some chips.  They are hard, feel somewhat like the old melamine plates and should be easy to clean.  If you and a significant other are camping or hiking, this is a great little set to bring along.

title: Nice size and stores easily
text: I love the Igloo coolers, but they take up so much space.  I am taking this camping - have an SUV tent, a mattress for the back of my SUV and now a nice-sized cooler to carry my food and drink for a couple of days out in nature.  This cooler can fold and pack down for storage when not in use and that's what makes it a better pick for me over the Igloo style (hard) coolers.

title: Excellent full and empty!
text: I live in an older part of northern Kentucky, just across the river from downtown Cincinnati.  The reason I mention this is that for camping this would be great, but what I used this for was walking the little downtown section of Bellevue, Kentucky - an old downtown of shops from ice cream, barbershop, antiques, coffeeshop - you name it, there is probably a store front of it in Bellevue.  The downtown section is about 6 blocks long and I walked there from my house in Dayton, KY.  Having this very lightweight bottle with the carbiner attached so I could loop it on my purse was really nice.  I am older and need to stay hydrated, so this was a great way to accomplish that without too much extra weight.  The cap was easy to open and drink from and when I finished off the water, I was able to unclip the carbiner and stash the empty in my purse.  Next time I walk Bellevue's shops, I'll take two instead - cheaper than buying a drink along the way and I get to choose what I am drinking!  I will be taking these with me on my next camping trip because they don't take up much room empty and are definitely great to carry when walking (whether in a downtown area or on a nature trail)!

title: These are sturdy and stay cold for quite a long time
text: Replacing some cheap ones that were falling apart. These are sturdy and stay cold for quite a long time.

title: Pass by the cheap-o blow ups - this one is well worth the money!
text:
I was shocked at the size of the box - it was so tiny, I thought, to contain a queen-sized bed! Opened the box, pulled the bag containing the bed out of the box and took a deep breath - is this going to work for me? Read the instructions, laid the mattress out where I wanted it, plugged it in and turned the pump handle clockwise. Wow! Three minutes for complete inflation - how cool is that?!? Somewhere I'd read to let the bed "rest" for a few hours to allow any air pockets to work themselves out. I did that and when it was time for me to lay down for the night, it had been about three hours. I added sheets, a blanket and my pillow, laid down and slept so well because it feels just like a regular mattress! None of that weird squeaky noise when you move around on a regular air mattress and the best part is getting up off the mattress. It is 20 inches tall and the edges are sturdy, just like a regular mattress. I'm older and trying to get up off the floor is difficult at best. This mattress, I had no problems stand up. I guess the only downside would be for tall people - I'm 5' 4" and this mattress is perfect for me. I think a 6' man might find it a bit short and harder to get off of, but that is my only thought for a downside on this mattress. Me, I love it!

August 2018 - Addition to this review. My original bed began losing air the beginning of this month. I contacted King Koil and they were quick to get back with me sending a UPS tracking number for my replacement bed! I can't say enough good things about them - they honored their warranty, they were FAST to get the replacement shipped and called me to ensure that I received the replacement and that it was working fine. Again I tell you - pass by the cheap-o air mattresses and buy King Koil. The mattress AND the company are worth it!

text: Loved it so much that I went and bought another.  Excellent water bottle.  Doesn't sweat.  Super easy to open and close and the best of all is the water that you put in it stays fresh and has a clean taste.

title: I like the Fitbit One much better
text: I have had a Flex but wanted something that I didn't have to wear on my wrist the entire time.  I like the Fitbit One much better.  It does everything the Flex did but also really tracks stairs.  Great little device.

title: Great nose clips
text: Great nose clips.  They don't slip and are very easy to adjust.  I wear them with my snorkel and no water gets up my nose.

title: This snorkel is amazing!!
text:
This snorkel is amazing!!! I had no idea this thing existed but it works fantastic. It didn't take long getting used to though I do need to use a nose clip otherwise I have a tendency to breathe through my nose. However, I think, over time that I will be able to learn to use it without the nose clip.

The snorkel is easy to put on and doesn't slip. I wear goggles with it and nothing moves.

Wearing this snorkel helps me to perfect my freestyle stroke and I also find I can swim a lot longer.

title: I wanted to continue my therapy at home and this roller is very sturdy and well made
text: I injured my shoulder and my PT had this roller.  I wanted to continue my therapy at home and this roller is very sturdy and well made.

title: Easy to make your shirts folded perfectly and neat
text: Totally works! Easy to make your shirts folded perfectly and neat.  It really gives you more room when the shirts are folded this way.

title: Elegant Scarf
text: I bought this Blackhawks fashion scarf because I was going to my first Blackhawks game and wanted to wear something to show my Blackhawks pride. When the scarf arrived, I was impressed with quality and softness of this scarf.  Very pretty and can be worn with a variety of attire. I will wear this pashmina for many years to come.

title: Keeps my head cool and dry
text: This is the second boonie type I bought. It's lightweight, made from a nylon type material and should shed water to a degree. The adjustable headband is a plus as it fits rather loose on me. The brim is nice and wide and covers my neck really well. The chin strap could be better and more towards the rear of the hat, but serves its purpose on windy days. It will get a lot of use, especially at the range and while out camping.

title: Great for limited space
text: These stands are great if you're on a budget or like me have have limited space. Very easy to assemble if you can look at a picture and read the list of what parts/bolts go where. It's not that hard on these stands, only a few bolts and the shorter ones are for the uprights. They're very sturdy once you get some weight on them. I used 45 lbs worth of dumbbells (2-25's and 2-20's) on the base and did a few bench presses and they didn't budge unracking or reracking. My first impression was these are going to be crap stands that are overpriced. I was wrong, they're really nice and the best part is that they can nest one on top of the other when not in use so you can save some space storing them. My only gripe would be that they have no rubber padding on the cradle or the safety catch. It's nothing I can't fix myself, just I think that's something that should come standard to not only protect your bar, but to reduce noise when reracking the bar. But as they say, you get what you pay for and I did get a fairly nice squat/bench press rack at a decent price and I can always either tape the catches or as I've seen others do, get some protective felt pads for furniture and line them with that. Either way it does what I wanted and lets me work out and not take up half the house like a full cage would do. A+

title: Works great with slight modification
text: This is great. Really sturdy, holds my weight really well and gives you multiple exercises other than chin ups/pull ups. I did however had the same problem as some reviewers had in that my door casings were too wide to let the hooks go over them in order to secure the bar, but rather than give up and send it back I just took a couple of scrap pieces 1x4 and measured where I needed to place them, attached them with six 3" long screws and problem solved, hung up and secured like a rock. It's a solid bar, it doesn't sway or even look like it's going to bend under my weight, but I'm only 175 lbs. I even did some leg ups and kicked outward as I did them and nothing, no creaks, didn't even budge. If you want a solid alternative to buying a full cage with built in pull up bars and are tight on space like I am, this is the one to get. If you are willing to make a few modifications to your door to make it work, or have a door you can modify a little like a garage door or inside of a closet, this will hang and hang solid and won't budge. I chose this one over all the similar bars like it because it has the center loop I intend to use for resistance bands. Just attach a carabiner, run the bands through and presto, I have an instant lat workout!!!

title: Work as advertised
text: These collars are great! Light weight, lock down securely and are easily put on and removed. I'm using a set on a curl bar and have no issues with them slipping around. At $15.99 a set it's worth the buy. I'm definitely buying more when I get the rest of my home gym put together!!! A+++ product.

title: Decent Curl Bar
text: This is a decent curl bar. Nice weight to it, 18 lbs, not 20 as some have stated, and not 16 in the product weight description. It's well balanced, the sleeves have good rotation and it doesn't have any slack in the bushings. The knurling is really good, aggressive, but not so much as to shred your hands. Mine too arrived with missing parts, the collars didn't have the set screws and wasn't loose in the box as it arrived beaten up and split open on one end. At least the bar wasn't damaged and I'm using Lock-Jaw collars so no biggie. Those included collars would damage the sleeves any way. All in all it's a great addition to my home gym and look forward to getting some much needed exercise with this bar.

title: Not bad for resistance bands
text: Great assortment of bands. Gonna take a little getting used to as I lift weights, but didn't want to spend a ton of money putting together a small gym setup in my home. I wanted something to double as a row, and a lat without having to buy a lat machine or a lat attachment for a power cage and these seemed to fit the bill. Great resistance, especially when really stretched out. The further you stretch these bad boys out, the more resistance you get. I'm not worried about what to attach them to, I'm worried about what's gonna hold me down!! LOL I stacked the 50 and 25 and almost ran backwards into the door!! They're that strong!! Covered to protect not only you in case they break, but to also help protect the bands from wearing out prematurely. Plenty of bands to stack as you get stronger (225 lbs when all stacked together), wrist/ankle straps, door anchors and handles. Looking forward for some different exercises.

title: Great for a home gym
text: I ordered this because of it's smallish footprint (small apartment) and it has the leg developer. I researched a ton of options and settled on this one based on a few factors. One being if I wanted to expand and do bench presses I can always buy a barbell rack later as an add on. I have seen similar benches in stores at more expensive prices with less features and cheaper build. This exceeded my expectations. It's build quality is top notch compared to others. The padding is comfortable and I had it assembled and using it in about 45 minutes. I read and pretty much ignored the reviews on this because of contradicting opinions about it's build quality, stability, and weight limit. I'm no power lifter, I'd like to get back into shape and stay in shape without having to pay a gym membership, so the weight limit is not a factor for me. If you assemble this and tighten the lock nuts, which have nylon washers built in, there's no wobble in the seat, stability is rock solid and make sure you grease the bushings in the leg developer where it pivots and you'll have a nice piece of exercise equipment that will last a good long while. Mine arrived in mint condition, no chips, scratches, padding wasn't mashed and all the parts were there. I've used it for leg extensions, leg curls and various dumbbell exercises and I can say from experience it's a rock solid bench. I'm happy with this purchase and am glad I went with this one. Now I can get back in shape, lose a few more pounds and stay that way for a healthier, longer life.

title: Gives some padding to floor exercises
text: This is an ok mat. It does give some padding to floor type exercises (pushups, situps, leg raises) but I guess my floor, even with carpet is super hard. It works great for pushups and my hands don't slip. Situps though, still gets that tailbone after a while. So instead of using the knee pad for the knees, I place it under my butt and it helps a lot. When I'm done exercising, I roll it up and it stores nicely in a closet. I can't state on how well it will hold up, but it does come with a two year warranty, so I have that if anything happens. Overall I'm satisfied. Great price for the features, plenty long enough and the width, although some say is too narrow, fits my needs. A+

title: Great Investment
text: This is by far one of my best investments this year. There are so many different exercises you can do with dumbbells it's insane. I was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and lost a ton of weight before I was diagnosed, and I'm still shedding the pounds, but a little slower now that my blood glucose levels have stabilized. Eating super healthy isn't enough and there's only so many crunches, situps, pushups and squats one can do without weights or a small home gym. I plan on setting up a small home gym, and these dumbbells are the first on my equipment wish list. Other than some shipping dust, they arrived in perfect condition. I read some reviews saying they arrived dirty, rusty, oily. Nope, just some dust and they even arrived earlier than expected. Now I can do some upper body exercises. Whatever range of motion your arms are capable of, that's the exercises you can do with dumbbells!! Here's to a leaner, healthier lifestyle!!!

title: Again?
text: I've reviewed this red dot scope like a dozen times, but it seems like Amazon keeps taking the item page down as it sells out?? Either way this is an ok beginner scope. It's easy to sight in, see the dot and semi co-witnesses with iron sights. Meaning the dot will be above the front and rear sights when zeroed in. Only drawback is the brightness level in bright sunlight is not sufficient, the dot is almost invisible if you're in really bright sunlight. In the shade it's easy enough to see. I've used it on a AR-15 chambered in 5.56 and it held zero, but have since moved on to a reflex sight with better optics, so I cannot comment on how well it holds up over time as I only had it on my rifle for a couple of outings since I had purchased it.

title: Doesn't conceal well
text: I have a Ruger LCP II and it prints really bad. I mean it's obvious I'm carrying by the bulge on the inside of my pant leg. I supposed if you wore boot cut jeans or straight legged jeans with boots, you may be able to conceal better, but unfortunately that's not the case with me and my jean/tennis shoe combo. I was at first attracted to the fact this was a universal ankle holster with an added strap at the top that would further secure from slipping down when worn in an all day active environment, that's great and the added magazine pocket was an added bonus. But for me it's added bulk that I was looking to avoid in a concealed carry environment. I'll just continue to carry with my pocket holster which prints a little, but with keys and pocket change, it just looks like I have my wallet in my front pocket. Nice quality and craftsmanship. but not for me. I was so wanting to love this, but not the case in my situation.

title: Super bright green laser
text: Wow, this laser is brighter than my bore sight and they use the same battery! Holds zero, not meant for long range shooting by all means, but for CQB up to 50-60 yards at most (do some research, longer the range, the larger the dot therefore you lose accuracy) and has a nice hefty weight to it. The adjustments have very good positive clicks and aren't loose or cheap feeling by all means. The mount could be better, but it's solid nonetheless. The button switch is solid, as well as the remote switch. Best bang for your buck in my opinion. A+

title: What I was looking for
text: This is a great reflex sight that co-witnesses perfectly on my rifle. Mounts up solid and easy to sight in. The brightness settings works well in both low light situations as well as sunny days. Built like a tank and half the price of some of the others that don't have the features this sight has. A++

title: Okay sling
text: This is an ok sling, kind of thin and really long. I do like that the hardware and adjustment buckles are metal vs. plastic, but I will more than likely use it on a shotgun or standard rifle, it's not really designed for the AR platform, I suppose that's why it's listed as "traditional sling" vs. tactical. Once adjusted for my AR, there's just too much slack left over. I suppose I could trim it down, but it's more suited for long guns or similar rifles, hence the four stars.

title: What I thought I needed
text: I bought this thinking I needed it on my M-Lok rail to mount a sling only to discover the rail has QD swivel mounts machined into it in six places LOL!! My bad for not paying closer attention to the rail as when I bought it, it didn't specify they were there. Oh well I'll use it on another build. The quality is top notch as usual with UTG products and the swivel snaps in tight and locks up solid. If I had to buy again, I would do so with confidence.

title: Not the worst I've had
text: These mounts aren't the worst I've had, but not the best. They will do for now, but they lack the quality most mounts have in this price range. The mounts themselves are the same aluminum alloy pretty much all mounts are made from, but the hardware it comes with is soft. The mounting nuts will more than likely strip out if you tighten them too much, and by that I mean if you tighten them to specs, they'll strip. So I opted to just use thread locker and snug them to what I think will hold. It's not like they will be under heavy recoil, just on an AR-15 in 5.56mm. So for now I'll use them, but will more than likely replace them and possibly the scope in the near future.

title: What I needed
text: I needed this to raise my scope up to proper eye level on my AR-15. Also my scope was in the way of the charging handle, this remedied my issues. Mounted up tight and made very well. UTG makes great products and I will continue to try and use their products.

title: Great price
text: Great price on these targets. Work well for sighting in at 100+ yards. 100 pack will last me a long while.

title: Perfect for an AR-15
text: Perfect size scope for an AR-15. Clear view, easy to zero and looks great. Don't know if I will use the Illumination much, but it's a nice feature to have in low light conditions when the cross hair is hard to see against a dark background. Has a nice heavy feel and not cheap plastic like some others in this price range. Overall a nice scope at a fair price.

title: Nice scope mount....but
text: This is a really nice scope mount, but unfortunately it doesn't fit the Monstrum Tactical scope I bought it for. The outside distance is too long. I was wanting the clean look of this type of mount, but now I'm stuck and don't know what will fit. This is the link to the scope I bought https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00OY8RRR8/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o00_s01?ie=UTF8&psc=1, any help would be appreciated. Luckily enough I do have a scope this mount will work with on another rifle, so not a total waste.

title: Heavy duty
text: This is truly a heavy duty bipod. Very well built and makes my AR-15 build look totally badass. Buying another one soon for my other build that's in progress.

title: Love'em
text: These are great capsules. Heavy aluminum, knurled for easy grip and have an o-ring seal and included an extra o-ring for each capsule. Great to stash/hide money, keys or any small item you wish. The uses are endless. Mine were a bit hard to unscrew, but a bit of chapstick on the threads fixed that and also keeps the o-ring from drying out.  I may get more in other sizes for my range bag for small tools/mics items. Overall I'm very happy with them.

title: All the basics
text: I bought one of these kits before for an SKS, but it didn't come with the right caliber bore brush. This kit is better quality, albeit the contents are the same but you get the bonus swabs and a better quality case. The case is thicker and the snaps are better attached. The cleaning rod is heat treated in a way to inhibit rust. The brushes are pretty much standard for the 5.56/.223 AR platform. The oil bottle that so many complain about not having oil in it seems to have a decent seal, my other kit has yet to leak. You also get some patches, a double ended brush and swabs. So for $10.99 you get a fairly nice basic field cleaning kit for your rifle that includes all the necessary items one would need to clean and maintain their firearm in the field, minus the oil in which is user supplied.

title: Works for me
text: I was needing a case for my 12ga pump and this seemed to fit the bill. It's a tight fit, but it fits. I have a Stevens 320 with a 28" barrel and most cases are too short, this one is the right length, but it is kind of narrow.  I think this case is more suited for a single shot. It's a well made soft shell case, good zipper, plenty of padding and the color is a lot darker than Amazon's stock picture, more of an OD green in color, so take this information into consideration before buying.

title: Great back up
text: Heavy duty sights. Strong spring, kind of stiff, but will loosen with use. Easily adjusted, positive clicks on windage. I know this is primarily for air-soft, but I think it will hold up on an AR-15 due to the fact there's no plastic and it's really heavy for it's size. Not cheap or cheesy at all.

title: Heavy Duty
text: Like the description states, this is a heavy duty QD swivel. Snaps in place nice and tight in my Hogue stock and is just as easily removed. So far I've bought 3 of these and they are holding up as expected, no issues and still fit as tight as the day I bought them. A true five star product from UTG!!!

title: Works as intended
text: These aren't the best, but not the worst gun hooks. they work for my needs to hang a couple of guns up in my closet. I wouldn't use these for guns with wood stocks as they may get scratched up. Both of mine have synthetic stocks, so worries.

title: Great sling
text: Perfect for my AR-15. Soft, durable and easy to attach. I plan on buying a few more for my other rifles and maybe on for my shotgun. Quality product.

title: Do what they're supposed to do.
text: These are pretty good safety glasses at a really good price for something that has Smith & Wesson endorsed on it. They're really comfortable, wear well under a ball cap, and are slightly tinted. Love the fact they come with a case and cleaning cloth. They do not fog, but the condensation does build up a bit and drip down the lens, but I can live with that. God only have you one set of eyes, best protect them. I got a chance to wear them a couple of times while at the gun range and the don't interfere with my vision like the wally world brand I had before, they would distort my vision to some degree and that's not a good thing while looking down the sights of a gun. I recommend these as a great budget pair, should last a good while.

title: It works like it should
text: I bought this despite the negative reviews as I didn't want to spend a ton of money on a bore sight that will get limited usage. I installed the battery and it works as it should. The laser looks like it isn't centered, but one simple test verified that it is in fact centered. Easy and simple to use and gets you on paper, as it's intended purpose. A few rounds to fine tune and good to go at 100+ yards. Great budget bore sight, recommend if you're in the market for one. On a side note,  I suggest getting the green laser, easier to see in daylight and it come with the more common CR2 battery you can buy at just about anywhere.

title: Really thin, doesn't protect furniture.
text: Ok so this is pretty much a large mouse pad with a tray attached to it. I thought it would be thicker and more durable, but it's pretty thin. I've bought mouse pads at the Dollar Tree that were thicker than this. The print and tray are about the best part about this mat. Don't know how long it will last, but if any of you are considering buying this to protect your table (mine is ceramic tiled top so it doesn't matter), look elsewhere. It's ok for protecting your gun, but that is about it.

title: Ok in a pinch, but would rather have one less slippery
text: Not the best tool for the job as others have stated it's really slick! it's ok for what I needed it for, but if I had to buy again it will not be this block. Other that that everything is aligned properly and allowed me to work on my 1911, but it's slippery, really slippery. Also to the one guy who said he received a used scratched up block, that just the molding marks from casting, mine has them also.

title: Highly visible on impact!
text: Splatterburst targets are the best out there. Highly visible on impact and a better price on Amazon than anywhere else I've looked. Stock up while they're cheap!

title: Splatterburst is the best!
text: I haven't used this pattern yet, but I've been using Splatterburst targets for a while now and love'em!! I bought these to sight in a scope. Should fit the bill nicely, if not, still fun to shoot at and see where you're hitting.

title: Just get them already
text: If you own a 1911, you need these!! These are really great grips, far superior to stock wood grips. They feel good in my hands and the texture is a really aggressive non slip grip. No modifications were needed on my ATI 1911, fit is perfect. Really makes the pistol look good. Attached is before and after pictures. The price is what made this purchase a sealed deal. Same G10 material as the competitor at half the price!!

title: Nice case better price.
text: Almost identical to the gun case that my pistol came in. I like these smaller cases as I can fit them into my range bag. They will hold a full sized 1911 .45 and maybe one spare magazine, but that's about it.  Only gripe is the foam isn't glued down so that is a little annoying, but can be fixed easily enough. Snaps secure and they stack on top of one another. A must have if space is an issue.

title: Great for field stripping 1911's
text: OK let me start off with a question. How are you guys chewing this thing up? I mean really? After a handful of uses you say? Are you putting your entire weight on your 1911 when removing the barrel bushing? I mean I do agree that it's not a practical tool for putting it back together, no bushing wrench is for that matter, but for takedown it's a life saver and an eye saver. Those of you that for the first time field stripped a 1911 know what I mean. Nothing like a recoil spring plug flying across the room and scaring the hell out of everyone including the cat LOL! But it works as intended for most part. I've never had a bushing wrench that really worked putting a 1911 back together. It's much easier putting one back together by hand than breaking it down, and this little gadget helps a lot in that area of breakdown while not marring the finish on the muzzle. I see over time and repeated use it may get a little chewed up, but some of those pics I saw while researching bushing wrenches......all I can say is wow, do ya know what you're doing there scooter?

title: Handy Tool
text: Handy little tool, especially if your choke tubes fit flush with the muzzle like most of mine do. Also comes in handy for adjusting elevation/windage on scopes. Seems durable enough and does what it's supposed to do. FYI/PSA those of you that's complaining about it only being stepped on one side, that's the way it's supposed to be in order to get a proper grip on the choke tube and not damage it or your barrel. That's why it's a "Universal Choke Tube Wrench". ;)

title: Wear these to avoid hearing loss!
text: These work great blocking out everyday sound and dramatically reduces the sound of gunfire at the range. Fit as expected, fairly comfortable (will be even more so once they break in) and fold up small and take up very little room in my range bag. Highly recommend these for saving your hearing.

title: Cotton patches
text: What can I say, they're cleaning patches. 100% cotton and do what they're made for, cleaning the bore on my guns. I opted for the 3" patches rather than buying a dozen different sizes, I can always cut them down for smaller bores. There's 500 to a pack and come in a ziplock bag. Should last a while unless I get trigger happy at the range lol.

title: A well oiled machine
text: Love the precision bottle. Lets you get into those hard to reach areas around the trigger and bolt. Never had any issues using Hoppe's products. I keep this on hand for everything from reels to power tools that need oiled. Works great and doesn't break down like some other brands that wally world sells. Price online is cheaper too!

title: Great stuff for any firearm
text: I recently got back into shooting/hunting and thought to myself "Wholly crap, I don't have much bore cleaner!" I had only a small bottle I bought when I purchased a pistol almost a year ago as I didn't think I would get to shoot it much. Now that I'm shooting weekly, sometimes twice a week on the traps range, I needed some cleaner. Hoppe's is a great bore cleaner. It's always worked for me without any issues and has never damaged the finish on any of my firearms. Just wet a patch and run it through and follow up with dry patches until clean, easy as that. Glad to have found the big 32 oz. bottle on here as at all the local places here only have the small 5 oz. bottles.

title: Nice and compact kit
text: Great little kit to have on hand. Fits nicely in my range bag without taking up much room. Love that fact the slotted tip and jags are brass and not plastic, so they should last a long time. As far as the bore brushes and mops are concerned, they're pretty much the same thing you would get with any kit no matter the price paid, you can always upgrade those when needed. Overall I'm very happy with it and would buy again.

title: Just get it!!
text: Really nice large range bag. Quality zippers, metal D-rings for the shoulder strap, tons of pockets and plenty of places for magazine storage for both pistol and AR type mags. As of now I have two pistols in their padded rugs, five magazines, shooting glasses, hearing protection, cleaning kit, targets, several 50 round boxes of ammo, a speed loader and still have room for more stuff. I couldn't be happier with this purchase.

title: Great for 7.62x39 Ammo
text: These stack better than the .50 cal cans by Fortress as the bottom indentation is deeper. Same quality as the military issued cans, but brand spanking new. Seal tight, event paint job and hold a lot of 7.62x39 Soviet ammo. I'll being getting a couple more of these puppies!

title: Perfect for a case of 12 gauge ammo
text: I bought this for shotshell storage. Holds a full case of 12 gauge ammo. I shoot traps so I go through a lot of shells and this is just the right size for taking to the range. Seems to be pretty sturdy and closes tightly. Also has holes for locks to keep children out and for extra security against potential theft. I'm going to buy more of these cases for extra storage and maybe some of the other cases of this brand for the rest of my ammo.

title: Nice shooters bags
text: Works for me. Nice shooters bags, seem to be pretty decent quality for the price paid. Easy to fill with a large mouthed funnel. I used rice against all suggestions as I thought sand would be too heavy for my needs and kitty litter would be too dusty despite the claims to be 99% dust free, plus the rice was cheaper. $10 and the plastic beads used in arts and crafts and corn hole bags was outrageously priced at $30 per 10lb . It takes more than 10lbs of rice by the way, 10lbs barely fills the large bag, more like 12-13lbs for both. Over all I'm happy for what it is and should provide me with years of use as It would be limited use for me. It would be more for sighting in scopes and open sights and once that's done, it's done unless you're careless with your guns.

title: Perfect for an outdoor range.
text: This great for the range, especially at mine which doesn't have a dedicated pistol range. 2x4's tend to make it a little top heavy while 1x2's are subject to the wind knocking it over, but it has holes at the base and I used tent stakes to secure it and works like a charm. Assembly is a no brainer, has four bolts with washers and nuts which you can use a wrench or a phillips screwdriver to tighten. 19" wide is perfect for most targets, I use 8" splatter targets and am able to place them two wide and ever how many you want vertical (I did two wide and two high), depends how you cut your backer board. I just used Amazon boxes, have plenty of those lol. All in all it's a great portable target stand. I would recommend this to any avid shooter or hunter.

title: Awesome targets
text: I love these targets. Easily visible from a range of distances and when shooting self defense ranges (10-30 feet) I can see my grouping right away. Love that these are self adhesive and come with extra dots to cover your shots, can get quite a few rounds fired into one before changing it out.

title: Big hull bag
text: A lot larger than I thought, but that's a good thing, means I won't have to empty it as often. Seems to be good quality, only time will tell. Easily adjusted belt and snaps tight. Should make life easier at the range.

title: Works for my needs
text: Nice soft shell case. Quality and material seem like it will hold up for a long while. Both my 12 gauge and SKS fit perfectly. Has plenty of room in the two pockets for shells/tools. I should get a lot of use out of it. May even buy another one so my shotgun and SKS both have their own individual cases.

title: My shoulder thanks you
text: Medium fits my Stevens 320 like a charm. Takes a lot of the recoil out, but more important for me it make the gun more comfortable to shoulder and increased the length of pull. I'll be getting more of these for my other rifles/shotguns in the near future.

title: Great holsters at an incredible price.
text: I love this brand of holsters. Fit and finish are great. Fits my Taurus PT-638 like a glove as it should. Easy draw and doesn't snag on anything. Can wear it as a clip on or with your belt running through the loop and can be changed for left or right hand draw. Will buy again for my other pistol and any other pistols I may buy in the future.

title: Just what I needed
text: Been a while and I no longer have an actual military ammo can to compare this to, but it looks and feels like the real deal. Heavy weight, great seal and the sticker on the side is like a vinyl material so it's easy to peel off and no residue is left. Fairly decent price for a new can, better than some places that I priced for an actual surplus can, most are going for $30+, guess they're in demand. Holds all my ammo, that's all that matters to me. I'll buy more of this brand as needed. A+ product ;)

title: Pleasantly surprised.
text: For a small it's kinda big, but it will hold my Taurus PT-638 along with an extra mag. The first one I ordered got stolen off my porch before I could get home from work to get the package, but was gladly refunded my money. I like that it lays flat when opened. Made from nice quality materials and has a soft interior and can be locked too if you have children in the house. I'll gladly buy more as needed. A+ product.

title: Will work until I can find a better fitting holster.
text: A very snug fit for the Taurus PT-638 .380 ACP but will work until I can find a proper holster. Very hard finding gun specific holsters as almost every manufacturer has a list a mile long of what guns fit in one holster based on dimensions.

title: A must have for any camper.
text: I had one of these burners way back, but I lost it somewhere along the line while moving. These are great for camping or when the power goes out. Large enough for regular sized pots and pans, but small enough to stow away when not in use. Heats really well and evenly, just like a regular gas burner.

title: Nice product.
text: Works really well sharpening my knives, especially the ones that have a serrated edge. Also like the fact that it has an emergency whistle and fire starter built in for just in case. I like that it comes in safety orange so it's easy to spot in case you drop it on the ground. Handy item to have for all situations good or bad.

title: Made for the average American male
text: Finally a sleeping bag warm enough for colder temperatures, small enough to fit my backpack and big enough for and average American man. Nice material, soft, warm and enough room to move around in and get comfortable. It has a zipper plow so as not to catch the material when zipping in for the night and it's plenty long and wide enough, I can zip it up from the inside. It has ties on the end to hold it in place after you roll it up and that really helps with putting it back into it's compression sack. It's really light too, only a couple of pounds, so that's another plus if you're hiking. The top also has drawstrings so you can cinch it up around your head to keep out the cold. Also the zipper at the bottom overlaps another zipper to keep the cold out and your feet warm Overall I'm really happy with this sleeping bag, only time will tell how well it holds up, but seems to be of really good quality.

title: Works great!
text: These are great to have in an emergency or while out camping when it's too windy or wet for a lighter or matches. They can get a fire going really easily due to the magnesium and flint all in one handy unit. It really produces a lot of sparks and the magnesium catches fire quickly.  I like that it's a three pack with three strikers and chains and fit in my pocket or backpack and do not take up any room. Really pleased with this purchase.

title: Just call me sparky
text: These are some big ferro rods! I bought these for a personal project and they're perfect for that. They produce a lot of sparks so I can get a fire going in no time. I like they have a pre-drilled hole on one end for a lanyard or paracord. Should get a lot of uses from these big rods for many years to come.

title: Perfect for set for camping/backpacking
text: Great dishes for hiking/camping. Lightweight and sturdy enough for my occasional use while out camping. The utensils could be a little sturdier, but I have a set for camping I use any way, so not a deal breaker, but handy to have nonetheless. Packs away neatly in it's own mesh carry bag and fits nicely in my backpack. All dishes are normal sized and I like that because I can down some camp chow lol. Would buy again if the occasion arises.

title: Great to have just because
text: I love this lantern. I like the fact that you have several ways to power/charge it. great for camping or any emergency situation. Solar, hand crank features are a plus these days due to "Green" power and if the electric is out/unavailable it allows you to power the unit regardless. Also you can power it by batteries as well. It has two brightness settings, which both are very bright. It comes with a cigarette lighter plug and a wall plug to charge the unit at home or on the go while traveling or car camping. Red light for ac/dc charging, green light for solar charging, plus you can charge usb devices like cell phones with this lantern. A side note the red/green lights do not shut off while charging and the battery is full, just give it at least nine hours when plugged in and 12 hours when charging by solar power. Overall this is a great little lantern and it will come in handy in my upcoming camping trips.

title: The Real Deal!
text: This is the real deal here folks. 750lb paracord for whatever you need it for. I bought this in safety orange originally to replace those cheap guylines that come with tents/rain fly's that are every color but one that's easily seen in any condition. This stuff is strong enough for that purpose and then some. I made a quick keychain also just to see if it was suitable for survival bracelets etc. and it's so easy to work with. Takes a bit more heat to seal the ends than what I'm used to, but that just shows me the quality that goes into making it. Overall I'm very happy with this paracord and plan on buying more colors in the future for various projects.

title: Perfect size for backpacking/hiking
text: Nice sized tent for two averaged sized people and gear or one adult and two children. Easy to set up, only takes a few minutes. Included instructions were a little confusing, I don't think they've been updated with this new version of tent. There's some toggles on the inside of the rain fly I had trouble figuring out where they attach to on the main tent, but I managed to get it all set up. Once all the  stakes and ropes are all tied off, it's a solid tent. I was worried at first my sleeping pad would be too long, but it fit inside nicely. Everything's included to get set up, right out of the package and it's lightweight and perfect sized for backpacking/hiking. Overall I'm very happy with this tent and the ease of setting it up.

title: Huge, but worth it!
text: Although this bag is huge and I won't be taking it hiking, it's great for base camp/car camping. It's big and long and I can toss an turn and won't wake up feeling like I'm stuck in a burrito! It's warm and soft, I may even use it at home on those cold winter nights lol. It is a bit of a struggle to get it back into the compression sack, but that's to be expected due to it's larger size, but once in there it doesn't take up a lot of room in the trunk of my car. Only one thing I would add would be a zipper plow to make it easier to zip up once inside. Other than that nit pick, it's a great bag for the price!

title: Good nights sleep with this pad.
text: Once this sleeping pad airs up and sits for a couple of days, it fills out nicely and is really comfy. I got the 3"x30"x77" and don't bottom out and that's not putting any extra air into it, just letting it air up on it's own. It's wide enough that if I roll in my sleep, I stay on it. Plus the added pillow area is a plus when using a camping pillow. Overall I'm really happy with this purchase and would buy again if need be.

title: Lightweight and packs small
text: Nice lightweight tarp. Got this as a footprint for my tent. Should do well, wouldn't want to put it on jagged rocks, or any tarp for that matter. Really water resistant and packs small as to not to take up much room in my backpack when I go hiking.

title: Great camp cookware!
text: I did a ton of research before settling on this camp cookware. It was suggested on many websites and rated pretty high as far as what you get in quality and what you get in pieces. Nice lightweight cookware set for backpacking/camping. You get a water kettle with lid, nice sized pot with lid, skillet, soup ladle, two bowls, a spatula, scrubby sponge and a cutting board all in a nice storage bag. I tried out the water kettle as soon as I got it and it's pretty nice. I can't wait to try the rest of the set. May have to scramble some eggs in the morning just to try the skillet lol. Overall this is a nice set. Seems heavy duty, but light in weight. Much better cookware than those that look similar but are half the price, they're really thin cheap aluminum just a tad thicker than a soda can, and certainly better than the cookware I had 20 years ago. So buy with confidence, these are really nice and should provide many years of use.

title: Nice set for work or camping
text: Wow this silverware set rivals the set I use every day at home. They're better quality than what you'd get at Dollar Tree. Nice full sized silverware at a great price plus a case and bottle opener to boot. Great to take to work or camping. Can't go wrong with this.

title: Great camp stove!
text: Lightweight stove that breaks down flat? Hell yeah! this thing rocks. Get a fire going and start cooking. I set it up as soon as I got it just to try it out before going camping. Had a good little fire going and boiled some water for my coffee. It was boiling before I knew it in less than 5 minutes. This is perfect for one or two people camping out, not big enough to do more due to it's small size and the fact you have to keep feeding it wood. But once you get it going it works really well and fits into my backpacks pocket and takes up very little room.

title: Great backpack mug.
text: Great lightweight camping mug. Large size for my morning coffee, keeps it nice and hot. I like the fact there's no off taste like with some metal cups and you can slide it out from it's cozy for easy cleaning.

title: Okay belt
text: Okay for what it is, but they've changed everything about this belt. No logo, thinner nylon. But for nine bucks it will serve it's purpose of a camping/hiking belt. I wanted something lightweight and cheap to carry my knife and flashlight while camping and this will serve that purpose along with keeping my pants up. Still a good quality and okay deal (cheaper on their website but you have to pay shipping). Should hold up well for occasional weekend use.

title: Essential for camping/survival
text: This fire starter is awesome. Small but very effective. The compass is a little hard to see, but then again my vision isn't what it used to be. The whistle is really loud and the magnesium rod produces a lot of sparks. I've learned over the years to carry some ordinary cotton balls in my gear. I put them in a sandwich bag and into an old pipe tobacco tin with a screw on lid to keep them dry. I can start a fire on one or two tries with the fire starter. They catch fire rather easily and with enough dry leaves and small twigs you can have a roaring fire in no time. This is a great item to have while camping or in any emergency situation where you might need a fire for signaling, cooking or warmth.

title: Good budget starter sleeping bag
text: Great sleeping bag for warmer temperatures. I would't dare try camping using this when it's below 50 out. It's not as wide as most sleeping bags, but it's plenty long enough. It's a tight fit, but I plan on using it as a blanket in my hammock this spring. I may buy another and zip them together for when I'm on the ground or sleeping in a tent because of the size it is in width, there's no way I could use it, like being wrapped up in a burrito. Other that that it packs small, it's lightweight and seems like a good budget sleeping bag.

title: Good for general use
text: Great to have when camping or around the house in general. I use them on my backpack to hang stuff and also to keep my gear off the ground when it's wet. Seem like good carabiners. Springs are strong and the screw locks all work well. Well worth the price paid. Only one thing, wished that the screw locks were textured, that would make it easier during cold wet weather when hands are wet and numb or have gloves on.

title: 100% satisfied!
text:
Update 02-21-2017:
Camp is Easy read my original review and reached out to me to make things right. They sent out a new tarp as soon as they became available again. It's the same color and size as the first one I received and the stitching on this one is perfect. No hanging loose threads or missed places along the hem like the first one. It's very lightweight but durable tarp, perfect for hammock camping or as a sun shade/rain shelter. Everything you need to get set up is ready to go right out of the package. It has a separate bag for the guylines and stakes and everything packs small and fits in my backpack. Camp is Easy stands behind their products 100% and gives a 5 year warranty on their tarps, so you really don't have anything to lose. I'm a very happy camper, literally, pun intended! Give this tarp a go, you will not be disappointed ;)

title: Light and packs small!
text:
Okay it's small. But isn't that the reason for a pillow designed for backpacking? It's really soft, lightweight and packs down small so it fits in your backpack for hiking/camping. It's comfortable and works great in a hammock. I haven't tried it with a sleeping bag as of yet, but I bet it will be good there as well. I like the fact that:
1- doesn't have the blown up and makes no noise like the blow up pillows do!
2- removable cover than can be washed.
3- packs down small as to not take up too much room in a backpack.
4- fluffs up really well.
5- comes with it's own stuffsack.
This is great for the car as well for long road trips when the kids nod off to sleep. So buy a bunch for everyone and happy camping!

title: Spacious Backpack
text: Okay so first impression was "Wow, this is a big assed backpack!" LOL The fit and finish are spot on for a backpack in this class. Plenty of attachment points/compression straps, hydration bladder ready, separate compartment for sleeping bag, several other separate compartments and has an included rain cover. Now at first I was worried about all the reviews stating that this pack was designed for smaller shorter people in the 5'5"-5'9" 125-150 lbs area. Not entirely true. I'm 5' 10" 225 lbs and with proper adjustments it fits as it should. The waist belt area rest right on top of my hip area as it should and the sternum strap adjusts where it should, at the sternum. I haven't packed it with a full load as of yet, just stuffed some pillows and some camping gear ti fill it out so I could make the proper adjustments and seems like it will be comfortable enough for a days hike while camping out this spring, I will update when I get a chance to use it in the field. The shoulder straps and back padding are comfortable as well as the waist belt. The only gripe, and it's just me, is that it's impossible to reach the side pockets while wearing the pack to get out your water bottle, so take that into consideration and do what I did and buy a hydration bladder. Also the pockets on the belt are kind of hard to get to, but manageable of you're in need and are determined. Other than that, so far this is a decent pack for the money and am looking forward to getting to use it out in the field this spring.

title: You need this!!
text: Okay my first impression after I removed the hammock from it's stuff sack was "This isn't going to hold up." Okay so I was wrong. I'm 5'10" 225 lbs. and at first there was some tearing noises, guess everything had to stretch first. But once I got it hung up and laid down in it I was pleasantly surprised. Nothing ripped and stitching is intact. Even if the stitching along the sides do rip, there's only two narrow strips! The bottom is one solid piece. It packs small, is comfortable, and the included straps and carabiners are a plus! For the price and what's included, THIS CANNOT BE BEAT!!! I live in an apartment and hung it up in my bedroom to test it out using: [[ASIN:B01FO3N9JG Premium Hammock Hanging Kit By Maky Outdoors | Load Capacity 1300lbs | Heavy Duty,Ultra Durable Hammock Hooks&Carabiners For Hammock Stand,Yoga&Brazilian Hammocks,Swing Chair,Multiple Indoor & Outdoor]] My apartment was built in the 40's and have hollow walls, so finding a stud was out of the question. So I drilled a hole through the door casing and was solid all the way through. Hung it up and was ready to relax. This is an overall great hammock given the price point and I cannot wait until spring to go camping with it!

title: Homemade Cooler-dor
text: Nice sized cooler. The color is a little darker blue than pictured, but I knew that as I have the smaller 48 quart cooler by Coleman. I didn't buy this for its intended purpose, but to make a cooler-dor. A humidor for storing whole boxes of cigars. Seals good and has plenty of space for my Spanish cedar trays, which four will fit perfectly side by side, and maybe five high, so I cannot attest to how long it will hold ice, but my smaller one holds ice at 80+ degrees outside temp for about 3 days, so maybe this one will hold for about 5 days if it's really packed with ice. Anyway this is a great cooler for the price and will serve it's purpose very well.

title: Good stuff. Helps lighten the load for camping trips ...
text: Good stuff. Helps lighten the load for camping trips or great in an emergency and has a very long shelf life.

title: I didn't like the beans in this
text: I didn't like the beans in this, let it sit for 20 minutes and they were still not really done. Flavor is good, just can't get past the hard half cooked beans.

title: This is great for camping or as emergency food
text: I was blown away with the flavor of this. This is great for camping or as emergency food. Has a long shelf life of about 3 years depending on the date you get, but you'll get at least two and a half years!

title: Five Stars
text: Pretty good. I think I like this one better than the eggs with ham.

title: Five Stars
text: Pretty good stuff for a freeze dried breakfast. goes great with campfire coffee.

title: Great grip. Stays where I put it
text: Great grip. Stays where I put it, no slippage even after having it for a while and cushions the recoil really well.

title: Five Stars
text: Great case, easily customizable  for your needs. I used mine for hand gun storage.

title: Stitching/quality issues, but still good
text: Holster was as described. Fits my S&W .45 perfectly. There is some quality/stitching issues with this last purchase, nothing I can't fix, but shouldn't have to, so knocking off a star for that. Other than that, still a descent holster for the money.

title: Nice liner
text: As I have gotten older my hands just don't stay warm like they used to.  I got these for wearing in my heavy weight leather snow blowing gloves.  They work great for that and keep my fingers nice and warm.  These are incredibly soft and comfortable.  They wick away moisture very well and keep my hands warm and dry.  They will also make good light weight cool weather gloves.

title: Great kit!
text: We recently were give a free pool table.  THe ques that came with it were ok and we were having fun.  Some family complained about our crappy cues and begged us for better ones.  Now they all fight over this cue.  The cue is straight and weighted perfectly and ultra smooth.  THe tip is great quality and the overall feel of the cue is amazing.  We are probably going to end up getting another one as this is just a really nice reasonably priced cue.

title: Swim lessons here we come
text: My grandkids are all going to be in swim lessons again this year.  THey all like to use ear plugs, and a couple of them like the nose plugs.  Now we have a set for each of them and there will be no fights over who's is who's as these are all different colors (note to self- ALWAYS choose different colors lol).  The quality is decent and they should last thru the season.  The case is handy and will protect them when not in use.  The kids all tried them in the towns open swim and they all were thrilled.

title: good set
text: This is a good set of ankle weights.  It is easy to put on and remove, but stayed on for the entire hour long workout.  They do get a bit sweaty underneath, but it was a very hot day when we used these.  Really like the adjustable weight idea, but removing and replacing the little bags of weight is a workout in itself.  NO way your going to do this on the fly, so I ended up just removing them when I got tired, then put them back on when I was recovered a bit.  My wife tried them out and had the same compliant.  Overall well worth the money if your in the market for ankle weights.

title: back stretch
text: This is a well made and very sturdy wheel.  We use it to stretch out backs to help relieve tension and sore muscles.  It is padded well and hardly flexes at all (even with my 225Lb body rolling around in it).  Be careful if you have never used one of these as they really cause your back to arch and you could hurt yourself if not careful.  As an added bonus we taught our dog to "jump" thru it!

title: Great first tracker
text: This is a great kids tracker watch.  It is super easy to use and fun for kids to see how active they are.  Linked seamlessly to the Fitbit app (we have it on our phones for our own personal watches).  Very easy to switch between accounts (surprising as I have had issues with the Fitbit app before). title: Look closely

title: Torn on this
text: I have been using a cheap basic tracker for over a year.  I liked how it worked for the most part but accuracy was way off (workouts would undercount steps but I could ride the mower for 45 mins and get 2 days worth of steps).  My wife talked me into upgrading to an actual fitbit.  After reading reviews and product descriptions and pouring over videos I had narrowed it down to the charge 4, the charge 3, and a Samsung offering.  Well the price tag on the Samsung put it out, and the charge 3 is selling for as much as a 4.  After a very frustrating wait on a prime shipment (7 days when it should have been 2) the watch arrived.  First and foremost there are NO directions so forget about learning any of the features by reading (whatever).  The app is somewhat complicated and very difficult to figure out.  After several hours of frustrating and useless attempts I finally have up and packed it all up to be sent back (mind you my battery went from 72% to 14%).  The next day I wore the watch to spite myself and it did record my steps accurately.  I played with it more that night and got some of the features to work but I still could not get my texts.  My daughter took over and figured out what I was doing wrong (had the do not disturb turned on at the watch- but not in the app) which brings me to my next huge issue.  Some of the features can only be accessed from the watch, some only from the app, and some from either.  SO frustrating.  So after getting everything FINALLY set up I wore the watch all day and night.  Everything worked and I got a sleep score and all was good.  3 days later and some of the features have stopped working.  Sleep score no longer records (but it tells me how much I sleep and all the jazz).  Workout target zone does not work now (I must have turned off something that records this info).  I can't seem to answer my texts thru the watch at all.  To activate the screen is a practice of futility.  Some times 2 or 3 taps will turn on the screen and sometimes I have to tap the screen 50 to 100 times, and sometimes the only way to activate the screen is with the button (I do have a cover on mine but still).  There are some really nice things about the watch.  Switch bands is a breeze and takes less than a minute, and the bands hold well.  Most texts are easy to read and I have not run out of space on longer texts (my last watch was limited to 2 screens and 2 words).  Battery life has been excellent (4 days of messing around with settings and what not and still at 48%).  Bluetooth range is amazing (15 feet in a lot of cases).  Step count is super accurate (often within 20 steps of my wife's watch when we do workouts together).  There are some cool faces and apps you can add to the watch.  Overall I'm feeling pretty neutral on Fitbit in general.  There is a lot of info provided but the app is so unfriendly and hard to figure out.  There is to much fiddling around between the watch and the app as to be frustrating.  Even the "How to Use" section on the app is worthless (it tells you features, but not how to turn them on or off).  I am keeping the watch because it does track what I want, but would not recommend it to anyone new to tracker apps as trying to learn this app is way to complicated.

title: Be safe

She is still not comfortable lifting her pushing foot onto the deck but that's fine with us.  There is not any safety equipment included so make sure you have at least a helmet for your little one. My only compliant is that you really need to get it moving pretty fast to get the wheels to light up,  She can't get up enough speed to light them and is frustrated that they won't light for her.

title: No leaks
text: This is a decent battle.  It helps motivate you to drink more. Easy flip up cap keeps the straw protected.  Zero leaks even when it was knocked over in a hot car.  These bottles are NOT insulated so they will sweat.  The supper tip is a bit odd and does not really stand upright.  Still easy enough to drink from but took a little getting used to when using during a workout.  Easy to take apart and clean.  Very easy to read the water level.  Fits in most cup holders.

Love the measure feature that helps keep you motivated to keep hydrated.  Color is great and bottle is easy to clean and has not leaked at all.  Very pleased.

title: well made but a bit stiff
text: This belt is very well made.  It is a lot longer than I thought it would be and it wraps around me 1 and a quarter times (38 waist).  I have lost some weight over the last 3 years so most of my pants are too big so a belt is a daily thing for me.  This works very well and holds tight.  I currently use a webbed jumpers belt so I like these heavy duty webbed belts.  This one has a seat belt like clasp (my other one is a slide buckle lock).
