title: Good for workouts
text: I like this bottle for workouts.  I did try it at work but the bottle sweats too much if you fill it with ice, and the water gets too warm without the ice.  For my workouts I keep it in the fridge so it should cold and ready to go.  Stays cold enough to last the hour to hour and a half that my workout takes.  Pretty easy to clean out and so far no problems with mold growth.  I have the grey color and it is easy to read and looks nice.  Pretty pleased with this bottle.

title: great products
text: This is a real nice handy set for workouts and sore back relief.  I also tried out the roller on my feet and it was amazing.  The roller is so nice to use and has a nice variety of vibration levels and is so comfortable and relaxing.  The workout balls are great for doing yoga and plaits workouts.  We will use them a ton.  The stretch bands offer a nice variety of resistance and we use these a ton already so it is always handy to have a few more.  The double grip band was something new and both my wife and I liked how well it worked for working arm and chest muscles.  Entire set is great quality and very useful for workouts.

title: easy to use
text: This is a nice sore muscle set.  Roller works well for back, leg, or foot rolling.  Feels real good and has just enough give to not cause pinching issues.  The stick roller is ok for large muscle use but is a bit difficult to use solo.  The ball and spoke rollers are great for smaller muscle target and can really get in and work out knots.  Great directions with a lot of ideas and pictures so you can target specific areas.

title: Zombies beware
text: This resettable target is just plain fun to shoot.  It works perfectly.  I set it out at 30 yards and stakes it down in very wet soil and ran the card back to my bench.  It reset perfectly every time.  Even after 50 shots the target was still resetting perfectly and did not move even in the wet muddy ground.  Yes the face gets beat up pretty bad (as far as the paint job goes). but I didn't buy it for the looks lol.  I only use a .177 call putting out about 15 to 18 ft/lbs of energy so no dents or dings on the metal plates.  I would be comfortable shooting this with a .22 airguns also but anything with more energy would most likely leave dents.  Also only use softer pellets (lead) as harder alloys or BBs will bounce back.  With proper care and a little paint this target should last for 100's of thousands of hits.

title: Works better than powder
text: I work out daily and at times get bad chafing.  This spray helps a lot and works better than cornstarch powder I usually use.  Sprays on evenly and last through an entire 45min workout.  It is important to remember to use this before a workout as it really does not help to spray it on after the damage is done.  Does not cause any irritation or skin issues (which is what it is supposed to do).  No scent or oily feel.  I really like this product to help prevent chafing.

title: Helpful drink aid
text: My granddaughter a obsessed with drinking enough water.  She loves this bottle and uses it daily.  So far no leaks or spills.  She washes it out every night and it is easy to clean and does not seem to be building up any mild on the seals (she is careful to scrub them real well).  She says the markings work great and she is sure she is drinking enough water at school.  Hey if it makes her happy and she is drinking enough water, then there is nothing to complaint about.

title: nice rings but run a bit small
text: I like the styling of these rings.  They are comfortable and the bands are smooth with no noticeable seam.  The colors are nice and I'm particularly fond of the camo design.  The sizing seems to run about a half size small so measure carefully.  The rings are wide but not too bad.  These rings are not the "vented" type so they can get a little sweaty underneath so make sure to wash underneath the ring.  If you have restrictions for metal rings then these make a great alternative.

title: FIt well and comfortable
text: THese are really nice winter goggles.  They will fit kids  (3 and 12) and are light weight and super comfortable.  Pretty decent fog free unless they get wet on the inside (like dropped in the snow lol).  Really nice for cutting glare on those sunny winter days.  They will also fit adults pretty well but do not work well with glasses.  I don't think they would fit over a helmet very well but I didn't actually try as My helmets are all up at my property.  THe kids paln on using these for skiing this year once the season really gets going.

title: only 1 set of lenses
text: These goggles do fit over glasses very comfortably.  The smallest smallest the strap setting  "barely" fit my hatless head,  With a cap theses should fit pretty good.  I got the Dark tint and it is pretty reasonable as far as tint goes.  I was disappointed to learn that despite all the talk about interchangeable  lenses, the goggles only come with one set of lenses.  It would have been nice if they included at least an extra set.  The included case is VERY tight and I struggled to zip it closed.  The lenses do snap on and off easily and do hold in place very well.  The strap  is very grippy and should hold to a helmet very well.  I tested out the fog proof by going from a warm room to the snow outdoors and after a few minutes of fogginess the lenses cleared and stayed clear.  The added benefit was my glasses also stayed clear.  These could be a 5 star goggles if they had included and extra set of lenses and had a case that was a little larger and more accommodating.

title: Good for younger kids
text: Not for older kids.  We tried these on our 12 yr old granddaughter and they would not fit (but she has a large head and wears adult size swim googles)/  On the 3 year old these fit just fine.  She didn't like wearing them for a long period of time but we were not in the pool so that was understandable.  The ear and nose plugs fit the older granddaughter fine.  These seem well made and pretty much fog proof.  Pretty easy to adjust and they stayed in place once we got them on.  We liked the larger one piece design rather than the 2 piece design we are more used to.

title: Not comfortable over glasses
text: Nice goggle that are practically fog proof.  The styling is very good and the mirror effect is very cool.  Without glasses the goggles are comfortable and fit is great.  With glasses (and I have pretty small conservative frames) these goggles are way too tight and will jam your frames into the bridge of your nose.  Not at all comfortable to wear for any length of time.  Too bad as these would be great if they worked better with glasses.

title: Work well
text: My granddaughter tried these out in gym class.  She said they don't leak and are indeed fog proof.  She had a little struggle getting these adjusted at first but once adjusted they stayed in place.  She also said not real great for driving but then she has never found good diving goggles

title: Odd but works
text: I thought this was kind of an odd item but my wife said let's try it out.  Well the dang thing works very well.  The hottest setting is a bit uncomfortable to hold (but would be great in a pocket of snow pants).  The medium setting is perfect temp wise.  The low is real nice for the car ride to keep the hand warm while the steering wheel warms up.  As for a power bank this works well also.  Took my Samsung s7 from 20% to 100% in about 1.5 hours (with light usage during that time),  Not sure how long the battery will last if you using both heating and charging (not even sure that is possible but even if it's not still not a deal breaker).  Takes a standard micro USB cord to charge (included) but do make sure your charging station is a 5 amp as I had this on a 3 amp charger and it took over 12 hours to fully charge.  It also comes with a nice to  velvet bag keep the unit in while it is in heating mode (and the bag is big enough to put a cord in also but I would other leave the cord in there while using it as a heater).  I would recommend getting 2 of these so you can have one in each pocket and can warm both hands at the same time. (They should sell this as a 2 pack- that would be great)

title: Very heavy duty
text: This bounder is very heavy duty.  It has a good strong rebound base and 6 legs for amazing stability.  The frame will support 240 lbs easily and probably more (they quote 264 lbs).  Setup was easy with just unhooking the legs and unfolding the frame.  The support handle is in 4 pieces and slides and locks together very easily and securely.  The upper handle is even nicely padded.  Both the wife and I tried it out and just 10 mins of bounding had us sweaty and out of breath (we both work out daily).  Our only complaint is this does take up a fair amount of room (even when folded up).  We end up keeping on the porch and bringing it when we need it.  The grandkids absolutely love it also and call it the inside trampoline.  Great for anyone with knee issues as the bounce really helps relieve the jarring that can occur when you work out on hard surfaces.

title: Good length but not super strong spring
text: THese reels have a great length and a very sturdy cable.  Retracting reel spring could be stronger as my simple ID holder with 2 cards in it won't fully retract without help.  Also the badge snap loop is attached to the permanent don't ring and not the split ring.  I had to cut mine off as I have a badge holder and did not need the additional strap.  Belt clip works amazing and holds well even getting up and down out of my work chair 3 or 4 dozen times a day, in and out of the car, lab coat on, lab coat off, pulling out to punch in and out, get in and out of the building, and scan from the desk to sign off on work orders,  Yea this is seeing a real work out no doubt.  For a single badge without a holder these would probably be perfect.

title: Great tie offs and power bands
text: These work great as tie offs.  they stretch out from like 18 inches to 3 feet with a nice solid bungee feel.  Loops at both ends and rubber grips make these perfect for any time off needs.  We added carabiners and use them to keep out mowers from bouncing around in the back of the jeep.  The you hold nice and are quick to remove.  They also work great as exercise bands  and the rubber grip makes them comfortable to hold and gives a great grip even when your hands are sweaty.  So many practical uses.

title: Great fit and adjustment
text: I suffer with bad knees.  I have locking issues and hyper extend my knees all the time.  I have only found a few braces that fit my rather thick upper thighs without cutting off circulation or rolling down all the time.  This brace works great for me.  It has a good stretch to it and easily slides on and stays put without causing numbness or discomfort.  The wrap around bands allow such a great variety of support and compression options.  The velcro stays put no matter what your activity level (including a very intense yoga stretching workout).  Material is soft and comfortable to wear and doesn't become sweaty and hot like neoprene braces do.  The padding level is perfect and there is an extra cushion ring that circles and protects the kneecap.  Probably the best part is the silicon dots at the top of the brace.  They keep the brace from slipping down but they don't grab or pull the leg hair at all (a painful problem I have had with a lot of other braces).  The Side support rods are flexible enough to do a good workout but do offer an extra level of support to help keep the knee aligned.  The only negative I have found is the attachment points for the compression straps are right at the edge of the brace and it the velcro tabs hang over at all the velcro can rub a bit and get uncomfortable (east enough to readjust)

She said the pants are super comfortable and don't bind or bunch.  Well made with all the seams solidly sewn.  Her favorite part is the zip off legs to make instant short. The legs also zip length wise so getting these on and off over shoes or boots is a breeze.  Material is soft and comfortable and does not shrink.  Zippers are well finished and no issues with getting them started or zipping them together.  Pants don't rub funny and the pockets are deep enough to hold your phone or whatever you need.  Great well made functional pants and shorts all in one.

Base is nice a wide for stability but not so wide that it interferes with any moves requiring movement around the steps. THe hat can be rolled or folded up for easy packing and takes up very little space.  Looks good on everyone from my 11 yr old granddaughter to my 72 year old mom.

We could not keep the goggles on her se we had the 11 year old try them out.  SHe said they were comfortable enough but a bit tight after a while.  She said they did not leak or fog up at all. My older granddaughter tried out the nose plugs but said she didnt like them (she is a level 4 swimmer and they don't let them use nose plugs in lessons so she has never really used them).  All in all a great set if you can convince your toddler to use it!  We shall see how she does with them at the pool this summer.

title: Grrat supportive workout socks
text: These are great workout sock.  Super support and just the right amound of compression.  They almost feel like they are messaging your feet.  Moisture wicking design really helps with sweaty feet.  You could wear these all day long but I only like a lowcut for workouts so thats all I use them for. title: Patience is key

There was a couple spots that the backing paper was stuck to the transfere paper and caused.the vinyl to lift but we worked thru them and im happy with how it went. title: Nice bike cover
text: This is a great bike cover.  We usually keep our bikes on our porch but if we have a party we need to put the bikes out in the driveway.  This cover works great for keeping them safe from the weather.  It is large enough to cover 2 bikes if you can get them close enough to each other.  Cover stays on well and even a good steady wind wont blow it off.  Cover is lite weight and packs down very well so it could be taken with you use in the field.  I would not use this for use on a travel hitch or trailering.

title: Good fit but odd tummy control
text: Thiese are nice leggings for cooler eeather.  They are heavy weight and warm.  Material is soft and comfy against the skin.  Fit is good.  They are high waisted and when you pull them up they tend to make the tummy look round.  They do trim up the hips and butt but at the cost of the tummy.  Not a deal breaker but just be aware depending on your body type your tummy may look more rounded.  They are well made and dont have any loose threads or wierd seams.

title: Super handy and easy to use
text: Great set of awning clamps.  I use these on my sun shade on my porch.  Really handy if you dont want to install a permanent grommet.  Super easy to use and has held up thru some pretty gusty winds (even held on when a bungeee cord snapped and the awning end was flapping in the wind).  Lots of possible anchor point and ways to anchor (hook on or tie up or bungee)  nice bright orange color so you wont loose track of this.

title: Great fit and soft fabric
text: My wife really likes these pants.  She says they are great for workouts and fit is perfect.  She says they are very soft and wick away moisture very well.  Didnt shrink in the wash which is always a good thing.  She said they didnt bind in the waist or at the ankles.  She also said they dont ride up and cause any discomfort in the crotch.  Her only complaint is that they were real staticy out of the dryer even when using 2 dryer sheets (of course thats more related to the dry air in the house than anything elese).

title: Not hands free
text: Im confused on this product.  Discription states hands free hydration.  To me that means you dont have to touch anything with your hands.  So this is a water bottle and a fanny pack.  Nothing hands free about it.  You want a drink you gotta grab the water bottle with your hands and unlock the cap and flip up the mud guard and put the bottle to your mouth and tip it back.  Nothing hands free about that.  The bottle is easy to drink from and will keep out debris.  The pack fits nice and is padded and comfy to wear.  I guess I dont understand what hands free means.  There should be a disclaimer that the only hands free part is the actually carrying  of the bottle.  The drinking part is completly hands on.  I would have rated this lower for the inaccuracy but it is a nice bottle and pack

title: Comfortable and supportive
text: These are really nice socks.  Fit was perfect for my 10.5 foot.  Like the length for workimg out and they really are anti sweat (well to a certian extent, intense workouts or no breathable shoes will make your feet sweat no matter what).  Support was amazing.  This is a real comfortable sock

title: Great jacket just watch the size
text: Nice quality built jacket.  Sizes run on the smaller side.  This is reversable but kind of plain on the inside.  Perfect weight for those chilly spring or fall mornings.  Pockets are nice and deep.  Zipper and snaps are high quality as expected from Columbia.  Length is good as is sleeve length.  No funny seams or odd lining bunches that can irritate.  Good comfort and good flexibility.

title: Great powerful pump
text: This little pump blew me away!  It is amazingly powerful.  We have a double queen size air mattress (it had an inflatable frame and and inflatable inner mattress)  Our old battery powered pump would burn thru a set and a half of D batteries and took close to half and hour to fill.  This pump filled them in about 5 mins.  It is a bit loud but not obnoxious.  The include hose extender works pretty good but the sound of the air rushing thru it produces a very high pitched whistling sound.  All the need adaptor sizes are included.  The cord is not real long but as long as your near an outlet you can fill comfortable (cord is about 6 feet long).  This also has a handy handle for moving around and honestly I think you could use this as a leaf blower if you wanted too (yea it is that powerful).  I really do like the way the way this works.  I got this in exchange for my honest review

title: Great comfy warm gloves
text: These gloves are great.  So super comfy and amazingly well thought out.  The 2 middle fingers have little loopsin them to allow easy removal.  The thumb has a little removable end if you need extra grip.  The fold over flap has a nice velcro dot to hold it open.  Material is very grippy and waterproof.  Wind and rain are not going to get thru these gloves.  The only negative I can find with these gloves is they do have a bit of a funky odor.  Fit is perfect.  I got these in exchange for my honest review

title: Better options out there
text: This doesnt make sense to me.  They say hands free so I invisioned a flex tube running up from the belt.  Nope this is just a water bladder with a sipper top.  Lots of odd pockets that dont zip or velcro closec.  Only one pocket actually zippers.  There is elastic pull bands everywhere and in every direction.  They dont seem to do a whole lot except scrunch the belt into pdd shapes.  My wife tried it on and said the fir was nice and comfy so thats a plus.  It also has nice little reflective strips so another plus.  The material is meshy and should breath well and dry quickly so thats another plus.  I just dont see this as being as functional as a lot of other camelback products.  I guess my big fear is something falling out of the open pockets or the water badder hitting the ground and getting all dirty.  I got this in exchange for my honest review

title: Good with a few design quirks
text: This is pretty nice in that it has generous sizing and a lot of storage.  Water bottle is held at an odd angle and is going to cause a lopsided feel no matter where you position it. title: Good watch that can get a bit finicky
text: I got this in exchange for my honest review.  This is a love hate relationship.  I love the features and all the different settings but I hate the interface.  Sometimes screens scroll super smooth and respond to touch inputs as they shoul and sometimes they wont scroll or lag so bad you want to smash this with a hammer.  Sometimes it links seamlessly with the phone and sometimes you canset it on top of the phone and it acts like it has never even haerd of bluetooth.  There is no rhyme or reason.  I used it in a workout yesterday and part way thru i must have bumped the screen because it turned off the fitness program.  Today it would not register i was working out at all.  Some of the data is super accurate (im wearing a second fitness watch just to compare) and some is so far off that according the the watch I may just be deceased (not really but i dont see my heartrate reaching 276 bpm just sitting watching videos)  The app is ok but does take some getting used to and some stuff that should be intuitive seems awkward and reversed.  They use odd terms for certian actions (like to unpair or disconnect from the phone they use the term unbind! )  There are a lot of nice features but are almost to specific (like there is no workout routine but you can choose tenmis, soccor, running, badmiton, basketball etc.).  And it stores messages (i thimk up to 5) but if you dont delete them new messages are not displayed only the old ones.  The band is real nice and the watch looks like a very expensive timepiece.  Charging was straight forward and batterylife was excellent.  The watch did get caught in an upgrade loop that kept telling us there was no devise connected.  We unbound and rebound the watch and it settled down.  There is a lot to do and set with this watch and when it is working it is really nice.  Patience is sometimes needed to work with it at times.  What i saw and used with this watch I really liked  and the app is a pretty good app once you get beyond some of awkward language

Update. I just love this thing to death. I have used it to tune my Hatsan AT-44 with a regulator. It now shots a consistent 910 (+/- 3 fps) for 30!!! shots. last 10 fall off by about 5 fps per shot. I could not have accomplished that feature without this chrono. I also used it to "tune" my Beeman p17. after trying several pellets I have a great idea of what to use for any application. title: Great for filling pcp
text:
This is really a nice compressor for filling pcp rifles. I did get it from a different seller at a much better price. Fill times for my wildfire pcp from 1000 to 2000 psi is about 35 seconds. For my Hatsan At44 tanks (180cc) from 2000 to 3000 psi is about 45 seconds. Unit stays under 125˚F. Couple of hints for optimal running. The water inlet is actually the lower inlet. Make sure to start the pump first. Start the compressor with the bleed valve open. DO NOT stop the compressor while under a load, open the bleed valve first. Leave the water pump running for a bit after shutting down the compressor. Make sure to remove and dry the filter in the fill line after every use. This has made my shooting so much more fun and easy.
Update: I have over 2 years on this compressor now. Zero issues. I added another inline moisture filter (about $40 here on amazon) and recently checked my gun cylinders (adding regulators) and there was NO moisture at all. I do frequent oil changes on this compressor with Royal Purple full synth. (every 50 to 75 fills or about 2 to 3 hours run time). I did add Cooper wire wraps around the SS tubes to help desperate heat more efficiently (and to help keep myself from burning my arm accidentally). I got this off flea-bay and went to purchase another one but the price has jumped a bit (249 to 349) Seller a toreal2018.

title: Works great and easy to do.
text: Got this to do some repair work on my 30 something year old xc skis.  Worked great and so easy to do.  I had some pretty bad gouges and scraps from skiing on frozen gravel.  Spent a bit of time preping the bases by removing the wax base and cleaning up the edges of the gouges.  I also used my waxing iron to preheat the bases.  Lit the candle and moved slowly and carefully.  Keep the candle close to your work and hold it at an angle to keep the carbon to a minimum.  After cooling down the included scraper mad quick work of leveling out the area.  A couple quick passes with the scotch brite pads and a finally buff with the white pad and I was ready for a base wax.  I have only been out once since the repair (figures all the snow melted) but the repair held perfectly.  I used about a third of a candle to repair about 4 ft. of scratches of at least a fingernail width wide.  So much cheaper than a new pair of skis.

title: If I could it would have 6 stars
text: Ok this light has its share of things that im not overly thrilled with, but it is such a cool light with really cool features.  So lets get the bad out of the way.  First the plastic clear cover isnt great.  It feels a bit on the cheap side and i fear it will either scratch bad or crack.  It is glued to the body and it just looks sloppy.  It would have been nice if they just left it unglued so it could be removed if desired. The diffuser works well but again it would be nice if it was removable.  So thats the bad.  Now for the good.  2 batteries came with mine.  An extra o ring and a decent keychain clip was nice touch.  Great knurling on the twisty end and i liked the attachment ring as it swings easily and lays flat.  Threads are smooth and work well.  Mode 1 is perfect for low level tasks.  Mode 2 is bright and would work well for closeup work or walking in a dark familiar area.  Mode 3 is solid red and will work perfect for astronomy or perserving night vision.  Mode 4 is red flashing, perfect for signaling or warning.  Mode 5 is solid green as is just way cool probably great for map reading but just love the cool factor of green light.  Mode 6  is green flashing.  Once again signaling or warning, and way high on the cool factor.  Mode 7 is white flashing.  Yea not the best mode but at the end of chain so no big deal.  The flashing is about a 1 second cycle so kinda perfect as far as a flashing mode is concerned.  Run times should be more than acceptable.  Other than the plastic cover durability should be amazing.  Twist end works great and cycling thru the modes is smooth and easy.  Weight is great at about an ounce or so.  Im so thrilled with this light.  No its not the brightest light but as far as useful multifunction lights are concerned this one is far and away the best one i have come across.  The price is steep...no getting around that.  If your looking for a bright light, look somewhere else.  Looking for cheap, not gonna find it here.  Want more colors and modes than you know what to do with?  Here it is.  About the only other thing i wish this had would be either blue or uv led.  Nice job fenix nice job

title: It does work....mostly
text: This is a product that I want to love, and wants to be useful...and comes very close- but just misses the mark.  I use it for holding open those sheet music books that a certain music book publisher (I won't name names but it kinda rhymes with Cal Centered)seems to refuse to put in spiral bound form... ARRRGH nothing worse than trying to play a guitar when the book keeps closing on you.  I've tried everything I can think of to keep the pages open.  Closepins, those metal music stand arms, metal 3 pronged page clips, paperclips, spring clips.... heck even rubberbands.  This little gadget is probably the best solution so far (but not perfect). It will hold the book open (yea) but often times with sheet music you gotta flip back and forth between pages- this is difficult (not impossible, but does mess up the flow of the music).  The pins do hold well and have not ripped any pages so far- but they are a bit long and always seem to fall on the one note that I'm unsure of.  I kinda modified the way I use this by only clamping down on side of the book, leaving the other side loose so I can fip pages easier.  It works, but not perfectly.  If I were using this for straight up reading, it would be a 5 star no brainer, but for music....well it earned 4 stars (I'm feeling generous as this is the best solution I have found so far)

title: Nice shoe Nice Price
text:
Really like these snowshoes. They are easy to adjust and stay on very well. The bag the shoes came in is first rate as are the poles. My only complaint is that the front binding only ratchets to a point then seem to hang up (it could be the strap end catching on the decking, or perhaps the hard boot material failing to flex)not a huge deal because it is snug enough. Also the pole carrying bag is separate from the shoe bag which means I got to remember to grab both. All in all a nice inexpensive snowshoe. Great for beginners or someone just needing a cheaper option.
12/29/11 UPDATE_ Got to try these out for the first time (not real deep snow- but enough to give them a trial run) These shoes are really nice. I tromped around for about 30 mins and had very few problems (main problem was some ice build up on my heel as I crossed a wet area and the water froze on my boot heel- not a big deal as it can happen with any snowshoe). The bindings did hold well and did not loosen at all. One shoe did seem to be toeing in a bit but that was probably an adjustment issue (it was also a new pair of boots I was trying out.) I'm gonna hopefully get out in some deeper snow next week (yea Lake Effect!)
1/15/12 UPDATE2- Finally got some REAL snow (18+ inches!) and tried these out at my hilly property in the deep woods. AMAZING how well they worked. It was pretty cold (hovering around 16° F in the sun) and the woods were untouched by anything but a few deer and turkeys. These shoes performed great. They never slipped and I did not have to adjust the bindings at all. They do seem to make a bit of noise as far as the bindings creaking (at these temps not to surprising), but nothing broke or loosened. Walked for a little over an hour; over logs, thru brush, uphill, downhill, level, tight twisty area, open fields, deep drifts, and even a snowmobile trail (that crosses the front of our property). These preformed as good as any other shoe. A bonus is I found I really liked the poles- so much so that I gave one to my wife and she really liked using it too. All in all a great purchase- These honestly hover on a 5 star rating- I did have to take away for the pole bag not being attached some way- also the poles are nearly impossible to closeup once they get cold (I think a bit of frost gets into the loosening cam and freezes the pole in place as once they warmed up there were no problems) also there is no place to store the rubber protection cap from the pole. The one show still seemed to toe in a bit- but I only notice it in very shallow snow (less than 6 inches) and the toe binding still only rachets to a certain point and then slips (still not an issue as it is snug enough). Oh and of course the noise factor (not real bad but your not gonna sneak up on anything with these on)

Most military items online are knockoffs. Some look nearly identical to the real thing. The canteen I recieved was the real deal. It is big and easy to carry but not too big to the point where it gets in the way. The lid has a flexible tether like thing to prevent you from losing it. The canteen is very well made and very comfortable to wear even when it is full. The threads are nice and sturdy and the plastic being used is very thick and tough yet soft enough to prevent it from being brittle and cracking from being tightened or bumped. Like all the other real military stuff out there it is pretty well thought out. Simple but functional and reliable. Mine arrived with a used cover and strap in near mint condition. The opening never leaks and is the perfect size for drinking. Big enough to easily drink from but small enough to prevent you from accidentally spilling all over yourself. If you are looking for an awesome canteen, this is it. Just make sure you rinse it thoroughly before you use it to prevent the water from tasting bad.

title: BUY THIS! Great fun for 20 year olds
text:
Really great foosball table! We started off buying a smaller one (32 inch, $99) and we pretty much instantly knew we needed a bigger one as the pool and ping pong were unusable on the small table. So we ordered this table and it is great!! No ping pong, but that’s fine.
We mostly use the foosball, but we also enjoy pool a lot! It’s mini, but not so much that you can’t play it. We play foosball multiple times a day, every day, and it has held up very well!
It’s definitely tricky to put together, we accidentally did ours backwards so now we just play left handed, but we like it anyway! When assembling the men, put them all on the poles and into the table before screwing them into place, we ended up having to take a side off the table to put ours in since we screwed them to the poles first!

The only downside is the ‘air’ hockey is unusable. The pucks do not slide into the goals at all, no matter how hard I push. While it may seem obvious that it wouldn’t be great since it is slide hockey more than air hockey, we were able to directly compare this with the small table we’d bought first and the ‘air’ hockey works great on that one!

Basically, this is mostly for foosball, and the other games are hit or miss. But worth it for the foosball nonetheless!

title: I am big and wide :) and heavy too, and love these chairs!!!
text:
To begin with, I am 5’7” and 265lbs woman with majority of the weight distributed within my middle part, so most of the backpacking chairs are passing by without even looking my way. I wave “hi-by” to them all the time when I see them without any regret.
This one is great! It loved me from the moment we met :). Comfortable, durable, nice looking and omg!!! lightweight and compact when folded!!!
I don’t understand those, who complain that it’s hard to assemble or to pack it back together. C’mon y’all! Read my little guide, and I hope it will help you somewhat.
Take it out of the packing bag, just slightly wave it in your hand and everything jumps together making the frame almost ready to go! All the parts are connected with rubbery string inside the aluminum poles, so it makes it magically come together.
Than check each elbow to make sure that it sits well together, pressing slightly towards the corners.
Take fabric, unfold it with letters on the top, so you can read it. Put on one bottom corner first. Than pulling by the loop put on a second bottom corner. Than put one of the top corners next (right one for right-handed person and left one for left-handed person). The last corner will be a little harder to put on. To make it much quicker and easier, set the frame on the ground facing towards you. Put one foot on the horizontal lower part of the frame under the fabric to insure that frame will stay in place and won’t move when you don’t need it to move. While holding the frame firmly with your foot, pull the last loop upwards with your right hand while pulling the aluminum pole towards you and slightly pressing it down. You’ll see that this way it gets very easy and takes about 5-10 seconds to put the last corner on. I showed this to my 6th grader and he picked up the order of assembling quickly.
The process of packing it back it also very easy, once you pay attention to those little white drawings on the aluminum base. You take apart the poles and fold them. First do one upper side pole and hold it with your hand. While holding it, twist the base, so sides of it will come together. Now you’ll have all four sides of the base and one upper pole together in your hand. Hold it tightly and, using an other hand, keep pulling apart and folding an other pole adding it to your hand for holding. To fix shorter legs in place just pull them slightly towards the middle and press them
down with the longer ones. When everything put together, just wrap that velcro cord around and voila!!! This took me about a minute the most. My son did it himself without my help too. It took him about 5-7 minutes when he was doing it for the first time.
Put everything on one side of triple-folded fabric and roll. It will be tight enough and will easily fit inside that carrying bag leaving some space for the small universal anti-sinking sand mat (14.5”x14.5”) that you can get for about $14-15. Buy it!!! It will make whole lot of difference! Your chair will never sink into sand or any other soft surface! Believe me you won’t regret. It will add just about 2-4oz of extra weight, but it worth it. Should of being included with each chair already, but it’s the problem of every chair of this category.
Once again, I love this chair as well as my whole family. I went and ordered more of them.

title: Such a game changer! Now I love riding my bike again!
text:
It was a long time since I loved riding my bike because of the seats. I always felt like my 265lbs body was splitting a half and those halves were flopping on the sides of the seats. Yeah, not a pleasant feeling. I don’t know why I didn’t look for a bigger seat before… I had no idea they exist.
After doing some research and reading al the reviews and specifications, I picked this one and so happy I did. I feel whole again!!! I love riding my bike again! My 265lbs body feels like a human, like a part of society valued by others and not judged by appearance. We deserve same level of comfort as others and thanks to this seat we have it.
It hold well, without sinking or flipping to either side. You can adjust desired angle by loosing the same bolt you used for putting the seat on the bike. Also if you feel like you are about to roll to the side, you can adjust the bolts on the back of the seat. I restricted all the movement that way and my seat won’t lean to the side. Also I lowered the front of the seat to prevent it from pushing hard onto my pelvis. No more discomfort at all. I feel like I am riding in my cozy sofa chair now.

title: The title says it all
text: Yes, it’s comfortable, yes it’s durable, yes it’s easy to install universal seat. If you have a bigger bum like I do, it won’t be as comfortable as you want (dah, I am 265lbs lol), but it’s awesome for everyone else in my family, who are 80-200lbs people. Respect to the engineer who created this seat.

title: This is great for bigger person 2X-3X
text:
This is very comfortable and cozy with plenty room to toss and turn especially for side sleeper too. Zipper is very sturdy and easily accessible from top and bottom. As to 20, I can’t tell it will be comfortable as is, but if you will use sleeping bag lining and put on your thermals plus on a good sleeping pad, you will be perfectly fine with it.
It’s very roomy. I am 265lbs+ and 5’7” and still have enormous amount of room at the bottom of my feet (it’s much longer than me) and great amount of room on the sides. I am a side sleeper and like to keep my hands slightly banded in front of me with slightly bended knees, and it works well with this sleeping bag. It is evenly filled and filled well. Compression bag is made of much stronger material than sleeping bag itself. Overall I am very satisfied with my purchase.

title: Nice lightweight set for two for backpacking
text:
[[VIDEOID:50781721eea8a78b7591a6190c50d039]] This is a nice lightweight set for two people. Anodized titanium, gray colored like pretty much all titanium silverware that is not coated. If you are expecting silverfish shiny color, than it’s not for you. This one is not shiny silverwear. It’s simple, titanium, gray, not so smooth, but lighter and pretty strong silverwear. Great price for the set of two. You’ll expect to pay much more if you’ll get this from other places or sellers. It is not scratch resistant, you can see from the pictures. But you should not expect that because this should not be scratched anyway. If your food is scratching titanium, than it should not be consumed at all. Also because it is anodized, do not place it in your dishwasher. Harsh chemicals and hight temperature with tamper with anodized surface and you will have your silverware constantly covered with darkening substance due to quick oxidizing.
Overall I really like this set. Maybe they should use less plastic to keep it more environmentally friendly, otherwise five stars.

title: HOT!  And a more logical shape
text:
These get as hot on the low setting as my other handwarmer does on its high setting!
I've owned a few different styles of handwarmers, mostly the pill-shaped ones - which I love and use regularly, since I am always cold.
When I saw these, the cylinder shape seemed like it would be an improvement over the pill-shaped ones, and I was right! The pill-shaped ones fit in the palm of your hand - but it's my fingers that get the coldest. These cylinder shapes are more effective at warming the fingertips, and feel much more natural to hold. If you've only got one of the pill-shaped handwarmers and you're trying to warm up both hands with it, you walk around looking like you're praying or about to dive.
The only thing is - and I don't know how to say this without sounding tacky - but the way these are shaped and the curvature of the tip looks a little...well...like a certain kind of intimate toy.

The third time we used it, the bumps were there again. The fourth time, no bumps appeared.
To be honest this seemed like a weird flaw and it really concerned me. We contacted FB Sport and they said it didn't affect the performance of the board, not to worry. We were still within the return window, but we decided to keep the board instead of returning it and going directly to a landfill. I hope it lasts.

title: No nonsense, all around good gloves.
text:
Fairtex makes a great glove. One of the things that sets these apart from many other gloves is their shape. Many gloves have a sort if lightbulb shape to them, rounded around the knuckles. Fairtex gloves are more flat across the knuckles, giving an evenly distributed amount of padding across the hand.

Their padding is also dense. This has 2 advantages:

1. The gloves are more compact, so during sparring they can slip through guards a bit easier.

2. They have a very satisfying sound and feel while hitting mitts and bags compared to more squishy gloves on the market.

I have other gloves as well. I really like my Boon gloves. But overall, there’s really no need to use anything but Fairtex unless you’re going to be fighting with gloves specified by an organization and want to train in the same gloves you’ll fight in.

title: Amazing mouthguard, communication slipped.
text:
This is the best mouthguard I’ve ever used. I’ll get that out of the way now. It’s very comfortable, and very thick and protective as well. It is so well fit that it has a sort of suction effect on the teeth so it won’t fall out. Love it.

The reason for the 3 stars: The reputation the company has for communication throughout the process is one of the reasons I bought. I wasn’t sure if I should try this or spend twice the money with my dentist, and I almost went with my dentist for the fact that I’d have somebody helping me.

When I took my mold, I emailed the photos to Impact as they recommend and got a reply pretty quick. That’s great. But that was the end of the communication. They’ve said in their promotional materials that they send an email when your mold arrives, and that they advise when the mouthguard is on the way. I didn’t receive any of this. I actually became concerned that my order was lost in the mail on the way to Impact after a week and a half or so, so I had to email to ask if it arrived. The following day it was confirmed, and I was told the turnaround was about 2 weeks from receiving and that I would get an email when it went out. I didn’t get that email either. But after about 3 weeks from when I sent the mold, my mouthguard arrived and it’s awesome.

If I lose this one or need another, I’ll buy Impact again. This said, I hope they see my review and step their communication game back up. I may very well be just a rare anecdotal case, and the product is great, but I didn’t expect to find myself wondering if my mold had gotten lost in the mail.

title: Directions Are Poor, Assembly Issues
text:
[[VIDEOID:2661cc1b118c93e5491199f99fa676b5]] Just go to a Big Box store and get a pre-built bike…you’ll thank me!

Assembly is a nightmare. I did some of it myself, but the front brakes were not making contact with the tire, so I got the help of my husband so we could make adjustments (he has some experience with mechanics). After about 30 minutes of adjusting the brake apparatus with no significant improvement, he decided to move the washer for the front brakes to the inner side just to give it a little more braking power by alleviating the gap between the brake and the tire—it was the only thing that worked. I also noticed that the bell on this bike doesn’t have an actual lever that you swing to the side to make a real bell ding—this one has a plastic bit that you hit and you hope it dings and reverberates off the metal circle it’s attached to—it’s not the best bike bell we’ve had.

It does look like a cute bike when everything is assembled, but it doesn’t seem as well constructed compared to our little 12 inch Minnie Mouse bike from Huffy. Strangely enough, some of the protective wrapping for this RoyalBaby bike said Huffy on it, so I’m not sure if this is a division of the larger parent company perhaps? I feel bad giving this 2 stars, but I honestly don’t think it’s spectacular for the money (probably a 3-star bike), but the assembly issues knocked it down to 2 stars, along with the poor instructions. I’ll be sure to buy a pre-assembled bike when we need the next size up.

title: Great Choice for Families with Kids
text:

I make a lot of quick microwave Mac & Cheese in my house, and this is reminiscent of that in the sense that you rehydrate everything and serve—This method just takes a little while longer (7 minutes or so).

At $5.50 per serving, it’s a little up there in price, but the longevity, high quality and peace of mind make it a good buy.

title: Great for Breakfast or Lunch!
text:
Compared to fresh food, this is obviously not on par, but for a big can of nutrient-dense meals you can prepare easily in an emergency, this is a 5 star item.

I’m not much of a savory breakfast person, so if you had it on hand, I’d stick with a quick oatmeal for breakfast and enjoy this for lunch. The robust flavors help with satiety, especially with all of the protein (13 grams) and a good amount of fiber (6 grams). It’s also a great way to get a plethora of vitamins and minerals through food.

At $5.50 per serving, it’s a little up there in price, but the longevity, high quality and peace of mind make it a good buy.

title: Good When You Need A Meal
text:

title: Essential Item!
text: This is THE perfect emergency milk with easy prep. As a parent, I worry about not being able to keep things as normal as possible in an emergency. Milk is one of those essential things (maybe even more than food), that I feel keeps things “normal.” The amount of servings you get in here is fantastic (60, 8oz servings), and all of the nutrients make this a tasty vitamin-packed drink (In concept, it reminds of a grown-ups version of powdered baby formula), so I know we’re not missing out on good things to benefit our health. The overall cost looks a little pricey, but it’s actually only .75 cents a serving, and you cannot beat that for this amazing quality!!

title: Convenient & Tastes Pretty Good Overall
text:
It was a good learning experience trying this emergency food kit. Like with any preparedness item, it’s always smart to do a test run.

Everything is well organized in each individual 24-hour bag. I received 2 sets of 3 varying meal options. I sampled the Potato Chive, Chocolate Shake and Maple Oatmeal kit today. I love the canned water for easy opening and pouring for both drinking and food preparation.

-The powdered potatoes re-hydrated well and didn’t taste too bad. They are very palatable and the texture was fine.
-The oatmeal is VERY fragrant and tasted similar to a typical maple oatmeal packet from the grocery store. I liked it.
-The Protein shake tasted great, but it was problematic trying to get the powder to incorporate with the water. I tried both shaking and stirring, and I still couldn’t get the powder to mix very thoroughly. A blender bottle would be ideal, but obviously not feasible in an emergency.

These meal kits will certainly get you through a hard time, however, I feel the calorie count is a little low for the average person coming in around 1,000 calories for each kit. I think it would be great if another oatmeal packet was included or just something to help you hit about 1,200-1,300 calories for more satiety, especially in a time of need. This kit is still a great nutritional boost and highly valuable when you need it most.

title: Essential Item, Funny Taste
text:
This emergency box of water pouches is such a great preparedness item to have. The individual pouches are convenient for portioning out daily amounts per person, for handing out to other family/neighbors, and also for transporting on-the-go. The 5-year expiration date is much better than bottled water, so the longevity is a great feature. My kit arrived fresh with 4 1/2 more years of shelf life.

The not-so-great, is the fact that this water does have an odd taste. Sort of a plastic flavor. It’s not a refreshing glass of water by any means, but it's absolutely something I’d drink in an emergency (it can be consumed directly from the pouch). I will probably put some drink flavor packets in this kit to offer some flavor variety and mask some of the funny taste. This is still a 5-star product for me, as clean water in an emergency is an essential item and the pouches are very convenient.

This software is close to the Spark People and My Fitness Pal apps without having to sync programs and be frustrated by companion apps. Overall a very useful product for me without the added bells and whistles I didn't need. I am getting everything I need out of this devise and I love the reminders to get moving. 3. No straw to deal with - I never feel like I get those silicone straws completely clean. There's always some hidden area I can't get to to clean and they end up gathering muck back there. That, and they always end up leaking!

But the truth is, running with them is like running with a slow strobe light: each time you plant a foot down and its light illuminates the ground in front of you on one side, the other foot swings back and it goes dark on that side.  They also point mostly towards the ground, not illuminating more than a few feet in front of me which makes for an uncomfortable running posture looking straight down.  I continue to use them, but also wear my headlamp for additional illumination further ahead (I had hoped these would replace the headlamp but no luck).  I like the idea of the red rear-facing light but haven't had a chance to find out if it is visible - if so, that's a great feature.
