text:
Wow, this is a BRIGHT flood headlamp / flashlight for the money, and very versatile. This surpasses several of my more-expensive headlamps in most categories, while only costing me $20 USD. I was expecting a decent light for the money, and - instead - wound up getting a light to replace both my primary headlamp and flashlight in my main toolbox.

Firstly, this baby really throws some nice light. Whatever LED its running has a nice clean white light that leans on the blue end of the spectrum, but still a little more warm than many LEDs I have (looks like somewhere around 5000K ~ 5500K color temp - just a tad more blue than sunlight). There's a refractive diffuser in front of the bulb that throws an extremely even flood light that fills most of my field of vision. This is excellent for work applications as well as navigating at night. At its High and Turbo setting, despite being more of a flood light, you can still see 50 ~ 100 yards depending on weather conditions. It has a well-defined cone of light, there's no tertiary light spilling onto you as long as it's aimed mostly-up (i.e., no glowing eyelashes blinding you).

It has several brightness levels. When you first click it on (just tap the power button) it defaults to High brightness. This very bright, and acceptable for surveying & navigating a work sight in pitch darkness. Click the power button again, and it dips to Medium brightness. This is my setting for navigating in the dark at jogging to fast-walking speed - I can still clearly see many yards in front of me, obstacles to the side, but I'm not blinding myself or anyone else as long as I keep my head aimed slightly down. A third click goes to Low brightness. This is my ideal setting for illuminating something I'm working on with my hands, or for strolling in the dark - I can still clearly see several feet in front of me, but I'm not blowing my night vision or blinding anyone else.

If you double click the button from any mode, including off, it'll activate the strobe. It's your common strobe setting that almost every other tactical light has, at its high brightness setting. It'll definitely get peoples' attention, or disorient someone looking at it. I don't generally use this setting, but it's nice to have in case of emergency. What I like most is that you can only activate it with a double-click - it doesn't activate while scrolling through the brightness settings, which I dislike in my other lights. As long as I don't double-click the button, the strobe doesn't turn on.

Now, let's talk about the TURBO brightness. They aren't joking - this light genuinely does approach 1000 lumen output in Turbo mode. I've compare it to the 900 lumen halogen bulb in my SUV's regular headlight, and this flashlight is definitely brighter at the center when illuminating a wall 15 yard away. You can't run this for very long, as it heats the body of the light quickly. Surely it's also quickly depleting your batteries, though I suspect it'll overheat well before it runs empty in Turbo mode. Turbo is good for a few minutes at a time when you need to survey a large area, see out past 75 ~ 100 yards (I can just make out objects to 125 yards in pitch black - really impressive for a flood light).

The build quality of the light itself is superb for the money. Frankly, I've spent WAY more for poorer quality lights. The light is ruggedly built, the switch has a nice satisfying clicky feel, the refractive diffuser works great for flood light, the cap screws / unscrews smoothly, there is no rattling with either battery options (it has a rechargeable 18650 cell installed by default, and comes with 2 backup CR 123A cells), and the metal body dissipates heat fine for all settings except Turbo (at most, you should probably only run Turbo for about 3 ~ 5 minutes before letting it cool). It has a small spring clip on it, as this can also double as an angled-neck pocket light when removed from the headband, which is a great feature. IMO, this is the best flashlight I've ever bought for $20.

Here's where they cut corners - the head strap and the mount. In fairness, it's still a better strap and mounting system than several other lights I own under $45. It's still the second best strap and mount I own, for a set that cost $20 or less. The strap is an adjustable elastic band that's modestly thick, and manages to fit my bigger-than-average head circumference at it's biggest setting. With retaining adapters, this would fit an adult hard hat, though it would probably over-stretch the elastic quickly - for normal sized heads, this will fit fine. It's comfortable enough with the plastic mounting clip, which has waterproof foam on the back (it doesn't make contact with the head, sitting over the strap). It's a simple design, but works well enough. The light mounts on and off with two retaining clips that hold it firmly. There's a small catch that sticks out of the mount, which engages the ribbing of the flashlight and keeps a firm angle. You can adjust the pitch of the light, though it's a little stubborn (it's easier to adjust when it's off your forehead). The elastic band and mount aren't as good as you'd get with more expensive sets; but it's still fine for this application, and definitely good quality for the price.

The charging cable is also kinda cheap, but it works fine. I replaced it after a week with a better quality $10 charging cable. I also swapped out the included no-name 2600 mAh rechargeable 18650 cell with a brand-name 3400 mAh rechargeable cell I had spares of, extending its run time from 3.9 hours (my first test) to at least 5.5 hours (I haven't let it run empty yet) - nice! It runs fine on CR 123A cells too, which I keep spares of in my emergency kits.

This Energizer hybrid LED headlamp / pocket work light is a hard-hitting underdog. IMO, this is one of the entry-level lights - easily outperforming the literal dozens (by my last count, around 60) of budget lights in my collection. I simply don't have a better light than this that cost less than $20, and it even puts several of my $30 ~ $60 lights to shame. I recommend it as a nice beater headlamp / pocket work light combo. At $20, I don't feel bad leaving one in every one of my kits. You can get better, but I don't think you can get much better for around $20.

title: Excellent Reflective Properties - Very Good Build Quality - Extremely Useful
text: Wow, these babies reflect a LOT of light!  I have these on my dog-walking kit, and in my emergency kits.  I've tested them out, and they are among the most-visible of all my reflective gear, at night.  They're extra-long, so they can be comfortably worn around arms, legs, and even attached to belts and straps.  I've attached them to tools and equipment, as well, to help them stand out better.  They even fit around the trunk of smaller trees, if you needed a makeshift trail marker.  At dusk, they reflect so much light, that you can be seen from hundreds of feet away by anyone with a flashlight or by passing cars.  The fabric-flocked back side is reasonably comfortable, even on hot days.  They seem to be very ruggedly built, and have managed to survive being attached to the back of my dog's harness on several occasions.  I'm really pleased at the quality and performance of the Cosmos reflective pop-bracelets, and will definitely add more to my kits.

title: Excellent Value-Priced Lantern
text:
Given the price, I was expecting a smaller and flimsier lantern, but this turned out to be a fairly robust LED lantern. Powered by only 3 AA batteries, and featuring an array of bluish-white LED emitters set in reflectors, the light output is surprisingly good. It floods the area with very usable light, easily capable of filling a small room or a 10' radius outside in the open. This is about the right amount of light I would want when walking through the woods, changing a tire, or cooking at a campground. You can clearly see what you are doing, can see/read details, but won't be blinded. You can lower the light output by lowering the array into the body, but it doesn't turn off the LEDs so you will still discharge the batteries as quickly.

The overall quality is very good, and I consider it a great light for the price. This product was provided at a discounted price in exchange for my honest review, and I'm considering the value based on the regular price. Unlike a few other lanterns in the price range, there is no audible hum when turned on. The light output is comparable to other lights in it's price range, and even a few other higher-priced lanterns, though won't match the high-end lanterns. While the build quality is good, it's also not nearly as rugged as some of the more-expensive lanterns out there. This lantern seems like it would resist a light splash or sprinkle of water, here and there, but would not likely hold up to driving rain or a dunk. Still, for the money, it's a good casual use light for quick backyard usage, and the occasional utility usage.

title: Good Build Quality - Good Light Output
text: I think the build quality is very good, for the price - comparable to the Duracell ones I tried at the store.  The light output is very good, and the modes seem to work well (though I don't use the other modes).  I tested the whistle feature in the woods, and it works well (though not as good as smaller metal whistles).  It held up in a light rain, and the o-rings look like they'd hold up to a quick dunking in water.  For the money, this seems like a quality lightstick.

title: Good Quality - Good Value!
text: A very nice coated hex dumbbell at a good price - I'm very pleased with these!

title: Absorbant 12ga Mop - Good Quality For The Price
text: Quality 12ga cleaning mop.  It really soaks up both solvents and oils, for various cleaning applications.  I have several of these, and they all last longer than the less-expensive Bushnell mops I used to use (they would leave threads behind that I had to pick out).

title: Great Stuff!
text: Top-notch stuff.  Very strong, with a fine finish on the sheath.

title: Great Water Container For Travel & Everyday Use
text: I love how this water container easily conforms to the limited space in my day pack.  It is surprisingly rugged, and is very easy to clean.  I've since added more of these flexible Vapur water containers to my collection.

title: Great Box For Projects!
text: I gave this box as a gift, to a very crafty individual, who could put the many compartments to good use.  All of the trays and individual compartments are secure, and the box is very rugged.  I will likely get a box like this for myself, as well as for other friends of mine who could use a great project box.

title: Good Quality Mylar Blankets
text: Reasonably good quality - very thick material for the price.  They feel just as good as the blankets I'm issued for my CERT kits.  The measurements were a little off...  Mine were 90" x 58", so I actually got a few more square inches - nice!  I tested a few of these, and they work as expected.  I use these to line chilled packages, and they're very easy to cut.  I've also experimented adding strategically-placed strips of this material inside the lining of some of my windbreakers, and I've felt a modest boost in warmth retained.  At such a value-price, these are great for such projects, and you'll still have a few left over to stash in emergency kits or car trunks.

title: Fairly-Accurate No-Frills Baseplate Compass
text:
I pretty much wanted a cheap baseplate compass that was reasonably accurate, which I could tuck into some of my sports bags and emergency caches - and I was NOT disappointed! This isn't going to replace my primary Brunton and Suunto compasses, which I pack in my daily kits, but they're good tier 2 backups (backups for my backups) and giveaway compasses. Of the half-dozen I bought, all of them were as accurate as my Suunto A-10 backups. All of mine were liquid-filled, with no air bubbles.

Really, the only negative thing I can say about them, is that the compass is wobbly on the baseplate, and the lanyard hole was really small. I needed to ream the lanyard hole, and add a grommet, to use 95 cord (replacing the flimsy string that came with). But that's a really minor gripe. At less than $3 a pop, I don't mind if they get lost, stolen, and I can hand them to people without worrying about them.

title: Excellent Backup Water Purification Product
text: I've owned quite a few of these, and have tested a few in the past.  They've always met or exceeded the set results for our water purity tests, from questionable water sources in the field.  However, I've never actually had to personally use one until just recently.  I'm pleased to report that it worked as expected, and I'm still among the living.  Despite the value price, the LifeStraw is among the better personal water filters on the market today, and is a great last line of defense against waterborne illness (when other means of purification are unavailable).

title: Nice Mini Containers For My Use
text: Very good quality.  The small jar that fits inside the aluminum container is just big enough to hold low-dose aspirin.  Larger pills can be put in the container, but without the plastic jar (advisable only for emergencies, so as to prevent deterioration or contamination of the pills).  The aluminum container seals up watertight, without any difficulty.  The tiny ring that comes with is decent, but I suggest replacing it with a nicer split ring if you intent to hang it on anything that gets regular usage.

title: Pretty Good Compass For The Money
text: This is a fairly competently made replica of the classing marching compass I used to own (I hope whoever stole it appreciates it).  It's very solidly built, using quality materials.  Compared to my digital and various calibrated compasses, this is actually quite accurate.  For the money, it's a very nice compass.  The case is lousy, but I don't intend on using the case that came with.  Overall, I'm quite pleased with this purchase.

title: Decent Little Clip-On Compass For The Price
text: Considering the price, I had modest expectations for the quality of this compass clip.  I hoped it would vaguely point north, for really quickly getting a heading after getting off a bus or train.  I didn't need anything too accurate.  This one is a little more accurate than I anticipated.  It quickly finds north, within a few degrees, and is surprisingly rugged for such a lightweight design.  If you depend on a compass for orienteering, get a nicer Suunto compass.  This is better suited for quick checks, or as a backup for your backup.  For that purpose, it's a pretty good deal.

title: Great Optics For The Money
text: I wanted a decent scope for a .223 Saiga, which surprised me by its accuracy...  Nothing too expensive, but nothing that was going to break in a few weeks or not hold zero.  I was quite pleased with my Bushnell Powerview 8x21 compact binoculars, and read many good reviews about the Bushnell Banner series of scope.  I bought this with reasonable expectations, and the Bushnell Banner 4-16x40mm Illuminated CF 500 Reticle Rifle Scope blew my expectations away.  I have a Nikon 4-16x50mm Monarch on my Remington, and I was impressed at how similarly the Bushnell performed.  It feels like a rock-solid build, all moving parts feel as smooth as glass on glass, the tube was perfect for my mounting hardware, and the optics...  Honestly, I think the Bushnell's optics are just as good, if not a little better.  The Banner CF 500 has a smaller objective lens than the Nikon Monarch, yet they're the same brightness in all of my indoor and outdoor tests.  The clarity is the same, and the reticle is brighter.  The only thing the Nikon excels at, is a broader eye relief (though the Bushnell still has a fair range at the lower magnifications) and the controls are just a tad more precise (I have to fine tune the Bushnell a few seconds more - though maybe it's just because it's still new to me).  For the money, I think this Bushnell Banner 4-16x40mm scope is a great buy.  For my purposes, I don't feel it lacks at all.

title: Great Glasses - Super Adjustable
text: For years, I've shot wearing [[ASIN:B000F7PPFS Remington T-71]] and [[ASIN:B002FC23GU Remington T-72]] glasses.  They're fine, for the price, but I felt like trying the Radians after seeing the good reviews.  They're great glasses for shooting, and the adjustability is incredible for the affordable price.  Since I can tailor the angle of the arms, there's less of a gap between my face and the lenses - something I need when shooting black powder guns.  I still like my Remington glasses, but I'll be slowly replacing them with Radians as they start wearing down.  I'm quite impressed at what fine adjustable shooting glasses the Radians are.

title: Strong & Long-Lasting Phosphorescent Glow - Convenient Size & Shape
text:
I recently bought several UVPaqlite items, and have had some time to test them out. Out of the 4 items I purchased; this was the second brightest, and was the most useful size. With fair exposure to light, it will glow strong for 10 minutes. Around the 15 minute mark, it has faded a bit, but is still bright enough that you can still read with it in total darkness, with adjusted eyes. By 45 minutes, it's faintly visible in a dark room, with your eyes adjusted. By 60 and 90 minutes, the Paqlite Mini was still faintly visible, but only just barely.

It glowed brighter and longer than either the [[ASIN:B0068QL4E6 Tooblite]] and [[ASIN:B0068QN7VO Tooblite Mini]]. While the Tooblite designs are convenient for many tasks, the UVPaqlite Mini is the lightest of the bunch, and quite compact. While it doesn't seem quite as durable as the two Tooblites, the rugged vacuum-sealed packet still feels like it would hold up well to a fair amount of abuse. It also floats, slightly, compared to the Tooblites that sink like rocks. As such, I think this is the most useful of the UVPaqlite products, for my needs. I have mine in my bedroom, next to a flashlight, attached to a quick-access gun safe. In the event I'm in my room, and the lights instantly go out, I can immediately see where my flashlight is - even before my eyes have adjusted to the dark (though I also have emergency lighting for additional assistance). In a pinch, the UVPaqlite Mini is strong enough that I could find my backup flashlight, or open my safe.

Of the 4 UVPaqlite products I purchased, I'd say that this is my personal favorite. I think the combination of convenient size and brightness make it the most versatile for my needs. I intend to get more of these, and use them to tag several other handy items I'd want to be able to immediately find, in the event of a power outage. As well, they're light enough and small enough, I can easily pin them to my clothing, whenever I go outside at night and wish to remain visible. They also glow like crazy, under a UV black light, which would make them fun at parties.

With these "charge and glow" phosphorescent products, they certainly have their uses - however, they can't replace a flashlight or chemiluminescent glow stick when you need on-demand light. So, consider what you might use them for, before purchasing.

title: Strong & Long-Lasting Phosphorescent Glow
text:
I recently bought several UVPaqlite items, and have had some time to test them out. Out of the 4 items I purchased, this was reasonably impressive. With fair exposure to light, it will glow strong for 10 minutes. Around the 15 minute mark, it has faded a bit, but is still bright enough that you can still read with it in total darkness, with adjusted eyes. By 60 minutes, it's faintly visible in a dark room, with your eyes adjusted. Even by 90 minutes, it's still faintly visible, but only just barely.

Out of the 4 UVPaqlite items I purchased, this didn't glow as strong or last as long as the UVPaqlite packets - however, that seemed natural, given its tubular design (less surface area exposed to the viewer). The clear resin had a lot of bubbles, which seemed to diffuse the glow a bit - making for a more even light, but also limiting its range. However, the tubular design is also its biggest strength. Compared to the UVPaqlite packets - which are fairly rugged in their own right - this seems much more durable, as well as convenient to carry or mount. As such, I mounted this next to my quick-release home shotgun mount. In the event the lights immediately go out, I can quickly - even before my eyes have adjusted - find my flashlight and unlock the shotgun, should I need it.

If you need stronger and longer lasting light, I recommend the UVPaqlite vacuum-sealed packets. Both the [[ASIN:B00698NBYE UVPaqlite Medium]] and [[ASIN:B00698HB1I UVPaqlite Mini]] out-performed the Tooblites I bought, as far as effective brightness. However, consider that the Tooblite shape is more convenient for certain tasks. As well, while these "charge and glow" phosphorescent products have their purposes, they can't replace a flashlight or chemiluminescence glow stick when you need on-demand light. So, consider what you might use them for, before purchasing.

title: Classic Hexamine Fuel Tab & Stove Combo
text: For many years, I've used Esbit / hexamine fuel tabs with a similar folding stove.  It's not my primary heat source, but rather I use it for times I need a little quick fire, or to get larger fires started.  One tab is enough to get 2 cups of water boiling, in most weather conditions.  The stove works fairly well with most mess kit items.  But, I more regularly use parts of a tab as tinder to get larger sticks going, so I build a bigger fire.  I can cook larger things on the large fire, and then I'll move some coals to the folding stove to heat up smaller items, or put hot rocks into it for portable heat.  The stove isn't all that rugged, but it holds up better than my improvised soda can stoves, and packs up very nicely (you can fit 4 tabs in the stove when it's folded).  I've also used trioxane, but the Esbit / hexamine tabs burn cleaner and hotter for longer, and are easier to find deals on.  For casual trips, where I don't need a big fire, don't carry any kind of gas fuel, sticks may not be plentiful, or I just need to heat up some coffee or a freeze dried meal - the combination of this stove, one hexamine tab and a steel cup works perfectly for me.  At such a low price, I won't feel guilty using up the tabs, or if the stove gets a little beat up.

title: Have Used For Years - Very Good For Fire Starting
text: I have used WetFire tinder for many years as a means to start a fire in the woods, or at home.  It's easy to shave a little bit amongst other tinder, and get more material going.  With any kind of spark or ember, I can get a flame more consistently with WetFire shavings than from any other commonly carried tinder (charred cloth, cotton balls with Vaseline in candle wax, birch bark, magnesium shavings, tinder fungus or dryer lint).  I can often get a flame from a single strike of a flint.  There have been a few exceptions, but never more than three strikes.  The variance seems to be from tab to tab.  I'll have one tab, from which shavings always light on the first strike.  I'll have another tab, from which shavings always take two or three strikes.  I'll get these inconsistencies from new batches, and old batches.  Age doesn't seem to be the issue, as I've had the same variances from brand new packs and 2-year old packs.  Out of a pack of eight tabs, there's always one - rarely two - that doesn't catch alight as fast as the others.  Still, that's far more dependable than other tinder types.  That said, I never go without AT LEAST TWO - often three - different types of tinder (in an emergency "one is zero, two is one, three is two, etc.").  I've been quite pleased with WetFire tinder for many years, and I'll continue to use it as my first tinder source - but I'll always have a backup.

title: This Has Become The Standard Water Bottle For Me
text: I've used all manner of bottles and containers for my outdoor activities, and they all were decent - unremarkable.  I had a low standard for plastic water bottles, and was content if I got three uses out of them before they fell apart or started leaking.  Ever since my first Nalgene bottle, I haven't looked back.  Special-purposes aside, the Nalegene Tritan Wide Mouth bottles have become THE STANDARD bottle for all of my use.  They of a significantly higher quality than previous bottles and canteens I've owned, and I appreciate the absence of Bisphenol-A.  They've survived ten times the abuse of bottles I've paid twice as much for.  The wide mouth has become essential, since I space became a premium for me while doing ultralite backpacking.  As well, the wide mouth makes it easier to use with my SteriPen and filters, and allows me to use it as a container when foraging for small edibles.  Partially filled with water, with an LED flashlight placed over it, the brighter-colored bottles make nice lanterns or signals at the campsite.  There's such a wide variety of colors available, to match most folks' styles - I'm partial to blues, gray, and black.  I'm quite pleased with their overall quality and versatility, and I only carry Nalgene bottles from now on.

title: Very Nice 1911 Spring-Action Airsoft Pistol
text: This is a very nice value-priced 1911 airsoft pistol.  Despite the low cost, if has a very high quality feel.  It's very well detailed, has nice heft, everything moves well, the magazine fits perfectly and doesn't rattle, and it's reasonably accurate.  I enjoy that it can be taken down, similar to real 1911s.  I use this as a nice surrogate for my Rock Island Armory 1911, for test-drawing and maneuvers.  I'm quite pleased with this airsoft 1911, for my purposes.

title: This Is The Perfect Holster For Me
text: I regularly carry around a narrow-diameter 2xAA LED flashlight (the [[ASIN:B003GXF9OA Streamlight 88033 Protac Tactical Flashlight]] or [[ASIN:B0041NE8TG Fenix E21 Flashlight]]), of which I have several of the same models.  I like to keep it on me, and the Nite Ize LHS-03 holster works much better than the stationary one that came with.  I particularly like the pivoting clip, which allows me hands-free use in numerous directions.  My last one survived 3 years of daily abuse, with only minor wear around the edges, before I had to replace it.  Since it's open back, it's easy to activate the tail-cap switch on my light.  Since my light has a uniform diameter, I can easily remove and replace my light, and it stays secure whenever I'm running around.  It's not ideal for every shape light, but it has worked well for my Streamlight, Fenix, Mini-Mag, two of my small Eveready C-cell lights (it's a snug fit, but works), and several cheap-o AA & CR123A Cree lights from Hong Kong - really, any flashlight with a long narrow body (between 0.75" ~ 1.5" diameter).  I'm very glad to have this Nite Ize flashlight holster!

title: Not Bad - One Of The Tastier Emergency Food Bars
text: These are one of the tastier emergency food bars I've had.  They are packed up very nicely, can survive a lot of abuse, but are possible to open without a knife.  I think I'll stock up on some of these, along with a few other brands.  They're a pretty decent value, for my uses.

title: Great Item For Camping & Emergencies
text: For many years, I carried around those Mylar 'space blankets' whenever I went camping, kept them in my car, packed them in my emergency kits, and used them under my clothes to keep toasty warm in the winter.  They were inexpensive, lightweight, but always felt a little small and too flimsy for more than two or three uses.  As such, I always wished someone made nicer heat-reflecting blankets, still at an affordable price - and Adventure Medical Kits delivers.  Each blanket is large enough to make a decent shelter, beef up a tent or makeshift shelter, or for two people to wrap themselves in.  They aren't as crinkly or loud as the older space blankets, which is also nice.  They come packed in very compact, taking up only a little more room and weight than the older smaller space blankets.  They unfold easily, with various instructions printed right on the blanket.  While it seems impossible to fold it up as compact as they come from the factory, they do still fold up pretty nice (I roll it up, and then flatten it out).  I have one blanket I've used dozens of times, and it's only just starting to show some wear here and there.  For the price, I definitely got my money's worth, many times over.  I recommend everyone have one or more in their car or home, in case of emergency.  For anyone involved in outdoor sports, these are phenomenal.  It's another great product from Adventure Medical Kits!

title: Good Waterproof Matches
text: These are very good waterproof matches - as good as any other set I've ever used.  Bear in mind, however, they aren't magical.  It's still difficult to keep anything alight in a driving rain or heavy winds.  And, yes, they will not light if the striking surface is ruined, if struck under water, or in the vacuum of space.  For waterproof matches, they are very good.  As a fire starter, matches - in general - are adequate.  These should be kept in a nicer sealed matchbox with a protected striking surface (Coghlans makes a nice one that also includes a whistle and signal mirror), and you should have AT LEAST one other backup fire source that might mitigate the shortfalls of matches, if designated for a situation where fire starting is critical.  I never have less than three, when I go off-trail - usually waterproof matches, a [[ASIN:B0013L8D9K Swedish Firesteel]], usually a lighter or two, and sometimes a fire piston along with some good emergency tinder.  I wouldn't feel right with just one of any of these firestarters.

title: Good Eye Protection For The Price
text: Despite it's value price, they fit very well, have a very clear picture, feel fairly rugged, and don't fog up too terribly even on a hot humid July afternoon.  They fit well, and work fine with my Howard Leight and Caldwell earmuffs (though I also pair up with earplugs).  They offer good coverage, with very little space for debris to get in.  They're a backup to a slightly nicer UV-protective set of glasses, but I would feel OK having them as my primary eye protection.

title: Nice Sturdy Sling With A Little Bounce To It
text: I just wanted a simple sling for my Sporter Saiga .223, but I couldn't pass up on the low price for this sling.  I'm glad I got it, though.  With a little effort, I was able to get the metal rings on the sling (they're quite snug, but a little bees wax made it easier).  The sling is very sold, the neoprene section is very comfortable, the non-slip dimples are great for keeping it on your shoulder, and the little bounce that the neoprene give it is actually really nice.  I was worried they might quickly lose elasticity, but from the quality feel of the material it should last a long time.  For the price, even if it didn't last that long, I'm still quite pleased with it.  After reading other reviews for Butler Creek Stretch Slings, though, I'm sure it'll be good for years and years.  The Mossy Oak Break-Up (MOBU) pattern is a nice accent.  I'm very pleased I picked up this sling.

title: Excellent Orinteering Baseplate Compass For The Price
text: I've trekked many miles, guided by the same Brunton 7DNL baseplate compass I received from my wilderness survival camp counselor, decades ago.  There are a few scuffs, and the edges aren't pristine, and yet it still works fine.  It's just as accurate as several $20 ~ $80 compasses my peers carry, and has survived a fair amount of abuse.  While it's not as rugged as some other models, for the price you can buy 2 or 3 of them so you have spares.  As well, you won't feel as guilty should one disappear, or be damaged.  Its compact size makes it handy, but also makes it a little harder to get precise bearings.  It also doesn't have true declination adjustment, only an etched-in scale, which can lead to some issues if you forget this nuance.  For casual trips, I'm quite comfortable with relying on the Brunton 7DNL.  For anything more critical, it's my backup compass (to a more-expensive [[ASIN:B000FEWA6S Suunto M-3DL Compass]], which I tend to baby).

title: Runs small IMO
text:
Either I’m fat or this is runs small.
Honestly, it’s probably a bit of both.
I sized up, and I still couldn’t get it to even come close to touching the two panels together.
There was zero hope for zipping it.

Normally I wear an XS, so I ordered a Small in this. Usually things end up being too big on me, so I was surprised I couldn’t zip it.

I may have gotten a defective one (probably not lol), or the size label attached was wrong (maybe). But most likely, I think this suit runs small.

5/10 would maybe purchase again, in a larger size.

title: Good, leaks a bit, well insulated
text:
My daughters love these cups!
My oldest (4), has a sensory processing issues and her occupational therapist recommended these.

A few cons:
1. They leak when left sideways. Sometimes it leaks even if the straw is closed (pressure issues, I assume).
2. The silicone part is hard to clean (I use a little scrub brush, but it still won’t get every nook and cranny).
3. My kids love to chew on the silicone piece and we have to replace it very often.

title: NOT SPRING ASSISTED /  NOT 4 INCH BLADE /  BUT STILL RECOMMENDED
text:
Nice knife, especially at this price point. BUT, there are some issues. To me it appeared that this this knife is inferred as being spring assisted. It is most definitely not spring assisted as all other knives are determined to be. The thumb hole is difficult for me to use in one smooth motion. I thought that surely the flipper would be spring assisted, but no. It takes it to half open and no more. You need to use a wrist flip or two hands to finish the opening. That would not be much of a problem, but that makes it illegal to carry here in central Ohio. Sad.

One last thing. This blade is nowhere near 4 inches. It is measured at 3.5 inches. How does Kubey justify these irregularities? Perhaps this is just something being lost in translation.

This knife is super sharp. Locks up like a vault. No wobbles anywhere. It handles well. And it is beautiful. It is definitely worth the money as long as you know up front what you are buying. The build quality is there. The cosmetics are there. It doesn't need this type of advertising to sell. Thus the four stars. I would buy again and I will probably buy from Kubey again.

title: Nice Knife
text: This is in the made in China series of Kershaw knives. The fit and finish, quality of build, and blade sharpness are perfect. The blade is perfectly centered for those of us who care about such things. The jigged bone scales are really nice with no gaps. This knife is the perfect size for EDC. It is large enough to be useful for everyday cutting needs but small enough not be threatening to folks who don't carry knives. If you want a Rambo style combat knife you will need to look elsewhere. That is not to say that it can't be used for self defense, but the Black Gulch and the Wildcat Ridge should be more effective for the zombie attacks. I own them both and they are great knives, too.

title: Big And Beautiful
text:
I bought this knife from another web site. The price was similar and it was a great deal. My first impression was "Wow! What a big knife"! My second impression was of the high quality that went into building this knife. Fit and finish are perfect. It was shaving sharp from the box. The brown leather sheath is of high quality and flawless.

In my city we are limited to knives with blades no longer than the width of our hands. This one squeaks by for me. I also have the Grant County, Black Gulch, Corral Creek all in clip point with jigged bone and the Corral Creek with the sheep's foot blade and ABS scales. Sure, they were all made in China and don't contain some highly exotic steel, but they work in the real world. And that's what matters to me.

I got a bad Black Gulch from a seller on Amazon and I am certain that it was a second because there were no info pamphlets and the knife was not in the usual plastic sleeve and it was dull as a brick. I gave it to a friend who is better at knife sharpening than I am. The Black Gulch that I got from 5 Starr was perfect. For me it just doesn't get much better than Kershaw and 5 Starr.

So, this is a large and beautiful knife for special occasions. No, I don't need knives as large as the Wildcat Ridge or Black Gulch for EDC, but if situation calls for it they are available. It is nice to know that I can carry a large knife without the Rambo tactical attitude that seems to be so popular now. It's a great knife at a great price.

title: Puzzling QC
text:
I love my Kershaw Grant County so I ordered this larger version. Fit and finish are beautiful. For those of us who care about such things the blade is perfectly centered. Unlike my Grant County however this knife was dull in the box. Not only that but I can't quite get it to take a shaving sharp edge. It appears that my Opinel will not be retired from its place in my pocket along with my Grant County in my fifth pocket. I'm still trying to sharpen my 3120JB though.

Updated 5-10-2013. I just received a second 3120JB, this time from Five Starr Knives. This one is shaving sharp out of the package and includes a leather sheath. The fit and finish are beautiful and the sheath is good quality. This is the third order that I have had with Five Starr and they will get all of my business from now on.

Updated 5-27-2013. With no work this knife has developed a mall gap between one of the jigged bone scales and the frame. The scale flexes. It won't fall off or anything. It just looks bad. I don't know why I have such problems with the Black Gulch. The other knives in this series are doing great. I guess they have me spoiled. My Black Gulch is now in the center glove box of my truck. The Grant County, both Corral Creeks, and the Wildcat Ridge are my EDC knives. I don't think that I will try a third Black Gulch.

title: A Wonderful Knife
text:
This is just the right size for my medium size hands and disappears in my pocket. Fit and finish are great. There are no flaws in the Opinel blade locking ring, or handle. When properly locked open there is no play in the blade in any direction. Opening and closing the unlocked blade require a little effort which is the way that I like it. The wood handle is varnished. The locking ring is stiff and requires quite a bit more than my 12 year old Opinel. This is reported to ease up after using it for a while and I don't find it to be objectionable. Shaving sharpness is there too. This knife totally meets my expectations and requirements.
The dimensions of this knife are:

4-1/4" closed
3-1/4" Blade
7-1/2 Total Length open

The best attributes of this knife are the curved handle and the carbon blade. The standard Opinel handle is one of only two ways to get an Opinel with a carbon steel blade. It has a straight body with a larger bump on the end. The handle of this Coghlan's version looks to be the same handle that comes in the Opinel Garden Knife #8. It is the curved design with the size and heft of the standard Opinel. This Coghlan's version is perfect size and model for me. This knife comes in three sizes, "7, #8, and #9. The #8 fits my hand perfectly.

The carbon blade requires special care. To avoid tarnishing and rusting keep a very thin coat of oil on the blade and avoid acid such as are found in fruits. If you want this knife in stainless steel with a drop point blade shape rather than the standard clip point check out the Opinel Garden Knife #8.

title: The Sharpest Knife I Have Ever Held

I went to shave some hairs from my arm and shaved a super thin layer of skin instead. No pain at all. This must be what folks call scary sharp. It cuts phone book paper with ease. I'm impressed. title: Perishables?  Well, Maybe...
text:
So far, I am underwhelmed. I purchased this in advance of a cross-country trip and an extended stay in a budget hotel that doesn't have a room fridge - hence the choice of dual power source. Being the prudent sort, I plugged it in at home to see whether it really would cool down to 40 degrees. House was 75 degrees, cooler after running all night was 55 degrees, at best. I'll probably keep it, and maybe as a beer or cola cooler it's fine, but as for being able to keep perishables such as eggs, milk, lunch meat and cheese in the hotel, or in transit for 1000 miles, for that matter, I'm not sure it's worth the risk of food poisoning to rely on its cooling capability. It's also smaller inside than I was expecting.

Update: On a second, and much longer, trip, I took this along, mostly for refrigeration in transit, but then when I reached my destination, I found that the full-size fridge was on the blink, so I plugged this in and it kept stuff reasonably cold, including the return trip, although still not much lower than 40-degrees. All told, some of the stuff I carried with me was still good when I got back home eleven days later, and maybe some of that was due to having also packed big bottles of frozen drinking water (ice) and starting out with other frozen foods; maybe some of it was due to my travel being in weather that was at freezing or below and the cooler rode for part of the trip in an unheated truck boot. All that being said, I still wouldn't be totally reliant on it in the summer, and would still pack the bottled ice - which is also a good way to gauge just how well the cooler is doing its job.

**UPDATE** Instruction say to use washer on rear, 2-part, screw, but there is no supplied washer. After a couple of emails to Lyman products (manufacturer), they say that the addition of the washer isn't necessary, but the instructions just haven't changed.**

title: Solid kit for the price and functions available.
text:
I had the micro kit and now I have the pocket kit and this Stage 2 tin. I liked their experimental micro kit years ago and this one builds up from that one and the pocket kit into this well rounded batch of decent quality items that should last a couple of years.
Recommended? For the price and function? Yes.

title: The best of this type on the market.
text:
I had an experimental kit by Vigilant Trails a few years ago and was impressed by the weight, ease of carry, and functionality. This kit is a slight improvement and will get you through an average camping trip or temporary SHTF kind of situation. Smartly laid out and packed in a sturdy see thru plastic bag.
Recommended? Yes.

title: Good deal and fits a Maverick 88 w/o a side saddle or light.
text:
Fits my Maverick 88 Security w/18.5" barrel perfectly. If you have a light underneath the mag tube or a side saddle, it will be an extra tight fit. I just took the light off since it has a quick detach, and it's snug in the scabbard. Has a strap that can go around a pistol grip to help keep it secure.
Recommended? It appears rugged and worked nicely.

title: Basic but works well.
text:
Fits my Maverick 88 perfectly after I added some Uncle Mike's sling adapters. Fully loaded can be a bit cumbersome as the material takes on an odd shape, but that may loosen up over time. 12 gauge shells fit pretty snug and didn't fall out after a round of vigorous shaking of the sling. Only thing that would've been better is to add some padding.
Recommended? Fairly basic, but sturdy and worth purchasing

title: Could be slightly better.
text:
Fits the stock on my Maverick 88 shotgun. Easy to adjust, BUT... on the smaller end, there is quite a bit of material that you either need to tuck in or cut off. It'll do in a pinch, but I would rather not cut material off or have to rig it differently than designed.
Recommended? If you're not adverse to cutting a bit or wrangling it so the strap doesn't get in the way, then it would be a good buy.

title: Easy and what I needed for my Maverick 88
text:
Absolutely what I needed for my Maverick 88 so it would be able to handle a sling. The small front screw is just that. Screw it in and done. The screw for the stock may be a little tougher if you have to drill a pilot hole for the standard stock. I do not have the standard stock anymore and my newer stock has a slightly carved out portion where the screw should go. Very easy. Make sure to use the blue goo on the rear screw so it grabs the material that your stock is made of.
Recommended? For a Maverick 88, yes.

title: Fits the need at a decent price.
text:
Very easy to install on my Maverick 88. Plenty of room on the 18.5" Security model forward of the forend. Securely holds a knock-off flashlight, which is good enough for home defense.
Recommended? Yes

title: Not quite what I expected.
text:
Not exactly what I like. A bit too cumbersome w/the zippered pouch. Would rather just have a slip on neoprene "sock" with the shell holders.
Recommended? Meh, it's just not for me and my Maverick 88 Security 12ga.

title: Does the small jobs well.
text: Super small, but does small jobs with ease. There's someone out there who would expect this to cut down a tree or baton wood like magic, but it Just. Won't. Do. That. Perfect for pocket carry. I don't want to carry it around my neck.

title: *UPDATE*
text:
Perfect for my AR15 when I use any 30 round mags (with collapsible buttstock). Not too heavy, not too light and made out of a seemingly durable material. Carry straps built in too.
*UPDATE 2-220* Both became hard as a rock. Useless now. Used it in Florida weather and always went back inside my house. No clue and don't want to investigate further because I'm not a happy camper at all.

title: Not awesome, but it serves it's purpose.
text:
This is for my Glock 30, which has double stack .45 mags. It sits well in the pocket, enough so that I have room for my car keys. Definitely takes a little practice to get used to, especially the placement of index finger and thumb and being able to apply pressure towards the rear, or back of your body so it snags (hence the name). Is it a necessary piece of gear? Not really, but it does serve a unique bit of the concealed carry market.
Recommended? Maybe if the price was $20 instead of $35, it would be more palatable to a larger segment of buyers.

title: Not a necessity, but nice to have anyhow
text:
No issues with my Glock mat. Stripping my model 30 and keeping all the bits & pieces in one area is the best way to go. I added a magnetic strip on the side to secure the itty bitty parts.
Recommended? While not necessary, it is nice to have something other than a white towel.

title: Works as intended
text:
Perfect size for stripping my Para-Ordnance P14.45 Expert. Laying the small-ish parts in the magnetic tray or even the other red trays is a smart way to make sure your bits & pieces don't disappear.
Recommended? Yes.

title: Superb product
text:
Very easy to install. Doesn't add any noticeable girth to the grip. I got the rubber version for my gen 3 model 30. Perfect fit and isn't a sticky rubber, but does give a more tactile & tangible sensation. Make sure you have a hair dryer to help conform the material to the gun.
Recommended? For the price and a Made-in-America product, it's hard to go wrong.

title: Satisfactory for what I need
text:
Not as bright as I thought, but that's probably a good thing. I mean, you don't really want a super bright light poking your eyes out when you're looking down the barrel, right? The on/off switch could have a better "click", in other words, it's a bit soft. The flexible neck helps it adapt to my rifle and pistol barrels.
Recommended? It gets the job done, barely.

title: Just what the AR15 doctor ordered
text:
Just what I needed for my reflex sight to "clear" my AR15's A2 front post sight. Easy to install. Finger screws tighten nicely and have a hole on one side, for what I assume, for an allen wrench (or anything that'll fit) so it can be tightened more.(?)

Recommended? Yeah, good price for what I needed

title: So many uses!
text:
What can you really say about paracord? If you like to camp or are a prepper or survivalist, having a solid amount of paracord is an absolute necessity. There are thousands of uses for paracord… shoe/boot laces, impromptu belt, clothesline, lash gear together, tourniquet, etc.
This batch of paracord is seven strands as evidenced in the photo below. Yeah, I didn’t get a perfect photo of the strands, but I did double count to make sure it was 7 strands. Whether its actual breaking strength is 550 lbs or not is something I can’t verify, but I’d hope you’d have strong rope for anything that heavy. Is it milspec? Don’t know and don’t particularly care as it doesn’t matter to me. I use the correct tools for the job I’m working on, so if 550 paracord can be used, then I use it. If not, I’ll find something smaller or bigger. 100 feet is a great length to own.
I did receive this product at a discount for my honest review.
Recommended? It’s like duct tape because it can work on so many different things.

title: Better than the generic models
text:
I've been looking at hand grip exercisers at a few big retail stores. Something inside just told me to wait to find something better. Well, I see the Enkeeo version and I think "Could this be the one?" It's definitely worth the extra $ to get this one versus your run-of-the-mill variety. This one gives you a total count, session count, timer, and calories burned info.Way more than I thought I'd be interested in knowing, but after using it a few days, it's kind of cool to see the stats. It has an auto-off feature which is necessary since there's no On / Off button. Text is easy to read. It is a little larger than the one's you're probably used to seeing, but that's not an issue. The resistance strength is on par with the other models. It's a hard plastic, but the texture lends itself to a solid grip.
I did receive this item at a discount for my honest review.
Recommended? Sure, spend a few dollars more for this one versus the generic ones.

title: Decent for the price
text:
A good price for six d-rings. Definitely not for climbing/rappelling, but it does state the in the description also. They all snap closed without any alignment issues... meaning when you let them spring closed, they don't get stuck in a semi-open position. Good for using on backpacks, purses, man-bags, and a variety of other places around the house where you'd like to hang something in a simple manner. For instance, I clipped one to the top of our broom and hung it in the closet so it stays out of the way.

I received these at a discount for my opinion.

Recommended? Sure, but I wouldn't pay more than $18

title: Great bargain. No frills.
text:
Inexpensive, bright enough that others will see you well enough in advance to maneuver out of harm's way. Incredibly simple to attach nearly anywhere on a bike. Comes w/batteries, which are easy to change out. Nothing fancy is what I wanted and I feel that I got a good price too.

Recommended? If you want no-frills and don't need a super giant bright light, these are for you.

title: Amazing! Well, it's pretty simple actually
text:
Does the job. Not much else can be said, I suppose.

Recommended? Yes, keep it secure and the dust bunnies away from the ammo.

title: Been looking for this for a while. Glad I found it.
text:
Just what I was looking for. I had wanted a swivel mount for my AR15 rail and this has what I wanted with the great addition of it being a quick detach mount.

Recommended? Yes

title: Buy it. Right now.
text:
Finally something that has all the features I've wanted in a sling. Dual/single point. HK clips. Good bungees. Decent adjustability. The stretchy material that covers the HK clips is a nice addition.

Recommended? For $20? Absolutely.

title: Pretty good, minimal design
text:
Fits nicely on my wife's coyote colored sling pack. Can hold various sizes of water bottles. A minimalist item, which is great when you want to conserve every ounce of weight in/on a pack.Appears to be good quality.

Recommended? Yes

title: Perfect!
text:
Perfect fit for my Para Ordnance Expert P-14.45 double stack magazines. With a little tightening of the screws, it's as snug as I want it.

Recommended? Yes, but it's not for single stack mags.

title: Right on the money!
text:
Perfect, snug fit for my Para Ordnance Expert P-14.45, which is the double stack .45. A bit tight to close the snap until I worked the gun in and out for about 10 minutes. I'm sure the leather will conform more to the pistol after a bit of time. Stitches look pretty solid.

Recommended? Great price for a leather holster. Be careful and make sure it will fit your pistol!

title: Just enough for my needs
text:
Not bad for the price. Wasn't quite sure what kind of quality I'd get for the price. I have some health issues and I wear these in our condo complex's pool. Maybe not for full-on scuba.

Recommended? Depends on usage

title: Do you need it? Maybe
text:
A bit of a pain to adjust if you're not used to these, especially if you do it by yourself. The mag pouches for the rifle mags are deep enough for 30 rounders and the pistol mag pockets are just big enough to hold some .45 double stackers.

Recommended? Not an absolutel necessity, but makes certain types of weapons practice much easier.

title: You kinda need this
text:
An absolute beast of a tool. Very sturdy and well made with just enough tools to make it a solid purchase. It's pretty much a great big multi-tool tha happens to have a few pieces that can be used on an AR type rifle. If you already have a bcg cleaning tool, you really don't need this and I thought the same thing until I decided I wanted something that had multiple uses and was easy to carry in my AR's cleaning- tools- and parts box.

Recommended? It's useful as a multi-tool and has a few pieces that can be used on your rilfe (BCG cleaner/scraper, pin punch, and the needle nose plier.

title: Pretty good and sharp!
text:
Wow. One of the sharpest knives right out of the box. It's a large-ish knife with a super tight sheath. Should fit in a front pocket w/o being seen, if that's your inclination.

Recommended? For the price? Absolutely.

title: If you like a stealth-y appearance.
text:
It's OK. Fits pretty darn good to the right side magwell. Easily adjustable.

Recommended? If you ask yourself if it's necessary, then it's probably not for you. I like the look.

title: Para Ordnance Expert 14.45
text:
Absolute spot-on fit on my Para Ordnance Expert 14.45. The finger swells and overall feel are much better than the stock grips.

Recommended? Yes.

title: Dang. Didn't work.
text:
I bought this for my double stack .45 magazines for a Para Ordnance Expert 14.45. Well, the fit is so loose, they slide out with ease and no feeling of being secure at all. An EMPTY mag stays in fine, but who carries empty magazines?

Recommended? Not this time.

title: Pretty decent
text:
Even thought I read the dimensions, this sucker is really, really big. The two rifle rests took a little careful muscle to lock on to the sides, but it was easy overall. I don't think I'll be carrying a thousand rounds, but it appears it could kind of handle that weight. There is more than enough room for my cleaning kits, lots of ammo, hearing protection, gunshot trauma kit, and a few other bits and pieces.

Recommended? Yes, it was a solid purchase.

title: Solid purchase
text:
Incredibly easy to cycle thru the different brightness levels. Low setting is really good for checking PERL (PERRL). It is bright enough with the other settings that make this a good multi-use flashlight.

Recommended? Yes

title: Blah. Sending it back after less than one day.
text:
Got it today, returning it tomorrow. It's bright, there's no doubt. The problem is the focusing mechanism. It is so loose that if you point it upwards, it slides down. If you hold it downwards, it slides down. There's not a bit of friction to keep it in place when you want to focus or widen the pattern. I've found that this is a fairly common occurrence. Did I get a dud? It's possible, but I think I'll pass and buy one from a solid manufacturer.

Recommended? Nope.

title: Might as well...
text:
Yeah, a little on the thin side, but what could you expect would fit in the knee pockets on the inside of the 5.11 EMS pants? They couldn't very well be on the chunky side. If they were, you'd be walking pretty funny. I'll just say that they do a better job than no padding at all and every little bit helps when you're kneeling down helping a patient.

Recommended? Sure, for the price (under $13) they do a minimal job.

title: Good purchase & price
text:
I've never had an assisted-opening knife. I really like it, especially with some medical issues that causes some pain in my hands. I do like the shape of the blade. Seems the way it's formed makes the tip stronger. I always like serrated blades. The snap-hook is a nice function and the fact that the blade will not open while the snap-hook is locked open. The cord/seat belt cutter is small, but I'm not looking to cut through 50 feet of fabric anyhow. The small screwdriver tip is nice, but probably won't need it. No idea when I'd use the hex key.

Recommended? Yes, a great price on a "budget" knife with extra features.

title: Works well for my purpose
text:
Here I am again, this time I'm looking for the best pouch possible for a very specific carry option. I've wanted something to carry one of my home made mini EDC kits, plus a few other items. I've found some really nice models, but they were usually too big or too small. Some were a great size for my needs, but were cost prohibitive.

Alas, I found a Monstrum Tactical MOLLE Utility Pouch on Amazon for about $14. I had narrowed it down to this item over a Condor Gadget MOLLE Pouch. The prices were nearly identical, so I went over both items with a discerning eye. The Monstrum was about a half-inch smaller, so it was a close call.

I believe some Monstrum products mimic their higher priced competition, yet still make a great value. There may be subtle differences here and there, but there were no major must-haves. I rarely go for the high end products when I find one that is similar for a lower price and good reviews. A quick note on reviews? Take them ALL with a grain of salt.

The Monstrum pouch appears to be very well made. The stitching appears sturdy and I only found one loose thread, which I burned down in about 3 seconds. It was a small detail, but it lent itself to the overall quality. The zippers, zipper pulls, and Velcro patches are also solid.

Features on the pouch were way more than I expected and what I saw online. As I looked it over, right after opening the Amazon box, I knew I had hit a homerun. From the front, there is a hard pouch cover with a zippered pocket. On the underside of that cover is a heavy duty patch of Velcro that connects to the front, expandable, pocket. On either side of that pocket are elastic loops that can be adjusted to hold the pocket tightly closed. In this front area, you have it subdivided into different sections. Behind this front area, you have the main pocket. It has 3 subdivisions and they held everything I wanted with a tiny bit of room left. This main pocket has two zippers w/pulls. On the back of the pouch, there are two MOLLE snap straps, which are useful to wear on a belt, if you know how to weave them correctly.

One of the main things that I liked was the expandable front pocket. It really protrudes as you add more stuff, so those adjustable elastic straps help it stay secure. It more than serves its purpose.

Pros:
Cost @ $14
Strong & sturdy
Perfect size for a mini-EDC kit and other small items
Multiple carry options

Cons:
It looks pregnant with all the stuff I put in there, so that's a bit odd.
(As was that statement).

Final verdict? Take a close look for yourself on the Monstrum or Amazon websites and see for yourself. If you have a couple of handfuls of small-ish gear you want to keep in its own pouch, this may work out perfect for you too.

title: Nice bargain
text:
For the price and what you get, this Coleman tent is great! Not much room, but 2 average size folks will fit. You better know that person really well!

Recommended? Yes

title: I'm so excited! (not really)
text:
Hmmm, where should I start? Well, it's a fairly sturdy plastic green box that holds my 5.56 / .223 rounds nicely. The actual plastic hinges on the back were a surprise.

Recommended? For under $5, yes.

title: Not bad, not bad
text:
Takes away fingerprint oils and general grime. Leaves a smooth, non glare, finish. I don't think I'll be washing it at all. I still like Frog Lube and Sentry Solution's products, but this cloth falls in line nicely.

Recommended? For the price, yes.

title: Meh
text:
Meh. Kind of neutral on this. Can't remember why I bought it. It's a good tool to keep in your range bag if you're incredibly new to AR15 style rifles. A few of the pages are for advertisements of Real Avid's other products, which kind of sucks.

Recommended? Not really.

title: Not bad, Not bad at all.
text:
Pretty damn good sleeping bag for the money! I definitely didn't want to go high-tech or crazy expensive and this set up fits the bill nicely. Comfortable bag, nice zipper that doesn't catch on the fabric. A great starter bag or one for use once in a while.

Recommended? Yes

title: Not bad. Not bad at all.
text:
Pretty damn good sleeping bag for the money! I definitely didn't want to go high-tech or crazy expensive and this set up fits the bill nicely. Comfortable bag, nice zipper that doesn't catch on the fabric. A great starter bag or one for use once in a while.

Recommended? Yes

title: Much better for me
text:
Ah, yes, much better. I tried some of the fancier 2 point slings and a 1 point bungee sling. They weren't quite for me. This one is more the style that I used in the Army back in the 80's. Simple design, easy to adjust and install.

Recommended? For under $8, it's hard to go wrong.

title: Great price, good name.
text:
Better to have a less expensive Leight model than one of the many substandard models out there. Easy to adjust and is a great fit on my big ol' noggin.

Recommended? Absolutely.

title: Recommended? Yes
text:
A very small tool that does a few things decently. Not a completely necessary item, but having it is worth the small price, plus it doesn't take up much space at all.

Recommended? Yes, for a low price, get a tool that is easy to carry.

title: Good entry level bipod
text:
Easy to add to a bottom rail. Legs fold out smoothly, but take a small amount of pressure to move, which is good. Adjustable legs are easy to operate, but may be a little awkward if trying to tighten the 'screws' with gloves on (which I highly doubt I'll ever do anyhow). Otherwise, all seems sturdy and tight.

Recommended? Yes, for a good price versus the big name brands.

title: Wicked edge
text:
Shovel has a sharp edge, which is great. Easy to sharpen after digging or hacking thru light brush. Solid connection from the handle to the shovel head. Wish it came with a cover/sheath, but I did buy one separately. Small enough to carry on my backpack. Barely notice it's there.

Recommended? Yes.

title: Good for what it is (for me)
text:
This packs well into my BOB. Barely weighs anything. I use it as a temporary shelter and it's easy to set up and take down. Heck, packing it back up is easy too. For me, it won't take the place of a tent and it shouldn't. When you need a little shelter without the workout in putting up a tent, this is for you.

Recommended? Yes.

title: Nice
text:
Not a bad sling for a low price. Easy to adjust, even while wearing it. Took all of 2 or 3 minutes to connect to my S&W M&P 15 Sport.

Recommended? Yes for the low price and good quality.

title: Great fit
text:
Fit easily to my M&P 15 Sport. Very simple to co-witness. Didn't have to mess with any of the different positions to have it work. Got it going right out of the box. Yeah, there is a galaxy effect when it's on the brightest setting (red or green), but I'm not worried about that since the brightness can be manually changed with the knob on the left side.

It is not a high end product, which is what I expected and what I received.

Recommended? Yes, a good price for a decent sight.

title: Better to be safe.....
text:
A little dry fire practice with these snap caps may not be completely necessary, but better to be safe than sorry, right?

Recommended? Yes. Practical and inexpensive.

title: Pretty nice
text:
Was worried about it fitting my subcompact Glock 30. After some adjustment of the velcro strap that goes around the grip, it fits just fine. Appears it will fit most any handgun. Straps feel strong and enough to fit some good sized people. I imagine if you're a giant treetrunk of a person, you may look for something bigger. Padding that goes along the leg is a bonus.

Recommended? Yes. UTG makes some decent weapons stuff.

title: A.W.E.S.O.M.E.
text:
Well, it's a bore brush, so not much to really like or dislike. Appears sturdy enough to last a while. I added it to the Otis M4/M16/AR15 cleaning kit (round pouch).

Recommended? Might as well. Doesn't hurt to have it and use it once in a while.

title: Very nice!
text:
Much better and sturdier than I had expected. Nice shoulder strap and top handle. Pockets on outside are sturdy with solid velcro closures. I fit a Magpul 30 rd. pmag in one with a tiny bit of room to spare. Two velcro straps inside will help keep your weapon sort of secure inside so it doesn't bounce around. There is a "pocket" on either end, inside, where the barrel and buttstock will slide into, further helping it from being jostled (which never concerned me anyhow). Padding is good, especially around the edges of the zippered portion, making it seem easier to close. I have a M&P 15 Sport and it fits fine, even with the stock fully extended.

Recommended? Yes, especially since I bought it for $38.

title: Very nice
text:
Much better than expected and I believe on par with some of the more expensive brands. Plenty of pockets with apparently strong velcro. Sturdy plastic feet on the bottom will help it not only last longer, but stay dry if you dare drop your Starbuck's coffee on the ground. Nice handles and shoulder strap. Bottom of the inside is padded and a nice surprise.

Recommended? Absolutely

title: Great fit
text:
Perfectly snug fit for a Smith & Wesson 642. The gun isn't going anywhere as it sits in this holster. Paddle is a good shape to fit big and small folks.

Recommended? Yes

title: Meh
text:
You get what you pay for with this combo. It's not bad, just not that... ummm... blah, I don't know. Don't forget to take off the plastic, transparent sheet on top of the mirror.

Recommended? Get it under $3 and it's a deal.

title: Whoot Whoot
text:
Works just as well as a .10cent ferro rod and striker. Fancier. The little room in one handle for some tinder is OK.

Recommended? I'd rather have an inexpensive version. You don't need "fancy" to make a fire with a ferro rod and tinder.

title: Better than I had hoped
text:
If you can make a taut line for your tent, or anywhere else for that matter, and you don't have to tie a knot... Well, it just makes it a little easier, especially if you're in need in a hurry. These things are painfully easy to use and well worth the moolah.

Recommended? Yes and not just for tents.

title: Pretty good
text:
Not too bad for the price. Rolls up pretty small and fits in the go-bag nicely. It is small, but that's fine because I wouldn't expect a full sized pillow for camping.

Recommended? Sure, for the price.

title: Get one (or two) now!
text:
I love this pointy stick. I have a small collection and this seems to be a favorite of others when they see what I own. Unfortunately, Cold Steel doesn't always put a good edge on its products and it was no different on this Gladius. Paint job is poor and edges had plenty of bumps. Took a lot of TLC and not it's in stupendous shape!

Recommended? For the price, yes, but be ready to clean it up a bit.

title: Good bulk matches
text:
Pretty darn good for the price. Not the super fancy waterproof matches, but folks rarely need those anyway. For a normal camping trip, these will do just fine. Probably want to keep them in a Ziploc type bag so the box doesn't get mushy if you go over a waterfall.

Recommended? Under $7 for 400 matches? Yes!

title: What I needed
text:
I needed straps long enough to help me compress my sleeping bags enough to store wherever. These do the job just fine. The directions on the back of the package are a bit weird though.

Recommended? For the price, absolutely.

title: Good choice
text:
A good choice for an inexpensive way to add individual matchbooks to your camping gear, bug out bag, survival kit.

Recommended? Yes.

title: Good deal
text:
Small pots/pans, but better quality than I had imagined. Since they nest inside one another, overall space is small. Looks to be a resilient cooking surface that should clean up easily.

Recommended? For the price, yes.

title: Meh
text:
I got this kit for the mallet and spare tent stakes. The mallet has a good weight and the tent stakes are much sturdier than I had figured. The little hand-broom and stake puller may come in handy.

Recommended? Yes, worth the price for a couple of the items. The other items are a bonus.

title: Perfect for my BOB
text:
These are great for my main BOB and for the mini survival kits that I put together. They are razor blades connected to a plastic sheath. The blade doesn't come out unless you manually do so, which is exactly what you'd want.

Recommended? Yes

title: Neat-o
text:
I bought this to send to a family's two young daughters (their Dad is serving overseas) who were interested in making paracord bracelets. They loved the colors and made all sorts of cool stuff.

Recommended? Yep!

title: Double check the measurements
text:
Make sure this is the size box that you're looking for. I needed one for my hobby projects and this one fits the bill nicely. I keep stuff for my paracord bracelets and mini survival kits inside. If I had to guess-timate, this box is about half the size of a regular ammo box. Make sense?

Recommended? Yes, if you need a smaller container.

title: Not bad
text:
Good ferro rods. Good striker. Scraped sparks from all three. Perfect for my mini-kits. I consider the scraper a bonus since I got the sparks from a multi tool.

Recommended? Yes.

title: Very nice
text:
This is a knife that has equal parts function and form. The stone-washed blade lends a worn appearance. It will also cover up most nicks and scratches as time goes by. It is sturdy in the hand and fits quite well with the jimping and micarta handle. I also like the full tang. Makes for a rough and tough knife. I pounded on some half inch hardwood and there's not a mark to be seen. A little love with a ceramic sharpener gave it a better edge than what it came with.

Recommended? Yes, for this price you get a solid knife.

title: for my BOB
text:
I think every BOB should have duct tape and the fusion tape. Perfect for small repairs on a lot of items.

Recommended? Yes.

title: More than one purpose
text:
I say more than one purpose because it's not just for cutting into wood as other reviewers have noted. It's perfectly fine for cutting thru twigs, but it's also good for sawing small diameter rope/cordage, webbing, and removing clothes (albeit carefully).

Recommended? Yes. Good price and fits easily in my BOB

title: Small and solid
text:
Yes, it is small. That much should be clear in the description. I had planned on putting together a small survival kit in a tin, so this is an absolute perfect way to start.

Recommended? Yes. Good price and good company in CRKT.

title: As described
text:
I like the Gadsden flag and this color and shape made for a nice addition to my small collection of patches.

Recommended? Yes

title: Great
text:
Great starter kit for me. Bought a paracord bracelet jig and it's much easier. If you're just starting out, this is a good place to start. If I can make the bracelets, ANYONE can.

Recommended? Yes.

title: Good stuff
text:
Well, you can't expect superior quality for the price you pay for 10 of these, but they do what they're intended to do. Not as noisy as I figured, so that's a plus too.

Recommended? Yeah, for the price, these are good for yourself and/or your bug-out-bag.

title: BAM! There goes my eardrums
text:
Holy crapola! Probably not a great idea to give this thing a full blast while you're in your house. I think my cats are going to hide under the bed for the rest of the day. Suffice it to say that it's very, very loud. Now I can combat the ever barking dog next door and bring it along when I drive so I can wake up people who are preoccupied with texting and blathering about on their cellphones.

Recommended? Yes. Great to have on a boat or anywhere else!

title: Gotta have it
text:
Well, it's just the sheath for the shovel. Why they don't sell them as a single unit is beyond me. But, in any case, the fit is perfect and adding a few strips of strategically placed duct tape helps strengthen a nice item.

Recommended? yes

title: Nice addition for stickier, but comfortable, grips on edged weapons
text:
I use these to custom fit strips for my fixed blade knives that need a sticky feel on the grip. Easy to cut and apply. My suggestion is to carefully outline the item that you will be placing these on so you don't waste any.

Recommended? Yes

title: Must have!
text:
I've been using Sentry Marine Tuf-Glide since I was in the Army long ago. I use it monthly for maintenance on my pistols and edged weapons. A good coating plus time to dry and lightly wipe down, leaves you with a well protected piece of equipment.I use it as a protectant and not as a lubricant.

Recommended? Absolutely

title: Been using these since mid 80's
text:
I've been using Sentry Marine Tuf-Cloth since I was in the Army long ago. I use it monthly for maintenance on my pistols and edged weapons. A good coating plus time to dry and lightly wipe down, leaves you with a well protected piece of equipment.I use it as a protectant and not as a lubricant.

Recommended? Highly!

title: Multi use towel
text:
It's a nice material that rolls up very compact. The straps attached to the fabric help keep it from unfolding, which is a nice touch. It won't dry off a whole body, but it's really good as a sweat rag and/or keeping electronic device screens clean.

Recommended? Yes

title: Nicely done, Cold Steel!
text:
Another good, solid product from Cold Steel. Reminds me of my Mora Kniv in an almost identical fashion. The ferro rod is just a nice touch and good to have.

Recommended? For the price, absolutely. I've grown to like my Cold Steel collection; low prices and good quality.

title: Very small, but works fine
text: Not much to these tinder tabs. They're small and stay lit for about a minute or two, which is all you need if you have the other parts of making a fire ready for use. Just pull 'em apart to fluff them up a bit and lit it with whatever you can and BAM! Fire.

title: Burns fairly clean
text: It burns hot pretty quickly and lasts a good amount of time. Sorry I didn't record how long it lasted, but you can find that info on YouTube, most likely. The smell is pretty nasty when you take them out of the package, but the stink goes away once they're lit and burning. I'd suggest getting an aLOKSAK bag to keep them in, otherwise your backpack will be smelly too.

title: Great design
text:
Wonderfully compact and does what it's meant to do, which is to heat stuff up. It can boil liquid, but I wouldn't (hopefully!) need to do that anywhere I go. Heating up water for coffee or to place in Mountain House food bags is what I like. It's not going to be useful for a group of more than 3 or four people because of it's small size. It does fit in my BOB along with the Esbit fuel cubes. Very light.

Recommended? Yes

title: Fits!
text:
Fits nicely on the cover of my laptop. You just have to be pretty careful not to fudge it up when applying. Take your time, take your time, and take your time.

Recommended? Sure

title: Just like the old days...
text:
... when i was in the US Army. This looks and feels exactly like the set I carried when in the field. For the price, you get a decent product. It's not heavy duty, but I really wouldn't want anything like that in something I have to attach to my BOB. Heck, even if you like to collect military memorabilia, this is for you too!

Recommended? Yes

title: Excellent product

My Maxpedition 32oz water bottle fits nicely inside with just a wee bit of wiggle room. The outside pocket is perfect for a pack of water purification powder/tablets and a small folding knife. I used the straps to secure it to my small BOB. Great price also when compared to the more expensive brands.

Recommended? Yes

title: Very very nice!

I'd say the sizing is going to be big for most folks, so maybe go 1 size down. That is my opinion, so be careful. Anyhow, if it's a little big, you have to remember that you're going to be wearing something underneath.

Recommended? Yes

title: Yikes!

These things hurt! Even when I just held them in my hand and smashed it against my shin, it was quite painful. These are easy to apply to almost any shoe, but I think you're going to need laces for a proper fit. You can't see them very well when I put them on my black Bates boots. Great price and awesome product!

Recommended? Yes

title: Perfect!

It fits my Maxpedition 32 oz water bottle. Nice and snug. Protects the water bottle from heat & cold. Nice shoulder strap that can be adjusted. Well worth the price. I might get another.

Recommended? Yes.

title: Needs a little trimming, but...
text:
For the price, it's pretty nice to have on my Glock 30. The palm swells help it fit my big mitt better. It did require a little trimming at the bottom, but that was easily accomplished with my baby Exacto knife. While not a necessary item for my gun, it does a better job on my grip.

Recommended? Yes.

*EDIT* It ripped without any additional pressure other than holding my Glock like normal. Oh well. Lesson learned.

title: Might as well
text:
For the price, I couldn't wait any longer to buy this little tool. Sure, you could use almost any 3/32 flat punch, but this one does the job and you're on the page right now looking at it, right? Go ahead. Buy it. You should not be disappointed.

Recommended? Yes.

title: A needed addition to my CERT gear
text:
Every single person that is associated with CERT anywhere in the country should have this in their bag. No doubt about it.
The case or pouch is made of tough material. The pen is just like a Fisher Space pen. It will write while holding it in any direction. The two small books are both waterproof, so reading or writing on them in the rain will pose no problem, especially with the pen that writes nicely in bad weather.
Don't delay. You know that it may be needed in an instant.

Recommended? Yes.
