title: It fits. Right size.
text: Kind of stiff getting out of the box and folded to make it a challenge to install on the rim and tire. A little bit at a time always works until it all fits together. The schrader valve stem kept dropping down with no pressure in the tube. There used to be a locking nut on valve stems that prevented that, but a simple plastic tube with the right inside diameter would probably work to keep the stem in place. Once inflated I could reassemble the unicycle. The object here was not only to leak-proof the tire because air pressure is extremely important for pedaling and balance, but also to give the wheel more weight, providing better feedback, a better ride control, and the heavier wheel has greater stability. It works!

title: Fits and works! More Better!
text: First of all the box was open inside the Amazon delivery bag. One of the 2 crank-bolts was missing and I had to visit a bike shop to find a matching set in the same style (with the rubber washer as a seal.) But the drive-train assembly with the new cartridge bearing was easy using the assembly tool (that was the another separate item in this order.) This is a smooth operating bike now, compared with the previous clanking and jerking caused by a bearing which looked like it exploded with metal fragments everywhere. The enclosure case around the bearing is supposed to make it more rugged and will certainly keep it clean, which is always a plus. The easy to install system with 2 threaded ends fits through the frame (you must remove the threaded end on the left side first) and when it's tightened on the right with the installation tool you use the same tool to close the left side of the bearing into the bottom bracket frame.  Yay!

title: Long cranks, easy ride!
text: The first unicycle I had was in Germany when I was with the US Army in Heidelberg. It was a VERY hard to ride 26 or 28 inch. Not a good one to learn on. Changing it to a 24 inch by rebuilding the wheel (but keeping the same long cranks) made it much easier to ride. That was in 1983 and that unicycle has since worn out. (I rode it a LOT, all over the World!) But newer unicycles lacked the same quality of that ride and the "feel" was all wrong. I didn't even know that cranks came in different lengths in 1983, but reducing the large wheel diameter while keeping the 6 inch cranks is what made the ride so nice. (With shorter cranks it's not as easy to balance or pedal, and you go too fast- not impossible but not as much fun.) Proof of that came with these 6 inch SUNLITE cotterless cranks which changed the performance of a 24 inch that came with 5 inch cranks to finding that "sweet spot" it had been missing. They're very heavy and strong, I doubt I'll be able to bend these.

title: Good tools to keep track of (for when you need them.)
text:
The crank puller comes apart by un-threading it all the way and the 16mm spanner can be put in before re-assembly. It works to both tighten and loosen both functions from it's position inside the tool. This is a nice design since by doing this you'll never lose the 16mm spanner wrench.
The other tool is essential for the newer, all in one piece bottom bracket bearing, to install and tighten. There are 2 ways to turn it, either 1/2" square drive (so you can use a torque wrench) on the inside or a spanner-wrench on the outside. I like tools that someone has obviously thought about to be flexible and not just used in one way.

title: Fits my bottom bracket (both tool ends)
text: It's a strong tool, but it's thin and a sort of balancing act to get it to turn the bracket locking ring. If it was thicker it would have greater purchase and be easier to use. But you don't use this tool often unless you work in a bike shop. Getting the BB open and seeing what happened to the bearing is what it's all about.

title: Raise your grip, straighten your back
text:
This WAKE stem riser comes with enough spacer-rings to put your existing handlebar riser at the right height and allow the stem cap and long stem bolt to fully engage. There was a little difficulty in keeping the alignment of the now top and bottom sections of this taller riser assembly, but I found getting the top on first and clamping it in position so the gaps in top and bottom line up vertically is easier than putting the tall riser on first and then aligning and tightening the top section with the handlebars to it. It can be done either way, but it took a lot of fussing, tightening and loosening and twisting. Getting that long bolt in to press the stem cap down to hold everything in position is complicated that the fork bearing will keep everything loose without the correct alignment, so you have to keep that as a goal because nothing can have a final position without that important fork bearing being seated. Then, all you need to do is clamp it all together on the bike. This is a 2 part operation: the long bolt and stem cap forces the assembled units together and down, then clamping the top and bottom riser sections together and to the bike for a solid steering connection. I think this better than the older-style threaded stem which depends on that single bolt to hold everything in place.
-Compressing in several dimensions makes it more secure.-
The test ride, once I was satisfied that everything had been aligned and tightened, was different from how the bike had been only an hour ago. My hands, arms and shoulders were at a more natural angle and riding was much easier. This riser extension is only 2.7 inches, but coupled with the top riser and raised handlebars the difference is more than 8 inches overall. A nice, comfortable ride!
There are youtube videos showing this operation in detail. //// It's important to do it properly! ////

title: Lightweight 25.4mm Aluminum handlebar - 520mm (21")
text: Wide handlebars are good when you're in rough terrain because the extra leverage really helps. But in a more urban setting where there are smooth and level surfaces shorter handlebars work better. Particularly when you're sharing the road with the automobile; where just a few extra inches of separation might make all the difference to you! This handlebar also has an 80mm rise to give the rider a better, more upright posture. Everything transferred from the flatter bar to this new one even though it's about 100mm (4") less. I just came back from a long test ride and I didn't miss bending over to reach the flat bars at all... The control is better and since my head is more upright I can see better all around and be more aware in traffic or with pedestrians doing their unpredictable things. You need to know what sort of setup is the best for you, and it takes time to get that experience. I bought this bike new only a few days ago and the handlebars just weren't right. I could have looked a little harder for bars with more of a rise, but if I want this one higher I'll get a stem-riser headset and some spacers.

title: Better to have and not need than to really need and not have!
text:
I had an accident on my skateboard yesterday, hit my elbow pretty hard and quit for the day. I was going to wait for this protective gear before I started practicing Ollies or doing anything else risky, but my sore elbow was a good reminder to wait for the proper equipment to use before something like that (or worse) happened again.
This set of knee, elbow and wrist protectors is fairly well-made although light. The only thing I really don't like is the logo. After years in graphic-arts I have decided that I truly dislike high-visibility logos so I remove them by sanding or cutting them off. In the case of this "Triple-eight" with a horrible intersection of 3 eights the best method was flat black enamel paint that seems to have obliterated everything except the raised portions of the embroidery. Otherwise it's all black and low key. (This was my intent when I bought this kit and it worked well. Yay!)
The fit is fairly good for a mass-produced set of items, the big factor and the determination for S-M-L being the hand and wrist-guard, which I ordered Large. It's a little loose, but I have all sorts of foam sheets and leather pieces to custom-fit these important pieces, even to reinforcing the external portions as required. The knee and elbow pads are sort of a one-size-fits-all, but the same rules for modification apply.
Essentially, a very good buy for protection that is far better to have and not need than to really need and not have!
This is important stuff to wear, because a skateboard can become very dangerous suddenly without any warning. This kit, in conjunction with a decent helmet and good shoes (skate shoes) can make the difference in protecting those parts of your body that won't function very well unless they move freely without pain. Try being an artist or musician with a broken wrist. Try driving you car or riding your bike with a bad elbow or knee. It's in your best interest to protect yourself, because nobody else will, and if you still haven't figured it out getting hurt costs $$$!

text:
Just the facts: One burgundy Fitbit One activity tracker with clip on case, charger and sleep band.

Pros: This tracker is great for privacy, I can clip it on my bra and no one ever knows it's there. When I opened the box to set it up the battery was completely drained but I hooked it up to the charger and in less than 15 minutes was ready to go. Syncing with my pc and phone was extremely easy, just plug in and go. The app on my iPhone is what I normally use to view my data and it is extremely user friendly, I love doing challenges with my friends that have Fitbits as well. The tracker keeps up with steps, flights of stairs, distance, sleep and has silent alarms. What REALLY sells me on this particular tracker is it's accuracy though. I had a Charge HR before and ended up giving it to a friend because it frustrated me how often it was giving me credit for steps when I was just petting my dog watching tv. With the One not being strapped to my wrist it truly only counts my actual steps as steps. I've tested it by keeping the app open on my phone while doing different things that can trigger false steps and it is exceptionally accurate. I actually wear an Apple Watch and it consistently has 200-400 more steps at the end of a day than my One just due to the wrist movements.

Cons: With it not being on my wrist it's rather awkward to check it to see my steps during the day - to solve this I just check them on my phone app.

Would I recommend this? I would recommend this and often do!

I could be four stars...
I was looking for a foldable bike to put in a car trunk. Other similar bikes, just half the price, are all shipped from china with 2-3 month wait time with no reviews or 2-3 reviews with 5 stars. Granted they all are made in the same shop from the same chinesium but this one has 30+ positive and was delivered in 4 days.
The good. Frame is steal and well welded and painted. Its heavy but sturdy. Front fork is just as good but has a little play in the springs, not critical. Rear suspension is good enough. Rims are straight.
The so-so. I am 5-11 and set the seat is almost as high as it gets. The handle bar could be higher at my preference.
The bad. Worst thing - the brake disks mounting. Front wheel all six and four on the rear wheel had broken threads. This is a major screwup as the wheels are all aluminum and the only way to fix it is to thread next size 6mm threads. Techicaly, easy fix but this should never happen! Next - the shifters are the cheapest i have seen. The left 3-grear broke while adjusting it. The push lever was grinding the base that caused the latch pin to deflect. I expected to replace them anyhow so it wasnt a show stopper.
And the special thing - the hand pump. This bike comes with a hand pump. I dont know what happened to it, either a $1-per hour laborer or rats on the container ship, either one is a shame for a bike with this price tag, but the pump was all chewed up. Dont believe me - see the pictures
So, two things, the disk brake screws and shifter - two stars,
I would not recommend this bike but there are not too many alternatives. Well, unless you are willing to take the risk and order one from china with no reviews.

text:
I wanted a new mask for snorkeling in Hawaii, and the pool. Very good/ comfortable fit. I like the tint, and the lens is
tempered. If the lens is tempered ,you should be able to use it for Scuba. They say no, OK fine. Only problem I had, one of that adjustment "Button's" broke, Kuyou -in China doesn't want to help me - You might look ,at other brands.
.

text:
I'm a Scuba Diver (Have been for 41 years) .Nothing, I mean nothing, seems to last very long . I have tried every brand, Joy - etc. I was diving in Tahiti, The Paul Gauguin . They used Aqua Lung Equipment. A fellow diver gave the gel to use.

text: I wanted a compact pair of fins (That don't take up much Room ,in a suitcase) To travel to Hawaii. I was impressed on how these were made .Blade  area still moves you well (I tried them in my pool)  Yes, they are not made in China.

title: Just handy
text: Definitely a must for your golf bag. Clean clubs, balls, etc. Seems to self clean as it dries as well. Heavy stuff sticks, but sand falls off as you travel.

title: Works, but not essential
text: It does clean typical dirt and such. I like having it in my pocket, but I don't stress if I forget it. Okay, but not an essential.

title: My second one - Really like them
text: I haven't fished with this one yet, but I bought one (2500) for a fly-in trip earlier. These reels are smooth, the drag works well, I caught a lot of fish in a week with no issues at all. Not sure I'd pay full price, but if you get them on a reduced price like I did grab it. That's why I bought a second one.

title: I really don't have a complaint
text:
This bag is for warm weather situations. It does well for summer camping.

The large size is nice and gives enough room to be comfortable.

No way I'd use it for cold weather, but I really don't have any complaints.

title: Comfortable and well made
text: I've had fishing pliers fall apart on me recently. So, I bought these as replacements. I'll say they are much better made than others I've used. No screws to come out and the alignment of the jaws if very, very good. I've only used them once for a hook removal, but they worked as expected. The handles are nice with the foam covering. I expect years of use without falling apart.

title: Better than other options and certainly better than nothing
text:
Went on a fly-in fishing trip and found no pillows. I know, should have packed my own, but they were supplied in the past.

At any rate, I bought these as soon as I returned home. Then I tried them out over a couple of nights. I found them to be very much acceptable. Not as comfy as my "real" pillows, but certainly acceptable.

Just two things that I didn't like. First, the cover may have cloth on it, but it's not particularly comfortable. A pillow case over the entire pillow is my plan of action. Second, without the pillow case it is somewhat noisy. I had an issue as a side sleeper, where slight adjustments made significant noise directly in my ear. I was able to get to sleep though.

Overall I see it as a great option. They pack very small and they are much better than no pillow at all.

title: Inexpensive, easy to pack, works okay
text: Probably a little small for a 14' boat and a strong breeze, but for typical drifting it's just fine. The price and packable size make it perfect for remote fishing trips. Of course it does result in more fish in the pan. Definitely a good add-on item.

title: Repeat Customer
text:
I've used KastKing products and braid in the past. It's good, dependable stuff. Not a lot of bells and whistles, just functional.

The only negative to this fishing line is the dye does come off on your fingers while loading it on the reel. It also losses it's color after several uses. I normally just cut off the discolored end and I'm back to normal. It's a good value and works well for me. I'll buy more I'm sure.

title: They are okay
text: I've used other brands in the past and these are no worse or better. The price is the reason I picked them. Not a miracle cure for the hot weather, but they do seem to help a little bit.

title: Acceptable, just not "long shank"
text:
Seem to be sharp enough out of the box. The color is nice. Sturdy as well. Not a "premium" hook, but well within the acceptable range.

The "long shank" is certainly an Aberdeen length, but I wouldn't call it anything special. Good for pan fish, but I wouldn't consider them for fly tying or anything that requires a really long shank.

title: Expensive, but my mother likes them
text: I don't use them, but my mother (83) really likes them. That being said, they seem over priced to me. Mom's happy though - LOL!

title: Looks good, takes some practice
text: The end result is very good. However, the stamp isn't lined up with the finger impressions on the side of the case. It takes some practice to get it lined up where you want it.

title: Initial Impressions
text:
Well I've fished only one time with it, but so far I'm pleased. It's smooth and handles the shock of hook setting well. I'm known for being tough on reels with my hook set. Again, only one fishing trip, but it's not showing any signs of failing. Casts well, puts the line on the spool evenly. Really no problems so far.

If it develops issues I'll update the review, but so far I have no complaints.

title: Sticky at first, but seems to be getting  better
text:
Initially the mechanism would stick. Took a lot of pressure to get it to trigger. As I'm used it, dry runs on the carpet, it seems to be getting better. I end up using it in muck and soft bottom more than anywhere else so the trigger needs to be lighter so I don't push the ball in to the mud.

Is is worth the purchase price. I'd say yes. Just be ready to tinker with it to get it to work more reliably.

title: For the price - fantastic
text:
I've just played a couple of rounds with them so far and I'm very happy. My score didn't reflect that happiness - LOL - but I can't blame the grips.

The strip on the back can be a pain to get lined up, but they are easily detected. I really like that. The remaining portions of the grips are easy to hold on to and hold up to sweat.

Definitely something I'll buy again in the future.

title: Helps with alignment
text:
I put mine so the flat size was parallel with the putter face. It definitely helps with alignment and catching me pushing or pulling. I did make more puts and my misses were closer to the hole. Perhaps most important is you can feel the pushes and pulls immediately. The puts don't go in, but it's instant feedback. With some more practice I think my putting will improve.

Worth the cost? That's up to me. Practice is definitely the key, but I'm pretty sure it will make a difference.

title: Tape is a little short, not enough solvent
text:
I've re-gripped several times. Needed a "travel" kit and bought this one. It worked, but there are two issues to consider. First, the tape isn't long enough to cover the entire grip. It's at least an inch short. Second, there's probably enough solvent to do the entire set of strips, but just enough. I like to get the tape and inside of the grip really soaked before sliding them on. No way you can do that with this amount of solvent, even with a pan to catch it.

Overall, it did work and the grips are holding well. However, it's not the same as a roll of tape and a big bottle of solvent.

title: Not much of an impact
text:
If your main reason for buying these is the visible impact, well I'd recommend another option. Two different rifles, multiple different bullet types, no visible hit other than the hole.

They may be okay for slower moving projectiles like from a pistol, but as for use with rifles, it's not going to be any more visible than other types.

All that being said, they are convenient, stick well and are nice to use. I've got multiple colors and this would be my second favorite. I like the lime green best.

Work the cost, but I just didn't want anyone to think they were going to provide really visible hits.

title: works as advertised
text: It works as advertised. However it is pretty loud.

title: Works well, graphics are okay, but not overwhelming
text: It works well as a convenient ball marker. The graphics are okay, but I'm not blown away by them. A good way to support the Buckeyes and functional. Something I think all OSU fans would appreciate.

title: Replacing old supply - good value
text:
Now keep in mind these are not reported to be the top of the line eyes. They function well and the variety of sizes make them a real value.

If you're building a custom rod I'd look at other options, but if you're replacing a broken tip it's definitely the way to go.

title: It fit, but that wasn't the problem
text: I I-pilot Link controller went dead. Bought the battery as this was the next step in the troubleshooting process. It did not fix the problem. I now have a dead remote, a new battery and discovered they no longer make the remote for the Link system. Very disappointed in Minn Kota.

title: Does NOT work with I-pilot Link
text: Don't be confused by the information. This remote does NOT work with the I-pilot Link system. I returned mine. It wouldn't "learn" the trolling motor head and after communicating with Minn Kota they advised I needed the specific controller for the Link system. Which they no longer manufacture. Very disappointed and unhappy with Minn Kota!

title: No issues
text: Worked as described - No issues.

title: Off the tee and from the ground - works very well for me
text:
Okay, I'm probably the odd ball out on this discussion. I've tried several hybrid styles, makes and models and struggled with consistency. Distance was also not what I was expecting, regardless of lie or contact. I even pulled the 3 wood (fairway metal) out of my bag for the same reason. I hit my driver very well, even drivers I haven't spent time with. So, I was left in a no win situation.

I started watching videos and found that the "utility clubs" were available and seemed to be very useable for the person who hits irons well. So, I made the gamble and bought this, relatively inexpensive, utility club to try. Well, it checked all my boxes. The 18* 3 iron gives me that hybrid/fairway wood distance without all the inconsistency. I hit it well and the ball flight is exactly what I expected it to be. So far I've played 3 rounds with it, hit it 2-3 times from the ground and 2-3 times off the tee (short par 4 doglegs) and virtually every shot has been spot on.

It's also forgiving. I've hit a few off the toe end without a large loss of yardage and no right fade. It just goes short and straight with the mishits.

If you hit your longer irons well and struggle with the hybrid/fairway woods, this is definitely worth a try.

FYI, I hit 5 or 6 shots in the backyard before taking it to the course. That's it!

title: Nice reel
text: I really like this reel. Small, but has some power. The fast gear ratio is an added bonus. I just don't see you buying a better reel for the price.

title: Fit my 40HP mercury 2 stroke
text: Fit my motor well. With youtube easy to install. Definitely worth the price.

title: Better option for keys on belt loop
text:
I bought two types for keys. These and the S type. I prefer these. Bigger opening and larger "hook" on the end.

I think they would hold up well for other uses, but I haven't tried that yet.

title: Adhesive is suspect, you don't always want that much weight, too long for some situations
text:
Okay, it's not rocket science, but I found that the pre-cut strips are too long for quick placement while away from home. I can struggle with snap hooks so I use weight on the bottom near the toe to help that. Unfortunately the strips are too long for the spot on my driver. They hang over. Yes, a pair of scissors would be the ticket, but how many of us have a pair on the range or the first tee.

I also find that a half strip is the correct amount of weight to make adjustments. Again with the scissors.

Last, I'm not impressed with the adhesive. I did put it on a "used" club that hadn't been cleaned, but it wasn't in any way "dirty". Yet by the end of one round the edges were loose and starting to peel up.

Okay, I'm being picky, but I've used the 1/4" wide rolls in the past and had better luck. Just something to consider if you're looking for tape for your clubs.

title: Using it for rain barrel garden watering
text:
This is an interesting pump. It works really well, but there are some things to keep in mind.

First, it's a 1/2" line. In and out. Hooking it up to a 5/8" or 3/4" hose really cuts the pressure. However, put it on a 1/2" line (I used PEX) and the pressure is good.

Second, the NPT connections work really well, but you will need some adapters if you want to connect it to other things. There is a Garden hose threat adapter out there for a fair price. However, the barbed connector provided doesn't work well with PEX. There are PEX to NPT connectors easily available.

Third, you need a good, ridged intake pipe. I tried some clear poly tubing and it more or less collapsed as the intake. Of course that really cut down on the output.

So, with the correct adapters you can get it to work well for things other than campers. Just don't expect it to be "plug and play".

title: Filters well, just requires a good bit of water pressure
text:
I'm using this on my rain barrel pump for my garden watering. It does a nice job of filtering the water and by my testing doesn't affect the PH of the rain water.

The only negative, and unfortunately it's significant, is you really need a lot of water pressure. I've been using a 1000 gpm bilge pump, but that's not enough to get the water to do much more than trickle out of this filter. I've upgraded my pump and that definitely helped.

I'm sure it would do a great job on a standard home water line or even a camper hook up. It's just not the best option for my specific purpose.

title: Odd review, but some things to consider
text:
Let's start with the product quality. It appears to be very good. Well made, heavy materials, the resistance knob works well as does the line gasket. I'd say it's a good value for the price.

Next, let's talk about how it preforms. Okay, I didn't like it. Not because of the product, but due to my lack of skill. I'm attempting to make PR knots and had a real issue getting the tension right. Curls in the line because I had the tension too tight. Then knots that didn't hold because I had it too loose. I also got things tangled trying to spin it around the line and to be honest made a big mess of things. After several attempts I decided to give up.

If you want to experiment with various fishing knots this may be a good, inexpensive, way to try your hand at the techniques. However, plan on spending a lot of time and line perfecting things. It's a skill that takes plenty of time to master.

I'm not a saltwater fisherman. The heaviest line I use is #30 braid. Usually to #8-#12 leader material. I don't need a knot that holds hundreds of pounds. I'm sure if you do this is a good investment of time and money. I'll just stick with my improved Albright knot.

One last comment. I do use a wrap knot for 7 stand wire leaders on occasion. Forceps work well for that in the past, but I'm guessing this will make some really tight and clean wraps. Haven't tried it yet, but that could be the ticket.

title: Not prefect, but seems to work
text:
Out of the box/bag it is a bit stiff. It appears the plastic notch will wear with use, which means it will trigger easier (that's good), but wearing of the plastic parts means it will fail eventually.

As for the extended pole. It seems to be okay, but I sure wouldn't force the issue. Hollow tubing extended all the way out will lead to a broken pole I'm sure. I'm also betting it will rust from the inside out so be sure to get it dry between uses.

title: Smooth
text:
I'm not sure about longevity yet. I'll update if that turns out to be a problem. However, this is a very smooth. Even with a good fighting fish it remained smooth. I didn't have any issues casting it, but I've got several years of experience with bait casters. This one really isn't any different than ones I've used in the past regarding birds nests or casting. If you throw in to the wind and don't pay attention you'll get a mess - LOL!

The reason for the 4 star versus 5 is I thought castking reels came with an internal clutch. Pins to open or close based on your needs. This in addition to the magnetic clutch that can be adjusted on the outside. This model doesn't have that internal clutch.

The clutch being said, this is a good reel for a very good price. Quality is definitely there. As a guy who fishes 20-25 times a year for a variety of species (bass, walleye, crappie, pike), I recommend it. An affordable option for a good quality reel.

title: Nice towel, nice clip
text: It's a nice towel for the bag. Price isn't the best, but it is high quality

title: Okay, but not a lifelong item
text:
It works well for divot repair. The ball marker and holder are okay as well. It's not junk, but I've notices the hinge isn't solid when you use it and the magnet for the ball marker isn't very strong.

Again, it's not junk, but I'm guessing you'll get a season out of each one before it breaks.

title: Nice Brush, but not perfect
text: It's a nice brush, the point tool is one of the best I've used. The brushes are made of good materials. My only reason for not giving it a 5 is the simple fact the wire brush snags everything. Certainly not the only one with this issue. I just can't give it a 5 because of it.

title: They work and are comfortable
text: Definitely make it easier to grab the club in the rain. Fit nicely and although they do keep your hands warm, they don't get too hot in the summer. Definitely something every golfer should have in their bag.

title: It works well
text: Okay, it's not the bait for every fishing trip. No top water lure catches fish every day. However, this is a functional, durable and less expensive option. It gives the plop sound, casts a long distance, and runs true on retrieve. Not much more you could ask. Now it's up to the fish - LOL!

title: The glove is fine - sizing runs big
text:
I'm a cadet XL. At least that's what all the other gloves I buy are. However, these are definitely larger than the other brands. A full size, probably not. I can use them, but they don't start out tight on my hand and do slip as my hands get sweaty.

Comfort wise they are very nice. I really like that!

title: For the grandson and he hits it pretty well
text: There really isn't a brand war out there for youth clubs. There shouldn't be. However, the grandson hits this club pretty well and that's the pay off. Is it going 200 yards? No, but it's going towards the hole, in the air, and he's happy.

title: Grandson definitely improved
text:
My 11 year old grandson struggled with a combination of youth and smaller adult clubs. First time out the size of these clubs proved to be worth every penny. He not only missed the ball fewer swings, but hit the ball in the air. The excitement in his eyes was good to see. He didn't give up after 4 holes and actually wanted to play all 9.

I can't testify to these being better than other brands. I haven't compared that. However, if you have a youth golfer get them the set that fits their age. It will pay off.

title: Lid doesn't fit well, No T-Post adapter, Certainly not a $20 item
text:
Okay first, it holds corn and the deer will eat from it. So, as far as that goes it does what it says it will do.

Now the negatives.
The lid won't stay on. Poorly molded and cut. Mine actually had a piece of "dangling" plastic on it left over from the final trimming.
The description indicates it can be mounted on a T-Post. That's a positive as it reduces the problems with non-deer species getting on and into it. However, the T-Post mounting requires u-bolts, sold separately and there were no instructions with the unit. I had to go to the web site to find the information
It's a piece of poor quality control, mold formed plastic. No way it's a $20 item!

I bought 2 and I'm sure they will function. However, if I had touched one prior to ordering I wouldn't have.

title: Long Story, but I'm very happy
text:
The long story:
A few weeks ago I hit a ball OB and found a Srixon Q-Star Tour that wasn't mine in the area. I dropped it and used it the rest of the round. Very soft feel, distance was good, and it spun the way I expected. I went back to my usual ball, which I like a lot and still like a lot, but every once in a while I'd pull that Srixon out the bag and play a hole of two with it. That soft feel just kept bringing me back to hitting it. Well, I lost it in a pond on a good shot - LOL! - that the wind pushed too far right. So, I decided to buy some on Amazon.

Jump to today and I used one of them on my weekly league round. Well I shot my best score of the season, putted, chipped, drove, everything was better than typical. On top of that, I used the same ball, literally the same one, for all shots on all 18 holes. Something I never seems to accomplish in the past.

Now I understand there are a lot of factors involved. Most of which fall on my shoulders. However, I'm really having a hard time going back to my old ball now. Even though I really like them.

So, bottom line, they may not give you the best round of the season, but they do preform as well as any ball I've played (better today). The price is half the super premium balls. I'd suggest trying them.

title: Shad spinners
text: Berkley spinners work well and the design is very nice. These are shad design and there are, as always, times of the year when they attract plenty of fish. I guess you get what you pay for, but these are a little more expensive than others. Do they catch more fish than cheaper options? Not sure, but the design makes me more confident - LOL!

title: It works, but you have to be careful
text:
The size is very good and it fits over a twin bed well. The mesh keeps out your typical insects. The only negative is you have to be very careful setting it up. Tuck it under the mattress, bag, but leave some slop so it can shift a bit. If you make it too tight it will split and tear.

I recommend it, just be careful installing.

title: Beautiful blade and rig
text:
I needed some shad colored rigs and saw these. Wow! the blades are amazing. Haven't tried them on the water yet, but I'm confident they will work well for eyes.

I only wish they sold the blades alone so I could use them in my own, homemade rigs.

title: Works, but not perfect
text: It does work as described. I found it to be a little too big for my liking.

title: They do work
text:
First day of league and it was cold and rainy. I wore these the entire round. They fit well, are comfortable, and did help the grip on the club.

Obviously not something you would wear every round, but I would recommend them for those rainy days.

title: Just Okay
text:
It's not a bad brush, but it has some faults. First, the button opened up the brush on one of them, but the second one sticks at a 90 degree angle. Second, the brass portion of the brush is not very sturdy. One use and the sides are bent. Third, the groove pin is exposed when the brass brush bends. Meaning you really have to watch scratching the club with the pin.

It's inexpensive so I really wasn't expecting much, but it's not something I would purchase again.

title: No hole
text: I've tried every way possible, on both ends, it isn't hollow!

title: Exactly what it says it is
text:
Nothing much to say except it's exactly what is says it is.
For those looking for the inside diameter (I was) it's larger than 45 wire.

title: Pros and Cons
text:
The pros are the netting will keep mosquitoes and other small to large critters away. I'm sure the micro bugs can get through, but that's not realistic for something you can see through. Being able to see through it is the second pro. It's also lightweight and the hat is a good boonie style hat. The sizing is accurate and it fit as expected.

The cons are it's not well made. Strings hanging everywhere. Also, and most important, the brim of the hat isn't big enough to keep the net away from your nose and ears. Meaning it can collapse and allow bites through the mess on those areas. This is a big one for me.

I'd recommend another version or a netting with hoops to keep the mess away from your nose and ears.

I'll try it and try to remember to pull the mess away before I get bit.

title: Definitely one to consider
text:
Keep in mind I received it today and haven't used it much, but I did hit some side by side shots with my CG16 wedge of the same loft. Distance was virtually identical. I definitely saw the Tour launched the ball higher. I'm sure that's related to the spin increase compared to a 10 year old wedge. That being said, I certainly don't have any complaints.

I really like the grind. I was able to play with some knock downs from tight lies, hit full shots from the back and front of my stance, even hit a few wide open flops (yeah I know a 52 really isn't the club). In all cases I was able to make clean contact.

The feel isn't what I would call "pure", but it was fine. A bit clicky to me, but as far as my game goes I am not going to consider that a negative. Some more accomplished players may see that as a bad thing.

The lie isn't right for me, I seemed to pull most shots with a slight draw. The opposite of my current clubs as I normally fade them. We will see how that plays on the course, but that's on me, not the club.

Bottom line: Let's face it, a functional club for an extremely affordable price is something we all can use. This club fits the situation perfectly.

title: Made a mess
text:
Okay, no one can tell me sent catches more fish. I cant say I caught more by using this product, but as a buddy of mine says, "it doesn't hurt". So, I've used it a few times this early spring. I did catch fish with it applied to crankbaits. Others around me also caught fish and they weren't using it.

I used this and the stick version on the same fishing trip. This gel made a mess of things, but the stick did not. Will I use the gel again, maybe, but my first choice will be the stick.

title: It seems to help
text: I've always had an issue with my swing rhythm. After a few practice sessions this does seem to help. Hopefully it will translate to the golf course - if I can keep my old habits from coming back.

title: Okay, not particularly sharp and appear to be undersized
text:
Strong, eyes are shut (even though the pics show they are open), finish is good. However, the points are really not very sharp. Yes, they will catch fish out of the box, but in removing treble hooks a noticed the old trebles were sticking in my skin slightly. These hooks didn't do that. Obviously the hooks I'm replacing on a 3 year old crank-bait are sharper than these new hooks. Again, they are going to be sharp enough to catch fish, but I'm going to sharpen them to increase my percentages.

Also the sizing seems to be smaller than reported. I know there is only a recommendation on what a 2/0 hook size is, but these do appear to be about one size gap size under my other hooks. It may be the large eye I guess, but I would definitely plan to use the larger hooks before I use the smaller ones.

All in all though the kit is worth the price. A really good value. Just be aware of some of the things I found.

title: Recommended
text:
I've used the Norman version for years. I like these better in some ways, but not as well in others. First, the pros. The large version is in between the Norman sizes. It's really better for most of my needs. The material seems equal to or maybe a bit better than Norman. The chrome finish should make them last longer - in particular in salt water. Really equal in about every other area and less expensive.

The only con I really have is the "hook" are more curved making an oblong circle versus a round. This also creates a bit of a lip on each side. It very much could cause the lure or attached items to get sideways and perhaps come off. Haven't experienced that yet, but I've only had them for a day.

title: Just One thing - logo alignment
text:
First these are nice grips. Not a lot of bells and whistles, but that's exactly what I need. I don't impress my golf buddies with my grips - LOL! I guess your buddies might be different, but I probably wouldn't enjoy playing a round with them.

They fell nice and have a flat finish texture that do improve the grip. Not tacky, just plenty of friction without being over the top. Let's face it, even if you clean your grips the most expensive don't grip when your glove gets wet.

The price of course is fantastic. They wear just as long as premium brands, at least for me. So, re-grip every year at this price instead of trying to get two years out of premiums and you can see why these are a wise investment for me.

I install them myself, and have done about 10 - 15 installs over the years. Nothing unique about the process with these grips.

However, there is one thing that can drive some folks crazy. The name label and the alignment arrows aren't lined up on about 30 percent of the grips. The logo isn't always in the center of the area and the writing is crooked.

Now, I don't use the arrows or logo to line up the club. I look at the club face itself. Also only 1 out of 20 is off to the point that you notice it from more than 3 feet away anyway. I just want anyone looking to purchase to know these that perfect alignment isn't what you get for the price.

If you're looking for functional grips for an affordable price. These are your best choice. Especially if you do your own installation.

title: No complaints
text: I really don't have any complaints. I've hit balls off of it a couple of times and it's holding up well. It certainly seems worth the price.

title: Nice Sample Pack
text:
I wasn't sure which height or heights I would need. This variety pack was a good idea. Allowed me to try them.

The rubber is very soft, even in cooler weather. I'm not sure how long they will last, just got them.

title: Not sure about these - Hype?
text:
An odd review here. Not that I'm disappointed with the balls. They seem to be durable and functional. I just fail to see how they differ from other, less expensive, options. The reference to them having a harder outer coating seems to be subject to interpretation. They sure look and feel like some foam, dimpled, practice balls I bought several years ago. They do work with the R-Motion sensor (except the putter) and do reflect an actual golf ball shot (fade and draw). Again, I'm just not sure what makes them so "special", or expensive.

If you're looking for a long term practice ball I guess these are a good choice. Just beware the hype seems to be just that, hype.

title: Mixed Feelings
text:
First, it's definitely going to get me to practice more indoors over the winter.

The setup is relatively easy, the software installs without any major issues.

The Android software isn't accurate. I'm not sure I'll really use it in the future, but adjusting the "length" of the club I may get it to have some value. I've found that getting the yardage accurate via the club length settings greatly reduces the accuracy of the spin readings. Put the sensor length to the accurate distance and the spin reads accurately, but the distance is off. I can't seem to get it to read both correctly at the same time. Before you ask, yes I was at an outdoor range with accurate distance markers when I tested it. Every club was 20-30 yards short of "real" distance at the actual club length setting. Increase the length setting a couple of inches long and the yardage was really close, but fade shots were reading as draws, draws as slices, even when turned the sensor trying to trick it. Move the sensor back to the real length the draws show as drawing and the fades as fading, but the yardage is back to short.

The TGC software is much more accurate and does allow for an enjoyable playing option. Playing with the length is needed, but it does show fades and draws pretty well. It does take some practice with putter though. I do use it on an older computer with the low graphics setting. It works just fine.

Probably the biggest issue is the club clamp. I purchased the option with only one and it's definitely a pain switching it from club to club. I tried the poster tack and it does work as long as it's relatively warm. Temps below 50 and it isn't sticky any more. If you have a range in the house it will work, but if you are in the garage (like me) after 3 to 4 shots you have to warm it up or it comes off the club and goes down range. I almost lost it at the local driving range. The cost of the OEM clamps are well out of my range, but I did find an option on ebay, but haven't used them yet. I'll update if these seem to be a viable option.

Overall it's worth the cost and as mentioned should help me improve my game. Experience is the best teacher so play with the length and software options. I'm sure you'll find it's worth the time.

title: Inpressed
text: Okay, Titleist is known for above average quality. That definitely true here. Includes the "sweat pad" above the bill, nice strap adjustment, and the ball marker magnet is really convenient. I've only worn it for one round, but I'm sure it will hold up. The only question is washing the hat. The magnet inside the bill is a concern. I'll update the review when I've experimented with that.

title: Nice value
text:
Good value, this is what I call a low rise hat. Not for everyone, but I like this style.

No issue with the fit or adjustments.

They are closed material so if cool is your first priority I'd recommend another option. However it's a good choice for the typical temperature I golf in.

title: Football Official - Recommended - But
text:
I'm a finger whistle football official and have used the fox 40 finger whistles for decades. I have worked all positions and found them to be very effective. The older version had a plastic liner on the finger holder. That made it very easy to put the whistle in your mouth and pull your fingers out. That way you can use both hands and arms to give signals while holding the whistle with your teeth. These on the other hand have a rubber liner on the finger holder. It is much more secure and much more difficult to pull off your fingers. That's a plus in some situations, but a negative if you need both hands to signal. I'm sure I'll figure out a way to get my fingers out of the holder when needed, but I think I prefer the plastic versus the rubber.

Top quality as always with Fox. The only whistle I'll ever use!

title: Basic, but full of features
text:
Just a basic unit but packed full of features. A must for any reloader! Highly recommended.

I will say I had some issues with my tablet. It's an older one and I just don't think it is up to date enough to work. Customer support was quick to respond with some suggestions, but it just won't pick up the reading. My phone does a great job though.

title: Quality and Price - wise choice
text:
I do a good bit of fishing, 2-3 times a week, so I go through a good bit of tackle. It's a hobby, not a profession, so if you're next paycheck of meal depends on your tackle you may want to spend more money on a named brand, but I'd suggest it not wise. These are a good quality swivel at a very affordable price. The issues mentioned in other reviews about missing parts or breaking don't apply to the ones I received. I use 6-8 pound test line for almost all my fishing (Pike, Walleye, Crappie, Perch, etc.) so if a #35 pound swivel pulls apart at 20 pounds I'll never know.

Consider you needs, typical line weight for example, when deciding which size to order, but there's no need to go overboard.

Bottom line, these are a wise choice for any fisherman any species.

title: Check the measurements on the XL bag
text:
The bag overall is nice. Lightweight, comfortable, perfect for summer camping.

However, be aware that the measurements includes the "hood". The length of the bag is 75" not the 80+ indicated. Certainly long enough for my 6'2" size, but those 6'5" and taller may find it a bit short.

title: Sturdy, Heavy
text: Nothing really negative, just heavier than I expected.

title: Strong and Sharp
text: These are nice strong and sharp hooks. Not sure what else needs to be said.

title: Good, but the metal covering does wear off
text:
I've used Lindy metallic beads for years. Very consistent, but the metallic covering does wear off rather quickly. It's not from the fish catching, although they do help you catch fish, it's from the rubbing other beads in the line. Fortunately this wearing is between the beads and doesn't affect the reflection on the "body" of the bead.

That being said, I recommend them.

title: Pros and cons
text:
Overall they are worth the purchase price. However there are some cons, listed below, that you should consider.

Pros: They are functional to a point. They seem to be well built. I used them on a recent fishing fly-in fishing trip to handle a variety of fishing tasks and they did not bend of fail to operate at any time. The pouch is convenient.

Cons: The split ring "nose" on the end makes it difficult to remove hooks when the fish has swallowed the bait. It actually causes additional damage as you have to push the tip in further to get the second side engaged with the hook. As mentioned the pouch is convenient, but the retention strap causes more issues then benefits. I found I had better luck leaving them outside the pouch while seated in the boat and across my leg. Then when I left the boat I put it back in the pouch and messed with the retention strap.

Is the tool overall useful? Yes, and for the price it's a good idea to have on hand while on the water. Can improvements be made - absolutely!

title: Nice, but quality control an issue
text:
Well made, sharp, seem to be a good bargain.

Several of the hooks are unusable due to manufacturing shortfalls. Primarily the eyes are closed or closed incorrectly.

Still worth the price, but if you need the entire 100 hooks you should order a second bag.

title: Okay, but not perfect
text:
For the most part these are nice hooks. They are sharp, the metal is strong and although others report they break I haven't found that to be the case. I really like the position of the bait holder barbs. Plenty of room to snell the line yet they hold the worm pretty well.

On the down side, the quality control is a bit lacking. Several of the hooks are just fine, but some have eyes where the tag end is sticking up and even sharp. I can't use these for fear of the line being cut by the eye. That being said, I'm guessing 15-20 of the hooks had some type of defect. So, consider you're getting 100 very usable hooks and this is still an affordable option.

Additional information - I found these do set themselves in the fish's mouth, but I also found they seem to tear the area more than other hooks. My experience is they seem to find the soft spot in the mouth of a walleye. It's more the size of the hook versus a poor design. Bottom line, I'd recommend going up a size (4 to 2) for walleye just so the hook catches deeper in the mouth.

title: Great option for repairs
text:
I've used West marine in the past without any real issues. This "Kit" is a great way to keep up on repairs and for a final finish coat. I've just done a couple of small things with it, but it mixes well. I really like the clear finish and no blush.

Recommended for those starting out with epoxy and for those who need a small kit for repairs.

The cost is really low compared to all the things you get. Definitely a good buy!

title: Does what it says, but not easy to use
text: I've loaded information from two of my favorite fishing areas. Getting it to show on the software correctly and then converting it to a map isn't the most user friendly. However, once you've figured it out the results are amazing. Still working on some of the bells and whistles though.

title: Heavy Duty
text: These are heavy duty hooks. Very strong and heavy wire. Good choice for situations that would dictate that. The points are sharp.

title: Sharp and straight
text: Work well for all the things I use it for. They are sharp and straight.

title: Replaced a roller - good choice
text: Haven't used these before but I needed to replace a troublesome roller so I gave them a try. They work very well!

title: Seem to be a good product
text: Haven't fought the "big one" yet, but they seem to be made well.

title: Expensive, but great results every time
text: I used this on my boat 6 years ago. I had to do some repairs and needed a small can to paint over the patches. Bottom line I've put several coats over the years and never had a bad result. Perfect for wooden boat hulls and it holds up very well.

title: Red or Black - Test them both and see which works for you
text:
I've used both the red and black now. I would have to say the red is better for hard, Florida style, courses. I used them in Florida this winter and was very impressed. The black is better for the northern (midwest) style courses. I've played on the soft early spring in Ohio and liked the black better. Without getting in to the technology (plenty of that available from the experts), let's just say I found the red held the greens better, but lacked a little ball flight. The black held soft greens very well and seemed to have more flight distance. As the summer heat dries out the local courses I'll switch back to the red, but early season the black is the better choice.

Bottom line, I suggest buying both red and black and use the better of the two depending on the course conditions.

Both are soft, bounce off the club face, hold the line, but can be worked (fade of draw) as well as any ball I've played. I'm a 10-12 handicapper so I'm not a "pro", but I'm planning to buy more later in the season. I'm very happy with them!

title: Impressed
text: Very strong, and the points are incredibly sharp! Definitely something I'll look for in the future!

title: They work
text:
They work well and have a lot of advantage for ice fishing. I'm going to try them from spring crappie as well and I'm sure they will work for that.
The only negative is the price. Not the most expensive materials, but bobbers are expensive for some unexplained reason.

title: They work as described
text:
They work well and have a lot of advantage for ice fishing. I'm going to try them from spring crappie as well and I'm sure they will work for that.
The only negative is the price. Not the most expensive materials, but bobbers are expensive for some unexplained reason.

title: Good investment
text: Definitely a value. They are well built, although small. Perfect for grub tails and various small plastics. The thin wire is just right for running through the hook eye. They hold well.

title: Well built, Strong
text:
These are definitely for large use. Well built, strong, long spiral. Should hold large swim baits well.
Keep in mind they don't have a section to secure about the hook eye.

title: Color comes off while spooling
text:
I haven't tested the strength yet, but when spooling it I hold it between my fingers for mild tension. The black in particular comes off on your fingers. Sticky, messy stuff. I contains some fibers as well and is a pain to get off the line as it balls up.

If the color wears fast I'll update the review, but at this point I can't give it more than 3 stars.

title: For magnet fishing - seems to work fine
text: I bought it for my magnet fishing magnet. It seems to work just fine.

title: Work, yes - Longevity, below average
text:
I bought 3 of these primarily because of price. I found they were a bit tight. That may lend itself to the wear problem I experience, but they did stretch to fit after a few holes of play. The issue is they seem thin and show signs of wear after one round. Still useful after 4 rounds, but based on what I see I'm not expected much more than 10 rounds before they start wearing through.

Good value for the price, yes, I think so. However, if you play 2-3 rounds a week I'd suggest looking elsewhere or plan on buying several of them to last you the season.

title: Perfect for panfish in ponds
text:
I've used this line in the past and didn't realize how nice it was until I tried a different variety. I'll only use it from now on!

Line doesn't retain memory, is smooth, doesn't accumulate ice. Just the right line for panfish in farm ponds. Highly recommended, at least for that use!

title: Small
text:
I don't really think these are truly for men. The temples are very short and extremely tight. Not something I could wear for any substantial time.

The lens do block the sun so if your looking for frames that are smaller than what an average man would wear these may be a good choice.

title: Nice
text: I've struggled for years cutting leader wire. These are exactly the right tool for that job. Haven't used them on anything larger than 40 pound sevenstrand wire, but it cuts it like butter. I'm sure it will handle much larger cable.

title: Perfect for fishing wire leaders
text: Using on sevenstrand wire for pike leader crimping. Definitely like the dimpled design it leaves. Price was excellent, good quality. Not sure they are suited for outdoor use though. I'm sure they will rust if left in the rain/salt water. Keep them inside or in a dry spot on the boat and I'm sure they will last for years.

title: Fit my old style FootJoy shoes!
text: Definitely extended the life of a good pair of FootJoy shoes. They fit the large screw in holes and are a good match for my use. Almost threw them away out of frustration.

title: It works
text:
What can you say about a pump replacement? Did it work, yes. Did it fit, yes. How long did it last, don't know yet- but it made it through the first season without any issues.

I'd buy it again. The price if good and it seems to be a quality replacement.

title: Wise option
text:
I've tied the cheap route and the hose split, broke, wasn't worth the cost. I've had this hose on another boat for years without any issue.

Bottom line, just pay the higher price for this hose. It's definitely worth the extra cost and it will pay for itself many times over.

title: Certainly worth every penny! If you need them, buy them.
text:
First, these are top quality hooks. True Mustad quality. Bait keeper barbs are good.
The only issue (loss of one star) is they really are a bit off color gold. Not something you would notice unless you have them side by side with other brands, but it's just a bit less of the pure gold color.

Will the fish notice? Probably not. In fact I'm certain it won't affect my catch numbers. Just something I noticed right away.

Certainly worth every penny! If you need them, buy them.

title: Amazon price makes them worth it - they do what they claim
text:
I've used these weights off and on for several years. The price is the only reason they aren't my exclusive weights. However, the amazon price is reasonable so I bought several to stock up.

They are almost snag proof. There is always that rare situation where the bottom wins.

title: A must for any fisherman
text:
Replaced an existing box that just wore out. Had that one for many years.
Much better than the Styrofoam boxes. The worms actually stay in this box instead of trying to crawl out.
Holds 4-6 dozen without any problem. May hold more, I've just never used it for more than that.

title: Recommended
text:
A fellow golfer pulled out a drizzle stik this week during league play. I had to fight my big umbrella the entire time and he didn't have any problems. So, I went looking for one. I found the "drape" version and believed it was a better idea. It is. The stik isn't as long and doesn't cover as well as the drape. Haven't had to use it in a rain storm yet, but I've dry fitted it on my bag and I'm definitely happy with it. Just one reason I didn't give it 5 stars. With my long shaft driver it just barely covers the edge of the bag in that area. Again it does cover the edge of the bag, but just barely. It will keep the rain out and it covers the other clubs with plenty of spare hang over. I'm just concerned the wind might flap it up near the driver.

Convenient, functional, nice idea. I recommend it.

title: Cool, but no sweat absorbing
text:
First of all I hate the hot weather. A midwest guy who would rather experience the 20's than the 80's. So, if you're not the same way move on to the next review - LOL!

If you are like me you want some sweat absorbing properties. This hat is weak in that area.

Cool, air flow is good, but not much to keep the sweat out of your eyes when the humidity is high.

FYI, the Litetech version is better at absorbing sweat, but still not as good as regular twill material.

title: Cool, good air flow, not much sweat absorbing
text:
First of all I hate the hot weather. A midwest guy who would rather experience the 20's than the 80's. So, if you're not the same way move on to the next review - LOL!

If you are like me you want some sweat absorbing properties. This hat is weak in that area.

Cool, air flow is good, but not much to keep the sweat out of your eyes when the humidity is high.

title: Unit it fine, template not so much
text:
The unit itself appears well made. Yet to test in the water, but based on reviews and past experience it should do just fine.

The 4 instead of 5 stars is due to the mounting template. It's very thin and is difficult to handle. I know it's a one time use item, but adding even a little more weight and rigidity to it would make it much easier to use. The markings and measuring units on the side and bottom are top notch. Just making it 60 pound versus 32/40 pound paper would do wonders.

title: Update- not worth it
text:
Nice unit. Everything was in place and works well.

Update the hose is crumbling. It actually broke about 3 inches from the connection. It wasn't in the sun, get in the garage. Avoid buying this system. It isn't worth it at any price.

title: No hole shot or speed improvement - Shattered!
text:
First, I owned one of these for about 8 years. I never did increase the time to get on plane, it didn't increase speed. I changed props, using three different ones in my Yamaha 15 HP motor on my 15' aluminum boat.

Second, it did reduce porpoising. That's all!

Last, it shattered! It was in winter storage and the weather was cold, but it literally broke in to dozens of pieces falling from a standing position to stone floor. It was on it's skag, not on a hanger or any distance off the ground. Ground was probably frozen, but come on......

title: ProV1X clone, yes - I'd say they are
text:
Interesting golf ball. Remind me a lot of the old "Snake Eye" golf balls, which I liked a lot.

They do have a click when hit, but feel relatively soft. The Pro Plus click is a slightly different click. Not louder, more a different sound.

Trajectory is typical of other premium golf balls. At least for me there's no difference. The Pro Plus seems slightly lower, but marginally so.

Distance is the same as other premium balls as well. The Pro Plus seems to roll a bit more due to the marginally lower trajectory - 2-3 yards is all.

Spin is noticeable with shorter irons. Drives seem to be lower spin - as advertised.

Are they a ProV1 clone, I would say yes. Thus, I'll buy some more and probably order more than one dozen to get the discounted price from Vice.

I also bought Pro balls and like the Pro Plus a little better, but that's a personal thing. I wouldn't hesitate to use either every round.

Regardless of Pro or Pro Plus, I definitely think you get the same ball for much less.

title: ProV1 Clone - Yes I think think so - Update: Cover does knick
text:

First one I thought it was just a small rock I couldn't see, but after 3 did it over 2 different rounds I'm convinced it's the cover and not the situation. All that being said, I'm also more convinced it's just as good a ProV1 otherwise. I'll definitely consider buying them again. Just keep a spare in my pocket for when the cover gets knicked.

title: Good product, just not what I needed
text:
First, the item itself isn't an issue. It's exactly what I ordered and exactly what was described.

Unfortunately, it isn't what I needed. I wanted something to wrap around hooks to keep lures and baits on the bottom. This wire is very flexible, good quality, etc. I just needed more weight (diameter).

I'm sure it works very well for tying flies and what it's designed to do.

All that being said, I'm going to keep it. I'll have to wrap a lot more times, but it will eventually have enough weight to serve my needs.

title: Line is good, spool stinks
text:
This is good line. Has all the positives of the brand named braided lines. Color does come off on your fingers, but not too badly.
The only negative is there's a notch in both ends of the spool lip. Meaning, you can't stand the spool on end on the floor and load up a spinning reel. It keep popping off the ground and bouncing around.

Fix this spool design issue and you've got a 5 star product.

title: Functional, but wish the smaller diameter was just as cost effective
text:
I like this product. The only reason it's not 5 stars is the extra cost for the smaller diameter version. This is just a bit too large, functional, but the next size smaller was about 50% more. Same overall weight.

I've used it to wrap around hooks and it does work well. By my scale, 1 1/2" equals 1/8 oz. at least close enough to that for my needs.

title: Perfect Cadet Fit - Great Glove
text:
I've used these before and really liked the feel and durability. Two lasted me all last season and one could be used to start this year. They don't dry out and get stiff like others I've used.

Perhaps most important, the cadet XL fits my hand perfectly. Some out there don't. The fingers are the right length and size and the width across the palm is definitely wider than standard.

I'll definitely buy these again in the future.

title: Mother recommended
text: Bought these for my mother. She used to play a lot and this was the only ball she ever really knew about. In other words, she could see and feel the difference. So, she now has a new dozen to use!

title: Work well and are sharp
text: As described, these are sharp hooks. They do spin the worm on the bottom bouncer rigs I use. Only one suggestion for improvement - bend the eye up or down. That would definitely help with tying a snell knot.

title: Great hooks, couple of negatives
text:
First let me say I really like these hooks. They do increase the action of the worm on my bottom bouncer rigs. The hooks are sharp and although thin are strong. I would say they need to be in everyone's tackle box.

The negatives - first with the swivel it's hard to get the worm on the hook all the way up. Just about the time you get it started (which isn't difficult) and adjust you grip to push it up the hook the darn thing swivels on you. Not impossible, but frustrating at times. Second, these darn things are expensive! Enough said.

title: Worked best for me
text: I've used several different connectors over the years. This one sure worked out the best for me. Fit the threads snug. You can turn it vertical versus horizontal. It fits the female connector well, but it isn't difficult to put on or remove.

title: Well Made
text: Definitely the hand tool to use. Well made,works well. Multiple uses. A must have for any rifle reloader! Highly recommended!

title: Interesting
text:
This camo pattern is interest. Probably not the best choice for making pike leaders.The colors change every foot or so. Meaning the 12 inch leaders are all the same color.

Seems to be very good line though. I just picked the wrong color for my needs.

title: Simple, works for me
text:
Reading the reviews I had mixed feelings about ordering it, but I'm not finding any of the issues by the negative reviews. I did do the firmware update, loaded local courses, followed the instructions (I know...) and it hasn't missed a distance yet. Haven't tested the shot function yet.

If you are looking for yardage to the green and trouble it seems to be the tool. If you want a picture of the hole it's not there - buy one for double or triple the price.

title: Stretch to fit well, for cooler temps
text:
Well made, played a couple of rounds and been to the range once. No issues with the material tearing. They do run small (tight), but they stretch out to form fit after a little bit of time. They actually end up fitting very well.

The missing start is because they are all weather. If you're looking for a cool summer glove these aren't the ticket. However, for early season golf they are perfect.

title: It works
text:
Not to down play the importance of a charge controller, but this is a cable. How complicated can it be?

Regardless, the cable did work and charges the unit. I've installed a USB 2 unit in my boat and of course I have a plug in in the car. I should be good to go for the season.

title: Glad I bought it!
text:
I haven't done any serious tugging yet, so I can't testify to the strength of the tip. However, I used a small tube cutter to cut to size and the tip seems snug enough to hold up well. It took a good bit of force to get the tip in place.

I have it on my TC Renegade (1990's version) and it fits perfectly! The "T" handle will definitely come in handy. All my accessories threads fit without any issue. So if they fit the original rod they will fit this unit.

title: Not difficult to install and works as advertised!
text: Although not on the lake with this yet, testing shows it will work very well. The installation was straight forward. Running the network cable was the most difficult part. Also be sure to register the units (sonar and link) on Humminbird.com. There are a number of firmware updates. The updates went in pretty easy and without loss of data. Back it up though just to be safe.

title: does the job
text: Well constructed does the job well

title: Could be less shiny
text: Sturdy, swivel well, not particularly "black" though. A little more reflective than I like, but function very well

title: It measures fish
text: Not particular complex, adhesive is good. The numbers will eventually wear out, but nothing you can do about that

title: Breaks on hook set
text:
No real complaints. It's just a bit stiffer than others. I suspect that translates to better abrasion resistance, but it's too early to confirm that. I'll buy again in other weights and use for leader material if that holds true. I can put up with the stiffness at the cheaper price.

Update - used it this spring walleye/saugeye fishing. It is very much invisible and incredibly thin, but the abrasion resistance is well below average. I have used 6 pound mono (cabela's Pro Line) for years and never had a break off setting the hook on a fish. I've had 3 break off the past two trips! Not at the knot, above the knot on the main section of the line. Is this less shock resistance, who knows? All I can say is it's no longer on my reels. I may try it again in next spring on my crappie - bobber rod, but it won't see another walleye/saugeye trip.

title: High quality - not cheap
text: Very good wire! Very high quality. Of course it isn't cheap. I used it on my boat, but only the circuit boxes. I couldn't afford it for all the wiring.

title: Very nice
text: Exactly what I ordered. Only concern is the line diameter it fits. Will follow up if there's a problem, but until then assume they worked perfectly.

title: Excellent quality
text: High quality wire, flexible, good insulation, easy work with. Recommended. I just wish it wasn't so darn expensive - but this is the lowest price I could find.

title: Well constructed, seals well
text: Used it for an circuit box on my boat. Well constructed, seals well. Watch the color though, it's not exactly as shown.

title: A little heavier than EC
text: Heavier than the Eagle Claw of the same design. Haven't fished with them yet, but they work well in my Do-It molds as a EC 570 substitute.

title: Perfect Solution for Boat wiring
text: Perfect solution for all my boat devices. It just makes sense and cuts down on the clutter.

title: Worth it, but not perfect

title: Great Ride - no helmet required!
text: Purchased in October.  Already "ridden" 180 miles.  On line tool for calorie calculations, but really I ride to get some movement - keep my brain energized and not simply sit all day at my desk.  While working (conference calls or doing email) I am able to pedal on level three or four and can still type easily.  Beyond level 4 - it gets a bit trickier, but I"m assuming with practice I might be able to continue to crank up the resistance and still work without too many typos!  It does take a little time (couple of days) to get used to peddling and working, versus simply stopping working and only peddling!  Super quiet and reverse is nice to stretch for a moment or two.  35 miles is the most I've done in any one sitting.  I use a three legged stool that converts into a walking stick - think a "cane" with a handle and a fold out seat.  I like it as it doesn't slide and allows plenty of room for my knees and the proper angle for heels etc...  on days when I know I have several hours of back to back calls, I actually wear padded bike shorts as the seat on the stool is hard plastic and pretty darn close to the discomfort of an actual long bike ride!

title: Fits a Toyota Tacoma Pre-Runner
text: After days of research (!) I decided to order this product.  I don't think I would have chosen this product it had been from a company other than Thule, Yakima, Saris, Hollywood etc... i.e. it needed to be backed by a company with market share as the concept is unique.  Installation was a breeze.  I was a bit worried when I first used it and found that my front tire sits up on the cross piece in a small "v" - but my concern went away after the first trip and I've not thought about it again after 15+ trips.  My bike is a Giant Hybrid (small frame).  The product shipped very quickly and the materials are quality.  Yes once you open the tail gate the bike does require you to use one hand to stabilize it, but thanks to other reviewers I was prepared and hopefully I'm preparing the next readers!  I am able to lock the bike to the rack and the rack to the truck and when I'm on the trail the rack folds down small enough I simply toss in the front floor board of the cab.  I've had to stop once and tighten it as I was traveling down a washed out "road" with deep ruts.  I looked in the rear view mirror and saw my front tire just beginning to move.  It could have been from the deep ruts or I simply didn't get the required "two clicks" tension.  Highway speeds have proven no issue.  I like the fact that my license plate and tail lights are not obstructed as with a more traditional rack and certainly nothing is sticking out beyond the width of my vehicle. 9/5/22 update: the bail is an absolute failure. the design has a semi sharp edge which like to catch and cut 30lb braid instead of allowing it to go on to the roller. I have never in my life used a worse designed reel between the bail, bad antireverse, bad handle. I tried the Kastking hype, had my doubts, checked for myself, and found the reels to be complete rubbish - went down to 1 star with the bail. // concept, failure in design and manufacturing. Kastking has potential, not there yet for anything close to salt water. Handle and anti reverse are the issues. For starters more of an fyi - the Megatron 6000 is about in between a 4000 and 5000 reel. I have a pic attached showing Megatron 6000, Penn Spinfisher V 4500 and a Penn Sargus 5000. The handle is about same length as the 4500 reel.

Ok for the bad. The handle screw and attachment is asking to be broke - weak flimsy and not designed well at all - even compared to Cabelas branded reels. The anti reverse is cheap plastic and far to much gap for salt water to enter. Kastking - please dump the anti reverse as it is weak and allows salt water to enter (like penn/pfleauger sargus/battle removed the switch); improve the handle attachment; use better quality springs that will not rust. I did open it and grease will penn reel grease and abu garcia oil which is how I know the anti reverse and switch is, to be blunt - trash. The handle is held on by a nut with barely any threads and has far too much flex - very bad. yes you fight fish with the pole and the reel is line holder - but your reeling constantly with luers/jigs and it needs to have stronger threads than it exists today. The internal springs with the huge hole on the anti reverse switch are very bad - too weak and wrong metal - heck I have rebuilt 1950's squiiders and they even used stainless springs or older versions brass leaf springs. I wanted to see the reel for myself and inspect it. with these two serious flaws your better going with A penn wraith/persiuit or a daiwa in same price point.
I would love to see kastking address the spring metal, anti reverse weakness/hole and a better handle then go from there. There is potential, but these cheap decisions listed above makes the reel seriously flawed.

title: 3 flaws on of which is dangerous!! Must read
text:
Three flaws and one of them is dangerous!
1. The factory pins fall out, and when lost the stove is useless unless you have something to replace the pins with. This could be a real big problem when your camping or survivalist situation.
FIX: use Bobby pins to replace the factory pins. the ribbed design of the Bobby pins cause a tight feel when slid into the hinges of the stove. When fully assembled it feels very sturdy opposed to using a loose fitting pin that gives the stove a "flimsy feel".
2. The spirit burner plate does not fit any spirit burner I have. My trangia burner gets stuck half way in and scrapes the sides of burner pretty badly. It only needs to be a few centimeters larger, but won't fit the largest brand of spirit burners made (trangia).
FIX: take the sand paper provided with the stove to widen the spirit burner plate. This will allow the trangia burner to fit perfectly
3. THIS IS THE DANGEROUS FLAW
If you place a weighted cup on the top it tends to force the sides outward slightly. This can lead to the spirit burner plate falling down and spilling burning liquid. I used the Stanley field cup, and a few different other stainless cups with the same results. The spirit burner plate needs longer tabs so there is no risk of it falling in anyway shape or form. Each side needs to be 1/4" longer or have bent tabs to lock into place. Burning sticks is about the only purpose this stove has safely..
FIX: buy something safer for liquid fuel burning, otherwise small stick burning only!!
