title: I LOVE this treadmill!
text:
I ordered this treadmill from Amazon.com. We put it together yesterday, it was fairly easy to put together, but it is HEAVY! Be sure you have more than one person to help get it inside and get it out of the box.

I absolutely love it already and I am so glad I made the choice to go with this particular treadmill. I did my research for quite a while before I made my decision. Being that it did not have one single negative review on Amazon, helped to seal the deal for me as I know that the people giving these reviews are the ones actually using it and not just some so-called "expert" giving their opinion, but not really using it.

It is very user-friendly, with good sized digital readouts making it so easy. The thing I love the most about it, is that it is so unbelievably quiet! I kept reading that in other people's reviews, but I didn't really think it would be as quiet as it really is! I have it positioned in front of my big screen TV and I didn't even have to turn the volume up to screaming mode to hear it! Last night I worked out on it for an hour and 15 minutes while I watched some of my DVR'd shows and I hardly even noticed that I was working out because it was so quiet and I was absorbed into my TV show. It is just fabulous! I love the magazine/book holder on the dash too, as that has always been my biggest complaints about other treadmills. I love to read while I am working out and this gives me the opportunity to do so without holding on to anything! I also love the i-pod hookup, that is another nice bonus!

I also LOVE the pause feature! On my old treadmill, if I had to stop for any reason, I lost all my settings (time, speed, etc.) and had to start all over. With this one, you just hit the stop button and it pauses right in the middle of your workout... you go do whatever and come back and hit start and it picks right back up on the time you had already completed and goes right back to the speed you were at.

Another great feature is the countdown. When you start the treadmill, it starts "counting down" to let you know it is going to slowly start. It doesn't just catch you off guard and start suddenly! I love that. This treadmill really has it all for a fabulous price!

The one and only complaint I have about it thus far is that it does not turn off on the dash! This is a bit puzzling to me, I have no clue why the engineers would not put the on/off switch on the dash! That is the first time I have ever seen that on a treadmill. You either have to unplug it or turn it off by the switch on the front of the belt down by the floor. Very odd to me. Overall, I highly recommend this treadmill! I do not think you can go wrong with this purchase!

UPDATE: A year and a half later, I still love this treadmill!! If you are like me, you realize that most people review items within days of receiving it and therefore you do not get the review from "tried and true" usage, so I wanted to add my year and a half later update that it is still wonderful and I have not had one single problem from it!! I still highly recommend it!

title: Good survival bag, ok price.
text: Feels like a Mylar blanket with a very heavy duty plastic trash bag fused together to form an enclosed bag with an opening large enough to fit in.  I unrolled one to try out.  At 5’10” and 220 lbs, I could fit in it and had a bit of room to move around.  If you are over 6 feet tall you will have a difficult time stretching out to full length.  It appears to be rugged enough for more than one use, and can with some difficulty be re folded to fit in the nylon storage bag.  It comes with a cheep but useful survival whistle, and a plastic toy like useless compass- (a gum ball machine button compass would be more useful).  Overall this survival bag will find a place in my 72hr. Pack.

title: This Digital night vision is no better (and maybe worse than)  Gen 1 light amplification units.
text: I bought this based on an outside recommendation (YouTube) review and took a chance.  It does work ok with the I/R illuminater active and useless (at night) without.  The viewing screen is extremely bright and makes this unit almost useless as a night security tool (it backlights the user). If their is a way to adjust the brightness level of the screen display I did not find it.  I had no use for the digital photo or recording features.  Overall it’s night vision capabilities are less then my 10+ year old bushnell gen 1 night vision monocular.  Back to Amazon it goes.  Someday I’ll stop expecting these low cost night vision devices to be on par with Gen 3 units costing $1000’s.

title: Exceptional pocket/duty light for the price. UPDATE; 1 year in and adding a star!
text: While I try to avoid MADE IN CHINA for critical items, this product does seem to be an exception.  As I’m typing this on an iPad quality products can be produced in China.  I chose this model because a few co workers have been using Fenix lights for over a year without any problems.  The feature that sold me on this model was the side button that allows the user to select the light output mode while the tail cap is ONLY for on\off function.  I also really like the recharging capability using a USB port and the option of two cr123’s as an emergency backup.  It’s pocket clip works well with blue jeans or 5-11 front pocket carry.  As to long term durability we will see, however this light does seem to be well constructed.  4 stars with about a month of service- if it holds up I’ll give it 5. UPDATE 05/2022: 1 year of use and this item has held up extremely well.  Factory battery still holds a charge as well as it did when new.  This is a 5 Star item!

The plastic used in the construction seems almost toy like, and I have serious doubts if it could hold up to ANY rough field use.  I remember buying these as a kid in the 1980's from military surplus stores, while these were probably not actual gi issue they were constructed with vastly superior materials.

title: Best, least expensive knife for the money!!!
text: I have heard about these knives for many years, but never purchased one.  I was looking for an inexpensive backup knife, and ordered one of these.  The knife, out of the box is really sharp, and has a very good cutting edge.  The sheath feels  very cheep, but does it's job, and is functional.  After using much more expensive knives (Buck, Gerber, SOG) this knife is ultra light, but effective enough for most outdoor activities.  I plan on purchasing a half dozen more of these pure WORK knives in the future for all of my vehicles, and emergency bags.  For under $20 you get a solid working/outdoorsmen knife that you will not be afraid to USE.

title: Good durable compact unit with many useful features
text: I was looking to purchase a new unit for sometime.  My previous unit was a Bushnell from the early 90's, and it delivered faithful service for almost 20 years.  It finally died, so I began to look for a good replacement.  This product has a backlit feature that really helps in either bright, or low light situations.  On large objects, (A surrounding hillside) I was able to get it to range out to 1200+ yards repeatedly.  The compact size and power of this unit is a major step up from my 1st generation unit.  I will have to see as to long term durability, but the case housing feels solid, and it has survived a few outings into the High Desert summer time extreme temperatures (115'+).  It comes with a fairly useful carrying case with a magnetic closure, and a rather complicated carrying strap I found to be useless.  The directions are straight forward, and the ACR (Angle Range Compensation) feature does work,  is not TOO complicated and has been useful in my target shooting.  I do not give this product 5 stars because I have not had it long enough to determine it's long term durability.

title: Don't let the NcStar name cause you to overlook this product
text: I usually completely discount any product from NcStar, Leapers, UTG, exc.  as chi-com junk.  I was directed to this product by a shoot'n buddy from back east.  On his recommendation,  the low cost, and some internet research I bought one with moderately low expectations.  I was very surprised at the construction level of this product, along with the myriad of special features.  It can be configured as a standard padded rifle case, a very comfortable backpack (w/ an adjustable  shoulder straps and waist belt that tucks away when not in use) and a reasonably comfortable shooting mat.  I have used this in the field for target shooting in our regional Hi Desert for about a year, and one successful mountain hunt.  So far it has held up well, and done everything advertised.  I would not recommend this for our boys deploying to any 'stans or sandboxes, but that is not what this bag is for. Those out for a day of target practice or limited to a few days in the hunting field and want a quality rifle case/backpack/shooting mat that does not cost $200+ will be hard pressed to improve on this bag.

title: Solid LED Flashlight for a good price.
text: I purchased this item for an emergency kit I was preparing for family members.  I wanted a durable AA cell light that would not cost a lot of $.  This Energizer light is of a decent size-not so small to be easily fumbled, and not to large it takes up valuable space in an emergency kit.  I cannot attest to long term durability, but it appears to be of  decently rugged construction, and throws a good amount of light. This package also comes with 4 Energenizer brand AA batteries.  I can recommend this product for any emergency kit or  for general home use.

title: Decent quality for a cheep price
text: I  purchased these to add to a number of emergency kits for the family.  The 10 blankets I received were from Everdixie USA EMS Supply Company, and made in China. All were packed in individual zip lock style bags.  Unfolding the Mylar blankets, I noticed they were of thin material, but held up to a test session during a cold evening in the Southwestern High Desert in late fall.  It did what it is designed to do- Radiate body heat, and block out wind.  Unfolded, it was large enough for me (5'11"/200lbs) to wrap around myself.  While I was somewhat careful in it's handling, the blanket did not rip or tear during this test use.  I would recommend this product for any emergency kit.

I thought it was something you had to pull loose from the keys and then spray.  I see no way for it to be "quick release" as you have to find the little indention and press it to release the container (if of course, you could find it in time).  Please NOTE:  You can't just pull it or press it, you have to do both. and then you have to move the lock (easily done for sure) and then spray.  Now I ask you, in an emergency situation how is this going to work?  The instructions say don't leave it in your car - so what good is this if I don't feel safe carrying it in or on my purse, and can't leave it in my car???  If anyone has any suggestions regarding remedying this situation or another type to buy, please let me know.

text: The price was right and for that price it's good. It is thicker but feels less sturdy than my preferred spork by a name brand maker. The thicker metal will mean less ease in cutting with the side of the spork, a little less ease sliding under food, and a little more difficulty cleaning food from between the tines. The anodized pink spork felt more slick than the plain sandblasted matte finish spork.

title: Looks same as many others

title: Stays in better than I thought it would
text: This stays in the mouth of the Nalgene bottle better than I thought it would.  To refill the Nalgene it's best to remove this but I'm not a fan of using my hands to pull it out to just refill the bottle. The trade off is worth it to me. Really controls the drink splash.

title: Never had a problem with Liberty Paracord
text: I never had a problem with Liberty Paracord and this is the same.  Granted it's not mil-spec cord but for my general use this did what it's supposed to.

title: Not as dark looking as the picture
text: Best lightweight and low priced titanium fork and spoon I've found.  I really like titanium sporks but prefer having an actual fork for some things and an actual spoon for others. These are exactly what I wanted. The fork head is wide enough to hold a good size bite and the tines are flat and effective. The spoon is essentially identical to other short handle titanium spoons I've tried.  These are a bit light weight and have some flex but for me they are sturdy enough. The color is not as dark as it appears in the pictures... it's the same grey color as my other titanium utensils.  The surface texture is likewise similar as well. My only wish would be to have the ends polished instead of that rough texture.  They feel a bit smoother after scrubbing them alot with a scouring pad. The same thing helped other titanium utensils I have so it does improve. If only they would make this very set at the same price but with a polished bowl/end, then it wouldn't have that drawback.

title: One is obviously defective and will leak
text: One arrived previously opened and obviously defective (the packaging bag was rolled down on one whereas the others were bagged differently and taped closed). The drinking lid does not fit on straight. You can see through the translucent cap that it is not making a seal on rim. As a result this will leak unless the cap is tightened way down. Even then there is no guarantee that it will seal when you put it on. I recommend sticking with Nalgene instead.

title: Loose stitching, otherwise would be good pouch
text: Workmanship is lacking. The stitching is very loose on both sides of the front panel. I bought a few of these for car kits and the quality varies considerably.  If it was made better it looks like it would be a really good pouch.

title: Essentially 325 paracord, just what I was looking for.
text:
BIG spool! I got the 3000 feet of "rainbow" paracord. Actually it's not rainbow because it's just alternating red, yellow, blue, and white. The colors look great though. Also, this isn't the regular 550 paracord we all know and love; this is thinner cord that has a coarser kermantle weave... It's comparable to something like 325 paracord or even 275 paracord, although I wish the kermantle was woven more finely like 550 cord. I suspect they did the coarser weave so the color pattern would be more pronounced. This paracord has only 2 inner strands. I do prefer finer woven 275 paracord from a different manufacturer but, hey, who can resist a 3000ft spool! One note, the description and the picture for 3000ft Rainbow listed the size of this paracord and 350lb "strength rating", however the listing was a bit confusing because other Rainbow options and other colors lacked descriptions or described normal 550 cord, and even showed showed images with packages that contradicted descriptions. Notwithstanding, overall I'm very pleased. There are specific uses where I prefer the thinner cord and this works great for that.

For size comparison, the second image shows this cord next to regular commercial 550 paracord.

title: OK but Awkward to open / close
text: Seems ok but the blade wobbles a bit when locked. It seems like a flaw of the dial lock mechanism. (It's much like a lock back but instead of a tensioned bar a disk rotates out of and into locking groves on the blade pivot area). The same dial lock that locks the blade open also locks the blade closed. This can be good or bad depending on how you look at it. Also for its size it is rather heavy. I like trying out a different folding knife designs so I'll keep it, but for the money I would recommend something else.

title: Kinda small for a blanket, smaller than it states, stitching coming out immediately
text: I bought several of these. They are rather warm and make great throw blankets (kind of slippery), however the size is 3 to 4 inches shorter than the measurements they provided.  I bought both the Slate/RedTrim, and the solid Black color. So far out of the 3 I've used all three are 3 to 4 inches shorter than the stated size. One of them has the quilting stitching coming out immediately all around up to about 6 to 12 inches from the edge (whoever sewed it did't lock stitch it back and the stitching is coming out). At some point this will need to get mended. I purchased others at the same time that I haven't checked for issues.  I got them for a good price when one of the colors was probably getting clearanced out, but if I had paid the subsequent higher price I would have sent them back. There are plenty of other puff blankets.  I am very critical of misstated dimensions and obvious QC/stitching issues, however I gave it a bonus star because the price was low when I bought it.

title: Two in a row had bad lens seals, doesn't put out a lot of light on one AA
text: First one had the lens o-ring seal incorrectly installed. Replacement had same exact problem. The flashlight works with a AA battery but not very bright. Zooming in produces a squarish pattern while zooming out makes an evenly distributed field of light. Has three modes: high, low, and flashing.  To switch between these modes you turn it off and the next turn on switches to the next mode. Kind of inconvenient.  The o-ring issue matches numerous reviews of identical designed flashlights for half the cost, the only difference is this has a nice camo paint job.  Waste of my time. Returned.

title: Big, heavy, good quality, look very very strong
text:
These are the beefiest, most heavy duty titanium tent stakes I've ever seen. It is kind of overkill, making these out of titanium when a good chromoly steel of the same weight would be nearly as good. I'm sure a company could make quality steel stakes (albeit a little thinner) that would be just as strong, but I'm digressing, when you go premium, go big, go really big! And these are that.

Unfortunately the listing is kind of messed up and ambiguous. When I received them, as I hoped these are the stakes that are 8mm in diameter and 300mm in length. They are also around 70 grams a piece, not the lighter weight which my understanding is for a shorter version. I was anticipating the extra weight since another reviewer gave meaningful and helpful feedback. I completely understand and agree with the criticisms expressed about the heavy weight and the high cost. I also don't think these are good for backpacking, possibly could work for staking down heavier things like EzUps or large canopies. These are SOLID and reflect that fact with heavy weight. I don't mind that they weigh a lot because I only plan to use two of these stakes for setting up a secure ridgeline across poles, with lighter weight stakes for the guylines.

The cordage loops at the end seem kind of cheap and low quality in comparison to the stakes themselves. The stake materials, welds and finishing all look great, although a couple stakes new-out-of-the-package have a slight curve/bend to them. There are no sharp edges or other apparent issues. Overall I'm very pleased.

title: Nice long handle to reach down into things
text:
I like the extra length to reach down into bags, cups, jars, etc. The shape and curvature of the bowl part of the spoon works great for getting the peanut butter off the sides and out of the bottom of a jar; and the length reduces getting my hands messy.

The spork is less effective at being a fork substitute because the tines are not designed to "poke" food, however it helps in eating foods that are more challenging to the spoon (such as noodles or larger pieces of food) - the tines give a bit of "grip" to pulling the food up and out of the container.

Both are lightweight and nest together well. The polished bowels release food well and clean easily. The titanium is thin so the edges of the handles may feel kind of sharp if gripping it tightly. There's a little bit of flex by the bowl of the spoon/spork.

Overall I don't think these would be very comfortable for regular use but they work great for when that extra reach is needed.

title: Heavy duty steel carabiner, but arrived chipped and scratched up
text: These are some heavy duty steel carabiners. Similar in dimension to the larger aluminum carabiners but with twice the rating, and probably way more than twice the weight!  I would have given these 4 stars except that they came scratched up with chipped paint, and the resulting bare exposed steel in places. The plastic bag these were packaged in was substantially insufficient to contain these...  Although I cannot tell whether the paint was damaged prior to shipping or when the cheap plastic bag split open and the carabiners tumbled throughout the box like heavy wrecking balls. I am amazed the box somehow stayed intact, but I'm still not happy with the poor condition.

title: Warm, not too scratchy, wish it was slightly longer
text: Overall I like this wool blanket. It's warm and not too scratchy. I keep it in my car and have used it a few times already. I haven't noticed any problems with shedding and the smell is mild. It says dry clean only, but when it eventually gets dirty I expect it to hold up to a gentle handwash (with lanolin washing soap) and a hang dry. I'm not a fan of the folded over end hem. It's also a bit short for my preferences but works well enough. This is not the same quality as old military wool blankets I have, but compared to other low price wool blankets I have gotten from Amazon this works well... again I just wish it was a bit longer.

title: Bought Used but a couple "Used-Very Good" were not "Very Good"
text: A couple of the Used-Very Good were not that condition. One had a lot of wear and had a hole in it at the snap and the snap was at the beginnings of pulling through. Another had a buckle with a male clip didn't match the female buckle. As a result it jammed horribly when trying to snap it together and made the pouch un-usable. This problem was an obvious shoddy "repair" likely done by whatever soldier had to turn it back in. The elastic shock cord also had been replaced with a non-matching cord. Others that I received were passing for the "Very Good" condition, but there should be better scrutiny.

title: Haven't used them yet but exactly as described
text: I haven't used them yet but they look exactly as pictured and described.

title: Barely opens to 3/16", some weak gates, didn't come with plastic box
text: Gate barely opens to 3/16", gate wires are rather thin. Also on some due to floppy tolerances wire gates can be pushed to the side breaching the opening. Since they have an awkward weak tiny gate I don't think it will work well for me for things like clipping keys to thick blue jean belt loops or clipping other things to cordage 1/4" or larger. I expect they'll work well with standard paracord, but then so do the much cheaper mini (round) carabiners that cost less.  Under the right circumstances I understand why people love these, I just wish the gates were better.

title: Seem sturdy, wire gates work like they should
text: I have a couple other brands of identical or nearly identical carabiners. These appear to be just as well put together as the others. Time will tell.

title: Sheds a lot, not very good quality
text:
Even with the other reviews I never expected the shedding to be that bad, but it turns out it is. I wanted to avoid washing it but the shedding was leaving hairs all over the place and putting them into the air. The manufacturer says it's normal for shedding like that so I'm giving them a pass for now, I'll see how it lasts.

Edit: I'm changing my rating from 4 stars to 2 stars. After having a chance to use this I found it to be very itchy while exposed to bare skin. It feels soft to my hands but against bare skin while trying to sleep it's intolerably itchy. With a sheet or other barrier it works ok. Also within a couple days of getting this and washing it I noticed a 3/8 inch size defect in the weaving (hole) in one spot as well as with numerous other small weaving gaps or looseness throughout.

title: Inspect it very closely, very poor quality control
text:
I bought two of these. On the first one the main compartment zipper was barely stitched in with only one of the two parallel stitching attaching the zipper. This means at one of the greatest load points only one single stitch holds it together. If a "tactical" load is put in this bag it will fail prematurely. On the second bag, besides some funky looking attempts at stitching, the secondary compartment had no zipper pull installed at all! It was one continuous closed zipper the full length with no zipper pull. So much for quality control!

If you get a good one then I'm sure it's a good bag.

title: Grn Camo: Quality Control lacking. Bad stitching on one, poor shoulder strap webbing on two others
text:
Out of three of the Green/Brown bags there was an issue of some sort with each. One had defective stitching (uneven thread tension in sewing) along the main zipper. Two others had issues with the shoulder straps. I don't think they're quality checking each bag. Also, the end pouches have two rows of stitching along the top as if it would be reinforced there, but the lower stitch row doesn't go through anything on the backside. Makes me ask, "Huh, what are they doing?".

All issues new out of the package

title: A lot of space but I think quality could be better
text: My first impression... it is much lower quality than I was expecting.  At 31 inches long it has ample and generous storage, but the zippers tended to snag, and the fabric and overall quality was lower than I'd expect for a bag in the 30 dollar range.  I paid much much less than that so I'm not too disappointed. If I was to fill the bag full with moderate weight items I don't think the bag would hold up long.  It has a lot of space, I'd estimate it could over the SHORT-term maybe handle up to 50 pounds. With a bag this size you could easily reach that weight.  On the other hand, this bag will work awesome for lightweight bulky objects, I could see myself throwing a rolled yoga mat, a couple towels, change of clothes, pair of shoes, and a bunch of other stuff in it and still have some room.  I'd be hesitant to use this as luggage although maybe it would work for just for car trips.  I think it will work great for storing bulky comforters or blankets for the summer.  Most of the 31 inch length is the main compartment and the zippered opening opens big and wide.  The end compartments each take up only a few inches of the full length. Again I was very impressed with the large size. It appears much larger in person than the picture. If it's stuffed full the proportions will probably be similar to what's pictured.

title: The Terrain Digital is printed, not woven, stains easily from other bleeding dyes, very very thin and too small
text: I got the Terrain Digital Shemagh. It's rather small. To my displeasure the colors are not woven into the fabric, the green is printed on the fabric. It has less green on it than the main image.  The green looks essentially single tone, not two tone like the image. The base fabric is very very thin and very light weight, the whole thing is less than half the weight of other shemaghs I have. The base fabric readily picks up any bleeding colors from other shemaghs you wash it with, even bleeding colors from itself... It bleeds quite a bit itself. I really dislike that it's printed not woven, and that it's so small.  I can deal with the lightweight and in some instances a lighter weight shemagh may be nice... but it's much different than I was expecting. The only good part is I washed it with some other green shemaghs so the overall tone of the "white" is now a greenish color.  Improves the look but this thing really isn't color fast at all.

title: Ample size but quality wasn't up to par, defects were deal breaker
text: Based upon other East West products I thought this was going to be good.  It's not, the quality is lacking; some parts are assembled uneven, some parts lack stitching or have inadequate stitching.  For example: the webbing meets up off center with one of the shoulder straps, an edge of the box x stitch for the same strap is off the webbing, and at the top where the shoulder straps attach to the bag the stitching looks like whoever was sewing gave up. The key clip on the back is only half-way sewn on (like they ran out of thread when sewing but didn't realize it). On the inside to cover the edges of the joined seams they used a fabric (although it's that type of "fabric" that is more closely related to kitchen paper towels than to fabric). Besides the problems, the overall quality was not what I was expecting.  I doubt this would hold up long under a regular load of school books.  On the plus side it does have an ample size main compartment.  I gave it two stars because this may work for someone

title: Seems well made, I'm liking the mustache design more and more
text:
I bought a few of these. One came with damage (a hole cut more than an inch long near the middle, yikes!). Other than that problem these are great. I also tried two other colors/styles and are made very similar. At first I thought the mustache design was silly, but it has started growing on me. It has a tactical look to it without being offensive to people who think guns, grenades, or skulls mean something bad. It seems colorfast/I didnt notice any bleeding. Except for the issue with that one, I give it 5 stars!

Edit: it does bleed a little. I recommend washing separate... if you have a front loading machine then maybe gentle cycle similar colors, line dry. Or wash by hand.

title: Fits 20oz bottles well
text: Fits 20oz bottles well (both soda and sports drinks).  Opening the draw string wide enough takes a bit of practice unless you unsnap it, then it's easy.  Smaller size bottles such as 500ml water bottles are kind of loose in there; the drawstring will keep it in however.  1 liter soda bottles (3 1/4 diameter) are too big and do not fit.  The only thing I'd improve is putting horizontal webbing behind the MOLLE straps to secure it more firmly to other PALS webbing. Seems well made. Thin padded lining, no drain hole.  I'd buy this again.

title: It's ok but the price was right
text: Used cover was in poorer condition than I anticipated, still probably can be considered Good condition.  The new plastic canteen itself seems generic and slightly lower quality than my old mil-spec one; same design as military canteens but the cap strap is a bit thin. The cap "seal" is plastic on plastic. Overall for the price, I like it.

title: Looks like a factory reject
text: So much for Rothco being a good bag. The pack arrived with poor stitching on bottom corners of outside compartment and damage to the shoulder strap mesh.  One of the corners of poor stitching looks like stitches had been partially taken out and re-sewn, as does a section along the bottom.  The other corner has the stitches pulling wide apart.  There are a variety of mystery holes that look like a needle went through the fabric for no apparent reason.  All throughout the fabric has small tufts of fray along the stitching as if they used sharp needles or needles with a burr. (The sewing needle did tiny damage to the fabric with each stitch... in numerous places).  This could have been an awesom pack. It will probably stay together but this is not anywhere close to what I expected from Rothco.  I'd consider this to be a factory second or a factory reject.

title: Smaller than 42x42, wish the manufacturer hadn't put a staple through one
text:
On one that I purchased the packaging had a staple going through two layers of a corner on the shemagh. I didn't think much of it at the time but after the initial washing this means there are now two 1/4 inch holes!

Also, the size is 2 inches shorter in both directions than the claimed 42" by 42". Other than that the quality of the shemagh fabric looks good. If it wasn't for the slightly smaller size and the holes through one I would have given it five stars.

I think their other style (5ive Star Gear Desert Scarf - NOT THE TROJAN PATTERN) is better because it is truer to size.

(Front loader washer, gentle cycle, cold, minimal detergent, no fabric softener, air dry... that's how I treat my shemaghs)

title: Well wrapped 1000ft roll.
text: Got the 1000ft navy blue. Good nylon paracord at a great price. Has a fair amount of stretch. Well wrapped on the roll. No tangling or kinking issues yet.

title: Used with a good edge striker they throw tons of sparks
text: Using a good edged striker throws tons of sparks.  There were heavier (actual weight) than I expected, probably because they are nice and big.  Love them.

title: Has held up well in my light duty uses
text: I haven't put it under load yet but I've been using one a while for my keys and misc strapping down using paracord, and it has done what it's supposed to.  The wire gate has held up with no issues.

title: Good phone holster... IF you get a good one
text:
If you get a good one this is a great phone holder. Unfortunately 2 out of the 4 holsters I got have major issues with how they were made. At first I thought it was just the way the case was laying but looking closer and comparing left and right sides I see stitches on each sides are in a slightly different position, causing the front part of the case to twist to the side. This also makes putting the phone in a more challenging, and the holster doesn't stay straight with the phone in it.

Other than the fatal flaw, some of the things it does well...

*Holds my phone with case. My phone is a bit taller than the default height for the case however the strap lengthens and will fit taller phones (with case my phone has exterior dimensions of 3 1/4" by 6 1/4" by 11/16")

*Has two "compartments" so I can carry something else with it (I don't think it will fit two phones the size of mine), and I can choose which to put my phone in (the outer one seems a bit slimmer than the inner.

*The female snap buckle is attached to the case so snapping in the closure strap is fairly easy one handed

*The lining on the inside means the phone is not exposed to the back side of fastener hardware.

Again, other than the major issues I had there are a couple ways it could be better...

*I'm not a fan of the open corners or the non-zippered top, because I feel that over time the phone and inside of the case may be exposed to dust and dirt which may scratch cheap phone screens. This shouldn't be a problem on better phones with better glass.

*Inside has a nylon webbing edging that catches on my phone case when my phone screen is facing out. This would be a big annoyance if I wanted to carry my phone that way.

title: great little decoy aid
text: There is a little lever that rotates over the batteries, so they don't fall out. therefore batteries falling out is not an issue.  The big thing is that you tighten the lid tightly so the water will not enter during the hunt.  I cut a small piece of  Remington camo cloth for the top of the lids to knock off the glare and place two or three of these among 6 decoys in several spots around the blind.  They give lots of movement to the decoys and they really draw the ducks on calm days.  Battery life is not very good, so you will need to change them daily if you spend more than four or five hours in the blind and I find that if I replace the batteries at the end of the hunt if needed it just takes a moment to set them out for the next hunt.  I can't imagine a cheaper easier way to put some movement in your spread and will always use them.  I buy the 100 box of AA batteries as that is the most economical purchase.  Don't buy the bargain batteries, just use copper top as they last the longest.

title: Great with a little extra effort
text: These little decoy aids are great, but you have to do a couple of things before you use them, or you will experience the problems others noted. 1. spray the switch, motor and battery contacts with a good Teflon oil. 2. get a package of Remington Camo wrap and cut to fit the top of the cover 3. be sure to tighten the lid securely.  I hunt a very natural blind with about 2 dozen decoys positioned in sets of six and I add three of these aids to each set. For storage and ease of setup, I keep them on slip rigs in sets of three separated with a D ring for each three.  As another hunter noted, they are not intended to move your decoys, but to add some motion to the water within your decoy set.  I can tell you they do make a big difference in bringing in the ducks, especially on still days.  When needed, take the time to replace the batteries at the end of the days hunt and you'll be ready for the next hunt.  One final tip, don't forget that mallards and other puddle ducks only feed in water 12" to 15" deep or less, and these aids mimic a feeding duck.

title: Great value, if not a little tricky to lock.
text:
Easy to setup and adjust, feels sturdy and secure. It really would take a bit of effort to remove a bike from it if you have it locked down.

Seems like a really good value.

There were a few stumbling blocks I encountered, though. First, the locking hitch pin that Sawgman sells is a bit expensive, compared to other locking pins you can find. However, because the rack had a threaded hole, a standard 1/2” pin won’t fit through. I ended up just yawing the supplied pin, and used a small Master Lock with a small enough shackle diameter to fit. Probably not as secure as the proprietary locking pin, but it should be enough to dissuade anyone looking for a quick grab and go.

Speaking of shackle diameter, it was a bit of a challenge to find the perfect locks to use on the bars. Your typical MasterLock is about 7mm, which is too big; and 5mm was small enough that you could still pull the trigger and move the bar up with ease. In the end I found the MasterLock 141T set of two locks (Keyed alike) with a 6mm shackle was the best fit. The shackle is just small enough to fit through the hole, but thick enough to keep the trigger secure.

So the TLDR, but a lock with a 6mm diameter shackle to secure your bikes.

title: The best Lighting Ever - A comparison of  lanterns and why the LE wins over RayOVac Sportsman
text:
Purchased this Lighting Ever 1000 lumens lantern and the Rayovac Sportsman 240 Lumen LED Lantern SE3DLNACOM on the same order. Not realizing the identical nature of each lantern at the time, having both in hand together allowed me to make a side by side comparison. This might help someone chose which one to buy.

The Rayovac I purchased on this page shows a 240 lumen lantern, however the one that arrived clearly states 305 lumens. Physically, the LE and RV are manufactured almost identically in composition. Both require 3 D sized batteries to operate. The LE is only one ounce more than the RV, but the LE feels and looks sturdier and of higher quality. LE and RV will be used when describing each lantern, but keep in mind that I am comparing the Rayovac 305 lumen that arrived, versus what is advertised on the Amazon page.

The LE's output on highest mode is 1000 lumens compared to the RV's highest mode at 305; both are daylight white on high. On high, the LE touts a run time of 18 hours (10 watts), to the RV's 70 hours (4 watts), RV wins on run time.

The LE's second mode both reduces the lumens (dimmer) and changes the color temp to a warm white. While the RV does not have a color temp variable, it does provide an option to dim the output to 140 lumens for its 2nd mode and can run 140 hours. LE wins due to the option to change to preferred temperature color.

The LE's 18 hour operation will increase to 25 hours when on mode 2 (warm white). The third mode of the LE further dims the light and combines the warm and daylight temperatures to somewhere in between. The paperwork for the LE shows that mode 3 will last only 12 hours, which does not make sense as to why it shortens the life by the most .

The last mode for both (LE's 4th mode, RVs 3rd mode) is a blinking / strobe light of the daylight / cool white color. I've not much to say on this mode - does not seem relevant at the moment to me. The RV has one final feature though, which is a dim green light on the power button that blinks very slowly, to assist the owner in locating it during periods of darkness. Personally, I do not like this feature and would either remove the batteries or put a dimmit over the light. Buyers might prefer this, I'm just not a fan of idiot lights with or without power.

Lastly, I mentioned these being cut from the same mold, and both have battery compartments in the base of the lantern. The LE has a stem mounted in the base that the cover's slot must align correctly to close the battery compartment. The RV has a slot (no stem) on the rim of base to align to the cover's slot opening. However, the LE cover is still much easier to close with the batteries in the unit. Once the appropriate alignment is met, you must push down and turn to close the base. Think of pushing a child-proof pill bottle's lid to open it. Do the same on these lanterns. The LE base closed after 3 tries, to the RV's numerous tries getting frustrated. LE wins on battery replacement procedures.

Overall, the LE wins hands down. For a 15 ounce lantern with more features, I paid approximately 17.00. The 14 ounce RV cost $24, but the Amazon page shows the list price at $34 and the buyer was getting a $10 discount at purchase. Though the 4 watt RV runs much longer at 2.9 days or 5.8 on mode 2 and the 10 watt LE has a run time of .75 days or 1 full day on mode 2, I am not using this to go camping. This was purchased for power failures, to be used as part of an overall emergency preparedness plan, and bright is what we need indoors during power failures. The hours will be broken up over various times and 18 hours will get us several days. For the money, same battery requirements and functionality, LE takes the cake.

I've never heard of Lighting Ever before, but the product packaging shows they have their home base in Las Vegas, NV, another in the UK and one in China, where this lamp was made. It comes with RoHS certification, 1 year warranty and the instructions are the most accurate regarding the English language than I've seen in a long time. How refreshing to receive grammatically correct documents included in the box (yes, a real box). The RayOVac has a limited lifetime warranty and came in a plastic transparent bag, unbranded. The TLC shows on the LE, while the product packing on the RV is a wrapped label with specs, and it is though product presentation was an afterthought. For the $24, some type of protection during delivery wouldn't hurt. Whoever LE is, I will buy again if they produce a product as good as this one.

title: But it's a solid 3-Stars... Update 07/13/2022
text:
I got this (obviously) because I wanted to do some car camping (also, obviously). All-in-all it's a very good design and I think it will work out well for me. But it does have some issues - including a misleading description - so I'll tell you about those too.

First, by myself, it was fairly easy to set up. It's a learning experience, so make sure you set it up in your yard before you're in some dispersed campsite in BF Outer Badlands. Running the poles was straightforward, but I found that Blue Tape is your friend when attaching the main poles to the corner fittings. A second person might make the tape unnecessary, but it would still make it easier. Getting the main structure set - for the first time - took about 20 minutes, the whole set up took about an hour but I was being slow and deliberate. The inside is great and the HUGE windows provide ample ventilation. If anything the tent is too tall (which makes it tough to put the rainfly on solo) but there's plenty of room to stand everywhere in the tent. The connection with the car is good but, as others have noted, you will get some gaps (especially if you have a roof rack) that will allow bugs to get in.

Now, the big downside. The rainfly and construction is described as offering the "ultimate weather protection". Not even close. While the fly's seams are sealed, the fabric itself relies on the weave to let more water run off than soak through. The night after my initial setup there was a light dew and the rainfly was as wet on the inside as it was on the outside. The only part of the tent that seems truly waterproof is the floor. I'm planning on waterproofing the fly, the whole front door panel of the tent, any part of the tent exposed under the fly, and seal all the seams. Pay particular attention to the ground seam as it's completely exposed.

Quality control was spotty. There were some poorly stitched seams (picture) that shouldn't have made it past QC. Also, the slide locks for the fly guy ropes were incorrectly tied so I had to take them apart and retie them (picture) to keep them from slipping. Not a big deal but indicative that somebody is not paying attention. (Note: There are a couple of different ways to tie a slide lock, one of which only uses the end holes, so I don't know why they made a 3-hole lock.) The guy ropes themselves are invisible in the dark. They're flecked with white but are not reflective so another corner cut (and thing to fix...)

Bottom line is a good design with some issues that need to be fixed to make it a usable tent.

Update - I've upped it a star. I just came back from my first camping trip using the tent. It went very well. The tent is very easy to setup solo. The screen material was 100% (well, 99.99%) effective at keeping the bugs out (and it was *very* buggy) and the height of the tent makes for very comfortable living. My original comments stand as to construction, etc, but I had a problem with a weak piece of fabric which I reported to Napier. Their customer service department was amazing. They addressed the issue quickly and totally fixed things. That earned them the extra star.

title: So close to great...
text:
First, the good: Man, does this thing keep cold. I wanted to test it before I decided to keep it so pre-chilled it with 8 pounds of cold packs, about 5 pounds of 32F (AKA water) freeze point and about 3 pounds of 28F freeze point gel packs. I let this pre-chill the cooler for about 4 hours which lowered the temp down to 40F. I then placed my test ice - 1 quart of water at about 0F - into the cooler. The test ice remained frozen for 2 1/2 days. At the end of the test all of the 32F cooling blocks had thawed but the 28F blocks still had some ice left in them. So, yeah, with some more high-tech ice and filled with more than a quart block of ice this cooler will keep things cold for a long time.

Now, the bad: Come on Lifetime, you make like Made in the USA is a big deal and then you allow seams like the attached photos past quality control. Finish matters. This was a surprise (particularly the open seam) as the rest of cooler seemed really well constructed. I'm not sure if that open seam would allow water into the insulation area but I'm going to slap some sealant on it to be sure it won't. I'll get rid of those rough spots, too.

Otherwise it's a really good cooler, it would have been a solid 5-stars if only it was as well made as the Chinese products.

Were the move over pavement or other very smooth ground, it may go well. I have to move my canoe from back of yard over uneven ground and that causes the straps to shift on one side or the other.

When strap on on side slides back, the wheels won't run true and the canoe will be pulling in that direction. This will continue until you can't pull the canoe at all and have to reset the whole thing. For a long portage, this won't work.

The second time I used this thing, I put the trolley on the front and pushed it and things went better over a short distance. It was still balking and it was not a smooth run.

Next time I use it, I will try to set the trolley in the center of canoe and see how that goes. I expect some more experimentation will result in usable solution. title: The box works well, once you rebuild the connectors inside.
text:
The box is excellent design and works very well, once I had to open it up and reattach the positive and negative cables inside.

The box has an outer red and a black lead for attaching device to the battery system.

The problem was the bolts inside the box were not well attached and were loose. Removing the covering device from the outer lead caused the two nuts on each lead to come off inside the box. There are several washers on each as well holding the inner cables that run from the battery.

It should be a simple task to restore the nuts and washers and cable to those outer leads. It is NOT at all as there is an inner plastic covering to protect the connections. The plastic is very rigid and it is difficult to get the cable, washers, and two nuts tightened.

It took about an hour wrestling with this simple task and regular ratchet and other tools were useless. The space is very constrained. A box end wrench would have been useful perhaps.

I got it all reassembled, installed the battery, charged the battery and it works great. The two external attaching ports for plugging in devices like phones or whatever work well.

The only other criticism is the handle and the band they use to hold the top and bottom of the casing together.

With a 52 pound battery, the fabric band will not tighten enough to really hold top and bottom together well. When you lift the encased battery by the handle, the band stretched a little and it is a bit shakey. Makes one wonder it the band may come off while carrying and the whole thing come apart. They need a better solution for the two parts of the case coming together.

But, it works well, I will keep it and use it. But, I have had a Minn Kota tilt trolling motor for 25 years that is a good as new. I expected a bit better in the craftsmanship of this

text:
I installed one of these on each end of an Old Town Pack canoe.

For installation, I cut a small board to act as platform for the pulley that I mounted onto the canoe. Then attached the pulley onto the board. This was necessary so the pulley would hang out over the end of the canoe enough.

The installation was easy enough with the screws received with the pulleys. But, I purchased separately 1/4" brass screws with nuts as I don't think the small screws would hold for long term. Not really a criticism.

But, the pulley has a restraining device that works very well, if your anchor rope is at least 1/2" diameter. Smaller cord I am using (purchased from Amazon with a Yak Gear Nylon Rope) will not restrain when you release the cord trying to hold the anchor in place. Must instead use cleats to hold the rope, which is difficult when you pull up the anchor and it is dangling off the end of the canoe. I have a 5# mushroom anchor on either end and that is significant weight to tie off.

Not sure this is the final solution with these pulleys and the nylon rope and I may have to go back to using larger diameter rope. Really did not want to do this as this would put more rope cluttering up the canoe when I fish.

These are well made metal anchors. Just not sure about for canoe/yak applications unless you can deal with the additional mass of rope in the boat.

I delayed reviewing for two years to make sure I could do a good review.

For walking or running, it is smooth and reliable. I like the many different workout profiles shifting speed and incline and they stand the test of time. If that is all you want, buy this machine.

But, they ship it without a USB storage device when using USB is supposed to be central to using the Fitness Club and better managing your workout and physical fitness.

So I bought a USB stick and followed instructions. The machine has never uploaded a workout to the stick following all the instructions. And frankly, that makes this machine worthless for fitness management. The interactivehealthpartner website would be a good tool if I could just get the link between machine and computer to work. Several calls to the company and I got the idiot treatment.

So, summary, I can't recommend or not recommend this machine. I assume there is an included cost for the membership and electronic brains of this machine and membership. title: Excellent Product! Follow directions!!!
text:
This is an excellent product. I have added those pads to both of my snowboards. They are very easy to apply, and look fantastic when applied.

Follow directions supplied with the pads. Clean the board with acetone, heat it up with hair drying, PEEL PLASTIC BACKING ON THE STICKY SIDE OF THE PADS, heat them up - stick them in and put some weight on top for 24 hours.

People who left negative reviews for sticking the pads on without pealing the plastic off of the adhesive side... Really should just read the manual and do a minimum of thinking.

title: Great product, very easy to use.
text:
I got this product last week. I have played tennis for 15 years, but never bothered with stringing my racquets. I play with heavy top spin, so it is not uncommon for me to break 4-5 racquets per months. After reading the reviews of the Klippermate, I took a plunge and bought it.

Product did not disappoint me. It is very sturdy, feels substantial, and very easy to use. So far I re-strung three of my racquets. First one took about 2.5 hours, next two were 1.5 hours. The instructions included with the stringer are excellent and do a fantastic job in guiding you through the stringing process.

I would definitely recommend.

title: Very good boat.
text:
I live in an apartment in Arizona, and I wanted a quality inflatable boat I could take to the local lakes. After researching my options, IM4 appeared to be the top boat.

Although manufacturer claims it is a 4 person boat, it is NOT true. Two people can be comfortable in this boat, three is pushing it. With the semi-solid floor the boat is stable on the lakes; however, you cannot stand or dance as some reviewers claim. Solid floor allows it some degree of stability, but not enough to stand up or walk while being fully upright.

The hull materials and ores supplied are very good. Boat has a solid feel to it. When inflating it to the max, it become very firm- raft like.

For $220 this is an amazing deal. I would recommend this boat!

Update from 10/05/2012. On my recent trip to the lake I broke one of the ores. The plastic on the coupling broke when I did five spirited rows, I was upset. I had to try to canoe paddle the boat to shore and mend the plastic coupling with some duct tape! Upon returning home I checked the Intex's website for the replacement coupling; it is being sold for $4+ shipping. Can't blame the boat for the broken ore, plastic coupling is the cheapest part of this boat.

text: Wow!  I was skeptical at first.  I got the sleeves to protect my arms while playing golf, here in Florida.  The sun here, near the gulf is intense. It's very easy to get sunburned. It comes with a charging cable or will work with one you have lying around the house.

text: I've always been a Penn fan and these reels will keep me a fan.  They are not expensive, have an excellent star drag system and stand up well in the salt environment where I use them.  We put them to the test, once again, on 25 Oct, 2016 and the lesser Amber-jack, Barracuda and Red Snapper were wearing out our arms. Perfect for fish from 5 to 50 pounds

title: Easy to get out and put back plus room left ...
text: Why didn't I get one of these sooner?  With all of the fishing I do, I've been keeping my stretch 30's in an old bucket where they get tangled up and are hard to get to.  I have about 20.  Now, they fit perfectly in slots especially designed for them.  Easy to get out and put back plus room left over for some of the smaller lures.  It also keeps them dry when the occasional wave decides to blow over the bow.

title: Perfect for my trolling motor
text:
I debated buying this for a week and finally made the plunge. All I can say is that it's been on the boat holding the MinKota RipTide 55 trolling motor for almost two years now and I've put it through some abusive weather and sea states. It's still rock solid. I remove the motor for long trips and over the winter when I store my boat and it takes about 30 seconds.

Just a little update after two years on the boat. I still love it and would buy one again but will probably never need another for this boat. It's as solid as the day I installed it. I've used the Min Kota ST55 in all kinds of water from dead still to 3 foot waves. The bracket has never loosened or deformed in any way.

title: Great for my skiff
text: I have 4 of these on my skiff along with 4 Cannon's.  I like the Scotty better because it has a better fit and the construction also seems better. I can use them for either light spinning rods or trolling poles. The adjustments for the rod position, both horizontally and vertically are strong and secure.

title: Small and Tough
text: You just can't beat Okuma.  I have 4 of these and 3 other Okuma reels.  Light on the pocketbook, lightweight and tough on the fish.  The depth counter is especially handy for getting to the right depths which is a must when fishing for the big Rock fish in the Chesapeake. With 300 yards of #40 braid (they'll hold a thousand) there isn't much they can't handle.  Only down side is that they are made in China, but the same goes for the other major brands.

title: Best of the best
text: Can't say enough about the Heddon Spook.  They are, with out a doubt, one of the best top water lures ever invented

title: Perfect for supplemental safey equipment
text: Just what I needed to attach to spare life preservers.  I got 5 of them.  The whistle is shrill, carries a long way and that's just what you need if you are in need of help. The best part is that it is a single piece and will stand up to a salt environment very well.  Great value for price

title: Reliable and long lasting
text: Berkley line is reliable and long lasting. I use this almost exclusively in 25 and 40lb test for "top shot" or leader.  It's diameter is large enough to tie but not unwieldy.  I also use it as base reel line so I don't "waste" to much braided line on the spool

title: Best there is.
text: Nothing, but nothing beats heddon spooks.  I use them in both salt and fresh water and they'll catch whatever is out there.  Bass, Rock, Trout, Blues, you name it. I have about 20 of these in different colors.  Have to change the hooks every once in awhile due to salt water corrosion and that's not a problem..

title: Lady! This ain't no lady
text: Berkley sells two versions of this hook retriever.  The pink one is less expensive and works just as well. Why they call it a lady is beyond me.  I used it just this past Monday on some toothy blues and it ain't no lady!  Don't get sucked into the more expensive one because you don't like pink.  I keep two of these on hand because, you never know.  Well worth it.

title: Best for fresh or salt water
text: Love all Heddon spook lures.  They are the best fish top water catchers ever made for both fresh and salt water.  I don't differentiate. I use both saltwater and freshwater heddons interchangeably. Bass love 'em, blues, rocks, lady fish and spanish macs too.  The hooks in the freshwater heddons will corrode a lot faster if used in saltwater.  I change the hooks to Gamakatsu (see my review) and keep them well rinsed

title: Hook 'em and Keep "em
text: All is good with these hooks.  I use them for Rock, when live lining, Red Drum with cut bait and have replaced some of my spinner bait treble hooks with them.  They are tough, maintain their sharpness (and they are very sharp! just ask a couple of my fingers) and corrosion resistant.  Well worth the $.

title: A great way to tune your swing
text:
A great, sturdy little gadget for tuning my swing. I've hit about 200 balls into it with various clubs, including driver. The hanging target makes a very distinctive sound letting you know you hit the shot on line. I use it to warm up before heading to the course. You can find less expensive ones, but they are not built and well and are more prone to the netting opening up (holes). When I get to a thousand balls, I'll add to this review

Now that I've had this awhile, I can truly say I've hit more than a 1000 balls at it. None got through! I took it down in December, put it back out again in March and have already hit another 500 balls. It was easier to put up the second time. Who knew? It still looks brand new even with the rotten rainy, windy and cold weather we've had so far this spring. So far, still well worth the money.

I gave it 4 stars because I think it would be nice to have included an LED voltmeter so you would be able to see the fully charged voltage.

title: Riptide 55 is a good buy
text:
I bought one of these for my 18' Carolina Skiff. I also bought the quick release mount. I bought the quick release mount so I could remove the trolling motor when travelling long distances with the boat. I fish from MD to the Gulf and bouncing down the road wouldn't be be good for it. First impression is that I'm going to like it a lot. I've been in the water twice using the trolling motor, both times in salt water, which is where I spend most of my fishing time. Installation was easy and deploying and retracting the ST55 is also easy. The iPilot anchor function worked well in 1.5 mph currents and 12 knot winds. I'll try it in the 8kt currents in the OBX in August. I like the iPilot control unit and no foot pedal because I'm not restricted to a certain place in the boat. I maxed it out and was surprised at how strong the motor was. I used the motor for about 2 hours and battery drain was about 1.4 volts from 14.2 to 12.8. Totally acceptable, especially for the size boat and winds. The instructions call for a 60 amp inline circuit breaker, however, I'm using a 40 amp and it was fine on full power. I've given it a 4 star rating right now and will return to add more to this review once I've used the programming features of the iPilot.

Update 24 Feb 15: I have nothing but praise for Min-Kota and the RipTide ST55. I've put about 70 hours on this motor and spent many hours in the anchor mode against 2-3 knot tides. I didn't use my boat anchor once during the summer and fall months because the RipTide's anchor function is spot on. I mainly fish in saltwater and I've used it from Florida, to North Carolina, to Maryland and its performance is outstanding. The only down side is it doesn't have automatic deploy and retrieve. I know Min-Kota is working on one. I love the iPilot! I can use it from anywhere on the boat and only have to remember when facing backwards, left is right and right is left. Duh. Most definitely 5 STARS

title: Catches em and keeps em
text: Don't know why it took me a year to get this review out, but it did.  I have the 40S and the 30S and the reviews are the same.  These are very good reels for the money.  I do lots of rock fish, sea trout and red fishing and these reels work like a charm.  Well put together, anodized metal, high impact plastic and a sealed transmission provide just what I need for fish up to 25-30lbs.  I would like them to come with a larger crank handle, but that's a personal preference.  Again, can't beat the value.

title: To fish or not to fish?
text: You just can't beat 'em! This rugged little removable rod holder is, in my opinion, the the best value on the market.  I own both a skiff and a kayak and both are of the fishing variety. The Cannon holder holds both my light tackle and my 6' and 11' trolling rods which have thick bases.  The Cannon is adjustable in both vertical and horizontal planes and has a locking ring on the barrel to make sure your fishing pole stays in the boat/kayak.  Easy to install using 1/4 20 stainless screws with flat washer and nylock nuts.  You can add a lock washer if you can't find nylocks.  The hardware must be purchased separately.

title: Universal Track Lok seat Extension for kayak seat
text: After some research, I settled on the Universal Trac-Lok seat to get some extra leg room in my kayak.  After a few engineering adjustments (bolt lengths and thicknesses,  I was able to gain abut 4" in forward and aft positioning and 11/2 " in vertical position of the permanently mounted OEM seat, giving me much needed extra leg room and unfettered access to my in yak tackle box that was heretofore blocked by the seat. What a difference!  When the Trac-Lok says universal, it's a true statement.

title: See my review on the 3700 series
text: See my review on the 3700 series.  I use the smaller one for fresh water but everything else applies. It's just a junior size and works great on the kayak.

title: Kayak fisherman's dream
text: I needed a fishing tackle box that would hold my required load of fishing lures, line, hooks, jigs, weights, etc. that I could strap on the yak for those 6-7 hour Atlantic and GOM fishing days.  This Plano box did the trick.  It's four separate removable containers within the box can handle all my needs and the storage in the top of the box is ideal for extra line, pliers, knives etc.  The boxes are easily removed from he unit so I can get what I need and get back to fishin'.  Because it's Plano, the individual containers , which aren't water tight on this particular model, can be interchanged with water tight ones that I purchased separately.  It's, of course, plastic bait proof.  This is my first season with it and we'll see how it stands up.  BTW, I have the smaller model for fresh water fishing.

title: Best bag hands down, superb for local and international exploring!
text:
I admit I am slow to write reviews. I want to see how a product holds up in the long haul.

This HEXIN 35L pack has held up and performed wonderfully!!!

Initially I purchased this to take with me to Ireland because I wanted to do a lot of exploring without dragging around large amounts of bags to encompass my gear. It was still in its comfy EASY TO USE self-pouch when I got to the Emerald Isle.

The first day I really used it was a lovely rainy Irish morning. I put all my gear in, from sensitive electronics to water bottles in the side pouches (hugely helpful to not have to dig in bag for a drink). Stored my inn keys and passport in the inner pocket where they were safe but not easily removed from my pack without notice.

I carried my larger Pixelbook, cameras and assortments; Change of clothes and extra layers to add or shed as needed; snacks and even an extra pair of hike boots in the bottom in case I didn't want to tromp around in wet boots.

There are so many pockets and secure dividers. This pack is well made. I have (before and since) tried a variety of styles and brands and I only swear by Hexin. It has lasted two full years and is still water resistant (and been through a LOT of rain), the zippers are still strong and safely covered. I can be really rough on gear, but I clean it after each adventure and I have had NO issues.

There is also a bright orange whistle which, I have only used for my dog, but is great for a small woman to have in emergency.

I love that I can also stick stuff in the straps in the mesh pockets and under the elastic band. You never know.

The straps and pack are nicely designed so they are always comfortable no matter what I stuff in the bag,

I love that when I am not using it I can fold it down so small that it lays flat in the bottom of my bag.

I am back to purchase another HEXIN now because I have given up on the rest. This is a really great bag. At 35L it holds more than enough gear, clothes, etc., and keeps things protected. I highly recommend it and that does not come lightly.

Bottom line: BEST BAG EVER!!!

title: M10-1.5 Bolted for finished garage and accessible attic
text:
I was specifically looking for a hook application like this that was bolted, rather than using a large lag screw. I have a relatively open attic above my garage with 2x4 joists and wanted to use this hook to hang ladders and my bike from the ceiling. I had looked at the smaller, and larger hook, and I believe this is a good compromise between price and size (not too small to make hanging things harder, not too large to be cumbersome). The rubber coating is very thick and seems very durable.

One thing not mentioned is the thread type. It is an M10-1.5. What I plan on doing is locating the hook in the ceiling of my finished garage from below. Then, utilizing a nut coupler with a ~3" bolt and some washers, securing through a perpendicular 2"x4" horizontally laid across my vertical 2"x4" truss chords.

I have used lag screw hooks in the past and I was never confident they would hold, or if they were centered properly, etc. If you have an open attic, and a finished garage, I think this is the proper application.

title: Greatest Marvel Set All-Time!
text:
My FAVORITE collection of cards!

I picked up a box of these cards back in '06 and they instantly became my favorite cards all-time.
Joe Jusko is the artist for the entire set and his work is off-the-charts-amazing.

You can do a Google "IMAGE" search for '92 Marvel Masterpieces and see the artwork...

This set (not this box - but the '92 MM set) includes 2 special sets in ADDITION to the 100 base cards.
Set 1: The Battle Spectra Cards 1-5D. These are all scenes of fights between various heroes & villians.
Set 2: The 'LOST' Cards 1-5. These are all individual females: Jubilee, Scarlet Witch, Typhoid Mary, Deathbird, and Feral

There are some other cards to this set that came as promos & prototypes, but I don't know enough about those to comment.

The reviewers who gave this set a low rating because the box was damaged or the cards are 'stuck together' should leave that as seller feedback - not on the item itself. There's no doubt this is a 5 STAR set - that's why you see boxes that originally retailed in '92 for around $15 now going for over $100. Collectors don't pay $100+ for junk sets. Crushed boxes and cards stuck together is a seller issue.

title: Good Value Solution for Bike Storage
text:
You could assemble the components for a better bike hoisting system at any decent hardware store, but the part you would buy would cost two or three times as much, and you would spend a fair amount of time figuring out what to buy and how to assemble it.

I see several review that report the packaging indicates a lesser weight capacity than the 100 lb indicated in the listing. My packaging shows the weight capacity as 45 kg -- 100 lb. Regardless, I am confident that, in fact, much more than 100 lb. could be supported by this hardware. The actual limiting factor on weight capacity will not be the hardware provided, but rather the installation method. The box includes screws with plastic anchors that are normally used for installing screws in sheetrock. Anyone who uses those to attach to a sheetrock ceiling will almost certainly have a problem. Even if the plastic anchors are used to attach the hardware to wood trusses the result will be weaker than if screwed directly into the wood after a proper size hole has been pre-drilled. Other reviews contain suggestions for mounting. The instructions provided fail to provide guidance on the need for a secure mounting.

It is easy to overlook on the installation instructions the correct routing of the rope used for lifting. There is a hole in the cam lock fitting through which the cord should be threaded. Unfortunately the hole is barely large enough for the provided rope, which would make it difficult to upsize the rope.

Which brings me to the issue of the gaps between pulley cheeks and the sheaves. The gap is enough that the provided rope can jump out of the sheave groove and become wedged. The sheaves are designed so that squeezing the cheeks to reduce the gap results in friction at the axle before the gap is significantly reduced. While a larger rope could eliminate the risk of jamming, the hole in the cam lock does not permit such a substitution. It is for this reason, and the potential that a person could be misled by the plastic sheetrock anchors and fail to attach to solid wood, that I am giving 4 stars rather than 5.

Additional comments -- As others mention, the hooks to hang the bike do not really have enough curve to hold securely and you probably will need to do some bending to get a good result. My seat does not have a structure to which the hooks would attach, so I use a cord under a frame section and secure the hooks to that. If you have a speedometer or the like mounted on handle bars there is a possibility of conflict with hooks, and you may need to be careful to avoid damage to any wire connecting to a sensor. The cleat provided to tie off the rope when the bike is lifted is definitely pretty cheesy, but the cam lock is good enough that the cleat is really not needed. If you are a belt and suspenders person you might want to upgrade the cleat. Otherwise the cleat basically just provides a method to get excess rope out of the way.

So while this is not perfect, it provides a good solution at a good price, and I would buy another one if I had a second bike.

title: Does not turn off, but does what one needs at a good price
text:
This computer never truly turns off so the battery will go dead and need to be replaced sooner than it should. After a few minutes of inactivity the screen display changes to show the time, and the computer constantly monitors for movement of the wheel. When it detects movement, it turns the speed/distance display on automatically. I know that these devices do not use much electricity, but there really is no reason that I cannot turn the display on and off manually, or at least have it automatically turn to a hard shut down after inactivity and turn on manually. Are bicyclists so lazy they cannot press a button to start their computer? Manufacturers of electronic devices have become lazy and foist devices with phantom loads on their customers. Perhaps I am more sensitive to wasted electricity than most people because I live off grid.

The installation is easy. I am a bit concerned how well the rubber band-like o-rings that hold the main components to the bicycle will hold up in sunlight. They seem like a bit of excessive cost-cutting in the manufacturing process.

If you have disk brakes you will need to mount the sensor on the fork on the side opposite the brake disk in order to have the proper clearance -- spokes on the disk side are likely to be too far from the fork.

The display is easily readable at a glance, even for the eyes of this old rider who relies on reading glasses, and even riding my mountain bike over extremely rough, rocky roads. The display is simple so one can quickly and easily spot the important information one wants. The single button makes it easy to scroll through the displays.

There are other computers available for not much more money that have many additional functions, but few people really need anything more than this, and adding functions just makes it more difficult to find on the go the data one is seeking.

It is easy to spend 2 or 3 times as much and still have no more than what this unit does. So while it is not perfect, it offers excellent value, I would buy it again over any of its competition, and I recommend it.

title: I was surprised how good this bottle cage was
text:
I was apprehensive. A plastic bottle cage? Previously all mine had been metal, and I liked and trusted them. But on a whim, I decided to try this for my new mountain bike. I've had some CatEye products, and have generally thought they make good products.

When it arrived, I was surprised how light it was. I knew the description says 29 grams, just a hair over 1 ounce, but I was skeptical. But it actually does weigh only 29 grams. Almost nothing. (Of course even the heaviest of bottle cages weigh little compared to the weight of the water they carry.)

So I thought this lightweight nothing was not going to hold a full water bottle. In my hands it felt just too flexible. But I mounted it, stuffed in a full bottle (a standard size plastic Specialized brand water bottle), and took off fully expecting the bottle would pop out. Much to my surprise this held the bottle more securely than a metal cage ever had.

In fact, one might say it holds the bottle almost too securely. A good, strong tug is needed to get the bottle out. With a metal cage I always could easily slide the bottle out, which made it easy to take a drink at high speed. With this cage one can pull the bottle out on the go, but it does mean focusing more attention on the bottle, which means less attention on the road. So for a road bike this might be less than ideal. But as I said, I bought this for a mountain bike. Where I ride this bike is incredibly rough and jarring, and I am perfectly willing to put a little extra effort into pulling the bottle out if it saves me from having to backtrack and pick up a bottle that popped out on its own going over a bump.

Because the cage is flexible I do not worry that it will be deformed if I crash like a metal cage might be.

All considered, I cannot imagine a better bottle cage for a mountain bike.

The cost of the tank seems high, but it is well made and more affordable than any alternatives I could find. I have owned boats and would select a Moeller fuel tank for use in a boat which needed a tank.
