text: A hit all the way around.  My grandson loves Mickey Mouse and I am a VOL fan,

title: Three Stars
text: Not enough padding to be effective for an adult

title: GREAT HEADLAMP.
text: I have a collection of headlamps...  I use them every day.  I have 3 different Fenix headlamps and several of their flashlights too...  This one is my favorite headlamp.  You can't really go wrong with any of the Fenix headlamps.  The quality is excellent, the design and engineering is intelligent and very user-friendly.  I used to like Black-Diamond, which are good quality; but, I don't like the way they design them and the way they function; the headbands are not designed as well as Fenix.  I could go on and on about the all the things I hate about the Black Diamond headlamps...  Fenix headlamps are much better.  Highly recommend this model.  You full control of all functions - even when wearing gloves.  The buttons are easy to locate.  Battery is easy to locate and replace.  Headband is awesomely comfortable.  Nice touch with the 'retro-reflective' logo design too.  Battery life is very good.  A nice battery tester function is very helpful.  The headband stays right where you put it, when you get it adjusted just the way you like it for your head - it locks in place.  Oh, and it's plenty bright for just about anything you want to do in the dark...

title: Great headlamp.
text: Great headlamp.  Several modes, including red-light mode for reading maps.  The proximity mode is excellent and the spot mode does a great job for walking trails in the dark.  Excellent quality.  Battery life is awesome (120 hours).  I have several headlamps and this one is my favorite.  Lightweight too.  The switch can be a little bit difficult to locate when it's on your head though.  It takes some getting used to to find it quickly.

title: Good tip, but for Leki poles it's a touch too wide.
text: This is a good tip.  I'm using it on my Leki poles, but it was a touch too big.  So I put a small piece of black electrical tape around my pole tip and this thing slipped on very snug.  It's good to go.  It looks like the same rubber that Leki uses, which is very high quality rubber.  I would have given it 5 stars if it had fit like a Leki tip!

title: Good tip.
text: Good tip.  Fits the Leki poles correctly.  These last a long time.  My last ones lasted about 10 years of regular hiking.  The rubber is very high quality.

title: Doesn't work.
text: Tried several times.  It just doesn't work.  The patch won't hold.

title: Well crafted and easy to get started.
text: I've tried several different kinds of stilts for entertainment costumes, mostly drywall stilts.  These were ready to use straight out of the box.  So refreshing as the dry wall stilts are a pain to assemble.  I was literally walking in these 3 minutes after opening the box.  It will take time to get use to but my lack of skill walking in these has nothing to do with this great product.

title: Warning... pedal may not go in correctly
text: They obviously didn't verify the parts they sent fit together.  One petal or the hole it goes in was not formed correctly and it will not fit straight.  So when you pedal its not in a strickly circular motion making going difficult.  I have no patience for product that are sent from manufactures without verification.  So sloppy and easy to verify.

title: Worst tent I've ever touched.
text: Other's posted this is a kid tent not an adult tent.  I wouldn't even qualify it as a kid tent.  It's not even a toy tent.  It's the tent that should sit in the box forever because it will break on the first attempt at putting it up.  One of the pole broken under it's own pressure in the first minute.  The netting is netted together with paper like material and instantly breaks.  I can only imagine that people posting positive reviews got it for free and post to keep up their free trials.  I buy a lot of tents.  This isn't a tent.

title: Cheap metal.
text: Within 10 minutes of trying this tent out... a small gust of wind blew into it while I was holding it and bent one of the poles in half.  It bent WAY to easily.

title: Good bed
text: Easy to carry and is very comfortable

title: Five Stars
text: Good quality and easy to setup, fast shipping

title: Four Stars
text: Is Ok for the price on time delivery

title: Perfect for a Fantasy Champ!
text: I've purchased several trophies for our work league the past few years for our FFL champions. This one happened to be picked out by the champ himself (not me unfortunately!). It wouldn't have been my first choice but he wanted the "diamond ring" look. When it arrived, I was a bit surprised at how hefty it was. He proudly displays it on his desk and I must say it does have the "bling" factor. When I ordered the plate, I made a minor error and the company was kind enough to send another one at no extra cost which was amazing! Not only is this a great product, but they were prompt and supportive when I had the issue and it was clearly my fault. I will gladly purchase next year's trophy from this seller. 5-stars!

title: Fits Like a Glove!
text: This is a great CCDW item to have with the Sig Sauer P365XL (with Romeo optics). I have carried it several times over the past few months since purchasing and it works well. I like that it's affordable. I did adjust the retention just slightly to my comfort zone. It has met my expectations and I think it will be durable. Highly recommend!

title: This Was a Dud
text: I purchased this for a cold outdoor event. Unfortunately, it didn't arrive in time but that is my own fault. I charged it as soon as I got it and throughout the first couple of days it was great. I was impressed because it would heat up quickly and was ergonomic. However, when I went to charge it for the second time it wouldn't hold the charge. So now I'm stuck with a defective unit. I don't think it got dropped or anything but even if it did it would speak to the durability of this product. I have initiated a return but for >$10 it's almost not even worth it (and I don't have the original box). Moving forward I'll try to find better options. . .

title: Great EDC Knife!
text:
I have been carrying this knife for the past couple of weeks. I've mainly used it to cut cardboard boxes and plastic or tape. Although I haven't tested in on anything real tough, it is razor sharp and it's perfect for slicing. The ergonomics make it super comfortable in hand and keeps the blade positioned nicely when bringing it down for a cut. It has a long cutting surface. The flipper mechanics are smooth and it flies out with snappy action. The carbon fiber scales look good but don't offer much texture for gripping so it could be an issue if your hands are wet or whatever. If you like carrying larger knives, this will be perfect for you. It is one of the larger knives in my collection, but the clip is deep pocket carry - it is flush with hilt of the knife and short so it's very discrete. Photos included show it between the Ontario RAT 1/2.

The CJRB Crag (AR-RPM9) offers great value in addition to the D2 variants. I already have my eyes on the Tigris which is bigger! I'm thrilled to have added this to my collection and look forward to putting it to good use.

title: Great Affordable FFL Trophy!
text: I ordered this for our newly appointed champion of our (unofficial) workplace league. We usually budget around $25 built in to the winnings for the trophy. This was perfect for the price. I was surprised at how quickly it arrived with the personalized plate attached. It is light but has adequate heft to it. It is also detailed quite nicely, you can feel the bumps and ridges in the football! The champion also approved! I would recommend this trophy for any league that needs an affordable option.

title: Perfect Fantasy Trophy
text: I purchased this for the winner of our work fantasy football league. The (free) engraved plate arrived within a week or so of the trophy and it was easy to apply it. This has just the right amount of size and heft. It was tough to hand this over to the winner because I lost to him in the finals!!! But he really enjoyed it and was showing it off to all of our co-workers. Maybe next year I'll be able to snag one myself! I would recommend this product.

title: Cozy Throw Blanket
text: This is a great throw blanket and it's made of soft and durable material. I will be giving these out as gifts after purchasing them on "Deal of the Day" at a great price just in time for Christmas. It has a simple and classic design. It seems very comfortable and smooth. Great BBN product. GO CATS!

title: Wear Your Sunglasses at Night!
text: Very nice pair of sunglasses! They are lightweight, thin, and flexible. I really like this gunmetal version, it is a classy look. They are comfortable and the lens are the perfect shade for me. I am traditionally rough on sunglasses so I just look for something that's affordable. I can see these selling for a lot more in stores because of the quality. I am satisfied with the purchase and would highly recommend this product!

title: Neat Little Gift
text: I bought this as a gift and the person I gave it to was very pleased. For the sports fans that have a shelf (or room) dedicated to team gear, decor, etc. this is a perfect addition. It doesn't take up much space, but has decent size and is noticeable. It is a great gift or stocking stuffer at this price.

title: Perfect Size, Excellent Cooler
text: I purchased this to take on vacation to the beach. The cooler held up in a 9 hour drive both ways, keeping all of our drinks  cold. I didn't have freezer packs, so I packed two large ziploc bags full of ice. Needless to say, the ice melted and there was some standing water in the bottom when we reached our destination. The cooler didn't leak at all. It also performed great at the beach, the sand shook right off and the inside needed a quick sweep with a paper towel. It folds flat very easily which is convenient. Zipper and mesh pockets were a nice feature and were useful. This will fit a lot of items and is just big enough to not be to awkward to handle in my opinion. For the price I paid I am very satisfied with this product. It seems like this will be a durable cooler that will get a lot of great use. Great product!

title: Decent First Bicycle
text:
This bike was bought as a gift for our daughter's sixth birthday. We assembled it the night before and it took about 30 minutes. As other reviews have mentioned the front wheel was challenging. Of course, our daughter was thrilled when she saw it and immediately took it for a spin. She was able to learn to ride it after literally riding the training wheels off. My only complaint is that they were hard to keep in place (as well as the seat) despite what I thought was adequate tightening. This could present a safety issue as they actually came off while she was in motion. Fortunately, her instinct kicked in and she didn't have any accidents. Overall, the price is right for this bicycle and the kid was very happy. This is good first bike if your child is able to exercise good caution at first and is ready to learn to ride.

Update: by the end of last fall (18') this bike was done. It's now sitting in our garage collecting dust. Despite proper assembly, the seat will sag and the back tire has separated from the rim. This is cheap but it may not last long. I removed a star for this reason.

title: Looking Forward to Camping with Bear Butt!
text: This is a really neat hammock. It is fun for kids and adults! It seems very well constructed and we look forward to using it while camping. The reviews say it all, this is a great product!

title: Nice Design, Great Quality
text: These sunglasses are the perfect size and shape. They seem well constructed and don't feel cheap at all. They are also well priced, I feel as though similar products in stores could be double or triple. I would recommend these for those looking for cheap, good looking shades.

title: Great Sunglasses!
text: These sunglasses really make a difference while driving and on the water. They keep the glare much more manageable and you see a lot more clearly when looking into water. They are light and comfortable as well. Another added bonus is the fact that a hard case AND soft case are included and the soft case doubles as a cleaning cloth. I purchased the dark gray pair and the white/ blue pair. However, the white/ blue pair I gave away as it wasn't my personal style. The recipient of the sunglasses was also impressed. I would recommend these as a pair to keep as a backup,  when driving, or near water. They work really well!

title: Cool Patch But Small...
text: This tactical patch is cool and does glow. However, I should have read the dimensions more closely as it is pretty small. I wasn't too happy about that considering the price, but I still put it on my tactical pack.

title: Excellent Product for Protecting Your Stuff Around Water!
text: This bag was a great purchase. We used it on a cruise ship vacation and it was essential when around the pool for protecting our phones, wallet/ cards, vape mods, and also stored our sunglasses, sunscreen, headphones, and other small items. We tested it and it didn't leak a bit when submerged. The phone case was an added bonus as we were able to take great pictures and video under water in the ocean! This bag is a really great product and it super useful around the pool or lake/ ocean. I would highly recommend, 5 star!

title: Great Tactical Pack!
text: I purchased this back pack for a trip and it was exactly what I was expecting. The design of the backpack is great and it is very spacious. The straps can go around the waist or tucked behind the back. I opted to tuck them and it was still comfortable as are the shoulder straps. I like how the extra slack can be folded and held down instead of hanging out. It seems to be very well constructed and durable. The MOLLE webbing is nice and I used it to attach a tactical light, a pen, and some carabiners. I used the hydration compartment for a hydration bladder, but it is padded and would work well for laptops. The tube came through the shoulder (there is space on each side) and came down through a clip in the shoulder strap. This tactical pack can be used for many different purposes including: backpacking, camping, bug-out, traveling, or even for school or gym. I think it is fairly priced and look forward to using this product often.

title: Wow!
text:
I purchased this product after seeing these types of tumblers pop up everywhere. I wanted to see what all the hype was about. I was pleasantly surprised with this tumbler and this has replaced my Tervis products. I am not sure how this directly compares to the popular YETI brand, but I'm almost certain it works just as well. I have also heard others tell me that some "knockoff" brands hold up pretty similarly to YETI, but I only have experience with this brand. I have left this at the office a couple of times and the next morning it still is cold and has ice! Amazing!

I bought another one for my girlfriend and she also ditched the Tervis and loves this product. We plan to get more of these. I highly recommend this product, try it!

title: My Kids Love It!
text: My five year old daughters love these scooters! They were easily assembled within about 10 minutes. I have seen others giving mixed reviews on the back wheel causing problems, but it doesn't seem to affect my children. I'm guessing this is possibly due to the child's height? The wheels are a good size and seem like they will be durable as well as the frame, handles, and deck. For around $20 I think these would make a great gift!

title: Iconic Kershaw Classic
text:
This is a great knife! My girlfriend carries this daily for various reasons: cutting loose threads/ tags, opening her Amazon deliveries :), self defense, etc. It is super thin and light and the blade comes razor sharp out of the box. There's not much I can say that others haven't said already, but I am very satisfied with this purchase! This is good steel (although it is thin) and just all around great quality and you can tell by holding it. The speedsafe works very well on this model - very snappy. The lock is a great feature also. Personally, I have to carry something a bit bigger, but for smaller hands it is the ideal tool for many different tasks.

I have included pictures to show the color and size - I have it next to the Ontario Rat Model 1 (which is a large knife) for comparison. I would highly recommend this knife for beginners and collectors alike!

title: Great Targets
text: I have been using these the past few times on an outdoor range. You can clearly see where your bullets have hit from a good distance. The extra stickers help freshen up the target and extends use. I really enjoy using these targets and will probably use more when I run out.

title: Perfect Pen Light (for Me)
text: I love this tactical pen light! I carry it every day and it is perfect for me. It has a very small profile, lightweight, and only takes one AAA battery which last a long time for my occasional use. The moonlight mode is great for when you need a small amount of light and the brightest light has helped illuminate dark areas quite easily when I needed it. The clip is tight enough to keep it in pocket. I really like the ease of the tail switch. I don't own any expensive pen lights, but for $15 or so I have to believe that this item ranks well for the price. I consider it to be a very good value.

title: The Hype is Validated!
text: This is a great knife for many reasons. For the price of this knife, you are getting great value as it can easily compete with other knives that cost 2-3 times as much. Although it doesn't have the popular G-10 scales, the nylon feels good in hand. The handle is a bit long, but not so much that it wouldn't still make a great choice for EDC. The AUS-8 steel blade comes super sharp right out of the box. I put it through some small tests and this thing just glides through most of items thrown at it (paper, cardboard, wood, paracord, etc.). The black finish will wear as others have mentioned, but this is not a problem for me. I purchased this because I am new to collecting knives and I felt like after reading all the information I could find that I needed to have the RAT model 1 in my collection. I am not disappointed as this knife holds up to the hype. I think this knife would be great for EDC, hunting/ camping, small cutting tasks, and would also make a really nice gift! If you love knives and don't have one of these yet, you should get one!

title: Cool Cooler!
text: This cooler was something I needed to take my lunch. I find myself using it all the time now for travel, going to the pool, etc. It keeps my drinks cool for several hours and will easily fit at least six 12 ounce cans or bottles/ aluminum pints. I am thinking about purchasing larger coolers of the same design. The zippered pocket on the front is handy as well as the mesh side pockets. I especially like the bungee straps on top, I use them to secure my Oontz Angle water-resistant bluetooth speaker when I am poolside.

title: Good for Concealment
text: I use this for my daily carry - a Glock 43 (size 3 holster). It is a tight fit, but I'm thinking that the 4 might be too loose. However, it doesn't always come out easily from inside the pocket. I know someone else who uses the same holster and size for a revolver and his worked perfect with my Glock, so that might change once it's broken in a little more. I have resorted to using on the waist more often and it feels comfortable as it has a light profile anyway. It comes out from the holster a lot better that way. For the price, I am satisfied with the purchase.

title: Great Product!
text: This is great for anyone with young children! It keeps my daughter's head above water at all times. I even trust it with her swimming in the deep end of the pool. This is a great product!

title: Very cute.
text: It is a nice scarf for my dog. It is too big for small dogs, but I used it anyway.

title: Nice mug!
text: Better than I expected

title: Great item, but not worth the struggle to close it.
text: Great tent. It is a great size for my family of 4. But closing it sucks. It is very difficult to close, if you can close it at all. We have to watch a video and still have difficulties closing it. I regret buying it only because it too hard to close and seriously who wants to deal with that after being in the sun all day.

title: Love it
text:
I've got a couple of the gyro balls with the spring starting mechanism - but I wanted to try out one of the old school ones that used a string to start. Comparing this one to those, I think this one is slightly heavier.

The string works great - easy to start up and get the gyro going. I hadn't realized this one had the LEDs - which look good inside the blue shell.

Trying it out - I believe I can get it going to the same RPMs as the other gyroballs.

The strings (you get a spare) aren't anything special - it wouldn't be that difficult to scrounge up a replacement if those were to get lost.

I'm more than happy with my purchase.

title: Basic Fitbit
text:
Just what I was wanting - something basic. Mainly wanted something to track my steps and somewhat monitor my pulse rate. This fitness band does both of those well. I also like that it reports on your sleep patterns. I typically don't like silicone watch bands, nor having a watch so snug on my wrist - but this band is so light and flexible that it doesn't bother me. I understand that you can wear this all the time - but I do take it off when showering and washing dishes.

The fitness tracker was not that hard to setup - mainly just downloading the app from the Google Play store. The app does require you to set up an account - name & email address, and then put in some data about yourself - birthdate, weight, height, sex.. About what you might expect for a fitness app. I did not activate the premium trial as I don't think I really need it.

All-in-all I'm satisfied with the fitness tracker, and happy with my purchase.

title: Cheaply made - but it works
text:
I purchased a Gryo Ball a few weeks ago and wanted another on that I could keep at work. Found this one selling for about 2/3s the price of what I paid for another brand. Looking at the product page they appeared identical - but comparing the two physically this one is not constructed of the same material.

I tried using it and was able to spin it up easily. So that's a plus. The other ball came with a zippered case - this one did not.

Am I disappointed that this gyro ball isn't as well built as the other? - little bit, but given the price and that it works (for now) I can't complain. If it quits working later I plan on buying a different one - but for now I'm happy with my purchase.

title: Takes some practice to get it going.
text:
When I first got this Gyro Ball I couldn't figure out how to twist my wrist in such a way to make it spin up. I kept at it till I hit upon the correct method. It takes some practice - but now I can keep it going for awhile. You can feel the effect of using this exercise ball in your forearms after using it for awhile. Gives the muscles there a workout.

I like the size of this and that it came with a zippered case. The lights add to the fun of using this. I'm happy with my purchase.

Edited to add: Purchased a second one of these - one without the lights. It's the same was the other one - just without the light module on the one side. Thought the lights were a bit much when using the gyroball at work.

title: Ok ping pong balls
text: As ping pong balls go - these are pretty average. But as a glow-in-the-dark items go.- these are pretty sub-par. Yeah they will.glow, for about half a minute. Even charging them up with a blacklight flashlight didn't help. Probably due to.the kind of plastic that ping pong balls are made of and it being so thin. These aren't great - but they will.do till.I find something better.

title: Works
text:
I set this trail camera up in the back part of my property - which is wooded - just to test it out. Seems to work Ok so far (more below). The camera didn't come with a memory card - so I purchased a 32GB Samsung EVO memory card to use in it - wanting to see if that would be adequate - and it was. I also bought a large package of the Energizer MAX alkaline batteries. The manual recommends using rechargeable batteries and I will probably do that later - as this camera can run down batteries fairly quickly.

I did have some issues with the camera - number one, there was a problem with the strap/buckle that lets you strap the camera to a tree or post. Nothing major - the stitching came loose. I was still able to make it work though and will probably replace the strap when I go to use this camera in the field. The second issues was with getting the motion-sensor function working. It would trigger once and then not again. I played around with the settings and seemed to get it to work - but have no idea what actually fixed the issue.

The camera takes great photos - I've mainly been using it in the time-lapse mode (since I was having issues with the motion function). The photos are very clear and sharp. Daytime photos more so than night, but that's to be expected.

All-in-all I'm happy with the camera and look forward to using it this summer and the coming fall.

title: Bristles are softer than I was expecting
text: I'be been redoing the security bars on the windows of my house. In the past 20+ years they have become a bit rusty and needed repainting. There is some scroll work on the bars which needs some more detailed cleaning. I've been using some other stainless steel brushes - which are larger than these and have a much more stiff set of bristles. I wanted to see if these would work better. They do - and don't. The smaller size helps a lot and the softer bristles do to - to some extent. But they wear out a lot faster. That really is my only complaint - that you can go through a package of these cleaning up the scroll work on the security bars of just two windows. I'll be buy more as I still have about ten windows left to do.

title: Interesting take on a wrist rocket slingshot
text:
I've been playing with these sort of wrist rocket slingshots for years (decades even). I remember getting my first one sometime back in the 1970's when I was a teen. But this is the first one that I've tried using that has multiple bands. Setting up the slingshot took a few minutes - getting the bands in place and straight - not hard to do, just being careful to make sure I was doing it right.

The build quality on this slingshot is pretty clunky/rough in places. It's made of metal so that might be part of the issue. Sizewise I found the slingshot to be slightly smaller than what might fit my hand. Still usable just not comfortable.

I did some target practice using some of my favorite ammo - glass marbles. I found that the multiple band did have an effect on the accuracy. How much was pretty random - more some times, less other. Enough so that I doubt I would use this for more than just playing around. Still it's an interesting design - and I'm having fun with it.

title: About what I was expecting
text:
If I was Tom Hanks stranded on that deserted island - then this kit would have really been a life saver. But, given the quality of some of these items - I think that you might want to have something better in any other sort of survival situation.

But I really don't see this so much as a survival kit - rather more a collection of useful items that can be used on their own. There is a lot of duplication in functionality with some of the items - several whistles and two compasses. The stand out item for me is the tactical pen - with the sharp point on the end. I really like it and have been using it as my daily writing pen. The flashlight is nice - but the battery compartment seems like it was made for some sort of different battery than the AA one I put in it. I've tried out the fire starter and it worked. The knife is a bit small , but it's sharp. Most of the other stuff will probably stay in the case for now.

Not a bad assortment of items - but some pieces are a bit more useful than the others.

title: Fairly well stocked first-aid kit
text:
This kit has pretty much everything you might need for a minor emergency. All sorts of bandages and first aid related items. The one an only thing that I though was of poor quality - was the little plastic compass. Which I'm assuming is in there in case you're hiking and lost in the woods. I would think someone hiking would have a better compass on them. I replaced the one in this kit with an extra one that I happened to have - a somewhat trivial complaint I know. I was surprised to find that you even get a couple tubes of eyewash in this kit.

You got to be a bit careful - I pulled everything out to check out what was in this, and then putting it back I had a hard time getting everything back in the case. This is a pretty full set of stuff - almost too much for the case. You get a little pocket kit - which I never really saw the point of. I've got about a dozen similar kits that I've collected over the years and have never had an occasion to use anything from one. I do carry kits like this full one - in my vehicles and on our boat (when we had one). Handy thing to have when you really need it.

title: Adequate for my needs
text:
I could have gotten something similar to this telescopic cane locally, and for nearly the same price. But this one appeared to have some advantages the others didn't. There wasn't any instructions on using this cane, but it wasn't too hard to figure out. To adjust the length there are three sections which can be pulled out to make the cane longer. The cane in it's fully collapsed state is 21" long, fully extended its 42". To change the lengths you twist the shafts which loosen or tighten the assembly depending on the direction you twist. You can actually pull out a section completely if you're not careful (it slips back in pretty easily). The tip of the cane is interesting. There is a rubber foot that can be removed which exposes a small diameter metal point, that I assume is for use on icy surfaces (we don't get that too often here in Texas). There is another thing that can be screwed on the end of the cane, some sort of round dome looking thing, I haven't a clue what it's purpose might be.

Over-all I happy with the walking stick, I like that it collapses down like it does for easy storage & carrying. And that it feels like pretty solid support when in use. I'm happy with my purchase.

title: Just enough weight
text:
Nice set of ankle weights. I was concerned that a 5LB set might not provide enough of additional resistance for my workouts, but I have to say that I don't think I really need more than that.

The box that these come in says that there are workout videos out on the Gaiam website - but I didn't find any specifically for ankle weights. I also looked through the workout videos on the Gaiam YouTube channel, which is pretty much the same videos. Still, I doubt that you really need something just for weights like this.

The weights fit Ok, and are pretty comfortable to wear - but I would suggest wearing socks that at least cover your ankles - the nylon and Velcro was a bit rough on my skin when I didn't. Overall, I like these weights and will be using them for most of my workouts.

title: I like it
text:
At first I was a little put off on how light this mug is - it's made from some pretty thin metal. But now that I've used if for awhile I appreciate it's light weight. The mug holds around 12 oz of drink - that is if you don't fill it to the rim and leave about 1/2" of space for the lid to be put on the cup. I hardly ever use the lid. My interest in this double-wall mug was more to have it insulating the outside of the mug from the hot liquid inside - not to keep the liquid hot for a longer period of time (I can usually drink 12 oz of coffee before it gets too cold to drink).

So if you're looking for a light-weight mug to use, that will also keep the outside cool to the touch this might be one to consider. I'm happy with my purchase.

title: Lightweight and safe
text: Foam balls are adequate for my needs. They are very lightweight, but still made of some pretty stiff foam. The balls are 2-3/8" in diameter. So far, even with some rough play they haven't damaged anything in the house. The foam surface does start to show some dirt the more they are played with. I'm happy with the product.

title: Strong plastic smell
text: This bar has a very strong smell (least to me) - sort of the smell of polyvinyl chloride (PVC). Not sure if that is what this bar is made of, but it does smell like plastic and it makes your hands smell like plastic. Hopefully the smell will diminish over time. I like using this and think the exercises will help with my hands and wrists. It's got some heft to it, almost like a rubber bludgeon. title: Lost it
text:
I do a lot of walking. A little over a year ago, I was diagnosed as being diabetic (type 2). I've been able to manage it by modifying my diet and daily exercise. I've been walking for at least 30 minutes every day, some days for an hour. Walking really brings down my blood sugar after eating. So I was happy to get one of these Omron pedometers to try out for a month.

Setting up the meter was pretty simple. You just had to install the battery and set the meter. Setting the meter entailed setting the time and putting in your stride length. To find your stride length you simply walk normally for ten steps - measure the distance (in inches), the divide by 10 (mine was 26 inches). There are some other settings - for example using km vs miles. Sounds more complicated than it is. Just be sure to read the instructions.

The meter comes with a few accessories such as a silicone case, a clip, and lanyard. The silicone case has a clip on the back of it, so that is what I used. I clipped the meter to the pocket-watch pocket on my blue-jeans. Which worked great, till I went out walking after lunch and came back without the meter. I'm guessing at some point the pedometer popped off and fell to the ground while I was walking. When I discovered it missing I retraced my steps and tried to find it - unsuccessfully. One of my co-workers even went out and tried to find it. Most of the path I walk in the after-noon is public sidewalks and tend to be heavily used by other walkers - so I'm guessing someone found it. I had the pedometer for about a week before losing it.

IMO -it was my own fault. I was wearing headphones at the time listening to an audiobook. And in hindsight, I should have attached the lanyard strap to the clip and hooked that to a belt-loop. I really suggest doing that.

The pedometer worked fine for me. I compared it to another meter and got similar readings. Operating the meter was easy - there are just three buttons. I really wish I hadn't lost mine.

Just recently I've gotten the urge to do some target shooting in my back yard - I can probably blame watching episodes of [[ASIN:B003NX6C1C Top Shot]] for that. So I wanted to replace my 1377, mainly because I still had all the accessories for it. So I got on Amazon and found this one to purchase.

One of the biggest surprise for me was that this model no longer makes use of Bbs. Gone is the magnetic tip on the end of loading pin. Anyway - even just shooting pellets I am having fun with this gun. I also bought packs of these pellets - [[ASIN:B001DCB61Q Crosman Destroyer .177 Cal, 7.9 Grains, Pointed, 250ct]] & [[ASIN:B002DM0ZIU Crosman Hollow Point Pellets, 0.177-Calibre]]. Both seem to work well.

title: Just what I was looking for
text:
I chose this workout system a bit blindly, but I'm glad I picked it to try out. Having recently been diagnosed as type-2 diabetic, I've been working on managing my condition by adding some daily physical activity and changing my eating habits. Just with walking 30 minutes a day has resulted in my losing about 20 pounds in the past three months (I want to lose 20 more). Now that I've lost weight, I find that I need to tone up. Being over 50, I wanted to do something that was easy to do and low-impact. This Firm Zip Trainer system is perfect for that.

Watching the videos for the first time I really didn't think this was much of a workout - but found trying the exercise that wasn't true. The series of movements that the instructors put you through really work and stretch your muscles. I think that is the thing I like most about these exercises, you get to use muscles that you probably don't use on a daily basis (especially if you're like me someone who sits at a computer for most of the day). I really feel my range of motion has improved since starting this program.

I've only been using this for about a month, and not every day at that. You need some room to do these exercise, and right now the largest clear space I can come up with is my unheated garage. And given it's winter, there's been a number of days when it was too cold to exercise out there.

With this kit, you get the large medicine ball - which can be zipped open to be used in a variety of ways. The medicine ball by itself is five pounds and when put the three pound core ball in it, it becomes eight pounds. That doesn't seem like a lot of weight, but when you're out of shape as I am you will get tired after just a couple repetitions. You also get three DVDs, two of which are the main exercise programs and a third which is a bonus video. You start with disc one, which walks you through the basics of the routines. There are four programs on disc one. Rev!, which is sort of introduction and runs for about 15 minutes, and three full length workouts (22 minutes each) - one for cardio, one to sculpt, and one that is and amped up routine. Each of the programs usually features three of the six instructors, with one leading the exercise and the other two in the background with one doing a modified starter version of the routine and the other doing a more advanced version. The instructor will explain the routine and do a quick demonstration before starting. It can be hard to follow along - so I would recommend watching the videos without doing them first, then go back and follow along. Also of note, the Zip ball doesn't get used in all the exercises - there are even some where they use regular weights (looks like they are using 10 pound dumbbells). They also use typical exercise mat for some things.

The exercise sets on the second DVDs are more of the same, but gives you more of a workout. The bonus DVD is a routine that works your feet (you do it bare foot) and your abs.

My guess is most people will watch the videos a couple times and then once they learn the routines quit playing them. I also think that people will cherry pick certain parts of the routines and create their own versions of the workouts (least that I what I will be doing). Like I mentioned before, I'm a bit over fifty and out of shape, so there is a limit to what I can do right now - as I improve I'll add in more.

Something to note - there are a couple booklets that come with this set. One of which has bios of the six trainers that are featured on the videos. These are some really fit women, and I assumed most of them were a lot younger that they apparently are. The youngest is 31 (or was when these were made), and the oldest is 43 (and most of them have had children). That really surprised me.

The other booklet that you get is a 48-page nutrition guide / meal planner. I mentioned I had already been losing weight and I've done that by going to a high-protein/low-carbohydrate diet (which is what my doctor recommended for my diabetes). This nutrition guide recommends that too. The booklet really doesn't provide any detailed recipes, but it does give you a pretty decent meal plan to follow (very similar to the one I was provided by my diabetes educator).

To wrap up this review I'll say that I'm enjoying this Zip Trainer kit, and I liked it enough that I went and bought the [[ASIN:B0056H4GHK The Firm Express DVD Kit]].

Something to maybe mention that might interest some people, these videos are a product of GAIAM, which is the company that also puts out most of the DVD sets for the Discovery Channel - shows like Mythbusters and Dirty Jobs.

title: Goes the distance
text:
I bought this pocket pedometer along with this book - [[ASIN:1566252873 10,000 Steps a Day to Your Optimal Weight: Walk Your Way to Better Health]]. Back in October (2013) I was diagnosed as having type-2 diabetes and as part of my management program I started walking in the afternoon. Plus I figured it would be a good way to maybe lose a few pounds (which my doctor encouraged). With the exception of a few days over the holidays I have kept to my goal and walked for 30-minutes every day. I've found this pedometer a great source of motivation - and for keeping track of all the steps that I take in a day. I very rarely get to 10,000 steps - but there are days that I come close. I have my meter set for a daily goal of 6,000 steps can usually achieve that.

This meter is simple to use - I just throw it in a pocket in the morning and keep it there for the rest of the day. I like that it also displays the time and use it as a pocket watch too. Once or twice a week I plug it into my computer and upload the data to the software that comes with the device. The software is very easy to use - and it keeps track of your records. You can look at individual days, or weeks, or months. The device can store a week (7-days) of data, so really all you need to do is upload once a week.

Like I mentioned, I've been carrying one of these pedometers around in my pants pocket every day for about three months. The meter is starting to show a bit of wear - the cap that fits over the USB plug has gotten to be loose. The outer plastic casing is getting pretty scratched up. The device still works fine, it's more of a cosmetic issue. I may end up purchasing another one near the end of the year.

Setting up this meter was really easy - I think you can do it with the buttons on the back of the device, but I found it easier to use the software. Main thing you have to set is your stride - how long each of your step is. The instruction sheet shows you how to get that measurement. You can also set a daily goal, and the meter shows your progress toward that as a bar graph.

I originally picked this meter at random from the large selection of such devices here at Amazon, but after three months of use I think I made a good choice and would recommended it.

title: What a workout!
text:
And that was just putting this bench together. Was given one of these as a Christmas present. But it was still in the box - so it had to assembled. From start to finish this took me more than an hour to do, and I built up a sweat doing it. This review is more about that experience as I haven't had the bench put together long enough to comment on how well it works for regular exercise.

First off, the model I got is a bit different than the one show in the photo on this product page. It's very similar, which leads me to think that there have been some recent design changes. The main differences I see comparing the photo to the one I got is that the two bars that rest on the floor are separate items that now attach with bolts instead of being welded. The only other thing I notice is that the pads on my bench are a solid color material, and not two -toned. There may be other differences but given the limited amount that I can see from the photo, that is all I can comment on.

You are going to need some tools to put this bench together. Number one on that list would be an [[ASIN:B000NIK9S2 adjustable wrench]] - you could probably use a socket wrench it you have a set. You also need at least a [[ASIN:B000NNFSKG wide mouth pliers]] - again you could use another adjustable wrench if you had one or even some regular slip-joint pliers. There are a lot of bolts & nuts that go into the assembly of this bench that need to be tightened. You're also going to need a philips-head screw driver. And in my case, I also needed a rat-tail file and a regular metal file.

Opening the box I was confronted with a lot of parts and pieces. Luckily the instruction were on top of all of that. Reading through them I found them pretty easy to understand and with the illustrations it was simple to follow the directions. All the hardware (nuts, bolts, washers, screws, and grease packet) was vacuum sealed to a piece of cardboard and everything was plainly labeled so that matching the right part to the directions was really easy. But be sure to read through the instructions before starting the assembly.

I found the bench fairly easy to assemble - but then I have had some previous experiences with doing this kind of thing. I would imagine some people might find the process a bit overwhelming. I did have one major hiccup. Step 5 has you connect the two parts of the frame (the bar that runs the length of the bench) together with two bolts. One piece of the frame slides into the other and you are suppose to line up to holes on one with the screw threads on the other. My pieces didn't line up. The holes didn't exactly match, so I could not get the bolts to screw in. I spent a half-hour with a rat-tail file trying to make one side of the holes larger, and then I got the bright idea to simply file down the end of the frame itself. That worked. If I hadn't been able to do that I would have had to return the bench and get a replacement. Once past that hurdle the rest of the bench was a snap to put together. I did think I had some 'spare parts' as I had a single nut and bolt left over when I was done - but reading through the directions again I found that I had missed putting those on the tip of the pivot bracket.

Now all I have to do is find the floor space to put this and time to use it. I'm giving this four-stars mainly due to the issue with the frame. I probably should give it an even lower rating because of that, but now that I have it all together it does look to be a decent piece of exercise equipment. I may later come back and update my review to comment on the use I'm getting out of it.

Every emergency/survival/outdoors kit should have at least one and for 10-11 bucks its hard to go wrong.

title: If you are used to L.E.D. flashlights you probably won`t like it
text: Dim yellowish light color. Irregularly shaped pattern. Good for close up spaces in total darkness. Any ambient light and you wont know it is even on. As a dive light, no way. Waterproof, small/lightweight it will serve some purposes. Not a main or primary light by any means. If you are used to L.E.D. lights (and the mini powerhouses that they have today) you will probably not like this. Pales in comparison to any L.E.D. I have, key chain flashlight included.

title: Not bad for a Xenon flashlight / not great either
text: Very dim, but it is a Xenon flashlight. About as much light (real yellowish light [Xenon]) as a dollar store key chain light. Short run time. Definitely waterproof. Easy to carry, lightweight. Not a serious dive light by any means. Decent little waterproof back-up light for my outdoors bag.

title: Works well...........
text: Bright strobe and passable flashlight. I paid 20 bucks, now 35 bucks. Of course if you need it in an emergency, cost is no issue and would overlook a less than stellar flashlight. Bought it just in case however my travels are usually on freshwater ponds/reservoirs (sometimes at night)for fishing. I also have a  EGear Splash Flash LED Light (Awesome product!) and a Pelican Mini Flasher 2130 LED Flashlight attached to my flotation vest and this flasher on my kayak. Better safe than sorry. Feel better having it. Works well, no problems or complaints. Actually had to use it once, almost got run over by a larger boat at night. Flipped it on (the strobe) and they veered away, slowed down, came back around and checked to see if I was OK. Have had it almost a year now and test it every month.

title: In my opinion a must have
text: This is the 1.5 inch version, kind of small but what great action. Good casting weight though. I have had good sized fish (bass over 5 lbs) follow this right up to shore. I catch mostly bass with it but have had some really, really big bluegill and crappie nail it. Lifelike action you can`t really fish it "wrong" For the bigger bass I use the 2.75" version of this. 40+ years of fishing I have always sworn by Rapala lures. Sure you can buy cheaper imitations, but these things always swim true and catch fish, period.

title: This thing dives
text: A little heavier/bigger (fatter) than I was expecting, I might have misread the chart when ordering. Dives deep and quick, lots of action. Runs true. Using a medium-light to medium action rod with 8 lb test it is a bit heavy but the rod tip tells the tale. A constant wiggle, tight but heavy wiggle. Good action. Did not test the depth completely, the one I bought was for a 10ft dive. Ran it in 6 foot of water and kissed the bottom in no time. It gets down fast. Should be a good lure, skips the bottom but doesn`t dig in. Large lip tends to bump off items.

title: Doesn`t run straight, not a 6-8 ft diver, but good action.......
text:
Runs a little sideways and tough to get it to dive beyond 3-4 feet. You really have to crank on it to get a good depth. Probably better for trolling. Granted at 4 bucks I wasn`t expecting a perfect bait. Good action though, real tight wobble and rattle. Will work throwing it across the tops of the weeds, won`t bore down into them. The slight sideways motion (from right to left but consistent) does have its advantages for my local spot. There`s a lot of overhanging trees/bushes and a few protruding pieces of structure. I can "swim it around" those areas with a well placed cast. If I lose it, 4 bucks.

Almost the same as the Norman Baby N 1/4-Ounce Crankbait that I reviewed only that one was supposed to be a 3-5 ft diver. Seems the claims are off by about 1/2, again 4 bucks...........

title: Not bad for the price........
text: First it says 25 pcs in the description, the package that came says 20 pcs, I got 22 pcs. Guess they couldn`t make up their mind. Anyways they are sharp though slightly smaller than my perception of the picture, The largest ones would fit a small to medium sized crank-bait say 2" - 2 1/2" maybe 3" but you don`t get very many that size. The bulk of them are the smaller ones that would work well for small baits 1" - 1 3/4". 4 bucks, definitely worth if using for smaller baits. Mostly for medium to small(er)baits. Smallest size would be for pan fish baits.

title: Can`t beat the price / functionality...update...........
text:
Bought this to replace an identical South Bend pair I had and lost. No not the absolute best pair you can buy, but the last pair I had for 20 years (regular use) or more and never had a problem with them whatsoever. Great for changing out treble hooks/split-rings on crank baits and other lures. Easy to use, comfortable non slip grip and you can`t beat the price for what you get. Think I paid $1.99 "back in the day" and still only 5 bucks now.

The downside I saw with my last pair was the plating started to come off after a few years (remember a ton of use). Showed signs of mild rust. Kept them lightly oiled but never had a problem at all.

***************8
Update, not quite as sturdy a pair as my "old school" ones. Still a very fair price for a pretty good item.

title: The cone of pros and cons
text:
I guess this would be useful for certain purposes. It turns the great AMP 1 LED flashlight into an "area" light. You get a uniform but relatively small area light and a small spot that shines through the tip of the cone.. The cone is thickly "frosted" and as an area light yeah maybe in a small two person tent. This diffuses the light and could be useful in a 3-5 foot range but of course more in total darkness, Outdoors at night with ambient light (starlight/moonlight-city lights) it does not do well at all. In total darkness it works fairly well, I got 7+ feet decent 360 degree area light though not too much more. Does not stay on very well. If you bump/drop it (even on carpet) or put it in a pocket, camping/gear bag etc. it will come off.

So the pros: Allows you the option of an small area light if you already have the AMP 1 LED flashlight. Small lightweight cone, easy to carry. Really a potentially good backpacking/light camping light, as you get 2 for one/flashlight(if you already have it ) and small area light "conversion". Feels pretty sturdy, not likely to get crushed in a gear bag. Diffused light not harsh on the eyes.

The cons: Not super bright, limited application. Does not attach/stay on very well. Easy to lose. 6-7 bucks for a buck worth of plastic.

title: Worth the price............
text: Versatile little light. Clips to the underside of a cap or you can clip it to a front pocket. Rotates more than 90 degrees (around 120 degrees) You can also set it down and use as an area light. 2 white LEDS are very bright, a good 50+ feet of lighting. The 2 green LEDS are very bright as well, almost too bright up close for reading a map etc. Either mode would work great if hitting the outdoors at night. Excellent trail light/night fishing etc. There is a ridge around the switch, takes getting used to but not likely to accidentally turn  on if in a pocket/brush up against something. Compact and light weight. Better lighting than most this sized/cap lights that I have seen. My new outdoor favorite clip light.

title: Good action though not a 3-5 ft diver.
text: Good action, could not get 3-5 ft even with a fast retrieve. More like 2 ft.(clear water situation visibility to 3 feet easy to gauge) Maybe if fast trolling you could get 3-5 ft. Runs a little sideways, may have had my knot a little off center. Looks good in the water. Did not catch any fish with it the first time out but then again I threw all my standard "confidence baits" and only got one 12" fish that day. No one else was getting them either that day. Nice action, I will catch fish with it I am sure and for 4 bucks if I lose it no great loss. I just took off one star for the depth claim. Should have known, usually claims are overstated and after a second look at the size of the lip, I should have known. The lip is small, could not get much depth. My bad. I will buy one of these rated at 6-8 ft and/or study lip length a bit more closely.

title: They`re sharp
text: Bought these for changing out hooks on my smaller deep diving crank-baits that hit the bottom/get dull fast and after I`ve sharpened them to death and new hooks are needed. Dial-a-size box design. Most sizes are pretty small here so be advised. More for the 1" to 1 1/2" length "crank" type baits not really for the 3" or 4" bass lures.

title: Not a "serious" survival tool but great in a pinch
text: I would not go into a survival situation counting on this as my primary tool. However it is useful and better than nothing. Inexpensive, compact and quite a few features that are useful. I carry it in my outdoor/fishing gear. Some of the features have been very useful to me, though I carry this as a back-up to my serious outdoor equipment and have only been in a "survival" situation a few times (without this but it would have come in handy had I not been so extremely well equipped and prepared for the situation) Worth it to have stowed away because of its compact/light weight and price....................... as a back-up

title: Tiny, bright, versatile and the price is right
text: I keep one in my fishing box (Night fishing) and I keep another one clipped to my fishing vest. Really works quite well for its size. Enough light to tie knots, go through the tackle box, walk around the lake etc. So compact and light it takes up no room and you I don`t even realize it is clipped on to my vest. Good area light (for its size) I surprise other fishermen/campers when  they see it clipped to my vest, they laugh, I turn it on and all I hear is "where can I get one?"

title: Bluegill pattern works very well
text: I use these at my local spot in the spring/summer when the bass are chasing the bluegill. Absolutely nail `em. I usually out-fish others 2 to 1. But you have to know how to use them. Too fast they seem to flap around and don`t have a natural look and will rise a bit. Medium to slow(er) retrieve they look more natural, maintain a good constant depth and they get nailed. At least in my location and experience with these. You can also bounce them off the bottom a bit kind of like a jig with  a  very slow and pause action. Another thing is to add a spinner rig to it much like a "Beetle Spin" lure. More attraction more vibration. A versatile and excellent lure.

title: Very nice
text: The rod goes together easily. Sturdy, casts very well and I have caught some decently large sized bass (7 lbs +) and it handled the fish with no problem. Sensitive feel yet the rod has some backbone to it. One of, if not the best portable units I have owned. Goes well on my motorcycle to some out of the way fishing spots. Extra space inside for some tackle. For 40 bucks this thing is really pretty inexpensive for what you get. I would definitely recommend it  and if you are looking for a good portable set-up, here it is............

title: Good all around unit
text: This is basically a like version of the Energizer Weather Ready 3 In 1 Flashlight. The comparison, the Kaito is a bit longer and a tad wider (square vs round). It also is not quite as bright as a flashlight. The Energizer has a focused bright white/yellow beam, the Kaito more white, wider pattern with a small spot and several rings around it. Both work well, just different. The Kaito is stronger as an area light. The amber/yellow night light is brighter as well on the Kaito. The Kaito being larger has a larger area light with larger "lens". Price, the Kaito is about half the price, 8 bucks vs 18 bucks. If size is the factor the Energizer wins, for all around light and price the Kaito wins. The energizers seems a bit better well made and is more comfortable in the hand. Both have the same adjustable strap.

title: Great all-purpose light.
text:
Magnetic end which easily supports it`s own weight, glow in the dark switch, pretty bright for a small little unit. Pocket (or pocket type) clip. Mine is not completely smooth like the picture. Mine is ribbed or bumpy (in the middle) which makes for a more non slip grip. (Think they might have sent me the 50 lumen version, it is ribbed in the picture and mine is definitely 35 lumens at least, ordered a 50 lumen one so we`ll see) For the flashlight nut or outdoors-person this is a must have, or a should have at the very least. Very useful item.

Update..............
Received the 50 lumen model. Just a tad bit brighter. Same everything, I can only tell them apart by the switch color or if I light them up in a dark room. At sunrise with some light coming up it is hard to distinguish ones brightness from another. 50 lumens only a buck more, well worth the price (either of them)

title: No question a good value
text:
Pretty bright, not quite 140 lumens but definitely 100+. Compact and lightweight. Good wide coverage, the adjustment to a concentrated beam is not as good as some in this class, but overall a great 10 buck flashlight. Mine is only single mode, but I sometimes hate to have to cycle through them all and am very happy with it the way it is.

Definitely worth the money.........

title: Work great for motorcycles........
text:
Bought these for those in-between rain / motorcycle days, when it isn`t raining but has been all night/roads are soaked. Keeps all that "spray" off your lower legs, keeps the old Levi`s dry. I wear them with waterproof boots. Perfect. Easy on-off/velcro (15 seconds to put on or take off!), easy to stow away, space savers. Much better than dealing with the old rain suit/pants on a day when that road "spray" is your only enemy.

Worth the price...........

title: Can`t beat the price for what you get, really........
text:
The light isn`t all that bright, it wouldn`t light up much at night with city lights around. On back country roads it would be fine though you can get much brighter for a few more bucks. 2 modes, the flashing mode can be seen from quite a distance You also get a separate red flasher/tail light. You get all the mounting for both headlight and taillight. Easy to remove from the mounting. The tail light also has a built in belt clip. 7 modes, waterproof seal, real bright (even with cheap batteries provided) and compact (smaller than most I have seen) That alone makes it well worth the price. Plus you get batteries for all (4 headlight, and 2 taillight albeit the batteries are major cheap)

Strictly as a bike headlight, eeehhh, 2 modes fair in brightness. Keep looking but a good back-up or small flashlight.

Taillight, worth 3 bucks easy. I will use this for walking.

For the price (unless you are looking for a serious bike light) you can`t really go wrong...................

title: Not bad at all, really good actually
text:
The one I received is very solid. No give at all yet all functions are easy to open. I was expecting a flimsy little unit for under 4 bucks. I was pleasantly surprised. I own several rather expensive Swiss Army Knives and some that are of that type that range from very inexpensive to lower/medium price range. This I would put as way better than the bargain ones I have and equal or better to the medium price range ones based on initial use. Do not know about longevity but it has a solid feel, it is very heavy, something the bargain ones lack because of cheap/flimsy materials. I figure I will use it and keep the really nice ones as the back-up (Fishing, camping) It`s under 4 bucks, what would you expect and if it lasts a season I`ll be happy (I would bet it will last for quite some time)

I`ll say this, it looks and feels like an expensive Swiss Army Knife and I have owned many of the real ones for several decades.

5 Stars, Price + function + sturdiness (longevity? but under 4 bucks) = A great deal

title: Good all around light
text:

This is the type of flashlight you would want (or I would) going into a garage/basement when the power goes out or if going outside to check a fuse box. Nice feel in the hand. Good to have on hand, in a drawer etc. Switch feels a little soft, no "click" in either position but I would buy it again............

*************************
Update, the switch started "clicking" with some use. Don`t know if that is good or bad. Simple design though, if switch goes you can easily "rebuild" it. I still would buy another one...........

title: Fabulous mid-size pack w/ Scabbard
text:
This is far and away the finest pack I've ever used. Basically a Halftrack with the addition of a removable scabbard.
Quality of construction is top notch pretty much everywhere. That's a good thing, because there are zippers in several key areas, which I consider a strategic weakness. The scabbard zips to the main ruck, with spring clips at the top. The zippers each have a little hook that they catch on to keep them from accidentally riding up and the scabbard coming loose -- very nicely done. The handles are very sturdy, and well placed. PALS webbing is very useful, and well placed. I have several pouches of assorted types in various places. I'm extremely happy with this pack.

Minor beefs:
-The shoulder straps are far apart, designed for guys with a large frame. I'm a bit on the small side, and it's uncomfortable if I don't have the front clip pulled tight to keep the shoulder straps closer together.
-The belt only attaches to the scabbard, and without the scabbard it's shoulder straps only.
-the bottom of the scabbard hangs down without a reliable means of pulling it up out of the way when not in use. I've tried folding mine up, but it doesn't stay. Not a big deal, but it should have some sort of hook or clip like the Scabbard's zippers do.
-Zippers form the critical connectors in several points, with no backup if they fail. Granted, these are some tough zippers, but I've seen tough zippers fail before. I have a half dozen very nice, heavy duty packs with zippers that have failed. I like the utility of the zipper, but it needs some contact points for a backup -- even just putting PALS webbing all along the zipper surfaces would allow field expedient 550 cord securement, though you could argue that the addition of such potential snag points increases the likelihood of zipper failure due to catastrophic hang-ups.

title: Light, durable, effective
text:
Used this during a 2 day hike in a cave in the southeastern US. At ambient 58F near ~2,100' AMSL, 1 Esbit 14g fuel tablet just brings 1.5l of water to a boil before burning out. They claim 12 min. burn time. I only observed around 8~9 min, but it did what I needed, was smaller and lighter than propane canisters, etc. Fuzzy guess says the cost per pot heated is similar to propane, with these being a bit more trouble/less flexible, but smaller and lighter.

Compared to Trioxane, these tablets seem to have about ~30% more energy per tablet, but that's just this backpacker's impression. They're harder to light than trioxane, but not overly difficult.

This little stove has a slightly wider base than the old US Army issue Trioxane stoves. This makes balancing a pot on it much easier. Note that canteen cups don't balance well -- it's just a bit too wide for them to fit comfortably. You can sort of jam one in, but it's precarious and falls over if you so much as sneeze at it. This makes sneezing at your canteen cup highly discommended. A great loss, to be sure.

title: Great lightweight light/lantern.  Perfect for camping/power outages with kids
text:
What doesn’t it do?

That was my son’s reaction when I first showed off this light to him. We had similar one from a popular manufacturer that recently broke. We used it all the time for camping and during power outages. This one does everything that lantern did and more.

I was skeptical about the brightness of the flashlight feature. It appears to be a fairly large COB with a projection (magnifying) lens over it. I used it in my backyard tonight and it’s just about as bright as a standard LED flashlight.
The strobes are a cool feature. I hope to never use them in an emergency but have some fun playing with them with my kids. The magnetic base is cool too. Good for use under a car hood or under the vehicle itself. Strong enough magnets to keep it in its place.

The lantern is why I bought this. It’s bright, lightweight, and somewhat durable. It lights up a tent or cabin real nice. We use them during power outages as well (we get a handful a year). I love the fact this is rechargeable and even though we all have the cables, this came with 2 of them. Nice touch.

title: Not for heavier bottles or feeble hands
text:
The cage is great but the mount is difficult. I tried several methods of attaching to handlebars, due to slippage - no matter how tightly the grip was set. The best was some black Gorilla Tape wrapped a couple of times around the bar, then tightening down the mount as much as possible. Even then it is likely only good for a road bike, not mountain biking - for two reasons:
1. The mount, as described above, has a tendency to slip under the weight of a water bottle and some jostling
2. The cage is not adjustable and therefore probably going to work best only with the "right-sized" bottle. A smaller bottle will bounce right out. Something a small bungee will fix..

NOTE: once closed you may want to use a large screwdriver to open the mount back up.
If you are looking for a product that will not move, at all, after mounting to a bar, check out the 'Topeak CageMount' (also available through Amazon). That one works very well, even for mountain biking.

title: It is a good product for flexible use-cases, but...
text:
Updated 6/18/14 - As predicted the plastic did break. While riding on a slightly bumpy road with a half filled bottle in the cage, the two plastic areas at the mount points simply gave way. The fix is fairly simple but may require a quick trip to a hardware store. Using rubber washers against the plastic and metal washers against the frame (mount points) and bolt heads, the cage is now [probably] better than new. I doubt it will break again, as the new mounting method distributes weight/load more evenly across the plastic, and the rubber washers offer a bit of shock-resistance. Hopefully the manufacturer will read this, having likely heard similar reports from other customers, and fix the issue - if not done already. I still like the design and flexibility.

Original Review: The only problem here is the plastic to metal nut that tightens down to hold the sliding cage in place. I do not see that lasting for a long time. But with a trip to the hardware store I was able to get all metal parts, with washers to protect the plastic cage, hoping to avoids cracks and snaps down the road. If you only use one size container, thus unlikely to move it around, the this should work just fine.
The great thing is that this does hold nearly any bottle within the size range in place, without issue. Even when mountain biking I had no problems with the 12oz Poland Springs bottle that was in there.

title: Best of the rest
text:
If you are looking for a bar mounted cage-mount that will accept pretty much any cage this is likely the best you will find. Competing products that use various types of vice-like mechanical mounts do not compare. They will probably always slide around, not strong enough to hold a full water bottle. But this Topeak CageMount works great. It grips tightly (with the help of the included "bar wrap" - a piece of rubber that protects from scratches and assists the mount in staying put), and with the cage attached holds even a 32oz cup full of iced-tea.
NOTE: if you want a product that can be easily moved from bar to bar / bike to bike, then this will not satisfy that requirement. In order for it to mount tightly and be functional there are a couple of bolts to loosen. Maybe the manufacturer sells the bar mount half, as the cage mount portion could be removed while leaving the bar mount piece in place. Just a thought for those Mountain and Road Bikers out there.

Other notes:
- these are packaged one per bag - not by pair, something to consider when purchasing a large box
- one warmer works incredibly well as a phone warmer. If you keep your phone in your front coat pocket while enjoying the outdoors, and it s***s off due to cold - that will... not... happen if one of these share the pocket with that phone.

title: These work very well, if...
text: Be sure to have tight-fitting socks, with as little slip as possible. If they are stuck to the bottom of the sock then they will easily bunch-up as your foot enters a boot; more than likely with a ski boot. I found that sticking them on top of my toes worked better - both for entering the boot without issue and the warming effect. title: Decent bottles, but with questionable longevity.
text:
Original Review (5 Stars):
I bought a pair of these in Indigo and Silver for my wife and I a couple months ago. We filled them with margaritas and took them to the beach. ;-) They worked beautifully. Now, we used them as overnight water bottles. I fill them about half way with ice then top with water, and they are still icy the next morning, and sometimes even the next day after work (about 18 hours later). The flip-up lid is great for 1-handed use. The little plastic ring, while looking a little weak, has actually stood up very well. The rubber grip and otherwise textured surface makes them easy to hang onto during long walks. I've never had the slightest problem with leaking or spilling. We absolutely love these, and will continue using them daily for years to come.

Update, reduced rating to 3 Stars:
My wife and I have been using these bottles daily for about two and-a-half years. After about a year, both bottles' vacuum seals failed, so water will no longer stay cold overnight, even when filled completely with ice right before bedtime. Further, the seal between the cap and bottle has proven to be less than adequate, as it lets some moisture out into the cap's threads every day. title: Good Eco-Friendly Exercise Mat
text: This is a good eco-friendly exercise mat.  It comes rolled up with some instructions wrapped around it.  There are some Yoga poses pictured on the label.  The label states that the mat is anti-slide, PVC-Free TPE, Waterproof, gentle, odorless, tearproof, material friendly, and resilient.  There are cleaning notes and a warning as well.  The mat cannot go in a washing machine or dryer, it needs to be spot cleaned or it can be cleaned inside a bathtub full of water to cover the mat.  The warning on the label states that the mat will decompose over time and that cracking and dryness over time are normal.  To extend the life of the mat, avoid excessive heat and direct sunlight.  With that said, it's difficult to say how long the mat will actually last.  So far, the mat seems to be holding up well and has not torn so far.  It is lightweight and thin, so the support it provides is good.  It is soft and comfortable to use.  I do think there is somewhat of an odor to it though but it's not terrible.  It is nice that it is eco-friendly.

My 5’’ screen shows me cal, distance, time, laps...
The folding process is super easy! And like I said before it is not super heavy, and when going down to the floor is smooth, soft and slow. It does not fall fast.
It has a space where you can put your phone or tablet on the front. 2 cup (or towels or whatever) holders on the sides. And the STOP button with the strap for emergency.
