I went with an XL in this shirt, but it's too big for my tastes, especially in the neck and shoulders. It seems nice and well made if you're looking for a polyester shirt, though.

title: Not what we'd call a wide mouth....
text:
This bottle is advertised as having a wide mouth, but ours didn't. I don't know if we ended up with a standard mouth, but what we got isn't what we'd call wide mouthed. My husband was disappointed in that. Otherwise, it's nice. It fits in a cup holder and the lid screws off and on. The lid is attached, too, so it won't fall off. That does cause it to get in the way sometimes when drinking from it, though. Unopened, it's kept ice for over 24 hours, so it does a great job of keeping liquid cold.

It also comes with a cleaning brush, but it's not the sturdiest thing. Ours didn't last long.

title: Longer than average from the seat to the handle bars...
text:
This is a nice bike and it looks great. It's a little longer than most bikes this size from the seat to the handle bars. My child has to stretch to reach on this one, so it's not his favorite to ride. He also doesn't like that it doesn't have a kick stand. While most smaller sized bikes don't have one, in our experience so far anyway, some do. Between our 3 boys, we've went through quite a few bikes as they've grown, and I believe only one of them has had a kickstand.

Keep in mind that when ordering bikes online there is assembly required and this one is no exception. In stores, they're already put together, but getting it home might be an issue. My husband has put together a few bikes now, so he's comfortable with the process. If you're not comfortable with it, there will be the extra expense of paying someone else to get it together. My husband didn't have any trouble with it, and it went pretty quickly for him.

title: Works Great....
text: This is a nice set. The ball has to be inflated, but it comes with a pump to do so. It takes a bit of effort, but it's not bad. As a bonus, one of my children finds the ball a great way to destress. It also comes with 3 resistance bands, with the green being the easiest and the grey one the hardest. I've been using them with Leslie Sansone videos and they work well. I much prefer these to the ones with handles. I was always afraid I was going to smack myself in the face with the dangling handles when I needed to pull them tighter. I've been pleased with this whole set.

title: Shrinks a great deal after washing....
text: These shrink a great deal in the wash, so it will fit tighter than what it fits before washing. (I was surprised at just how much these did shrink.) Still, I like this shirt. I normally wear a medium to large. I have a large and an x-large(for different teams) in this shirt. The shoulders in the x-large is the only thing that makes me prefer the large. Otherwise, I prefer a looser fit, like the x-large gives me. The material is soft and comfortable. It's not too thick, nor too thin. I like the feminine cut to the design, too.

title: My children have had fun with it....
text: My children have had fun playing with this ball. It's lightweight and great for them. They don't play any type of organizational sports, but simply play for fun(and by their own rules). The lighter weight of it might make a better practice/playing ball for those with weaker knees/ankles(etc) or for younger players.  It arrived without needing additional air, but after play it does need more. That's true of any ball we've ever bought, though. It looks like a nice ball that will last a decent amount of time.

title: Super light duty....
text: My oldest son has been using this bin in his room for a bit of extra storage. There is an open hole on the front, like a handle. Most of the other storage bins like this that we've used have had a piece sewed on to grip and these don't last long with any kind of pulling and tugging. I would have thought the hole grip would help this bin last longer, but the chrome piece that is supposed to surround the hole has already came off. I can see the cardboard in between the cloth pieces. My son doesn't move it around much, either. I only recommend this type of bin for super light duty purposes. I wouldn't use it for storing anything that has to be moved around often.

title: Nice little work table for us....
text:
We put this table in the corner of our dining room for my boys to have a workspace, without always having to use the main table. (It's a pain to have to clean off unfinished work to eat.) It's proved to be sturdy so far for that use. It looks nice, too. It has plenty of room for work room, whether it's on the laptop or paper work(art/workbooks). We also have a lamp, a couple of small potted plants, a diffuser, and a globe on it, so it's pretty roomy for a small table. There is one corner that arrived banged up a bit, but it's not too bad. It's easy to simply turn the bad corner into the corner of the room, so it doesn't show. If we were using it in the center of the room, I'd be more concerned, though.

Assembly was easy. We've enjoyed having it around. Aside from the banged up/dented spot, it looks nice.

title: Great for cold days...
text: These are on the snug side, like most exercise wear, but they do have a good bit of stretch to them. They're actually not as snug as many exercise pants I've tried. I normally wear a large in pants and go up for exercise wear, since I usually don't really care for overly tight clothing. These in size large are surprisingly comfortable for me. I like that the waist is a bit higher, so it doesn't cut into my stomach. They're thick and lined with fleece, so I'd only recommend these for exercise in a colder climate. They'd be great for extra warmth on walks/runs/bicyling/etc on cold days. There's a pocket in the top of the waist that's great for a card or key or any little thing that's needed, too.

title: Despite some negatives, it's soft and warm....
text:
When I first pulled this out of the box I was disappointed in the material. It's the shiny, easily snaggable type of material. (While I don't overly care for this type of material, a benefit is that it doesn't seem to fade as quickly.) My husband also commented that the quality, with the vinyl sticker logo on the front, wasn't as good as he was expecting. Those types of stickers aren't typically all that durable and will peel with washings. It also fits on the smaller side. I like my hoodies to fit loose and while this isn't tight, it's not as loose as I've come to expect from hoodies. I normally go for a medium to large. I also have an XL Rams hoodie and it fits much closer to what I'd expect. If you're wanting it to be loose and comfy, I'd say size up. If you want a closer fitting hoodie, you'll most likely be happy with your normal size.

Despite the negatives, it is a super comfy hoodie, at least when sized up. It's soft and while it's not for bitter cold weather, it's kept me warm on colder days when I'm mostly just walking from a vehicle to a building.

title: Works, but not the best fit for me...
text:
I've been using this band with a couple of Leslie Sansone DVDs. (I got the DVDs at a thrift store, so it didn't have the included band she uses.) It works, but it's not the most comfortable thing. I've frequently thought about just getting a smoother band to work with. While I appreciate that the braided band is more durable, it hasn't been the best fit for me. When I pull it around my back or pull back on my stomach to work out various arm muscles, it's uncomfortable. While I also appreciate the hand grips, the band is too long for most of the exercises I do with it. I have to pull on the band itself to get the proper resistance, so the hand grips are left flopping around. (I'm surprised I haven't hit myself with them yet. This part doesn't sway my rating, since that comes with the territory of hand grips, but it is something to consider.) The braid isn't the most comfortable even on my hands.

That said, my husband is taller and uses it a little differently than me. He's able to use the hand grips properly and he likes it fine. So, depending on height and arm length and how you use it will probably alter how well you like it.

title: Super Comfortable...
text: I absolutely adore this hoodie! It is soft and comfortable and keeps me warm on cool days. (It's not for bitter cold days, for sure, though.) It's longer than the average zipper hoodie, which I love. The pockets are just right and it looks well made. The color comes with an already worn in look. It's not a bright navy blue, but a faded one. It's so wonderfully cozy, I've had a hard time wearing anything else when I go out.

title: They help keep my husband's legs warm on cold days.....
text: My husband likes wearing these to work. They're super long, so they come up above his calf. He's a paramedic, so he's often out in the weather when on a run. His uniform pants are on the thin side(which is great for summer, but not for winter), so these socks help keep his legs warm on cold days. They also have a tightness around his arch for support. He works long hours, so he likes this feature. He also prefers his socks have a "L" and "R" for the pairs, which these do have. He finds them soft and comfortable and he's been pleased with them.

title: You'll have to buy 6 D cell batteries to go with it.....
text:
This lantern wasn't exactly what I was expecting. I thought the whole thing would be rechargeable, but it's not. It takes 6 D cells, which are not included. The 3 removable lights on the side recharge from those D cells. (Batteries are included for the 3 removable lights.) You can also charge a phone/kindle/etc from those D cells. Since replacing D cells can get pretty expensive, we used rechargeable ones. This makes it super hard to get the bottom back on the lantern. After becoming incredibly frustrated with it myself, I passed it onto my husband. It took him awhile, but he finally got the bottom back on.

The 3 removable lights are pretty handy. They have a handle on the back and a button to press to turn them on and dim them. During a power outage(or when we suspect one might happen through the night), I can give each of my children one of the removable lights. Afterwards, it's easy to charge them back up. They give off a pretty nice light, too.

Overall, this is a nice lantern and it's super handy to have around. That said, it's disappointing that it gets much more expensive by having to buy D cells to go with it, especially for someone that is replacing them frequently. (Rechargable is much more expensive in the beginning, but it'll probably be cheaper in the long run, depending on how much you use it.)

title: Gives more variety to exercise routines....
text:
I like the variety of exercises this ring can add to my days. It has cushioned handles on the inside and outside, making the variety more than the average ring. It feels like a metal ring covered with a soft cushion, but it says it is made of "glass fiber and rubber-like NBR and EVA". (After looking closer around the handles, I can see a plastic-like ring.) It comes with a few exercise ideas to make use of it, but a quick search through Pinterest will give you tons more ideas.

So far it seems mostly durable and it's been comfortable to use. It's pretty easy to store without taking up tons of room. It's on the flat side, so it can easily slide under a bed or couch(or tons of other places). Then it's not in the way, but handy. I've enjoyed using it.

title: It has a few faults, but overall, we love it.
text:
This is a nice bike and a much better quality than the average old bike out there. It has a few faults, but overall, my husband and I have been pleased with it.

I'm partial to the color blue, so I think it's absolutely gorgeous with its color. It rides well. My husband and I ride on a little trail behind our house. There are lots of curves and bumps and ups and downs with hills and it does well with them. That said, the seat is the worst that I've ever ridden on. It is awful! I know the average bike seat is uncomfortable, but this one is most definitely so. It left me incredibly bruised the first time I rode it. I've mostly adjusted to it now and know when to raise myself off the seat to avoid more bruising, but it took some time. If you don't like skinny and hard bike seats, prepare to swap this one out.

It's also sometimes hard to swap gears. When I'm moving up a gear, it's like it doesn't fully swap over and I hear clicking. I have to move back down a gear and try again. This happens pretty often, though not every time. My husband has the same complaint. The kickstand isn't the best, either. This one simply won't hold the bike up on its own. I have to prop it up on something else to keep it from falling. We have a couple of cheaper bikes that we're able to keep up with just the kickstand.

There is some assembly required, which is a negative to ordering online. My husband did all the assembly work, but didn't have any trouble. This does take time, though, and is most definitely something to consider when ordering. (In stores, most bikes are already put together for you, without an extra fee...if in store is an option for you.)

Despite a few faults, we've been happy with this bike, overall.

title: Nice for basic needs...
text: This is a convenient tool to have around. It has many of the basic things that I need regularly, like both Phillips and flat head screwdrivers and knife. It's not super high quality, but it is nice enough. I do wish is had a locking feature, particularly for the knife. If you need something for basic needs, this is a good choice, but if you need it for tougher needs, I'd probably go with something else.

title: Great for a bit of silly fun!
text:
These are lots of fun, but I wouldn't recommend them if you're hoping for lasting power from them. For the average child, these probably won't last too long.

They are big once they are blown up. Either prepare yourself for a great deal of lung power, or invest in a small pump(if you don't already have one). There's a repair patch included, but it's easy to miss it. I happen to look inside the box, and noticed a piece of paper stuck to the bottom. If I hadn't pulled it out, I wouldn't have known it's actually for repairs.

Overall, these are great for a bit of silly fun!

title: Very small
text:
This set is WAY smaller than I was expecting. The opening for the gloves are tiny, too, so they're definitely not for a larger hand, even for children. My 8 year old was able to get them on his hands perfectly fine, but he's very small for his age.

Other than the size being so incredibly small, this is a decent set. The bag and the gloves are very soft and padded. It's cute! With a punching bag set, "cute" usually isn't the goal, though.

title: Decent, basic hand weight
text: This is a decent, basic 5 lb hand weight. It is covered in neoprene, so it's mostly comfortable to hold. There are little bumps and lines around it, though. (It's actually 4 little bumps that if connected would make a rectangle. I'm sure this formed while the covering was put on.) This may bother you enough that you couldn't use it comfortably. It hasn't bothered me too bad, but I do have to readjust it in my hand occasionally, if one of the bumps are especially "jabbing" into my hand. (It's really not bad, though.)

title: Lovely backpack!
text:
As far as looks go, this backpack is really nice! If a backpack can be called "lovely", I'd have to say that about this one. It's well made and appears very sturdy. It looks to be a high quality backpack.

I think all body types will be different, but for me, this backpack is comfortable to wear. The shoulders and hips have extra padding, so it doesn't rub into those parts. There's plenty of adjustable straps to make it more likely to fit each person just the way they need it to. The padding on the hips and shoulders are also removable, so you can (hand)wash those parts most likely to get sweaty and stinky. I haven't washed these parts yet, but right now they are attached very well. You have to really pull it to get it off, but it's not so hard that you're going to pull a muscle.

There's a rain guard attached within one of the pockets, so you can easily keep the backpack and your belongings dry if it rains. (This is the bottom pocket and the zipper is on the underside of the backpack.) There's extra room in there if you wanted to store anything with the rain guard. The middle space within the backpack is accessed from both the top and the middle, and it is open the whole length of the backpack. It is very roomy, and can be expanded with the 4 adjustable straps on the sides. (2 on each side) There's also a pocket behind the main one. Though it's not as roomy as the middle space, it still gives you lots of extra space. There's a pocket(without zippers or extras) on each side also. Each side of the hip strap has a little zippered pocket and one without a zipper. There's also a zippered pocket on the top cover. There's lots of adjustable straps all around, and also a couple of hooks.

Overall, this is a super nice and comfortable backpack, and I think most ladies will be extremely pleased with it.

title: Super hard for me to keep up with!
text:
If you're just beginning to get an exercise routine in your days, and you're as uncoordinated as me, this probably isn't the best place to start. It was super hard for me to follow! I couldn't even get the leg/feet portion straight, but then there would be arm movements thrown in the mix, too. It's been frustrating. If you're like me, just be prepared to give this plenty of time. That said, this was my first venture into the world of Zumba. I wasn't sure what to expect, other than it was an enthusiastic kind of experience. In case you're like me, it is a very high energy workout. There's basically lots of dancing, and you'll need lots of coordination. There's cultural music that plays in the background, and it was pretty cool, even if the whole package did make me feel old. The people within the videos are all high energy, with big smiles. They made it look so easy!

The good news is even though I haven't been able to do every move(not even close), I can still feel my muscles burning.

Another negative is that fact that these workouts make getting hurt more likely(based on workouts I've done in the past). There's lots of twisting and turning, and there were plenty of times that I could feel unnatural pain, so I'd stop before I did damage. Plus, if you have little ones, there's more danger of getting hurt. In one of the "chair" workouts, during a part where I was standing up, my little came in and turned my chair legs up without me knowing. It hurt when I sat down! ;) (Note: They DO try to warn you about what not to do to hurt yourself in the starting video.)

The videos do range in difficulty, but even the easy ones were pretty tough to keep up with for me. So, again, I wouldn't recommend this as a starting place for beginners. If you're coordinated and like to dance, give this a try!

(This set comes with a pair of 2.5 lb weights. They rattle as you move them. There's also 5 DVD's. It comes with a box that makes it easy to store it all in, and put on a bookshelf when not in use(which is what I do).)

title: Great little game for rainy days!
text: This game is on the small side, so it's perfect for indoor rainy day fun. The quality of it is great, and there's no batteries or electricity needed. You really can't go wrong with it! Aside from babies, any age can have fun with it. It can be played on a table or in the floor. The only noise you'll hear from it is cheering from the players.

title: Overall, a nice bike
text:
This bike comes in a large box that makes it obvious what’s inside of it. If you have people that might steal your packages around, you might want to make arrangements to be there when this arrives. It’s on the heavy side, also, so the mail person might appreciate some help, too! ;)

You’ll have to assemble it, so make sure you set aside a good hour/hour and a half to put it together. It’s pretty simple and straightforward, though.

This bike has Bluetooth connectivity, but we never could get proper connection. Thankfully, the bike works perfectly fine without it. My husband has a Bluetooth device, but I don’t. That means we can both use it, with or without Bluetooth(should it ever connect properly).

One feature I like is that the seat slides back and forth with ease. While sitting on the seat, just pull down a little bar beside the seat, and slide it into the perfect position. Then, just push the bar back up to lock the seat in place. This makes the bike work for lots of various positions and leg lengths.

The main part of the bike comes fully assembled. (It’s the seat and top and all that needs assembly.) At one point, I was pedaling along and I started hearing a rattling noise. I became worried, thinking the bike was already messed up. Thankfully, it was only one of the circle pieces around the pedal that had popped off. I had to turn it a bit to lock it back into place. This part and most of the base is plastic, so I’m a bit concerned about the lasting quality of it.

The power cord is detachable. To me, that gives it a bit of a cheaper feel, but at the same time, it does make it easier with little ones around. When not in use, I can roll up the cord and tuck it out of sight, and no one is tripping around cords. But, once again, I’m a little concerned about the lasting quality of such a “light” power cord.

Overall, though, it’s a pretty nice bike. It’s comfortable to use, and for a piece of exercise equipment, it really doesn’t take up a ton of space.

title: Provides a great workout, without taking up lots of space!
text:
The material this fitness band is made out of is kind of like a heavy duty rubber material. It seems to be made to last, but it’s also flexible. The great thing about it is the fact that you can get an excellent workout with it, and when you’re done, you can just roll the thing up. It doesn’t take up much storage space.

It comes with a one year limited warranty. It also provides you with a website to visit to get workout ideas using this fitness band.

The only somewhat negative issue is the fact that there’s not any true handles on it. There are spots on each side for your fingers to fit, but when you pull on it, it’s kind of awkward. It rolls between my fingers(and my husband’s), and it is a bit uncomfortable when it rolls just wrong. It’s not a major issue, though, and otherwise, this is a pretty awesome fitness band!

Overall, this band will give you a great workout without taking up a lot of space!

title: A Great Starter Tee
text: This is perfect for my two oldest sons(2 and 5). (My 2 year old IS taller than my 5 year old at the moment, though!) It's a perfect beginning tee. It's sturdy, so it doesn't fall over easily. It's also easily adjustable.

title: Great Flashlight!
text:
I LOVE how compact this flashlight is! It's perfect to keep in each room in case of an emergency and it won't take up much room.

It's not heavy, but it's heavymade. There's a beam adjustment from spot to flood, and it's BRIGHT. (You click the on/off button at the end of the flashlight and it comes on either spot or flood, and then you click it again, and it goes off. Click it again, and you get the opposite from the first time, spot or flood. Click it again and it goes off). To focus the light beam, you pull or push the top of the flashlight. I really like this feature!

It comes in a gift-type box, so if you're buying it as a gift, it's good to go. It also comes with a pouch and lanyard. It's all packaged really nice.

Overall, I have no complaints! It's an excellent flashlight, and I hope to add more of them through our house!

title: ... protector was either previously used or kept in very bad conditions. It was pretty dirty on the inside ...
text: My protector was either previously used or kept in very bad conditions. It was pretty dirty on the inside and out, kind of the opposite of what you want to protect your rubber from dirt. It wasn't that big of a deal to clean it off, but it was definitely lame.

title: Sturdy and perfect for picnicking
text:
I love this insulated cooler backpack! I have used it to keep food and liquids cold on hot day trips in the car to enjoy boating on lakes. I have packed 3 water bottles, a variety of canned beers, and lunch food including fruit and egg salad with about 4 cold packs for a day trip from Seattle to Mt. St. Helens (3 hours driving, followed by 6 hours in our boat, and another 3 hours return journey) on an ~80 degree F day and everything stayed nice and chilly the from start to finish. Depending on how many cold packs you put it in, that will impact how much room you have for food and drinks but this backpack can really hold a lot! There are two additional non-insulated zipped pockets on the front that are perfect for napkins, hand sanitizer, or cutlery.

One of my cheaper cold packs busted on a day trip and there was no spilling or dripping outside the backpack, everything stayed in the bottom of the bag and was actually really easy to clean out when we got home!

title: Great value, great item.
text: Excellent anchor. Purchased with the suggested chain and rope, all worked excellent together. 10lbs is perfect for rocky lake in my inflatable boat with 1 other adult on board.

title: Don’t buy. Broke first use.
text: Snapped on first use, did not exceed the weight limit at all. Total waste of money.

title: Sturdy pump, great price.

title: Room for Two: The Safer Option
text:
As you know, the point of these emergency blankets is to use them when everything else has failed. You are not at home (or the power and gas is out), you can't get to relatives, a hotel, or a Red Cross shelter... Or perhaps you are literally lost in the woods and thanking your lucky stars you threw an emergency blanket in your daypack..

The only difference here is that two people can fit, and if you have ever had to worry about hyperthermia, you know that the body heat of another is about the only way to bring up the body heat of the severely chilled person.

On a trail crew as an older teen and we got one guy into a fairly serious hyperthermia situation after using a cold mountain lake to float materials for trail bridges a shorter distance than hiking them around the lake. Great idea, but several us of took too many trips. We had a sleeping bag with us in a day kit, but it lost most of its thermal capacity when it got wet from the guys soaked clothes (dumb us: take the wet clothes off first!...) One of these emergency blankets and with room for a second person would have been an easier way to get him back to normal, and taken a lot less space.

From a price point of view, you can find single blankets for $5 to $20 bucks, depending on sale prices, quality and so forth. Thus, this double-sized version is priced at essentially no difference in cost and works for two. Construction is great. Four stars only because it's not a super premium version (which of course would cost more.) (EDITED to five stars, responding to a comment -- I agree.) These are designed for emergencies, so you are not buying this for multiple uses. This version seems to be at the right price point.

Hope this is helpful.

Well PT actually. I purchased this strap to assist with calf stretches as part of an injury recovery program. It has worked wonderfully and exactly as I need it to. The multiple segments make this much easier to use than a standard yoga mat strap and I feel that I have more control with this than I do a towel. title: Terrible design
text: The table top connects to the base at 4 points.  One one side of the table top fits together with pins in a hole and on the other side it uses two clamps that fit over the top of some pins.  The problem is the pole(s) that connect those opposite sides and hinged in the middle.  Setting the joint of those two poles perfectly straight and it will go together.  That assumes you will never move the table again.  Once you pick up the table of do anything to it those two poles will change at the hinge causing the end that fits over the pin to come lose.  I have only had it set up for 5 minutes and one of the clamps that goes over the pins is shot.  It is light weight and a nice looking table but I have no desire to wrestle with this thing anymore and it won't be long till the plastic is going to break for the top connection.  This is going back in the morning.

title: Very nice bottle holder

title: Really good wristband although as others have said
text:
Really good wristband although as others have said, the pulse feature isn't that accurate as compared to a chest strap monitor. It seems best when to record low pulse, resting rates. When I exercise it just doesn't keep an accurate count. Also, doesn't do well tracking things like elliptical machines but that I can understand since the method it uses just can't figure out how to count steps. But it seems to be pretty accurate on things like treadmill, walking, stationary bike.
The nice thing is the combo of the watch and a smartphone app which is really a pretty good app (iPhone version). Even with the problems I would highly recommend the watch.

title: Quality product
text:
Unfortunately I had to use this product a lot in recent weeks.

The good:
There are two patch sizes included. This is nice since not all flats are created equal.
Ample volume of patch glue which can continue to be used after opening.
Small footprint in your saddle bag (or jersey).
Levers are adequate.

The bad:
You have to apply the glue and wait for about five minutes prior to placing the patch. This doesn't seem like a problem until you are at the side of the road and become very impatient wanting to get back to your ride.

title: Good product but a bit large.
text: A bit on the large size, but the valve is simple to operate, quick and reliable. My only complaint -- and a small one at that -- is that it is on the bigger size of the spectrum.

title: Easy, inexpensive way to be more visible
text: When it comes to bike safety, more is always better. It's quick and easy to add these to the spokes to make your bike more visible to drivers at night. The individual sticks snap on well and seem to stay put. Clean your spokes before installing for a better experience. You still need good front and back lights and high-viz clothing, but these are an inexpensive addition to your safety solution.

title: Quality bands at a good price
text:
I was given a loop band by my physical therapist to help build hip strength for running. Unfortunately, the one they provided was just made by tying a longer piece of latex together and it quickly broke. At my local sporting goods store, these bands were being sold for $10 each. I like having the three different tensions and the quality seems very good for the price here. I found some additional good exercises for them at http://greatist.com/fitness/resistance-band-exercises
The vendor has been very good, too, shipping quickly and checking on my satisfaction with the product.

title: Not so bright
text:
I based my purchase in part on the picture of the vest on Amazon. Here's an instance where a picture is worth a thousand words; unfortunately, they're poorly-chosen words.

The problem with this reflective vest is that the triangular shape you see in the picture here on the product page--there's also one on the back--isn't actually a different shade of yellow, it's a surprisingly dark grey, a second mesh over the yellow you can see for the rest of the vest. This isn't a reflective grey material, it's simply grey, reducing the overall visibility of the rather short vest. I cannot understand why the grey is there; the yellow material is pretty visible, but putting the quite large grey triangle on the front and back makes it much less effective.

I'm disappointed enough that I'll be looking for a replacement.

title: Great upgrade to an endurance bike
text: This was a great upgrade on an endurance bike which spends most of it's time on a well groomed gravel trail.  They were substantially heavier than the road tires we removed but weight wasn't too much of a concern for us.  We were more concerned with stability and durability. Durability seems good but only time will tell, no issues so far.

title: Not as comfortable as everyone suggests, for a big guy
text: I have to say I was really disappointed by this saddle.  I have never ridden a brooks saddle or leather saddle before but I would not rate this as comfortable. The cutout and overall size of the seat felt right, I just couldn't get past the very firm feel of the material.  Immediately after sitting on it I could feel my sit bones making direct contact with the material and the material not offering any sense of relief.  I did give this saddle about 40 miles before deciding it was not for me. I will admit the seat seemed to maintain the same level of comfort for the entire trip which is an improvement over other saddles I've owned, which become unbearable after 20 miles.  This saddle never felt unbearable no matter the time spent on it.  I am a large guy, weighing in at 220 lbs, which is what I am attributing to my issue. I did replace it with a gel saddle and it initially feels much better.  I have a feeling if you carry less weight, the lack of padding might work for you.

title: Great flavors, would have preferred pro pack serving size
text: Should have bought the vacuum sealed smaller pro pack version.  IMO pro pack is the perfect portion size for the solo backpacker. this was a bit larger than I needed.  Flavors were great and would buy again.

title: Pro pack great for solo backpacker.  Great flavors
text: Pro pack is the perfect serving size for one backpacker, especially if you are doing decent miles.  Flavor was great and would buy again.

title: Apricot Peanut - good, chocolate banana- alright, cranberry almond - DO NOT BUY
text: Overall I would say I would buy again.  I expected to really like the banana chocolate flavor and it ended up being fairly dry.  My favorite flavor was the peanut apricot.  The worst and one I would never order again is the almond cranberry.  These are super easy to pull out for quick lunches on the trail and the calories count is primarily why I would recommend.  Flavors are not their strong suit, peanut apricot is good, and chocolate banana is acceptable.  The almond cranberry was not very flavorful and super dry would not buy.

title: Will be buying more, worked great
text: Water resistant, lightweight and super easy to use.  Worked exactly as expected and would buy more to better compartmentalize my gear in the pack

title: Made for super skinny men
text: Not made for anyone except skinny jean people.  If you are like me and have typical MEN sized legs, go with KUHL pants.  These high end hiking pants are made for super skinny people.  Waist fit just fine but the thighs were SUPER tight.  I actually pulled a stitch when I tried to bend down.

title: Great except for bite valve, STILL RECOMMEND
text: Please use a different bite valve.  The bite valve included is garbage but even with that I still highly recommend this product.  Just replace the bite valve with something like a $10 osprey bite valve.

title: Great storage bag
text: Cotton bag for storing your sleeping bag.  Not mush else to say and hard to really mess that up.

title: The best quality for the price
text: These trekking poles are well worth the money.  I spent half of what others spent for poles and these outlasted all the others and were as light if not lighter than the rest.  The locking mechanism is super strong,  I weigh about 220 lbs and they never collapsed on me once.  I never had to readjust them due to slippage either.  Friends that weight closer to 150 lbs were struggling with their poles the whole trip and some even bent their aluminum poles.  By the end of the trip these things looked like hell.  Decent amount of scratches from use but I imagine they still have plenty of life left in them, I have barely even scratched the surface.  Now I should note I am not a trekking pole person, generally I don't use them so that also means I probably used these about half as much as the others used theirs. This trip kind of required them to help with the extreme boulder terrain and portions of off trail hiking up mountain passes. After buying these I would probably always bring them on trips like this.

title: Slight heavy and tough to open but does its job
text: I never tend to use bear cans much but this one proved to be fairly decent.  Never had a bear/animal attack it which could mean it is doing it's job but I am sure a bear could smell straight through it.  I have probably just been lucky so far.  I don't eat a lot, so this proved to be more than spacious enough for a week long backpacking trip for one person.  I feel it is strong enough to withstand some abuse and makes for a great spot to sit as long as you have your food out already. Really there is only two marks against it, weight and ease of opening.  The weight seems more substantial than you would expect but when compared to other cans I am sure it is normal.  Opening these things on a cold morning is not fun at all.  I think they need to come up with a better locking mechanism, but that being said I am fairly positive an animal won't open it on it's own.

title: Great test/texture for freeze-dried chicken
text: This was the best addition to my backpacking meals. Tasted great and had a decent texture given it being reconstituted.  I would buy this again for making freeze dried meals.  Don't waste money on backpacker meals when you can create them yourself.

title: Great, well made socks.  Doesn't work as expected
text:
I like these socks but not as much as I was hoping. I have a lot of problems with my small toe getting blisters during day long hiking/backpacking. I was hoping these would eliminate that but they appear to still cause the hot spots which lead into blisters. The other thing to consider is that these socks will require slightly larger tow boxes in your shoe due to the extra material. I already have wide feet and use wide shoes so some of my shoes/boots seemed a bit tight with these socks but I feel it is just something I need to get used to,

As for the good aspects, the material is amazing. I always use wool socks for hiking and these wool socks are made of durable materials. They don't pill like many of my other wool socks do. I actually feel the material is better than a lot of my Smartwool socks. The fit is also amazing. I was somewhat concerned if the toe bit would fit properly but they fit perfectly fine. I also really like my toes being spread out slightly given the extra material. As for durability I expect them to last. The material is holding up so far, but I am slightly concerned about the friction between the toes but the build quality would make me assume they will last a long time.

title: The best heart rate tracker
text: This heart rate sensor work flawlessly.  I have very little to compare the Hr measurement to but it seem extremely accurate and most of all consistent.  I have had odd spikes and drops in Hr which i know for certain is a bad reading but after a month of using it everyday I can only think of once or twice that it happened.  It pairs extremely well and extremely fast with all devices.  Works great with my iPhone and pairs immediately with the workout machine I am using.  My phone tracks the Hr history while I can use the machine to keep track of my Hr during the workout.  If you do light to heavy cardio, this is a great way to really keep track of your effort and allows you to push yourself when you know you are starting to plateau.  If you only lift I might consider passing on Hr tracking. I find Hr a horrible indicator of lifting progress.  I do both and almost never wear it on lifting days anymore.

title: The best stomp pad for snowboards
text: These stomp pads work great.  The second one I have purchased and it makes a big difference especially for beginners.  The clear color allows you to see the boards graphics unobstructed, yet giving you amazing grip with your board.  The install is easy, just make sure you plan it out before removing the backing and use heat.  The original one I bought over 3 years ago and it still has a solid hold on the board and looks brand new.

title: Cheaper than T2 and still just as amazing
text: I was trying to figure out if I wanted the Thule T2 or this one.  I am so glad I went with this rack.  It seems really sturdy.  It is extremely easy to load/unload.  And extremely easy to install.  This rack is extremely heavy.  Install it in the beginning of the season and leave it until the season is over.  I originally thought I would take it off when not using it, but it is too heavy to worry about that.  If you have a garage that may be different.  It also kind of looks cool on the golf.  The best part is that it is 100 cheaper than the T2.

text: Great replacement tube and can be tough to find schrader valves for 700c tubes.

title: Great buy

title: Good cheap bottle cage

title: Great Water bottle
text: Good water bottle.  Great to have on the trail an easy to use.  Nothing else to really comment about,

title: Lighter than expected
text: These are super light.  I am sure I could have looked at their weight and found that out but when you see them you expect them to be much heavier than they are.  I also didn't buy them for the weight.  They seem really tough and gives me a really well planted foot hold for those downhill rides.  The pegs do some damage to the shins if they hit so you may want to get some shin pads.  As for longevity I have not had them long enough to really say, but they seem like they're built really well and seem like they will last a lot longer than those plastic pedals that come with your bike.

title: Great buy
text: The webbing seems really secure and should last for a long time. The only comment I would make is that I don't think the color is green, it is more grey.  It looks just like the picture but when I bought it I thought the picture may have been wrong.  But color was of no matter to me.

title: Great figure eight
text: I had a chance to use these on a rappelling trip just south of Columbus.  I bought these because I had a lot of first timers and I wanted to run two ropes.  They worked great for all the new users.  We could easily run two ropes through the figure eight for added security and control.  It also managed the heat a lot better, we had a really tall rappel which usually makes the figure eight over heat.

title: Great Stomp Pad
text: This thing works great.  No matter ho much snow you have packed on the board these will always give you plenty of grip.  The clear plastic allows you to see straight through them so graphics on the board are still visible.  I have had no issues at all with them falling off and I have had it on for two seasons now.

title: Great Tool
text: I am extremely new to the world of snowboard maintenance.  This is the first tool I have ever used to sharpen a board.  It seemed to work great and I could really tell the difference on the slopes.  The only reason I didn't give it five stars was because there were no instructions included.  I looked online but I am still not sure if I am using this specific tool properly.

title: First clipless pair, but love them
text: These are the first pair of clipless pedals I have owned.  I am currently using them on a hybrid so I can get used to them, but I want to put them on my mountain bike soon.  I just don't have the confidence yet to use on a mountain bike.  They are really easy to get in and out of and are smooth to ride on.  I am probably going to buy a pair for my mountain bike soon.

title: It works OK
text: The only reason I bought this was becasue I didn't want to hassle with finding one that would fit my current bike and the price is hard to beat. You will be looking at speanding at least 60-70 at a bike shop to replace a crankset and then there is the hassle of will it fit on my current bottom bracket. One major thing I don't like about this is the chain rings are riveted on. You can not replace or swap chain rings on this. You have to replce the entire crankset. They seem to be much more common.  Be careful of sizing.

title: Works perfectly, and could do what a shimano couldn not
text: I originally purchased a shimano crank remover to remove the crank off of an old bike.  It was on their so tight it ended up destroying the inside part of the tool, basically flattening the metal and making it worthless.  I then bought this one and with a little bit of effort the crank came off.  The tool was still in perfect condition after being used.  I would recommend and don;t waste your money on the shimano tool.

title: Works great for a fluid trainer
text: I was reading a couple of commnets about how difficult this was to install, and how it fell apart and threw red peices all over the place.  I've had it for about a month already and I would completely disagree with all of those comments.  It was fairly easy to install.  About as easy as any other 700 x 23 tire that I have ever installed. It is way more quiet than my hybrid tire on the trainer.  It is holding up just fine.  There are no red pieces flying all over the place and from my initial perspective, it should last a long while.  It also grips the trainer very well, almost like glue, so very little pressure is required to keep the wheel from slipping.  I would absolutely recommned.

title: This kit worked great for repairing my snowboard
text: I used this kit to repair a long gouge in my snowboard.  It took two applications to completely remove the gouge.  Some residue is visible from the ptex burning but for the most part you can't even tell it is there.  Everything you need besides the lighter is in this kit.  Enjoy.

title: The best gloves ever
text: The only gloves I have ever found to actually be water proof.  I use for snowboarding and when you are strapping into binding all day, your gloves will be in contact with snow constantly.  Never felt wet once.  The insulation is great too.  The best part is the removable liner.  When doing tasks that require slightly more dexterity than you can pull off with the mittens, you can just pull the liners out and tada you have gloves.  Inserts are not water proof so I wouldn't recommend tightening bindings with them.  They do dry fast even if you get the inserts wet.  Absolutely amazing gloves and not crazy expensive either.

title: Durable
text: My nephew loved this. Not to familiar with roping but all I know is my nephew loved it and after months of him learning/tearing it up it's still intact.

title: Tigernuts catch carp
text: Tutti frutti prepared tiger nuts work great for carp. I like both the smaller and jumbo sized tiger nuts. These tiger nuts have strong flavor, are not brittle so they are easy to insert into hair rig. Carp attracting flavor/scent seems to last a very long time. Highly recommend trying this product for carp fishing.

title: Great method feeder, works fantastic
text:
This is by far my favorite method feeder I have ever used. Perfect size for castability vs. how much pack bait can be used. Pack bait sticks very well to method feeder while casting. Both smaller catfish and carp are hooked up reliably with very little misses. I like both the 50g and 25g models. 50g casts very, very far. It's very rare with this method feeder to get hook stuck inside method feeder which has happened to me too often with some other method feeders.

Sometimes if I want more bait I use the mold 2 times to pack more bait into feeder. This allows for more bait without significant down sides. I tend to do this is bite is slow or if there is a lot of small fish around eating the bait.

title: Great product, catches fish like nothing else
text: I have been using these fake corns for carp and catfish. They work great. Fake corn smells wonderful. These bait keep working even after the smell is gone. I usually use 1 or 2 fake corn in a hair rig. These worked great on summertime and have kept working through the fall. The fake corn is buoyant and the fish have no chance of knowing there is a hook below.

title: Great set
text: Great set. Does exactly what I need

title: 0 star rod, broke on fifth cast(when casting, lure used was withing specified range for this rod)
text:
Broke on fifth cast when casting a lure that is within the spec of this rod. Ruined fishing trip I had been looking forward to. St. Croix policy for defects is bad and it would cost me money and time to even try to get the situation fixed. This feels like poor quality control at factory as these kind of things should just not happen when casting a lure withing spec.

If the rod had broken after serious use my view would be different as perhaps then would have done something to the rod to damage it. In this case it literally broke on fifth cast and half of the rod flew into ocean.

I value my time greatly and hence I bought online. In this case my best option is to lick my wounds, buy another rod from a other brand and give warning to other potential buyers.

I would avoid this 0 star product or at least prepare to use extra time and money in case same happens to you that happened to me.

title: Great rod for price
text: I like this rod a lot. Rod has good sensitivity for lures I use. Casts accurately and far. I like the smooth cork handle which feels great in use. Rod is lightweight and nicely balanced which is great when fishing for long periods of time. I would buy this rod again if I needed another similar rod.

title: Five Stars

title: Perfect little utensil
text:
These are the most fantastic camping/travel utensils that I have ever used! I can’t recommend them enough. The spoon shape took a little getting used to but now I love it. It’s just right for digging into corners of jars and cleaning out flat areas but not so big that it won’t go in your mouth! If you are a backpacker with the a classic Lexan spoon and then you know what I’m talking about. The fork side works really good too. It doesn’t look like it would be very good at picking things up but does a remarkable job.

The only place this utensil is weak is cutting. If something is tough enough that fork cutting it would be hard then you are out of luck. Fortunately I carry a pocket knife so the lack of a proper knife on this utensil is not a problem for me. In a way, I like that they’re not trying to do everything in one utensil.

Some people complain that it is a little bit too short. I have found that for general purpose eating it is just right and the fact that it is one piece makes it easy to hang onto. If you want the same functionality as this tool but in something with longer reach, look at the two piece one that they make that can be clipped together and gives you about a 1 foot long implement. That one is perfect for cooking and cleaning out jars or stirring large pots.

This utensil is best for eating and it does it so well that I love using it. With all these different colors each person in the family is assigned one that is their very own!

title: Easy to put up, breaking down takes some practice.
text:
I got this tent to have a little pop up tent for the beach. I was assuming it was pretty small, easy to pack in the car and to the beach. But this tent is quite large. In its case it comes up to my waist or so (Iʻm 5ʻ7"). When opened up it easily fits my entire family inside. So itʻs a little large for my intended use, but I think it will be very useful when family camping.

Setting up this tent is the very definition of simple. I took it out of itʻs case and threw it on the ground. At first it took a while to open up, since all the windows and doors were shut and creating a vacuum in the tent. But once I cracked a window and air could get in it popped right open. The tent is quite spacious. I can lie down the short way and not touch the walls of the tent. If you are very tall, you probably would have to lie down the long way in the tent though. I canʻt stand up in the tent, itʻs about the height of your standard 4 man dome tent.

There are doors on either end, both with screens and rain flies. There are also windows on both sides. The windows have a zipper, so you can pass small objects through the window.

Breaking down this tent was challenging. It took me quite a while to figure it out. I watched the promotional video for this tent which briefly showed how to put away the tent. It was slightly helpful, but I was still confused. But now that I figured out how to do it, I can get it broken down pretty quickly, within 20-30 seconds at the most.

I think this tent will be great for a quick camping trip with the family when I donʻt want to lug around our huge cabin tent. Putting it up is simple, there is more than enough space for me, my wife, and two kids, and it is now pretty quick to break down. Even if we do bring the big tent, I think we will still use this tent. Either the kids can have their own tent or have it as a play area.

text:

He would hold my seat post and most of the time bury his face in my back so that he wouldn't fall off. He also had to hold his legs out so that his feet wouldn't get caught in the chain or the tire. With this seat, he can sit back in comfort, he has his own little handlebars to hold, and the seat is nice and soft for him. He is extremely happy that I got this for him.

Installation was a little difficult, but nothing crazy. I would have loved a second pair of hands to help me install, but the rest of my family was suddenly busy when I started putting it on. The only part that was hard was getting the crossbar on under the rack. One of the support beams would be right next to the bar, no matter how I installed the seat. It took a little maneuvering, but I managed to wedge the crossbar in and get the seat bolted down. Even if a nut falls off, I don't think the seat will move because of the way it is wedged on. So I feel it's very safe. One thing I wouldn't mind is having the brace that holds the backrest be a little more sturdy.

It's been a few weeks now and so far everything has held up. The bike was left out in the rain a few times, but I don't notice any rust appearing. I'm pretty pleased with this purchase.

But in this set, it left a lot to be desired. Aside from many quality issues, the one that stood out the most are the dents on some club faces. This is a brand new set, why does it have dents? The bubble wrap and packaging were acceptable and it looked well packaged, there’s no reason for having dents. Quality issue? I’ve had clubs that were at least 10 years old and have been beat up; aside from superficial scratches, those clubs still were dent-free and serviceable. The set is slightly more expensive than some no-name beginner sets but I’m thinking the quality could be comparable. I get it, it’s a teen set, but I expected better quality control from the Tour Edge name. As I’m writing this, I’m actually pondering if this could be a knock off set, I hope not.
The good thing is that it is a complete set, the irons were of better quality it seems, and although the bag seems flimsy, it’s very light and will help with walking the course.

title: So disappointed - utter crap
text:
I had high hopes for these electric socks. I mean, electric blankets have been around forever, right? So maybe, just maybe these would work. Sadly, they are utter crap.

When they arrived, they didn't look too bad. I was concerned about how much of the sock would have a heated area, but I figured, even a relatively small area might be helpful. I got some fresh AA batteries and loaded up the battery compartments. (There is a little pocket near the top outer side of each sock. There is a wire inside each of these that connects to the battery box.)

I felt just the faintest bit of warmth from one sock and nothing from the other. I put them on and honestly could not tell a difference between the non-working side and the one that was faintly warm. I thought perhaps they needed more time to warm up, so I continued wearing them hoping that would happen. I was busy working and after a couple of hours realized that they had never warmed up. So I decided to check the batteries, 'just in case,' they weren't fully charged. When I checked them on my battery tester, all four were completely dead even though I had gotten them from my fresh supply. I wondered if they could possibly have been bad to begin with, though that seemed highly unlikely. Then I wondered if the box had somehow drained the batteries.

Still holding out a tiny bit of hope the socks would warm, I got out more batteries. This time I checked them with my battery tester first, to make sure they were fully charged. They were. Again I felt the tiniest bit of warmth and thought, "Great! I guess the last batch of batteries were no good."

Put them on and again, could not feel the warmth. I later checked the fully charged batteries and .. you guessed it, they were drained. So not only did the stupid socks not work, they somehow drained EIGHT AA batteries!! What a waste of time and money. Needless to say, I want to send these back.

It's really a shame because a lot of people would love to have socks like this if they would actually work. I hope the manufacturer figures out a way to make them work AND do so without having to go through dozens of batteries each week.

title: Solid headlamp, but I'll probably go back to Petzl the next time around
text:
Everyone I know uses Black Diamond headlamps, but I've always owned Petzl. I've always wondered if I'd like BD better. When I had a bag stolen that had my newest Petzl headlamp in it I thought I'd try out the Black Diamond Revolt. For a headlamp that can recharge batteries with a USB cable it was a really good price, so I pulled the trigger on it. It has adequate lumens for my purposes (backpacking, evening hiking, and use around the house), although it isn't quite as bright as my similarly priced Petzl models. It has an awesome, fully adjustable dimmer setting that is the one thing that stands out as better than any other headlamp I've used. It also has a red LED setting, which is important to me - I actually find that I use the red LED way more than the white for late night use. As far as features go, I'm happy with everything you get with the Revolt.

The more I've used this headlamp though, I have a few minor complaints compared to similar offerings from Petzl. As mentioned above, I use the red LED setting often. It's great when you want to maintain night vision. I also like that if I wake up in the middle of the night and quickly use my lamp, the red LED wakes me up less than a bright white light. The problem for me is that the red setting on the Revolt is way too dim. It's hard to see anything that's more than just a few feet away. This makes it so that I can't use it in as many situations as I could with my old Petzl. I definitely wish it were brighter in the red mode.

Another feature on most headlamps is an adjustable angle setting where you can click it up and down to choose how high the lamp points. The Revolt has solid detents that seem like they will hold up well over time. This is kind of splitting hairs, but I don't like how widely spaced the detents are. It always seems to be too high or too low. YMMV, but I liked Petzl again here for the finer adjustments. I have to fiddle with the Revolt more often.

On the other hand, I'm not gentle with my headlamps. I use them constantly at home and work and any time I backpack or travel. I cram them into bags, toss them around a bit, bump them on things and occasionally drop them. It's hard to say, but friends that I work with and backpack with seem to have better luck with their Black Diamond lamps' durability. The Revolt is solidly built and seems to use batteries very efficiently. It seems like it might be a little sturdier and maybe last longer than my previous Petzl lamps, but that's purely a guess at this point. We'll see, but so far so good. I'm basing that more on friends' experiences with BD lamps. Either way, it's certainly no worse.

Overall, I think this is a pretty good headlamp. It's a solid value for the price and does everything I want it to. I'll continue to use it pretty happily, but when it comes time to replace it, I'll go back to Petzl. Even if the Revolt is a little sturdier, I like the way Petzl lamps work and feel. They're less clunky and they just seems to have their headlamps really dialed across the board. They're comfortable, intuitive and very well designed. Get a Revolt if you want a solid, functional headlamp, but get a Petzl if you really want to love it.

The worst part is not even that water gets into the bag - it's that the water collects and pools at the bottom of the main compartment and in the small front compartment and is difficult to clear. Even after shaking the bag upside down and running a cloth through it, there was still water tucked in the corners and edges of the pockets that I just couldn't get out. It took a long time to air dry. As I mentioned above, I love my other Fishpond gear, including another hip pack (that has since been discontinued). title: Spend a bit more money on a real tent.
text:
This tent seems like a great value at first. But when you can't sleep because of water seeping in, then drive yourself mad trying to tear down the tent in the morning you'll regret not buying a real tent.

The only plus I can give to this tent is that it sets up super easily. But to be honest, it's not really that much better than just setting up any other tent. The mechanism they have to pop the tent open works. But you're adding a lot of weight and mechanical complexity to something that's not very difficult in the first place.

On to the negatives.

It's impossibly annoying to tear down. While the tent pops open easily, it's a total pain to close. All of the plastic arms will start popping out of the mechanism. There's 8 joints you need to pull and close, one by one. And then you have to figure out which way the thing actually closes. But there's so much tension in the arms attached to the central hub that if you don't do it just right everything starts popping out.

So instead of just popping your tent poles out of the ground and pulling them out of the tent, you have to tear apart and rebuild this complicated lever mechanism spring loaded hub thing in the middle of the woods. And that's after you got no sleep because there's water in your tent.

The rain fly doesn't cover nearly enough of the tent. So if there's any rain it will rain directly on the tent, where as I said above, water will start seeping through into the tent. not just a little dampness. We had actual puddles in the tent.

I've had $20 Walmart tents that did a better job than this thing. It's not worth the money. It's overly complicated. And worst of all it just doesn't provide adequate shelter.

I can switch between the razor and the heavier blade quickly and don't have to keep track of 2 knives. It's not very large and not even that heavy. Given all that and the price, I must say that I am pretty happy with it. I did my first deer with this knife shortly after I purchased it and am really happy with it.

I know everyone has their preference on knives when it comes to skinning, but this thing is perfect for my needs and I'm very happy with it.

title: True to size
text: Almost perfect fit, little high in the back neck area where the Velcro is so will have to see if that hinders anything while swimming. Otherwise, seems like a good starter product!

title: Light, Warm & Does Not Obstruct Hearing
text:
I used this for a Mid-to-Late October Elk/Bear hunt in Eastern Idaho. Weather ranged from anywhere to high 20's during the early mornings and low-to-mid 60's and sunny during the day. Most days were active hiking combined with times where I stayed motionless for many hours.

Super light weight and warm. Did not obstruct hearing at all which is a nice feature. I would put in on and take it off as needed and easy to store. Some of the mornings of my hunt were cold and when I was stationary for extended periods this beanie was not enough. However, it's hard to retain heat if you're not generating it. Good overall beanie and I recommend it as a good option for all active hunters.

title: Buyer beware!  Poor quality sweatshirts for the money you pay!
text: The sweatshirt is a thin material like a cheap t-shirt. Plus, the logo isn't centered from side to side or in relation to the front pocket so it looks really bad, like someone who didn't know what they were doing applied the logo. I paid $35.00 for this cheap-looking sweatshirt when I could have bought a thick, good quality sweatshirt from the school itself. I'd return it, but I washed it before I wore it and noticed the logo being so off-center!

title: Somewhat Leaky???
text: This packed would leak whenever it would get refilled with water, but the leaking would stop after a bit. Think the cap might be a bit faulty because otherwise it didn't leak. Wish this one came with a protective sleeve for the tube like the other packs. Otherwise, fit great and worked fine. No real bad plastic taste either.

title: Neat gadget!
text:
I've had mine since November (5 months). I've thusfar loved having this thing - I'm not sure if it provides any tangible workout benefit, but it helps keep me motivated. It has been neat to see what my heartrate is doing!

I will leave off one star because the rubber band on mine is already peeling off. The band has not seen excessive wear conditions and I keep it away from water etc. I will say though, that I contacted FitBit and they've been gracious enough to send me a replacement free of charge, without having to send in the defective unit! :)

title: Heavy duty plastic clip
text: This reflective belt comes with a heavy duty plastic clip and seems to be made of quality materials. The primary reflective material goes down the center of the belt with the underlying material being a similar woven material. The added hook allows for attaching a dog leash or your keys. Could be a good gift for the runner or dog walker in your life.

title: Fun filled adult game
text:
What a hefty board game. This is filled with a huge variety of fun activity cards that encourage you to drink and drink a lot. Its for up to 8 adult (21+) players that are encouraged to drink while playing. There are physical activities on the some of the cards that require you to get up and move around. Others that require you to drink due to board movement. It takes a few rounds to understand all the rules but they come pretty quickly and make it a fun time. A unique way to imbibe.

Game contents:
- game board
- 2x die
- 8 game pieces
- 100 trivia cards
- 30 cards for each category
- a bouncy ball

title: Great all purpose athletic tape
text: This rainbow pride tape has sections of about 3" that change colors. The tape itself sticks well and has a good thickness to it. It's great for lacrosse shafts because it transitions the colors consistently after each wrap of the shaft. Very happy with the final color and feel of this tape.

title: Quality materials but a bit small for foraging
text: This waxed canvas drawstring bag is made with quality waxed 16 oz canvas that folds into thirds and secures with a single metal button. The center is reinforced with a leather band and there is a flexible pull tie to close the top of the bag. The overall size of the bag is a bit small to forage anything larger than herbs or small mushrooms and it doesn't have the flexibility for anything soft. If it were bigger that wouldn't be an issue but since it is small and not very flexible in depth, do not expect to stuff it full without damaging some of your harvest. But great to carry in your day bag in case you happen upon something worst harvesting.

title: Compatable with Canik
text: This laser/light combo fits great on a standard picatinny rail. It fits tight around the trigger guard with no rattle. The mounting screw uses a wide flat head, which is provided in the form of a penny tool. It also comes with an adjustment hex tool for all of the various height adjustments for the lasers. There is a red and green laser, both are bright and extend a good distance. The light is bright but not super blinding. The ad states 500 lumens which is more than enough for using as a light, not enough to blind. I was surprised to see that it was nearly entirely aluminum exterior. It does use a micro USB to recharge, it would have been nice to see USB C or a comparable magnetic charger. Really not a bad introductory light/laser combo at a pretty ridiculous price point. A perfect item to try it on and see if you want to purse higher quality/more reliable items.

title: Perfect for kids learning self defense
text: This plastic inflatable punching bag comes in the shape of a dinosaur. It's meant to have a small layer of water at the bottom to prevent toppling over. It is quite large at 47", be sure to plan where it will go to prevent things from getting knocked with it weaves and bobs. It has a 180 degree bounce back movement so it needs some room. It also does not include a pump to inflate the punching bag. Important if getting as a gift or if you do not own a pump. It is made out of plastic and with anything new it will offgass for the first initial opening. It will eventually subside but can be left outside if needed. The seams do not seem to be refinforced which definitely worries me if this will be hit numerous times.

title: Lots of size adjustability
text: These goggles arrive in clear clamshell cases for protection. They have many adjustable notches for a large range of kids head sizes. I was worried my 4 year olds head was going to be too small to get a good seal but these worked great. There was plenty of tightening adjustment to spare so she should be able to use these for many years, as long as they last. They arrive with protective films on the goggles to prevent scratches. Price is great for a four pack and the bright colors are a big plus.

title: Very solid emergency single person emergency kit
text: This quake kit comes in a high quality bag that can be worn as a backpack with one primary storage area as well as a couple small zippered pouches. Each type of disaster kit is in its own plastic bag with a resealable zipper. There is a bit of everything in this bag that you would need in an emergency. It claims it can last 1-3 days and I could believe that if you had to do some major rationing. I envision this as more of a car bag in case you get stuck in a bad storm or your car breaks down somewhere, and for the price I think it's a good deal. You do need batteries for the included flashlight. The items included are not top of the line, but will work if you're in a pinch. It think this is a good middle ground between a very cheap survival kit and a custom made kit in both price and quality of items you're receiving. From all of the survival kits I have ordered, this one is at the top of the list that I would buy again for my other vehicles.

title: Material collects dust and debris a lot
text: [[VIDEOID:1f315434fb6469877077689777a257dd]] This 1 KG telescopic dumbbell is covered in a soft plastic that unfortunately collects dust and debris like crazy. Thankfully, it is basically a type of silicon so it can be cleaned easily, but that does make it a maintenance task. The mechanism is similar to a shake weight, it can be shook up and down to move the weight around. Or it can be placed between the knees and pushed with your thighs. Long term results will determine if this is a sham or not. As of now, it's a well made dumbbell.

title: Super easy assembly, can feel the ab burn fast
text:
Assembly was very quick with this ab workout bench. It has two locking pins for height adjustment and two bolts to secure the upper hand mounts to the frame. The rest are foam pieces that slide on and plastic end caps. It took less than 5 minutes to assemble and start using. It definitely takes some practice to sit comfortably, but you can quickly start to feel the burn. Removing the locking pins allow it to be stored in a more compact form. I overall the size is quite manageable, moreso than lots of workout equipment.

The counter uses a single AA battery which does accept Amazon basics rechargable batteries. It only has one button but tracks time, count, calories, and reps per min. It connects via a small wire that has a locking clip, this could be shorter so I don't have it dangling around.

My biggest complaint is the leg rest where you sit when operating this machine. it has four foam pads to aid in comfort, but the plate between them is solid metal and should also have a foam cap. It's not comfortable to sit on unless you stay entirely on the foam rods, which can be difficult if you're doing side crunches.

title: Needs adjustable feet for unlevel surfaces
text: [[VIDEOID:9793864d86692b1a957114733c9e658c]] This dumbbell rack is surprisingly heavy-duty. The main side supports appear to be square aluminum tubing white the horizontal L supports are a heavy duty steel. All of which are powder coating with plastic end caps to protect the corners. The instructions are a one page diagram showing bolt and nut locations. The bolts are all the same. It was a bit confusing when the vacuum pack of parts breaks them into four groups when they are all the same size and thread. The logos on the side supports are meant to go on the outside. The bolt holes are square to connect with the square bolt head so you only need a 5/8" socket to tighten these bolts down. I recommend loosely installing all bolts first and the tightening. You need to shift things around to get everything to line up nicely. My biggest complaint is the lack of adjustable feet for unlevel surfaces. I got done assembling this and put it against a garage wall just to see it rocking almost a 1/2". This may resolve itself when weighted down with dumbbells but I don't have a set right now to test that. The easy solution would be adjustable feet so this can be placed on any surface.

title: Pretty thin plastic bottle
text: This review is for a 64 oz. bottle with leopard cover. The bottle is completely plastic and only a single layer, so any condensation that forms on the bottle will be absorbed into the leopard cover. I forsee this cover getting really dirty pretty fast. The cover also has no zipper or drawstring to easily remove it from the bottle. Its actually quite hard to get off. So cleaning it is an experience. There is a lock switch on the lid to prevent it from popping open, which is nice. The drinking mechanism is a straw with silicon tip. The lid to the spout doesn't lock backward, so it flaps around which is annoying. It does come with a small cleaning brush to clean the spout. It is quite expensive for a thin plastic bottle and I would only recommend it if it's on a sale. The material quality overall is a bit cheap.

title: Tightly wound on arrival, easy to remove core
text: This Paracord is for my go bag to be used when necessary. It arrived tightly wound in a neat roll with both ends heat sealed. It appears to have a 10 line inner core when cut, the inner core is easily removable if you intend to wrap cables. It easily heat seals with a flame. I don't have a way to test the 650 lb weight capacity but it feels like a solid paracord at the price point.

title: A bit longer than expected
text:
These athletic shorts are what I think of for exercising and sports activities. They are not thick material, but rather thin with some mesh accents for airflow. They do have pockets, which aren't zippored. The waste band is slightly elastic but the majority of your tightening ability comes from the internal draw band that you can tie if loose. They are longer than my usual athletic shorts. These go past my knees by a few inches, some may prefer that but I prefer closer or above my knee.

Otherwise, these are lightweight and allow for good airflow while also providing pockets for day to day wear. They do come with a price tag saying 36.00 PER short. So not sure if these are excess or discontinued shorts but if that's the real retail price then these are a steal.

title: Sturdy and heavyweight but finger print reader could be improved
text: This was a lot larger than I expected. It can definitely hold two pistols easily. It is heavyweight and can be easily secured to a table top. The fingerprint reader usually takes one or two attempts to open, which is regrettable since you want this to open on the first try every time. You have a backup pin code you can use or the key. I'll still use it since it was meant to easily secure firearms from my children. But I may look at other options for quick retrieval.

title: Easy to Assemble and responsive customer service
text: Unfortunately my package arrived opened and missing some parts. However, the seller was quick to respond to my query and send the parts that were missing. The overall build quality of the storage rack seems sturdy and connects via pins for quick setup and removal. Ultimately the sturdiness depends on your ability to drill into studs. This is a cost effective storage solution for bikes and other miscellaneous garage items. I will update accordingly accordingly if it does not meet my expectations.

title: Great portable daypack.
text: This is the third backpack I have ordered; one for myself, one for my wife, and now another for my mother-in-law. She saw our backpacks and liked the small form factor and light weight material. I have used one of these bags for all sorts of traveling with a variety of different weight loads. I would definitely recommend one for an easy solution for a daypack.

title: not durable enough
text: This watch worked great for about 6 months. Then the buttons on the sides fell off. A month after that, the alarm completely stopped working. The watch is easy to use and has several different functions, but for the price I didn't expect it to fall apart after 6 months.

title: Pedometer is great, software not so hot
text:
The pedometer itself works great. It seem to be very accurate. I've held it up and watched it count steps as I walk and it seems to do this very accurately. The distance you've walked will only be accurate if you precisely measure your stride length. If you incorrectly measure your stride length, the distance the pedometer says you've walked will be off.

I'm not impressed with the "health management software." It looks very old-fashioned. It does make bar graphs that show whether you're meeting your goal everyday and it does average the number of steps you walk per day, but it looks very low-tech.

title: Good product considering the low price
text:
This product does exactly what it's supposed to do - monitor your heart rate during exercise. The chest strap is fairly comfortable and doesn't move around. Put a few drops of water on it before strapping it on.

My only complaint is that the alarm is not quite loud enough to hear when I'm listening to music. You can spend a lot more on a heart rate monitor, but I'm guessing that the expensive models don't work any better.
