title: Small and light; lacks lifetime memory
text:
The Omron is quiet small and light. I can have it in a pocket along with my wallet or iPhone and I don't notice it's there. But I'm skeptical about its accuracy.

I took a few walks and compared the distance it recorded with the route mapped out as a walk in Google Maps. The Omron would typically under measure my distance anywhere from 30 to 60 percent. I re-checked the height, weight and stride settings but that had no effect. I guess it's unrealistic that a pedometer can accurately measure distance.

A more serious flaw is that the unit does not keep lifetime stats -- it's memory is only 7 days. If you have a workout schedule where you need to keep a log of your daily steps, the 7 day memory feature is quite nice for when you forget to write down a day's results, but I would think most people would like to know how many steps they've taken after a year.

While I suppose the distance issue is forgivable -- most people buy a pedometer to keep track of steps, not miles traveled -- the lack of lifetime memory makes it hard to recommend this unit.

title: Good value
text:
This light has two practical safety functions:

It helps make your presence on the road more apparent to on coming traffic. The light is bright enough from even a few hundred feet that a driver would have to be extremely oblivious and distracted not to see it.

Perhaps more importantly, the light will illuminate street signs and signals that are made with a reflective material at distances of over 450 feet away (I measured using google maps). When I first used the light (in flashing mode), I was genuinely shocked to see how the street signs up to two blocks ahead of me were pulsating. I say that this is important because it helps you spot stop signs in the distance - assuming you're being a safe cyclist, biking in a lane, with traffic, abiding by traffic laws, you're probably most likely to get killed by accidently running a stop sign. When I bike home from work at night, I take streets that have no traffic lights and only stop signs, so being able to spot them is very important for me.

The light attaches to your handle bar through via a mount; the light can easily slid off the mount so you don't have to bike around with it during the day, nor leave it on the bike when it's parked outside.

The light does what it needs to do for a reasonable price. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.

I had carpal tunnel surgery on both hands because of the pain from doing repetitive gripping, lifting and wrist action during my work (Laborer's Union). I was in so much pain I couldn't even open my car door or even the door to the house without excruciating pain.
I wish I would have had these prior to surgery because the surgery didn't help! In fact, the surgery made me lose strength in my grip and I still get pain in my hands and forearms if I go a long period without using the handmaster system.
Using the Handmaster is the only way to release the pain and strengthen my hands and forearms. When I first started using these, the soft ball was almost too firm for my grip.
There are 9 muscles that open the hand and 9 muscles that close the hand and these exercise balls help increase circulation and strengthen these muscles.
The bands are tight, but they need to be because otherwise they would just roll down your fingers and wouldn't stay put through the exercises.
You can go to Doctor Zac's website (handmasterplus dot com) and there are videos to help you work out your hands and arms and education about how the muscles work.
These really work, but you need to give it time to work. After all, the problem didn't happen over night and it will not just go away.

In fact, I had to deflate it some as it became too tall to sit on and I was leaning over my desk. It is common, at least with the balance balls that I have owned, to have a break in period.
You have to allow the material to stretch and soften. This material is made to be flexible and stretch with your body weight. As for the locks on the wheels, they are annoying, but I do understand their purpose. I used some twisty ties to tie them up until I wish to use them. So far they have not come down.
All in all this is a great chair, especially if you like to wiggle on a balance ball instead of being stationary. I find myself moving around from side to side and bouncing every so slightly the whole time I am sitting on it, except while I am typing.
If you are they fidgeting type of person, this chair will make you very happy.
I did buy the cover by Gaiam that is velvety and it is a little large for this ball, but I was able to make adjustments to the cover and it looks great on the chair.

title: Same Package That Total Gym Sells but Better Price!!
text:
I just wanted to clear this up, this is the same exact package that is sold by Total Gym Direct! The only difference is that TG Direct offers the AbCrunch as a bonus, but their package is more expensive and you can purchase the Abcrunch on Amazon and still be way below the cost of purchasing the package from TG! I ordered the Abcrunch, which comes with a DVD, and the Weight Bar and still paid way below the 60% off price of TG Direct. I would say to wait until you get your TG before purchasing any attachments because I received a promo code with my TG for $20 and $30 off for accessories to use on the TotalGymCatalog dot com. This Total Gym came with 5 DVDs (workouts at every level and includes a pilates dvd), the Pilates package, wall chart, training deck and holder, wing attachment. Everything you need to workout!

There is no assembly, it comes fully assembled. I do recommend watching the set up dvd so you do not hurt yourself setting this up and you fully understand how it folds and unfolds. I did my first workout yesterday and I really feel it today. This machine is as smooth as butter! It is very quiet and appears to be of good solid quality. I bought a lesser quality type machine similar to this years ago and the difference is like night and day. My boyfriend is 6'4 and has no problems working out on this machine. The bench is almost 47" long x 16" wide and most of the exercises are done with your legs either bent up and crossed or sitting on your legs or with them hanging to the sides of the bench. This machine is 90" long and even doing squats there is still plenty of room.

The workouts are fun to do and don't take that much time. I was shocked how fast time went by as I was working out. That is what keeps people motivated. The workout never felt redundant. I feel fortunate to have a room dedicated to working out because it is not a small machine and I will leave it unfolded. In a small apartment this might feel like an elephant sitting in the room, but if you are willing to fold it up after each workout, it folds up very compactly.
Another bonus, if you have amazon prime you receive this machine in 2 days of ordering it!!! Whereas, the TG Direct site may take 10days! I am very happy with my purchase and will update if I notice any changes with this machine.
If you are looking for a less expensive Total Gym you might want to check out the Total Gym 1800 Club package. It is 399. and comes with many of the same equipment as this package. I just happen to come across it on youtube. In fact, watching the video, it looked as if it came with the AbCrunch. It is worth checking out if this package is not in your budget. Now that I have the XLS, I do not see much of a difference between the two machines except for the price and change in the bench style. There may be other differences, but it looks to be very similar and at a much lower price!
Update 7/27/2012 - I have been using the TG every other day with the beginning DVD and LOVING it!! I get really excited about working out now. Using the DVD is truly like having a personal trainer and I really sweat with the workout. I am so happy that I made this purchase and would recommend to anyone at any level wanting to get in shape. It gives a great cardio and toning/strengthening workout! At first I was a little worried I wasn't going to be able to keep up, but I just kept doing the best I could and now I love it and can't wait to work out. On days that I am not on the TG, I work out on my recumbent bike and am amazed how I feel now just in this short time. Sometimes I use the TG and the Bike on the same day and am working on doing that more.

title: Best water bottle I've ever used. I love it and I think you will as well!
text:
I live an on-the-go kind of life. I'm always running from point A to point B with a big tote or a backpack full of things that cannot get water damage. I've used dozens of water bottles over the years and there's always been a problem: one is too big so it doesn't fit in my purse or water bottle pocket on my backpack, another leaks like nobody's business, another has a straw that just won't stay attached so you're sipping air most of the time, and others just don't lock up nice and tight.

One day, I was talking with my sister over lunch and I had noticed she pulled this water bottle from the dark recesses of her tote and nothing in her purse was wet. I was impressed. She had gotten this water bottle when she bought a 4 years ago and had used this water bottle exclusively since. She took it with her abroad and takes it to college classes everyday with no problems. After I hear her rave reviews, I decided to buy one.

I've been using this water bottle for a few months now and I honestly am in love. The slim design makes it unique compared to the typical Nalgene but it still feels very sturdy. Not quite a liter of water but it's more than the typically grocery story water bottle. The loop on the top makes it easy to grab on the go and even hook, via carabiner, to a strap or your bag. My favorite feature is the locking mouth piece.

In order to drink water, you have to flip the metal lock down and push the button to pop the lid off. I've read some reviews saying that this is too much effort but honestly, I love it. I know that the water bottle won't leak and it hasn't. I work in a school and I carry this around all day. Sometimes my students accidentally kick it across the floor and no water ever leaks. I also drop this bag into my gym bag and nothing gets damp ever. The small mouth piece also makes it great to grab a quick gulp of water while you're in the middle of a run. No twisting off lids: just flip the lock down, press the button and delicious H2O is delivered to your mouth with no spills.

Bottom line: buy this water bottle. I love it and I think you will too.

text:

So why only 3 stars? These 20lb weights have exactly the same velcro strap design as the smaller ones I have. When you're dealing with only 5lb per ankle, velcro works great. At 20lb, not so much.

title: Love the visibility, don't love the breathing
text:
I snorkel maybe once a year, and never really love it. I tend to do most of my day-to-day breathing through my nose, and when forced to use my mouth I go into a bit of subconscious panic mode that takes a while to wear off and makes the whole snorkel experience less fun and relaxing than it should be. So when I read about full-face masks I was excited to be able to finally snorkel with no issues at all. I read up on the potential safety risks as well, and decided on this model, as one of the few on the market that appears to have been tested for CO2 issues.

Upon receiving the mask I tried it on and found it to be easy enough to deal with. I tried it on in my house and found it to be pretty comfortable and breathing to be no issue at all. Later I took it to a pool to give it a better test before going into the ocean and discovered that I had to lock down the straps quite a bit in order to get a waterproof fit. This made it less comfortable -- but not too bad all in all. Visibility, I noticed right away, was amazing, and a huge upgrade from what I'm used to with "traditional" snorkel gear.

As I swam around in the pool I started feeling a touch lightheaded and realized that I didn't see any bubbles coming up around me when I breathed out -- which struck me as odd, given that the mask is designed to release air through holes on the bottom.

After experimenting a bit I realized what was going on. Although I could breath fine and normally on land, the additional pressure exerted on the outside of the mask by being in water was causing the flaps to not open enough to release the stale air. Eventually I found a solution to this problem: Do not breath normally. Instead, take a fairly large breath, hold it for a bit, and then forcefully exhale. This produces enough counter pressure to open the flaps, releasing the stale air and allowing enough new oxygen to flow in to keep your brain happy.

Problem sorted I went on my vacation, went out on a boat, and spent some time in the water snorkeling. I was able to see lots of great stuff thanks to this mask, and I was able to swim more naturally/comfortably and keep my head down for longer than I've ever been able to before. And that's great. But I had to remember to do my "special" breathing pattern the whole time. Occasionally my focus would wander, I'd forget, and I'd feel my head getting foggy. And every time that happened, in the back of my head there would be a little voice telling me "this may not be safe. You're going to suffocate." And that sort of ruined the experience.

Plusses after that big negative: No fogging at all. Perfect visibility. No water leakage at all. That was a first for me when snorkeling -- I didn't taste salt water even once.

Maybe there's a better solution to the breathing problem. Maybe I just need more practice. Or maybe the tech is simply not there yet. Either way, I can't really recommend this product based on my experience. I really wanted to love it, and I hope that someday I can have a truly amazing snorkel trip. But for now I'm not really sure what I'll do. Part of me wants to try this again, and part of me is afraid. Possible that I did a bit too much research prior to this purchase!

title: Great Bench at a Great Price
text:
I spent a LOT of time researching benches (really, way too much time), but bottom line was that I wanted something stable, adjustable, and of course I didn't want to break the bank. There are a lot of really questionably pricey benches out there -- and when it comes down to it a bench is a very simple piece of equipment. Why are they so expensive? After all of my time investment I am confident in saying that absolutely no other bench on the market combines the features of this bench and its low price.

Specifics:

Delivery -- Typical, left outside of my house.

Packaging -- Decent. The inner boxes were a bit torn up as Rep didn't put enough padding in place. But none of the parts were damaged.

Instructions -- Complete joke. The "assembly" instructions are a single page parts diagram and then a second page of "tips." Come on, at least provide a step-by-step guide? Please visit any IKEA store to learn how it's done.

Assembly -- The instructions are not completely useless; everything can be figured out from the diagram. There is some mention of videos to be watched, but I couldn't be bothered. Overall it wasn't bad but it definitely took longer than the stated 15 minutes -- probably closer to 45.

The biggest issue for me was getting the seat bolted into place. The "tips" sheet shows it being done with the cushion up, which would require some extreme form of dexterity that I don't possess. After a while I realized that I could un-bolt the seat from the base of the unit (this requires removing a bolt that comes already in place from the factory) and then just flip the whole thing back -- after that the rest of the assembly was very simple.

Note that the bolts are a bit on the large side. Neither of my two ratchet sets had anything quite big enough (mine go up to 9/16"), so I had to use a combination of an adjustable wrench and the provided sheet metal "multitool." This undoubtedly slowed me way down.

Overall assembly includes screwing in maybe 8 bolts for the seat and back, two for the ankle pads, and then another four or so for the rest of the unit. Then you go through and tighten everything down, including the bolts that were put on at the factory.

Utilization -- Once assembled, the unit feels extremely sturdy. It sits perfectly on the floor without rocking, and gives me full confidence. The pads are plenty comfortable in my opinion; sure they're a bit stiff, but it's not like I'm going to take a nap on the thing. Also I suspect that these pads will hold up better over time than softer ones would.

Adjustment is simple for both the seat and the back and there are plenty of options for what I need to get done on a daily basis. One important note is that when flat or in decline there is definitely a considerable gap between the seat and back. I know this bothers a lot of people. I don't mind it and don't find it uncomfortable, but I do notice it; if you're looking for something gap-free, look elsewhere.

Not much else to say. I think despite the few flaws, for the price this bench is absolutely unbeatable and will serve me for many years. I'm very happy with my purchase...and I can use the money saved to buy more weights to test that 1,000 pound capacity limit!

title: If you are buying a Kleen Kanteen, this is the one.
text: I quite like this bottle.  I bought this in the 16 oz size and i maybe should have gone larger, as i really like the design.  I use this one for coffee, though If it were larger i would keep water in it.  The thing I like about this over others in the Kleen Kanteen range is the lip and threading.  The classic bottles have threading on the outside of the lip of the bottle with a cap which screws over the lip, clamping its edge against a gasket.  I have come to find this design prone to leaks if the gasket isn't properly seated.  The TKWide range just doesn't have this problem.  The threading is on the inside, low, under the lip of the bottle and the cap screws into it with a simple o ring.  I'm not a huge fan of the "cafe cap" but i just remove it and drink from the lip of the bottle which is itself quite comfortable.  It's kleer that kleen kanteen designed this bottle to work in exactly this way, as the lip of the bottle is the most comfortable of any i've ever encountered to drink from and they even make an assortment of different caps for this line with different features.  I'm considering getting the simple steel loop or bamboo cap to eliminate all remaining unnecessary parts.  The user experience drinking from the bottle with cap removed is similar to drinking from a tall glass tumbler.  The threading is recessed from the lip and doesn't interfere with drinking at all.. I also like that the 'cafe cap' is easily disassembled.. I hate cleaning these things, once a few weeks of coffee residue gets on them.  I've dropped this bottle twice and it has a dent now, but nothing severe.  I find it well made and well engineered and though, in my head at least, this bottle rivals the yeti ramblers which are similar, its about half of the price or less.

title: It's a single walled steel bottle with a slight design flaw.
text: I don't know how to rate the sturdiness or durability of such a product.  It's a steel bottle.  If you drop it, particularly when full, you'll put some dents in it.  If you're planning on driving over it with a tank, maybe just get a polycarbonate Nalgene.. And I can't really speak to using this on a campfire, which i know some folks do out in the wild.  What i can say is that I really like this bottle.  It has one flaw:  I'm not a huge fan of the cap.  The cap threads onto external threading and this snugs the lip of the bottle up against a gasket seated in the cap.  If this gasket isn't properly seated, the bottle leaks and more than a couple of times have I thought I closed the cap tightly ( you kind of have to crank it down due to this design) only to realize that, though I had, the gasket was allowing water to slowly leak out.  This is a problem on leather car seats or even in a pack, and though I haven't had any major property loss as a result, i still check this bottle for leaks before i stow it.  Say what you will about Nalgene bottles, but they simply don't have this issue.  Nor does the TKWide line, with an internal threading and o-ring cap, made by this same company..  The gasket itself is removable and i think the tab (which is how you pull the gasket out) might get caught in the lip of the bottle occasionally.  Anyway, I do quite like this bottle and I use it almost everyday now, though I've gotten in to the habit of checking it for leaks every time i use it.

title: Sodbuster.  The RAT1 of the traditional era.
text:
This review is going to be biased. Can't be helped. My first three knives were a Barlow (a really cheap one) a Victorinox and a Case stockman (or was it a trapper) . Idk, my dad stole all of these from me when I got old enough to do any damage with them. The case is the only one I miss. I'm tempted, as a 40 year old grown man, to go rifling through his drawers to find it. And my pellet gun.
The Sodbuster is the biggest Case knife I've ever seen. My father-in-law carries a trapper and usually I got my Tx toothpick on me, but when I got this sucker, I was pretty impressed with its size. Let's get the obvious stuff out of the way, it's a slipjoint (a really easy one too), no pocket clip, no newfangled blade steel. It's a work knife for digging around in a garden. Some folks will be turned off by all of these things. I look at them as plusses. I'm not sure where the idea that a non-locking blade = dangerous came about. You really do have to handle slipjoints slightly differently than locking blades but they are just as safe if not safer in most contexts. It's a matter of exposure. I carved wood with my barlow for years, and occasionally the blade would stick or something but I always knew that could happen. I did have one close on my fingers once or twice but there wasn't any force behind it and not really anything happened as a result. I think most modern knife folks grew up with a slipjoint and maybe injured themselves with one as a kid, possibly while clowning around with it, to the point where as adults they think of them as an unnecessary hazard. The pocket clip... well I could take it or leave it. It's easier for a work knife not to have to fish around in my pocket for it repeatedly. That said, mostly I leave this one on my desk or table. Not sure I would carry it around in public. It's mighty big for a pocket. As for the blade steel, I generally prefer high carbon steel. I can sharpen such a knife really well with a stone. I'm not sure that I really like the edge retention of modern steels. I have an r2d2 - I have yet to sharpen it, but I'm guessing it will be a pain in the butt. I know exactly what to expect with softer steels.. In short, this is a fine knife appointed well for the last millenia. It's the folksier version of a RAT 1 and it will appeal to any who like the shape.

title: A solid tool knife.
text: I quite love this blade.. I bought the coated version to leave in my car as a utility knife, but very quickly it found its way into my pockets.. There are a few issues with this knife:  I had to immediately borrow a star key tool to change the clip over to the tang.. I don't really care if it carries tip up or down (comes tip down) but the clip is a bit large on this knife and just in the way, particularly for a knife with such great ergonomics.  The coating on the blade is also not the best.. Also mine had a few little imperfections throughout the blade- just a little pitting here and there.  Still, pretty quickly this knife has made it into my rotation.  The main reason is its ease of use.  The washers have worn in quite well and though it was a bit stiff out of the box, within a week, it opens like butter.. I've typically always favored old-school slipjoint pocket knives over locking knives for carry, but i really see the ease of one-hand use in this design.  The weight and size of the blade also really add to the inertia upon opening so it's just a really satisfying knife to flip open.. Other people might balk at the grips- I thought they felt a little cheap in the hand when I first inspected the knife, but they've turned out to be pretty solid, textured just enough to prevent slippage if they got wet.  Is it the best knife for the money?  I don't know- I bought mine for around 15 bucks and at that price wasn't expecting much:  Just a decent linerlock with a soft enough blade to easily keep sharp- something for the car-  but its size, ease of use and just good solid blade design make for a really practical tool knife which i carry more and more.

title: This electric bike is compact and a joy to ride! Highly Recommend!
text:
[[VIDEOID:e7db44ebf2cc5b42c4a2213aa6e49919]] We really love our new electric bike. The set up was super easy and only required that we remove the packaging, insert the seat, unfold the handle bar, adjust the grip, and screw the pedals in. The recommended initial charge is 5 hours – ours took about 4 hours for the light to turn green.

The bike will provide assistance while pedaling or you can use the throttle on the handle bar to power the bike unassisted. I’m 145lbs and the bike cruises at 12-13mph on flat ground using just the throttle without pedaling. The battery display adjusts according to how hard the assist is working. Pedaling uphill will seemingly drop the remaining charge, but you “gain” it back when the elevation levels out. As far as we can tell, pedaling does not recharge the battery.

I am 5’8” and the bike fits just fine. My husband is 6’4”. He can still ride it but it’s certainly not the most comfortable – much taller than that and you’re likely to hit the handle bar with your knees.

Pro’s:
-Compact enough to fit into a small trunk
-Easy Set up
-3 Pedal assist modes (Mode 1 Full, Mode 2 Partial, Mode 3 Next to nothing)
-Built in headlight, taillight, and horn
-Taillight flashes when braking – even if the lights are turned off
-Comfortable, wide seat
-Rear suspension works great
-Comes with 2 keys and electric functions will not work without the key in place and turned

Con’s:
-Not great for airline travel because the battery is not designed to be removable
-Display shows metric speed and distance only
-A bit heavy
-The manual leaves a lot to be desired – not a lot about the bike BUT its all fairly self-explanatory

Update: the seller contacted me and sent a replacement bottle that didn't have the imperfections.

title: and the perfect amount of battery that I never have to think ...
text: Vast improvement over the original Charge HR, and the perfect amount of battery that I never have to think about it. And just enough notifications as a "smartwatch" - Calls, Texts and Calendar alerts only. Really the only improvement I'd want is for the text to be faster/easier to read. Perfect otherwise.

title: Pretty good product/idea
text: Pretty good product/idea, but after some use it sprung a leak. Still sorta works, but this was a disapointingly short lifespan.

title: The stupid triangle design doesn’t fit through D hoops
text: The stupid triangle design doesn’t fit through D hoops.

title: Comfortably wide. Great improvement for my stationary.
text: Works for my fat ass. 280lbs is probably the max you’ll be comfortable on. Needed a wider seat for my home stationary bike. It made it rideable. Would like to see another version handling even more weight. Powerlifters need love too.

title: Great bike. Awkward angle for handle bars.
text: For the money it's a great bike, the handle bars are awkward. It would be great to be able to reach them from a more upright position. My elderly dad is short and I'm over 6'0 neither of us can comfortably reach the bars. Everything else about this bike is great.

title: I love this fitbit
text: I love this fitbit. I did a ton of research before purchasing the zip. I like that I can just clip it to my pants/shirt and forget about it. For me, the wrist versions were distracting and had features I didn't necessarily need. My only complaint is that the plastic piece on the clip fell off within the first month. Fitbit was quick to replace the outer shell within days.

title: Great umbrella.
text: Very durable.  Shipped in time for Christmas!

title: nice & durable
text: This is a very nice ping pong paddle.  It's just the right weight and the handle seems like it's very durable.  Shipped quickly!

title: Slippery
text: So soft and comfy warm. Very slippery though.

title: Great addition to my camping/hiking gear
text: Love this hammock and the Talon tree straps. Super easy to hang and very sturdy but comfortable. I love the bright orange because I can see it in the dark, so I don't get tangled. Way lighter than my old cotton hammock and I will gladly schlep it around when I am backpacking. All my kids are getting the same setup for Christmas.

title: Torn
text: Torn

title: Five Stars
text: Best pack I've owned.I use it every day

title: Very sturdy and easy to assemble
text: This is very sturdy. My sister in law put it together in probably 20-30 min. I have 35 and 40 lb dumbbells on The bottom with other dumbbells on other rows and plates on the sides. Kettlebells on the top. This is not wobbly at all. It has saved so much space and doesn’t take up a lot of space. This was a great purchase and very affordable.

title: Great skates
text: My daughter learned to roller skate. These are solid and good quality. We are on our second pair since her feet grew.

title: Pricy but you know what you’re buying
text: It’s expensive but unlike the garbage you get from the No-name brand tools on Amazon, you know what you’re getting

title: Disappointed
text:
Torqued to spec, these were “fine” except that they kept coming lose on me during a ride. I tried thread lock but it didn’t seem to help much. I tried to manually torque them down a little further and the threads immediately gave out. Maybe I had a bad batch, idk, but I’ve had much better luck with your regular old no-name ring bolts.

One thing I will say, though. Having a 6mm hex head on the inside and a 4mm on the outside js genius. I wish more chainring bolts were like this.

title: Works well, build quality is just ok
text: It does what it’s supposed to but it’s not without issues. The friction mode does not have any sort of ratcheting like some nicer lever do. This just makes it a little easier to move the lever and tell how far you’ve moved it when you shift quickly. It works fine but it would have been nice to have a smoother actuation in friction mode. In indexed mode, the lack of smoothness when shifting is less of a problem as you have the index points to overcome anyway and there’s enough resistance at each index position that you’ll rarely shift past your intended gear on accident. The lever does have quite a bit of play it it, however. It would have been nice to have seen tighter tolerance in the index positions. I have enough slop in mine after just a year of use that I can partially disengage a gear without bumping past the index notch. Not a huge deal, and sometimes its actually nice to have that wiggle room, but it would be better in my opinion if the indexing was more precise. If I wanted to finesse it in to gear, I’d use it in friction mode…

title: Good derailleur for the price
text: It’s a solid, reliable, cheap derailleur with a clutch. I’ve got it on my daily commuter/gravel bike. It reaches up to a 46T cassette without issue. I’m using it with the Microshift BS-M11-R bar end shifter. They work well together.

title: Great quality for the price
text: This is my second Bolany cassette I’ve used on my builds (two different bikes). They’re a bit on the heavy side but they are sturdy, easy to install and they seem to last just as long as any of the name brands out there. I’ve had the older of the two (11-46T) on my Surly Disc Trucker for over two years now. I have ridden it almost every day as my primary mode of transportation during this time and have had no problems at all.

title: Absolute garbage
text: The chain snapped off on the first use. Save yourself the time and headache and just buy a proper chain whip.

title: Great but needs a clutch version
text: Needs a clutch but is otherwise a great derailleur for those who need a Shimano compatible, 9spd, long cage derailleur.

title: Perfect for some extra adjustability with Brooks saddles
text: This seat post is exactly what I needed after upgrading to a Brooks B17 saddle on my touring bike. As described on the product page, Brooks rails do not as long as more modern saddles and as a result I was unable to slide my saddle as far back as needed. This seat post not only looks great but provides AMPLE setback to fix this issue.

title: Great product, not 100% compatible with all bikes!
text: Great for the price. Very light weight and easy to mount. Important note for buyers who don’t have a fork with three mount points such as on my Surly LHT, you will only be able to attach one screw. I used the lower one on the top mount on the cage and then a hose clamp for the lower. I tested various methods to attach these and settled on this  and have had zero problems with it for hundreds of miles of riding now. ZIP TIES ARE NOT ENOUGH! Use a hose clamp and make sure you put something between the cage and your fork to protect the fork. I used a piece of inner tube with some light adhesive spray to hold it on the frame, it works very well.

title: Perfect
text: Perfect for attaching my Nalgene and dry bags to my fork cages.

title: Works great, needs long cage derailleur
text: Works great, comes with a derailleur extender. My only complaint is that it was hard to find a 9-spd derailleur that has a long enough cage. I ended up with a Microshift M26 (discontinued) that I found second hand. I’m still on the hunt for a Shimano compatible, clutch derailleur for it, though. The chain slap is unbelievable with such a big cog.

title: Durable and great for commuters
text: Installed these in my commuter bike. I almost always ride with clips but recently have been making shorter trips and feeling lazy so I want to just jump in and ride without the fuss. These pedals work really well. They were adjusted a little tight from the factory but otherwise I’ve had no issue with them riding hundreds of miles in all kinds of weather. Very durable.

title: Quality brand makes a quality product
text: Wonderful tires, not much else to say about them. Top quality from a top brand. Enough said.

title: The pin removal tool is garbage
text: The pin removal tool is complete garbage. The other tools are fine but the threads on the pin remover don't even mesh well enough to get any meaningful pressure on the pin. Save yourself the headache, spend more money and go with Park Tool or some other reputable brand.

title: Bit flimsy but they've held up well
text: I am not easy on my bike. I have these on my "do everything" bike and I mean do EVERYTHING. I go everywhere on it. On road, off road and everywhere in between. While I wish the mounts were a little less flimsy, as the fender isn't mounted very rigidly, it is on well enough that it hasn't taken any damage in the nearly 6 months of hard riding they've been through. The black paint holds up well too. I debated getting silver to avoid the scratches showing but, honestly, these haven't scratched any that I can tell. I was also worried about "clanking" from rocks getting thrown up in to the metal fender but I haven't noticed this either... either these don't make a lot of noise when stuff hits them or rocks getting thrown up in the fender is not as common as I'd imagined.

title: Nice and thick. Sturdy
text: I do a lot of bike maintenance for people in my neighborhood and buy stuff like cables and cable housing in bulk regularly. This has probably been one of the better cable housings I've purchased in recent memory. Nice and thick, has a nice nylon coating on the inside and is lined with a nice solid metal coil running along the inside for extra rigidity.

title: My go-to
text: I've purchased a couple of these and they are excellent. I run a small bike shop out of my garage and I keep a stock of these on hand at all times for quick replacements. The price is very reasonable and the quality is good and they're nice and long so they work in a variety of bikes.

title: Perfect replacement
text: Got a new frame and had to route a longer hose to the rear brake. This is a perfect replacement and has held up well. Would definitely purchase again.

title: JUNK. Don't waste your money
text: The manufacturing tolerance on this thing is a joke. The threads for the center piece don't even mesh correctly with the handle so when you try to apply pressure to the rivet to remove a link, it just slips and it can't do the one job it is supposed to. Spend a little more money and get Park Tool.

title: Fantastic bags
text:
I have had these for about a year now. They saw light use for the first 8 months or so but I have now gotten rid of my car and bike most places now so they're getting a lot more use. They've proven to be very well constructed and waterproof as advertised. The clips do seem like they minght be a little flimsy but I've not had any problems with them yet (fingers crossed). I could see how, if you were clipping and unclipping them frequently you might want to be a little careful. Thankfully, my use case has them always attached to the bike and, for this, they have been perfect. The material is very sturdy as well. There's a spot along one of my routes where it gets really narrow and if I've loaded the panniers full, one will rub against the stone wall next to the path. This has happened dozens of time and the material, while scuffed, has not ripped or really take any damage. Additionally, as testimony to the durability, I crashed my bike about a week ago and the bags survived fully in tact. There were, again, scuffs on the outside of the bags but no tears or broken parts.

Overall, for the money, these have been wonderful. You should be careful if you're regularly clipping and unclipping them as the plastic clips seem like they might be a little flimsy but they're otherwise very sturdy and waterproof.

title: Great for commuting but not very good in the rain
text:
I've commuted with this bag for two weeks now. I also have the Ibera waterproof panniers. I wish this was as waterproof as those panniers. I also wish it mounted better to the Ibera brand bike rack. It mounts "ok" but it's not as great as you would expect for a product that is made to work together. The clip mechanism is relatively easy to use to release the bike but it's fickle sometimes; often requiring quite a bit of effort to get clipped on or release. It feels like the clip mechanism does not move very freely and gets jammed with dirty easily. I strongly recommend getting the rain cover if you plan on using this in the rain without any other bags to put stuff in when the rain starts. I've been stuck in the rain a few times and the first time I didn't realize how porous the material of this bag was and my stuff got damp. Now, if I am expecting rain, I put my phone, hat and other things I want to keep dry in the waterproof pannier instead of the trunk bag.

Overall, this bag is great for light, dry weather commuter use. The removable shoulder strap is a nice touch. If you plan to ride in the rain either buy the rain cover, buy a different trunk or put your stuff in a waterproof bag.

title: Fine for everything, not great at anything
text:
I got these to put on my mountain bike that I was going to start using for commuting to work. Overall I'm happy with them. Ride quality is not as great as a road tire. Grip in mud/dirt is not as great as a knobby mountain bike tire. Road noise is less than a knobby tire if you run a higher pressure but then the ride quality is really harsh. To make them more comfortable, I run them around 35lbs in the front and 45lbs in the rear (heavy rear cargo). Doing this makes them ride considerably better but then they're noisier too a more of the "tread" is contacting the ground. This is also amusing in the rain, they make a funny "splop splop splop" sound (kind of like a wet suction cup?). They're also advertised as more puncture resistant due to them being "thicker". I find this to be a dubeous claim at best since I have only been riding these for about two weeks and I've already had a flat.

Overall Opinion: They're fine. If you know you're going to ride strictly on paved trails, however, get a road tire.

title: Much better than the stock clip
text: Much better than the stock handlebar clip.

title: Installs Easy, made safety cable for some extra insurance
text:
Kind of small but overall seems sturdy enough. I wish it was a little bit larger but I understand that this particular rack is designed to be small on purpose. I have a plastic milk crate zip tied on to the top of mine and it has worked well so far.

I heeded the warnings of other comments here and bought a small length of metal cable to provide a safety catch in case the metal bracket that mounts to the brake caliper snaps. It does seem like a fairly week design and a few dollars at the hardware store for some insurance seemed reasonable given that it's still cheaper than most other racks of similar design.

title: Great but did not fit Trek 1000c
text:
These do not fit the back wheel on a Trek 1000c

Overall I really liked these but unfortunately the back fender did not fit between my brake and tire without rubbing on the tire due to the plastic clip that attaches it to the brake bridge. The front fender fit well, however, and the quality of these fenders seems more than adequate. If I had been able to make them fit I'm sure I would have loved them.

title: I'd recommend this reel to anyone
text: I somehow managed to get one of these from Warehouse Deals for less than $120 due to a small cosmetic scratch. For that price this reel is an absolute phenomenon. Very lightweight and responsive. Casts all types of line and lure weights with ease. I'd recommend this reel to anyone.

title: ZT 0450
text: You cannot go wrong with Zero Tolerance. Look up Youtube reviews for this knife and see if it's what you really want. For me it's perfect.

title: Excellent, Just Like My Old Swimteam Goggles, but More Comfort
text: These are really great goggles.  I hope that if you're reading this and getting into swimming, you give these a try.  I swam for about 20 years on youth and school teams and always wore Swedish goggles.  These combine the performance of the Swedish style with a rubber eye gasket for comfort.  The best of both worlds and for the price, you can't go wrong.  Skip all of the fancy eyewear and stick with the basics that work

title: Well Worth the Cheap Price
text: Took a while to charge, but provided nice bright light for my 3 day trip.  For the price, I think it's hard to beat this guy since it's rechargeable.  The build quality is decent, the carabiner it comes w/ allows it to hang conveniently from the ceiling of a tent, and the rate of power consumption seems very reasonable.  I ran this light for a few hours a night during a recent trip and it hadn't run out of juice.  I'm not sure what the formal operating time is on a single charge, but 3 days is pretty good.

title: Good for the price
text: I used these to add a bit of comfort to my camping cot.  Based on 2 camping trips, I'd say they're worth the reasonable price. I felt like they added a bit of support to my cot; I usually find that my hips sag slightly in cots and I've woken up w/ sore hips before.  I didn't experience that on either night w/ these pads.  I also think they add a nice barrier b/w your body and the air beneath the cot.

title: Sweet Irony! Device Meant to Prevent Bending Over Causes Bending Over
text:
This is a fairly simple product and, as such, you would think it would be pretty difficult to screw up. The theory behind item's construction is sound, but the construction is lousy. Specifically, I will point you to the cap at the top of the tube; this cap is poorly fitted to the tube and readily falls off w/o much prompting. There are only two things keeping balls inside this tube, the plastic claw at the bottom of the tube and the top cap. If one of these fails, you're left with an open tube that balls can fall out of at their leisure, which is exactly what I experienced. The top cap repeatedly fell off of my tube during use, a couple times from tipping the tube to where the balls pressed against the cap and a couple times after leaving the tube in my car filled with balls. I've owned other ball tubes and have been able to carry them horizontally and man-handle them fairly roughly w/o ever having this issue. The end result of owning this product that was supposed to keep me from having to bend over to pick up golf balls was that I was bending over to pick up balls that had fallen out of the tube. Sweet sweet irony!

I thought I may have just received a defective product and requested a refund from Amazon and was content to leave it at that. However, one of my golfing buddies said he purchased this tube and experienced the same issue, which leads me to believe this product is just generally poorly made.

title: Solid Bar
text:
This is a solid pull-up bar, sturdy construction, good variety of hand holds with comfortable grips. I have a few minor criticisms, but they don't really detract from the functionality of the bar.

First, the pads the manufacturer placed on the parts that come in contact with your door jamb and wall can leave black marks after a full workout. I solved this problem by wrapping wash cloths around the pads, so there's a buffer b/w the pads and my door jamb. The same goes for the top pad that braces against the wall. It was a matter of 60 seconds of labor to put some cloth on the pads and secure them w/ rubber bands. My second criticism is that the bolts used to hold the whole bar together do not come equipped w/ washers of any kind. Inclusion of 25 cents worth of locking washers would have made this product's construction pretty outstanding. I would recommend going to a hardware store and grabbing some locking washers to use during construction. As the bar comes from the manufacturer, there is nothing that prevents you from over-tightening the nuts and damaging/warping the bars.

The resistance bands are great, I have not had any problems with them whipping me in the face, like some other reviewer complained of. The hand grips are very comfortable and sturdy. The weight provided by the bands is pretty heavy, if all 5 bands are used together it provides ~75lbs of resistance. An ankle attachment is included for leg exercises, as well. A booklet is included with 6 example exercises to be done w/ the bands.

title: Perfect for Wheelchair
text: Bought this for my father who is wheelchair bound.  This is perfect for keeping him warm while supporting his favorite team and safe from getting anything stuck in the wheels.  He has had many compliments and loves the attention he gets.

title: Item is not the same as pictured
text:
I bought this after quitting the gym as it makes doing abs much easier. I chose this unit as I am tall and in the image the pad comes short of the floor but a good amount. In the actual product it is no more then 1/2-1
" from the floor. It is also not very comfortable, The leg pads are a bit annoying. Some of the plastic was also broken, so its a bit frustrating when I'm spending $180 on this thing to have these issues.

title: One Star
text: While I initially liked it, it cracked after only 2 uses.

title: Doesn't last long
text: Only lasted a few months, then started leaking.

title: Alternative Uses
text: I use this tent to let my sugar gliders run wild. It's a great size to fit into an indoor room and perfect to let them have outside time. I only wish that there was a way to weight down the ends when inside and unable to stake them down.

title: Absolutely NOT water tight
text: I'm camping in Maryland. One of the days has been rainy all day. The tent is leaking from six different seam points. Additionally, the rain fly comes only partway down on the ends. The windows on those ends do NOT zip closed. There is no panel to do so. Rain is being blown in that way as well.

title: Matte coating wears off easily
text: It’s a very functional water bag. Didn’t leak on me yet after 1 week of constant use in Morocco. Reason for less stars is the matte finish starts wearing off after one day of use and it looks cheap and very used. The clip is also made if cheap plastic and easy to accidentally unclip.

title: Temperature required to melt solder deteriorates shrink
text: The shrink on this turns to goo well before the solder inside melts making these nearly useless. The adhesive works well, but the electrical connection is terrible inside due to cold solder at best; at worst you have a breach in the shrink ruining insulation.

title: For the money, solid tool set.
text: The hammer, box cutter, level, allen keys, vise, and pliers are all very solid quality--as a home-gamer, I still use these as my primary tools. The bits aren't the best, but you can use them for as long as they last. There's a good assortment.

title: Best Shot Timer I've Used
text:
So, I bought this product and loved it. It was great at the indoor/outdoor range for pistol or rifle but one problem I kept having was that half of the screen would black out whenever it was reset. I tried different batteries and contacted customer support. Let me say, they were fantastic! I sent off the product and it was replaced and back to my house without a hitch (even faster than they quoted for turnaround).

Ever since the bug was fixed, I have had zero problems and it records my times/splits methodically. I enjoy being able to adjust the random delays to help with my response time and seeing all of my previous times at the click of a button. I would def buy this again if my timer ever died.

title: Awesome Knife for EDC
text:
I recently moved up in the knife world and I couldn't be happier with this purchase!
The only reason I took off one star was that the black coating on the blade comes off (expected) with a decent amount of use. Otherwise, this knife is a monster! It the blade holds up well to all different types of materials and it sits in my pocket perfectly balanced. It is a large knife, but it is not heavy/noticeable to me. I would buy another one in a heartbeat if something happened to this one.

title: Great Training Bag
text: Great workout/training bag. I train Muy Thai and use this bag occasionally to work on my drills. It works great and is a great alternative to a heavy Thai bag if you cannot use one at home. It does move, but I treat it similar to a heavy hanging bag. It helps you work on your footwork to adjust with the bag. Overall, I would suggest this to anyone if they cannot use a hanging bag.

title: Nice!
text: Great quality with a cool design. I use it for Muay Thai and really like it so far.

title: Just what I needed!
text: Worked great for a quick cleaning. Easy to wash/store. If you need a quick cleaner after the range then this is perfect!

title: Cheap Zippers and Short Mat Straps
text: This bag is a great idea but it has cheap zippers and the straps to hold a yoga mat aren't quite long enough. Some of the pockets are hard to open and even the large compartment can be a hassle to open and close. Also, the yoga mat straps are too small for my B Mat and Alo Warrior Mat. The Manduka Pro is skinnier so it fits. Overall I don't recommend this product. If they made a few changes I'm sure it would be great.

title: Works pretty well
text: This fan worked surprisingly better than I expected. The light isn't bad, but I avoided using it so as not to impact the function of the fan. We used the fan for 3 nights while camping in 80+ weather, and worked well at night to cool the tent with solid air circulation. The battery didn't quite last all night, but long enough for us to get a comfortable sleep in.

title: They work!
text: These work great, in fact the only issue with them is that they're easy to misplace. I highly recommend if you're looking to secure your bike wheel and fork while traveling.

title: Absorbent, once.
text: These are very light, pack down nicely, and come with a helpful carrying case. And in all of those categories, I'd give it a 5+ stars. The problem is that when it comes to being a towel they're awful. Once they absorb water, it's impossible to wring them out and get another use out of them. I have several pack towels from other manufactures (REI), and everyone of them can be wrung out and used again immediately. That's a key aspect of a pack towel. So due to that, this towel gets an over all rating of 2.

title: I wish I found this sooner
text: We used this for our 1 year old when camping. It gives him a portable place he can sleep, without taking up as much space as a pack'n'play. Once inflated the mattress is perfect for a little baby, the product folds up easily, and the material strikes me as easy to clean. This thing is great!

title: One of the worst microfiber towels out there.
text: I purchased this towel hoping it would be an affordable alternative to the handful of REI brand pack towels I already had. Initially the towels felt soft, their size was perfect, and the print looks great. They were also pretty absorbent, but when it came to wringing them out for continued use, they failed miserably. My other towels will wring out nicely, allowing you to continue to use them. This towel quickly because water logged, and would not wring to or dry quickly, which significantly limits use.

title: Disappointing Quality
text: I purchased two of these in 2018 for camping. I camp any where from 8 to 10 times in the summer/fall, so although I use my ground pads, they don't see a ton of use. Of the two, one still works great, while the other started leaking this season. When compared to my older Therm-a-rest that still works after 10+ years, that's a pretty poor performance, especially at over $100. The pad is very comfortable, you notice the insulation in the fall, which is nice, and it packs down nicely. So really the only drawback is that 3 years later I either have to buy a new one or go back to my uninsulated Klymit.

title: Lezyne makes great products, and this chuck is no different
text: Lezyne makes great products, and this chuck is no different. The one that came with the pump was lost, so I just replaced it with this one. I've had no issues using the chuck to inflate all tire values and types.

title: Well made and affordable, there's really no reason to ...
text: Well made and affordable, there's really no reason to buy this for your kid. I did find that it ran a little small. Be sure to measure your childs head.

title: Solid Daily Carry Knife
text: This the second time I have owned this knife. And not because it broke, but because it was stolen from me. The first time I received it free in a contest. Within a couple of months I became quite attached to it, and it's proven to be a very effective daily carry. It comes out of the box relatively sharp. You can sharpen a bit if you want, but it's ready for most tasks. The blade retains it's edge nicely, and is easy to maintain. I abuse my every day carry, and this one has held up. The handle material isn't slippery when the knife is wet, but it can be broken. I used the end to open a beer, and did break of a piece. The hole makes controlling the knife a breeze, and the lock is easy to operate. There's just enough serration to cut rope or other fibers, and the tip is good for prying. All and all it's a good affordable knife perfect for the rigors of daily use.

title: Great product for a good price.
text: Amazon has several different sizes of this product, and they're all fairly well made. The tube, zippers, and pouch hold my split rod very well. However there is a plastic buckle that holds the shoulder strap to the rod holder case. This makes the strape removable, but creates a weak spot. One of the cases I order came with the buckle already broken, and when I got a new one I saw that it was fairly flimsy. But for the price, you can't go wrong.

title: Doesn’t work
text: Glasses fogged up minutes after cleaning with this stuff.  Did not work.

title: Men's shoes don't fit shoe bag
text: Men's size 10 shoes will not fit in the shoe pocket of the without force (Size Small bag).  You can angle them to force the zipper closed, but they bulge and place stress on the zipper and seams, which would wear out pretty fast.  They can be placed in the main compartment and fit there, but would of course stink up anything else in the bag.  Small shoes (women, kids) may work.  Bag is actually 22 inches long, not 25.

title: Glad we bought these
text:
Worked great for a week-long snorkeling trip. We bought a different color for each family member, which made it easier to identify each other underwater. The carry bags were most handy. The smallish flippers did not slow us down, and made it easier to travel with these sets.

For women, check out the female version [[ASIN:B001QBHT1K U.S.Divers Diva 1 Lx / Island Dry Lx/ Trek / Travel Bag]] which is exactly the same, but in other colors and sizing.

title: These are nice, but much too narrow
text: These are 4 star handlebars by any measure. However, they weren't what I needed and I'll take full responsibility for not having really read the other reviews. I'm putting together a bike for my wife. She likes grip shifters and brakes. There isn't space on this handlebar for both. I'm not sure what these are designed for, kids' bikes maybe? But don't buy these without considering the layout.

title: Nice bag
text:
I've travelled with this in Central America and I liked it very much. I'd been looking for a daypack that I could carry with me in my luggage, or in my larger travel backpack. This bag does the job nicely. It's well made, doesn't have any features I don't need, and has nice pockets for carrying water bottles. I took a star off because when I first received it, it had a terrible, floral smell that took a few weeks to dissipate.

Edit: I've now had this for 2 years and I've used it constantly. I added the star back because the floral smell is now barely a memory. I would get another of these if I lost mine.

title: Comfortable and functional
text: Comfortable and compact. Great for camping in apartment living-rooms.

title: Three Stars
text: It could use more pockets.

title: Crumbly cakes
text: Agreed with Mikael Dillon Sink, this chalk does not function as it needs to. Ours arrived in fine condition but once we opened it, the chalk just crumbles but not enough into a powder that you would expect chalk to do. Trying to rub it on hands is almost impossible since it's like rubbing rocks on your hands. What's interesting is that we used this brand a year ago and it was fine. Seems like something changed in their process or it just went "bad" if that's possible.

title: Love my new FitBit Charge HR!
text:
My first one wouldn't hold a charge for longer than a day and a half, but I was able to rather easily get a refund for that one, and purchase a brand new one.

I use the iPhone app almost exclusively, since the Windows program is inexcusably bad. Theoretically any device with Bluetooth 4.0 should be able to talk to the Charge, but my Android tablet was unable to, so until I got my iPhone I was forced to use the Windows program along with a small USB FitBit dongle.

The Windows program has absolutely no other function then to sync with the Charge, Which in theory you can do anytime that the charge is within range. But my installation of Windows 7 ultimate was unable to perform this task without me specifically launching the program and telling it to sync.

With the exception of doing a little of the initial setup, other than that single function of retrieving information from the Charge, passing it on to the FitBit website and vice-versa, the Windows desktop program does nothing. Literally nothing.

The fact that the desktop app does nothing, forces you forces the users without a FitBit compatible phone or tablet to perform everything that ought to be able to be doable locally on the webpage.

Things like, choosing a watch face, or determining the order in which things are displayed, or determining what, if anything, a double tap on the watch face does.

Some other useful changes I would like to see are:

+ Personally, since the FitBit communicates via Bluetooth, I see no reason why the FitBit Bluetooth dongle that comes with the device can't be used by the computer that you plug it into as a Bluetooth dongle. They just need to write drivers specific to their dongle, which they already have, that have a way of seizing control of the dongle when it needs to transmit, and then return control of the dongle to the regular Bluetooth system when it's done. We've already paid for the Bluetooth dongle, we might as well be able to use it, even if we only ever use the app.

+ Most usefully, change the clock faces to show:
1) Remaining battery charge! (Could just be asterisks, periods, or even the pipe symbol | .)
2) The Day of the Week!
3) The Date! (MM/DD)
4) Option to display AM/PM with 12 hour watch faces.

+ Add the "Connected GPS" that the new Blaze boast's!

+ Of course, change the desktop program so that you can do all the things that you can do on both the website and the apps, on your computer.

+ Changing how the app displays your sleep data so that it includes the amount of time that you slept deeply, or were in interrupted sleep.

+ Making the website more intuitive.
+ Have the website display your sleep data in a useful manner.

+ A larger range of watch faces to choose from, not just the current four.
+ The option of an analog watch face.
+ Add a screen to the charge that displays at least some of your sleep data.
+ Allow the Charge to be accessed via Bluetooth, so that even phones unable to install the fit bit app can still send text and caller and information to it.

title: Decent watch, not as large as I had feared.
text:
I had been afraid that the PHRM26 was going to be HUGE, like it looks in the pictures, but in actuality it is really quite reasonable in size. What seems like a 4"x3" face is more like 1¼"x1". Part of what makes it look so large is the black bump in the at the top of the watch. That bump is NOT mirrored on the bottom, and is actually INSIDE the band. What is inside the bump is a naked USB connector for plugging the watch into your computer. The connector fits into a little notch in the wristband to protect it, and the bump as actually much larger than it need be.

I had purchased the PHRM26 for it's ability to measure my heart rate. The instructions are a bit hard to follow, and there is no mention of how to activate the Heart Rate Monitor belt. APPARENTLY, you just put it on, and it works. No need to turn the belt off and on. (Makes no sense to me, the battery would last longer.)

I had a heck of a time getting the heart rate monitor to work because I was taking my cell phone with me, and it was interfering with the signal from the band. I didn't like the idea of having to leave it behind, but once I realized the problem, I used a Cell Phone Arm Band on my right arm, and kept the watch on the left arm, with my body between the two. After that it seemed to work perfectly.

Pyle Audio is a German company, and the manual is pretty poor translation into English, one that I doubt was done by a fluent English speaker. In fact, one of the most important parts of the manual was written by hand, is really in the wrong place in the manual, and gives a very slip-shod impression. Especially when you realize that the list price is well over $100! They could spend a little money and fix their manual.

Calling the included program disappointing would be an understatement of huge proportions, and is the reason why I don't give the PHRM26 a 5 star review. Oddly, it REQUIRES both a username AND password to use. In some ways this is neat, as multiple usernames allow people to SHARE the watch, as long as they exercise at different times. But the PASSWORDs can cause problems if, like me, you forget the password you used. I actually had to abandon my first username because I forgot it's password. Leaving me with an account I can neither use, nor delete. Once you get into the program itself, it's rather difficult to really make a lot of sense out of what it shows you, though it DOES allow you to both EXPORT and IMPORT CSV files that you can use in a spreadsheet program, which is nice. That allows you to keep your own records and manipulate the data in any way you see fit.

One pretty major drawback, is that the PHRM26 can only hold data for your most-recent exercise. Meaning if you forget to upload the data from the watch, the next time you exercise you will either delete the data from the previous exercise, OR you will ADD your current exercises to your last exercises, so when you finally upload the data, the current day will show the data for both days. So basically you need to upload your data every day.

The Pyle Audio (the manufacturer) website lists the PHRM26 at like $135 or something close. IMHO that is FAR above it's value. I see them regularly going for $45 - $75 in different places including Amazon, and IMHO that is STILL more than what it is worth. I was fortunate to find this one being sold by Amazon Warehouse Deals as an open package for about $25, and I feel that I paid just about the right amount for what I got. Now, the fact is that I'm a cheapskate, and I'm sure that there are many others who feel that it's worth much more, but the fact is that comparing the software that comes with the watch with the free exercise website LoseIt.com, and it's free Android app, the PHRM26 comes out very far on the low side of that comparison.

title: Great, After Repairs
text:
The bike arrived via UPS in a carton that looked as if it had been through an aerial bombardment. At his suggestion, we went over it with the UPS driver and took pictures, but it looked as if the contents had somehow survived unscathed. We were wrong. After assembly (about 45 minutes) my son sat on the bike and THE PEDALS WERE FROZEN IN PLACE.

We called the Nautilus help line. After a short wait (perhaps 2 minute), we connected with a helpful worker who transferred us to the right tech department (and gave us a direct number in case we were disconnected (YES!). In short order the problem was diagnosed and a tool shipped to us. It arrived 4 days later. We were then able to complete the repair (the coupling controlling the resistance force had slipped from its mounting during shipping).

SINCE THEN - All is well. The bike is very quiet, easily adjusted to different riders and has all the bells and whistles that could be asked for in a sub $1000 machine. It was a bit more expensive than some of its competition, but not withstanding our problem, the build quality is first rate. Welding, hardware, electronics assembly, and even upholstery all seem well done, often with fasteners that seem larger than might be thought neccessary.

Our problem was a consequence of mishandling. Was it the fault of the manufacturer, Amazon or UPS? I don't think we can tell. But it makes us much less likely to order large box items from Amazon.

But, luckily the second tone sounds more like a whistle. I like that there's the option.

There are two controls, a switch to choose between off, tone 1 or tone 2. Also, a button to activate the whistle. So, if it's in the off position, then it won't accidentally go off in your bag or suitcase. It takes four round batteries, type CR2032. Those are really easy to get, and they last a long time in this whistle. It could be used for self defense, as well as coaching, because like I said, it's super loud. Or, it's good for anything where you need a blindingly loud noise. It's really easy to hold, and it's pretty discreet so you can conceal it easily in a pocket or purse. The cord you can hang around your neck is pretty high quality, too.

text:

title: A must have for beginners and for experts
text:
I love this amazing balance board. I've tried out quite a few balance boards, and this one is the absolute best of this style. The thing that I like most about it is that it's very comfortable to use when I just have my bare feet. I mostly use it with shoes, but I really like that I have the option of using it with just bare feet.

The whole surface has a grip coating. It's kind of like what they have on skateboards, but like I said, this is much more comfortable to stand on with your bare feet. If you're super uncoordinated like me, then you might be wondering if you should wait until you're stronger to start working on your balance. But, I totally recommend this to be one the first pieces of fitness equipment that you get. The biggest reason is that it's pretty easy to balance on, and when you're balancing then you generally aren't locking your knees, which is the biggest reason why beginners get injured.

The other thing that I really like about this is that the bottom is smooth. This might not seem like a very important feature, but with this style of balance board, it actually is, because all of your weight gets concentrated into a very tiny area on the floor. If the bottoms of these aren't smooth, they will indent even the hardest of floors. So, because it has a smooth bottom, then it makes it perfect to use on almost any surface. True, it does slip just a tiny bit, over a grip surface, but I don't mind a little slipping because it's supposed to be teaching me balance.

The construction of this is great. It's about seven layers of board, stuck together. The bottom is an extremely firmly secured piece of very sturdy plastic. Overall, this is an awesome balance board. It's awesome for beginners like me, but if you're already a fitness expert and in awesome shape, then I really think you'll like it too.

I really like how this device encourages great posture and discourages hyper-extension of joints. Push-ups would be a nearly perfect exercise if people didn't hyper extend their joints or over strain their weak parts when doing them. This device fixes everything by using your body weight to give you exercises that you can actually do.

This has helped me a ton with my upper body strength. It works, and I definitely recommend it.

Now, for the negatives.

The tension bands are a joke. Unless you either cut them apart or use all 65 lbs of them, they'll make a horrible snapping noise. You'll end up just throwing these away.

This won't last forever. It's not the sturdiest construction, and the design puts some weird strains on some of the joints, so it's only a matter of time before this falls apart. But you should get about a year of good use out of it, and by that time you'll be doing push-ups on your own.

The legs/feet of this should have been about twice as long, to make this sturdier. As it is, the only balanced position is with the seat placed on my upper stomach. If they were longer, then I could pick where I wanted to place my body on this.

And dismounting takes a lot of practice, and the fabric part peals off the first day you use it.

But overall, I'd heartily recommend it, especially if you've always dreamed of being able to do a lot of push-ups. No matter what your fitness level, this will definitely push you to the next level with push-ups.

text:
Best towable we have EVER found!! This thing is super stable which is a plus for kids who are new to tubing, or who have been scared off by other tubes. The wings keep it from tipping, and also make for a very gentle landing if you need to fall off. Just roll off a wing. For those that say it is unstable, that is only really for adult riders, and you need to get your butt in the right position. Experiment. For me it is 3/4 of the way back. Lighter riders don’t seem to have that issue.
My FAVORITE part: Jumping in and out of the wake! This is what makes this tube so great! I am not strong or athletic, you just have to know the trick and COMMIT! While still straddling the middle, put ALL of your weight on one wing and pull the other wing completely off the water. If you do this slowly, you will mainly just steer within the wake. I usually do this as a warm up to make sure I feel stable. Then do it quickly!! Commit! You may need to do it back and forth quickly within the wake, but then you WILL jump it! To get back in, you need to go even quicker and COMMIT!
For those who say it splashed water, again, you are probably too far forward. Back up a bit. For those that are concerned it will hurt your legs, try this. Try sitting back on your haunches on something soft, mimicking the position you would be in on the tube. If it stresses your knees too much, it might not work for you. If not, get it! You will be fine.
It is technically a one person tube, but 2 kids, or 1 adult and 1 kid can ride on it together. I would not recommend towing an adult and child together frequently as I can see how it would stress the seems, but to help a child overcome their fear, or teach them how to jump the wake, go for it.
Durability: I weigh 200 pounds and ride it just as much, if not more, than my kids. We go boating at least 4-6 times per month in the summer, and have used it for 3 seasons now. I am hoping it is still awesome when I pull it out for this summer! Regardless, it was definitely worth the money. I plan on buying a couple more for when the one does break. I love it that much!
If you have questions about how to do something, ask. I will answer if I see the question. The only thing I haven’t figured out is barrel roles.

I had purchased this product as it was one of the only ones which offered a "family account" and I have 2 children so I did not want to have to install the same app twice. We bought this item as a test run to see if our kids would enjoy using a smartwatch enough to justify investing in decent ones. I would not recommend this item if you intend to use it long-term - save yourself the money and buy a better quality device.

title: Best blade covers on the market
text:
The Edge-Mag blade protectors are perfectly designed, protecting your knife edge and knife roll from damage. The magnets clamp down tightly on the blade, preventing it from slipping out even with rough handling. The cover can be fully opened up to clean and dry it, preventing it from harboring bacteria, grease, or water. The covers are also adaptable to a wide variety of blade, bolster, and handle shapes, and can be cut down to size with a pair of scissors. The taper at the rear ensures they fit Forschner knives. Finally, they are thin enough to not cause problems when fitting a lot of knifes into a roll.

All of these give the Edge-Mag covers a serious advantages over cheap slip-in plastic guards and BladeSafe style locking covers. If you are professional cook or chef, you owe it to your knives and knife bag to buy these covers, so both will last.

title: Great Choice for Heart Rate and Sleep Monitoring
text:
I wanted this specifically for its heart rate monitor and sleep monitor--something I can basically wear all the time. I specifically did not want a watch, because I wear a watch on my other arm. So this is just right for that. It's a tad bigger than it ideally could be. I hope future generations will slim down and maybe be more flexible and/or add more interesting sensors.

The sleep monitor seems to work okay. I previously had a Microsoft Band 2, and I feel it may have been better at that.

Since I don't use it as a watch, I like the option to turn off the feature to show time when lifting it up. So it stays black unless I really want it to show me something.

It lets you set like 7 alarms, which can repeat, and I use them to remind myself to drink water. So that's a nice plus.

It does seem a little slow to sync. Specifically, I often want to set a silent alarm right before bed, and it takes like a minute to sync. Then I set the alarm, and it takes several seconds to sync that. Then I can finally turn it on, and wait a few seconds to sync that. Pretty cumbersome. The Microsoft Band let you set it quickly on the Band, so it's much better in that way. (But my Band broke during normal use, and I went through a LOT of trouble to get Microsoft to replace it. A lot. Very bad customer service, so I can't recommend it.)

The battery life is good on this, but it's not great. That said, it's much easier to charge than the Blaze, which I also tried. I basically just charge it while I'm in the shower (a trick I learned for the Band), and that's more than enough. I have to say, I have almost gotten in the shower with it a few times. It is easy to forget you have it on!

So I think it's probably the best continuous HR and sleep monitor option that is specifically not trying to pretend to double as a smart watch.

title: 30 day sleeper. slept better then my old spring mattress
text:
I used this XXL cot for 30 days straight and had little issues with it. 5'10" & 240lbs. Being on the shorter side I could not swing my legs out of bed in the morning and easily reach the ground while still seated on the fabric portion. Being mindful of that if you do have to briefly sit on the edge of the frame aim for the center point, it's the strongest. Sitting cross-legged in fabric sections while reading or watching movies did not feel uncomfortable at all.
If you are a dedicated back sleeper you could use it as is without padding if you had to. Side sleepers might want some padding, I found even a 1/4" went a long way. However, I am looking in to a camping pad for the next excursion.
No matter the cot the fabric will stretch with prolonged use, so don't be surprised that there is more slack after a couple of days then when you started. Sag was minimal after 30 days of use and I didn't feel it affected my comfort level at all.
I wanted a sheet to give me a barrier between the rough textured padding I used and my skin and my biggest issue was keeping it from bunching up in the cot thru the night. If you go this route I would suggest trying a drawstring sheet. If using blankets for top cover go Full size or bigger. The added fabric drapes and helps form a seal to keep out cold air.
Still more comfortable than my aged spring mattress, and after going back to my real bed I am now rethinking having put the cot away...
