The machine itself is nice and sturdy - a decent quality once put together. The pulley/pulldown machine attachment is a good addition but it's not as smooth as it could be. It still is effective and works well. The squat rack portion is solid. the most weight I've put on it is only about 170lbs, but I'm sure it can handle more. Adjusting the rack is quick and easy. I can do squats, Romanian deadlifts, lat pull-downs, chin-ups and more all with this one machine. I also attach my TRX to the pull-up bar and do some exercises with that as well. The addition of the lat pull-down attachment adds stability to this, but being able to store weights on the back is also a plus and keeps the gym organized.

Oh, and you can use standard or olympic size weights with this. We have both since our home gym has been built slowly over time and have acquired various pieces.

Bottom line - excellent value, decent quality, and great for small spaces and home gyms.

title: perfect for short hikes!
text:
I got this for short hikes when I need to bring water and a few items but not deal with the backpack. It works great! I can fit my iphone, ID, and keys in the pouch along with a powerbar or energy gel pack. Note, though, that I have an iPhone SE so it's not huge - larger ones may not fit too well. There's a zipper pouch with a pocket inside and a thin outer pocket with a velcro closure. The velcro is pretty strong, but if you need easy access to an energy bar or gel, you could put it in there. Personally I use that one for any garbage (gel/bar wrappers) to toss out properly when I get back home. (also good to have a little T.P. and ziplock baggie along for bathroom emergencies - put the used T.P. in the ziplock and dispose properly when you get home - leave no trace! :) )

The 2- 10oz water bottles are good and easy to access. I like that the holders they go in have elastic to keep them snug and in place. I'm not sure how these would do for running as I've only used this for hiking so far. But I don't think they'd fall out while running - at least not at the pace I would go! The belt it comfortable and easy to adjust. I can size it to fit me (I'm a women's size 2) or my hubby (32" waist) quite easily.

There are those extra elastic loop things on the belt where you can clip things to it, like maybe a hat or - I don't know what. Have not used them, but could come in handy some day.

title: love the design
text: I love the design of this. However this towel isn't exactly what I had hoped for. I wanted to use for backpacking but it is not as lightweight as it seems. It is definitely compact, though so fits well in the backpack. however my regular towel is lighter. this one is dense, which is great for a beach towel. It is also a good size and soft. So for its intended purpose, a beach towel, this is great. I haven't taken it to the beach so can't say that it repels sand, but its smoothness would make it easy to brush the sand off of it.

title: I want to love it...
text:
I have an Osprey Sirrus 36 backpack that I bought at a local retailer a few years ago. I got this Sirrus 24 hoping the smaller version will be great for shorter day hikes that we often go on. it is good, but I'm having trouble getting it to fit me well.

What's good: This pack overall has an excellent amount of space for day hikes. the waist pockets are plenty roomy to hold things you need at your finger tips - keys, lip balm, small snacks (Gu, powerbar, etc). There is an internal pocket to hold a water bladder and a hole for the straw. It does NOT come with a water bladder. I use the bladder and straw tube that came with my other Osprey Sirrus 36 pack and that works great. The side pockets are deep, much deeper than on the other pack so they hold my hiking hat easily without worry of it falling out.

What's not so good: Really the only problem I have with this pack, as mentioned previously, is trying to get the right fit. I was thrilled with all the adjustments you can make to this pack to get it properly fitted, but so far I have not found that "sweet spot" where it fits comfortably. I've worn it on 4 hikes so far - from 7 to 14 mile day hikes on mountainous terrain. It has been good, just not as great a fit as the Sirrus 36. It could be that I'm just used to the way my old pack fits so I'll keep using this one intermittently to get used to it.

The fit: the back straps have a really neat feature where you can adjust the straps for a longer or shorter torso - I am only 5'2" tall and am short-waisted. So I've tried it on the shortest and places in between but it still hasn't felt perfect. I may just need to go into a local outfitter and have it professional fit to me so that I will have the correct fit.

bottom line - this is a really nice backpack. It is definitely high quality and holds plenty of stuff for long day hikes.

title: durable and comfortable - nice size!
text: Got this large mat to use in our home gym, which is in the garage. We had previously pieced together several different pads and hubby an I would use the area for warm-ups, stretching, and floor exercises like planks and pushups. This has been an excellent replacement for multiple mats! It's perfect size for the floor area we have.  We don't use it at the same time, as it's not quite that big. It's thick and the material is a sturdy memory-foam style that goes back into its original shape after you use it.  great addition to the gym!

title: I like it!
text:
I have tried so many different helmets for mountain biking. Most of them fit awkwardly and some end up giving me a headache due to the awkward fit. This helmet, though, i think I finally found one that fits me! It's comfortable and lightweight. And, the holes in the back are just right so that I can pull my ponytail (hair) through one with little effort. I can't believe how some helmets there is no way to do this. I can't stand having my hair down around my neck when riding - sweaty and uncomfortable! obviously this helmet and all the others are not designed to accommodate long hair, but the design of this one luckily works out pretty well for that.

oh, and I really like the flat red color, a nice change from the blacks and grays I usually end up with.

title: helpful!
text: Hubby laughed at me when I got this - thought it was just too "gimicky" but boy does it come in handy! Who knew such a simple thing would make life easier in the gym? No more lifting the bar with one hand while I awkwardly try to put a large weight plate on the end. simple, easy, and helpful addition to our home gym!

title: lightweight, easy to put on, and perfect for short hikes
text: This vest is lightweight, easy to put on, and perfect for short hikes, especially if I have my dogs with me.  I can put my keys, phone, chapstick, and tissues in the vest, place a collapsible water bowl in the back pocket and we are ready to go.  I use a small 2 liter hydration bladder that fits fine in the back bladder pocket.  The collapsible water bottle that came with the vest leaked around the lid when ever squeezed or if the bottle was full and moving too fast.  I tried putting the lid on several different times, yet it always leaked.  Therefor one star deducted for that.

title: Just what I needed
text: Large opening makes this easy to fill, and add ice for those hot summer days.  The neoprene covered drinking tube keeps the water cool.  Bite valve works well.  The on/off is a simple push/pull of the bite valve.  The dust cover for the mouth piece is a good feature for keeping it clean when removing your pack and setting it on the ground.  The drinking hose easily attaches and detaches from the bladder and so far is seated securely with no leaks.  And it fits great in my hydration vest.

title: Does what it is intended for.
text: Does the job.  Brushes are perfect to reach the little nooks and crannies that can be difficult to clean and the long brush for the drinking tube slides smoothly inside the tube for thorough cleaning.  The hanging bracket was a little awkward with my bladder and wouldn’t fit in per the instructions, however I made it work and the bladder dried out well.  Mesh storage sack keeps everything dry, together and easy to find when you need it.

title: perfect for camping or home storage
text: These bins are perfect for a sink when camping.  One to wash, one to rinse.  They pop up then collapse back down easily.  The hard plastic bottom makes them sturdy on any flat surface.  They also make great little bins for assorted pet toys, as you can see from my attached photos. I may have to get another set for camping, now, though!

title: Very easy to install, instructions were decent.
text: The seat is cushy and soft and comfortable enough for my recreational use.  The shape fits well and the air flow design helps with sweating and overheating.  It does come with a rain cover that I hope to not have to use, since I live in the arid southwest, but it’s nice to have if needed.

title: nice quality
text: Got myself a new lat-pulldown machine but unfortunately it came with a few attachments so I picked this up to go with it. These are well made and sturdy. There's a nice variety in the pack, too. I got the one with the tricep rope, double D handle, v-shaped bar, and straight pulldown bar. These attachments are a perfect compliment to what I got with my machine.

title: works okay but...
text:
Be prepared to do some Internet searching for instructions. Instructions were completely useless, unless you had an hour to spare just to be frustrated. The instruction pictures were all black and white and the parts you are putting together are black. Impossible to see the details needed to mount the simple mechanism. I finally went online to find similar products that had videos on how to put this together. Once I had that, the installation took less than 15 minutes.

Overall the stand works well and I can get a nice workout with it. When increasing tension though, I do find the movement of the tire sometimes jerky and the texture of the tension wheel against my bike tire does pull off a small amount of rubber: loosening the pressure against the tire helped with that, but then the resistance is not quite as strong. The adjustment dial requires more than a few clicks to change the tension resistance, but overall it works for me as I only want a good workout and won't be using this for any serious training. Once set up on the stand, my bike feels stable and secure. It meets my needs for a good in home cardio workout.

title: just what I was looking for!
text:
I have several weight benches by other brands and one Finer Form sit up bench. The sit up bench is great- decent quality and both hubby and I use it in our workouts. What I have been missing is a way to do back extensions - this bench covers that! it has just about everything I need in a bench.

Assembly is pretty simple but does take some time. Once together it is a solid bench - not quite commercial grade but very close, just like the sit up bench they make. Really a good, versatile bench and great addition to our home gym!

title: beyond expectations
text:
This is a beautiful little compass/sundial. It's solid and well made. the added sundial is a nice touch. All the markings/engravings are well done although I struggle to actually read the Roman numerals on the outer sundial, I know what they are by location. It's me, not the product, because sundial and Roman numerals just go together.

I can't get over how much I like this thing. It would make an absolutely wonderful gift for anyone into mapping, surveying, hiking, etc.

title: A bit thick
text: I like the feel of the neoprene cover on this dumbbell, but the handle is a bit thick for me. I got a 20# dumbbell and when I hold it my grip doesn't quite fit all around the bar. I wish it was a bit thinner. otherwise it's a quality dumbbell. I didn't do a scientific measurement of the actual weight, but it certainly feels like 20# to me.

title: nice, wide brim
text:
this is a nice hat. I like the fact that it has such a wide brim - perfect for gardening! The ponytail feature is probably my favorite part and works great. It's nice that the hat is adjustable. The material is thin and it fits big, but being able to adjust it makes it work out fine. I've used this for hiking a few times, too. The brim is larger than my regular hiking hat. I like that you can snap up the sides if needed - makes it sort of a "cowboy hat" look.

It doesn't do well holding its shape though - not sure anything really can, but when I have it shoved in my backpack it's a bit deformed when I need to pull it out and doesn't go back to its usual shape too easily, though it is often good enough. I do like that I was able to get it in a sort of "neutral" color (gray) - bright colors may be fun for gardening but when I'm hiking I prefer neutrals.

title: not accurate
text:
okay, I admit that I'm not the best jump-roper but this should at least be close to counting the number of jumps I do. It doesn't. It always undercounts and has only come in close to what I jumped one time. This was using the rope and not the cordless version. If it cant count the number of jumps correctly I wouldn't trust that it can count calories burned either.

Let's talk about the cordless version. It's a little difficult to get the hang of using that. I originally thought it would be pretty simple to do, but it's hard to get the rhythm going (for me anyway). I'm not sure but in addition to me not quite able to master the technique of a cordless jump rope, the weighted balls may need more weight. They seem really light to me and why I cant quite get them to spin correctly.

The few good things about this are that the handles are comfortable to hold and it is pretty simple to switch between corded and cordless. The cord holds well in the handle. I am able to easily adjust the length of the rope or switch out to cordless jumping. I just have to count the jumps manually or go by timed jumping instead. oh, it also comes with a spare battery and a small screwdriver to open the battery compartment when its time to switch out.

title: good quality
text: This is a nice addition to our home gym. I was tired of changing out the weight plates on our adjustable dumbbells so having this lets me keep working with little pause between exercises. I use the 35lber for one arm rows which works great. Hubby uses it for tricep extensions mostly. I only got one and didn't actually measure it to make sure it's 35lbs, but it's close enough for us. The "ergonomic" handle is easy to grip and hang on to. I like the hexagon shape of the ends to keep the weight from rolling around since we keep them on the floor rather than in a rack. This seems like the same quality that I've used in commercial gyms.

title: good weight
text: I got the 40lb dumbbell weight to use for goblet squats and hubby uses it for one arm rows and tricep extensions. It does the job well. I haven't actually checked the weight to make sure it is exactly 40lbs, but it seems close enough to me! A good addition to our home gym.

title: durable, heavy duty
text: This is a nice variety pack of durable, heavy duty carabiners. It comes with 3 screw-lock and 3 clip-lock carabiners. They are not huge, but work well for a variety of different things. We keep these in our camper for use on camping trips. they come in handy for a variety of things. I did keep one at the house and use that to hang one of my hummingbird feeders, which works out great.

title: just what I needed
text: This review is for the "puzzle piece" style of the exercise mat. These are great for a home gym. I needed to add a bit of padding under our power rack for when I do sets with pushups. these are the just the ticket! They are easy to put together and being in pieces allows for different configurations. this came in handy as I don't need it as wide under the machine as the outside part. They work great and are easy to sweep off or wipe down as needed. Great for a home gym, especially garage gyms!

title: heavy duty
text: This is a package of 2 heavy duty carabiners. They are heavy duty, a decent size, and the screw-lock works fine. I got these to have on hand for camping trips but ended up using one to hang a bird feeder that one of our local squirrels (or maybe it's a racoon??) keeps knocking off its hook. The carabiner does the trick, that's for sure!

title: thick cotton material, fits true to size
text:
First of all these are not hiking shorts and I'm not sure I'd call them real cargo shorts either. The pockets are mostly a joke. I assume they are just for show and not for actual use. The front and side pockets are small and the back pockets are faux - as in non-existent, just a flap to pretend there is a pocket there. Kind of a bummer to me as I was hoping to use these for hiking but now they will just be some everyday wear shorts.

The fit is pretty much as expected. I got a small and it fit fine. I'm a size 2 and the small fit good, not too tight. It is a high-waisted short, so if you prefer a mid-rise, they are not for you. Personally I prefer the mid-rise, but these are not that bad and comfortable enough for casual wear. The material is thick, so they are probably not going to be a pair of go-to shorts in the hot southern Arizona summers here. They wash up fine and I have not experienced any shrinkage that I can tell - I've washed/worn them 2 or 3 times so far (at the time of this review).

title: Easy to use but not high quality photos
text:
[[VIDEOID:2e4398db1ad197e9850764c065cdc483]] This is a decent trail camera. The menu interface is simple enough to use with easy to follow instructions in the manual. I had no problem getting it set up. I was able to capture several of the critters that visit our backyard pond, both on photo and video. I set it for the highest resolution possible but the images are not very good. Sure they are 4608x2592 pixels but there is so much JPG artifacting that its really not very useful. I have other trail cams that produce much sharper/clearer images. I included a 100% crop of one of the javelina (collared peccary) photos along with the fullsize version for review. Along with a night photo and a night video (of our fox!)

I dont expect very high quality from night shots so these are what I expected for that. The videos are good and, again, the night ones are good. We finally got a decent video of our resident fox, too! (video included, if it uploads okay!)

Overall I'd say if you're looking for some quick images to capture wildlife this will do the trick. It's simple to use and produces "good enough" photos and videos. But if you want clearer, sharper images, you will be disappointed with this camera.

Oh, the largest memory card (SD) it will take is 32MB. We get a lot of critters at the pond - this was still taking photos/videos after 10 days out there even at the highest resoluation settings for both video and photo.

title: Fit fine, thin
text: These are nice headbands/ear warmers, although they are pretty thin. They work well under a hat or or light winter days but in real cold, windy conditions, they are a bit thin, but the material is soft. I do like the light colors (got the light green and gray). They do fit well and are not too tight, but stay on. I've worn them on a few hikes. They are thin enough that I can stash them in my pocket to have on hand if the wind picks up or sudden temperature drop.

title: best camping soap!
text:
We use CampSuds exclusively when camping! We always have some in our camper. I use it for washing dishes, washing hands, and even bathing! It works great - doesn't leave a residue and everything comes clean. I even use it to wash my hair.

It's concentrated so you only need a small amount to get a good lather and clean. One small bottle will last quite awhile as you only need to use a little bit. I especially like that it is biodegradable and environmentally friendly. Seriously, don't go camping without CampSuds!

title: Love this ab-roller
text:
This is our second ab-roller of this style. I love the wide wheel and ergonomic handles. The handles especially because they are easy to grip and help keep me steady when rolling back and forth. Out of the box, it is really simple to put together, just make sure you put the handles on the correct way.

The inner spring helps to get a full range of motion and back into to the staring position. It does not seem as tight of a spring as the other brand of ab roller we have that is similar to this, but then I think our other one is on its last legs as it sometimes stops before I get all the way extended. It rolls smoothly. Hubby will do 100 in one set with no problems from the roller. Me, I do about 25 at a time, then rest for a minute before doing more. I can definitely feel the workout the next day.

Honestly have not used the little pads that come with it because I have a thicker pad that I prefer. Still, this is my go-to for ab rolling and it definitely works the abs!

title: These are the best lids!
text:
Love our Yeti tumblers! we use them every day. The lids are getting a bit worn so I ordered these extras to have on hand. The magnetic slider is genius! it makes it super-easy to clean these and slides open/shut with ease.
Also I didn't realize how the outer seal on the lids that came with our cups has worn until we got these new lids. The new ones seal really tight and snug! I must say, though, that the old ones still stay sealed well. We've had them for a few years now and with practically daily use they have lasted quite well. That certainly speaks to lasting quality!

title: love the colors!
text:
These are almost exactly what I was looking for and the colors are great. i wear them under my hiking hat to keep the sweat from dripping into my eyes and they work well for that. I was hoping they'd be a little bit wider but these are pretty close. They add a nice touch of color to my usual black and earth-tone hiking clothes. They're also great for bad hair days - just slap on a headband and I'm good to go!

They are soft and wash up great. Just throw them in the laundry with my other workout clothes.

title: keeps the bugs away
text:
I got this to use on hikes when the bugs get just a little bit too much to handle. The hat is a one-size fits all sort of thing but is a little bit loose for me and I dont have that small of a head. My usual hiking hat is sized a small/medium.

Still, this hat has kept me from going insane with the bugs flying in my face and buzzing around my ears while I'm trying to climb up a mountain trail! The netting is thick enough to get the bugs out but thin enough so that I still get a breeze through it and don't sweat to death. It also helps shade from the sun, which is handy. I can easily pull it down or roll it back up on the hat when the bugs are gone.

The brim on the hat is not very easy to mold/fold, but hey, it keeps the netting on and away from my face. This hat is now a permanent part of my hiking gear and I keep it in an external side pocket of my pack so I have ready access as I hike.

title: excellent coverage of public lands!
text:
Hubby and I do a lot of hiking and "at large" camping so knowing where public lands are is a must. The ONX: hunting maps is perfect for this! We aren't hunters, but this is really good for our needs. It works easily with the Garmin GPSMap 64st - just put it in the card reader slot turn on the layers. the only thing is I wish there was a way to toggle the labeling on/off. The private land owner names is a wonderful feature, but the labels often clutter up the small screen on the Garmin, making it difficult to read the map.

We've also signed up for access to the onxmaps website and that makes it easy to plan our routes ahead of time using a larger device (computer monitor) . The web map has added features that let you add additional layers and turn layers on and off. You still cannot turn the labels off on the webmap though, either.

The ONX Hunt maps have some of the best coverage I've seen with regard to land ownership. This makes it excellent for hunters and people like us who may not hunt but do enjoy exploring the great outdoors in remote places.

title: great addition to our home gym
text:
This is a good, lightweight sit-up bench for a home gym. It took hubby and I about 25 minutes to assemble it. There were a few things that were annoying when putting together - some of the bolt openings were a bit small and we had to use a mallet to get one of the bolts into the hole. One of the plastic end caps was broken - not sure if that happened during shipping or just came that way from the factory. Not that big of a deal, it is mostly aesthetics anyway. Oh, and I thought there were 2 bent washers -- and, well, there are 2 bent washers, but they are actually curved to fit on the handle attachment part that has a curved surface. So don't freak out when you see that, just be sure to use them on the correct spot.

The bench itself is much more lightweight than I anticipated but that does make it easier to move around since we haven't quite decided the best dedicated spot for it in our home gym. This could be an issue for larger people. Hubby and I aren't big people so this bench size works fine for us - I am 5'2", 120lbs, hubby is 5'9" 155lbs.

I love the red color - adds a nice splash of color to our mostly black gym equipment. It felt like it was leaning a bit toward one side when we first tried it out, but a little adjustment on the feet and it seems to be fine now. That is one nice feature - a dial to make adjustments simple. Speaking of adjustments - to change the height and the feet rollers is pretty simple - it uses the typical pull out knob and adjust. Overall it's a great addition to our gym and adds an additional option for ab workouts.

title: works fine so far
text: Got this to replace my band that has cracked with age and wear. The quality so far seems to be just fine. I use this about once a  week when doing chin-ups to help me out a bit since my upper body strength is not so good. I go the purple band based on the chart - i can do about 3-5 unassisted chin-ups and I'm 120lbs. With the band I can do several sets of 10.

title: light works fine, helmet is okay
text: This helmet is okay. the light works fine with it's 3 settings - flashing, slow pulse, and constant on.  It charges easily with a USB cable.  The visor is okay, but the vent holes seem to be large so that the visor doesn't shield the sun all that well for me. The fit is okay. You have to turn the plastic knob in the back to tighten and loosen it. I have worn it just a few times now and can't seem to get a comfortable fit with this. It's okay, but just not perfect for me.  Perhaps I just need to get used to it.

title: Better than the lanyards I was using
text: This is a nice clothesline set for camping. We mainly use it to hang up our sweaty/stinky exercise clothes after a workout (hiking, biking, running) when we are out camping. Previously I was using some old lanyards and attaching those to our camper to hang the clothes up to dry.  This is much more convenient and longer so I'm able to hang it better. It has a really nice variety of hooks/caribeaners but they are all very lightweight so I have some pause in hanging up anything very heavy. Still for what I need/use this set for it is perfect.

title: Larger than expected, works well
text:
I got this hydro ball to add a little variety to my strength training routine. It was fairly simply to fill up with water, although I did make a bit of a mess filling it in my large kitchen sink. Once filled, I weighed it and it was 25lbs. Granted, I didn't do a precise measurement - just stood on the bathroom scale with it and subtracted my weight from that and it came to 25lbs. The weird thing is there is no "fill line" that I found on it - the instructions indicate that you can put different amounts of water to have different weights (up to 25lbs for the one I got). But there are no markings on where to fill it for these different weights.

I have used this a few times now in my workouts. Did some goblet squats and some ab-twisters. The Surge Ball is easy to hold on to, although it takes a little getting used to as due to its size. I'm not a big person so this may not be an issue for most folks. (5'2", 120lbs). It's too big for me to do kettle-bell swings as it hits the floor, but I'm still playing around with how to add in workouts using it.

I like using it thus far. It does suggest you hang it to keep it from getting distorted, but when I hung it from a handle, the handle got a little distorted. Ha ha! Time will tell how it will hold up.

title: Lucky socks!
text: Got these for my son, the raving Blues Fan!  Of course he loves anything with his favorite teams' logo on it so these were a hit. They are thick and quality made, too. Socks are always a great gift for someone who you're not sure what to get for them - I didn't want to give him just cash for a gift, so added these to give him a little extra gift to open at Christmas.

title: nice bike helmet
text: have to admit I was a bit skeptical of this when I first saw the listing.  I measured my head to make sure I ordered the correct size and found that I was in between sizes! Honestly it's very difficult to measure that precisely!  I took a chance and went to the small/medium.  it fits pretty much prefect. I was worried that it was too small but after putting it on and taking it for a short ride, it seems to be made for me!  I guess time may tell a different story (like after a 5-hour ride!) but for now I like it.  This appears to be a good quality helmet with such a low price point that you can't go wrong.

title: a bit overrated but works for what I want it for
text:
So the red band, which I got, is marketed as "heavy" resistance. I use these types of bands for pullup assistance because my upper body strength is not as good as I'd like. I'm a 54 year old woman and I weight lift (strength train) about 3 times a week - sometimes 4. I have used another brand that was 1.1/8" wide and offers a tension of 40-80lbs. This red band, that is 1" wide is probably more like 20 to 40 lbs tension. It works great for me because I've "graduate' from the stronger band and need one with less tension so that I am working harder but still have a little bit of help.

The band does come with a guide that provides a few exercises if you need that. But, as previously mentioned, I use these bands only for pull-up/chin-up assistance. This one seems decent enough. If you're a beginner, the exercises provided could be helpful and would work great when traveling and you don't have access to a gym.

title: Love this hat!
text:
This hat is so much fun. It's warm and waterproof and that fun aviator style (a more styled version of the traditional ushanka-Russian hat) that is pretty much timeless. Great for snowshoeing, cross-country skiing, or surviving icy winter storms.

It is well made and the lining is thick and warm. Would make a great gift, too.

title: Great gym alternative when traveling
text:
I got these for use when we are camping, which we do a lot. We sometimes spend a week or more overlanding (or dispersed camping) and even though we do a lot of hiking and mountain biking, we do miss the gym. Having this set helps to get our strength training exercises in when we do not have access to a gym.

this set is very well made with quality hooks and attachments. I like how each one is marked with its resistance level and they can be combined to increase the resistance as needed. I am a little worried that the laytex won't last as long in the heat of our camper (we live in the dry southwest US) but I guess time will tell. They do carry a great warranty but really at this price as long as the set lasts me a few years, I have no complaints! My last set was not this good of quality and after 5 years one of the handles snapped off during use. I expect this set to last at least that long as the quality seems far superior.

title: I want to like these but
text:
Until I got these I had been wrapping a towel around my bar when I do squats. the towel works okay, but I then I got these pads. At first I loved the added padding! but after a few sets of squats, the pad became too much. It's just a bit too thick for me. Maybe because I'm small - I dont know (5'2" 120lb woman). I have been using one of these pads for my first set then switch back to the towel for the remainder.

The pad is thick (slightly too thick for me) so it is comfortable (at first) and easily attaches to the bar. Like I mentioned, though, after a few sets my neck starts to get a little sore and having the bulky pad becomes awkward. I continue to try using it in case I just need to get used to it, but after a few weeks, I still find myself going back to the towel. It's odd, too, because for the first set it always feels great! But then it goes downhill on subsequent sets. Just wish it was a bit thinner.

title: works with standard and olympic plates!
text:
I got this for our olympic plates but when I realized it also works for standard size plates I decided it use it more for those. We have slowly built or gym over the years and thus have acquired a variety of weight plates and bars. We were just laying the plates on the floor or storing those that would fit on the small pegs of our portable rack stands on there. It started to get a little messy so this weight tree has helped to keep us a little better organized.

Assembly wasn't too difficult, though it did take about 20 to 30 minutes. the parts seem decent quality and even the plastic that goes over the pegs to make them Olympic size seems heavy duty. Overall I'm pleased with this rack and glad to have it on our home gym.

title: just what I was looking for
text: Good product, easy to put together, and sturdy. We needed something to keep organize the weights in our weight room. This weight stand fits nicely in the corner and now we have a place for our weights other than laying on the floor!  And, not that color coordination is big deal in our gym, but this just happens to match our barbell/squat rack with the red and black.  Anyhow, I'm pleased with this - it is exactly what we needed.

title: super easy to use
text: This is a great little bottle and handy for taking along in my backpack on hikes. I'm not quite sure how to test the filter but so far I've only used it with tap water and the water came out tasting fine, plus I didn't get sick so there's that. :)  I guess if I decide to take this on a long backpacking trip and want to know if the filter is good for filtering pond/stream water then I would invest in a test kit. Still for now I like that it folds down pretty small and holds a decent 20 oz - as much as the gatorade bottles we often carry.

title: Worked well for keeping out weeds and stickers
text:
We don't do a lot of water or snow hiking, but tried these out on a recent hike through some tall grasses with a lot of dry grass and dry weeds with stickers. The gaitors worked well to keep from getting a bazillon little stickers all over my hiking socks and boot laces. That alone makes these things totally worth it! The sizing was good in that it fit over my thick calves. I actually measured my calves to make sure they would fit and was a bit surprised that the large was for me. I didn't think my calves were that big! haha. Still I do a lot of bicycling, mountain climbing, and weight lifting, so I guess large calves are to be expected.

Anyhow these gaitors are pretty good - easily fit over my hiking boots. Perhaps I'll venture out this winter into someplace with snow and try them out there.

title: Good backpack
text: The Camelbak MULE backpack is good for day hikes. the target audience is mostly for bicyclists, I believe, but I got this for a daypack and it works well. If you need more room, I'd definitely recommend trying out the HAWG which is a slightly larger version of this backpack. Still the MULE has the same size hydration bladder (100oz) and you can carry quite a bit of stuff in it. The bladder in the lumbar position is new for me but seems to work just fine.  This is made with the quality I expect from Camelbak. And it is a nice neutral color, too.

title: nice, solid bike rack
text:
This is a nice, solid bike rack. It was pretty simple to put together, took us only about 20 minutes. We have 2 Canondale Lefty (F-29) bikes. His is larger than mine. We had some trouble getting the two bikes to fit on the frame with the center pieces that are different heights because the Lefty bikes have a sort of unique frame, I guess. Still we were able to get them on there okay and prefer how this rack has the center part that holds the bike at the frame while our previous/other bike rack only holds onto the wheels. This seems much more stable.

After getting the bikes on we did have some trouble accessing the lock feature but managed to work out a way to do it. I think with more use we'll get a system worked out. Overall this is a quality rack and well made. I'd definitely recommend it.

title: good utility cord
text: We do a lot of camping and having parachute cord around is always useful.  This is a good, standard paracord and comes with a decent carabiner. You really can't go wrong. We haven't used it a whole lot yet but I like knowing that we have the cord handy in our camping gear when and if needed. The few times we've used us that far it has worked out just fine and it is a good quality.

title: wonderful table!
text:
This is a great little camping table! We use it a lot! it's super simple to put together and stores perfectly in the side bin of our camper. In fact, I'm using it right now while I write this review - out camping, got a strong enough signal to connect to the Internet, a nice breeze, and a beautiful day in the Sonoran Desert. We actually have another table almost identical to this one that we picked up a popular outdoor store, it cost a bit more and instead of the plastic connectors on the side of the table top that are used as pivot points when you fold the table up, it has elastic bands so that you stretch the top to attach it to the base. I kind of like this version better- hard plastic connectors, hook one side into the end poles then snap the other end on. (sorry about the crappy markup text in the pic of the connectors and pivot points - I used the "markup" feature on my smartphone and it is very easy to write text with your finger on that small screen lol!)

We've used this a few times now - both hubby and I can work sit at the table with our computers and get some work done. Nothing like teleworking in the great outdoors!

title: Good utensil set for camping
text:
Got this to use in our new camper. It's a great way to keep everything organized and in one place. The utensils are nothing fancy, but they are functional and decent quality. We've augmented this with a plastic spatula for use on our frying pan with a teflon coating and a wooden spoon. I like that it comes with a small cutting board and sharp knife. The cutting is just the right size for use in our small camper "kitchen." The knife needed to be sharpened, but it seems to work good enough for us.

Everything gets put away neatly at the end of the day, zipped up in the bag, and then placed in one of the camper cupboards for easy traveling. Honestly I never knew how much we needed something like this until we got it!

title: Ab Wheel.  Ab Wheel. Ab Wheel.
text:
seriously, this kit was all about the ab wheel for me. If you don't feel your ab muscles burning the day after an ab wheel workout, you're doing it wrong. This is definitely not easy, but work it the best you can. Some day I hope to be able to get a full extension roll like those young boys do at the gym, but for now I'm taking what I can do with this! It is such a simple piece of equipment but very valuable!

The other items in this kit are useful, but honestly, as other reviewers have pointed out, this is mostly about the wheel. Still, I've found the other items useful. The peanut ball thing was a new one for me, but wow - what a difference for my lower back having that thing to brace against. It is just a small ball that fits at my lower back and is great for doing crunches and Russian twists.

The other great thing about this kit is that it can easily travel with you. The bands come in handy when you do not have access to weights or use them for stretching and warm-up/cool-downs.

Overall great kit and will get plenty of use at our home gym!

title: fun game, nice quality set
text:
I had never heard of this game before, but saw this on Amazon and thought it would be a fun thing to take to our next family reunion. It comes in a very nice bag to store everything in as well as take it to parties and gatherings. The instructions are okay, but they were not perfectly clear to me - I couldn't figure out if only the very first team uses the batons or if they switch back and forth like in horseshoes. So I did some googling and found some instructions that are more detailed. I cannot post the link here, but it was simple enough to find with a search - look for the Rules of Kubb poster. I had no idea that this game is such a big deal - there are tournaments for it even! (of course there are :) ).

The kubbs, stakes, and batons are all very well made and I would imagine will hold up well for some time. We've only played a few practice games with my small family but this summer I expect this will be a hit at our huge family reunion. I can't wait to get everyone together to play! It's pretty much its own game, but if I had to compare it to something I'd say if you like horseshoes, bocce ball, curling, bowling, or shuffle board, you'll like this game. Fun for the whole family!

title: nice quality
text:
I'm not sure why you'd want to buy singles of these plates, but I'm glad they offer them in pairs. I got a pair of 5 lb plates and they are good quality cast iron and fit just fine on our olympic barbell and cable pulldown machine.

These are a great addition to our gym so hubby and I aren't always fighting over the smaller weights as we add weight to our sets with one of us using the barbell and the other using the cable pulldown machine that also uses olympic weight plates. The price is also decent - you can't really go wrong.

title: Nice quality leggings
text: These are a nice quality capri legging for workouts. I usually have to get an extra small in these, but the small fits almost perfectly.  They do ride up in the crotch just a bit on me when I first put them on, but once I get exercising that doesn't seem to be an issue. The high waist band is thick and supportive with a decent-size pocket embedded in the front of the band. The pocket will hold a key, a small ipod/mp3, or an ID card but it is not big enough for one of today's typical smartphones.  The material is thick and soft, perfect for strength training as it allows for plenty of comfortable movement like squats and lunges.

title: nice set of exercise bands
text:
I use these bands for pull-up assist. I have a hard time with pull-ups (let's face it, ladies genetically do not have the same upper body strength that men have), so I use a pull-up assist band. I have one band that I've had for about 5 years now and it's about ready to break so when I saw this set of 4, I knew it would be a great way to transition from band-assisted to unassisted!

These are well made and work great. I''m currently using the green and purple bands (depending on how many reps I need to do). And soon hope to transition to the lower resistance bands as I gain strength. oh, for the record, I'm 120lbs female - in my early 50's and do strength training 3 to 4 times a week. I have no problem with deadlifts and squats, but chin-ups are my weak point.

These bands come with a bag so you can also tuck them away in your suitcase and use them for resistance training when you're traveling and do not have access to a gym. There are tons of options with resistance bands. I'm very happy with this set.

title: lightweight trekking poles
text:
I got these to use with snowshoeing. I don't use trekking poles when hiking in general, but as I'm about to take on snowshoeing, I thought poles may be a good thing to have with that. So I plan to use these exclusively with snowshoeing.

These are good quality and lightweight. They easily expand and come with both a small trekking basket and a larger basket for use on snow (or mud). The grip is thick and comfortable with an adjustable strap for the wrist. I'm 5'2" so these expand just fine for me to get the perfect length.

title: Good quality and super easy to get on/off
text:
This is my first pair of snowshoes. Haven't had a chance yet to try them in the snow but as an avid hiker, I'm jazzed to try these out. The bindings are super easy to get in and out of. The aluminum frame keeps them lightweight. The heel riser I find interesting. I wasn't sure what it was for so checked out some online videos and discovered that is an aid for going uphill - makes it a little less strenuous on the calves, I guess. Since i haven't had a chance to try these out yet, I will have to update my review. They are simple enough to engage, so it will be fun trying them out.

I don't live in snow country so these are going to be part of our winter excursion trip in a few weeks. I'll provide an update after I've gotten them out in the snow!

oh - I got the 8x21 size. I am 120lbs, size 8.5 boot (I always go up a size in boots for toe room). I dont anticipate caring too heavy of a load so I think this size is appropriate for me.

title: Good bench
text:
This is a decent quality weight bench. You will need to assemble it but it's a fairly simple process. You will need an adjustable wrench but other than that it comes with what you need to put it together. A metric socket wrench would probably be faster, though. I did have some trouble getting the longer bench part to go in straight. Not sure what that was about I as removed and reset the screws several times, but once tightened it would go slightly crooked. See the pic with the stand at 20-degrees, you'll see how it is off center due to the whole section being slight askew. Even with that once it was all together, I couldn't really tell the difference and the bench works fine.

The steel parts are great and the rubber feet keep it from sliding around. The red wheels on the back make it easy to move around the gym as needed, too. The pads are comfortable and it is super quick to adjust the angle of the back. the front seat pad has 3 adjustment angles for doing sit ups. We have a variety of CAP products in our home gym and this has been a good addition.

title: Almost exactly what we needed!
text:
This is a simple and easy to assembly bike rack. It works perfect for us.

it took me all of 15 minutes to put together for 3 bikes. I love that you have the option to expand it to 5 bikes if needed. (more on that later). The instructions were easy to follow (I've included a pic).

What's in the box: This comes with everything you need to assemble your frame, even a little hex wrench which is the only tool you need other than your two hands. All the pieces are nicely packed in the box and have plastic over them to protect them from getting scuffed up in the box. Your box should have 2 frame tube ends, 10 frame tubes, 10 wheel arms, 5 wheel arm binders, 20 hex-head screws, and one hex wrench.

Assembly: The bottom bars for the frame pretty much snap together with little push in metal buttons to hold them in place (see pic). The holes for the buttons are nice and oblong so you have room to twist/maneuver them when attaching the wheel arms to get the holes aligned when screwing them in. The only slight issue I had is the hex screw heads. A few of them seemed to easily strip when I was doing the last few turns with the provided hex wrench. I was not even tightening them very tight so there was not a lot of torque. I figured they were probably just cheap screws, but they still did the job fine. The screws you can twist by hand easily once you get the holes aligned correctly then just use the hex wrench to finish up. Once you have the wheel arms attached the wheel arm binders easily attach at the top of the wheel arms but squeezing them together slightly then just slide the binder down next to the frame once it is on. And that's all there is to it!

using the stand: we have 3 bikes - 2 mountain bikes and 1 road bike. I thought I may have to add a spacer to the frame since the mountain bike handle bars will not fit if the two of them are right next to each other in this stand. I did try putting one in backward, with the rear wheel in the stand, but the bike stand arms were too narrow for wheel and derailer to completely fit into the stand. however, my road bike is small enough that it fits just under the mountain bike handle bars. putting that in the middle solved the issue! Now we have all three bikes neatly parked in a corner of the garage rather than leaning against the wall and boxes. yay! And if we happen to acquire more bikes, we can always expand it.

Overall this is a decent, simple bike stand that does what we need.

title: Easy to put up, adds a nice design touch to the room
text:
This was super easy to put up and looks great! I love that you can reposition it as needed. I had one piece stick to itself after I peeled it off the backing which caused me a mild panic. But I was able to get it apart fairly easily (being gentle) and stick it to the wall. In certain light the clear parts between the letters shines a bit, but the photo shoes it more than in real life and it's honestly not that noticeable.

There were directions that came with this, but in every language except English, but seriously I didn't even need them for this. It's that simple.

I like this so much I'm looking to get more other designs for some of the other rooms in my house. What a great way to add design touches to a room!

title: Decent lock, fairly compact, easy to use
text:
This is a decent bike lock. it's small enough to attach to your bike. It's super easy to lock and unlock - just set it to your combination and push the button on top and it comes right apart. Changing the combination is also easy. The company rates this as a medium security (5/10) - it seems heavier duty than that to me, but it is not as substantial as my other 2 locks. It's also not as big as the locks I use for our bikes when they're on the car bike rack (see pic). It's just about 9" long and the opening is 6.5". It also has an attachment bracket to attach it to your bike quite easily. remove it from the bracket with the push of a button and slide it out. simple.

There aren't any instructions on attaching it to your bike, but I think it's pretty simple. I assume the clear plastic things that dropped out of the packaging see those in the pic) are to act as a buffer between the bracket and your bike, but I'm not sure. Maybe they were just part of the packaging? I haven't put it on my bike and not sure I will actually attach it to my bike or not. May just use it for when the bike is on the car bike rack and we're traveling. or if I'm out for along ride I either have panniers or a small camelback backpack that this will easily fit in.

If you need a decent lock that attaches to your bike and doesn't take up a lot of space, this will work nicely.

title: my first medicine ball and I like it!
text:
I've never used a medicine ball in my workouts, but given the opportunity to try one out, I decided it would be a good addition to the home gym. A quick Google and I found a bunch of workouts with a medicine ball. Who knew there were so many great exercises you can do with one of these? I got the 16lb ball, which seems just about right for me. yes, I'm a girl in my 50's but I lift regularly (3x a week) so this weight works well for me.

The AmazonBasics ball seems well made and has a grip and size like a basketball. I haven't done any of the slamming, bouncing, or throwing exercises with this yet, but have used it for core and upper body exercises (lunges, v-ups, etc).

I'm really happy with this new addition to my workouts and may add some other weights as well since the pricing is very reasonable for this!

title: nice and lightweight. Pouch doesn't hold much, as you might expect.
text:
This really is a nice, lightweight belt. However, look pretty much all belts I've tried, this one rides up while I run. with the water bottles full in the back of me, they pull down the back and front starts to ride up. I must also add that I run on rocky, rough terrain not smooth streets or sidewalks, so any belt gets jostled around a lot during my run. Having something in the front pouch other than some emergency toilet paper, though, may help keep things weighted down a bit more. Just not sure what I'd put in there other than maybe a Gu pack and my house key. an iPhone will not fit in the pouch. I guess the main problem is that I like to have the belt low riding on my hips, but it, of course, wants to slide up to my waist. During my first run with this belt I just gave in and wore it high at the waist. That ended up not being too bad and was not uncomfortable at all.

I do like this belt, though. The bottles snap in and out easily and I've not had any issue with leaking, so far, like I do with my Nathan brand belt. This is the Nathan belt I have: [[ASIN:B000RJHU98 Nathan Speed 2 Waist Pack with Two 10-Ounce Nutrition Flasks (Grey, Large)]]. This FuelBelt also does adjust nicely with the velcro straps and can fit large to small. I have a 27" waist and 35" hips and can tighten this belt enough so that the excess straps are not hanging at my sides or flapping as I run. It can easily accommodate much larger and the velcro is tough. The product is also well made, good stitching, excellent hooks for the water bottles (each hold 10oz of water), and the zipper on the front pouch is also well made.

if you need to carry your smartphone with you (I personally only need to when I run alone, usually I'm with my hubby and we run together), you'll need to use an armband or add a FlipBelt to your gear (totally recommend FlipBelts!) [[ASIN:B00JF9DZTK Level Terrain FlipBelt Waist Pouch, Black, Small/26"-29"]]

title: comfortable and accurate heart rate recording
text:
I've a had a polar HR strap in the past and really liked it. This one is nice as well, it is comfortable and appears to give accurate heart rate readings. one thing is that I got the M-XL size and wish I had the small instead. this one still fits a little loose even all the way the tightest it can be. For reference, I wear a 34 band in my bra (sometimes a 32, I'm sort of in between). Wearing this under the bra band holds it up okay, I've worn it for 2 workouts now and haven't had an issue of it falling down, though I have yet to wear it on a run. I wanted this to work with my Concept 2 rowing machine, but so far I have been unable to get the concept 2 to recognize the polar H10. I have had no problem getting the Wahoo Run and the Wahoo X HRMs to connect with my rowing machine, but for some reason no go on this. I've tried 3x and no luck. However, it does connect with my iPhone just fine and I use the FitDigits app to do the tracking (so I can't speak for a Polar app, as I dont use that).

I attached a screenshot of the heart rate tracking. You can see in the middle where I was switching from the NordicTrack (it does not have any electronics, it's an old school NordicTrack skier) to the rowing machine where my heart rate is down, that I spent about 4 minutes fiddling with trying to get the Concept 2 to recognize the Polar and no go. Kind of a bummer, but not a deal killer to me since I have the app.

I still rely on my Wahoo HRM, but it's been a little flaky lately with the heart rate, I think. I use it for runs and bike rides with my old Garmin 310XT watch since that only has an ANT+ connection. Can't use this bluetooth polar with it. (would love any recommendations for an upgrade for my Garmin 310xt to use for running and biking if anyone has a comment on that!)

So overall, I'd say this is a good HRM - if I do get the rower to finally recognize it, I'll update this review.

*****UPDATE***** June 4, 2017:

Thanks to a tip from Geekrevival, I updated the firmware on my Concept2 rowing machine and now it recognizes the Polar H10! yippee! To be clear, if you have the Concept2 rower you need to have the PM5 performance monitor for it to recognize Bluetooth Smart (BLE), otherwise only an ANT+ connection will work. You can easily tell if you have the PM5 as it is right in the upper right corner of the monitor.

I updated the review to a 5-star because there's nothing I see as a flaw or downside on this Polar H10 heart rate monitor.

Now I just need to convince hubby that I need that new Garmin fenix5 GPS watch which uses Bluetooth Smart (and ANT+). :)

title: Goes on super soft!
text:
This is my first time using an anti-friction lotion, and I must say I'm impressed. this really does go on smooth - not oily or greasy feeling at all! I was surprised how it felt like a soft powder as I rubbed it in to my skin. I use it for under my heart rate monitor during my cardio workouts (mostly running). I was a bit put off at first by the peppermint/eucalyptus/tea-tree scent, as I didn't really want to be smelling that during my workouts. However, the scent is really not that strong at all and I didn't even notice it after I rubbed it in. perhaps I just don't use that much, but it was not a bother once rubbed in.

I didn't have any chaffing after my workout and the usual irritation from the heart rate monitor strap was gone. So it works to reduce chaffing/irritation for me and I really love the soft, silky feel of it.

title: solid squat racke
text:
this rack is far superior to what we are currently using in our home gym. I didn't pay enough attention, though, and our bar bells are slightly too short for this. Plus we have standard bars, not Olympic. We've been using the Valor Squat stands, and while they were wonderful when I first got them, they've since slipped to a 3-star product. [[ASIN:B006CW02ZS Valor Fitness BD-9 Power Squat Stand]] They are good still, but the knobs that hold the arms in place stick and don't work like they used to. (granted, they've been through 3 moves across states so far). What I liked about the stands is they are adjustable width being they they are independent stands.

This Reebok Squat Rack, on the other hand, is built with good quality. It was pretty simple to put together and there are no knobs to pull out and twist, like on the Valor stands, which end up causing problems. I did notice that rack is made by Cap Barbell and we've gotten several Cap products that are of decent quality.

My husband and I have been having to take turns using the Valor stands so we jumped at the chance to add this to our home gym. of course, as previously mentioned, now we have to upgrade our barbell (which we have been wanting to do anyway). We work out in our home gym 3x a week and this is an excellent addition.

title: solid, well made, quality weight plate
text:
I wish they sold these in pairs - I mean really, how often do you really just use one weight plate?

Anyhow, that aside, these CAP plates are solid built and do not have that cheap feel to them like some plates I've gotten. I received one 5lb plate to review (I'll be purchasing a second one so I have a set - one for each end of the barbell or dumbbell). The 5lbers do not have the grip holes in them, they are solid.

The quality of these are well made. I have a set of CAP dumbbells that I really like and this will add to the set to extend my options. It's always good to have a few extra 5lbers around to add to my lifts.

The price seems reasonable since it includes shipping (if you're an Amazon Prime member).

title: So much quicker to change weight plates with these things!
text:
These work great! so much better than screwing on the collars that came with the bars! just slide them on and clamp down- easy-peasy!

Like them so much I'm ordering a second pair for the other bar we have.

title: it's a jump rope, it works once you figure out the proper adjustment
text:
First off, I'm not good at jump rope, and am a total newbie. the last time I used a jump rope was when I was about 10 - over 40 years ago! I am hoping to use this as another cardio alternative at the end of my weight lifting workout.

This is a decent rope, and does the job once you figure out the correct length. I did some googling, since nothing about sizing came with this rope and discovered that for sizing, all rope lengths are measured from handle tip to handle tip, NOT just the length of the cord. To determine the exact length for an individual, stand on the center of the cord. The handle tips should reach your armpits, or just below the shoulders. To adjust this jump rope you'll need a small philips head screw driver and wire cutters.

The problem I had with the adjustment is that I'm just 5'2" so had to shorten it quite a bit. this left a long length of cord hanging off one handle as you can only adjust one side. I now need wire cutters to cut it down to size because the rope is not just vinyl, it is steel wires that have a vinyl coating. It hurts when it slaps against unprotected feet (wear shoes!) and shins. I won't be trimming it completely the first time as I may need to adjust the length again as I use it more and get used to it.

I suppose if I was more experienced at jumping I'd probably give this 4 stars, but I'm still trying to get the hang of it and not sure right now if it is me or the rope. I may come back and change the rating as I get more experience with it.

title: My new favorite water bottle
text:
wow, great water bottle! This is a BPA-free water bottle that seals nicely and stays sealed - no leaks! I've used it for plain water as well as my afternoon Starbucks Refresher. It's great, I just pour in the instant packet of Starbucks Refreshers, shake it up, and enjoy!

At first I wasn't sure I'd like the opening that you drink out of, but it's been just fine and did I mention no leaks? This handy bottle also has a secondary closure to help prevent additional leaks where you just squeeze the button on the back of the neck while you drink. You can even lock this in place for extra leakage security, because, well, you certainly don't want that pesky beverage of yours to escape from this container while you're not looking.

The bottle is the perfect size and fits great into my vehicle's cup holders. I've not used the clip on thing at the top to see how well that works, but once the weather warms up I'll take it with me on hiking and camping trips. This thing also cleans up nicely in the top rack of the dishwasher (it's a little tall, but I just have to give it more of a slant and it fits okay).

I really like this water bottle, and I've been through a lot of them!

title: strong, sturdy, and a good workout
text:
These are nice for all sorts of exercises. I do weight lifting at home so these are a nice addition to my routine. I found them to be well made, strong, and solid for doing the variety of exercises shown on the video. The bag that comes with them is nice but these bad boys are pretty big so they are a snug fit in the bag. Still I like the little sling-back bag and intend to use it for a carry-on when I travel rather than to store these things. It has a nice little outside pocket to put your phone, I.D., and boarding pass in - very convenient! ah..but I digress...

I would have preferred that this "system" came with a poster or booklet for the exercises rather than the 12 minute DVD video. Seriously, I'm a skimmer and I hate when I am forced to sit and watch a video just to figure out how to do something. Just let me read it so I can skim to the parts that are relevant for me.

As other users have pointed out, these don't work too well on carpet, but they do work a bit there. I'm in a small apartment with no real non-carpeted space except my tiny kitchen or bathrooms. so I don't get the use out of this system as I should. Still, I'll be moving in a few months and hope to put these to better use in my new place. Until then I will keep using them as I can. They've been great so far with the few exercises I have done with them.

title: Best shaker bottle I've used so far
text:
This is a well designed bottle. The lid screws on nice and easy, plus the cap where you drink out of also screws on. title: Timex "Ironman" Run Trainer good for Running, Swimming, No biking features
text:
The Timex Ironman run Trainer 2.0 GPS watch is a very good gps watch for runners and probably swimmers, too. I don't swim, so couldn't test that part. Despite the name "Ironman" this watch is designed for running and "approved" for swimming (that's from the Timex website where they cite "water resistant approved for 50 meters"). When I think of Ironman, I think of the big three: running, biking, and swimming. So don't let the name fool you into thinking this will connect to your bike sensors as well. That being said, if you are looking for a good watch with a heart rate monitor, this is a decent choice.

I used the watch with my existing ANT+ heart rate monitor and foot pod (both are Garmin devices). The watch synched perfectly with both. If you use a foot pod it can (and should) be calibrated so that you can then accurately track your distance and pace when you're forced to run indoors on a treadmill. The display is clean, easy to read and customizable. I also have small wrists, so was a little concerned about fit, but the watch fit comfortably on me while wearing. It is smaller and a bit more comfortable than the Garmin 310xt (the only other GPS watch I own, so compared it to that). You can even set reminders for when you need to hydrate or fuel up during a long run. Plus you can also create intervals to do interval training.

The thing I dont like about the watch is that I can't also use it for biking like I can with my [[ASIN:B0025VKUPM Garmin Forerunner 310XT]]. Which seems contrary to the fact that not only do they call it "ironman" but it even has the word "triathalon" on the watch face. however, that being said, you can use it for swimming, as I previously mentioned, as it supposedly is water resistant up to 50 meters. I am not a swimmer, so didn't try that, but I am a cyclist (as I already mentioned -- I guess I'm getting redundant here).

The GPS accuracy on the watch is pretty good. It appears to be a little more accurate than my Garmin 310xt, but the difference to me is negligible, especially if I set my Garmin to capture data every second rather than have it on "auto" - then the resulting map traces are almost identical.

Another feature that I'm not too keen on is the way you view the data. They have you use their web-based system, which I found to be too "bulky" - it has too many options and too confusing. Many of the options are only available if you pay for their premium plan. You can't even export the data into a GPX or TCX file without having paid. this is something that pretty much every other company allows for free. I did find a way around that, though. With the watch connected to your computer via the USB port, it becomes just like another USB drive on your machine and you can navigate to the folder that has your activities stored in it. Timex uses the FIT format. Luckily, Strava (a great app and website for tracking cycling and running), will import these files. Just drag the FIT file to your computer somewhere and import it into Strava. It takes a few minutes for Strava to get process the file after it imports, so if all your run information is not showing up right away, wait a few minutes and then refresh or go back to it and you should see it. Then Strava will let you export it to a GPX format which then can be imported into Runkeeper or many other popular fitness apps. Kind of some extra steps, but if you stick with this and Strava, you'll be set. Strava also has a premium (paid) feature, but I only have their basic (free) account and can do everything I need with it.

Overall, this is a really nice watch, and hopefully they will come up with a "lighter" version of their software, but for now, I am not even going to mess with it and stick with Strava.

title: works just fine with my iPhone 5
text:
This is my 3rd heart rate monitor (HRM). Not because they break, but because I got a better phone! Anyhow, I received this Wahoo BlueHR at about the same time I had gotten a [[ASIN:B007S088F4 Polar H7 Bluetooth Smart Heart Rate Sensor]] to use with my new iPhone 5. I preveiously was using a a Garmin HRM, which I still have, but it uses the ANT+ technology and I need an adapter on my iPhone in order to use. The bluetooth is nice because it pairs easily with the DigiFit app that I use. I can't speak for the Wahoo app, because I have not tried that as I've been using DigiFit with a lot of success since the beginning of the year and love that app so why change?

Anyhow, if I compare the Wahoo BlueHR with the Polar H7 they is not too much difference. They are about the same size and the strap is similar with the same fit. The one thing I do not like about both of them is the sensor part (or whatever it's called - the big transmitter-like piece that snaps on). It's not really that bad, but when I'm wearing it and doing some exercises that require me to lay on my chest (like on a bench or stability ball) the thing is not as comfortable as the old Garmin HRM [[ASIN:B000UOD5QM Garmin Heart-Rate Monitor]] which is flat all across the front. Honestly, it's not that big of a deal for the few times I do those types of workouts, but important to note.

the Wahoo HRM does seem to take a few seconds longer to sync up than the Polar when I first start my workouts, but once connected, I haven't lost signal for it. I've been using the Wahoo HRM for about 3 weeks now - have used it for weight lifting 3 days a week, running 2 days a week and bicycling 2 days a week. No problems at all and I love that I can keep track of my heart rate throughout my workouts. the DigiFit app even has some health assessments that I use to get custom heart rate zones based on a prescribed workout. I've run the Advanced Cardio assessment, the Cooper Running Test, and the Critical Power 30-minute (CP30) assessments to determine my heart rate training zones. (these are through the DigiFit app which guide you through them).

I did not experience any issues with this as others have stated, and hopefully the "dead out of the box" is not because they can't find it showing up in their bluetooth settings because with these devices you need to sync it within the app. I think it may have something to do with the Bluetooth 4.0 technology - because they only work with the smartphones/devices that support Bluetooth 4.0, also called Bluetooth Enhanced or BLE. does not work with the iPhone 3Gs - that much I know. There really is little documentation that comes with the device and there really should be something to make it clear that it needs to be paired through an app if you're using it with a smartphone.

oh, and I also have the Wahoo Speed & Cadence sensor on my bike which works great as well.

title: Works great with iPhone 5 and DigiFit app
text:
I have been using the Digifit iPhone app for several months now and the first speed/cadence sensor I got for my bike was the [[ASIN:B000BFNOT8 Garmin GSC 10 Speed/Cadence Bike Sensor]]. that worked great except the magnets on the crank arm/pedal were troublesome. I did, however get some strong ("rare earth") little magnets and stuck those on the end of my pedal and that worked like a charm. The thing about the Garmin GSC10 is that it uses the ANT+ technology. It worked okay with my iPhone 3GS, but the battery life on that old phone didn't always last through my 2+ hour rides. So, I upgraded to the iPhone 5 and now I'm able to take advantage of the Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE or Bluetooth 4.0) technology.

I got this Wahoo speed and cadence sensor that uses the BLE technology to connect to my iPhone 5 and send the data to the DigiFit app that I use. The device attaches just fine to my road bike. I was able to connect it with the thick rubber band provided, but I was weary that it would pop off during my long rides, so I used the zip-ties instead. The magnets that I needed/used with the Garmin were replaced with the ingenious little magnet band that slips easily onto the pedal crank arm. Wahoo got that figured out nicely!

The other thing I like about this device over the Garmin GSC10 is the use of the Bluetooth. Granted, you need a device that uses it, but I notice that my iPhone 5 gets connects to the sensor much quicker and stays connected better than the Garmin did. When I stop for a period of time on my bike rides I usually pause the DigiFit app. With the Garmin and iPhone 3GS using the ANT+ technology it often wouldn't find the device right away and I'd have to retry the connection to get going. I haven't had that issue at all with this Wahoo. Granted, this could be a function of the iPhone, the ANT+ or the Garmin - any combination of those could have caused the issue.

I can't speak to how it works with the Wahoo app, since, as mentioned, I only have used it with the DigiFit app on both the iPhone 3Gs and the iPhone 5. But I really like this sensor and would definitely recommend it.

title: Great cooler so far
text:
I purchased the Igloo BMX Cooler to replace an Ozark Trail 25qt rotomolded cooler that I purchased from Wal-Mart before an impromptu camping trip. I was very disappointed with the OT cooler, it claimed to hold ice for 4.5 days but on day two of my trip over half the ice was melted. I had a family member coming out to visit and camp with me so I decided to order the 52qt version of the Igloo BMX. It was actually cheaper than the Wal-Mart cooler and twice the size.

We filled the Igloo up on a Sunday afternoon packed pretty full with food, beer and water. We were planning on a 3-day trip. I saved as much ice as I could at home and we bought one more bag on the way out of town. Day 1 after over 24 hours I opened the drain and only a tiny bit of water came out. Already much better performance. On Tuesday we moved campsites and got gas and added another bag of ice since we bought more food to replenish. Day 3 on Wednesday a fair amount of water drained from the cooler but it still had plenty of ice and was plenty cold. I had put 8 frozen water bottles inside and they were all frozen still.

I went to empty the cooler on Day 4, a full ~96 hours of use and there was still a lot of ice left in it. I have no doubt that you could make this last 5 days or even longer if you keep adding fresh ice every couple of days. If we didn't add the second bag, most of it would have probably melted by day 3/4.

At the time of this review I purchased the red/black 52qt cooler for $77. I'm impressed enough with it that I decided to order a 25qt one was well for solo trips and returned my Ozark Trail cooler. I will add another review or update this one after I use the 25qt cooler. But $140 for a nice rotomolded 52qt and 25qt cooler is less than half the price of ONE comparable Yeti. So glad I didn't buy into the hype.

title: So far, so good!
text:
I bought this tent in 2017 when I saw it on sale for $39.99 without any intention of using it anytime soon but having one just in case. Due to everything going on this year, I was going nuts being stuck inside so I finally took the plunge and started using it for camping adventures in the Rocky Mountains. So far, so good! I've used this tent 4 separate times now and about 6 nights of sleeping so far. My first trip was a solo one and I had never pitched a tent before by myself. The instructions on the bag tag didn't make the most sense but after about 20 minutes I figured it out on my own. Now I can setup or take down the tent by myself in 5-10 minutes, even less if I have some help.

The included rain-fly is very nice for that purpose as well as providing shade over the mesh openings if you're trying to sleep in a little in the mornings. There are two side windows you can open up for a nice breeze and viewing. Everything zips up nice and easy, however I would advise using both hands when zipping or unzipping the main door. It does have a tendency to catch fabric in the zipper if you're not careful.

I have only slept in the tent by myself so far using a 4" memory foam mattress. Plenty of room for 1-2 people. A family of 3-4 could probably fit comfortably in here with sleeping bags and small children. I don't think 4 adults could sleep too comfortably unless everyone was very cozy with each other.

The included tent stakes are pretty weak. I've already bent almost half of them, so anticipate buying a new set of them at some point. Not a big deal. I had to use rocks to secure my tent better after some high wind gusts blew it around a little bit.

Overall the quality of this tent is very nice and I would buy it again, especially at the price I paid. I see now the price is $69.99 which is probably still a fair price but in that range I would recommend doing some research and seeing if there is a better buy but even at full price this is a good quality tent. So far the coldest I've slept in it was around 40° weather with some light rains and I stayed warm with just a couple blankets, no sleeping bag. I don't know if this would be a good tent for winter camping but I think it would hold up just fine for some late fall snowfall and cold temps when the off-season has begun.

title: Great to have on hand, tastes great too!
text:
We do a lot of camping and living outdoors, and something we enjoy is easy to make food when we are outdoors. We look for ways to keep the cooler, extra stoves, skillets, dutch ovens and cast iron at home. I think we found our answer in Mountain House freeze dried entrees.

We purchased the Mountain House Just in Case 72 Hour Kit. In it we chose the Beef Stroganoff and took it to a scout meeting to try. During the scout meeting we talked about light weight backpacking as well as food options for emergency food at home.

After we boiled two cups of water we poured it into the pouch and zip locked it for 8 minutes. The contents where stirred and then served to many hungry scouts at the meeting. Every scout got a sample to try and a lot of them were hesitant. The overall surprise on their faces was priceless. They liked it and said it tasted great.

They wanted a pouch of the Beef Stroganoff for themselves. The scouts were surprised how easy the meal was to make and how simple the cleanup is. We did also like the zip lock feature not only for the re-hydrating process but also to keep the uneaten food for later if needed. They were also coming up with ways to reuse the pouch for other needs in the forest or on the trail to keep from throwing the empty pouch away.

Most of the scouts have never re-hydrated food or eaten MREs before. They were impressed with the ease of cooking and how lightweight it is to add to your day pack or back pack.

For camping, outings or emergency preparedness I would recommend Mountain House Just in Case 72 Hour Kit to have on hand. For one it has a long shelf life, for two you won’t starve as the contents of each pouch will satisfy a hungry kid or adult. A very tasty meal…especially in the middle of the forest!

Our only complaint (and the reason we deducted a star) is not all the water absorbed into the food, so it was very runny. The pack instructed to use 2 cups of water and I feel that was too much.
