title: Coleman Has Always Been A Good Name In Outdoor Products
text:
I still have and use my father's original Coleman gas lantern that we took to our deer shack every year in upper Wisconsin. That would make it about 65 years old! We've even used it here in Florida when power goes out because of hurricanes and severe storms.

That being said I wouldn't pay $59.99 for this particular LED lantern. While it is a well-made and effective product it is out- priced and out-performed by many alternative products of its type. The only way it might make some sense is if you subscribed to Coleman's theory of a "OneSource" rechargeable camping system and purchased most or all of its components.

That would be a similar strategy to me buying all DeWalt 20V battery tools in order to use the same batteries and chargers for all of my cordless tools. Now that has worked out extremely well for me. But camping is not even on our "to do" list. My wife's idea of camping would be to stay in a motel without all the usual amenities.

title: There Is No One Perfect Holster
text:
If there was such a unicorn of a holster I wouldn't have a large cardboard box full of various holsters. Everything from the big names (Alien Gear, VersaCarry, Relentless, DeSantis, etc,) to the reasonably priced alternatives that you held "high hopes" for but don't deliver what you thought they would.

This Sportula pack is priced very cheaply and MAY solve a short term need for you on occasion -- but only if you're looking to carry a compact pistol. "One size fits all" doesn't work for any holster. You would have to spend big bucks to have a custom holster made for a particular gun and even then it wouldn't be "perfect".

However this isn't a bad first choice given its reasonable pricing. Consider it to be a training holster so that you can wear it to find out what is good and bad about this particular construction. There are actually more things wrong than right with this product and wearing it for a considerable period of time will let you know what configuration might be more comfortable or useful for you in particular.

This is a low risk purchase on your part and Sportula offers a "No hassle warranty" on their products with a 100% satisfaction guarantee.

title: If You've Got To Do It -- Do It Right!
text:
Since we live in SW Florida with its year around bright sun, certain people (like me), are basically holding our feet to the frying pan by being outside. Having blond hair and blue eyes, being older than dirt, and already diagnosed and treated for melanoma once, I know what I have to do in order to wake up on the right side of the dirt.

Yes, this USHAKE sun cap is a bit more expensive than the myriad others that I have bought and tried, but it appears to be well worth it:

I like the UPF 50+ protection.
I like the khaki color and adjustable sizing.
I like the water resistance and quick drying fabric.
I like the removable face protector and the ability to take off the neck protection.
I like the fact that the removable pieces are made of a breathable mesh.
I like the sweatband built around the inside of the cap.
I like the chin strap that avoids having the wind blow it off my head.
And I like the robust buttons that are far better than those used in other caps.

What I don't like is the fact that these hats are made in China. Next time I will be a little smarter.

title: WHEW! The Slew Of Initial Reviews Had Me In A Stew.
text:
When I order a product I am more interested in the negative reviews than the positive ones. What problems are other people having? Do the buyers understand how the product works or are they misusing it? Are there design errors in the product? Does it function as advertised? Is it possible that a string of bad reviews is due to a switch in manufacturers? That by the way is often the case and a company has to own that choice.

My first use resulted in an unintended torture test. After filling up the mug with my first cup of coffee in the morning -- when I am still a bit fumble fingered -- I dropped the full mug on our marble floor. You know that moment when the dropped item appears suspended in the air and you are anticipating a horrible crash and the resulting mess? Didn't happen here! Boy was I relieved. I hate to catch flak from my wife to start the day.

Since my wife will be using this mug on her commute to work I was most interested in the claim that it would keep liquids "hot for up to 7 hours". So I filled it up with hot coffee at 10:00 pm and opened it this morning at 7:00 am. For the mathematically challenged, which most of the younger kids seem to be these days, that is nine hours. When I popped the lid one-handed (which takes a bit of practice) and took a sip, I was rewarded with coffee that was better than warm but not quite hot.

Most users of course will not use this as a thermos to keep something hot or cold for 8-10 hours. Instead they will be steadily drinking/sipping from the cup until the beverage is finished. Constant repetitive opening and closing of the tab is bound to release heat faster and the remaining liquid will no doubt be at less than a desired temperature, but it was nice to see that it would function as promised.

So Contigo got it's act together, either by changing something in the product or finding a better manufacturer. The mug is a subtle pleasing color and fits perfectly in our vehicles. The lid opening mechanism comes stiff and takes a bit of use to work it loose. Even though the company says that you can put the lid (only) in the dishwasher, I always get better long-term results by hand washing them. Made in China.

title: I Bought This For My Youngest Daughter, Her Husband And Their New Peloton
text:
The only complaint I ever heard from the kids was that their new Peleton had a hard and uncomfortable seat. I figured that was easily remedied if I found a good gel seat cushion cover to give them for Christmas. They expressed gratitude for the gift but didn't look overwhelmed by it.

When I finally asked them how it worked on their Peleton I received the following answers. And I quote:

"no problems"
"none at all"
"fits the seat well"
"cushioned well"
"durable"
"easy to clean with baby wipes"

Knowing how discriminating their tastes are, these are resounding testimonials for this product.

title: Surprisingly Good For The Money
text:
This fishing outfit met the criteria I had for picking out a fishing kit for our three year old granddaughter. She went from cane pole to spincast reels in record time and I figured that it was time for her to step up and have her own "starter" equipment. Either her father or I could cast for her initially and let her get used to using the reel while bringing in a fish (hopefully).

The color is perfect for a young lady who idolizes Elsa and the other Disney characters and the set is strong enough to work until she is ready to step up to a "big girl" outfit. Having her own set lets her learn how to take care of it and will be a good marker for when she is ready to step up again. That and of course being able to cast a spinning reel.

I wouldn't use this for anything but a beginner's set for a young child. This is not a solid or durable enough rig to survive the stress a teenager or adult would subject it to. However the related lures and equipment lend themselves to learning how to tie knots and retrieve various baits. Don't expect it to last long but it should last long enough! At least until that elusive big fish breaks the pole or reel for her.

title: What A Surprise!
text:
This old bird still has some of the original low power hunting scopes made by Simmons back in the day. I always wondered why my Dad had a 4X Leupold scope on his .22 while I had a Simmons 4X. Although the Simmons did an acceptable job, it was in no way comparable to the Leupold. Of course my Dad's .22 rimfire rifle was also far superior to the Sears model that he bought for me. But believe me, I was just thrilled at age 10 to be able to go squirrel hunting. And since I trained all winter at the local armory, I could hold my own against him.

But enough of the old days. Simmons then was considered a fairly mediocre manufacturer. Now Simmons is a brand owned by Bushnell Corporation (acquired by them in 2008) which in turn is owned by Vista Outdoor. Competition in the optics market and great strides made in this technology has resulted in current offerings superior in quality and also very reasonably priced. That is an example of "value engineering" at its finest.

This Simmons spotting scope was shipped in a hard case and had the scope itself also wrapped in plastic and inside a separate soft case. Well protected indeed! A bench sized tripod is also included as are directions for both locating the instruction manual and for registering the product for potential warranty coverage. Fear not for the instruction sheet is offered in five languages.

Being an older guy and not a hunter, I don't have to worry about lugging this rather large scope through the bushes. However it does serve two needs for me. The first is that it is extremely useful when testing .22 ammo at a 100 yard range. These old eyes are not what they used to be and this Simmons scope makes it simple to track and score my shots. Most of my shooting is suppressed and testing various subsonic ammo has been interesting to say the least.

Since we live on beautiful Charlotte Harbor in Southwest Florida, Mother Nature offers us constant reminders of how the animal kingdom functions and survives. Being able to focus on long distances off our back lanai has really increased our visual reach even to the far shore. We are able to watch Bald Eagles and Osprey fish, Red Tailed Hawks and Florida Barred Owls home in on their prey, and alligators and manatees cruise through the harbor. Entertaining for us and our guests.

For roughly $150.00 this is a heck of a deal for the quality you receive. Simmons has worked its way back into being competitive with most of the mainstream firms. If you're looking for a big increase in quality, plan on spending a lot more money. In the old days we would call this "the law of diminishing returns". That means that you have to spend a lot more money just to get an incremental return in actual performance. Simmons proves that you don't have to spend that much.

title: DON'T TAKE AN UNLOADED GUN WITH YOU (ANYWHERE) WHERE YOU MIGHT NEED TO USE IT!
text:
Just like verifying that you are comfortable using a pistol or rifle, you also have to know that any weapon that you have reason to depend on is functional and loaded. It's only common sense to test out any weapon prior to depending on it to defend yourself and/or your family. A firearm that goes "click" when you pull the trigger is of no use to you -- and neither is this Sabre Bear Spray if the can/fixture is faulty or filled with ineffective spray.

When I was in the pepper spray distribution business many years ago, I always had to test out sample batches of the product to make sure that the sprayer worked and the spray itself was as powerful as promised. I got tired of being sprayed in the face (like all police officers who carry a personal defense spray are required to do) so I devised an alternative test that was not as intrusive or disabling.

Taking the canister outside of our building, I'd find a quiet space with no wind and spray a small amount on the back of my hand. That accomplishes two things; it shows that the can is pressurized and discharges properly and it also demonstrates how irritating the spray is to the back of your hand. As you will find out for yourself, a good can will provide an instant burning sensation. However you must be extremely careful to not get it in your eyes or transfer it to other parts of your exposed skin. That can end up being almost as bad as taking a full blast in the face.

My youngest daughter and my wife each carries one of these units. SABRE has always been highly regarded in the industry but in the past I did test one of their products and find it to be totally ineffective. They took care of the problem, replaced the faulty unit with a good one, and now I feel that my wife and daughter have the advantage in a confrontation should they practice "situational awareness" and keep their wits about them. I told them to keep spraying until the criminal, dog, or whatever threat targeting them is down for the count and does not remain a danger to them. They each have a concealed carry permit so I am confident that if they have to they can move on to the next step.

title: A Versatile In-The-Pocket Holster For Only $11.97?  Lucky Me!
text:
I originally bought the smallest Blackhawk TecGrip Pocket Holster for my NAA .22 magnums. At first I thought that the smaller holster was too large but realized that it fit the gun loosely and that it was shaped to force the outside of the holster to contact with the material inside my pocket. Since it rode deep in my cargo short's front pocket it worked out perfectly, letting the gun be drawn without bringing the holster with it. I also discovered that I could even carry larger weapons comfortably in that same smaller holster.

One of the reviews I read about this Blackhawk holster is that on occasion they are put on sale. Since I was interested in picking up a larger one and seeing how it fit some of my bigger carry weapons, I found this size 3 holster on Amazon for only $11.97. It allows me to carry anything from a Kahr .380 to the Smith & Wesson Backpacker in .44 magnum. This works extremely well in deep front pockets like cargo shorts but don't depend on it working in shallow front pockets.

Nice, comfortable, versatile, and separates from your weapon when drawn. Even up to the MSRP of $19.95 it provides a great value.

title: Sticky Holsters Better Watch Out -- Blackhawk TecGrip Has You In Their Sights
text:
I often carry small (NAA) .22 magnum revolvers in a Sticky Holster. Southwest Florida provides us with heat and humidity almost all year around. Being able to pocket carry a small caliber weapon really fits the bill for me, especially since shorts and swimsuits are normal attire here.

Just for a lark I decided to order a Blackhawk TecGrip holster after reading an article about it. Right away I was $10.00 ahead of the game since the TecGrip only costs $19.99 instead of $29.99 for the Sticky. The Blackhawk is actually big enough to carry other small pistols I have and you can place it virtually anywhere it suits you.

I currently (after corresponding with Blackhawk) carry a Smith and Wesson 351PD, a seven shot .22 mag revolver in this holster. Believe it or not, this OO size will also fit a Colt Defender and a Smith & Wesson .44 mag Backpacker -- as well as other pistols of that approximate size. This holster stays where you put it until you need to get to it.

Well-made, comfortable even in hot weather, and stays where you put it. Time to order another one, a size O3 listed on Amazon for $11.97. Hard to go wrong here!

title: Buying This Is Just The First Step!
text:
Every method of self-defense involves a level of awareness and confidence. Exercising "situational awareness" will often allow you to avoid placing yourself in a position where you have to protect yourself. Escape of course is the second option assuming that there is an effective way to avoid a confrontation. But if you are finally forced to bring your use of force to the situation, you must be confident of your method and how to effectively deploy it.

Many years ago I tested a Sabre product for effectiveness. Having a wife and two young daughters motivated me to find something legal that they could carry and use properly without hurting themselves in the process. The particular Sabre unit I tested DID NOT PERFORM AS ADVERTISED! I wrote a poor product review and explained why I came to that conclusion. Unfortunately my review was targeted by numerous individuals who trashed my reasoning and perspective. Yes, the Sabre products have an outstanding reputation. But not every individual unit will work as promised!

About 35 years ago I worked as a product development manager for a company lastly known as We Care America -- formerly Weapons Corporation of America (WCA). One of the products we brought to market was a pepper spray intended for self-defense use. I couldn't put my name on the recommendation until I satisfied myself as to its effectiveness. That meant that I had to be sprayed in the face. Many law enforcement organizations require their officers to be sprayed so that they understand the proper use and deployment of their spray -- and so they know what their targeted individuals will go through.

My suggestion to you is to take your unit outside the house, find an area that is not windy, hold your off-hand away from you with the palm down, and spray the back of your hand a quick burst. You should feel sharp pain on the back of your hand. If you don't, you have a defective unit. If you do, simply wash off with soap and warm water. DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS NEAR YOUR EYES!

A unit failure can be caused by a short expiration date, poor storage, or less than optimal shipping conditions. Even on this product page Sabre states that other brands experience a 30% failure rate (University of Utah study). If your unit produces the desired irritation, shoot a full burst away from you to get an idea of how well your can is pressurized. Your spray may not go the promised 18 feet. Be aware of its particular limitations. In any event, return it immediately if it doesn't perform as advertised.

Once you determine that your individual unit is effective, make sure to view the offered free training video and then practice deploying your unit without actually spraying it. You must have confidence in both your individual unit and in yourself. Practice may seem redundant but it can be a life saver.

title: Rain, Constant Heat and Humidity, Gnats, Mosquitos, Biting Yellow Flies
text:
Hot and humid Southwest Florida, high heat and humidity virtually all year. That type of climate, which is subtropical, is perfect for bugs. And boy, do we have them. I looked at a few hats with mosquito netting added to it but realized that I couldn't get the total head and neck coverage I needed for proper UPF sun protection.

Since I just had a melanoma removed from my back (with surgery including 56 stitches), I'm very careful about what I wear in the sun when working on our landscaping. I couldn't find beekeepers' hats which provided both UPF 50 in the hat as well as side and back flaps to protect my neck. So I quickly realized that the solution was to buy the netting separate and simply use it over the proper sun protection hats that I already had.

I ordered this triple pack of mosquito head netting for a number of reasons. They are economical, well-built, are loose fitting, are a very neutral khaki color, and have a very tight mesh to protect against the tiniest buggers. The khaki color does not absorb heat from the sun and is easy to see through. Since our Florida yellow flies are attracted to dark colors, khaki is the way to go.

title: My First Firearm:  A Bolt Action Single Shot .22 With A Leupold 4X Scope
text:
Growing up in central Wisconsin almost required you to become a hunter. It didn't matter whether your passion was rabbits and squirrels, pheasants or ducks, deer or bear. Sometimes it was all of them and when everything was out of season, it was time to go ice fishing.

My father gave me my first firearm. I don't remember the model of the single shot .22 but the Leupold scope probably cost more than the rifle. "One shot, one kill" was the order of the day with headshots on small game required. During the winter we shot NRA targets indoors and in warmer weather we shot rats at the local garbage dump. You active shooters know how important technique and practice is.

Good optics are just as critical as the other components of successful shooting, especially when you have 20/400 vision. So the Leupold scope proved itself up to the task and resulted in a lot of game on the table. My father and I used to compete when we hunted and the tie breaker was often a partridge or quail shot out of the air when startled on your stalk.

This Bushnell Engage scope is perfect for my Ruger Precision .22. We live on 2.75 acres outside of town that is bordered by woods and wetlands. For some reason the snakes, bobcats and hawks can't keep the rat and rabbit populations under control -- which occasionally results in river rats in the attic and families of rabbits destroying my lawn and landscaping.

Being prey all of their lives has made these animals very difficult to surprise, so taking longer shots is critical to engagement. Having a good suppressor is important so that the neighbor's don't notice -- and it can also give you the opportunity for a second shot if necessary. (Fortunately that doesn't happen too often).

For the money, this is a very well built and engineered scope. The good field of view helps the shooter to discern the varmints through the thick plants, the glass is clear, the reticle does not overpower the target. and this scope balances well on my Ruger Precision Rimfire. My surging varmint population is now on a serious decline.

title: There Are Two Rules I ALWAYS Adhere To When I Purchase A Product
text:
Everyone knows the first rule: You get what you pay for. In this case though I think that you get more than what you expect. My experience so far is that this scope functions flawlessly. That has proven how well the Chinese can reverse engineer some products and manufacture them to relatively high standards. I would certainly be afraid to drop it but it is screwed together very well.

The second rule I abide by is: The more complicated the product, the more things that can go wrong with it. And this particular product has a lot of technical features. Think of it as a Swiss Army Knife but with battery powered components. It is actually designed quite well and looks good properly mounted but I doubt that it would continuously handle the recoil from a large caliber rifle or shotgun. However there is a 30 day "Money Back Satisfaction Guarantee" and a 12-month warranty if it goes bad.

The third rule that I usually follow is to buy at least one model higher (in price and quality) when I determine what I might need. In this case though it makes more sense to not get a more complicated scope/laser combo. Shooting/hunting is complicated enough depending on how your weapon functions, the conditions you're shooting under, and your ability to master the situation to end up successful. Typically the more things that can get in your way during a shooting situation can limit your results dramatically. So I always try to keep it simple.

This is a fun product however -- just make sure that you use it a lot during the initial 12 months. By then you will know what functions are most important to you, which weapon pairs with it the best (for you), and how dependable it is. Perhaps you only need a fixed blade knife instead of that Swiss Army Knife.

title: Surprisingly Good Quality For The Price
text:
I needed a new pair of waders to replace the ones I ripped to shreds when trimming mangroves in our wetlands. It turns out that the old ones couldn't handle some of the spikes and thorns encountered in our Southwest Florida location. While the leaks did help me cool off when in the water you have to be careful of flesh-eating bacteria down here. If a spike/thorn comes through your pants it will probably lodge in your skin. That is not something that I want to deal with.

For a big guy like me (6'3" and 235 lbs) I was very happy to find that they fit so well. The weak spot tends to be the suspenders which normally don't lock properly or fall apart quickly. The clips on these locked up good and tight so I didn't have to worry about losing my coverage. However whether it's backup for my waders or for the tactical pants I wear with boots tromping around in the wetlands, I have a bright orange pair of Carrhart clip-on suspenders to keep my britches on nice and tight. Some of the surplus military pants that come with suspenders fail immediately.

Two obstacles I always watch out for when chest deep in our brackish water are cottonmouths and alligators. There is a large 12' bull alligator we often see crossing the harbor to forage on our side. While gators are common in these parts and normally don't bother humans, a big one like that can make a nice meal out of me. So I'm constantly searching the water for ripples or other disturbances that might indicate that I have company.

As I was completing my trimming on one section of the shoreline I happened to glance to my right and found a 4' gator floating right next to me. Instinct kicked in and I smacked him on the head with the flat side of my machete. He probably wouldn't cause me any trouble but the big bull could just as well be in the area hunting for his next snack.
They often eat smaller gators but I didn't want him to have to make a choice between the little one and big old me. Perhaps the camouflage worked well enough so that they couldn't see me.

title: This Sticker Is Perfect For Us!
text:
We rescue and rehabilitate Irish Wolfhounds so it was nice to find a sticker that lets people know what those crazy big dogs are that are hanging their heads out of our vehicles.

This sticker is a decent size to put on a side rear window near where they stick their heads out. The image of a IWH is passable but could be offered in slightly better detail but the "Wolfhound Rescued" logo is perfect.

Hopefully this decal will survive Southwest Florida's constant heat and humidity. Fortunately it won't cost much to buy a replacement.

title: A Well Made, Versatile Sling Bag To Grab On The Way Out
text:
This is a perfect bag to have hanging in the closet for a quick grab on the way out of your home. The green color comes looking somewhat distressed instead of screaming "Brand New" and the bag is made of a high-density 600D fabric, a good solid water resistant material that is a strong weave.

The many compartments provide you with enough room for properly concealing a full size revolver/pistol with the necessary magazines and extra ammo. Add in a good quality flashlight and folding knife and you're pretty much 'good to go'. Anything else that you manage to stuff in it is just an extra bonus.

The carry strap is padded and comfortable to wear and the fasteners will keep your gear properly secured and handy even if you leave the house at a sprint. There are many more expensive shoulder bags out there that don't provide anywhere near the versatility and quality of this Barbarian bag.

title: A Good Citrus Degreaser But A Bit Spendy As Far As Value
text:
I went outside this morning to find that a vulture had strafed our new Honda CRV. One of the many hazards in Southwest Florida is the abundance of bird droppings from several relatively large species, with the vultures and pelicans giving the most bang for the buck. Sometimes I swear that these birds know when you have a new car in the driveway.

I always spray the offended area with a mist from our hose and let it sit for about a minute to help break up the chalky residue from bird poop. Afterwards you can apply a quick shot of any good quality cleaner and degreaser, let it soak in for another minute, and then wipe away gently with a clean cloth.

This Star Brite works well on this particular problem but I wouldn't categorize the product as being "ultimate". However I was pleasantly surprised when I used it to clean the burned on grease on our countertop burners. It was just a simple matter of spraying a bit on, letting it sit for a bit, and then scraping the residue off with a razorblade.

The only thing that I have found that works better cleaning cooktops is the Cerama Bryte Complete Cooktop Cleaning Kit which sells for about $2.00 more for the kit. However the Cerama Bryte cleaner is less useful on other projects around the house. The Star Brite smells better and gives you 32 oz. of a more 'all purpose' formula to use.

title: Another Great Backyard Game To Add To Jarts And Cornhole
text:
Some folks enjoy their backyard barbecues without alcoholic contests like 'flip a cup' and 'beer pong'. Those people in particular should consider adding this Bocce Set to their lawn entertainment. Bocce is a classic Italian lawn game that is easy and fun to play. This Franklin Sports set is well made and reasonably priced and allows you to add an uncomplicated game of skill that virtually all of your attendees can participate in.

People of all ages love Bocce and it won't take long before those who have never played it will initially watch how it's played and quickly ask for their turn in rotation. Think 'horse shoes' without the spinning metal shoes or 'lawn jarts' without the potentially damaging metal tips. Harmless, fun, and easy to understand. What's not to like?

title: You've Gotta Love This Umbrella!
text:
Every company seems to think that it can make the "next big thing" in umbrellas. It seems as though I've tried dozens of folding umbrellas that promise "this and that" but ultimately fail in one (or more) of the stated advantages. Most have some type of catastrophic failure after only a few uses, some so bad that they make the umbrella totally inoperable. So it was with some skepticism that I ordered this blue Bodyguard Travel Umbrella. It made a lot of promises on its product page -- but would it work as promised?

Finally I've found an umbrella that delivers on its promises. This Bodyguard Travel Umbrella sells for the impressive price of only $20.99, and puts a very useful collapsible umbrella in your hands. You can tell as soon as you pick it up that it is well-made and durable. It has some heft to it, snaps open with the push of a button, and collapses its canopy when you push the 'close' button. Then all you have to do is push the collapsed canopy down into the handle and your compact umbrella can be put into the supplied travel case.

The extra ribs give it additional strength when using it in the wind. It is probably more likely that it would be blown out of your hand than have the umbrella turn inside out on you. The handle is comfortable, fits my hand well, and has a wrist strap to keep it from the aforementioned potential flyaway. Yup, someone finally brought out a good one.

title: You Can Always Make A Large Patch Smaller But You Can't Make A Small Patch Larger
text:
I use these Birchwood Casey Gun Cleaning Patches on almost all of my firearms by simply cutting the patches down in size to use on my smaller bore weapons. Instead of using the Hoppes No. 9 solvent (the old standard) I now use the Breakfree CLP-4 Lubricant Preservative cleaner. Sometimes I also use the Froglube CLP Paste Gun Cleaner which is a bio-based lubricant which is made from "USDA Certified Good-Grade" ingredients. Smells good too.

These patches have a good texture which helps in the cleaning process, absorbs the material you're trying to remove, and are basically lint-free -- which is a real 'plus'. Of course keeping your firearms cleaner for longer periods of time depends on using higher quality ammo. Using these patches on lower caliber weapons simply involves cutting them down to size. Having one large package of patches simplifies everything.

title: A Well Built And Solid Knife
text:
I ordered this knife not only because of its style but also because of how rugged it looked. As a knife collector my leaning is toward the larger and stronger knives that I could rely upon for a long time should the need arise. Even if that need never comes up, I enjoy having a collection of good looking blades at hand.

The knife came wrapped in a plastic sleeve which was inside a zippered camo bag and packaged in a reinforced box. Also included was a polishing cloth and a warranty pamphlet. The knife is guaranteed against defects in material and workmanship and has a limited lifetime warranty to the original owner.

Now on to the knife itself. I paid the vendor $184.44 and expected to get the blue knife as shown in the picture on the product page. Unfortunately the knife was delivered in the standard steel grey color with the only blue color being on the accent ring on the ball bearing pivot. Aside from the missing color, this is one well-made and smoothly functioning flipper. The titanium handle fills your hands and the 3.25" blade is a thick and well finished CPM-535VN stainless steel.

This thing locks up tighter than a bank vault and lends credence to the company's reputation for tight tolerances and great quality. There is absolutely no blade wobble when the blade is extended and releasing the frame lock is easily and smoothly done. The blade came sharp enough to cut paper and also shave the hair on the back of my hand. It could be made sharper though without comprising the integrity of the blade.

So I'm impressed with the quality of the Kizer knife at this price point, actually very impressed. I would like to have the original knife in the color I ordered so I will contact the vendor and ask for a replacement.

title: Seems Fairly Well Built For The Price -- Which Means Don't Expect Too Much.
text:
What did you expect from a $10.00 sling? I almost get the feeling that it was designed as a fashion accessory. The color combination is nice and the braiding sturdy but there are a few shortcomings to be aware of:

It is not long enough for taller (and broader) users.
The webbing is comfortable but you can't wear it unless the simple nylon cord rests on your shoulder--not the webbing.
The connectors are cheap and won't take much (if any) abuse. Don't try carrying anything heavy.
The length of the cording when unwound is far too short to be useful in most emergencies.

I certainly wouldn't trust this sling to safely and effectively carry any type of expensive firearm. Perhaps you could give it to your kids for playing army or hauling plastic weapons around. I always find out how tough a tool might be by lending it to our kids and seeing what they are able to do with it before it breaks.

title: Nothing Is Ever Perfect -- But This INNO Rack Is Easy To Use
text:
As I get older I have come to appreciate products that are lightweight and easy to use. This INNO Bike Hitch Mount hits both marks for me and is reasonably priced to boot. There's no sense at our age to injure ourselves when getting ready to benefit from a long bike ride. With this mount we can take our two road bikes anywhere at a moment's notice without having to worry about working with a cumbersome and heavy rack.

Since I had a few very expensive bikes stolen while I was doing my graduate work at Indiana University, I never leave our bikes on the rack without being able to keep an eye on them. "What one man can create another can defeat". And in my experience, they can defeat just about any product more quickly than you think.

We're happy with this purchase for a number of reasons and have learned over time to work around any negatives that we come across. The negatives here are tiny and easily worked around.

title: Perfect Size For Taking With You Just About Anywhere
text:
This "tailgate" model is all aluminum, has legs that fold up under the board, weighs 22 lbs. and comes with its own cloth carrying case. It is about one foot shorter than a regulation sized unit but its portability makes it great to take wherever you might be off to. In Southwest Florida where we live it's a real bonus to have it made out of aluminum. Any steel products, even stainless steel, will have a coat of rust on it if left outside overnight. Wood products are subject to the morning dew and high humidity resulting in wood absorbing moisture and eventually cracking or rotting.

It comes with eight regulation size bags made of all-weather fillers. They have the proper heft to them and are a good match for the shortened boards. Everyone seems to love cornhole down here and it is a "must have" for any outdoor party. Rotating through this game with 'beer pong' and 'flip-a-cup' should keep everyone happy and engaged. Just make sure to drink a lot of water too.

title: A Nice Solid Tool To Have Along "Just In Case"
text:
It's always a pleasure to hold a tool in your hand that is not only useful but also durable and well-designed. Any road warrior would be happy to have this compact Crank Brothers tool along for the ride. You never know what might happen when you're many miles from home so anything that can cut down on your repair time is greatly appreciated.

I always carry a Victronix Swiss Tool along with this when leaving populated areas. Having the combination of tools provided by the Victronix and Crank Brothers covers most of my potential needs. Just be sure that you don't torque either tool too much or you'll end up with a bent set of useless metal.

title: Glad I Found It -- Serves All My Sharpening Needs
text: Small enough to sharpen hand pruners and large enough to handle riding lawnmower blades, I have also used it to keep my machetes sharp and even to smooth the blade on a dinged up shovel.  The unique size and shape of this Lansky sharpener allows it to be used on several types of cutting tools, from small to large.  Long enough to grip easily and rough enough to help you maintain that grip, this is the one sharpener I keep in my pocket when venturing into the Southwest Florida wetlands to keep my machetes and hatchets sharp when cutting down Brazilian Pepper trees.

title: One Of The Original "Mil-Spec" Tools
text:
I have tried out, bought, used, and even broken several cutting tools in my 68 years. Axes, machetes, hatchets, swords and saws are all made at various pricing points, offering a confusing array with types of steel, various lengths and weights, shape and sharpness of the blade, different materials used for the handles, and whether it's full tang or not. Ontario has been cranking out these 18" machetes for about 70 years. Of all the cutting/chopping tools I've used over the years I've found that machetes are the most versatile and useful, the one cutting tool I would carry if I could only have one

This mil-spec Ontario machete at $22.99 is one of the most value oriented sharp tools that I have ever used. It holds a good edge and is easy to sharpen. It is well balanced and easily performs any cutting task assigned to it. My absolute favorite is the Esee Lite Machete but that one comes in at around $81.00. You might consider the Ontario machete a poor man's Esee Lite, but at a cost of only one quarter of the Esee it represents a true value for what you get. Since I work so much in the Southwest Florida wetlands I always spray the handles with fluorescent orange. So much easier to find them if dropped in dense foliage.

A good machete can be used to chop down large diameter trees, clear brush, slash through hanging vines, sharpen tent stakes, cut up firewood, and makes a great defensive weapon against creatures large and small. If you need to have a good cutting tool with you this Ontario 18" Military is a great way to start. It is simultaneously one of the best and also reasonably priced.

title: This Was A "Honey" Of A Purchase!
text:
There are two things that I want to tell you about this buying experience. First off, the hat is well-made and comfortable. I bought it for our youngest daughter who is leaving sunny SW. Florida for a one year fellowship training program at Brown University (Providence, R.I.) That and a Tervis Tumbler with the Brown logo should help warm her up while she's there.

The second and probably most important part is that you need to sign up for the "Honey" program. Whenever you shop at Amazon or any other participating organization, Honey automatically checks all the listings (in this case on Amazon) to see if there is a cheaper total price available on this item.

In this case Honey informed me that there was another offering on Amazon for $3.30 less! Honey compares not only the price of the item but also the cost of any tax or shipping. The Honey program is free and often offers coupons on other sites that helps to reduce the total cost of your purchase. It's easy to use and can save you money. That is "one Honey of a deal".

title: This Is Exactly What I Was Looking For!  An Excellent Value Engineered Tool.
text:
I am a knife collector who also buys knives as tools to use while trimming mangroves and removing invasive vegetation from the wetlands on our property in Southwest Florida. Twice a year I find myself in the wetlands trimming away so that we can maintain our water view as per current regulations in place. Because of the hazardous footing, thick vegetation, and dangerous flora and fauna -- I primarily use machetes and hatchets for my work. I want to be able to see and hear any of the frequent obstacles I encounter daily in that dangerous mess.

The average width of the limbs I am currently trimming require a short chopping motion since the trees are so tightly packed together. I usually depend on an Esee Lite Machete for most of the work but it is too long and requires swinging it to be most effective, hence my serch for a good chopper. This Ridge Runner Brimstone Canyon Machete fits the bill. It is well built with a full taexng ending in a butt plate. The blade is a full 12" of 440 stainless steel and it has a pommel to help protect your swinging hand.

It arrived sharp enough to shave hair off my arm and to pass the paper test. The cutting side is thin and curved with the top of the blade carrying the weight for more effective chopping. It even has several serrations at the top of the blade for cutting/sawing. The pakkawood handle is fastened to the full tang blade with three bolts and the machete itself has a nice solid feel. The handle is a bit small and slippery for me but that is easily remedied with grip tape and gloves.

Here's the kicker. Some people might collect this type of knife because it is well assembled, visually appealing, and feelsgood in the hand. However I bought this as a working tool for a very reasonable price and feel that it offers considerable value for the cost. Looking for an effective chopper? Search no more. And by the way, it comes with a black nylon sheath that should last as long as it is properly used and cared for.

title: Perfect for Sighting In Small Caliber And Air Guns
text:
This is a purchase that is hard to beat. One hundred large and highly visible targets, each with four bullseyes on them, bringing a total of 400 individual targets to your door for only 25 cents per sheet. These are perfect for sighting in your small caliber weapons or air guns and the included 150 repair stickers extend their usefulness even longer.

I have a simple firing range set up in our backyard that I have used not only for sighting in new guns but also to teach my children gun safety and range etiquette. The key is to only use suppressed weapons and air guns. No outside distractions, no interfering neighbors, plenty of time to do things safely and correctly.

These targets are perfect for that, well-constructed and high quality, colorful and easy to see, and very reasonably priced. Buy them -- you'll like them!

title: God, This Thing Smells Good.  Besides That, It's A Great Holster Too!
text:
I had heard of Relentless Tactical before I started looking for an OWB holster for my Colt Defender. When I found it listed on Amazon with 240 reviews giving it an average rating of 4.8 stars, I followed my own advice to others and relied on the reviews written here. Normally I use an IWB, Belly Band, or pocket holster for concealed carry, but I also wanted to try an outside the waistband holster for a heavier weapon to see how it felt, how well it concealed (without printing or causing discomfort) and how easily it could be deployed.

So this was a new experience for me as I normally carry smaller and lighter firearms since we live in hot and humid Southwest Florida. I've never accidently displayed any weapon by mistake and have never been called out for "printing". I once even tried an experiment with my wife and had her guess what gun I was carrying and where I had it -- either in my cargo pants or tactical long-sleeved shirt. She guessed that I had a NAA .22 magnum in my right front pocket (Sticky Holster) only because she knew that I had carried one there for over 30 years. What she missed were the three.380's and three 9mm's that I had concealed in two ankle holsters, a Belly Band, another Sticky Holster, and two IWB's (appendix and 6 o'clock).

Now I'm breaking in this Relentless Tatical leather OWB holster which I can use in winter under jackets and in summer under untucked short-sleeved shirts. The holster is extremely well-made, is comfortable to wear, and fits my Defender perfectly. The price is on the money and there's just something about that new leather smell that still gets to me. Not many holsters have 240 reviews written about them. That alone says a lot about how the concealed carry market has recognized and put their stamp of approval on this piece of gear. Give it a fair trial, get used to it, and it it isn't your cup of tea just send it back within the 30 day trial window. I don't think that you'll be disappointed.

title: You've Gotta Have The Best Tools If You're Going To "Do It Yourself".
text:
Back in 1994 when I bought my waterfront property in Southwest Florida the first bid I got to (legally) trim my mangroves was $1,000.00. Even then I thought that the price was outrageous and I decided to do it myself. Needless to say it involves a lot of time and and some really good cutting tools (and skills). There's not a lot of room for maneuvering in the wetlands, the footing is hazardous, the flora and fauna always a challenge (most Florida plants either have thorns or some type of poison), and the bugs can drive you nuts. Now that I think about it, maybe the $1,000.00 would have been money well spent.

Now at age 67 the current bid for the same job is up to $8,000.00. Either the workers are a lot smarter or they don't really want to do this type of work. About 10 years ago I had some major surgery and had to hire three people to do the job for me. When I was watching them the youngest picked up and held a very pretty snake for his father to see, causing me to yell at his father to "put it down". I was really surprised to find out that they didn't know what a coral snake was. That hiring experience also resulted in all of my tools being damaged to the poiint of no return. But the real capper was that they cut the mangroves to a height of 4 feet -- when I had specified 6 feet. Fortunately no one reported me to the mangrove police.

So I have trimmed my own mangroves for 22 of the past 23 years, even at my advanced age. The secret is to keep your eyes and ears open, to use adequate insect repellant and sun protection, wear boots, long pants and long sleeves, and an SPF 50 hat. But the key to being able to trim mangroves for up to six hours at a time is to have a really good medium length machete. This CRKT Chanceinhell(CIH) really fits the bill. It has a durable, heavy and sharp blade, a well-constructed rubber grip for comfort, and a decent sheath that you can hang from your belt when you are using a different tool. This machete is blade heavy which gives you better balance for chopping versus slicing.

When I have the room to swing a machete, I rely on an Esee Lite machete (around $80.00), a blade perfect for slicing thicker wood. For the crowded areas where taking a full swing would be impossible (or foolhardy) I find chopping to be more efficient and safer. That is where the CIH hits the mark and is the best tool to use. You might wonder why I don't use a small chainsaw instead. There are a multitude of reasons: the high noise level masks other sounds that I need to be aware of ( like the movement of snakes, alligators and other critters), chainsaws are dangerous even when operating in the best of conditions (which is far from true in the wetlands), the probability of bounce-back or dropping a running chainsaw is pretty much guaranteed, and trucking in and out of the wetlands to refuel sets you up for additional problems.

So this year I'll be heading into the wetlands with my Chanceinhell and Esee, splitting my time between slicing and chopping, hoping to avoid any injuries. One thing that I can guarantee is that the experience is always interesting.

title: Something Wicked This Way Comes!
text:
When I first opened the soft case that this knife came in my initial response was "WOW". What a beautiful looking piece of art! Brian Tighe is a highly respected knife innovator with 30 years of experience and valuable tactical expertise. He specializes in making top-quality custom tactical knives that start in the mid-$500's and go up into the thousands of dollars. If you call up his website you will see why he is so highly regarded.

This is Mr. Tighe's first collaboration with Spyderco and he has hit a home run. Unfortunately some of Spyderco's collaborations with famous knife makers come in as a disappointment, not as dramatic as the maker is capable of, somewhat dull and often under-built. Not this Tighe Stick however. It is a real beauty. The picture on the Amazon product page doesn't do it justice. The solid titanium scales give a real 3D appearance to the handle that is perfectly accented by the beautifully cut and sharp blade. This knife fits my (somewhat) large hand as though built for it and inspires instant confidence in the holder. I am not a knife fighter but the tactical aspects of this knife practically scream "look out".

And look out you should when handling the blade. It conquers the paper test like it's not even there. The tip of the blade is obviously sharp enough to pierce just about any material and there is absolutely no blade slop (wobble) when the blade is extended. I like carrying large knives to know that I can handle just about any project it is subjected to. On the other hand, this thing is so darn beautiful that it might end up in a display case with some of my other curved blades. If you want to own an excellent example of a Spyderco collaboration, this is your knife.

I was fortunate to pick this up 'on sale' at a specialty knife seller and had to post this review to let prospective customers know what a great build and value this knife is. Now if I can only find a Spyderco Brend-PireIa Mamba on sale I will be one happy collector.

title: The Price/Performance Ratio Is Easily On Your Side
text:
We live in hot and humid Southwest Florida and I have blond hair and blue eyes, a perilous combination in this environment. Since I've already battled a few skin cancers and have to undergo an annual skin peel by my Dermatologist, I try to be extra careful when working outside on our landscaping. The UPF 50+ is important to me as are the flaps that can be positioned to cover both all sides of my neck and my face. Even with this hat on I continue to use 50+ lotion protection on my nose and face, reapplying it every 60 minutes. If I posted a picture of my face during a skin peel you would quickly understand why I'm so much more careful now.

The material used in this hat is very flimsy and is easily moved about by any wind. However it is easy to wash and takes up very little space when packing for a trip. If this Jitty hat is indeed providing the degree of protection specified in the product description, then buying it for only $9.99 is a great deal. While it may tear easily if it gets snagged on something, the cost of replacing it is minimal. Good deal all the way around.

title: An Efficient, Well Designed, And Effective Lamp
text:
I wish that we would have had six of these when Hurricane Irma knocked out our power for six days. They are compact, cast enough light to read by in total darkness, and function perfectly as a night light for those quiet evenings when you're trying to get your mind around what just happened. The second of the three intensities is almost as bright as the highest setting and would be suitable for just about anything short of reading. Just make sure to have a bunch of AA batteries handy.

Compact battery powered LED lanterns are safer , much easier to use, and cast more light than any candle. When you have children around you looking for some safety at night, this pleasant little lamp generates a nice little circle of security and comfort. My only quibble is the price. It would seem to be priced more realisticly at around $10.00.

title: Evasion And Extraction -- This Hawk Is Built For Action.
text:
For what it is, and for the price I paid, this is a sturdy and well-made full tang hawk that will blow through most things that get in its way. It is elegantly designed as a working tool to help get you out of tight spots. Being a one piece chunk of steel with a comfortable handle fastened to the shaft with four bolts, this is not a flimsy tool that will fly apart when confronted with heavy work. It is well-balanced and comfortable to hold with either one or two hands. It's also big enough to allow choking up if you need more control and a shorter stroke.

Its uses are virtually endless. Because of its solid construction and reasonable price, I wouldn't hesitate to use it in any situation. The chances of this breaking are slim and even if it does, you're only out about $30.00. Very few tomohawk makers have a straight spike on the opposite end of the blade. There are a few situations that I can think of where you would use the spike but would have to rapidly pull it out before striking again. It won't do you any good to kill a zombie and have your hawk stuck in its skull. Of course that would only happen with a fresh one, an older model will be brittle and your spike should blow right through it.

This hawk came sharp but didn't pass the paper test. A little extra elbow grease and that can be rectified. It's weight might be a little restrictive for people without much arm strength and it might be a bear to carry all day if hiking. The sheath that comes with it will cover the axe head and ride on your belt. Just don't expect that to work too well for you. This ideally would be carried in your vehilcle and used when unexpected circumstances arise. Even if you don't know what you're doing with it, just holding it will inspire confidenc. And often times attitude can be the tipping point in getting any job done.

title: Who Cares About What Color You Get -- These Are Great!
text:
I have had two of these Hyskore 6 Gun Pistol Racks for some time now and needed to add two more for the additional pistols/revolvers I have collected. The original models came in black and were elegant in function and design. Although these were supposed to be OD Green, they came in a gray color. Either that or my ability to distinguish colors has declined like everything else as I get older.

For this very reasonable price, this modular system is easily added to my existing racks. In fact, it is just a matter of lining them up next to each other. I appreciate the design because the foam used cushions the pistols without marring the finish, it does not absorb moisture or lubricants, and they can hold a wide variety of pistols/revolvers.

If you looked at my current display you would see an orderly presentation of various sized firearms ranging in size from an Uzi Pistol and Desert Eagle .44 Magnum to a Colt Pocket Nine and a Glock 42. Not only are all of them adequately protected but the display itself almost looks professional -- even with such a wide variation in pistol size.

So to heck with the color. Anyone focusing on the guns will not pay any attention to racks that they may be different colors. These modular pistol racks are great for organizing, displaying, and protecting your firearms. At a price of $15.99 for the six gun model they are cheap. Consider buying several!

title: BAD TO THE BONE
text:
My knife collection is kind of eclectic. I prefer big, heavy, sturdy, "do it all" knives, but I also buy unique and unusual blades. Anything from a Busse Gladius to Rob Dalton OTF automatics. I enjoy handing an odd knife to a friend and watching them puzzle out how to open the darn thing (safely). Well-made but unusual knives don't typically sell well so they tend to appreciate over time.

I knew that I had a hit on my hands when I picked up the box holding this Bad Blood Dreadnaught folder. It was hefty in that satisfying way that tells you to expect to find something substantial inside when you open it up. And it was just what I expected. If it were a dog, I would name it something like "Chunk" or "Tank". The over-sized grip has finger grooves cut into it that fit my hands perfectly. The blade is a big chunk of steel that looks like it can handle any task easily. The flipper makes (one-handed) deployment swift and smooth and the blade locks up tight immediately. There is just a little (tiny) bid of blade play when it's locked -- so tiny that it hardly bears mentioning. Right out of the box the blade passes the paper test. Be careful!

This is my first Bad Blood knife and it has impressed me enough (at only $21.96) that I plan to keep my eyes open for any new models. Yes, it's made in China but obviously to exacting standards. The design, materials, and construction resemble that of a knife costing in excess of $100.00. I can hardly believe the value you get for only $21.96. I never thought that I would spend such a reasonable amount of money to add a knife to my collection. Get one (or two) while you can.

title: Very Unusual Knife With Rainbow Colors
text:
This Boker Magnum Flipper was made in China. Well made I might add. Since I'm used to composite handles, I was surprised how much this steel knife weighed but it feels good in the hand. I don't normally go for "ornate" knives, preferring instead thick bladed workhorses that will do the tough jobs over and over without fail. But now I've started looking for unusual knives that everyone else doesn't have.

This thing is heavy which isn't a bad thing. You can get an excellent grip on it and the scale and blade work are functional and attractive. This flipper works a little differently, requiring you to hold the knife upside down and pushing the flipper as you snap the knife in a downward motion. It deploys rapidly and locks up tight. No blade "slop" in this $35.00 knife. The design and coloring is a bit outrageous but that results in not every collector having one. I always keep in mind that the more unpopular a good knife is in the marketplace, the more it might be worth in the future. And if it doesn't appreciate, your friends and neighbors are bound to notice how it stands out compared to the other knives in your collection.

Boker is a well-respected German knife maker who sometimes farms out their designs and specifications to some of the emerging countries. This particular knife came in an aluminum presentation box with an outer cardboard sleeve. It was wrapped in plastic and fits in a molded form in the box. It comes with instructions on how to register your knife with Boker. In case you don't speak English well, it also comes in three other languages. It's getting to the point that quality knife companies are out-sourcing their products more and more. The cheap manufacturers are losing ground to quality producers who build each design to spec with the best materials. Remember when "Made In Japan" meant that the product was probably a cheap piece of junk? Several of the emerging countries are now earning the respect of high quality companies. That makes it a win-win for the consumer and the company.

title: I Believe In The KISS Addage -- And This Ain't It
text:
When I pulled it out of the box I thought that Amazon had sent me a labeler --you know what I mean, you pull the handle and a label with the price on it is placed on a product. Lots of moving parts which of course implies that several things can go wrong with it.

Using it is much better than simply loading your magazines by hand, especially if you're as old as I am and have started to lose the strength in my fingers. Arthur Itis also comes to visit fairly often and this Caldwell Universal Pistol Magazine Loader really takes the stress off my hands.

On the other hand (pun intended), it is much more complicated than the Maglula UbLULA Magazine Loader. The UbLULA is a bit cheaper, is way simpler and faster to use, and pretty much seems to be the standard in the industry. Don't just take my word for it. Currently there are about 15,000 reviews on Amazon with an average rating of 4.9 stars. That is almost unbelievable!!!

title: An Inexpensive Solution To Avoiding A Big Problem
text:
These Tipton .380 Snap Caps are the perfect solution for helping to break in the trigger on my new Glock 42. Glocks are known to be tight as far as tolerances and do require some time and effort to break them in (both the slide and trigger) to smooth out the operation. Of course the trigger action on Glocks are a bit different from other pistols and require some practice to get used to the staging and length of pull. When you park your butt in front of the TV at night, try to get off about 50 trigger pulls using the snap caps. When you tire of that, switch to racking the slide 25 times to help loosen that up.

These Snap Caps allow you to dry fire your pistol without causing any damage to your firing pin and the repetitive practice will help you to learn how to become comfortable with the trigger pull. After you feel comfortable with the function of the trigger and slide, it's time to hit the range. Glocks (and most pistols) need a few hundred rounds through the gun for a good break in. If it doesn't function like you want it to, as not all guns are perfect for all people, get yourself on Glock's blog and see what your alternatives are. There may be a quick fix for your problem or you may need to switch to another brand. Good luck!

title: Better Quality Than I Was Expecting -- Great Value For The Money
text:
Working outside in sunny and humid Southwest Florida requires a lot of protection from the sun and bugs -- especially as you get older. I ordered this particular boonie type hat because it offered a wide brim, UV protection (SPF 50), adjustability, and mesh covers over the breathing holes. The mesh covered holes are a nice touch during our 95 degree plus days because they keep the bugs out while still allowing a bit of air to circulate under the hat.

I wore my last boonie hat until it virtually rotted. When I removed this new hat from the packaging I was immediately impressed with the quality of the construction and the vividness of the colors (Military Green). There is no question that this new Micoop Wide Brim Military Camouflage Hat is a big step up in quality from my old boonie. The material is thicker, the grommets for the breathing holes are properly anchored, and the adjustable chin strap makes it easy to get a comfortable fit.

My normal hat size is 7 3/8. While this particular hat runs big, it can be adjusted to fit properly. Combining that with all the other features and you end up with a great hat for the money. As an added bonus, when I tried it on for my kids at the dinner table, they said that they couldn't see me when I had it on. I guess that the camouflage works too!

title: A Great Tool for The Average Warrior
text:
First off I have to say that I bought this Cold Steel Recon Tanto from another source at half of the price offered on Amazon. But after removing it from the packaging and handling it for a while, I can tell you that even at the Amazon price, this is a great value. Yes, you can buy a better version of this knife from Jake Hoback, but you will be spending almost three times the money for incremental improvements. In my case, I would have had to pay five times the money. Like most collectors I have several "safe queens" but at this price I don't feel bad about using and abusing this well-made tool.

Your first glance at this knife will confirm its utilitarian/industrial good looks. It is obviously a knife that is built strongly to be used in tough tasks. Don't bother confirming the blade sharpness with the paper cutting test, you can simply look at the edge under a good light and see the small serrations that line the cutting edge. If you want to be bold and test it with your finger, TREAD LIGHTLY! Cold Steel has taken a thick piece of steel and tapered it into a razor-sharp blade. You will even be able to feel the small serrations pulling at your skin as you touch the edge.

Good useful length, full tang, great balance, sticky rubber grip, this tool inspires great confidence when you hold it. Take a look at some of the posted videos to see what types of abuse this knife has been subjected to and survived handily. If I had to leave our home suddenly and enter the woods and swamp lands of Southwest Florida, I'd probably select my Busse Hellrazor to take with me. On the other hand, if I showed up at a rendezvous point with a Cold Steel Recon Tanto, no one would laugh at me. They know better.

PS: A decent (not great) kydex sheath is included. If you're like me, you don't like a sheath hanging off your belt that can catch on various objects and/or make noise while you're trying to be quiet. A simple band threaded through the lower part of the sheath will keep it secure against your thigh.

title: Necessity Is The Mother Of Invention
text:
It never ceases to amaze me how thoughtful and adaptable we humans are. Well, maybe I can't include myself in that category, but some people are incredibly intuitive when confronted by a need or a problem. This Alloy Rifle QD Sling Mount and Swivel is an elegant solution to those wanting to mount a sling to a rifle that is not designed for one.

This tool is sturdy, strong, simple to attach/detach, and is priced very reasonably. If it doesn't work for you, and I don' t know why it wouldn't, you can always send it back to the company under their money back guarantee.

title: Cold Steel -- Andrew Demko -- Tri-Ad Lock:  Three Phrases To Pay Attention To
text:
Cold Steel normally does a pretty good job of designing and bringing to market robust products at reasonable prices. I collect bladed weapons and am always looking for the unusual. It's my experience that the more unusual items tend to rise in value since not as many are made. This Cold Steel Frenzy II is probably going to fall into that niche. Not everyone is going to like this look.

When I first removed it from the box I clearly saw and felt the heavy steel and robust construction of the knife. Opening the Tri-Ad lock the first time required patience and pretty good hand strength. The Tri-Ad locking mechanism is well known for its reliable and strong mechanics. Consequently it took some proper oiling and repetitive opening/closing to finally smooth out the action.

The blue and black sculpted G-10 handle is long and thin, requiring more of a "wrap around" grip. The way that the grip is contoured and constructed results in your hand being forced to mold to the front of the handle, leaving about 2" of the handle poking out from behind your hand. In all, it just feels kind of strange, but the long handle is necessary to properly secure the 5.5" blade when folded. I expected this knife to be blade heavy but you will see by looking at the picture below that it is fairly well balanced for such a long knife.

The blade came sharp enough to pass the paper cutting test, putting me on notice that there wasn't much margin for error to avoid being cut. When extended from the handle, the blade does not have any play (wiggle). This is a solid piece of construction. The total length of this knife is 12.25", it has a solid pocket clip, there is a lanyard hold at the very end, and the overall look and feel screams "look out, the big boy is here".

It is somewhat odd looking and you will probably either love it or hate it. However you will not be able to quibble with the obvious quality. Anyone wanting the capability of a 12" fixed blade knife packaged instead as a folder will be impressed. It is strong, it is radical sharp, and I wouldn't want to be facing it in a fight -- unless of course I brought a gun to a knife fight.

title: "Beware The Old Man In A World Where Men Die Young"
text:
I have gone back to a wheel gun for concealed carry because I can't afford the one time that I might need to use my defensive weapon and have it jam. I know, I know! The modern semi autos are basically fool proof and malfunctions only happen occasionally. And I know that even with a subcompact you can easily carry 8-10 rounds of whatever, but I learned a long time ago that the more moving parts in any machine/tool, the more potential problems can happen -- and usually at the worst possible time. (Thank you Mr. Murphy).

My new defensive carry is a Smith & Wesson Model 327 2" Performance Center that holds eight rounds of 38 Special/ 38 +P/357 Magnum. It is a rather large revolver made of scandium and has a large grip which fits my hand perfectly. I'm a big guy so it's really no problem to conceal and the 2" barrel should make it qualify (in court) as a defensive weapon should I have to use it. My backup is a Ruger LCR in 357, a light and tiny gun that is a devil to shoot full power loads in. Fortunately I'm a big fan of 44 magnums and am comfortable handling a lot of recoil. Why the Ruger LCR as backup? There's nothing like redundancy in personal defense. A second gun using the same ammo covers most of the bases.

The result is that I can carry two revolvers loaded with a total of 13 rounds -- equaling or surpassing any of the subcompact/compact autos -- that will both go "Bang" when needed. And, and this is a big "And", any family member or passerby will also be able to operate either one of them should I be in trouble/incapacitated. All you have to do is pull the trigger. The alternative is a semi auto that might pose operating difficulty to whomever tries to be of assistance. There won't be enough time to lecture anyone on the operating mechanics of a semi auto.

So I picked up two QuickStrips and this pouch. Putting in two of the strips, one facing up and one facing down, creates a relatively slim package holding an additional ten rounds -- on top of the thirteen already loaded in the two revolvers. The total of 23 rounds should be enough for 99% of the potential situations encountered in most areas. I try to keep myself out of dangerous areas/predicaments (situational awareness), but if I have to enter one I will have a Glock 19 as my backup. A good man knows his limitations.

title: A Good Value For $18.78
text: Wider strap than usual makes this more comfortable to use with a relatively heavy weapon.  Mine is mounted on a CZ Scorpion and makes the extra weight of the accessories more manageable for long hauls.  Of course it looks good too.  This a well constructed piece using good quality materials.  In a pinch, the nylon cordage could come in very handy.

title: It's Better To Have Them And Not Need Them Than To Need Them And Not Have Them
text:
This is a great way to carry extra ammo for your concealed carry weapon. They are easy to load, lie flat in your pocket, and easy to take out when reloading. It sure beats using a bulky speed loader. Yes, the speed loader is quicker, but your chances of needing more than eight shots to defend yourself is minimal.

Eight shots you ask? I bit the bullet (so to speak) and purchased a Smith and Wesson .357 Magnum Model 327 Performance Center, an eight shot revolver. It is a scandium snub nose that holds .38 specials, 38 + P, and .357 magnums. Light but bulky, it fits my large hands well and the recoil (even under full magnum loads) is manageable. Expensive but unique, it is a gun that will become a collector item in the future. Not many revolvers can hold eight large bullets.

And yes, it is a wheel gun for personal protection. My first gun purchase 41 years ago was a Ruger Blackhawk in .44 magnum, carried while salmon fishing in Alaska. I also own a Smith and Wesson .44 magnum Alaskan, another snub nose revolver. So recoil isn't an issue for me. Why a revolver instead of one of the excellent semi autos out there? If I ever need to use it to protect myself or my family, I need to know that it will go BANG when I pull the trigger. I also need to know that my spouse can use it without fumbling around.. Just aim it and pull the trigger. And then again, and again. The simplicity and "bullet proof" action inspires confidence -- especially when you find yourself in a very stressful situation.

My backup piece is also a revolver that will handle the same three calibers. Just in case. Kinda like wearing a belt and suspenders. Redundancy is not a bad thing in personal protection.

title: Perfect Match If Your EDC Is A Stainless PARA Warthog
text:
Not familiar with the PARA Warthog? It is a short, stubby, relatively heavy .45 acp semi auto pistol available in stainless steel.. While it won't win any beauty contests, it has a presence all its own and the intimidation factor it provides is awesome. It's the kind of weapon that when you run out of ammo you can hit your opponent in the face with it for the game winner.

This ZT 0456 has that kind of look to it. It has some (short and stubby) curves but the overall construction is what draws attention to itself. Yes, it is a bit on the (slightly) heavy side, but this knife wasn't designed to be slim and beautiful. It is designed to work, and work hard, taking on any task from cutting to prying that you come up against. How many knives do you have in your collection that can be carried in your pocket, can dispatch any simple cutting jobs with aplomb, and then allow you to pry open a door with it. Most EDC blades don't have the spine for it, much less the overall design and build that would allow even attempting that task.

As I have aged I have learned that a knife should be much more than just a cutting tool. None of my automatic knives can even approach the type of hard work that this Zero Tolerance knife can conquer. The blade is sharp but heavy, the locking mechanism is tight and solid, and the flipper works like butter. People notice it when I pull it from my pocket, not just because it's a knife but because of the attractive and unique design. Everyone wants to know what it is, how much it costs, and where can they "legally" get one. This is one of those places.

title: There Is No Perfect Tactical Shirt -- But This One Is Getting Closer
text:
I am a fan of the Blackhawk Warrior Lightweight Tactical Short Sleeve shirt, owning a few in each of the four offered colors. The Warrior shirt is made of a heavier material and is almost as flexible and handy as a tool box. It has two large front pockets that have Velcro fasteners. The right one has a smaller pocket inside it and also an opening at the top to slide a pen in. The left side pocket has a deep zippered pocket inside it and a ring hanging off the side for hanging your sunglasses. There is also a zippered pocket on the lower left side of the shirt that would be hidden if you tuck your shirt inside your pants/shorts.

On the left sleeve is a smaller pocket to carry anything up to about 5 inches long. Buttons are used to fasten the shirt. Although you can see through the material when you hold it up to the sun, it is heavy material (100% Polyester) and gets pretty warm in sunny Southwest Florida. The heavier material does keep the shirt looking crisp longer but the cut is pretty boxy as far as shape. There are three eyelets below the back of the collar for ventilation. An interesting feature is that the three vent holes are covered with mesh to keep biting insects out, a great feature for our climate. All-in-all the Blackhawk Warrior is a durable shirt that is double sewn and should last you a long time.

What about this new Tac Convertible Long Sleeve shirt? It appears to be mostly an improvement on the Warrior shirt. Although it is also made of 100% Polyester, it is significantly lighter and easier to see through if you hold it up to the sun. The fabric is designed to dry quickly and offers UPF 50 protection. The material is soft and the Teflon Shield+ fabric protector repels water, oil, and stains. It is more tailored than the Warrior shirt and definitely cooler to wear. It might run a little larger than stated size but the tailoring keeps ir from looking too large.

This shirt fastens with snaps instead of buttons although buttons are used for the collar and sleeves. Even though this comes as a long sleeved shirt you can turn it into a three-quarter sleeve shirt by folding the fabric up and buttoning it. Nice touch that! If you're in the hot sun it would be cooler with the sleeves buttoned up yet when night falls and the bugs come out you can simply revert to long sleeves. There are two large main (Velcro fastened) pockets on the top front of this shirt. Each of these two pockets has a zippered side document pocket behind it. There is a vent in the back to help keep you cool but in a pinch you could also roll up your boonie hat and carry it there.

I admit to not knowing what a "break away snap placket" is, and I plead ignorance in not understanding why there are two upside down mesh pockets (inside the front of the shirt) which could be used to great advantage if they had fasteners or were mounted in reverse. They might be used to provide extra stability by covering a holstered gun but perhaps I just don't understand the intention of the design. I'm sure that someone out there will enlighten me.

title: Great Value For Only $5.94
