title: Temper the Cooler Before Filling and Your Food Will Stay Colder Longer
text:
Having owned one of these for a few years I feel more than qualified to review this.

- To the people who say it doesn't work, first "temper" the cooler. That means you bring it inside, put cold items in it and let it sit. I temper mine for several days before use.
- Second, use block ice. I use the square ice cream containers from Wally-World. They pack nicely, stack nicely and are easy for me to get in my freezer to make the blocks. Barring that, keep the ice you guy in bags. The greater the ice mass, the less quickly it melts. I also use water bottles filled close to the top. I'll freeze them, cap them after they're frozen and put them in the cooler. You've a double use: ice and cold water when it melts.
- Third, make sure the products you put in the cooler start out cold. Again, the colder they are, the longer they'll stay cold.
- Fourth, don't expect anything in direct sunlight or on hot ground to stay cold. If you need, park this on a couple blocks of wood to get it off the ground and get air flow under it. Hot ground will eventually cause the cooler to become hot. Insulation doesn't care whether it's keeping cold things cold or hot things hot. If you get it hot, it'll start making things inside hot.
- Lastly, if you have water and still have ice, that COLD water makes a good conductor of cool temperatures. If you drain the water you're not doing yourself a favor. You should have your foods in ziplock bags for best protection.

I've used this cooler on an extended trip to the Sequoias from Eastern Washington State. This rode in the back of my pick up with only a tarp for shade. The trip south took three days (owing to stops at family and friends). No additional ice required. Once at the campground, still no ice required.
We were at the campground a week. After that week we did drain off excess and add more ice. The return trip was through Lake Tahoe on to Nevada, staying at Carson City for three days, over to Oregon - staying in Ontario, OR and then back home. Yup, most of the ice had melted, but the larger pieces kept the water cold.

If you take care of your cooler, it should take care of you. The handle is nice and wide with an easy grip. The wheels move nicely and everything feels comfortable when pulling it along.

title: Nice, But Be Warned, Definitely Not a "Regular" Card
text: It's finally happened.  Here's a set I wish I hadn't gone through the trouble of buying.  The SPx set shows a divided front with the player's photo in upper left half and the team logo and player's number in the lower right half.  These are some thick cards, and that's good, but I'm not really impressed with them.  The photo's are harder to see than a standard card's photo.

title: Fantastic Reservoir, Easy Fill, Easy Clean
text:
Having owned several bags over the years I was really pleased to get this Platypus Big Zip. Not only is filling so much easier but cleaning and air drying as well.

The only negative comment I have is that I paid much more than this price when I bought mine. And not only have I bought one, I've bought two!

title: Very Comfortable in Hand and Locking Devices Hold Tight
text:
When something says, in essence, you get what we pick for color, you've got to take a chance on it. I was lucky in that I got blue poles. These are very good condition, lock well and are comfortable in the hand. I'm not really certain about the "foot," but I suppose I'll get used to it. It is definitely not something I've come across before in the poles I have elected to use.

Stansport Trekking Poles are known for their locking ability. I have tried intentionally and unsuccessfully to get them to fail. They just seem to lock well. Hikers know, it DOES make a difference. I've had a pole fail while I was crossing a river with a very heavy pack on my back.

I can't wait to really put these things through their paces.

title: Large and Awesome Hawvuhd Pennant
text:
We got this pennant for my son's "cubie" in his computer programming class at a Technical Skills Center where I teach culinary arts. This is a fairly large pennant and looks awesome. His aspirations are to attend Hawvuhd Law and this pennant will be a reminder to him to bust his heinie getting there.

The colors are bright and everything is just right.

title: Heavy Duty but Much Darker than the Photo Shows
text:
The actual cup is much darker in color than what is shown in the photo. Also, and because of the darkness and the "splatter effect", the emblem is somewhat difficult to see. However, on the defense to that, the emblem is etched in the cup. This is a VERY HEAVY cup and feels to be extremely high quality.

It is because of the color and difficultness to view the emblem I have chosen to give this a Four Star review.

title: This Package Had the Exact Players I Wanted Cards From
text:
As a diehard Maple Leafs fan I recently began buying and collecting autographed hockey pucks. I wanted a good card to go with it. I saw this, et voilà, sold! This package had exactly the players I wanted: Nazem Kadri, Colby Armstrong, Tyler Bozak, all of whom I have pucks from.

Additionally, this package had cards from players I felt the Leafs should have never traded, but c'est la vie, I'm not in charge of anything there.

What I can say about this is the cards are first rate and I will likely look for more from different years.

title: Don't Believe the Hype
text:
I bought three of these bottles for a backpacking trip. They do NOT keep the water any colder than anything else. In fact, they were good for about a couple hours at best case.

On the plus side, the opening was the exact size as my water filter. I didn't have to filter into one and transfer the water. I could screw the filter on, pump it a couple of times and have it filled.

title: Easier Than Gas Grills
text:
If you have one thing for your charcoal grill, this should be it. These chimney starters are the best thing going to get your charcoal ready to roll. It's surprising to me that these haven't been around for ages. The design is simple, it takes only a piece or two of newspaper, a lighter and charcoal to get it going.

Using this, I've changed my mind (again) about gas grills. THIS is easier than gas!

title: Great Product, Crappy Quality Control
text: I love the Toronto Maple Leafs. In my family this is no secret. My son saw this and had my wife buy it under her private account for my Father's Day gift. I love it. So why only three stars? The TML Leaf is printed askew on the cup. C'mon people. Where's your quality control? And, while I'm at it, the company sticker was placed over top the NHL hologram.

title: Impressively Constructed
text:
Edit: 08/16/15: One point and comment the needs clarified: this waistband, when tightened to its fullest is still bigger than a 34" waist. Nowhere in the description is that noted, only that it supports up to a 48" waist.

Original review: This lumbar pack has was we needed: two water bottle holders. The pockets in the pack are all lined as if you could easily put a lunch in there with a freezer gel pack to keep it cold.

I'm certainly impressed with the hip padding and nice wide straps. Speaking of straps, the bottle pockets each have straps to cinch down. That too is impressive.

title: Quite Happy with this Purchase
text:
Edit: Dropping One Star (6/3/2015)
After seeing the little icon "T" flashing, I attempted to download the information according to their procedures. For whatever reason, the Omron Tri-Axis does not seem to want to share the information with my computer. I've tried numerous times. The computer recognizes that the drive is there but downloading the data hasn't happened. I'll attempt to do so a few more times and eventually just call it a day.

I'm not sure that I should do a review based on just one day's usage, but here goes:
· Setting up was much easier than I had anticipated. Even after screwing up my height and continuing on I was able to get back to the proper spot to make the necessary correction without losing information already inputted.
· The pedometer tracks your movement for four seconds then begins adding steps. Not to worry, steps taken during those four seconds are added as well. Downside, if you do movement that DOESN'T last at least four seconds, it's lost to you and those steps do no count for anything.
· The clip is secure to the pedometer but it actually did slip off my belt once while at home. If a leash or tether is provided, I sure didn't see it. While hiking the pedometer felt secure and seemed to do exactly what it was supposed to do.
· The instructions seem more complicated than they actually are. I believe it's a case if too much info in the form of written instructions AND diagrams.

Overall, I'mvery happy with this purchase. I had considered several far more expensive items. In some respects, newer isn't necessarily always better.

title: Well Crafted Flies
text: As a newbie to fly fishing I'm more about learning technique than I am trying my own flies.  When I see something like this with good reviews, I'm in it.  As it turns out, these are some incredibly good looking flies.  I can't wait to get a chance to put them to work.

title: Not As Good As Expected
text:
I was actually surprised by the smallness of the actual pouch. Having owned another messenger bag, [[ASIN:B002TUSSY4 UTG Multi-functional Tactical Messenger Bag]], this bag has only the waist/hip strap in its favor. The waist strap is the ONLY reason I bought this anyway. Had the UTG bag had one, I'd been a happy camper from the get-go.

Adjustment is fairly easy. I know many have thought this to be a good bag for Concealed Carry, personally I had intended to use this bag for short (less than 10 miles) hiking trips. This bag has no place for water bottles which also makes it kind of pointless for the function which I had intended.

It appears to be constructed decently. The stitching seemed secure and I didn't notice loose ends anywhere. I'll take it out for a trip, but I'm not expecting much from it.

title: Bass Set Looks to be Worthwhile
text: I bought this to add to my son's ever growing tackle box.  The South Bend items seem to look good and be in good repair.  There were no misshapen pieces in the kit.  With six lures, the price per piece works out to about $2.00 each.  It's not the cheapest, but it certainly isn't bad.

title: Nice Beginner Bass Fishing Kit
text:
As with all the Ready 2 Fish products, this has a nice assortment for bass fishing. Included are:
· Various colored rubber worms,
· Hooks,
· Leaders.

This is not an all inclusive set but a small kit with which you add and subtract as needed.

title: Ruggedly Constructed, Comfortable to Use
text:
I bought this soft bag for my son as he fishes with a baitcaste and I use a fly rod. I own a similar Plano bag as well as the appropriate Plano tackle box. This will allow us to load the tackle box as needed then each withdraw the appropriate Plano boxes for our own type of fishing.

The construction is rugged yet comfortable. There's more than plenty room inside the bag. Again it will be easy to load and unload uaing the Plano tackle box for a "bank".

title: Decently Tied Flies
text:
Ten flies costing, at the price of buying 03/15, about 75¢ each. Considering I don't tie my own flies that's a bargain.

The flies look to be pretty decently tied. I see no stray ornaments in the box. That's a good sign.

title: Lightweight and Rugged Holster.  Perfect for my Springfield XD9
text:
I was impressed with both the lightweight and rugged construction of this holster. I had been improvising by using a holster owned by my son for one of his Airsoft pistols. This is far better. My 4" Springfield XD9 fits here perfectly. (Sometimes finding holsters for the 4" is more difficult than for the smaller barrels.)

As someone else had reported, this holster, and especially using the supplied clip, is perfect for use with the [[ASIN:B003Z0HA1E 5.11 Tactical Operator 1 3/4-Inch Belt]] which I also own and use specifically when hiking, backpacking, camping and going out just plinking. When things go together like that, life's much better.

The weapon my be drawn by either releasing the Velco strap or popping open the snap. This holster is not made to used for concealed carry and that's fine by me. My philosophy is if someone sees me with a weapon at my side, that's already a deterrent.

title: Nice, Heavy Duty, Bag Great for Hauling Weapons to the Range
text:
This is a pretty sweet bag. It features metal pull tabs and nylon zippers. The bag clip is HUGE. It's large enough to use with gloved hands to get it opened. (Yeah, I checked.) There's plenty of compartments. The single sling is wide and padded and is not like any razor strap.

We will be using this to carry our Springfield XD9 and Taurus 38 Special pistols plus ammo and earmuffs when taking it to the range.

Nice bag! If I had a need for another, I'd be on it N-O-W!

title: 96 Flies in 4 Different Styles
text:
I'm not an expert on fishing flies by any means. These, from a quick look, appear to be fairly decent. I did notice loose feathers our some such material in a few places. When they say 96 pieces they are telling the truth. However, those same 96 pieces are merely 24 rows of the same four flies. Again, that's how it looks to me. Maybe and perhaps there are minute differences between the styles that I cannot discern, but it is what it is.

These are Chinese made as evidenced by the Chinese characters in the box top. And no, I cannot read them.

A trip to the water will give these dry flies a test or two. Perhaps they see far better then I know.

title: A Darned Good Little Knife
text:
I was a little apprehensive about buying this knife in the first place. I didn't really NEED it, but it sure looked like a good idea and a good addition to my hiking/backpacking/fly fishing arsenal. First, let me say I was impressed with the quality. As a full piece of steel with a full tang, it is unlikely to separate at any time. While the handle is small owing to the size of the blade, it is still manageable. The handle has a nice big eyelet to which a safely line could be tied or, should one be in the mood, to use as a starter to tie to a branch to make a spear.

The sheath is also much better than I had expected. I had originally thought the sheath was just going to be straight nylon. This is not the case. There is a hard plastic liner within that secures the knife blade and keeps the blade from cutting up the sheath. Also, what looks like a thumb spot from the handle doubles as a non-mechanical locking mechanism within the sheath. It requires a decent tug to pull the knife out. This would certainly curtail accidental fallouts while walking or sprinting.

The nylon strap is both strong and adjustable. Overall, I'm quite impressed with this little gem.

title: Nicely Tied Natural Looking Flies
text: These flies are actually very well tired.  I would venture to say of all the flies I've bought through Amazon, these we're the best.  One downside is they are received in a single small cup-like container.  There is no delineation between hook sizes and fly styles.  For what it's worth, hook sizes looked to be 8, 10 and 12s.

title: Awesome, Comfortable, Warm, Weather Resistant, BRIGHT ORANGE, Jacket
text:
EDIT ORIGINAL 2/23: Yesterday as I was wearing this jacket, I could feel a cold breeze channeled into my pockets. I realized this was from the grommet holes in the pockets to allow the waist tightening cords to be there. If you pull these tight, the breeze reduces/stops. However, if allowed to stay loose, the chill is there.

The North Face Chromium Thermal jacket is a cut above many other similar jackets. The exterior shell reminds me of a neoprene wetsuit. As one of the 2* reviewers reported, the arms ARE long but I felt if anything it was a tad tight.

Regardless, today's weather had rain, sleet, snow and wind and I was toasty warm. I absolutely love the Valencia Orange. It is BRIGHT, sharp looking and guaranteed to be seen.

Normally I would balk at a price such as this, but my wife actually paid a bit more than this asking price.

title: This Kit Offers a Great Generic Freshwater Starter Kit
text:
I know some people have dinged this set less than 5* because they believe it should be more than a starter kit. Personally, that's why I'm giving it 5*s. I bought it as a starter kit for my son.

The basics are here. There's plenty of pieces to get anybody going for genetic fishing. Should you be after trout, for example, I would suggest the [[ASIN:B003ZZ8A0O Eagle Claw Trout Kit]].

title: A Great Addition for Trout Fishing
text:
This is a great little augmentation kit for anyone who plans on trout fishing. All material seem to be in good order.

There are six different lures, weights, swivels and a couple other hooks. Those with decent tackle to start with or those just starting to full their tackle box will find this a useful addition. Eagle Claw is a company with a reputation to keep.

title: Fly Sizes Range from Size 8 to Size 16 and Quality is Straight Forward Top Notch
text:
Flies in this assortment range from Size 8 to Size 16 with the majority being smaller hooks. The quality is top notch. While inspecting the flies, I didn't see a single loose thread or offsized hair. Without a doubt, these are far better than anything I could have tied. (Caveat: I'm an idjut when it comes to tying flies.)

I'm looking forward to taking these out for a dip.

title: Plano Products with Plain Ole Great Quality
text:
This Plano product is the perfect companion for the Plano 3500 Monstrosity of a [[ASIN:B00Q36X9GW 737002 Three Drawer Tackle System]] and any/all 3500 series [[ASIN:B000E39T4Q Stowaway with Adjustable Dividers]] boxes.

Complete with two Stowaway boxes of its own, this pack is loaded with features. There's one width sized inside pockets with a zipper, one exterior front zippered pocket as well as one side pocket with a zipper. The other side has an elasticated mesh pocket suitable for various tools, phone, etc. There's even an elasticated water bottle holder which works in conjunction with the mesh pocket. Should the use as a waist (fanny) pack not appeal, a shoulder strap is included.

Plano just for not disappoint!

title: Great Plano Quality for the 3500 Series Tackle Box or Pack
text:
Plano products have not let me down. Worst case scenarios are boxes and packs tend to be bigger than expected. As long as you know/remember what size box you are working with, you can buy inserts that properly fit. (Not saying that I've had that problem because I've been using the 3500 series.)

Anyway, this box is far more appropriate for non-fly fishing material. The diagonal dividers are best for lures. The compartment dividers are thick and well constructed. The box itself has good latches and you can manipulate up to 13 compartments.

title: Excellent Quality Flies!
text:
Being new to fly fishing, I've managed to amass a great deal of flies within the past six months. Of all the flies I've purchased, these from South Bend seem to show the best quality.

Taking a close look at them I see no loose threads, feathers or the like. All the hooks look to be of good quality and all the eyes on the hooks are clear of glue or any other extraneous substance which might otherwise hinder their use. I'm very glad that I purchased these.
. o O ( Now if they only came in a barbless option for Washington's rivers. )

title: Plano Stowaways Are Plano Good Products
text:
This is a nice four-pack of Stowaways for my large Plano tackle box. These will for perfectly in the empty lower right compartment.

I have been very happy with my recent purchases of Plano products. They seem to actually care about making something of quality.

title: Nice Large Fly Box (For Me to Store More Flies to Lose)
text:
This fly box is the perfect accompaniment to my big ole honkin' Plano tackle box. It looks to hold plenty of flies.

As noted, when this is bought it is the fly box that is being bought. Yes, the visual is misleading, but the sale is for Large Fly Box, not box of flies. One shouldn't ding the product because of that.

title: A Perfectly Sized Case for a 3 Piece Rod and Reel
text:
The TFO Rod and Reel Carrying Case is perfect for my [[ASIN:B000X5Z8J0 Crystal River Fly Fishing Combo Kit]] (purchased from Amazon). There is a compartment for each segment of the rod and the handle segment fits nicely with the reel still attached. That's a serious bonus to me.

The zipper has a nice short lanyard attached so that opening with gloves would not be a problem. The triangular shape of the tube actually cups and cushions the rod segments. Faux lambs wool is sewn into the reel compartment. There's an adjustable sling and a D ring.

This, at least from my perspective, is a very nice carrying case.

title: H-U-G-E!!!
text:
Holy Moly it's HUGE. I had no idea when I bought this tackle box that it was large enough to house several small nations. This tackle box is insanely huge.

There is more than enough storage room that I know there's no way I will currently fill it and I have a lot of flies. My wife commented upon my opening the box, it was large enough to be used as footstool.

The tacklebox shows three boxes in the lower right compartment, these do NOT come with this "kit" sold by Sportco Wholesale and must be purchased separately. The spinner bait racks are provided and must be disengaged from the original form and place into position. This is also true of the compartment separators. (A little youtube googling and I found the information on that. Video at http://youtu.be/2CXehgEBzIE

title: Great Tackle Box with Okay-ish Tackle
text:
This tackle box looks more then adequate to do the job for which it was purchased. The construction seems sound and the box study. All hinges open and closed smoothly and the latch locked securely.

The tackle, however was laughable. When they said 138 pieces that included the count of individual hooks, swivels, and I believe, pieces of lint, fuzz, etc. Granted, I did not buy this solely based on the tackle included, but it was a factor in my selection.

All in all, this box looks as though it will provide my son with a good many years of use.

title: Decent Enough Quality for Being Chinese
text:
I'm by no means a fly tying guy at this point in my fishing "career" so I have to rely on flies tied for me.

These flies are decent enough and even though they all look basically the same, at the rate I lose them it won't make a difference.

Coming directly from Beijing, they do take some time to get here (two weeks) even on the West Coast. If you're not in a hurry and don't tie your own, these seem worth it to me at 33¢ per fly.

title: A Decent Back-Up Rod/Reel Combo
text:
Having finally gotten around to putting this together today, 6 weeks after receipt, I've got the following comments:
- The reel is about the noisiest thing around;
- The reel is plastic;
- You have to put (the supplied) line on the reel;
- You have to tie the tippit line to the fly line;
- The flies are downright cheesy;
- For the price, I'm glad I bought it for a reserve combo.
Just because there's all those negatives doesn't mean I don't like it. As a novice, I'm too dumb to know if there are any other problems. Sometimes ignorance IS bliss.

title: Corland Products Do The Trick
text:
Cortland Professional products are definitely good things to have around the tackle box. Like several other items I've reviewed recently, this item was bought by my wife under her own account for a Christmas present. This review won't show Amazon Verified Purchase, but it certainly was - only under her own account.

The Fly Line cleaning pad looks like it isn't much on the outside. It's a small plastic case which hold what appears to be cotton patches within. You merely wipe your line down and it cleans off all the gunk. I think it also help to keep the line from sinking.

This works well in conjunction with the Cortland Vest Pack Assortment!

title: ALPS Mountaineering Makes Great Under Rated Products!
text:
Having had, and liking, several ALPS Mountaineering products ([[ASIN:B004R7L7YU ALPS OutdoorZ Commander Backpack, 5250 Cubic Inches]] and [[ASIN:B006H1YL1U ALPS Mountaineering Stuff Sack]]), and being in the market for another tent, I chose the 4 Person tent knowing that (1) I'll never really need it to hold four people and (2), I will not be carrying this in my backpack. This tent was specifically bought for car camping.

I like that it has a carry case instead of stuff sack. I'm not quite certain why, but this just seems to make more sense to me. I'm probably less likely to forget the case. I'm also happy with the set up. Instead of sliding poles through a sleeve as several of my other tents do, this is simply a connect the poles, lay them out, put the ends into the stoppers and clip the tent to the poles. It's much easier going up and, if you were in a good location, you really wouldn't need to put in pegs and could freestand.

The one thing about this tent that I didn't like or understand is why they were put a pole under the fly and have you pull the fly up and over the erected tent like that. Honestly, I looked and looked at the instructions and did not see a single thing about that. YouTube came to the rescue in the form of "Mr. Tent".

Since I've not had the opportunity to actually test it out of yet - sure I could put it up in the livingroom and have "Camp InHouse", and I may yet do that, I'm going to leave this review as is and modify it in the future should the need arise. I do not anticipate any problems because I am familiar with the brand, style of tent and my expected usage.

title: Nice Looking Flies at a Decent Price
text: A nice assortment of flies with varying sizes of hooks.  At first look these flies seem well tied and to my eyes offer a degree of lifelike looking critters.  I'd bite.

title: Questionable Materials
text:
On the surface these flies look pretty decent. However, when pinching the barb closed the entire hook end broke off, ricocheted to my forehead and is now lost somewhere in with my couch or carpet. I know the only way I'll find that missing piece will be when I'm least expecting it while walking barefoot.

For something labeled "Hi Qualitg", yes, with the "g", I suppose I can't honestly expect too much.

title: Showing My Support for the Maple Leafs
text:
Edit: January 2015 - the decal peeled at an edge and while driving flew off. Up until then it was a 5* rating.

I'm a Maple Leafs fan from way back. I've always had some kind of decal on my car or truck. Since buying a canopy for my pick up, I needed something else on the back window to show my support for the Make Beliefs.

Go LEAFS GO!!!

title: A Scream for Help Would Be As Useless As a Whisper
text:
Whether your children have ever camped before or not, a whistle should be given to each and every child with the explicit directions of "This is not a toy. This is in case you are lost or feel for your safety.". Far too often established campgrounds are most with the sounds of people's generators, children, animals, music, etc. A scream for help would be as useless as a whisper. A whistle has the ability to be heard over long distances and other man-made and natural noises.

Three blasts from a whistle is the same as an SOS. People, especially emergency and first responders are trained to respond to SOS whistles. These are not toys.

title: Great Trekking and Hiking Pole
text:
Very sturdy hiking pole. My wife and I both have problems hiking. She has ankle and feet issues, I have bad knees. I saw these poles at my local brick and mortar outdoor store a few years back at the end of summer. They were on Going Out Of Stock discount sale. I snapped up three, including one for our son, and let another hiker at work know about them.

I have no idea how many miles I've used my pole. If I were to guess 100, that might be close. I've used it several summers now. Only one time has it let me down, and sadly, it REALLY let me down while crossing a stream. I had thought either the pole had bent our slipped off a rock. Instead, it had collapsed on itself just as I was putting my weight on it. Slash! Right into the water, backpack and all. It turned out the locking device had worked itself loose at the most inopportune time conceivable. No matter, I still give this five stars.

title: Great For Guys, But Not So Great for Women and Their Hips
text:
I bought this ground pad for my wife. While it's definitely suitable for me, there is an issue with her hips and being uncomfortable. So, while it's definitely a good product if you're a guy, it's not really a good product if you're a lady.

I own a decent amount of ALPS equipment and that's the reason I went to them first. They are pretty much a sure bet for quality.

title: Water, Water - Can't Live Without It and This Container Keeps That Water Handy
text:
While some say it's a poorly designed spigot, I've had no problem dealing with it. This is a nicely built 7-gallon rigid water container. Filling this will add 56 lbs to whatever's carrying it, but those are 56 lbs that anybody in their right mind want and need.

This "jug" is the last in my pack-up for camping and first out for use. I don't go on any long trips without it even if I don't plan to use it. Better safe than thirsty. Oh yeah, you could also use it to top off a radiator!

title: Double-sided Case with Individual Clasps
text:
Very satisfied with this case. It is two sided, fits easily into a pocket. It is capable of holding numerous flies on each aide, depending on hook size. Using 12's I have approx 15-20 flies in one section.

Each side of the case has an individual catch/clasp which allows user to open the caae without spilling the undesired aide all over the ground or worse, stream.

In fact, I liked what it looked like so much just from viewing, I bought two.

title: Fantastic Starter Fly Fishing Rig
text:
Wow! Having just taken to fly fishing, I had borrowed gear previously. When I began my search for my own rig I spent numerous hours doing research both online and in mortar and brick stores. After reviewing all my information I landed squarely on this set-up. I couldn't be happier!

Not only did the starter kit arrive weeks before anticipated, but the quality and price were phenomenal. I had specifically looked for a four piece rod so that I could pack it in my backpack for hiking. The size is perfect and weight minimal.

After showing several of my camping friends what I had bought, including one who has not only taken the time to show me how to properly cast, but has loaned me great as well, they were all in agreement about the quality and price.

title: Excellect Selection of Wooly Buggers
text: An excellent selection of wooly buggers.  They seem to be well crafted.  None of my flies looked as though they would be experiencing problems from the start.

title: A Nice Selection of Styles and Sizes
text:
I'm ratger satisfied with both the quantity and range of styles of these flies. I do have to pinch the barb, but I'm sure I'll survive.

The box is actually much larger than I expected - in a good way. The numerous compartments can be adjusted and resized for your particular preferences.

The flies appear to be fairly decent quality for the money.

title: Decent Enough for Dayhikes But Not Much More
text:
Columbia day pack is just that. I doubt it would be good for more than a weekend's worth of clothing.

All the buckles are plastic making it look more like a toy than an actual pack. As one reviewer commented, adjusting will take time. The first time I put it on I was worried about the height of the chest strap. It was nearly at my chin. I didn't notice at the time that the strap connector has slides which allow you to tweak it to your actual chest.

With that in mind, the sides of the bag are also held close but by disconnecting those plastic clasps can open the bag for more storage.

Even the shoulder straps have a rubbery-plastic feel to them. Supposedly this same type material on the back gives the wearer a better feel. Only time will tell.

The two water bottle pockets are actually deep enough to carry my [[ASIN:B000F7Z0KI Polar Bottle Insulated Water Bottle]], however if I carry two bottles, the left one falls in such a way that it always interferes with the swing of my arm.

If needed I will update this evaluation at a future date.

title: Go Leafs Go!
text:
This is the second of my two Toronto Maple Leaf shirts. I'm not normally a polyester kind of guy as it tends to cause me to itch. This is a nice weave that looks and feels great.

This is a very bright white which shows off the Maple Leaf emblem wonderfully.

As noted in size comment, I think it's a tad big for a medium that I would normally wear, but not enough for me to get nit-picky about.

title: A Backpacking Family Favorite
text:
This one is a family favorite for our backpacking expeditions. Even my Picky Eater Son admits his like of the "Strogie".

As with all other of the brand, this is freeze dried and easily reconstituted with boiling water either in the Mylar(?) bag or a traditional pot or pan. Personally, I like to bulk it up a bit with spinach flakes from Harmony House.

title: Decent Length, Decent Stakes at a Decent Price
text:
Sure, these are NOT titanium stakes. Then again, you're not paying for it either.

I have a handful of these stakes to go along with a wide variety I keep to use depending on the soil. These are no nonsense stakes. They are shaped well to hold up for the beating one might expect them to give them.

For the price, they're good to have around. If you're an ounce shaver you probably already know that these aren't what you're looking for.

title: Very Nice
text:
I'm not a fan of polyester. Normally I don't like the feel of it on my skin. However, I'll make an exception to this nice Maple Leafs logo'd shirt.

I wear this as one of my work shirts at a high school in the Pacific Northwest. Few people are hockey fans and fewer yet are Leaf fans. They'll learn yet. Go Leafs Go!

title: Excellent Protein Extender for Backpacking Meals
text:
As with my other Harmony House reviews, I bought a 30 item kit from another source to compliment my Mountain House backpacking meals and extending the serving size from two to three.

I used the chickenish bits along with a chicken centered entrée from Mountain House. Using it along with the spinach I successfully stretched the meal to serve three very hungry adult backpackers.

The bits and spinach rehydrated at the same rate as the entrée. Perfect. I would highly recommend it for backpackers. It's lightweight, healthy, doesn't reek of "fake food" and can be filling.

title: Great For Extending Meals on the Trail
text:
While I didn't actually buy this container (size), I have beefish bits from a large selection I bought elsewhere.

As one reviewer noted, it tends to lose flavor when cooked. However, that flaw is also an extra unexpected bonus if you look at it differently. I use this product to extend Mountain House entrées fron two to three servings. Having a more neutral flavor allows me to use the product in more items without fear of collision of tastes. In this case, neutral (bland) is good. I'm merely looking for a protein extender.

I gave it 5*s because of the neutral flavor issue. Oddly, if it had been TOO strong of a flavor it would have received a lesser review due to my intended purposes.

title: Great Product for Extending Backpacking Entrées
text:
I bought a 30 item kit recommended by an Amazon reviewer. Among the items received that I have used was the spinach. Since Mountain House entrées are made for two and I was feeding three during a recent weeklong trip, items from Harmony House Foods were employed to stretch the meals appropriately.

The spinach is easily "hidden" in other items allowing consumption of the iron and calcium nutrients. Almost flavorless and mostly inconspicuous, this was the perfect add to most meals.

The products are well manufactured, sealed, lightweight and perfect for backpacking.

title: Very Pleased
text:
I bought this and a Platypus this summer for our backpacking needs. I have to say I was thrilled that this was available.

During a 6 day backpacking trip I used this sparringly at the beginning due to lack of places to refill. Once my trail brought me along a river and stream and water was plentiful, this baby got a workout.

My camping partners were in awe of the squeeze bulb pressurization feature. I was more thrilled with the ease of refilling with filtered water.

While weight of water cannot be changed except by reduction, water equals life.

title: Got A Dragonfly? Get the Maintenance Kit
text:
If you've ever had a backpacking stove fail on you when you need it most, you'll know the importance of routine maintenance.

Parts get old, crusty, possibly corroded, clogged, frail, what have you. The Expedition kit is prepared for nearly every eventuality to keep you fat and happy while on the trail. I can think of little worse than knowing you've GOT the food, you just can't eat it rehydrated or hot. I say this from experience. It ain't fun.

You take care of your Dragonfly up front and it won't let you down out back.

title: MSR is a Standard for Backpacking Equipment
text:

I have two fuel bottles. I've got the 11oz and 30oz. The 11oz is my primary use bottle and the 30's for back up fuel. I've never had a problem with them and am glad I've got 'em. I had an 11oz with my first [[ASIN:B002IAMPEE MSR WhisperLite Stove]] and more recently with my [[ASIN:B002IAJ5VA MSR Dragonfly Stove]]. Not that it matters to the review of the fuel bottle, but I've also got the [[ASIN:B000BBF2TC MSR Dragonfly Expedition Service Kit for Liquid-Fuel Stove]].

title: So Far, So Good - With Edit after Extended Use
text:
I bought three of these bad boys mostly based on a whim to have a pillow and the thoughts of comfort when sleeping. I've recently equipped my family to be able to do some decent backpacking. These were sort of afterthoughts.

I based my choices largely on Amazon user reviews. With few exceptions, and I hope we shan't be one, I was taken with the price, size and comfort.

I'm looking forward to giving this a night's use.

EDIT 08-25-2013
After a week of backpacking use, this little pillow became my best friend. As it is I already have problems with my neck and shoulder. Throw in an extra 40+ lbs tucked into my [[ASIN:B004R7L7YU ALPS OutdoorZ Commander Freighter Frame Plus Pack Bag, 5250 Cubic Inches]] including sleeping bag, tent, ground pad, clothing, food... you know, essentials, and I was a tired, sore puppy each night.

This pillow was exactly what I wanted and needed. It was comfortable when inflated, cushioned the head nicely whether laying on my side or back and took up minimal space and weight when deflated. I HIGHLY recommend this.

I hope it continues to give me nights upon nights of comfort and rest. I'd hate to think of it failing me when I needed it most.

I spent a lot of time eyeballing these in town and online. When I saw the price The Wonderful World of Amazonia(tm) was charging for it and read many of the reviews I was sold.

This cooler did what we needed to do. We camped at that one place for four days. I loaded it up with ice ONCE and kept it outside under the shade of the bedends. I won't say there was 100% of the ice remaining, because there wasn't. What there was remaining was enough ice to keep the melted water cool to keep the items in the cooler cool.

For what it's worth, I'm a retired chef. I know all about HACCP. I know what needs to be refrigerated for how long and at what temperature. I wasn't worried about this cooler and my food in it.

title: A Lot More Than I Had Anticipated
text:
I went through and read the good and the bad reviews. Taking all that into account and knowing what I know about knives, which as a retired chef is quite a bit, I decided to take a chance on this one.

First, even after reading the numerous reviews and manufacturer's info, I was astounded by the length of this knife. It is LONG. Not only is this knife long, it's heavy.

Second, as many noted, the knife blade wasn't all that sharp when received. Again, noting my background as a retired chef, taking care of knives and bringing them from the land of the dead to an item with a wonderfully usuable blade isn't all that difficult providing you've the equipment to do so.

I honed the knife using the medium grit on my tri-stone about 10 minutes then moved to the fine grit stone. That put a good edge on it. While watching Firefly (http://www.amazon.com/Firefly-Complete-Blu-ray-Nathan-Fillion/dp/B001EN71CW/ref=sr_1_3?s=movies-tv&ie=UTF8&qid=1363822981&sr=1-3&keywords=firefly), I pulled out the tri-stone again and continued with the medium to fine grit honing getting an even better blade on it.

The scabbard is appropriate for the knife. That, to me, says a lot. There's a lot of knife, there's a lot of scabbard. One other reviewer succinctly defined the contents of the pockets on the scabbard. I needn't do the same. Nor shall I wax about which pieces are good and which aren't. Everybody's entitled to their own opinions about that. That said, I'm keeping "most" of the prepackaged stuff there. I'm sure over the course of a few trips I'll update, tweak and tune what I want, but for the time being, it all stays.

I'm very satisifed with this knife. I know while I'm backpacking, hiking or camping I'll keep it close at hand. My son's got HIS knife, Whetstone Usa Full Tang Stainless Steel Jungle Survival Knife, (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B003U7SC6O/ref=oh_details_o06_s00_i01?ie=UTF8&psc=1), I've got mine.

Happy honing.

title: Finally!
text:

I learned how to shoot bearings, read charts and figure out where I was. I had one of these some years later but lost it along the way. Now, thanks to Amazon and the seller, I finally have another GOOD compass again.

My hiking days are ahead as the weather breaks. A new area of life and more charts and I'm good to go! Compasses like these are a lifetime investment. Get one, keep it (don't lose it) and you'll never need another again.

These poles are the epitome of versatile. I've had them in use from tree lined state parks of NC to the shores of Myrtle Beach, SC to the hot skies of San Antonio, TX and now in the Scablands of Eastern WA.

The Poles will probably be the last you ever need.

As a retired chef, sharpening knives was just as important to my job as the restaurant's P&L statement but less daunting. I have a tri-stone at home which allowed me to put a better edge on it than your average block stone.

Also, for those who cannot figure out what those "sawtooth" like things are at the top near the hilt, I'm thinking they could be used to twist wire as in tightening a fence. I could be wrong, but I could see it as so.

All in all, when I give this blade to my son to carry while we backpack, I think he'll be quite happy.

As for the interior room it gets high marks from me. I can fit my Taurus .38 Special AND my Springfield 9mm with both magazines in there. Sure, the weapons are stacked on top each other but that gives you an idea of the depth, width and length.

I would highly recommend this unit to others and will likely buy another in the future. Amazon's Prime makes it worthwhile with both free and fast shipping.

title: Comparison Between the Earth Therapeutics Pillow and the Ayazen Lavender Eye Pillow
text:
Good anti stress eye pillow. What I like about the Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy pillow
1) I like the fragrance of the lavender and chamomile pillow.
2) The fragrance is not overwhelming it is subtle.
3) It is not overstuffed so it drapes nicely over your eye and sinus area when you are lying flat.
4) The silk has a cooling effect
5) I have chronic sinusitis and this pillow feels like it helps to relieve some of that tight pressure pain. It also seems to calm the area around my eyes.
I have used several different sinus pillow type remedies over the years for that "ahhh relief!" moment when you can feel the swelling and ache diminishing.Not many were very effective but this one and the Lavender eye pillow by AyaZen are both effective. However, I would choose the one from AyaZen over this one because:
1) It can be heated and froze as long as you put it in a plastic sealed bag so it doesn't absorb freezer odor.
2) It has more filling and a more balanced filling making it a little weightier than the Earth Therapeutics eye pillow
3) The velvet like cover of the AyaZen is soft and luxurious yet it also has a griping effect so it doesn't readily slip off your face.
4) It has a stronger lavender scent that is soothing but not overwhelming.
5) For me, this pillow relieves the pain and pressure associated with my sinusitis better.

As a comparison, they are both good eye pillows but AyaZen wins for me.

The reason Earth Therapeutics is not a perfect five stars and doesn't win for me:
1) It doesn't have the balanced filling the AyaZen does
2) The silk used to encase the Earth Therapeutics pillow slips very easily unless you are lying down flat.If your head happens to turn a little while sleeping at an angle or with your head raised at any height, it slips off. Even though you can conform it to your eyes and nose it won't stay because of the silkiness of the material and the almost whisper light weight of the pillow. If your head is raised at any angle or your head happens to fall sideways while napping, you must continually reposition the pillow.
3) you cannot heat it in the microwave or put it in the freezer. I know this pillow is suppose to be Therapeutic based solely on the oils it harbors and the silk that encases it but it just needs a little more to really reach that Therapeutic level.

This is a great tool if you are looking for a way to boost your confidence and self esteem without having to actually improve anything--you know, kind of like the filters in photoshop that make you look thinner and younger. text: OK, so I had to have one of these contraptions.  Both my kids had Zootrs for Eco Challenges and tootling around Chicago but I was going to use mine for exercise.  Good choice since cleaning out a clogged sewer ranks above running and biking on my list of druthers. My initial considerations were finding one for an adult weighing more than 90 pounds and costing less than $300.  This seemed to be about the only one.  Had just purchased a motorized Razor (300) for my daughter to ride back and forth from the train station and was very impressed with its quality. However, the size and weight of my new Razor A4 kick scooter surprised me. It's a trick scooter and one should seriously consider its handlebar warning stating "this object moves when in use. Take safety precautions."  OK, I just turned 65 and I'm probably not in the target demographic group, but I'm getting pretty good on it and look less like an idiot every day.  Caution though because the standing area is short and narrow and I have big feet so I tend to switch legs a lot while using the opposing leg for propulsion.  The wheels are tiny and buck whenever they hit a piece of gravel or a twig.  The "trick" is avoiding obstacles in the street.  Have fun.  It's a good uphill cardio workout, strengthens the quads and glutes and helps get rid of some of those extra butt-cheeks.  I'm going to borrow one of my kids' Zootrs though and save the Razor A4 for exhibition!

title: Heavy, thick
text: I find the extra duty balls to be somewhat heavy.  And they don't bounce as high.  The outer shell is thicker, hence heavier.  I prefer a lighter ball and would not buy these again.

title: So comfortable
text: These are my all time favorite slippers.  Soft, comfortable, perfect.  I don't understand people who complain about the sizing being too small.  I bought two sizes larger than the chart and found them too large.  I then bought one size larger and found them too large as well.  They do stretch out after two to three weeks, since they are all cotton.  So now I have had to go down another size to 37 (6 1/2), which is exactly what the chart recommends.  Keep in mind that in addition to stretching a bit, the inside lining is thin cotton, so they will wear through a bit in the heel area.  They are padded, however, so they don't wear through the sole. The comfort is extraordinary, and I would rather buy a few pairs at this price.  I will use an inner pad in the larger pairs and wear socks when the weather gets cold.

title: Very difficult to walk on...
text: This took three weeks to arrive.  Yes, there has been severe weather throughout the country, but three weeks?  I put it together tonight with the help of a friend, and it seemed easy to do.  The small wheels on the front don't make any sense as far as moving it around. They should be on the back.  The photo shows them on the back, but they aren't.  What looks like wheels are just metal half-curved molds.  The instructions were followed exactly. My friend is a contractor. As far as using it...oh boy. I am used to the electronic treadmills at the gym.  I could hardly get the track to move.  I had to buy Horizon Silicone Treadmill Lubricant from Amazon.  I used half a bottle before I could get it to move at all.  The bottles (3 to a pack) are 40ml each, and I used 20ml, squirting thoroughly under the tread and around all the moving parts.  It's still hard.  I go about 20 steps and then it stops.  Very difficult.

title: Not what I ordered
text: In the photograph, the match boxes are the "greenlight matches", in green boxes, which I have had before.  They have thicker, stronger wooden sticks and they light more easily and stay lit longer.  That's not what was sent.  I received boxes of the regular Diamond strike on box matches with the red tips in the red boxes.  This is bait and switch Amazon.

title: Wonderful, wonderful, wonderful!
text:
This is the best fleece throw I've ever owned or found. Finally, it's large enough...79" x 63"! It is plush, soft, and comfy. I bought the charcoal, which is a deep, rich, dark gray. It has finished edges with a double stitched hem of additional fabric, which stretches. I wish I had discovered this long ago. I have several throws from Lands End and other online websites, and nothing can compare to this. Love it.
Update: I bought a second charcoal gray last night. I washed the first one by itself on gentle in warm water and put it in the dryer on low. It was completely dry in 40 minutes and came out looking and feeling just as wonderful as it was before I washed it. You can ignore the label that says not to put it in the dryer. It's polyester and comes through the dryer beautifully. Just don't put it on high. Make sure the heat is medium or low. It dries so quickly you don't need to put on high.

title: Great little light!
text: I ordered this the week before we had a power outage, and it certainly came in handy.  When I opened the box I was initially a bit miffed at how small it is, but when I had to use it, I appreciated that it is lightweight, easy to carry and hang, and the light itself is actually brighter and farther reaching than I expected.  I plan to order several more.  And yes, the tiny flashing light does bother me at night in the bedroom, where I keep it for emergencies.  So I just face it away from me and put a dark sock over it.

title: Great Value, Greater Compromise.
text:
Im deducting one full star for the assembling process for the wooden rower. Horrible (and incorrect) instructions that dont match the parts sent, and then missing parts (bolts) also. As someone that's actually really really good with putting things together, I think this is more than doable if youre capable. If youre not good at assembling stuff, consider using some of the money you'll save to pay for assembly.

Im deducting another star because they listed the rower as 330lb capacity but its actually 260lb when you get the product. This may not matter much to most people but both of us are athletes/body builders so an increased weight capacity matters. The seller did compensate me a bit for this discrepancy, but Im 100% sure that they knew this all along and just refuse to update the info on the listing, hoping that most people either dont care or dont notice.

This thing supposedly has a 3mo warranty, but once again Im pretty sure that its worthless if you ever have to use it.

Compared to other rowers, at this price point, I would actually say this is a 4 or 5 star product. Its solid quality, looks great and so far functions properly. Im very pleased and looking at rowers that are much more expensive, I dont regret buying this product at all.

But the misleading listing details/specifications and the horrible assembly instructions cannot allow me to rate this product higher than 3 stars. If anything It makes you see how much markup there is on more expensive rowers that are essentially the same product but with an actual useful instructions manual.

It's definitely not an overnight lock solution - for that, a sturdy u-lock won't eliminate the probability of theft, but it will at least make it more challenging for some bolt choppers (which go through this in literally no time given the flat shape).

title: Mobility of bike lock (without added security) makes this a poor purchase

I own a chain just like this. See my review here: [[ASIN:B000AMVPUM Kryptonite New York Chain 3' With Key Lock]]

The problem with these giant chains is a sense of added security, but I'm not convinced you get it with something like this. Big bolt cutters will demolish this thing (for evidence, search youtube for "security chains vs. bolt choppers", skip to 6min24s... this chain gets demolished in less than a minute. Granted, they're huge bolt cutters. But someone running around in a van at 3AM isn't going to care.). Couple the questionable security with how big of a pain this thing is to lug around (I've owned the chain for years) and I can't imagine it's worth it.

Anyway, since no bike lock seems to be impervious to bike theft, it's important for people to realize the only true security is to store the bike within sight (your home, place of work, near you on a restaurant patio, etc.). I imagine the latest and greatest u-locks are a better option due to the shear time it takes to grind through them (with bolt cutters not being an option), but I'd wager all bike chains are susceptible to big bolt cutters.

I usually swim for around an hour whenever I go to the pool, and so far, I have not notice the goggles fogging up or letting any water in. It has been almost a month since I got this, and it is holding up very well. I expect to use this for a long time.

title: Great lightweight backpack
text:
Traveling with two toddlers means that the more we can keep our hands free, the more helpful the luggage. Ultimately this means adding more weight to our backs. This backpack was a great help for our recent trip to Aruba and I recommend it to other parents.

Pros
- VERY lightweight - your back will thank you
- Very durable - the material seems thick and the seams are secure
- Lots and lots of pockets
- Good bright and unique options - it's very easy to spot my bright yellow school bus colored backup amidst the sea of black ones out there
- You can bring this on board an airplane as your carry-on - you may not be able to swing it as a personal item if it's too full

Cons
- It does not have a strap that attaches to the handles of a rolling suitcase - this means that it has to stay on your back! This is the biggest con in my opinion.
- Shoulder straps could be a bit thicker to alleviate the weight
- Unclear why there is an open hole at the top of the backpack (it isn't the headphones hole)

title: Great for the lazy river!
text:
The family took a trip to Aruba and our hotel had a lazy river. This was great for that purpose! We had float inflators, so it was easy to blow up. For my husband who is 5' 11" and 170 pounds, this was very comfortable, though it was definitely one of the larger floats in the lazy river. He in particular appreciated the handles - he said it made it a lot easier to get onto the float and to carry it around the resort. The cup holders also came in handy as he had to carry drinks for the entire family, since our other floats did not have cup holders.

The confetti looked pretty, but doesn't actually do anything since you're not moving the float - so they just kinda stay wherever they are. Otherwise, really did the job!

title: Nice Protection Against the Sun
text: This hat with neck flap cover is great whenever I go out fishing. It blocks the deadly rays of the sun from my head and my neck. No more sun burns due to forgetting to apply sun block. It also protects me from those dastardly mosquitoes for the most part. I still ended up getting bitten near the eye. Now, I would spray some bug repellant on the hat and so far that did the job. I would recommend for anyone who enjoy fishing like I do.

title: Great stroller for active people!
text:
Who says you can't get your work out in when you have kids?

This stroller makes an outing exciting for both you and your kid. For you, this adaptive stroller allows you multiple ways to exercise, including two ways to run with it, ski with it, or as a bike attachment. For your kid, of course there is a thrill in going high speeds.

It's also sturdy - the big wheels and wider body do seem to help prevent it from tipping like many other strollers do. One potential downside is that the straps seem a little lower quality - they still work, but I kind of expected more given the overall construction of the stroller.

title: Works well - easy to assemble
text:
Very satisfied with this sunshade. It is surprisingly easy to set up - no tricks, nothing to snap together - you just pull it open and spread it out - that's it! Definitely does help to have another person to help you since, it's big, but it's really straightforward. The coverage is great and provides ample shade - enough for a family of four with ease. The bag is also excellent - the wheels make it so easy to bring around. Without them, it would certainly be too heavy for most people to consider portable.

I may have slight concerns about the quality - I have not yet taken this out on a very windy day, but do worry it may not hold up as well under those conditions. Just consider that given how big the umbrella is, it will catch a lot of the force of the wind - hence, you will need heavier bags to hold it down.

title: Pretty good bike!
text:
As someone who has gained a lot of weight during COVID-19, this bike was my attempt to start losing some of it now that things are opening back up. So far - so good! I especially like how many adjustable options it has, so I can find the perfect positioning for my arms and legs. Furthermore, it was not hard to put together - it's mostly assembled really so you just need to put a few more things on - I am not particularly handy and no problem doing it.

There are a few drawbacks. One is that the bike is a little squeaky - I think it could probably fixed with some oil or grease, but I haven't been bothered enough to try. Another is that the seat can be a bit firm - while it might seem cushioned, it's sot so you sink into it and after a while it hurts. If you plan to do a LOT of bicycling that much be an issue, but isn't really one for me.

He rocks on it like he's surfing waves, he sits on it like he's in a rocking chair, he flips it over and uses it to reach things he shouldn't be reaching, and so on. The quality is very nice - I was originally worried that it might crack or splinter from the weight, but no worries in practice. I also got the version that has handles - that does make transporting it around the house much easier.

title: Does its job
text:
For the longest time, I’ve been using the cheap yoga mats – for instance, the kind you find at the dollar
store / etc. You’ve probably seen them – they’re cheap, plastic-y, and have the pebbled texture. Now
that we’re in a pandemic, I figured I would start working out more and so started to look for something
a bit more able to withstand regular wear and tear.

This mat is actually so good, I cannot believe I had been using the cheapies for so long. I’d say there are
three major areas where this mat really shows it’s quality: 1) the grippiness – on the cheaper mats, it’s
easier for your fingers and foot to slide in positions like downward dog. This keeps you in place. 2) the
quality of the material – on the cheaper matters, when you do a position like downward dog, you
literally see the mat stretch – this is rigid. 3) the thickness – on the cheaper mats, doing things like cat
stretch hurt my knees – this has enough padding where it’s much more bearable.

The only downside for this mat, is it does get kind of dirty easily. But hey look, it's proof of the work put in. In short, a great mat – good balance of cost and quality.

title: Excellent exercise mat, mediocre yoga mat
text:
This is a great 5* exercise mat. However I did not love it as a yoga mat - I would give it 2* for that. So the
compromise is 4* for this product overall

Pros:
- Extra wide
- Pretty thick and foamy
- Decent grip on the floor

Cons:
- Top of the mat is not ‘grippy’ - it gets slippery when wet

That is really the only con I can think of for this mat. However, it’s a pretty big one when it comes to yoga. When I do downward dog, my hands and feet cannot help sliding out of place once they get even a little sweaty. In fact, the degree to which this happens is probably the worst I have experienced across yoga mats - including the really cheap ones you can get at discount stores.

However, I have been using it for pylometrics and kickboxing and other high impact cardio activities. It works just great for those - it gives a nice cushion. Certainly beats bare floor or interlocking foam tiles that never stay in place.

title: Low quality
text: It's not great.  My husband had another one of these for many years and I wanted replace it with something newer.  But very clearly, the quality has diminished.  First, there was no instructions provided - and the pictures on the box did not fully match the items in the box.  Second, the holes weren't fully perforated, so my husband had to sand it off.  Third, they changed the screws to just nuts and bolts instead of end caps.  Fourth, the supplied tools are so low quality that the wrench was 'stripped' through the installation.  Fifth, the thing is significantly lighter than the other pull-up bar that my husband had previously - indicating that it's not as sturdy.  Lastly, and most importantly, the whole thing just seems WEAK.  In the prior model, when my husband did a pull up, the middle barely made any movement.  In this new one, not only does the middle bow, but the entire thing bends.  He only weigh 178 pounds, but this thing gives him safety concerns.  Therefore we will be giving it away to someone who weighs significantly less.

title: Not really a major improvement for dumbbells
text:
I work out primarily at home, and only have access to dumbbells. For many exercises, like a dumbbell shrug or a dumbbell step-up, I am using fairly heavy weights - e.g., 40 pounds or more in each hand. It had gotten to the point where my grip strength was not sufficient to hold these dumbbells comfortably while working out. I thought these hooks would be a good way to distribute the weight. Unfortunately, while I think the idea is still good, these hooks are not doing it for me. There are two problems for me:

a) the hook is large enough where cupping it in my hands is very uncomfortable - in fact, now instead of gripping the whole handle, I can only use 3 fingers to grip the hook

b) the hook is not deep enough - I feel like there is a risk of the weights slipping out of the hooks and dropping

Ultimately this was not an improvement over just gripping the dumbbells without any additional assistance. I can't speak to how useful or not this is for barbell users.

title: Works great - just Ditch the supplied hardware (bolts and screws)
text:
1. - determine which way your joists run if you have a finished garage. More than likely, they will run parallel to the garage doors, but you still need to locate them with a stud finder.
2. - If you are hanging your kayaks perpendicular to the joists, you will more than likely need to get a couple of 2X4s long enough to span the required length, and bolt them to the joists as there will not be enough surface area to attached the mounting brackets.
3. - Go to the home improvement store and buy (5) 3 1/2" X 5/16 lag bolts and washers to bolt the 2x4 to the ceiling. You need 3 1/2 inches to make sure you have enough to go thought the thickness of the 2x4 and the sheet rock. Buy replacement 2" x 1/4" lag bolts supplied with kit for the mounting bracket (four needed per kayak).
4. Attach 2x4s to ceiling making sure you hit the joists. Pre-drill with a bit one size smaller than the 5/16" lag bolt.
5. Follow the bracket placement directions provided in the instructions and attach brackets to ceiling.
6. The rest is as straight forward as you can get. The pulley system is self explanatory.
7. Attach the wall anchor using two of the supplied 1/4" lag bolts intended for the brackets in the kit. You should have these left over if you bought the replacements mentioned above. DO NOT use the screws provided. They sheared off while I was installing them.

Bolts are super cheap. I think they were 25 cents a piece and well worth the peace of mind. It's still a cheaper solution than trying to make it yourself.

Note #1: The weak point of the entire system is the little pins that attach the hooks to the pulley. If any one of these fail the entire yak will fall to the floor. I suggest a static safety strap or cable to run under the yaks when stored at each attachment point.
Note #2: This system will not lift the yak flush with the ceiling. It will be suspended a little low -16 to 18".
Note #3: Under no circumstance attempt to lift the kayak without first tying a taunt cord between the pulley brackes at either end. Otherwise, if you lift unevenly the straps will spread apart and the yak will fall (I learned this the hard way because I was impatient). See picture of yellow kayak. (I used reflective para cord for this instead of cutting the supplied black cord).
Tip - don't cut the black cord provided. leaving it connected prevents the cord from slipping through the pulley; especially on high ceilings. Basically, you will end up with a loop at the wall end if you didn't cut it and did it right.

title: Great Customer Service from Coleman - Excellent car camping tent
text:
Updated Sept 2022. Purchased in 2018:

We use this tent three to five times per year depending on how many people are going. This is a great tent! The instructions on whether or not to use the black poles or the grey poles for the main tent could be clearer, but we wrote that on the bag after setting it up incorrectly twice.

I would not classify this as a three season tent, unless you live in a warmer climate. I live in central Texas, so this will work for me almost year round.

The good :
-very spacious, Large framed door on hinges.
-Good Head room.
-Lots of mesh on roof and two sides.
-Rain fly has excellent coverage over all openings but still allows adequate ventilation.
-Bath-tub floor comes up really high.
-Appears to be good reinforcement at stress points.

The bad :
- Really needs two people to set up (but I suppose if you are buying a tent this large you will have help).
- Stakes. As with any tent now a days, you probably won't be using the stakes that are included.

Buying experience - The tent arrived well before the stated delivery date, and the packaging was in excellent condition.

We now have six tents and three of those are Coleman Tents of various sizes. I have been generally pleased with the products overall, but I do not subject them to harsher environments as I would my Marmot or Eureka.

Warranty - Coleman stepped up and replaced this tent way past the warranty period. We got a rip in one of the sleeves for the main pole. Even though it still sets up OK, we felt it best not to use the tent in case a storm with gusty wing came up (because of the tear).

Hope this helps somebody.

title: High quality, works well on carpet
text:
This is a very nice standing desk board. It's very sturdy and the curve is great for moving back and forth so that your weight is distributed back and forth as you rock.

It's made of tough spongy material, but still feels nice with socks on your feet. I prefer this one that moves over the stationary ones. Being able to shift your weight puts less pressure on the hips and I don't get the same back strain as standing on a flat surface.

It's really well made and sturdy. The wood sandwiched in-between the bottom and top hard rubber surfaces gives it a lot of strength. It has a nice little leather loop that works as a carrying handle -- because of the weight, it would be hard to grip without it.

It also works as a nice footrest when sitting. It's not as high as some others, but it still feels good with the bumps giving a nice massage to the feet.

I'd recommend this if you use a standing desk frequently. I end up using my desk in standing mode a lot more than before.

It's not a bad price, especially for this quality.

title: Quality set with case. Orange balls are for indoors.
text:
I like that this comes with its own little zippered carrying case. That's just an extra that makes it nicer than having to find a duffel-bag or some other place to carry the set.

It comes with 4 paddles that are the same except for the colors. It has 3 indoor and 3 outdoor balls which are almost identical except for the spacing of the holes. They're like Whiffle™ balls. The holes prevent them from going too far from the air resistance. The ones for indoors are the ones with the bigger holes because you can't hit them as far.

I know it says that you can play indoors and technically that's true, but it depends on where you're playing. A big game room with lots of space would work. A place where you can trip over furniture or knock over lamps isn't a good idea. It also depends on how aggressive you want to be with your swings. The indoor balls are not the problem because they couldn't easily build up enough momentum to break anything except very delicate or top-heavy things. But the paddles swinging around are more of the issue with playing indoors. A big swing or stretch if you aren't aware of the stuff around you could be where you'd break something or trip over something. But still, about the same level of caution you'd have with Ping-Pong, but without the table to keep you in place.

The paddles are pretty nice quality and lighter than they look like they should be. But they have a lot of surface area and the balls are easier to hit than with Ping-Pong paddles.

You'll have to look up the rules online because they aren't included, but really that's only if you want to play "official Pickle-ball". You can play it with Ping-pong rules, badminton rules, volleyball rules, tennis rules -- just about any of the similar kind of games that I can think of -- it's just a bit easier and has requires less skill or movement. It's really about the same level of activity that you'd have with badminton and the same sized area if you're playing outdoors.

Personally, indoors is just if we want to play "hit-the-ball-back-and-forth-down-the-hallway" because it's too hot/cold/wet outside.

This doesn't come with a net, and I thought the rubberband strips might have been to map out the court area, but it's supposed to be for the grip on the paddles. If you're going to play "official" you'll need a net which is pretty much the same as a badminton net just not as high. It's basically a mini tennis court with much the same net.

It's good exercise, and I can't imagine this being a competitive sport, but I was wrong about tag being an 'official' sport when I heard someone mention it -- but it actually is and surprisingly fun to watch -- with sponsors and everything. Pickleball might be the same because why wouldn't someone take something that's fun and add a bunch of rules so they can make some money from advertising.

It's good for staying active and just about everyone likes to play because we don't play with any real rules. Not because we have odd ideas like "there are no losers here", but because it's just that unimportant.

I can't comment on the price with the way things are these days, but it seems to be about the same price as other options, and the quality is decent. The bag is a bonus and even the dog likes to play -- but that's where it goes from being 'pickle-ball' to 'slobber-ball'.

Overall, this is a nice set, especially the paddles. Five stars.

title: For a $10 pair of yoga pants, you really can't go wrong with these
text:
These are much better than I expected for a $10 pair of yoga pants. They are soft and very comfortable. There's a pocket that's supposed to be for your phone and it works, but not when I'm working out. It slides around too much to be comfortable with exercise.

They are fairly squat proof.

They do seem to run a little small and I wasn’t sure which size to get as I usually wear a medium, but after reading the other reviews, I got the large. The large definitely fits better, and I think a medium would have been a little too tight, but the material is stretchy so it might have still worked, but I'm glad I got a size-up anyway. I don't like super-tight.

It has good compression and I think because I got the large, it's not painfully tight. No big issues (other than the pocket not being very useful with high-activity.

Overall this is a decent pair of yoga pants, and with the current $10 price point, definitely a keeper. 5-stars.

title: Not a bad set of workout gloves, not the best, but a decent value
text:
These workout gloves came in handy this winter when working out outside. They fit well for my small hands and they look nice.

They aren’t really designed for warmth but they did help some. I used them with hand weights and when doing bear crawls, etc., on the ground, It protected my hands.

I found them to be adequate with weights but not as much protection as my fingerless padded weight gloves.

But when you're outside and its cold, they work to keep your fingers mostly warm.

I ordered the medium and they fit fine with my small hands. The Velcro™ straps helped to keep them on during an active workout.

Overall, for a simple pair of workout gloves, these are okay as long as you don't need a lot of padding. They'd be great for just keeping your hands warm on a chilly morning workout. The price isn't that bad either.

title: Comfortable and fit snugly
text:
These are great gloves that I use when working out with weights. They have good padding in all the right places and are a nice lightweight, breathable material.

They keep my hands from getting too sweaty and make it less likely that I'll slip or drop something.

I got the small size and they fit my small hands perfectly. They have a couple of handy tabs on two of the fingers to help pull them off which are almost a necessity. It would actually be nice if there were tabs on a few more of the fingers, because they can be a little difficult to pull off sometimes because they are very snug -- but that's also one of the things I like most about these.

The Velcro™ fastener around the wrist works well, too, and can be loosened or tightened depending on the exercise.

Overall, a very nice pair of workout gloves for only $10 (the current price).

title: Nice wide-mouth feature, but the lid can be a pain at times.
text:
I use this water bottle primarily to take to my workouts. It holds plenty to keep me hydrated and is easy to drink from. I like the wide mouth feature so it’s easy to fill and clean.

I really like the pretty colors too.

So far no leaks and cap twists on and off easily.

A few small nitpicks:
I have found that the closing mechanism on the flip top lid malfunctions so that you can’t close the lid sometimes. You have to use the locking mechanism to get it to close. This doesn’t happen all the time but most of the time and enough to be a little annoying.
Also, I feel like the carrying handle is not really big enough or flexible enough. When you have a finger looped through it and are tying carry other things like weights and a towel, it gets hard to hold.

So overall a decent water bottle but with a few annoyances and could be a little better for the $12 price.

title: Decent quality water-bottle
text:
This gallon water bottle is great for keeping me on track during the day. The time marker is handy so I try to keep up with it. The photo shows a different band -- the one I received is a loop of braided para-cord which I actually prefer over the plastic loop pictured.

It's a bit big and heavy when it’s full so I fill it up in the morning and keep it on the kitchen counter. I pour it into a smaller bottle I keep at my desk. The paracord strap makes it easy to carry even when it’s full. I like wide mouth on it so it’s easy to fill and clean.

I don’t use the straw option because it's just too heavy and cumbersome to bother with. I just pop open the lid and pour into my smaller bottle.

Love all the color options. The only annoying thing I have found is when I am pouring it, it tends to splash and pour unevenly unless I find just the right angle. Other than that, this is really helping me keep up with my water consumption through out the day.

Overall, not a bad bottle for keeping hydrated, but maybe a bit overpriced at the current $22.

It’s not like a thick regular beach towel, though, so it won’t be very cushiony. But if you need to pack light or need a quick drying option, then this is a good choice.

title: Soft, absorbent, and great for workouts

title: A little overpriced at $20, but good for its intended purpose
text:
This is purely a jug designed for people who want a little nudge in their quest for increasing their daily water intake. Whether or not everyone needs a full gallon of water per day is very debatable, but this bottle is a great way to accomplish your goals if that's what you're working on.

If you are like me, then you don't drink enough water most of the day and you end up being a little dehydrated later in the day -- especially on the days when you workout or are active.

This bottle is a great little helper for assisting you with drinking your goal amount of water for the day. You might not need a full gallon, and you may need more depending on your lifestyle. Either way, this is a nice bottle with a nice set of markers to help you finish your goals.

I think it might be a bit overpriced at the current $20 for what is essentially a plastic water-bottle, but it does have some nice extras that make it worth the money. The lid has a double locking mechanism and it's got a decent silicone seal that makes it leakproof as long as you've put the lid on tightly. Nice paracord handle on this which is a plus and a minus. Hopefully the handle will last a while and won't come untied after a lot of usage. I can see this possibly being an issue.

Overall, even though this might be slightly overpriced for just a water-bottle -- the little extra $ will be well worth it for the help this bottle will give you in reaching your daily hydration goals. Even if the "motivational" labels are a little bit on the cheesy side. A solid five stars.

title: Nice quality sock, but shows a little
