That being said, these are pretty good for a pair of workout socks. They seem to be fairly moisture-wicking and are very comfortable. They fit true-to-size. I wear a size 6 and these are in that range and fit well.

title: Too tight! I even ordered a size up

One plus is that the material is soft. It might make a nice underlayer for another top or sweater

If you like your workout tops super-clingy, then you might like this one, although only the boldest of bold would be comfortable wearing this without something underneath.

Overall, it's a good price for a top, but the fit and design make it only worthy of three-stars.

title: Good for low-intensity workouts, but not for high-intensity activities
text:
I like this because it's longer than most yoga mats. It's thick and cushy, offering a nice amount of padding.

The one thing that I don't like as much is that the mat can get pretty slippery with your sweat. Possibly using a yoga-mat towel might help with that. I used this on carpet, so I can't comment on how well it would stay in place on, say the hardwood floors that you might find in a typical yoga studio or an outdoor surface such as blacktop or concrete.

I think this would be great if all you needed it for was doing yoga, which is slower than some exercises. If you're using it for general workouts, it might be stay in place well and it might not offer as much friction for motions like burpees and quicker, higher energy workouts.

Depending on your usage, I'm not certain about the durability of this mat. It looks about the same as most other softer foam mats and it will eventually wear out, but it doesn't seem flimsy or cheap.

Overall it's a decent mat, but only for low-intensity activities.

I don't expect them to last for super long because the ones at the gym that are supposedly "commercial grade" snap after repeated use. And unless you plan on sharing these with the neighbors, you don't have to worry about whose sweat it is.

It comes with a little mesh bag that is a good thing because these will need to be dried out after you work up a sweat.

title: Good quality bike, quiet, strong, but poor bluetooth software.
text:
I have only had this a few days so will update the review if needed in the future.

Initial impressions have been very positive so far for the build and quality of the bike. I found the instructions very good and easy to follow. They were well written which is amazing all by itself. I had no problems following the instructions and it took about 45 minutes to put together. The only issue I ran into was the handle bar cover (small plastic piece that covers mounting screws), almost got thrown away, as it is in the packing material where everything else was a bit separate. Just make sure you don't accidently throw it away.

The bike seems to be very well built, and parts all lined up without any issues during assembly. A couple of parts are a bit on the heavy side so you might need someone to help you hold the handle bar support bar while you make the electronic connections, other than that I expect most folks should be able to put this together on their own.

Pros:
Once assembled the bike itself is very sturdy and feels very strong. I am a big person 6'8, and it supports me without any issues.
Very quiet, in fact the little fan is louder than peddling the bike. The fan is not load by any measure, but the bike is very quiet.
Great assembly instructions and packaging
Nice mat included

Cons:
Bluetooth integration -- This is very poor unfortunately. While you can sync to the app, you can't sync to your music or audio on your device so the speakers will not work without attaching the included cable to your device.
Andriod app -- This is very poor. Basically it shows you your speed and some of the stats, but you lose all functionality of the built in computer in this mode. this means you have to set the resistance manually and can't use any of the programs or features. The app itself has no built in programs so you have to manually adjust the resistance as you go along. Also doesn't seem to work with any other of the much better rated apps that are available. The current app has a 2 star rating, and I think 2 stars would be stretch for this software.

I purchased TurboJam and went from a size 18 to a 12 in five months in 2006. I'm currently a size 16 and have been stuck since 2008 after the birth of my son 4 years ago. TurboJam was just boring and after seeing my long lost friend Chalene on an infomercial advertising this product I was excited to try this. I quit smoking on March 23, ditch the wine and laced up my shoes and got busy. The choreography is difficult. The Fire Starter class took me two weeks to learn. (May take you less, I was struggling to quit smoking while learning this).Thank God some of these moves I learned from TurboJam or I would have given up.
I tried the new to class option and its not cued well and it takes forever to work off the clock. I'm a college student and busy mom and the New Class option can take longer. Every DVD the choreography is different and I hate that aspect as well. I just want to do the workout and get on with my day. I decided to learn all the moves on the cardio DVDs first before I add the HIIT, Core, Sculpt, Abs. You don't have to learn any moves for these, they are cued workouts. The only thing I don't like is the "fake" spray tanned women in the video because its misleading. Spray tans bring out the best on your body and make you look lean, sculpted, and thinner. I was disappointed Chalene allowed that.
I think the positive I've gotten out of the video is I'm approaching day 60, and I went from 240 to 220. I'm still a size 16, but the results are real and noticeable. Im almost in a size 14 and I'm excited about my 90 days being up in June 2013. I will do another 90 days of TurboFire, which will be a total of 180 days. I will then incorporate ChaLean Xtreme Hybrid Program.
I think if you are tired of being fat and overweight you can achieve anything. Just keep pushing play and don't give up. Also I don't count calories I just picked a few meals from breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and eat them and use portion control. Good Luck.

CONs

- Lastly, the side pockets are barely large enough to fit shoes. They do fit, but they bulge into the ball compartment. It's not a big deal. In one of my photos I drew a pink line indicating the width of one of the side pockets with a pair of shoes in it.

As long as you're not dropping/plopping the bag down onto a hard surface regularly, this bag will do very well.

title: Excellent little insulated tote...
text:
I call this a tote rather than a cooler because it does more than a cooler does. In fact, I'll be using it mostly to transport warm items than I will cold.

PROs
- I love the dark blue color(C2-blue). I saw a photo on a different review and it looked like a brighter blue. Unless there was a different color offered that I'm unaware of, the dark blue is true to color on the listing.
- This will hold quite a bit. If you're like me and plan on using it to bring food items to potlucks, this will do well.
- The top pocket (also insulated) can hold any utensils, spices, napkins, or other items you may want to bring along. Or more ice packs, if using it as a cooler.
- There's an additional front (insulated) pocket and two side mesh pockets for whatever your heart desires. Pockets galore.
- It's collapsible.
- There are two handles that meet in the center and can be held together with a short hook and loop sleeve. That makes it so convenient, particularly if you're carrying heavier items. The handles aren't digging into your hands then. Instead there's a sleeve adding comfort.
- There is an optional shoulder strap, however, see the cons below for further detail...

CONs
- The optional shoulder strap is nice to have, however, the point of weight bearing lies upon two plastic hooks on each side. I've included a photo of one of them. I don't believe I would trust those when carrying heavier loads.
- The bottom of the bag does not have a hard surface. I will likely find something I can put on the bottom to make it firm when carrying items of different sizes, etc. Perhaps I'll double up on some cardboard and wrap it in foil or something. I'm not sure yet.

All in all I love this bag and would definitely recommend it.

title: Vest has saved me while retraining a spooky horse
text: I've had  a 11 year old quarter horse/connemarra mix gelding for almost three years. His history was unknown when I bought him.  He's a beautiful horse, but has needed complete re-training. He can be spooky on trails when we go out alone - which is something I do a lot (3-5 times a week) as there aren't many people to ride with where I'm located. So, I wear the vest every time I go out and carry my cell phone to be safer.  I've come off 3-4 times in the last three years when he has spooked while trotting because he tends to spin around -- and this vest has allowed me to get up with NO injuries, no soreness and NO fear.  Before I bought the vest, I would be very tense during our rides, but now I'm relaxed knowing that if he does have a bad spook while trotting through a field, I'll be ok. AND as he has gotten more used to trail riding alone, it is happening less and less. Highly recommend this vest. My only issue is deflating it when I re-mount after is has deployed. I'm sure there's. a way to do It, but I haven't taken the time to figure it out.....yet.

title: SHOUTS OF JOY TURNED TO GNASHING OF TEETH AS WE DISCOVERED THIS HAMMOCK IS PLASTIC!!!
text:
We were so looking forward to receiving this hammock - but when it arrived, our hopes and dreams were dashed to the ground like refuse thrown into a gutter! The hammock took longer than expected to arrive - but not to worry-- we patiently checked Amazon tracking on a daily basis to see when the refreshment of lying on a soft, sturdy hammock whilst sipping a cocktail - would arrive at our door. After waiting on the edge of our plastic lawn chairs for two weeks, the big day finally arrived! The hammock was delivered by our friendly Amazon courier and shouts of joy could be heart resounding through the halls of our home! Two of our sons ceremoniously carried the long hammock box into the house like a wealthy Roman patron being carried through the streets on a litter. The box was opened and said hammock was unrolled like a precious scroll. Visions of hours spent snoozing under a canopy of trees danced in the heads of family members as they clamored to put this 'Object of 'Liesure and Rest' onto the stand that had carried our old, canvas, LL BEAN hammock. After 14 years of service, that good sanctuary had finally rotted away. (Actually, I wasn't home for this part, but I'm sure this is how it went.)

Our faithful and strong sons set the hammock up beneath towering Tulip Populars, wafting in the refreshing breeze and waited for me to come home hoping to unveil a pleasant surprise for the beloved mother. I arrived home, hot, sweaty and tired from a long day of horseback riding with my faithful steed. A persistent headache was pounding in my brain from hours of tracking desperados through the forests. (Ok, I was actually trying to catch up to my friends who had galloped away rather prematurely.) Anyway, as I slogged through the house, wilted and exhausted, my god-like son winked at me whilst ushering me through the back door to the paradise that awaited in the back yard.

THERE IT WAS! THE HAMMOCK for which I had been longing! I sat down on the side and stretched my battered frame onto the hammock like Cleopatra reclining under a gold-embroidered canopy dressed as Aphrodite, (but wearing riding boots and half-chaps).....only to discover that the hammock of my dreams was an imposter!!!! THIS WAS NO SOFT BED OF ROSES TO LIE ON! NO! IT FELT LIKE BAD CARPET ON THE WALLS OF A CHEAP MOTEL! I stifled my revulsion and tried to get comfortable but it was no use. The fabric wasn't fabric at all - it felt like plastic water bottles woven into a nightmarish tapestry by well-intentioned environmentalists! I leapt from this bed of vipers disgusted and disappointed. My family pleaded with me to give it another chance, saying "It's not so bad, we like it!" "Philistines!!!!" I retorted! " THIS. WILL. NOT. DO!" whilst gnashing my teeth to the best of my ability. To which they shrugged and got the box out of the trash so we could return it.

Postscript - If you want a comfy hammock made out of sunbrella fabric, you have to spend about $250 these days. I found one on Wayfair and now we are anxiously awaiting that one to be delivered. Cheers! :)

title: The Mirrycle's Assembly similar to a Greek Tragedy.....
text: Alas, dear friends, I admit....... somewhat reluctantly of course........ that i found the assembly of the "Mirrycle" somewhat of a challenge and never actually arrived at that happy moment I had dreamed of -- riding contentedly on my road bike and being able to cast a glance down at my "Mirrycle" to see if some danger was lurking behind as I peddled my beloved bicycle through the wicked city streets.  This thing has not been machined as well as one would hope.  Despite my heroic efforts, I just could not get the first screw into it's intended spot on Mirrycle's extension piece because the threads on the screw do not seem to match up with the interior threads cut into the plastic 'tapped hole' on the plastic extension that screws to the mirror.  I found that I had to expend a Herculian effort just to get the first screw into the hole.  And, while I'm not an engineer, auto mechanic or strangely gifted with screwdrivers, I do consider myself competent enough to use one.  Maybe if I had hands as big as bear paws, I could have forced it...but alas...I do not possess such paws.  SO.... I went in search of my old standby, WD40, to loosen the screw which was - at this point, hopeless stuck in the hole.  --Only after applying more WD40  was I able to complete the task of getting the first poorly machined part together.  To my surprise, they fit well or seemed to --as that was as far as I got in this overachiever's nightmare. Because, as we 'lovers of WD40" know, all too well, it drips terribly and makes everything that you didn't want to slide, very slippery. So, what I had thought was going to be a pleasant hour spent putting on my new bike mirror started to twist and turn into something else....a maddening morning cavorting down the road of imbecilic incompetence!  I had unintentionally involved myself in someone's diabolic effort to create havoc in our Republic by using the simplest of methods: assembling a plastic mirror!  Still - I was not to be defeated! I carefully  wiped the small, smooth pieces of plastic down, NOT ONCE, NOT TWICE...but THRICE! No, nothing could stop me from getting this wretched product together at this point, even if I was still in my pajamas.  BUT, little did I know I faced an even more diabolical obstacle because the second screw presented me with the identical problem.  And, yes, I had to repeat the application of WD40 again.  It was almost too much to bear, but then I remembered!  "I'm not a mere mortal, I'm a cyclist! I can bike 100 miles a week! And everyone else who reviewed this thing on Amazon LOVES IT!"  Tragically, I was not victorious in my quest to fully assemble my nifty Mirrcyle MTB Bar End Mountain Bike Mirrow, because at the quintessential moment when it seemed like victory was within my grasp -in when the second screw was about to be turned into place, ....tragedy struck!  The whole slippery mess  slipped  -  literally - from my grasp and went crashing to the wooden floor in my kitchen and the glass mirror cracked into many pieces........... taking with it all my hopes and dreams of having a mirror that actually functions on my road bike.  I was as shattered as my broken Mirrycle and slumped over the couch in defeat.  I did order another mirror - but decided that I'm just going to do without one for now.  I haven't wanted to waste precious riding time wrestling with it.  If I do, I'll update.  Cheers and happy riding!

title: Very nice!
text:
I bought this for my fiancé for Christmas, he needed a new emergency backpack. You never really know what you’re getting when you’re ordering stuff like this online...one review will say it’s garbage, the next will say it’s the best thing ever. I’m pretty good at judging which ones are accurate, and which ones are super-biased - either for or against.

This is a very good backpack! It’s worth more than what they’re charging for it. I looked (in person) at some 3.11 Tactical backpacks, and, this measures up in every single aspect, at a fraction of the price (for those that haven’t seen them, they’re generally well over $100). Also, the 3.11s that I looked at didn’t have padded waist straps like this one, and didn’t come with the bladder, like this one does. The padded waist straps alone up the value, plus there’s small zipper pockets on them to stash keys or whatever in...they don’t hold a plus size iPhone though. Just a smidge too small. You don’t realize how important padded waist straps can be until you’re stuck with carrying 30lbs on your back and those plain straps are digging into you, even through a heavier coat.

The padding in the back is just as good as the Swiss Army backpack I have, it’s not itchy if it gets against your skin, and it does pretty good at keeping you cool...as cool as you can be with a bag strapped to your back, at least.

There’s plenty of pockets so you can organize you’re supplies for better accessibility and it does have the nice straps on the bottom to attach a bedroll (yoga mat, if you choose) or pup tent. There’s plenty of places to add/attach other accessories and pouches. Also, the compartment for the bladder is insulated. I can’t really say how well because we haven’t tested it, but it seems it would be decent.

All around, this is just a really, really good pack, especially for the price! I fully intend on buying myself one very soon because all of my backpacks are shot (my “everyday”, and my emergency bags), and this just fit the bill...I almost kept it for myself! 😁

title: Expensive but worth it - 5 stars
text: The worst thing about these speed clips is the price.  Other than that, they are easy to use and virtually indestructible.  I have never had a PROPERLY attached speed clip come unattached.  Actually, once you get them installed, they can be a real b*tch to take out, but generally it's worse installing them.  Do at your own risk, but I use a butter knife or a small or in some cases a large flat head screwdriver to spread and guide these clips thru webbing.  I think I paid about $13-15 for a pack of 6 of the #5 black which I find myself using more than any other size.  Have to begrudgingly give 5 stars, even if they are expensive pieces of "plastic".

title: Really like this vest - 5 stars
text: For less than $50, and you can find them occasionally on sale/discount, this was almost exactly what I wanted.  I wanted a vest I could wear OVER my armor carrier, and this fit the bill.  I know it says "paintball" in the title/description.  As a former paintball player and paintball field owner and Blackhawk gear dealer, I can tell you so far this vest is very good.  If I am not satisfied later, I will come back and modify my rating.  The first thing I checked out was the zipper.  The zipper seems to be very strong and very good.  Also, there are 2 small speed fastener buckles across the chest.  Normally, I don't like anything adding more bulk, but these fasteners SHOULD help keep that zipper from pulling apart.  I have put attachments on and off and back on and off this vest, and the vest has done very well so far.  The vest is highly adjustable and customizable.  Again, this fit my special purpose of having a body armor carrier underneath with the vest with all my gear on top of the armor carrier.  I wanted to be able to still wear my armor even after I took my tactical vest off, and this fit the bill almost perfectly.  MOLLE attachment points all over this thing makes it possible to set up pretty much however someone wants, and it's still not too bulky for me.  5 stars for now.

title: Wish they were less expensive but 5 stars anyway
text: Extremely strong.  I did NOT put 150# on these to test, but these hold a full set of firefighter turnout gear no problem.  Lightweight, strong, waterproof, and I haven't seen and flakes or chips after dropping these hangers on the floor.  I've bought 3 sets so far.  I don't love the price at about $25 for 2, but really that's the only thing I can complain about.  I suppose somebody SHOULD get paid for their creativity.  About $13 each is an ouch tho I paid it anyway.  Imagine me spending about $75 for 6 hangers....but what is the alternative?  Flimsy plastic coat hangers?  If you need these then buy once cry once, I think.  5 stars overall.

title: I really like this carrier - 5 stars
text: I have 2 sets of plates/inserts.  So I bought 2 carriers.  The 10x12 fits great.  The 11x14 did NOT fit my set.  It was too tight, just FYI, and I really had to jam my 11x14 plates in there, and I didn't like it.  But we're talking about the 10x12 right now.  Simple, lightweight, surprisingly well-made with just 1 stitch out of place.  I was looking for a very compact carrier to wear UNDER my tactical vest so I could still have armor on even after taking off my tactical vest.  The only place this carrier might be a LITTLE bulky is up on the should straps, but this carrier is still wayyy better and slimmer than any other I have found so far in the $50 price range.  For this price point and construction and simplicity and fit, this gets 5 stars.  If I am every unhappy with this carrier, I will change my review.

title: Perfect fit - 5 stars
text: I use this holster exclusively to carry my CZ75 compact and CZ75 full-size.  It is a perfect fit, except my compact barrel is a little short of the end of the holster.  I also have the full-size CZ75, and the holster is a perfect fit all-around.  I am a big fan of FOBUS products.  5 stars

title: 2 pack of Kill Flash - 5 stars
text: For $13 for 2 of these, they can't be beat.  I did read the item description that said they fit up to 43mm, but I took a chance that they would fit on my 44mm rifle scopes objective lenses.  These are cushioned spring clips.  They are NOT super heavy duty, but they are functional.  They do fit onto a 44mm objective lens.  They could easily be knocked off in the brush, should you have to run thru any.  They do what they are supposed to do, tho.  I shined a flashlight into the unit, and I got no flashback, so I'd say it's good in sunlight.  I also intend to take a small but stout rubber band and put the rubber band over the clamps to help keep the kill flash clamps more snug onto the front of the scope objective lens.  I say again, these will come off if scraped or rubbed very hard against something.  I do believe the best flash killers are the ones that thread directly inside of the objective lenses that have internal threads.  Those options are also a lot more money.  So for the money and function, these flash killers get 5 stars for now.  If they happen to fall off under heavy recoil (I shoot 308 and 30-06), I will change my rating.

title: Tactical sling adapter - 5 stars so far
text: I've used these adapters on several builds.  I'm not sure what the breaking point on these units is, and I don't want to find out.  They seem to be fine so far for every day sling attachment points.  They are aluminum or similar alloy.  The mounting screw goes completely thru one side and threads into the the other side making a very solid attachment onto a rail.  You do need to have a slotted rail, as the adapter needs to be slid onto the slotted rail, then the screw needs to be threaded into the slot and then back into the other side to work properly.

title: My every day lawful concealed carry magazine carrier (and holster) for 1911
text: This is what I use for lawful concealed carry for my full size 1911.  I have tried MANY different holsters and mag carriers, and I am using the Fobus C-21 for my pistol and the original 4500 for 2 mags.  I want to mention that I bought these 2 items many years ago when they first hit the market.  I have had ZERO problems with either in that time.  I believe it's been at least 10 years since I bought these.  I also bought for Glock, and they are flawless as well.  These items are super lightweight and durable.  They don't crack, peel, soak up sweat, shrink, or "give" like a nylon or leather holster might.  As another review mentioned, they are super concealable.  I use mine in conjunction with a concealed carry dress belt I purchased here, and the fit is impressive and perfect when the paddle locks in.  Until something better comes along, this is what I will continue to use.

title: Neoprene toe warmers
text: These are great little toe warmers.  My feet are always cold and damp in the deer stand it seems.  These will keep your feet warm, but in my experience, your feet will be moist BUT warm.  I bought 2 pair so I can wash a set at deer camp and have them drying while I wear the other set.  I wash them by hand in a small quart size container in the sink with soap and water and squeeze out as much water as I can and then hang them to air dry.  Personal preferences may vary, but I like mine.  I do wear mine over bare feet and then put wool socks over them to keep them in place and the rest of my foot warm.  Use at your own risk and discretion.

title: Best on-gun camera I've found so far
text: Best little on-gun camera I've bought so far.  I got the one without the laser and the one with the laser when it first came out.  The laser is good for short range or indoors, but pretty much a novelty outdoors, in my opinion and experience.  I've shot a lot of videos with this unit already this year, and they came out very well.  The audio is almost too good on my unit.  This microphone picks up almost every single creak and groan and breath and movement within a wide radius.  On several of my videos, it picked up deer walking thru leaves 20 yards away.  I really like how the operator just flips one lever, and then the red light comes on to let them know the unit is recording.  The mini SD card is a little tricky getting in and out, but what did you expect on a compact unit of this nature?  I use a wooden toothpick and gently push the card in to release the catch taking it out and put it in by hand as far as I can, and then I click the card into place with theh toothpick.  Battery life has been good so far, even in cold weather.  I love the fact that the recording magnification is fixed.  No more fumbling around with a zoom trying to get just the perfect magnification.  It is what it is, so just make sure it's recording (and don't forget to take the lens cap off like I did one time) and point and shoot.  It takes videos of deer-sized animals at 50 yards and under very well, and I also shot a nice buck this year with my muzzleloader at 116 yards, and it wasn't bad video at all.  Operator error is drastically reduced.  Also, if you have it indoors and take it outdoors, makes sure to wipe the lens with an scope lens cloth or similar if it fogs up on the outside of the lens.  Had that happen as well.  Again, operator error.  My unit has held up to 12ga 3" slug recoil from a bolt action shotgun, my 50cal muzzleloader, and a 175lb crossbow, and 70lb compound bow so far with no problems.  I paid about $88 on here, and $15 for the memory card (not included).  If you have a weapon that has a rail and you want to video, this is the one to get.  I imagine it would work great for paintball as well.  Buy it.

title: This is a great little rail adapter
text: This is a great little rail adapter.  I don't love the price, but it was about $15.  I use this in conjunction with my Shot Trak HD for video on my shotgun, muzzleloader, and crossbow so far.  Mounts left or right on a standard rail.  Be sure not to over-tighten, as some rails are fatter, and some rails are thinner that you will attach it to them.

title: A little pricey, but a very sturdy cot for smaller people 5' or so
text: This has been a very good little cot so far.  It's not big enough for me unless I curl up on it (which I have--I'm 6'), but my 5'1" partner thinks it's perfect.  She likes silk pillows, and they will slide around on the covering for the mattress, so be aware.  When I use it, I wrap the pillow in a towel or blanket, and that keeps the pillows from skidding around so much.  This unit folds up nicely, and is pretty easily store-able.  You have to pull out the mattress pad and turn it around when you receive it, but it's not a big deal.  Also, the "legs" snap into plan firmly and have never collapsed on me or her, but they are a pain in the butt the first time until you get used to manipulating them.  I wish the price were about $35 instead of $55.  Overall, a very good item.  I recommend it.

title: Great IWB concealed carry holster for great price
text: Great holster.  Great price.  I have worn this holster almost every day since I received it.  It is a bit stiff when new.  I have had to wear it and let body heat, body shape, and wear and tear (so to speak) mold this holster.  There is another brand out there that is very similar to this holster, and it is about double the price.  I carry my full size 5" 1911 in this holster with a high-quality concealed carry belt I purchased on Amazon for about $50.  I also use a crossover design with Perry suspenders to help support this weight.  I carry my pistol on one side and 3 mags in pouches on the other side as this rig is supporting a very heavy full-size pistol on the one side and 3 full mags of 45ACP on the other side.  I like how this is molded.  When brand new, it was very difficult to pull out until broken in.  My front sight did scratch up the leather inside a bit, but not a big deal.  I do like this is made is USA.  The spring clips are very sturdy.  I believe but cannot guarantee it would be almost impossible for my 1911 to fall out of this holster.  I also believe it is almost impossible (but cannot guarantee) for someone to snatch my 1911 out of the holster.  If I have any negative experience, I will report back.  Very good product so far.

title: wetsuit XXXL
text: One of my best purchases this year.  I use it in conjunction with the 5mm neoprene socks.  I wear a long john top and bottom under this when I go deer hunting.  Works great for blocking wind.

title: 5mm neoprene socks
text: I love these things.  They have kept my feet warm so far this deer season, and they are wayyyy less expensive than sealskins or goretex socks, and they are MUCH more comfortable.  I have owned just about every kind of booty for trying to keep my feet warm.  I have bought just about 1 pair of everything out there, I think.  The only downside to these is they ARE neoprene, so if your feet sweat, your feet will be moist inside the booty/sock.  You will be wet, but they will stay warm, and your feet will stay warm, in my experience.  I put on a medium pair of wool-type socks, these socks over that, and then my insulated felt pack boots.  I am size 11 foot, and the XXL fits almost perfectly over 1 pair of socks for me.  Also, when I go back to the hunting cabin, I turn these inside out and hang them about 3 feet from the woodstove about 4 to 6 feet high, and they dry very quickly.  I would warn against getting them too close to any intense heat source.  Overall, very, very good for my purposes, even tho I realize this is not their intended purpose.

title: Expandable Arbor
text: Works great with my kit thru .50 caliber I had bought years ago.  Got me on the paper with my 12 gauge bolt action at 50 yds first shot using a 4x compact scope.  With the price of these high-performance shotgun slugs (my Winchesters are about $2.50 each shot), you can pay for this arbor pretty darn fast.  I was 12ft up in the stand, and the target was on the ground about 50 yds away, about 10 inches in diameter about 2 feet off the ground, similar to a kill zone on a deer, and I put 4 shots in that area.  I actually was 10 inches low and 10 inches left from boresighting, but got kill shots on #3 and #4.  Very happy with this arbor.  I recommend bore sighting and then shoot from the height and distance you are most likely to shoot at a deer, and zero your scope in.  Good luck.

title: MB 19 Vol 2 - or is it Vol 1?
text: My DVD case says Vol 2, but the DVD says Vol 1.  I don't really care which Volume it is...  The hunts were pretty good.  I'm not overly impressed with someone using a high powered rifle to shoot deer over 100+ yards away, and I'm definitely not impressed with someone using a rifle while they are sitting in a box to shoot deer.  I do realize all these hunters need work and videos need to be sold, and I realize it is difficult to get a camera operator and a hunter and the deer to all come together in one location at a precise moment and capture the whole thing on film.  A person could argue it is not a "fair fight" pitting a human against an animal to begin with, let alone, having the human in a stand or in a box using a bow, shotgun, or rifle.  Not a big fan of Tyler Jordan, who I am jealous of (LOL) because he gets to hunt because his Daddy owns Realtree...  RHIP, I guess, lol.  Nobody forced me to buy their video.  Their camo patterns are really good.  Overall, I enjoyed watching the videos,and I felt I got my money's worth.

title: reversible blaze orange and camo--great cap
text: I really like this cap.  I've had it out in the rain, and it does appear to be waterproof.  It is also very warm.  I have a very thin full camo face mask, and I wear this over the top, and it is great.  I also like the fact that I can wear it during seasons requiring blaze orange by just reversing it.  This cap also has stitching around the fold to keep the cap fold-over even when wearing the camo side out.  I guess that's so you have to cut the stitch out of fold it over for the blaze orange side.  I am just going to leave it the way it is.  I like the blaze orange on the inside for when I harvest a deer, I can reverse that cap and show the blaze orange side for safety when dragging my deer out. title: Leupold RCX-2 with viewer - so far so good *UPDATED* 11/6/13
text:
I read some of the other reviews on this camera, and it appears the reviews of this kit are either really good, or really bad. My review is really good, so far. If my experience changes, I will revise my review. I must give a disclaimer that I've only used this in my office indoors so far and have not used any nite photography yet, but I am impressed--so far. Not too much bad I can say about this camera so far. Do NOT pay $179.99 or more for this setup. Go to sportsmansguide and get it for under $170 (plus shipping)last time I looked. I actually bought mine from SG on a Whitetail Wednesday last week for $122 plus shipping thru the club. I comes with everything shown in the kit, I think, except the "jumper cables" to hook up to an external battery. I have (2) Wildgame Innovations Night Shots (see my review), and I haven't used any others, so I will compare this camera to them. Leupold has thot of almost everything for this camera and viewer. The pictures are very good. The video is decent. The time-lapse function is great--I hadn't expected it on this camera. The "viewer" is a viewer on steroids, lol. It's got almost everything I could think of on it. Controls for day and nite, frames per second, video, camera resolution, AND--a big deal to me--it has ZOOM up to 4x AND you can scroll around the screen while in ZOOM. Very, very good option. I bought the cheaper Moultrie viewer (about $65 when I bought it), and this viewer/controller blows it away hands down. I would actually recommend a person buy this camera and viewer setup almost just to get the viewer. Moultrie has a viewer that is about $100, and it looks pretty good, so maybe if you don't need another trail camera, just buy their viewer and try it. I wish I had discovered this setup sooner because I would have sent the $65 Moultrie back, but it's OK. I love the fact that I can drill a small drywall or similar screw into a tree and just hang this camera. That is really, really helpful. This camera also has a cable slot so I can cable-lock it onto a tree if I want to leave it. It also has a padlock latch on it so I can lock up my flashcards and on/off switch access door. I've read that this unit will not function properly without lithium AA batteries. I'm currently using Duracell alkalines. I'll report back how well they hold up. I've ordered (24) lithium AA batteries to try out just in case. Amazon has them here for $40 for (24). Best price I've seen so far on Prime membership. I'm very interested in seeing how it works out hooking a motorcycle or car battery up to this as well. It would also be interesting to see how some other lithium battery hook-ups might perform with this unit. I used to be an avid RC airplane flyer, and there have been some amazing breakthrus in RC lithium batteries. Just a thot...do so at your own risk. I will report more later.

*** UPDATE 11/6/13 ***

Lowering my rating from 5 stars to 3 stars. For Leupold to put their name on this product (made in China also) and produce such crappy video is a travesty. The photos and video looked fantastic in my office, but not in the woods. The video is (I believe) 640x480 which used to be referred to as VGA. Horrible, given today's technology. I am by no means a trail cam expert, but comparing this to my Lights Out--there is no comparison. My WI Lights Out runs circles around this camera. There is no comparison to the HD video on the WI LO camera and this camera using technology from 10 years ago. I am also downgrading for the Night / Day operation hours. Unless I'm doing something wrong, and I will apologize if I am, whatever the last thing you punch in on the controller for hours of operation (other than 24 hours), say Night from 1600 to 2000, that's all you get. Even if I typed in Day operation hours of 0600 to 1000, and then punched in 1600 to 2000 for Night, the only thing the camera recognizes is 1600 to 2000 for operation, with no Day pictures. It is possible I did it wrong several times in a row, but I don't think so. This camera does not trigger unless a critter is almost dead in front of it and loiters for a while. I tried all the angle settings and sensitivities. Now, the time lapse operation is almost flawless, and if you want a decent time lapse camera, this might be for you. I have a 32GB flashcard in my camera now, and I check it once a week. I had it set on taking a picture every 30 seconds. I have adjusted that to taking a picture every 15 seconds now. I'm also having it going from 0500 to 2000 every day. I know it's taking a crapload of pictures that I have to look at, but that is the only way I could "trick" the camera into getting my morning and evening photos. If anyone has any solutions to getting the DAY / NIGHT settings to function properly, please let me know. Anyway...the 10MB pictures are really good, altho I still like my WI LO wide-angle HD cameras better. The bottom line for the good is the Leupold RCX-2 has an almost bulletproof housing, it is really handy to hang it on a screw drilled into a tree (I use pan-head self-drilling cabinet screws 1 7/8 inches long with a cordless impact driver)compared to using straps or bungee cords, the time lapse option is very handy, and the controller/photo viewer is really nifty. The downside to this setup is/are the camera does not trigger until game is right in front of it (my camera, anyway) and I mean like 10 to 15 feet from the camera maximum, the operations hours do not work properly, and the video technology is ancient and grainy--horrible, in my opinion. I think the saving graces to this setup are the controller/viewer and the time lapse option with the 10MB photo capability. I expected better from something that says Leupold on it.

title: Moultrie Digital Picture Viewer - 4 stars
text:
I like the viewer pretty well overall. I will tell you what I like first. It's fairly compact. The rubber grip surfaces make it easier to hold. I like that it has uses 4 AAA batteries. Devices with 4 batteries USUALLY have very long battery life, in my experience. It appears that all the covers to the buttons and hatches, etc, are water resistant and maybe waterproof. I like the positive slide on-off "click" of the power button. I love that I can leave one 16gb flashcard internal, and plug in a 2nd flashcard, and then without looking at any of the pictures, transfer everything off the 2nd card to the 1st card (assuming there's room), and then put the 2nd card back into the trail camera. That might be this viewer's best feature--the 2 SD card slots feature. The screen is adequate, altho I feel to really look at the pics, you should look at them on a laptop or desktop computer.

OK, here's what I don't like. I don't like the SD card sticking out of the bottom of the viewer. I would rather it be pressed into the slot and catch with the spring-loaded catch like the internal card slot, and be able to completely close the cover on the SD card. BUT, I realize they may have made it that way so you could take the card out with gloves on, cold fingers, etc. I also don't like how that rubber flap kinda hangs in the breeze when I peel it off to insert a card. I don't like how you can't see all the pics on the screen in a matrix (unless I haven't figured that out yet, and if I'm wrong, I will apologize) and choose from them. I don't like how you have to scroll thru the pics. I also think it takes too long to transfer photos from the trail cam card to the internal card.

I know I'm being nit-picky about some of my dislikes, but I still gave it 4 stars. Oh, also, I paid about $65 (with shipping) not on Amazon Prime, because it wasn't available for Prime when I ordered it, and I noticed today that it was about $51 on Amazon Prime from another vendor. Oh well, it's a decent buy, for sure at $51 and Prime shipping, and an OK buy at $65.

title: Be prepared with this 16-in-1 survival kit with durable tactical gear
text: We have been working on assembling a couple go bags for our family in case of an emergency, such as a natural disaster, fire, etc. WORSPODAY's 16-in-1 survival kit is the perfect addition to it. First of all, the price is on point and provides a huge savings over having to buy each of the items included individually. Second, we love the watertight hardback case that the tools come in. It has strong clasps on three sides and they don't just pop open. You have to tug pretty hard on them, so that actually is important so you don't lose your gear when you're on the move and may need it most. Second, the tactical gear that is included isn't cheaply made. These are durable products, such as the tactical pen (with a glass breaker on one end), flashlight (needs one AA battery), and the knife. Even the compass is fairly weighty in your hand and works very well. Also, because of the amount of detail that goes into these items, this whole kit makes a handsome gift that any outdoorsman would appreciate too. We also like the tactical bracelet because even if that is all you have on you, there is also a flint built in so you can start a fire, a whistle, and a compass. Also, it is made of paracord, so you can use it to tie up an emergency shelter or go fishing if need be. The manual that comes with it is detailed, but you will want to become well familiar with each item included and how to use it before you head out to the woods or on your trek as you may try to outrun a storm. Also, there are a few items included such as the glass breaker end of the pen, the saw, and of course the knife, which could cut someone, particularly a child, so you'll want to make sure those who handle it aren't going to accidentally injure themselves because these items are definitely not toys. All in all, however, this is an exceptional product, and I plan to recommend it to everyone I know who may be putting together their own go bag.

I used whole milk from a regional dairy, mid-price range. I don't think the brand matters as much as the freshness of the milk. I made 7 small cups (4-6 oz ea) in an Epica yogurt maker with one packet of starter culture. However, I did add 10 tablespoons of non-fat dried milk to the 3.5 cups whole milk because I wanted a firmer yogurt. My instructions were to cook 10 hours for firm but I went 11 hours because it was my first time. I will probably do 10 next time because I bought a strainer to make greek yogurt after cooking.

I think this starter will work for you as long as you follow instructions, and the vendor provides lots of instruction. Making yogurt really is simple and once you get used to it you will not want to go back to store bought. I received nothing for my review. I never do. I just share my experiences.

title: Best tent ever.. An investment that will last for a lifetime!!!!
text:
LOVE LOVE LOVE this tent!!!
We have previously owned the classic cheaper coleman tents and when ours wore out, we bought a new coleman... upon opening it, it had tears in the seams...I boxed it up and sent it back. We were so upset by the lack of craftsmanship we decided to research better quality canvas tents. We are a young family and liked the idea of a tent that we could use for years to come. We decided on the 10x14, it's very spacious and we are able to set up a queen, and twin air mattress with plenty of room to store our bags/totes and a large dog/bed. I am a petite lady and I was able to put this tent up by myself (only took 25 min from box to erect, while stopping to look at the directions) it is a very heavy tent, but I was able to put it up with a bit of effort.
Once up I was able to really get a look at this tent... WOW! This tent is large and heavy duty! The floor is a thick rubber-like material that you can tell isn't gonna leak (and it didn't, even when there were puddles of rain water between the tarp below and tent) I sprayed the tent down (as per directions) prior to our first camping trip. And off we went...
This tent has turned heads every time we camp, it is a heavy duty, quality tent that we know will last for years to come... It is so simple to put up, and we are so pleased with our investment.
We have not yet had it stand the test of a storm, but I have no doubt it will hold up well.
As far as staying warm, the larger tent makes it difficult to stay warm, so bundle up and use warm blankets ;)

Oh, did I mention the tent storage bag?!?! It's awesome, and your tent will always fit, no need for super tight refilling to make it fit in the bag, this bag adjusts and will always fit your rolled up tent (we fold in half, then half again, roll and adjust the bag to fit )

To summarize:
Pros:
Large roomy tent that you can stand and walk around in, the walls are straight so you don't lose storage room
Durable canvas that is waterproof
Quality thick floor that will not leak
Heavy duty metal rods/poles and steaks
Large doors and windows makes the tent feel even more open and allows a cross breeze
The ingenious tent bag that will always be able to fit the tent once rolled up

Cons:
The long poles (when storing) and the weight of the tent
No electrical slot for extension cords (have to put them through the door)

Overall If you are in the market for a quality tent that will last for years to come...buy this tent!

title: A dingo ate my baby? ☹️
text:
My nickname has been turtle since I was 3 yo, thanks to my dearly departed dad who also happened to be my best friend. My dad was pretty much a single parent who had to be both my father & my mother, until he met my “adoptive mother” when I was 18 yo.
This past Christmas my “mom” got me this ring as a gift but she pointed out that it wasn’t a ring from my “ mother” but it was a gift from my dad who spent many years being a mother to me. My “adoptive mother” got me a different ring altogether from a mother to her daughter & I’ve cherished both of my rings since I put them on. Unfortunately the baby turtle fell off the mama turtle w/in the first 24 hours of receiving it. I’ve done numerous searches to find where the ring came from (my adoptive mother has early stages of Alzheimer’s so she couldn’t remember where she got the ring) I still cherish my ring for what it stands for but I really wish the baby was still intact. I thought if I could find where she bought the ring from I could just buy a replacement ring w/the baby attached so it would it would make me feel better but now that I finally found the same original ring I realized that it has nothing to do w/the ring itself, but more what it signifies to me.
It seems pretty obvious that the ring has a major defect & the baby turtle falls off on most of the reviews so I won’t bother trying to replace it anyway but I would give it WAY more than 5 stars if the baby didn’t fall off.
I’m giving it 3 stars regardless bc of the sentimental value. It’s not fancy & doesn’t look expensive but if you understand the turtle “lifestyle” then I would recommend this ring.
It’s just one of those things, if you know, then you’ll get it. 🐢
Long live the slow & steady lifestyle. You might not win any races but you’ll definitely be able to appreciate everything else along the way 😊

The second scooter came in COMPLETELY different packaging. Looked legit this time - graphics on the box, in plastic sheeting, etc. Just used the scooter to go about a mile each way (with hills) and it was fine for a 6ft 1in 190lb guy. Did use 1/4 of the battery doing so. The throttle and break levers both stick, so pay attention as it will continue to power even after letting go of the throttle and vise versa for the break. We shall see if it can stand the test of time. I did get the insurance as based off many reviews, this thing is not going to make it long, so I did want to be covered.

You are getting what you pay for here. DO NOT step on the rear fender and I would also not recommend folding, as it snaps onto and stresses the fragile rear (plastic) fender. They also structurally tied the rear foot breaking mechanism into the rear fender as well. Cannot stress enough how not strong and flimsy this rear fender situation is. However for whatever reason, it is an integral part of the functional design of the scooter in many ways. If it snapps off, you are done with the rear foot break.

title: Excellent GPS watch at a very good price
text:
This is my first GPS running watch. So I have limited comparison experience.
I have been running for about 30 years now. For many of those years I have used a Polar heart rate monitor. When I saw the GPS watches, I thought they might be useful to monitor my runs in unfamiliar territory. I figured I could run a set distance even on vacation.
This watch can do that, and more. It measures distance, time and heartrate, but it also links to a website that maps the run and tracks elevation and calories burned. I am enjoying this very, very much.
I gave it four stars, not five, because it sometimes takes a few minutes to pick up the satellites. In all honesty, I don't know firsthand how that compares to other GPS watches, but reading about them it seems some take longer but some less time.
Another great thing about this watch is the transmitter. It is a standard chest transmitter that can work with other brand watches as well.
All in all, a great device at a very good price.
I'm pleased with the value.

title: Awesome For Large Dog Neuter Surgery!
text:
I purchased this for my 90 pound German Shepherd after his Neuter surgery. He is a 10 month old, very large “puppy” who had a LOT of problems with the cone he was sent home from the vet with.
When the doctor called to check on him the following day I advised her that I’d purchased this suit and she told me she didn’t think it would work for him because most of these suits are created for abdominal surgeries and not for Neuter surgeries. She didn’t think the suit would cover his incision area well enough and told me to let her know.

After receiving the suit the following morning I placed it on him and texted photos to her to ask if it gave enough coverage. She asked for the name of the suit and said she’s never seen one that covers the hind flanks area so well.
Bolt (my Shepherd) and I were thrilled to be able to remove the cone of shame and I was happy for the added benefit the suit gave in calming him a bit.

I still put a “blow up” type guard on him at night or if I have to leave him home alone for a little while but the suit has been awesome for most of the day and evening.

The only thing I would (and did) change is the neck of the suit. As you can see from my first photo, the suit is made with a type of “turtle neck” that folds down. I’m not sure why it’s made this way and it could be necessary for smaller dogs or some
kind of neck or chest surgery but for my needs it was just too much uncomfortable fabric around his neck. I corrected this problem with a pare of scissors and a simple cut down the back of the neck portion. This allowed the neck area to loosen up and also allowed for an easy repair should
I ever need the suit for a surgery that the high neck would be beneficial for. I would definitely recommend this surgery recovery suit, both abdominal AND/OR Neuter surgery.

title: Rated 5 Stars By Gym Owner

The thickly padded curve rests against your hand and over the bar. The grips were tried against using regular chalk and lifting gloves. The lifting grips provided better hand protection - preventing callouses and raw hands. Further they provided a longer and stronger lift time than using regular chalk or comparable lifting gloves. It also doesn't have the mess and clean-up that using chalk creates. They are definitely built to last and have been subjected to multiple handling by various trainers and trainees of different sizes/weights. The Large/Xlarge size was perfect for most of the users. Those with smaller hands could still use them but likely would have benefited more with a smaller size. The gym and its patrons will be ordering more of the Harbinger Lifting Grips because of the rave reviews it received from those who used them. Cost wise, $29.99 with free PRIME shipping is a good deal on grips that will last. The price is comparable to retail stores but with free Prime shipping, Amazon was the better deal.

text:
I ordered one of these for my daughter's bike. Thanks to Covid-19, it took forever to get.

Once I got it, I installed it. I've bought and built well over a dozen bikes, and I know how to change a tube. I pumped up my daughter's new tube and we planned to go biking the next day. Next day, front tire is flat again. The tube had a hole in it without ever being ridden. Checked the tire and rim, absolutely nothing that would have punctured the tube.

Ordered two new tubes, again, waited a long time for them arrive. Installed one of the tubes in the front tire the exact same way, it's absolutely fine weeks later.

I'm not about to go through the hassle of trying to return a bum tube on Amazon, but frustrating that the QC on this tube was not up to snuff, and I purchased three to make sure the family could ride together.

title: Fantastic e-bike, fantastic value and fantastic customer support
text:
This review is for the sixthreezero EVRYjourney Women's Step-Through 500-Watt Electric Bike

The short version is: This is a great bike, sixthreezero has great support, and I highly recommend the bike and company.

My mom has some back issues, including fused vertebrae, and over the years, the number of physical activities she's able to participate in has declined. Long family bike rides on a normal bike were no longer an option. For that reason, in February we decided to go to a local Pedego store and rent e-bikes for my mom and wife. We did a 15 mile ride, and everyone, including my mom and wife, loved it.

My mom liked it so much that she reconfirmed the prices when we got back, but it was definitely outside of her budget.

We both spent the next several months looking for an e-bike deal that was too good to say no to. There's some cheap options online, a Costco mountain e-bike, some nice bikes that are out of our budget, both online and locally, but nothing that was amazing...

Until Prime Day 2019.

sixthreezero's 250-watt bikes were on sale during Prime Day. I don't even see them available now, but it was a great deal, and I did some research before phoning my mom and telling her I think we'd found the deal she was looking for. After telling my mom about it, she ordered one, then asked if I was getting one for my wife. I was on the fence, because it's still a lot of money, until she said, "Don't think about how much you're spending per ride. Do you want to have lots of happy memories of the family riding together or are you OK without those?"

Well said, Mom. I ordered one the next day.

Now, I don't see the 250-watt bikes on Amazon anymore, but when they were here, the online documentation, both here and over at sixthreezero at the time we ordered made the basic functionality seem the same between the 250-watt and the 500-watt bicycles. The key feature both my mom and wife were looking for was the ability to pedal with adjustable resistance, but leverage the throttle with the left thumb to accelerate with the motor when needed to either catch up quickly or tackle hills without issue. (And without changing the level of pedal assistance.)

Some of our first impressions were not great. My mom's bike showed up looking amazing, and my dad assembled it without issue, but the throttle did not behave as expected. (The boost was limited to the level of pedal assist you were in.) My wife's bike showed up, but the fender and rack were both badly bent.

Before buying the bike, I saw that sixthreezero, if you bought directly from them, was willing to offer 365 day test drives, and seemed really focused on customer satisfaction. The Amazon reviews seemed positive, and the box the bike came in offered free assembly at a local bike store. (I'm not sure how that works because I've built over a dozen bikes and this bike is easy to assemble.) That said, I had a damaged bike and it didn't perform as I was expecting. I was definitely concerned when I reached out to sixthreezero.

After multiple calls, photos and a video to confirm that my 250-watt bike did not perform the way their 500-watt did (the technician I was working with only had a 500-watt readily available to troubleshoot with), they were willing to work with my mom and I to find a satisfactory proposal that would allow us to send back the 250-watt bikes and they would ship us 500-watt versions.

They were polite and reasonable throughout the process, but I was still nervous about bike number two, since the first bike did arrive with issues outside of the e-bike functionality. I was pleasantly surprised that they seem to have people working there who seem to genuinely want to make sure their customers love their bikes.

The 500-watt bike went together very easily, and after assembling and tuning the bike, I took it for a ride. The bike was a blast.

The only thing that jumped out at me as being substantially different from the Pedego my wife rode was the seat post. The Pedego had a shock in the seat post, which doesn't do a lot, but is better than nothing. I ordered a "Sunlite Pillar Suspension Seat Post, 27.2 x 350mm, Silver" from Amazon, which seemed like a good improvement to the bike, which is otherwise fantastic. (The rigid seat post makes the ride a tad rough, which is why I gave comfort 4 stars, I'd bump that to 5 with the suspension seat post.)

My wife says she finds the sixthreezero 500-watt basically the same as the Pedego. I'm sure there are differences, but the only big one we see is the price.

I can't adequately describe an e-bike in words alone, but if you have the option to rent one locally, I highly suggest you try it. It's a lot of fun. I'm not a fan of skilled cyclists tearing up mountain bike trails with heavier, faster e-bikes, nor would I advocate road bikers throw electric motors on their bikes, but the joy e-bikes are able to bring families by leveling the field for families that want to ride together is awesome. And sixthreezero's EVRYjourney cruiser is a fantastic bike for those people.

We're averaging speeds of more than half a mile per hour more as a family than we used to, and my wife comes home with a smile on her face while my kids come home having used up more energy and me having gotten a better work out. I know this bike is not cheap, but I like the way my mom put it to me:

Would you rather be out riding with your loved ones? This is a fantastic option for those who can't match the speed or stamina of the people they're riding with.

title: VP-Vice Pedals are fantastic!  Get a pair, but check the buyer!
text:
There are some interesting patterns that you'll see if you read through the reviews. Some people recevied their pedals shrink wrapped, and they scratch the other pedal in transport. Some people get new pedals in a box, and life is wonderful because they got an awesome pedal set at an awesome price. And some people get pedals in a box that look brand new, but have blown bearings. I'm in that third group.

I bought this pair from cyclingdeal_usa, fulfilled by Amazon. I was happy to see the pedals arrive looking brand new in a box similar to the one my first Vices showed up in about five years ago. I'm a huge fan of these pedals, and the fact that I have a the titanium pins for my primary bike, and that they're now as ridiculously affordable as they are means it makes sense to put these on the other bikes in the house.

I bought these for my son's bike, and the look great, but there was a click with each stroke on the left pedal. I threw them on my bike, on the titanium pins, and there was still a click with each stroke. I changed out the bearings (I had a rebuild kit on hand) and boom, the pedals are exactly as they should be, and the click is gone.

Like some other people's reviews, my VP-Vice Pedal set showed up with blown bearings. The right pedal was fine, but the left pedal clicked out of the box, and that's the first time I've seen a pair of Vice pedals do that. I see they're currently at the best price through VP Components. I'm hopeful that means they're shipped in a new box, and that if there's any issues, I know from a past experience with them, that VP Components will make it right.

I'm rating this purchase 4*, because I love the pedals, I love VP components, and I'm very happy with the bang for the buck of getting all my bikes on Vice pedals, but I hate that I had to use my rebuild kit to get working bearings in left pedal. (Yeah, I know I could have returned them, but I wanted to get them on my son's new bike, and we were all excited to go riding.)

title: it seems like they could easily be included
text:
I recently bought and tried to use the HHP-2 to install a bottom bracket and headset on a brand new frame.

Unfortunately, what this products description doesn't make clear is that the #669 bushings used to install a press fit bottom bracket are not included with HHP-2. For the price of this tool, it seems like they could easily be included. Yes, this is a good press fit tool, but it should only be used with bottom brackets with the #669 bushings which are not included with the tool.

I've purchased a lot of Park Tool tools in the past, and this is the first time I've felt that an expensive tool of theirs has really come up short, as it is really only a Headset Bearing Cup Press without the purchase of the additional #669 bushings, which are a significant additional cost for the average home bike mechanic. (The #669 bushings are included as part of BBT-90.3, which also includes the tool to remove an existing bottom bracket.)

If you're looking at buying this tool to install press fit headsets and bottom brackets, make sure to factor in the cost of the BBT-90.3, at which point you're looking at roughly $200 all in. Ouch.

My cell phone was able to fit in the bottom strap pocket and in the other pocket I put my fuel! The one downside, and it is not the product's downside at all but just the nature of its use, is that it rubs on your shirt a lot. It ruined my shirt because it rubbed on it for 3 hours, but I plan to just use that same top every time I use this pack! A different fabric (mine was a spandex compression) like a cotton/polyester mix probably wouldn't have an issue.

title: Helps to relieve the muscle tension in my back!
text:
Why did I wait this long to add this into my daily routine?? I have had serious trouble with my back since a bad car accident. 12 surgeries later and most of my pain has subsided, but some residual nerve pain still tenses up my back muscles, and I end up with a lot of tension and knots. As much as I would love to have a weekly massage, those get expensive. And begging my fiancé to rub my back every night gets old for him, I'm sure. I've been using this every night since I received it, and it's made such a difference in the tension of my muscles. My back muscles are way more relaxed, and I'm noticing less pain throughout my day.

I use this every night before going to bed, I find that doing it right before bed to work out some knots in my back really helps me sleep. I've not been able to lay this on the floor to roll on it, I don't have the coordination to hover over this roller to use it on my low back, so I've been using it against a flat wall. This is perfect for me, because I can control the pressure, and it keeps it from kneading in too deep. The squats that I do when using against the wall aren't bad for me either! I also use it to massage the sides of my hips, again pinned up against the wall.

If you ever get tense muscles I would highly recommend trying one of these out! I received this product for free/at a discounted rate in exchange for my honest review. I'm very happy with the product and can confidently say it is a 5 star quality product.

title: Battery drains quickly
text:
First impressions.
1) The Inspire watch came with about a 14% charge which was insufficient for the required firmware update. It came with a large band and a small band. I have a small wrist but the small band looked child-size. I purchased a set of clips for the Inspire for when I want to clip it to my pants rather than use it as a watch.
2) The Inspire charged to 100% in about 90 minutes.
3) I used an Inspire Charger Dock which I'm very glad I purchased after reading reviews. It has a long USB cable, magnetically clicks to the Inspire and makes charging very easy.
4) The watch was at 92% after the required firmware update via the Fitbit app.
5) Today, after less than 24% the watch is already at 82%. There were a lot of reviews about how quickly the Inspire loses battery charge. I have 'all day sync' and 'always connected' turned off and only synced with the app three times today, but it still lost 10% of the charge.
6) I had some problems connecting the Inspire to the Fitbit app. I tried about 6 times before the app connected. I kept getting a Fitbit maintenance error. The app then took about an hour to update the firmware on the Inspire. I did have to reboot my phone before the Inspire successfully paired with the app.
7) Since pairing the Inspire quickly synced each time I opened the app.

I'll update my review after trying out out for a few weeks.

NOTE: The Inspire can be returned to Amazon within 45 days and has a limited 1 year warranty with support via Fitbit customer service (2 year warranty if purchased in the EEU). You will receive an offer in the app to extend the warranty to 2 years. I didn't personally feel like spending an additional 24.99 for an extended warranty. If the Inspire fails after a year I'll purchase a different brand.

title: Larger masks are not always the best masks!
text: I am no stranger to sleep masks. I am always searching for one that is better than the one I am using. I saw this one and decided to purchase it.  I will say that I disagree with the description calling it a "larger" size sleep mask. It definitely is not that.  When I got the package in the mail, I opened the mask and thought this is way too small for me. BUT, I soon realized that while average in size, this sleep mask is really amazing!  First, it isn't the typical fabric (satin) that you find in masks.  It is a sort of microfiber fabric. It really helps the mask stay in place while sleeping. It isn't fancy as far as the way you put it on. It is the same velcro you find in nearly all masks. I remedy this by sewing a tube of fabric around the velcro part because I don't like it pulling my hair.  I was amazed at how well this small mask really does block out the light.  I am almost ready to say that it blocks out light better than any of the dozens of masks I have purchased over the years.  All in all, I am super happy with my purchased and I would recommend it!

title: Good quality products and fun to do plus it's learning a new skill to make gifts for christmas and friends at school, etc.
text: Would be five stars but their not rolled up the way the picture shows.  It's more like they layed them all together and then rolled it up, so getting one strand out without making a knotted mess of them all is difficult.  Other than that the kit is fine and paracord seems good enough.  It's my first time with paracord and it's thinner than what I expected.  I watched a you tube video to do my first bracelet and kept starting and stopping so I did double loops from wrong side a few times.  It still came out pretty cool, but word of advice be prepared to spend a half hour or so dedicated to this cobra bracelet project.  Clasps seem good enough quality, which is something I was worried about, but their fine.  Full ten foot pieces, enough for most size wrists.  Just measure around wrist with string then measure string and then one foot per inch plus a half foot for safety.  So my eight inch wrist was a eight and a half foot piece of paracord cut from ten foot piece.  Colors are very nice and clean and bright, clip colors may vary from exactly what is shown.  Bracelet takes time I guess to get used to wearing feels awfully scratchy and I don't like that, I'm hoping I get used to it though it looks so cool.  Oh note some colors may be different than picture too, mine has two yellow one with yellow with black marking and white in it and one plain.  Suppose that could be the fifth one but it doesn't look like it in real life.  So beware you may not get what is pictured for all of them but pretty darn close and all the colors like I said are nice and cool looking.  Bracelet making requires a lighter to singe ends so parents beware that you may need to help younger children and even older children may get burnt from hot paracord that was just burnt.  Pretty safe the stuff doesn't flare up into a fire, just melts pretty much.  I am going to buy a block kit to make these I think,  it might help their like thirteen bucks  and have measurements built right on it.  I really like my new bracelet and recommend this as a new hobby skill to all that think paracord bracelets are cool but don't want to spend ten bucks on just one bracelet.

title: Does It All for a Lot Less Money
text:
My new job requires me to wear a watch and at the same time I joined a gym so rather than a regular watch I opted for an inexpensive fitness band. (I once had a FitBit. Didn't like it so I returned it and vowed never to buy another health monitoring wristband. Any device that counts waving and typing as step counts is too sensitive, therefore inaccurate and useless. Why spend the money only to be one of the cool kids!?!?)

I went into this with a bit of a negative attitude. But given the price even if all it did was tell time I'd be content. Wow! It is good to be wrong!! I have worn this constantly for 2 months resulting in the following review.

Once it paired with my Samsung Galaxy I was impressed with the size and brightness of the clock display. Then came the fun stuff. Setting up for local weather; current, tomorrow, and next day and it's always accurate.

Caller ID, texts, email and incoming calls notifications are a higher intensity vibration than others I've tried. I have always felt the Mi Band 3 vibration regardless of what I'm doing. I really like this while my phone is muted so I remember to check it later. I can also read the shorter messages if my phone is out of reach.

I can't vouch for degree of waterproofing but it's certainly shower and dish washing proof which is good since the Xiaomi Mi Band is lightweight and very comfortable so I often forget I'm wearing it.

I like that I can set it when I go to the gym and get a reading on steps, distance, heart rate, etc. This becomes a subset of the daily activity record.

The sedentary reminder is helpful when I'm ‘in the zone’ while working on a project. I'm not convinced the heart rate is accurate but I suspect it's fairly close for those if us not needing a medical reason to monitor our heart. I don't believe much of anything the Sleep Monitor says but then I don't care about that either.

The battery life is at least 2 weeks. I've only charged mine 3 times in 2 months.

Nothing is perfect, including this Mi Band 3. Navigating through the myriad of settings can be frustrating. There is definitely a learning curve when trying to figure out how to see a specific option : Swipe up? Swipe down? Swipe to the side? Which side?

The other issue is when it changes to military time or suddenly jumps an hour or two ahead/behind for no reason. It took me awhile to find the fix for these problems. Shut down Bluetooth and turn off phone for a minute or two. Turn phone back on, turn on Bluetooth and after about a minute everything should go back to the way you had it originally. I've only had each of these problems happen once.

I am very impressed with the Mi Band 3. And the options can't be beat, especially for the price. This would be a good starter fitness band for a kid or someone just wanting to see if a fitness band is useful to have.

title: I hope I never need it but I’m glad I have it.
text: The Sabre Red Runner Pepper Gel personal alarm is a product you don’t want to review after having to use it.  But looking it over thoroughly I find it to be very well thought out.  It’s about the size of a tube of mascara yet weighs less.  Hardly noticeable when strapped to my arm.  The comfortable adjustable strap and uncomplicated trigger safety – just slide the red trigger over about half an inch then push to spray – make it appear to be simple to use, even in a frightened state.  But what I like best is the alarm that comes with it.  It has a very sturdy clip that can be successfully attached to a flimsy T-shirt or a fairly thick coat.  There is a green light that has three options: On, Slow flash, and Fast flash.  The light is also used to test the battery.  Holding the light button down for 3 seconds and seeing if the light quickly flashes green or red indicates battery strength.  The four LR44 batteries (included) can be replaced.  I think the alarm alone would deter most criminals.  To say it’s loud is an understatement.  The brochure states to avoid prolonged exposure as it could cause permanent hearing loss.  I’d recommend trying this away from children and pets.  It is painfully loud!  I hope I never need it but I’m glad I have it.

title: I Recommend Keeping It Assembled
text:
This Auoxer hula hoop comes with no instructions or suggestions. The picture on the box is the only hint as to its assembly however, it is fairly intuitive. The difficulty is joining segments 5 and 6 if you want the smallest opening size. It requires some muscle to force the ends to line up. I sat in bed and pushed the opposite (assembled) end against the top of my foot to force it into a somewhat round shape so I could join 5 to 6. The more segments used the easier it is to assemble.

Disassembly is more difficult and don't do it after a fresh manicure - it can be a nail breaker. You have to roll back about an inch of the foam covering and find the orange button, depress it hard, then continue depressing as you pull the segments apart. This alone will burn a few calories. Personally, I'll only be using it at home so I won't be disassembling it.

The opening size by number of segments:
6 segment opening size: 26”
7 segment opening size: 31”
8 segment opening size: 35”

There is a mild chemical-like plastic smell, but after 2 days out in the garage it went away.

I suppose if the assembly/disassembly were easier the hula hoop might not hold up to repeated use, so I forgive that difficulty. I do like that it's adjustable and the foam covering is a nice touch. Now if only I could remember how I hula hooped as a kid. I used to have simultaneous hoops on both arms and my waist while moving around. Now I have to concentrate to keep this one hoop from falling to the ground! That's ok, it will come back to me and in the meantime I have some hearty laughs each morning.

The first few times it was like drinking from a dribble glass. My nose (which is not big!) hits the opposite side from the small drink opening which leads to the dribbling. title: Best Dog Frisbees Ever
text:
My Black Lab can't get enough Frisbee, she demands it at least twice a day. Unlike the flying discs made specifically for dogs, these fly just like a real Frisbee (both in distance and flight pattern) yet have the soft rim so the dog"s mouth isn't injured when she catches it in mid-air. The brightly colored rim makes them easy to find when my throwing gets too wild and they end up somewhere she can't get to. The rim is squared off and ever so slightly raised above the actual disc which makes it easier for her to pick up if it lands flat on a slick or level surface.

I have tried many versions of Frisbees through the last 40 years of Labs in my life and these are by far the best. The one I just had to throw out was over 5 years old and eventually cracked in half but up until then flew perfectly despite being riddled with teeth marks, dents, and small cracks.

The size makes them unsuitable for small dogs (obviously) and because the rim is the only color they may be difficult for dogs (and humans) with imperfect eyesight to see.
