title: Decent fitness equipment for the price
text:
I’ve only started exercising in the last few years. My focus has been 99% cardio. After losing a pretty significant amount of weight, I decided maybe I should start focusing on strength with cardio and stretching mixed in.

I’ve tried a few things. Hand weights. Resistance bands. When I saw this it seemed like it would be useful for both resistance and some stretching too. I’ve only used it a handful of times so far but it’s a pretty decent piece of equipment for the price.

You get the bar, sets of 20. 30, and 40 lb resistance tubes, an anchor for attaching to doors, and a booklet with directions with some sample exercises. You can find a ton of free pilate bar video workouts on YouTube.

The only thing I would change is to add a little thicker foam on the bar, but that’s personal preference - it would make it a bit comfier when say resting it on the back of your shoulders.. I’m around 5’8” and it’s a good size for me. The strap that connects to the tubes is adjustable so it should work for most.

The foot straps are very wide, I have wide feet and can fit both feet while in socks anyway, probably not with shoes, but still they’re very wide.

Easy to put together and take apart. The metal rods just screw into place. Comes with a storage / carrying bag.

title: Tricky at first but works well
text:

Swapped my original for one band, decided I wanted a different color and immediately swapped it again. First try was frustrating, by the second I felt like a pro. Useful tool. I wrapped the string around my extra straps so I can easily find them with the tool next time I feel like swapping them out again.

text:

text:

The one with half stretchy loops is good for when I am kind of between loops and it allows me to stretch a bit more on the one loop without having to change loops in the middle of stretching. The down side to that strap is it’s a touch shorter than this one and the loops are also smaller so if you have large feet it might not be as comfy.

The one though is a bit longer and had much larger loops, so it will accommodate more people. If you want loops with no stretch, I’d highly recommend this one.

title: There is no XX-Heavy, it’s X-Light instead
text:
The main image in the listing currently shows these bands as:
Black band = XX-Heavy
Red band = X-Heavy
Yellow band = Heavy
Blue band = Medium
Green band = Light.

What you actually get is from the other picture in the listing:
Black band = X-Heavy
Red band = Heavy
Yellow band = Medium
Blue band = light
Greet band = X-Light

Personally I wish I had gotten what the main listing picture showed as the X-light is really too light so having the XX-heavy would have been more useful as I progress. Even with MS and hand issues, I find the X-light just too light for me for most exercises but it could be good if you’re really weak / using these as PT.

I also just find it a little weird that there’s two different pictures in the same listing and the main one that most people will see if they don’t click through every image isn’t what this product is.

That said, they’re nice bands. You can definitely feel the difference in resistance. There’s a huge difference between the lightest and heaviest included. Nice drawstring carrying bag is included. Love that they are clearly marked from X-Light through X-Heavy. While that doesn’t tell you the specific resistance level, it is more than I have seen from other bands I’ve used.

Overall: great bands. The only complaint I have is thatI got the x-light instead of the xx-heavy.

title: Nice bands
text: I’ve tried a couple of resistance bands. The straight flat ones. The tube bands with handles. The smaller loop ones. And now these. These are really nice. Like most bands I’ve tried they don’t actually list the resistance level on the bands themselves but they do list that on a paper that is included (I store it in the included storage bands in case I need to know that later). You can easily tell by looking at them which is more resistance and which has less as they increase in size as you add more resistance. Feels like a very nice quality of band.  I found that the smaller loop ones I use don’t stretch enough to be useful in all exercises I find in the workout videos I use, this bridges that gap for me perfectly and is easier for me to hold than the tube bands.

title: Nice idea but…
text:
I’ve tried two of these smart hoops and so far I like the concept more than the product itself, but this does serve a purpose.

First off, this one is smaller than the other I tried, so note the size if you’re on the larger side. I’m a women’s xl and it fits me with maybe 2 pieces out, so if you’re much larger than an xl or carry all of your weight in your waist, you may need extra pieces than are included.

The motion actually feels pretty good. I can waist hoop just fine, but there’s a slightly different feel with this. It’s almost a waist massage. You feel the weight in a very different way from a standard weighted hoop as the weight isn’t constantly going back hit the smacking into your waist. I know people who have found themselves bruised from a standard weighted hoop, that shouldn’t happen with this.

The downside is that these are pretty loud. I’m rather sensitive to sounds and with the hubs still working from home, I cannot do this at the front of the house without disrupting his meetings in the back of the house. Not super overpowering at that distance, but still loud enough to be an annoying clicking back there.

If they were quieter I’d love them. As this hoop is, I like it but not nearly as much as my standard, not weighted, adult sized hula hoop.

I don’t think the screen adds much to this one over the cheaper smart hoop I have without a screen, in fact I don’t bother turning it on, I just use my usual fitness tracker to tell me how I did, it may not tell you how many turns you did like this screen is meant to, but the fitness tracker is getting my heart rate and feels like a more personal / accurate account of what a hooping session did for me.

Overall, I think a standard hoop is better. But this is nice for a change, for those who cannot keep a hoop going (be sure you’re trying with a large adult hoop and not a kids toy store one), for those who want a weighted hoop but who bruise easily, and for those like who like repetitive sounds as they exercise.

title: Great for the price
text:
I’m a cheapskate, especially with fitness items because I’m also lazy + have MS so some workouts are easier to keep going and spending a lot on something I might not use regularly seems like a bad idea. Enter this rowing machine. Knowing what I know now, I’d likely have spent a bit more on one of their magnetic machines, but for now I am pretty happy.

It was easy to put together, no issues there. I’ve used it most days since I received it on February 9th, it’s April 6th now. I have a pretty sedentary lifestyle when not exercising so I really wanted something that could workout my whole body without leaving me in pain or taking all day to burn a respectable number of calories as weight loss is a goal of mine in addition to just being healthier. And this seems to do that for me.

I am not sure how good the monitor is as the batteries died almost as soon I put them in and honestly I just use my watch to track my workout as it feels more personalized.

So far the only cons have been:
- It gets squeaky after a few weeks of use so keep some silicone oil handy.
- The hydraulic cylinder - it’s suggested you only use this machine for 20 minutes at a time. I use it for up to 30 at a time. But it does lose the resistance fairly quickly . I once paused a 20 minute workout at the 10 minute mark to answer the door. Came right back and totally lost the resistance for the rest of the workout. Usually that happens somewhere between the 20 and 30 minute mark.

Neutral:
I am between 5’8” - 5’9” and wouldn’t suggest this machine to anyone more than say 5’10-6’ tall as I almost reach the back of the machine at my height.

Things to consider:
- I like that this is a full motion arm movement, but once you start using it you’ll likely naturally use the wide arm movement, which I’ve found makes it hard for me to keep pace with workout videos that use a pulley style arm movement. You can use use more narrow but for me anyway that doesn’t feel natural on this machine.

- the weight limit is 350 which seems pretty high for this price range, making it more accessible to more people than some of the other cheap rowing machines.

Overall:
If you’re pretty sure you’d use a rowing machine often, I’d probably save up for a nicer model but for those on a budget or who only do shorter workouts this is more that good enough and is probably one of the better options in its price range, especially for larger folks since it has a 350lb weight limit and many cheaper models don’t support as much weight as this machine does.

title: Nope.
text:

They were offering free gifts for reviews but asked that Amazon reviewers not contact them though Amazon for their “account security”. Probably because this violates Amazon’s rules. Sometimes it counted perfectly. Sometimes it literally did not count even one jump. Sometimes it did count but was way off. Sometimes it counted Many jumps when I was just holding it in place. It is simply not consistent enough to trust it. If you don’t care about the electronic counter, it is just okay.

title: Only Owala lid for carbonated drinks
text:
I currently have 3 Owala bottles (1 stainless steel (24 oz), 2 plastic (25 oz) and all three lid styles).

Personally I prefer the stainless bottle but I use the plastic ones at home for things where keeping them hot or cold isn’t as important (smoothies and carbonated water). The twist lid that this bottle has is the only one Owala recommends for carbonated drinks. It is also the lid that feels the cheapest, so I only use it for carbonated drinks. They are all great quality bottles. Easy to clean. Fun colors.

The lids are not a standard wide mouth, so not interchangeable with other brands but they are interchangeable with other Owala bottles. If temperature control is necessary then go with the stainless version (I donated my other stainless bottles as this brand’s was best at keeping things cold longest). If carbonated drinks are your norm, do get this twist lid version.

title: Love this lid
text:
I have 3 Owala bottles. A stainless steel with the flip lid. Two plastic - one with the twist lid and this one with the free sip lid.

They are all 5 stars. I only got the plastic ones for carbonated water and smoothies at home. The free sip lid like on this bottle is my favorite lid with the flip a close second. This free sip lid means you can chug your drink through the lid or use a straw from the same lid.

My advice is if you need to keep your drinks hot or cold? Buy the stainless steel one. If you drink carbonated drinks, you need the twist lid as it is the only lid they list as safe for use with carbonated drinks.

Otherwise go with whatever you prefer. My fave for just water or tea is the stainless steel bottle with either the flip lid or the free sip. If I am at home / drinking carbonated water, I used the plastic with the twist lid.

All of them are top quality, well made, easy to clean. I do only use the twist lid for carbonated drinks as it is the lid that feels cheapest or like it maybe won’t hold up as long as the others. The lids are not a standard wide mouth threading so these lids are not interchangeable with other bottles but have been interchangeable with each other even between the plastic and stainless steel versions.

text:

If you are sensitive to smells, this is not something you will want to use. If you don’t have sensitivities to scents and want a thicker mat, it is decent for that.

title: Not as good as the older Bubba we own, still good
text:

So this is not as nice as that older Bubba. But for what it is, it is nice. The lid can be quickly opened so long as you leave the locking latch open. If you have someone who is always getting into your mugs? The latch is really good and can take me a second to open with real effort. I suspect that is a feature that is appreciated by mamas.

The other problem with this compared to the older powder coated mug is that this is not as grippy, so not as easy for those of us with hand strength issues. But the two grooves do help.

Overall: not perfect, not even the best Bubba bottle. But for what it is, it is pretty nice. Fits in cup holders and most water bottle pockets on my bags.

title: Good luck
text: I wish I could review without giving stars, because the thing is this is a good tracker.  It just wasn’t ready for release.  I set mine up, the app removed my old Charge 3.  All seemed well until I realized it was sending my notifications to the Charge 3 it had removed.  Didn’t want to reset that one until I was sure the Charge 4 was set up, but I did in case that was causing conflicts.  Then I went to do the firmware update.  My internet works.  My device works and syncs.  After a day and half it still refuses to update.  It starts to, the device recognizes and displays the check mark, the app goes to finish it, gets to around 60%, hangs, dies, start over.  Repeat, repeat, repeat.  Support was clueless.  I have decided to return it.  This is the third FitBit I’ve owned, the second to have issue while newer.  I suspect I will move on to another brand.  Great when they work, but they seem to release before the devices are ready and I am tired of paying  to be a beta tester.

title: No directions
text:
This doesn’t come with directions but it’s easy to put together. A washer between each key. I accidentally put two on in a way they didn’t fit together right, so I had to undo it and redo it. Basically just be sure you know they’re in a good position before tightening. Keeps your keys organized. No jangling unless you attack keychains that do so. A great alternative to regular keychains.

So why 3 and not 4 or 5? No directions + not as nice as the one my hubby has from another brand. Had I not seen another brand first this might have been 4 stars but since I had something to compare it to? It lost a star for not being as nice as others in the same price range. The stone wash finish is so light, it just looks like metal that someone at home tried to spruce up a little instead of a nice polished look.

title: Our second 6’X6’ and...
text: Okay this is our second 6’x6’ yoga mat.  We bought the first and this, our second, was a vine product.  If we ever needed a third, I’d go with this brand.  Both mats are similar in thickness and quality.  The difference for us was that this mat came with both carrying straps and a carrying case.  That’s a super nice touch for if you have to move it.  The bag alone (what our other mat came with) is probably fine for smaller mats but when moving one that is 6’x6’ even getting it into the bag can be tricky so the included straps were a super nice detail.  Also came with gloves.

title: Works well
text: Was a bit of a struggle to get this on my bottle, but once it’s on, it’s secure.  Easy to push out of the way when it’s just sitting around or when you’re drinking from it.  Yet offers a sturdy carrying handle.  Can also be attached to bag via the carabiner clip  (of you can open the handle via a clip and attach it to things that way too).

title: Works for us
text:
The only thing stopping me from giving this 5 stars is that the clasp feel very cheap.

Otherwise we like it. We got it to organize screws, leftover pieces from furniture, etc. It’s great for that, especially since it’s set up the way craft boxes for beads and floss are with the dividers being removable so you can have small or large compartments as needed.

title: Nice bottle design, horrible at maintaining temps
text:
I thought for sure this would be my final bottle. Double stainless steel + a copper lining? Sounds amazing. Tall and thinner than most so it fits in cup holders? Nice! Multiple lid options available for purchase? Cool.

Thing is I tried this next to my other bottles and this was by far the worst at keeping drinks cold. Ice melted in 3 hours or less every time I tried, that’s with half a tray of ice cubs + refrigerated water. All others kept the ice solid for at least 6+ hours.

The style of the bottle is a 5. But if it cannot keep ice from melting and drinks cold as long as my other bottles and tumblers? It’s useless to me. May be good for at home when you can constantly refresh ice and drinks. When traveling? It’s not going to work for me and that’s the main reason I got it. I feel very disappointed especially when they send me emails bragging about how they keep drinks colder way longer than others claim to. They don’t they’re the opposite or what they claim to be.

I tried to review it on their site, but couldn’t get it approved so the product has 5 stars there but I wouldn’t trust that star count.

*update* got a different brand and decided to compare how fast they lose their ability to stay cool. This bottle went from 35 degree water to 66.3 in 3.5 hours. While the other bottle took over 24 hours to get that warm.

title: Fits my Eco Vessel Summit
text: I’m using this on my Eco Vessel 24 ounce Summit.  I’ve tried it on a few other bottles we have in a similar size range and it fits those.  I think the only bottle i tried that it wouldn’t fit is 40 ounces and rather large so I didn’t expect it to fit that one.

title: Great for the emergency kit
text: I crawl around under my desk a lot so a light like this is really useful.  Oddly enough, though, I don't clip it to my hat or clothes, I clip it to my watch-band.  Very handy  I'm considering keeping an extra one in the car as part of the emergency kit!

title: Nice
text: I read some confusing reviews about this product.  Some said there were no metal D-rings, others said there was.  The strap I got does have metal D-rings.  It’s a nice sturdy strap.  Well made and stitched.  A good length for both me and my husband.

title: Sturdy but...
text: This looks just like the picture.  It seems sturdy but it does make me a little anxious as the risers don’t have anything locking them into place.  If you bump this, they move.  I’m using this to try to improve my balance as I have MS and am pretty wobbly on stairs.  While this seems sturdy enough, seeing those pieces move and having to constantly check on them as they get just slightly out of place is a bit frustrating.  Otherwise it’s nice.  Heavy duty plastic.  Non-slip top.  Easy to adjust the risers.

title: Nice Quality
text:
I’ve had several items by Gaiam, they’ve all been of a good quality and this is no exception.

The pump is useless — as in I’ve had lung issues in the past and I could blow this up 4 times faster than the included pump could. That’s the only downside. It’s a nice quality of balance ball. The ring bad is pretty sturdy. Comfy to sit on (I’m around an xl - so well below their weight limit, but also not small) and I have no issues with using this. There’s a white strip with a single hole in it, no clue what it’s full as it isn’t mentioned anywhere.

title: We have a few of them
text: We now have more than one of these, if that tells you anything.  They’re a decent thickness.  Comfortable to sit on.  Easy to roll up.  Because of where our yoga area is, they get walked on A lot and are still holding up well.

title: Comfy mat!
text: I love this mat.  It’s a good thickness.  We have hardwood floors and my hubby sometimes has trouble being on the floor, even where there’s a rug.  But he also wants to do yoga at home.  We bought a larger mat for our yoga area and I thought this would be perfect to add on top of that so that he has a comfortable place to do so.  There was a tiny rolled edge on one side when I first laid it flat but that section went perfectly flat within a day.  If we need another mat later, I’d definitely replace it with another like this one.

title: It is what it says it is
text: It’s a nice size.  The padded foam makes it comfortable to hold.  Color coded with the weight listed on the ends.  No complaints.

title: Nice bands
text: Nice quality bands.  Just enough resistance.  Nothing fancy.  A better quality material than some, but nothing too special.

title: Nice socks
text: Fit well.  Keep your feel cool.  The only down side is that the material does grab onto everything.

title: Very helpful
text: I got these because the hubby and I are newbies when it comes to yoga and we both have issues that make some of the positions tricky.  I have MS and the hubby has back issues.  We have another strap style that came with a yoga set (one long strap and some d rings for adjusting the loop).  If you have serious mobility issues and are trying stretches to help?  I’d probably start with that style.  But if you’re fairly mobile already, this is a better option as it requires no adjustments (but also isn’t as versatile as the length isn’t adjustable).  One loop is just the webbing material while the other loop includes a plastic handle that is covered in foam.  For me, for most yoga positions, I think I’d prefer this one as I sometimes have hand issues and don’t like fiddling with adjusting the other strap.

title: Comfortable
text: A nice thickness for a mat that offers you comfort without being too bulky.  The carrying strap does that job but isn’t anything special.

title: Easy to carry with you for emergency situations
text: Nice thin blankets that each come folded and stored in a plastic ziplock style bag.  We put three in our car for emergencies and opened the fourth so we could actually use one before reviewing them.  The title claims it’s not noisy, it totally is.  But who cares?  It’s designed for emergencies and you’re not really going to care if your blanket makes crinkling noises in those kind of situations.  It’s a nice size.  If you were in a situation where multiple people needed to be bundled up, each blanket should definitely work for at least two people, maybe more.  They do keep you warm.  If you’re careful with them, you might be able to fold them back into the plastic bag they came in.  Otherwise, I’d advise getting a small drawstring bag or fabric zippered bag as the plastic one it comes in is a really tight fit if it’s folded perfectly.  If you don’t fold it perfectly, it’s a pain to get it back into that.

title: Good starter hoop
text:
This is the third hula hoop I’ve owned that breaks down this way. I also own an empower fitness hoop (it’s the pink and orange hoop in my picture while this hoop is the pink and grey hoop) and gave away a hoopologie one (couldn’t stand how squeaky it was).

I’d put this in the middle. The empower fitness one is made of a thicker more sturdy tubing. But this is perfectly fine especially for beginners who don’t want to spend much.

I would ignore advice about going to a toy store to get a cheaper hoop. This is very reasonably priced for adult hoops. There’s a video out there of olympic athletes trying with those kid hoops. It was a failure. Those hoops are designed for kid sized bodies and even athletes on the snaller side struggle with kid hoops. When starting out most hooping sites suggest you have a hoop that comes to about your waist when resting on the floor.

As far as weighted hoops go, this is just right, not too heavy (have never seen any proof that weighted is better and many believe it’s not). If they’re too heavy most recommend using them for only 10-20 minutes, lighter hoops get no such warnings.

So far so good with this one. I will update if my opinion changes but I would put this as a good starter hoop. In addition to the three collapsible hoops I’ve used another non-weighted hoop. Have never bruised but bruising isn’t uncommon when starting out so I’d advise starting out with a few minutes here and there to build up a tolerance if you bruise easily.

title: Nice enough towel
text: A nice towel.  No real shrinkage after washing/drying.  Soft enough yet grippy.  I’ve not owned any other yoga mat towels so I don’t know how it compares to others, but I like this one enough I would consider buying a second.

title: Almost perfect.
text: Just the right amount of firmness for a Yoga pillow.  We took a class recently and the hubby found that he really needed the provided bolster pillows, so I snatched this up.  It’s a very nice quality, easy to clean the cover which zips right off.  My only complaint is that the handle on mine was sewn on twisted, so the handle never lays flat.  A minor goof that doesn’t affect the quality of the pillow but may bother some folks.

title: Softer than official bands
text:
I got this through Vine and don’t actually know what size I got, based on the fit, I’d say small.

Cosmetically I find that the pattern on the band is really faint, almost impossible to see, unlike the similar pattern on my official Fitbit band. Also the clasp isn’t the vibrant silver of the picture but a more muted color. It’s not perfectly flush with my Fitbit the way the official band is. That’s the bad.

The good is that conplaints are minor. The biggest pro is that this is a softer more flexible band than the official one. No one will really notice that it’s not flush with your device unless they’re perfectionists and up close.

Easy to get on and off the Fitbit.

For the price difference, I do find this a better deal than official bands even if they’re not as flush with the device.

Overall: it depends on what you want from a band. Want perfect? Invest in the official bands. Want a ton of color choices? Go with a cheap knock off like these.

title: Nearly perfect
text:
Honestly I rounded up. I’d put these at 4.5 but for the price? They’re pretty darn good.

They hold both heat and cold drinks well (their estimates are pretty accurate). I have used a different larger Bubba mug for awhile so I somewhat knew what to expect. The hubby, however, was surprised to find some cold water he had in his mug during the evening was still cold the next morning.

The 24 oz size seems accurate (some seem to cheat, listing their max ounce capacity by filling it to the rim, no accounting for the lid). It fits in our car’s cup holder.

The only dislike for me is that the other Bubba mug I have has a twist lid. That felt more secure. This lid you just push into place. And while it’s secure enough for general use, if I were to have one fall, I’d want that twist lid. Especially so since some days this lid fits better than others — sometimes it will rest flat against the mug and sometimes there’s a slight crack between the two. Again it’s still fairly secure, it just seems weird and less secure when compared to the twist lid. Otherwise this is a perfect set of mugs. We use them daily with no issues.

title: Really disappointing
text:
Wanted to like this product but it was problematic from the moment it came out of the package.

The plastic parts are made with a really cheap thin plastic that already had white flaws that you get when plastic has been pushed to it's limits and is about to crack. Straight out of the package, no use. The plastic pieces that cover the coil in the center so not stay together so it's keeps popping open. And finally, I just don't see how the tension on this is going to work for anyone. I am pretty weak and often a little shaky from MS, don't work out at all, any exercise I get is from walking and occasionally using a hula hoop (so basically not fit at all). And yet, this is not a challenge for me at all. There's just not enough tension to make this feel like an exercise. Whatever is inside of the foam is really lightweight. A child could probably bend it.

title: A great bottle.
text:
As someone who like cold drinks and who lives in a warm climate, I realized my plastic bottles weren't keeping me happy. I had two stainless steel bottles around the house but one was designed for hot coffee and therefore a bit on the small size for someone who wants to fill it with a cold drink and a few cubes of ice. The other bottle was really similar to this only it had a twist off top and the top part was too small to squeeze standard ice cubes in. Took a chance on this one. The mouth is perfect for fitting ice cubes in. I went with the "bite" lid because I kind of get tired of opening and closing the bottle constantly and the straw lid seemed to get mixed reviews. The bite lid, so far, is perfect. I use it all day every day for my water. I have found the bite lid works best if you don't fully extend it, more like pull it up half way. When closed I shook it around and it didn't leak but I probably still wouldn't keep it in say a bag with anything important in it. I was using a slightly larger plastic bottle but find this bottle in this size is great as I don't need to cram as much ice in the bottle to keep it chilled.

I have seen some reviews that say the color coating peels off, I haven't had that experience thus far but I have heard of other bigger brand name bottles having the same issue when coated like this one is, so it wouldn't surprise me. Will update when / if I experience it.

title: Great if you get one not prone to cracking
text:
The bad:
Like many others have mentioned, it cracked with light use by people who aren't small but who are also nowhere near the weight limit.

The good:
Easy to use
It's fun! The only fitness product I enjoy more is my hula hoop!
Gentle on your body
Helps me focus on balance, which is a problem for me.
Excellent customer service. When I experienced the crack, they made it easy to get a replacement and since mine would soon be out of warranty they offered me two replacements.

If there weren't prone to cracking this would be a 5 star item. Because they do crack so easily I was tempted to give it one star, but their CS was so excellent and it is a good device if it doesn't crack... I went for three, but if they fix the design to be less prone to cracking I'd easily go back to 5.

title: Only one complaint...
text:
This is exactly what it says it is. A good tool for working on hand strength issues.

I have MS which occasionally causes a tremor in one hand and which frequently causes a little weakness in that hand.

If you have problems like that in one hand you'll definitely see and feel the difference between your hands when using this. Because the tremor comes around less often than it used to, I don't notice any ongoing issue in that hand. When using this and comparing it to what my other hand can do, it becomes obvious that there is a deficiency.

The only thing keeping me from giving it five stars is that the counter reset button is a bit wonky. I don't know if mine was damaged or if that's just how it works but when I press in and turn as the device instructs, it really struggles to move and often lands the dial between numbers in such a way that you have to just start clicking to see if you're really back to zero. Otherwise this is a perfect tool for strengthening hands that need a bit of an at home rehab.

title: Nice quality but has some faults.
text:
Its claims about how long items will stay hot or cold seem pretty accurate. I left cold water in it and checked the next day, it was still a bit chilly, though definitely nowhere near the fridge level of cold it started at. Boiled water was nearing room temperature after 12 hours but was still a little on the warm side.

The bottle looks just as pictured. It fits well in the hand, making it comfy to carry.

Now for the bad. I do dislike the size of the bottle opening. If you want ice in your drink, you'll be buying speciality cube trays as neither my pretty traditional nearly square cubes nor my newer slightly smaller with a rounded bottom will fit in this opening. Also none of my bottle brushes will fit in this. Even if you do only use it for water, you'll still want to clean it once in awhile -- stainless steel or not -- and it's tough to do. Again you'll probably have to buy a special brush or settle for doing something like boil water, pour it in the bottle, and shake it up a lot -- preferably with a little dish soap.

Because of those things I don't love it. I do like it enough to keep in in use for when I need water with me but don't want to bring a larger bottle. It's just not an every day bottle for me.

title: Goes from awesome to maddening with very little use
text:
I bought this just before a move so I put it together, used it a few minutes, then dismantled it and packed it up -- an easy thing to do with a travel hoop.

Had I rated this after that brief experience, I would have given this hoop 5 stars! It's the perfect height for a taller hooper (especially a newbie) but leave a piece out and it's good for once you get better or ideal if you're on the petite side. It looks nice. It's neither too heavy nor too light.

So why have I now dropped my rating to a very low three, working its way to two or lower? After an hour or so of use it has gotten so very loud. When I've got maxed out headphones on, wharever... But when I don't? Makes for a very distracting and aggravating experience. Basically now feel I've wasted my money and will have to buy a different brand that doesn't make me want to smash it. Squeak squeak squeak. I contacted their customer service department who told me that's normal for hoops that are in sections. My [[ASIN:B005QVRTW0 Empower Cardio Core and More Weighted Adjustable Hula Hoop]] is also a multiple piece hoop, albeit it ones covered in foam, and it is silent after significantly more usage. Beyond disappointed given the fact it's otherwise perfect for me. I feel I wasted my money and gave it away to someone who didn't mind the squeak the way that I did. Replaced it with a custom hoop.

title: Is exactly what it says it is.
text:
It is exactly what it says it is.

The material is pretty sturdy (thicker than that of the yoga ball I had by the same company). It is easy to blow up but you will want your finger at the ready to fill the hole as you work at putting the plug in place (I overfilled it just a little so that the air lost didn't really affect the ball in the end).

Some products made of similar material can be just tacky enough to pick up every little thing. I used this ball on a rug that my cat frequently sheds on, when it hadn't be vacuumed for a few days and purposefully rolled it around pressing into it with some pressure and did not pick up any fluff.

I'm a big girl and it does hold up to my weight.

The exercise sheet leaves something to be desired, but there are a lot of good workouts on YouTube.

title: I'm not a fan of these
text:
Cons:
- There are a total of 12 weights on each arm, 4 are removable. That's fine except they're maybe too removable. The nylon flap isn't enough to keep them secure. A small piece of velcro would go a long way.
- The size of this. It's pretty small. I can get the wrist part closed all of the way, so I don't think I'm some giant. The top part is pretty snug as there's only have a half inch difference between the wrist and upper part when closed.
- The nylon material snags easily, I did so getting it out of the box, and I don't really have nails, so that's not a good sign.
- Simple, not reinforced stitches. Already saw a loose thread. Also not a good sign for something holding weights in place.

Pros:
- It is a night lightweight fabric, making it comfortable
- Adjustable weights
- Affordable

Overall: I wouldn't recommend this as there are surely better options out there.

title: Tubing feels pretty lightweight, but overall a good set
text:
This set consists of 5 different bands, two handles, an ankle strap, a door strap, a zippered carrying case, and a booklet.

If you've never used bands before, I highly recommend starting with the yellow band. It's the lightest resistance and while just pulling on the band tubing might seem like even the highest resistance is fine, you will really feel it once you start doing actual exercises.

What I like:
- It's portable enough that you take it anywhere.
- Easy to pick up and use with little to no knowledge of this type of equipment.
- Good for those with medical issues (obviously consult your doctor). I have MS and find these easy enough to be able to do something with even on bad days. If you have hand issues, I would suggest leaving the bands you're using most attached to the handles so you won't have to clip then on and off as it's got a sturdy clip.

What I don't like:
- The tubing does feel a bit lightweight, even the higher resistance ones. I'm not sure how well it will hold up. We'll see. If there are no further updates to this review, assume it did hold up as I'd post if they fell apart.

Overall:

An inexpensive and easy to use form of exercise equipment, suitable for most fitness levels.

title: Overall a great bottle though one piece feels cheap
text:
[[VIDEOID:55f4bd70462ef38b4003375b381a2780]] I've included a video to show you my personal experience with leakage (which is none). It is a larger bottle than most personal sized infusers (to go larger you may need to move into pitcher territory). The infuser itself is large enough for a bottle of this size. The part of the lid that opens (via push button and a latch both) has a small extended piece that fits perfectly into the drinking spout and seems to prevent leaks. My only complaint with this bottle is that the lid for the infuser section and the hinge both feel a bit cheap compared to the rest of the bottle. I guess I'll see how long it holds up.

Although I personally haven't experienced leaks, if you are carrying this or any liquids in bags with electronics and other valuables, I'd recommend storing the bottle in something like a small wet/dry bag just in case.

title: Great for crunches not sure about as a push up or dip bar
text:
Let's just start off with the negatives:

While it is mostly easy to put together, the last piece really really really did not want to go into place. I had to wait for my hubby to get home to do it for me and even he had to use quite a bit of effort.

I only want to use it for crunches but when I put it into place for the other exercises and attempt them it feels a bit flimsy. I'm not exactly skinny but I'm nowhere near the maximum weight limit. It doesn't feel like it'll actually break and I am naturally just a little wobbly due to MS so it might just be me, but yeah I because I tend to feel shaky anyway it made me feel like I'd feel too off to use it as the push up bar or dip bar.

Now for the positive:

Aside from that last piece, it was actually easy to get it together. In fact it was basically together enough to use before the hubby got home since it was all screwed together with that final section basically stuck almost in place but not quite.

The main reason I got it is that I want to attempt crunches but do suffer from a lot of pain issues, so positioning and doing them right is going to be key for me. I figured something like this would be ideal. So far, it is. It's simple to use (currently it doesn't include instructions in the box and originally the site did not have them but it does have a printable sheet now).

The neutral:

It's a little bigger than I expected. My own fault. We're in a fairly small apartment so space is a premium and this isn't ideal.

title: Love My Fitbit Surge!!!
text:
Received my Fitbit Surge as a present for my birthday early April.

Pros: Love being able to track my HR, activity, and sleep. It has made me aware of the areas where I needed to improve. Fitbit has an app for the smartphone, (I have the Samsung Note 4) where I am able to see more details about my daily routine without any difficulties. Also, I have been keeping a track of my dietary intake and realized that I was eating excessively. I am now eating healthier and doing much better on my caloric intake. I have lost 17.2 lbs. My BMI went from 29% down to 27%. I am feeling more energetic and have a much better self esteem. Would recommend this product to anybody who is trying to improve their health. I give this two thumbs up.

Cons: Get a screen protector for the display A.S.A.P, I gave it a nasty scratch somehow and regret not placing a screen protector right away.
Fitbit should consider using Sapphire Glass for durability and scratch resistance.

Still love my Surge.

title: Does NOT hold up to WINDS :(((
text:
Yes, it Does work. Tension is the key.
Looking at the pictures of this tent you can see that it Should work, but you Doubt it, right??
Here on the NorthCoast of California right next to that big body of water, we have normal breezes running around 15 mph. When it gets a bit Windy it'll run around 35 mph. Then there's when it gets brisk ;>
It's still hanging out in the place I'd staked it when other tents had hopped the fence and wandered down the street.
I'd gotten tired of having to replace those nylon things every year or two and wanted something a lot more permanent in a temporary structure.
The canvas is IT for me!
I like that they'd used a white for the roofing giving you a more open feeling than you'd have otherwise if they'd gone with the base color.
I'm very happy with the construction. Tabs, zipper-pulls, netting in doors and windows. The floor is sturdy enough to dance on.
The tie-downs and stakes need to be replaced. I'm really very disappointed that this tent has such a poor finish after all the fine work they'd done for the main structure.
The skinny and very stretchy nylon strings and skinny smooth metal pins they give you stretch when dampened and the pegs pull out. It's an easy fix, not to worry. Just get a length of REAL Rope and re-do the tie-downs and buy a handful of those lovely orange plastic pegs that have teeths and you'll Keep the proper tension in the roof you need for when you get 3 inches of rain dumped on you, even With the rain-fly covering the roof. You will of course need to re-adjust the tie-downs after this happens. Good News!! Even with a couple of tub fulls of rain on the tent that you'll need to dump off, the tent Remains STANDING!

UPDATE:
After the ground got SUPER saturated with days of rain and some SERIOUS winds and GUSTS, it's collapsed Twice and the rain fly has completely died. The tie down banding along one edge RIPPED OFF and the ties From the tent to the Center pole ripped off.
The rain fly needs to be anchored SEPARATELY if you also have issue with winds. Since it's integrated with the tent, it causes Severe wall flapping and even with heavy duty metal tent pegs doing their Best, it still collapses.
NOT A HAPPY CAMPER :(((
2ND UPDATE:
We have some fairly Serious WIND and RAIN issues here and this tent does NOT hold up. The first thing that went was the rain fly, as you might have noted from my First post.
I'd replaced the useless tie down strings that came with and got some screw in the ground pegs to hold the metal framing, also noted above.
Now, the loops are ripping out.
I'D RETURN THIS TENT IF I COULD. Not sure what I'm going to do with a $600 bit of canvas that I CANNOT USE AS A TENT :(((
(too bad the vendor doesn't monitor these reviews)

title: A quality set for all exercise needs

I have now had my GoYoga set for an entire year so I feel qualified to write a balanced review. As an immunocompromised person I was very limited with my options during lockdown and even after our building started opening our common areas in limited amounts (including our gym) as I could not risk exposure to COVID19. I looked for a fitness option I could partake in safely and comfortably at home. I purchased the GoYoga 7 piece set and have no regrets.

Aside from being well made and sturdy, the set has multiple pieces that suit all of my home workout needs and will also be perfect when I return to the studio. Each piece is very comfortable and allows me to reach positions in my workout pain free and with ease. It’s easy to wipe down and in an entire year has not shown any wear or tear. I could not be happier with this purchase.

title: Night fox SWIFT VS RED
text:
I was curious about both Version the SWIFT and RED so here’s a review for both:

SWIFT - 199$
- Tiny Field of View
- Walking is barely possible on a street with no obstacles, but not recommended
- Viewing Distance is no further than your backyard
- You will be visible at night with it’s Red eyes when IR is On
- Comes with a convenient and good quality hard case to keep your device safe

RED - 299$
- Massive improvement in Field of View
- Display seems slightly blurry but in general better quality (Less Noise)
- Viewing Distance is the same
- Great improvement with the Camo for the IR eyes - You will not be as visible at night even on full IR setting
- Does NOT come with a hard case - which is a shame
- Supports Video and Photo recording with Audio (1080p)

In conclusion, if you are considering cheap night vision, you may just skip the SWIFT and take a look at the RED HD
They are both mildly useful but more of a toy

title: Good Toy but a Digital Zoom is useless...
text:
... they do work well at night however two major disadvantages.

1. The POV is very small
2. You are basically fixed at one viewing distance as when you zoom in with a digital zoom everything becomes blurry, so no use at all.

What can be improved:

- Make it possible to use them as actual night vision googles (larger POV, minimal zoom)
- Actual Optics to zoom in (As if that'd be possible, this device is definitely capable to view things in the dark at far distance)
- The screen needs to be adjustable in brightness.
- Holding the buttons to zoom in and out takes unnecessarily long.

For 100$ no big complains, but I'd rather spend a bit more to get moving optics and versatility

So, as far as the actual product goes, it seems to be fine quality wise. title: Ridiculously Picky Food Snob LIKED the Chicken a la King!
text:
I am a VERY picky eater who doesn't like junk food, unhealthy food or Chef Boyardee anything that comes from a can. My father-in-law had a selection of Mountain House pouches and offered to let my husband and I try some as we were talking about camping food. He was already adding water to the Chicken a la King when I frowned at the selection. This is NOT the flavor I would have chosen to try but I kept my mouth shut. He handed me a small bowl of the food, which looked similar to the Lipton pasta pouches my husband ate when we were first married. I cautiously nibbled at a noodle. To my shock, it actually tasted good to me and I happily finished the whole bowl.

For reference, I'm a bit of a food snob. I cook most of my meals from scratch. I bake artisan breads and rolls for fun. I love Italian food and always make my own cream sauces from scratch. Sometimes I even make my own pasta. I maintain a small herb garden so I have access to organic, fresh-snipped herbs. Yeah, I'm that kind of food hobbyist. My picky tendencies thoroughly annoy my husband but he frequently gets to eat restaurant quality meals at home so he doesn't complain too much. Despite my picky palette, I STILL enjoyed the Chicken a la King! So much so that I bought a big #10 can for our hurricane kit.

If you like the flavor of a hearty, homemade chicken noodle soup with veggies, you are most likely going to like this meal. It has a light sauce instead of a soup broth but that description will give you a good idea about the flavor. My husband also liked the flavor very much but he's not nearly as picky as I am. Our 9 year old, who is somewhere in between our tastes and pickiness, also enjoyed the Chicken a la King and ate his portion eagerly. I'd say this is one meal that pleases just about everyone.

Tip: Use 1/4 cup less water than the pouches call for and let it sit for ten to fifteen minutes to soften the noodles properly. This goes for just about every Mountain House meal!

title: I survived 2008 Hurricane Ike 12 days without electricity. Here is why I now store this Premium Quality Freeze Dried Fruit:
text:
These strawberries are beyond delicious! These big #10 (one gallon) cans of freeze dried fruit are IDEAL if you are new to using freeze dried fruits or if you want to put away a couple cans for your family in case of emergency but you don't want to spend $150 on a 6 can case plus shipping from somewhere else. (You simply cannot beat Amazon Prime!)

• • • #10 cans typically hold 12 cups of food and about 11 cups of freeze dried fruits and veggies • • •

It is hard to find information about how much food is actually in a #10 can and have it be accurate enough that you can plan your meals. When filled to the brim with something like rice, the #10 cans hold 12 cups. But freeze dried food is light and not compacted, with air space between the dry pieces so you get about 11 cups (bananas) to 11.25 cups (strawberries and raspberries) in a big can like this. The cans are "full", the difference is simply air space between the fruit pieces. (To be safe, always assume there are 11 cups per #10 can of freeze dried fruits and veggies. I have found this to be accurate and a great way to calculate how much you have stored.)

Now let's talk about how yummy the food is! As I took pictures I could hardly stop my 9 year old son from grabbing handfuls of strawberries behind my back as I tried to snap a quick photo. (The bowl of strawberries was dumped straight into his mouth mere seconds after I got that picture!) The fruit is positively DELICIOUS for snacking straight from the can!

We live in Houston and personally lived through Hurricane Ike in 2008. At the time my son was 18 months old and I would have given anything - ANYTHING - to have these freeze dried strawberries to have offered him. Grocery stores were picked clean the day before the storm. Some of the grocery stores flooded and most of them had damage to roofs, glass doors and building structures from being hit by flung tree branches, fence pieces and debris. We went 12 days without electricity in our home. Grocery stores were without power for the first 5 or 6 days and stayed closed for about a week in our area as they had to be cleaned up before reopening. It was almost 3 weeks after the storm before stores were restocked with fresh produce beyond a few local items like tomatoes and jalapeños. Please, take the advice from someone who has lived through a natural disaster and invest in freeze dried fruits and veggies for your family. Everything in our refrigerators and freezers were ruined by day 2 without power and we still had 10 days to go. The only thing you have to rely on is what you have on your pantry shelves. That is it. These cans will keep for 25 years unopened and truly are a wise investment.

So, since I have been through a natural disaster, I have learned how to bake with freeze dried food since I still live in Houston and may have to deal with another storm in the future. These strawberries did GREAT and I'm going to include the recipe I used so you can have success with them, too. It is wise to open and try the food you are storing but since this company gave several reviewers like myself a discount to test their products, this work has been done for you. You can simply store the cans of food knowing it is superior quality. (I have purchased and used Thrive brand fruits and these taste identical to theirs! In my opinion these strawberries were even better quality.)

• Strawberry Chocolate Chip Muffins •
--> This recipe also works with freeze dried blueberries or other freeze dried fruits
1/4 cup butter, softened
1/3 cup sugar
1 egg, beaten
1/2 cup milk (a small can of evaporated milk is fine to use)
1 cup flour (up to 1.5 cups depending on humidity; batter should be a thick muffin batter)
1 and 1/2 tsp baking powder
1/2 cup freeze dried strawberries (or raspberries or other fruit) rehydrated in 1/2 cup water with the excess liquid drained off
1/2 cup milk chocolate chips

Preheat oven to 400°. Cream butter and sugar. Add the egg and mix well. Add flour alternately with splashes of milk and combine until a thick batter has formed and all ingredients are incorporated. Gently fold in rehydrated fruit. Spoon into 12 paper lined baking cups, filling halfway to 3/4ths full. Bake for 20 minutes or until tops begin to turn golden.

• Tip •
The leftover powder at the bottom of each can is AWESOME for making strawberry butter or adding to oatmeal to make your own fruit and cream flavor. If nothing else, dump the powder in your pancake batter. Don't let the powder go to waste, it is delicious!

Also, if you want to know about the countries of origin on the fruits, this was posted on the seller's FAQ page: "We source our Nutristore foods from some of the following countries: USA, Canada, Ecuador, Greece, Costa Rica, Uruguay, Argentina, Serbia, New Zealand, India, Poland, Mexico & Chile. [We] no longer source foods from China."

I was very fortunate to be able to purchase this pack of freeze dried strawberries at a discount so I could try it, eat it and bake with it before writing a review. I hope that by sharing my photos and experience that you are able to make the best buying decision for your own family! Hugs from Houston!

title: Excellent paddle that was used by everyone ages 9 to 55! LOVE the bigger, wider blade!
text:
This paddle has been great for our stand up paddle board! This is the second one purchased so I will be comparing it to a $35 paddle that was bought from a big box sporting goods store that starts with the letter A. We will call this Paddle A for comparison.

Out of the box, the Super Paddle seemed to be fairly comparable to Paddle A. Both were lightweight and could be disassembled for storage. The Super Paddle had some distinct advantages that quickly became evident as it was used:

• Packs Smaller: The Super Paddle pieces are better designed to break down into an easily portable size. The thought put into this feature was appreciated.

• Wider Blade: The Super Paddle had a wider blade than Paddle A, giving you more forward momentum with each stroke and more powerful maneuverability overall. It was noted that the Super Paddle blade was standing up to wear, tear and scratches much better than Paddle A.

• Sturdier: When it was assembled, the Super Paddle shaft felt very sturdy and firm in your hand. Paddle A was acceptable in this regard but it was noted that the Super Paddle was the one that seemed to be preferred, no matter who was on the board.

The Super Paddle was used by several family members on an 11 foot Alpine Explorer Stand Up Paddle Board (SUP). Everyone ages 55 to 9 was able to use the paddle board and the Super Paddle easily on the open water. The paddle is adjustable for persons 5 feet and above but even our 4’8” (56 inch) tall paddlers were easily able to use the Super Paddle for learning to SUP and exploring around the lake. If it is dropped by an inexperienced beginner, it is no big deal since the paddle floats.

I was fortunate to be able to purchase this piece of sporting equipment at a significant discount to try it out with family members on the SUP (and snap some pictures!) before writing this review and comparing the two paddles. We hope our review and the pictures of our fun help you to make the best buying decision for your family!

All you need to do is flip the rope in the direction you want it to go and the ball bearings seem to do the rest with the smallest flicks of your wrists.

The cable is exactly that - sturdy wire CABLE - with a protective plastic coating. It whips through the air and it doesn't hurt that much at all if it strikes you when you misstep (and that is coming from someone who bruises easily). The cable can kink if you fold it and pinch it really hard, which is probably why the seller includes a second cable so you don't have to order a whole new jump rope nor jump with a wonky, crinkled cable. I thought that was a very thoughtful touch.

The hardware that makes the jump rope adjustable is really neat and unlike anything else I have seen. It's actually a tiny screw-bolt on each end of the rope that tightens down onto the cable giving you a no slip sizing option. Again, this is a very thoughtful touch, both for those who are tall and short. (The jump rope worked just fine for my 5'10" hubby and 5'7" me.)

The green color is not quite the electric neon color shown but is more a pleasant grass green. I uploaded a picture taken in natural light so you can get a good idea of what the color is like in real life. It's a great unisex color that is not too girlie and is easy to spot in your gym bag or the stash of work out at home gear. It was easy to roll up after using and slides effortlessly back into it's nylon storage pouch.

I was fortunate to be able to purchase this product at a discount to try it out and write a review. This jump rope is not junk, this is a quality fitness item that has had some impressive thought and effort put into its design. Rest assured you are buying a good, quality item!

title: Thick & Sturdy Stainless Steel Containers are PERFECT for Pantry Storage, too!
text:
I love this canister! It is heavy, sturdy and incredibly durable. This is my fourth purchase from the Klean Kanteen company and I've been incredibly pleased with everything I have purchased. This canister is no exception!

I got tired of knocking over the orange box of baking soda in my pantry and began looking for a stainless storage jar. Most of the stainless pantry jars had poor reviews and were so thin you could deform them with your bare hands. I wanted something that could withstand lots of bangs and bumps if I decided to throw the baking soda in the chuck box for a camp out. (Baking soda + water makes a great first aid paste for bites and stings.) When I stumbled across this one, I knew it would be ideal.

The 16 ounce canister easily held the full 16 ounce (1 pound) box of baking soda with room leftover to stash a small scoop. At 3.75 inches tall and 3.5 inches wide, it doesn't take up a ton of room on my pantry shelf but I no longer have to deal with gritty white baking soda spilling all over the tile floor of my pantry and lingering in the grout lines until I vacuum every nook and cranny. I also like that it will protect my baking soda from absorbing any stray odors that may affect the flavor of my cookies and baked goods.

I took a chance and ordered this one Used - Like New from Amazon warehouse deals. They said it had surface imperfections affecting less than 10% of the surface area. When mine arrived it had a sticker stuck on the lid and residue from another sticker on the side of the canister. It took around 10 drops of Goo Gone and doTerra wild orange to get all the residue off. I thought that was the only "surface imperfection" but then I noticed there are faint scratches along the circular rim of the lid, as if the lid was twisted against a slightly rough surface. Buffing with a drop of orange essential oil helped reduce the appearance of the scratches. Buying used saved me about $3 but be aware that if they say it is scratched, it really is scratched and may or may not have stickers all over it. Buy new if you don't keep Goo Gone on-hand...

In short, I am very, very pleased with this canister and am now wanting to purchase the 8 ounce size to store baking powder in. If you are considering stainless steel pantry storage containers, I highly recommend the thickness, heft and durability of this brand!

This pair looks so handsome on my pantry shelf! I am happy that I invested in Klean Kanteen’s high quality stainless storage containers that are going to last my family for years.

Update October 2016: I have just ordered my third Klean Kanteen canister to store pink Himalayan sea salt. The trio continues to look very handsome on my baking shelf! title: If a Carabineer and a Paperclip Got Together and Had a Baby, This Would Be the Result!
text:
These carabineers are functional and have a use, so long as you realize how teeny tiny they are. Each one is only slightly larger than a quarter. They cannot hold a full set of keys but would be ideal for holding one or two standard metal keys. (My minimalist hubby loves things this small and simple.) I feel they would be great for suspending an extra key and hanging it from the branch of a tree so you always have a hidden spare.

I'm not joking when I say they are the midget love child of a carabiner and a paperclip. We have some little carabineers floating around the house but these are smaller than any I have ever seen. If your daughter needs a carabiner for her American Girl Doll, you've come to the right place!

All joking aside, these are great for securing small items to your purse or backpack such as hand sanitizer, lip balm holders and other small incidentals. The carabineers have a sporty look to them and are sure to draw a few "Aww! A tiny baby carabineer!" comments from random strangers. They don't open wide enough to hold the back strap of a hat (max opening is 0.4 inches - less than 1/2 inch). I suspect they will last longer if they aren't opened repeatedly but only used to suspend lightweight items. They are ideal if you need to loan out a single key and provide a way for the borrower to not lose the key. They would also be a great way to quickly attach luggage tags to bags and should hold up to minor wear and tear.

All five of mine were delivered working with paint finishes that were in very good shape. The pink (my favorite) is already starting to show some signs of the paint rubbing away and revealing the shiny silver aluminum underneath from use.I was kind of bummed that I received a cobalt blue instead of an aqua blue bineer.

I was fortunate to be able to receive this set of 5 for free to write a review. If you are aware of the tiny size and lightweight duty carabineer you are buying, the product is accurately represented.

title: BlastMatch is so easy even kids can operate it (with proper adult supervision of course)
text:
Obviously, judging by my profile name, I'm a girl. When it is time for me to start a fire, I need something that works right the first time with my smaller hands and does not break all my short but feminine nails. I have used a number of strikers and fire starters with hilariously varying results. Most are okay-ish. I don't like skinny little strikers that you have to rub with a piece of hacksaw blade which often has a back side that is almost as sharp and jagged as the business end of the blade. I don't like short micro strikers where you end up lighting your hangnails on fire along with the tinder because your hand was so close. (This doesn't actually happen but you get the picture.)

When I first bought this BlastMatch my husband immediately claimed it as his and it disappeared from the face of the earth for over two years. That should have been my first clue that it was the best striker out there. Every once in awhile it would resurface to light the fire pit in the back yard but it would quickly be whisked away to a back pocket and once again vanish from existence as rapidly as it had reappeared. I had no idea where he was hiding it so I simply had to resort to using other strikers I had purchased that worked well enough. They just were not as quick and easy as this one.

Let's talk about what I love. First of all, it has a big, thick firesteel rod that is the thickest I own. (See the picture I uploaded.) This means it will most likely last for the advertised number of strikes. Second, my son has been able to use this to start a fire on our camp outs since he was 7. It's really, really easy. to use. Not really that easy to open but you quickly get the hang of it. Basically you open it, use your thumb to depress the metal scraper on one side and then push down. A bright yellow, orange and white colored shower of sparks will greet you like an angry sparkler gone awry and set alight anything remotely resembling tinder. (A friend who first demonstrated his to us set the fine fibers of our living room rug on fire. After tamping out the little glowing embers, we were sold.)

My husband confiscated the first one I bought and would not so much as let me lay eyes on it so I decided to buy myself a second one. I had given the other crappy fire rods we had somehow picked up along the way to my boy scout son, which was surprisingly safe since they don't hardly light a thing, and proceeded to replace them all with a tool that worked. Since we have one BlastMatch from 2014 and one from 2016, I decided I would compare them side-by-side to see if the product has had any visible changes or become more flimsy as reviewers have insisted. I couldn't find a single difference. The plastic on each was the same thickness, the rod was the same diameter and they both opened with the same springy force.

They give a generous shower of sparks and if you get it anywhere close to a tinder ball, you are going to start a fire with one push. It catches that easily. I am very pleased with BOTH purchases and will continue to use these until they break. (If they do, I'll be right back here to complain.) While we don't use our BlastMatch every single day, we have used the original one somewhere around 50 or more times since my husband is a scout leader and it is still going strong with no cracks in the plastic and no damage visible anywhere to the striker. If you want to be on the safe side, wait until the price drops to twelve or less and then make your purchase. I have seen them as low as ten at various times of the year so your patience can pay off. And do not use your BlastMatch while drunk or trying to impress women. Not that the reviewers who broke theirs were either drunk or able at all to impress women - I'm just giving you some general good advice.

I bought both of my strikers at full price. I do not work for BlastMatch. I don't even particularly like catching things on fire. I just like roasting marshmallows. And Starburst. Happy camping everyone!

title: Great for Halloween Trick or Treating and Awesome to Have On-Hand for Emergencies!
text:
Little lantern puts out a lot of light! This was really handy for our Halloween trick-or-treating. It rained this year, adding slick roads to the danger of nighttime traffic. We took the children around as a group and this light lit the way for all the adults (no one had brought a flashlight) and made it easy for our son to spot his parents in the crowd, ensuring he didn't get to far ahead of the group.

I set the Luci to charge in a windowsill for about 8 hours of sunlight, deflated it and stored it flat on a shelf until it was needed Halloween night, about two weeks later. It lit up and glowed for several hours that night without even flickering or dimming. Multiple people admired it, switching it on and off through it's various settings of low, high, flash and off. It even got curious inquiries and compliments from strangers out with their children as well.

Not only is this a great light to have on hand for emergencies but it's going to prove useful during family camp outs (we camp as a family about 6 times per year and my husband and son rack up another 3-6 camp outs with boy scouts). I also plan on using it during night time activities at New Year's and July 4th. I love that I don't have to suddenly worry about batteries as the sun is sinking in the sky during busy, eventful holidays when it would be difficult to run to the store in all the traffic - if you can even get to the store because the roads have been shut down for the parade/fireworks show/trick or treaters. This light makes my life a teensy bit easier!

title: You go camping? Alrighty then, you'll want one of these! Just hit "add to cart" now.
text:
Okay, this thing is flat-out handy! Whoever came up with this must have done a lot of camping. You've been there, yes? When you're trying to find something in your tent at night and you bump your head on the lantern that is hanging from a flimsy fabric scrap sewn into the top of your tent with a single piece of thread (with love from China) and the simple swinging action of your micro LED lantern releases the tab and sends it plummeting into the plushy depths of your sleeping bag where the brilliant glow is muted to nothing RIGHT when you really needed to see if you were putting your underwear on backwards. Or - even more fun - when you've rented a screened shelter at a state park for the night and you realize there is not a single dang nail to be found from which you could hang your light so you have a set it down, pick it up, set it down, pick it up then shove it in your mouth kind-of a problem solving experience.

Ah, Nite Ize. How did you know?!! Now I can hang my lantern just about anywhere I want. I can even bend it around a small tree branch and clip it up high while I scrub the dishes with about a thousand spiders in the dark. I can also quickly loop the gear tie holding the micro lantern around my son's neck so he doesn't drop his flashlight in the magical blue pit of the campground Port-a-Potty. (*Splash* MOM!!!) And - probably the most valuable use - I can clip frequently used items from your neon yellow self and hang you in a really obvious place so I don't have to be asked {repeatedly} where the grill lighter/roasting stick/marshmallow bag/trash bucket is. And at night, when I remove the lantern and let you hold my spider spray, I know you've got my back. Thanks, Nite Ize, for making camping a little bit easier!

text:
I purchased these grips after getting tired all of my other pairs getting stretched out to their limits after a short period of time.. I was hoping these would stand the test of time. Even rogue wraps gave in after a month of 2-3 times a week wearing! It so happened I hurt my wrists after a strenuous lengthy workouts and was looking for a solid support at all costs.I came across of Grip Power Pads and after reading the reviews decided to give them a try and here is what I found:
Pros: they are very sturdy, they stretch but not too much, hence keeping the shape longer. They are long enough to wrap around your wrist and provide strong support to the wrists.
Cons: The loops around the thumb stretch out too fast and loosen up way too fast.. they don't have much support for holding the wrist wrap in place, so overall I don't see much point in using them in the way they are. Even putting both loops around thumb doesn't create enough stability to keep the wrap in place.. so what I do, I just adjust the wraps each time I have to lift or pull-up and once done - I release them.
Overall the wraps are perfect except for the weak thumb loops support but I'd buy them just for the stability of the wrist and overall durability.
Update 09/2017: Disclamer: For reviewing the grips company sent me another pair for free, and to my surprise!!! title: Rope stinks
text:
I'm a grown adult and wanted to get back into the tetherball game. My husband built me a tetherball pole/base as the reviews on standard ones just didn't cut it. However, the base is not a concern in this review.

We've only played with the tetherball a total of 3 times. First time was fine (it was also the very first time my husband had actually played thetherball). But the second time when I played with a friend, the rope from the pole to the ball tore right at the base of the ball. I thought "no big deal I'll just tie it back on"

False. I tied it back on and within 30 minutes, it tore off again. I added on several knots and even went to YouTube to look up sturdy knots but that's not the issue. The string for this ball is VERY flimsy and weak.

On the third go around, the ball came flying off mid-serve and could have injured someone. Ball itself seems to be fine and sturdy. The rope itself, again, is just crappy overall. It keeps breaking and it's not easy to "re-string", if you will.

Overall, the ball is great and seems to be sturdy. However, if you're a grown adult looking into smacking the heck out of a tetherball, definitely be prepared to get a new, sturdier rope because the one that comes with it just doesn't cut it.

title: Perfect for small to medium adult woman.
text:
First the colors and quality of these pads are quite nice. I'm 50 and using them for roller skating safety. They are comfortable and easy to put on. The wrist pads feel extremely sturdy and safe to me.

Sizing: I can see why so many reviews comment on the knee pads. They do run small. The sizing is a bit confusing because you are supposed to order based on your palm size only. This will determine the ideal wrist guard size. The knee pads are apparently the same size for everyone, regardless of what size you order. For reference, I'm 5'3" 135 pound woman. My palm size is 7". I followed the chart and it suggested I order small, so I did. Everything fit me just fine. I am especially happy with the fit of the wrist pads and elbow pads. I will say that the knee pads definitely run small. If you are woman who wears a small or medium ( approximately size 2-10) pant...then these are likely going to be just fine for you. But for the rest of the world, maybe not. They really need to make longer straps for the knee pads. Even for me (who wears a size 4-6) I was only able to secure the knee straps about half way over the velcro base at the front of the knee. See photo with red arrows where I have them secured. This is tight enough without being too tight. I mean, I could get them tighter as the straps are quite stretchy. But this was a comfortable/secure fit at the halfway point. Its perfectly fine for my smallish legs (I'm wearing a size 6 Lulu legging in this photo). But I can imagine how others might have issues securing the knee pads if they have healthier sized legs.

Overall, I think these are a very quality and affordable set of pads, best for medium sized adult females or smaller.

title: Good quality for beginner skater.
text:
Color: Watermelon. Skate Size: 7 (My normal shoe/boot size is 8-8.5 in US womens)
First, they are soooo cute! I love the color combo. I'm 50 yrs old and decided to get back into roller skating. I used to do this casually when I was in my teens, but was never exceptional at it. I thought this would be a fun way to get some more exercise in my life. So far its working! You engage so many muscles when roller skating. It takes balance, core and leg strength to keep from falling on your bum. These are made of vinyl so they are quite stiff at first and take some time break in. My hubby purchased these as a gift. He purchased according to the size chart and they fit well/snug with a thick sock. I normally wear a size 8 in U.S women’s shoes. When it comes to boots I typically buy 8.5 (to allow for thicker sock). Hubby purchased the size 7 skates as the chart indicated. This was just right. I thought they might be a bit tight at first. But with use, I realized the size was perfect. You want your foot to be held firmly as you will be moving around a lot. I imagine if they were looser, my foot would flex more and potentially cause strain in the foot muscles so I think the snug sizing is perfect. Measure your foot and look at size chart and you should be fine. I like that the skates have a metal base plate instead of plastic. This feels sturdier/safer. The wheels roll well on blacktop streets (even better on my hardwood floors inside my house). There are a couple things that were a bit odd. First the vinyl is so thick its a bit uncomfortable (specifically around the ankle) until they get worn in. And it takes a while to wear them in.
Second, the laces on one skate were a whole foot longer than the laces on the other skate. This trips out my OCD brain. I will have to replace them.

Overall, I think these are good skates for beginners (of all ages). They are made well and of good quality. Just be patient with the wear in period.

title: Pretty bottle, Not very functional.
text: This water bottle has some definite pros and cons. Lets start with the good: for sure it's great to be able to drink fruit infused water! I don't drink any sodas or sugary drinks, so this is a great idea. The bottle is also very pretty (i got the yellow) and it's really awesome to see my yellow top with my yellow lemon slices in the bottle. It's also nice that the fruit is contained in the inner tube and not able to come out when poured. There is also a nice flip top with a handle so it can be clipped onto a bag or just carried by the little top handle. Thats about all the good points. The unfortunate problem with this bottle is that it doesn't allow you to drink all the water in the bottle! Because of where the holes are to let water in, it prevents you from finishing your last 2 inches of water. So thats a problem because if i want to finish my water i have to take the whole top off and then the wet tube with the fruit drips everywhere and it's just awkward. You also cant fill the bottle with water all the way up because the tube of fruit displaces so much of the water. Then on top of it, when you have drank about half of the bottle, the water isn't even touching the fruit anymore! Plus, when you go to drink it, it's hard to get any water out because the fruit from the tube bumps up against the water hole and blocks it. The water will come out but only a little bit, it's very obstructed. Then we have the problem of the flip top itself. It does seal well, however in order to open the top to drink it, you have to pinch your finger under this brittle plastic piece to open it. I feel like it's very difficult to open and hurts my finger. I also feel like it's so brittle its only a matter of time before it breaks. So, overall I don't see myself continuing to use this bottle. It doesn't hold much water and doesn't function very well. I did receive this product at a discount in exchange for a review and I always give my honest opinion.
