title: Works as good as an expensive reel
text:
I ran my new JOHNCOO Baitcasting Reel reel out to the lake today for a test spin, as they say. I'm using braided line with a fluorocarbon leader.
After a bit of adjusting, drag, resistance knob, and magnets it gets the bait on out there as it is supposed to with zero professional overlap. Max distance with no fear of a bird's nest. From this standpoint it's a solid addition to your arsenal. Couldn't be more pleased.
I gave it 4 stars because to my amazement it would not work with my first choice of rod, a Speed Stick whereby the reel tightens down in the front with the tightening screw on the bottom. The problem, I found, is that for reasons I can't fathom the screw that holds the line guide in place sticks out too far. The head contacts the top of the restraining clamp on the rod as it goes back and forth, putting into a bind and shaving off plastic from the reel screw.
My solution was to go to my second choice of rod..one that has threads on either end of the reel...You screw the top of the rod down towards the handle...that sort of arrangement. For that it works dandy with plenty of clearance.
So if you plan to put the reel on a rod that clamps with a screw from the bottom...it probably isn't for you. Else, it's low cost and perfect. The obvious fix for the manufacturer is to use a flatter screw head.

title: Best for you
text:

title: Sheer, lightweight, and a good value for your hard earned dough
text:
I know the SAN Like Baitcasting Fishing Reel is advertised for salt water foremost...but I can't see it. To my way of thinking it's more of a lightweight bass reel. And it is light and small of frame. Two hours after I got mine I was on a local public lake trying it out. Been looking forward to it.

Size-wise it would be at home on a lighter rod if that's your notion. I mated mine to an old comfy Speed Stick. First thing I noticed was the spool isn't solid. It has holes in it. I'm sure there is a more scientific way to say it but I don't know what it is. A small matter, but it makes tying the line onto it much easier, as you can pass it through the holes. Next up, something I haven't seen before...the drag 'clicks' as you adjust it. An improvement, I think, as it gives more finesse to the operation. Otherwise the reel behaves much as any other.

I have a ton of reels. Some mine, some hand-me-downs. Some are top o' the line too. But one thing I have noticed...high dollar or low dollar they ALL wear out just the same. Point being that since this is the case for the money, you can't do better with high dollar than you can with the SAN Like Baitcasting Fishing Reel. If you're just starting out you can purchase 3 or 4 for less than you'll spend on one of the big names. Functionally there isn't much difference and like I said, they all have a lifespan. Heck, rod and reel makers could give away their products to sell their branded lures. That's where all your money is going anyway.

One tip. The brake knob. On power casts with mine time and again at the apex I'd get that professional overlap thing. My reel, at any rate, is pretty finicky about having enough resistance. Typically you set that knob so your bait drops slowly and that's it. But this reel needs a bit more braking... then it works like a charm. So if you get a tangle, just run that knob up a bit more. You'll still be able to get that bait way out there without the birds nest effect.

Only time and use will tell how my new reel holds up, but for my money, I'm tickled with it. It's as much as I hoped for and nary a complaint. I'd love to see some validation with good reviews.

title: Unique Tasty Lure For Big Bass
text:

title: Worked better than hoped!
text:
Season end update: Everything below still goes but I wanted to run back over here and mention that the thing worked for me mid-season. Sitting in my chair in the open watching over a field I had a spot of luck. A deer worked around at 85 yards frequently glancing in my direction which was normal as I was on the edge of the road leading into the place. Sitting still with my binoculars I watched it for awhile before leisurely taking aim. If I had not had the suit it would have made me immediately. And one more thing, though the suit is full of holes it is amazingly warm. So happens I have another suit which is pretty much camo material with some cutouts. It's better than nothing but the EAmber Ghillie Poncho Suit Camo is far superior for the purpose. Couldn't be more tickled!

Update: I did manage to take it for a hunting spin. It is its own ground blind. I couldn't be more pleased with it. Didn't get a chance to deer or turkey test it yet. The invitation was out but no one showed up. Drat!

One caveat. The suit comes with a pretty nasty chemical smell. The dyes, I suppose. It's manageable out of the box but I don't care much for it. Don't know if you can wash it and I'm not going to experiment. So far it's been hanging out in the garage for nearly two months. The smell is half of what it was but it's still there. So be advised, buy early and hang long.
====================

I am what you call 'old' hunter and I know my climbing days are growing fewer. I have always used a camo net for ground bow hunting with mixed results so I thought I'd try a Ghillie suit. That's different.
So here's what happened. My wife was at work when my dandy EAmber Ghillie Poncho Suit arrived. My first plan was to crouch in the hall. But I nixed that because I don't care for screams. My screams when she would either kick or shoot me. So on to Plan B. I told her that a monster had shown up in the back yard and that I had fed it, though I shouldn't have...and to be real careful when she got home. Told her RIGHT WHERE TO LOOK... Photo proof provided. Hid in plain sight.

She got home, looked. Went inside. I called her. She came out two more times. (I was astounded!) She ONLY figgered it was me when the new cedar stump started giggling. Or pile of moss or whatever. Worked beyond my wildest dreams.

The suit is very light and consists of wads of camo string glommed onto thin netting. It has a head hoodie thing with an opening for your face (thus my addition of my camo skeeter head net). You *can* see through the netting if you decide to go completely native. The hoodie has snaps and pull string closures. Comes with a bag...and unlike you might think at first, as the bag is small, the suit easily stuffs back into it. Worth mentioning, the sides where your arms rest are made in such a way that when it's time to get to work with your trusty bow you won't gather in much suit. In other words, there is more freedom of movement than you'd think. You should do a little practice with your new EAmber Ghillie Poncho Suit and it'll make perfect sense.

The suit should only be put on AFTER you get your stand set up. It will snag on everything. Air it out before use.

So...I think you're going to like it. A lot...and you sure can't beat the price. A lot of work goes into these things. Wow! I like it because unlike the others for sale where you look like a human beast thing with leaves on it... wearing the EAmber Ghillie Poncho Suit you look like just another rotted soggy woods glump. Invisible.

And PS...I see everyone else is including photos. There is a reason for that. First thing YOU will want to do with yours is to have someone snap a pic of you. It's fun!

title: I'm impressed
text:
I have never used braided line before so I thought I'd give it a try. It promises to reduce professional overlap....and that would be marvelous. At the time of writing it will be bit before I get to put it to the fish test. I ordered 15# multicolored line. I'll say this much...it comes in a NICE plastic box with a doodad that lets you unspool to your reel right from inside that same box. Most impressive. If I'm this delighted by the superior packaging I can't wait to get it on the water. If the thought put into the product matches the end result then wow! I'll be back a little later with the report.

Part Deux: Finally had a chance to go test out my new GLUREE 4 Stands Braided Fishing Line in a local public lake a few minutes ago. I wrapped it around a new reel, so you might call it a multi-test. I tied on a pretty hefty crankbait, and first cast and several more I got that nasty pverlap. I kept fiddling with the reel until I pretty much eliminated that mess. In the meantime I found that correcting the line was easier than I ever had in the past.

Part Tre: I guess I'm the only guy who didn't know that braided line doesn't break. Subsequently I have been enlightened by no less than two different fishing pals. When you go braided, which I like a lot, you really need to tie on a leader with regular monofilament fishing line attached at the end so when you get hung up you can break off when you put on the old tug. Braided is strong stuff!

The line itself, even at 15#, is like handling sewing thread. As it spools out of the handy box you get different colors. (I'd love to know the yardage per different color.) In the water the line is easy to see while working the lure. I doubt the fish would mind. So, if you haven't tried braided line before, you should go for it. I'll be putting it to the big test a little later in the season. As of this writing, still a little early. So far I like it better than the plastic stuff.

title: Works for me!
text:
I gave the A SLICE RED Ultra Lightweight Packable Backpack (In black) 5 stars as you can see.

Here is my situation. I hunt. Don't find much but I hunt a lot and I have this big professional camo honkering GREAT backpack. I could survive everything but a nuclear war with only that thing. And that's a good thing...but...

I also often hunt out of a portable tree stand and that big old pro back unit is just a mess in that situation. Clunky, And it's heavy! So I was really looking forward to my new backpack for the purpose. I moved the essentials from my pro pack to the new one and it's exactly what I was looking for.

The A SLICE RED Ultra Lightweight Packable Backpack is a baby backpack for sure. It's a dufflebag put together in the shape of a backpack actually. When you get it stuffed it becomes the backpack. It has a front pocket. A mesh side pocket, good for a bottle of water or necessary paper..whatever you like. And the interior, at least for my purposes is plenty roomy. I have room to spare. That surprised me. Unlike the big boys this little pack adds zero weight to whatever you put in there. That's a bonus. The zippers worked fine, btw. Backstraps are adjustable. A little flimsy compared to high dollar, but they don't slip

Is it rough and tumble? Probably not. I wouldn't trust it in rough country with briars and such...but for normal use, it's fine. It is a day hiker or a day hunter. From the cost point and utility it's a fine choice for normal wear. I'm very pleased.

title: This Minn is the Max for the Minimum
text:
What I meant by the catchy headline is that this is about the minimum horsepower for the small boat application. In my case I have it hooked to a Sun Dolphin 8.5 play boat. My calculation was that more power was not only not needed, but not wanted. I need those lower speeds for trolling and such. Also I need to make sure that when I go out I can get back in, less paddle.

Here is the deal. The thing is NOT a power hog. As of this writing (super rainy wet year) I have battled winds and currents in our overflowing rivers and having to stay on it all the time has been the test. I haven't got back to the pull out with less than a half battery yet.

My notion is that if you have a 14ft boat or less this engine is adequate. No need to break the bank if you're on a budget. For my purposes it is perfect!

The gadget that tilts the thing. Over the years I have fought with those releases. Not so on the MinnKota Endura Transom Mount Trolling Motor. Smoothest one I have ever seen.

The one thing that is not perfect is the reverse. Don't plan on running it from the front of the boat in reverse. Ain't happening. I don't know if the blades aren't pitched right or what, but the reverse really froths the water without giving much ooomph. I mean, it will back you out of the shallows, but it's not for full time use. Forward, on the other hand works just like you like.

About the handle.... Well, I wound up putting my trolling motor in the back and I was kinda worried about steering. You know, twisting around and all. But with the extension handle which you can pull out a lot or a little....it ended up being zero problem. I think I might actually like it more better on the aft now.

And one heads up. If you plan on putting a transducer onto the foot...be advised, it probably won't fit as the foot is too short. However...my workaround was to put my transducer all the way to the rear against the fin and shim it with some rubber pads on an edge so that I got it near to vertical. And my depth finder works just fine. So no harm done. You could use most anything that won't rot. Your wife's Tupperware, for instance.

I like my MinnKota Endura Transom Mount Trolling Motor a LOT and you will too. If your boat be smaller grab one. You'll be thankin' me!

text:
Love it! Using it for short errands in the neighborhood. Unfortunately it seems that there is no way to moderate speed. Its either off or full on.

UPDATE: Downgraded from 5 to 4 stars.
It CRITICAL that your rear tire is fully inflated to the recommended pressure. Your new scooter may come with under-inflated tires and it needs HUGE WARNING IN RED LETTERS to inform people to inflate rear tire.

If the rear tire is under inflated,, when torque is applied to the rear wheel, it might start to slip inside the tire. This will eventually cause a damage to the air valve letting more air out. That will in turn result in more slippage until the valve gets completely sheared off of the inner tube, cause ALL air to rapidly escape. You might lose control of the scooter, or, if you don't, you will have to push it all the way back home.

Tube replacement cost me $56 at the local repair shop. If you do not have a repair shop nearby - good luck! :)

title: One of the BEST!
text:
This small lantern is a little less than 5 1/2" tall and about 3 1/2" in diameter. If you need smaller, then you need a flashlight! As for light, it has plenty! I have 2 LED lanterns 10" tall by 5" dia. and they put out half as much light as these smaller ones. My bigger ones are not efficient enough to read by, these are. I need these strictly for outages, which we seem to have a lot of, and I appreciate the area coverage of these. No, it will not make it easy to read a few feet away from them, no lantern does that, but it will make it easy to see and navigate in a 15' x 15' room.
They are adjustable in only one way, and that is how much you open them. (At just high enough to turn them on, they make great guiding lights for a footpath or a cluttered area.) All the bulbs are on no matter how close to closed it is, so there is no power saving advantage to having it lowered. 12 Hours of emergency or evening lighting outside, is a lot of hours! It will more than stand up to all emergency needs except getting lost in a cave! LOL If it only had 3-4 hours of good light, I would not be happy with this, my first thought is always 'how to extend the emergency light time' and 'is it adjustable'. Well, you can't, and its not....Because of that this would not be an economic idea for an extended camping trip. But this is not being touted as a night after night lighting fix, as an emergency light, I don't need to worry about that.
I joined Etekcity's review program, because I have purchased several of their products and haven't found one I didn't appreciate a lot! As such I don't feel bad about getting one of their products at a reduced price or free for reviewing them. I take my time, and look at all the negative reviews and see if any apply to the product i received. So far.... yes it is pretty light, but no it would not blow away in less that 50mph winds. And i don't think you would be outside enjoying an evening in that kind of wind anyway. It has the hard anodized look and feeling of a well coated flashlight. The handles are wide enough to be easy to carry and a bungee cord or rope will attach them to the side of any tree or post, or you can hang them from a limb or tent pole. Heavy enough not to tip over, and good quality plastic instead of glass or cheep plastic that cracks. I don't see anything cheap or flimsy feeling about them at all!
Don't know what else to say about these, except my other two larger ones are going out into storage and I will be getting 2 more of these to store inside for emergencies. I highly recommend them!
PS: If you DO get a lemon, for Pete's sake tell them! They are very quick and easy to talk to. There is a card in the box with a toll free number, their e-mail address and their website on it (etekcity.com).... all for customer support.

title: light easy hiking or bugout bag addition
text:
I've had this on my bug-out list for a while now. At last I got it. I had questions I had doubts, because I was at first thinking of this as a filtration system. Yes it filtrates water.... no it is not a general filtration system. It is a "Personal" filter. A sip straw with advantages. Emphasis on the 'sip'. If you got as far as the comments section, you've seen what they say about it. This is for hiking, rather than camping use. Something to get water from point A to your mouth. However.... I did want to find out if I could use the bag to filter water into a cup for heating and it DOES work! You fill the bag with water... as clear as you can find, screw it into the straw, and gently but firmly squeeze. Filtered water will slowly dribble out of the sipping end. Not fast, but if you need a cup of coffee or some soup, it would be worth it. We are not talking kitchen magic here folks, we are talking survival.
To make this last as long as possible, use the clearest water you can find, use the little blue add-on filter, and backwash every time you use it. Just remember, water from a street gutter is not a good source, because of all the chemical contaminates that might be in it. This is for dirt, microbes, and insect contamination, not oil, anti-freeze and cleaners!
Picture 1 shows the bag screwed into the base, 2 shows the long folded tube attached to the base. you can also take off the short tube from the blue filter and attach it to the end of the long tube. Picture 3 shows the blue filter and the disk replacement filters for it (you get 6 total), and 4 shows the back-flow set-up. The plunger tube snugs 'into' not 'over' the mouth piece and the small blue filter's tube as well.

This was one of the Eteckcity products that I could get free or at reduced price in exchange for a review. I won't 'guess' if it works I won't say something I don't believe. This my honest opinion of a product I acquired to use personally.

title: Lee Precision Breech Lock Classic Press
text: I studied long and hard on whether to purchase this fine heavy duty Lee Cast Iron Breech lock press. I have used many presses over the last 40 years and still own some of the finest ones made. I was introduced to the unique breech-lock system 2 years with their hand press. The additional cost of bushings is somewhat of a downside but outweighed with speed of die change over. I have replaced all of Lee's rubber "O" ring lockrings due to their instability and lack of accurate repeatable settings. Hornady's  side lock clamping and Forster rings are far better and do not mar the 7/8"X14 threads due to frequent adjustments. My use of the Breech Press was another press for more mundane belling,universal decapping,expander mandrels and case forming of pistol and 300 B.O. This usage for me reduces the number of needed breech lock adapters. The only fault that I have found is that the shell holder mounting slot is pointed to the right of the press opening sharing the same slot to allow the primer kicker arm to deflect spent primers into the scrap tube. I find that by using the shell holder opening pointed to the left during use with a right mounted handle will sometimes push the shell holder to the right thus dismounting the shell holder. I wish that Lee would modify the right sided shell holder installation slot to the middle and re-mill the area and still keep the primer deflector as is.All in all 5 stars for sure and a great product. If you have any irregular shaped case mouth,this expander spindle will straighter out the eccentricity while using. I find it a little time consuming if used for other .30 caliber change-overs such as .308 and 300 Win as you have to dismantle the setting in order to accommodate longer or shorter cases. I'm not a fan of Hornady's "Zip Spindle" system as it requires 3 tools to properly tighten the zip knob or the spindle will slip if the nut is not squeezed tight enough against the interrupted threaded nut. A second necessary wrench absolutely is Hornady's New Dimension red die wrench for this propriatory flatted die lock ring also available from Amazon. I lock the flatted die ring and die into my press,then finally tighten the small zip spindle nut using my Hornady wrench. The new dimension lock rings are great as the tightening screw impinges the 7/8-14 die threads at a tangent to the threads thus not marring the steel threads as most setscrews do. title: Best Daypack I've Ever Owned
text:
The Osprey Pandion Daypack (OPD) is the best backpack I've ever had. No detail has been overlooked. It has everything. I'm still discovering features I didn't notice over the first few days.

I use my backpack for four things - schlepping my documents and portable office supplies for work back and forth to the office, for carrying my portable electronic supplies, for clothes/toiletries etc. for short airplane trips, and for long day hikes. I did all of this and more last weekend when I traveled to New Hampshire for three days which included a four mile hike, and two days when I needed to check in at work using my laptop.

There are three main compartments, each of which has its own partitions, sleeves, a lanyard, and in one of them, a waterproof lining. The pack itself has a stiff outer frame that comes in hand for a long hike, makes it easier to stand the pack up on its own, and allows for pack to be flattened out for light cargo, or fully expanded for air travel or a large payload. There are multiple exterior sleeves for water bottles, papers, and other items that are convenient to have quick at hand. Each zipper features a plastic loop which makes them easier to grab and pull.

The pack has multiple pull tight straps in a variety of places, including waist and chest straps that makes it easier to carry heavier weight, or using the straps on the outside, compress it down for lighter trips back and forth to the office. Its got a stout handle at the top. Taught mesh fabric has been stretched between the frame in the back, which provides good comfort for toting heavier weight, and allowing air to get in behind your back as you are moving along.

It's good looking, light, and it comes with a lifetime guarantee. Please peruse the multiple photos I took of the pack a few days ago (as usual, having difficulty with Amazon photo upload functionality. I'll add photos after balance of review posts.) This is a very impressive daypack from all standpoints including function, appearance, features, and weight.

title: Design Too Heavily Influenced by Watersport Dry Bags
text:
First the good news. The bag definitely keeps things dry. I decided to test the bag with paper towel stuffed inside and dunking the sealed bag in my kitchen sink. I attempted to squeeze out air from the outside and this wasn't easy to do. The sealing clamp at the top of the pouch, similar in design to full sized Dry Bags that I have seen in my scuba diving adventures, works well to seal out water. The paper towel remained dry.

Also, the touch screen and all the buttons on the FACE of my Droid Turbo are easy to operate and work well enough through the plastic material.

Now the not so good news. I found it nearly impossible to operate the buttons on the side of my phone while it is in the pouch. The pouch is manufactured by heat sealing two plastic rectangles together at their edges, so the edge seams are at a 90 degree angle and perpendicular to the buttons located at the edge of my phone.

Like other reviewers, I found the clamps, though effective, difficult to open and close. Sitting in the kitchen in comfortable conditions is one thing. Out on the boat, in the cold and/or wet, this could be a real nuisance.

Also I found the two Velcro straps to be ridiculously short. No way would they fit around my bicep without an uncomfortable stretch, and I am not that big! I don't want to wear my phone on my forearm when I am rowing or casting. Someone goofed on the specifications for these straps. They should be at least twice as long allowing for larger bicepts, particularly if someone is wearing a layer or more. And that is not only to allow for larger arms, but also to make it easier to attach the bands with one hand!

In conclusion, this pouch looks and operates like a miniature dive dry bag, which is great for waterproofing, but not so good when trying to operate your phone or wearing it on your bicep. I'm not sure what else is out there, but I might look around a little before settling on this model, particularly since a ziplock baggie can do almost everything this pouch can do.

title: Does the job but sticks out a bit
text:
I installed this on a Cannondale Adventure 400 Hybrid with Jumbo frame. The installation was slightly difficult because the long installation bolt had trouble clearing my front derailleur bracket as I'd insert if from the top. This Cannondale bike has a built in cross-member with a hole for a kickstand and the bolt needs to go in from the top at an exact 90 degree angle. I finally managed to get it through w/o having to loosen the derailleur bracket. Once past that issue the installation was simple. You'll need large allen wrench to do it. It's not usually a wrench size found in a bike repair kit like an Alien wrench.

This kickstand operates and holds up my bike just fine. However, the adjustment button does stick out near my heel as I ride. I'm 6-4 and wear a size 15, so perhaps not an issue for smaller riders, but then smaller riders probably ride a smaller bike and have that kickstand set for a shorter length. I found I can loosen the attachment bolt and slightly reposition the kickstand to help keep this button closer to the lower chain-stay, but my foot can still catch it when my foot isn't completely straight on the pedal. Plus the adjustment made with the attachment bolt means the kickstand mount isn't as firmly locked in as I'd like given the shape of the mount.

I'm an intermediate level cyclist who recently moved to the Denver area. After nearly dying on a 2800 foot climb over 15 miles I noticed my riding buddy had about a gear and a half lower than me. I looked around and finally swapped my stock Ultegra 12/23 to this 12/27 on my 1998 Specialized Allez Sport with a triple crank (52-42-30).

After pricing the extra tools I needed to do a swap, it wasn't much more $ to just hand this cassette and a new chain to my local bike shop and have them do the work - still saved $50-$60 using my own parts. Since I have a triple, I also have a long derailleur, so besides the chain, there's nothing more needed for the swap except for adjusting the derailleur for the bigger sprocket. I think 27 is as big as I can go, BTW, given the range of teeth on my crank.

I haven't been back to that hill yet, but this cassette and new chain are doing fine so far. My second gear (running middle ring) is now like my first gear was. Given the 12T top end, I didn't give up any high gearing, but I do need to get used to the bigger jump between 5th and 6th gear (I think that's the spot).

My riding buddy has a double with an 11-speed cassette. I think we're pretty close on highest and lowest ratios now. Sorry, I don't recall what he's got. But its a fairly high end bike with 11x2.

title: Sturdy rack, good price point. Good for occasional use; otherwise may want a rack that locks to car
text:
After reading the pros and cons of fork-mounting vs upright (wheel-mount) I decided to go with these, figuring the mostly aluminum structure would last a while and the fork-mounting would secure the bikes well. I've used the product one time on a short trip, but so far it seems sturdy and the bikes are locked on firmly. My one concern, which I knew in advance of purchase, is that the fork mount only holds the traditional thin skewers/axles. That works fine for our family fleet of tourers and hybrids from years 1998 through about 2012. However, a lot of new bikes now have the much fatter through-axles (particularly bikes w/ disc brakes). So if i get a new bike I'll probably need a new rack.

Vehicle: 2016 Subaru Outback

Pros:
-My big Cannondale Adventure 400 and my wife's Giant Sedona fit perfectly and are secured with front quick release and included rear hold-down strap.
-Reasonable price, though not as inexpensive as some all-steel models out there.
-No tools required, no customization needed for our Outback with factory folding roof rack.
-Seems and looks solid for those worried about appearance.

Cons:
-May need to fiddle with how many spacers to use with each bolt. There are six bolts on each rack.
-Installation, certainly the first time, might take up to 20 minutes for each rack. And sometimes it's hard to get those big wingnuts to thread properly given the awkward angle since the bolt is vertical and you may not have much space to install the wingnut between bolt and roof of car.
-Very easy to have the spacers fall off the bolts before wingnut is threaded. I had two or three roll off the back of our vehicle. No biggie on a flat concrete driveway but can be a problem on gravel or camping.
-It doesn't lock, which is okay for our needs. I can probably run a cable lock through the frame/tires and part of our roof rack. This may not keep the racks from being stolen but it would be a real pain to remove with bikes mounted. -Of course, it's nice to leave the rack on all summer if you use it frequently, but note someone can get a rack off in 3 minutes if there's no bike on it.
-For any roof rack, it may take a little strength and height to put the bike on top of a car/SUV and simultaneously align that front fork with the locking axle (built into the rack). I'm over 6 feet but my wife is 5'-6" - no way can she use this rack w/ her hybrid. Might be different w/ an ultra-light tourer and a foot stool.

title: What You Need To Know About This Tent
text:
It's always a crap shoot buying an item that you have never seen in person. Our tent arrived yesterday, fast shipping and the product is just what we ordered. So, we set it up in the yard. We plan to take this on a cross country camping adventure in the summer so it's good to have time to get acquainted with the thing before we look like idiots out on the road.

It set up fairly fast and easily being our 1st time with it. It is extremely big, as advertised. The "Front Porch" area DOES have flooring material. Some descriptions said it had no floor, that you'd be on dirt - but this one does have tent flooring attached which is great. It will hold our 3 camp cots comfortably and give us space to move our stove, etc into the porch if we get a rainy day, which was the plan when choosing this tent.

Now for the things you Need To Know:

Its big therefore it catches a LOT of wind. Even with all the windows/doors open, it still catches a boatload of wind. The stakes that come with it will NOT hold it. Invest in bigger better tent stakes and lots of them.

The screen roof is nice, get to look at the stars, but also you need to know that those do not zip shut. The only way to shut the roof screens is to put on the rain tarp that comes with the tent. That's not so easy to do and you will probably need at least 2 people - more if it's windy outside. ALSO - you cannot close the roof of the sleeping quarters while keeping the roof of the porch open. It's all or nothing with covering the roof.

Leaving the tent set up over night, the rain tarp was the first thing to blow off today when the winds moved in with approx. 20 mph gusts. The tent is not set up in a barren field, it's sitting between the house and the woods, which says that out in the open that tarp is going to fly off in a jiffy! You will need to find better ways to keep your rain tarp / sun shade tarp on. Part of that is going to be bigger better tent stakes, and maybe a few more guy-lines to give it more support.

As for waterproof, I don't know yet. We are going to saturate it with water-proofer no matter what.

The last thing you should know is that you WILL need more stakes and guy-lines to keep the tent itself up. Think of this tent as a 1 room house with a front porch. That wall between the house and the porch is held up with 2 metal poles - one on each corner there. In the wind today those keep falling over, then bouncing back upright with the wind. The whole tent is not collapsing, it's not 'that' bad, but you don't want to be in there with your walls falling in and popping back up randomly with wind gusts. If you were using your camp stove in there, the wall could very well knock the stove over, or simply fall on a flame and catch on fire. It's a big deal. So we plan to get paracord and solidify those two posts with lines coming out and staked. I might edit this review when we figure out the best way to keep the wall and rain tarp working right.

All in all, still love the purchase and can't wait to go use it in a few months for real.

title: Good value security safe
text:
I've had my safe for a couple weeks now and I am pretty happy with it. I was looking for an inexpensive safe to keep valuables away from the casual thief. This safe is not going to stop a professional thief. For that type of safe you need to pay upwards of $500. This safe is also not fire or waterproof so if you need those types of features look elsewhere.

The safe weighs about 40 pounds so it is critical to bolt it down, otherwise a thief can just walk off with it. There are 4 holes in the back of the safe and 4 holes in the bottom. There were 4 pretty hefty screws provided, I mounted my safe inside a large cabinet and it seems pretty secure. The safe and door are made of pretty heavy gauge steel so it is not going to be easy to just pry it open.

Inside the safe there are two metal shelves held in place by cheap plastic fasteners. But I will get into that later. Programming the security code was very easy and I had no problem opening and closing the safe. The safe also comes with two keys in case you forget your code or if the batteries die. There is a pretty loud beep when the buttons are pressed but that can be turned off.

I just have two minor issues with the safe. First, the cheap plastic fasteners used to hold the shelves in place are useless. When I opened the safe they were laying in the bottom of the safe with the shelves and half of them were broken. Easily resolved though, I just used metal bolts and screws I had to hold the shelves in place. I think manufacturer should provide these. The second issue I had was with the cheap shelf liners provided. They are very thin foam material and don't stay in place when sliding things in and out. Again though easily resolved by replacing with more substantial liner.

Overall I am pretty happy with this safe. I looked at others in the price range and many seemed to have significant quality issues. The issues I have with this safe are very minor and to be expected for a safe at this price point. This safe is a good value for your money as long as you are just looking to protect valuables from a casual thief

title: Great home gym equipment. 5* For Value & Functionality, 3* For build quality
text:
This calf raise machine is a great value piece of equipment for any home gym, on a budget. It's fairly comfortable, and allows you to easily do seated calf raises, and standing if you want to improvise a little bit. The big selling point is price, since many weight loaded seated calf machines are much more expensive for such a relatively simple movement. A big upside is there is pretty decent options for size adjustment to fit most people's needs.

The downsides are probably what allow the cost to be so low. While QC isn't necessarily bad, many pieces are not 'tight fitting', and need additional washers/spacers to make for a snug fit. Some pieces also needed to be manually widened so others would fit. Mechanically, this is a simplified seat calf machine, and takes several shortcuts in design that hurt QOL, such as the seat is mounted on the fulcrum, so you move as you perform the calf raise, and the handle to mount/unmount the machine from rest is on the rest-bar itself, in front of your knees, making it a little awkward to get in/out of. These are not deal breakers, but if you're used to 'gym-quality' equipment, this is does not meet the standard. However! it's so cheap that it doesn't even matter. Still get nasty calf pumps with this machine, 10/10 would buy again, as long as the price is cheap ~150$.

title: Great value!
text:
Excellent value and quality. I needed them to use on standard disposable 16.9 oz plastic water bottles. They work as intended...and I recommend. Before using I put them in the dishwasher to disinfect and then hung outside to dry. Washed up nicely!
Just want to note two things that might bug others (as other reviewers mentioned).
1. They fit right up to the height of the base of the bottle cap area. I would have preferred more clearance... But there is no issue drinking out of it... your mouth/chin do not come into contact with the cover as long as you avoid it bumping into it.
If you are concerned about that, just fold the edge down into the cover. It stays put without issue along with the handle. Actually, having the extra coverage is a good thing for folks that toss the bottle in a backpack, purse, car seat, etc. That way less condensation has a chance to drip out.
2. They are super tight to get on at first. I had a heckuva time getting them on. But you can stretch them out so they slide on and off more easily. With repeated use, they will likely just get better.

I'm very happy with the purchase....! Great deal!

title: UPDATE: Signs of wear too soon, didn't seem to keep their sticky
text:
Update, 1 Let me say customer service is a 5 Star easily, prompt, courteous, and willing to make it right. We are well into our second pair of gloves at this point (got them in AUG, now Dec), and they have held up much better. However, the sticky factor is long gone as the material doesn't seem to keep that aspect. I purchased a bottle of GloveGlu which has fixed that issue.

I have increased the review to three stars, had the initial pair of gloves been as good as the second pair this would be a 4 star review. I think it odd, that the "pattern" in these reviews is the first pair of gloves tend to be less than quality, and then the second pair meets expectations. I would suggest that whoever is "making" the gloves need to improve their quality inspection as they gloves do not seem to be meeting the owners expectations, and it can't be good for the bottom line of the company to continue to reissue new gloves and give discounts on the original purchase to make it right. We purchase a new set every year, if the product would have had the quality of the second issue, I would have bought next years set from this company; however, given the pattern of the reviews, that may not be the case.

Once again customer service was 5 star, in the end the review is about the product, customer service should have never been involved nor a second pair of gloves. That combined with the pattern of the reviews, I feel 3 star (for this experience) is justified.

A bit disappointed in the gloves, we bought on May 18th it is now July 24th and they seem to showing signs of wear already the last set of gloves didn't show for 8 months or so. They also do not seem as "sticky" as the previous pair.

With that said my 11 year old plays year round both indoor and out, uses the gloves three times a week for practice plus 1-2 games a weekend. Seems as if he is dropping more balls than he use to as they gloves don't seem to have kept their grip. So now I am stuck with either paying $15 - $30 bucks for some glove stick or applying that amount toward another pair of gloves 2 months after these were purchases.

All in all fairly disappointed in the gloves.

UPDATE: WOW! What Customer Service, within two days of this post, I heard from the owner of the company who believed the gloves could have been defective AND he sent overnight a new pair so my son would have them for his weekend games.

I am certainly eager to see how the new set of gloves wear this go around and really hope they are as good as the customer service. Will Update later.

title: For the price this bike rack is awesome. I highly advise a hitch mounted over one ...
text: For the price this bike rack is awesome. I highly advise a hitch mounted over one for your trunk in general. I have one major qualm with this rack however. The ability for this rack to tilt is a nice luxury. But I just happened to be washing my car and noticed the nut and washer on the pivoting bold at the bottom was missing. This is extremely dangerous. Had I loaded my bike or bikes up and overlooked this then headed out onto the highway I could have easily lost the entire rack with the bikes and all at 60 mph!!  IF YOU ARE GOING TO BUY ONE OF THESE RACKS. Realize you are responsible to maintain the rack and keep a close eye on such things. The manufacturer should really redesign this. It's not secure enough. There should be some sort of back up that keeps the rack attached if that one bolt fails or loses the nut. At the end of the day this is a good purchase. Will hold up for 5 plus years (if maintained) and doesn't come with the 500 dollar price tag like THULES!.. Absurd price IMO.

title: Decent bike rack, but need to know Metal Shop 101
text:
We bought the last one in stock, and wondered if there was something wrong with it. When attempting to install the rack onto a 2" hitch, noticed that the bolt didn't screw in. Learned from reading many reviews of bike racks NEVER to force it in, so took it out. Read online that the threads in the receiver may have some bits and pieces of excess metal (due to hasty manufacturing) that was causing the bolt to get stuck. Found out that this can be easily fixed if you "clean up" the threads in the receiver using a 1/2" steel drill tap (and WD-40). Bought one for $5 and screwed in the tap just like you would the bolt. The drill tap took off the excess metal. Tried the bolt next, and screwed into the receiver hole nicely.

A similar situation happened with the top of the rack: the hole for the folding arms was too small for the bolt on one side, and needed to be widened. No problem. Spent another $5 to buy a round metal file, and filed inside the hole, widening it. Problem solved.

Now many customers don't want to take the time and money to fix these minor annoyances. They want the product to be perfect and easily installed. But the product is solid, and under normal circumstances would receive 5 Stars. Because of the extra work, must give it 3 Stars.

title: Love this rack.  Here is how I "modified" it to become a cable-crossover machine.
text:
I'm extremely pleased with the product. Assembly was straightforward and all the holes lined up! Very sturdy construction.

The attached pictures show an addition I made to turn give the rack a cable-crossover functionality. These pictures represent my Version 1.0.

All the parts can be purchased at Lowes. The rack has two perfect attachment points for the pulleys. See picture 1. This shows a threaded eye bolt and 1 1/2" fixed pulley. Two lock nuts hold it in place but it is purposely NOT tight so it has the ability to rotate. Picture 2 shows a length of zinc coated square steel tubing from Lowes. Three threaded eye bolts connect the additional cables to the center cable on the rack. Picture 3 shows me pulling on the two handles.

I think this works really well. Keep in mind, this is Version 1. One could probably cut the steel tubing length down. With the full length, it doesn't seem to hit the cage but it potentially could. NOTE: I did try this without the steel tubing and I didn't like the feel. As one completes the motion, the angle change in the cables was significant enough to notice. Your mileage may vary and you may prefer that characteristic. That tubing was the most expensive piece at about $20. Everything else is dirt cheap.

If you decide to try something like this, please be EXTREMELY careful. I am a Mechanical Engineer by education so this was something I was comfortable doing. Review the load limits of ALL the components you intend to use. For instance, the two fixed pulleys from Lowes have a safe working load of 420 pounds. I used 1/8" vinyl coated braided wire rope. Blue Hawk brand with a safe working load of 340 pounds.

Make sure ANY carabiners you use to make connections are rated for HIGH LOAD and NOT for hanging keys on your belt loop. I can't stress this enough. You do NOT want something breaking on you during full extension.

IMPORTANT: Make sure you terminate the ends of the cables correctly. Properly swaged deformable collars are likely the best approach but I used a threaded clamp for this setup. I will likely change to a swaged connection because the clamping hardware can rub against your arm during use. Also, use thimbles on the ends of both cables to protect the cable attachment points.

title: Not bad so far!
text:
Originally it was shipped to me broken. The cable the measures the speed of the motor had been sheared (possibly during the final assembly). I called their customer service, but it took several tries over multiple days to reach an actual person. They shipped me the part and hired a local technician who was familiar with this treadmill to come out and fix it. Since then, its performed beautifully. I feel like the console is placed a little too far forward of the belt as my feet sometime bump into the plastic on the front. There's plenty of belt behind me, so moving back slightly when using it fixes the problem.

I've been using it pretty frequently since it was installed and so far its been working perfectly. Be sure to follow the maintenance schedule religiously. Dust and a dry belt are not your friend. Keep it clean and lubed and it should work for a long time.

title: Broken out of the box. Terrible customer service.
text:
I unpacked and installed the treadmill per the instructions, but as soon as I started it, the belt moved for a few seconds, then stopped and displayed an E1 error code on the display. I opened up the motor cover and discovered that a wire that connects the circuit board to the magnetic speed sensor had been cut/ sheared. I spliced it back together, but still got the same E1 error code.

I called their customer support number, but after 15 minutes of listening to their hold music, a recording said that they were experiencing an abnormally high call volume and that I should call back tomorrow. Then it hung up on me. I called back again and after 15 minutes got the same response and got hung up on again. I called back a third time, but now it was past their normal business hours so I will have to call back tomorrow anyway.

So now I have a very expensive piece of equipment sitting in the middle of my living room that I cant use. I'll be happy to change this review as soon as I have some kind of communication with a human being to get the problem resolved. But until then, I have to say that if I could give this less than one star I would.

title: Destined to fail, and after 4 months, replaced
text:
FINAL UPDATE - I ordered a Fitfort set, which has the same function as this package but doesn't seem destined to fail. I donated this set to Salvation Army the day Fitfort arrived. End of story.

UPDATE - After 4 months, the nylon bands on one handle failed. I'm improvising with rope earlier, the attachment to one band had to be fixed, and the black band has now torn. Was this worth four months' gym membership?

After one use, I find this adequate. I find good all-around routines, inlcuding one for straps, on darebee.

This kit provides a lot more resistance than the latex straps I'd been using. And the concept of being able to adjust your resistance by combining the five bands is good in principle. It's clear this will work better if you have good technique—slow, smooth movements, not jerky Yanks. But the small problems add up:

The concept is cool, but not unique. Post-COVID, there are a lot of these packs available, many for $10-15 less. Consider them!

Many reviews cite the handles as a weak point, and it's clear they will fail in time. They lasted fine through the first workout. (See below.)

These bands give different levels of resistance, but I'm not sure how much. There are 2 contradictory weight schemes in the Amazon posting (diff weights, diff color). Hint: blue is stronger than green. Also, I have no confidence that the numerical values are right. Is black really 40/50 pounds? Either I'm really strong...

Reviewers also reported snapped bands, and maybe it might be good to warm them up with a stretch before your workout. I believe the black and blue will snap if I stretch from from the floor to overhead, no I will have to kneel for military presses. And move smoothly thru your exercises, don't jerk or yank. It's better form, and will avoid snapping.

The Velcro ankle straps? Ha! Loop them through and they are secure!

UPDATE after 3 months: this set works, but it's not durable. One of the handles will tear, and then I'll have to re-sew it. The black band came loose from one of its hooks, and I re-fit it. The convenient carrying sack is fraying, like the ankle bands. This has been a lifeline during the lockdown that made my gym unsafe, but this is not a long-term fitness tool. It just won't last.

(CAUTION - the high rating for this set is because the reviews are mixed with what must be a very good beanie. Users of this set average 1-2 stars.)

title: Great reel, although the Alloy M is better for me
text: Works well, super fast retrieve. You can burn buzz and crank baits with ease. Honestly need a better rod to evaluate the reel better. Too heavy action rod (not enough whip) makes it more difficult to dial this reel in without backlash. I actually prefer the Alloy M over this reel. This reel is larger and holds more line, but for freshwater / bass fishing from a boat, I think the Alloy M out performs it. If you fish heavier test line for larger species, this reel would win. I have 6 different piscifun reels, from carbon x spinning, phantom, alloy m, and this one. Their higher end reels can compete with anyone. The lower priced ones are comparable to the Walmart reels in blister packs. Spend the extra few dollars for the Alloy series, it's a huge jump from the lower tier.

title: Light reel, very smooth
text: I have a few piscifun reels, couple alloy M bait casters, phantom x, etc. Very pleased with the Alloy Ms. As long as you stay with their "higher end" models, I don't think you'll be disappointed. Decided to try their spinning reel for the kid. The carbon x is very light and nicely balanced. Running the reel in my hand only (not attached to a rod) the balance is noticable compared to other/older spinning reels. This is the 2000 series though, and I'm comparing it to older and larger 3000 series reels purchased from local retailers. Can not review it on durability yet, this will be it's first season. 2nd season for the alloy m, which have become my go to rigs, 3rd season for the phantoms. The phantom/torrent combos are now my guest rods. There is that much difference in quality, between the lower/mid/upper lines. The phantoms are not bad reels, but the alloy and carbon series are just better.

title: Epic reel, until.... (update)
text:
I started with this brand using the phantom X, thought I wouldn't be out much money; if it was a flop. It was impressive for the price. Stepping up to the alloy M was amazing. The phantom X impressed me enough that I ordered 2 alloy Ms ( one in the 6/1 the other in the 7/1 ratios ). I paired them both with falcon rods and 30lb braid. I've got older curado reels on all-star rods with mono line. These alloy Ms were easy to set up, I've never cast a buzz bait so far. The other rod was rigged with a fluke swim Jr and I could easily cast it to docks and structure. I fished a whole Saturday with only those 2 combos. I picked up the phantom x on the piscifun rod, man it felt heavy compared to the other 2. But it is a medium/heavy rod compared to the falcons medium. I've got 7 bait casting rods on the boat now, but I'll mainly be fishing these Ms with the falcon rods. I might in the future step up to the top tier reel, but these Ms throw the lure further than I've ever been able to with other equipment. Great little reels, just lube them up before going out with them.

(Update)
Both of these reels became very stiff to release to cast at the beginning of this year. One doesn't trip the release upon trying to crank back in. So I guess they are good for one to two seasons

title: Good if you are not in a hurry
text: First off let me say that for the money this is a decent wood burning stove. I have used it now about 4 times and in a pinch, I am glad I have it. Positives: it works, its durable, the casing does not get super hot so you won't burn your self if you have to move it,  and it packs down small. Areas for improvement: First, I think the air flow holes/vents need to be a bit larger. After burning some wood some of the ash began to clog up the holes which did not allow good air flow. Second, (probably my biggest concern) it is difficult to keep adding fuel to this stove. Once you put the pot on top of it...it only leaves a small gap so in order to keep adding fuel you have to remove the pot for a second to add fuel so when you take the pot off the direct heat it starts to cool down. It would be nice if it had a cut out on one of the sides to be able to add wood without removing the pot. It took about 20 minutes to get a nice boil for two cups of water. So if you have time to just kick back not a big worry but if you are on the trail and want to stop for a quick lunch probably not the stove for you. Overall, I am glad I have it but probably will use it for emergencies and not so much on the trail.

The sheath is made of high quality leather and once the knife is housed in the sleeve is feels very secure. I love that it came with its own fire starter kit. I took this out backpacking and it did great in processing wood and started a fire with no problems. The only thing you really have to take into account is that it is D1 steel which means that you will need to take care of this blade. It came pretty sharp but to keep the edge you will have to work it and keep it cleaned and oiled. When not in use the company recommends you keep it out of the sheath. This is one blade that I think if you take care of it....it will take care of you for a long long time.

title: Lot of knife for the money.
text:
I recently lost my beloved old Cold Steel Recon 1... The first issue with the Axis lock. The one Benchmade threatened to sue over....
Daily carry for about 20 years. Alas... Gone.

I wanted an axis lock, but didn't particularly want to shell out the bucks for a genuine Benchmade... So after looking at a couple of YouTube reviews I bit on this Chinese product.
Very well-made, very sturdy. Quite heavy in the hand. Sharp out of the box.

2 immediate problems. The axis-lock stud is too recessed into the grip... Hard to get a hold of. And... The springs (two) are too strong.
I ground away the top portion of the grip material with a Dremel to improve access, and removed one scale (T8 Torx driver) to allow me to remove one of the tension springs.
Now... Works fine. Flips open easily and still locks securely.

Sufficiently impressed that I've sent off for one of their automatics.....

text:
When I read the description of this product I was excited but a bit worried about what kind of quality this would be. I have 3 very rough and tumble grand kids that I have recently been taking to the parks and lakes and was uncertain if it would stand up to their antics. Boy was I surprised!!

The fabic is thin making it light weight, but I found it to be very durable as well. Enough that having the kids run over it, even when advised not to, it stood up very well. It is very strong for being so thin and light weight, I have no doubt this is going to hold up fantastically on our next camping trip and beach trip.

The shipping was super fast and it arrived just as we were leaving for the lake to let the kids play on the beach and in the water. I was super stoked that when we were done, the sand and dirt feel right off, NOTHING was tracked in my car. I hate trying to get sand out of my car upolstry and carpets! But one of the best features is that because it is water proof, when we got to the car it was large enough that I could put across my seats and keep my seats dry from the kids' wet clothes. I am very happy I don't have to have that wet/damp smeel permiating my car, especially in the Texas hot sun.

Also, I should mention, unless I missed it I didsn't see where it stated it came with stakes to hold it down against the wind, so I was super excited to see that they were included! Awesome bonus! We didn't need the stakes, but will certain use them in the future on our next camping trip.

Great product, great price!! Definintely worth recommending!!

Overall I would recommend this to family and friends. It is super light weight, water proof, has many great uses, I found it to be extremely durable with having no worries about it ripping or falling apart.

title: To costly for bad construction.
text:
This is really a mixed review. I will have to break this down in to pro's and cons as I have only had this for 1 day. I will do a follow up review if there is any change.

Pros:
1. It is a nice sized and a bit bigger than I thought (if you're looking for a space saver you might want to check the size specifications.)
2. It was very easy assembly, my 4 year old grand baby and I had fun putting it together. She could line everything up and turn the screws, I just had to make sure a snugged them down for her.
3. It has plenty of space for my Computer, mouse and mouse pad plus all my other stuff I toss up there while I work. (My glass or cup of coffee, my cell phone, pen, a small pad of paper.) My son is already eyeing it for his school work as well. I got it as an extra laptop table as we already have 3 computer desks that are full of computers, printers, etc and didn't want a 4th desk, but wanted something more mobile. Which leads us to the Cons.

Cons:
1. The easy to assemble also means the construction was poorly done. It is not sturdy at all. I constantly worry if it is going to collapse or break. While the screws are reinforced with metal so as not to strip in the wood, the table can be easily wiggled to and fro.
2. The second con, is a play off the first con. The table wiggles and shakes. I would not put an open drink on the table. The wiggling and shaking as you are typing, moving the mouse or working is enough to splash your drink out of your cup. I let my son-in-law borrow it briefly. After a few minutes of trying to play a game on his laptop using this table, he wiped up more than one spill until he finally moved his drink and then found a lid for his cup. A bit later he was done as he said it was awkward to use with the table so wobbly.
3. The price is a more than should be charged for this item. Since the return fee is almost $15.00 it is almost cheaper to keep it. I probably will keep it and cross my fingers that it lasts.
4. I like having the wheels for portability, but there are 2 down sides to the wheels. First the wobbling and shaking makes it hard to roll across carpet. I feel like it is going to fall over or break. Secondly, because of the size of the wheels you cannot put it under a regular couch or char. You would need to have a couch or chair with a high lift between the floor and the bottom of the couch. At least 3-4 inches or greater. (Sorry I did not measure the casters, but they are quite large)
5. I remove the casters as I don't see us dragging it about my apartment so figured this would allow us to sit on the couch or in our recliner and use the table. The problem with this now we have to be extra careful if we slide it away from the couch or recliner to get up. There are exposed screw ends on the bottom that can easily snag or get stuck in the carpet.

Overall: To expensive for a unstable work environment. I am just hoping it will last long enough to get my monies worth.

UPDATE: 03/22/2015 Today I was working on my computer and with out warning the main portion of the table where my laptop set snapped and fell. The pipe completely busted in half. I knew overall it was unsturdy and wobbly, but I no way expected this to happen. I am returning it and will by a completely different brand.

title: Good price, great product!
text:
I purchased this less than a month ago. I read reviews on basically every treadmill out there that I could find before purchasing this one. No matter how expensive or in expensive they were I saw that none had a 5 start rating overall. After reading this description and reviews I purchased this model and I am really glad I did! I love this treadmill! I am 5'8" and weight 235 lbs. This treadmill works perfectly with no signs of stress or pressure. It has a good strong motor and the panel is excellent in helping me see how far I walked as well as my heart rate. I have not used the full work out settings yet, (there are 6), but my daughter ran through the cycle of them and they seemed to be very nice. I am working on getting to a full work out as I have a desk job that I work about 12 hours a day so never really did a home or gym work out. Now that my schedule is adjusted it is perfect! I am very happy I bought this product.

Things you should know before you purchase it:

1.It did take 2 people to put it together as adding the bars to the bottom section required someone to hold it in place, but other than that my son was able to do the rest by himself.
2. This is not a light weight machine. So moving it and the parts around you may need help until it is assembled. After that you can simply roll it to the desired location.
3. It is not "compact" or storage friendly. While you can "fold it" to get more space when not in use, you are not going to gain that much space to make a difference. The walking portion of the treadmill folds upward, but not to a straight angle, so it is still slanted, so the storage "area" is still larger than the bars that you hold on to when you walk.

Over all after reading the other reviews and such, I think I did a great job with this purchase. If anything happens over the next few months I will report back, but I don't see any potential issues with this purchase.

title: Great for the price - fits many people
text: I literally looked at every single tent that was 4 stars or higher and slept at least 8 people or more.  We are 6 in our family but we always seem to have the neighbor kid wanting to stay over or my daughter's and son's friends.  So we tend potentially need room for at least 8 but would be better to have a 12 person as it gives room for more than 3 queen size mattresses.  We actually had 4 queens and a twin mattress in there.  Kids just had to roll from one to the other while we had little station areas setup in each room for the kids to have their laptops/ipads and even a small 32 inch tv.  Yeah I know it is not real raw camping it is in our backyard but still it is fun. Strung lights up along the way. Bought some 2 way radios for all of us to communicate while the kids and my teenage son stayed out in the tent.  We even have an extra Air conditioner we may use at some point if it is too hot in the tent.  I like the fact that it does not let water in.  The way the door area zips up it has a lower lip if you will that gets pulled upwards to create sort of a ledge that stands so the water cannot leak on the ground up into the tent.  If you keep all the windows and doors zipped, there are protective sheer pieces that zip up the windows, that keeps the water out as well.  We had a pretty bad rain/wind storm about 2 weeks ago.  I looked out and saw the tent was collapsed.  Not a thing wrong with it. Wife and I went back out after it let up, popped the tent right back up.

title: Awesome power fan for its size
text: I wanted to buy a fan to put into a huge outdoor tent.  I had so many fans to look at after spot checking them that I finally narrowed it down to buying this one.  Well I did not realize it was only 4 inch blades.  I started to send it back but decided to see how well a fan like this actually works when charged.  I knew I was not going to use it in a tent or at least not for everyone since the tent is divided by little velcro screens.  I plan on buying a larger fan for the tents.  However, this fan was my perfect choice other than my mistake with the size.  I wanted a fan that could be not only be recharged but recharged via USB.  Most of the other fans I saw are rechargeable by getting rechargeable double A or triple A batteries. I don't want another device laying around the house on a table that is used just to recharge batteries for a fan. I wanted to be able to plug it into any computer, or a USB port on a docking station or use any of the two powerbanks I have.  We carry the power banks with us when we go away. I bought the tent for the back yard for the kids but I am sure we will use if we decide to travel with the tent.  My ultimate goal is to get a solar panel or panels and some how mount them near the tent so the sun can recharge our powerbanks all day. Almost forgot, I decided to keep this thing right above my monitors.  I only need it on setting 1 or 2 and I am cool.  It has 3 settings and the third one is very good.  See the photo of the light as well. It is built inside of the fan itself.

title: Garbage
text:
If you have a heart rate monitor that refuses to be accurate why use it? When I first got it, not bad, seemed to work well. All of a sudden, this thing decides to freak out, giving obviously wrong readings. Standing still it reads 30 bpm which is wrong. The next minute it reads 116, I'm still standing in place, have not moved. But wait now it's at 160. I have been on the bike for ten seconds. How is this possible?? I replaced the battery, that "fix" lasted one day I made sure the band was wet, that lasted one day. I shaved my chest, that lasted one day. I replaced the band, that lasted one day. I bought and used electrode gel, that lasted one day. I flipped the battery, as per the wahoo website, that lasted one day. Now I am pissed! I read on the internet to take the battery out overnight. That works every time. Why in the world would I have to do that every night. That tells me this is garbage! No device should have to be reset every night.
So I thought I've had this for a year, maybe that is it's expected life span. Sucks but OK. I buy the new generation HRM. Same exact problem!!!!!! BYE, BYE wahoo. You have gotten your last dollar from me. I have an 8 year old New Balance HRM that works every time I put it on and Is accurate.

title: Gym owners HATE these!!!!!
text:
I bought this 2 months ago to the day. I wanted to write a review, but I wanted to give it time for the excitement to wear off so I could give a more everyday impression of it.

My quick background as a lifter... I'm in my early 30s, been lifting since my mid 20s... only recently got my diet and routine dialed in though. Anyway, I always knew I wanted a home gym, as whether I go to a local gym near work or home I lose a good 30-40 minutes getting there and coming back. My wife likes working out but hates the gym environment as well.

Alright, enough of my life story... how is the RACK?

Assembly was pretty easy. Just get a hand drill with a 3/8" socket adapter, a 17mm socket and a 17mm wrench. I think that's all I needed. Instructions were pretty straightforward and it took about an hour. The cage itself feels pretty high quality... I can see myself using this for decades.

Using the rack itself is pretty good. I have it in a room that is 11x12' in size, with a vertical leg press machine, a plate tree and some plastic dressers. The room is definitely full, but I can move around and have enough room to either go through my routines, which are all supersets, or to be in the room with my wife while she works out without feeling like we are on top of each other.

I know what you want to know. WHAT IS THE DEAL WITH THE PULLEYS? Well I have used them 4-5x per week for the last 2 months, and so far they feel great. I tried various things to lubricate the pulley shaft... the last thing I tried was Vaseline, but I haven't touched that in weeks. Ultimately it works, though I do wish it had more sophisticated bearings for the weight holder itself. I read some reviews about the pulleys getting chewed up so I pre-emptively ordered some metal pulleys... I have not installed them yet though. The stock units are working fine so far, even when I load them up with ~170+ lbs. The unit just feels very solid.

My only gripe, and it's so minor I don't feel it's enough to take any stars off, is when I rack bench weight in the cage the unit leans back a little bit. It needs stabilizing feet in front and in the back. But that is really minor. It doesn't feel like the unit is going to fall backwards or is dangerous at all. Other thing is the weight holders are too close together. I would love more space to have the flexibility to put 45s on both levels.

So to sum up here are the pros and cons from my POV:

Pros:
- Phenomenal price
- Good build quality
- High/low pulleys work great even with heavy weight
- Quick and easy assembly
- Height gives enough clearance for chinups

text: I ordered this bike because the saddle on my used Walmart (I admit it) road bike was killing my nether regions.  I have been riding for a year now and despite the origin of my bike, I have fallen in love with the sport and I usually go out for 15-20 mile rides and just enjoy the freedom it provides.  However, this season, my saddle became so painful that the fun was turning into sort of torture-endurance.  I decided to look for a new saddle but I hear so many stories of people spending all kinds of money trying to find the "right" saddle and if my bike is any indication, I don't have hundreds of dollars to spend to go through different saddles.  Anyway, I read the reviews on this saddle and being a bigger guy (240 lbs), I decided to give it a whirl based on the cheap cost. I did notice that there would be a little pain when the bike short padding would get bunched up but after a readjustment, I was fine again.  It makes me wonder if the seat would have caused pain without the shorts.  I highly recommend buying shorts if you don't own any!  I wish I hadn't waited so long.  The padding makes a big difference.  I did notice the stickers coming off after the first ride but I don't really care about that.  I would rather have a plain seat then one with logos anyway.  I was surprised at how soft the seat was.  Some people have said that it is still a firm seat but after riding on my previous torture device, I feel that this is almost too padded.  I do feel that this is a great seat.  For the price, I figured I could give it a shot.  I'm definitely happy with the purchase!

title: Capacity Rating is Deceptive, Not well designed, some parts are not high enough quality
text:
The bracket is listed as capable of a use with a 25hp motor, up to 110 lbs. When I installed my 54 lb 4hp Yamaha the spring provided NO Lift support and the motor dropped all the way to the brackets lower limit. Lifting motor back up required excessive effort. After a single lowering and raising of the motor, the single spring had permanently stretched (without any load) about 1", providing even less lifting force. The bracket had excessive side movement due to the installation of all-thread bolts at the four bracket pivot points. The all-thread bolts would eventually damage to the bracket pivot points and the movement would increase. In doing additional research I identified other buyers of this bracket (different seller) had experienced failure of the exact same plastic motor support plate, used on my bracket, "breaking in two and the motor falling off into the water".

YAE Marine (seller) contacted the manufacturer, but were unable to get any support from them. Since I had already drilled four holes in my boat's transom matching this bracket, so I decided to fix it instead of returning.

FIX: I replaced the four all-thread pivot point bolts with 5/16" bolts that had smooth shanks and only threads at the very end (good fit). I replaced the single spring with three new springs, one 5-1/2" and two 3-1/8" (added a 1/4" bolt to existing bracket hole to attach back end of springs) side by side, below 5-1/2" spring. Lifting force is now adequate to raise motor with reasonable effort. The plastic motor plate is now reinforced with an aluminum plate and two steel mending strips bolted to the plastic plate (at the top and bottom) and trans-versing the weak point at the upper plastic plate holes used for mounting bolts (where the plastic motor plate broke in two) to the steel bracket. The attached pictures depict the new springs and reinforced plastic motor plate. New parts cost a additional $20 at Lowes, but now bracket is usable.

BUYER BEWARE! DON'T BUY THIS BRACKET UNLESS YOU ARE INSTALLING A VERY LIGHT MOTOR OR ARE PREPARED TO UP-GRADE IT AS I DID. BUY A BETTER BRACKET!

title: Great Bench
text:
To start off, I bought this because I needed a bench that could fold up and be put under a bed or in the closet. It does fold up nicely. Putting it together was extremely simple, all you have to do is attach the two bottom legs, and the roll bar. It feels comfortable to use during lifting, and I like all of the adjustments or angles that could be used. I am 6-2, and I fit perfectly fine on it.

I do have some minor issues though . First, the plastic caps on the bottoms. These caps in the front can adjust to fix any wobbles on uneven floors. This is great, and works great, especially on carpet. However, I am using this mostly outside or in the garage, and they can slide on the cement. My solution is to use a piece of nonskid (like you use in the kitchen drawers) under it. Also the front caps are not attached, so they can come off. Next, I have not figured out the roll bars to do crunches comfortably. I am sure it is just an issue of finding the right adjustment that does not put a lot of pressure on the back side of the knees. Then again I did not buy this bench specifically to do crunches.

Overall, I feel like this is a great weight bench and would recommend it.

title: Great striker - just don't forget to bring the tender or accelerant...
text:
I had a couple older magnesium stick fire starter for years and was really excited to try this out. Most people I've listened to swear by them.
Here are the PROs:
- This performs medium to well for giving you a spark. Having never used one (and probably using poor technique), I was still able to generate a decent spark at least 1 out of every 2-3 strikes.
- Doubles as a whistle. This thing actually works extremely well. If you ever need it, it's simple and high-pitched, a great space-saver.
- Feels good to use. I'd rate it at around 6 out of 10. It's a little short and I found the striker attached to the steel via the cord a little restricting, but the thumb grooves make up for it. It's funny how a small depression in plastic can make that much of a difference in comfort.

Here are the CONs:
- This requires that you have good tender or some type of fuel/accelerant. I miss having my pile of magnesium scrapings to be honest. While it's another piece of equipment, I'm probably going to keep my magnesium stick with me. It seems like the majority of times I've gone packing or camping, it's been damp out, and finding a decent amount of usable tender isn't always a sure bet.
- A little small. This is my complaint with just about any striker. They're just about a 1/4"-1/5" too small to be really comfortable. This is being picky, but still worth mentioning.

Overall, I'm enjoying using this thing and I'll probably make it a mainstay of my gear.

This, as the name suggests, is a heavy bag gloves. I bought this pair after I started having some finger and wrist pain while hitting heavy bag. I have spend about 10 hours with these now.
They are AMAZING!
When you are hitting heavy bag, you don't want your fingers and wrist to be your weakest points, and these gloves make sure of it. They are extremely comfortable and have enough padding that I don't feel the pain at all. These gloves provide that without taking away too much feedback either. So I can feel the punches I am hitting but there is not more pain, not more worrying about twisting arms or hurting fingers !!

I am absolutely happy with these. The use of heavy bag gloves is to hit as hard has you can on heavy bag and I had never been able to really push myself until I got these. Now I get tired but my hand don't hurt !

I would highly recommend these, only for heavy bags though.
Also, I would suggest another heavy bag gloves in addition https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B001FX5L4G/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o09_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1 for a more feedback based punching where you can feel the punches and correct them without hitting too hard .

title: A great everyday bike
text:
Usage : Everyday commute, weekend long trips.

This is my first bike after about 10 years. Overall I am pleased with the bike.

Cons:
- It runs on the heavier side and you can feel the weight, but I could not find anything much lighter in similar dollar range. Again it's not too heavy. I carried the bike after an accident for about 2 miles.
- Carrying the bike isn't the easiest. I wish the ergonomics allowed for that better.
- Seat could be a little softer but it's not the bike's fault. You can easily find a better seat. I have used the seat for longer rides and it gets painful after about 2 hours for me. So not bad at all.

Pros:
- The brakes are really good. They can bring you to a halt in a pretty high grade descent really fast if you need that to happen. Of course they need tuning and maintenance like anything else.
- The handlebars are very comfortable. I loved the overall handling of the bike.
- Riding it is fun. I went for a 5 hour ride. The bike maintained it's fun except the hard seat.
- Giantnerd's ready to ride made it possible to get this bike rolling out in 20 mins. Highly recommended.

Overall, I would highly recommend this bike to someone who is new, is on budget or needs a bike for daily commute and occasional long rides. So basically everyone except pros could use this bike.
