title: Not recommended for commuters who need a reliable tail-light for safety.
text:
This is a sturdy light with a metal housing and a very bright tail light. Unfortunately, road vibrations cause the light to shut off. Before I gave up on this light, I tried to keep it on by checking every 10-15 seconds on my 20-minute ride to work. I had to turn the light back on at least 20 times. So aggravating! At least the crappy $10 lights stay on!

I give it 2 stars due to Fortified's stellar customer service. I wrote them about the issue and they mailed me some rubber bumpers to help hold the battery inside the housing. The reason the light shorts out is because the battery slides loosely into a chamber with the light bulb connection at the base. Amazingly minor road vibrations break the battery-bulb connection and the light shuts off, and doesn't come back on.

Fortified has refunded my purchase, which I really appreciate. I believe there is a chance I received a defective product. I cannot say this for sure, as I was offered rubber bumpers instead of a full replacement.

Check one of these out at your local bike shop, and make sure they have a refund policy.

text: This product does not measure oxygen accurately and, therefore, can be dangerous to people with low oxygen. Over the course of a few months, I purchased three of these. I wore it to one of my doctor appointments and when my oxygen was being measured by my doctor on one of my right hand fingers, I used this wristband to measure the oxygen on my left wrist.  My doctor's oximeter read 85 and the wristband read 97.  I then wore the wristband upside-down so that the measuring beam of light would be facing the artery veins and the false measurement was the same.  This could potentially be dangerous to a person with low oxygen who believes the false measurement is accurate and then overexerts himself/herself.

title: Finished a round (3 months) of P90X with these bands...
text:
I'm going to post this review in bullet-points to make it faster to read, with a note at the end:

--I'm a male, age 23, no serious prior workout experience before starting P90X with these bands--

Pros:
- Very affordable, especially when comparing prices to weights.
- Comes with a variety of weight resistances.
- Clip on multiple bands to the handles to increase tension.
- Amazing costumer service; band breaks? They'll send you a new one--FAST AND FREE.
- They get the job done if you're using them right; great results.
- Comfy handles.
- Ankle and door straps are great bonuses, along with the carrying bag.
- Easy to travel with; lightweight and they fit anywhere.

Cons:
- Band could get in the way on some exercises.
- A little too much slack between the handles and clips on the bands; removes resistance.
- Doing some exercises with the bands could be a bit of a hassle; needing to extend your legs or arms awkwardly.

Other Notes: My experience using the bands has been limited to P90X, but considering P90X covers just about every kind of common exercise I think it's safe to say I've put these bands through a good test. I've had to get the red band replaced twice so far in 4 months. The first time I noticed a rip, and the second time the metal clasp broke off and hurt me quite bad during the 'box lifting' exercise. However, the second time was most likely my fault; I shouldn't have put THAT much tension on it. I sent them an E-mail both times and got a response the next day with my replacement bands arriving just 3 days later; the quick and kind costumer service made up for my minor injury (metal clasp shot my side and left a bruise). Overall, I'm very satisfied with my purchase and would recommend these bands to anyone looking for an affordable way to get in shape.

text: This is a nicely constructed solid steel tension rod with silicone paddings at the ends. There are two clamps at both ends to prevent the tension rods from rotating loose. What I have discovered is that the rods be placed such that the tension is adjusted in an clockwise motion when facing the rod for the Chin-up. The Chin-up action can cause the rod to move clockwise downwards even with the clamps in place and the tendency for the rods to loosen is avoided. Unfortunately though the tension increases and can cause your door frame to creak and damage. The silicone pads at the ends will also lean outwards and the only way to prevent that is by doing the Chin-up from inside the room which is highly inconvenient.

title: Works great and is 2/3 or less the price of a ...
text:
Works great and is 2/3 or less the price of a comparable Bushnell range finder. I give this 4 instead of 5 stars only because the optics are somewhat sensitive and require the unit to be precisely in front of your pupil to be able to see well. More expensive optics have a slightly more forgiving area in which the image is easily viewed.

More generally, the unit finds targets quickly and appears to generate the same distances as more expensive Bushnell finders. The Nikon may be very slightly slower than the Bushnell at locating a flag stick instead of trees behind it, but I'm talking about 2 seconds instead of 1 second... hardly enough to delay your golf round. The comparable Bushnell range finders are technically better, but can be close to double the price. This Nikon works extremely well. Potentially the biggest problem with the Nikon relative to Bushnell range finders is they are less common. You will have a more difficult time finding accessories like carrying cases and friends who borrow your range finder to shoot a distance are more likely to have to ask you questions about how it works. If you want the absolute best and finest that all your friends can use and that has a bigger selection of third party accessories, get the Bushnell. If you want to save $200 and get a very high performing range finder for yourself, this Nikon is perfect.

I've purchased a lot of different ones from other manufacturers around, and the one provided is the best of the cheaper clones that I have found. With those clones I can get occlusion quickly and easily on both upper arm and thigh placement on large (250lb +) and smaller (95lb) sized people. The windless will hold up well, its is well made and strong. The compressed gauze is a great little addition to this bag as well. The Israeli bandage is well made, vacuum packed and does not need to be opened and "staged" like some that are sewen through. The tactical pen is very heavy and a nice rollerball style refil, the glass break on the back is very sharp and appears to be tool steel or high carbon.
I added about $15 worth of add-ons to make it complete Bleed/IFAK. A pair of chest seals, additional rolled gauze, some 4x4's, some tape and an "ouch pouch" consisting of some band-aids, sting pads, loperamide and Benadryl. Even with the added items, there is still room for more in the kit if needed. I did go through and vacuum seal all of the items I added other than the ouch pouch as I do in all my IFAKs I build for spaace and to keep things clean.
I noticed that I bought these when they were deeply discounted at $24 each, and if they drop down to that price again I will be buying more.

title: DO NOT BUY THIS WATCH!
text:
This is the absolute worst training watch I have ever used and infuriates me to no end. Quick overview. I am a professional athlete, i train 6 days a week, usually twice a day. I take good care of my equipment. I rinse the watch after most workouts as directed. I do not swim with it. I do not sleep with it on. I do not wear it throughout the day. I use it for running, skiing, strength training. I am not hard on it, I do not throw it around. I have gone through 6 of these watches in less than 1 year. THEY ALMOST NEVER CONSISTENTLY SYNC VIA BLUETOOTH OR COMPUTER CABLE. I have a new iPhone 6S, and Macbook Pro. No issues with them at all, ever, except for f***ing syncing this watch.
Do not waste your money. The timer works great, the hr is great, the gps is great, the modes are awesome, the morning orthostatic test is awesome, I love everything about this watch. But the fact that it fails 19 times out of 20 tries whenever I try to sync it makes it utterly useless. I f***ing hate using this watch. Buy a Suunto or a Garmin. Just do it. Do not waste your money on this. You will get frustrated, you will get infuriated. I keep sending this watch back to be "fixed". Sometimes they try and fix it, other times I get a brand new watch in plastic. Literally. And then a week later it stops syncing.
Buy a Suunto or a Garmin. The syncing feature and flowsync software for this watch is awful and years behind the competitors. I bought a Garmin for back up and much prefer using it. My garmin (forerunner 610 used from ebay) never has an issue and syncs in about 10 seconds. It takes 5 minutes for the polar v800 to sync and it fails 19 times out of 20. Such a waste of time, especially if you're busy and spending 45 minutes of your evening swearing at your stupid polar watch that won't upload your workouts to your computer or phone.
DO NOT BUY THIS WATCH, WASTE OF MONEY, FOR THIS MONEY BUY A SUUNTO OR GARMIN!
You have been warned. If you buy this and end up pissed off waiting for the thing to work, then you'll remember reading this and knowing it was a waste of money.

title: A MUST HAVE for my high hamstring tendinopathy
text:
In 2018 I was diagnosed with high hamstring (or proximal hamstring) tendinopathy. My leg ached and cramped when sitting for any period of time, and the sit bone area where the tendon attaches got aggravated and sore. This disc on my office chair allowed me to sit more comfortably, and with the work I did in physical therapy, its support allowed me to heal and fully recover from this injury.

Today my almost four year old disc split a little on one side and the air came out. This was after someone else sat in my chair, plus I've been using it to rehab a foot injury, balancing on it on the floor. I am buying a new one right away! I may not need it for the original intention, but it does help provide additional cushion when sitting for long periods.

title: Won't sync on Android or Apple
text:
9/15/21: I've worn the Fitbit Alta HR for about 4 years but the battery won't hold much of a charge anymore, so I ordered the Luxe. The band is extremely comfortable and I love being able to customize the clock face. I prefer slim watches, and this is a very nice device! BUT...I cannot get the device to sync to the app on Android (11) or Apple (latest iPad iOS). I have to reset the Fitbit by pressing the button on the cord three times to sync, so I'm only getting my data about once a week now. I am glad to modify my review if a future update fixes the issue, but to me, not being able to get my information at least once daily via the app is a huge downside. I may go back to the Alta, even if I'm having to charge it constantly.

I did notice that if location services are "on" and I don't go out of range of the iPad, it stays connected, but as soon as I walk away from it too far I have to reconnect with the Fitbit reset button. On Android, I haven't found any pattern to keep it connected.

title: Upgraded for the heart rate option, but hate the band
text:
I had just purchased the previous version of the Fitbit Alta but due to some health issues I need to track my heart rate, so I purchased this on release. I had read that the resting heart rate is pretty accurate, and it recently helped me know I needed a medication change due to a marked difference in HR.

What I didn't know when I got it was that having this heart rate feature allows the device to record different stages of sleep: deep sleep, light sleep, REM and awake time. I'm addicted to seeing this daily!

My one complaint is the band. Even the smallest segment of the band seems to catch on everything. I like the previous snap band version much better.

I researched tons of gloves but thanks to one particular reviewer I decided to give these a try.  I am so glad I did.  The padding is excellent.  The wrist wraps also provide excellent protection. I'm returning these and purchasing a safer model, costs about $5 more.

title: Great for many applications besides just a headset - invaluable tool for a great price
text:
I don't know what brute strength these people giving it such a poor review are using. Maybe they have gorilla strength? I'm only 5'8" 180 lbs and while I'd like to think I'm not a total weakling, I'm not Superman, either.

I've gotten into rebuilding old 80's BMX bicycles in the last year (6 of them total) and this tool has been great for installing headsets, tightening bottom brackets, and even holding detanglers in place. While not available currently on Amazon, I think I paid like $6 for it. Expecting very little, but for the 10-12 times I've used it, was a Godsend.

I think I even caught myself using it to loosen a axle nut on my truck, when I didn't have a wrench large enough. Couple taps with a rubber mallet and it worked wonderfully.

Headsets and bottom brackets should be finger tight, then a 1/4 to 1/2 turn with a wrench most of the time. A light touch. If you're torquing them down, you'll likely crush the bearings. Or at least restrict their movement.

This wrench - for the price - works great for my needs. Would definitely buy again.

After reading through some of the reviews, I wasn't sure it was going to fit my bike. So, let me set the record straight:

If you are replacing a gyro, or building a 80's-90's BMX/freestyle bike with a threaded 1" fork, then THIS IS FOR YOU! If you aren't hung up on brands, or labels or being era-perfect on your rebuild, I can't imagine a better solution for the price. It comes with EVERYTHING you need (top and lower rotor plates, the actual rotor itself, and the cables.

And while I can't be exactly sure it comes with every order, mine came with brake cables for the front AND rear brakes, so you can replace all your cables at once if you run f/r brakes. Honestly, I was surprised at what I got, and the quality, for the price. For what most companies charge for just the cable, you can replace the entire thing.

I do wish the actual metal parts came in colors, besides black and silver, but for the price its hard to complain. Will definitely be ordering again!

This is my fifth and favorite headlamp. I really like the single battery design. It's lightweight and doesn't bounce while running. The lamp body tilts on a ratchet so you can pick a beam location on the ground and it will stay there. I wear mine under my hat. Worn for 2.5 hour runs and it's still comfortable. The switching sequence is simple and intuitive: simple on/off for the most often used beam, with the ability to toggle through for options if desired.

On the sailboat, the red lamp option is great for night watch or rustling about the cabin in the dark while preserving night vision acuity. And the fact that it's waterproof is great for winter running in Oregon. I'm quite happy with mine.

title: Happily Hydrated Pups and Owner All Summer Long
text:
UPDATE: I've been using this pack for two full years now and it's still holding up great. I've gone through and made a few edits and filled in updates where applicable.

This has been my best purchase ever. I have been using this lightweight, high volume capacity, hydration backpack daily on my dog walks. There has been more than enough water for my old Labrador who thinks he is a puppy, my puppy who thinks she is a fish and for me who is constantly thirsty and makes sure I stay hydrated.

The tall zip enclosure is just the right size to fit my 11" compact umbrella, which has come in handy on many occasions. The lower pocket holds my cell phone and if I want to carry a wallet and keys as well. There is another mesh pocket on the strap which holds my poop bags and could hold my keys, but I've added a carabiner clip to the hook on the shoulder which I clip my keys to.

The straps cinch down to fit me perfectly, and are neatly folded and tucked back into themselves so they don't dangle in my way. I don't often use the clip which goes across my as I don't like anything to feel constricting across my chest. But I have used it occasionally, such as over a heavy coat, and it is great at making the pack feel even more snug and secure. I would have rather had that strap across my diaphragm, but that's just a personal preference.

I love that the height of the mouthpiece can be adjusted up and down along the straps.

I haven't had any issues with leaking, dripping and it's easy to use the no-drip lid.

UPDATE: I DID have an issue with leaking along the lid once for a short while. I fixed the issue by re-adjusting and straightening the black O-ring around the edge. Everything is back to perfect once again after I did that.

I also haven't had any issues with any sort of odor or taste from my filtration pack. I am pretty sensitive to strange smells and tastes, so I definitely would have noticed anything odd.

UPDATE: I did notice the inside of my bladder had a bit of a sheen to it, there was a good bit of green algae inside of the hose and lots of black specs of mold inside of the mouthpiece. I attempted to clean everything out using first denture tablets, then mouthwash and finally I targeted the mouthpiece with a concentration of water and bleach since I was unable to eliminate all of the mildew/mold from it. Even after soaking overnight in the bleach and scrubbing and scrubbing I still couldn't get rid of the issue. I've never put anything other than water in my Camelbak. I did have to remove the hose and create a brush out of pipe cleaners in order to remove the algae from the hose. Unfortunately, once I removed the hose and then reassembled the mouthpiece I now have a leak at the mouthpiece. So I guess I need to cut the end of the hose to ensure a tight connection again. And everything smells minty from the mouthwash and dental cleaner. I think I'll be buying a new bladder and will be sure to get a quick-link connection for the hose at both ends.

My dogs and I have been well hydrated all Summer despite the heat and humidity. They love drinking from the stream of water.

UPDATE: I've started carrying my Camelbak all year round as my dog reached his Senior years and is much more sensitive to temperature and dehydration. I've also started carrying a collapsible bowl with me and will fill the bowl for him to drink out of it instead of using the straw. It's made a huge difference and I can see how he will go from having a difficult time walking to having renewed energy to keep going. Like a wilted flower being brought back to life almost. If other people could see the effects, even on a moderately cool day, I think many more people would be wearing hydration packs while walking their dogs. I WISH they would!!!

I wish Camelbak would make a pack which either has a pouch on the side perfect for slipping an umbrella inside for people who hike/walk, or is tall enough to fit one inside. This one is just perfect if I can find the right umbrella that's small enough to fit. But the new version has been revised and I don't know if it still is able to fit an umbrella, which is crucial to me.

title: It's decent. 4/5 for normal folks. Personally 3/5 for me.
text:
So like a good many people, being stuck at home with the parks closed, limited space, and etc, I looked into a bike to use during periods of extended stay at home.

I looked into many bikes on amazon within my budget, and this one (originally the previous version) was the one that caught my eye.

For build quality, if I were to rate this out of 5...it would get a 3. I say this because during the build, the quality of the parts didn’t feel like how all of the reviews made it seem to be. My father helped me out during the build, and commented and the bare minimum level quality of the tools you get and etc. That’s really what makes the build a minor issue. You would think that you could go firm when screwing things in, but trying to do that, it makes you feel like you’re going to break the bike piece! A comment my father made rings a bit true. “They don’t build these things to be put together by people who know parts or tools. They just dumb it down for people who have never touched a tool!” That’s my quick quip about the building process. Parts seem good. Your tools are bare minimum level quality and don’t go too firm or hard when screwing things in. It's sturdy, but I would not put all of your weight on one point of it. For example, don't lean all the way forward, or put all your weight to one particular side!

Using the bike, I would say things are a 3.5 or 4 out of 5. Look, you’re not going to get the same workout you would comparing this product to a bike you would use at the gym or one of those $500-$700 bikes. These bikes are more for being “active” versus training or working out. It’s better than doing nothing at all. If you think that you’re buying this bike to train or workout, it’s the wrong product for you! Resistance levels feel good, and gives a decent warmth to the muscles after some time. But I would not risk trying to do HIIT training too often on this bike. MAYBE 2-3 times a week at most. The seat cushion could be better. For something so wide or large, you're not actually using the whole seat when you're using the bike and prolonged use of the bike will cause discomfort below. Maybe you get used to it, or more cushion to where you personally need it most!

Overall, I would say this product is good for BEGINNERS or those who feel intimidation, shyness, or some kind of adverse feeling towards going to the gym or being out in public. Or, like in recent situations at the time of this review, you’re stuck at home! This bike is a “better than nothing” solution (one of many). This can definitely compliment a healthy diet and lifestyle, but don’t expect this to be the sole way to workout and lose weight. They say, abs are made in the kitchen and that’s 1000% true. Burn like 100-200+ calories using this bike and use that to compliment you eating less each day (250 to 500 calories a day less!) You will lose weight that way if you’re looking to lose weight.

I will revise this review if, over time, the parts break quickly or if there’s something that’s worth mentioning. Or if this gives some results after a good 2-3 months of use! For now, this product gets a decent 4/5, for those who are new to exercising (note I don't say working out and training). 3/5 for those who are used to the gym or are more experienced!

title: Ah-freakin-mazing.
text:
CONTEXT:
After watching a documentary about teflon and plastic etcetera, and learning that all similar products leech into the water, I opted to start using glass. After using a Hydro, I was a little bit bummed that my water wouldn't be cold AF for hours on end, but I figured it was worth the sacrifice. I have smaller glass bottles, but with as much as I workout, I needed a way to track and increase my intake. I found this one and immediately needed it because of its size!

PROS:
- The neoprene sleeve it comes with actually does a pretty good job of keeping the water cold AND helps with keeping the condensation at bay. It never gets soaking wet.
- It holds so much water! One bottle of this a day is one 1.4 liters.
- Water just tastes so much better. I don't care what anyone says... water tastes better out of glass.
- The handle addition on the neoprene is a huge plus! It helps with lugging this thing around.

CONS:
- This isn't really a con for me, BUT I know it will be for others. The water doesn't stay cold for hours... I live in Hawaiʻi, so naturally, it gets warm pretty quick (but keep reading for tips). If you live somewhere cold, like Washington, I don't think you'll really have a problem. :)
- Obviously, this bottle is pretty freakin large. So carrying it around can be a b-word.

TIPS:
- I learned that putting ice in my bottle helps a lot with keeping it cold throughout the day (not even kidding). I usually fill the bottle with 1/4 ice and the rest with filtered water. By the time I am getting to the bottom of my bottle, the ice has melted, but the water is still cold.

OVERALL:
I can't recommend this bottle enough. It is perfect for me!

- As easy as it is to set up, it's the same amount of ease to breakdown.
- It's very sturdy! We've had cheap Walmart cots before and this is not that. You don't feel like you're gonna fall through, or like it's going to break!

CONS

title: Gorgeous & functional!
text: After watching a documentary about plastic, I was immediately drawn to the idea of glass water bottles. I kept finding the small ones, but after a little digging came upon this one and fell in love. Especially with the bamboo lid which is more sustainable than regular wood, I knew I had to get it. I live in Hawaiʻi and it is HOTTT during August and September, so when I filled this bottle a 1/4" of ice and the rest with water (from the refrigerator) I was a little bummed to see the ice melt so fast. I knew it was something I would have to expect with glass (versus a Hydroflask), so I shrugged it off. My parents and I went shopping at the mall and I left the bottle in the car. I have an all-black interior so it gets HOTTT. When I came back, I figured the water would be hot too! And while it wasn't cold, it was surprisingly cool and not even a lick of hot! Stood the test of Hawaiʻi heat for me, so I give this bottle five stars!

title: Amazing Grip, Better isolation.
text:
I bought mine off their personal website at dynepic-sports.com

I've lost use of 2 fingers on my left hand pretty much, so being able to squeeze the grips with a rope attachment has been so vital. I honestly had given up on the basic conventional tricep ropes cause my wrist wrap straps with grips couldn't even allow me to hold the rope well.

This tricep rope attachment is just flat out better. I felt my triceps pump and work itself like I had 2 hands again. I can't tell you how elating it is for me, it's pretty emotional LoL, this simple equipment has felt like it's given me back part of my old self when I had 2 hands. But only when I use this Tricep rope <3

Now I can do face pulls again, tricep pull downs, rope pull downs for back, bicep curl rope pulls, shoulders etc. I could go on with it.

Krissa was a big help too, came clutch with the shipping modification.

title: I liked it, wanted to love it. Tip already Broke
text:

It was a good blade, it stayed together even when dropping it. It didn't loosen or open on it's own. When it locks, it's a safe blade, never worried about it slipping.

I just wish the blade part was stronger. Just use it as a box cutter, not for food cutting or butchering around bones/joints. I work as a meat cutter/butcher and used this for multiple things.
For $50 almost, I can't justify it. Is worth $30 at most. I think you're paying extra for the carbon fiber look to it, nothing special about it.
It is a nice blade though, overall I just wouldn't buy it again. Might try a different one from CJRB but I couldn't even find a website online to contact customer service about a warranty considering it was 2 months I had this thing.

title: Good product and some suggestions
text:
This is my first use of a trap -- used for cats in NE suburban backyard. Pretty good product: caught 5 cats, 2 possums and 1 raccoon in a couple of months over this winter. There were 3 escapees.
Some suggestions:
The trap I received was an entirely wire grid device. Older photos show a solid sheet metal closing door.
Several of the clips from critical places had not been installed and were rattling about in the box. In particular, one of two clips that holds the
trap door to the roof of the trap had to be installed or substituted for with wire. These clips are not the sturdiest. One escapee pulled one loose.
I found that it took some practice to set the trap to have a just so sensitivity, and a little bending of the spring catch. It's not complicated, but plan on practicing. Furthermore, desperate animals will dig up enough soil to cover many important joints, so there is need for cleaning and oiling to keep the mechanism working properly. Snow or soil underneath the trap lever will prevent closure.
I also found that the rear door closure with a large clip and a metal rod is not adequate. A small, determined animal can escape. I simply added a piece of telephone wire to hold the rear door to the roof of the trap securely.

It definitely was nice to not have a metal bottle going through security and on flights, but if you're in and out of a car you'll miss being able to use the cup holder, and the ease of drinking from the bottle. This wasn't that bad for drinking, but the whole act of opening and holding definitely was a two handed affair. I suppose my wife appreciated that it was "soft" in her purse vs rigid and hard to store, but that's probably quite purse dependent.

title: Works, but imo only if you're all the way forward on the handles
text: Inexpensive and easy to put together. Seems like decent quality. Only reservations are that it wobbles if my hands are any further back than 1" from the front of the handle pad - not off the front of the pad so there is more room to move forward if you feel like you need it. If you tried to do a dip only grabbing the end I bet you'd come crashing down. 180lbs btw, well within the spec of this thing. Also, slow and steady would be advised due to the rocking around...a longer base would make me more confident.

title: When in doubt, swap it out!
text: Bought a very cherry ~20yr old road bike with Ultegra all around.  Rode it around for a bit and everything, surprisingly, was working perfectly (3x9 shifting perfectly!) - or so I thought.  After riding it for 1/2 a summer (incl. a trip up and down Vail pass) I figured I'd start to think about any deferred maintenance that the bike needed.  I noticed the brake pads were a little thin so why not replace them.  After the quick install and brake tension adjustment I am amazed at how nice braking feels now.  There actually is some feel that I didn't know I was missing, not to mention grip!  Feel kind of dumb not doing it sooner and really wonder how much more enjoyable a Vail pass descent might be w/ these vs 20y/o rubber.  Guess I need to ride it again. 😛

title: Probably way more bits than you need
text: Nice kit that seems to have all that you need and more.  Really the only think missing for you to perform a brake bleed is some allen wrenches.  It would be nice if there were labels on the bits to tell you which fits with what brand etc. as with trial and error you could screw up the threads on these little plastic bits.  Tubing could be more flexible but this was cheap so what do you expect.

title: I might be wearing almost as much water as I'm drinking
text: I can't decide if I need to tighten it more or less, but when I squeeze it dribbles out under the lid constantly.  The stream is actually quite harsh as well and I found myself choking a bit and having to learn how to drink from this.  Even putting it to my lips the thing leaks.

title: Hard to buy a hat online
text: Love the colors and design, turns out it wears like a train conductor's hat which is not my style.  Would look good if you've got a very large and round head (not oval) and like to do the flat bill thing.

title: A little cheaper than other options, working perfectly
text: Good value here imo.  Purple matches my wife's bike so she's happy.  No issues, just as good as the stans brand.

title: Handy for occasional use
text: I wish I had bought one sooner, but after using quite a bit to true a fairly out of whack MTB wheel, I wish I had bought a more purpose built size vs a multi-size tool - I feel like the grooves are getting worn and starting to round the spoke nuts.  Live and learn...if you're a pro or intending to do this sort of thing a lot I'd get a set of dedicated wrenches.

title: Really thick
text: These have a lot more padding than you'd think, like double sided foam tape thick.  They stick well, and I have confidence they will protect from rub wear, but due to the thickness it might be hard to use in certain areas due to its reluctance to bend.

title: Flawed
text:
I have other Mazama water bladders, and really wanted to like this. I bought it for a trip to the national parks in UT where you should be carrying more water. The good is that its a big reservoir, and the hose is thicker so the rate of flow is higher than their other hoses. What I love about Mazama is the magnetic holder for the hose, and this one is even better because there is some play in it where as the normal version can pop off at times (I generally wear it while mountain biking and its fine, but if there isn't enough slack in the hose it will pop off the magnet).

What I don't like about this one...the closure for the bladder is not secure. I found out by dumping about two liters of water over me when it was in my backpack and I bent forward. I know it looks like it should work, but because its plastic and malleable there is play there and its not perfect. The "lock" wiggles even without pressure, so its suspect to begin with. The way it opens is nice for cleaning, drying, and filling, and the "spine" is helpful for carrying and moving it around. These features cannot make up for the closure however, and I worry about it whenever the bladder is full. I'm also not a fan of the way the bite valve works...it can be left full open and water will just run out, or you can get it to work if you bite a little...but just a little because if you bit too much the rubber tip falls off. Squirely bugger.

When using in the future I might add a clamp or something to ensure the closure can't slip off, and will use my other hose vs this one.

title: Not perfect but they work
text: Nine out of ten places I put these are working just fine.  One stubborn area is too tight of a bend for the sticker, and because its stiff its wanting to peel off/refusing to conform to the shape of the bike.  I suppose I could accomplish the task with a couple of smaller stickers but thats not very efficient.  All the others have stuck well, survived bike cleanings and maintenance, and protected the frame from scratches and wear.  We'll see how easy they are to remove if I ever decide to do so, but can't imagine some goo-gone wouldn't get it if it was difficult.

title: It works
text:
After a good cleaning and re-lubricating with this the drive train feels new. Most of my riding is in dry dusty conditions so I like how it doesn't attract dirt like a wet lube would.

Only complaint is how the tip works...when you're on a fresh bottle the lube comes out quick and things can get messy fast - I also imagine a fair amount of waste. When you get to the bottom of the bottle, gravity no longer helps and you have to squeeze to get the lube out, which presents a whole new set of challenges. I might try to poke an air hold in the side somewhere to allow it to work a bit better. I'm also not sure you can truly get the bottom bit of lube out of the bottle without removing the nozzle.

title: ehhhh
text:
Thats how I feel about it...ehhh. It was cheap so thats the risk I take. The brushes are fine, and don't seem like they're going to fall apart. The bristles are stiff enough without being too stiff. The sponge is pretty unnecessary imo because who doesn't have a rag or old dish sponge they used for cleaning their bike anyway. And the scouring pad is aggressive.

The chain cleaner is the main reason I bought this, and its just ok. Its a bit of a pain to use and keep all the gears in order. The handle locks the top and bottom together, so you have to disassemble to put your chain in it. The gears kinda fit together, and you can see what the goal was, but its hard to keep them all straight and I'm not sure the brushes do much anyway. The fluid volume is low, and there are two little holes on top to add more but its hard to do. When using it water definitely gets pulled out with the chain so you'll have to refill at least once. I'm not sure it cleans super well either, but I try to stay on top of cleaning so maybe I'm not giving it a fair shake. I think in order for it to work really well it needs a ton of degreaser/soap, and a few refills to clean one chain.

title: You can spend a lot more for no reason
text: I'm not saying this was cheap, but I'm certainly not complaining.  Well built, solid aluminum, easy to install, low profile.  Been riding it for a few weeks with no issues.

Also, depending on how tightly you secure it, the bell might be much louder or quieter.  In general its on the quiet side.  Was the cheapest option but its pretty incognito which is what drew my attention.  I don't think I'd buy it again.

text: Like the visor and MTB style.  Its light, the MIPs helps secure a comfy fit, and it was inexpensive!  Only drawback is that the chin strap adjusts only one way...you can't play with how forward or back it is, simply how tight it is.  As with most helmets you can get used to it, but it can be annoying.

title: A bit heavy but its got all the goodies
text: If you can't find what you need here you probably should carry a toolbox with you and full size bike (and other) tools.  Not sure what else you could really need tool wise while out on a ride.

title: Grippy
text: Huge upgrade from stock, although quite heavy.  Doesn't bother me as I'll gladly trade weight for grip and durability.  I expect these to last some time with how tough they seem.  Running tubeless, no issues installing.  I almost always wish quality things were cheaper, but you usually get what you pay for and with these I have no regrets.

title: Feel bomb proof
text: Upgraded from stock and along with the rear version of this I think my bike gained 4lbs.  I'm not concerned about that however as these feel way more durable though time will tell.  They're really grippy too, which is very confidence inspiring - lots of loose gravel hitting my frame & fender now vs before.  Running tubeless and installing was simple with no issues.  I feel like I'm on a motocross bike now with these beefy, knobby, grippy tires.

text: I needed an upgrade to the cheap weight bench I previously had.  This one lacks a foot hold so when doing decline bench you can slide a bit - proper form and notching your butt in the gap between the seat and back helps.  The pads don't line up perfectly and I hope that over time this doesn't lead to it loosening or getting wobbly.  It is heavy duty however.  As others have said, no idea how you'd break this unless you were abusing it.  I wish the decline were a bit more declined, but otherwise there are plenty of adjustments.

title: It works
text:
In case you were skeptical of it actually locking up your bike...if you're using a through bolt it will work. It grips the bolt well and you can't turn it by hand - perhaps w/ some pliers or a pipe or something.

If you need the adapter to use with a skewer it won't lock your bike.

I wouldn't trust any form of lock on a bike locked to my roof rack over night or for hours out of sight, but its good enough for me if I'm stepping away for lunch or just using for transporting.

text: Heated my wheel up with a heat gun, then put the tape on. It's not easy to work with, but it stuck and while it didn't stretch I haven't had any problems.

text: First was smaller but I needed a bigger one for longer days. Even though the plastic clip at the top ripped off immediately (no way it holds the weight of the bag and water), I love the noted valve, connection, and most importantly the magnet.

text: Got this so when I put my bike in the car I don't also leave a trail of dirt, and it works.  The elastic is just big enough to fit my large frame 29er mountain bike. I'm happy with it and it seems durable enough to last a while - the elastic is actually pretty good quality and I don't expect that it will wear out and lose shape....but I'm not storing my bike in this so its only stretched when I use it.

title: A worthwhile investment
text:
You keep your $200+ goggles in their case off the mountain....so why not do the same on it? When you take that lunch break or perhaps apres, are you really paying attention to where your helmet and goggles might roll off to? Are other people in the lodge (bar) paying attention to what they're bumping into or kicking around on the floor? No....the answer is no.

Spend a few bucks, put this lightweight, packable, soft cover in your pocket, use it as an emergency handkerchief if you need to, but when you're taking a break slip these over your $150 lenses and focus on where you are...nothing will stress you out or annoy you more than a careless scratch staring you right in the face every time you gear up or try to take in the bluebird powder day

title: Ratchet straps still have their place
text: I love ratchet straps.  I use them for everything.  However, they're sometimes a pain to deal with and you feel silly spending 5 min strapping down a large feather (or more likely sheet of foam) to your roof rack w/ something so aggressive.  That's why I got these, for those quicker tasks (securing a propane tank in your truck bed for example) where a ratchet strap is overkill and more work.  While ratchet straps come with hooks, this comes with A hook.  So you have to figure out how you're going to attach the other side of the line.  Once you come up with your strategy it'll be quicker to use, but for the first time it might take some thought/effort.  We used two of them most recently to attach a semi inflated 10' paddleboard to the car and drove 50mph with no issues.  Another plus is that they take up much less space than ratchet straps

Its big.  Really big, almost comically.  Doesn't matter, I can still catch a softball.  Its not leather through and through and its not trying to be.  That makes it lighter and more breathable, but we'll see how that impacts durability.

title: its a beast!
text:
Got this on prime day after a friend had been doing tons of research and was going to buy two of these, I figured for $280 I could take a chance as well. Before taking it out I pumped it up to check it out and its a monster. It is thick....really thick. If you're only experienced with fiberglass surfboards or SUP boards you'll be surprise how thick this is when you pump it up. I think its even thicker than a lot of inflatable boards, but I honestly haven't studied many up close or taken a tape measure to them, so who knows. Anyway, just for giggles I put one end on the couch and the other on a chair, with the middle totally unsupported, and got on. It held my 180lbs only bending an inch or two which impressed me. It left me wondering why we didn't buy one or two of these sooner.

So I finally was able to take it out on the lake and it took me about 5min to pump it up - I was going fast and wanted to push myself. I forgot to put the bigger fin in, and the wind was a constant 5-10mph with gusts to 25mph. Without that fin I definitely had tracking issues and could only get 2-3 strokes per side before I was turning one way or the other. I can't say for sure, but really think it would've been much easier if I had put that fin in....oh well. Its pretty light, the D rings are pretty strong, and I'm super confident it can hold a ton of weight (my friend put himself, his wife, and his kid on it in calm waters and had no issues).

A couple of concerns:
its a little bigger than it needs to be,
it didn't come with the patch glue, just the patch,
in time I could see abrasions from parking lots, sand, rocks, branches/logs, etc. breaking it down quickly (and any other inflatable),
and I already have a little ding in it. I'm not sure how it happened because I don't remember hitting any rocks and don't think its from the parking lot or sand, but so far it isn't impacting its ability to hold air.

In the future I wouldn't hesitate to buy another one of these, but might look for one thats smaller and less bulky.

title: Great clasp
text: I bought this helmet for my semi-casual bike rides to work and for when I ride my electric skateboard around.  Its a helmet so it'll work in any situation, but won't look out of place unless you're doing some serious cycling (it probably would look fine on the ski hill too).  The straps are leather and aren't as adjustable as a real sports helmet, but for casual use its fine.  The way the straps clasp together is wonderful....just get the two sides close and a magnet pulls them together and locks them into place (the magnet doesn't hold them together, it simply helps connect the attachments).  Taking the clasp apart is just as easy - way better than ski and cycling helmets.  The lock hole is a nice idea but if you don't have a lock set up that is compatible its useless.  It was pricey but if you care about style than you probably don't mind.

title: Feel Safer Riding With This Horn, Gets You Noticed (In A Good Way)
text:
I'm a regular and responsible bike commuter. That means following traffic laws, obeying stoplights & stop signs, signaling before changing lanes or turning and working very hard to ride visibly and give vehicles lots of time/space to see and react to me. That being said, there are distracted (or simply bad) drivers that are either not aware of their surroundings, traffic laws related to vehicle/cycle interactions or both.

This horn gotten the attention of several vehicles (including a city bus) that were not otherwise paying attention to the cyclist (read: Me) that they were literally about to run over, pull in front of, open their door into, etc. It's *really freaking loud* (DON'T try it out in your house!!), and only once out of a dozen or more situations has it failed to get someone's attention. In that particular case an SUV pulled right into the bike path and stopped directly in front of me, despite my clear right of way, and I almost t-boned her at 18mph. She had her windows up, music blaring and was on the phone. (Unrelated to this review, I hope she gets a wart on her face. I'm a bad person.)

title: Just sort of odd choices
text:
I am not a fan. The construction is simple, 6 total screws, 3 screws per leg. will take anyone, literally, a minute to assemble. Wood looks nice. Construction is sturdy and well made.

My problem:

It doesn't fit my skateboard. It seems to be the wheels. I have larger than I guess the average wheels. nothing ridiculous, a friend told me to get a bit larger diameter to assist in running over cracks/rocks and such while learning. so they have a larger diameter that what the most vanilla build would be. It created a tight fit. I had to really push into it a bit to get the skateboard on there. I could tell the larger size of wheels made the fit tighter. So that's a con, only works with specifically medium to small wheels. Or, perhaps trucks a bit longer. Either way, it requires a level of specificity I don't feel like looking in to.
Edit: Another reviewer mentioned low trucks. I suppose that could also be a cause. To reiterate, the trucks and wheels I am using are right off the shelf at a Zumiez. Standard, vanilla built skateboard, and this thing does not fit it.

I don't understand why the lean. In order to see the graphics of the skateboard, you have to face the stand backwards. So instead of looking at the solid wood design, you are looking at the legs and screws on the backside. Otherwise, you will be looking at the grip tape.

And the lean itself, while not extreme, why? There are less than 10 dollar plastic options that work well enough, and keep the board upright. So with the cheap plastic ones, not only is the board upright, it isn't reliant on trucks/wheel dimensions, and faces the graphics to be visible on display. For a product that is made of better material, I would have expected to be able to do that. The lean is just too awkward for my OCD.

I opted for the cheap 8 dollar plastic solution. Works well enough, board is upright, cool graphic showing, right in the corner of the room.

title: TRX3500 Folding Treadmill
text:
First off, I am 58 yrs old, 6'5, and weigh 300 lbs. This machine, in packaging, is very heavy. 250 lbs, long and difficult to get moved around, especially around corners or up stairs. Make sure you have help.

The set-up to assemble the machine, un-package it, clear the area, lay everything out, make sure tools and power access are all ready, took about an hour.

The machine has the minimum tools required to assemble it, all the parts were there and in good condition. The machine was undamaged, the packaging is excellent and protected the unit very well.

The actual assembly was VERY easy, the assembly instructions were clear and correct. Assembly took 45 minutes.

**The one problem we have had is: If the machine is plugged in and the power switch is on, but the key is not inserted (in E0 displayed mode) it trips the circuit breaker in our home panel. The 15 amp circuit breaker on the unit does not prevent this.

We just make sure the unit is powered OFF when not in use as per the instructions. However, this didn't happen with our other Treadmill.**

Regardless of this one issue we have noted thus far, this is a great product, and I recommend it. I have about 12 miles on it this week. It is smooth, stable, quiet, durable, and we really like it. The display is easy to see, and the layout is user friendly.

The price was a bit on the higher side, but the value for that price is worth it. If we have any real negative issues in the next few months of use, I will update as needed.

This is a very good product, and the company did a great job designing and manufacturing it.

title: Nice job on this one husband (maybe he'll see this?)
text: This is perhaps my husband's only purchase ever that he has made on behalf of our child. I had zero involvement and I was happy to let go of one of "my chores". I approved of the fact that he did his research. Research for me involves countless hours weighing options on the internet, reading reviews, analyzing cost, looking for coupons or discounts, and finally leaving it and a few other finalists to sit in cart limbo for a week or more while I wait for the clear choice to present itself to me in a dream. Research for him involved eyeing a few samples he liked on the beach, talking to the owners about their thoughts, taking a few pictures and then finding the right one online and clicking "add to cart" in One. Single. Day. The tent came quickly. Arrived on time. I picked it up from the post office and was already judgemental and catty about how much the box weighed. Sigh. Why am I like this? Overall the tent is good. We needed something for our 2-year-old son to nap in on the beach so we don't have to pack up and leave at 11:30 everytime. It's time, after all, that we try to reclaim some semblance of our own lives. For this purpose it has worked 3 times. It's too big for our needs but that's not really a complaint and it is a bit heavy but my husband has taken ownership over the whole thing and insists on carrying it himself. He's the only one who has ever assembled or disassembled the thing and he insists it's easy. It seems a bit tall for me to assemble on my own. I wanted it to be the kind that just pops up and folds flat but he liked this one because it had vents. Vents are infinitely more important because it gets hot as a mofo inside when in the direct sunlight and if you can't catch a breeze. I thought the fold up part that stretches to the outside and acts as a sort of patio was stupid at first because who wants to sit or walk on that texture fabric at the beach but it occludes the view of people doing way more fun things than sleeping and for that reason it is essential. It lost a star because of the weight and because one of the loops that secures one of the windows has torn off already and I can foresee it happening again.

title: Outdoor exercise and transportation
text:
I'm 72 years old and like to think my physical activities are above average. I don't write many reviews and trust them even less.
When I received this bike the Eahora XC100 I found it easy to assemble however the seat had a crack in it as a result of pressure in the box during shipment, I suspect. I e-mailed and sent a photo to customer support and they responded promptly and resolved the issue by sending me a new saddle.
This was done promptly as well. This bike requires that you read the Manual because for it to be used to anyone's great advantage you should understand the power assist levels 0,1,2,3, proper shifting procedures, and the E-pass systems which is awesome.
Since the covid 19 has kept me out of the gym's I need an exercise method and routine to maintain my physical health.
I ride 10 miles each day when the weather permits, assured that no hill will be too challenging, also personal participation like your own effort is selectable as you learn to use the machine to your best advantage, not to mention the fresh air and great scenery while you work out.
This my use for this bike, the materials are good all around, a bit of a heavy bike but feels sturdy and manageable.
It even has a walking mode.
I recommend this bike to anyone who's looking for transportation or exercise. The dependability of the bike cannot be determined by me
I have ridden 349 miles time will establish dependability. Personally, I love this bike.

title: I would also recommend, as others have
text: I just recently discovered MTB and having a blast. Straight out of the gate I went ahead and converted to SPD but found I was having trouble. After doing a little research I found that most people were recommending platform pedals when first starting out on the mountain bike. So, a little research later and I found these Saint pedals by Shimano. It took a while to get used to not being securely attached to the bike (feet were bouncing off on rough terrain) but once I got the hang of being on a platform things improved quickly. I am far from being an expert rider but the Saints have certainly helped to improve my skills and my confidence as well. Along the way I have whacked some rocks very hard on multiple occasions but the Saints have just shrugged that off and kept right on going. I would also recommend, as others have, that you remove the washers from between the studs and the pedal and add the additional studs. If you're looking for some affordable, rugged platforms look no further.

title: Solid machine
text:
Pros:
The packing was sufficient and Assembly was a breeze, even with one person. Be prepared to break down a lot of shipping material.

For reference, I am 6’3” 240lbs- the belt is big enough to accommodate my stride and the machine is really solid.
It folds up easily and the noise is about average for a treadmill.

Cons:
The fan is almost non-existent, so don’t count on that cooling you down.
The speakers are okay at max volume, but another speaker or headphones would be better.
The heart rate monitor is absolute garbage! It works probably once out of every 30 attempts or so. It’s the only feature of the treadmill that I’d like to use, but it’s worthless.
It has Bluetooth and its own app, but it seems very basic.

Overall I gave it 5 stars because it is a nice machine to use for running. If I cared much about the speaker, HR monitor, fan, or app I would have rated it lower. It is sturdy and durable and handles my weight with no problem, and that’s what I was looking for.

title: Absolutely terrible delivery & shipping
text:
This product was delivered by XPO. I proactively chatted with them to describe the entrance and delivery situation to be sure they had the proper equipment. I was assured by their rep "no worries". They did call ahead on the appointed day. It was 2 delivery people in a box truck with about a 4 foot drop out the back. I asked them how they would move it and they told me "It's big and heavy." They had no idea how to handle it. There was no drop gate on the truck. I went to get a hand truck from my garage and when I came back, it had been slid off the truck onto one smashed corner. I helped them load it onto the hand truck and did the majority of the heavy work to get it into the "inside entrance" delivery per the Amazon order. Per instructions from Amazon I opened it to check for damage. The frame was broken on both ends, the bumper was separated, the felt was torn. I said, "Take it back." They said they could not because it had been opened! I had to go through Amazon's return processing. This required another couple weeks to set up a pick-up time. Another carrier picked it up. They had a lift gate. All went well. Then I had to wait a few more weeks for my credit. I called Amazon and they credited me over the phone. So the indoor winter months are passing without a pool table. Rather than go through this again as a "Reorder" I purchased a used table.
The original delivery people watched me open the box to review the damage and all they could do was ask if I wanted to pay them for assembly. This was not part of the Amazon order, but was something these two wanted as a cash transaction.
Amazon can deliver a lot of products, but they don't seem to have carriers vetted to deliver large items.

I was an Eagle Scout and we've used these bags a few times in temps down to freezing, and they work great if you get a fleece bag liner and put it in there. We were really nice and toasty warm.

PROS:
- HUGE - really really big. I'm 6ft and not small, and there's loads of extra room. If you don't like being cramped, look no further.
- WARM - It's actually pretty darn warm on it's own.
- GOOD ZIPPERS - they're on the left if you're laying in the bag, and they work well without getting caught a lot.
- TWO ZIPPERS - One down the side and one on the bottom. Why is this good? Zippers tend to have issues going around corners, and this seems to help.
- ZIPPER DRAFT TUBE - Huh? They made an extra...insulated tube of fabric next to the zippers running lengthwise that helps keep air out. And it's made of tougher material almost like a backpack which means...drum roll...the zipper finally doesn't get caught on the bag itself!!!
- GOOD HOOD - The hood is really nice and roomy, like put a full size pillow in it roomy. If you sinch it up with the draw string you can have a face-size opening.
- FLEECE FOOT - the inside bottom foot and a half has an extra layer of warm fleece.
- BURROW - I like to kind of burrow down in a sleeping bag and there's so much room you can bend your legs, sleep on your side, have your arm curled under your head, and there's just so much room. I can put my fee at the very bottom and have the opening above my head.
- LOOKS COOL - I know, it's a sleeping bag and how cool do you expect it to look, really? But it really does look pretty cool.

CONS:
- BIG - We put them in stuff sacks that sinch down and they're still pretty big bags.
- NOT FOR BACKPACKING - like everyone says.

HOW TO SLEEP WARMER:
- Put an inexpensive and washable fleece liner inside the bag. There's plenty of room. It adds to the warmth significantly.
- Change your clothes before you sleep. During the day your clothes get moisture from your own body heat. Change before you sleep and not only will you be warmer, having clean clothes inside the bag makes it stay cleaner.
- Don't over-dress. Start off in like shorts and a t-shirt, no socks, and you'll be warm without sweating. If you start off too warm, you'll build up heat, sweat, and then be colder.
- Put your extra layers down in the foot. Got a sweatshirt you'll probably wear in the morning? Shove it down in the foot. There's room, and it'll be warm when you're ready for it in the morning.
- Wear a beanie, helps with heat loss on your head if you stick your head out for fresh air.

FLEECE LINER:
We used something like this (though not this exact one) and it gets even warmer.

STUFF SACK:
We used a compression stuff sack like this and were able to fit the sleeping bag and the fleece liner in it together.
https://www.amazon.com/Lewis-N-Clark-Compression-Drawstring/dp/B079JRVVD1/ref=sr_1_4?dchild=1&keywords=lewis+n.+clark+compression+sack&qid=1592870350&sr=8-4

title: Best tent I've ever bought - great design
text:
I'm an Eagle Scout. We go Jeeping a lot. As an adult, we take our kids camping a LOT.

We've had this tent for 2 1/2 years and taken it camping probably 15-20 times. It's been all over the desert of NM, the mountains of Colorado, and the red rocks of Utah.

This tent is AWESOME.

PROS:
- Dome design doesn't require stakes in the ground - we have a lot of rocks up in the mountains.
- Dome design is super simple and quick to put up - usually about 2 minutes for us if we're taking our time.
- Walled sides - with the tub shape, water never gets in.
- It's HUGE. We usually put a full size air mattress AND two twin size mattresses in it PLUS there's about enough room for another twin mattress as well. We could probably fit two queen mattresses in there.
- It's TALL - my wife and I are both 6ft tall and can stand up in the middle very easily, not the "standing up but hunched over kind of" actually standing upright.
- The BAG IS AWESOME - hate trying to get a tent back into it's bag? This is the tent for you! Fold it into quarters, roll it up around the poles, throw it in, and because the bag is a little bigger than you need, it fits easily. (No, it's not loose and baggy, just right). We've had nights of "quick, just shove it in the bag" and it fits fine that way too. Easy to put away.
- HUGE POLES - you won't believe it till you see it, these poles are about as big around as a finger, not the little wimpy poles.
- BIG VENTS AND GIANT RAIN FLY - The vents on the sides are basically everything from the tub up to the top, so lots of ventilation. The Rain fly easily covers the mesh though and we've never had rain get in at all.
- No stakes necessary - we never use stakes, and the fly doesn't go anywhere and the tent stays put. We've shoved gear in the corners or occasionally a big rock, and done really well with this.

CONS:
- We had one of the bungee strings break in the poles, but that's to be expected after some use. It was easy enough to fix. The overall design is sturdy enough we used it a few times with no bungee at all and it was ok.
- Cooler weather - it has huge vents on the sides under the fly, so heat gets out when it's cold. But, we've also shoved a blanket or one of those two person hammocks between the tent and the fly and that helps keep the heat in a little better. Let's just say, it's probably not any colder than most other tents like this.
- Size. It is big, and if you need space to sprawl it's there. But if it's a cramped area because of trees, it is pretty big. If you're out west, and there's lots of room, this is a great tent.

CONCLUSION:
I've owned a 6-8 different tents, most of them dome tents, and this one is the toughest built, the most well-thought out, and the easiest to work with. I'd definitely buy this tent again.

(and if you have the space in your vehicle, throw some of those foam puzzle floor pieces in the tent and it makes it really, really posh)

(No, I didn't get this tent for free or anything, bought it outright).

title: It WILL fit, but I wish there was a better version of this.
text:
PRO: This WILL fit inside a regular jetboil with the orange stand and with the gas canister, but it's all about stacking order.

Canister, pot support, burner, then orange stand (If I remember correctly)

AND - as a friend of mine suggested, put all of that inside a large ziplock bag and then cut the zipper off, so you have a clear plastic sleeve to put inside the canister and then you won't have metal against metal. Makes it easier to load and unload.

CON - This thing really is kind of a sharp, pointy, clumsy design that doesn't fold up very well. You can bend the pieces to make them fit easier. But there ought to be a re-design of this piece to fold up differently or better. Awkward all around.

title: Just buy it already! (and a tip)
text:
I bought a tiny little micro stove you could screw onto a canister, which even came with an igniter. It was like $10 or something. That works fine in a pinch.

BUT, the Jetboil works much better (sorry, I know I'm late to the party). Having it actually connect to the water holder really makes it a LOT easier than having the micro stove with a water canister separate. sturdier and easier. Packs all together nicely.

TIP - Put the gas can, stand, and burner in a plastic bag before you put it inside the canister to avoid scratching the inside.

title: Best pedometer ever!
text:
I bought the OMRON HJ-112 pedometer through Amazon.com at $[...]. It's easy to clip on or put in a pocket and has become part of my everyday routine. The LCD display is easy to read and understand. The security strap with a little clip helps keep it from getting lost. I love it and highly recommend it.

The first couple of weeks my wife and I just enjoyed talking about how many steps we had done that day. Then about a week ago I found the "aerobic STEP" display. If you walk 60 steps or more per minute for 10 minutes or more the pedometer displays this as "aerobic" steps. Walking articles suggest 30 minutes a day of "aerobic" walking. With the pedometer you can record an easy pace of 60-80 steps per minute for 30 minutes during a lunch break. Or split it into two sessions of 15 minutes and let the pedometer add them together. The picture I uploaded shows 3396 aerobic steps I did 5 days ago. It took me 34 minutes so that's about 100 steps a minute. For me 100 is a very easy pace to maintain (on level ground, good shoes, etc.) but even a slower 60 a minute is perfectly OK.

So thanks OMRON for adding this much needed activity to my life and helping me measure it. Gadgets are great and this one is highly recommended. $[...] is a real bargain for such proven health benefits.

title: Never again.
text:
You get what you pay for with braided line. Ignore the LB ratings and pay more attention to Diameter vs Average Breaking Strain. I've found many of the lower priced braids will break at or below the "LB rating" - Where the premium braids break at a higher number than the "LB rating". Then you have to consider abrasion, slickness of the line, and how well the coatings and/or dyes stay on the line. If you are targeting smaller freshwater or panfish you might be ok with this line - If you are hitting bigger fish and using premium gear, personally would invest in a better braid and have confidence in your connection.

title: 40+ years of fishing - Best line I have ever tried.
text:
Picture shown is 40lb on a Tranx 401HG

I have been buying from Australia and dealing with the shipping cost and time to get here, so very happy to see it here in Amazon.

This is an excellent braid. Over the years I have spent thousands and thousands of dollars on fishing braid trying to find that "one". If I don't like a braid after one or two sessions, I will pull it all off my reel and throw it in the garbage. I don't like lines that have dyes that bleed off. I also don't like lines that depend on coatings on them as they can have a waxy feel to them, which I feel affects the casting. Some coated lines also take time to break in, and some coatings eventually just wear off. This is one of the many things that makes Tasline so different. They don't use any dyes or coatings. So there is nothing to break in, wear off, or bleed.

Due to the diameter to breaking strain ratio of this braid, and I am able to get more line on my reel. I recently just spooled up 1000m of 20lb braid on my Tern 400. Tasline 20lb has a PE rating of 1.7 and breaks at 34lb which is absolutely perfect for slow pitch jigging setups.

Casting is phenomenal. I think that the 8 strand braids in general are just smoother than the more common 4 strand braids. This line is very quiet going through the guides, and knot retention is excellent.

*Each spool has a hand written number on the back which correlates with breaking strain testing data for that specific spool. My testing has shown that these numbers are accurate and true.

title: Start Here!!!
text:
I have zero business affiliation with amazon or Shrade. I just like to help people make a decision on purchasing affordable gear. Many times I have bought less expensive gear and was sorry I did. However this won’t be the case with Schrade. If you are just getting into camping/bushcraft start with this knife. I bought my knives directly from the Schrade website (shut down now) about 2-3 years ago. I have 3 of their knives Sch37, Sch57, and Schf52; and was only out of about $60 for all 3. They are great knives for a beginner. Yes, they have some issues. But they may not bother everyone.

The Bad: The basic handles are not the most comfortable over long periods of use. Later, get the micarta scales the basic scales are not comfortable when chopping or don’t chop.

The chimpping on top is a bit aggressive when not wearing gloves and doing percussive tasks.

The protective coating scratches and stains but; it can be removed and cleaned if you have the time. I like to keep my things looking brand new. I may remove the coating at some point.

The sheath is not the greatest but at least you don’t have to buy one.

The good: it comes with a sheath, a sharpening stone, and a fire steel. You don’t get that with $500 knives.

It can accomplish every task a $500 knife can.

You can sell the knife/knives for what you paid; if you want to upgrade.

You can keep them to loan out or for a buddy to use.

Best of all is the price. You get to test out your skills for less than $30 bucks with this knife.

text:
The Skyline 17 oz premium insulated stainless steel bottle is a great choice! I own several S'Well bottles that look and function identical to this one at a MUCH lower price. A co-worker really liked my S'Well bottle but as previously stated, S'Well bottles are $25+ a bottle and that's more than I wanted to spend on a gift, so I was looking for a comparable alternative and I found it with the FLY Skyline. I wanted to make sure the Fly Skyline would keep water ice cold all day, I filled the Skyline bottle with ice cold water the before work and the bottle was effective at keeping the water ice cold the next day. The bottle is constructed of high quality stainless steel and looks/feels like it will last forever. The bottle holds 17 ounces of liquid, which is perfect for taking to work to be able to drink ice cold water at your desk. The lip on the bottle provides a very comfortable surface to drink from. The bottle includes a screw on lid that provides a leak-proof seal eliminating the worry and fear that the liquid will spill out of the bottle. The bottle states that it can keep beverages hot for 12 hours and cold for 24; I have only used the bottle for keeping beverages cold so I can only confirm that it can keep beverages cold for 24 hours (not sure about effectiveness of ability to keep beverages hot as I have not tried). The opening will easily accommodate "half moon" shaped ice but you will struggle to place ice cubes in the opening. Overall I was very satisfied with this bottle so if you are looking for a bottle that will keep your beverage hot/cold all day the Skyline stainless steel coke bottle is a great choice!

Pros:
-Keeps water cold/hot for a long time
-Stainless steel construction will last forever
-Screw top provides leak-proof seal
-Great textured surface makes holding onto bottle easy and slip free

I was fortunate enough to have received this product at a discount for my honest and unbiased opinion. I would definitely purchase this bottle again.

title: Saved us loads of money since we didn't have to buy a new beach cart that would work on soft sand
text:
We loved the Rio Wonder Wheeler concept, but it didn't work so great in practice. When loaded, it was very difficult to pull over the sand. We then looked at higher-priced ones with balloon wheels, knowing that those would work better on soft sand. I convinced my husband to try these wheels on the Wonder Wheeler first. We followed the advice of other reviewers and bought a 36" length - 3/8" diameter steel rod from ACE (couldn't find one at Home Depot) and 4 metal flat washers to fit the rod (which would be used as new axle). We drilled a hole 1/2 inch from both ends using a titanium drill bit (the carbide one we bought was useless). We used 1/2" pvc pipe cut to the width of the new wheels. We inflated the tires to 4 lbs. with an electric pump; removed linch pins from original axle (don't lose these or plastic bushings), removed original big plastic wheels, bushings, and axle.
To assemble with new tires: 1) We inserted new axle; 2) then the original bushings (with end protrusion cut off); 3) then a metal washer; 4) new tire with pvc inserted through center; 5) another washer; and 6) inserted original linch pins through drilled holes (repeat steps 2-6 on other side). It now works like a dream and saved us several hundred dollars since we didn't have to buy a new cart.

title: Save your money and make your own.
text:
At first this seemed like a good item. I practiced with 2 small branches close to the ground and was surprised how quickly it cut.

Then I decided to move on and tackle the ones I needed gone. Unlike so many others reviewing, I had no problems getting the blade to flip the right way. I used a simple lasso style toss and made suree the metal weight was facing the right way before the chain reached the branch.

The first branch went fine but I realized I did need to figure out a way to undercut the bigger ones I was going to work on before moving on and cutting them. The suggestion in the manual is pretty useless: you can't just stand to one side and undercut if you're trying to cut something 15-20 feet in the air, at best you'll cut at about a 45 angle. This meant I was going to need to cut the branches in a multitude of cuts to avoid the weight of a partially cut branch pinching the chain as it started to cut.

The first few cuts using this method worked. Then the inevitable happened: the chain got pinched and stuck. I tried the common sense solution of simply throwing the weight bag back over the opposite way to try and relieve the bind and wiggle it free while someone else put some force on the branch. The good news was the branch ended up breaking this way. The bad news: the chain broke too.

There appears to be absolutely no way to repair the chain supplied in this kit. There are no spare rivets or links supplied to perform what has to be a very common issue. This means you basically have just spent $40ish for two 25' pieces of nylon (that btw aren't even finished at the ends so they unravel), a bean bag, 2 "handle straps" that are next to useless and a clear plastic case marked "Made in the USA". And it pretty much looks like there is no warranty, replacement parts or even customer service of any kind.

I'd have to think anyone thinking of needing one of these rope saws can make one with a baseball drilled and with a string strung through it, 50' of nylon from your local hardware store and a replacement chain for any brand chain saw. And that too would be "Made in the USA".

As a sufferer of "tennis/golf elbow", I wanted to get ahead of the pain by having some specific exercises -- the FlexBar is it. After a few weeks of regular use (2-4x/day, up to 5 days/week), there has been a definite decrease in pain when playing (or practicing) golf.

If you already have good arm+grip strength (and the pain is currently mild, but annoying), then definitely consider the 25lbs over the lower units. After the few weeks of use, 25lbs still provides good resistance, but I could see the market for something around 35lbs.

If you don't have much strength and/or pain is already too much, these exercises could easily be too much for 25lbs -- go with the base unit.

Flex tells me the brutal truth that I am way below the amount of sleep I need and am way more restless during the little sleep I do get.  I am trying slowly, but surely, to increase the amount of sleep I get.  I have a bit of frustration while gardening because some of my activities create enough vibration to cause the device to think I'm going to sleep.  I've worn it in the shower from the beginning and everything still works well.  In fact, the only time I've removed it except for recharging was for a formal event (and only because I could not find a bracelet that would camouflage it well enough!!).
