title: Excellent for Coordination Training
text:
[[VIDEOID:36c82b800aaf42202e179eeb3c1739a5]] I got this bag for my 9 year old son because he has some coordination issues. I wanted him to work eye hand coordination and get some exercise. He really enjoys working out with this reflex bag.

We filled our base with a 50 lb bag of sand rather than water. I figured that it would end up in the house and I didn't like the idea a flood on wood floors if it leaked. Also that quanity of sand is twice as heavy as the same amount of water. This means the bag will stay upright if it gets hit hard. The play sand that we used had to be dried on a tarp to get it to pour into the opening. When it was damp it had to be forced into the opening and it took a long time to get a small quantity of sand inside. Other than that it was very easy to assemble. Everlast provides a hex key and a cheap stamped out wrench to assemble the bag.

It does unscrew slightly form the base as it is struck. This should not be a deal breaker for you, but something you need to be aware of.

Other reviewers have posted negative reviews must be hitting this bag with powerful blows. From my experience a reflex bag is more for speed and reflex training than power blows. If you want to lay into something with power, get a heavy bag. It will suit you much better.

For our use we are very happy with the bag. I think any kid would really enjoy this as a gift. Dad likes it too, and I like that my son getting some exercise rather than sitting in his room playing with his Nintendo DSi.

We got the Everlast 8 ounce Youth gloves to go with this Reflex Bag. I would recommend them as they offer good wrist support and excellent construction.

[[ASIN:B000QSQKDW Everlast Pro Style 8-Ounce Youth Training Gloves]]

Update5/26/10: Yesterday one on my son's friend used a bat on the reflex bag. It is not bat proof. It knocked the bag off. I poured Gorilla glue into the hole and on the post and let it dry with the post pointed up for a day. It seems as good as new.

Update 7/3/10 The bag is better than new. Two kids parties and near daily use and the bag is still firmly on the pole. The Gorilla glue has secured this bag with no sign of wiggle. They should manufactur them like this.

Update 11/8/11 The bag is still on as good as when I first glued it. No wiggle. The unit has been stored on our patio and is starting to rust at the spring and shaft. Nothing that affects the performance. It's just not that sightly. My son wants a B.O.B. Body Opponent Bag It is a training bag that looks like a torso. $250...ouch.

title: Good Sack, Easy to control, But..
text:

title: Magnets block Flex 2's sleep mode and notifications
text:
I got a Flex 2 and these magnetic holders in the same order because I wanted to keep it in my pocket rather than on my wrist, just as I had been using the Fitbit Flex for years. Unfortunately the Flex 2 wouldn't track my sleep. I tried all of Fitbit support's recommendations multiple times (reset 3x, reinstall app, change sleep sensitivity, etc.), but nothing helped. I didn't try the notification settings but knew vibration worked because it vibrates when you reset it. So I exchanged the Flex 2 for another.

The next Flex 2 didn't track sleep either, and it didn't vibrate! I knew this because when I put it in the charger and pressed the reset button it didn't vibrate. I tested all the notification settings to make sure, and repeated all the support procedures but still no sleep tracking OR vibration. So I exchanged it for a third one.

The third one was EXACTLY like the second one...no sleep or notifications! *sigh* I have been using a Flex in my pocket for years and didn't want to lose that. So, I would give it just one more try. I sent the 3rd one back and then went to Walmart for a 4th one. Maybe Amazon had a detective batch?

The 4th still didn't track sleep, but it did vibrate when I reset it! Maybe this time resetting it would fix the sleep tracking? No! Then I noticed that it did vibrate when I pressed the reset button but not when I turned on notifications. What the?Then I happened to try notifications again with it out of the holder and it worked! Then I put it back in the holder and it didn't work. Ah ha! Maybe it was the magnet all along! I cut off the "tail" of the holder with the magnet and tried it again. This time it vibrated, but very lightly. That's when I discovered that there is a second magnet in the holder. I had assumed that the little studs inside the holder were just metal for the magnet to stick to, but they are in fact a magnet as well. Could this have also been the problem with the sleep mode all along?

I tossed the holder and put the Fitbit in the small wristband and put that in my pocket. Now EVERYTHING works exactly as it's supposed to. So now I know. The magnets in these holders breaks the Flex 2's sleep mode and notifications...and it only took four Fitbits to find that out! I cut off the straps of the included band and now use that as a holder in my pocket. I didn't want a "clip" holder anyway so that will work fine for me.

I hope this saves someone the weeks of irritation and wasted hours that I went through.

title: Can't recomend because the handle broke.
text:
ORIGINAL REVIEW: I replaced my previous Igloo cooler with this one and I really like it. The top compartment is handy. I put a camper type salt shaker in it along with a few other small items. The ice packs that I use fit perfectly and so far the handle seems like it will last. The previous igloo cooler was a bit smaller and was bought in 1992. It still works great except the handle wont stay on so it was time for a new one. I mention this because it's 24 years old and still works. that says a lot for igloo quality. I hope to get that kind of service from this cooler. The only reason the handle failed was because I stumbled and sent the cooler flying. If that had not have happened I probably would not have needed to buy this one. Igloo is rugged, last a long time and with 2 ice packs about the same size as the sides of this cooler, everything stays cool for at least 24 hours as long as it's not in direct sunlight. I'm not one for change, especially when I have a product that works and lasts. I really did need a little larger cooler so yes, I miss the old cooler but not so much because I really like this new one much better. I donated the old one and found it good home. Yes I know it's just a cooler but I used t every work day for 24 years, I got a little attached to it. They still make that model and I nearly bought it but my wife found this new one. Due to the handle issue and the fact this one is way better, I do not recommend the older version any longer in favor for this one. Yes I know run on sentences its 1 am give me a break. Buy this cooler, slap a Cowboys sticker on it and you will be happy with it.

UPDATE: Guess I was wrong about the handle lasting, it didn't. I still use it for now but plan on replacing it with a similar cooler called Igloo Quantum. This may be an updated version of the ice cube model who knows. The handle feels better but attaches the same so i expect it to fail as well. It has a few additional features like 2 places to put a lock or locks on it, useless because it can be easily cut. 2 cup holders that I find too shallow to be useful and the top compartment is half the size. The cover is thicker and opens easier from the center as opposed to the corners like the ice cube model. Lastly; it's 3 tone. Had I know the Quantum was available I would have purchased it over the ice cube model. In my opinion, they should lose the cup holders and increase the top compartment size, ensure the handle wont come off and you would have a great cooler.

title: Good Stuff!

I do find it quite expensive but because refillable butaine comes in a variety of sizes and grades it dificult at best to determine what you are actually paying for. Like when you buy a gallon of gas, we can esily compare pricing even on premium grade. Someone needs to resolve this issue to assure customers are not getting ripped off. I'm not saying I was, I'm saying I have no clue and I feel it is way over priced compared to other brands that I have previously bought. Then again I need one thats refined to work in mini torches and this one does the trick. So its a matter of, you get what you pay for. Vectors super refined butane costs more in my opinion but one has to pay for quality. Were not talking a huge difference in price. To me a few bucks more for a quality product that I can be sure will work properly is well worth it. Concider the alternative, you clog up, mess up and possibly destroy your torch with an infirior product is not going to make you very happy. I got this advice direct from the torch manufacturer and I quote "I cant recomend a specific brand but make sure you use high quality butane refill to avoid fuel delivery system clogging". Thats enough for me. I cant find any other butain refil thats refined 5 times. Quintuple? Thats 5 right? I don't know but it seems to be alot of refineing going on here. The more it is refined the cleaner and purer it is. It is also nice to know that I am buying butane in a can and not butane combind with who knows what else but what ever it is it can ruin your torch. The only reason I gave it 4 stars is, I am a tuff cookie to earn 5 stars from me it has to be perfect. I want a larger size can and I want to see some priceing so I can be an informed consumer and understand what I am paying for. Yup I am picky I know. title: Doesn't live up to the brand in my opinion
text:
I've gotten Petzl headlamps before, and I've always been relatively happy with them. When my last one would no longer hold a charge on the batteries for longer than a n hour or two, I did not hesitate to get a new Petzl. This one has a brighter light (300 lumens versus my previous 250), but otherwise, I'm not convinced it was worth going with the Petzl name here- overall, I'm pretty disappointed. For one thing, the whole casing feels pretty cheap and not of great quality. The button at the top is difficult to push and it's really hard to remember how many pushes/how long you need to push to get the lighting you want (it cycles through from dim to bright, but to get red light you need to hold it for longer). And, for the first time, this headlamp hurts my face to wear. Overall, I don't really feel like I can recommend it, I'm pretty disappointed, and might consider going with a different brand in the future.

Pros:
Has a red light (this is important to me as I work with animals)
300 lumen bulb is certainly a pretty solid light
3 brightness levels is convenient and also helps save battery
Battery life is decent
Only uses 3 AAA batteries at a time

Cons:
Uncomfortable to wear
Variable lighting conditions (particularly red light and strobe) are difficult to get to
Relatively expensive

My husband purchased a Black Diamond headlamp for around the same price, it had a brighter light bulb (400 lumens), has a blue and a green light option (not sure what you'd use it for, but it's there), seemed more comfortable, and was slightly cheaper.

title: Amazing wrist bands for FitBit Flex2! I would DEFINITELY recommend!
text:
My husband and I are really happy with these replacement bands (reasons detailed below). Ideally, honestly we would give them a 4.5/5 star rating if possible due to one flaw (lining up of the lights) but otherwise, they are great and we would both recommend!

Look: We got the black, grey, and blue bands and we both really like the colors. Although the black is standard with FitBit Flex2, the dark blue costs extra, so I really like that we can get all three colors here. One thing I can say about the colors though is that the blue band looks much darker in person than on the photo (although, I actually like it better in real life than on the photo). It's not really a big deal, but I think the different color makes it look just a little more professional and a little less like a typical fitness band. And, since there are three bands, you have choice and can change up your band as you change up your outfits!

Feel: I really like how soft the rubber/silicone material is. It is not stiff (as I have found other after market fitness bands to be), nor is it "sticky" (sometimes rubber can catch fine hairs on the arm and feel like it's ripping them out....that is NOT the case with this band!) The clasp on the back is comfortable and doesn't push into the wrist. Overall, it is very soft and comfortable to wear both during the day and at night.

Fit: there are two aspects here- first how the FitBit Flex2 fits into the band and how the band fits on the wrist. The FitBit fits nicely into the "pouch" left for it- it is secure (does not feel like it will fall out) but is not difficult to get it in either. One of my (only) complaints, however, is that the holes on the bands do not line up PERFECTLY with the lights on the FitBit. Honestly, this is such a minor thing and most people might not even notice it at all. I think it's actually largely because the rubber/silicone is a little bit thicker on this band than it is on the normal band, so it looks a little further away, so depending on your angle when you look at it might look like the entire light isn't on (but I have to say you can always tell which light is on or off, it never covers a light or makes it impossible to see- I think I might be slightly anal retentive to even notice!!). As far as the wrist fit goes...I'm actually really impressed here. It fit my husband without a problem and it even fit my (super dainty) wrists in the second to smallest hole! I feel comfortable to say that this would fit (almost) any adult's wrist. There's no need to keep multiple bands around- one size will definitely fit all.

Security and Protection: Although I have never (ever) worried that the clasp on my Fitbit will wear down and I might eventually lose my FitBit, I can see how that might happen (particularly after long periods of wear and removal to charge). Either way, this band removes any slight concern about that fact with the steel (watch like) clasp. It is obvious this clasp will not accidentally loosen and fall off. Ever. I also like that it feels soft and like it will protect my FitBit in case I (inevitably) bang it into something. The band provides enough protection that I won't break it. That being said, one difference between these bands and the band that comes with is the holes (to view the lights) are open on these bands whereas the are covered with a piece of clear plastic on the regular band it comes with. I'm not sure how much protection that clear plastic provides (I tend to find dust and things on the FitBit regardless), but something to mention.

Overall: I would definitely recommend these bands. I think they're high quality- they look and feel really nice on the wrist. And for the price (3 for ~$10) you really cannot lose.

title: Great sleek, slim, and comfortable design to help you get moving!
text:
This is my second Fitbit but my first Fitbit Flex (I have used the One in the past). I really like it and haven't had any problems with the accuracy.

I love the community involved when you use the Fitbit brand (challenges with friends and family to keep you going). I REALLY like that this is water proof- I haven't gone swimming with it on yet, but it's nice that I don't have to think about it when I shower or when I'm washing the dishes.

It is a relatively small and simple design. There are 5 lights on the top, 4 to indicate the proportion of your daily steps you've done that day (with the goal of 10,000) and the fifth to give you notices. You have to remember what each of the colors is, but I haven't had any problems with that- green to indicate when you're checking on your steps, red to tell you your battery is getting low, and blue or purple when you're getting a phone call or text (I'm not totally sure about these as I don't use them for that). You can connect to you phone to notify you when you get a phone call or text message; you get get hourly reminders to move; you can track your sleep schedule; and what I love the most about is that you can seamlessly change activity type (running, elliptical, swimming, outdoor biking) without manipulating the information on your app.

Easy and comfortable. I have definitely found that it has helped me increase my daily steps!

title: Working well as a seiza-training tool
text:
I'm over 60, and wanted to learn to sit seiza again; however sharp pains in my calfs and ankles made it difficult to maintain. I figured I could work up to it with this little bench, and it's doing the trick!! I gradually lowered the height to the lowest level...then I took a 7/8" diameter dowel and some scrap wood, and made a substitute "T" to fit under the seat. As my comfort with a height increases, I take the dowel and saw off about 1/4" at a time to reduce the height a bit. I'm finally able to sit seiza, even without the bench, without serious pain; I'll continue to lower the height and practice daily until I don't need the bench at all, but in the meantime, it makes sitting seiza for extended periods much more comfortable.

As others have noted, the bench has little padding (just a thin layer of dense foam), so this may not be comfortable if you're carrying much excess weight, since that would increase the pressure on your thighs. Since it looks like free returns aren't offered, you might consider buying a used bench (if available) to try it out less expensively; it's very sturdy, so a used one should work fine.

title: Good little kayak for a great price
text:
Grabbed one of these on sale on Black Friday, and finally got to try it out. Goes together easily and not difficult to pump up. One person can carry it, though it's less awkward for two. Between the netting on the front and the stowage in the stern behind the seat, we were able to take all our stuff with us and not have to worry about possible pilferage.

The instructions are a bit vague, so take note that there are TWO chambers to inflate, and the first one to be inflated is NOT the obvious top chamber (with the number 2 beside it), but the hidden number 1 chamber, which is located on the starboard (right) side, inside wall above the floor and a little aft of the middle of the boat. Each valve has two lids, one on top of the other; undo the upper one (with the 4-lobed lid) to inflate, and undo the lower lid (larger and round) to deflate. Don't over tighten the upper lid, or it's difficult to open it without the bottom lid opening too, and losing air. You may hear a hissing sound while inflating the second chamber, but don't worry—the air passage narrows at one point and it tends to hiss while filling; you're not actually losing the air.

Had a little trouble with back support on the front seat—next time I'll bring a rolled towel to support my lower back. It's good to bring a towel anyway so you can dry off the kayak before deflating and storing it. I suggest before taking the boat out you inflate it, test for leaks and do a test-sit to figure out how you want to arrange the seats and straps ahead of time; then use a sharpie to indicate who the seat is adjusted for, and where it needs to be stuck on the velcro.

Be gentle with the pump and paddles; some reviews mentioned they broke easily, though they seem sturdy enough to me—I don't think they'll stand up to much abuse, though.

Lots of fun for the price!

P.S: If you don't have PFDs, the ONYX MoveVent Dynamic Paddle Sports Life Vest (sold elsewhere on Amazon) works very well, and doesn't get in your way when paddling. Don't forget to buy a couple of paddle leashes with carabiners, too!

title: My favorite collapsible water bottle
text:
It's nice to be able to roll this little sucker up and stick it in my pocket, so I don't have to carry a bulky water bottle everywhere. It's got a nice wide filling spout (so it doesn't take long to fill), and the flexibility also helps when I have to try and fill it from a shallow basin (because I can "fold" the bottle so it fits under the tap). It comes with it's own spring-loaded D-ring that you can clip to your belt loop, purse, or pack-strap, and it also works for storage—you can roll the bottle up and flip the ring over the roll to hold it. It's got a flip cap for drinking and the spout is not too small, so you can get a good drink quickly. I like the new, translucent cap—my old one had an opaque cap, and mold developed in it without my knowing it—this makes problems easier to see before they develop.

To prevent any mold growth, don't forget to COMPLETELY air dry the OPEN bottle and OPEN cap between uses, and store with the cap open.

title: Happy feet!
text: I suffer from the dreaded Popsicle Toes: my feet get frosty even when the rest of my body is comfortable...and once they chill down, they refuse to warm up, even in a nice warm bed.  I've had to get up at 2 a.m. and run hot water into a foot basin just to get my feet warm enough to let me fall asleep!  But with this little number on the floor in front of my favorite chair, I just flip the switch, park my chilly tootsies on top and let the blessed warmth soak in.  This heater is not intended to warm up larger areas (though it might do for warming a tiny room or under a desk), but it's perfect for keeping your feet toasty.  Saves energy, because I don't have to run the furnace as much.  The angled feet can easily be removed so you can hang it vertically or keep it flat on the floor (that's how I keep it; so far it hasn't damaged the carpet beneath, even though I forget to turn it off sometimes).  I've been using it for 2 years without any problems, but if it ever conks out, I'm getting another one—I wouldn't want to be without it!

title: Excellent little waist pack for sport or travel
text:
I'm heading off on a cruise, and don't want to carry a purse around. This holds the essentials without that "I'm wearing a dorky fanny pack" look. It's quite streamlined (not quite enough to not be noticeable under a shirt or tunic, but a jacket covers it up fine). It has 4 compartments: a front zippered pocket, and a back pocket that, when unzipped, reveals two compartments in front and back of a third zippered pocket (good place to keep the moolah and credit cards, since a pickpocket would have to unzip two zippers to reach it). A compact camera will fit, as will a passport, etc. It expands, if necessary, to about 3 inches—but at that point, you may as well have worn the fanny pack ;-). There's also a plastic D-ring on the front, to which you could attach items with carabiners or clips if you wished...I suppose that would be one way to keep the ol' Purell bottle handy!

My only quibble was that little red embroidered bar and the label on the front—I don't wear red much. The label cut off easily, and I fastened a pretty blue turtle pin over the red bar. Problem solved!

text:

Before I purchased it, we contacted the company. I have a Galaxy Smartphone and we wanted to make sure it was compatible. Customer service was very helpful but they couldn't guarantee my phone would work since it was one phone they hadn't tested. We appreciated their honesty. We gave it a try anyway since it was so highly recommended and it works like a charm.

I didn't rate it 5 stars because I haven't had it long enough. I will do a follow up review after a longer time period but right now I'm very pleased with the product. It gives me the piece of mind that I can get an accurate reading on afib.

text:

I'm a walker and hiker and love the light, flexible bottle. We travel a lot and will soon be taking them on a month long trip to China. Will do an update (and hopefully change to 5 stars) after we return from China and see how they hold up. Love the bright colors!

Great customer service with the owner answering my questions in a very timely fashion. Since I volunteer with rescue groups, love that a portion of sales goes to rescuing dolphins. Nice touch.

2/7/19: I never do a follow up review for a product. I typically wait to do a review until I know the product deserves one. However, I'm breaking my rule here. In a little over a year, these two original bottles have been with us through an extensive trip through China, a month long trip through the western US and a month in Germany. They hang on our backpacks so they have been thrown in the back of rental cars, hoisted up on racks on high speed trains, etc. and have passed every test. They are still going strong and next month they will go back to Europe with us for a month. I've tried other roll up travel bottles and they broke on the first outing. We even freeze these half full of water in hotel refrigerators and then fill the rest of the way the next morning so we have cold water.

I gave them 5 stars this time and when they do finally wear out, I will reorder. They have been put through enough abuse that I'm convinced they are great!

So in other words - this item may have cost more than my wood jig, but in time along since I've got it I've probably saved that money twice over. title: Great backup bag for unexpected needs or emergencies
text:
This is a lightweight (in all aspects) bag that is great for limited purposes. It is made out of extremely thin and flexible material. It can fold up into itself and zip up (see picture) for easy storage and transport when not using it to carry items in. I can see this bag as being an excellent option for travelers who might find themselves needing another bag/storage option at the last minute. Like when you realize at the airport your bag is overweight and to avoid a huge baggage fee, you wish you had a small bag you could put some heavy items in and carry it on the plane instead. This would be perfect for that. Or you spend the holidays with relatives and they send you home with more goodies for the kids than you have room in your luggage for.

It's not a primary use bag. There is no padding at all. Not in the bottom of the bag. Not in the shoulder straps. There is no protection for items within the bag or your shoulders. It would not be comfortable carrying this with anything substantial or heavy inside. The material reminds me of an inexpensive windbreaker or poncho.

Pros:
Great backup bag for unexpected situations
Lightweight and very compact
Folds and zips into itself for easy storage and transport

Cons:
Flimsy shoulder straps with no padding
Questionable ability to carry heavy, rigid items like books or glass bottles
No padding in the bag itself, thus no protection for items inside

I received this bag for minimal cost in exchange for my unbiased review.

title: Make sure you order one that guarantees it comes with a plug
text:

The issue I had was that the ball I received did not come with an adapter that would allow me to inflate it with a bicycle pump, nor did it come with a plug. title: Powerful, Simple, Motivating
text:

The step, activity, and sleep tracking seem to be quite accurate. The pulse and oxygen saturation monitoring are simple and precise. Battery life seems to be superb, and integration/connectivity with my iPhone have been no problem. Both the wristband and the belt clip are well-made and comfortable. I find that it really helps to motivate me to maintain and improve my health.

If I were to provide four pieces of constructive criticism they would be:
1) Make the Pulse OX waterproof or at least very water resistant.
2) Improve the Apple Healthkit Integration. I've had some issues, not in the Withings App, but within Healthkit, with doubling of steps.
3) Provide a means for background measurement of pulse and oxygen, rather than requiring the fingertip read. It is not practical to use for Zone Training or to see peak heart rate during a workout.
4) Allow for customization of the step and sleep goals.

Overall it has been a great little device though. Used in my "App Ecosystem" of the Withings App, WebMD, MapMyRun, and Healthkit...it is a nearly complete solution for my personal wellness goals.

title: Unique
text:
I purchased this knife because I am getting tired of carrying around my Tomcat 3.0 in a sheath. A big selling point for me was the pocket clip of the new model Vision, the knife being all metal, and the VG-10 steel blade. If I had received the older model, well I would have had to return it. The knife arrived with a razor sharp blade right out of the box.

This knife took some getting used to compared to the Tomcat. The Vision is much thinner than the Tomcat in regards to the whole knife. The Tanto blade has additional unique grind lines. I believe SOG did this so that the knife blade being only .125 thick would have the strength of a knife of .150 - .160 thick when it comes to possibly breaking the knife tip.

It appears to me that SOG invested much into the knife being very thin, convenient to carry, and a very large blade for how small the knife is. That is exactly what I needed, I always have a knife with me. It is a little more difficult to handle compared to the Tomcat due to the thinness of the knife.

With the thinness of the Vision, it still seems very strong. There was no sacrifice in strength with this design. I love the handle. I wish SOG offered the same type of handle with more of their knives.

After playing around with my new Vision, until my thumb bled LOL! (that is expected with any new knife for me), then going back to the Tomcat, now my Tomcat feels big and bulky. For a sheath knife and heavy use, I do like the Tomcat better. For convenience to carry, and personal protection, I think I like the Vision better.

The Vision is a great knife, it has a very unique heavy duty thin feel to it.

Would definitely recommend. A word of caution to those with large hands. It may be difficult to get used to.

Sincerely,

10Wolf

title: Quick tip for any owners/potential buyers
text:
The other reviews mentioning the finely threaded battery compartment are pretty accurate. The first thing I did when I got mine was wipe down the threads, there was definitely dust that immediately wiped off that I could see being a problem. After it was cleaned I applied a little bit of mineral oil to the threads (probably something better, but it is what I had), and the screwing/unscrewing was much smoother.

Once I added in the batteries and began screwing the cap back on, I could understand why so many people are worried about it. It is really hard to tell if the resistance you are feeling when screwing it back in is because of the spring on the cap, or because it is not threaded well. If you go carefully it should screw back on fine - especially if you clean the threads and apply a little oil.

The laser seems to function exactly as expected, the strobe mode blinks a little faster than I was expecting, but that is hardly a problem.

Will update once it gets some usage!

UPDATE (2 days later): Well the laser started acting weird... Randomly won't turn on, can't rack a shotgun more than a few times without it turning off - and I wasn't even shooting. I'm actually impressed by just how unreliable it is. Going to roll the dice and get an exchange, but my hopes are not very high at this point.

EDIT: I got a second one of these and am pleased to report that it is more reliable. Was able to put a few dozen rounds thru my shockwave with no issue.

I want to give it 5 stars, but considering the problems so many people have had (myself included) I simply can not.

...But let me say, I was underwhelmed when I unpacked this from the huge Amazon box in which it arrived. Chill Chest is comprised of hinged or interlocking panels of some kind of extremely lightweight plastic foam - it's not waterproof (there are relatively large spaces between the panels, in the seams, around the hinges, etc.), nor is it terribly attractive and it squeaks when the panels rub against eachother. Since I haven't actually used the Chill Chest yet, I can't speak to its durability but from the looks of things, I'm wondering if that's going to be disappointing too.

To be honest, I was primarily interested in getting this product as a way to keep hot things hot. During the Christmas holidays it seems like there's always an opportunity to engage in that frustration-inducing, logic-defying necessity of taking perfectly good, hot food out of the oven, swaddling it in layers of towels, and driving it miles away to a friend's or relative's home, all the while keeping my fingers crossed that it will still be a little hot when we arrive. title: Great Resistance Training for Older Folks Too
text:
The physical therapist at the hospital had me work on hers when I came in. She thinks the TRX system is the bee's knees. When the thearopy was over I bought one.

Importantly note that the physical therapist specifically told me not to get a knock off unless it had a single strap. If the straps were not connected I would lose the balance building part and she said it would hurt me more than help. The TRX was the only one I saw, at the time, that met her criteria.

I love working on it. In my opinion, There are a couple of things to consider. First is that at my age and inflexibility, the lower body work outs are difficult. You have to get your feet in the straps a certain way and sometimes I find it hard to keep the feet in and do the workout.

The next consideration is that it is difficult to use in a closed door. You really need a fair amount of space around you to work out, and I find a closed door is a hindrance.

Overall i must grudgingly admit the physical therapist is right and the TRX system is just about perfect for getting that resistance training which is so important.

It makes a light and lofty cover by itself in warmer spaces or to add insulation to a sleep system that isn't quite right for colder weather.  There are plenty of snaps to fasten the quilt into a sort of garment to use on 'game day' in cold autumn weather.  I never have tested water resistance, aside from light and intermittent drizzle.  It did well then.  The quilt compresses well for packing.

title: Compact cot for tent camping
text: This is a compact cot featuring good materials and a sturdy design.  Leg height can be varied for different tent conditions or for personal comfort in getting up and sitting down.  This also works well for 'sleepovers' for grandchildren!

title: Good Tent Materials; Pole Failed
text: On my first setup, one section of the pole system failed near a joint.  The pole materials do not seem to be the same quality as the rest of the tent.  I did a quick repair with fine copper mesh and electrical tape:  this tent fabric and the poles system just withstood exceptionally high, swirling winds with no other failure in the material.  For me, it is a plus that I can (just) fit an OneTigris cot with legs into the tent and still have headroom to sit on the cot.

title: 'Real' Pillow size and Loft; Quality Materials
text: Need a good night's sleep in the woods?  Even Nessmuk required a pillow!  This 'made in China' inflatable product has been tested and reviewed by hardcore campers like SIMON, BLOKE IN THE WOODS.  His experiences led me to get one.  The 'up' side of the product is a decently comfortable (not 'sticky-face') material.  The compressed packed size is 2.5 x 4.0 inches.  The product comes in a 'right-sized' travel bag.  When inflated, there is a well-designed hollow to support the head and neck, even for people who sleep back, sides, and stomach on a given night.  For extra coolness, I bring a pillowcase. For car camping, bring an inflator.  For off-grid use, inflate by mouth.  Either way works well.

title: Quality Steel, Two-Person Size, Induction Capable; Scandi Design
text: FIVE STARS: I use this camp item at home on an induction cooktop.  One boil provides ample hot water for two of anything from tea to coffee to cocoa to rehydrating meals on the trail. It 'boils up' on an Esbit heater, a Butane stove, or a twig stove.  'SCANDI DESIGN' is more than the lovely form of the kettle.  The ergonomics of the piece works.  The heavy-duty curved stainless wire handle installs 'inward' to provide a stable balance when lifting and shifting the kettle.  Heat is not transferred to the handle.  The relatively broad base sits securely on a variety of cooking surfaces.  Steam is vented in two ways.  A spout and triple vent holes in the lid keep hot vapor away from your hands.  A decent quality wooden knob provides a way of comfortably lifting the lid.  The knob is fastened to the lid by spot-welding a screw.  This will be the 'weak point.'  Modern superglues (sold on Amazon) will make desired repairs to the screw contact surface.

title: Extra Strong Construction; Better Insulation; Holds Temperature Longer
text: CONS up front: expensive and heavy.  Strap type handles are sturdy and work for gloved hands but are not so comfortable. PROS:  market leader for toughness; available in many sizes; uses a convenient freezer block as well as store ice to keep things cold.  Thicker walls than my top Coleman; Yeti holds temperature longer.

title: Sturdy and Useful Solid Fuel Tab Stove
text: All function and no frills in this exceptional folding pocket stove design.  This stove has been tested and approved of on Bushcraft/Survival YouTube chanels.  I had to buy and try for myself.  Two sturdy steel wings fold in or out of a central tray, with a third free panel tucked inside to be slotted into the tray as needed as a wind screen.  Three sections inside the main tray will each hold a Dragon Fire solid fuel block (or gel fuel).  Fuel must be purchased separately. One, two or three blocks of fuel can be ignited to produce varying levels and expanses of heat.  The wings can be securely hand-adjusted to support a metal cup or metal pots or a small fry pan.  I tested my copy with a 6-inch cast iron frying pan with no support problems.  Typical uses of this stove/fuel system are to  boil water for purification or a quick hot beverage, or to provide water to reheat prepared food packets.  The system is not for space heating.

title: Classic Sturdy Cup; Handle; Cool Lip Cups
text: So many ways to consider camp cook gear.  This is a  Classic for a reason.  When I was young and fit and backpacked most weekends in the summer and autumn, the difference between stainless steel and titanium was that one metal warped more than the other and one weighed a bit less...but not enough to matter.  Both metals were uneven in the transfer of heat; foods stuck.  We 'loved' our stainless Sierrra Cups...but they were too hot on the lips...and cooled the contents too fast.  This Stanley product with its expanded poly cups provides extended warmth to beverages, soups or stews.  The metal pot has clearly visible volumetric markings.  The cup sits very well on folding alchohol or small wood burning stoves like the Firebox.  'Bug Out Kits' benefit from this setup:  we cannot rely on available wood but we need a pot to boil water and something to eat a small meal in...for two.

title: Heavy Duty Construction Aids Temp Control; Get Wire Basket and Coolant Block
text: YETI products are EXPENSIVE.  I kept this on my wish list for over a year!  Lately, 'prepping' seems to make more sense to me.  "Serious Kit" seems to have more value.  A lifelong Coleman Cooler owner, I am IMPRESSED with the Yeti's thicker walls and 'means it' sealing gasket inside the lid.  Should we need to empty our freezer or refrigerator to store important nutrients for several days THIS is our mid-term choice.  Early on, we still have a fine Coleman product.  Longer term, canned goods and freeze dried/stabilized goods will do.  The YETI can be strapped (belt grooves on the lid) and it can be locked to secure items.

title: Compact, Friendly Lighting; Each Requires 3 AAA Batteries; Clip-on Hanging Feature
text: Some LED lights are too powerful or tightly focused for lighting in tents, bunks and bivvys. These are just right in both respects...and they come in cheerful body colors.  Lighting levels can be changed from bright (but not piercingly so) to dim to strobe.  Their light weight permits hanging them from ridgelines or clipping them to shelter support poles.  I found their little round 3-way switch to be difficult to find in the dark.  If you want to string all of them around the front of a lean-to, you will need TWELVE batteries.

title: Light Weight, Limited Loft, Quality Build
text: I like the air cell design, with numerous sections like coiled springs to spread my weight over the surface.  My bag did not slide off during the night. The design minimizes surface wetness.  Inflation is fast, partly because capacity is limited.  Overinflation will blow out the plug-in valve seal.  Deflation is the quickest I have ever experienced.  The mattress is long enough for someone a little over six feet tall.  Dimensions are best suited to mummy-style or tapered barrel style sleep systems.

title: Great For Old Hands; Enthralling for Grandchildren
text: Yes, I have 'fidgety' hands.  Yes, I have (somewhat) arthritic hands.  These colorful and cheerful 'eggs' are fun and fine for my needs. title: Throat Baffle Makes Bag Outstanding for Warmth
text: For sure, this is a well-designed bag for winter warmth.  The offset battens and the neck baffle set the pace.  I use this with and without a silk liner.  Either way is equally comfortable to the touch.  Heat regulation comes in a variety of ways:  unzip the bottom edge and stir around a bit and heat is dispersed.  Unzip the top and peel the cover away and heat is dispersed.  Loft here is amazing for me based on my decades of backpacking and car camping.  As an 'Old Guy', I have owned and used a number of well-regarded bags.  Lately, I am using a Dramur Amok hammock and this bag removes the need for an underquilt in moderate winter climates.

title: Sturdy, Great for Melting Butter; Warming Sauces; Pre-Seasoned
text: Lodge still makes wonderful cast iron pots and pans and Dutch ovens.  I use this small pot to melt butter for baking or for use in sauces.  Cast iron is heavy weight but offers even heating and good heat retention if butter or sauces need to be held before using.  This pot is pre-seasoned with a food safe Lodge formula.  I reseason my cast iron with beeswax.  Any vegetable wax with a high smoking point will work as well.  To clean, I simply scour with coarse Kosher salt, rubbing residue away with a paper towel.  The pot is decorative enough to use at the table in an informal setting.  The pour spouts work well for left and for right-handed people.

title: Compact, Two Grit; Hook Sharpener Groove
text: This is a 'value for the dollar' field or pocket sharpening system.  The pen format makes it easy to take along.  The 'cap' slips off and installs over the body of the casing and stays put through touch-up operations.  I say 'FOUR STAR' only in comparison to bringing along a bit of emery cloth in a suitable grit: that is more compact and is equally effective.  Of course, this decent sharpener is not comparable to the diamond hones and fancy stones we probably have in our shops.  But then, we are not in our shops when we will need this item.

title: Ultra Comfortable, Compactly Packable; Washes and Dries Well
text: I LOVE this sleeping bag liner-style travel sheet even more since it is sewn into a bag.  No feet sticking out the bottom in the middle of the night!  Normally agile people will have little trouble in opening the bag the one-third down way it is designed to open and then sliding over the silk to plant one's feet at the bottom. title: Stainless Steel Weights Like This Are Necessary in Submerging Sous Vide Vacuum Pouches.
text: This Scuba Diving accessory has been repurposed as a weight in sous vide cooking.  These stainless steel pieces provide just enough weight to  hold down sous vide vacuum pouches, especially if you have more than one of these weights and if you are using them to keep a stainless steel screen submerged.  The stainless steel is rust resistant:  other weights oxidize quickly in the sous vide hot water bath.  They will also work as paperweights and can be used as a conversation piece in the office, especially if you dive.

title: Earns Its Way Onto Your Load Out
text: Backpackers faced with cold, wet and/or dirty ground will REALLY LIKE this cushioned seat from a long-term, top-tier maker.  This model has a heat-reflective side and a padded side.  I am a 'wide ride' and would appreciate a somewhat larger pad...but even my butt-print is accommodated well enough by this compact item.  Speaking of 'compaction', this small pad gives 'just enough' knee relief or buttocks relief for a 200 Lb. person.  Even if one is 'going light', there will quickly come a time when this easy to tote item will earn its way onto your load out.

title: Even Distribution of Tension For Rehab Exercises
text: Off and on, I have purchased a variety of Theraband fitness/rehab products.  Lately, our (Senior Citizen) fitness trainer has introduced band exercises (BYOB: Bring Your Own Band).  Our trainer has the opinion that this level of band strength suits a wide range of people:  those wanting more resistance need only work a narrower length of band.  I fall into the 'somewhat trained' category; my exercise partner deals with neuromuscular issues and we both can use this blue roll.  I DO recommend it to you.

title: Good Back Up Water Treatment
text: How can a typical backpacker or survivalist review this?  I cannot analyze water before and after through a chemical analysis.  I have to operate a bit on trust and  on taste.  The technology has been evaluated by labs over the years.  So I have tested these according to a 'taste test.'  I do not taste the water purifying compound our fine municipal service uses for our daily water supply.  Brewed coffee tastes 'just that little bit better' when I filtered the water.  I read that Sawyer products are used in serious 'Third World' situations, so I think we will be 'good to go' in the 'Wilds' of Charlottesville, VA or the Great Smokey Mountains or the Blue Ridge Mountains.  I like the standard 'bottle' neck size on these:  I can swap out the small squeeze bag for a larger, empty energy drink bottle.  The straw option that fits on the filter inflow permits sucking up water from pools in shallow streams.  The set comes with a syringe-style backflow flusher to clean the filter of debris.

title: One Difference Bewteen Fire and Failure
text: After years of blowing at camp fires through pursed lips and getting a face and eyes and lungs full of smoke, I saw a product demonstrated on a Bush Craft video.  It was only available in Europe...  Then I found this on Amazon.  It is stainless steel so it is not light weight for its (small) size.  Its value is in its function and in its collapsiblity.  From a collapsed state of just under 4 inches, it extends to 19 inches,  The larger (.5 inches, diameter) end is placed in the mouth and the narrow end concentrates  oxygenated air from your lungs to a focused stream at the narrow end. Once an initial spark or flame has begun to produce an ember, combustion can be sped up by directing more air precisely at the ember.  That sure beats watching helplessly while the initial spark fails to catch and fades to nothing.  On a dry day with dry, finely processed wood, this might not be needed...but on a cold, damp day with wood that is a bit damp, this makes all the difference between fire and failure.  At first, this device will be stiff to open and close but a little lubricant will help.  Opened up, the rod is sturdy and should last for a good many fires.

title: Sturdy, Well-Packaged, Reasonable to Assemble Weight Rack
text:
Tired of storing your dumbbells in corners or under the bed? I was and I chose this Apex rack because I like the slight slant, like we have in our fitness room and it looked sturdy in the photos. It IS sturdy up to the listed weight capacity and it is stable on the floor. Some assembly is required. The 'parts' come nicely wrapped and shrink wrapped nuts, bolts and washers kept the project in order while I was putting things together. My unit came with holes matching up nicely: it is always a good idea to leave the fasteners a little loose until the pieces are all fitted together, since some nudging is almost always required at some point to achieve a proper alignment. Be sure to tighten things then. I do NOT have a matching set of hand weights so I was interesting to see how well/IF the shorter, lighter weights would fit on the rack as I hoped. My SHORTEST weight is a 4 LB 'Yes4All' coated vinyl number, 6 3/4-inches end-to-end and it just fits securely on the rack. Shorter length weights would fall through the front and back rails any way you can install the rails.

I keep my weights and rack in a large walk-in closet where the rack fits under the clothes bars. I only have a few weights here but I have found that the bottom rails work fine as a shoe rack. Now both the weights and the shoes are being kept in good order.

title: For Toddler Balls; Takes Time to Inflate Serious Sports Balls
text: The Franklin Ball Maintenance Kit helps me be a go-to grandpa when my toddlers have problems with ball deflation.  I have more serious inflators but smaller play balls are best inflated with this hand-pump system.  The included plastic pouch keeps things all together between uses.  The needles have different air delivery openings and the flexible couple might help (and can't hurt) in a variety of situations.  Many excellent reviews point to the value of the pressure gauge in the kit:  this, alone, would justify a purchase.

title: LOVE These; LIKE Many Other Grippers
text:
I LOVE this set in comparison to the many other grip exercisers I have used over the years and LIKED. I use grip exercisers to relieve tension, to maintain forearm and wrist and finger strength and to work finger joints and tendons. Just in the last three months I have purchased and used (and reviewed for Amazon customers) Theraband graduated twist bars, graduated 'egg' grip and finger exercisers and now these. In the past I have made regular use of Theraband's silicone band powered frame grippers, the spring-powered 'pliers' type grippers and the brass instrument-type finger tip plunger exercisers. Shoppers will get satisfactory results from any of these options provided they are made by a quality manufacturer.

I agree with another reviewer that a choice of one of these Iron Crush grippers is easy to 'take along' in a pocket or to pull out of a desk for workday use where the mind and eyes are occupied and the hands are free. The Chinese silicon is of good quality and, due to differences in formulation, each ring does have a noticeable difference in resistance. Cleaning/sanitizing these rings is easily done. Differences in resistance hold up after each ring has been 'warmed up' by repeated use. Just like with dumbbells, start with the lowest resistance for a few reps and move up! Since I'm also offering comparisons, the silicone eggs offer beginners' graduated resistance and this set picks up where they leave off. These will not 'snap' like the rack-mounted silicone band exercisers. I often have to replace one or another band unexpectedly. As an exercise suggestion, take the 50 lb. resistance ring and link the fingers of both hands and do a compression exercise by pressing your palms together. This is a more practical use of these devices than finger 'extension' exercises suggested on the packaging. Guys and Gals with normal hands will have difficulty fitting more than two fingers and a thumb in the doughnut hole on these items!

title: Our Go-To Barbells
text: I lead a strength and balance class for active seniors and the weight portion of our routine led me to York hex coated dumbells in this very usable 5 pound weight. An 'Old Fellow' myself, I started by buying these for myself and then I bought two for the class and then people in our community started to move up a bit in weight resistance...and we needed more!  I love the positive knurled grip handles.  I have medium-sized hands for a man...these work for small and large hands equally well.  Big-handed guys seem to feel they would like a 'beefier' grip. Shoppers will get 'pro'-style equipment in a high quality package.  The hex design means I can grab two to provide ten pounds of resistance...or than I can move two in each hand to pick up after class...or that the weights stay put on our weight rack.  I even like the 'fresh from the package' carbon rubber smell!  We are 'into' santitization in our complex and these are easily sprayed and wiped down with our go-to sanitizer.  These really beat the textured vinyl/polymer light weight units we have in our rack---those are grey and grungy and difficult to clean.

title: Hand Exerciser Also Has Play Value
text: As I have been aging it has been difficult to maintain hand and finger strength/circulation.  I began with tennis balls(too large), moved to therapy putty(a bit messy); then to rubber band resistance hand grips and finger tip trumpet-key like exercisers and on to these eggs (just right for medium-size hands.)  The blue egg offers moderate resistance, the red offers easy resistance and the yellow offers light resistance. With this style of product I can do both grip and individual finger strengthening exercises.  The gel eggs are textured a bit for grip and they feel comfortable in the hands.  They are washable.  As a bonus, toddlers love them and treat them like Easter Eggs!

title: Seniors: Not Just For Rehab!
text: I love this flexbar for its application to different joint exercises as part of an everyday exercise regimen.  My wife and I were noticing difficulty in opening jars and I have been having cervical neck pain.  My orthopedic consultant recommended progressive exercise and my physical therapist pointed to this type of device  as being useful for wrist strengthening and flexibility as well as for other uses in mobilizing muscle groups.  How these types of exercises work is illustrated in a handy multi-page manual that now comes with this device.  I had not imagine the range ways to use such a simple flexar.  I worked my way through a bunch of different ones and they each had value.  Many reviewers seem to be looking for a quick-fix rehab application for this tool and they ignore the value of progressive resistance training.  We are not all at the same start point in strength or in a recovery program.  "Guys" are always looking to jump back in the middle with poor results or prolonged injury time.  I've had it proven to me that it pays to start slow and be patient.  Having worked on my wrists and fingers with other Theraband devices, I moved up to the green flexbar recently.  Time will tell if my over-55 joints will benefit from the even higher blue level of resistance.

title: Necessary to Operate My Gold and Silver Lighters
text: Red Dupont Gas refills are necessary in order to keep enjoying my classic ST Dupont lighters.  A key feature is that the cartridge needs to match the threading on the fill valve in the base of the lighter.  A key drawback is that there always seems to be a little gas that is left in each cartridge after the lighter has taken all it can hold.  Other Dupont lighter families use different refills so check for compatibility before purchasing.

title: All the Cooler Many Shoppers Will Use

The new chest has a tighter seal around the rim and a more positive rotary lock. True, this cooler is not designed for bouncing around a truck bed. title: Therapist-quality, Latex-Free Excercise Bands for Gentle Progress

Still, it works fine and there is a noticeable, if slight degree of increased resistance in this band over the green band just below it in the therapy series. I'm just one recovering hip transplant patient so buying a whole 25 some yards of this might have been 'overkill.' I enjoy using stretchy bands and therapy putty to strengthen and improve the flexibility of my hands and wrists. The process is restful and yields gentle improvement that I didn't get from hand weights or the machines at the gym or rehab center. At the same time, it is more convenient for me to use different lengths of band than it is to grab a long band closer to the middle for some exercises and farther out on the ends for others. Each section is long-lasting but I still feel that I will want to use more lengths as time goes by for maintenance purposes.

The LATEX-FREE part of this is very significant. Some people react to latex or to the powder that was applied to the band material to keep it from sticking together. I did not find this non-latex formula to be irritating.

title: Some Pros and Cons for you to take into account before purchasing.
text:
Let me start by saying I have been lifting in gyms for about 30 years and even qualified for Nationals as bodybuilder when I was 27....I'm 43 now. Still going at it strong but wanted a home calf raise machine and an alternative to barbell squats. I've probably lifted on just about any and all commercial grade equipment out there. Here are my thoughts on this piece of equipment and why I only gave it 3 stars. I hope it helps.

1) As others have stated...there are no directions and let's be serious...how irritating is that? If you can't bother giving your customer assembly instructions how much can you really honestly care about your customer? Just my two cents.

2) The contents are ill packaged and yes, I understand that Fed Ex shakes the boxes. But both boxes looked like they were packaged by a 5 year old. Just a total mess...screws...bolts...washer...thrown around in the box with shredded styrofoam and broken tight downs. I can't possibly see how any shipper could have created this total mess. Again, extreme sloppiness leads me to believe there is a lack of concern for the person receiving it.

3) 50% of the reason I purchased this piece of equipment was for the standing calf raise, my local gym only has the seated calf raise. I've had this exact same piece of equipment before by PowerTec....and I wasn't sure how I was going to feel about the rounded calf raise platform versus the flat one that power tec made and every other commercial grade piece of gym equipment uses. Now I know why they don't use a rounded platform. U have less contact material with your foot when you raise up. Is it the end of the world? No...but I'm just not a huge fan of the rounded platform. I much more prefer the standard flat platform that feels natural and more comfortable on the feet.

4) The step up from floor level to the calf raise machine is a bit hairy once you get some heavy weight on the machine...3 to 4...45's on each side. I wish the platform was designed differently so all that weight is not stacked onto on leg and your back is torqued when you step up. Commercial grade equipment is made in such a way that the platform is directly under you....you start on the calf platform...you don't load the weight and then step up. This machine is set up so that in order to have the weight directly on your shoulders...where it needs to be....you are standing one step behind the calf platform. Then in order to do the calf raise...you have to step up onto the platform...one leg at at time with all the weight on your back and one leg down...and one leg taking a step. Not good in my opinion.

5) The angle of the squat. Ahh...its okay....makes you feel like you are doing a deep squat but in reality even a deep squat on this machine is not even a parallel squat. If you have someone else do a deep squat and watch their lower leg in relation to their upper...you will see that the deepest squat on this machine is still a high squat in reality. Your leg is simply at a different angle and gives the false sense that you are performing a deep squat...when in fact you are not.

Will this take the place of a regular squat?

Yes, and No.

If you are a gym rat and you perform squats correctly than this piece of equipment will never take the place of or produce the same results.

If you are like 95% of the guys in the gym that never ever reach parallel when they squat because they were too busy stacking on the weight instead of learning good form at the beginning...than yes...this piece of equipment will keep you squatting a bit high and allow you to keep stacking the weight on and the ego flying high.

Can you get a good calf workout on this machine?

Absolutely. Even with the rounded platform that I do not like...you can still get a great calf workout.

Would I buy it again?

I'm on the fence with this one. I wouldn't cry if it was removed from my home...but I wouldn't send it back either.

I use the squat portion in addition to my leg workout....not as my primary piece of equipment...and I think that is what it is good for...and addition to regular squats....leg press...lungs...extensions...curls...etc. etc.

Hope my review helped somone.

JMO. Happy Hunting!!

Update: Nov 5th, 2018. I was cocking the crossbow yesterday and cross-string came off, what happened is the C-Clip that holds the right cam pulley on was missing and the shaft rode up allowing the bottom pulley to rotate and the small string retaining eye to let loose. I looked in the box when I got home and the C-Clip was under a piece of cardboard. This is not part of buyers assembly and is handled by the manufacturer, so pay close attn. to both Cam Pulleys and make sure there are C-Clips in place x 4 (1top and 1 bottom on each side). A new crossbow was sent with no problems, I'll only miss 2-3 days of hunting. There were no injuries, thank God.

The new crossbow was sent and arrived fast. I still give this crossbow 5 stars, given the price. This one had all c-clips intact and is functioning perfectly. Nov. 11, 2018

title: Excellent EDC
text:
3-20-18: Well after years of searching for a great budget EDC knife, I found the RAT and she's ah beauty. Aus-8 sharper then sin and easy to maintain. Secure lock - very secure. Comfortable handle with good grip, jimping, good blade design for skinning during hunting season. 90 degree spine that works well with Mischmetal ignition sticks. I lubed the pivot with some lucas gun oil after cleaning it out with WD-40. This knife will see daily use 365 days a year so I will report back.

3-27-18: I really like this knife! After a week of clear-cutting I've had plenty of opportunities to test this knife out. It removes slivers well, very mild sharpening once (it went back to razor sharp quickly as AUS 8 does). stabbed knife into log so I could process some shavings from a cherry stick for a fire (by pulling stick across fixed edge). The usual opening of packages. All duties performed so far were done so with complete ease, the knife just feels naturally pre-apt to work from the ease of opening to the balance, weight and action.

No complaints so far!

title: High Quality, narrow handle awkward for big hands.
text:
I'm giving the knife 5 stars, although I personally do not like it due to it's very narrow handle. It would be a great knife for a child or lady or man with small hands. The quality of the blade and handle are very good (the AUS 8 blade came Perfectly sharpend with no burr detected along edge, the lock is very secure, and the thumb flicker works ok (to open this knife the quickest push down and up parallel with the handle on the thumb button, it takes some practice. Better engineered knives with this style of opening typically have the pressure to open follow the same tangent as the groove in which the thumb peg rests, on this knife that will result in a failed or partial opening of the blade.

I ordered the larger RAT 1, it will be interesting to see how the functional geometry of that knife is. I'm on the hunt for a new EDC (which I rely on heavily in my line of work).

title: Not bad but with minor issues
text:
Actually, I think this is a good buy. It has a piezo ignition that works. It puts out plenty of heat. Although I don't envision cooking on it I can see where it would handle the task ok but I would be worried about boilovers putting out the flame. This thing puts out a ton of heat and is sufficiently adjustable in output.

Pros. It easily lights. Puts out sufficient heat and does so at 360 degrees all around. It is larger than expected which I think is a good thing. The base seems stable. The output is adjustable.

Cons. The biggest fault I find is the warning on the outside of the heater which states "For Outdoor Use Only" when in fact the Title or Heading states, "AKUSAKO Camping Propane Heater - 2 In 1 Outdoor Portable Gas Heater & Stove Included Tent Heaters " Note it says "tent heater." So, now I am not so sure. It would likely be fine but I would not operate it indoors without a CO and Oxygen monitor, which I own anyway. It is not a good idea to operate any propane device in a tent without the monitors anyway.

The rubber feet (3) are all stripped out. The rubber feet screw through a fairly thin metal plate that was stripped out at the factory. Note that this can probably be easily remedied by using a slightly larger sheet metal screw instead of what appears to be a small wood screw, just don't overtighten.

title: Fantastic Buy
text: I use these, not as slip cork stops, but as a method of affixing a hopper dropper. I run my leader through the eye of the hopper. Do not tie to the eye. Feed the stopper onto the barb with the wire facing forward toward the eye of the hook. Pull about a foot of leader through the wire loop then pull the loop back through the stop which will pull the leader through the stop. I then tie on my dropper. This allows you to set the depth of the dropper simply by pulling the dropper up or down. Note that I use the small. The amount of tension on the line is controlled by the tippet size as well as the hook size of the hopper. The larger the diameter of the hook the smaller the tippet size that can be used. You just have to experiment for your needs. I find a size 8 hook and #5 tippet hold well. This is one of the best methods I have found for an adjustable  strike indicator.

title: Ok But Needs Improvement
text:
Ok but needs some design improvement. Just returned from a trout fishing vacation and used two of these on my trip. Both were for 10 foot rods. The case is actually pretty good considering the price. However, the tube should have some relief cut length wise (4" or so) into the top end to assist in removing the rod. The rod has to be removed straight out the back without any angle but the pouch itself interferes to some degree. A 4" or so notch cut out at the top end would facilitate easy removal. The little storage pouches on the sides might be a nice touch for some but to me they were an unnecessary nuisance. Also, a nice dense closed cell foam fly patch would be nice.

CAUTION: I broke an Orivs 10 foot rod right off the bat putting it in this case. I use this type of case so that I can pull the rod down into two pieces, keep the reel on with the leader and fly so that all I have to do is put it together the next pull over or stream. That is the point of having the reel pouch. When I placed the rod into the case, apparently the tip went into one compartment and the butt into another. When I pushed the r\od all the way in the line came tight against the compartments and snapped the very tip of the rod....My bad, but just a word of caution. I now make certain that both sections of rod go into ONE compartment.

title: Feels Great in The Hand... very comfortable grip.
text:
Just received my rod. Shipping was fast. Although I have not yet used this rod, the look and feel is awesome. It appears to have just the right amount of backbone yet has a fast tip. Very light and very comfortable in the hand. It has micro eyes near the tip. This rod feels as good as a lot of rods that are $100+. I have shopped hard for just the right rod and I think this is it.

I purchased this rod for drop shot fishing for bream or whatever else is stupid enough to bite. Drop shot fishing is my new passion. I have been killing the large bluegill using sonar to see them and then drop shot to them. Just like a video game....awesome. I can't wait to use this rod.

Update 5/26/2016: Fished this rod again yesterday with fantastic results. I was on some huge bream and chinquapin located in 13 feet of water around some deep structure. This rod has the perfect flex and perfect tip. With my set up the rod length couldn't be better for drop shotting.

UPDATE: 5/20/2016 Used the rod this a.m. on some really nice bream. They were in 10-13 feet of water. The rod is perfect. Easy to get your shot in the cone with the length being perfect. The action is ideal with perfect backbone and perfect tip action for a "just raise the rod" hook set. I love this rod. It has the most comfortable grip of any spinning rod I have used.

title: Not bad for the price.
text:
Haven't tried it out yet but seems wimpy. Almost doesn't stop shaking in your hand. Was hoping for more backbone and faster tip but for the cost you can't expect much. The rod is not bad looking with eyes that are nicely wrapped and smoothly epoxied. The handle is full cork and seems to be average quality natural cork.

I will be using this for bream and crappie fishing with an ultra light Shakespeare reel...so it might be a lot of fun. Quite sure it is to limp for drop shotting bream. Probably not sensitive enough with such loose action. I will update this after sticking a hook in a bream or two. I catch huge chinquapin and I am afraid they will have their way with me on this rod and 4# test line.

UPDATE: Ok....I got a chance to try this rod out yesterday on some monster bluegill (bull-a-gator) bream. Giant fail. Catching these large bream around stumps was virtually impossible as the rod was way to limp to allow much horsing. If you enjoy a micro-light fight this is the rod for you.....if you want meat in the boat....not so much.

I had a serious problem with them breaking even while tying on a fly, using extreme care in tightening the knot, making certain they were wetted etc. Almost all of them broke well below test. Examining them I also found that on some the beginning of the taper was an abrupt change...no taper or very little taper at all. Which I found to be really strange. I intend to continue using Umpqua products but I will be darn careful to try them again in smaller lots. I ended up throwing away at least 5 packs.

title: Worth the Extra Money...Awesome reel.
text:
I love this reel. I have had mine for over two years maybe three and the only problem I have had is the bail trip spring mechanism recently started hanging. Opened it and cleaned it out and oiled it...no problems now. I caution about removing the bail covers. A spring and rod can come out and it took some doing to get it back in. I had to get the schematic from Shimano. The easiest way to re-assemble is to put the rod and spring in its place at the rear of the compartment replace the chrome cover and then insert the spring shaft into the bail housing in the hole provided. Then put the bail in place and put in the screw. Really no big deal but others not mechanically inclined may want to just send it off to have it completely cleaned.

This reel casts a mile due to the aero line wrap system that prevents line from becoming entrapped under other line. The retrieve and reeling is smooth as butter. The knob has bearing so there is no dragging whatsoever.

I fish this reel in salt and fresh water and have had no issues due to saltwater use. It is certified by Shimano to be saltwater safe.
I will be ordering my second one soon.

text:

NOTE: I will put the Coleman on a shelf in remembrance of it saving my life one time...literally.

Note: This item apparently ships from China so it takes some time to arrive but the wait is worth it. The little orange box is about 3 in. tall and maybe an inch and a half thick and two inches wide....very small and compact.

UPDATE: 11/28/2016
Fishermen. Put one of these in your tackle box or boat. If your hands get wet while it is cold just hit the piezo starter and it is up and running providing life saving heat. After your fingers have warmed ....a turn of the dial and it is off and cool in no time flat. I wouldn't go out in boat without one....you just never know.

UPDATE: I just received an additional 4 of these stoves to give to friends and family. They were blown away by how fine they were. I just ordered 4 more to give as a "no particular reason gift"

title: I love this style of stringer!
text: This style of stringer is really the best kind to use if you want to keep your fish alive and well while you are fishing. The nylon versions pile the fish on top of each other, and it literally suffocates them and you end up with a lot of dead fish to clean. (if anyone reading this knows anything about fishing and actually eats the fish they catch like I do....they know that this is kind of a bad thing. makes the meat taste all funky) with this stringer, you can easily pierce the lower lip of the fish (do NOT put it through their gills as this will kill them quicker than anything! just a little tip for those who may not have known this) it will keep them alive pretty much until the time you clean them depending on where and how you transport them to the cleaning station. But essentially it's a good all around stringer that will serve you well if used properly. they DO tend to rust if you let the water dry on them over time especially if used in salt water conditions, but they are pretty inexpensive over all so easy to replace as needed. I will often use this in unison with the nylon stringers to kind of extend the stringer a bit for when I am fishing from the shore as it gives the fish more room to swim around and stay active. but it is a good one for clipping to the side of the kayak or canoe. just don't use it on a motor boat. title: Twin size review with a heads up
text: There were great expectations—but, for the twin size, there are troubling issues. Please know that “all” the initial inflation and use directions were followed to the letter. However, over the first few days, though it didn’t lose any air—it did literally lose its shape. It went from a true rectangular twin mattress shape to an ever widening oval that easily added 6-plus inches to its width (see photos). The expected bump inflation was only needed after a week. I’m 5’8” at 160 lbs. so my weight couldn’t be the cause for this twin air mattress going hugely egg shaped. Only sleeping was done on the mattress—no other activity. What’s more, when you roll atop the mattress you can feel the column supports popping up—strange. The King Koil company gets a 100% fantastic customer service rating. They quickly sent a replacement mattress but it did precisely the same thing—it became a huge oval blob shape. The simple fact is, the lower priced air mattresses I’ve used on a daily basis were generally better. Finally, I rarely write critical reviews—however, in this case it was felt that a caution needed to be raised. Please let me know if you’re having a like problem with the TWIN model of this King Koil air mattress.

title: Winner.
text:
Suffice to say that I have a medical condition that requires me to not get too hot. Bad things happen and they are very obvious, and not in my head. I can die if I get overheated. I just have to live with it. I also live and often work outside in one of the hottest and most humid parts of the country. Oh, and I'm not rich so I can't just hire people to do my bidding and stay inside all day. The clash of these issues has caused me to try numerous gadgets to stay cool and, honestly, this one works the best (and is one of the cheapest though it could be cheaper).

Chilling vests are ridiculously expensive and marginally effective.

"Snap towels" are a joke. Don't waste your money.

You need something with ice in it, people. And the plastic ice cubes don't work, either, and here's why: real ice melts and makes your shirt cool, too, and lasts LONGER, and is cheap.

So far this towel has worked great. I've used it a dozen times or so in very harsh conditions and bought another as a backup. You buy two dollars worth of bag ice, put it in a cooler, and you have at least two days of continuous personal cooling. The towel is long enough to fit around my big neck.

My niece tried it and told her dad she's never mowing the yard again without one. My daughter has never mowed the yard so I'm still astonished about that on two levels.

So tskile it from someone whose life and vision actually depends on staying cool (I know, sounds crazy, but it is true) : if you live in a HUMID area, this is the best balance of price and cooling you can get.

I am so serious about this product I left without it on me day and drive twenty miles back to get it, then twenty miles back to where I realized I'd forgotten it. Now that's a testimony.

title: Image is not the product...
text:
So the image on this ad is obviously not the product for sale. 6+ months after verifying this with the seller, the wrong image is still in place. Seller is great though. Ordered 2 of these in April '21 and finally got around to fitting them in October '21 only to find out one of the cables was a 20' cable. Even though I was well out of return window, TX Parts LLC stood behind their sale and sent me the correct part and a label to return the wrong one.
As for the part itself, it is the correct part for my 1986 Mercury 9.9hp outboard, but the round plastic cylinders that lock into place inside the engine are slightly off in their shape. The small cylinders in the new cables are the same overall length as the originals, but the new ones have flat ends and the original parts have a slight dome end to them. Due to this, the new cables will not lock into place. However, a quick sanding of the edges of the cylinder to make it a dome shape and it fits perfectly. Even with this small hassle it is well worth it for the price. I would buy these cables again and I would definitely buy from TX Parts LLC again.

title: Not perfect overall, but a great spring assisted knife
text:
So I'll start by saying, I *love* the opening function of this knife. I have, and have had, other knives with the thumb post for "easy opening" but they never work as well as I had hoped. This thing is quick and opens fully every time with the slide button so I don't have to stop and put down whatever I have in my hand to pull out the knife and open it. It's also scary sharp new. I just hope that it will hold that edge through most everyday tasks and later, when needed, be easy to put that edge back on.
That said, this thing is a beast. It is both heavy and thick. I don't know if it is the internal mechanics causing both of these but it would be awesome if they could cut both the thickness and weight down by about 1/3. The heft in your hand is nice until that has been riding in your pocket all day.
All said it's still one of the best knives I've owned and anyone looking for a knife that is easy to open with one hand, should consider this.

Update 18 months later:
Still loving this knife. I have the $25 suction cup knife sharpener from Amazon and with that I have kept an edge on on this blade that shaves hair off my hand. Everyone who uses this thing comments on the knife and the sharpness. The mechanical opening of the blade can be a little much for some of my friends who are women, but they can open it manually so they still appreciate the knife in general. I still wish they could shave the size & weight of this down, but until that exists, this is the "opening assisted" knife to get.

text:
