title: Will not work with TLR-2G light.  Fits G21 Gen4
text:
ORIGINAL REVIEW: This DOES fit a G21 Gen4 setup. When I got the package it states that it won't fit the TLR-2G. My goodness, why couldn't this info be shared during the product description here or the manufacturers website? I really needed this to work because my TLR-2G doesn't stay activated after a few rounds of fire with the regular cumbersome reach and toggle switch.

UPDATE 07/28/14: After having to sell my TLR-2G, I picked up the standard red-laser TLR-2HL. The directions are a little lacking but I was able to figure it out. Fit is very tight, but that is how you want it so the switch doesn't fly off during use.

TIPS: The push pin for the original battery door will need to be removed. If you are looking into the battery compartment, you will be pushing the RIGHT end of the pin towards the left. Once you have about an 1/8 inch of exposed pin, you will need to use some needle-nosed pliers to pull it out the rest of the way. Save the pin for later use just in case.

Here is where the included directions are a little lacking. The thin metal 1/4 inch wide clamp that held the original door down is NOT to be removed. You will be using that same clamp to clamp down the new hinge-less remote. It took me a few minutes to realize this. I was getting ready to take the clamp completely off via another push pin. I'm glad I didn't. Now, loosen the rail clamp on the light as wide as you can, trust me on this. Insert the trigger end first, then the light's rail clamp to your Glock's rail.

Single press and it lights up. Double tap and you get strobe. At least that what seemed to be working for me.

Like another reviewer shared, ff you have big hands, yes, you will notice that your fingers are slightly off natural position. This is a trade-off I'm willing to make so that I am not toggling with the original switch with my off hand. I am not a LEO, this is strictly for home defense use. I'd rather keep my off hand supporting my shooting hand or holding an extra mag if needed.

title: "MTB Specific" means Micro Floor Drive HV (High Volume)
text:
Read good reviews of the Lezyne Micro Floor Drive HV on [...] and figured I'd give it a try. My previous hand pump was too tiring on the arms when pumping up 2.2" tires on the trail. I needed a small floor pump version to carry with me in my CamelBak on my mountain bike rides. The pump I received weighed in at 210g. The mounting bracket was another 18g which I won't need. With my previous hand pump I could easily fit 2 fingers on each side of the T shaped handle for more grip. The Micro Floor Drive HV handle is quite small and I can only fit 1 finger on each side of the handle which feels awkward, but since I can now use 2 hands to press down it's not too bad. Overall I'm happy with this product, but wish it was a bit smaller in length and width.

Pros:
+ Feels very solid
+ Very nice screw on Presta AND Schrader valve
+ Can use like a floor pump
+ Made for pumping MTB tires, pumps air fast

Cons:
- Longer and wider than a typical hand pump
- Small T shaped handle
- Somewhat heavy, weight 228g (210g pump + 18g mounting bracket)

UPDATE (11/5/2014)
I've been using this pump for almost 4 years now and have had zero problems pumping tires with Presta and Schrader valves. 100 pumps will get a 26 x 2.0 tire to a comfortable pressure (I estimate just below 30 psi). 120 pumps will yield a very firm tire. The foot peg makes pumping a breeze. I've updated the rating from 4 to 5 stars and added measurements below.

title: an "aye dee" waiting for a place to happen?
text:
I got this as a gift for a glock owner. but I did do a bit of evaluation on this product.

it is a good minimalist "holster" in that it protects a Glocks trigger. but I noticed that there are some not so good features of this device.

The web site of the manufacture says to put the device on the weapon, then work the slide to charge the weapon. when you "draw" the weapon, it is ready to go, BUT when you need to re-holster, you then have to drop the magazine, and eject the round, then put the magazine back into the weapon, then re-insert the device on the gun. then charge the weapon again.

seems like a lot of work to just put the weapon back, when a small holster would accomplish that without all the working of the action of the weapon.

another aspect is that the weapon has no protection of its sights with this "holster". I have some fiber optic sights that I would not like to have rubbing against clothing when using this type of holster. something to think about.

another problem would be if the weapon slipped down inside your trousers while using this device alone, you would then have a weapon, charged, and hanging upside down, pointed at your upper body. the weight of the gun could make it "unholster" itself if you were engaged in any physical activity. not a pleasant thought.

Even though I am an experienced carrier, I will stick with traditional and IWB holsters.

title: A Best Buy!
text:
Believe the reviews that say this is terrific! I had some concerns about the small receiver shaft wobbling in my 2-inch hitch, but Allen Sports has really figured it out with their "wobble bolt." My rig is tight and vibration free.

From the pictures it looked like the plates on the hitch were plastic shims, but they are well-designed (removable) plates screwed to the main shaft. And their design -- again -- contributes to the rigidity of the frame when mounted.

I mounted this rack in less than 10 minutes, threw on the bikes and drove 700+ miles without any issues whatsoever. Bikes arrived without a scratch and as secure as they were when I left the driveway.

There are only three factors of this hitch that I'll point out:
1) It is an inch or two higher than it needs to be, so the bikes are in the rear window of my SUV. (This could be an adjustable setting of the rack if Allen Sports (or I, I suppose) would drill a couple of different holes in the upper piece of the rack.)
2) It does trigger the proximity sensors in my rear bumper. So I had to dig through the owner's manual to figure out how to disable that.

As others have mentioned, the frame of the bike will bang on the vertical section of the rack if not attended to. I wrapped a thin sheet of foam rubber around the upright and secured it with some black duct tape I had handy. You can't even see the pad, and it cushions the frame of the first bike when tied down with a bungee cord.

My favorite feature of this rack is the tilting mechanism. It makes it trivially easy to move the bikes out of the way for access through the tailgate.

Overall, one of my best Amazon purchases this year. I've compared Yakima and Thule racks at 3-5+ times the price and can't find anything in them that is superior to this one.

title: Full disclosure...it hasn't snowed yet
text:
Amazon keeps asking me to review this but it hasn't snowed yet! I'm going to give you my first impressions though because this is an awesome sled!

I was shocked when I opened it and realized how sturdy this sled is. While I can't attest to its sleddy-ness I can say that this thing is legit. It's not your average plastic sled, that's for sure. I live in a very cold climate where we can get lots of snow so we have plenty of experience with sleds.

This one is worth every penny for a few reasons. If you don't live in a cold climate it might not make much sense to spend this much on something that you might only use for fun. However, this sled has the potential to be very utilitarian because of how sturdy and heavy duty it is.

You could use this to bring groceries in from the car, if you laid down something to protect the seat, you could use it for firewood, you could use it to move just about anything around you need in the snow because of how large it is and how thick the plastic is. I like that it's smaller than our toboggin that we have for the snowmobiles but it's not so small that you can't use it for something other than sledding. Plus, it's easy to move around manually. Some utilitarian sleds are really only good when pulled by a snowmobile or a 4 wheeler which is great when you need them but sometimes you just need to have something you can move around by yourself.

title: Test for leaks!
text:
Full disclosure, our first cooler leaked out of the plug and had to be returned. I highly recommend testing this cooler for it’s watertight seal before your return period runs out. We literally filled our second cooler to the brim with water and let it sit for 2 days to test the plug and I am happy to say it didn’t leak!

As for it’s ability as a cooler, we ave been impressed. My husband filled it to the brim before heading off from Montana to Yosemite. We did everything you’re supposed to do, we chilled it the night before loading it, we used a combination of block ice and frozen 9x13 casseroles along with non-frozen perishable items but we filled it completely full.

He left it in a hot car for the entire day he worked before taking off to Nevada, staying the night and finally arriving in CA the next day. He said the ice was just starting to melt hence, finding the leaking cooler. He said there was a ton of ice left and most of the frozen items were still frozen.

We like the size and shape, we find that the square shape vs rectangular fits in the back of our small SUV better. We also love the tote! It’s extremely heavy and so handy for packing and moving stuff around

title: Purchased for college
text:
I had a hard time finding a pack to replace my Jansport Penelope 34. I needed something at least that size or bigger and that proved more difficult than expected. I had no idea my pack would be considered so large, it barely fit everything I needed as it is! I only gave it 4 stars because it has only a very small pouch for school supplies. While I understand that it isn't necessarily built for a student, it does have a pouch for a laptop so I guess I assumed it would be more business/student friendly.

In any case, it's large enough but that space is much taller than it is wide. So far, it seems to fit everything I need. I put 2 medium sized text books, 2 spiral bound single subject notebooks, a novel sized book, a 13'' mac in the laptop sleeve and a spiral bound textbook with room to spare. Empty, it's much lighter than my JanSport pack which I appreciate.

It seems to be very well made but I wish it had some of the features of their other packs like the pockets on the waist strap or shoulder straps. It'd be nice to have my phone in front of me instead of in the pack itself but I guess that's what pockets are for. There are 2 stretchy water bottle pockets that seem to accommodate large bottles but they are hard to reach and impossible to put back without taking the pack off. At least that's what I've found out carrying a 1 liter sized bottle today.

The color is gorgeous! I love, love, LOVE it! It's a very deep aqua/turquoise color that's not overly bright or obnoxious. It's seriously one of the nicest looking packs I found in this price range when shopping and I looked at everyone and I mean EVERYONE! I spent about 2 days doing research and this was one of the best deals for the most volume out there. Overall, I think most students would be happy with it but it might be considered very large if you don't pack your books around all day. I carpool so I get dropped off at school in the morning and don't leave until early evening. I need to take all my books, workout clothes, food etc... So this pack still might be a little tight for all that but we'll see.

UPDATED 08/28/14

The bag has held up extremely well. I questioned how the elastic pockets on the front and sides would hold up and they seem to be just fine. After having it for a year I have to say the shape is frustrating. It's too tall and narrow so it wastes too much space. I find myself having to stack things on top of my books to take full advantage of the size of the bag. Other than that, it's been comfortable, kept my stuff dry on rainy days and still looks new! I'm glad I'm graduating in December because I'd probably want to buy another bag and I don't think my husband would appreciate that very much ;-)

title: Simple, Reliable Basic Wood-Stick Matches
text:
This is my second box of these basic, old fashioned wood-stick matches and I love them. They are super handy to have around and I use them for everything - from lighting candles, to starting the barbecue, lighting pilot lights, bathroom odor elimination and everything you can think of where striking a match is needed.

They are reliable - every single match in the box easily lit and I don't think I experienced a single failure. The safety feature of striking on the box prevents these matches from being used inappropriately because they won't ignite if struck on most surfaces. They actually need to be in contact with the striking surface of the box in order to catch fire. On my first box, I worried that the striking strips on the sides of the box wouldn't last long enough for every match, but they held up through the whole box and had some power leftover when all the matches had been used.

I am super-satisfied with these matches! Old fashioned wood matches are one of those low-tech basics that every household needs!

title: Love The Bike!  WORTH. EVERY. PENNY!!!
text:
This is a great bike for working out. I have bad knees and so am limited in the types of exercise I can safely do. Swimming is OK once per week, but the chlorine gets to me and I don't like doing it more than that. Rowing is OK but it doesn't give me much of a lower body workout. The fancy electronic stationary bikes at the gym are fine for legs, but it is a waste of time for the upper body. Elliptical machines give a nice full body workout, but my knees won't tolerate much of that. Resistance training is also good but only once or twice per week. Pilates, Yoga and stretching are great exercises and have their place but they don't fill the need for cardio. Walking, Running, and Stair steppers are absolutely out of the question for me. So, my personal favorite form of exercise is the Dual-Action Stationary Bike for a well rounded workout that gets my heart pumping, uses all of my limbs, and puts absolutely no pressure on my knees.

For 30 years, I have enjoyed an old time Schwinn Airdyne Comp which served me well. It has preserved my health by keeping my handicap from making me hopelessly sedentary. But for the past year or so I could see the end of the line coming when my old faithful Schwinn started making unusual noises and shuddering in a strange way. Much to my surprise, I couldn't find anyone who could work on it. No one could get parts for it, no one even knew how it was put together. Even Schwinn no longer makes these and they do not support repairs of a bike that they no longer produce. I kept my Airdyne going for as long as possible, but the day finally arrived when I knew that I had done my last ride on "old Faithful". I was forced to look for a new bike.

Imagine my dismay when I set out to find a new bike and there was NOTHING that even remotely measured up to my beloved Airdyne Comp! Everything was flimsy. Everything was plastic. I even tried out one of the new-fangled Airdynes in the store and it actually collapsed with me in the saddle! Yikes! To tell the truth, I was scared that I might not find a worthy successor to the bike I had come to know and love. Then, I was researching bikes online and reading as many reviews as I could find, when one reviewer mentioned that he had returned his bike for a refund and spent the necessary bucks for and Assault Air Bike. I immediately googled that term and was delighted to find a bike that looks like the younger, cooler, and more hip granddaughter of my old, worn out Schwinn! I ordered it immediately!

It came today and I am in love! If possible, it is even better than the old Airdyne that served me so well. It was really, REALLY fast and easy to assemble because of the clearly presented video that is included in the ad on this page. Within 30 minutes, my new bike was up and running and I had my first workout. The ONLY negative is that the seat of the Assault Air Bike is atrociously painful! I am not sure why such seats are made, but by the time I finished my hour ride, I was weeping in pain. For awhile, I was regretfully considering that I might have to send the new bike to Amazon for a refund. Then, as I looked longingly at my old Airdyne Comp and dreamed about former days of riding in the comfort of the wide, cushy Schwinn seat, it dawned on me that I could probably ditch that nasty instrument of torture that came with the Assault, and replace it with my old fave, the Schwinn Airdyne Seat! Yay! Within 10 minutes, my new bike was just as comfy as the old, and I was so inspired that I indulged in a second, oh-so-comfy spin!

Some of the great features of the Assault that make it a step beyond the old Airdyne is the way the seat adjusts not only to height, but also to length. This gives a great custom fit to my body. I also learned very quickly that the onboard computer is much more complete than my old Comp and gives me great choices for incorporating HIIT training, which is just the perfect compliment to my new-found Paleo lifestyle. The new Assault computer is a little bit different in the way it counts calories, but that is not a problem for me, since I don't measure calories burned, but only time, distance, and heart rate. A few things are different that I wish they had kept but those things are minor. All in all, it is a worthy successor to my old Airdyne.

So. I purchased my Schwinn when I was 30 years old, and now I am 60. If the Assault gives me the same amount of years that I got from the Airdyne, I will be 90 by the time I need to buy yet another bike. Do you guys think the Assault will still be around by then, or should I just go ahead and purchase a back-up Assault Bike just in case? ;-)

title: Very Useful Device
text:
I am surprised at how functional this little gadget is. My smartphone fits right into the protective case and the tiny speakers plug into my phone's headset jack. I can play music or talk on the phone.

* One thing that is especially nice for me is that it holds my phone securely in place and zips shut. I like that because I have one of those phones with a slide-out keyboard - making the rubberized protective case an awkward fit, and the protective case that fits my phone will not stay on. I have dropped my phone several times without any protection and I am surprised that it hasn't broken. This case solves that problem, by containing the entire phone zipped in. It is VERY protective and secure.

* Another thing I like is that the speakers (though small) have a surprisingly good sound. I can listen to music or audio books easily, as long as there is no loud noise around to drown out the sound. This is especially pleasing to me because my phone speakers are not really loud enough to hear much and I have a lot of trouble with my bluetooth device. Since the audio is not wireless and plugs directly into the headset jack, it really simplifies my listening experience.

* Additionally, the speaker jack is not confined to a cell phone. My laptop had terrible sound and when I want to give it a boost, I plug this little device into my computer's headset jack and it gives me just the amount of volume I need without having to mess with bulky speakers.

The negatives are:

* This case is larger than some people would like. I don't mind it, but if you like to carry your cell phone in your pocket, you will not be able to do that while the phone is in this case. It fits nicely into a purse, though.

* The audio uses 2 AA batteries and does not interface with your phone battery. The case cannot be recharged or plugged in, but you will need to continually replace batteries. So far, I have had this case for a week and use it constantly. It still has the original two batteries that I put into it. Your phone will need to be recharged separately from the audio case.

* If you use your phone for other functions besides simply listening to music or talking, they you have to take it out of the case. When secured in this case, the phone is not accessible except for the audio and for answering calls. You will not be able to make calls, use navigation, check email, etc, unless you take your phone out of the case. Again, this isn't a problem for me, but a lot of people like to have their phone immediately accessible for all functions.

* While the sound is perfectly adequate for inside a car or indoors, I think it might be a challenge to hear it well outdoors. This is a SMALL case wirh SMALL speakers - think old fashioned transistor radio. This is NOT a boombox! ;-) If I want to listen to music outdoors, I use headphones. This functions well if I am driving, sewing, or doing dishes, etc.

All in all, I am getting a lot of use from this device. I really love it and don't know how I ever got along without it. I can see how it might not serve everyone's needs but it is great for mine.

title: The good, the bad, and the "still-to-be-seen..."
text:
These were our family's first Combat Sports brand gloves. It's kind of hard to explain but these gloves kind of ride up instead of staying put, and that is not only distracting but dangerous. I guess it could be a sizing thing. The Regular size fit two of my boys and my own hands. They felt good and solid on, firmly fitting with only being the slightest bit restrictive. That's why it was surprising that in action the finger openings kind of shift around a tiny bit.

Besides that, the padding is thick and firm where it needs to be. None of us were fans of the strap that goes across the palm to go in between the thumb and index finger. The strap itself and the angle of it are good, but the material is scratchy, irritating, and too much of a distraction. Our conclusion is that we're going to see if a longer break-in period will make these Combat Sports gloves a better fit so we can get down to business when sparring. They will belong to one son, so we can see what they are like when they have the chance to belong to one person. We'll update this review in a few months to let you know how it went and how they are performing. Thanks for reading this review.

title: While most use this band for athletic purposes, we have a whole different use altogether.
text:
We have a whole different reason for using a band like this, and it doesn't involve any running or other strenuous activities. One of my children and I both have significant health problems, and debilitating fatigue. Using this band gives us more information to share with our doctors about our fatigue levels, sleep patterns, etc. It is an interesting piece of the puzzle to add to our other medical information. This can help our doctors to find ways to help us to cope better with the incredibly low energy levels and difficulty logging any decent kind of sleep.

I've read the many reviews that sing the praises of this band for athletic purposes, and that is wonderful. I just thought I'd share with you that it can also serve you well as a good chunk of information for your medical situation. I hope this helps someone and thank you for reading my review.

title: You say "outside summer game?"  I say "inside winter basement game!"  Break up the winter blues with this light-up dart game.
text:
Long dark winter days. Cabin fever. Snowed in. No activity. Kids climbing the walls. What to do...

We're all heading into the basement where we have collected fun games over the years, like an air hockey table, Foosball, electronic darts, an electronic basketball hoop....and now our new addition, the light-up lawn darts game. It is a blast in the basement (although we keep a little bit of lighting on). This is so much fun, and really adds a unique game to break up our wintertime boredom.

Here are a few tips that may help you.

1) We put a few streaks of glow-in-the-dark paint on the rings, to brighten them up a bit, and it worked wonderfully. We got this super bright green glow in the dark paint for about $10 here on Amazon and it worked great: [[ASIN:B00BD63C8W Ultra Green V10 Glow in the Dark Paint 1/2Oz]]

2) Don't give a second thought to replacing the batteries. It's easy. I buy all my replacement button batteries from Amazon. In fact, these lawn darts take the LR41 batteries, which you can get 10 of them from Amazon for about $6: [[ASIN:B000AQ7ME6 Maxell Watch Battery Button Cell LR41 AG3 192 Pack of 10 Batteries]]. Or if you want more, you can get 50 of them for about $13-14: [[ASIN:B0057ON2JA 50 Pack Maxell LR41 AG3 192 button cell battery "NEW HOLOGRAM PACKAGE "]] .

3) If you need replacement parts, which is honestly unlikely, as these things are sturdy as heck. And if you need information on replacement parts, you can email: replacementparts@franklinsports.com or you can call 1-781-341-5178.

Thanks for reading my review. I sure hope it helped you.

title: I love mine, and my family loved them as gifts!
text:
I have this exact same cooler from another team, and got this one as a gift for my cousin, who is a huge fan. This cooler is incredibly well-made and I'm thrilled that I got it! (I ended up buying everyone their favorite team's cooler in this same brand, and they were a huge hit over the holidays!)

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of quality extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can securely stash a few things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is wide, strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

Made by Coleman, like I said, and with lots of nice features, this high quality cooler is a must-have and a great gift. Check out the same cooler with other team logos. Just make sure you get the one like this one from "TLG8," to get the high quality one I just described. Thanks for reading my review. Hope it helped someone.

text:
We are a gaming family. Handhelds, consoles, phone apps...and it's really hard to get the kids motivated to go outside to get some exercise. When I saw this portable net, I thought it might be a great way to get the kids excited about playing outside.

When it arrived, I was so excited to see it's bigger than I thought, and it set up surprisingly easy. It took us about a half hour from start to finish, and would have been faster except that I wanted to use the opportunity to teach the kids how to follow the directions to assemble something. It went really well, they loved putting it together, and the whole family has had a blast using it. We've kicked the soccer ball around, mostly.

The kids called me out to play badminton and told me they had a special spot for me to stand. The little comedians put me right in front of the net so that all the missed birdies would at least be caught in the net!

Love this net, and since it's only spring, we're looking forward to using it all summer.

title: purse-handles, belt-loops, & gym bags!  Everyone in our family has one.
text:
As a busy mom on-the-go, this multi-purpose flashlight has come in handy so many times. I clipped it onto my purse when I got it, and thought it would basically be used "for emergencies." Wow. It ended up being so useful for everyday situations, too. When one of the kids got a splinter at a football game, we needed its nice bright light to see well enough to get the pesky splinter out. Of course, it always comes in handy for finding the right key in the dark and unlocking the door. When the light on our garage door opener died, we used this light to maneuver the obstacles in the pitch-black garage. At that point I bought a second one to keep in the car with the First Aid kit.

We used it to find the dog when he takes too long to come in. I used it to quickly signal my husband when he was loaded up with popcorn and couldn't find our seat at the movies! Then, at that point, I decided to just bite the bullet and buy a few more: one to put in our "tornado shelter" area of the basement because where we live the power goes out frequently with bad storms. Candles are OK for adults, but obviously not safe with small kids around, so I bought one for each child (which they promptly "customized" with strips of different color duct tape, so we know whose is whose! When the storms start to get bad, each child gets their Energizer light out, and if the lights go out, they click theirs on. They like to clip it on the belt-loop so they have constant light around them the whole time.

By the way, we also use rechargeable batteries all the time. One of the chargers we use is this one: [[ASIN:B003D7LHJU Rayovac Everyday-Use 4 Position AA/AAA Easy Charger with 2AA and 2AAA OPP Low Self Discharge NiMH batteries]]. It saves us a fortune in batteries, and we can use our Energizer Carabiner lights without worrying about chewing up batteries and cash.

UPDATE: September 27, 2012.
Absolutely LOVE these flashlights! It's been a year since I wrote the initial review, and they are holding up wonderfully, with STEADY use. I'm ordering more today, as I like to give them as gifts, and now I've put one next to every bed. Just a reminder, make sure you use the rechargeable batteries in them (takes 4 AAA batteries) to increase your savings. These buggers are so durable. Dropped numerous times, too. Just can't say enough about them. HIGHEST of recommendations. I only wish I'd found them years ago!

title: Super convenient, easy to use, reliable, and durable over many uses!
text:
Had no idea how much we needed an air pump like this till we actually had one to use! We have used this for the kids jump-o-lene [[ASIN:B000068DMD 71.5" x 40" Jump o Lene Jump n Gym]]for rafts and other pool toys, for inflatable mattresses when company visits. Never had one before, and we purchased it specifically for the Jump n Gym, but once we had it, we were shocked at how many times it came in handy!

What's great about it is that it has several different sized nozzles, so you can use it for so many things! Oh, and the fact that you can also use it to deflate stuff really makes life a lot easier! It's super-fast, and I can't
believe we went so long without it. Now that I've gotten used to just grabbing the pump when we
need something inflated or deflated, I can't imagine not having one.

We highly recommend this air pump. It has been reliable, durable, and very very convenient. By the way, it's not heavy and doesn't take up much space, so you can easily take it with you if you need to. Super-duper recommend it! ;)

EDIT: This pump is so user-friendly that our 5 year old can use it, under adult supervision for safety, of course! It is so handy to have around.

UPDATE, April 8, 2012. We still use this pump, it works great, & we've had no problems with it at all. I just read the comments that said this review must've been written by Intex. I'm just a mom in the Midwest. Not a company. LOL. And I'm kinda embarrassed.....does this mean I did too good of a job on the review, or I like the pump too much, or what? I get pretty excited about products that I like, & I'm passionate about sharing my experiences, good and bad, with my family, friends, and other people who might make the same purchase. I can understand why the people who wrote the comments thought I worked for the company, but I can assure you....I'm just a plain ole mommy. Thanks. And I hope my reviews are helpful to you.

title: Review after 16 months - fantastic bang for the buck and great support!
text:
[[VIDEOID:22f19394a4eb7cc9583d0dd8639034c0]] Finally coming back to review this bike, purely because of the fantastic support I received. I bought this bike to bridge a 2 month gap where I was going to be without my road bike, but we (wife and I) ended up using it up until now (~16 months). Usage is ~30 mins a day per person, almost every day, with...medium intensity? My wife and I are both ~140lbs for what it's worth.

Downsides are:
1) no electronics (cadence, resistance level indicator, etc)
2) The saddle wasn't great for us, but we swapped our own saddle in anyway
Upsides are:
1) Price
2) no electronics to break - yes, i listed that as a downside as well : )
3) dirt simple setup

After setting up, it did take a bit of tightening and tweaking here and there to get out all the kinks in terms of squeaks and whatnot, but this is to be expected with any bike IMO. Also worth noting that we both ride with noise cancelling headphones.

Product support story:
After a year and half of daily riding, we finally noticed a little bit of a clunk in the crank, that would happen as soon as weight shifted onto each pedal. Now, I had already gotten my money's worth out of this bike, but on a whim I decided to investigate a bit. I eventually discovered that the main weld on the axle was starting to crack (see photo/video). Figured it was worth a shot to see what product support would say, even though this isn't covered under warranty. What happened next blew my mind - support got back to me within one day, covered the part for me for FREE, and shipped it out immediately using FEDEX! I swapped the part in and all is well again.

I would absolutely buy this bike again, or any other Sunny bike.

title: For what it is, very nice

Me: Cranky, 75yo, ex-Marine that's done a lot of hiking, in my younger days, most everywhere.
This is a medium-small, very light weight, easily packable, occasional use pack. Seams are well sewn but single stitched (I will double stitch them). It is not designed for heavy loads nor day in, day out use. The zippers work smoothly and evenly. Nice details: Attachment rings halfway up the shoulder straps, height adjustable chest strap, attachment loops near the bottom of the back to work with the adjustable pole/compression straps half way up the sides or to tie on a a rolled raincoat, a pocket inside the main compartment for a water bladder (nonsense-if you really need such, this is the wrong pack for you), side mesh pockets for water bottle and my espresso thermos. Its attached (nice detail) zippered storage bag, inside the main compartment, makes a handy inside pouch for phone, PLB, first aid, etc. The material appears to be a ripstop nylon, fully lined, except the back, with taffeta nylon. No back padding but a thin piece of styrofoam from the trash or a sweater works. Covered zippers and fabric coating renders it water resistant to short, light rain (NO backpack is waterproof; use plastic bags). Beautiful aquamarine color. I like it. Again, for what it is.

title: Practicality and utility personified
text:
I have no need for the fighting knives, or pseudo-fighting knives, that predominate that seem to predominate in all the catalogs and websites. I was trained as a Marine, years ago, and so have enough knowledge of hand to hand combat to realize that to effectively fight with a knife requires years of training and practice. Besides, a folding knife for such purposes is nonsense.
What I required was a practical, everyday utility knife for town and country, the mall and the hunters camp. At first glance, I thought this knife a bit large for that purpose but it is actually perfect. The blade is a perfect combination of very hard but brittle steel, with superior edge holding abilities, for the edge and much tougher, flexible steel for the "backbone" supporting it. Of course, the Japanese have been doing this for centuries in their Samurai swords. Blade wide and thick enough for good practical function without excess that only adds to weight and provides little practical value. The grip fits the human hand ideally. It fits my hand (size 7.5-8 glove) perfectly. The thumb and forefinger "pinch" close together in their respective, appropriately shaped, knurled "notches" giving one a superior grip for slicing, skinning, stabbing motions and provide a barrier to the hand slipping forward into the blade. The rest of the grip, is nicely shaped to enhance your hold again without excess. The scales are G10 epoxy - amazingly tough and strong but light - with a perfect degree of abrasive crosshatching. One can easily open AND CLOSE it with one hand, something one might need to do when aloft striking the topsail in a squall and wondering what possessed you do do such a thing without a riggers knife on your belt. Yes, it's made in the USA but who cares; like my fine shotguns and tools, with some things, the world is one community.

title: Easy to set up, and very robust
text:
A great product. Last winter we lost a much beloved trampoline to extreme winds. I set out on a search for a product that could prevent the loss of the replacement trampoline. I found a number of products on various websites that could best be described as variations on a tent stake design. They offered stakes that were straight or U shaped, and I was very nervous that in a windy situation (especially with rain softened ground), that the stakes would just pull free. I was about to fashion my own solution using spiral dog stakes when I found this kit.

Suffice it to say that the components are sturdy and well made. They are packaged well, and the instructions are clear and easy to follow. However, what makes this a five star product is that it contains everything you need to create a stable tie down for a trampoline, and it contains enough anchors to tie it down for wind from any direction. The anchors are not trivial to "screw" into the ground. I did it on a day after heavy rains and still required a tool for leverage. This was reassuring, because it meant that they would hold fast when the ground dried, and would allow the straps to transfer load from the trampoline frame to the stakes and the ground effectively.

I was very pleased with the product, and would heartily recommend it.

UPDATE: This stakedown kit works very well. Since installing, we have had four windstorms with gusts over 20 mph, and the trampoline has stayed perfectly in place. Highly recommended.

title: Simple and sturdy
text: Easy to install over my disk brakes, instructions are perfectly clear and rack is study once mounted.  It is certainly not as flexible as the beam racks, but that is the price you pay for a much higher load capacity.

title: Really comfortable
text: I have both a road and mountain bike.  I am not a particularly serious biker, but enjoy riding both for recreation.  This saddle was significantly more comfortable than the stock Bontrager saddle that came with my Trek MB, both the front (reduction of the pressure point) and the back with the additional padding.  I would not consider this an adequate replacement for my road bike saddle, as it does get in the way a touch more than a traditional road saddle, but it is a good compromise for those wanting a more comfy saddle for long distance mountain or hybrid biking.

title: Great product design
text: Easy to set up, lightweight, and just enough adjustability for my needs.  I give this 5 stars with a slight caveat.  It has been nearly impossible for me to adequately cinch these down on trees (my primary setup) to prevent a significant (e.g. 1 foot) amount of sag in the hammock when I sit down.  They are very sturdy, but there is some slop in the initial setup.  Once I got used to this, it was no problem to start my initial setup a little higher.  There is a bit of zen hammock art to how to properly gauge the height of the straps, which strap point to anchor too and how far apart the trees should be to get the perfect hammock setup.  With time it comes naturally but at first it can be frustrating.

title: Comfort in the extreme
text: This hammock is, in a word, amazing.  I am a good sized guy (6'2", 220), and it has ample room for me to relax and sway in the breeze.  Easy to set up at home or camping, and really comfortable.  I was a little concerned that I would have a hard time getting it back into the stuff sack, but that was a misguided worry.  You don't even have to try very hard, simply grab the carabiners and roll and smoosh it into the sack, then cinch it down with the included strap.  Takes up almost no room in my backpack, and well worth the space.

title: Truly Mondo!
text:
A great product, certainly up to Topeak's standards. The pouch is huge and very roomy. It has a great side compartment to prevent your tools from beating up your snacks, and has a nice mesh pocket perfect for CO2 cartridges. Two caveats are worth considering. First, there is a temptation to stuff the main compartment full of stuff, and this is a great idea for a long ride. If you do so, it will require some unpacking to get to all of the gear, so pack the stuff you want to access quickly (e.g. food!) near the zipper. You can pack the tubes out of the way, if you blow one, you likely don't have a problem with the extra minute it takes you to get to it. The second issue to be aware of is that this pack is HUGE. Measure your bike to make sure that it fits, and make sure that you are happy with the look (it looks nothing like a wedge pack).

I was aware of both issues, and I love the pack! It lets me ride VERY long rides on my road bike without support and without a trunk bag.

title: Great Top Tube Pack
text:
This pack is a great top tube pack for having things close at hand. It has a pocket with a mesh covering (I don't know why), a pocket with a full nylon covering, and a small pocket for energy gels or a very small phone. It is very well constructed and holds my things nicely. The large pocket is big enough for a mountain bike inner tube (still in the box) and the smaller mesh pocket holds my iPhone and several Clif bars.

The velcro attachments to the front tube and the top tube cannot be made as tight as you might want. While I can understand the design constraints in making a product that must interface with all of the bikes on the market, I can't imagine how this would be for a thin tubed bike (it is a little loose on my mountain bike).

title: Fun toy
text:
I bought this bow and arrow set for my 3-year-old granddaughter. It is recommended for ages 4-8, so she’s a little young, and indeed it took her a bit of practice to master loading, drawing, and releasing an arrow. It’s been great training for both fine and gross motor skills.

The bow doesn’t have flexible limbs to power the arrows, like a traditional bow. Instead, it has rigid limbs and an elastic string that really does send the suction cup arrows sailing. Our favorite thing is shooting it at the sliding glass patio door. When the arrows fly true, they stick to the glass with a satisfying “splat”. We also like to shoot the stuffed chairs and sofa in the living room. We’ll shoot our bows outside once it warms up and some of the snow melts.

The bow has built-in LED lights that come on and start flashing when you grip the handle. That was an immediate hit with our toddler, and drew her to the bow right away. We mostly ignore that now. I don’t know how long the batteries will last but I expect that by the time they die, she will be more interested in sending arrows across the room than watching the flashing lights. Who knows - maybe this will be the start of a longer term interest in real archery.

Let me know if you found anything in my review helpful.

title: Good home fitness bike
text:
[[VIDEOID:bf4a381ea2346e023f15723581aa57ec]] This bike is easy to set up and adjust, and it has lots of features that make it a useful addition to my fitness program. I've uploaded a short video showing the adjustments and features, but I'll run thru them quickly here, too. Let me know if you find anything here useful.

You'll want to set the seat height so that your thigh) (hip to knee) is parallel to the ground at the top of the rotation. Then slide the seat back to where it's an easy reach forward to the handlebars without holding a lot of your weight there.

The tension on the pedals is adjusted by a big black knob just below the handlebars. There are also separate tensioned handles that you can pull to get an upper body (arms, shoulders, back, and abs) workout as you ride.

You can scroll through various screens on the electronic display. The best of these, in my opinion, is a heart rate monitor that reads your pulse while your hands are on the handlebar sensors. You can also get distance, time, and speed traveled. Its really a pretty capable machine, considering the low price.

This little bike folds up when not in use, so you can store it in a closet, lay it on the floor along a wall, or lean it in a corner. It isn't as beefy (or likely as durable) as one of the fancy spinning bikes at the gym, but this one is a lot more affordable, and meets my needs at home just fine. Check out the video, and let me know this was helpful.

title: Game changer for me
text:
I've used a mask and snorkel for fun, for at least the last 50 years, and spent over 20 years as a professional scuba diver, as part of my job. I've always used a traditional mask for snorkeling and diving, and have had my share of leaky seals, fogged glass, broken hardware, and mouthfuls of salty water. This new generation of full-face masks with an integrated snorkel really does represent a breakthrough, in several respects.

I was intrigued when I first saw integrated full-face snorkel masks like this one a few years ago, and have finally decided to give one a try. I'm glad that I did.

There are many design features that really do make this snorkel mask a game changer for me. I particularly like the separate, sealed compartments that separate your eyes/cheeks/forehead from your nose and mouth. This minimizes fogging that can be caused by inadvertently breathing into a traditional mask through your nose, making it hard to see in the water. It also keeps any water that leaks in around your chin away from the glass that you see through. That's important to me, because I have a beard that does sometimes let water leak into my mask.

The seal on this mask is a soft, doubled-over flap that does an admirable job. I have a thin face and it is often difficult to find a mask that seals well. This one does. And it does a surprisingly good job sealing over my beard, which I try to keep short.

The air comes in through the top of the mask, and travels through one-way valves to the lower chamber where your mouth and nose are. Exhalations exit through purge valves near your jaw. This system works well, but I wish that the air opening at the top of the mask, where the snorkel enters, was larger. It sometimes feels like I have to work too hard to get a big breath of air, which can lead to a feeling of claustrophobia and, for some users, I expect, panic. A bigger airway would probably alleviate this.

There is a place to install a go-pro style action camera, which I will be using for sure. It's a thoughtful addition that will simplify saving and sharing my adventures.

The snorkel has a float valve that keeps water from flooding the mask when you dive. This sort of valve is great for playing near the surface, but probably not reliable for deep diving.

You can't use this mask for scuba diving, because there's no way to get your regulator into your mouth. For regular snorkeling though, I have a new favorite mask!

title: Nice pocket heater with limited battery
text:
This is a useful hand warmer for those cold days. It is sized to fit in a pocket, and conveniently recharges with a USB outlet.

I've been using my hand warmer while hunting in the cold November rain. It turns on with a long press of the lone button near the top of the unit. There are 3 heat levels: 35, 45, and 55 degrees C. You can cycle through the 3 levels with short pushes of the control button. The unit heats up quickly, and the display switches automatically to show how much battery is left, once its up to temperature.

The battery, unfortunately, doesn't last very long. At full heat (55 degrees) you get about an hour or two. At the lowest setting, the heater will last longer, but it seems like that depends on how cold the air is where you are using it. If its really cold and you have the heater out and exposed to it, your battery will drain pretty quickly. It will last much longer indoors at room temperature. The lesson here is to keep the heater in your pocket when you can, rather than getting it out and holding it as it warms your hands. If you want it to last all day, turn it on when you need to warm up, then shut it off once you've knocked the chill off. If you only need it to last for an hour or two, to get you through a football game or something like that, you can just let it run.

The recharging port accepts a USB-C plug, the latest format. A charging cord comes with the heater, but there's no adapter to plug it into the wall. Most of us likely have an extra block or two around from our phones or other USB devices.

I wish that the heater was waterproof, or at least weather resistant, to be more useful in really crappy weather. The charging port, for example, is open to the weather so I usually keep the heater in a small ziplock bag when I'm using it in the snow or rain. It works OK that way.

If you haven't used up all the juice in the heater's battery, you can use it to recharge your phone or other USB device. That's a potentially useful utility. I haven't used mine that way yet, though.

The pocket-sized heater works best in a central pocket that you can reach with both hands, like the Joey pouch on the front of a pullover hoodie. If you don't have that, you have to either cradle it in both hands, outside your pockets, to warm both hands at once, or switch it from one pocket to another, to warm your hands one at a time. Another potential use is in the foot of your sleeping bag or bed, to warm your feet, but the heat won't last all night.

Electric heaters in general are notorious for demanding lots of energy. This little heater does produce a nice warm glow in your pocket, but it doesn't seem to have resolved the inherent inefficiency of electric heaters.

Please let me know if you found anything in my review helpful.

title: Fun tool for young adventurers
text:
[[VIDEOID:2187373aca733f879c0dd8e6a9bc255]] This a fun headlamp designed primarily for kids who like dinosaurs and adventure.

The LED lamp is housed inside a rather large plastic T. rex head. You turn it on by squeezing the open jaws together slightly. The moderately bright light comes on, the eyes light up red, and the dinosaur makes several loud roaring sounds (see attached video). Another squeeze of the jaws and the light turns off.

The adjusable headstrap is decorated with stylized reptilian footprints, in a color scheme that suggests lizard scales. There's a strap down the middle that rides on top of the wearer's head, in addition to the band that goes around your head, to support the weight of the dinosaur and its electronics.

I like that the unit comes with AAA batteries installed. Just pull out the plastic strip that keeps the unit shut off in its package, and it's ready to go. The original batteries probably won't last long, so plan to replace them, preferably with NiMH rechargeables, if you or your young explorers will be using the headlamp much.

This lamp is intended to be a functional novelty, something between a toy and a tool. It doesnt have the brightest light or the most durable housing, among available headlamps, and I'd advise against testing its ability to resist water, especially submersion. The roaring noise could be annoying if someone is trying to use the lamp in a dark room or tent when others are trying to sleep. I do wish that there was some way to turn off the sound. The sound effects may be useful, though, for parents keeping tabs on their young explorer's nighttime activities.

The colorful stripes and loud roar are fanciful embellishments that will likely appeal to young explorers, but I doubt that anyone would defend them as accurate or realistic. Neither of those features are preserved in the fossil record that we have for dinosaurs, so we probably can't say they are inaccurate, either. The thing is intended to fun. Just go with it.
